**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 9-13: broken passage; the sufferer resolves to renounce the god and roam**
- The despairing sufferer resolves to forsake home and possessions, trample the god's rites and roam the streets like a vagrant (Theod SB –:133-142)

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 14-19: the friend reproves; the sufferer on social inversion; wealth and poverty ordained**
- Long life is the god's to grant; wealth and poverty were fixed by the gods since days of old (Theod SB –:196-198)

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 20-24: the scoundrel will fall; god does not block the demon; firstborn and younger son**
- The sufferer observes that the god does not bar the way of a demon: evil is left free to roam (Theod SB –:243-244)
- The father hauls the boat while his firstborn lies in bed; the heir idles in the street while the younger son feeds the poor (Theod SB –:245-250)
- Saying: the cow's first calf is inferior, the next twice as big; the first child is a weakling, the second a warrior (Theod SB –:258-263)

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 25-27: society honours murderers; the gods gave humans lies; final plea**
- Society extols the powerful murderer and oppresses the powerless innocent: they call the wicked truthful, drive off the truthful, fill the oppressor's treasury and empty the poor man's larder (Theod SB –:267-275)
- The creator gods themselves gave humankind twisted speech, lies and falsehood forever (Theod SB –:276-280)
- Society extols the powerful murderer and oppresses the powerless innocent: they call the wicked truthful, drive off the truthful, fill the oppressor's treasury and empty the poor man's larder (Theod SB –:281-286)
- The sufferer protests his humility: he walked unobtrusively, did not raise his voice, did not hold his head high but looked at the ground (Theod SB –:291-294)

**The Story of the Poor, Forlorn Wren: the wren appeals to Šamaš against the eagle**
- A small weak bird (the wren) appeals to the sun god as just judge against the predatory eagle, and the god binds the eagle (Wren SB –:6-11, Wren SB –:23-26, Wren SB –:29-31)
- Moral: let the lofty no longer boast of their height nor the lowly lament their lowliness, for whoever has the god with him builds his nest and raises his young (Wren SB –:38-42)

**SAA 2 1: Treaty of Šamšī-Adad V with Marduk-zākir-šumi of Babylon (clauses and curses)**
- Curse: may the god pour out the oath-breaker's life like water (SAA 02 001 b.e:16'-19')

**SAA 2 8: Zakūtu (Naqiʾa), queen mother, imposes a loyalty oath for her grandson Ashurbanipal**
- The queen mother herself imposes a loyalty oath on the royal family and the whole land in favour of her grandson the king (SAA 02 008 o:1-11)

**SAA 2 2 iii-vi: Matiʾ-il's obligations, curses (famine, cannibalism, prostitutes, mule) and the divine witnesses**
- Curse: may the dung of oxen, donkeys, sheep and horses not be found in the land (livestock wiped out) (SAA 02 002 r.iv:7')
- Curse: may a city of a thousand houses be reduced to one house, a thousand tents to one, one man left in the city (SAA 02 002 r.vi:3-5)

**SAA 2 5: Esarhaddon's treaty with Baal, king of Tyre: deputy, shipwreck, ports, and curses by the gods of the West**
- An Assyrian royal deputy (qēpu) is set over the vassal: the vassal must heed him and may not open the king's letters without him (SAA 02 005 r.iii:6'-14')
- The overlord entrusts named ports and trade routes along the coast (Akko, Dor, Philistia, Byblos, Lebanon) to the vassal (SAA 02 005 r.iii:18'-30')
- Curse: may the storm gods (the Baals) raise an evil wind against the oath-breaker's ships, loosen their moorings, tear out their masts and sink them in the sea (SAA 02 005 r.iv:10'-13')

**SAA 2 14: Literary account of Esarhaddon's succession oath for Ashurbanipal and Šamaš-šuma-ukīn**
- The seven planets (bibbu) of heaven are themselves bound by, or cursed for, the king's oath (SAA 02 014 o.i:4-5, SAA 02 014 o.ii:2')

**SAA 2 13: Treaty with an Arab ruler: no peace with the enemy, no secret messages, report every hostile word**
- The vassal is bound to fear the overlord and do what is good for him (SAA 02 013 o.ii:5'-7')
- The sworn party must not send messages secretly, 'whether by the hand of a fish of the sea or a bird of the sky' (SAA 02 013 r.iii:1-3)

**SAA 2 15 v: the prince's brothers, succession at the king's death, no annulment rites, whole-hearted oath taught to sons, the sealed tablet**
- Formula: in future days the national god is 'your god' and the crown prince 'your lord'; your sons and grandsons shall fear him (SAA 02 015 o:393_T_v_58-395–396_T_v_60)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: seal of Aššur, preamble and divine witnesses (SAA 2 6:i-40B)**
- The sworn are adjured 'swear by X!' god after god, each line repeating 'ditto' (MIN) (SAA 02 006 o:25-40B)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: guard Assurbanipal, enthrone him, swear to no other king (SAA 2 6:41-72)**
- The sworn must guard the king or prince in the country and in the town, falling and dying for him if need be (SAA 02 006 o:49-51)
- The sworn must speak with the prince in truth of heart, give him good counsel with their whole heart and set a good way before his feet (SAA 02 006 o:51-54)
- The sworn must not change or alter the king's word (his designation of the heir) (SAA 02 006 o:57-58)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: report any evil word from kin, officials, prophets or anyone; protect Šamaš-šumu-ukin (SAA 2 6:73-122)**
- A seditious word from the mouth of a prophet (raggimu), an ecstatic (mahhû) or an inquirer of the divine word must be reported to the crown prince (SAA 02 006 o:116-119)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: do not harm the prince; seize and kill instigators; no conspiracy oath (SAA 2 6:123-161)**
- If the sworn cannot seize and kill the rebels themselves, they must inform the prince and stand with him (SAA 02 006 o:142-146)
- The sworn must not join conspirators who swear one another by setting up gods, a table, a cup, fire, water, oil and touching breasts (SAA 02 006 o:147-161)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: sieges, desertion, after the king's death, the palace coup and the false message (SAA 2 6:162-211)**
- If anyone revolts and the sworn are seized by force, they must not side with him but flee to the prince (SAA 02 006 o:173-179)
- The king (heir) is described as one who brings down the mighty and raises the lowly, kills whom he will and keeps alive whom he will (SAA 02 006 o:192-194)
- A messenger arrives unseasonably saying the king has summoned the prince ('your father has lifted your head'); the prince must not go until a loyal man has seen the king is well (SAA 02 006 o:198-211)
- Treaty provision for a revolt in the palace by day or night, on the road or in the land (SAA 02 006 o:198-202)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: no assembly to make a king, usurpers from royal kin, minority of heirs, the pregnant wife, poison and sorcery (SAA 2 6:212-265)**
- The sworn must not form an assembly, swear to one another and give the kingship to one of themselves (SAA 02 006 o:212-213)
- If the king dies while his sons are small and a courtier kills the heir and seizes the throne, the sworn must not serve him but kill him and enthrone the heir's son (SAA 02 006 o:237-248)
- The sworn must wait for the king's or prince's pregnant wife, raise the child when born and set him on the throne (SAA 02 006 o:249-253)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: love him as yourselves; slander and royal gifts; teach this treaty to your sons (SAA 2 6:266-301)**
- Fields, houses, orchards, people and livestock the king gave to his sons may not be taken from them (SAA 02 006 o:273-278)
- A word (the succession) is declared acceptable before gods and men, and the sworn are asked to accept it too (SAA 02 006 o:295-301)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: fight a usurper; resist incitement to set the prince against his father and brothers (SAA 2 6:302-372)**
- The treaty quotes the envious instigators' persuasive speech ('where is what the gods said about him? ... guard your lives') to forbid it (SAA 02 006 o:328-335)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: curses by the gods one by one (SAA 2 6:414-493)**
- Curse: may the high god not grant long days, old age and extreme old age (SAA 02 006 o:414-416)
- Curse: may the sky god rain illness, exhaustion, headache, sleeplessness and wailing on all your houses (SAA 02 006 o:418A-418C)
- Curse: may the goddess show you no mercy or favour (SAA 02 006 o:457-460)
- Treaty curses invoke western gods (Bethel, Anath-Bethel, Kubaba of Carchemish, Aramiš) alongside the Assyrian pantheon (SAA 02 006 o:466-471)
- Curse: may an irresistible flood come up from the earth and devastate you (SAA 02 006 o:488-489)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: the vassals' first-person oath and further curses by Aššur, Palil, Ea, Girra (SAA 2 6:494-525)**
- Curse: may the god of the deep give you water of death to drink and fill you with dropsy (SAA 02 006 o:521-522)
- Curse: may water and oil become taboo to you (SAA 02 006 o:523)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: analogical and simile curses I: iron earth and bronze sky to the stinking bug (SAA 2 6:526-611)**
- Curse: instead of rain may burning coals rain on your land (SAA 02 006 o:532-533)
- Simile curse: as these lambs are slit and their entrails rolled round their feet, so may yours and your children's be (SAA 02 006 o:551-554)
- Simile curse: as snake and mongoose do not share a hole but plot each other's death, may husband and wife not share house or bed (SAA 02 006 o:555A-559)
- Curse: as honey is sweet, may the blood of your wives and children be sweet in your mouth (SAA 02 006 o:568-569)
- Simile curse: may your flesh and your family's be consumed like the flesh of a chameleon (SAA 02 006 o:591-593)
- Simile curse: as a honeycomb is pierced with holes, may holes be bored in your flesh while you live (SAA 02 006 o:594-598)
- Curse: may you be like a fly in the hand of your enemy, who crushes you (SAA 02 006 o:601-602)

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: analogical curses II: bloody chariot to the overturned throne (SAA 2 6:612A-663)**
- Curse: may an evil fire surround you (SAA 02 006 o:621)
- Curse: may you be shaken like a reed-bed in water and pulled out like a reed from a bundle (SAA 02 006 o:630-631)
- Simile curse: as the inside of a hole is empty, may your hearts be empty (SAA 02 006 o:641-642)

**Love lyrics of Nabû and Tašmetu (SAA 3 14)**
- Confession of trust: 'let whoever trusts, trust (in his own); we trust in our god' (SAA 03 014 o:1-2)
- The lovers' meeting place is the shade of cedar, cypress and juniper (SAA 03 014 o:9-11)
- The beloved's body is praised part by part in similes (thighs a gazelle, ankles an apple, heels obsidian) (SAA 03 014 r:5-8)
- The lover wishes his eyes to see the plucking of her fruit and his ears to hear her birds' song (garden imagery for love) (SAA 03 014 r:20-21, SAA 03 014 r.e:30-32)
- The divine wedding of Nabû and Tašmetu is celebrated with the goddess taken to the cella and bed (SAA 03 014 o:6-8)

**Fragment on Elamite affairs and a eunuch (SAA 3 20)**
- A eunuch official carries out or is caught in a royal intrigue and crawls before the king (SAA 03 020 o:2'-5', SAA 03 020 r:10)

**Pasquinade against Bēl-ēṭir son of Ibâ (SAA 3 29)**
- The fool praises himself, speaks and boasts, and becomes a byword and taunt among the people (SAA 03 029 r:6-9)
- A mocking monument (stele) is set up 'forever' for a despised person (SAA 03 029 r:3-5)
- The demon Pazuzu son of Hanbi is named in an invective (SAA 03 029 r:2)

**Prophetic or scholarly blessing-address to Assurbanipal: gods at his right and left, propitious planets, cheap grain (SAA 3 25)**
- Formula: 'in your days, which the god loves', introducing good signs and blessings (SAA 03 025 o.i:9', SAA 03 025 o.ii:20', SAA 03 025 r.i:6'-7')

**Fragmentary address to Assurbanipal: Šamaš older than heaven and earth; 'do not fear battle' (SAA 3 26)**
- The god gives the king the face (radiance) of a lion (SAA 03 026 r:8'-9')
- The speaker declares 'I shall not be put to shame' (SAA 03 026 r:13')

**Dialogue between Assurbanipal and Nabû: 'Fear not, I will give you long life' (SAA 3 13)**
- A king's prayer and the god's answer alternate as a dialogue (SAA 03 013 o:1-r:11)
- Prayer: 'do not abandon me in the assembly of those who wish me ill; do not let my life fall into their hands' (SAA 03 013 o:2, SAA 03 013 o:6, SAA 03 013 o:20-22, SAA 03 013 r:4-5)
- The petitioner's life is written before the god (SAA 03 013 o:21)
- The goddess placed her four teats in the infant king's mouth: two he sucked, two he milked (SAA 03 013 r:6-8)
- The god promises the king that his feet will not tire, his hands not tremble and his lips not weary of praying (SAA 03 013 o:8-11)

**Fragment of a royal text about Nabû-bēl-šumāti and the goddess of Arbela (SAA 3 21)**
- The goddess who created the king grants him kingship and makes him proud over his opponents (SAA 03 021 o:1'-6')
- The rebel enemy is characterized as speaking lies (SAA 03 021 o:13'-14', SAA 03 021 r:3'-5')
- Hunting nets are spread for the king's enemies (SAA 03 021 r:7')

**Hymn to Nineveh and its goddess, with blessing for Assurbanipal (SAA 3 7)**
- The capital is hailed as a date palm and a stag of the lands (SAA 03 007 o:1-2)
- The goddess (Ištar of Nineveh) wears a beard like the high god Aššur (SAA 03 007 o:6)
- The goddess's tiara shines like the stars and sun-discs glow on her breast (SAA 03 007 o:7-8)
- On the goddess's festival she goes out in procession, the king enters with pure offerings and her chariot is harnessed (SAA 03 007 o:10-17)

**Hymn to Nanaya with blessing on Assurbanipal (SAA 3 5)**
- A hymn praising a deity is combined with blessings by several gods on the king (SAA 03 005 o:1-22)
- The king is called the priest (šangû) of the gods (SAA 03 005 o:4)
- All the lands hear of the goddess and tremble in fear (SAA 03 005 r:1-4)
- The goddess favours the king 'with all her heart' (SAA 03 005 o:11, SAA 03 005 o:20)

**Assurbanipal's hymn to Marduk: creation, the defeat of Anzû and Tiamat (SAA 3 2:1-44)**
- The god is a merciless storm and furious fire that burns up the enemy in battle (SAA 03 002 o:32-33)

**Assurbanipal's hymn to Marduk: prayer for appeasement; hymn to Zarpanitu (SAA 3 2:r 1-25)**
- Prayer that the god's furious heart rest and his angry liver be calmed and reconciled (SAA 03 002 r:12-14, SAA 03 002 r:20-21)
- A hymn ends with a subscript counting its lines and naming the deities praised (SAA 03 002 r:24-25)

**Assurbanipal's hymn to Aššur (SAA 3 1)**
- A hymn opens with the singer's resolve: 'let me magnify the god, make his greatness manifest, extol his name' (SAA 03 001 o:5-13)
- The god is creator of those of heaven and earth, fashioner of the mountains and creator of the gods (SAA 03 001 o:15-16)

**Hymn to Nanaya with blessing for Sargon II (SAA 3 4)**
- The goddess bears sword and axe, arrays battle right and left and goes before the seven warrior gods (SAA 03 004 o.i:2'-6')
- The goddess is wife of Nabû and beloved daughter-in-law of Bēl in Esagil (SAA 03 004 o.ii:1'-6')
- Refrain: the powerful, the exorcist, the physician, each 'whom she has not led' fails; apart from her who can do anything? (SAA 03 004 r.ii:1'-10')

**Incantation: a goddess asks her brother Adad for beauty and healing; women in labour (SAA 3 48)**
- A goddess refuses offerings of oxen, grain and sheep and asks instead for beauty, manliness and the gift of healing (SAA 03 048 o:10'-12')
- Healing rite: the patient's chest is rubbed with oil and a finger is put into his mouth (SAA 03 048 o:13'-b.e:17')
- In the house of the birth goddess pregnant women are in labour and weep (SAA 03 048 r:1-4)

**Elegy on a woman who died in childbirth (SAA 3 15)**
- A woman dead in childbirth is pictured as a boat adrift in midstream, its rope cut (SAA 03 015 o:1-4)
- The mother recalls her and her husband's joy in pregnancy, then her clouded face in labour and her death (SAA 03 015 o:5-8)
- A woman in labour prays to the birth goddess 'mother of those who give birth, save my life!' (SAA 03 015 o:9-12)
- Hearing the prayer, the deity veils her face and refuses help (SAA 03 015 o:11)
- Death creeps stealthily into the bedroom and takes the person from her house and husband (SAA 03 015 r:6)

**Literary letter of Ninurta to the king, with Assurbanipal's library colophon (SAA 3 47)**
- The god declares himself distressed, raging and angry and asks who will appease him (SAA 03 047 o:6-11)

**Mystical cultic commentary: the king's rites explained as Marduk's victory (SAA 3 37)**
- A rite is explained as the goddess lifting up the child god and kissing him (SAA 03 037 o:7'-8')
- The slain rebel gods are soaked in blood and dung, which is sprinkled over mountains and lands (SAA 03 037 o:13'-14')

**Letter of Aššur to Assurbanipal on the defeat of Šamaš-šumu-ukin (SAA 3 44)**
- Because of his evil deeds the rebel king's gods became angry, abandoned him and went aside (SAA 03 044 o:20-22)
- The god tears out the foundation of the rebel's throne and overthrows his reign (SAA 03 044 o:4)
- A historical disaster (siege famine, cannibalism) is presented as the god's punishment matching the treaty curses (SAA 03 044 r:8-10)
- The god breaks the enemy's bow and strengthens the king's bow (SAA 03 044 r:5)
- The king calms the god's heart, makes peace with him and is entrusted with renewing the gods and their shrines (SAA 03 044 r:19-25)
- The king sends the god a tablet of good news, joy and reconciliation (SAA 03 044 r:28-29)
- At the king's supplication the god stands at his side in battle and pours out the blood of his foes (SAA 03 044 o:28-29)

**Fragmentary letter of a god to Assurbanipal: Elam's nobles tremble (SAA 3 45)**
- Princes and governors kneel before the king and praise his heroism (SAA 03 045 o:5')
- The king constantly sets out offering arrangements and strews offerings before the god (SAA 03 045 o:11'-12', SAA 03 045 r:3')

**Fragmentary letter of Aššur to the king: chosen for shepherdship and sent with arrows (SAA 3 46)**
- The god sends the king out with strong weapons and burning arrows to fell the enemies (SAA 03 046 o:9-10)

**Fragmentary lament: wailing like an ecstatic; 'who taught you kingship?' (SAA 3 23)**
- Mourners holding their garments wail like ecstatics (mahhû) (SAA 03 023 o:2'-7')
- A mother sheds tears for her son (SAA 03 023 r:2)
- Question and answer: 'who taught you (kingship / this lament)?' 'her beauty, her weeping taught me' (SAA 03 023 r:4-6)

**Fragment: burning and prayer for Assurbanipal (SAA 3 27)**
- Fragmentary reference to burning in the cult of Marduk (SAA 03 027 o:2', SAA 03 027 r:2)

**Assurbanipal's prayer to Ištar of Arbela against Teumman and the victory (SAA 3 31)**
- The enemy king boasts that he will not rest until he comes and feasts in the midst of the Assyrian capital (SAA 03 031 o:5'-13')
- Hearing the enemy's insolence, the king opens his hands to the goddess in prayer: 'what is he against me?' (SAA 03 031 o:14'-17')
- The goddess answers the king's prayer with an oracle (SAA 03 031 o:18')
- The defeated enemy king and all his family are brought in neck-stocks before the goddesses and put to the sword (SAA 03 031 r:8-11)
- The conquered land is 'put to one mouth' (unified in submission), settled with Assyrians and given tribute (SAA 03 031 r:13-17)

**God's answering letter on the campaign against Der and the flight to Elam (SAA 3 41)**
- Fearing the god's awesome radiance, people abandon their cities and flee to save their lives (SAA 03 041 r:5-18)

**Hymn to Tašmetu and the procession of Nabû, with prayer for Assurbanipal (SAA 3 6)**
- Hymn to Tašmetu, wife of Nabû, praising her beauty, rank and intercession (SAA 03 006 o:1-7)
- A deity processes out of the temple on a fixed day each month (SAA 03 006 o:8-11)

**Mystical miscellanea I: the body of a god, Ištar as Tiamat, the three heavens and three earths (SAA 3 39:o)**
- Esoteric identification: Ištar of Nineveh is Tiamat and the wet nurse of Bēl, with four eyes and four ears (SAA 03 039 o:19-23)
- The king in his chariot with captured Elamite chariot and horses is explained as Ninurta with the corpse of Enmešarra and the ghost of Anzû (SAA 03 039 o:24-29)
- Three earths: the upper holds the spirits of mankind, the middle the god Ea, the lower the 600 Anunnaki (SAA 03 039 o:34-37)
- Each heaven is made of a different precious stone (luludānītu, saggilmud, jasper) (SAA 03 039 o:30-33)

**Mystical miscellanea II: Tiamat split like a dried fish, ghosts of the slain gods, secret colophon (SAA 3 39:r)**
- The circuits of the sun and moon are measured in double-hours; gods are said to be 'in' the sun and moon (SAA 03 039 r:4-5)
- Wild animals (onager, wolf, camel, gazelle) are explained as the ghosts or daughters of defeated gods (SAA 03 039 r:9-14)
- The god bound the defeated monster and showed it so that the people would not forget (SAA 03 039 r:15-16)

**Coronation hymn of Assurbanipal: 'Aššur is king!' (SAA 3 11)**
- The sun god raises the king to shepherdship of the four quarters (SAA 03 011 o:1-3)
- Blessing: may eloquence, understanding, truth and justice be given to the king as a gift (SAA 03 011 o:8)
- Coronation blessing: let the small speak and the great listen, the great speak and the small listen; concord and peace in the land (SAA 03 011 o:12-14)
- Whoever speaks lies or plots evil against the king: the important die by the weapon, the rich become poor, their foundation a storm, their hem chaff (SAA 03 011 r:9-14)
- Call to all the gods of heaven and earth to assemble and bless the king (SAA 03 011 r:15-18)

**Hymn in praise of Arbela and its goddess (SAA 3 8)**
- The holy city is high as heaven and its foundations firm as the heavens (SAA 03 008 o:14-16)
- A holy city is called the image of Babylon and the likeness of Assur (SAA 03 008 o:17)
- Produce and wealth of every land brought to a sacred city (SAA 03 008 o:18-19)
- Those who go out of the holy city and those who enter it rejoice (SAA 03 008 r:2'-4', SAA 03 008 r:18')

**Cultic calendar commentary: Marduk binds Anu, Qingu thrown from the roof (SAA 3 40)**
- Rite explained: Qingu and his sons were thrown from the roof; oil and honey on the effigies are their blood (SAA 03 040 o:3-4)
- The younger god binds the sky god Anu, cuts off his neck and takes the kingship (SAA 03 040 o:6, SAA 03 040 o:13-14, SAA 03 040 r:16-17)
- A leper sunk in the river in a rite is explained as the leprous god Anu (SAA 03 040 o:16)
- The victorious god flays the bound god's skin (SAA 03 040 o:22)

**The Marduk Ordeal I: Bēl held in the house of confinement, Nabû searches, Bēl prays for life (SAA 3 35:1-27)**
- The chief god is held captive in the 'house of confinement', beaten, his garment gathered in the dungeon (SAA 03 035 4, SAA 03 035 21, SAA 03 035 23)
- The captive god is taken to the river ordeal and questioned on its bank (SAA 03 035 7, SAA 03 035 20)
- A messenger of the gods brings the captive god out of his prison (SAA 03 035 5-6)
- The captive god becomes thirsty in fear and weeps; the hand-washing water is his tears (SAA 03 035 24, SAA 03 035 27)
- A guard-god denies involvement ('I am not a sinner'), and the high god declares him innocent (SAA 03 035 17-18)
- Pig offerings and reeds are laid on the road of the god coming from Borsippa (SAA 03 035 15)
- The exorcists going before the god reciting incantations are his people lamenting him (SAA 03 035 22)

**The Marduk Ordeal II: Enūma eliš recited, Zarpanitu prays, Bēlet-ilī at the grave, Ninurta defeats Anzû, curse colophon (SAA 3 35:28-72)**
- The head of the evildoer who counselled against the god is tied to the goddess's chariot (SAA 03 035 35-37)
- The goddess who raised (nursed) the captive god shows him compassion; milk is milked before her (SAA 03 035 39)
- News of the warrior god's victory is announced to all the gods, who rejoice (SAA 03 035 53-54)
- The dog that crosses Gula's temple is the messenger she sends around the city (SAA 03 035 62-63)

**Fragment naming Gilgameš, scribes and a goddess with writing reeds (SAA 3 49)**
- Gilgameš is named in a later literary or scholarly text (SAA 03 049 o:1, SAA 03 049 o:9)
- The palace of the herald of Assyria is mentioned in a literary text (SAA 03 049 o:7, SAA 03 049 o:10)

**Assurbanipal's hymn to the Ištars of Nineveh and Arbela: 'I knew no father or mother' (SAA 3 3)**
- The goddess has no rival among the great gods; her word is fire and firm forever (SAA 03 003 o:1-7)
- The king is the creation of the goddesses and their temples, his kingship made great since the House of Succession (SAA 03 003 o:8-12, SAA 03 003 o:23)
- The great gods guided the king like a small child and walked at his right and left (SAA 03 003 o:14-15)
- The king declares: not by my own strength nor the strength of my bow, but by the might of my gods I subdued the lands (SAA 03 003 r:4-6)
- Lands that never submitted to the king's fathers now bring tribute yearly and kiss his feet (SAA 03 003 o:20-22, SAA 03 003 r:7-10)
- The goddess is called the mother who bore the king (SAA 03 003 r:14-17)

**Fragment from a Sargonid epic: guards, horsemen, the bow of Elam (SAA 3 18)**
- The bow of Elam is broken (SAA 03 018 r:8'-12')
- Fragment of a literary account of an Assyrian king's campaign in the east (Elam, Ellipi, Anzan) (SAA 03 018 r:3'-14')

**Fragment: Assurbanipal trod the path of the sea; 'ask, ask!' (SAA 3 19)**
- The king treads the road of the sea and opens the gate of loyalty (SAA 03 019 o:3'-4')

**Epic fragment of Assurbanipal's Elamite war: Madaktu broken, graves violated, Nabû-bēl-šumāti (SAA 3 22)**
- In his anger the king breaks the enemy's royal city (SAA 03 022 o:7'-8')
- The graves of the enemy (Elamite kings) are violated (SAA 03 022 o:10')

**Fragment of a royal praise poem: Šamaš who does not accept slander; products from the upper sea, Tyre and Elam (SAA 3 28)**
- The sun god revives the righteous, does not accept slander and saves the wronged (SAA 03 028 o:7'-9')
- The few are turned into many (SAA 03 028 o:12')
- A catalogue of choice products (pomegranates, ghee, aromatics, oils) from distant lands (SAA 03 028 r:3'-15')

**Mock incantation against Bēl-ēṭir son of Ibâ (SAA 3 30)**
- An invective is framed as a mock incantation (beginning with the incantation rubric) (SAA 03 030 o:1)
- An invective quotes an obscene oath of its target (SAA 03 030 o:6-10)

**The Sin of Sargon: Sennacherib divines why his father died unburied (SAA 3 33)**
- The king ponders daily in his heart: who can understand the works of the gods? (SAA 03 033 o:1'-7')
- A king investigates by divination the sin for which his father died a bad death (SAA 03 033 o:10'-16')
- The diviners, divided into separate groups so they cannot confer, give the same answer 'with one mouth' (SAA 03 033 o:21'-22')
- The king's father sinned by honouring the gods of Assyria above the gods of Babylon and not keeping the treaty of the king of the gods (SAA 03 033 o:17'-19')
- Court scribes prevent the king from making the statue of a god, and his life is cut short (SAA 03 033 r:21'-23')

**Fragment of a mythological-ritual text: the Lady of Kidmuri, Aššur gives arrows to Lahmu (SAA 3 36)**
- A goddess presents herself: 'I am (the Lady of X), the great lady' (SAA 03 036 6'-7')
- The chief god draws arrows from his bow-case and has them given to a champion, telling him to set out (SAA 03 036 r:1-6)
- The god goes up in procession to Arbela (SAA 03 036 9'-15')

**Fragment of a divine letter: 'Which god is it who ...? Which king ...?' (SAA 3 43)**
- Rhetorical question in a divine letter: 'which god is it who ...? which king who ...?' (SAA 03 043 8'-9')

**Fragment of an invective: 'the bread of slander of your lips' (SAA 3 51)**
- A slanderer is rebuked for 'eating the bread of slander' with his lips (SAA 03 051 1'-6', SAA 03 051 r:1-4)

**Fragment: 'I am your god who guards you, the herald of the land' (SAA 3 52)**
- The deity declares: 'I am your god who guards you' (SAA 03 052 o:3')

**Divine love lyrics: the goddess loves Uruk, Babylon and the cult cities; their fires consume her (SAA 3 9)**
- Litany: the deity declares 'I love' each of a long list of cult cities and their gods (SAA 03 009 o:1-17)
- The love-sick deity says the fires of each city consume her (SAA 03 009 o:19-27, SAA 03 009 r:1-12)

**Underworld Vision: Ereškigal appears in a dream; Kummaya weeps like a dove (SAA 3 32 obv. 35-40)**
- The visionary wakes from the dream and moans like a dove (kīma summe idmum) (SAA 03 032 o:37)

**Underworld Vision: the fifteen hybrid gods of the netherworld (SAA 3 32 rev. 1-10)**
- In a vision of the netherworld the seer sees a row of gods and demons with composite bodies (lion, bird, ox, serpent-dragon heads; human hands, bird feet), each named (SAA 03 032 r:2-9)
- In the netherworld vision one young man, his body black as pitch and his face like the Anzu bird's, wears a red garment, holds a bow and sword and treads on a snake (SAA 03 032 r:10)

**Underworld Vision: before Nergal's throne; Išum intercedes; the prince is sent back (SAA 3 32 rev. 11-21)**
- The netherworld king (Nergal) sits on a royal throne with a crown, holding two fierce maces, lightning flashing from his arms, the Anunnaki kneeling right and left (SAA 03 032 r:11-12)
- The seer is seized by the forelock (abūsātu) and dragged before the enthroned god (SAA 03 032 r:13)
- Overwhelmed by the god's radiance, the seer trembles, kisses the god's feet and kneels (SAA 03 032 r:14)
- A divine adviser (Išum) intercedes with the angry god who wants to kill the seer: 'Do not let the young man die' (SAA 03 032 r:16)
- The angry god's voice roars over the seer like a raging storm (SAA 03 032 r:15)

**Underworld Vision: the dead king, Nergal's warning, the prince's terror and the scribe's report (SAA 3 32 rev. 22-35)**
- In the netherworld vision the seer is shown the corpse (pagru) of a great king, his own father, conqueror from sunrise to sunset (SAA 03 032 r:22-23)
- After the vision the seer runs into the street like a man who has shed blood, crying 'woe, my heart!' and putting dust of the street into his mouth (SAA 03 032 r:29-31)
- A scribe who hears the vision takes it to heart and reports it to the palace as a warning (namburbû) for himself (SAA 03 032 r:33-35)

**Epic of Shalmaneser III's campaign against Urartu (SAA 3 17)**
- Epic of an Assyrian king's campaign against Urartu: the enemy flees into mountains and forests, cities burned, booty taken, stelae set up on mountain and sea (SAA 03 017 o:14, SAA 03 017 r:6-25)
- Overwhelmed by the king's (or god's) terrifying radiance, the enemy abandons its cities and flees into mountains and forests (SAA 03 017 r:11-13)
- The conqueror sets up his image (stele) of power in the mountains and by the sea (SAA 03 017 r:22)

**A righteous sufferer's prayer to Nabû (SAA 3 12)**
- The sufferer protests that he is afflicted though he did not sin or act wrongly toward his god (SAA 03 012 o:4)
- The sufferer complains that old age overtook him before his time and lifted him onto his bed (SAA 03 012 o:11-12)
- The sufferer, made small, stretches his hands toward the poor and prays even to slave and slave-girl (SAA 03 012 o:15-17)
- Lament: on the people the god rains abundance; on me he rains poison and gall (SAA 03 012 r:7-8)
- The sufferer has reached the gate of death (abul mūti) and asks the god: why have you abandoned me? (SAA 03 012 r:10-11)
- The sufferer begs the god not to abandon him or shame him before the assembly of those who rejoice at his misfortune (SAA 03 012 r:11-13)
- By the god's breath (wind) the dead lives again (SAA 03 012 r:5, SAA 03 012 r:19)

**Cultic song of blessing on the Inner City (Assur) and Esarhaddon (SAA 3 10)**
- A litany-like blessing on the god's city and its king: may he enter and enter, oil poured on the head, wool beyond count, bread great and beer flourishing (SAA 03 010 o:14-21)

**Fragment of a Middle Assyrian royal epic: the Ahlamû and Naʾid-Šihu (SAA 3 50)**
- The enemy eats and drinks wine to drunkenness and is then attacked (SAA 03 050 o:24)
- The king weeps in his chariot, his eyes filled with tears (SAA 03 050 o:28)
- The king plunders nomadic raiders (Ahlamû-Aramaeans) of the steppe (SAA 03 050 o:21)

**Mystical cultic commentary: Ištar weeps for her brother, the flayed god, Orion, Dumuzi (Q009249, SAA 3)**
- A goddess weeps and wails for her slain brother god and sees his body, its blood flowing to the earth (Q009249 o:4-7)
- The victorious god treads on the neck of his insubmissive enemy (Q009249 o:10-11, Q009249 o:41-42)
- A defeated god is bound and flayed; his skin is put on a constellation (Orion) and his body handed to the Anunnaki (Q009249 o:18-27)
- Rites of the month Tammuz: day of lamentation, Dumuzi is questioned and goes up, roasted grain cast on him (Q009249 r:4-8)
- A god's body parts are equated one by one with plants, trees and substances (tamarisk his tuft, cedar his knee, myrrh his moisture ...) (Q009249 r:9-17)
- Colophon: the secret of the great gods; the knowing may show it to the knowing, the unknowing may not see it, taboo of the great gods (Q009249 r:20)
- A child or heir is hidden away (by parents or goddesses) to protect him from a killer (Q009249 o:28-31)

**The Marduk Ordeal: Bēl held captive, sought by the goddess, the criminal killed with him (SAA 3 34, obv. 1-33)**
- A criminal (bēl hiṭṭi) is held with the captive god and killed; his head is tied to the goddess's chariot (SAA 03 034 o:17, SAA 03 034 o:20-21, SAA 03 034 o:25-26)
- Milk is drawn before Ištar of Nineveh because she raised the god and showed him mercy (SAA 03 034 o:33)

**The Marduk Ordeal: Enūma eliš recited, Aššur before heaven and earth, Anzû defeated, the god freed; curse (SAA 3 34, obv. 34-76)**
- A goddess as wailing woman (bākītu) goes round the city lamenting (SAA 03 034 o:67)

**Prophecy for Assurbanipal: vision of a golden star (SAA 9 11)**
- In a vision the king or prophet sees a golden star and an offering table with bread (SAA 09 011 r:6-13)

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.1: Ištar of Arbela, through Issār-lā-tašiyaṭ (SAA 9 1 i)**
- The deity promises: the king's enemies will roll (writhe) or be laid down before his feet (SAA 09 001 o.i:8'-10', SAA 09 001 o.i:13'-14')
- The goddess promises to go before the king and behind him (SAA 09 001 o.i:22'-24')
- The deity asks: what wind has risen against you whose wing I have not broken? (SAA 09 001 o.i:6'-7')
- The goddess shares the king's distress: 'you in pain, I in woe; I rise, I sit' (SAA 09 001 o.i:25'-27')

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.3: rejoicing with the king, through Rēmūt-Allati (SAA 9 1 ii)**
- The goddess declares she rejoices with the king and calls on his city to rejoice (SAA 09 001 o.ii:11'-12')

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.4: Bēl, Ištar and Nabû speak, through Bayâ (SAA 9 1 ii)**
- Divine command: do not trust in man; lift your eyes and look to me (SAA 09 001 o.ii:27'-29')
- The scribal god Nabû, 'lord of the writing stylus', speaks in an oracle (SAA 09 001 o.ii:38')

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.6: midwife and wet-nurse; the golden chamber of heaven, through Issār-bēlī-daʾʾini (SAA 9 1 iii-v)**
- The goddess declares herself the king's great midwife and good wet-nurse (SAA 09 001 o.iii:15'-18')
- The deity keeps watch over the king from a golden chamber in mid-heaven, making a light of amber shine before him (SAA 09 001 o.iii:23'-29')
- The goddess holds the king by his lock of hair in the great heavens (SAA 09 001 o.iv:26-28)
- The deity promises smoke on the king's right and fire on his left (SAA 09 001 o.iv:29-32)
- With a furious dagger in her hand the goddess finishes off the king's enemies (SAA 09 001 o.iv:7-10)
- The deity declares 'I am your good shield' (SAA 09 001 o.iv:18-19)

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.7: the Lady of Arbela answers the queen mother, through Ahāt-abīša (SAA 9 1 v)**
- The king's mother complains to the goddess that she favoured others while her own son was left roaming the steppe (SAA 09 001 o.v:13-20)

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.9: former word fulfilled, sons and grandsons, through Lā-dāgil-ili (SAA 9 1 vi)**
- The deity asks to be praised when the day declines, with torches held before her (SAA 09 001 o.vi:14-18)
- The goddess fills the king's lap with good things (SAA 09 001 o.vi:3-6)

**Words of the Elamite god: the snake in the javelin (SAA 9 8)**
- A god announces 'I have come' and that he cut the snake inside the enemy's javelin, broke the javelin and will crush Elam (SAA 09 008 o:3-8, SAA 09 008 b.e:9, SAA 09 008 r:1-2)
- The god repeats his oracle several times (five or six times) (SAA 09 008 o:4)

**Covenant of Aššur 3.1: peace to heaven and earth and Esarhaddon; dominion east to west (SAA 9 3 i-ii)**
- Oracle opening proclaiming peace (šulmu) to heaven and earth, the temple, and the king (SAA 09 003 i:9-11)
- The king has no rival; he shines like the rising sun (SAA 09 003 ii:6-7)

**Covenant of Aššur 3.2: 'I heard your cry' from the gate of heaven; fire and stones on the rebels (SAA 9 3 ii)**
- The god hears the king's lament and from the gate of heaven sends fire down on the rebels (SAA 09 003 ii:10-17)
- The god rains (hail)stones of fire on the king's enemies on the mountain and fills the river with their blood (SAA 09 003 ii:19-23)
- The god acts so that people may see and praise him, recognizing that he is lord of the gods (SAA 09 003 ii:24-25)
- Traitors surround the king and he stands in their midst before the god rescues him (SAA 09 003 ii:10-12, SAA 09 003 ii:18)

**Covenant of Aššur 3.3: the covenant tablet brought in; the water of the oath (SAA 9 3 ii-iii)**
- A covenant (adê) tablet of the god is brought into the king's presence with oil, sacrifices and incense, and read before him (SAA 09 003 ii:26-32)
- The people are given water from a jar to drink, sealing a covenant ('you will drink this water and remember and keep the oath') (SAA 09 003 iii:3-15)
- Warning that once back in their towns eating bread they will forget the covenant (SAA 09 003 iii:7-11)
- People say of the deity that she is 'narrow' (stingy, mean) (SAA 09 003 iii:8)

**Covenant of Aššur 3.4-5: Ištar's complaint about her meal; rebels impaled, through Lā-dāgil-ili (SAA 9 3 iii-iv)**
- The deity collects the king's enemies like butterflies (or insects) (SAA 09 003 iii:23-24)
- The deity complains that the king has given her nothing: no banquet, no food or cup as in a temple, and demands bread and beer (SAA 09 003 iii:25-37)
- The deity sets out and treads the mountains under her feet (SAA 09 003 iv:10-12)

**Oracle to Assurbanipal through the prophetess Mullissu-kabtat: the nurse goddess (SAA 9 7)**
- The goddess rules the kings of the lands, shows them their borders and puts roads under their feet (SAA 09 007 o:12-13)
- The oracle uses an obscure word and then explains it in answer to the king's question 'what is ...?' (SAA 09 007 r:3-5)
- The deity embraced and protected the king in the crown prince's palace before his accession (SAA 09 007 o:6)

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.2: the good sailor; sixty gods at right and left, through Bayâ (SAA 9 2 i)**
- The goddess guides the king like a good sailor who brings the ship to a good quay (SAA 09 002 i:16'-17')
- The deity goes round about the king and keeps watch over him (SAA 09 002 i:18'-20')

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.3: bird over its young, the good puppy, 'I am the speaker and doer', through Lā-dāgil-ili (SAA 9 2 i-ii)**
- The goddess roams the king's palace like a good puppy, sniffing out his enemies (SAA 09 002 ii:9'-11')
- The deity declares mankind treacherous (untrustworthy) (SAA 09 002 ii:17')
- The deity declares herself 'the speaker and the doer' (qābītu ēpištu) whose word is carried out (SAA 09 002 ii:18')

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.4: 'I see and I hear'; Elamites, Manneans, Urartians, through Urkittu-šarrat (SAA 9 2 ii-iii)**
- The deity says: I see and I hear, I search out the disloyal and put them in the king's hand (SAA 09 002 ii:29'-33')
- The people complain 'when, when will the land change?' (SAA 09 002 iii:7'-10')
- The deity tells the king to keep silent while she acts for him (SAA 09 002 iii:11')
- The deity asks 'who is alone, who is wronged?' implying she defends the wronged (SAA 09 002 iii:16')

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.5-6: 'I am your father and mother'; Urkittu, between my arms (SAA 9 2 iii-iv)**
- The deity tells the king 'I am your father and your mother; I raised you between my wings' (SAA 09 002 iii:26'-27')

**Oracle: Mullissu heard the cry of her calf; Ninurta at the king's right and left (SAA 9 5)**
- The goddess is told (or tells herself) to gird her loins for the king's defence (SAA 09 005 4)

**Oracle to Assurbanipal through Dunnaša-āmur: the goddess roams the steppe for his life (SAA 9 9)**
- The goddess, longing for the king's life, roams the steppe, crosses rivers and seas and mountains, exhausted and sleepless for him (SAA 09 009 o:8-15, SAA 09 009 o:25)
- The goddess speaks for the king's life and good in the assembly of all the gods (SAA 09 009 o:16, SAA 09 009 o:23-24)

**Record of a rite in the Aššur temple, Sargon II year 9: the basalt seat, the sacrificial table and the scribes' portions (SAA 20 55)**
- Ritual record: a new throne or furnishing is brought into the temple; a mistake in procedure is reported to the king (SAA 20 055 o:3-5)
- A damaged altar or sacrificial table is repaired and rededicated with offerings and new plaster (SAA 20 055 o:7-18)
- Particular cuts of the sacrifice are assigned to named officiants (scribe, priest, cook) to eat (SAA 20 055 r:12'-14')
- Remains of the sacrifice are thrown into the river (SAA 20 055 r:10'-11')

**Assur cultic calendar: gods at Aššur's right and left at the akītu; the chariot procession (SAA 20 53 obv.)**
- White horses draw the god's chariot in the procession (SAA 20 053 o.i:20')

**Assur cultic calendar: seating in the Dagan temple tested by oracle; baths and drums of the gods (SAA 20 53 rev.)**
- A god stands at the prow of a boat and ferries the gods of the land across before him (SAA 20 053 r.vi:14'-15')

**Fragment of a royal ritual: gods enter the palace, priests in sedan chairs (SAA 20 5)**
- Priests of the gods are carried in sedan chairs (ša-šadādi) in procession (SAA 20 005 r:7-9)
- A roasted kid is offered and a vat opened when the god sits at the city gate (SAA 20 005 o:8'-9')

**Fragment of a royal ritual: mouth-washing on the 23rd; the king in the Dagan temple (SAA 20 6)**
- The mouth-washing rite (mīs pî) is performed for divine images (SAA 20 006 o:1)
- The king presents censer and torch before the god (SAA 20 006 o:2-4)

**Middle Assyrian coronation ritual: 'Aššur is king!'; the crown blessing (SAA 20 7 i-ii)**
- In the coronation procession the priest cries 'Aššur is king! Aššur is king!' (the god, not the man, is king) (SAA 20 007 i:26'-29')
- The king is carried on a chair on men's necks (shoulders) to the temple (SAA 20 007 i:26', SAA 20 007 ii:43-49)
- In a royal ritual the priest strikes the king's cheek (reading disputed) (SAA 20 007 i:28')
- The king lays gifts (gold, silver, garment, oil) at the feet of the god (SAA 20 007 i:32'-37')
- A stone (bead) and a sheep are given as gift to each god of a long list (SAA 20 007 i:41'-46', SAA 20 007 ii:1-13)
- Blessing at coronation: may the gods crown you for a hundred years, widen your land under your sceptre, give you truth and peace (SAA 20 007 ii:26-36)

**Middle Assyrian coronation ritual: enthronement, gifts, the officials lay down their staffs; offerings to all gods (SAA 20 7 iii-iv)**
- The officials bring greeting-gifts (šulmānu) to the newly enthroned king (SAA 20 007 r.iii:4-8)
- At the coronation the officials lay their staffs of office before the king and are told 'let each hold his office' (SAA 20 007 r.iii:8-14)

**Ritual in the Bit-Eqi of Ištar: offering to 'Mouth-and-Tongue' and the charge to keep Ištar's secret (SAA 20 29)**
- 'Mouth-and-Tongue' (Pû-lišānu) is a minor god who receives offerings and speaks good words to the goddess (SAA 20 029 o:2-9)
- A model of a womb (sassurtu) in metal is offered to a deity (SAA 20 029 o:8-9)
- The initiate is charged to guard the goddess's word and secret: whoever divulges it will not live (SAA 20 029 o:14-15, SAA 20 029 r:5'-7')
- Blessing with a torch: as this torch is bright, may the goddess decree brightness and well-being for you (SAA 20 029 o:12-13, SAA 20 029 r:3'-4')
- The priest blesses the offerer at the end of the sacrifice (SAA 20 029 o:10-11)

**List of temple doorkeepers, images and courts: the Papahu holy of holies and the Apsû court (SAA 20 43)**
- A court or basin of the temple is called Apsû, the cosmic sweet-water deep (SAA 20 043 7')

**Fragment of a ritual: Dais of Destinies, the chief priest, Neberu (SAA 20 35)**
- The planet Jupiter as Nēberu is named in a royal ritual (SAA 20 035 o:9')

**Assurbanipal's new rites of Shebat-Adar: the king kisses the ground; 'Šeruʾa has given birth!' (SAA 20 9)**
- A king institutes new rites (parṣū eššūtu) for set days of the calendar (SAA 20 009 o.i:1-4)
- A female musician announces as good news that the goddess has given birth, crying it three times (SAA 20 009 r.iii:22'-24')
- A priest carries a torch through the city crying 'may the city shine, may the wall shine' (SAA 20 009 o.ii:19-22)

**Assur ritual compendium: gods at Aššur's right and left; provisions; Ištar's akītu; the Sarrānu dance (SAA 20 52 obv. iv-v, rev. i)**
- The copyist marks the breaks in his damaged original with 'broken' (hepi) (SAA 20 052 r.i:3'-12')
- Cultic performers (Sarrānu) raise their arms three times before the god and dance a dance (SAA 20 052 r.i:31'-39')
- At the festival the whole city enters the god's bed-chamber house (SAA 20 052 r.i:40'-42')
- Rule: libations before one goddess are not poured while the chief goddess is seated (SAA 20 052 r.i:20'-22')
- The Seven (Pleiades) are given food offerings in the ritual (SAA 20 052 r.i:28'-29')

**Assur ritual compendium: baths and drums; bowls set by the stars; oracle queries 'good / not good' (SAA 20 52 rev. ii)**
- Bowls of water are set out at night by the position of named stars, timing the king's entry into the temples (SAA 20 052 r.ii:20'-31')
- The chief god's old cloaks are used to cover other divine images (SAA 20 052 r.ii:41'-43')
- Women dance around (surround) the god before his statue at the 'Gate of Heaven' (SAA 20 052 r.ii:49'-52')

**Assur ritual compendium: incense burners tested; names of Aššur's gates; stars identified as Aššur (SAA 20 52 rev. iii)**
- The gates of the temple bear names (Gate of Kingship, Gate of Sunrise, Gate of Heaven, Gate of the Igigi, Gate of the Wagon star) (SAA 20 052 r.iii:43'-51')
- Stars and planets are identified with gods, and several constellations with the high god himself (Jupiter is Sîn, and Sîn is Aššur) (SAA 20 052 r.iii:55'-60')
- A goddess's statue is to be veiled with the same cloth as her companion goddess (SAA 20 052 r.iii:52'-54')

**Assur ritual compendium: Sargon's provisions to the tomb; positions of Sennacherib's gods fixed by extispicy; the queen may enter before Aššur (SAA 20 52 rev. iv)**
- Provisions decreed by a dead king are carried daily to the royal tomb (SAA 20 052 r.iv:1'-4')
- The relative positions of the gods' statues in the temple are fixed by extispicy and by public opinion (SAA 20 052 r.iv:5'-26')
- Truth (Kittu) and Justice (Mīšaru) are deities attending the sun god (SAA 20 052 r.iv:45')
- Ruling (by oracle) that the queen may enter the Strong House before Aššur whenever she wishes (SAA 20 052 r.iv:52'-54')

**Assur ritual compendium: extispicy, Mullissu's offerings; 'Šeruʾa, wife of Aššur' sung (SAA 20 52 rev. v)**
- Extispicy finds the liver of the king's seed (offspring) sound (SAA 20 052 r.v:5'-12')
- A goddess is hymned as the wife of the high god (Šeruʾa wife of Aššur) (SAA 20 052 r.v:55'-56')
- The head of a sea creature is brought into the temple in the festival (SAA 20 052 r.v:47'-49')

**Royal ritual for days 23-25: the king goes down to the temple, sacrifices, raised-hand prayer (SAA 20 3)**
- The king lifts up a 'raised-hand' (šuʾila) prayer before the deity (SAA 20 003 r:7)
- The calendar notes a day on which the king does not go down to the temple (SAA 20 003 r:9-10)

**Ritual of Ištar and the bed: ribs, seven jars of wine and beer, head and feet (SAA 20 20)**
- A rite is performed before the god's or goddess's bed (mayyālu) (SAA 20 020 i:2'-5')
- Seven jars of wine and seven of beer are poured out in libation (SAA 20 020 i:14')
- Heads and feet (trotters) of the sacrificial animals are offered with bread, wine and beer (SAA 20 020 i:8'-9', SAA 20 020 i:17'-18')
- Nine ribs of the sacrificial animal are slit and laid out (SAA 20 020 i:12'-13')

**Ritual of the Daughter of the River: the 'man of judgment', the lamb dressed as a bride, the seven Judges (SAA 20 32)**
- In the ritual the singer pronounces the formula of guilt ('lord of sin') twice and thrice (SAA 20 032 o:5-6)
- An unmated ewe-lamb is tied at the head of a bed in a tent by the river and dressed as a bride with white garment, earrings and bracelets (SAA 20 032 o:9-19)
- The blood of the substitute lamb from the bed is carried into the river (SAA 20 032 r:15-16)
- The feet of the person under judgment are washed with water and beer (SAA 20 032 r:10)
- The penitent declares 'I am released from the hand of my god' (SAA 20 032 r:22)

**Rituals of Ninittu and Kulittu: offerings poured into a pit; the king sets his foot on it (SAA 20 19)**
- Blood, honey, oil, beer and wine are poured into a pit (apu) dug for the rite (SAA 20 019 r.i:10'-12', SAA 20 019 r.ii:25'-28')
- The king puts his foot on the filled pit and kisses (the ground at) his foot (SAA 20 019 r.ii:29'-30')
- The deified fire (Lisikutu) is 'fed' with meat and bread (SAA 20 019 r.i:16'-17', SAA 20 019 r.ii:21'-22')
- After the rite the people are cleared away and the king enters the bed-chamber (SAA 20 019 o.ii:10-11)
- Honey and oil are burned as offerings (SAA 20 019 o.i:14, SAA 20 019 o.ii:27, SAA 20 019 r.i:8')

**Tākultu of Aššur-etel-ilani, obverse - the gods, temple and its parts bidden to drink**
- In the divine banquet (tākultu) the gods of the pantheon are called one by one by name and each is bidden 'drink!' (SAA 20 042 o.i:1-6)

**Tākultu of Aššur-etel-ilani, reverse - land, rivers, cosmos invoked; blessings for the king who gave the meal**
- The king is blessed to exercise priesthood and kingship together (SAA 20 042 r.iv:13')

**Royal ritual - entry to the akītu-house, blood offered into the spring, offerings before the gods of heaven and earth**
- A cultic performer (assinnu) lifts weapons and shouts before the goddess (SAA 20 015 o.i:6'-7')
- Sacrificial blood is offered into a spring, fish and crab are placed in it, and oil, honey and wine poured in (SAA 20 015 o.i:8'-12')

**Royal ritual - a message and a seal received before Aššur and Nergal; colophon of the priests of Aššur**
- A royal message or seal arriving from the road is carried in a cart, seated before the god and honoured with a sacrifice (SAA 20 015 r.iii:1-11)

**Assur temple ritual - Aššur and the gods go to Bīt-Dagan; offerings in the palace courtyard; mouth-washing on day 23**
- A mouth-washing (mīs pî) ritual is performed in the temple (SAA 20 001 r:25)

**Assur temple ritual, day 8 - the king kisses the ground, the god goes to Bīt-Adad, incantations recited**
- The exorcists recite named Sumerian incantations as the king and the god pass in procession (SAA 20 011 r:4-5)

**Assur temple ritual, days 17-21 - sacrifices before the god's weapons and chariot, the god seated on the Dais of Destinies**
- At the end of the rite the king gives gifts to the priest and temple staff (SAA 20 010 o:8, SAA 20 010 r:2, SAA 20 010 r:11)

**Ritual before Aššur and the Lady of the Mountain - libations, rams, kispu, dust on the king's head, dancing loaves**
- The king puts earth on his own head during a rite (SAA 20 021 o:16)

**Nisan ritual at the temple of Assyrian Ištar - early-morning and evening rites, singers, colophon**
- The king rises early and goes to the temple at dawn, and again at evening (SAA 20 017 o:1-2, SAA 20 017 o:6-8)

**Ritual for Gula and Šarrat-ēqi - the banquet hosts, exchange, hair burned, kispu, cakes before Šamaš**
- The participant's hands and feet are anointed with fine oil in the rite (SAA 20 030 o:1'-2')
- The hosts of the cult banquet pray that the goddess give well-being, life, name and seed (SAA 20 030 o:6'-8')
- A person is declared to be 'of the exchange' (pūhu), a substitute in the rite (SAA 20 030 o:10'-11')
- A tuft of hair is cut from a participant's head and thrown into the fire (SAA 20 030 r:14'-15')

**Duties of the Aššur temple personnel - who bears responsibility for what**
- The temple is fanned and cleaned from the foot of the dais to the foundation and from the gate to the threshold (SAA 20 050 o.ii:14-15, SAA 20 050 o.ii:20-21)
- The garments and ornaments of all the gods are inspected and kept by a temple official (SAA 20 050 o.ii:9-10)
- The temple scribe inspects and receives the votive gifts brought to all the gods (SAA 20 050 r.i:10'-13')

**Cups established by Shalmaneser; officials and priests of the Aššur temple; an order of Sennacherib**
- A list of the temple's officials and priests of each god, in order of rank (SAA 20 051 o.i:5-18, SAA 20 051 r.ii:1'-14')
- A king's order on temple personnel and practice is quoted (SAA 20 051 r.i:1'-10')

**Calendar of laments (eršemma) and hand-lifting prayers for Aššur and Mullissu, Šabāṭ-Addar to Nisan**
- A calendar assigns a named lament to be sung to the god after the sacrifices on each day (SAA 20 012 o:2'-24', SAA 20 012 o:27'-34')
- A 'hand-lifting' prayer (šuilla) is assigned by its incipit to a deity in the ritual programme (SAA 20 012 o:25'-26', SAA 20 012 r:17-18, SAA 20 012 r:25-26)
- The king is made to recite a penitential psalm (eršahunga) to the bronze kettle-drum (SAA 20 012 o:35'-36')

**Laments and penitential psalms of Aššur 'for removing the enemy', day by day to each god**
- Laments and penitential psalms are performed before the gods so that the enemy may be removed (SAA 20 013 o:1)

**Funerary ritual for a royal woman - the bed displayed, feet washed, cedar burned, tables for Antu, Gilgameš and the boatmen**
- The dead person's bed is set up and the body displayed; the feet are washed and mourners go round the bed three times (SAA 20 034 o:1-6, SAA 20 034 o:15-21, SAA 20 034 o:28-b.e:31)
- A ram's heart in flour is placed in the middle of the effigy of the dead (SAA 20 034 o:7-9, SAA 20 034 o:21-23)
- At the burial the name of the dead is called out (SAA 20 034 r:2)
- A boat of flour is broken with a dagger and oil and honey poured into it at a burial (SAA 20 034 r:6-8)
- The palace women cry 'come!' to the dead woman and the mourners seal themselves with blood from their noses (SAA 20 034 r:9-11)
- At a burial tables are set before Antu, Gilgameš and the boatmen of the netherworld journey (SAA 20 034 r:12-16)
- Kneeling before the sun god, mourners declare the dead woman 'girded and released' and ask blessing for the king and his seed (SAA 20 034 r:17-20)

**Tākultu (Assur version) - blessings for the king; gods of Esagil; sacrifices before the stars; colophon of the chief scribe**
- The king sacrifices before the stars and planets, named one by one (SAA 20 040 r.vi:15'-28')

**Ritual of Šarrat-nipha - the goddess brought to the bath-house**
- The goddess's image is brought into a bath-house, a ritual bath (rinku) is set up and she comes out of it (SAA 20 022 o:11'-17')

**Ištar ritual - the king's meal before the goddess, the sīru brought in and led seven times by the singers**
- A performer is brought before the goddess, given beer on a lion's head, and the chief singers walk before him seven times (SAA 20 016 o.i:14'-25')
- The king 'strokes his nose' (labān appi), the gesture of humble prayer (SAA 20 016 o.i:26')

**Tukulti-Ninurta's rite for the Lady of the River - tent on the bank, metals, strewn offerings and hymns to each god**
- A named king establishes and gives a rite to his deity (SAA 20 025 o:1-3)
- One mina each of iron, lead, gold, silver, bronze, tin and glass is laid out in a ritual (SAA 20 025 o:13-14)
- Fatty tissue (himṣu) and roast portions are presented before each deity (SAA 20 025 o:46'-48', SAA 20 025 o:51')

**A rite led by the singer for the sacrificer - seated on fleeces, hands bound, offering graded by rank**
- A singer (nāru) leads the rite, singing named hymns, washing hands and offering water to the sun god (SAA 20 031 o:6', SAA 20 031 o:15'-17', SAA 20 031 o:22'-24', SAA 20 031 r:5, SAA 20 031 r:9, SAA 20 031 r:18-20)
- The sacrificer is seated on fleeces laid fourfold beneath, at head and feet, his hands bound with red wool, and released after the rite (SAA 20 031 o:18'-21', SAA 20 031 r:1-2)
- The offering depends on the offerer's rank: a prince burns a turtledove, a commoner roasts a sheep's heart (SAA 20 031 r:6-8)
- A hymn to the sun god as 'opener of darkness' who treads down the wicked is sung (SAA 20 031 o:10', SAA 20 031 o:22')

**Protocol of the king's banquet - officials' entry, braziers, towels, hand-water, torches at sunset, the cups**
- The protocol of the royal banquet: officials enter in order, kiss the ground, report, tend braziers, towels, hand-water, torches and cups (SAA 20 033 o.i:1-19, SAA 20 033 r.i:32-52)
- In the cold month palace servants watch the brazier, put back fallen embers and add or remove fire and wood (SAA 20 033 o.ii:7-15)
- The dishes of the royal meal are listed: meats, fowl, turtledoves, jerboas (SAA 20 033 r.i:30-31)

**War ritual - the god-impersonators face the enemy, the king bends the bow before Šamaš, arrows shot, the enemy conquered**
- Performers representing gods (sarrānātu) set their faces against the enemy, murmur and dance (SAA 20 018 o:10-18)
- In a war ritual the king bends the bow before the sun god, takes and kisses an arrow, arrows are shot into the enemy figure, and the king 'conquers his enemy' (SAA 20 018 o:22-49)
- After the ritual victory the king hangs the great drum on his shoulder and goes before the gods (SAA 20 018 o:29, SAA 20 018 o:51-52)
- After the ritual conquest the king enters his camp, a meal is set and the king rejoices (SAA 20 018 o:54-56)

**Ritual fragment - the king carried in the sedan chair, sacrifice before Bēlet-balāṭi**
- The king is carried in a sedan chair (ša-šadādi) during the rite (SAA 20 004 ii:5', SAA 20 004 ii:7')

**Tukulti-Ninurta I's nāṭu rite for the Lady of the Mountain, in a tent by the river (SAA 20 24)**
- A tent is pitched on the river bank with its door facing the sun for a royal rite (SAA 20 024 o:3)
- A rite asks that the heart of a man's angry god and goddess be 'loosened' and his evil released; the angry protective spirit of the house is reconciled (SAA 20 024 r:7-10)

**Tukulti-Ninurta I's rite for Nusku in the temple of Sîn (SAA 20 27)**
- Part of the rite is performed on the roof before the sun god, with oil and a censer lifted up (SAA 20 027 r:33'-34')

**Fire rite before Aššur on the evening of the 16th (SAA 20 8)**
- On a set evening fire is kindled in the temple and a ram is burnt on a brazier before the god (SAA 20 008 4'-7', SAA 20 008 10'-11')
- A bed is set up for the god in a rite (SAA 20 008 13')

**Divine directory of Assur, part 1 (gods in the Aššur temple and the other temples) (SAA 20 49)**
- A statue of a king stands among the divine images in a temple (SAA 20 049 12, SAA 20 049 57, SAA 20 049 60, SAA 20 049 80)
- Justice (Mišaru) and Truth (Kittu) are worshipped as gods with places in a temple (SAA 20 049 24, SAA 20 049 28, SAA 20 049 34-42, SAA 20 049 65, SAA 20 049 71)
- Named gods serve as the divine gatekeepers of a temple (SAA 20 049 44-48)

**Divine directory of Assur, part 2 (gates, city guardians, temple names, ziggurats, colophon) (SAA 20 49)**
- The gates of a city each bear a sentence-name praising a god or the king (e.g. 'Aššur subdues the rebels') (SAA 20 049 120-133, SAA 20 049 191-196)
- A list gives each temple's Sumerian ceremonial name with an Akkadian rendering ('House of life', 'House of the secret of heaven and earth') (SAA 20 049 144-185)
- The ziggurats of a city are listed by their ceremonial names and gods (SAA 20 049 186-188)

**Nabonidus' impiety, Marduk's anger and pity, and the call of Cyrus (Cyrus Cylinder 1-19)**
- An impious king makes a counterfeit of the chief temple, introduces improper rites, stops the regular offerings and ends the fear of the chief god (Cyrus II 01 3-8)
- The tyrant ruins his own city's people under a corvée yoke without rest, daily (Cyrus II 01 8)
- The people's complaint (tazzimtu) reaches the chief god, who becomes furious at the ruler (Cyrus II 01 9)
- The god surveys all the lands looking for an upright ruler after his own heart (Cyrus II 01 11-12)
- The god takes a foreign king by the hand, calls his name and names him to rule the whole world (Cyrus II 01 12)
- The god makes whole peoples bow at the feet of his chosen king (Cyrus II 01 13)
- The god goes at the king's side like a friend and companion on his march (Cyrus II 01 15)
- The king's army is as countless as the water of a river (Cyrus II 01 16)
- The conqueror enters the enemy capital without battle or fighting, by the god's will (Cyrus II 01 17)

**Cyrus' titles, peace in Babylon, return of the gods and peoples (Cyrus Cylinder 20-36)**
- The new king relieves the city's weariness and frees its people from an unfitting yoke (Cyrus II 01 25-26)
- All the kings of the west (Amurru), from the upper to the lower sea, including those who live in tents, bring heavy tribute (Cyrus II 01 29-30)

**Offerings increased, the Imgur-Enlil wall rebuilt, Ashurbanipal's inscription found (Cyrus Cylinder 37-46)**
- Geese, ducks and turtledoves are offered daily to the gods (Cyrus II 01 37-38)
- The king sets up great cedar doors bound with bronze in the city or temple gates (Cyrus II 01 42-43)
- While rebuilding, the king finds an inscription of an earlier king and honours it (Cyrus II 01 43)

**First campaign against Merodach-baladan and the Arameans (Sennacherib 22 i 20-64)**
- A list of Aramean and Arab tribes (Hagaranu, Nabatu and others) conquered together (Sennacherib 022 i:43-49)
- From a conquered district the king fixes a perpetual yearly offering of first-fruits (oxen, sheep, wine, dates) for his gods (Sennacherib 022 i:61-64)

**Second campaign to the Kassites, Ellipi and the Medes (Sennacherib 22 i 65 - ii 36)**
- The king settles peoples from other conquered lands in a captured city and puts it under his governor (Sennacherib 022 ii:1-5, Sennacherib 022 ii:30-31)
- The king has a stela inscribed with his victory set up in the conquered city (Sennacherib 022 ii:7-10)

**Third campaign, part 1 - Lulî of Sidon, the tribute of the western kings, Ṣidqâ of Ashkelon (Sennacherib 22 ii 37-72)**
- A rebel king is deported with the gods of his father's house, his wife, sons, daughters and brothers (Sennacherib 022 ii:60-64)
- Coastal cities of Philistia (Joppa, Bene-berak, Azor, Beth-Dagon) are captured (Sennacherib 022 ii:68-72)

**Third campaign, part 2 - Ekron, the Egyptians at Eltekeh, Hezekiah shut up in Jerusalem (Sennacherib 22 ii 73 - iii 49)**
- Rebels put their loyal, treaty-bound king in iron fetters and hand him over to a hostile neighbouring king (Sennacherib 022 ii:73-77)
- The conqueror kills the guilty officials and deports the sinners, but releases the rest who bore no guilt (Sennacherib 022 iii:8-14)
- The invader besieges and takes forty-six walled cities of Judah and countless villages (Sennacherib 022 iii:18-23)
- The besieger throws up fortifications around the city and blocks anyone leaving its gate (Sennacherib 022 iii:29-30)
- Cities taken from a rebel are cut off and given to loyal neighbouring kings, so his land is diminished (Sennacherib 022 iii:30-34)
- The troops brought in to strengthen the besieged capital desert or leave (Sennacherib 022 iii:39-41)
- The besieged king sends gold, silver, precious goods, his daughters, palace women and musicians after the conqueror to his capital (Sennacherib 022 iii:41-49)

**Fourth campaign to Bīt-Yakin; Merodach-baladan flees with his gods by sea (Sennacherib 22 iii 50-74)**
- The conqueror sets his own son on the throne of the conquered land (Sennacherib 022 iii:71-74)

**Fifth campaign to Mount Nipur and Ukku (Sennacherib 22 iii 75 - iv 31)**
- Mountain cities are set on the peaks like the nests of the eagle, prince of birds (Sennacherib 022 iii:75-79)

**Sixth campaign across the sea to Nagitu in Elam; Šūzubu captured (Sennacherib 22 iv 32-53)**
- The king has his army cross the sea in ships built by western shipwrights to attack the enemy (Sennacherib 022 iv:37-44)

**Seventh campaign against Elam; the Elamite king dies before his time (Sennacherib 22 iv 54 - v 16)**
- A long list of conquered towns is given by name (Sennacherib 022 iv:61-76)
- The smoke of the burning cities covers the face of the sky like a heavy cloud (Sennacherib 022 iv:79-81)
- Bitter cold, heavy rain and snow in the winter month force the king to turn back (Sennacherib 022 v:6-10)
- By the god's command an enemy king dies suddenly within months, 'on a day not his fate' (Sennacherib 022 v:11-14)
- The enemy king's successor is a man without sense or counsel (Sennacherib 022 v:14-16)

**Eighth campaign - Babylon's bribe to Elam and the battle of Halule (Sennacherib 22 v 17 - vi 35)**
- A fugitive rebel gathers runaways, outlaws and murderers round him in the marshes and is made king (Sennacherib 022 v:20-24)
- The allied enemy armies advance like a great swarm of locusts in spring (Sennacherib 022 v:56-57)
- Before battle the king prays to his gods for victory and they hear his prayer at once (Sennacherib 022 v:62-67)
- The king puts on armour and helmet, mounts his chariot in fury and roars like the storm god (Sennacherib 022 v:67-75)
- The blood of the slain flows like a river over the plain and the chariot wheels are steeped in blood and gore (Sennacherib 022 vi:3-10)
- The bodies of the slain fill the plain like grass (Sennacherib 022 vi:9-10)
- Fleeing enemies in terror urinate and defecate in their chariots (Sennacherib 022 vi:29-32)
- The victor cuts the throats and hands of the slain and strips their gold ornaments (Sennacherib 022 vi:2, Sennacherib 022 vi:11-15)

**The rear palace (ekal kutalli) at Nineveh; blessing and curse for a future king (Sennacherib 22 vi 36-85B)**
- A palace of limestone and cedar is built 'in the Hittite (Syrian) style' (Sennacherib 022 vi:53-55)

**Esarhaddon chosen over his elder brothers; their revolt; his march on Nineveh (Esarhaddon 1 i 1 - ii 11)**
- The gods remove the threatened heir to a secret place and spread their protection over him (Esarhaddon 001 i:38-40)
- After the father's fall the brothers rebel and butt each other like young goats for the kingship (Esarhaddon 001 i:41-44)
- Hearing of the revolt, the king cries 'woe', tears his princely garment and rages like a lion (Esarhaddon 001 i:55-57)
- The king sets out at once in the cold of winter without waiting a day or preparing his troops (Esarhaddon 001 i:63-69)
- The war goddess stands at the king's side and breaks his enemies' bows (Esarhaddon 001 i:74-76)
- The opposing troops declare 'this is our king' and go over to him (Esarhaddon 001 i:77-81)
- The defeated rival princes abandon their troops and flee to an unknown land (Esarhaddon 001 i:82-84)
- The king has his whole army leap across a broad river as if it were a ditch (Esarhaddon 001 i:84-86)
- Messages of ecstatic prophets (mahhû), sent by gods and goddesses, constantly reach and encourage the king (Esarhaddon 001 ii:6-7)
- The king gathers the guilty who incited the rebellion, punishes them and destroys their seed (Esarhaddon 001 ii:8-11)

**Esarhaddon's titles, the restorer of the gods, and the gifts of the gods (Esarhaddon 1 ii 12-39)**
- Each great god gives the king a gift: destiny, name, fear of his kingship, fury, a strong bow and arrow (Esarhaddon 001 ii:32-39)

**Nabû-zēr-kitti-līšir breaks his oath, flees to Elam and is killed there (Esarhaddon 1 ii 40-64)**
- A rebel who broke the oath of the great gods flees abroad and is killed there by the sword (Esarhaddon 001 ii:55-57)
- A vassal who did not keep the treaty or remember the 'salt' (kindness) of his overlord rebels (Esarhaddon 001 ii:41-42)
- The rebel's brother flees from his refuge to submit to the overlord and is given his brother's land (Esarhaddon 001 ii:58-64)

**Sidon destroyed, Abdi-milkutti and Sanduarri beheaded, Arzâ by the Brook of Egypt (Esarhaddon 1 ii 65 - iii 42)**
- An island city trusts in the sea to protect it and throws off the overlord's yoke (Esarhaddon 001 ii:67-68)
- The conqueror levels the city like the deluge and throws its wall and buildings into the sea (Esarhaddon 001 ii:68-70)
- A king who fled to the sea is caught 'like a fish' from the midst of the sea and beheaded (Esarhaddon 001 ii:71-74)
- The severed heads of rebel kings are hung round the necks of their nobles, paraded through the capital with singers and lyre (Esarhaddon 001 iii:32-38)

**Cimmerians, Hilakku, Mannea, Bīt-Dakkūri and Gambulu (Esarhaddon 1 iii 43-83)**
- The Cimmerians (Gimirrāya, Gomer), a horde from far away, are fought (Esarhaddon 001 iii:43-46)
- The king returns to the citizens of the holy city the fields a robber chieftain had seized (Esarhaddon 001 iii:62-68)
- Struck by terror, a chieftain brings tribute of animals to the king and kisses his feet; the king has mercy on him (Esarhaddon 001 iii:71-79)
- A fortified city is set up 'like a door' barring the way of the enemy (Esarhaddon 001 iii:80-83)

**The gods of the Arabs returned to Hazael; Tabūa made queen; Uabu caged at the gate (Esarhaddon 1 iv 1-31)**
- The king renews captured gods, writes the might of his god and his own name on them, and gives them back to their people (Esarhaddon 001 iv:6-16)
- Queens rule Arab tribes (Apkallatu, Tabūa, Iapaʾ, Baslu) (Esarhaddon 001 iv:4, Esarhaddon 001 iv:15-16)

**Median chiefs, Patušarri, and the desert land of Bāzu (Esarhaddon 1 iv 32-77)**
- A far desert land of salt and thirst, where snakes and scorpions fill the ground like ants (Esarhaddon 001 iv:53-58)
- The kings and queens of a far desert land are killed and their corpses spread out (Esarhaddon 001 iv:62-70)

**Kings of the sea tremble; enemies scattered; envoys sue for peace (Esarhaddon 1 iv 78 - v 39)**
- The kings of the sea, whose walls are the sea and who ride ships instead of chariots, tremble and their hearts flutter (Esarhaddon 001 iv:82-v:1)
- The king moves the people of the sea to the mountains and of the mountains to the sea (Esarhaddon 001 v:20)
- Distant kings send envoys of friendship and peace and swear by the great gods (Esarhaddon 001 v:26-35)

**The arsenal palace of Nineveh, built with cedars hauled by twenty-two western kings including Manasseh (Esarhaddon 1 v 40 - vi 75G)**
- Twenty-two vassal kings of the west and the islands (including Judah) are made to haul cedar beams from Lebanon and Sirara for the king's building (Esarhaddon 001 v:54-vi:1)
- A royal park is planted as a replica of a far mountain with all aromatic and fruit trees (Esarhaddon 001 vi:30-31)
- The workers carry hoe and basket in joy and song, the mortar mixed with beer and wine (Esarhaddon 001 vi:36-41)
- At the inauguration the gods are invited and given offerings, and the officials and people are feasted with wine and their heads anointed with oil (Esarhaddon 001 vi:49-53)

**Esagil completed, deep foundation, gods' images, personnel, Etemenanki and the wall; the gods of the lands and Babylon's citizens restored (Esarhaddon 105 v 1 - vii 43)**
- The king makes the temple's utensils of gold and silver of fixed weight (Esarhaddon 105 vi:5-12)
- The king reinstates the temple's purification priests, lamentation priests and singers before the gods (Esarhaddon 105 vi:21-29)
- The temple tower is rebuilt on its old site (Esarhaddon 105 vi:29-34)

**Babylon stele: the Assyrian king's evil against Babylon and Marduk's 21 years in Assur (Nabonidus 3 col. i)**
- A conqueror carries the city god's image off to his own capital, where it dwells for a counted number of years (Nabonidus 03 i:14'-17')

**Babylon stele: Marduk gives Nabopolassar the Medes as ally; Assyria's shrines destroyed (Nabonidus 3 col. ii)**
- The god gives the wronged king a foreign ally (the Medes, Umman-manda) who sweeps the oppressor's land like a flood and takes revenge for him (Nabonidus 03 ii:1'-13')
- The victorious king does not lay a hand on the cult of the defeated land's gods, though his ally ravages their shrines (Nabonidus 03 ii:32'-38')
- The king lets his hair grow matted and lies on the bare ground as a sign of grief or penitence before the gods (Nabonidus 03 ii:39'-41')

**Babylon stele: Anunītu restored by Neriglissar; the child-king Lābāši-Marduk (Nabonidus 3 col. iv)**
- A young king's son, without understanding, sits on the throne against the will of the gods and is removed (Nabonidus 03 iv:37'-42')
- When a man's days are full he 'takes the road of fate', i.e. dies (Nabonidus 03 iv:34'-36')

**Babylon stele: Nabonidus brought to the palace and acclaimed king (Nabonidus 3 col. v)**
- A usurping king presents himself as the strong envoy and true heir of the great kings before him, unlike their own sons (Nabonidus 03 v:14'-24')

**Babylon stele: the dream of the great star and the moon, and Nebuchadnezzar in the dream (Nabonidus 3 col. vi)**
- The king dreams of the conjunction of a great star and the moon; a figure at his side tells him it portends no evil (Nabonidus 03 vi:4'-12')
- A former king appears to the reigning king in a dream and asks him what good thing he has seen (Nabonidus 03 vi:12'-30')
- In a dream the great star or god in heaven calls the dreamer by his name (Nabonidus 03 vi:36')
- A young man (eṭlu) stands at the dreamer's side and explains that the sign he fears portends no evil (Nabonidus 03 vi:6'-8')

**Babylon stele: offerings to the stars, Gula's face turned, prayer to Marduk (Nabonidus 3 col. vii)**
- The healing goddess who 'revives the dead' turns her face to the praying king and gives him long life (Nabonidus 03 vii:11'-22')

**Babylon stele: a throne for Ea, garments for the gods, silver-clad cedar doors (Nabonidus 3 col. viii)**
- The king makes new temple doors of cedar and clads them with silver or bronze so they shine like daylight (Nabonidus 03 viii:31'-54')
- The king provides the gods' statues with new ceremonial garments (tēdīqu) befitting their divinity (Nabonidus 03 viii:13'-15')

**Babylon stele: New Year gifts of silver and gold, 2,850 captives for the gods, journeys to Uruk, Larsa and Ur (Nabonidus 3 col. ix)**
- The king gives thousands of war captives to the gods to carry the hod (tupšikku) in their temples (Nabonidus 03 ix:31'-41')
- The king travels to the ancient cult cities (Uruk, Larsa, Ur, Keš) and brings silver, gold, stones and fattened bulls before their gods (Nabonidus 03 ix:48'-59')

**Babylon stele: Ehulhul of Harran desolate for 54 years; Sîn returns at the appointed time (Nabonidus 3 col. x)**
- A temple lies desolate for a fixed number of years (54) after the enemy destroys it, until the god's appointed time of reconciliation comes and he returns (Nabonidus 03 x:12'-24')
- A precious seal of an ancient king bearing the god's image and praise is recovered and hung again on the god's statue (Nabonidus 03 x:32'-51')

**Babylon stele: the favourable extispicy (Nabonidus 3 col. xi)**
- An extispicy report lists the marks of the sheep's liver and lungs one by one with their favourable outcomes (Nabonidus 03 xi:2'-42')

**Sippar cylinder: titulary; destined for kingship in his mother's womb (Nabonidus 28 i 1-6)**
- Gods fix the king's destiny for kingship while he is still in his mother's womb (Nabonidus 28 i:4-5)

**Sippar cylinder: Sîn's anger at Harran; the dream of Marduk and Sîn; Cyrus scatters the Medes (Nabonidus 28 i 7-33)**
- Commanded to rebuild, the king objects that an enemy power surrounds the site; the god answers that the enemy will soon cease to exist (Nabonidus 28 i:21-25)
- The god raises a young 'servant' king (Cyrus of Anšan) who with a small army scatters a vast foe and carries its king captive (Nabonidus 28 i:26-29)
- Hearing the god's unchangeable command the king becomes afraid, worried and pale-faced, but does not slacken (Nabonidus 28 i:32-33)

**Sippar cylinder: Ehulhul rebuilt on Ashurbanipal's foundation; Sîn's return and prayer (Nabonidus 28 i 34-ii 46)**
- Temple mudbricks and mortar are mixed with beer, wine, oil and honey at the founding (Nabonidus 28 ii:1-6)

**Sippar cylinder: Ebabbar of Sippar rebuilt on Naram-Sin's foundation, 3,200 years old (Nabonidus 28 ii 47-iii 21)**
- The king is afraid and pale when the walls of the god's house collapse, and moves the god to another house while he rebuilds (Nabonidus 28 ii:51-55)
- The god himself shows the king the long-lost ancient foundation of his temple on an auspicious day (Nabonidus 28 ii:59-61)

**Sippar cylinder: Eulmaš of Anunītu rebuilt; charge to a future king (Nabonidus 28 iii 22-51)**
- The goddess of battle carries bow and quiver, flattens the enemy, destroys the wicked and marches before the gods (Nabonidus 28 iii:22-26)

**Harran stele: Sîn's great deed; the only son named king; the sin of Babylon (Nabonidus 47 i 1-22)**
- A wonder of the god is proclaimed that no one had known since distant days, that had never come to the land nor been written on a tablet (Nabonidus 47 i:1-7)
- The god himself comes down from heaven to the land before the king (Nabonidus 47 i:5-7)
- The people of the cities sin against the god, forget his rites and speak lies and untruth (Nabonidus 47 i:14-20)
- Sinful people devour one another like dogs, and the god sends disease and famine among them (Nabonidus 47 i:20-22)

**Harran stele: ten years in Tema and the Arabian oases (Nabonidus 47 i 23-ii 2)**
- The king leaves his capital and for ten years wanders among the Arabian oases (Tema, Dedan, Fadak, Khaybar, Yadiʿ, Yathrib), not entering his city (Nabonidus 47 i:23-28)
- The Arabs who stood to plunder are broken by the god's word and bow at the king's feet (Nabonidus 47 i:45-48, Nabonidus 47 ii:1-2)
- The gods entrust a guard of well-being and life to the king while he wanders far from his city (Nabonidus 47 i:28-31)

**Harran stele: hymn to Sîn, lord of the gods (Nabonidus 47 ii 3-42)**
- Hymn to the moon god: his weapon touches heaven and smashes earth; he holds the rites of Anu, Enlil and Ea, and the gods quake before him like reeds (Nabonidus 47 ii:14-20)
- The land the god chooses stands firm for ever; the land he decides to break, he removes his fear from it and casts it down (Nabonidus 47 ii:25-31)
- Without the god's command no land is founded and no light exists in the land (Nabonidus 47 ii:36-39)

**Harran stele: return from Tema, homage of kings, Ehulhul completed, charge to future king (Nabonidus 47 iii)**
- The gods and goddesses who had turned away and gone far return and speak favour for the king (Nabonidus 47 iii:11-14)

**Adad-guppi stele: devotion to Sîn after he left Harran in anger (Nabonidus 2001 i 1-28)**
- A king's mother has sought the moon god and his consorts from her childhood and reveres them all her life (Nabonidus 2001 i:1-5)
- A devout woman renounces fine wool, silver, gold, new clothes, perfume and oil and wears a torn garment and sackcloth while she prays (Nabonidus 2001 i:22-26)
- The devotee prays day and night that the angry god return to his city so that the people may revere him (Nabonidus 2001 i:19-22)

**Adad-guppi stele: her lifespan through the reigns; Sîn's anger rests; her only son named king (Nabonidus 2001 i 29-ii 4)**
- A long life is measured out by the regnal years of a series of named kings (Nabonidus 2001 i:29-33)
