- A mother lifts her hands to the god and prays that her son, whom the god named for kingship, be protected and restore the god's rites (Nabonidus 2001 i:44-46, Nabonidus 2001 ii:1-4)

**Adad-guppi stele: Sîn promises in a dream; Nabonidus restores Ehulhul (Nabonidus 2001 ii 5-25)**
- The dreamer heeds the god's word spoken in a dream and lives to see it fulfilled (Nabonidus 2001 ii:12-13)
- The god lifts up the devotee's head and gives her a good name in the land with long days (Nabonidus 2001 ii:23-25)

**Adad-guppi stele: 104 years in health, four generations; service of the kings and their funerary offerings (Nabonidus 2001 ii 26-iii 4)**
- A woman of over 100 years keeps clear eyesight, keen hearing, sound hands and feet, choice words and good health (Nabonidus 2001 ii:26-32)
- A dying mother entrusts her son to her god and asks that the god pardon him if he sins (Nabonidus 2001 ii:35-40)
- The devotee makes monthly kispu offerings (incense, oxen, sheep, bread, beer, wine, oil, honey, fruit) for the dead kings she served (Nabonidus 2001 ii:51-59, Nabonidus 2001 iii:1-4)

**Adad-guppi stele: her death in Nabonidus' 9th year, burial and seven days of mourning (Nabonidus 2001 iii 5-55)**
- The king buries his mother's corpse wrapped in fine linen and gold, anointed with oil, with sacrifices and a gathering of princes (Nabonidus 2001 iii:8-23)
- The whole land mourns a royal death: loud weeping, garments and dust, seven days and nights of lament, and the people shave their hair (Nabonidus 2001 iii:29-31)
- At the end of mourning the mourners are fed, anointed with sweet oil on their heads, their faces brightened and sent home (Nabonidus 2001 iii:34-43)

**Gilgameš VIII (STT 1, 15): Gilgameš' lament for Enkidu and the statue of his friend**
- The mourner calls on animals, rivers, trees, elders, young men, ploughman, shepherd, brewer and harlot to weep for his dead friend (GKAB P273162 o:5-19, GKAB P273162 o:22)

**Gilgameš VII (STT 1, 14): Enkidu addresses the door, Gilgameš weeps, Enkidu curses the trapper**
- The dying hero addresses the door he made for a god's temple, regretting it, wishing he had cut it down and given it elsewhere (GKAB P273163 o:5'-14')

**Gilgameš I (CTN 4, 199): prologue, the tablet in the cedar box, the hero two-thirds god**
- The hero returns to their places the shrines destroyed by the flood and re-establishes the rites for the people (GKAB P273200 o.i:25'-26')

**Gilgameš III (SpTU 4, 124): Ninsun prays to Šamaš and adopts Enkidu**
- The sun god raises thirteen named winds (south, north, east, west, blast, gale, ...) to darken the monster's face and stop him (GKAB P273248 o.iii:8-13)
- The mother pleads that her son, though not a god, shares heaven, the sceptre, the Apsu's wisdom and rule of the black-headed with the gods (GKAB P273248 o.iii:21-26)

**Uruk New Year ritual (BRM 4, 7): Anu's procession to the akītu house**
- In the New Year ritual the god's image goes in procession from his cella to the akītu house while priests recite incantations at each station and pray seven times (GKAB P296523 o:1-27, GKAB P296523 r:1-4)
- A litany of all the gods of heaven, earth, Apsu, and day, month and year is asked to bless (karābu) the processing god (GKAB P296523 r:5-11)
- A prayer or incantation is recited seven times at each station of a rite (GKAB P296523 o:14, GKAB P296523 o:21, GKAB P296523 o:27, GKAB P296523 r:14)
- A tablet is headed with the wish 'by the word of god X may it go well' (GKAB P296523 t.e:1)

**Enūma eliš I (STT 1, 1-2): Apsû plots against the gods; Ea kills him; Marduk born; Tiāmat roused**
- The primeval father and his vizier plot to destroy the noisy younger gods so that he may rest by day and sleep at night (GKAB P338317 o:5'-16')
- The newborn champion god has four eyes and four ears, doubled divinity, and is clothed in the radiance of ten gods (GKAB P338317 r:1'-18')
- The high god creates the four winds and gives them to his young son to play with (GKAB P338317 r:19'-22')
- Restless gods rebuke the primeval mother for sitting silent when her husband was killed and urge her to take revenge (GKAB P338317 r:23'-34')

**Enūma eliš IV (STT 1, 5): Marduk armed and enthroned; battle; Tiāmat split**
- To test the new champion's word, a constellation is destroyed and recreated at his command (GKAB P338321 o:1'-4')

**Enūma eliš IV, further Sultantepe fragments (STT 1, 6, 7, 8+)**
- Hearing the challenge, the primeval sea-mother becomes like an ecstatic (mahhû) and shrieks (GKAB P338322 o:6'-9')

**Enūma eliš V (STT 1, 12): rivers from Tiāmat's eyes; gods prostrate; Marduk proposes Babylon**
- From the slain monster's spittle and body the god makes rain, clouds and fog (GKAB P338328 o:2'-4')
- The victor makes images of the defeated monsters and sets them at the temple gate as a sign never to be forgotten (GKAB P338328 o:21'-23')

**Enūma eliš VI (STT 1, 9): humankind bears the gods' toil; gods build Esagil; the bow; Marduk's names**
- Seven gods of destinies are appointed in the assembly to decide fates (GKAB P338325 o:39'-40')
- The victorious god's bow is kissed by the high god, given names and set in the sky as a constellation (GKAB P338325 o:41'-46', GKAB P338325 r:1-5)
- The gods swear an oath with water and oil and touch their throats, binding themselves to the new king of the gods (GKAB P338325 r:8-12)
- What the god does in heaven is to be done likewise on earth: the earthly cult is the image (tamšīlu) of the heavenly (GKAB P338325 r:24)
- The god is the shining 'son, the sun of the gods', in whose bright light the gods walk for ever (GKAB P338325 r:38-39)

**Enūma eliš VI, fragment (STT 1, 14a): Marduk resolves to make humankind; the battle recalled**
- The high god asks the assembly who instigated the strife and made the battle (GKAB P338331 o:10'-13')

**Enūma eliš VII (STT 1, 11): the names of Marduk as giver of fertility and conqueror**
- The divine warrior's names make him the giver of grain, pasture and furrow, the irrigation lord of the gods (GKAB P338327 o:4'-13', GKAB P338327 o:18')
- The vanquished sea is the god's vehicle and he its sailor (GKAB P338327 o:16')
- The god sits high in the 'house of prayer' and the gods bring their gifts before him (GKAB P338327 r:17-18)

**Erra and Išum II (STT 1, 17+): Marduk's radiance dimmed; the craftsmen; families scattered**
- The god gives the craftsmen wisdom and skill so that the god's statue and its adornment are refurbished brighter than before (GKAB P338334 o:3'-10')
- The warrior god is set to stand guard before the god's image night and day without ceasing (GKAB P338334 o:11')
- In the catastrophe people are driven from city to city, fathers and sons separated, mothers mock daughters, wild beasts roam (GKAB P338334 r:2'-8')

**Anzû II (STT 1, 19 and 22): Ninurta fights Anzû; the arrow sent back**
- In the divine battle armour is bathed in blood, clouds of death rain down and arrows flash like lightning (GKAB P338336 o:12'-14')
- The monster's spell sends the arrow back: reed to the reed-bed, bow to the forest, string to the sheep, feathers to the birds (GKAB P338336 o:17'-19')
- The hero sends his messenger back to the wise god to report his failure and ask for new instructions (GKAB P338336 r:17-21)

**Anzû III (STT 1, 23 and 25): Ninurta's storm-army; Anzû slain; Enlil rejoices**
- The warrior god's fierce radiance and awe-inspiring glow cover the land and envelop all countries (GKAB P338340 o:19'-22', GKAB P338342 o:18'-21')
- At the warrior's battle-cry the gods of the underworld quake and the dwelling of Arallu darkens (GKAB P338340 o:25'-29', GKAB P338342 o:25'-28')
- The victorious warrior god's fame is boundless; there is none like him (GKAB P338340 r:26-32)

**Nergal and Ereškigal (STT 1, 28) i: the gods' banquet; Kakka goes down through seven gates**
- Because the underworld queen cannot go up to the gods' banquet, the gods send a messenger to her, and she sends her vizier up to receive her portion (GKAB P338345 o.i:51'-53', GKAB P338345 o.i:67'-72')

**Nergal and Ereškigal (STT 1, 28) ii-iii: Nergal fails to rise; Ea's chair and warnings; Nergal at the gates**
- Only one god in the assembly does not stand up before the underworld queen's envoy, causing offence (GKAB P338345 o.ii:17-21)
- The underworld vizier sees the arriving god in the shadow of the door and turns pale, recognising the one who did not rise for him (GKAB P338345 o.iii:22-29)
- The visiting god refuses the underworld chair, bread, meat, beer and foot-water until the queen shows him her body (GKAB P338345 o.iii:53-65)

**Nergal and Ereškigal (STT 1, 28) rev. i-ii: six days in bed; Nergal escapes; Ereškigal's demand and Namtar's search**
- The underworld queen demands that the god who slept with her be sent back as her husband, or she will raise the dead to eat the living (GKAB P338345 r.ii:8-15, GKAB P338345 r.ii:24-30)
- Pure water is sprinkled through a house to purify it (GKAB P338345 r.i:44-47)

**Nergal and Ereškigal (STT 1, 28) rev. iii: Nergal storms the seven gates and takes Ereškigal as wife**
- The god forces his way through the gates, seizes the underworld queen by her hair, and they embrace and become husband and wife (GKAB P338345 r.iii:31-38)
- The underworld queen offers her divine husband to share the throne and the rites of the great Underworld (GKAB P338345 r.iii:7-14)

**The Poor Man of Nippur, Uruk fragment (STT 1 39+)**
- A ruler or lord asks a petitioner 'what is your wish?' and the petitioner hopes to attain his desire (GKAB P338356 o:6-8)

**The Gilgameš Letter (STT 1 41): Gilgameš demands fabulous tribute for Enkidu's memorial and threatens the recipient's cities**
- A royal letter threatens that if the recipient does not comply, the sender will crush his cities, plunder his palaces and gardens, block his rivers and dwell in his city (GKAB P338358 r:11-13)

**Šuʾila to Ea (STT 1 67): 'King of wisdom, creator of understanding', prayer of Banītu-ēreš against evil portents**
- The god bears the high flood and plenty, gladdens the rivers and makes abundance sprout in sea and reed-thicket and life for the people (GKAB P338385 o:6-8)
- The wise god is the one who gives counsel to the great gods, while Anu and Enlil rejoice over him and the Anunnaki pray to him (GKAB P338385 o:9-12)

**Udug-hul compendium (STT 2 173): Namtar and the evil messengers; Ea's remedy of a clay substitute figure taken to the steppe before Šamaš**
- The illness is hidden: no one knows its inside, and its poison cannot be seen (GKAB P338492 7-10)
- Asalluhi (Marduk) sees the affliction and reports it to his father Ea, who answers 'what I know you know; go, my son' and prescribes the ritual (GKAB P338492 o:6, GKAB P338492 r:8, GKAB P338492 13-14)
- A bird (dove) of heaven is released and the direction of its flight, toward sunrise or sunset, is taken as an omen (GKAB P338492 o:7, GKAB P338492 17-20)
- The demons are 'evil messengers' (mārū šipri lemnūtu) who attack the land, fill it like locusts and lay sickness on man (GKAB P338492 31-42)
- At dawn the substitute figure is carried out to the steppe before the sun god, given provisions in a leather bag and set at the root of a thornbush facing sunset (GKAB P338492 r:13, GKAB P338492 58-61, GKAB P338492 r:16-18)
- Closing wish: may the evil demon stand aside and the good protective spirits (šēdu, lamassu) be present (GKAB P338492 t.e:1-3)

**Ninurta's Return to Nippur (An-gim), bilingual fragment (STT 2 180): Ninurta born of the mother goddess, praised for his strength**
- The warrior god, born of the mother goddess, grew up in the mountains (hursaĝ) (GKAB P338499 4-5)
- The singer repeats 'let me praise, let me praise' the god's might and strength (GKAB P338499 6-15)

**Namburbi against an ominous sacrifice (STT 2 231): when the slaughtered sheep does not bleed and its entrails are faulty**
- Instead of prostrating, the supplicant goes straight to the god's house and kisses its door frame (GKAB P338550 o:12-13)
- The client of a ritual is dressed in a strange costume of debasement: grain and silver on the head, jaw bound, rings on fingers and toes, a lead belt, one sandal, wall plaster on the head (GKAB P338550 o:13-19)
- Circling his house, the client declares 'I change my house: my evils are your evils' and tears out the evil the gods placed (GKAB P338550 o:26-28)
- Wish that the evil cross the river, cross the mountain and be thousands of double-hours from the body, rise like smoke and like an uprooted tamarisk never return (GKAB P338550 r:12'-13', GKAB P338550 r:24'-25')

**Namburbi against 'hole-birds' that land on a man (STT 2 235)**
- Ominous birds (hole-birds) stand or alight on a man, an evil requiring a namburbi (GKAB P338554 o:1-4)
- The patient's body is wiped with dough or flour paste (kuppuru) to absorb the evil (GKAB P338554 o:6-9)

**Namburbi against the hole-birds, bilingual (STT 2 236): praise for release, a Sumerian incantation, and the birds released east and west**
- Clay images of the ominous creature (bird, dog) are made and disposed of to remove its evil (GKAB P338555 r:3-4)
- The client recites the incantation three times and sinks three times into the river water, then is anointed (GKAB P338555 r:5-7)

**Ritual against bed-wetting, 'hand of Ninmah' (STT 2 238)**
- The mother goddess is hailed as creator of heaven and earth and lady of the gods (GKAB P338557 o:5)
- The mother goddess (Ninmah) is addressed as merciful mother who has compassion (rēmu, also 'womb') (GKAB P338557 r:1-2)

**Namburbi against the evil of a dog (that lay) on a bed (STT 2 259)**
- A dog lying on a man's bed (or entering his house) is an evil portent requiring a namburbi (GKAB P338578 o:3'-5')

**Ša-zi-ga potency texts (STT 2 280 obv. i): amulets and potions for a man whose 'heart does not rise', bewitched with the dead**
- Roots or dust taken from a grave are used as ritual ingredients (GKAB P338598 o.i:27)

**Ša-zi-ga (STT 2 280 obv. ii): wrath of Marduk and Ištar; 'as Ištar did for Dumuzi, Nanāya for her husband'**
- A sacrifice with juniper incense is offered to Ištar of the stars (Venus) (GKAB P338598 o.ii:63)

**Ša-zi-ga (STT 2 280 rev. i): prayer to Nanāya against figurines buried in the ground; 'may he spread like a donkey'**
- The charm wishes the man's virility to be like a donkey's, a stag's or a ram's (GKAB P338598 r.i:27-28, GKAB P338598 r.i:47-49)

**Ša-zi-ga (STT 2 280 rev. ii): 'Let the wind blow, the garden sway, the clouds gather': potency like river water**
- Love charm: 'let the wind blow, the orchard sway, the clouds gather and the drops fall; may my desire be flowing river water' (GKAB P338598 r.ii:37-39)
- The lover will not be sated with the beloved's charms (lalû) (GKAB P338598 r.ii:19)

**Elegies on the death of Tammuz (STT 2 360): the Babylonian merchant, the killed shepherd, farmer and gardener, the tall tree cut down**
- A mourning mother (or sister) asks where the dead son's feet went, and how he was turned back alone (GKAB P338675 o:24-27)

**The Uruk Prophecy (SpTU 1 3): kings who will not judge, the protective goddess of Uruk carried to Babylon, and the coming king who restores her and founds an everlasting dynasty**
- Prophecy foretells a succession of anonymous kings: 'after him a king will arise ...', each characterised by his rule (just or unjust) (GKAB P348424 r:1-3, GKAB P348424 r:7-9, GKAB P348424 r:11, GKAB P348424 r:16)
- A bad king gives the people of a city away as a present (GKAB P348424 r:5, GKAB P348424 r:14)
- An oppressive king lays heavy tribute on a city, ruins it, lets its canals silt up and its meadows lie abandoned, and carries its goods abroad (GKAB P348424 r:6-7, GKAB P348424 r:8)
- The coming just king judges rightly, re-establishes the city's rites, rebuilds its temples, returns the gods to their houses, renews the city with lapis gates and fills canals and fields with plenty (GKAB P348424 r:11-15)
- A prophecy is presented as a written document ('this is its writing') (GKAB P348424 o:8)

**Adapa and Enmerkar (SpTU 1 4): fragment in which Enmerkar of Uruk and the sage Adapa disturb an old corpse and destroy a tomb gate**
- The antediluvian sage Adapa appears beside a primeval king (Enmerkar) (GKAB P348425 flake:11', GKAB P348425 flake:15'-16')
- A king disturbs an old corpse and destroys the gate of its tomb, causing an evil noise in the palace (GKAB P348425 flake:19'-22')

**Catalogue of namburbi rituals (SpTU 1 6): snakes in the house, lightning, a child born in Nisan, red ants, the man who sold his father's house**
- A snake (or intertwined snakes) seen in a man's house is an evil portent (GKAB P348427 side.a:1'-2', GKAB P348427 side.a:5'-6')
- A man who has sold his father's house for silver needs an apotropaic ritual (GKAB P348427 side.a:4')
- A child born in a certain month (Nisan) is an omen requiring a ritual (GKAB P348427 side.a:12')
- A man who carries glowing embers (kurāru) needs a ritual against its evil (GKAB P348427 side.a:24')
- Rituals and incantations for renewing a canal and opening a river gate (GKAB P348427 l.e:1'-3')

**Ša-zi-ga (SpTU 1 9): male and female clay figurines, potency rites 'at the command of the goddess', a man bewitched with the dead**
- A plant is purified at sunset and uprooted in the morning before the sun god (GKAB P348430 o:26')

**Ša-zi-ga (SpTU 1 10): 'Who took away my desire like slack flax?' with a Sumerian love-bedroom line**
- The lovers' bedroom is cool and agreeable (Sumerian love-song phrase) (GKAB P348431 flake:2'-4')
- The impotent man complains: who took away my desire like slack flax? he hates me all day and bewitches me all night (GKAB P348431 flake:11'-14')

**Incantation and ritual against angry gods (SpTU 1 11): sweeping, torch and censer through the house, door frames anointed; Night, bride of Anu, invoked**
- A god is invoked as 'releaser of guilt' (pāṭir arni) (GKAB P348432 o:4')

**Namburbi, bilingual fragment (SpTU 1 16): praise after release, holy-water vessel, white garment**
- After the holy-water rite the client is clothed in a white garment (GKAB P348437 o.i:7'-9', GKAB P348437 o.ii:2')

**Bilingual incantation (SpTU 2 4): the evil torn out of the house; door frames smeared with bitumen and gypsum; adjured by the life of the great gods**
- Incantation: may the god make the evil tremble in the house and tear it out of the house (GKAB P348609 5-12)

**Bīt rimki varia (SpTU 2 12 obv.): the prince washes off guilt and curses, 'may my tablet of guilt be broken', the bound sheep released before Šamaš**
- Purification: may the curse and complaint from the mouth of many people be removed and poured away (GKAB P348617 o.ii:1, GKAB P348617 o.ii:5-6, GKAB P348617 o.ii:13)
- Wish that the king's life be (as constant) in people's mouths as silver or beer (GKAB P348617 o.ii:14, GKAB P348617 o.ii:16)
- The sun god is asked to guard the petitioner's life daily, renew his reign and grant long days (GKAB P348617 o.ii:21-25)

**Bīt rimki varia (SpTU 2 12 rev.): scapegoat and reed figure, holy water sprinkled seven times, birds of heaven, a gazelle, fish, goose and duck released; figurines of the sorcerer**
- After the purification bath, animals are released (fish, goose, duck) or a gazelle is shot, each with its incantation (GKAB P348617 r.i:23-26)

**Šurpu II (SpTU 2 13 obv.): the catalogue of sins - good for evil, bribed judges, the widow wronged, father set against son, captives kept in darkness, false measures**
- Catalogue sin: he knew but did not say, said but exaggerated, said 'there is' for 'there is not' (GKAB P348618 o.i:7'-8', GKAB P348618 o.i:33')
- Catalogue sin: he separated son from father, father from son, daughter from mother, daughter-in-law from mother-in-law, brother from brother, friend from friend (GKAB P348618 o.i:11'-19')
- Catalogue sin: he did not release the captive or loosen the bound man, and did not show light to the prisoner (GKAB P348618 o.i:19'-23')
- Catalogue sin: he despised father and mother, was hostile to his elder brother and sinned against his elder sister (GKAB P348618 o.i:28'-31')

**Šurpu II (SpTU 2 13 rev.): litany of gods and temples asked to 'release' the curse, from Anu and Ea to the gods of Susa and the four winds**
- A litany names god after god and sanctuary after sanctuary, each asked 'may he release' (lipṭur) the curse (GKAB P348618 r.ii:1-36)
- Gods of a foreign land (Elam: Inšušinak, Humban, Napiriša) are invoked alongside the native gods (GKAB P348618 r.ii:24-25)
- The four winds (south, north, east, west) are asked to blow and release the curse (GKAB P348618 r.ii:26-27)
- The Brazier (Kinūnu), deified as son of Ea, is invoked (GKAB P348618 r.ii:5)

**Šurpu III (SpTU 2 14): the litany of 'oaths' (māmītu) each released by the exorcist of the gods, Asalluhi**
- A curse is contracted by speaking with an accursed man or a sinner, eating his bread, drinking his water or his leftovers (GKAB P348619 r.ii:1-8)
- Catalogue offence: swearing (friendship) to a friend and then killing him (GKAB P348619 o.i:16')
- An oath sworn by the sun god at his rising (GKAB P348619 o.i:25')

**Šurpu VIII (SpTU 2 15): curses of field and garden, boundary stone, ship and quay, broken table, cut hem, small and large measures**
- Breaking a table, a cup, a dress-pin, or cutting a hem brings on a curse (GKAB P348620 r.i:11-14)

**House-building ritual (SpTU 2 16 obv.): pots broken at the gates, the brick god Kulla goes down into the house, prayer to Ea and Marduk as builders who decree fates; 'hostile one, go out!'**
- Offerings are made to the god of the house, the goddess of the house and the protective spirit of the house (GKAB P348621 o.i:10'-13')
- The gods are hailed as builders of city and house, who fix fates and draw the plans of life with their hands (GKAB P348621 o.i:16'-21')
- Shouting 'Hostile one, go out!', the ritualists drive the evil spirit from the new house (GKAB P348621 o.ii:9', GKAB P348621 o.ii:17'-19', GKAB P348621 o.ii:23'-25')

**House-building ritual (SpTU 2 16 rev.): Kulla escorted to the river bank with provisions and adjured by heaven, earth and the primeval divine pairs never to return**
- A Sumerian incantation adjures the great storm and evil away with the repeated word 'oath' (GKAB P348621 r.i:1-3)

**Ritual to see a ghost and get a decision (SpTU 2 20): oil anointed on the eyes, Namtar made to speak, the Anunnaki talk with you**
- A clay figure of Namtar (fate) is anointed with oil and then tells the practitioner whatever he asks (GKAB P348625 o:6'-12', GKAB P348625 o:15'-20')
- Altars before the sun god and an underworld god are set with rations, wine, milk and beer for the rite of the Land of No Return (GKAB P348625 o:21'-29', GKAB P348625 r:1-3)
- The dead man asks: what sin did I commit that I was turned into clay? (GKAB P348625 r:12-14)
- An uprooted plant goes up and down the mountain, sees the gods its brothers, carries the word and brings back their decision (GKAB P348625 r:16-21)
- If the consulted ghost stays silent and the case is not resolved, an apotropaic ritual is performed (GKAB P348625 r:6, GKAB P348625 r:26-27)

**Amulet stones against evil (SpTU 2 22+ obv. i): eye disease, the man who sees flashes ('I belong to Enlil and Ninlil'), the man always afraid, slandered and dreaming of the dead**
- Diagnosis: a man is constantly afraid, groans day and night, loses his profit, is slandered, unwelcome at the palace and sees the dead in dreams (GKAB P348627 o.i:21-30)

**Amulet stones (SpTU 2 22+ obv. ii): incantations to Ea, Asalluhi, Šamaš and Sîn as creators; to Gula against the adversary's sorcery; to Marduk for bright days**
- A man has an adversary and slanderer; hatred, injustice, 'cutting of life' and 'seizing of the mouth' surround him (GKAB P348627 o.ii:13-21)
- The healing goddess (Gula) is hailed as creator of mankind and giver of share, ration and offerings, and asked to stand by the petitioner in court (GKAB P348627 o.ii:34-38)
- Petition that bright days shine on me and god, king, noble and prince be reconciled with me and rejoice to see me (GKAB P348627 o.ii:47-55)

**Amulet stones (SpTU 2 22+ rev. i): gift to the exorcist and to Šamaš the judge, 'may my adversary be reconciled, may who spoke evil speak good'; stones to undo the knot of the angry god's heart**
- The client gives a gift to the exorcist (and grains of silver and gold to the sun god) before the god (GKAB P348627 r.i:7, GKAB P348627 r.i:14, GKAB P348627 r.i:25-26)
- Petition that the male and female adversary be reconciled, and whoever spoke evil speak good (GKAB P348627 r.i:15-17, GKAB P348627 r.i:36)
- A flask of cold water is held so that the cold water may calm the angry god (GKAB P348627 r.i:25, GKAB P348627 r.i:30)
- Stones are worn so that the knot of the angry god's heart toward the man is untied (GKAB P348627 r.i:41-44)

**Amulet stones (SpTU 2 22+ rev. ii and edges): for favour, love, against the sin of father and mother, curses turned back, safety in battle, 'I am lapis, I break the mountain'; colophon of Iqīšâ**
- Whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants (GKAB P348627 r.ii:7-8)
- A man who keeps cursing his god and goddess and speaking lies against them is detestable to his god, who will not accept his prayer (GKAB P348627 r.ii:14-16)
- In the incantation the amulet speaks: 'I am lapis lazuli, I break the mountain; I am gold, tribute of Esagil' (GKAB P348627 r.ii:32-35)
- Stones guard a man's footsteps in battle and lengthen his life; 'guard my footsteps, Marduk' (GKAB P348627 r.ii:36-41)
- Stones and plants are worn so that the punishment (guilt) of god and king may not approach the man (GKAB P348627 r.ii:50, GKAB P348627 b.e:2-4)

**Šu-du₈-a 'loosened hand' (SpTU 2 23): amulet of the Anzu's claw - 'Who will bring me up to the roof of Anzu?' - so that whatever one asks is given**
- Incantation: 'who will bring me up to the roof of the Anzu bird and put its sated claw in my hand?'; a goddess answers and the Anzu's claw becomes an amulet of success (GKAB P348628 o:10-17)
- Holding the amulet, whatever the client requests will be given him (GKAB P348628 o:19-20, GKAB P348628 o:25-26)
- The sun god is addressed as 'great dragon of heaven and earth', strong heir and offspring of the moon god (GKAB P348628 o:21-24)

**Incantations for being welcomed (SpTU 2 24): 'Why have you risen like a lion?'; anointing so that all who see you rejoice; turtles of the rivers; the sandal on my foot**
- The adversaries rise like a lion, rage like a wolf and gather in assembly (GKAB P348629 o:1-3)
- The client anoints face and arms so that whoever sees him rejoices and he is welcome wherever he goes (GKAB P348629 o:13-16, GKAB P348629 r:11-15, GKAB P348629 t.e:1-2)
- Incantation image: turtles of the river and of dry land beat their weapons into the river, yet the speaker passes among them unafraid (GKAB P348629 r:1-6)
- Charm: 'placed is the sandal on my foot; laughter, the flower of my face, the charm of my eyes' - to win love or favour (GKAB P348629 r:16-19)

**Ritual against epilepsy, 'fall from heaven' (SpTU 2 48): a sow and the patient's torn garments, roots in a leather bag**
- An illness (epilepsy) is transferred from the patient to a pig, which is released or taken away with his torn garments (GKAB P348653 flake:4'-9')

**Šurpu III, second Uruk copy (SpTU 3 70): the māmītu litany, ending with the oaths of the great gods**
- The curse of a dead man, of a wronged man, and of what is known and not known (GKAB P348673 r.ii:6'-8')

**Šurpu IV (SpTU 3 71): Asalluhi's power to raise the sick, save from distress, bring up from the pit; the gods stand to release the oath; 'by whose incantation the dead live'**
- The god raises from illness, pulls out of distress, spares in guilt, saves in hardship, brings up from the pit and rescues from catastrophe (GKAB P348674 o.ii:1-4)
- Litany 'may god X stand': each god (moon, sun, storm, warrior) stands to release the curse or remove illness in his own domain (GKAB P348674 r.i:2'-9')

**Šurpu varia (SpTU 3 72): the ancestors of Enlil; 'the man, son of his god, belongs to Anu and Antu'; without Anu no counsel, without Enlil no decision**
- The great gods are assigned mystical numbers (Enlil 50, Ea 40, Sîn 30, Šamaš 20) (GKAB P348675 r?:15')

**Namburbi for a man and woman estranged, to bring them together again (SpTU 3 79): Šamaš and Marduk 'who gather the scattered and bring the distant near'**
- A ritual before the sun god brings together again a man and woman who have become distant (GKAB P348683 o:1, GKAB P348683 o:5-6)

**Ša-zi-ga potency incantation: as Ištar did for Dumuzi; amulet against the dead in dreams (SpTU 4, 135)**
- Potency (ša-zi-ga) incantation: as Ištar did for Dumuzi, Nanaya for her husband, Išhara for Almanu, so I do for so-and-so; may his flesh be aroused (GKAB P348729 o.ii:4-9)
- In a potency rite the man's penis and the woman's vulva are anointed with oil into which an incantation has been recited (GKAB P348729 o.ii:1-3)

**Namburbi against the evil of a snake in a man's house; prayer to Šamaš the judge (SpTU 4, 136)**
- A namburbi ritual undoes the evil portended by a snake seen in a man's house (GKAB P348730 o:1-2, GKAB P348730 r:10')

**Unidentified incantation with the ashar stone of kingship and 'the lord of my lawsuit' (SpTU 5, 234)**
- A ritual or amulet is used against 'the lord of my lawsuit' (bēl dabābi), the speaker's adversary at law (GKAB P348821 o:6, GKAB P348821 r:2')

**Šuʾila to Šamaš: lord of Sippar, the bolts of heaven; Justice at my side (SpTU 5, 238)**
- The sun god opens (or passes through) the bolted locks of heaven (GKAB P348825 r:5')
- Prayer that personified Justice (Mīšaru) stand at the supplicant's side and well-being (šulmu) follow behind him (GKAB P348825 r:11'-12')
- Prayer that the supplicant's omens and signs (ittātu) become good and his speech find favour (GKAB P348825 r:8'-10')

**Amulet stones for favour, reconciliation with god and protection; rite before Venus (SpTU 5, 244)**
- An amulet is said to keep away a list of named evils: hatred, injustice, 'cutting-off of life', 'seizing of the mouth', terror, and every evil deed (GKAB P348831 o:11-15)
- Amulet stones are strung on cords of linen, red wool and blue wool (GKAB P348831 o:18, GKAB P348831 o:21)

**House protection: turning back the breast of the enemy; Sumerian litany 'be favourable to me' (SpTU 5, 246)**
- Ritual 'to turn back the breast of the evil one and the enemy' from a man's house (GKAB P348833 o.ii:4'-6', GKAB P348833 o.ii:13')
- Litany asking sun god, judge, personal god, the gods, man and humanity in turn: be favourable to me (še-ga-me-en) (GKAB P348833 o.ii:16'-21')

**House protection: armed clay figurines buried at the threshold, blood and milk sprinkled, a dagger buried point upward (SpTU 5, 246)**
- Clay figurines of protective spirits, armed with weapons, are buried upright under the threshold or at the gate, addressed and sworn by Šamaš to bar evil from the house (GKAB P348833 o.iii:1'-16')
- The clay for the protective figurines is taken from a garden ditch and mixed with water 'of bowing down' (GKAB P348833 o.iii:6'-7')
- The house is sprinkled with the blood of a kid mixed with temple-well water and milk (GKAB P348833 o.iii:17'-20')
- The house is swept with a palm spadix and its sweepings thrown into the river (GKAB P348833 o.iii:21'-22')
- A bronze dagger is buried under the threshold of the outer gate, hilt downward and point upward, against epidemic (GKAB P348833 o.iii:23'-30')

**House protection: spell to the prowling evil 'like a lion, like a wolf'; seeds and figurines buried at the gate (SpTU 5, 246)**
- An incantation addresses the evil prowling round the house: I have gone round, seen and sought you; since you are like a lion without mercy, like a wolf, I have flattened you with my weapons and shut you in (GKAB P348833 r.i:3-8)
- Seeds of seven plants mixed with honey are buried at the right of the outer gate so that illness and epidemic do not come near the house (GKAB P348833 r.i:14-21)

**Monster figurines buried at the four sides of the house; plants, metals and temple water for the lamassu (SpTU 5, 247)**
- Pairs of figurines of monsters (laḫmu, uridimmu, bašmu, mušḫuššu) are buried right and left at the north, east, west and south of the house (GKAB P348834 o.ii:4'-8', GKAB P348834 o.i:6'-8')

**'You are the image that pushes back the evil one': incantation to the protective figure; evil sent 3,600 leagues away (SpTU 5, 247)**
- The protective figurine is addressed: you are the image that pushes back the evil one and the enemy; guard my right and left and do not slacken (GKAB P348834 r.i:6-10)
- A pit is opened at the gate and honey, milk, wine and oil are offered into it (GKAB P348834 r.i:3-4)

**Figures drawn on the doorposts and door with spells naming the fierce demons; evil mouth and tongue go out (SpTU 5, 247)**
- Figures are drawn on the right and left doorposts and on the door, and an incantation is spoken to each, naming the fierce demons it bars (GKAB P348834 r.ii:1-18)
- Date-palm thorns are buried at the right and left of the gate like a whip against demons (GKAB P348834 r.ii:20-21)

**Ritual fragment: clay and straw, wool of a virgin kid, flour drawn round the bed, birds released (SpTU 5, 250)**
- A boundary of flour is drawn round the patient's bed in a ritual (GKAB P348837 flake:6')

**Gilgameš dweller of the netherworld; the crossing of the Ḫubur (SpTU 5, 251)**
- The crossing (nēberu) of the netherworld river Ḫubur is passed by the dead (GKAB P348838 o:3', GKAB P348838 o:6'-7')

**Covering the kettledrum: the unblemished black bull, the spell whispered in its ears, its hide on the drum (BagM Beih. 2, 5)**
- Before the sacrifice an incantation is whispered through a reed into the bull's right ear and another into its left ear (GKAB P363269 r:2-4)
- The sacrificial bull is addressed: 'Bull, you are the offspring of Anzû' (GKAB P363269 r:4)
- The body of the sacrificed bull is wrapped in a red cloth, anointed and buried facing the setting sun (GKAB P363269 r:14-16)
- Twelve bricks are laid and the twelve gods are seated on them for a rite (GKAB P363269 o:7-11)
- A rite is to be performed in a favourable month on a propitious day (GKAB P363269 o:7, GKAB P363269 r:14)

**Bilingual šuʾila of the great bull for the bīt mummi: 'may this god renew his brilliance like the moon' (BagM Beih. 2, 6)**
- The great gods are hailed as creators of all that has the breath of life (GKAB P363270 o:5)
- The sacrificial bull was born in the moon god's pure sheepfold and suckled true milk, fit for divinity (GKAB P363270 o:11-14)
- The priest declares he has set out pure offerings, poured pure libations and burned pure incense before the gods (GKAB P363270 o:7-10)

**Ritual for renewing a temple: offerings at night to Ea, Šamaš and Asalluḫi, eršemma laments sung on the roof (BagM Beih. 2, 10)**
- When a temple is to be renovated, the lamentation priest sings eršemma laments at dawn on its roof to calm the gods (GKAB P363274 o:1, GKAB P363274 o:7-8, GKAB P363274 o:16-20)
- A pile of brushwood is set alight for Ea and Asalluḫi in the course of a ritual (GKAB P363274 o:5)
- Three portable altars are set up for Ea, Šamaš and Asalluḫi with linen, cakes, honey, ghee, dates and libations (GKAB P363274 o:10-13)

**Lunar eclipse ritual at Uruk: the kalû's lament ('the Dilmunite whose ship sank am I'), the brazier, kispu, mourners with covered heads (BRM 4, 6 obverse)**
- During a lunar eclipse a brazier is lit at the temple gates and the lamentation priest performs laments until the moon becomes bright again (GKAB P363407 o:14'-18', GKAB P363407 o:28')
- In a lament the god (or his mourner) says: I am the one who roams and does not sleep, who ate no food and drank no water in his weariness (GKAB P363407 o:5'-6')
- Lament: I am the Dilmunite whose ship sank in the reed thicket (GKAB P363407 o:10')
- Mourners smear their faces, hands and feet with river mud and hang a dagger at the collarbone (GKAB P363407 o:24'-25')

**Lunar eclipse ritual: temples purified, drums set by the dais, lamentation priests in torn linen, eršemmas sung by phase (BRM 4, 6 reverse)**
- One exorcist stands at the right of the house and another at its left, reciting incantations together (GKAB P363407 r:5-6)
- Bronze drums (ḫalḫallatu, manzû, lilissu) are brought out and set by the dais when an eclipse begins (GKAB P363407 r:12-13)
- A different lament is sung according to how much of the moon the eclipse covers (GKAB P363407 r:18-22)

**Consecration of a priest: incantation of the seven pure garments; Uttu who wove the wool (CTN 4, 93)**
- Incantation of the seven pure garments: the priest is clothed in pure garments so that he is clean and the evil tongue stands aside (GKAB P363507 flake:5'-7')
- The weaving goddess Uttu, daughter of Enlil and beloved of Ea, takes white wool of good sheep and makes the sacred garment (GKAB P363507 flake:8'-11')
- The sacred garment is entrusted to the fuller of the land and washed in pure water (GKAB P363507 flake:12'-13')
- The exorcist's spell is given him by Asalluḫi (Marduk) (GKAB P363507 flake:4')

**Šurpu VII: the oath-curse came down from heaven like a sparrow; Gula reviver of the dead, Marduk who loves to revive the dead (CTN 4, 94)**
- The oath-curse (māmītu) is a demon that came down from heaven (like a sparrow from the apsû), wrapped in radiance to the four winds (GKAB P363508 o:1-4)
- The curse sickens the people of the settlements; city and land, small and great, young man and girl lament, as it rains down like fog on heaven and earth (GKAB P363508 o:5-8)
- The demon or curse meets the man whose god has withdrawn from him and covers him like a garment (GKAB P363508 o:10)
- By his pure incantation of life the god looses the sufferer's bond (eʾiltu) (GKAB P363508 r:6')
- The healing god Damu is the great exorcist whose utterance makes things good (GKAB P363508 r:3')

**Muššuʾu V: Amašuḫalbi, catalogue of diseases, the word of Ea; demons and diseases (CTN 4, 95 obverse)**
- A goddess is 'mother of all living creatures' (ummi šiknat napišti) (GKAB P363509 o.i:2')
- Closing formula of an incantation: may the word of Ea shine forth, may Damkina make it go right, Marduk eldest son of the apsû (GKAB P363509 o.i:9'-11')
- May the goddess's great and gentle hands tear out the illness (GKAB P363509 o.i:7'-8')

**Muššuʾu V: adjured by all the gods and temples; 'Arise and live, you belong to Marduk!' (CTN 4, 95 reverse)**
- The demon is adjured by a long litany of gods and of their temples, one per line ('by Enlil, by Ea, by Sîn ... by Esagil, by Ekur') (GKAB P363509 r.i:2'-28')
- The four winds (east, west, north, south) are made to blow upon the patient (GKAB P363509 r.ii:2'-5')
- May Asalluḫi cut off your Namtar (fate-demon), cast him from you, and spare you (GKAB P363509 r.ii:11'-14')
- The healing incantation ends with the command to the patient: 'Arise and live, you belong to Marduk!' (tibī-ma bulluṭ ša marduk attā) (GKAB P363509 r.ii:15'-18')

**Lipšur litany: how the curse was contracted — he ate the bread of a cursed man, kissed his lips, sat on his chair; swore at the river crossing (CTN 4, 109)**
- The curse was contracted by contact: he ate the bread of a cursed man, drank his water, kissed his lips, lay in his bed, sat on his chair, ate at his table, drank from his cup (GKAB P363523 o.i:10-17)

**Lipšur litany: may each god in his temple release; may each month and each day of the month release (CTN 4, 110)**
- Each month of the year is assigned to a god in a litany (Nisannu of Anu and Enlil, Ayyaru of Ea ...) (GKAB P363524 o:27'-36', GKAB P363524 r:1-2)
- Each of the thirty days of the month is assigned to a god or a named feast in a litany (GKAB P363524 r:3-32)
- The seventh day of the month (also the 3rd and 16th) is the 'evening rest' (nubattu) of a god (GKAB P363524 r:9, GKAB P363524 r:5, GKAB P363524 r:18)
- A fixed day of the month (the 19th) is a 'day of wrath' (ibbû) of a deity (GKAB P363524 r:21)

**Lipšur litany fragment: oaths sworn by bow and bellows, garden plot; the reed stylus in a quarrel, untruth (CTN 4, 111)**
- Among his offences the sufferer used the scribe's reed in a quarrel or wrote untruth (GKAB P363525 o?:11'-15')

**Namburbi with a hymn to the River: 'You, River, creator of all; the great gods dug you'; earth and river receive my evil (CTN 4, 127)**
- Hymn: You, River, creator of all; when the great gods dug you they set goodness on your banks, Ea made his dwelling in you and named you 'irresistible flood' (GKAB P363541 r:6-10)
- The supplicant asks the River to receive his evil, spare him and take the evil down into its depths (GKAB P363541 r:13-17)
- The gods decree fates and draw the designs (plans) of life; from their mouth comes life (GKAB P363541 o:8-12)

**Grave-building ritual with namburbi: evil sign not to approach, like smoke may it go up; brick mould purified; kispu (CTN 4, 157)**
- A namburbi averts the evil that building (opening) a grave may bring on the builder and his house (GKAB P363571 o:1-3, GKAB P363571 o:12-13)

**Muššuʾu V (second copy): animals of the steppe, diseases, Madānu; litany 'X is he' (CTN 4, 158)**
- A litany identifies the patient (or his body) successively with gods and goddesses: 'he is Aya, he is Zarpanītu, he is Gula ...' (GKAB P363572 r:1'-11')

**Grave-building ritual: ransom silver weighed before Šamaš; kispu and prayer to the Anunnaki; Sumerian spell of the grave as 'house of silence' (CTN 4, 163)**
- The builder of a grave weighs out ransom silver (ipṭiru) before Šamaš, saying 'Šamaš, this is his ransom', the exorcist holding up the scales (GKAB P363577 o:5'-6', GKAB P363577 o:14'-17')
- The worshipper offers funerary food to the Igigi and Anunnaki who dwell in Duku and the wide netherworld, whose seat is terrifying (GKAB P363577 o:22'-26')
- Spell of the grave: its foundation reaches the netherworld, opened by Enki king of the Apsû; may it be a house of the netherworld, a house of silence (GKAB P363577 r:13'-16')

**Šuʾila to Ea: king of wisdom, by whose incantation of life the dead does not die; may my speech please god and king (CTN 4, 167)**
- Prayer: may my speech please god and king; may god and king do what I say; may my mouth and tongue counsel me well (GKAB P363581 o:18-20)
- Prayer that the god loosen the evil bonds tied by sorcerer and sorceress (GKAB P363581 o:22, GKAB P363581 r:1-3)

**Šuʾila to Nisaba, creator of god, king and mankind, reconciler of the angry god and goddess (CTN 4, 168, prayer 1)**
- The goddess is hailed as creator of god, king and humankind (GKAB P363582 o.i:1-3)
- Prayer that the supplicant's guilt be loosed, his sins forgotten, his bond undone and his constraint slackened (GKAB P363582 o.i:8-11)

**Šuʾila to Nisaba-Ninlil, goddess of abundance: without you no people are begotten; all the black-headed are yours (CTN 4, 168, prayer 2)**
- The grain goddess (Nisaba) is goddess of abundance who doubles plenty for Enlil (GKAB P363582 o.i:16-21, GKAB P363582 o.i:27-29)
- Without the goddess no people are begotten and no living being created; all the black-headed people and everything that exists are hers (GKAB P363582 o.i:35-36)
- The goddess judges cases and makes decisions, establishes god and king and exercises kingship (GKAB P363582 o.i:32-34)
- Of a goddess: the earth gave birth to you, the heavens raised you (GKAB P363582 o.i:41-42)
- Prayer posture: prostration with the nose stroked to the ground (labān appi) (GKAB P363582 o.i:46-47)
- Rubric: incense is lit in a censer and strewn to the supplicant's personal god (GKAB P363582 o.i:48-50)

**Šuʾila to Ištar, lady of cities, creator of people; ritual before the evening star with a bent stick (CTN 4, 168, prayer 3)**
- Hymnic question of incomparability: who is your rival? your greatness surpasses all the gods (GKAB P363582 o.i:51-55)
- Anu her father decreed her fate, in the assembly of the gods her name was exalted, Enlil gave her kingship of heaven and earth (GKAB P363582 o.i:57-61)
- The king squats (kneels) before the goddess and waits attentively on her (GKAB P363582 o.i:63)

**Šuʾilas to Tašmētu: she raises the lowly above princes; 'I have seized your hem'; ask Nabû your husband for me (CTN 4, 168, prayers 4-5)**
- The supplicant seizes the hem (sissiktu) of the deity's garment in supplication (GKAB P363582 o.ii:54-55)

**Šuʾila to Tašmētu, lady of hearing, who soothes the anger of god and king (CTN 4, 168, prayer 6)**
- The goddess is lady of hearing, who makes the settlements heard and soothes the anger of god and king (GKAB P363582 r.i:51-53)

**Šuʾila to Nanaya, queen of the regions, beloved of Nabû, shaper of all creation; incipit to Išḫara; colophon (CTN 4, 168, prayer 7)**
- The goddess is shaper of all creation who brings living beings safely to birth (GKAB P363582 r.ii:36-37)

**Catalogue of šuʾilas: to Anu, Papsukkal, the Arrow star (Sirius), Nergal (CTN 4, 179)**
- A catalogue lists prayers (šuʾilas) by incipit and the god each is addressed to (GKAB P363593 o:2-10)

**Enūma eliš II (Nimrud fragment): Marduk answers his father: 'If I am to be your avenger and keep you alive' (CTN 4, 200)**
- A god is sent to calm the raging monster with his incantation, but turns back (GKAB P363614 flake:1'-5')

**Ludlul bēl nēmeqi I: hymn to Marduk, lord of wisdom, whose hand heaven cannot bear and whose soft hand saves the dying (CTN 4, 201, obverse 1-40)**
- Hymn: the god is furious by night but relents by day; his rage is a storm and a flood, his breath a gentle morning breeze; his heart turns back (GKAB P363615 o:1-8)
- The weight of the god's hand the heavens cannot bear, yet his soft palm rescues the dying (GKAB P363615 o:9-12)
- The god relents quickly like a mother and keeps turning back like a cow to its calf (GKAB P363615 o:17-20)
- The rescued sufferer resolves to proclaim the god's anger and his quick mercy and to teach it to the people (GKAB P363615 o:37-40)

**Ludlul bēl nēmeqi I: the sufferer abandoned by his gods, omens confused, seven courtiers plot, friends turn, property divided, tears day and night (CTN 4, 201, obverse 41-reverse 54)**
- The sufferer's property is shared out among the riffraff, his canal silted up, the harvest song silenced, his city made silent like an enemy's (GKAB P363615 r:31-34)
- The sufferer's office is given to another and a stranger installed in his cultic duties (GKAB P363615 r:35-36)
- The sufferer's heart burns like fire as he prays, his prayers are a squabble, his lips stiff as in gloom (GKAB P363615 r:46-50)
- Each morning the sufferer hopes for good; a month passes, the sun shines; a whole year passes to its term (GKAB P363615 r:51-53)

**Uruk ritual: Anu's procession to the Dais of Destinies; water for the hands, the king with the golden libation vessel (TCL 6, 40)**
- The king walks in the gods' procession carrying a golden libation vessel (maqqû) (GKAB P363712 o:8', GKAB P363712 o:13', GKAB P363712 r:5, GKAB P363712 r:12, GKAB P363712 r:17)

**Uruk nocturnal ritual: offerings on the ziggurat roof to Anu and Antu of heaven and to the seven planets; the great torch; fire carried to every temple and house; gates open till dawn (TCL 6, 41)**
- At nightfall on the temple tower a purification priest lights a great aromatic torch with sulphur fire and recites the hymn 'Star of Anu, lord of heaven' (GKAB P363713 o:28'-32')
- Fire from the temple's great torch is carried down and kindled in every temple of the city, and the people light brushwood fires in their houses (GKAB P363713 o:33'-r:16, GKAB P363713 r:22)
- On the festival night the city watch lights fires in the streets and squares and the city gates stay open until dawn (GKAB P363713 r:24-27)
- On the festival night the gods sit in the temple court in a vigil (bayyātu) until dawn; the gate is not shut (GKAB P363713 o:13', GKAB P363713 r:14, GKAB P363713 r:20-22)
- The ritual torch is extinguished in holy water mixed with beer, milk, wine and oil (GKAB P363713 r:19-20)
- A large ḫarû jar is broken before the god during the festival rite (GKAB P363713 r:1, GKAB P363713 r:4)

**Uruk Ištar ritual: the gods come down to the court, the king performs the installation of the en-priest, procession with Anu's chariot to the akītu house; kurgarrû and assinnu circle (TCL 6, 42)**
- In the festival the king performs the elevation to en-ship and clothes himself in pure garments (GKAB P363714 o:16')
- The sage Adapa appears as a cult figure in an Uruk temple procession (GKAB P363714 o:3')

**Namburbi for a prince whose chariot yoke, pole or lance breaks on the road, or who falls from his chariot (TCL 6, 50)**
- A namburbi averts the evil portended when the yoke, pole, lance or any part of a prince's chariot breaks on a journey (GKAB P363722 o:1-6)
- The evil of a king or prince falling from his chariot is undone by a namburbi (GKAB P363722 r:8'-9')
- Offerings to the great gods, Nergal and the god of the steppe, so that they show mercy and are reconciled with the traveller (GKAB P363722 o:6-12)
- Šamaš is the one who illuminates darkness (GKAB P363722 o:15, GKAB P363722 o:20)
- The supplicant confesses the guilt and sins he has committed, sought out and transgressed, and waits for the god's word (GKAB P363722 r:14'-16')

**Uruk akītu ritual: gods seated right and left of Anu, the king prostrates before Antu, procession of chariots and gods to the akītu house (KAR 132)**
- The high god is enthroned with one great god on his right and another on his left, the others in fixed places beside them (GKAB P369109 o.i:7'-13', GKAB P369109 r.ii:8-19)
- The king goes to the goddess's cella and prostrates himself (GKAB P369109 o.i:13'-14')

**Anzu tablet 2 (Sultantepe): Sharur's reports, Ea's advice, Ninurta sets out again; colophon (GKAB Q002770 70-155)**
- A literary tablet ends with a colophon naming the series by its incipit, the tablet number and its total line count (GKAB Q002770 154-155)

**Rib-Addi of Byblos: send archers or we die; the land is not plagued; the commissioner Piwuri killed (EA 362)**
- A vassal assures the king that reports of plague (death) in the land are lies of other men and that the land is healthy (EA 362 r:46-53)

**Rib-Addi: my city, house and wife urged peace with Abdi-Ashirta's son; returning from Beirut I found my house shut against me (EA 136)**
- A ruler's wife, household and townsmen urge him to make peace with the enemy; he refuses (EA 136 o:8-15)

**Rib-Addi: a deed never done before: Pihura's Suteans killed a Sherdan and took three of my men to Egypt (EA 123)**
- A Sherdan or other later 'Sea People' appears in a Levantine text (EA 123 o:14-15)

**Rib-Addi to Amanappa: may Amon give you honour; three years our grain has been seized; Ummahnu, maid of the Lady (EA 086)**
- For three years the grain has failed or been seized and there is nothing to eat or feed the horses (EA 086 r:38-48)

**Rib-Addi to Yanhamu: may the Lady of Byblos give you honour before the Sun of the lands; the chief and lords of Ambi are at peace with the enemy (EA 102)**
- The chief and the 'lords of the city' make peace with the enemy behind the loyal ruler's back (EA 102 r:20-23)

**Rib-Addi: Sumur taken; send 300 men, 30 chariots, 100 men of Kush; otherwise there will be no lands of Canaan for the king (EA 131)**
- The dead lie with no one to make their funerary offering (kispu) (EA 131 r:28-30)

**Ammunira: my eyes shone at the king's tablet; I keep the man of Byblos; his brother gave Rib-Addi's sons to the king's enemies (EA 142)**
- At the overlord's letter the vassal's heart rejoices and his eyes brighten (EA 142 o:6-10)
- A ruler's own brother seizes his city and hands over his sons to the enemy (EA 142 o:15-r:24)

**Abimilki: my lord is the Sun who rises over all lands, gives life by his sweet breath, thunders like Baal; the servant who obeys keeps his name for ever (EA 147)**
- The servant who obeys his lord keeps his city, house and name forever; the one who does not loses city, house and name (EA 147 r:41-51)

**Abimilki, servant of Mayati: Tyre has no wood, water, straw or clay; before the king I was afraid and could not speak (EA 155)**
- A vassal city is said to belong to the overlord's daughter or queen, whom the vassal calls 'my lady' (EA 155 o:8, EA 155 r:41-42, EA 155 r:50-51)
- Brought before the overlord, the vassal was so afraid he could not speak (EA 155 b.e:31-r:35)

**Satatna of Akko to the king, the Sun from heaven: I guard the cities; I send raw glass (EA 235 (+) 327)**
- At the king's request a vassal sends raw glass (ehlipakku) by weight (EA 235 o:16'-21')

**Aziru defends himself: do not listen to the false men who slander me; I was in Tunip, may your gods and the Sun know it (EA 161)**
- A vassal says he provided for the overlord's envoy and carried him 'like a mother, like a father' (EA 161 o:19-24, EA 161 r:27-29)

**Akizzi of Qatna to Naphuriya, son of the Sun: the Hittite king took the Sun god of my fathers; send gold to remake him (EA 055)**
- A vassal's ancestral god-statue, made by the overlord's forefathers and bearing their name, is carried off and gold is asked to remake it (EA 055 r:53-t.e:66)

**The citizens of Tunip: the gods of Thutmose III dwell in Tunip; for twenty years we have written; now Tunip weeps and its tears flow (EA 059)**
- A subject city reminds the overlord that the gods of his ancestor dwell in it and asks him to consult his old men (EA 059 o:5-11)
- A subject city asks the overlord to send back its prince held at his court (EA 059 o:13-20)
- A city is personified as weeping, its tears flowing, with no one to take its hand (EA 059 r:39-42)

**Biryawaza: Biridashwa gave the chariots of Ashtaroth to the Habiru; the kings of Busruna and Halunni said 'let us kill Biryawaza'; I guard Kumidi (EA 197)**
- Neighbouring kings say to one another 'come, let us kill' the overlord's loyal vassal (EA 197 o:13'-18')

**Abdi-Ashirta was killed when the army's ships did not reach Amurru; Arwad's ships stand against me; are Tyre, Sidon and Beirut not the king's? (EA 101)**
- A rebel leader against the overlord is killed (by his own people or the overlord's men) (EA 101 o:1-10, EA 101 r:29-31)

**Ili-rapih and Byblos, the king's maidservant: Byblos is to the king like Memphis; Aziru killed the kings of Ammiya, Ardata, Irqata and the commissioner (EA 139)**
- A vassal says his city is to the overlord as dear as the overlord's own capital (Byblos like Memphis) (EA 139 o:5-9)

**EA 227: the king of Hazor guards the cities and rejoices at the king's word**
- The vassal says the gods have looked upon him (with favour) since the king's word came (EA 227 o:12-13)

**EA 298: Yapaḫu's younger brother goes over to the Habiru at Muḫḫazu**
- The ruler's younger brother turns hostile, enters a town and 'gives his hands' to the enemy (EA 298 r:22-27)

**EA 296: Yaḫtiru, raised in Egypt, will not move from under the king's feet; he carries the king's yoke**
- As a youth the vassal was brought into Egypt, served the king and stood at the king's gate (EA 296 r:25-29)
- The vassal has set the king's yoke on his neck and carries it (EA 296 t.e:37-l.e:39)

**EA 252: Labʾaya of Shechem: 'when an ant is struck it bites the hand that strikes it'**
- A speaker invokes 'the god of my father' (EA 252 o:13, EA 252 r:30)
- Proverb: an ant that is struck does not curl up but bites the hand of the man who strikes it (EA 252 b.e:16-r:20)

**EA 270: Milkilu of Gezer: Yanḫamu demands silver, 'give your wife and your sons'**
- An official demands silver from a ruler: 'give your wife and your sons, or I will strike' (EA 270 o:10-r:21)

**EA 269: Milkilu asks for archers and myrrh for healing**
- A ruler asks the overlord to send myrrh for healing (EA 269 o:14-b.e:17)

**EA 256: Mut-Baʿli denies hiding Ayyab and lists the towns of Garu taken**
- A ruler denies having hidden a fugitive king and names witnesses to be asked (EA 256 o:4-r:19)

**EA 245: Biridiya of Megiddo: Labʾaya was taken alive, but Surata released him for a ransom**
- A captured rebel, who was to be sent to the overlord, is released by his captor for a ransom in silver (EA 245 b.e:24-r:35)
- The speaker complains he is made light (qll) while his younger brothers are made heavy, honoured (kbd) (EA 245 r:36-40)

**EA 082: Rib-Addi to Amanappa: a man struck me nine times with a dagger; I will leave the city**
- A man stands over the ruler with a bronze dagger and strikes him (EA 082 r:36-39)

**EA 116: Rib-Addi: Ṣumur like a bird in a trap; the gods set you on your father's throne**
- The gods (the Sun, the city goddess) have given the king the throne of his father's house (EA 116 r:61-66)

**EA 134: from eternity the gods have not gone out of Byblos; Aziru sends troops to seize it**
- From eternity the gods have never gone out of the city; now the enemy sends troops to seize it and its gods (EA 134 o:4´-12´)

**EA 075: Rib-Addi: the field like a wife without a husband; Ammiya kills its lord; Hatti seizes the lands**
- The men of a city kill their own lord (ruler) (EA 075 r:32-34)

**EA 158: Aziru to Tutu: 'you are my father, my house is your house'**
- A client calls the official 'my father and lord', himself 'your son', and says 'my lands are your lands, my house is your house' (EA 158 o:1-3, EA 158 o:14-16)

**EA 052: Akizzi of Qaṭna to 'my lord, my storm god'**
- A vassal addresses the Egyptian king as 'my storm god (Addu)' (EA 052 o:3-4)

**EA 195: Biryawaza, the king's footstool, awaits the words from his lord's mouth**
- A vassal calls himself the ground the king treads, the throne he sits on and the footstool of his feet (EA 195 o:7-10)
- As one waits for the sun to come forth from heaven, so servants wait for the words that go out of their lord's mouth (EA 195 r:18-23)

**EA 244: Biridiya: Labʾaya besieges Megiddo; we cannot harvest; pestilence in the city**
- Because of the enemy the people cannot harvest or go out of the city gate (EA 244 o:13-17)
- A ruler fears his city will be finished off by pestilence (mūtānu, Canaanite dabru) (EA 244 r:30-33)

**EA 250: Baʿlu-mehir: the two sons of Labʾaya continue their father's war**
- After the rebel father's fall his sons carry on his hostility and seek to destroy the land (EA 250 o:5-8, EA 250 r:36-41)

**EA 280: Šuwardata: Keilah restored; Labʾaya is dead, but Abdi-Ḫeba is another Labʾaya**
- A dead rebel is succeeded by 'another' like him who takes the cities (EA 280 b.e:17-r:35)

**EA 049: Niqmaddu of Ugarit asks the Sun for Kushite palace boys and a physician**
- A ruler asks the overlord to send a physician, 'for there is no physician here' (EA 049 r:22-26)

**Rib-Addi in exile at Beirut: driven out of Byblos by his brother; old and sick; send archers and give me a town (EA 137)**
- The ruler's younger brother turns the city against him, drives him out and plans to hand the city to the enemy (EA 137 o:15-25, EA 137 r:57-58)
- The vassal pleads that he is old and gravely ill in his body and so cannot travel to the overlord (EA 137 o:27-30)
- A ruler attributes his severe illness to sin he committed against the holy gods of his city (EA 137 o:31-34)

**Aziru of Amurru: I have done all the king commanded; I will build Sumur this year; do not listen to slanderers (EA 160)**
- A vassal accused of neglect promises to (re)build the king's city within the year (EA 160 b.e:20-r:28, EA 160 r:38-40)

**The king to Milkilu of Gezer: Hanya brings silver for forty fine cup-bearer women; the king is well like the Sun (EA 369)**
- The overlord orders a vassal to send beautiful women cup-bearers, without blemish, at a fixed price in silver (EA 369 o:5-18)

**The army commander to Rib-Addi, 'my son': is there plague in Sumur on men or on donkeys? Send men to guard the city (EA 096)**
- People from a plague-stricken town are refused entry to another town for fear of contagion (EA 096 o:6-15)

**Labaya: I am the king's servant as my father and grandfather; I am not guilty: my only sin is that I entered Gezer (EA 253)**
- Accused, the vassal protests 'I am not guilty, I have not sinned' and names his only 'sin' (EA 253 b.e:16-r:22)

**Tagi: I looked here and there and there was no light; I looked to the king and there was light; I will not move from under his feet (EA 266)**
- Loyalty image: a brick may slip from under its partner, but the vassal will not move from under the feet of the king (EA 266 r:19-25)
- A vassal sends the king a gift of horse harness, bow, quiver, spear and garments (EA 266 r:26-t.e:33)

**Ipte-...: there is no faithful servant like me; the king like the Sun and like Baal; Puhuru does not protect me; the cities are lost to the Habiru (EA 207)**
- The overlord is likened to both the sun god and the storm god (Baal/Addu) (EA 207 r:16-17)

**Your servants: what we heard about the Ahlamu and the king of Karduniash (EA 200, fragment)**
- The Aḫlamû (early Aramaean nomads) appear as a threat in a letter (EA 200 o:7-11)

**Rib-Addi: the mayor of Tyre was killed with my sister and her children; Tyre's wealth is like the sea, its palace like Ugarit's (EA 089)**
- The wealth of Tyre is as great as the sea and its palace is like the palace of Ugarit (EA 089 r:46-53)

**Rib-Addi: the sons of Abdi-Ashirta, slave and dog, take the king's cities; once Canaan's kings fled from an Egyptian, now they treat Egyptians like dogs; death is good for me (EA 109)**
- The sufferer declares that death would be better for him than his present plight (EA 109 r:49-55)

**Rib-Addi, footstool of the king's feet: Abdi-Ashirta the dog lay in my lord's bedchamber and opened his treasury; Byblos is like Memphis to the king (EA 084)**
- The usurper lies down in his lord's bedchamber and opens his treasure-house (EA 084 o:12-16)

**Abdi-Heba: the king has set his name at sunrise and sunset; I am a soldier, the king's companion; like a ship in the sea; rulers slain at the gate; we will die with the king (EA 288)**
- The beleaguered vassal likens himself to a ship in the midst of the sea (EA 288 r:33)

**Abdi-Heba: Milkilu and the sons of Labaya gave the king's land to the Habiru; the king is righteous to me; Cushites nearly killed me; my caravan was robbed in Ayyalon; the king has set his name in Jerusalem for ever (EA 287)**
- The vassal declares 'the king my lord is righteous (ṣaduq) toward me' (EA 287 o:32)
- The caravan carrying the vassal's tribute to the king is plundered in the fields on the way (EA 287 r:53-57)

**ʿAbdi-Ḫeba of Jerusalem: Milkilu, the sons of Labʾaya, Shechem given to the Habiru, send 50 men (EA 289)**
- A Canaanite ruler (Labʾaya) is said to have given the land of Shechem to the Habiru (EA 289 o:21-b.e:24)

**ʿAziru: you are like Baal and like the Sun; I am the king's dog, rebuilding Ṣumur; the mayors lie (EA 159)**
- A vassal tells the overlord 'you are like Baal (Addu, the storm god) and like the Sun' (EA 159 o:7-8)

**ʿAbdi-Aširta to Paḫḫanate: I am no enemy of Egypt; I saved Ṣumur and four men from the Šeḫlali troops; the mayors lie (EA 062)**
- A vassal accused of treason answers that he rescued the king's city and its men, and that the officials who accuse him are lying (EA 062 o:4-23, EA 062 r:26-34)

**The Lady of the Lionesses, 'your maidservant': the land lost to the SA.GAZ; they were sent to Aijalon and Zorah (EA 273)**
- A woman ruler writes to the overlord as 'your maidservant' (amtu) and reports the land lost (EA 273 o:4-5)

**Zimreddi to an official: the breath of the king's mouth restored me; all your servants wait for you (EA 145)**
- A vassal says all the king's servants wait for (qwy) the overlord and look to his eyes (EA 145 r:27-29)

**A ruler: my brother in Tubiḫu went over to the GAZ; the king's god gave and I seized Tubiḫu and cursed my brother (EA 179)**
- A ruler retakes his father's city from his brother who went over to the Habiru, and curses the brother (EA 179 o:14'-r:29')

**Akizzi of Qaṭna: I trust in my lord's troops and chariots; Etakkama has seized the cities; the kings allied with Hatti (EA 056 + EA 361)**
- A vassal declares he trusts (taklāku) in the overlord's troops and chariots (EA 056 + EA 361 o:9-13)

**Baʿlu-meher: I have put my neck in the yoke I carry; I serve the king very much (EA 257)**
- A vassal says he has put his neck into the yoke that he carries for the overlord (EA 257 b.e:12-r:16)

**Ṣur-Ašar of Ginti-ašna: groom of your horses; who is the dog that would not obey the king, the Sun from heaven, son of the Sun? (EA 319)**
- Rhetorical question: 'who is the dog that would not obey the words of the king?' (EA 319 r:19-22)

**Zimreddi of Sidon: breath of my life; my head was lifted and my eyes shone at the king's word; cities given to the SA.GAZ (EA 144)**
- On hearing the overlord's word the vassal's heart rejoices, his head is lifted and his eyes shine (EA 144 o:13-b.e:18)

**Rib-Addi of Byblos: Abdi-Ashirta the dog is taking the king's cities, the Habiru gathered against Shigata and Ambi; send 400 men and 30 pairs of horses (EA 076)**
- Rhetorical 'Who is he?' scorning an upstart who acts like a great king (is he the king of Mittani or of the Kassites?) (EA 076 o:13-16)
- Formerly the overlord's troops (archers) went out every year to inspect and secure the vassal lands (EA 076 r:30-33)

**Mut-Baal, son of Labaya: who am I not to send on the caravans to Hanigalbat and Karduniash? (EA 255)**
- A vassal undertakes to escort and guard the overlord's caravans through his land to foreign kingdoms (EA 255 o:8-r:25)

**Rib-Addi: I am the footstool of the king's feet; Sumur attacked up to its gate, its commissioner dead; send Yanhamu, a wise man whom all love, and 20 pairs of horses (EA 106)**
- An official is praised as a wise man whom all men love, and is asked for as the king's representative (EA 106 r:36-40)

**Rib-Addi: the king is like Baal and the Sun in heaven; the sons of Abdi-Ashirta took the king's horses and chariots and gave men to Subaru; who are they, dogs, to resist the archers? Send 20 men of Meluhha and 20 of Egypt (EA 108)**
- The overlord king is likened to the storm god (Baal) and the sun in heaven (EA 108 o:8-10)

**The king to Aziru of Amurru: you received the man of Byblos whose brother cast him out at the gate; you ate and drank with the man of Qadesh; serve the king and live, or die by the king's axe with all your family; come or send your son; send these enemies of the king in copper chains (EA 162)**
- A vassal is charged with making peace with the king's enemy, eating bread and drinking beer with him (EA 162 o:22-25)
- The overlord tells a vassal: serve the king your lord and you will live; plot falsehood and you will die with all your family (EA 162 o:33-39)

**Rib-Addi in exile in Beirut: my brother swore to the city and gave it to the sons of Abdi-Ashirta; half the city loves them, half my lord; they say 'Rib-Addi is dead'; I sit in Beirut like a dog (EA 138)**
- A city is divided, half of it loving the rebel party and half the rightful lord (EA 138 r:71-73)
- A rumour that the absent ruler is dead ('our lord is dead') is used to hand his city over to his rival (EA 138 o:63-b.e:67, EA 138 r:111-113)

**Rib-Addi: Abdi-Ashirta the dog; the king wrote to the kings of Beirut, Sidon and Tyre to help me, but none came; we are three brothers; if no troops, I will leave the city (EA 092)**
- Neighbouring kings ordered by the overlord to help a besieged vassal do not come or even send to ask after his welfare (EA 092 r:31-40)

**Ari-Kirnihe to his brothers Ewri-huda and Tadie: send blue wool and linen; I will not send my messenger empty-handed (RSO 07, 022)**
- A writer will not send his messenger back empty-handed and asks for goods to be sent with him (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 022 b.e:1-r:3)

**Dagan-baal to Urtenu, his good brother: may the gods of the king seize your hand before him; the custom between brothers is gifts, but no one sends gifts into the house of his enemy; send tin, copper, wool, alum and oil by Anani-Sharruma: it is death and life (RSO 07, 032)**
- Gifts go between brothers and friends; a man does not send a greeting-gift into the house of his enemy ('am I your enemy?') (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 032 o:11-17)

**Issur-Rashap to his big brothers Anani-Sharruma and Baal(?): from afar I fall at my brothers' feet; may the gods of Ugarit and the gods of the tablet-house guard you (RSO 07, 034)**
- A writer says he falls at the feet of his addressees 'from afar' (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 034 o:5)

**Shalmaneser I of Assyria to Ibiranu of Ugarit: Tudhaliya of Hatti sent tablets of war and of peace, refused to return fugitives or to touch the oath-tablet before the Sun; at Nihriya I entered the Hittite army and made a great slaughter (RSO 07, 046)**
- An enemy king's messenger carries two tablets of hostility and one of peace, showing whichever suits the situation (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 046 o:21-30)
- A king asks why we, who are brothers, are enemies to one another (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 046 o:38-41)
- Challenged to touch a tablet of oath before the sun god to prove his peaceful intent, a king refuses (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 046 r:17-20)
- A herald cries to the camp: put on your coats of mail and mount your chariots, the enemy king is drawn up and coming (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 046 r:28-33)

**Hellu to his lord: may I go as your substitute; may Addu, Dagan and Itur-Mer, the great gods of Mari, guard you; my heart laughed to see you; send good horses for the king's chariot, save my life (RSO 07, 047)**
- A servant greets his lord with the wish 'may I go as a substitute (dinānu) for my lord', taking any evil on himself (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 047 o:1-2)

**Fragment: servant to king Akihinni(?), prostrating; Hazilu, Panishtayu, Halbini; the bull of the oath; the men of Halbini and Hazilu made an oath with each other (RS 01.0056)**
- The men of two towns make an oath (māmītu) with each other (Ugarit RS 01.0056 o:12, Ugarit RS 01.0056 r:11-14)

**Fragment: I made you swear before Nabu and the gods of your land and of Emar, and you have thrown my oath behind you; you do not remember me, have mercy on me (RS 12.0005)**
- A writer reproaches his addressee: the oath I made you swear before the gods you have thrown behind you (Ugarit RS 12.0005 o:6'-10')

**Muarihu to the prefect: you bought back my slaves for 400 silver from Hehea the Egyptian; you swore in the house of the gods; give me their ransom silver and the rest, let there be no debt between us, we are one man (RS 15.0011)**
- A creditor asks that the account be settled so that there be no debt between the two, 'for we are one man' (Ugarit RS 15.0011 r:6-10)

**Abiramu to Silabanu, his brother: take 45 silver from Pilsu son of Ebe for the merchants; the stones sealed with my seal, weigh and pay; guard my seal until I come (RS 15.0063)**
- Goods sent under the sender's seal are to be weighed and paid for in silver, and the seal kept intact until he arrives (Ugarit RS 15.0063 o:5-r:12)

**Deed of Niqmepa, sealed with the dynastic seal of Yaqaru: Ammistamru transfers to Sinaranu son of Siginu houses and fields in Mahraba and Atallig, each for its silver, for ever; no stranger, royal messenger or Habiru may enter his house; whoever alters the tablet, may the gods destroy his name (RS 15.0109 + RS 16.0296)**
- A royal grant decrees that no stranger, no royal messenger and no Habiru may enter the grantee's house (Ugarit RS 15.0109 + RS 16.0296 r:25-27)

**Before Niqmaddu son of Ammistamru, Ahi-malku fixes the shares of his sons: Tubammu is clear of his father and brothers as the pure sun; houses, fields, cattle and slaves go to Mashshu and Sheniyanu (RS 15.0120)**
- The high god (El) is called the great god, creator of man (Ugarit RS 15.0120 o:6-7)
- A legal release formula: a son or party is 'clear as the sun is clear' of claims from his father and brothers (Ugarit RS 15.0120 r:4-6)

**Ulmi to the queen of Ugarit, my daughter: may the gods of Ugarit and Amurru guard you; you know my whole house was put to fire; chairs for my daughter and the king (RS 16.0111)**
- The writer tells her correspondent that her whole house has been put to fire (Ugarit RS 16.0111 o:10-14)

**Fragment of a deed: in feudal service, the post of administrator; he gave Ishtar-Hurri, the gods of Harganu, and his house and share, and that of Attanu (RS 16.0173)**
- The gods of a man's house (his Ishtar, his gods) pass with his house and inheritance share to another (Ugarit RS 16.0173 r:1-7)

**Baal-danu (?) king of Tyre to Baal-zakaptu, prefect of Ugarit: Abdu son of Ayahhu, overseer of the quay, took a tax of silver on 14 jars of oil from my man; my own merchants never paid tax from of old: ask the elders of Ugarit (RS 17.0039 + RS 17.0397,b + RS 17.0424)**
- A ruler tells his correspondent to ask the elders ('fathers') of the city whether a tax was ever taken, appealing to custom from of old (Ugarit RS 17.0039 + RS 17.0397,b + RS 17.0424 r:10-13)

**Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+)**
- The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant (Ugarit RS 17.0079 + RS 17.0374 + RS 17.0338 o:2-4)

**Letter to a 'brother': the wife who wronged her husband sent back to her brothers; 'we are brothers, sons of one man' (RS 17.0116)**
- A woman who wronged her husband and slandered another is taken away and sent back to her brothers (Ugarit RS 17.0116 o:8'-r:2)

**Šuppiluliuma I's tribute treaty for Niqmaddu: Ugarit refused to join Nuhašše and Mukiš against Hatti; tribute to king, queen, crown prince and court; the thousand gods know (RS 17.0227)**
- A treaty fixes the vassal's tribute in gold, gold and silver cups, linen and blue-purple wool, graded for the great king, the queen, the crown prince and named court officials (Ugarit RS 17.0227 o:20-r:10)
- The vassal comes in person and throws himself down beneath the feet of the overlord (Ugarit RS 17.0227 r:16-19)

**King of Amurru to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': the Umman-manda, enemy lords of your father, made peace and sent on to you (RS 17.0286)**
- The Umman-manda, a hostile horde of uncertain origin, appear as enemies to be pacified or fought (Ugarit RS 17.0286 o:6-r:4)

**Šuppiluliuma I's edict of Ugarit's borders: Mukiš, Nuhašše and Niya attack Ugarit, Niqmaddu appeals, the Hittites rescue him; the frontier towns sealed for ever (RS 17.0339,a+)**
- Attacked by neighbouring kings, the vassal writes to the overlord: 'I am your servant; save me from the hand of the enemy' (Ugarit RS 17.0339,a + RS 17.0340 + RS 17.0366 o:9-14)
- The overlord's army drives out the invaders and he gives all the recovered captives and booty to the loyal vassal (Ugarit RS 17.0339,a + RS 17.0340 + RS 17.0366 o:15-24)

**Hittite verdict between Ugarit and Siyannu: oaths about Habiru of the tower, cut vines, provisions to raiders from Beirut, and the return of slaves (RS 17.0341)**
- The people of a town must swear that they did not strike, rob or harbour raiders, or else pay threefold compensation (Ugarit RS 17.0341 o:1'-6', Ugarit RS 17.0341 o:13'-r:1')
- Whoever, after the tablet, is found to have sold a fugitive slave of the other kingdom must pay compensation like a thief (Ugarit RS 17.0341 r:11'-12')

**Verdict of Ini-Tešub: the prefect v. Mašanda over 4,000 shekels and a broken sealed tablet; Mašanda to swear or repay (RS 17.0346)**
- A sealed tablet recording a debt is broken to cancel the obligation, and the parties dispute which debt the broken tablet recorded (Ugarit RS 17.0346 o:2-r:2)

**Before Ini-Tešub: queen Ahat-milku gives her sons Hišmi-Šarruma and ʿAbdi-Šarruma, who sinned against ʿAmmistamru, their share and sends them to Alašiya, under oath before Ištar of the steppe (RS 17.0352)**
- Princes who sinned against the king receive their share of the inheritance (silver, gold, goods) from the queen mother and are sent away to a foreign island, with an oath that they and their descendants will never claim more (Ugarit RS 17.0352 o:4-11)
- An oath between royal brothers is laid down before Ištar of the steppe (Ištar-ṣēri) (Ugarit RS 17.0352 o:12-13)

**Šauška-muwa of Amurru swears not to do murder against ʿAmmistamru of Ugarit, his ships or troops, over the daughter of the Great Lady; heaven and earth and the gods to know (RS 17.0365+)**
- A king swears not to do murder (nērtu) against a neighbouring king, his ships or his troops; if he does, the gods are to destroy him from his father's house, land and throne (Ugarit RS 17.0365 + RS 18.0006 o:1'-5', Ugarit RS 17.0365 + RS 18.0006 r:1-3)
- A king divorces (or harms) his royal wife, 'the daughter of the Great Lady' (a Hittite or Amurrite princess), and the case is decided by the great kings (Ugarit RS 17.0365 + RS 18.0006 o:5', Ugarit RS 17.0365 + RS 18.0006 r:4-9)

**Taguhli to the king of Ugarit: I fall twice seven times; the king is angry at the fake lapis; I was near death but recovered, and owe the god Apšukka offerings; send blue wool (RS 17.0383)**
- A gift sent to the king turns out worthless (a common stone sent as lapis lazuli); the king is filled with anger and accuses the sender of mockery (Ugarit RS 17.0383 o:10-r:10)
- A writer reports he was gravely ill, 'a finger from death', has now recovered, and owes the god who requested him offerings and many gifts (Ugarit RS 17.0383 r:11-20)

**Fragmentary letter: the gods of Mount Hazzi and Irridu guard you; men of the great queen, the daughter of the Sun; barley for his donkey (RS 17.0429)**
- A daughter of the Hittite Great King ('daughter of the Sun') is married into or resides at the court of a vassal king (Ugarit, Amurru) as great queen (Ugarit RS 17.0429 o:5'-8')

**The scribe Matkali-Nabû to the scribe Naheši-šalmu: why are you angry with your brother? write my sin on a tablet; send peas and lentils; the wax tablet and the sandals (RS 19.0053)**
- A letter asks 'why are you angry with your brother? you are not as before toward me; if I have sinned, write my sin on a tablet and send it' (Ugarit RS 19.0053 o:8-13)
- A wax-covered writing board (ṭuppu ša iškūri) is requested or sent in a letter (Ugarit RS 19.0053 r:1-7)

**Oath between Niqmaddu of Ugarit and Aziru of Amurru: all old claims broken, Aziru clear as the sun; 5,000 shekels paid; Aziru to fight Ugarit's enemies and Habiru raiders (RS 19.0068)**
- On the day the oath is sworn all past claims between two kings are 'broken'; one party is declared 'clear as the sun' (zakû kīma šamši) of all claims (Ugarit RS 19.0068 o:1-19)
- A treaty partner must come with chariots and troops if Habiru raid the other's land or if there is upheaval in it (Ugarit RS 19.0068 r:6-13)
- Silver is paid as ransom (ipṭiru) for one king's captured troops and horses (Ugarit RS 19.0068 r:20-21)
- The sun god is invoked to watch over or see the oath and its breaker ('may the Sun of that day see him') (Ugarit RS 19.0068 l.e:1-3)

**King of Ušnatu to the king of Ugarit: Baʿliya and his witnesses sent to swear and take his silver; the man whose companion left him to the Egyptians; set this agreement between us (RS 20.0021)**
- A man's companion leaves him to (or with) Egyptians and they take his goods (Ugarit RS 20.0021 b.e:1-r:9)

**King of Carchemish to ʿAmmistamru: Takiya and his witnesses to swear about the 800 shekels; vineyard cut at Šurašu; the men of Arzigana to swear they did not kill the woman's husband and do not know who did (RS 20.0022)**
- A woman's husband is killed in a town; the townsmen must swear that they did not kill him and do not know who did, or else pay compensation into her hand (Ugarit RS 20.0022 r:15-l.e:4)

**Šumi-[...] to the king his lord: five months in Amurru guarding the passes; winter cold has destroyed my chariots and horses; a captive says the king of Egypt is coming out; if the gods give him into our hands (RS 20.0033)**
