- A war captive and a woman of the enemy land are dressed in the king's garments and given to the enemy god as an adorned substitute to carry the plague back to the enemy land (CTH 407 §2:7-26, CTH 407 §3:27)
- The human substitute is praised as great in head, heart and limb, worthy of the god (CTH 407 §2:22)
- If it does not suit the king, he may send another to perform the rite in his place (CTH 407 §2:17-18)
- Red, yellow-green, black and white wool is drawn out of the king's mouth, removing the colours of disease he has taken on (CTH 407 §4:32-37)
- A bull with ringed ears and an adorned ewe are given to the enemy god (male or female) to carry the plague back to the enemy land (CTH 407 §4:28-30, CTH 407 §4:40-45, CTH 407 §5:47, CTH 407 §6:48)

**Uḫḫamuwa of Arzawa against dying in the land, the wreathed ram driven to the enemy and the god's horses fed (CTH 410)**
- A ram crowned with a wreath of five-coloured wool is driven onto the road to the enemy land (CTH 410 §2:5-9, CTH 410 §2:18)
- A ram is driven to the plague god 'for peace': as the strong herd makes peace with this ram, so may the god make peace with Hatti (CTH 410 §2:10-17)
- Fodder and sheep fat are brought for the god's harnessed horses: may they be sated, and may his chariot be greased with fat (CTH 410 §3:19-24)
- A goat is offered to the Seven gods and a sheep to the Sun, another sheep slaughtered and cooked (CTH 410 §4:27-31)
- Cheese, bread, wine, beer and fruit are prepared for the god of the road (CTH 410 §4:32-33)

**Uruwanda against the effects of slander, the tongue pulled down with sinew and seven fires each side (CTH 411)**
- A ritual treats a person for the effects of slander (lala- 'tongue') (CTH 411 §1:2)
- A sinew plaited with cords is tied to a reed, cut through and thrown into the flame (CTH 411 §1:3-8)
- The practitioner declares she has pulled down the tongue of evil and of sorcery and bound it with a cord (CTH 411 §2:10-11)
- Obscure spell: may the evil sorcerer protect the evil ones behind the shoulders (CTH 411 §3:13')
- Seven fires are kindled on one side and seven on the other (CTH 411 §4:16'-20')

**Building ritual for a new temple, copper nailed under the pillar and foundation stones of nine materials (CTH 413.1 §1-11)**
- Copper is laid in a pit at the place of the pillar, nailed round with pegs and struck with an iron hammer: as the copper is protective and eternal, so may the temple be on the dark earth (CTH 413.1 §1:4-9, CTH 413.1 §2:10-12)
- Blessing: may the one who built this temple be eternal before the gods, with grandchildren and great-grandchildren (CTH 413.1 §3:13-16, CTH 413.1 §11:51)
- Analogic blessing: as the four corners of the house are eternal on the earth and do not move, so may the patron's wellbeing not turn away (CTH 413.1 §4:17-20)
- The builders declare to the deity: 'not we built this temple; all the gods built it' (CTH 413.1 §7:27-31)
- The materials of the temple are said to have been brought from named lands and mountains: gold, silver, lapis, alabaster, quartz, copper (CTH 413.1 §9:37-45)
- Black iron 'of heaven' (meteoric iron) is said to have been brought from heaven for the foundation (CTH 413.1 §9:44)
- Analogic blessing: as gold is eternal, pure and strong, good for gods and men, so may this temple be eternal and good for the god (CTH 413.1 §10:46-50)

**Building ritual, pegs of precious metal, the golden lion and iron oxen, models of hearth, door and trees (CTH 413.1 §12-22)**
- Pegs of silver, gold, iron and bronze, one shekel each, are laid under the pedestal, the pillars and the corners (CTH 413.1 §12:52, CTH 413.1 §13:53-55, CTH 413.1 §14:56)
- A golden lion and two pairs of iron oxen yoked with a silver yoke on a base are set under the first middle pillar (CTH 413.1 §15:57-61, CTH 413.1 §16:62-65)
- Two copper foxes are set in the gate as a foundation deposit (CTH 413.1 §20:72-73)
- Sixteen apple trees of gold, silver, iron and bronze are laid as foundation deposits (CTH 413.1 §21:74-75)

**An incantation ritual, the AZU-priest, the bound bird, the reed gate, the arrow shot against oath and curse (CTH 413.2)**
- The gods of heaven and earth are addressed: the offering is for you, may the land be sated (CTH 413.2 §2:4-6)
- A bird is tied up at one side of the ritual gate (CTH 413.2 §3:7)
- The practitioner takes the patient's garment for himself (CTH 413.2 §3:11-13)
- The ritual priest shoots an arrow from a bow in a rite against oath and curse (CTH 413.2 §4:14-17)

**Parallel incantation ritual, the ancient gods, offerings to the Hurrian gods one by one, seven tongues in the hearth and seven oaths (CTH 413.3)**
- The practitioner declares 'now may the ritual patron be pure' (CTH 413.3 §11:14, CTH 413.3 §12:17, CTH 413.3 §23:32, CTH 413.3 §25:40)
- Flat bread is thrown into the hearth for the gods so that they may be appeased (CTH 413.3 §12:15, CTH 413.3 §13:18-22)
- A kupti- offering is given in turn to the Storm god, Ninurta, Kumarbi, Aya, the Moon, the Sun, Aštawe, Ḫebat and others (CTH 413.3 §14:23, CTH 413.3 §15:24, CTH 413.3 §16:25, CTH 413.3 §17:26, CTH 413.3 §18:27, CTH 413.3 §19:28, CTH 413.3 §20:29, CTH 413.3 §21:30, CTH 413.3 §22:31)
- Seven tongues are thrown with flat bread into the hearth (CTH 413.3 §24:34-35)
- Spell: if the Sun and Storm god (swore) the oath, may it be one; with seven oaths … with fire; may the patron be pure (CTH 413.3 §25:36-40)
- In the oath rite before the king the ritual is called out repeatedly (CTH 413.3 §34:52)
- Something in the rite is divided into halves together (CTH 413.3 §35:53)

**Another building ritual fragment, plastering and scraping (CTH 413.4)**
- In a building rite the house is plastered or scraped (CTH 413.4 §2:2-4)

**Palace-building ritual opens - plaster long years inside, awe outside (CTH 414.1 §1-2)**
- Before a palace is built the Sun god and the Storm god are consulted (by oracle) about it (CTH 414.1 §1:4-5)

**The king, the throne-goddess and the mountain's trees (CTH 414.1 §3-14)**
- The king speaks to the throne (the throne-goddess Halmasuit) as his companion and asks her to hand over the mountain's timber (CTH 414.1 §3:11-16, CTH 414.1 §10:41-§11:47)
- The throne-goddess brought the king rulership and the chariot from the sea, and he was named Labarna (CTH 414.1 §7:27-29)
- Trees that grew under heaven, under which the lion and leopard slept and cattle and sheep grazed, are claimed from the storm god and felled for the palace (CTH 414.1 §8:31-§10:40)
- The felled timbers are told to reveal what is in their heart, whether grief, evil, curse or illness, and sweep it out (CTH 414.1 §13:53-§14:63)
- The king Labarna comes and pours tin and iron into the heart of the timbers (to make them firm) (CTH 414.1 §14:64-65)
- The king and throne-goddess go to the mountain together, eat zapzaki, and the throne is told to protect the mountain (CTH 414.1 §4:17-20)
- Mutual avoidance formula: 'Do not come into my house, and I will not come into yours' (CTH 414.1 §5:23-24)
- The king praises the Storm god as 'my father' (CTH 414.1 §8:30)

**The eagle sees the fate goddesses spinning the king's years; the king renewed (CTH 414.1 §15-33)**
- In a ritual a speaker sends the eagle out to spy and report who is in the green forest (CTH 414.1 §15:66-71, CTH 414.1 §16:72-73, CTH 414.1 §26:122-125)
- Ancient netherworld goddesses (Išduštaya and Papaya) kneel with distaff and full spindles and spin the king's years (CTH 414.1 §16:74-§18:81)
- Litany 'take from him': illness, fear, headache, the evil words of men, revenge, knee and heart illness are taken from the king (CTH 414.1 §20:89-§21:98, CTH 414.1 §24:112-§25:119)
- Named mountains are told to stay in their place and not drive away the great one (CTH 414.1 §22:99-§23:107)
- The gods take away the king's old age and give him back youth and fighting strength (CTH 414.1 §25:119-121, CTH 414.1 §32:148-149)
- Lion's and leopard's paws are braided into one so that the king's soul be intertwined with his heart (CTH 414.1 §27:126-§28:131)
- The gods make the king a figure of tin with a head of iron, eagle's eyes and lion's teeth (CTH 414.1 §30:137-140)
- All the gods are gathered on the mountain and rejoice in the king and esteem him (CTH 414.1 §31:141-147)
- Grain is poured out and crushed: may the gods give over to evil and crush whoever plans evil against the king (CTH 414.1 §33:151-155)
- Skilled weaving women and weavers receive figs and raisins and are told to appease the king, his eyes, and take his ills away (CTH 414.1 §20:84-89)

**Provisions for the building stages; the new hearth and the tree analogies; colophon (CTH 414.1 §34-55)**
- As the household sits at the new hearth (king, queen, daughters, brothers), the hearth says 'This is good for me' (CTH 414.1 §43:183-§45:194, CTH 414.1 §47:197-200)
- Wish that sons, daughters, grandchildren and great-grandchildren become numerous (CTH 414.1 §47:198)
- Fat, honey, cheese, white and black wool, malt, nuts, raisins, salt and sprigs are laid under the new hearth (CTH 414.1 §48:201-202, CTH 414.1 §53:221)

**Palace-building ritual, second manuscript - thigh and vine analogies, effigies, a man's new house (CTH 414.2)**
- Replicas or effigies (ḫimma-) are handled in a royal ritual and someone bows (CTH 414.2 §6:12-§7:16)

**Festival ritual fragment - zintuḫi women, lambs brought from Hattuša (CTH 414.3)**
- Groups of cultic women (zintuḫi-women) sit to right and left in a festival (CTH 414.3 §1:2-4)
- Lambs are brought out of the capital and one handed to the king and one to the queen (CTH 414.3 §4:10-13)

**Temple-building ritual - offering in the pit; the place told to admit no other god (CTH 415 §1-13)**
- The ritual place (pedan) is given food and drink and told: eat, drink, rejoice; let no other god and no evil sign enter; watch over the god you are assigned to (CTH 415 §6:39-§7:43, CTH 415 §11:62-§12:71)
- Silver and gold are put into the ritual pit or vessel at the site of a building (CTH 415 §5:33-§6:35, CTH 415 §9:49-51)
- During the rite no deity is invoked aloud by the mouth (CTH 415 §8:44-47)
- The officiant 'drinks' (toasts) the altar, the place, the throne, the offering table, the censer and the brazier (CTH 415 §10:52-58)
- The ritual place is told it has received offerings of command and has had its thirst quenched and been anointed with oil (CTH 415 §11:64-68)
- Meat and bread that are not pure are taken by the officiant for himself (CTH 415 §13:72-79)

**Temple-building ritual - the foundation deposit with bronze statues and winged bull for Ea (CTH 415 §14-39)**
- Bronze statues of the house-building goddess (NIN.É.MU.UN.DÙ) are set at each corner of the foundation and a winged bronze bull at the place of the pillars (CTH 415 §14:83-84, CTH 415 §15:85, CTH 415 §17:90-95)
- The foundations are filled with every seed and fruit, oil, butter, honey, salt, silver, gold, precious stones and glass (CTH 415 §15:87-88, CTH 415 §16:89, CTH 415 §18:96-98, CTH 415 §19:99)
- Breads shaped like ears are put into the ears of the bronze foundation statues and the bronze bull (CTH 415 §21:101, CTH 415 §23:109-111)
- A wooden offering table for Ea is set before the central pillar with bread, cedar and libations (CTH 415 §21:102-104, CTH 415 §22:105-106, CTH 415 §23:107-108)
- A sheep is sacrificed and its blood smeared on the statues (and other ritual objects) (CTH 415 §26:116-119)
- The officiant, seated, 'drinks' named gods a set number of times, breaking a bread for each (CTH 415 §28:125-129, CTH 415 §29:130-§33:144)
- The deposited statues become the gods of the building (or place) (CTH 415 §25:115)
- The site is levelled and the foundation stones are poured (CTH 415 §14:80-81)

**Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple I - iron tongues, slanders taken, the Ḫantašepa deities (CTH 416 §1-19)**
- Tongues of iron are put in the mouths of king and queen and the 'tongues' (slanders) of the population are taken from them (CTH 416 §4:11-15, CTH 416 §9:34-37, CTH 416 §10:44)
- King and queen spit three times on a clay figurine, an ox, or a clay army that carries off their evil (CTH 416 §7:22-26, CTH 416 §14:67-68)
- A basin holds a 'heaven' of iron and one of copper with nine nails (CTH 416 §8:28-33)
- Wooden Ḫantašepa deities with blood-stained eyes and blood-red garments hold human heads and spears (CTH 416 §11:50-53)
- Clay cups filled with a liquid (tarlipa-) are carried in and called 'blood' (CTH 416 §12:54-55)
- After removing the royal couple's evil the expert sacrifices and asks the gods for mercy and protection (CTH 416 §17:78-§18:84)

**Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple II - the eagle waved over them and released to the sky (CTH 416 §20-32)**
- An eagle waved over the royal couple is released to the sky and told to tell the Sun goddess and Storm god that king and queen should be eternal (CTH 416 §21:96-97, CTH 416 §23:112-116, CTH 416 §25:130-131, CTH 416 §29:148-155)
- Analogy: as the Sun goddess and the Storm god, heaven and earth, are eternal, so may king, queen and children be eternal (CTH 416 §28:146-147, CTH 416 §29:154-155)
- The ritual expert disclaims the act: 'Not I released it; the king and queen released it' (CTH 416 §29:150-151)
- An eagle is presented to the Sun goddess and Storm god (as the royal couple's substitute) while king and queen hold sickle and millstone (CTH 416 §27:140-145)
- Cups are given to the king, the queen, the throne and the hearth (CTH 416 §22:107-110, CTH 416 §24:122, CTH 416 §25:133-134)
- Two palace attendants clash bronze spears together three times (CTH 416 §23:117-119, CTH 416 §25:135)

**Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple III-IV - the goat driven off, coloured threads, startled by birds (CTH 416 §33-51)**
- A billy-goat with breads hung on its horns is driven away after the royal couple's evil is taken (CTH 416 §33:181-183, CTH 416 §36:195-199)
- At dawn the expert and the physician inspect the blood-filled cup and the hearth and report whatever sign appears to king and queen (CTH 416 §41:220-226)
- Threads of five colours are hung on a tree and tied to the fingers of king and queen, then cut with a thorn bush to remove pain and constraint (CTH 416 §43:235-239, CTH 416 §44:252-253, CTH 416 §45:259, CTH 416 §46:262)
- The expert secretly holds two birds and releases them toward a branch; king and queen are startled and he cries 'I have taken your pain' (CTH 416 §46:267-271)
- King and queen spit into a clay cup which is closed with a lid of lead (CTH 416 §46:263-266)
- Pain, woe and constraint are taken from the royal couple's throne, bed, heart and limbs and handed to the Sun of heaven and Sun of the earth (CTH 416 §49:279-282)
- The expert tells the clay figurine to take the pain, woe and constraint of king and queen (CTH 416 §45:257-258)
- A deaf man assists the ritual expert (CTH 416 §44:248-250)
- Bound heads of barley and wheat are set in a covered basket over the royal heads and at their feet, so that no one sees (CTH 416 §43:241-246, CTH 416 §45:260-261)

**Ritual against the king's enemies - figurines of cedar and clay bearing names (CTH 417.1)**
- A ritual is attributed to named women experts who speak in the first person (CTH 417.1 §1:1-2)

**Ritual against the king's enemies - a name incised, six silver sun-discs (CTH 417.2)**
- Silver sun discs are used in a ritual against enemies (CTH 417.2 §1:5)

**Ritual against the king's enemies - oath-breakers addressed, rites in the enemy's field (CTH 417.3)**
- Speakers address those who keep breaking the oaths and announce they will go against the enemy troops (CTH 417.3 §2:3-10)
- Ritual actions are performed in the enemy's cultivated field (CTH 417.3 §3:11-14)

**Ritual when a foreigner offends against the royal couple I - substitutes, burnt animals, washing, hawthorn gates, pit offerings (CTH 418 §1-13)**
- Substitutes for the royal couple are prepared on the first day and released on the second (CTH 418 §2:7-8)
- After the treatment king and queen wash themselves in a tent (CTH 418 §4:12-14, CTH 418 §5:17)
- King and queen pass through two gates made of hawthorn, with cloth stretched beneath, breads and burning logs on either side (CTH 418 §5:18-§7:28)
- A sheep and a goat and the substitute's implements are thrown down into the pit-storehouse of the Sun goddess of the earth and the male gods (CTH 418 §10:42-43, CTH 418 §12:48-50)
- The netherworld queen (Ereškigal, Sun goddess of the earth) is told: 'Be compensated!' (CTH 418 §11:44-45)
- The ritual expert (Old Woman) takes the coloured cloths and the table for herself (CTH 418 §11:46-47)

**Ritual when a foreigner offends against the royal couple II - hearths nailed, arrows turned down, the foreigner thrown on his face (CTH 418 §9'-29)**
- The ritual expert reads the burning-down of the fire on the hearths as a favourable or unfavourable sign (CTH 418 §16:62, CTH 418 §19:65-69, CTH 418 §26'':79, CTH 418 §26:80-83)
- The hearth where the fire burns is fastened all round with nine bronze nails (CTH 418 §20:70-§21:72)
- Arrows are drawn and let down point first into a jar: as they fall, may the gods throw the foreigner who plots evil against the king on his face (CTH 418 §27:84-87, CTH 418 §28:88-90)
- A fox of bronze is placed in front of something in a ritual (CTH 418 §23:74)
- The ritual expert takes the names (written or spoken) in the rite (CTH 418 §22:73)

**Ritual of Zarpiya of Kizzuwatna I - in a plague year, an oath sworn with Šanta and the armed Innarawanteš (CTH 757 §1-15)**
- Offerings (kelu-) of lion-skin cap, stones and bear part, breads and wine are hung on pegs of medlar and cornel driven into the gate (CTH 757 §2:6-12, CTH 757 §3:13-17, CTH 757 §4:18-21)
- A named healing herb is buried on both sides in front of the gate (CTH 757 §5:22-24)
- Bronze axes, a dagger, a strung bow and an arrow are laid on a table for the plague gods (CTH 757 §5:25-28, CTH 757 §7:34, CTH 757 §8:47)
- The plague god Šanta comes with the Innarawanteš demons who wear blood-red clothes and mountain-dwellers' cloaks, girt with daggers, bows strung and arrows in hand (CTH 757 §7:36-39, CTH 757 §8:40-44)
- The householder swears an oath with the plague god and his demons by biting the same raw liver and drinking from one straw (CTH 757 §8:45, CTH 757 §9:49-59, CTH 757 §10:60, CTH 757 §11:61-62)
- A goat is dedicated with wine, slaughtered, and its blood smeared on the drinking straw (CTH 757 §7:32-33, CTH 757 §8:48, CTH 757 §9:49-52)
- The gods are called on: 'Be witnesses of this oath!' (CTH 757 §13:78)
- Eight boys who have not yet gone to a woman are brought; one dressed in a goatskin goes ahead howling like a wolf (CTH 757 §14:84-88)

**Ritual of Zarpiya II - Luwian incantation at the gate, the door anointed; colophon (CTH 757 §16-24)**
- The householder steps into the gate with a staff and incants in Luwian to King Šanta and the blood-clad gods (CTH 757 §16:96-98, CTH 757 §17:99-100)
- The plague demons are told: eat sheep and cattle, but do not eat a human being (CTH 757 §18:102-103)
- The great Sun god, the father-gods and Ea are invited to feed in the houses (CTH 757 §20:106-108, CTH 757 §21:109)
- The door is shut and anointed with fine oil: 'May it lock the evil out and keep the good inside' (CTH 757 §22:110-113, CTH 757 §23:114-115)

**Arad ostraca - orders to Eliashib to issue wine, flour and bread to the Kittim (Arad 1-4, 17)**
- A letter adds 'tomorrow; do not delay' (Arad ostraca W2:6)
- Provisions (bread, dough) are sent on donkeys to a named fort (Arad ostraca W3:1-8)
- Supplies or a document are sealed with the official's seal (Arad ostraca W5:1-2, Arad ostraca W6:1-7)

**Arad ostracon 18 - 'YHWH ask after your welfare'; the man in the house of YHWH**
- Letter greeting: 'may YHWH ask after your welfare' (Arad ostraca W8:1-3)
- A letter reports that a man stays in 'the house of YHWH' (Arad ostraca W8:6-9, Arad ostraca W9:1)

**Arad ostracon 24 - men sent to Ramat-Negev 'lest Edom come there'**
- A Judahite military letter warns that Edom may come against a fort in the Negev (Arad ostraca W10:8-9)
- Men are sent from forts to reinforce a threatened outpost (Arad ostraca W10:1-5)
- A military order stresses 'the word of the king is upon you, upon your lives' (Arad ostraca W10:6-8)

**Elephantine Passover letter - Hananiah to Yedaniah and the Jewish garrison, by order of Darius**
- An order 'from the king' (Darius) regulates the Jewish festival of unleavened bread (Elephantine (selection) W1:2)
- Festival instruction: be pure, take heed, do no work (Elephantine (selection) W1:5)
- During the festival everything leavened is brought into the chambers and sealed away (Elephantine (selection) W1:6, Elephantine (selection) W1:8)
- The Jewish military colony at Elephantine (Yeb) writes and receives letters as 'the Jewish garrison' (Elephantine (selection) W1:1, Elephantine (selection) W1:10)

**Petition to Bagohi (excerpt) - the temple of YHW at Elephantine, spared by Cambyses**
- Jews maintain a temple of YHW outside Jerusalem (at Elephantine), founded under the kings of Egypt (Elephantine (selection) W2:1)
- A conqueror (Cambyses) destroys the temples of the local gods but leaves the temple of YHW untouched (Elephantine (selection) W2:2-4)

**Marriage document of Ananiah, servitor of YHH, and Tamet the handmaid of Meshullam**
- Marriage formula: 'she is my wife and I am her husband from this day and forever' (Elephantine (selection) W3:3-4)
- A man marries another man's handmaid by agreement with her master, who renounces claim on her (Elephantine (selection) W3:2-3, Elephantine (selection) W3:13-14)
- A marriage contract lists the bride's goods (garment, mirror, sandals, oil) with their values in silver (Elephantine (selection) W3:4-6, Elephantine (selection) W4:1-2)
- Divorce is effected by a spouse rising in the assembly and declaring 'I hate my husband/wife', paying the 'silver of hatred' (Elephantine (selection) W3:7-10)
- The wife, like the husband, may declare the divorce and leave with what she brought (Elephantine (selection) W3:9-10)
- Marriage contract: if either spouse dies childless the other inherits all the goods (Elephantine (selection) W3:10-13)
- A contract ends with its scribe's name and the names of its witnesses (Elephantine (selection) W3:14-15)
- A man is called servitor (lḥn) of YHH the God in Yeb the fortress (Elephantine (selection) W3:2)

**Ahiram sarcophagus - the son's coffin for his father and the curse on whoever uncovers it (KAI 1)**
- A son makes the coffin for his father, the dead king (KAI 1 main:1-2)
- Tomb curse: may the violator's sceptre of rule be stripped, his royal throne overturned and peace flee from his city (KAI 1 main:7-9)
- The dead is laid down 'for eternity' (the grave as eternal home) (KAI 1 main:2)

**Yehimilk of Byblos - the temple restored; may the gods prolong the days of a just and upright king (KAI 4)**
- The king calls himself 'a just king and an upright king' (mlk ṣdq wmlk yšr) before the gods (KAI 4 W1:6–7, KAI 4 W1:7)

**Shipitbaal of Byblos - the wall built; may the Lady prolong his days (KAI 7)**
- The king names himself, his father and his grandfather, kings of the same city (KAI 7 main:1-3)

**Yehawmilk stele - the Lady of Byblos made him king and heard his voice; altar, gold door, curse (KAI 10)**
- The king called on his deity and the deity heard his voice and did good to him (KAI 10 main:2-3, KAI 10 main:7-8)
- The king makes a bronze altar, a gold doorway and a portico with pillars for the goddess (KAI 10 main:3-7)
- Blessing that the deity grant the king favour in the eyes of the gods and of the people of the land (KAI 10 main:9-11)
- Any future king who adds to the work must put the founder's name beside his own (KAI 10 main:11-13)

**Tabnit sarcophagus - priest of Astarte and king; no silver, no gold; do not open me (KAI 13)**
- The king of Sidon is also priest of Astarte (KAI 13 main:1-2)
- Opening the tomb is 'an abomination of Astarte' (tʿbt) (KAI 13 main:8)

**Eshmunazar II - carried off before his time, the orphan son of a widow; curses on the tomb-opener (KAI 14 Lid 1-13)**
- The dead king says he was snatched away before his time, of few days, an orphan, son of a widow (KAI 14 Lid:2-3, KAI 14 Lid:12-13)
- The reader is warned not to listen to people who urge him to open the tomb (KAI 14 Lid:6)
- Curse: may the holy gods hand the violator over to a mighty king who will cut him off (KAI 14 Lid:9-10)

**Eshmunazar II - temples built with his mother the priestess; Dor and Joppa granted by the lord of kings (KAI 14 Lid 13-22)**
- The king's mother, priestess of Astarte, builds the temples together with him (KAI 14 Lid:14-16)
- The king and his mother build temples for Astarte, Eshmun and Baal of Sidon (KAI 14 Lid:15-18)
- The king and queen set the deities (Astarte, Eshmun) in the 'mighty heavens' (or a district so named) (KAI 14 Lid:16-17)
- Astarte is called the 'Name of Baal' (KAI 14 Lid:18)

**Kilamuwa of Samʾal - kings before achieved nothing; hired Assyria; father and mother to his people; curse (KAI 24)**
- The king lists his predecessors one by one, each of whom 'did nothing', and boasts that he did what they did not (KAI 24 main:1-5)
- The king's house was among mighty kings and they 'ate' it as fire eats a beard or a hand (KAI 24 main:5-7)
- Image of misery: a young woman given for a sheep and a man for a garment (KAI 24 main:8)
- The king says he was father, mother and brother to his people (KAI 24 main:9-11, KAI 24 main:13)
- The king boasts that men who had never seen a sheep, an ox or linen became owners of flocks, herds, silver and gold in his days (KAI 24 main:11-13)
- Curse that two social classes of the kingdom (muškabim and baʿririm) shall not honour one another (KAI 24 main:14-15)
- The king sat on the throne of his father (KAI 24 main:9)

**Arslan Tash amulet 1 - incantation against the Fliers and Stranglers; eternal covenant; the doorpost (KAI 27 AT1)**
- Incantation: 'The house I enter you shall not enter, the court I tread you shall not tread' (KAI 27 W1:4-8)
- Female demons called Fliers and Stranglers attack by night in the dark chamber (KAI 27 W1:1-4, KAI 27 W1:19-21)
- An incantation claims an eternal covenant made with the household by a high god and all the divine beings (KAI 27 W1:8-12)
- An incantation bars the demon from the doorway and the doorpost (mzzt) (KAI 27 W1:22-26)
- The night demon is told to vanish like a moth when the sun rises (KAI 27 W1:26-29)

**Arslan Tash amulet 2 - against the Splatterers: Baal's chariot, 'Flee, Eye!' (KAI 27 AT2)**
- In an incantation the storm god harnesses his chariot and goes out like fire against the demon (KAI 27 W2:1-5)
- Incantation: 'Flee, Eye!', driving the evil eye from the head of the sleeper (KAI 27 W2:7-12)
- The speaker says his incantations correspond to the written scroll (KAI 27 W2:13)

**Mesha Stele - Mesha son of Chemosh-[yat], the high place for Chemosh who saved him (KAI 181 lines 1-4)**
- Royal inscription opening 'I am X, son of Y, king of Z' (KAI 181 main:1-3)
- The king builds a high place (bmh) for the national god in thanks for deliverance (KAI 181 main:3-4)
- The king's father reigned thirty years before him (KAI 181 main:2)

**Mesha Stele - Omri oppressed Moab because Chemosh was angry with his land; Israel perished forever (KAI 181 lines 4-9)**
- The national god was angry with his own land, so a foreign king oppressed it for many days (KAI 181 main:5-6)
- The enemy king boasts he will oppress the land, but the king sees his downfall and the enemy perishes forever (KAI 181 main:6-7)
- A land is held by its enemies for forty years (KAI 181 main:8)

**Mesha Stele - Ataroth taken, the ariel of Dawdoh; Nebo devoted to Ashtar-Chemosh, the vessels of YHWH dragged before Chemosh; Jahaz (KAI 181 lines 9-21)**
- The king builds (rebuilds) towns and makes a reservoir in them (KAI 181 main:9-10)
- The men of Gad are said to have lived in the land of Ataroth from of old (KAI 181 main:10-11)
- A conquered city's whole population is slain as a 'satiation' or spectacle for the national god (KAI 181 main:11-12)
- The conqueror settles people of other places in a captured town (KAI 181 main:13-14)
- The king marches by night and fights from dawn to noon (KAI 181 main:14-15)
- A conquered city's entire population (men, women, children) is slain because it was devoted (ḥrm) to the god (KAI 181 main:15-17)
- The cult vessels of YHWH are taken from a conquered sanctuary and dragged before the victor's god (KAI 181 main:17-18)
- The national god drives the enemy king out before the king (KAI 181 main:18-21)
- A double-named deity, Ashtar-Chemosh, receives the devoted city (KAI 181 main:17)

**Mesha Stele - Qarḥoh built with Israelite prisoners, a cistern in every house, the highway by the Arnon; Chemosh sends him against Horonen (KAI 181 lines 21-34)**
- There being no cistern in the city, the king orders every man to make a cistern in his house (KAI 181 main:23-25)
- The king uses prisoners of war to cut the works for his city (KAI 181 main:25-26)
- The king makes the highway by the Arnon (KAI 181 main:26-27)
- The king's home city is wholly obedient to him (KAI 181 main:28-29)
- The king brings the shepherds (nqdm) and sheep of the land to a town (KAI 181 main:30-31)

**Gezer calendar - the months of the agricultural year**
- A calendar lists the months of the farming year by their work: ingathering, sowing, late planting, flax-hoeing, barley harvest, harvest, pruning, summer fruit (KAI 182 main:1-7)

**Siloam tunnel inscription - the cutters meet axe to axe; the water flows 1200 cubits**
- Two teams cut a tunnel from both ends; hearing each other's voices through the rock they meet axe against axe (KAI 189 main:1-4)
- The thickness of rock over the tunnellers' heads is recorded (a hundred cubits) (KAI 189 main:5-6)
- A monumental building inscription names neither king nor god, only the work and the workmen (KAI 189 main:1-6)

**Lachish ostracon 2 - 'May YHWH let my lord hear news of peace'; 'who is your servant but a dog'**
- A letter calls on YHWH to deal with (call to account) a matter or person (KAI 192-199 W2:5-6)

**Lachish ostracon 3 - 'As YHWH lives, no one has ever read me a letter'; the commander goes down to Egypt; the prophet's letter 'Beware!'**
- An officer protests that he was accused of not knowing how to read and swears no one ever read him a letter (KAI 192-199 W3:4-13)
- A Judahite army commander goes down to Egypt (seeking aid) in the last days of the kingdom (KAI 192-199 W3:13-W4:2)
- A letter from a prophet reaches an official with the word 'Beware!' (KAI 192-199 W4:3-5)

**Lachish ostracon 4 - watching for the signals of Lachish; Azekah can no longer be seen**
- An officer writes his lord's orders 'on the door' (KAI 192-199 W5:2-4)
- A Judahite outpost watches for the fire-signals of Lachish because Azekah can no longer be seen (KAI 192-199 W6:1-5)
- Report that at a named house there is no one any more (KAI 192-199 W5:4-8)

**Lachish ostraca 5-6 - letters returned; the words of the officials 'weaken the hands of the land'**
- A subordinate urges his lord to write a reproof: 'why are you doing this?' (KAI 192-199 W8:7-10)
- An officer reports he has returned the letters sent to him (KAI 192-199 W7:4-7)

**Lachish ostraca 8-22 - greetings, 'the prophet', rations, the day of the ninth, names and Beth-Achzib**
- An unnamed or partly named prophet (-yahu the prophet) appears in military letters (KAI 192-199 W9:3, KAI 192-199 W15:5)
- A broken letter mentions work and digging at the dung-gate (or heap) (KAI 192-199 W14:1-3)
- An officer promises to send the letter before evening (KAI 192-199 W18:1-2)

**Yavne-Yam ostracon - the reaper's petition for his seized garment**
- A field labourer petitions the governor because an overseer took his garment though he finished his work (KAI 200 main:1-9, KAI 200 main:12-14)
- A worker appeals to his fellow reapers, who will testify that he is innocent (KAI 200 main:10-11)
- A non-literary Hebrew text mentions the Sabbath (or a 'stopping') (KAI 200 main:5-6)

**Zakkur stele face A - besieged by Bar-Hadad and sixteen kings, Zakkur lifts his hands and Baalshamayn answers through seers 'Do not fear' (KAI 202 A)**
- The king calls himself a humble (or lowly) man whom the god saved and made king (KAI 202 W1:2-3)
- A king is besieged by a coalition of many named kings with their armies, who raise a siege wall and dig a moat (KAI 202 W1:4-10)
- Ben-Hadad son of Hazael king of Aram is named (KAI 202 W1:4)
- The king lifts his hands to the god and the god answers him (KAI 202 W1:11)
- The god answers the king's prayer through seers (ḥzyn) and diviners (KAI 202 W1:11-12)

**Zakkur stele faces B-C - Hazrach and temples built; curse on whoever removes the stele (KAI 202 B-C)**
- The king sets up a stele before his god and writes on it the deeds of his hands (KAI 202 W2:13-15)
- Curse formula invoking the gods of heaven and the gods of earth (KAI 202 W2:23-26)

**Hadad statue of Panamuwa I - the gods gave him the sceptre; let the heir sacrifice and say 'may Panamuwa's soul eat and drink with Hadad'; curses on kin-murder (KAI 214)**
- The gods stood with the king and put the sceptre in his hand (KAI 214 main:1-3, KAI 214 main:8-9)
- The land is praised as a land of barley, wheat and garlic, field and vineyard (KAI 214 main:5-7)
- Prosperity formula: 'in my days the land ate and drank' (KAI 214 main:9-10)
- 'Whatever I asked of my gods they gave me' (KAI 214 main:4, KAI 214 main:12-13)
- The heir who sacrifices is to say: 'may the soul (nbš) of the dead king eat and drink with the god' (KAI 214 main:15-18, KAI 214 main:20-22)
- The heir who sacrifices to the god must invoke the dead father's name (KAI 214 main:16-17, KAI 214 main:21-22)
- Curse on the heir who does not sacrifice and invoke the dead king's name: may the god not accept his offering and withhold sleep from him (KAI 214 main:22-24)
- Curse on any of the king's kin who plots or causes the death of a kinsman, by sword, violence or command (KAI 214 main:25-34)
- A kinsman counsels destruction to annihilate his kin (KAI 214 main:29-31)

**Panamuwa II memorial by Bar-Rakib - usurper's massacre, flight to Tiglath-pileser, death at Damascus, the Assyrian king weeps (KAI 215)**
- A son erects a statue or stele as memorial for his dead father (KAI 215 main:1, KAI 215 main:20)
- The gods of the land rescue the young king from the destruction in his father's house (KAI 215 main:2)
- A usurper kills the king and seventy of his kinsmen (KAI 215 main:3)
- Under a usurper prisons are full, cities ruined and grain dear (KAI 215 main:4-6)
- The vassal king 'held fast to the wheel' of his overlord (ran beside his chariot) (KAI 215 main:6-7, KAI 215 main:13)
- Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria is named in a vassal inscription (KAI 215 main:13, KAI 215 main:15-16)
- The vassal king dies on his overlord's campaign; the overlord and his whole camp weep for him (KAI 215 main:16-18)
- The body of a king who died abroad is carried back by the overlord for burial (KAI 215 main:18-19)
- By his wisdom and righteousness the vassal seizes the hem of his overlord (KAI 215 main:11)
- The memorial is a 'remembrance' before the named gods of the kingdom and before men (KAI 215 main:22-23)

**Sefire I face A - the treaty of Bar-Gaʾyah of KTK with Matiʿel of Arpad and the gods as witnesses (KAI 222 A 1-13)**
- The treaty is concluded before a long list of named gods, paired, ending with heaven and earth, abyss and springs, day and night (KAI 222 W1:7-12)
- The treaty is 'cut' (gzr), the Aramaic counterpart of cutting a covenant (KAI 222 W1:7)
- The witnessing gods are told 'open your eyes to look on the treaty' (KAI 222 W1:13)
- The gods El and Elyon are invoked as a pair (KAI 222 W1:11)

**Sefire I face A - futility curses, seven years of locust, Arpad a tell, simile curses of wax, bow, calf (KAI 222 A 14-41)**
- Treaty formula: 'if the vassal is false (šqr) to the overlord, his son or his offspring' followed by curses (KAI 222 W1:14-16, KAI 222 W1:23-24)
- Futility curse: seven daughters go looking for bread and find none (or do not conceive) (KAI 222 W1:23-24)
- Curse: may no grass come forth and no green be seen (KAI 222 W1:27-28)
- Simile curse: 'as this calf is cut in two, so may the oath-breaker and his nobles be cut in two' (KAI 222 W1:39)
- Simile curse: as a man of wax is blinded (or stripped), so may the oath-breaker be (KAI 222 W1:38-39)
- Simile curse: as a harlot is stripped, so may the oath-breaker's wives be stripped and struck on the face (KAI 222 W1:39-41)

**Sefire I face B - the treaty of the gods, its extent; stipulations on loyalty, avenging the overlord's son, fugitives and bread (KAI 222 B)**
- Not one of the words of the treaty inscription is to be silent (unfulfilled) (KAI 222 W2:9-10)
- The treaty's territory is defined by named limits (from Lebanon to Yabrud, from Damascus to Aroer) (KAI 222 W2:10-12)
- Refrain: if the vassal does this, 'you will have been false to all the gods of the treaty written in this inscription' (KAI 222 W2:24, KAI 222 W2:28-29, KAI 222 W2:33-34, KAI 222 W2:38-39)
- The vassal must not excuse himself: 'I am a man under oath and cannot raise my hand' (KAI 222 W2:25-27)
- If anyone kills the overlord's son, the vassal must come and avenge his blood (KAI 222 W2:26-28, KAI 222 W2:32-34)
- If an enemy attacks the overlord, the vassal must come with all his army (KAI 222 W2:29-33)
- The vassal must give food to the overlord's men (KAI 222 W2:38-40)

**Sefire I face C - 'thus we have written for remembrance'; whoever effaces the words, the gods overturn him and his house (KAI 222 C)**
- The treaty is written as a remembrance for the vassal's son and grandson who will rise after him (KAI 222 W3:1-9)
- Blessing: may the gods guard the king's days and his house (KAI 222 W3:15-17)
- Curse on whoever 'turns the good into evil' in the inscription (KAI 222 W3:18-20)
- Curse: may the gods overturn the violator's house and make its lowest part its highest (KAI 222 W3:21-24)

**Pyrgi tablet (Phoenician) - Thefarie Velianas builds a holy place for Astarte at her request; years like the stars (KAI 277)**
- A goddess asks a king for a sanctuary, and he builds it (KAI 277 4)
- A holy place (ʾšr qdš) is made and given to Astarte (KAI 277 1-3)
- A dated festival day called 'the burial of the deity' (KAI 277 4)
- A non-Phoenician king dedicates a sanctuary to a Phoenician goddess in Phoenician (KAI 277 2)

**Tel Dan stele - Hadad made me king and went before me; the king of Israel and the king of the House of David slain (KAI 310)**
- Death formula: 'my father lay down and went to his fathers' (KAI 310 3)
- The dynasty of Judah is called 'the House of David' (bytdwd) in a foreign inscription (KAI 310 8-9)
- The god 'went before' the king in his campaign (KAI 310 5)
- The conqueror boasts that he killed seventy kings with thousands of chariots and horsemen (KAI 310 6-7)
- The conqueror turns the enemy's towns into ruins and his land into desolation (KAI 310 9-10)
- Jehu is named as ruling over Israel (KAI 310 11-12)
- The conqueror lays siege to a city (KAI 310 13)

- The ruler moves the population into cities from one end of the land to the other (Gen 47:21)
- Priests' land is exempt because they receive a royal allotment (Gen 47:22, Gen 47:26)
- A fifth of the harvest is paid to the king as a perpetual statute (Gen 47:24, Gen 47:26)
- Dying patriarch bows down on (or over) the head of his bed (or staff) (Gen 47:31)

**Jacob adopts and blesses Ephraim and Manasseh**
- Grandfather adopts two grandsons as his own sons, equal to his firstborn (Gen 48:5, Gen 48:6)
- Children placed on or taken from the knees of a patriarch as an adoption gesture (Gen 48:12)
- The angel who redeemed the patriarch from all evil is invoked to bless (Gen 48:16)
- Blessing that descendants teem like fish (Gen 48:16)
- Blessing formula 'May God make you like X and Y' coined by a patriarch (Gen 48:20)
- Patriarch bequeaths a portion (shekhem) he took from the Amorites with sword and bow (Gen 48:22)

**The Testament (Blessing) of Jacob and his death**
- Father curses two violent sons' anger and decrees they be scattered among the tribes (Gen 49:5, Gen 49:6, Gen 49:7)
- Tribes characterized by animal images (lion, ass, serpent, hind, wolf) (Gen 49:9, Gen 49:14, Gen 49:17, Gen 49:21, Gen 49:27)
- Judah likened to a lion's whelp crouching that none dare rouse (Gen 49:9)
- A tribe likened to a serpent by the road biting the horse's heels so the rider falls (Gen 49:17)
- A brief prayer ('For your salvation I wait, YHWH') interrupts a poem (Gen 49:18)
- Blessings of heaven above, of the deep crouching below, and of breasts and womb (Gen 49:25)
- The favored son called 'nazir (consecrated/prince) among his brothers' (Gen 49:26)

**Embalming and burial of Jacob; Joseph's last words and death**
- A great funeral procession with royal elders, chariots and horsemen escorts the patriarch's body (Gen 50:7, Gen 50:8, Gen 50:9)
- Locals name a place for the great mourning they witness (Abel-Mizraim) (Gen 50:11)
- Hero refuses to judge or avenge, asking 'Am I in the place of God?' (Gen 50:19)
- Dying hero foretells 'God will surely visit you' (paqod yifqod) and bring you up (Gen 50:24, Gen 50:25)
- Embalmed hero laid in a coffin (aron) in Egypt (Gen 50:26)

**Israel multiplies; oppression; the Hebrew midwives; decree to drown sons**
- The people 'swarm' (sharats) and fill the land like creatures in creation (Exod 1:7)
- A new king arises who did not know the former benefactor (Exod 1:8)
- Ruler fears the immigrant people will grow numerous and join his enemies (Exod 1:9, Exod 1:10)
- Oppressed people forced to build store-cities with mortar and bricks (Exod 1:11, Exod 1:13, Exod 1:14)
- The more the people are oppressed, the more they multiply (Exod 1:12)
- Two named midwives fear God and disobey the king's order to kill boys (Exod 1:15, Exod 1:17)
- Midwives observe the newborn on the birthstool (ovnayim, 'the two stones') (Exod 1:16)
- Midwives excuse themselves: Hebrew women are vigorous and give birth before the midwife arrives (Exod 1:19)
- God rewards the God-fearing midwives by making them houses (families) (Exod 1:20, Exod 1:21)

**Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry**
- The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman (Exod 2:1)
- Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov) (Exod 2:2)
- The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion (Exod 2:6)
- Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land (Exod 2:22)

**The burning bush and the divine name**
- Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God (Exod 3:6)
- The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain (Exod 3:12)
- God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh) (Exod 3:14)
- God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews' (Exod 3:18)
- God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion (Exod 3:19, Exod 3:20)

**Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood**
- The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs (Exod 4:17, Exod 4:20)
- Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead (Exod 4:19)
- God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him (Exod 4:24)
- Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man (Exod 4:25)
- Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood' (Exod 4:25, Exod 4:26)
- Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God (Exod 4:27)
- The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship (Exod 4:31)

**First audience with Pharaoh; bricks without straw**
- Slaves must make the same quota of bricks while gathering their own straw (Exod 5:7, Exod 5:8, Exod 5:10, Exod 5:11, Exod 5:12, Exod 5:16, Exod 5:18)
- Foreign taskmasters over native foremen who are beaten for unmet quotas (Exod 5:6, Exod 5:10, Exod 5:14)
- Tyrant accuses the oppressed of idleness for wanting to worship (Exod 5:8, Exod 5:17)
- The oppressed blame the deliverer for making things worse (Exod 5:20, Exod 5:21)
- Prophet complains to God that his mission has only made things worse (Exod 5:22, Exod 5:23)

**'I am YHWH': the name not known to the patriarchs; genealogy of Moses and Aaron**
- God says he appeared to the ancestors under another name and did not make his proper name known (Exod 6:2, Exod 6:3)
- God's promise of redemption phrased in four verbs (bring out, deliver, redeem, take) (Exod 6:6, Exod 6:7)
- The people cannot listen to the prophet because of their broken spirit and hard labor (Exod 6:9)
- A genealogy interrupts a narrative at the hero's commissioning (Exod 6:14, Exod 6:15, Exod 6:16, Exod 6:17, Exod 6:18, Exod 6:19, Exod 6:20, Exod 6:21, Exod 6:22, Exod 6:23, Exod 6:24, Exod 6:25)
- Hero's father married his own aunt (Exod 6:20)

**Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs**
- God makes the prophet 'as God' to the king with his brother as his prophet (Exod 7:1)
- Wonders done so that Egypt shall know 'I am YHWH' (Exod 7:5)
- Hero is eighty (and his brother eighty-three) when they confront the king (Exod 7:7)

**Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice**
- Egyptians dig around the Nile for drinkable water (Exod 7:24)
- Prophet lets the king choose when the plague should end, to prove God's power (Exod 8:5, Exod 8:6)
- The dead frogs are piled in heaps and the land stinks (Exod 8:10)

**Plagues 4-6: swarms, pestilence of livestock, boils**
- Israel's sacrifices would be an abomination to Egyptians who might stone them (Exod 8:22)
- Pestilence kills the oppressors' livestock while sparing the oppressed's (Exod 9:3, Exod 9:6)
- God sets a fixed time ('tomorrow') for a plague (Exod 9:5)
- Soot from a kiln thrown skyward becomes boils on men and beasts (Exod 9:8, Exod 9:9, Exod 9:10)
- The magicians themselves are struck and cannot stand before the prophet (Exod 9:11)

**Plague 7: hail and fire**
- Plagues sent so the king will know there is none like God in all the earth (Exod 9:14)
- God has kept the tyrant alive to show his power and make his name known in all the earth (Exod 9:15, Exod 9:16)
- A plague unlike any since the nation was founded, or ever again (Exod 9:18, Exod 9:24)
- Some of the king's servants fear God's word and bring their slaves and cattle indoors (Exod 9:19, Exod 9:20, Exod 9:21)
- Narrator dates a plague by the growth stage of named crops (barley in ear, flax in bud, wheat late) (Exod 9:31, Exod 9:32)

**Plagues 8-9: locusts and darkness**
- The king's own servants urge him to let the people go (Exod 10:7)
- A west wind carries the locusts into the Sea of Reeds (Exod 10:19)
- During the plague of darkness the Israelites have light in their dwellings (Exod 10:23)
- King tells the prophet never to see his face again or he will die (Exod 10:28, Exod 10:29)

**Announcement of the death of the firstborn**
- God announces one final plague after which the king will drive them out (Exod 11:1)
- The prophet becomes very great in the eyes of the king's servants and the people (Exod 11:3)
- God goes out through the land at midnight to strike (Exod 11:4)
- Not even a dog will growl at the Israelites on the night of the plague (Exod 11:7)

**Passover law, matzot, the night of the firstborn, departure from Egypt**
- The spring exodus month becomes the first month of the year (Exod 12:2)
- An unblemished yearling lamb selected on the tenth and slaughtered at twilight on the fourteenth (Exod 12:3, Exod 12:5, Exod 12:6)
- Small households join neighbors to share one sacrificial lamb (Exod 12:4)
- Sacrificial lamb roasted whole, head, legs and innards, eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs (Exod 12:8, Exod 12:9)
- Leaven must be removed from houses; whoever eats it is cut off (Exod 12:15, Exod 12:19)
- Festival days are holy convocations on which no work is done except preparing food (Exod 12:16)
- No one may leave the house until morning on the night of the destroyer (Exod 12:22)
- Defeated king asks the departing prophet to bless him too (Exod 12:32)
- The people carry their unleavened dough in kneading-troughs on their shoulders (Exod 12:34, Exod 12:39)
- About 600,000 men on foot leave Egypt, besides children (Exod 12:37)
- A mixed multitude (erev rav) of non-Israelites leaves Egypt with Israel (Exod 12:38)
- Israel's stay in Egypt lasts 430 years to the very day (Exod 12:40, Exod 12:41)
- No uncircumcised foreigner may eat the Passover; circumcised slaves and converts may (Exod 12:43, Exod 12:44, Exod 12:45, Exod 12:48)
- No bone of the paschal sacrifice may be broken (Exod 12:46)

**Consecration of the firstborn, sign on hand and forehead, Joseph's bones, pillar of cloud and fire**
- The exodus month is Aviv, the month of ripening grain (Exod 13:4)
- Firstborn sons must be redeemed (Exod 13:13, Exod 13:15)
- God leads the people by a roundabout route so they will not see war and turn back (Exod 13:17, Exod 13:18)

**The pursuit and the parting of the sea**
- Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth (Exod 14:2, Exod 14:9)
- God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him (Exod 14:3, Exod 14:4, Exod 14:17, Exod 14:18)
- The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness (Exod 14:11, Exod 14:12)
- God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward' (Exod 14:15)
- God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers (Exod 14:19, Exod 14:20)
- At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy (Exod 14:24)
- God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots (Exod 14:25)
- The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore (Exod 14:30)
- After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant (Exod 14:31)

**The Song of the Sea and Miriam's song**
- By the blast of God's nostrils the waters pile up and the deeps congeal (Exod 15:8, Exod 15:10)
- The earth swallows the enemy at God's outstretched right hand (Exod 15:12)
- God leads the redeemed people to his holy abode (Exod 15:13)
- Neighboring nations and chieftains tremble on hearing of God's deeds (Exod 15:14, Exod 15:15, Exod 15:16)

**Bitter water sweetened at Marah; Elim's twelve springs and seventy palms**
- Three days in the wilderness without finding water (Exod 15:22)
- At a desert stop God gives statute and ordinance and tests the people (Exod 15:25)

**Manna and quail; the first Sabbath**
- Food is given daily, a day's portion at a time, to test obedience (Exod 16:4, Exod 16:16, Exod 16:21)
- Manna appears as a fine flaky layer like hoarfrost when the dew lifts (Exod 16:13, Exod 16:14)
- Each gathers an omer per person; the one who gathers much has no excess, the one who gathers little no lack (Exod 16:16, Exod 16:17, Exod 16:18)
- Manna kept overnight breeds worms and stinks (Exod 16:19, Exod 16:20)
- Ungathered manna melts when the sun grows hot (Exod 16:21)
- A double portion of manna falls or is gathered on the sixth day (Exod 16:5, Exod 16:22, Exod 16:29)
- Manna kept for the Sabbath does not spoil or breed worms (Exod 16:24)
- Those who go out to gather on the Sabbath find nothing (Exod 16:27, Exod 16:28)
- Explanatory gloss defining a measure (an omer is a tenth of an ephah) (Exod 16:36)

**Water from the rock at Massah and Meribah**
- God stands upon a rock before the prophet (Exod 17:6)
- The people put God to the test (Exod 17:2, Exod 17:7)

**Battle with Amalek; Moses' raised hands**
- Joshua leads Israel's fighting men (Exod 17:9, Exod 17:13)
- Battle outcome depends on the leader keeping his hands raised (Exod 17:11)
- Two men hold up the leader's tired arms, one on each side (Exod 17:12)

**Jethro's visit and the appointment of judges**
- The hero's wife and sons were sent away and are brought back to him (Exod 18:2)
- A father names his sons after events in his own life (Exod 18:3, Exod 18:4)
- A foreign priest offers sacrifice to Israel's God and shares a meal with the elders (Exod 18:12)
- The leader judges the people alone from morning to evening and is overburdened (Exod 18:13, Exod 18:14, Exod 18:18)
- Minor cases are judged by subordinates; hard cases go to the leader (Exod 18:22, Exod 18:26)
- The prophet adopts an administrative reform suggested by a foreigner (Exod 18:24)

**Arrival at Sinai, covenant offer and theophany**
- Israel arrives at Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exod 19:1)
- God comes to the prophet in a thick cloud so the people may hear (Exod 19:9)
- God descends or reveals himself on the third day (Exod 19:11, Exod 19:16)
- A ram's horn blast signals that the people may go up the mountain (Exod 19:13)
- Men must not approach a woman before a holy encounter (Exod 19:15)
- Moses speaks and God answers him with a voice (thunder) (Exod 19:19)
- Priests are mentioned before the Aaronic priesthood is instituted (Exod 19:22, Exod 19:24)

**The Ten Words and the people's fear**
- God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves (Exod 20:2)
- The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation (Exod 20:18)
- The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is (Exod 20:21)

**Altar law**
- God declares that he spoke from heaven (Exod 20:22)
- Altar to be made of earth (Exod 20:24)
- God will come and bless in every place where he causes his name to be remembered (Exod 20:24)
- No steps up to the altar, lest nakedness be exposed (Exod 20:26)

**Covenant Code - Hebrew slaves**
- A wife given by the master and her children stay with the master when the slave goes free (Exod 21:4)
- A daughter sold as a slave-wife keeps rights to food, clothing and conjugal relations or goes free (Exod 21:7-11)

**Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox**
- Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall be put to death (Exod 21:12)
- Striking or cursing father or mother is a capital crime (Exod 21:15, Exod 21:17)
- One who injures another pays for his lost time and his healing (Exod 21:18, Exod 21:19)
- A master who beats his slave to death is punished, unless the slave survives a day or two (Exod 21:20, Exod 21:21)
- Men fighting strike a pregnant woman and she miscarries (Exod 21:22, Exod 21:23)
- A slave whose eye or tooth the master destroys goes free (Exod 21:26, Exod 21:27)
- Laws of the goring ox and the warned owner (Exod 21:28-32, Exod 21:35, Exod 21:36)
- An animal that kills a person is stoned and its flesh not eaten (Exod 21:28)
- The owner of an uncovered pit pays for an animal that falls in (Exod 21:33, Exod 21:34)

**Covenant Code - theft, deposits, seduction**
- A thief who cannot pay is sold for his theft (Exod 22:2)
- A thief pays double (Exod 22:3, Exod 22:6, Exod 22:8)
- A dispute over deposited goods is brought before God (ha-elohim) for decision (Exod 22:7, Exod 22:8)
- A herdsman brings the remains of a torn animal as evidence and is not liable (Exod 22:12)
- Liability for a borrowed animal that dies when the owner is absent (Exod 22:13, Exod 22:14)

**Covenant Code - sorceress, stranger, widow, loans, firstborn**
- Lying with an animal is a capital crime (Exod 22:18)
- Whoever sacrifices to other gods is devoted to destruction (Exod 22:19)
- Flesh torn by beasts in the field is not eaten but thrown to dogs (Exod 22:30)

**Covenant Code - justice, enemy's animal, sabbatical year, festivals**
- Neither favor nor pervert justice for the poor in his lawsuit (Exod 23:3, Exod 23:6)
- Return your enemy's stray animal and help his overloaded donkey (Exod 23:4, Exod 23:5)

**The angel sent ahead and promises of conquest**
- Obedience is rewarded with health, fertility and full lifespan (Exod 23:25, Exod 23:26)
- The promised borders run from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines and to the River (Exod 23:31)

**Covenant ratified in blood; the elders see God**
- Only the prophet may approach God; the others stay at a distance (Exod 24:2)
- The prophet writes down all of God's words (Exod 24:4)
- Young men, not priests, offer the covenant sacrifices (Exod 24:5)
- Sacrificial blood splashed on altar and people seals the covenant ('blood of the covenant') (Exod 24:6, Exod 24:8)
- People see God and are not harmed (Exod 24:11)
- A meal eaten in God's presence seals a covenant (Exod 24:11)

**Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days**
- Joshua serves as Moses' attendant (Exod 24:13)
- The cloud covers the mountain six days and God calls on the seventh (Exod 24:16)
- God's glory appears as a devouring fire (Exod 24:17)

**The high priest's vestments**
- Aaron and his sons are designated as priests (Exod 28:1)
- Priestly garments are made for glory and beauty (Exod 28:2, Exod 28:40)

**Ordination of the priests**
- A basket of unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers is offered (Exod 29:2, Exod 29:3, Exod 29:23)
- The high priest's vestments pass to his successor, who wears them seven days (Exod 29:29, Exod 29:30)
- An outsider may not eat holy food (Exod 29:33)

**The daily offering and God's dwelling**
- The tent of meeting is where God meets Israel and speaks with Moses (Exod 29:42, Exod 29:43)

**Incense altar, half-shekel ransom and bronze laver**
- Incense is burned every morning and evening (Exod 30:7, Exod 30:8)
- Unauthorized ('strange') incense or offerings are forbidden on the altar (Exod 30:9)
- Once a year atonement is made on the altar's horns with blood (Exod 30:10)
- Atonement money funds the sanctuary as a memorial before God (Exod 30:16)

**Recipes of the holy anointing oil and incense**
- Copying the sacred oil or incense for private use is forbidden on pain of being cut off (Exod 30:32, Exod 30:33, Exod 30:37, Exod 30:38)
- Sacred incense of stacte, onycha, galbanum and frankincense in equal parts, salted (Exod 30:34, Exod 30:35, Exod 30:36)

**The golden calf**
- The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith (Exod 32:1)
- Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH (Exod 32:5)
- The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol (Exod 32:6)
- Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Exod 32:13)

**Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer**
- The tablets are written on both sides by God (Exod 32:15, Exod 32:16)
- The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle (Exod 32:17, Exod 32:18)
- Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire (Exod 32:22, Exod 32:23, Exod 32:24)
- The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies (Exod 32:25)
- The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies (Exod 32:26)
- The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven (Exod 32:32, Exod 32:33)
- God strikes the people with plague for idolatry (Exod 32:35)

**Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back**
- God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way (Exod 33:3, Exod 33:5)
- A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go (Exod 33:7)
- The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God (Exod 33:8, Exod 33:10)
- Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent (Exod 33:11)
- God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor (Exod 33:12, Exod 33:17)

**New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue**
- The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time (Exod 34:21)
- God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage (Exod 34:24)

**Moses' shining face and the veil**
- The people fear to approach the prophet after his encounter with God (Exod 34:30)
- The prophet covers his radiant face with a veil (Exod 34:33, Exod 34:34, Exod 34:35)

**Sabbath fire ban and the people's donations**
- No fire may be kindled in any dwelling on the Sabbath (Exod 35:3)
- Men and women donate their jewelry to the sanctuary (Exod 35:22)
- Skilled women spin yarn and goat hair for the sanctuary (Exod 35:25, Exod 35:26)
- The tribal chieftains bring the gemstones, spices and oil (Exod 35:27, Exod 35:28)

**Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames**
- God gives the master craftsmen the ability to teach others (Exod 35:34)
- The people bring more than enough and must be told to stop giving (Exod 36:5, Exod 36:6, Exod 36:7)

**Altar, laver of mirrors, court and the metal inventory**
- The bronze laver is made from the mirrors of the women (Exod 38:8)
- Women who serve at the entrance of the tent of meeting (Exod 38:8)
- Ithamar son of Aaron supervises the Levites' work (Exod 38:21)
- The count of Israelite men is 603,550 (Exod 38:26)
- One hundred silver talents make one hundred sockets, a talent each (Exod 38:27)

**The vestments made; the work completed and blessed**
- Gold is beaten into sheets and cut into threads for weaving (Exod 39:3)
- The leader sees the finished work and blesses the workers (Exod 39:43)

**The tabernacle erected; cloud and glory fill it**
- When the cloud lifts from the tabernacle the people set out; otherwise they stay (Exod 40:36, Exod 40:37)

**The burnt offering of cattle, flock and birds**
- God calls to Moses and speaks from the tent of meeting (Lev 1:1)
- The victim is flayed and cut into its pieces (Lev 1:6, Lev 1:12)
- The entrails and legs are washed with water before burning (Lev 1:9, Lev 1:13)
- The bird's crop and feathers are thrown on the ash heap east of the altar (Lev 1:16)
- The bird is torn open by its wings but not divided in two (Lev 1:17)

**The grain offering; no leaven or honey; salt of the covenant**
- A grain offering of fine flour with oil and frankincense (Lev 2:1, Lev 2:15)
- Grain offerings baked in an oven, on a griddle or in a pan (Lev 2:4, Lev 2:5, Lev 2:6, Lev 2:7)
- No leaven or honey may be burned on the altar (Lev 2:11)
- First-fruit offerings are brought but not burned on the altar (Lev 2:12)
- First-fruits grain offering of fresh ears roasted in fire (Lev 2:14)

**The well-being (shelamim) offering and the ban on fat and blood**
- The sacrifice is called God's food (lehem) (Lev 3:11, Lev 3:16)
- All the fat belongs to YHWH (Lev 3:16)

**The purification (hattat) offering for unintentional sin**
- An offering is required for sins committed unintentionally (Lev 4:2, Lev 4:13, Lev 4:22, Lev 4:27)
- The required sacrifice is graded by the sinner's rank: priest, community, chieftain, commoner (Lev 4:3, Lev 4:14, Lev 4:23, Lev 4:28, Lev 4:32)
- The anointed priest's sin brings guilt on the whole people (Lev 4:3)
- The priest sprinkles blood seven times before the veil (Lev 4:6, Lev 4:17)
- The elders lay hands on the offering on behalf of the community (Lev 4:15)

**Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering**
- Touching an unclean carcass or human impurity makes one guilty (Lev 5:2, Lev 5:3)
- The poorest bring a flour sin offering without oil or frankincense (Lev 5:11)
- Sacrilege (me'ilah) against the holy things of YHWH (Lev 5:15, Lev 5:16)
- Defrauding a neighbor with a false oath is a trespass against God (Lev 5:21, Lev 5:22)
- Restitution to the wronged person precedes the atonement offering (Lev 5:23, Lev 5:24, Lev 5:25)

**Priestly instructions for burnt, grain and sin offerings; the perpetual fire**
- The priest removes the ashes in linen garments and changes clothes to take them out (Lev 6:3, Lev 6:4)
- The anointed priest offers a daily griddle-cake grain offering, half morning half evening (Lev 6:13, Lev 6:14, Lev 6:15)
- A priest's own grain offering is wholly burned and not eaten (Lev 6:15, Lev 6:16)
- A garment spattered with sin-offering blood is washed in a holy place (Lev 6:20)
- An earthen vessel that held sacred meat is broken; a bronze one is scoured and rinsed (Lev 6:21)
- A sin offering whose blood is brought inside the sanctuary is burned, not eaten (Lev 6:23)

**Guilt and well-being offerings; priests' portions; fat and blood bans**
- The officiating priest receives the hide of the burnt offering (Lev 7:8)
- The thanksgiving offering is accompanied by leavened loaves (Lev 7:12, Lev 7:13)
- Sacrificial meat must be eaten within a fixed time and leftovers burned (Lev 7:15, Lev 7:16, Lev 7:17)
- An impure person who eats sacred meat is cut off (Lev 7:19, Lev 7:20, Lev 7:21)
- Fat of a carcass or torn animal may be used for work but not eaten (Lev 7:24)
- The offerer must bring the offering with his own hands (Lev 7:30)

**Moses ordains Aaron and his sons**
- The whole congregation is assembled at the tent entrance to witness a rite (Lev 8:3, Lev 8:4)
- Moses himself performs the priestly rites at the ordination (Lev 8:15, Lev 8:19, Lev 8:29)

**The eighth day - Aaron's first offerings and the divine fire**
- Cult inaugurated on the eighth day after a seven-day ordination (Lev 9:1)
- High priest's own sin offering is a calf (Lev 9:2, Lev 9:8)
- The breast and right thigh are waved before God and given to the priests (Lev 9:21)
- The glory (kavod) of God appears to all the people (Lev 9:4, Lev 9:6, Lev 9:23)
- The people shout and fall on their faces at the theophany (Lev 9:24)

**Strange fire - death of Nadab and Abihu; priestly rules**
- God says he is sanctified through those who are near him, after a fatal cultic error (Lev 10:3)
- Father remains silent on the death of his sons (Lev 10:3)
- Bodies of priests struck by God carried out of the camp in their tunics by relatives (Lev 10:4, Lev 10:5)
- Moses is angry that the priests burned the sin offering instead of eating it (Lev 10:16, Lev 10:17, Lev 10:18)
- The bereaved priest declines to eat the sin offering on the day of his sons' death, and Moses accepts this (Lev 10:19, Lev 10:20)

**Clean and unclean animals; carcass impurity**
- The camel is unclean because it does not have a split hoof (Lev 11:4)
- The hyrax and the hare are described as chewing the cud (Lev 11:5, Lev 11:6)
- Certain kinds of locust with jointed legs for hopping may be eaten (Lev 11:21, Lev 11:22)
- Touching or carrying a carcass makes one unclean until evening (Lev 11:24, Lev 11:25, Lev 11:27, Lev 11:28, Lev 11:39, Lev 11:40)
- A list of eight swarming creatures (mole, mouse, lizards, chameleon) whose carcasses defile (Lev 11:29, Lev 11:30, Lev 11:31)
- Food or seed becomes susceptible to impurity only once water has come on it (Lev 11:34, Lev 11:37, Lev 11:38)
- A spring or cistern collecting water remains clean even if a carcass falls in (Lev 11:36)
- Creatures that go on their belly or have many legs are forbidden as food (Lev 11:41, Lev 11:42)

**Impurity after childbirth**
- Mother's impurity after a daughter's birth lasts twice as long as after a son's (Lev 12:2, Lev 12:4, Lev 12:5)
- Woman after childbirth may not touch holy things or enter the sanctuary until her days are complete (Lev 12:4)
- Mother brings a burnt offering and sin offering at the end of her purification (Lev 12:6, Lev 12:7)

**Diagnosis of tsara'at in skin, scalp and fabric**
- Priest inspects and declares a skin affliction clean or unclean (Lev 13:2, Lev 13:3)
- Hair turned white in the affected spot is a sign of skin disease (Lev 13:3, Lev 13:10, Lev 13:20, Lev 13:25)
- Priest shuts up a suspected affliction for seven days and re-examines it (Lev 13:4, Lev 13:5, Lev 13:21, Lev 13:26, Lev 13:31, Lev 13:33, Lev 13:50, Lev 13:54)
- Raw (living) flesh in a swelling is a sign of skin disease (Lev 13:10, Lev 13:14, Lev 13:15)
- A person whose skin disease covers the whole body and turns white is declared clean (Lev 13:12, Lev 13:13)
- Skin disease diagnosed in a healed boil or burn scar (Lev 13:18, Lev 13:19, Lev 13:23, Lev 13:24, Lev 13:28)
- Skin disease of the scalp or beard (neteq) judged by yellow or black hair (Lev 13:29, Lev 13:30, Lev 13:37)
- Ordinary baldness of the head or forehead is declared clean (Lev 13:40, Lev 13:41)
- Fabric or leather with spreading green or red 'leprous' mold is burned (Lev 13:47, Lev 13:48, Lev 13:49, Lev 13:51, Lev 13:52, Lev 13:55, Lev 13:57)

**Purification of the healed leper; plague in houses**
- Priest goes out of the camp to examine the healed person (Lev 14:3)
- Bird slaughtered over running water in an earthenware vessel (Lev 14:5, Lev 14:50)
- Oil poured on the head of the person being purified (Lev 14:18, Lev 14:29)
- God himself puts a 'leprous' plague in houses of the land (Lev 14:34)
- House is emptied before the priest inspects it so its contents are not defiled (Lev 14:36)
- Infected stones and plaster removed to an unclean place outside the city (Lev 14:40, Lev 14:41, Lev 14:42, Lev 14:45)
- House whose 'leprous' plague returns after repair is torn down (Lev 14:43, Lev 14:44, Lev 14:45)

**Impurity of bodily discharges, semen and menstruation**
- A man with a genital discharge is unclean (Lev 15:2, Lev 15:3)
- Impurity passes to the bed, seat or saddle of the unclean person and to whoever touches them (Lev 15:4, Lev 15:5, Lev 15:6, Lev 15:9, Lev 15:10, Lev 15:20, Lev 15:21, Lev 15:22, Lev 15:23, Lev 15:26)
- Spittle of an unclean person defiles the person it falls on (Lev 15:8)
- Person with a discharge who has rinsed his hands does not transmit impurity by touch (Lev 15:11)
- After a discharge ends, seven clean days are counted and the person bathes in living water (Lev 15:13, Lev 15:28)
- Menstruating woman is unclean seven days and defiles what she lies or sits on (Lev 15:19, Lev 15:24)
- Woman with bleeding beyond her menstrual period is unclean all the days of the flow (Lev 15:25, Lev 15:26, Lev 15:27)
- Human impurity defiles God's dwelling in their midst and endangers them (Lev 15:31)

**The Day of Atonement and the goat for Azazel**
- High priest may enter the inner sanctuary behind the veil only on the annual day of atonement (Lev 16:2, Lev 16:34)
- High priest wears plain linen garments to enter the holy of holies (Lev 16:4, Lev 16:23, Lev 16:32)
- Lots cast over two goats to decide their roles (Lev 16:8)
- A goat is designated by lot 'for Azazel', a named wilderness recipient (Lev 16:8, Lev 16:10, Lev 16:26)
- Cloud of incense covers the ark cover so the priest does not die (Lev 16:12, Lev 16:13)
- Blood rites purge the sanctuary and altar of the people's impurities and transgressions (Lev 16:16, Lev 16:18, Lev 16:19, Lev 16:20, Lev 16:33)
- No one may be in the tent while the high priest makes atonement in the sanctuary (Lev 16:17)
- Priest confesses the people's sins over the head of a live animal (Lev 16:21)

**Slaughter only at the tent; the blood is the life**
- Animals may be slaughtered only as offerings at the sanctuary entrance (Lev 17:3, Lev 17:4, Lev 17:5, Lev 17:8, Lev 17:9)
- Eating blood is forbidden because the life (nefesh) of the flesh is in the blood (Lev 17:10, Lev 17:11, Lev 17:12, Lev 17:14)
- God gives blood on the altar to make atonement for lives (Lev 17:11)
- The law applies to the resident alien (ger) as to the Israelite (Lev 17:8, Lev 17:10, Lev 17:12, Lev 17:13, Lev 17:15)

**Forbidden sexual unions; the land vomits out its inhabitants**
- Do not follow the practices of Egypt where you lived or of Canaan where you are going (Lev 18:3)
- Sexual relations of a man or a woman with an animal are forbidden (Lev 18:23)

**Be holy - ethical laws and love of neighbor**
- Each person must revere mother and father (Lev 19:3)
- Do not stand idly by the blood of your neighbor (Lev 19:16)
- Do not hate your brother in your heart; rebuke your neighbor instead (Lev 19:17)

**Mixtures, orlah fruit, mourning cuttings, alien and just weights**
- Prohibition of cross-breeding animals, sowing mixed seed and wearing mixed cloth (Lev 19:19)
- Fruit of a new tree is 'uncircumcised' for three years, holy in the fourth, eaten in the fifth (Lev 19:23, Lev 19:24, Lev 19:25)
- Rise before the gray-haired and honor the elderly (Lev 19:32)

**Penalties for Molech worship, necromancy and sexual offenses**
- In bestiality the animal is killed together with the human offender (Lev 20:15, Lev 20:16)
- Sibling incest is called 'hesed' (normally 'kindness'), here a disgrace (Lev 20:17)
- God separated Israel from the peoples as clean animals are separated from unclean (Lev 20:24, Lev 20:25, Lev 20:26)

**Priests' mourning and marriage limits; blemished priests**
- High priest may not defile himself even for father or mother (Lev 21:11, Lev 21:12)
- Priest with a bodily defect may not approach the altar or veil (Lev 21:17, Lev 21:18, Lev 21:19, Lev 21:20, Lev 21:21, Lev 21:23)
- Blemished priest still eats the holy and most holy food (Lev 21:22)

**Who may eat holy food; unblemished sacrificial animals**
- Priest in a state of impurity may not eat holy food until he washes and the sun sets (Lev 22:3, Lev 22:4, Lev 22:5, Lev 22:6, Lev 22:7)
- Impure person becomes clean when the sun sets (Lev 22:7)
- A priest's purchased or house-born slave eats holy food, but a hired worker or lodger does not (Lev 22:10, Lev 22:11)
- Widowed or divorced childless priest's daughter returns to eat of her father's holy food (Lev 22:12, Lev 22:13)
- Animal with an overgrown or stunted limb accepted as a freewill offering but not for a vow (Lev 22:23)
- Animals with crushed or cut testicles may not be offered, nor may such be done in the land (Lev 22:24)
- Blemished animals may not be accepted as offerings from a foreigner either (Lev 22:25)
- An animal and its young may not be slaughtered on the same day (Lev 22:28)
- Thanksgiving offering eaten the same day with nothing left till morning (Lev 22:29, Lev 22:30)

**The appointed times - sabbath and annual festivals**
- First sheaf (omer) of the harvest waved by the priest on the morrow after the sabbath (Lev 23:10, Lev 23:11, Lev 23:12)
- New bread, parched grain or fresh ears may not be eaten until the first sheaf is offered (Lev 23:14)
- Two leavened loaves of new grain offered as first fruits (Lev 23:17, Lev 23:20)
- A holy day is kept from evening to evening (Lev 23:32)

**Perpetual lamp, showbread, and the blasphemer stoned**
- Son of an Israelite mother and Egyptian father blasphemes the Name in a quarrel (Lev 24:10, Lev 24:11)
- Pronouncing or pricking 'the Name' of God in blasphemy is a capital offense (Lev 24:11, Lev 24:16)
- Offender held in custody until God's ruling is given (Lev 24:12)
- Those who heard the blasphemy lay their hands on the offender's head before stoning (Lev 24:14)
- Killing a person is capital; killing an animal is compensated life for life (Lev 24:17, Lev 24:18, Lev 24:21)

**Sabbatical year and the jubilee; the land is mine**
- Every seventh year the land rests: no sowing, pruning or harvesting (Lev 25:2, Lev 25:3, Lev 25:4, Lev 25:5)
- Spontaneous growth of the fallow year is food for owner, slaves, hired men, aliens, livestock and wild animals (Lev 25:6, Lev 25:7)
- Fiftieth year after seven sabbatical cycles is the jubilee (Lev 25:8, Lev 25:10, Lev 25:11, Lev 25:12, Lev 25:13)
- The shofar is sounded throughout the land on the Day of Atonement to begin the jubilee (Lev 25:9)
- Land is sold by the number of harvests remaining until the jubilee (Lev 25:14, Lev 25:15, Lev 25:16, Lev 25:17)
- God promises the sixth year will yield enough for three years (Lev 25:20, Lev 25:21, Lev 25:22)

**Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen**
- A house in a walled city can be redeemed only within a year and does not return at the jubilee (Lev 25:29, Lev 25:30)
- Houses in Levite cities can always be redeemed and their fields never sold (Lev 25:32, Lev 25:33, Lev 25:34)
- An impoverished Israelite sold to a brother serves as a hired worker, not a slave, until the jubilee (Lev 25:39, Lev 25:40, Lev 25:41, Lev 25:53)
- Do not rule over a fellow Israelite with harshness (perekh) (Lev 25:43, Lev 25:46, Lev 25:53)
- Permanent slaves may be bought from surrounding nations and resident aliens and bequeathed (Lev 25:44, Lev 25:45, Lev 25:46)

**Covenant blessings for obedience**
- No idols, carved image, pillar or figured stone set up to bow down on (Lev 26:1)
- God promises to walk about in the midst of the people (Lev 26:11, Lev 26:12)

**Covenant curses, exile, and remembered covenant**
- Punishments escalate sevenfold each time the people do not listen (Lev 26:18, Lev 26:21, Lev 26:24, Lev 26:28)
- Curse of consumption and fever that waste the eyes and the soul (Lev 26:16)
- Curse: you will flee though no one pursues, chased by the sound of a driven leaf (Lev 26:17, Lev 26:36, Lev 26:37)
- Curse: the sky like iron and the earth like bronze (Lev 26:19)
- God answers the people's 'walking contrary' (qeri) by walking contrary to them (Lev 26:21, Lev 26:24, Lev 26:27, Lev 26:28, Lev 26:40, Lev 26:41)
- Curse: ten women bake bread in one oven and it is doled out by weight (Lev 26:26)
- Curse: your corpses will be heaped on the corpses of your idols (Lev 26:30)
- Curse: God will not smell the pleasing odor of their offerings (Lev 26:31)

**Valuation of vowed persons, animals, houses, fields; herem and tithes**
- A person vowed to God is valued in silver by age and sex (Lev 27:2, Lev 27:3, Lev 27:4, Lev 27:5, Lev 27:6, Lev 27:7)
- A poor person who vows is assessed by the priest according to his means (Lev 27:8)
- A vowed animal may not be exchanged; if it is, both become holy (Lev 27:10, Lev 27:33)
- Value of a dedicated field set by the amount of seed it takes (a homer of barley = 50 shekels) (Lev 27:16, Lev 27:17, Lev 27:18)
- A dedicated field not redeemed becomes the priest's holding at the jubilee (Lev 27:20, Lev 27:21)
- A firstborn animal already belongs to God and cannot be dedicated by vow (Lev 27:26)
- Anything devoted (herem) to God cannot be sold or redeemed; a devoted person is put to death (Lev 27:28, Lev 27:29)
- Every tenth animal passing under the shepherd's rod is holy as tithe (Lev 27:32)

**The census of fighting men in the wilderness of Sinai**
- Divine speech dated to a precise day, month and year after the exodus (Num 1:1)
- Census of all males twenty years and older able to go to war (Num 1:2, Num 1:3, Num 1:18, Num 1:20)
- Twelve tribal leaders listed by name and patronymic (Num 1:4, Num 1:5, Num 1:6, Num 1:7, Num 1:8, Num 1:9, Num 1:10, Num 1:11, Num 1:12, Num 1:13, Num 1:14, Num 1:15, Num 1:16, Num 1:44)

**The Nazirite vow**

**The priestly blessing**

- Priests 'put God's name' upon the people by blessing them (Num 6:27)
