- Twelve leaders give six covered wagons and twelve oxen for transporting the sanctuary (Num 7:3)
- Wagons and oxen allotted to Levite clans according to their loads (Num 7:6, Num 7:7, Num 7:8)
- Most holy objects must be carried on the shoulders, not on wagons (Num 7:9)

**Altar dedication gifts, days seven to twelve; totals; the voice from between the cherubim**
- After itemized gifts, the grand totals of silver, gold and animals are summed (Num 7:84, Num 7:85, Num 7:86, Num 7:87, Num 7:88)

**Lighting the lampstand**
- Sacred object made after a pattern shown by God (Num 8:4)

**Purification and dedication of the Levites**
- Community lays hands on persons to transfer or consecrate (Num 8:10)
- Persons themselves 'waved' or presented as an offering to God (Num 8:11, Num 8:13, Num 8:21)
- A priestly class is taken in place of the firstborn owed to God (Num 8:16, Num 8:17, Num 8:18)
- Sacred service bounded by fixed ages (start and retirement) (Num 8:24, Num 8:25, Num 8:26)
- A ritual or class prevents a plague when people approach the holy (Num 8:19)

**Silver trumpets and departure from Sinai**
- Blowing trumpets in battle makes God 'remember' and save (Num 10:9, Num 10:10)
- Tribes march under banners in a fixed order around the shrine (Num 10:14, Num 10:18, Num 10:22, Num 10:25)

**Hobab invited as guide; the Song of the Ark**
- Hero asks his foreign father-in-law to be the people's 'eyes' in the desert (Num 10:29, Num 10:30, Num 10:31)
- The sacred chest goes ahead to scout a resting place (Num 10:33)

**Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail**
- Fire from God burns part of the camp for complaint (Num 11:1)
- A 'rabble' or mixed crowd among the people instigates sin (Num 11:4)
- Leader refuses to silence prophets outside the sanctioned place: 'would all were prophets' (Num 11:26, Num 11:27, Num 11:28, Num 11:29)

**Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses**
- Prophet's own siblings challenge his unique authority (Num 12:2)
- Hero called the humblest man on earth (Num 12:3)
- Ordinary prophets receive revelation in visions and dreams (Num 12:6)
- Afflicted person shut outside the camp seven days (Num 12:14, Num 12:15)

**The twelve spies and their report**
- Leader renames a disciple (Hoshea to Joshua) (Num 13:16)
- Founding of a city dated relative to an Egyptian city (Hebron seven years before Zoan) (Num 13:22)
- Single grape cluster so large two men carry it on a pole (Num 13:23, Num 13:24)

**Rebellion after the spies' report and the forty-year sentence**
- People have tested God 'ten times' (Num 14:22)
- Those who slandered the land die by plague (Num 14:36, Num 14:37)

**Grain and drink offerings, dough offering, inadvertent sin**
- First of the dough given as a gift (challah) (Num 15:20, Num 15:21)

- Man gathering wood on the Sabbath is stoned by divine ruling (Num 15:32, Num 15:35, Num 15:36)

- Rival claimants offer incense in fire-pans so God may choose the holy one (Num 16:6, Num 16:7, Num 16:17, Num 16:18)

- Rebels' censers beaten into altar plating as a memorial (Num 17:3, Num 17:4, Num 17:5)
- Priest with incense stands between the dead and the living and stops the plague (Num 17:11, Num 17:12, Num 17:13)
- Chosen leader's rod sprouts, blossoms and bears almonds overnight (Num 17:17, Num 17:18, Num 17:20, Num 17:23)

**The red heifer and corpse impurity**
- Those who prepare the purifying agent are themselves rendered impure (Num 19:7, Num 19:8, Num 19:10, Num 19:21)
- Ash mixed with running ('living') water sprinkled to cleanse (Num 19:9, Num 19:17)
- A corpse defiles everyone and every open vessel in the tent (Num 19:14, Num 19:15)

**Miriam's death; water from the rock at Meribah**
- Death and burial of the hero's sister (Num 20:1)
- Leader strikes the rock (twice) instead of speaking to it (Num 20:10, Num 20:11)

**Edom refuses passage; death of Aaron at Mount Hor**
- Messengers appeal to a neighboring nation as 'your brother' (Num 20:14)
- An angel sent to bring the people out of Egypt (Num 20:16)
- Dying high priest is stripped and his vestments put on his son (Num 20:26, Num 20:28)

**Hormah; the fiery serpents and the bronze serpent**

- People call the miraculous food 'worthless bread' (Num 21:5)
- God sends fiery (saraph) serpents that bite the people (Num 21:6)

**Stations to Moab; Book of the Wars of YHWH; Song of the Well**
- Citation of a lost source, the 'Book of the Wars of YHWH' (Num 21:14, Num 21:15)
- Song to a well dug by princes with their staffs ('Spring up, O well') (Num 21:16, Num 21:17, Num 21:18)

- A king hires a foreign seer to curse an enemy people (Num 22:5, Num 22:6, Num 22:11, Num 22:17)

- Seven altars with seven bulls and seven rams (Num 23:1, Num 23:2, Num 23:4, Num 23:14, Num 23:29, Num 23:30)

**Census of the second generation on the plains of Moab**
- A second census counts the new generation by clans (Num 26:2, Num 26:4, Num 26:51, Num 26:63)

- Leader ordains his successor by laying hands and sharing his 'splendor' (hod) (Num 27:18, Num 27:20, Num 27:23)

**Calendar of public offerings**
- Tenth of the seventh month: day to 'afflict your souls' (fast) (Num 29:7, Num 29:11)
- Diminishing series of bulls over Booths (13 down to 7, totaling 70) (Num 29:13, Num 29:17, Num 29:20, Num 29:23, Num 29:26, Num 29:29, Num 29:32)
- A concluding eighth-day assembly ('atseret) after the feast (Num 29:35, Num 29:36)

**Vows of men and women**
- Silence on hearing counts as confirmation (Num 30:5, Num 30:8, Num 30:12, Num 30:15)
- Vows of a widow or divorced woman stand on their own (Num 30:10)

**War against Midian and division of the spoils**
- Leader given a final task to complete before he is 'gathered to his people' (Num 31:2)
- Army of a thousand from each tribe (12,000) (Num 31:4, Num 31:5)
- Priest accompanies the army with holy vessels and trumpets (Num 31:6)
- Five named kings slain together (Num 31:8)
- Warriors and captives purified outside camp seven days after battle (Num 31:19, Num 31:20, Num 31:24)
- Commanders report that not one man of the army is missing (Num 31:49)
- Captured gold jewelry offered to atone for the soldiers' lives (Num 31:50, Num 31:52, Num 31:54)

**Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh settle east of the Jordan**
- Tribes pledge to fight in the vanguard before returning home (Num 32:16, Num 32:17, Num 32:18, Num 32:27, Num 32:32)
- 'Know that your sin will find you' (Num 32:23)

**The stages of Israel's journey from Egypt to Moab**
- Moses writes down the stages of the journey by God's command (Num 33:2)
- Itinerary of about forty-two encampments from Egypt to Moab (Num 33:5, Num 33:48, Num 33:49)
- Aaron dies aged 123 on the first of the fifth month of the fortieth year (Num 33:38, Num 33:39)

**Borders of Canaan and the land commission**
- Named commission of a priest, a leader and one chieftain per tribe to apportion land (Num 34:17, Num 34:18, Num 34:19, Num 34:29)

**Marriage of heiresses within the tribe; colophon of Numbers**
- The Jubilee year considered in tribal land transfers (Num 36:4)

**Setting of Moses' speech; appointment of judges**
- Eleven days' journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea (yet it took forty years) (Deut 1:2)
- Moses 'expounds this Torah' in Moab on the first of the eleventh month of the fortieth year (Deut 1:3, Deut 1:5)
- People multiplied 'like the stars of heaven' (Deut 1:10)
- Blessing: may God make you a thousand times as many (Deut 1:11)

**The spies episode retold**
- Children 'who do not yet know good and evil' will inherit (Deut 1:39)

**Passing Edom, Moab and Ammon; the giant aboriginal peoples**
- The rebellious generation dies out before entering the land (Deut 2:14, Deut 2:15, Deut 2:16)

**Defeat of Og of Bashan and allotment of Transjordan**
- Kingdom of sixty walled cities with gates and bars (Deut 3:4, Deut 3:5)
- A giant king's oversized bed (Og's iron bed, nine cubits) displayed as a relic (Deut 3:11)

**Moses pleads to cross the Jordan and is refused**
- God is angry with the leader on account of the people (Deut 3:26)

**Exhortation at Horeb's memory; no image; exile and return**
- Keeping the law will make the nations call Israel wise (Deut 4:6, Deut 4:8)
- No other nation has a god so near whenever they call on him (Deut 4:7)

**The Shema and the instruction to teach**
- When your son asks what the laws mean, recite the exodus story (Deut 6:20, Deut 6:21)

**Dispossession of the seven nations; Israel the treasured people**
- God chose Israel not for their numbers, being the fewest of peoples, but from love (Deut 7:7, Deut 7:8)
- Silver and gold on idols must not be taken; it is abomination and herem (Deut 7:25, Deut 7:26)

**Lessons of the wilderness; the good land; beware of pride**
- Man does not live by bread alone but by every word from God's mouth (Deut 8:3)
- When you eat and are satisfied, bless God for the land (Deut 8:10)
- Wilderness of fiery serpents and scorpions (Deut 8:15)

**Not for your righteousness; the golden calf and Moses' intercession recalled**
- Land given not for Israel's righteousness but for the nations' wickedness (Deut 9:4, Deut 9:5, Deut 9:6)
- Intercession appeals to what the nations would say of God (Deut 9:28)

**Second tablets and ark; Levites set apart; what God requires**
- Wooden ark made to hold the stone tablets (Deut 10:1, Deut 10:2, Deut 10:3, Deut 10:5)
- Aaron dies and his son Eleazar becomes priest in his place (Deut 10:6)

**The land that drinks rain; blessing and curse; Gerizim and Ebal**
- Egypt watered by foot like a vegetable garden; the promised land drinks rain from heaven (Deut 11:10, Deut 11:11)
- God's eyes are on the land continually from the beginning to the end of the year (Deut 11:12)
- Oaks (terebinths) of Moreh near Shechem as a landmark (Deut 11:30)

**The chosen place; profane slaughter; blood prohibition**
- Every man doing what is right in his own eyes (Deut 12:8)
- Meat may be slaughtered and eaten anywhere, like gazelle and deer, when far from the sanctuary (Deut 12:15, Deut 12:20, Deut 12:21, Deut 12:22)
- Do not inquire how the nations served their gods in order to imitate them (Deut 12:30)

**False prophet, enticing kin, and the apostate city**
- A city that turns to other gods is put under the ban, burned and left a mound forever (Deut 13:13, Deut 13:15, Deut 13:16, Deut 13:17)

**Mourning rites forbidden; clean and unclean food; tithes**
- Animal that died of itself may be given to the resident alien or sold to a foreigner (Deut 14:21)
- Annual tithe eaten by the owner before God at the chosen place (Deut 14:22, Deut 14:23)
- If the place is far, convert the tithe to silver and buy what you desire there, wine and strong drink included (Deut 14:24, Deut 14:25, Deut 14:26)

**Release of debts, release of Hebrew slaves, firstlings**
- There will be no poor among you, yet the poor will never cease from the land (Deut 15:4, Deut 15:11)
- Base thought refusing a loan as the release year nears; the poor man cries to God against you (Deut 15:9)

**Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah**
- Passover in the month of Aviv, at evening, at the chosen place (Deut 16:1, Deut 16:2, Deut 16:5, Deut 16:6)
- Unleavened bread, bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste (Deut 16:3, Deut 16:4)
- Feast of Weeks counted seven weeks from the first sickle in the standing grain (Deut 16:9, Deut 16:10)
- Justice, justice shall you pursue (Deut 16:20)
- No Asherah tree planted beside God's altar and no standing stone (Deut 16:21, Deut 16:22)

**Idolater's trial; witnesses; high court; law of the king**
- Hand of the witnesses first against the condemned, then the people's (Deut 17:7)
- King must be chosen by God from among brothers, not a foreigner (Deut 17:14, Deut 17:15)
- King writes a copy of the Torah and reads it all his days (Deut 17:18, Deut 17:19, Deut 17:20)

**Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses**
- Priest's due: shoulder, two cheeks and stomach of the sacrifice, and first of the fleece (Deut 18:3, Deut 18:4)
- Be wholehearted (tamim) with God (Deut 18:13)
- A prophecy that does not come true shows the prophet spoke presumptuously (Deut 18:21, Deut 18:22)

**Cities of refuge, boundary stones, false witnesses**
- Axe head slips off the handle while cutting wood and kills a companion (accidental homicide) (Deut 19:5)
- Deliberate murderer who flees to refuge is handed over by the elders to the avenger (Deut 19:11, Deut 19:12, Deut 19:13)

**Broken-necked heifer; captive bride; firstborn; rebellious son; hanged body**
- Captive woman shaves her head, pares her nails, mourns her parents a month before marriage (Deut 21:11, Deut 21:12, Deut 21:13)
- Captive wife who is no longer wanted must be freed, not sold (Deut 21:14)
- Body hanged on a tree must be buried the same day; the hanged is a curse of God (Deut 21:22, Deut 21:23)

**Lost property, bird's nest, mixtures, tassels, virginity and sexual offences**
- Return a brother's lost animal or property; you may not hide yourself (Deut 22:1, Deut 22:2, Deut 22:3)
- Help lift a brother's fallen ox or donkey (Deut 22:4)
- Send away the mother bird before taking the young, for long life (Deut 22:6, Deut 22:7)
- Build a parapet on a new roof so no one falls (Deut 22:8)
- Prohibition of mixed seeds in a vineyard (Deut 22:9)
- Do not plough with an ox and a donkey together (Deut 22:10)
- Tassels (gedilim) on the four corners of the garment (Deut 22:12)
- Parents display the bride's virginity cloth before the elders (Deut 22:15, Deut 22:17)
- Bride found not a virgin stoned at the door of her father's house (Deut 22:20, Deut 22:21)
- Betrothed girl lain with in the city dies for not crying out; in the field only the man dies (Deut 22:23, Deut 22:24, Deut 22:25, Deut 22:26, Deut 22:27)
- Man who lies with an unbetrothed virgin pays her father fifty silver and must marry her without divorce (Deut 22:28, Deut 22:29)

**Admission to the assembly; camp purity; slaves, interest, vows**
- Edomites (brothers) and Egyptians (hosts) admitted in the third generation (Deut 23:8, Deut 23:9)
- Man unclean from a nocturnal emission stays outside the camp until evening and washes (Deut 23:11, Deut 23:12)
- Latrine outside the war camp; dig with a spade and cover excrement because God walks in the camp (Deut 23:13, Deut 23:14, Deut 23:15)
- Harlot's hire and the price of a dog may not be brought to the temple for a vow (Deut 23:19)

**Divorce, newlyweds, pledges, wages, gleanings**
- Newly married man exempt from army for one year to gladden his wife (Deut 24:5)
- Millstones may not be taken in pledge, for that is taking a life (Deut 24:6)
- Remember what God did to Miriam (skin disease) on the way (Deut 24:8, Deut 24:9)

**Forty lashes, muzzled ox, levirate and halitzah, weights, Amalek**
- Flogging limited to forty stripes so your brother is not degraded (Deut 25:2, Deut 25:3)
- Widow removes the refusing brother-in-law's sandal and spits in his face (Deut 25:7, Deut 25:8, Deut 25:9, Deut 25:10)
- Woman who seizes a man's genitals in a brawl has her hand cut off (Deut 25:11, Deut 25:12)
- Remember Amalek who attacked the stragglers; blot out his memory (Deut 25:17, Deut 25:18, Deut 25:19)

**First-fruits creed, tithe declaration, mutual covenant**
- First fruits brought in a basket to the priest at the chosen place (Deut 26:2, Deut 26:3, Deut 26:4, Deut 26:10)
- Historical creed: a wandering Aramean was my father, went down to Egypt... (Deut 26:5, Deut 26:6, Deut 26:7, Deut 26:8, Deut 26:9)
- Tithe declaration: I did not eat it in mourning nor give any of it to the dead (Deut 26:13, Deut 26:14)
- Look down from your holy habitation in heaven and bless your people (Deut 26:15)

**Inscribed stones and altar on Ebal; the twelve curses**
- Six tribes stand on one mountain to bless, six on the other to curse (Deut 27:12, Deut 27:13)
- Levites pronounce twelve curses on secret crimes and all the people answer Amen (Deut 27:14, Deut 27:15, Deut 27:26)
- Cursed is he who misleads a blind man on the road (Deut 27:18)
- Curses on lying with father's wife, a beast, a sister, a mother-in-law (Deut 27:20, Deut 27:21, Deut 27:22, Deut 27:23)

**Blessings and the great curses**
- Blessed in city and field, in coming in and going out, basket and kneading trough (Deut 28:3, Deut 28:4, Deut 28:5, Deut 28:6, Deut 28:16, Deut 28:17, Deut 28:18, Deut 28:19)
- Enemies come out one way and flee seven ways (Deut 28:7, Deut 28:25)
- God will make you the head and not the tail (Deut 28:13, Deut 28:44)
- King and people exiled to an unknown nation to serve gods of wood and stone (Deut 28:36, Deut 28:64)
- The stranger in your midst rises higher and higher while you sink (Deut 28:43, Deut 28:44)
- God puts an iron yoke on your neck (Deut 28:48)
- Delicate woman who never set foot on the ground secretly eats her afterbirth and children in the siege (Deut 28:56, Deut 28:57)
- As God rejoiced to do you good, so he will rejoice to destroy you (Deut 28:63)
- God will send you back to Egypt in ships to be sold as slaves, and no one will buy (Deut 28:68)
- Covenant at Moab in addition to the covenant at Horeb (Deut 28:69)

**Covenant at Moab; the secret apostate; the land like Sodom**
- All ranks stand before God, from the hewer of wood to the drawer of water (Deut 29:9, Deut 29:10)
- A root bearing poison and wormwood among you (secret apostate) (Deut 29:17)

**Return from exile; the near commandment; choose life**
- God himself will circumcise your heart and your offspring's heart (Deut 30:6)

**Joshua commissioned; Torah written and deposited; the Song commanded**
- Torah read before all the people, men, women, children and strangers, every seventh year at Sukkot (Deut 31:10, Deut 31:11, Deut 31:12, Deut 31:13)
- God foretells to the dying prophet that the people will go astray after him (Deut 31:16, Deut 31:20, Deut 31:27, Deut 31:29)
- God knows the people's inclination (yetzer) before he brings them in (Deut 31:21)
- Book of the Torah placed beside the ark as a witness (Deut 31:25, Deut 31:26)

**The Song of Moses (Ha'azinu)**
- Teaching falls like rain and distils like dew (Deut 32:2)
- Jeshurun grew fat and kicked, forsaking the God who made him (Deut 32:15)
- God as the Rock that bore you and the God who writhed in labor with you (Deut 32:18)
- God will provoke Israel to jealousy with a no-people, a foolish nation (Deut 32:21)
- God refrains from annihilating Israel lest the enemy boast it was their own hand (Deut 32:26, Deut 32:27)
- Their vine is from the vine of Sodom; grapes of poison, wine of serpents' venom (Deut 32:32, Deut 32:33)
- Nations called to rejoice as God avenges his servants' blood and atones for his land (Deut 32:43)

**Song delivered; Moses ordered up Mount Nebo to die**
- Prophet told to ascend a mountain, see the land, and die there, gathered to his people (Deut 32:49, Deut 32:50)
- Moses and Aaron's breach of faith at the waters of Meribah (Deut 32:51)

**The Blessing of Moses on the tribes**
- Dying patriarch or leader blesses each tribe in turn (Deut 33:1, Deut 33:6, Deut 33:7)
- A fiery law (esh dat) from God's right hand (Deut 33:2)
- God dwells between Benjamin's shoulders (Deut 33:12)
- Zebulun and Issachar suck the abundance of the seas and treasures hidden in the sand (Deut 33:19)
- A tribe likened to a lion or lion's whelp (Deut 33:20, Deut 33:22)
- Asher dips his foot in oil; sandals of iron and bronze (Deut 33:24, Deut 33:25)
- Underneath are the everlasting arms (Deut 33:27)
- Happy are you, Israel, who is like you, a people saved by YHWH (Deut 33:29)

**Death and burial of Moses**
- From Nebo/Pisgah God shows Moses the whole land from Gilead to Dan to the western sea (Deut 34:1, Deut 34:2, Deut 34:3, Deut 34:4)
- Moses dies 'by the mouth of YHWH' (al pi YHWH) (Deut 34:5)
- At death his eye was not dim nor his vigor abated (Deut 34:7)
- Successor filled with spirit of wisdom through laying on of hands (Deut 34:9)
- No prophet arose again like Moses whom God knew face to face (Deut 34:10, Deut 34:11, Deut 34:12)

**God commissions Joshua; Transjordan tribes pledged**
- People pledge to obey the successor as they obeyed his predecessor; rebels to die (Josh 1:16, Josh 1:17, Josh 1:18)

**Rahab hides the spies in Jericho**
- A prostitute (Rahab) shelters the spies in her house (Josh 2:1, Josh 2:4)
- Host deceives pursuers to protect the hidden guests (Josh 2:4, Josh 2:5)
- Spies hidden under stalks of flax on the roof (Josh 2:6)
- Spies swear to spare the helper's whole family in return for her kindness (Josh 2:12, Josh 2:13, Josh 2:14, Josh 2:17, Josh 2:20)
- Spies let down by a rope through a window in the city wall (Josh 2:15)
- Scarlet cord tied in the window as the sign of protection (Josh 2:18, Josh 2:21)
- Whoever goes out of the door, his blood is on his own head (Josh 2:19)
- Fugitives hide three days in the hills until pursuers give up (Josh 2:16, Josh 2:22)

**The ark goes before; the Jordan stands in a heap**
- People follow the ark at a distance of 2000 cubits (Josh 3:3, Josh 3:4, Josh 3:6)
- Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow God will do wonders (Josh 3:5)
- The ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth (Josh 3:11, Josh 3:13)
- Twelve men chosen, one from each tribe (Josh 3:12)
- The Jordan overflows its banks all the days of harvest (Josh 3:15)
- Priests bearing the ark stand on dry ground in the middle of the river until all have crossed (Josh 3:15, Josh 3:17)

**Twelve memorial stones from the Jordan; the river returns**
- Twelve stones, one per tribe, taken from the riverbed as a memorial of the crossing (Josh 4:3, Josh 4:8, Josh 4:20)
- Stones set up in the middle of the river where the priests stood, visible 'to this day' (Josh 4:9)
- The crossing into the land is dated to the tenth day of the first month (Josh 4:19)
- Gilgal as the first camp and sanctuary in the land (Josh 4:19-20)
- A miracle is done so that all the peoples of the earth may know God's power (Josh 4:24)

**Mass circumcision at Gilgal, Passover, end of manna, the commander of YHWH's army**
- Circumcision performed with flint knives (Josh 5:2-3)
- A place called the Hill of Foreskins, where mass circumcision took place (Josh 5:3)
- The generation born in the wilderness was not circumcised (Josh 5:4-7)
- Passover kept at a decisive turning point (entry into the land) (Josh 5:10)
- The manna stops the day after the people eat the produce of the land (Josh 5:11-12)
- A figure with a sword reveals himself as commander of YHWH's army (Josh 5:14)

**Fall of Jericho; Rahab spared; curse on the rebuilder**
- A besieged city is circled once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh (Josh 6:3-4, Josh 6:14-15)
- Seven priests blow seven rams' horns before the ark (Josh 6:4, Josh 6:6, Josh 6:8, Josh 6:13)
- The army must keep total silence until the leader gives the signal to shout (Josh 6:10)
- City walls collapse at a trumpet blast and a great shout (Josh 6:5, Josh 6:20)
- Captured silver, gold, bronze and iron are holy, for the treasury of YHWH (Josh 6:19, Josh 6:24)
- The harlot who hid the spies is spared with her family when the city falls (Josh 6:17, Josh 6:22-23, Josh 6:25)

**Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan**
- Leader complains to God after a defeat: would that we had stayed where we were (Josh 7:7-9)
- The culprit is urged to 'give glory to God' by confessing (Josh 7:19-20)
- The sinner's children, animals and property are destroyed with him (Josh 7:24-25)

**Ambush and capture of Ai; altar and Torah inscribed on Mount Ebal**
- Leader holds out his javelin and does not lower his hand until victory is complete (Josh 8:18, Josh 8:26)

**The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty**
- Locals disguise themselves with worn clothes and old provisions to pass as travelers from a far country (Josh 9:4-6, Josh 9:12-13)
- Dry, crumbled bread shown as proof of a long journey (Josh 9:5, Josh 9:12)
- Leaders make a decision without asking the oracle of YHWH (Josh 9:14)
- The congregation grumbles against its chiefs over a decision (Josh 9:18)
- A subject people made perpetual woodcutters and water-drawers for the sanctuary (Josh 9:21, Josh 9:23, Josh 9:27)
- A people is cursed to perpetual slavery (Josh 9:23)

**Battle of Gibeon, hailstones, sun and moon stand still, five kings in the cave, southern campaign**
- Five kings form an alliance and are defeated together (Josh 10:3-5)
- A king of Jerusalem bears a name with 'tsedeq' (Adoni-zedek, Melchizedek) (Josh 10:1, Josh 10:3)
- The army marches all night and attacks the enemy by surprise (Josh 10:9)
- God heeds the command of a man, a unique event (Josh 10:14)
- Defeated kings hide in a cave, which is sealed with great stones (Josh 10:16-18)
- Idiom: no one 'sharpened his tongue' against Israel (Josh 10:21)
- Summary of a sweeping conquest of the whole south from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza (Josh 10:40-42)

**Northern coalition under Jabin of Hazor; hamstrung horses; Anakim destroyed**
- An enemy army as numerous as the sand on the seashore (Josh 11:4)
- The enemy is pursued as far as Great Sidon (Josh 11:8)
- Hazor, 'head of all those kingdoms', is the only city burned in the north (Josh 11:10-11, Josh 11:13)

**List of the kings defeated by Moses and Joshua (thirty-one kings)**
- A numbered list of conquered city-kings (thirty-one) (Josh 12:9-24)
- A 'king of the nations (Goiim)' among the conquered kings (Josh 12:23)

**Land still to be conquered; Transjordanian allotments; Balaam's death**
- God tells the aged leader that much land remains to be possessed (Josh 13:1)
- The Shihor 'before Egypt' as the land's southern limit (Josh 13:3)
- Five named Midianite princes (Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, Reba) (Josh 13:21)

**Allotment by lot begins; Caleb at eighty-five claims Hebron**
- The sons of Joseph count as two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim (Josh 14:4)
- The faithful spy receives the land his foot trod on (Josh 14:6-9, Josh 14:14)
- An old hero says he is as strong as on the day he was sent out forty-five years before (Josh 14:10-11)

**The boundaries of Judah**
- The 'Ascent of Scorpions' (Ma'aleh Aqrabbim) on the border (Josh 15:3)

**City list of Judah by districts; Jebusites remain in Jerusalem**
- The City of Salt and En-gedi listed in the Judean wilderness (Josh 15:62)
- Philistine cities listed with their 'daughters' (dependent villages) (Josh 15:45-47)

**Manasseh's lot; the daughters of Zelophehad receive land**
- Machir, the warrior firstborn of Manasseh, receives Gilead and Bashan (Josh 17:1)

**Joseph's complaint of one lot; clear the forest; iron chariots**
- A tribe complains that its allotment is too small for its numbers (Josh 17:14)
- A tribe is told to clear forest to make more land (Josh 17:15, Josh 17:18)

**Tent of meeting set up at Shiloh; land surveyed in a book; seven lots cast**
- 'The land was subdued before them' (kivshah), echoing the creation command (Josh 18:1)
- Surveyors walk the land and write it in a book in portions (Josh 18:4, Josh 18:6, Josh 18:8-9)
- Leader rebukes the people: how long will you be slack to possess the land? (Josh 18:3)

**Benjamin's borders and cities**
- Beth-aven, 'house of iniquity', near Bethel (Josh 18:12)

**Simeon's inheritance within Judah**
- A tribe's territory lies inside another tribe's (Josh 19:1, Josh 19:9)

**Lots of Zebulun, Issachar, Asher and Naphtali**
- A second Bethlehem in Zebulun (Josh 19:15)
- Towns named after the goddess Anat or the sun (Beth-anath, Beth-shemesh) (Josh 19:38)
- Tyre called a fortified city on Asher's border (Josh 19:29)

**Joshua's own inheritance at Timnath-serah; end of allotment at Shiloh**
- The leader receives his own inheritance only after all the tribes (Josh 19:49-50)

**Six cities of refuge designated**
- The fugitive manslayer states his case to the elders at the city gate (Josh 20:4)
- Killing counts as unintentional if there was no hatred 'yesterday or the day before' (Josh 20:3, Josh 20:5)
- The cities of refuge are open to resident aliens too (Josh 20:9)

**Forty-eight Levitical cities by lot; all promises fulfilled**
- The priests, sons of Aaron, receive thirteen cities in Judah, Simeon and Benjamin (Josh 21:10-19)

**Eastern tribes dismissed; the altar 'Ed' by the Jordan nearly causes civil war**
- Command to love God, walk in his ways and cleave to him with all heart and soul (Josh 22:5)
- Phinehas the priest leads a delegation of tribal princes to investigate (Josh 22:13-14, Josh 22:30-32)
- The sin of Peor recalled as guilt not yet cleansed (Josh 22:17)
- Land outside YHWH's possession east of the Jordan is suggested to be unclean (Josh 22:19)
- Fear that future generations will say a group has no portion in YHWH (Josh 22:24-25, Josh 22:27-28)
- A replica of the altar built not for sacrifice but as a witness (Josh 22:26-28, Josh 22:34)

**Joshua's farewell warning against intermarriage and foreign gods**
- The aged leader gathers the people for a farewell exhortation before death (Josh 23:1-2, Josh 23:14)
- As every good word came true, so will every threatened evil (Josh 23:15-16)

**Covenant at Shechem; 'choose this day whom you will serve'; deaths of Joshua and Eleazar**
- God set darkness between Israel and the pursuing Egyptians (Josh 24:7)
- Leader warns: you cannot serve YHWH, for he is a holy and jealous God (Josh 24:19-20)
- A priest is buried on the hill belonging to his son (Josh 24:33)

**Judah goes up first; Adoni-bezek's thumbs; Luz betrayed; list of unconquered cities**
- A captured king's thumbs and big toes are cut off (Judg 1:6-7)
- Seventy mutilated kings gather scraps under a tyrant's table (Judg 1:7)
- A man from the city shows the attackers the way in and is spared (Judg 1:24-26)

**Angel at Bochim; death of Joshua; the cycle of apostasy and deliverance**
- The angel of YHWH rebukes the people for making covenants and not destroying altars (Judg 2:1-3)
- A new generation arises that did not know YHWH or his deeds (Judg 2:10)

**Nations left to teach war; Othniel defeats Cushan-rishathaim**
- An oppressor bears a mocking name (Cushan of Double Wickedness) (Judg 3:8, Judg 3:10)

**Left-handed Ehud assassinates fat King Eglon; Shamgar's oxgoad**
- The City of Palms (Jericho) is taken by enemies (Judg 3:13)
- A left-handed hero uses his unexpected hand to strike (Judg 3:15, Judg 3:21)
- The bearer of tribute uses the audience to assassinate the king (Judg 3:15, Judg 3:17-18)
- A short double-edged sword hidden on the right thigh under the garment (Judg 3:16, Judg 3:21)
- A very fat king is stabbed so the fat closes over the blade (Judg 3:17, Judg 3:22)
- The assassin claims a secret message (a word of God) for the king alone (Judg 3:19-20)
- The 'carved images' (pesilim) at Gilgal used as a landmark (Judg 3:19, Judg 3:26)
- Servants delay at a locked door thinking the king is relieving himself (Judg 3:23-25)
- A hero kills six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad (Judg 3:31)
- A hero is called 'son of Anath' (Judg 3:31)

**Deborah and Barak defeat Sisera; Jael kills him with a tent peg**
- A woman prophet judges Israel (Judg 4:4-5)

- Gift of loaves, crumbled cakes and a jar of honey brought to a seer (1Kgs 14:3)
- The dynasty will be swept away as one burns up dung until it is gone (1Kgs 14:10)
- The sick child dies the moment his mother's foot crosses the threshold (1Kgs 14:12, 1Kgs 14:17)
- Israel struck like a reed shaken in water and scattered beyond the River (1Kgs 14:15)

**Rehoboam's reign and Shishak's invasion**
- The king's mother is named and is a foreigner (Naamah the Ammonite) (1Kgs 14:21, 1Kgs 14:31)

**Abijam and Asa of Judah**
- David did right all his life except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite (1Kgs 15:5)
- King sends the temple's silver and gold to a foreign king to break his treaty with a rival (1Kgs 15:18-20)
- The enemy's half-built fortress is dismantled and its stones and timber used to build one's own (1Kgs 15:22)

**Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha; Elah and Zimri**
- God raised the ruler 'from the dust' to be prince over his people (1Kgs 16:2)
- King is assassinated while drinking himself drunk in a steward's house (1Kgs 16:9-10)
- Usurper who reigned seven days burns the palace over himself and dies (1Kgs 16:15, 1Kgs 16:18)

**Omri founds Samaria; Ahab and Jezebel; Jericho rebuilt**
- The people split in half between two rival claimants to the throne (1Kgs 16:21-22)
- King buys a hill for two talents of silver and names the new capital after its former owner (Shemer, Samaria) (1Kgs 16:24)
- King marries Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and serves Baal (1Kgs 16:31)
- King builds a temple and altar of Baal in his capital and makes an Asherah (1Kgs 16:32-33)

**Elijah announces the drought and is fed by ravens**
- Prophet declares there will be neither dew nor rain except at his word (1Kgs 17:1)
- Prophet hides by a brook east of the Jordan and drinks from it until it dries up (1Kgs 17:3, 1Kgs 17:5, 1Kgs 17:7)
- Prophet hiding by a wadi is fed bread and meat morning and evening by ravens (1Kgs 17:4, 1Kgs 17:6)

**The widow of Zarephath and her son**
- God commands a foreign (Sidonian) widow to feed the prophet in famine (1Kgs 17:9-11)
- Widow gathering two sticks to bake a last meal for herself and her son before they die (1Kgs 17:10, 1Kgs 17:12)
- Prophet asks the starving widow to bake for him first, promising abundance (1Kgs 17:13)
- Bereaved mother accuses the man of God of coming to recall her sin and kill her son (1Kgs 17:17-18)
- Prophet carries a dead boy to the upper room, lays him on his own bed, and revives him (1Kgs 17:19, 1Kgs 17:21-22)
- Prophet stretches himself over the child three times, praying that his life return (1Kgs 17:21)
- A witness of the miracle confesses: now I know you are a man of God and God's word in your mouth is truth (1Kgs 17:24)

**Obadiah meets Elijah in the famine**
- Queen kills the prophets of YHWH (1Kgs 18:4, 1Kgs 18:13)
- Pious royal steward hides a hundred prophets, fifty to a cave, and feeds them bread and water (1Kgs 18:4, 1Kgs 18:13)
- King searched every nation and kingdom for the prophet, making them swear he was not there (1Kgs 18:10)

**Contest on Mount Carmel**
- Contest of gods: the god who answers by fire on an unlit sacrifice is God (1Kgs 18:23-25)
- Prophet mocks the silent god: perhaps he is musing, relieving himself, travelling, or asleep and must be woken (1Kgs 18:27)
- Prophet repairs the ruined altar with twelve stones for the tribes of Jacob (1Kgs 18:30-32)
- Sacrifice and altar drenched with four jars of water three times, filling a trench, before the miracle (1Kgs 18:33-35)
- The people fall on their faces crying 'YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!' (1Kgs 18:39)
- The prophets of Baal are seized and slaughtered at the brook Kishon (1Kgs 18:40)

**Elijah prays for rain and runs before Ahab**
- Prophet on the mountaintop bows to the ground with his face between his knees praying for rain (1Kgs 18:42)
- Servant sent seven times to look toward the sea sees a cloud as small as a man's hand (1Kgs 18:43-44)
- Hand of YHWH upon him, the prophet girds his loins and runs ahead of the king's chariot (1Kgs 18:46)

**Elijah flees to Horeb; the still small voice**
- Queen swears by the gods to make the prophet's life like the slain prophets' by this time tomorrow (1Kgs 19:2)
- Despairing prophet sits and sleeps under a broom tree in the wilderness (1Kgs 19:4-5)
- An angel touches the sleeping prophet twice and gives him a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water (1Kgs 19:5-7)
- On the strength of one meal the prophet walks forty days and nights to the mountain of God (1Kgs 19:8)
- God twice asks the prophet 'What are you doing here?' and he twice answers the same complaint (1Kgs 19:9, 1Kgs 19:13)
- Prophet claims 'I have been very zealous for YHWH... and I alone am left' (1Kgs 19:10, 1Kgs 19:14)
- God passes by: a mountain-splitting wind, earthquake and fire, but God is not in them (1Kgs 19:11-12)
- After the fire comes 'a sound of thin silence' (qol demamah daqqah) (1Kgs 19:12)
- Whoever escapes the sword of the first avenger, the second will kill, and the third (1Kgs 19:17)
- God keeps a remnant of seven thousand whose knees did not bow and lips did not kiss Baal (1Kgs 19:18)

**The call of Elisha**
- The called man is plowing with twelve yoke of oxen, himself with the twelfth (1Kgs 19:19)
- Prophet calls his successor by throwing his mantle over him (1Kgs 19:19)
- Disciple called while plowing asks to kiss his parents goodbye first (1Kgs 19:20)
- Called disciple slaughters his oxen, boils the meat with the yoke for fuel, feeds the people, and follows (1Kgs 19:21)

**Ben-hadad besieges Samaria and is routed**
- A great king leads an alliance of thirty-two kings (1Kgs 20:1, 1Kgs 20:16)
- Besieging king demands the besieged king's silver, gold, wives and sons (1Kgs 20:3-7)
- Besieger swears the dust of the city will not suffice for handfuls for all his followers (1Kgs 20:10)
- Proverb: 'Let not the one who girds on his armor boast like one who takes it off' (1Kgs 20:11)
- Enemy king drinking drunk in booths with thirty-two allied kings is routed at noon (1Kgs 20:12, 1Kgs 20:16-21)
- Victory won by a small vanguard of 232 young men of the district governors (1Kgs 20:14-15, 1Kgs 20:17-20)

**Battle of Aphek; Ben-hadad spared**
- Enemies claim Israel's God is a god of the hills, not the valleys; God proves them wrong (1Kgs 20:23, 1Kgs 20:28)
- City wall falls on the 27,000 survivors who fled into it (1Kgs 20:30)
- Defeated men come to the victor wearing sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads to beg for life (1Kgs 20:31-32)
- Enemies rely on the reputation that the kings of Israel are merciful kings (malkhei hesed) (1Kgs 20:31)
- Victor calls the enemy king 'my brother'; envoys seize the word as an omen (1Kgs 20:32-33)
- Treaty grants trading quarters (hutsot) in the enemy capital and returns captured cities (1Kgs 20:34)

**The wounded prophet's parable against Ahab**
- Man who refuses a prophet's command to strike him is killed by a lion (1Kgs 20:35-36)
- Wounded prophet, disguised with a bandage over his eyes, tells the king a case and the king condemns himself (1Kgs 20:37-41)

**Naboth's vineyard**
- Commoner refuses to sell or trade his ancestral vineyard to the king: 'God forbid I give you my fathers' inheritance' (1Kgs 21:2-3, 1Kgs 21:6)
- Queen writes letters in the king's name, sealed with his seal, ordering a judicial murder (1Kgs 21:8-11)
- A fast is proclaimed and two worthless men falsely testify that the victim 'blessed (cursed) God and king' (1Kgs 21:9-10, 1Kgs 21:12-13)
- Innocent victim is taken outside the city and stoned to death (1Kgs 21:13)

**Elijah's sentence on Ahab and Jezebel; Ahab's repentance**
- Prophet confronts the king: 'Have you murdered and also taken possession?' (1Kgs 21:19)
- King greets the prophet: 'Have you found me, O my enemy?' (1Kgs 21:20)
- King 'sold himself' to do evil, incited by his wife (1Kgs 21:20, 1Kgs 21:25)
- King tears his clothes, wears sackcloth, fasts and walks softly; God postpones the doom to his son's days (1Kgs 21:27-29)

**Micaiah son of Imlah and the lying spirit**
- Prophet imprisoned on short rations of bread and water until the king returns in peace (1Kgs 22:26-27)

**Ahab's death at Ramoth-gilead**
- Dogs lick the dead king's blood at the pool of Samaria where harlots bathe (1Kgs 22:38)
- King builds a 'house of ivory' (1Kgs 22:39)

**Jehoshaphat of Judah and Ahaziah of Israel**
- Ships built to sail to Ophir for gold are wrecked at Ezion-geber (1Kgs 22:49-50)

**Ahaziah inquires of Baal-zebub; fire on the captains**
- King falls through the lattice of his upper chamber and is injured (2Kgs 1:2)
- Sick king sends to inquire of Baal-zebub, god of Ekron, whether he will recover (2Kgs 1:2-3, 2Kgs 1:6, 2Kgs 1:16)
- Rebuke: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you go to inquire of a foreign god?' (2Kgs 1:3, 2Kgs 1:6, 2Kgs 1:16)
- Doom oracle: 'From the bed you have gone up on you shall not come down, but shall surely die' (2Kgs 1:4, 2Kgs 1:6, 2Kgs 1:16)
- Prophet identified by being 'a hairy man' (or wearing a hair garment) with a leather belt round his loins (2Kgs 1:8)
- Fire from heaven consumes two captains of fifty and their men sent to seize the prophet; the third begs and is spared (2Kgs 1:9-14)

**Elijah taken up in the whirlwind**
- Guild prophets at each town tell the disciple 'today God takes your master'; he answers 'I know, be silent' (2Kgs 2:3, 2Kgs 2:5)
- Prophet rolls up his mantle, strikes the Jordan, and the waters divide so they cross on dry ground (2Kgs 2:8)
- Disciple asks for a double portion (pi shnayim) of the master's spirit, granted if he sees him taken (2Kgs 2:9-10)
- Successor picks up the master's fallen mantle and repeats his miracle, striking the waters (2Kgs 2:13-14)
- Successor strikes the water crying 'Where is YHWH, the God of Elijah?' (2Kgs 2:14)
- Fifty men search three days for the ascended prophet, fearing the spirit dropped him on a mountain or valley, but do not find him (2Kgs 2:16-18)

**Elisha heals Jericho's water; the bears of Bethel**
- Prophet throws salt from a new bowl into the spring and heals the deadly, miscarriage-causing water 'to this day' (2Kgs 2:19-22)
- Small boys jeer 'Go up, baldhead!'; the prophet curses them and two she-bears maul forty-two of them (2Kgs 2:23-24)

**Jehoram's campaign against Mesha of Moab**
- A sheep-breeding vassal king pays tribute of a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams (2Kgs 3:4-5)
- Allied kings on a seven-day detour run out of water for army and beasts and despair (2Kgs 3:9-10)
- Prophet says he would not even look at the wicked king were it not for the righteous ally (2Kgs 3:13-14)
- Prophet calls for a musician; as he plays, the hand of YHWH comes upon him (2Kgs 3:15)
- Dry wadi fills with water though no wind or rain is seen (2Kgs 3:16-17, 2Kgs 3:20)
- At sunrise the water looks red as blood; the enemy thinks the kings have slain each other and rushes to plunder (2Kgs 3:22-23)
- Besieged king offers his firstborn heir as a burnt offering on the city wall, and 'great wrath' falls on Israel, who withdraw (2Kgs 3:26-27)

**The widow's oil**
- Creditor comes to take a dead man's two children as slaves for the debt (2Kgs 4:1)
- Widow's little oil fills all the borrowed vessels behind a shut door and stops when vessels run out (2Kgs 4:2-7)

**The Shunammite woman and her son**
- A wealthy woman has a small roof-chamber built for the holy man with bed, table, chair and lamp (2Kgs 4:8-11)
- Offered a favor with king or general, the hostess replies 'I dwell among my own people' (2Kgs 4:13)
- Woman protests the promise of a son: 'Do not lie to your maidservant' (2Kgs 4:16, 2Kgs 4:28)
- Child in the harvest field cries 'My head, my head!' and dies at noon on his mother's knees (2Kgs 4:18-20)
- Mother lays her dead son on the prophet's bed, shuts the door and rides to fetch him (2Kgs 4:21-24)
- Husband asks why she visits the prophet when it is neither new moon nor sabbath (2Kgs 4:23)
- Bereaved woman grasps the prophet's feet; the servant tries to push her away (2Kgs 4:27)
- Prophet admits 'YHWH has hidden it from me and not told me' (2Kgs 4:27)
- Servant sent in haste must greet no one and answer no greeting on the road (2Kgs 4:29)
- Servant lays the prophet's staff on the dead child's face but there is no voice or response (2Kgs 4:29, 2Kgs 4:31)
- Prophet lies on the child, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands, until the body warms (2Kgs 4:33-35)
- Revived child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes (2Kgs 4:35)

**Death in the pot; loaves for a hundred**
- Wild gourds in the stew make the prophets cry 'Death in the pot!'; flour thrown in makes it harmless (2Kgs 4:39-41)
- Twenty barley loaves of first fruits feed a hundred men with food left over, as God said (2Kgs 4:42-44)

**Naaman healed of leprosy; Gehazi's greed**
- A great foreign general, mighty warrior and favorite of his king, is a leper (2Kgs 5:1)
- A captive Israelite servant girl tells her foreign mistress that the prophet in Samaria could cure her master (2Kgs 5:2-4)
- Prophet sends word to wash seven times in the Jordan; the foreigner is cured (2Kgs 5:10, 2Kgs 5:14)
- Proud foreigner is angry that the prophet did not come out and wave his hand, preferring the rivers of his own land (2Kgs 5:11-13)
- Healed flesh is restored like the flesh of a little boy (2Kgs 5:14)
- Prophet refuses any gift for the healing (2Kgs 5:16)
- Convert takes two mule-loads of Israel's earth to worship YHWH on in a foreign land (2Kgs 5:17)
- Convert asks pardon in advance for bowing in the temple of Rimmon when his master leans on his arm (2Kgs 5:18-19)
- Prophet's servant runs after the healed man and lies to obtain silver and garments (2Kgs 5:20-24)
- Prophet reveals clairvoyance: 'Did not my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot?' (2Kgs 5:26)
- The healed man's leprosy clings to the greedy servant and his descendants forever, white as snow (2Kgs 5:27)

**Elisha at Dothan; the blinded Arameans**
- The prophet tells the king even the words the enemy king speaks in his bedroom (2Kgs 6:8-12)
- At the prophet's prayer the servant's eyes are opened to see the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire (2Kgs 6:15, 2Kgs 6:17)
- Enemy army struck with a blinding confusion (sanwerim) and led by the prophet into the enemy capital (2Kgs 6:18-20)
- Captured enemies are given a great feast and sent home instead of being killed (2Kgs 6:21-23)

**Famine in besieged Samaria; the cannibal mothers**
- Two mothers agree to eat their sons in turn; after the first is eaten the other hides hers (2Kgs 6:28-29)
- When the king tears his clothes, the people see sackcloth underneath on his body (2Kgs 6:30)
- King swears to behead the prophet, blaming him for the disaster (2Kgs 6:31)
- Prophet calls the king 'this son of a murderer' (2Kgs 6:32)
- 'This evil is from YHWH; why should I wait for YHWH any longer?' (2Kgs 6:33)

**The four lepers and the end of the siege**
- Prophet foretells that by this time tomorrow fine flour and barley will sell for a shekel at the city gate (2Kgs 7:1, 2Kgs 7:16, 2Kgs 7:18)
- Skeptic scoffs 'even if YHWH made windows in heaven'; told he will see it but not eat of it, and is trampled (2Kgs 7:2, 2Kgs 7:17, 2Kgs 7:19-20)
- Four lepers at the gate reason that they will die anyway and go over to the enemy camp (2Kgs 7:3-5)
- God makes the enemy hear the sound of chariots, horses and a great army, and they flee abandoning their camp (2Kgs 7:6-7)
- Finders of plunder say 'this is a day of good tidings (besorah); if we keep silent, punishment will find us' (2Kgs 7:9)
- King suspects the abandoned camp is an ambush by feigned retreat and sends scouts (2Kgs 7:12-14)
- Fleeing army leaves the road to the Jordan strewn with garments and vessels thrown away in haste (2Kgs 7:15)

**The Shunammite's land restored**
- Prophet warns the family to emigrate because God has called a famine of seven years (2Kgs 8:1)
- The woman arrives to petition the king at the very moment the servant is telling him her story (2Kgs 8:4-5)
- On returning from seven years abroad, the woman petitions the king and her house, field and its produce are restored (2Kgs 8:3, 2Kgs 8:6)

**Elisha and Hazael; Ben-hadad smothered**
- Sick foreign king sends a lavish gift by forty camels to ask the prophet if he will recover (2Kgs 8:7-9)
- Prophet says 'tell him he will surely recover', though God has shown he will surely die (2Kgs 8:10, 2Kgs 8:14)
- Prophet fixes his gaze until the man is ashamed, then weeps at the atrocities the future king will commit (2Kgs 8:11-12)
- Usurper smothers the sick king with a wet cloth spread over his face and reigns in his place (2Kgs 8:15)

**Jehoram and Ahaziah of Judah**
- Judahite king marries a daughter of Ahab and walks in the ways of the house of Ahab (2Kgs 8:18, 2Kgs 8:26-27)
- Edom and Libnah revolt from Judah's rule 'to this day' (2Kgs 8:20-22)
- Wounded king returns to Jezreel to be healed, visited by his royal kinsman (2Kgs 8:28-29)

**Jehu anointed king**
- A young prophet anoints the army commander king in an inner room with a flask of oil, then opens the door and flees (2Kgs 9:1-6, 2Kgs 9:10)
- Officers spread their garments under the new king on the steps, blow the shofar and proclaim 'Jehu is king!' (2Kgs 9:13)

**Jehu kills Joram and Ahaziah**
- Watchman on the tower reports an approaching company; messengers sent out do not return (2Kgs 9:17-20)
- Watchman recognizes the rider by his driving: 'he drives like a madman' (2Kgs 9:20)
- 'What peace, while your mother Jezebel's harlotries and sorceries are so many?' (2Kgs 9:22)
- Usurper draws his bow and shoots the fleeing king between the shoulders, through the heart (2Kgs 9:24)
- Slain king's body is thrown on the plot of the man his father murdered, fulfilling the oracle (2Kgs 9:21, 2Kgs 9:25-26)

**The death of Jezebel**
- Queen taunts the usurper: 'Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?' (2Kgs 9:31)
- Eunuchs throw the queen down from the window; her blood spatters the wall and horses trample her (2Kgs 9:32-33)
- When they go to bury her, only her skull, feet and palms of her hands are found (2Kgs 9:35)
- The corpse will be like dung on the field so no one can say 'this is Jezebel' (2Kgs 9:37)

**Ahab's seventy sons and the kinsmen of Ahaziah**
- Guardians behead the king's seventy sons and send the heads in baskets; they are piled in two heaps at the gate (2Kgs 10:6-8)
- Usurper tells the people 'you are righteous; I conspired, but who killed all these?' (2Kgs 10:9-10)
- Forty-two kinsmen of the Judahite king are seized alive and slaughtered at the pit of Beth-eked (2Kgs 10:12-14)
- Jehonadab son of Rechab gives his hand, is taken into the chariot, and goes to see the king's zeal for YHWH (2Kgs 10:15-16)
- 'Come with me and see my zeal for YHWH' (2Kgs 10:16)

**Jehu's ruse against the worshipers of Baal; his reign**
- King feigns devotion to Baal, gathers all Baal's worshipers in vestments into the temple, and has them all killed (2Kgs 10:18-25)
- The temple of Baal is torn down and made into a latrine 'to this day' (2Kgs 10:27)
- As reward, the king's sons to the fourth generation will sit on the throne (2Kgs 10:30)
- God begins to 'cut off' parts of Israel, as the foreign king seizes all of Transjordan (2Kgs 10:32-33)

**Athaliah's usurpation and the hidden prince Joash**
- Deposed ruler tears her/his garments crying 'Conspiracy, conspiracy!' or 'Treason!' (2Kgs 11:14)
- A condemned person is taken out so as not to be killed inside the sanctuary (2Kgs 11:15, 2Kgs 11:16)

**Joash repairs the temple; the collection chest; assassination**
- A chest with a hole bored in its lid set by the altar to collect donations (2Kgs 12:10)

**Jehoahaz and Jehoash; Elisha's death and the miraculous bones**
- In answer to prayer God gives Israel an unnamed 'savior' (moshia) (2Kgs 13:4, 2Kgs 13:5)
- An army is reduced by the enemy to a tiny remnant ('like dust at threshing') (2Kgs 13:7)
- Prophet has the king shoot an arrow out of the window as a symbolic act of victory (2Kgs 13:15, 2Kgs 13:17)
- Prophet lays his hands on the king's hands on the bow (2Kgs 13:16)
- King strikes the ground only three times, so his victories are limited to three (2Kgs 13:18, 2Kgs 13:19, 2Kgs 13:25)
- A corpse thrown into a prophet's grave touches his bones and comes back to life (2Kgs 13:20, 2Kgs 13:21)

**Amaziah's war with Jehoash and the fable of the thistle; Jeroboam II**
- New king executes his father's assassins but spares their sons, citing the law of Moses (2Kgs 14:5, 2Kgs 14:6)
- A conquered city or rock is given a new name 'to this day' (2Kgs 14:7)
- A section of the city wall is broken down by the victor (2Kgs 14:13)
- God saves Israel out of pity for its affliction though the king does evil (2Kgs 14:26, 2Kgs 14:27)

**Azariah the leper; the usurper kings of Israel; Tiglath-pileser**
- God strikes a king with skin disease; he lives in isolation while his son rules (2Kgs 15:5)
- Prophecy that a dynasty will last to the fourth generation is fulfilled (2Kgs 15:12)
- A usurper reigns only a month (or days) before being killed (2Kgs 15:13)
- Conqueror rips open the pregnant women of a city (2Kgs 15:16)

**Ahaz sacrifices his son, buys Assyrian help and copies the Damascus altar**
- King copies the design of a foreign altar and installs it in the temple (2Kgs 16:10, 2Kgs 16:11)
- The king personally approaches the altar and offers sacrifice (2Kgs 16:12, 2Kgs 16:13)
- The old bronze altar is reserved for the king 'to inquire' (divination) (2Kgs 16:14, 2Kgs 16:15)
- The temple's bronze stands and the sea on bronze oxen are dismantled (2Kgs 16:17, 2Kgs 16:18)

**Fall of Samaria and the sermon on Israel's exile**
- Vassal king withholds tribute and seeks help from Egypt, and is imprisoned (2Kgs 17:4)
- God warned the people by all his prophets and seers, 'Turn from your evil ways', but they would not listen (2Kgs 17:13, 2Kgs 17:14)

**The resettled peoples, the lions and the syncretistic cult of Samaria**
- Empire settles foreign peoples in the cities of a deported population (2Kgs 17:24)
- God sends lions to kill settlers who do not know the 'law of the god of the land' (2Kgs 17:25, 2Kgs 17:26)
- Each land has a god whose 'manner' (mishpat) newcomers must learn (2Kgs 17:26, 2Kgs 17:27)
- A deported priest is sent back to teach the settlers how to fear the local god (2Kgs 17:27, 2Kgs 17:28)
- Catalogue of foreign gods brought by settler peoples (Succoth-benoth, Nergal, Ashima, Nibhaz, Tartak, Adrammelech, Anammelech) (2Kgs 17:30, 2Kgs 17:31)

**Hezekiah's reform; Sennacherib's invasion and the Rabshakeh's speech**
- King smashes the bronze serpent made by Moses, called Nehushtan, because people burned incense to it (2Kgs 18:4)

**Manasseh's apostasy and its doom-oracle; Amon's assassination**
- The worst king rebuilds the high places, sets up altars to the host of heaven in the temple and practices every forbidden rite (2Kgs 21:2, 2Kgs 21:3, 2Kgs 21:11)
- God will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down (2Kgs 21:13)
- Kings buried in the garden of their palace (garden of Uzza) (2Kgs 21:18, 2Kgs 21:26)

**Josiah's temple repair, the finding of the book and Huldah's oracle**
- A newly found sacred book is read aloud before the king, who tears his clothes (2Kgs 22:10, 2Kgs 22:11)

**Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo**
- Idolatrous cult objects are burned and their dust carried away or thrown on graves (2Kgs 23:4, 2Kgs 23:6, 2Kgs 23:12, 2Kgs 23:15)
- Women weave 'houses' (garments, hangings) for Asherah in the temple precinct (2Kgs 23:7)
- Priests of the high places may not serve at the altar but eat unleavened bread among their brothers (2Kgs 23:8, 2Kgs 23:9)
- The Tophet in the valley of Ben-hinnom is defiled so no one may burn children to Molech (2Kgs 23:10)
- Horses dedicated to the sun at the temple entrance and chariots of the sun burned (2Kgs 23:11)
- The high places Solomon built on the 'mount of destruction' (Mount of Olives) for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom (2Kgs 23:13)
- The bones of a prophet are left undisturbed when other graves are desecrated (2Kgs 23:17, 2Kgs 23:18)
- Priests of the high places are slaughtered on their own altars (2Kgs 23:20)
- A Passover such as had not been kept since the days of the judges (2Kgs 23:21, 2Kgs 23:22, 2Kgs 23:23)
- Despite the righteous king's reform, God does not turn from his anger over a predecessor's sins (2Kgs 23:26, 2Kgs 23:27)
- The righteous king is killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho (2Kgs 23:29, 2Kgs 23:30)

**Nebuchadnezzar's first conquest and the exile of Jehoiachin**
- God sends bands of raiders from surrounding nations against his people (2Kgs 24:2)
- King goes out to surrender to the besieger with his mother, servants and officials (2Kgs 24:12)

**The siege and destruction of Jerusalem; Gedaliah; Jehoiachin released**
- The temple, palace and great houses are burned by the conqueror's chief of guards (rav tabbahim) (2Kgs 25:8, 2Kgs 25:9)
- Only the poorest of the land are left behind as vinedressers and farmers (2Kgs 25:12)
- The bronze pillars, stands and sea are broken up and their bronze carried away (2Kgs 25:13, 2Kgs 25:14, 2Kgs 25:15, 2Kgs 25:16)

**Asa bribes Ben-hadad, imprisons Hanani the seer, seeks physicians and is buried with spices**
- A king fortifies Ramah to blockade the rival kingdom; the stones are later carried off (2Chr 16:1, 2Chr 16:5, 2Chr 16:6)
- A seer rebukes the king for relying on a foreign king instead of God (2Chr 16:7, 2Chr 16:8)
- In his illness the king sought physicians rather than YHWH (2Chr 16:12)
- A king is laid on a bier of spices and a very great fire is burned for him (2Chr 16:14)

**Jehoshaphat's piety, itinerant Torah teachers, tribute and army**
- The king walks in the ways of his father David (2Chr 17:3)
- Officials, Levites and priests go round the cities teaching the people from the book of the Torah (2Chr 17:7, 2Chr 17:8, 2Chr 17:9)
- Arabs bring rams and he-goats as tribute (2Chr 17:11)
- A commander described as one who volunteered himself to YHWH (2Chr 17:16)

**Micaiah ben Imlah, the lying spirit in the divine council, and Ahab's death**
- A righteous king allies by marriage with a wicked king's house (2Chr 18:1)
- One king entices (hesit) another into a disastrous war (2Chr 18:2)
- Two kings sit in royal robes on thrones at the threshing floor by the city gate (2Chr 18:9)
- The prophet swears to speak only what his God tells him (2Chr 18:13)
- Prophet imprisoned on 'bread of affliction and water of affliction' (2Chr 18:25, 2Chr 18:26)
- 'Hear, all you peoples' (quotation linking the prophet to Micah) (2Chr 18:27)
- The enemy commander orders his chariots to fight no one but the king (2Chr 18:30)
- When the threatened king cries out, God turns the attackers away from him (2Chr 18:31)

**Jehu son of Hanani's rebuke; Jehoshaphat appoints judges and a Jerusalem court**
- A seer rebukes the king for helping the wicked and loving those who hate God (2Chr 19:2)
- Despite his sin, good things found in the king mitigate the judgment (2Chr 19:3)
- The king goes out among the people from one end of the land to the other to bring them back to God (2Chr 19:4)
- Judges are told they judge not for man but for God, who is with them in judgment (2Chr 19:6)
- Chief priest presides in matters of God, a royal officer in matters of the king (2Chr 19:11)
- A king named 'YHWH judges' reforms the judiciary (2Chr 19:5, 2Chr 19:6)

**Jehoshaphat's fast and prayer; the Levite oracle; enemies destroy one another as the choir sings**
- A coalition of Moab, Ammon and their allies invades Judah from beyond the Dead Sea (2Chr 20:1, 2Chr 20:2)
- The king proclaims a fast throughout the land in a crisis (2Chr 20:3, 2Chr 20:4)
- The king stands in the temple court before the assembly and prays in a national crisis (2Chr 20:5, 2Chr 20:6, 2Chr 20:9)
- Nations Israel was forbidden to attack during the exodus now repay this by attacking (2Chr 20:10, 2Chr 20:11)
- 'We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you' (2Chr 20:12)
- All Judah stands before God with their little ones, wives and children (2Chr 20:13)
- Prophetic assurance: 'the battle is not yours but God's' (2Chr 20:15, 2Chr 20:17)
- 'Believe in YHWH and you will be established' (wordplay ha'aminu/te'amenu) (2Chr 20:20)
- Singers praising God march ahead of the army into battle (2Chr 20:21)
- The army arrives to find the enemy host all corpses on the ground, none escaped (2Chr 20:24)
- The spoil is so great that gathering it takes three days (2Chr 20:25)
- Ships built in alliance with a wicked king are wrecked, as a prophet foretold (2Chr 20:35, 2Chr 20:36, 2Chr 20:37)

**Jehoram kills his brothers; Elijah's letter; death by bowel disease, unlamented**
- On accession the new king kills all his brothers (2Chr 21:4, 2Chr 21:13)
- The king does evil because he married a daughter of a wicked dynasty (2Chr 21:6)
- God will not destroy David's house, having promised him a lamp (nir) forever (2Chr 21:7)
- A subject people revolts and sets up its own king (2Chr 21:8, 2Chr 21:10)
- A wicked king is struck with an incurable disease and his bowels come out (2Chr 21:15, 2Chr 21:18, 2Chr 21:19)
- Raiders carry off the king's wealth, wives and sons, leaving only the youngest (2Chr 21:16, 2Chr 21:17)
- The people make no funeral burning for a wicked king as for his fathers (2Chr 21:19)
- The wicked king dies and departs 'with no one's regret' (2Chr 21:20)

**Ahaziah counselled by his mother, killed by Jehu; Athaliah's purge and Joash hidden**
- The queen mother counsels her son to do evil (2Chr 22:3, 2Chr 22:4)
- A king's ruin through an ill-judged visit is said to be 'from God' (2Chr 22:7)
- A slain king is given burial for the sake of his pious grandfather (2Chr 22:9)

**Jehoiada's coup with the Levites; Joash crowned, Athaliah killed, Baal temple destroyed**
- A priestly coup is timed to the Sabbath change of temple guards, keeping both shifts (2Chr 23:4, 2Chr 23:8)
- The newly crowned king stands by his pillar at the entrance (2Chr 23:13)
- The usurping queen tears her clothes and cries 'Treason, treason!' (2Chr 23:13)
- The usurper is led out so that she is not killed in the house of YHWH (2Chr 23:14, 2Chr 23:15)
- After the usurper's execution the people rejoice and the city is quiet (2Chr 23:21)

**Joash repairs the temple with the collection chest; after Jehoiada's death he stones Zechariah**
- A child king does right as long as his priestly guardian lives (2Chr 24:1, 2Chr 24:2)
- The priestly guardian takes two wives for the king (2Chr 24:3)
- The Levites are slow to carry out the king's command and are rebuked (2Chr 24:5, 2Chr 24:6)
- A levy instituted by Moses collected for the sanctuary (2Chr 24:6, 2Chr 24:9)
- A chest is set at the temple gate for donations, emptied daily by royal and priestly officials (2Chr 24:8, 2Chr 24:10, 2Chr 24:11)
- Surplus donations are made into gold and silver temple vessels (2Chr 24:14)
- The priest dies old and full of days at 130 (2Chr 24:15)
- A priest is buried among the kings because of the good he did (2Chr 24:16)
- A king who was righteous under a mentor turns to idolatry after the mentor's death (2Chr 24:17, 2Chr 24:18)
- God sends prophets to warn the people but they will not listen (2Chr 24:19)
- A prophet is stoned in the temple court at the king's command (2Chr 24:21)
- A murdered prophet's dying words call on God to see and avenge (2Chr 24:22)

**Amaziah spares the assassins' sons, dismisses mercenaries, worships Edom's gods and is humbled**
- The king does right, but not with a whole heart (2Chr 25:2)
- Once secure, the new king executes the servants who murdered his father (2Chr 25:3)
- The king musters men from twenty years and up by ancestral houses (2Chr 25:5)
- A king dismisses hired troops from the north at a man of God's warning (2Chr 25:6, 2Chr 25:7, 2Chr 25:8, 2Chr 25:10)
- 'YHWH is able to give you much more than this' (compensation for an obedient loss) (2Chr 25:9)
- Ten thousand captives are thrown from the top of a rock and dashed to pieces (2Chr 25:12)
- Dismissed mercenaries vent their anger by raiding the king's towns (2Chr 25:13)
- A victorious king brings home the gods of the defeated and worships them (2Chr 25:14, 2Chr 25:15)
- A king cuts off a prophet: 'Have we made you the king's counselor?' (2Chr 25:16)
- A king's refusal to listen is 'from God' so that he may be defeated for his sin (2Chr 25:20)
- The victor breaks down 400 cubits of the capital's wall (2Chr 25:23)
- The murdered king's body is carried home on horses for burial (2Chr 25:28)

**Uzziah's prosperity, war machines and agriculture; struck with leprosy for offering incense**
- The king's mentor is one who understands the visions of God (2Chr 26:5)
- A king who 'loved the soil' with farmers, vinedressers and herds (2Chr 26:10)
- The king equips the whole army with shields, spears, helmets, mail, bows and sling-stones (2Chr 26:14)
- Devices invented by skilled men are set on towers to shoot arrows and great stones (2Chr 26:15)
- A king enters the sanctuary to burn incense, a right reserved to the priests (2Chr 26:16, 2Chr 26:17, 2Chr 26:18)
- A king stricken with skin disease lives in a separate house while his son governs (2Chr 26:21)
- The prophet Isaiah is named as author of a king's history (2Chr 26:22)
- A leper king is buried in the burial field of the kings, not in their tombs (2Chr 26:23)

**Jotham's building and Ammonite tribute**
- A son follows his father's good ways but avoids his specific sin (2Chr 27:2)
- The king builds extensively on the wall of the Ophel (2Chr 27:3)
- The same regnal age and length are repeated within one short account (2Chr 27:1, 2Chr 27:8)

**Ahaz's child sacrifice and defeats; Oded and the Ephraimites release and tend the captives**
- A king makes molten images for the Baals (2Chr 28:2)
- An enemy kills 120,000 men of Judah in a single day (2Chr 28:6)
- An enemy warrior kills the king's son, palace chief and second-in-command (2Chr 28:7)
- Israelites take their kinsmen of Judah captive as slaves (2Chr 28:8, 2Chr 28:10)
- A prophet rebukes victors whose slaughter of kin was a 'rage reaching to heaven' (2Chr 28:9, 2Chr 28:10, 2Chr 28:11)
- Northern chiefs obey the prophet and refuse to bring the captives in (2Chr 28:12, 2Chr 28:13, 2Chr 28:14)
- Captors clothe, shoe, feed, anoint and carry the weak captives on donkeys back to their kin (2Chr 28:15)
- A king appeals to Assyria for help, but the Assyrian king oppresses rather than helps him (2Chr 28:16, 2Chr 28:20, 2Chr 28:21)
- Edomites and Philistines raid a weakened Judah and take its towns (2Chr 28:17, 2Chr 28:18)
- A king of Judah is called 'king of Israel' (2Chr 28:19)
- A defeated king sacrifices to the gods of his conquerors, hoping they will help him (2Chr 28:23)
- A king cuts up the temple vessels and shuts the doors of the house of YHWH (2Chr 28:24)
- A king sets up altars at every corner of the capital and high places in every town (2Chr 28:24, 2Chr 28:25)

**Hezekiah reopens and purifies the temple**
- King does right in God's eyes like David his father (2Chr 29:2)
- A reforming king acts in the first month of his first year (2Chr 29:3, 2Chr 29:17)
- Former kings shut the temple doors, put out the lamps and ceased incense and offerings (2Chr 29:7)
- Impurity removed from the temple is carried out to the Kidron valley (2Chr 29:16)
- Temple purified in two eight-day stages, ending on the sixteenth of the first month (2Chr 29:17)
- Sin offering of seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven he-goats (2Chr 29:21)
- Sin offering made explicitly 'for all Israel', including the northern tribes (2Chr 29:24)
- The song of the LORD begins when the burnt offering begins and continues until it ends (2Chr 29:27-28)
- Levites praise God 'with the words of David and Asaph the seer' (2Chr 29:30)
- Levites are more conscientious than the priests in sanctifying themselves (2Chr 29:34)
- Rejoicing that God accomplished the matter suddenly (2Chr 29:36)

**Hezekiah's Passover in the second month for all Israel**
- Proclamation sent through all Israel from Beersheba to Dan (2Chr 30:5)
- Southern king invites the remnant of the northern tribes left by Assyria to return to God (2Chr 30:6-9)
- Royal messengers are laughed to scorn by the northern tribes (2Chr 30:10)
- Idolatrous altars and incense stands are thrown into the Kidron valley (2Chr 30:14)
- Impure participants eat the Passover improperly and the king prays God pardon all who seek him (2Chr 30:17-20)
- Assembly decides to keep the festival for another seven days (2Chr 30:23)
- Resident strangers from Israel and Judah join the festival (2Chr 30:25)
- The priests' blessing and prayer reach God's holy dwelling in heaven (2Chr 30:27)

**Destruction of high places; heaps of tithes and Levite divisions**
- Firstfruits include honey along with grain, wine and oil (2Chr 31:5)
- Tithes and offerings are piled in heaps over several months (2Chr 31:6-8)
- Priests report they have eaten, been satisfied and left over in abundance because God blessed the people (2Chr 31:10)
- The gatekeeper of the east gate is in charge of the freewill offerings (2Chr 31:14)
- Levite males enrolled for temple portions from three years old (2Chr 31:16)

**Sennacherib's invasion, blasphemy and the angel's slaughter**
- Defenders stop up the springs and streams so the besieger will find no water (2Chr 32:3-4)
- Besieger mocks the king for removing high places and commanding worship at one altar (2Chr 32:12)
- The enemy king writes letters reviling the God of Israel (2Chr 32:17)
- Enemy envoys shout in Judean to the people on the wall to terrify them (2Chr 32:18)
- Enemies speak of Israel's God as of the gods of the nations, the work of human hands (2Chr 32:19)
- King and prophet pray together and cry to heaven against the invader (2Chr 32:20)
- An angel of God annihilates the besieging Assyrian army (2Chr 32:21)

**Hezekiah's illness and sign, pride, wealth, tunnel, Babylonian envoys and burial**
- King falls sick to the point of death, prays and receives a sign (2Chr 32:24)
- God gives the sick king a sign (wonder) that is not described (2Chr 32:24, 2Chr 32:31)
- King's heart grows proud after a favor, then he humbles himself and wrath is averted (2Chr 32:25-26)
- King builds treasuries for silver, gold, gems and spices, storehouses for grain, wine and oil, and stalls for cattle (2Chr 32:27-29)
- God leaves the king alone to test him and know all that is in his heart (2Chr 32:31)
- A king's acts are said to be written in a prophet's vision or the words of seers (2Chr 32:32)
- Honored king buried on the ascent (upper part) of the royal tombs (2Chr 32:33)

**Manasseh's apostasy, captivity in Babylon, repentance and restoration**
- A king builds altars to and worships the host of heaven (2Chr 33:3, 2Chr 33:5)
- A wicked king builds altars to other gods inside the temple courts (2Chr 33:4-5)
- A king sets a carved image (semel) in the house of God (2Chr 33:7, 2Chr 33:15)
- A wicked king humbles himself in captivity and God hears his prayer (2Chr 33:12-13)
- A repentant king's prayer is preserved in a prophetic record (2Chr 33:18-19)
- The Fish Gate of Jerusalem (2Chr 33:14)
- People still sacrifice at high places, but only to YHWH (2Chr 33:17)
- A king is buried in his own house rather than the royal tombs (2Chr 33:20)

**Josiah's early piety and purge of the land**
- While still a youth the king begins to seek the God of David (2Chr 34:3)
- Smashed idols ground to dust and strewn on the graves of their worshipers (2Chr 34:4)
- Bones of idolatrous priests burned on their own altars (2Chr 34:5)

**Temple repair, finding of the book of the Torah, Huldah's oracle and covenant**
- Money collected by the Levites is given to the workmen to repair the temple (2Chr 34:9-11)
- Levites skilled in music oversee the burden-bearers and workmen (2Chr 34:12-13)
- The scribe reads the found book aloud before the king (2Chr 34:18)
- Prophet announces that the curses written in the found book will come upon the land (2Chr 34:24)
- King stands at his place and makes the covenant before God (2Chr 34:31)

**Josiah's great Passover**
- King tells the Levites to set the ark in the temple: they need no longer carry it on their shoulders (2Chr 35:3)
- Levitical divisions follow the writing of David and the document of Solomon (2Chr 35:4)
- Levites prepare the Passover for priests, singers and gatekeepers who cannot leave their posts (2Chr 35:14-15)

**Josiah ignores Necho's divine warning and dies at Megiddo; Jeremiah's lament**
- A foreign king's warning is described as coming 'from the mouth of God' and ignored to the hearer's death (2Chr 35:21-22)
- Formula 'what have I to do with you?' (mah li va-lakh) (2Chr 35:21)
- Archers shoot the king, who says 'take me away, I am badly wounded' (2Chr 35:23)
- Mortally wounded king moved from his chariot to a second chariot and carried home (2Chr 35:24)
- A king dies in battle in the valley of Megiddo (2Chr 35:22)
- Male and female singers lament a fallen king every year as a fixed custom (2Chr 35:25)
- Jeremiah composes a lament for a dead king (2Chr 35:25)

**Last kings of Judah, burning of the temple, exile and seventy years**
- Overlord imposes a fine of 100 talents of silver and a talent of gold (2Chr 36:3)
- God's wrath rises until there is no remedy (2Chr 36:16)
- The enemy kills the young men by the sword in the sanctuary (2Chr 36:17)

**The edict of Cyrus closes the Hebrew canon**
- A canonical book ends with the summons 'let him go up' to Jerusalem (2Chr 36:23)

**Cyrus's decree and the return of the temple vessels**
- Event dated as fulfilling the word of God by the mouth of Jeremiah (Ezra 1:1)
- Neighbors equip the departing exiles with silver, gold, goods and cattle (Ezra 1:4, Ezra 1:6)
- An inventory's stated total does not match the sum of its items (Ezra 1:9-11)

**List of the returnees with Zerubbabel**
- Returnees' horses, mules, camels and donkeys are counted (Ezra 2:66-67)

**Altar rebuilt, Sukkot kept, foundation of the second temple laid amid weeping and shouting**
- Returnees rebuild the altar on its former foundations before the temple itself (Ezra 3:2-3)
- Burnt offerings resume from the first of the seventh month before the temple foundation is laid (Ezra 3:6)
- Temple building begins in the second month, as Solomon's did (Ezra 3:8)
- Elders who saw the first temple weep aloud at the foundation of the second (Ezra 3:12)
- The sound of joyful shouting cannot be distinguished from the sound of weeping (Ezra 3:13)

**Offer of help from the deportee peoples rejected; opposition and accusations**
- Deported settlers claim they have sacrificed to Israel's God since the Assyrian king brought them (Ezra 4:2)
- Neighboring settlers offer to help build the temple and are refused (Ezra 4:3)
- The 'people of the land' weaken and frighten the builders and hire counselors against them (Ezra 4:4-5)
- Enemies write an accusation (sitnah) against the people to the king (Ezra 4:6)
- A letter written in Aramaic script and Aramaic language is quoted (Ezra 4:7)

**Rehum and Shimshai's letter to Artaxerxes and the king's stop order**
- Imperial officials list the deported peoples settled in Samaria (Ezra 4:9-10)
- 'The great and noble Osnappar' (Ashurbanipal) deported peoples to Samaria (Ezra 4:10)
- Imperial letters quoted with Aramaic chancery formulas ('and now', greetings of peace) (Ezra 4:11, Ezra 4:17)
- Officials denounce Jerusalem to the king as a rebellious and wicked city that will withhold tribute (Ezra 4:12-16)
- Officials justify loyalty because 'we eat the salt of the palace' (Ezra 4:14)
- Royal archives confirm that mighty kings in Jerusalem once ruled all Beyond the River (Ezra 4:20)
- Imperial decree stops the rebuilding until further order (Ezra 4:21-23)
- Narrative places documents of later reigns before earlier events (Ezra 4:8, Ezra 4:24)

**Haggai and Zechariah spur rebuilding; Tattenai's letter to Darius**
- Prophets (Haggai, Zechariah) urge and support the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:1-2)
- Provincial governor demands who authorized the building and the names of the builders (Ezra 5:3-4, Ezra 5:9-10)
- 'The eye of their God was upon the elders', so the work was not stopped (Ezra 5:5)
- Temple built of great (rolled) stones with timber laid in the walls (Ezra 5:8)
- Builders declare themselves servants of 'the God of heaven and earth' (Ezra 5:11)
- Exile explained to a foreign ruler: the fathers angered the God of heaven so he gave them to Nebuchadnezzar (Ezra 5:12)
- Sheshbazzar is credited with laying the temple foundation (Ezra 5:16)

**Cyrus's memorandum found at Ecbatana; Darius's decree; temple completed and dedicated**
- A lost royal memorandum is found in the archive of a distant citadel (Ezra 6:2)
- Building with three courses of great stones and one course of timber (Ezra 6:4)
- King orders daily supplies of animals, wheat, salt, wine and oil for the temple sacrifices (Ezra 6:9)
- Violator of the decree is impaled on a beam torn from his own house and his house made a dunghill (Ezra 6:11)
- Edict closes with a curse on any king or people who alters it or harms the temple (Ezra 6:12)
- Completion credited to the decrees of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes (Ezra 6:14)
- The second temple is finished on the third of Adar in Darius's sixth year (Ezra 6:15)
- Twelve he-goats offered as sin offering by the number of Israel's tribes (Ezra 6:17)

**Passover of the returnees and those who separated from the nations' impurity**
- The Persian king is called 'the king of Assyria' (Ezra 6:22)

**Ezra's priestly lineage and journey to Jerusalem**
- A priest's genealogy traced back to Aaron the chief priest (Ezra 7:1-5)
- Hero called a skilled scribe (sofer mahir) in the Torah of Moses (Ezra 7:6, Ezra 7:11)
- The journey from Babylon to Jerusalem takes four months, first to fifth month (Ezra 7:8-9)
- The scribe set his heart to seek (study) the Torah, to do it and to teach it (Ezra 7:10)

**Artaxerxes' rescript to Ezra**
- Priest bears the imperial title 'scribe of the law of the God of heaven' (Ezra 7:12, Ezra 7:21)
- Royal grant up to 100 talents of silver, 100 kor of wheat, 100 baths of wine and oil, and salt without limit (Ezra 7:22)
- Emperor provides for the temple lest wrath come on his realm and sons (Ezra 7:23)
- Priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and temple servants are exempt from tribute, poll tax and toll (Ezra 7:24)
- Emperor empowers a priest-scribe to appoint judges who know the law of his God and teach those who do not (Ezra 7:25)
- Imperial decree enforces 'the law of your God and the law of the king' with death, banishment, fines or prison (Ezra 7:26)

**Ezra's doxology for the king's favor (start of first-person memoir)**
- Blessing God who put it into the foreign king's heart to glorify the temple (Ezra 7:27)

**Ezra's caravan, the search for Levites, fast at Ahava and the weighing of treasure**
- A descendant of David (Hattush) is listed among the returning exiles (Ezra 8:2)
- Leader reviews the caravan and finds no Levites, and must recruit them (Ezra 8:15)
- A center of Levites and temple servants in exile called 'Casiphia the place' (Ezra 8:17)
- Leader proclaims a fast at a river to seek a safe way for the journey (Ezra 8:21, Ezra 8:23)
- Leader is ashamed to ask the king for soldiers after boasting that God protects his seekers (Ezra 8:22)
- Gold, silver and vessels weighed out to priests for the journey and weighed again on arrival (Ezra 8:24-30, Ezra 8:33-34)
- Leader tells the bearers: you are holy to the LORD and the vessels are holy (Ezra 8:28)
- God delivers the caravan from enemies and ambushers on the road (Ezra 8:31)
- Twelve bulls offered for all Israel by the returned exiles (Ezra 8:35)
- Royal decrees delivered to the king's satraps and governors (Ezra 8:36)

**Report of intermarriage; Ezra's mourning and confession**
- The 'holy seed' has mixed itself with the peoples of the lands (Ezra 9:2)
- Leader sits appalled until the evening offering, then rises to pray (Ezra 9:3-5)
- Our iniquities rise above our heads and our guilt reaches to heaven (Ezra 9:6)
- God gives the remnant 'a peg in his holy place' as a foothold (Ezra 9:8)
- God has punished us less than our iniquities deserved (Ezra 9:13)
- God has left an escaped remnant (Ezra 9:8, Ezra 9:13-15)

**Covenant to send away foreign wives; assembly in the rain; list of offenders**
- Leader prays and confesses weeping, prostrate before the house of God (Ezra 10:1)
- 'There is still hope for Israel concerning this' (Ezra 10:2)
- Community covenants to send away all foreign wives and their children (Ezra 10:3, Ezra 10:11, Ezra 10:44)
- Leader makes the priests, Levites and all Israel swear to carry out the reform (Ezra 10:5)
- Leader neither eats bread nor drinks water in mourning for the people's sin (Ezra 10:6)
- Whoever fails to attend loses his property (herem) and is separated from the congregation (Ezra 10:8)
