- The assembly sits trembling in the open square in the winter rains (Ezra 10:9, Ezra 10:13)
- Named individuals are recorded as opposing the assembly's decision (Ezra 10:15)
- A tribunal of family heads examines each case at appointed times (Ezra 10:14, Ezra 10:16-17)
- Sons of the high priest are among those who married foreign wives (Ezra 10:18)
- Named list of men who had married foreign wives (Ezra 10:18-43)
- Mixed marriages have already produced children, who are included in the dismissal (Ezra 10:44)

**News from Jerusalem and Nehemiah's prayer at Susa**
- News that Jerusalem's wall is broken down and its gates burned (Neh 1:3)
- A Jewish exile serves as cupbearer to the Persian king (Neh 1:11)

**The king's question, Nehemiah's commission and the night inspection of the walls**
- A courtier fears because his face is sad before the king (Neh 2:1-2)
- Jerusalem described to a foreign king as 'the city of my fathers' graves' (Neh 2:3, Neh 2:5)
- Courtier prays to the God of heaven before answering the king's question (Neh 2:4)
- Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite and Geshem the Arab oppose the rebuilding (Neh 2:10, Neh 2:19)
- Leader secretly inspects the ruined walls by night with a few men (Neh 2:12-16)
- A spring at Jerusalem called the Dragon (Tannin) or Jackal Spring (Neh 2:13)
- Builders are accused of rebelling against the imperial king (Neh 2:19)
- Leader tells the enemies they have no portion, right or memorial in Jerusalem (Neh 2:20)

**The builders of the wall and gates, section by section**
- High priest and priests build and consecrate a city gate (Neh 3:1)
- Nobles refuse to put their necks to the communal work (Neh 3:5)
- Goldsmiths, perfumers and merchants work as groups on the wall (Neh 3:8, Neh 3:31-32)
- A district ruler builds his section of the wall with his daughters (Neh 3:12)
- Each builder repairs the wall section opposite his own house (Neh 3:10, Neh 3:23, Neh 3:28-30)
- The pool of Shelah (Siloam) by the king's garden (Neh 3:15)
- The tombs of David used as a landmark on the wall (Neh 3:16)
- The 'court of the guard' beside the upper royal palace (Neh 3:25)
- The temple servants live on the Ophel (Neh 3:26)
- Province divided into districts and half-districts (pelekh) under named rulers (Neh 3:9, Neh 3:12, Neh 3:14-18)

**Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders; Nehemiah's imprecation**
- Enemy ridicules the 'feeble Jews' reviving stones from heaps of burnt rubble (Neh 3:33-34)
- Mocker says even a fox climbing on the wall would break it down (Neh 3:35)
- The whole wall is joined up to half its height (Neh 3:38)

**Conspiracy against Jerusalem; builders work with a weapon in one hand**
- Neighboring peoples conspire together to attack the rebuilding city (Neh 4:1-2)
- Workers' rhythmic complaint that the porters' strength fails and the rubble is too much (Neh 4:4)
- Neighbors warn 'ten times' of attack from every side (Neh 4:6)
- Defenders posted by families behind the wall with swords, spears and bows (Neh 4:7)
- God frustrates the enemies' plot once it becomes known (Neh 4:9)
- Half the men work while half stand guard with spears, shields, bows and armor (Neh 4:10, Neh 4:15)
- Builders work with one hand and hold a weapon in the other, swords at their sides (Neh 4:11-12)
- Trumpeter beside the leader: wherever the shofar sounds, rally there (Neh 4:12, Neh 4:14)
- 'Our God will fight for us' - rally at the trumpet call (Neh 4:14)
- Work continues from the rising of dawn until the stars come out (Neh 4:15)
- Leader and guards never take off their clothes while on watch (Neh 4:17)

**Outcry over debt slavery; Nehemiah's remission and his refusal of the governor's allowance**
- A great outcry of the poor and their wives against their fellow Jews (Neh 5:1)
- In famine the people pledge fields, vineyards and houses for grain (Neh 5:3)
- The poor borrow money against fields and vineyards to pay the king's tax (Neh 5:4)
- The poor protest: 'our flesh is like our brothers' flesh, our children like their children' (Neh 5:5)
- Leader shakes out the fold of his garment: so may God shake out whoever breaks the oath (Neh 5:13)
- Governor refuses his official food allowance so as not to burden the people (Neh 5:14-15, Neh 5:18)
- Governor feeds 150 officials and foreign visitors daily at his own expense (Neh 5:17-18)

**Plots against Nehemiah, the open letter, the hired prophet and the wall completed in 52 days**
- Enemies invite the leader to a meeting in the plain intending to harm him (Neh 6:2)
- 'I am doing a great work and cannot come down' - leader refuses a meeting (Neh 6:3)
- Enemy sends the same message four times, then a fifth with an open letter (Neh 6:4-5)
- Enemy sends an unsealed letter so its slanders can be read by all (Neh 6:5-7)
- Enemies allege the leader builds fortifications because he plans to make himself king (Neh 6:6-7)
- Enemies hire a prophet to frighten the leader into sin with a false oracle (Neh 6:10-13)
- A layman refuses to hide in the temple sanctuary to save his life (Neh 6:11)
- A prophetess and other prophets try to frighten the leader (Neh 6:14)
- The wall is completed in fifty-two days (Neh 6:15)
- Surrounding nations realize the work was done by God and are humbled (Neh 6:16)
- Local nobles exchange letters with the enemy, bound to him by oath and marriage (Neh 6:17-19)

**Gates guarded; underpopulated city; the genealogical register of the first returnees found**
- City gates not to be opened until the sun is hot (Neh 7:3)
- An official is appointed because he is a faithful man who fears God more than many (Neh 7:2)
- The city is wide and large but the people few and houses unbuilt (Neh 7:4)
- A list repeated elsewhere with differing figures (Neh 7:10, Neh 7:13, Neh 7:15, Neh 7:17)
- A parallel list lacks the horses and mules counted in its source (Neh 7:68)

**Ezra reads the Torah at the Water Gate; the day declared holy; Sukkot restored**
- Reader stands on a wooden tower made for the purpose, flanked by named men (Neh 8:4)
- When the reader opens the scroll all the people stand up (Neh 8:5)
- Assembly answers the blessing 'Amen, Amen' with uplifted hands and prostrates (Neh 8:6)
- Levites explain the Torah reading so the people understand it (Neh 8:7-8)
- Leaders forbid weeping and mourning because the day is holy (Neh 8:9-11)
- On the holy day the people eat, drink and send portions to those who have nothing (Neh 8:10, Neh 8:12)
- 'The joy of the LORD is your strength' (Neh 8:10)
- Studying the Torah, the leaders find a forgotten commandment written in it (Neh 8:13-14)
- Festival booths built on rooftops, in courtyards and in public squares (Neh 8:16)

**Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession**
- The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners (Neh 9:2)
- A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing (Neh 9:3)
- Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice (Neh 9:4)
- Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting' (Neh 9:5)
- 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation (Neh 9:6)
- God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham (Neh 9:7)
- God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him (Neh 9:8)
- God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai (Neh 9:14)
- God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness (Neh 9:20)
- God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them' (Neh 9:29)

**The sealed pledge (amanah) and its stipulations**
- A written covenant document (amanah) sealed by leaders (Neh 10:1-2)
- Named list of those who sealed the covenant document (Neh 10:2-28)
- The people enter into a curse and an oath to walk in God's Torah (Neh 10:30)
- Pledge not to buy wares or grain from foreign traders on the Sabbath or holy day (Neh 10:32)
- Community pledges an annual third of a shekel for the temple service (Neh 10:33-34)
- Pledge: 'we will not forsake the house of our God' (Neh 10:40)

**One in ten chosen by lot to live in Jerusalem; residents of the city and the towns**
- One in ten of the people chosen by lot to live in Jerusalem (Neh 11:1)
- The people bless those who volunteer to live in Jerusalem (Neh 11:2)
- Jerusalem called 'the holy city' (ir ha-qodesh) (Neh 11:1, Neh 11:18)
- Judahite residents traced to Perez son of Judah (Neh 11:4-6)
- An Asaphite Levite leads the thanksgiving at prayer (Neh 11:17)
- A royal command fixes the singers' daily provision (Neh 11:23)
- An official stands 'at the king's hand' in every matter concerning the people (Neh 11:24)
- Resettlers live in towns with ancient names (Kiriath-arba, Beersheba, Ziklag) (Neh 11:25-30)
- A 'valley of craftsmen' (Ge-haharashim) (Neh 11:35)

**Lists of priests and Levites; the high-priestly succession**
- Levitical choirs stand opposite each other, watch facing watch, in antiphonal praise (Neh 12:9, Neh 12:24)
- A king called 'Darius the Persian' dates the priestly records (Neh 12:22)
- A 'book of the chronicles' is cited as a source (Neh 12:23)
- Gatekeepers guard the storehouses at the gates (Neh 12:25)

**Dedication of the wall with two thanksgiving choirs processing on the wall**
- Singers have built themselves villages around Jerusalem (Neh 12:28-29)
- Priests and Levites purify themselves, the people, the gates and the wall (Neh 12:30)
- Two thanksgiving choirs walk atop the wall in opposite directions and meet at the temple (Neh 12:31-40)
- Priests blow trumpets in a festive procession (Neh 12:35, Neh 12:41)
- The rejoicing in Jerusalem is heard from far away (Neh 12:43)

**Ammonites and Moabites excluded; Tobiah expelled from the temple; Levites' portions, Sabbath and mixed marriages**
- A priest gives a foreign enemy a storeroom in the temple courts as his residence (Neh 13:4-5, Neh 13:7)
- Reformer throws an intruder's household goods out of the temple chamber (Neh 13:8)
- Temple chambers defiled by an outsider are purified and the holy vessels restored (Neh 13:9)
- The Persian king is called 'king of Babylon' (Neh 13:6)
- Unpaid Levites and singers abandon the temple for their fields (Neh 13:10)
- Treasurers appointed because they are counted trustworthy (Neh 13:13)
- City gates closed when they grow dark before the Sabbath and opened only after it (Neh 13:19)
- Merchants spend the night outside the wall waiting to trade, until threatened away (Neh 13:20-21)
- Purified Levites guard the city gates to keep the Sabbath holy (Neh 13:22)
- Children of mixed marriages speak their mother's language and cannot speak Judean (Neh 13:23-24)
- Reformer curses, strikes and pulls out the hair of the men who married foreign wives (Neh 13:25)
- Solomon, beloved of God, was made to sin by foreign wives (Neh 13:26)
- A grandson of the high priest is son-in-law of the Samarian governor and is driven away (Neh 13:28)
- The priesthood and the covenant of the priests and Levites are defiled by mixed marriage (Neh 13:29)

**Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal**
- King holds a banquet showing his riches for 180 days (Esth 1:3-4)
- At the royal banquet drinking is by rule, no one compelled (Esth 1:8)
- The queen holds a separate banquet for the women (Esth 1:9)
- Seven named eunuchs serve the king (Esth 1:10)
- Merry with wine, the king orders the queen brought in her crown to show her beauty to his guests (Esth 1:10-11)
- The queen refuses to come at the king's command and the king is enraged (Esth 1:12)
- A decree written into the laws of Persia and Media cannot be revoked (Esth 1:19)
- The disobedient queen is deposed and her royalty given to 'another better than she' (Esth 1:19)
- Royal decree that every man shall rule in his own house (Esth 1:20-22)

**The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot**
- Virgins gathered from all provinces so the king may choose a new queen (Esth 2:2-4)
- A royal eunuch keeps the harem and supplies the women's cosmetics (Esth 2:3, Esth 2:8, Esth 2:14-15)
- Hero's genealogy runs back to Kish the Benjaminite (Saul's father) (Esth 2:5)
- Hero's family was deported from Jerusalem with King Jeconiah (Esth 2:6)
- Orphan girl adopted and raised as a daughter by her cousin (Esth 2:7, Esth 2:15)
- Heroine has a Hebrew name (Hadassah) and a foreign one (Esther) (Esth 2:7)
- Heroine wins the favor of her guardian official, who gives her special treatment (Esth 2:9, Esth 2:15)
- Heroine at the foreign court hides her people and kindred on her guardian's orders (Esth 2:10, Esth 2:20)
- Twelve months of beautification: six with oil of myrrh and six with spices (Esth 2:12)
- Each maiden goes to the king for one night and passes to the concubines' house (Esth 2:13-14)
- Heroine asks for nothing beyond what the eunuch advises when she goes to the king (Esth 2:15)
- An orphan girl is loved above all and crowned queen (Esth 2:17)
- King grants the provinces a remission and gives gifts at the new queen's feast (Esth 2:18)
- Hero sits in the king's gate as an official (Esth 2:19, Esth 2:21)
- Two eunuch doorkeepers plot to kill the king; the hero learns of it and reports it (Esth 2:21-22)
- A courtier's service is recorded in the royal book of chronicles before the king (Esth 2:23)

**Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman; the lot is cast and the decree of extermination issued**
- Villain called 'the Agagite' opposes a hero descended from Kish the Benjaminite (Esth 3:1, Esth 3:10)
- King promotes a courtier and sets his seat above all the princes (Esth 3:1)
- Courtiers press the hero day after day to obey the order, and he refuses (Esth 3:4)
- Offended by one man, the villain seeks to destroy his whole people (Esth 3:6)
- Villain offers the king ten thousand talents of silver for permission to destroy a people (Esth 3:9)
- King takes off his signet ring and gives it to a courtier to seal decrees (Esth 3:10, Esth 3:12)
- Decree to destroy, kill and annihilate an entire people, young and old, women and children, on a single day (Esth 3:13)
- King and his vizier sit down to drink while the city is thrown into confusion by their decree (Esth 3:15)

**Mordecai's mourning and Esther's resolve to approach the king**
- No one may enter the king's gate dressed in sackcloth (Esth 4:2)
- A mourner refuses the fresh clothes sent to replace his sackcloth (Esth 4:4)
- Anyone who enters the king's inner court unsummoned is put to death (Esth 4:11)
- Relief and deliverance will arise 'from another place' if the hero stays silent (veiled reference to God) (Esth 4:14)
- 'Who knows whether you came to royal power for such a time as this?' (Esth 4:14)
- Heroine resolves to risk death for her people: 'if I perish, I perish' (Esth 4:16)
- Deliverance narrated without any explicit mention of God (Esth 4:14)

**Esther before the king; first banquet; Haman's gallows**
- The heroine delays her real request, inviting king and villain to successive banquets (Esth 5:4, Esth 5:8)
- The villain boasts to wife and friends of his wealth, sons and honors just before his fall (Esth 5:11, Esth 5:12)
- The villain's wife and friends advise him to build a gallows for his rival (Esth 5:14)
- A stake or gallows fifty cubits high is erected for hanging the rival (Esth 5:14)

**The king's sleepless night and Mordecai's parade**
- A sleepless king has the royal chronicles read to him and discovers an unrewarded benefactor (Esth 6:1, Esth 6:2)
- The man who exposed a plot against the king's life has gone unrewarded (Esth 6:2, Esth 6:3)
- Asked how to honor 'the man the king delights to honor', the villain, thinking it is himself, prescribes the honor his rival receives (Esth 6:6, Esth 6:7, Esth 6:8, Esth 6:9)
- Honoree is dressed in the king's robe and paraded through the city on the king's horse with a herald (Esth 6:8, Esth 6:9, Esth 6:11)
- The villain himself must lead his rival's horse and proclaim his honor (Esth 6:10, Esth 6:11)
- The villain's wise men and wife foretell that he cannot prevail against one 'of the seed of the Jews' (Esth 6:13)

**Second banquet; Haman exposed and hanged**
- Queen protests that her people have been sold to destruction; had it been slavery she would have kept silent (Esth 7:3, Esth 7:4)
- The queen reveals her hidden ethnic identity to the king to save her people (Esth 7:3, Esth 7:4, Esth 7:6)
- The enraged king leaves the banquet for the palace garden and returns to a compromising scene (Esth 7:7, Esth 7:8)
- Villain falls on the queen's couch pleading, and the king takes it as assault (Esth 7:8)
- A eunuch informs the king that the villain's gallows stands ready (Esth 7:9)

**Mordecai elevated; the counter-decree**
- The condemned enemy's household is given to the intended victim (Esth 8:1, Esth 8:7)
- The king takes back his signet ring from the fallen vizier and gives it to the hero (Esth 8:2)
- Since the first decree cannot be revoked, a second edict permits the threatened people to defend themselves (Esth 8:5, Esth 8:11, Esth 8:13)
- Mounted royal couriers on swift royal steeds carry the edict in haste (Esth 8:10, Esth 8:14)
- The hero goes out in royal blue and white with a great gold crown and a purple linen mantle (Esth 8:15)
- 'The Jews had light and gladness, joy and honor' (Esth 8:16)
- Many of the peoples of the land become Jews (mityahadim) because fear of the Jews fell on them (Esth 8:17)

**The thirteenth of Adar; Haman's ten sons**
- 'It was turned about' (venahafokh hu): the day meant for the Jews' destruction becomes their victory (Esth 9:1)
- The villain's ten named sons are killed and then hanged (Esth 9:7, Esth 9:8, Esth 9:9, Esth 9:10, Esth 9:13, Esth 9:14)
- The victors explicitly refrain from taking plunder (Esth 9:10, Esth 9:15, Esth 9:16)
- The queen requests a second day of reprisal in the capital (Esth 9:13, Esth 9:15)
- Villagers of unwalled towns keep the festival on a different day from the capital (Esth 9:18, Esth 9:19)

**Letters instituting Purim**
- Annual festival of Purim (14th/15th of Adar) instituted with feasting, joy, portions to friends and gifts to the poor (Esth 9:21, Esth 9:22, Esth 9:27, Esth 9:28)
- The month 'turned from sorrow to gladness and from mourning to a holiday' (Esth 9:22)
- The festival is named Purim after the 'pur', the lot cast by the villain (Esth 9:24, Esth 9:26)
- A festival is established by letters of a lay leader and a queen, not by a prophet or priest (Esth 9:20, Esth 9:29, Esth 9:32)
- The festival binds the Jews, their descendants and all who join them (Esth 9:27)

**Coda on Ahasuerus and Mordecai**
- The king imposes tribute on the land and the islands of the sea (Esth 10:1)
- Citation of the 'book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia' (Esth 10:2)
- A Jew becomes second to the foreign king, great among his people, seeking their good (Esth 10:3)

**Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test**
- The exemplary righteous man is a non-Israelite living in the land of Uz in the east (Job 1:1)
- A patriarch's wealth is listed in precise numbers of sheep, camels, oxen and asses (Job 1:3)
- Grown sons hold feasts in turn, each on his day, and invite their sisters (Job 1:4)
- Father offers burnt offerings in case his children 'blessed' (cursed) God in their hearts (Job 1:5)
- The verb 'bless' (barekh) used as a scribal euphemism for cursing God (Job 1:5, Job 1:11)
- 'Does he fear God for nothing?': piety suspected of being motivated by reward (Job 1:9)
- God has set a protective hedge around the righteous man, his house and goods (Job 1:10)
- Messenger after messenger arrives while the last is still speaking, each the sole survivor of a disaster (Job 1:14, Job 1:16, Job 1:17, Job 1:18)
- 'Fire of God' falls from heaven and consumes flocks and servants (Job 1:16)
- A great wind from the desert strikes the four corners of the house and it falls on the feasting children (Job 1:19)
- Mourner shaves his head and falls to the ground (Job 1:20)

**The second test; Job's wife; the three friends**
- Adversary's proverb 'skin for skin': a man gives all he has for his life (Job 2:4)
- The sufferer is struck with sore boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head (Job 2:7)
- The sufferer sits among the ashes scraping himself with a potsherd (Job 2:8)
- The sufferer's wife urges him 'Curse God and die' (Job 2:9)
- 'Shall we accept the good from God and not accept the evil?' (Job 2:10)
- Three friends from distant places arrange to come together to console the sufferer (Job 2:11)
- Mourners throw dust on their heads toward the sky (Job 2:12)
- Comforters sit on the ground with the sufferer seven days and nights without speaking (Job 2:13)

**Job curses the day of his birth**
- The night personified as announcing 'a man-child is conceived' (Job 3:3, Job 3:7)
- Professional cursers of the day, who are ready to rouse Leviathan, are invoked to curse a day (Job 3:8)
- The dawn imaged as having eyelids (Job 3:9)
- 'The thing I greatly feared has come upon me' (Job 3:25)

**Eliphaz's first speech, the night vision**
- The roaring lion's teeth are broken and its cubs scattered (image of the wicked's end) (Job 4:10, Job 4:11)
- Revelation comes as 'a silence, and a voice' (demamah vaqol) (Job 4:16)
- God puts no trust in his servants and charges his angels with folly (Job 4:18)
- Humans are dwellers in houses of clay founded in dust, crushed like a moth (Job 4:19, Job 4:20, Job 4:21)

**Eliphaz continues - seek God, accept discipline**
- 'To which of the holy ones will you turn?': appeal to heavenly intercessors (Job 5:1)
- The 'sons of Resheph' (sparks, or the plague god's brood) fly upward (Job 5:7)
- 'Man is born to trouble' (as sparks fly upward) (Job 5:6, Job 5:7)
- God catches the wise in their own craftiness (Job 5:12, Job 5:13)
- Suffering as divine discipline: happy the man whom God reproves (Job 5:17)
- The righteous will have a covenant with the stones of the field and peace with wild beasts (Job 5:22, Job 5:23)
- The righteous come to the grave in ripe age like a sheaf gathered in its season (Job 5:25, Job 5:26)

**Job's reply - the weight of grief and the treacherous wadi**
- Sufferer wishes his anguish weighed in scales: it would outweigh the sand of the seas (Job 6:2, Job 6:3)
- The arrows of Shaddai are in me; my spirit drinks their poison (Job 6:4)
- Proverb: does a wild ass bray over grass or an ox low over its fodder? (Job 6:5, Job 6:6)
- Sufferer prays that God would let loose his hand and cut him off (Job 6:8, Job 6:9)
- 'Is my strength that of stones, or my flesh bronze?' (Job 6:12)
- Faithless friends are like a wadi that swells with ice and snow but vanishes in heat, disappointing caravans of Tema and Sheba (Job 6:15, Job 6:16, Job 6:17, Job 6:18, Job 6:19, Job 6:20)

**Job - human life as hard service; 'Am I Sea or Dragon?'**
- The sufferer's flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; his skin cracks and festers (Job 7:5)
- Life's days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle (Job 7:6)
- 'What is man that you make so much of him?' turned into a complaint against divine scrutiny (cf. Ps 8) (Job 7:17, Job 7:18)
- God called 'watcher of humankind' (notser ha'adam) who targets the sufferer (Job 7:20)
- Sufferer says God will seek him in the morning and he will be no more (Job 7:8, Job 7:21)

**Bildad's first speech - the papyrus and the spider's web**
- The friend argues the sufferer's children died because of their own transgression (Job 8:4)
- 'Your beginning was small, but your latter end will greatly increase' (Job 8:7)
- Appeal to the wisdom of former generations, since 'we are but of yesterday' (Job 8:8, Job 8:9, Job 8:10)
- The godless are like papyrus or reed that withers without marsh water (Job 8:11, Job 8:12, Job 8:13)

**Job - cosmic power of God and the impossible lawsuit**
- 'How can a man be in the right with God? He could not answer one in a thousand' (Job 9:2, Job 9:3)
- God commands the sun not to rise and seals up the stars (Job 9:7)
- God treads on the back (bamot) of Sea (Job 9:8)
- God made the constellations Ash (Bear?), Kesil (Orion) and Kimah (Pleiades) and the chambers of the south (Job 9:9)
- God passes by the speaker and he does not see him (Job 9:11)
- The helpers of Rahab bow beneath God's wrath (Job 9:13)
- 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked'; God mocks the calamity of the innocent (Job 9:22, Job 9:23)
- The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; God covers the faces of its judges (Job 9:24)
- Life's days flee faster than a runner, reed boats, or a swooping eagle (Job 9:25, Job 9:26)
- Even if washed in snow and lye, God would plunge him into the pit so his clothes abhor him (Job 9:30, Job 9:31)
- Lament that there is no umpire (mokhiach) to lay his hand on both God and man (Job 9:32, Job 9:33)

**Job - 'Your hands fashioned me'; land of darkness**
- The sufferer reminds God that God's hands shaped him yet now destroy him (Job 10:3, Job 10:8)
- 'Have you eyes of flesh? Are your days like a mortal's days?' (Job 10:4, Job 10:5)
- God hunts the sufferer like a lion (Job 10:16)

**Zophar's first speech - the unsearchable depth of God**
- Secrets of wisdom are 'double' (manifold); God's depth cannot be found (Job 11:6, Job 11:7)
- God's extent is higher than heaven, deeper than Sheol, longer than earth, broader than sea (Job 11:8, Job 11:9)
- Proverb: a hollow man will get understanding when a wild ass's colt is born a man (Job 11:12)

**Job - ask the beasts; God's sovereign overturnings**
- Sarcasm: 'No doubt you are the people, and wisdom will die with you' (Job 12:2)
- The just and blameless man has become a laughingstock to his friends (Job 12:4, Job 12:5)
- Ask the beasts, birds, earth and fish and they will teach you that God's hand made this (Job 12:7, Job 12:8, Job 12:9)
- In God's hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of all humankind (Job 12:10)
- God withholds the waters and they dry up, sends them out and they overturn the earth (Job 12:15)
- God leads counselors, judges, kings and priests away stripped and makes fools of them (Job 12:17, Job 12:18, Job 12:19, Job 12:20, Job 12:21)
- God uncovers deep things out of darkness and brings deep shadow to light (Job 12:22)
- God makes nations great and destroys them, enlarges and disperses them (Job 12:23)
- God takes away the reason of leaders and makes them wander in a trackless waste (tohu), groping like drunkards (Job 12:24, Job 12:25)

**Job - worthless physicians; 'though he slay me'**
- The friends are plasterers of lies and worthless physicians (Job 13:4)
- 'If only you would keep silent; that would be your wisdom' (Job 13:5)
- Will you speak falsely for God and show him partiality? (Job 13:7, Job 13:8, Job 13:9, Job 13:10)
- The friends' maxims are proverbs of ashes, defenses of clay (Job 13:12)
- 'Though he slay me, I will hope in him' (qere) / 'I have no hope' (ketiv) (Job 13:15)
- Sufferer asks God for two things: withdraw your hand and do not terrify me; then call and I will answer (Job 13:20, Job 13:21, Job 13:22)
- Will you frighten a driven leaf and pursue dry straw? (Job 13:25)
- God writes bitter things against him and makes him inherit the sins of his youth (Job 13:26)
- Man wastes away like rot, like a garment eaten by moths (Job 13:28)

**Job - 'man born of woman'; the tree has hope**
- 'Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one' (Job 14:4)
- Man's days are determined; God has set limits he cannot pass (Job 14:5)
- The dead will not wake until the heavens are no more (Job 14:11, Job 14:12)
- Sufferer wishes God would hide him in Sheol until his anger passes and then remember him (Job 14:13)
- 'If a man dies, will he live again?': hope of a release (chalifah) after hard service (Job 14:14, Job 14:15)
- Transgressions sealed up in a bag (tseror) and iniquity plastered over (Job 14:16, Job 14:17)
- As waters wear away stones and mountains crumble, so God destroys human hope (Job 14:18, Job 14:19)
- The dead man does not know whether his sons are honored or brought low (Job 14:21, Job 14:22)

**Eliphaz's second speech - the first man and the fate of the wicked**
- Windy knowledge: filling one's belly with the east wind (Job 15:2)
- 'Were you the first man born? Were you brought forth before the hills?' (primal man of wisdom) (Job 15:7)
- God puts no trust in his holy ones, and the heavens are not clean in his sight (Job 15:15)
- Wisdom passed down from fathers to whom alone the land was given, with no stranger among them (Job 15:18, Job 15:19)
- The wicked man writhes in pain all his days, with dreadful sounds in his ears (Job 15:20, Job 15:21, Job 15:22, Job 15:23, Job 15:24)
- The wicked stretches his hand against God and charges at him with a thick-bossed shield (Job 15:25, Job 15:26)
- The wicked man's face is covered with fat and his loins with blubber (Job 15:27)
- The wicked are like a vine shedding unripe grapes and an olive casting its blossoms (Job 15:32, Job 15:33)
- They conceive trouble and bring forth iniquity; their womb prepares deceit (Job 15:35)

**Job - God the assailant; a witness in heaven**
- 'Miserable comforters (menachamei amal) are you all' (Job 16:2)
- God tears the sufferer in his wrath, gnashes his teeth and sharpens his eyes against him (Job 16:9, Job 16:10)
- God hands the sufferer over to the ungodly and the wicked (Job 16:11)
- God seizes the sufferer by the neck, shatters him and sets him up as his target for archers (Job 16:12, Job 16:13, Job 16:14)
- The mourner sews sackcloth on his skin and lays his horn in the dust (Job 16:15)
- 'Even now my witness is in heaven, my advocate on high' who will argue for man with God (Job 16:19, Job 16:20, Job 16:21)
- The dying man goes the way from which he will not return (Job 16:22)

**Job - a pledge with God; the grave as home**
- Sufferer asks God himself to stand surety (pledge) for him with God (Job 17:3)
- The sufferer is made a byword (mashal) of peoples, one in whose face they spit (tofet) (Job 17:6)
- Sufferer calls the Pit 'my father' and the worm 'my mother and sister', making his bed in Sheol's darkness (Job 17:13, Job 17:14)
- Will hope go down to the bars of Sheol, to rest together in the dust? (Job 17:15, Job 17:16)

**Bildad's second speech - the king of terrors**
- 'The firstborn of Death' (bekhor mavet) devours the wicked man's limbs (Job 18:13)
- The wicked is marched to 'the king of terrors' (melekh ballahot) (Job 18:14)
- Brimstone is scattered over the wicked man's habitation (Job 18:15)

**Job - abandoned by all; 'I know my redeemer lives'**
- 'These ten times you have reproached me' (Job 19:3)
- 'Know then that God has wronged me and closed his net about me' (Job 19:6)
- 'I cry out Violence! but I am not answered' (Job 19:7)
- God's troops come together, cast up siegeworks and encamp around the sufferer's tent (Job 19:12)
- Even young children despise the sufferer and speak against him (Job 19:18)
- 'Have pity on me, have pity on me, O my friends, for the hand of God has touched me' (Job 19:21, Job 19:22)
- Wish that his words were written in a book, engraved with an iron pen and lead in the rock forever (Job 19:23, Job 19:24)
- 'I know that my redeemer (go'el) lives, and at the last he will stand upon the dust' (Job 19:25)
- 'After my skin is stripped off, from my flesh I shall see God' with my own eyes, not a stranger's (Job 19:26, Job 19:27)
- The sufferer warns his accusers to fear the sword, so they may know there is a judgment (Job 19:29)

**Zophar's second speech - the portion of the wicked**
- The joy of the wicked is brief since humans were placed on earth (Job 20:4, Job 20:5)
- Though the wicked man's height reaches heaven, he perishes forever like his own dung (Job 20:6, Job 20:7)
- The wicked flies away like a dream and is chased off like a vision of the night (Job 20:8, Job 20:9)
- Evil held sweet under the tongue turns to the venom of asps in the belly (Job 20:12, Job 20:13, Job 20:14, Job 20:16)
- The wicked man swallows riches and God makes him vomit them up (Job 20:15, Job 20:18)
- God sends his fury into the wicked man's belly and rains it upon him as his food (Job 20:23)
- Fleeing an iron weapon, the wicked is pierced by a bronze bow; the glittering arrow comes out of his gall (Job 20:24, Job 20:25)
- A fire not blown by man consumes the wicked (Job 20:26)

**Job - why do the wicked prosper?**
- The wicked men's children dance to tambourine, lyre and pipe (Job 21:11, Job 21:12)
- Sufferer rejects the idea that God stores up the wicked man's punishment for his sons: let him feel it himself (Job 21:19, Job 21:20, Job 21:21)
- 'Have you not asked those who travel the roads?': testimony of wayfarers (Job 21:29)
- The wicked man is borne in honor to the grave and a watch is kept over his tomb; the clods are sweet to him (Job 21:30, Job 21:31, Job 21:32, Job 21:33)

**Eliphaz's third speech - Job accused of social crimes**
- God is in the height of heaven above the stars; the wicked think thick clouds hide him as he walks the vault (chug) of heaven (Job 22:12, Job 22:13, Job 22:14)
- The old way trodden by wicked men, snatched away before their time, their foundation poured out as a river (flood generation) (Job 22:15, Job 22:16)
- 'Receive instruction (torah) from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart' (Job 22:22)
- Lay your gold in the dust and Ophir gold among the stones of the wadi; Shaddai will be your gold (Job 22:24, Job 22:25)
- The penitent righteous will decree a thing and it will be established for him (Job 22:28)
- God delivers even the not-innocent through the cleanness of the righteous one's hands (Job 22:30)

**Job - 'Oh that I knew where I might find him'**
- 'Oh that I knew where I might find him, that I might come to his seat' and argue my case (Job 23:3, Job 23:4, Job 23:5, Job 23:6, Job 23:7)
- Going east, west, north and south, the seeker cannot find God (Job 23:8, Job 23:9)
- 'When he has tried me, I shall come out as gold' (Job 23:10)
- The righteous has treasured God's words more than his daily bread (Job 23:11, Job 23:12)

**Job - the oppressed poor and the rebels against light**
- 'Why are times (of judgment) not stored up by Shaddai, and why do those who know him not see his days?' (Job 24:1)
- The dispossessed poor go out like wild asses in the desert foraging, gleaning the wicked man's vineyard (Job 24:5, Job 24:6)
- The poor sleep naked without cover in the cold and hug the rock for shelter from mountain rain (Job 24:7, Job 24:8, Job 24:10)
- Workers carry sheaves while hungry and tread winepresses while thirsty (Job 24:10, Job 24:11)
- From the city the dying groan and the wounded cry out, yet God pays no heed to the wrong (Job 24:12)
- Murderer, adulterer and burglar are 'rebels against the light' who love darkness and fear dawn as deep shadow (Job 24:13, Job 24:14, Job 24:16, Job 24:17)
- The adulterer waits for twilight and disguises his face, saying 'no eye will see me' (Job 24:15)
- As drought and heat snatch snow-water, so Sheol snatches those who have sinned (Job 24:18, Job 24:19)
- The womb forgets him; the worm finds him sweet; wickedness is broken like a tree (Job 24:20)
- The wicked are exalted a little, then gone, cut off like the heads of grain (Job 24:24)

**Bildad's third speech - man a worm**
- Dominion and fear are with God, who makes peace in his high places (among the heavenly hosts) (Job 25:2)
- 'Is there any number to his troops?' (heavenly armies) (Job 25:3)
- Even the moon is not bright and the stars are not pure in God's sight (Job 25:5)
- Man is a maggot, the son of man a worm (Job 25:6)

**Job - the earth hung on nothing; Rahab smitten**
- The shades (Rephaim) tremble beneath the waters and their inhabitants (Job 26:5)
- God stretches out Zaphon (the north) over the void (tohu) (Job 26:7)
- God veils the face of his throne, spreading his cloud over it (Job 26:9)
- The pillars of heaven tremble and are astounded at God's rebuke (Job 26:11)
- By his wind (breath) the heavens are made fair (Job 26:13)
- God's hand pierced the fleeing serpent (nachash bariach) (Job 26:13)
- These are but the fringes of his ways, a whisper of a word; who can understand the thunder of his power? (Job 26:14)

**Job's oath of integrity; the wicked man's portion**
- The sufferer swears 'As God lives, who has taken away my right' (Job 27:2)
- 'Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me'; holding fast to righteousness (Job 27:3, Job 27:4, Job 27:5, Job 27:6)
- The wicked heaps up silver like dust and clothing like clay, but the righteous will wear it and the innocent divide the silver (Job 27:16, Job 27:17)
- The wicked man builds his house like a moth's (cocoon) or a watchman's booth (Job 27:18)
- The wicked man's widows do not weep for him (Job 27:15)

**The hymn to hidden wisdom**
- Miners sink shafts far from habitation, dangle on ropes, and search out ore in darkness to the farthest bound (Job 28:1, Job 28:2, Job 28:3, Job 28:4, Job 28:9, Job 28:10, Job 28:11)
- From the earth comes bread, but beneath it is turned up as by fire (Job 28:5)
- A hidden path no falcon knows, no kite's eye has seen, no proud beast or lion has trodden (Job 28:7, Job 28:8)
- 'But where shall wisdom be found, and where is the place of understanding?' (refrain) (Job 28:12, Job 28:20)
- The Deep (tehom) says 'It is not in me' and the Sea says 'It is not with me' (Job 28:14)
- Abaddon and Death say 'We have heard a rumor of it with our ears' (Job 28:22)
- Only God understands the way to wisdom; he saw and appraised it when he set weight for the wind and measure for the waters (Job 28:21, Job 28:23, Job 28:24, Job 28:27)

**Job remembers his former glory**
- The sufferer longs for the months of old when God watched over him and his lamp shone on his head (Job 29:2, Job 29:3)
- In his prime the friendship (sod) of God was over his tent and his children were around him (Job 29:4, Job 29:5)
- In prosperity his steps were washed in curds and the rock poured out streams of oil for him (Job 29:6)
- When he took his seat in the city square the young hid, the aged rose, princes fell silent with hand on mouth (Job 29:7, Job 29:8, Job 29:9, Job 29:10)
- 'I put on righteousness and it clothed me; my justice was a robe and a turban' (Job 29:14)
- 'I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame, a father to the poor' (Job 29:12, Job 29:13, Job 29:15, Job 29:16)
- The righteous man broke the jaws of the wicked and snatched the prey from his teeth (Job 29:17)
- 'I shall die with my nest and multiply my days like the chol' (sand, or the phoenix) (Job 29:18)
- The prosperous man's root spreads to the waters and dew lies all night on his branches (Job 29:19)
- His glory fresh and his bow ever renewed in his hand (Job 29:20)
- Hearers waited for his words as for rain and opened their mouths as for the spring rain (Job 29:21, Job 29:22, Job 29:23)
- He sat as chief and dwelt like a king among his troops, as one who comforts mourners (Job 29:25)

**Job's present humiliation**
- Now he is mocked by younger men whose fathers he would not have set with his sheepdogs (Job 30:1)
- Outcasts driven from society gnaw the dry ground, eat saltwort and broom roots, live in gullies and caves and bray among the bushes (Job 30:2, Job 30:3, Job 30:4, Job 30:5, Job 30:6, Job 30:7)
- 'Sons of fools, sons of no name', whipped out of the land (Job 30:8)
- The sufferer has become their taunt-song and byword; they spit in his face (Job 30:9, Job 30:10)
- Terrors are turned on him; his dignity is chased away like the wind and his safety passes like a cloud (Job 30:12, Job 30:13, Job 30:14, Job 30:15)
- God lifts the sufferer up on the wind, makes him ride it and dissolves him in the storm (Job 30:22)
- Death is 'the house appointed for all living' (Job 30:23)
- 'I hoped for good and evil came; I waited for light and darkness came' (Job 30:26)
- His skin turns black and falls from him, his bones burn with heat (Job 30:28, Job 30:30)

**Job's oath of innocence**
- Self-curse: may I sow and another eat, and my offspring be uprooted (Job 31:8)
- Self-curse for adultery: may my wife grind for another and others kneel over her (Job 31:9, Job 31:10)
- Adultery is a fire that consumes unto Abaddon and roots out all one's increase (Job 31:11, Job 31:12)
- Master respects his slaves' lawsuits because the one who made him in the womb made them too (Job 31:13, Job 31:14, Job 31:15)
- The poor were warmed with the fleece of the righteous man's sheep and blessed him (Job 31:19, Job 31:20)
- Self-curse: may my shoulder fall from its socket and my arm break from its bone (Job 31:21, Job 31:22)
- Disavowal of making gold one's hope or rejoicing in great wealth (Job 31:24, Job 31:25)
- The righteous did not rejoice at his enemy's ruin nor curse his life (Job 31:29, Job 31:30)
- 'No stranger lodged in the street; I opened my doors to the traveler' (Job 31:31, Job 31:32)
- Disavowal of concealing transgressions 'like Adam' (or like men), hiding iniquity in one's bosom (Job 31:33)
- 'Here is my mark (tav); let Shaddai answer me': the litigant signs his deposition (Job 31:35)
- The sufferer would wear his adversary's written indictment on his shoulder and bind it on as a crown (Job 31:35, Job 31:36, Job 31:37)
- Self-curse should his land cry out against him and its furrows weep for stolen produce or murdered owners (Job 31:38, Job 31:39)
- Editorial colophon: 'The words of Job are ended' (Job 31:40)

**Elihu is introduced and explains his intervention**
- A young bystander, angry at both the sufferer and his elders, breaks in after waiting out of deference (Job 32:2, Job 32:3, Job 32:4, Job 32:5, Job 32:6)
- Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, a fourth speaker unmentioned before (Job 32:2)
- Understanding comes from the spirit in man, the breath of Shaddai, not from age (Job 32:8, Job 32:9)
- The speaker is full of words like unvented wine about to burst new wineskins (Job 32:18, Job 32:19, Job 32:20)
- The speaker vows to show no partiality and to flatter no one, lest his maker take him away (Job 32:21, Job 32:22)

**Elihu - warning dreams and the interceding angel**
- 'The spirit of God has made me, and the breath of Shaddai gives me life' (Job 33:4)
- God speaks once, even twice, but people do not perceive it (Job 33:14)
- In dreams during deep sleep God opens people's ears and seals their warning, to turn them from pride and spare them from the Pit (Job 33:15, Job 33:16, Job 33:17, Job 33:18)
- The sick man's soul draws near the Pit and his life to the 'destroyers' (memitim, angels of death) (Job 33:22)
- An angel, an intercessor (malakh melits), one among a thousand, declares a man's uprightness and pleads for him (Job 33:23)
- 'Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom (kofer)' (Job 33:24)
- The healed man sings before men, 'I sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not requited to me' (Job 33:26, Job 33:27, Job 33:28)
- God does all these things two or three times with a man, to bring him back from the Pit to the light of life (Job 33:29, Job 33:30)

**Elihu - God cannot do wrong**
- If God gathered his spirit and breath to himself, all flesh would perish together and return to dust (Job 34:14, Job 34:15)
- God shows no partiality to princes, nor regards the rich above the poor, for all are the work of his hands (Job 34:18, Job 34:19)
- In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away, the mighty removed without a hand (Job 34:20)
- God shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place (Job 34:24, Job 34:25, Job 34:26)
- God keeps a godless man from ruling, that he not ensnare the people (Job 34:30)
- Elihu wishes that Job be tried to the end for answering like wicked men (Job 34:36)

**Elihu - human righteousness does not affect God**
- 'If you sin, what do you do to him? If you are righteous, what do you give him?' (Job 35:5, Job 35:6, Job 35:7, Job 35:8)
- God 'gives songs in the night' (Job 35:10)
- God teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens (Job 35:11)
- The oppressed cry out but are not answered because of the pride of evil men; God does not hear an empty cry (Job 35:9, Job 35:12, Job 35:13)

**Elihu on God's justice and suffering as discipline**
- Who has prescribed God's way, or who can say 'You have done wrong'? (Job 36:23)

**Elihu's hymn on rain, thunder, snow and the storm**
- The number of God's years cannot be searched out (Job 36:26)
- God draws up drops of water which distill as rain from his mist (evaporation and rainfall cycle) (Job 36:27-28)
- God's booth or canopy (sukkah) is made of thunderclouds and darkness (Job 36:29)
- Storm-wind comes out of a chamber (heder) and cold from the scattering winds (Job 37:9)
- Ice and frozen waters are produced by the breath of God (Job 37:10)
- God beat out the skies hard as a molten mirror of cast metal (Job 37:18)
- Golden splendor comes out of the north as God's awesome majesty (Job 37:22)
- In the winter storm God seals up every man's hand (stops human work) so all may know him (Job 37:7)

**God's first speech from the whirlwind - foundations of earth, sea, light and the heavens**
- The sea bursts out of a womb at creation and is swaddled in cloud and thick darkness (Job 38:8-9)
- God fixes a limit, bars and doors for the sea: 'Thus far you shall come and no farther' (Job 38:10-11)
- Dawn seizes the edges of the earth and shakes the wicked out of it (Job 38:12-15)
- The springs of the sea and the recesses of the deep (tehom) as unexplored regions (Job 38:16)
- Light and darkness each have a dwelling place and a road to it (Job 38:19-20, Job 38:24)
- Rhetorical question whether rain has a father and from whose womb ice and hoarfrost are born (Job 38:28-29)
- Lightnings sent by God report back 'Here we are' (Job 38:35)
- God has put wisdom in the tuhot and given understanding to the sekhvi (ibis/cock) (Job 38:36)
- The clouds are the water-skins (bottles) of heaven which God tips over (Job 38:37)

**God's first speech from the whirlwind - the wild animals**
- The wild ass, set free by God, laughs at the city's tumult and hears no driver's shout (Job 39:5-8)
- The wild ox (re'em) will not serve man, plow the furrow or spend the night at his crib (Job 39:9-12)
- The eagle nests on the crag; where the slain are, there it is, and its young drink blood (Job 39:27-30)

**Job's first reply and God's challenge to rule like God**
- God dares the human to put on majesty, pour out wrath and humble every proud one (Job 40:9-14)

**Behemoth**
- Behemoth, a colossal land beast made by God, eats grass like an ox, has bones of bronze and drinks a river (Job 40:15-18, Job 40:23)
- The monster is 'the first of the ways of God'; only its maker can approach it with his sword (Job 40:19)
- The mountains bring the monster their produce and all wild beasts play beside it (Job 40:20-22)

**Leviathan**
- No one has given to God first that he should repay; all under heaven is his (Job 41:3)
- The monster's back is rows of shields sealed so tight no air comes between (Job 41:5-9, Job 41:15-16)
- The monster's eyes are like the eyelids of dawn (Job 41:10)
- The monster makes the deep boil like a pot and leaves a shining wake; the abyss seems white-haired (Job 41:23-24)
- The monster is king over all the proud beasts; none on earth is its equal (Job 41:25-26)

**Job's final reply**
- I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you (Job 42:5)

**Epilogue - the friends rebuked, Job's intercession and restoration**
- God declares his anger at the sufferer's friends for not speaking rightly of him as his servant did (Job 42:7-8)
- A burnt offering of seven bulls and seven rams is commanded to avert divine anger (Job 42:8)
- The vindicated sufferer prays for the friends who wronged him and is restored as he prays (Job 42:8-10)
- Kin and acquaintances console him and each gives a qesitah (coin) and a gold ring (Job 42:11)
- The restored sufferer has again seven sons and three daughters (children not doubled) (Job 42:13)

**Psalm 2 - the nations rage; the king as God's son**
- God installs his king on Zion, his holy mountain (Ps 2:6)
- God gives the king the nations as inheritance and the ends of the earth as possession (Ps 2:8)
- The king will break the nations with a rod of iron and shatter them like a potter's vessel (Ps 2:9)
- Rulers told to serve God with trembling and 'kiss the son' (nashqu bar) (Ps 2:12)
- Happy are all who take refuge (hosim) in God (Ps 2:12)

**Psalm 3 - David fleeing Absalom**
- Individual lament: the speaker's foes are many and say God will not save him (Ps 3:2-3)
- God strikes the enemies on the cheek and breaks the teeth of the wicked (Ps 3:8)

**Psalm 4 - evening prayer of trust**
- Speak in your heart upon your bed and be still (Ps 4:5)
- God's gift of joy exceeds the joy of abundant grain and new wine (Ps 4:8)

**Psalm 5 - morning prayer against the deceitful**
- The petitioner prays and sets out his case in the morning and waits (Ps 5:4)
- The enemies' throat is an open grave; they flatter with their tongue (Ps 5:10)

**Psalm 6 - plea of the sick sufferer**
- The sufferer's bones are terrified or wasted in sickness (Ps 6:3)
- The speaker turns on his enemies: 'Depart from me, all evildoers, for God has heard' (Ps 6:9-11)

**Psalm 7 - Shiggayon concerning Cush the Benjaminite**
- The congregation of peoples surrounds God as he takes his seat on high to judge (Ps 7:8)
- God whets his sword and strings his bow, preparing deadly fiery arrows (Ps 7:13-14)
- The wicked conceives mischief, is pregnant with trouble and gives birth to falsehood (Ps 7:15)

**Psalm 8 - what is man**
- Refrain: 'How majestic is your name in all the earth!' (Ps 8:2, Ps 8:10)
- From the mouths of infants and sucklings God established strength against his foes (Ps 8:3)
- The heavens, moon and stars are the work of God's fingers (Ps 8:4)
- Man made a little lower than elohim and crowned with glory and honor (Ps 8:6)

**Psalm 9 - thanksgiving for God's judgment of the nations**
- God sits enthroned forever, his throne established for judgment of the world (Ps 9:5, Ps 9:8-9)
- God who avenges blood remembers and does not forget the cry of the afflicted (Ps 9:13, Ps 9:19)
- Let the nations know they are but men (enosh) (Ps 9:21)

**Psalm 10 - why do you stand far off**
- The wicked says in his heart that God has forgotten, hidden his face and will never see or require (Ps 10:11, Ps 10:13)
- YHWH is king forever and ever (Ps 10:16)

**Psalm 11 - in YHWH I take refuge**
- The righteous is told to flee like a bird to the mountain (Ps 11:1)
- The wicked bend the bow and fit the arrow to shoot the upright in darkness (Ps 11:2)
- If the foundations (shatot) are destroyed, what can the righteous do? (Ps 11:3)
- God's throne is in heaven; his eyes behold and his eyelids test humankind (Ps 11:4)
- The upright shall behold God's face (Ps 11:7)

**Psalm 12 - flattering lips and God's pure words**
- The godly man is gone; the faithful have vanished from among humankind (Ps 12:2)
- Flattering lips and a boastful tongue: 'With our tongue we prevail; who is lord over us?' (Ps 12:3-5)
- Embedded divine oracle: 'Because the poor are plundered, now I will arise,' says YHWH (Ps 12:6)

**Psalm 14 - the fool says there is no God**
- All have turned aside; there is none that does good, not even one (Ps 14:1, Ps 14:3)
- Evildoers devour God's people as they eat bread (Ps 14:4)

**Psalm 15 - who may dwell on your holy mountain**
- The righteous keeps his oath even to his own hurt and does not change (Ps 15:4)

**Psalm 16 - YHWH my portion; not abandoned to Sheol**
- Obscure reference to 'the holy ones who are in the land' and 'the mighty ones' (Ps 16:3)
- The speaker will not pour the blood libations of other gods' followers nor take their names on his lips (Ps 16:4)
- YHWH is my allotted portion and my cup; you hold my lot (Ps 16:5)
- The measuring lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; a goodly inheritance (Ps 16:6)
- My kidneys (inner self) instruct me in the night (Ps 16:7)
- I have set YHWH always before me; he is at my right hand (Ps 16:8)
- God will not abandon the speaker's soul to Sheol nor let his faithful one see the pit (Ps 16:10)

**Psalm 17 - prayer of the innocent; shadow of your wings**
- God has tried the speaker's heart, visited him by night and refined him and found nothing (Ps 17:3)
- The worldly men whose portion is in this life fill their belly and leave their surplus to their children (Ps 17:14)
- On waking the speaker will be satisfied with seeing God's form (temunah) (Ps 17:15)

**Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany**
- The king gives thanks for God's deliverance from all his enemies (song also in 2 Sam 22) (Ps 18:1, Ps 18:51)
- God makes darkness his hiding place and dark waters and clouds his canopy (Ps 18:12)
- At God's rebuke the channels of the sea are seen and the foundations of the world laid bare (Ps 18:16)
- 'Who is God except YHWH, and who is a rock besides our God?' (Ps 18:32)

**Psalm 19 - the heavens declare; the Torah is perfect**
- God has set a tent for the sun in the heavens (Ps 19:5)
- The Torah of YHWH is perfect, restoring the soul; its precepts make wise, gladden the heart, enlighten the eyes (Ps 19:8-10)
- 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before you, my Rock and Redeemer' (Ps 19:15)

**Psalm 20 - may YHWH answer you in the day of trouble**
- Congregation's prayer for the king's victory and acceptance of his offerings (Ps 20:2-6, Ps 20:10)
- May the name of the God of Jacob set you on high (Ps 20:2)

**Psalm 21 - the king rejoices in God's strength**
- God sets a crown of fine gold on the king's head (Ps 21:4)
- The king asked for life and God gave him length of days forever and ever (Ps 21:5)
- God makes the enemies like a fiery oven at the time of his presence; fire devours them (Ps 21:10)

**Psalm 22 - my God, my God, why have you forsaken me**
- 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' (Ps 22:2)
- God is holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel (Ps 22:4)
- Appeal to the ancestors: our fathers trusted in you and you delivered them (Ps 22:5-6)
- The sufferer calls himself a worm and not a man, scorned by people (Ps 22:7)
- Onlookers mock, wag their heads and say 'He trusted in YHWH; let him rescue him' (Ps 22:8-9)
- Dogs and a band of evildoers surround the sufferer (Ps 22:17, Ps 22:21)
- Crux 'like a lion my hands and my feet' (ka'ari), read by others as 'they pierced my hands and feet' (Ps 22:17)
- The emaciated sufferer can count all his bones while enemies stare (Ps 22:18)
- The enemies divide the sufferer's garments among them and cast lots for his clothing (Ps 22:19)
- Rescue from the lion's mouth and the horns of the wild oxen (Ps 22:22)
- The rescued speaker praises God in the great congregation and pays his vows before those who fear him (Ps 22:23, Ps 22:26-27)
- All the ends of the earth and families of the nations will remember and turn to YHWH and bow (Ps 22:28-29)
- Even those who go down to the dust (the dead) will bow before God (Ps 22:30)

**Psalm 23 - YHWH is my shepherd**
- Walking through the valley of deep darkness (tsalmavet) without fear, comforted by rod and staff (Ps 23:4)
- God sets a table before the speaker in the presence of enemies, anoints his head with oil, his cup overflows (Ps 23:5)
- Hope to dwell in the house of YHWH for length of days (Ps 23:6)

**Psalm 24 - lift up your heads, O gates**
- God founded the earth upon the seas and established it upon the rivers (Ps 24:2)
- Gates and everlasting doors are told to lift up their heads that the King of Glory may come in (Ps 24:7, Ps 24:9)
- Antiphonal question 'Who is the King of Glory?' answered 'YHWH strong and mighty, YHWH of hosts' (Ps 24:8, Ps 24:10)

**Psalm 25 - acrostic prayer for guidance and forgiveness**
- Plea for forgiveness of iniquity 'for your name's sake' (Ps 25:11)
- The secret counsel (sod) of YHWH is with those who fear him (Ps 25:14)

**Psalm 26 - judge me, for I have walked in integrity**
- Petitioner invites God to examine and test him and refine his kidneys and heart (Ps 26:2)
- 'I love the habitation of your house, the place where your glory dwells' (Ps 26:8)
- 'Do not gather my soul with sinners nor my life with men of blood' (Ps 26:9)

**Psalm 27 - YHWH is my light; one thing I ask**
- 'YHWH is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?' (Ps 27:1)
- One thing I ask: to dwell in the house of YHWH all my days and behold his beauty (Ps 27:4)
- 'My heart says to you: Seek my face. Your face, YHWH, I seek' (Ps 27:8)
- Though my father and mother forsake me, YHWH will take me in (Ps 27:10)

**Psalm 28 - to you, my Rock, I call**
- Petitioner lifts his hands toward the inner sanctuary (devir) (Ps 28:2)
- Prayer that God requite the wicked according to the work of their hands (Ps 28:4)

**Psalm 29 - the voice of YHWH over the waters**
- The sons of gods (benei elim) are summoned to ascribe glory and strength to YHWH (Ps 29:1-2)
- The voice of YHWH thunders over the many waters (Ps 29:3)
- The voice of YHWH hews out flames of fire (lightning) (Ps 29:7)
- The voice of YHWH shakes the wilderness of Kadesh (Ps 29:8)
- The voice of YHWH makes the hinds writhe in labor and strips the forests bare (Ps 29:9)
- In his temple all say 'Glory!' (Ps 29:9)

**Psalm 30 - song at the dedication of the house**
- Superscription: a song for the dedication of the house (hanukkat ha-bayit) (Ps 30:1)
- What profit is there in my blood if I go down to the pit? Will the dust praise you? (Ps 30:10)

**Psalm 31 - into your hand I commit my spirit**
- 'Into your hand I commit my spirit (beyadkha afqid ruhi)' (Ps 31:6)
- 'My times are in your hand' (Ps 31:16)
- How great is the goodness God has stored up for those who fear him (Ps 31:20)
- In panic the speaker said 'I am cut off from before your eyes' but God heard (Ps 31:23)

**Psalm 32 - happy is he whose sin is forgiven**
- Keeping silent about sin wastes the body like summer drought; confessing brings forgiveness (Ps 32:3-5)
- When the great waters overflow they will not reach the faithful one (Ps 32:6)
- Be not like horse or mule without understanding, curbed with bit and bridle (Ps 32:9)

**Psalm 33 - by the word of YHWH the heavens were made**
- By the word of YHWH the heavens were made and all their host by the breath of his mouth (Ps 33:6)
- God gathers the waters of the sea as a heap and puts the deeps in storehouses (Ps 33:7)
- God frustrates the counsel of the nations; his own counsel stands forever (Ps 33:10-11)
- No king is saved by a great army; the horse is a vain hope for victory (Ps 33:16-17)

**Psalm 34 - acrostic when David feigned madness before Abimelech**
- Superscription: David feigned madness (changed his sense) before Abimelech, who drove him out (Ps 34:1)
- The angel of YHWH encamps around those who fear him and delivers them (Ps 34:8)
- 'Taste and see that YHWH is good' (Ps 34:9)
- Young lions suffer want and hunger, but those who seek YHWH lack no good thing (Ps 34:11)
- Who desires life? Keep your tongue from evil, turn from evil, do good, seek peace and pursue it (Ps 34:13-15)
- YHWH is near the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit (Ps 34:19)

**Psalm 35 - contend, YHWH, with those who contend with me**
- Petitioner asks God to take shield, buckler and spear and fight those who fight him (Ps 35:1-3)
- The angel of YHWH drives the enemies like chaff and pursues them on a slippery dark path (Ps 35:5-6)
- 'My prayer returns upon my bosom' (Ps 35:13)

**Psalm 36 - transgression's oracle and the fountain of life**
- Transgression speaks an oracle (ne'um pesha) to the wicked in his heart; no fear of God before his eyes (Ps 36:2)
- The wicked devises mischief upon his bed (Ps 36:5)
- God's steadfast love reaches to the heavens, his faithfulness to the clouds; his righteousness like the mountains of God, his judgments the great deep (Ps 36:6-7)
- God saves both man and beast (Ps 36:7)
- God's guests feast on the fatness of his house and drink from the river of his delights (adanekha, cf. Eden) (Ps 36:9)

**Psalm 37 - acrostic: do not fret; the meek shall inherit the land**
- Do not fret over evildoers nor envy the wrongdoers; they wither quickly like grass (Ps 37:1, Ps 37:7-8)
- 'I have been young and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken nor his seed begging bread' (Ps 37:25)
- The wicked spreads like a luxuriant native tree, then passes away and cannot be found (Ps 37:35-36)
- There is a future (aharit) for the man of peace; the future of the wicked is cut off (Ps 37:37-38)

**Psalm 38 - the sick penitent abandoned by friends**
- Superscription 'to bring to remembrance' (lehazkir), linked to the memorial offering (Ps 38:1)
- God's arrows have sunk into the sufferer and his hand pressed down on him (Ps 38:3)
- Because of his sin the sufferer's wounds stink and fester; no soundness in his flesh (Ps 38:4-9)

**Psalm 39 - my days a handbreadth; I am a sojourner**
- Superscription names the Levitical singer Jeduthun (Ps 39:1)
- The speaker muzzles his mouth in silence until his heart grows hot and the fire burns, and he speaks (Ps 39:2-4)
- Prayer to know one's end and the measure of one's days: life a few handbreadths, every man a breath (hevel) (Ps 39:5-6, Ps 39:12)
- Man walks about as a mere image (tselem) and heaps up riches not knowing who will gather them (Ps 39:7)
- God's rebuke consumes a man's beauty like a moth (Ps 39:12)
- 'I am a stranger (ger) with you, a sojourner (toshav) like all my fathers' (Ps 39:13)
- Plea that God look away so the speaker may smile again before he departs and is no more (Ps 39:14)

**Psalm 40 - out of the miry pit; sacrifice you did not desire**
- Happy is he who does not turn to the proud (rehavim) and those who go astray after lies (Ps 40:5)
- God does not desire sacrifice and offering, burnt offering and sin offering, but obedience and a hearing ear (Ps 40:7)
- 'Ears you have dug (karita) for me' (Ps 40:7)
- 'Behold I come; in the scroll of the book it is written of me' (Ps 40:8)
- God's Torah is within the speaker's inward parts (me'ai) (Ps 40:9)
- The speaker proclaims God's righteousness in the great congregation and does not restrain his lips (Ps 40:10-11)
- The speaker's iniquities are more than the hairs of his head (Ps 40:13)

**Psalm 41 - happy who considers the poor; the friend who lifted his heel**
- Happy is he who considers the poor; God sustains him on his sickbed (Ps 41:2-4)
- Enemies say 'When will he die and his name perish?' and whisper together at the sickbed (Ps 41:6-9)
- Even my close friend whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me (Ps 41:10)
- Doxology 'Blessed be YHWH God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting, amen and amen' closes a book of the Psalter (Ps 41:14)

**Psalm 42 - as the hart longs for water brooks**
- As a hart longs for streams of water, so my soul longs for God (Ps 42:2)
- My soul thirsts for the living God: when shall I come and appear before (see) the face of God? (Ps 42:3)
- The exile remembers leading the festal throng in procession to the house of God (Ps 42:5)
- Remembered from the land of the Jordan, the Hermons and Mount Mizar (Ps 42:7)

**Psalm 43 - send out your light and your truth**
- Prayer that God send his light and truth to lead the speaker to his holy mountain and altar (Ps 43:3-4)

**Psalm 44 - national lament; why do you sleep, O Lord**
- Our fathers told us what you did in their days: you dispossessed nations and planted them (Ps 44:2-3)
- God sold his people for no price and scattered them among the nations (Ps 44:12-13)
- God made his people a byword (mashal) among nations, a shaking of the head among peoples (Ps 44:14-15)
- All this came upon us though we have not forgotten you nor been false to your covenant (Ps 44:18-22)
- God crushed them in the place of jackals (tannim) and covered them with deep darkness (Ps 44:20)
- For your sake we are killed all day long, counted as sheep for slaughter (Ps 44:23)

**Psalm 45 - royal wedding song**
- The poet's tongue is the pen of a ready scribe (Ps 45:2)
- The king is fairer than the sons of men; grace is poured on his lips (Ps 45:3)
- The king girds his sword on his thigh and rides victoriously for truth and righteousness; his arrows are sharp (Ps 45:4-6)
- The king's garments are fragrant with myrrh, aloes and cassia; music from ivory palaces (Ps 45:9)
- The queen (shegal) stands at the king's right hand in gold of Ophir (Ps 45:10)
- The foreign bride is told: 'Hear, daughter, forget your people and your father's house' (Ps 45:11-12)
- The daughter of Tyre and the rich of the people seek the bride's favor with gifts (Ps 45:13)
- The princess is all glorious within, in gold-woven robes, led to the king with her virgin companions (Ps 45:14-16)
- Instead of your fathers shall be your sons; you will make them princes in all the earth (Ps 45:17)

**Psalm 46 - God is our refuge; a river makes glad the city**
- God is our refuge: we will not fear though the earth changes and mountains topple into the heart of the sea (Ps 46:2-4)
- Refrain: 'YHWH of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold' (Ps 46:8, Ps 46:12)
- 'Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations' (Ps 46:11)

**Psalm 47 - God has gone up with a shout**
- All peoples are called to clap their hands and shout to God with joyful cries (Ps 47:2)
- YHWH Elyon is a great king over all the earth (Ps 47:3, Ps 47:8)
- God has gone up with a shout (teru'ah), YHWH with the sound of the shofar (Ps 47:6)
- God reigns (malakh) over the nations; God sits on his holy throne (Ps 47:9)
- The nobles of the peoples are gathered as the people of the God of Abraham (Ps 47:10)

**Psalm 48 - Mount Zion, the recesses of the north**
- Assembled kings see the city, are astounded, panic and flee, seized by trembling like a woman in labor (Ps 48:5-7)
- Walk around Zion, count her towers, consider her ramparts, to tell the next generation (Ps 48:13-14)
- God will guide us 'unto death' (al-mut), an obscure closing phrase (Ps 48:15)

**Psalm 49 - no man can ransom his brother**
- The poet opens his riddle (hidah) and proverb (mashal) to the lyre, addressing all peoples rich and poor (Ps 49:2-5)
- Refrain: man in his pomp does not abide; he is like the beasts that perish (Ps 49:13, Ps 49:21)
- Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol; Death shepherds them (Ps 49:15)
- God will ransom my soul from the hand of Sheol, for he will take me (yiqqaheni) (Ps 49:16)
- When he dies he takes nothing with him; his glory does not go down after him (Ps 49:17-18)

**Psalm 50 - God summons heaven and earth; do I eat the flesh of bulls**
- Superscription ascribes the psalm to Asaph (Ps 50:1)
- Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth (hofia) (Ps 50:2)
- Our God comes and is not silent; fire devours before him and a tempest rages around him (Ps 50:3)
- God's faithful ones made a covenant with him by sacrifice (Ps 50:5)
- Every beast of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills, and the ziz of the field (Ps 50:10-11)
- 'I kept silent, and you thought I was one like yourself' (Ps 50:21)

**Psalm 51, David's confession after Bathsheba (Miserere)**
- Prayer that God create a pure heart and renew a steadfast spirit within (Ps 51:12)
- Prayer 'Lord, open my lips and my mouth will declare your praise' (Ps 51:17)

**Psalm 55, wings of a dove and the treacherous friend**
- Wish for wings like a dove to fly away and rest in the wilderness (Ps 55:7-9)
- Cast your burden on YHWH and he will sustain you (Ps 55:23)
- Men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days (Ps 55:24)

**Psalm 57, in the shadow of your wings (in the cave)**
- Speaker lies down among lions, i.e. ravenous enemies (Ps 57:5)

**Psalm 58, do you gods truly speak justice?**
- The wicked go astray from the womb, speaking lies from birth (Ps 58:4)
- Prayer that God break the teeth in the mouths of the young lions (enemies) (Ps 58:7)
- Curse that the wicked dissolve like a snail or be like a stillborn that never sees the sun (Ps 58:9)
- The righteous will bathe their feet in the blood of the wicked when vengeance comes (Ps 58:11)

**Psalm 59, when Saul sent men to watch David's house**
- Enemies prowl around the city at evening howling like dogs (Ps 59:7, Ps 59:15-16)

**Psalm 61, from the end of the earth I call; long life for the king**
- Petitioner calls to God from the end of the earth (Ps 61:3)

**Psalm 64, the hidden archers shot by God's arrow**
- The wicked plot in secret saying 'Who will see us?' (Ps 64:6)

**Psalm 65, praise in Zion; God crowns the year with bounty**
- The 'channel of God' (peleg elohim) is full of water to water the earth (Ps 65:10)
- God's wagon-tracks or paths drip with fatness (abundance) as he passes (Ps 65:12)

**Psalm 66, come and see; the sea turned to dry land**
- Invitation 'Come and see the works of God' / 'Come and hear, I will tell' (Ps 66:5, Ps 66:16)
- If one cherishes iniquity in his heart, God will not hear his prayer (Ps 66:18)

**Psalm 68, let God arise; the rider of the clouds marches from Sinai to his mountain**
- A great host of women heralds (mevasserot) announces the victory and women divide the spoil (Ps 68:12-13)
- A dove's wings covered with silver and its pinions with yellow-green gold (Ps 68:14)
- When Shaddai scattered kings, it snowed on Zalmon (Ps 68:15)
- Many-peaked mountains (Bashan) look with envy at the mountain God chose for his dwelling (Ps 68:16-17)
- God's chariots are myriads, thousands upon thousands; the Lord among them as at Sinai (Ps 68:18)
- God ascends on high leading captives and receiving gifts among men (Ps 68:19)
- God says he will bring back (enemies or people) from Bashan and from the depths of the sea (Ps 68:23)
- God rebukes the beast of the reeds (Egypt as hippopotamus or crocodile) and the herd of bulls (Ps 68:31)
- Envoys come from Egypt and Cush (Ethiopia) stretches out its hands to God (Ps 68:32)
- God rides in the heaven of heavens of old and utters his mighty voice (Ps 68:34)

**Psalm 69, the waters have come up to my neck; gall and vinegar**
- Prayer that the pit (be'er) not close its mouth over the sufferer (Ps 69:16)
- Enemies give the sufferer poison (rosh, gall) for food and vinegar to drink (Ps 69:22)
- Curse that the enemies' table become a trap and snare (Ps 69:23)
- Curse that the enemy's encampment be desolate with no one dwelling in his tents (Ps 69:26)

**Psalm 71, do not cast me off in old age**
- Prayer not to be cast off or forsaken in old age when strength fails (Ps 71:9, Ps 71:18)
- God will revive the speaker and bring him up again from the depths (tehomot) of the earth (Ps 71:20)

**Psalm 72, for Solomon; the ideal king; end of Book II**
- The king descends like rain on mown grass, showers watering the earth (Ps 72:6)
- The king's dominion extends from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth (Ps 72:8)
- The king's name will flourish (yinnon) as long as the sun; later read as a name of the Messiah (Ps 72:17)
- All nations will bless themselves by the king and call him happy (Ps 72:17)
- Colophon: 'The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended' (Ps 72:20)

**Psalm 73, Asaph on the prosperity of the wicked; afterward you will take me to glory**
- The wicked have no pangs at death; their bodies are sound and fat (Ps 73:4-5)
- Arrogant set their mouths against heaven while their tongue struts through the earth (Ps 73:9)
- Speaker's perplexity is resolved only when he enters the sanctuary and perceives the end of the wicked (Ps 73:16-17)
- The wicked vanish like a dream on waking; God despises their image (tselem) (Ps 73:19-20)
- God will take (laqah) the righteous afterward into glory, beyond death (Ps 73:24)

**Psalm 74, the burned sanctuary and God who crushed the heads of Leviathan**
- Enemies burn all the meeting places (mo'adei El) of God in the land (Ps 74:8)
- Complaint that there are no signs and no prophet anymore, none who knows how long (Ps 74:9)
- God is king from of old (qedem), working salvation in the midst of the earth (Ps 74:12)
- God split or shattered the sea (Yam) by his might (Ps 74:13)
- God split open springs and torrents and dried up ever-flowing rivers (Ps 74:15)
- Prayer not to hand the soul of God's turtledove to the wild beast (Ps 74:19)
- Call 'Arise, O God, plead your own cause' (Ps 74:22)

**Psalm 75, I set firm its pillars; the cup in YHWH's hand**
- God declares 'When I seize the appointed time (mo'ed) I will judge with equity' (Ps 75:3)

**Psalm 76, God's lair in Salem where he broke the flaming arrows**
- Jerusalem called Salem (Shalem) (Ps 76:3)
- At God's rebuke the enemy warriors sleep their last sleep, horse and chariot stunned (Ps 76:6-7)

**Psalm 77, the waters saw you; your footprints unseen**
- Sufferer lies awake at night with hands outstretched, refusing to be comforted (Ps 77:3-5)
- Speaker asks whether God has forgotten to be gracious or shut up his compassion forever (Ps 77:8-11)
- The waters saw God and writhed; the deeps trembled (Ps 77:17)
- God's way was through the sea, his path in mighty waters, yet his footprints were not seen (Ps 77:20)

**Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David**
- The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis) (Ps 78:12, Ps 78:43)
- Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels (Ps 78:25)
- God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return (Ps 78:39)
- God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath (Ps 78:49)
- In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament (Ps 78:63-64)
- The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine (Ps 78:65)
- God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids) (Ps 78:66)
- God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion (Ps 78:67-68)
- God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever (Ps 78:69)
- God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people (Ps 78:70-72)

**Psalm 79, the nations have come into your inheritance**
- Bodies of God's servants left as food for birds and beasts; blood poured like water around Jerusalem with none to bury (Ps 79:2-3)
- Prayer that God not remember against us the iniquities of former generations (Ps 79:8)

**Psalm 80, Shepherd of Israel enthroned on the cherubim; the vine from Egypt**
- God fed his people the bread of tears and gave them tears to drink by the measure (Ps 80:6)
- The boar from the forest ravages God's vine (Ps 80:14)
- Prayer for 'the man of your right hand, the son of man you made strong' (Ps 80:18)

**Psalm 81, blow the shofar at the new moon; O that my people would listen**
- Speaker hears 'a language I did not know' at the exodus (Ps 81:6)
- God removed the burden from Israel's shoulder and freed his hands from the basket (Ps 81:7)
- God answered from the hiding place of thunder (Ps 81:8)
- God says 'Open your mouth wide and I will fill it' (Ps 81:11)
- God gives his disobedient people over to the stubbornness of their hearts (Ps 81:13)
- God laments 'O that my people would listen to me' and promises victory if they do (Ps 81:14-16)
- God would feed his people the finest wheat and satisfy them with honey from the rock (Ps 81:17)

**Psalm 82, God judges in the council of El; you are gods, yet you shall die**
- Because of injustice all the foundations of the earth totter (Ps 82:5)
- God sentences the gods (sons of Elyon) to die like mortals and fall like princes (Ps 82:6-7)
- God is called to arise and judge the earth, for he inherits all the nations (Ps 82:8)

**Psalm 83, the ten-nation conspiracy; do to them as to Midian**
- A list of named nations conspires to wipe out Israel's name (Ps 83:6-9)
- Prayer that God do to the enemies as he did to Midian, Sisera and Jabin, Oreb and Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna (Ps 83:10-12)
- Nations will know that 'you alone, whose name is YHWH, are Most High over all the earth' (Ps 83:19)

**Psalm 84, how lovely are your dwellings; the sparrow at the altar**
- Soul longs and faints for the courts of YHWH, the living God (Ps 84:2-3)
- YHWH God is called a sun (shemesh) and a shield (Ps 84:12)

**Psalm 85, steadfast love and truth meet; righteousness and peace kiss**
- Personified virtues meet: steadfast love and truth meet, righteousness and peace kiss (Ps 85:11)
- Truth sprouts from the earth and righteousness looks down from heaven (Ps 85:12)
- Righteousness walks before God as herald and prepares the way for his steps (Ps 85:14)

**Psalm 86, a prayer of David; there is none like you among the gods**
- Prayer 'Unite my heart to fear your name' (Ps 86:11)
- God delivered the speaker's soul from the lowest Sheol (she'ol tahtiyyah) (Ps 86:13)

**Psalm 87, Zion mother of nations; this one was born there**
- Zion's foundation is on the holy mountains; God loves its gates more than all Jacob's dwellings (Ps 87:1-2)
- Zion is the birthplace of foreign peoples; of each nation it will be said 'this one was born there' (Ps 87:4-5)
- Singers and dancers declare 'All my springs are in you' (Zion as source of waters) (Ps 87:7)

**Psalm 88, Heman's lament from the pit; darkness my companion**
- Speaker's life draws near Sheol; he is counted among those who go down to the pit (Ps 88:4-8)
- The dead are 'free' (hofshi) among the slain, forgotten by God and cut off from his hand (Ps 88:6)
- God has removed the sufferer's friends and made him an abomination to them (Ps 88:9, Ps 88:19)
- Abaddon, 'destruction', as a name of the underworld (Ps 88:12)
- The underworld is darkness, the land of forgetfulness (erets neshiyyah) (Ps 88:13)
- Lament ends without any turn to praise or hope (darkness my only companion) (Ps 88:19)

**Psalm 89, Ethan's hymn of the divine council, Rahab crushed, and the broken Davidic covenant**
- God created Zaphon (north) and Yamin (south); Tabor and Hermon sing his name (Ps 89:13)
- God sets the king's hand on the Sea and his right hand on the Rivers (Ps 89:26)
- The king calls God 'my father' and God makes him firstborn, highest of the kings of earth (Ps 89:27-28)
- The dynasty will be established like the moon, a faithful witness in the sky (Ps 89:38)
- If the king's sons sin they will be punished with the rod, but God's love will not be withdrawn (Ps 89:31-35)

**Psalm 90, prayer of Moses; a thousand years as yesterday**
- A psalm is ascribed to Moses, 'the man of God' (Ps 90:1)
- Before the mountains were born and the earth was brought forth in labor, God existed from everlasting (Ps 90:2)
- God turns mortals back to dust (dakka), saying 'Return, sons of Adam' (Ps 90:3)
- The span of human life is seventy years, or eighty with strength (Ps 90:10)
- Prayer 'Teach us to number our days that we may gain a heart of wisdom' (Ps 90:12)

**Psalm 91, shelter of the Most High; the noonday demon; angels bear you up**
- God delivers from the snare of the fowler (Ps 91:3)
- A thousand fall at your side, ten thousand at your right, but it does not come near you (Ps 91:7)
- The protected one treads on lion and cobra, young lion and dragon (tannin) (Ps 91:13)

**Psalm 92, a song for the Sabbath day; the righteous flourish like the palm**
- Psalm designated for the Sabbath day (Ps 92:1)
- The wicked sprout like grass only to be destroyed forever (Ps 92:8)
- The righteous still bear fruit in old age, full of sap and green (Ps 92:15)

**Psalm 93, YHWH reigns; the floods have lifted up their voice**
- The floods (neharot) lift up their roaring, but YHWH on high is mightier than the breakers of the sea (Ps 93:3-4)

**Psalm 94, God of vengeance; he who planted the ear**
- Invocation 'God of vengeance, shine forth; rise up, judge of the earth' (Ps 94:1-2)

**Psalm 95, come let us sing; today if you hear his voice (Venite)**
- The depths of the earth and the peaks of the mountains are in God's hand; the sea is his, for he made it (Ps 95:4-5)
