- Warning 'Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as at Meribah and Massah' (Ps 95:7-8)
- God swore in anger that the wilderness generation would not enter his rest (menuhah) (Ps 95:11)

**Psalm 96, sing a new song; the gods of the nations are nothings**
- Formula 'Ascribe (havu) to YHWH glory and strength', addressed to divine beings or the families of peoples (Ps 96:7-8)
- Bow down to YHWH in the splendor of holiness (hadrat qodesh) (Ps 96:9)

**Psalm 97, YHWH reigns; clouds and thick darkness; all gods bow down**
- Light is sown for the righteous and joy for the upright in heart (Ps 97:11)

**Psalm 98, new song; rivers clap their hands**
- Trumpets and shofar sounded before the King YHWH (Ps 98:6)

**Psalm 99, YHWH reigns enthroned on cherubim; holy is he**
- Threefold refrain 'Holy is he' (qadosh hu) (Ps 99:3, Ps 99:5, Ps 99:9)
- God was a forgiving God to them yet avenged their misdeeds (Ps 99:8)

**Psalm 100, a psalm for the thanksgiving offering**
- A Masoretic written/read (ketiv/qere) variant changes the sense of a key phrase (Ps 100:3)

**Psalm 101, the king's vow of integrity**
- The king vows to walk blamelessly, banish slanderers and the proud, and purge the wicked from God's city (mirror for princes) (Ps 101:2-8)

**Psalm 102, prayer of the afflicted; the heavens wear out like a garment**
- Heading 'A prayer of the afflicted when he faints and pours out his complaint before YHWH' (Ps 102:1)
- Sufferer's days vanish like smoke and his bones burn like a hearth (Ps 102:4-6)
- God's servants cherish Zion's stones and pity her dust; it is the appointed time to favor her (Ps 102:14-15)
- This is written for a later generation, a people yet to be created, to praise Yah (Ps 102:19)
- God looks down from his holy height to hear the prisoner's groan and free those doomed to die (Ps 102:20-21)
- Prayer 'Do not take me away in the midst of my days' (Ps 102:24-25)

**Psalm 103, bless YHWH, O my soul; youth renewed like the eagle**
- God renews one's youth like the eagle's (Ps 103:5)
- God knows our frame (yetser) and remembers that we are dust (Ps 103:14)
- When the wind passes over man he is gone and his place knows him no more (Ps 103:16)

**Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten)**
- Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures (Ps 104:1-35)
- At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place (Ps 104:7-8)
- God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him (Ps 104:15)
- Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks (Ps 104:12, Ps 104:16-18)
- Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with (Ps 104:26)
- God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth (Ps 104:30)
- God rejoices in his works (Ps 104:31)

**Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus**
- The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation (Ps 105:12-13)
- God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed') (Ps 105:14-15)
- God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave (Ps 105:17)
- Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true (Ps 105:18-19)
- Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom (Ps 105:22)
- God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them (Ps 105:24-25)
- At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble) (Ps 105:37)
- Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it (Ps 105:38)
- God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert (Ps 105:41)

**Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile**
- God grants the people's wilderness craving but sends wasting (razon) into their souls (Ps 106:14-15)
- Israel ate 'sacrifices of the dead' (zivhei metim) at Baal-peor (Ps 106:28)
- Phinehas's intervention 'was reckoned to him as righteousness for all generations' (Ps 106:31)
- Provoked at Meribah, Moses spoke rashly with his lips and suffered because of the people (Ps 106:32-33)
- God caused the exiles to be pitied by all their captors (Ps 106:46)

**Psalm 107, thanksgiving of the redeemed (wanderers, prisoners, sick, seafarers)**
- Thanksgiving liturgy for four groups rescued by God: desert wanderers, prisoners, the sick, seafarers (Ps 107:4-9, Ps 107:10-16, Ps 107:17-22, Ps 107:23-32)
- Refrain: 'Let them thank YHWH for his steadfast love and his wonders to the sons of man' (Ps 107:8, Ps 107:15, Ps 107:21, Ps 107:31)
- Prisoners sit in darkness and the shadow of death (tsalmavet), bound in affliction and iron (Ps 107:10, Ps 107:14)
- God shatters doors of bronze and cuts through bars of iron (Ps 107:16)
- God 'sent his word and healed them', the word acting as an agent (Ps 107:20)
- Storm-tossed sailors reel and stagger like drunkards and all their skill is swallowed up (Ps 107:27)

**Psalm 109, curses on the accuser**
- Curse: let a wicked man be appointed over him and an accuser (satan) stand at his right hand in judgment (Ps 109:6)
- Curse: 'let his days be few; let another take his office (pequddah)' (Ps 109:8)
- Curse that the enemy's children be fatherless beggars, his wife a widow and his name blotted out in the next generation (Ps 109:9-13)
- Curse that the iniquity of his fathers be remembered and his mother's sin not be blotted out (Ps 109:14)
- The wicked loved cursing; let it clothe him like a garment, soak into him like water and like oil into his bones (Ps 109:17-19)
- Sufferer is shaken off like a locust (Ps 109:23)
- God stands at the right hand of the needy to save him from those who judge him (Ps 109:31)

**Psalm 110, the lord at God's right hand, priest after Melchizedek**
- God sends forth the king's mighty scepter from Zion: 'rule in the midst of your enemies' (Ps 110:2)
- The king's youth (or begetting) is like dew from the womb of the dawn (mishhar) (Ps 110:3)
- God swears irrevocably: 'You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek' (Ps 110:4)
- The victorious king drinks from the brook by the way and therefore lifts his head (Ps 110:7)

**Psalm 111, acrostic hymn on God's works**
- God 'made a memorial (zekher) for his wonders' and gave food to those who fear him (Ps 111:4-5)

**Psalm 112, acrostic on the blessed God-fearer**
- Light rises in the darkness for the upright (Ps 112:4)
- The righteous man lends graciously and scatters gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever and his horn is exalted (Ps 112:5, Ps 112:9)

**Psalm 113, God on high raises the poor and the barren**
- God settles the barren woman in her home as a joyful mother of children (Ps 113:9)

**Psalm 114, when Israel went out of Egypt the sea fled**
- Egypt called 'a people of strange speech' (am lo'ez) (Ps 114:1)
- At the exodus the sea saw and fled and the Jordan turned back; the poet taunts them 'What ails you?' (Ps 114:3, Ps 114:5)
- Mountains skip like rams and hills like lambs before God (Ps 114:4, Ps 114:6)
- The earth is commanded to tremble/writhe (huli) before the Lord, the God of Jacob (Ps 114:7)
- God turned the rock into a pool of water and flint into a spring (Ps 114:8)

**Psalm 115, not to us, polemic against idols**
- 'Not to us, YHWH, not to us, but to your name give glory' (Ps 115:1)
- 'The heavens are YHWH's heavens, but the earth he has given to the sons of man' (Ps 115:16)

**Psalm 116, thanksgiving after rescue from death**
- Speaker bids his soul return to its rest because God has dealt bountifully (Ps 116:7)
- In alarm the speaker said 'All men are liars' (Ps 116:11)
- The delivered speaker lifts 'the cup of salvations' and calls on YHWH's name (Ps 116:13)
- 'Precious (costly) in the eyes of YHWH is the death of his faithful ones' (Ps 116:15)

**Psalm 117, all nations praise**
- The shortest psalm (and shortest chapter of the Bible), two verses (Ps 117:1-2)

**Psalm 118, festal thanksgiving, the rejected stone and hosanna**
- All nations surround the speaker like bees, but in YHWH's name he cuts them off (Ps 118:10-12)
- 'I shall not die but live and declare the works of Yah'; chastened but not given over to death (Ps 118:17-18)
- 'Open to me the gates of righteousness'; 'this is the gate of YHWH, the righteous enter through it' (Ps 118:19-20)
- 'The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner' (Ps 118:22-23)
- Cry 'Ana YHWH hoshi'a na' (Please, YHWH, save now = hosanna) (Ps 118:25)
- 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of YHWH; we bless you from the house of YHWH' (Ps 118:26)
- 'Bind the festal offering with cords up to the horns of the altar' (Ps 118:27)

**Psalm 119, stanzas alef to he**
- Torah praised under a fixed set of synonyms (torah, edut, piqqudim, huqqim, mitsvot, mishpatim, davar, imrah) (Ps 119:1-8)
- Prayer 'Open my eyes that I may behold wonders out of your Torah' (Ps 119:18)
- Speaker calls himself a stranger (ger) on the earth (Ps 119:19)

**Psalm 119, stanzas vav to kaf**
- 'It is good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn your statutes' (Ps 119:67, Ps 119:71)
- The arrogant have hearts gross (unfeeling) as fat (Ps 119:70)
- Speaker has become like a wineskin in the smoke (shriveled) (Ps 119:83)

**Psalm 119, stanzas lamed to ayin**
- 'Forever, YHWH, your word stands firm in the heavens'; all things are his servants (Ps 119:89-91)
- Through Torah the speaker is wiser than his enemies, all his teachers and the elders (Ps 119:98-100)
- 'It is time to act for YHWH; they have made void your Torah' (later read as license for emergency measures) (Ps 119:126)

**Psalm 119, stanzas pe to tav**
- Speaker's eyes shed streams of water because people do not keep God's Torah (Ps 119:136)
- Speaker rises before dawn (neshef) and anticipates the night watches to cry out and meditate (Ps 119:147-148)
- 'Seven times a day I praise you' (Ps 119:164)
- Speaker strays like a lost sheep and asks God to seek his servant (Ps 119:176)

**Psalm 120, song of ascents against the lying tongue**
- Punishment of the lying tongue: a warrior's sharp arrows with glowing coals of broom (rotem) (Ps 120:4)
- Speaker laments sojourning in Meshech and dwelling among the tents of Kedar, among haters of peace (Ps 120:5-6)
- 'I am for peace, but when I speak they are for war' (Ps 120:7)

**Psalm 121, the keeper who does not sleep**
- 'I lift my eyes to the mountains: from where will my help come?' (Ps 121:1)
- God will guard your going out and your coming in from now and forever (Ps 121:7-8)

**Psalm 122, pilgrim's song, pray for the peace of Jerusalem**
- Jerusalem built 'as a city that is joined together' (shehubberah lah yahdav) (Ps 122:3)
- In Jerusalem stand thrones for judgment, thrones of the house of David (Ps 122:5)
- 'Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: may those who love you prosper' (Ps 122:6-8)

**Psalm 124, had it not been YHWH, the snare is broken**
- Refrain 'If it had not been YHWH who was for us, let Israel say...' (Ps 124:1-2)
- Enemies would have swallowed us alive (Ps 124:3)
- Raging (arrogant) waters and torrent would have swept over our soul (Ps 124:4-5)

**Psalm 125, those who trust are like Mount Zion**
- Those who trust in YHWH are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved (Ps 125:1)
- As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so YHWH surrounds his people (Ps 125:2)
- The scepter of wickedness will not rest on the allotment of the righteous, lest they stretch their hands to wrong (Ps 125:3)

**Psalm 126, restoration of Zion, sowing in tears**
- When YHWH restored Zion's fortunes, 'we were like dreamers', mouths filled with laughter (Ps 126:1-2)
- Prayer to restore fortunes like streams (wadis) in the Negev (Ps 126:4)
- Those who sow in tears will reap with songs of joy, returning with sheaves (Ps 126:5-6)

**Psalm 127, unless YHWH builds the house; sons as arrows**
- 'Unless YHWH builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless YHWH guards the city, the watchman wakes in vain' (Ps 127:1)
- Sons of one's youth will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies in the gate (Ps 127:5)

**Psalm 128, blessing of the God-fearer's household**
- Blessing: may you see your children's children (Ps 128:6)

**Psalm 129, plowed upon the back, grass on the housetops**
- Israel: 'Plowers plowed upon my back; they made long their furrows' (Ps 129:3)
- YHWH the righteous cuts the cords (avot) of the wicked (Ps 129:4)
- Enemies become like grass on the housetops that withers before it is pulled, filling no reaper's hand (Ps 129:6-7)
- Passers-by will not say 'The blessing of YHWH be upon you; we bless you in YHWH's name' (harvest greeting) (Ps 129:8)

**Psalm 130, out of the depths**
- 'Out of the depths (ma'amaqqim) I cry to you, YHWH' (De profundis) (Ps 130:1)
- 'If you, Yah, kept account of iniquities, Lord, who could stand?' Forgiveness is with God that he may be feared (Ps 130:3-4)
- The soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen for the morning (Ps 130:6)
- God will redeem Israel from all its iniquities; with him is plentiful redemption (Ps 130:7-8)

**Psalm 131, a soul like a weaned child**
- Humble speaker does not occupy himself with great things or wonders too high for him (Ps 131:1)
- Speaker has calmed his soul like a weaned child with its mother (Ps 131:2)

**Psalm 132, David's vow, the ark and the oath to David**
- 'We heard of it in Ephrathah, we found it in the fields of Ya'ar' (the ark at Kiriath-jearim) (Ps 132:6)
- God's priests are clothed in righteousness or salvation and his faithful shout for joy (Ps 132:9, Ps 132:16)
- God swore to David: 'of the fruit of your body I will set on your throne', conditional on the sons keeping the covenant (Ps 132:11-12)
- God chose Zion and desired it for his seat: 'This is my resting place forever' (Ps 132:13-14)
- In Zion God will make a horn sprout for David and has prepared a lamp for his anointed; his crown (nezer) will blossom (Ps 132:17-18)

**Psalm 133, brothers dwelling together, oil and dew**
- Unity likened to the fine oil on the head running down the beard of Aaron onto the collar of his robes (Ps 133:2)
- Like the dew of Hermon descending on the mountains of Zion, where God commanded blessing, life forever (Ps 133:3)

**Psalm 134, servants who stand by night in the house of YHWH**
- Servants of YHWH who stand in the house of YHWH by night are called to bless him (Ps 134:1)

**Psalm 135, hymn on God's power, election and the idols**
- Whatever YHWH pleases he does, in heaven, on earth, in the seas and all the deeps (Ps 135:6)

**Psalm 136, litany 'for his steadfast love is forever' (Great Hallel)**
- God spread out (roqa') the earth upon the waters (Ps 136:6)
- God cut the Sea of Reeds into parts (gozer ... lig'zarim) and led Israel through its midst (Ps 136:13-15)
- God gives bread to all flesh (Ps 136:25)

**Psalm 137, by the rivers of Babylon**
- Exiles sit and weep by the rivers of Babylon remembering Zion (Ps 137:1)
- Exiles hang their lyres on the willows (poplars) in Babylon (Ps 137:2)
- Captors demand 'Sing us one of the songs of Zion'; 'How can we sing YHWH's song on foreign soil?' (Ps 137:3-4)
- Self-curse: 'If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget; let my tongue cleave to my palate' (Ps 137:5-6)
- Edomites cried on Jerusalem's day 'Raze it, raze it, to its foundation' (Ps 137:7)
- Blessing on whoever seizes the enemy's (Babylon's) little ones and dashes them against the rock (Ps 137:9)

**Psalm 138, thanksgiving before the gods**
- Speaker sings God's praise 'before the gods' (neged elohim) (Ps 138:1)
- All kings of the earth will praise YHWH when they hear the words of his mouth (Ps 138:4-5)

**Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo**
- 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken (Ps 139:1-6)
- 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me' (Ps 139:9-10)
- Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike (Ps 139:11-12)
- 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred' (Ps 139:19-22)

**Psalm 140, deliverance from violent men with serpent tongues**
- God covered the speaker's head in the day of battle (weapons) (Ps 140:8)
- Curse: let burning coals fall on them, let them be cast into fire and into pits never to rise (Ps 140:11)

**Psalm 141, prayer as incense, guard on the mouth**
- 'Let my prayer be set before you as incense, the lifting of my hands as the evening offering' (Ps 141:2)
- Let the righteous strike and rebuke me in kindness; it is oil on the head (Ps 141:5)
- Their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock (cliff) (Ps 141:6)
- 'As when one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol' (Ps 141:7)

**Psalm 142, David's prayer in the cave**
- Speaker looks to the right and sees no one who knows him; no refuge, no one cares for his soul (Ps 142:5)
- Prayer 'Bring my soul out of prison (masger) that I may praise your name' (Ps 142:8)

**Psalm 143, enter not into judgment**
- 'Enter not into judgment with your servant, for no living being is righteous before you' (Ps 143:2)
- The enemy made the speaker dwell in darkness like those long dead (metei olam) (Ps 143:3)
- 'Your good spirit will lead me on level ground'; prayer to be taught to do God's will (Ps 143:10)

**Psalm 144, royal prayer for victory and prosperity**
- God trains the speaker's hands for battle and fingers for war (Ps 144:1)
- 'Bow your heavens, YHWH, and come down; touch the mountains that they smoke' (Ps 144:5)
- Refrain: deliver me from many waters, from the hand of foreigners whose mouth speaks falsehood and whose right hand is a right hand of lies (Ps 144:7-8, Ps 144:11)
- Sons like well-grown plants, daughters like corner pillars carved for a palace (temple) (Ps 144:12)
- 'Happy the people for whom it is so; happy the people whose God is YHWH' after a picture of prosperity (Ps 144:13-15)

**Psalm 145, acrostic praise of the King (Ashrei)**
- YHWH upholds all who fall and raises up all who are bowed down (Ps 145:14)

**Psalm 146, do not trust in princes**
- When man's breath departs he returns to his earth; on that day his plans perish (Ps 146:4)
- YHWH frees the prisoners, opens the eyes of the blind, raises the bowed, loves the righteous (Ps 146:7-8)

**Psalm 147, builder of Jerusalem, counter of stars, giver of snow**
- God heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds (Ps 147:3)
- God counts the number of the stars and calls them all by name (Ps 147:4)
- God takes no delight in the strength of the horse nor pleasure in the legs of a man (Ps 147:10-11)
- God's word runs swiftly; he gives snow like wool, scatters frost like ashes, casts his ice like crumbs; his word melts them (Ps 147:15-18)
- God declared his statutes to Jacob; he has not done so for any other nation (Ps 147:19-20)

**Psalm 148, praise from heaven and earth**
- Sun, moon and shining stars are summoned to praise God (Ps 148:3)
- 'The waters above the heavens' are summoned to praise (Ps 148:4)
- God commanded and they were created; he established them forever with a decree (hoq) that will not pass (Ps 148:5-6)
- Sea monsters (tanninim) and all deeps are summoned to praise God from the earth (Ps 148:7)
- Fire and hail, snow and smoke, stormy wind fulfilling his word (Ps 148:8)
- Kings and peoples, princes and judges, young men and maidens, old and young together praise God (Ps 148:11-12)

**Psalm 149, new song, dance, and the sword of the faithful**
- The faithful exult in glory and sing for joy on their beds (Ps 149:5)
- The faithful have God's praises in their throats and a two-edged sword in their hand to take vengeance on the nations (Ps 149:6-7)

**Psalm 150, everything that breathes, praise Yah**
- God praised in his sanctuary and in the firmament (raqia) of his might (Ps 150:1)
- Catalogue of instruments for praise: shofar, harp, lyre, timbrel, dance, strings, pipe (ugav), sounding and clashing cymbals (Ps 150:3-5)

**Proverbs 1:1-7, title and purpose; fear of YHWH**
- Prologue states a book's purpose: to give the simple shrewdness, the young knowledge, and the wise more learning, to understand proverbs and riddles (Prov 1:2-6)

**Proverbs 1:8-19, warning against the gang of robbers**
- Parental teaching or wisdom is a graceful garland for the head and necklace for the neck (Prov 1:9)
- Sinners entice the youth to ambush the innocent, share one purse and fill houses with plunder (Prov 1:10-14)
- 'In vain is the net spread in the sight of any bird'; the ambushers lie in wait for their own blood (Prov 1:17-18)

**Proverbs 1:20-33, Lady Wisdom's speech in the streets**
- Wisdom promises to pour out her spirit (ruhi) and make her words known to those who turn (Prov 1:23)
- Rejected Wisdom will laugh at the scorners' calamity and mock when terror comes like a storm (Prov 1:26-27)
- When disaster comes they will call on Wisdom and she will not answer; they will seek her and not find her (Prov 1:28)
- The fools eat the fruit of their own way and are sated with their own devices (Prov 1:31)

**Proverbs 2, seeking wisdom as treasure; the strange woman**
- Seek wisdom like silver and search for her as for hidden treasures (Prov 2:4)
- YHWH gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding (Prov 2:6)
- The strange woman forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God (Prov 2:17)
- None who go to the strange woman return or regain the paths of life (Prov 2:19)
- The upright will inhabit the land and the wicked be cut off and uprooted from it (Prov 2:21-22)

**Proverbs 3:1-12, trust in YHWH, firstfruits, the Lord's discipline**
- 'Trust in YHWH with all your heart and do not lean on your own understanding'; do not be wise in your own eyes (Prov 3:5-7)
- Honor YHWH with your wealth and firstfruits; your barns will be filled and vats burst with new wine (Prov 3:9-10)

**Proverbs 3:13-35, wisdom a tree of life; creation by wisdom; neighbor ethics**
- Wisdom holds length of days in her right hand, riches and honor in her left (Prov 3:16)
- Wisdom 'is a tree of life to those who grasp her' (Prov 3:18)
- By God's knowledge the deeps were split open and the clouds drip dew (Prov 3:20)
- Do not withhold good from its owner or tell your neighbor 'Go and come back tomorrow' when you have it (Prov 3:27-30)

**Proverbs 4, a father's father's teaching; the two paths**
- Teacher recalls being a tender only son taught by his own father, passing the teaching to his sons (Prov 4:1-4)
- 'The beginning of wisdom: acquire wisdom; with all you have acquired, acquire understanding' (Prov 4:5-7)
- Love Wisdom and embrace her; she will exalt you and set on your head a garland and a crown of glory (Prov 4:6-9)
- The wicked cannot sleep unless they do evil; they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence (Prov 4:16-17)
- The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn growing brighter to full day; the way of the wicked is deep darkness (Prov 4:18-19)
- Guard your heart above all, for from it are the issues (springs) of life (Prov 4:23)

**Proverbs 5, the strange woman versus the wife of one's youth**
- Drink water from your own cistern and running water from your own well; let your springs not be scattered abroad (marital fidelity) (Prov 5:15-18)
- The wife of one's youth as a loving doe and graceful mountain goat whose breasts satisfy always (Prov 5:18-19)
- A man's ways are before YHWH's eyes and he weighs (levels) all his paths (Prov 5:21)
- The wicked is caught by his own iniquities and held fast by the cords of his sin (Prov 5:22-23)

**Proverbs 6:1-19, surety, the ant, the scoundrel, six things God hates**
- Warning against striking hands as surety for a neighbor or stranger; free yourself without sleep like a gazelle from the hunter (Prov 6:1-5)
- The worthless man (adam beliyya'al) winks with his eyes, scrapes with his feet and points with his fingers, sowing discord (Prov 6:12-14)

**Proverbs 6:20-35, commandment as lamp; adultery as fire in the bosom**
- When you walk it will lead you, when you lie down it will watch over you, when you wake it will talk with you (Prov 6:22)
- 'The commandment is a lamp and the teaching (torah) is light; reproofs of discipline are the way of life' (Prov 6:23)
- Can a man carry fire in his bosom and his clothes not burn, or walk on coals and his feet not be scorched? So is adultery (Prov 6:27-29)
- A starving thief is not despised, yet when caught he repays sevenfold, giving all the wealth of his house (Prov 6:30-31)
- The jealous husband shows no mercy on the day of vengeance and will accept no ransom (kofer) or bribe for adultery (Prov 6:34-35)

**Proverbs 7, the youth and the seductress at twilight**
- Keep my teaching as the pupil (ishon) of your eye (Prov 7:2)
- 'Say to Wisdom: You are my sister; call Understanding your kinswoman' (Prov 7:4)
- The teacher looks out through the lattice of his window and sees a youth lacking sense (Prov 7:6-7)
- At twilight, in the pupil of the night, a woman in harlot's garb lurks at every corner, seizes and kisses the youth (Prov 7:8-13)
- The seductress says she has offered peace offerings and paid her vows today (so has sacrificial meat) (Prov 7:14)
- Her bed spread with colored Egyptian linen and perfumed with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon (Prov 7:16-17)
- 'The man is not at home; he took a bag of silver and will come home at the full moon (keseh)' (Prov 7:19-20)
- The youth follows her like an ox to the slaughter, a fool to the stocks, a bird hastening into the snare, till an arrow pierces his liver (Prov 7:22-23)
- Many are the slain she has cast down; numerous all her killed (Prov 7:26)

**Proverbs 8:1-21, Wisdom's public speech, by me kings reign**
- 'I, Wisdom, dwell with prudence and find knowledge and discretion; counsel and strength are mine' (Prov 8:12, Prov 8:14)
- 'By me kings reign and rulers decree justice; by me princes rule' (Prov 8:15-16)
- 'I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me' (Prov 8:17)
- Wisdom walks in paths of justice to endow those who love her with substance and fill their treasuries (Prov 8:18-21)

**Proverbs 8:22-31, Wisdom before and at creation**
- 'YHWH acquired (or created, qanani) me as the beginning (reshit) of his way, the first of his works of old' (Prov 8:22)
- Wisdom was 'installed' or 'woven' (nissakhti) from eternity, from the beginning, before the earth (Prov 8:23)
- Wisdom was present when God established the heavens, drew the circle on the deep, fixed the clouds, set the sea's limit and marked earth's foundations (Prov 8:27-29)
- Wisdom was beside God as an 'amon' (master craftsman, or nursling/child) (Prov 8:30)
- Wisdom was God's delight day by day, playing (mesaheqet) before him always, playing in his inhabited world (Prov 8:30-31)
- Wisdom's delight was with the sons of man (benei adam) (Prov 8:31)

**Proverbs 8:32-36, happy who watch at Wisdom's doors**
- Happy the man who watches daily at Wisdom's doors, waiting at the posts (mezuzot) of her entrance (Prov 8:34)
- 'Whoever finds me finds life and obtains favor from YHWH; all who hate me love death' (Prov 8:35-36)

**Lady Wisdom's house and banquet versus Woman Folly**
- Personified Wisdom slaughters meat, mixes wine, sets a table and invites guests to eat her bread and drink her wine (Prov 9:2, Prov 9:5)
- Wisdom (or Folly) calls out from the heights of the city to passers-by (Prov 9:3, Prov 9:14)
- Wisdom and Folly issue the same invitation: 'Whoever is simple, turn in here' (Prov 9:4, Prov 9:16)
- Do not reprove a scoffer, he will hate you; reprove a wise man and he will love you (Prov 9:7, Prov 9:8)
- Folly personified as a loud, ignorant woman who sits at her door luring passers-by (Prov 9:13, Prov 9:14)
- 'Stolen waters are sweet and bread eaten in secret is pleasant' (Prov 9:17)
- The guests of the seductive woman are already among the dead in the depths of Sheol (Prov 9:18)

**First Solomonic collection begins (antithetic sayings on righteous and wicked)**
- The prudent son gathers in summer; the shameful son sleeps in harvest (Prov 10:5)
- The memory of the righteous is for blessing but the name of the wicked rots (Prov 10:7)
- When the storm passes the wicked is no more, but the righteous is an everlasting foundation (Prov 10:25)
- Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes is the sluggard to those who send him (Prov 10:26)
- The righteous will never be moved and will dwell in the land; the wicked will not inhabit it (Prov 10:30)

**Sayings on honest scales, generosity and the fate of the wicked**
- A city exults at the prosperity of the righteous and shouts for joy when the wicked perish (Prov 11:10, Prov 11:11)
- Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman without discretion (Prov 11:22)
- The people curse him who withholds grain, but blessing is on the head of him who sells it (Prov 11:26)
- He who troubles his household will inherit the wind (Prov 11:29)
- The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life and the wise man 'takes souls' (wins people) (Prov 11:30)
- If the righteous is repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner (Prov 11:31)

**Sayings on the capable wife, speech and diligence**
- The righteous knows the soul (needs) of his beast; the mercies of the wicked are cruel (Prov 12:10)
- The way of the fool is right in his own eyes, but the wise listens to counsel (Prov 12:15)
- Anxiety in a man's heart weighs it down, but a good word makes it glad (Prov 12:25)

**Sayings on discipline, hope and companions**
- One pretends to be rich and has nothing; another pretends to be poor and has great wealth (Prov 13:7)
- Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life (Prov 13:12)
- He who walks with the wise becomes wise; the companion of fools suffers harm (Prov 13:20)

**Sayings on the wise woman, the poor and the king**
- Where there are no oxen the crib is clean, but much produce comes by the strength of the ox (Prov 14:4)
- The simple believes every word; the prudent considers his steps (Prov 14:15)
- A king's glory is in a multitude of people; without people a prince is ruined (Prov 14:28)
- A tranquil heart is life to the body, but jealousy is rot in the bones (Prov 14:30)
- Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a reproach to peoples (Prov 14:34)
- The king's favor is toward a wise servant; his wrath toward one who shames (Prov 14:35)

**Sayings on the soft answer, prayer and better-than proverbs**
- Better a dinner of vegetables where love is than a fattened ox with hatred (Prov 15:17)
- The way of the sluggard is like a hedge of thorns; the path of the upright is a highway (Prov 15:19)
- The path of life leads upward for the wise, to turn away from Sheol below (Prov 15:24)
- YHWH tears down the house of the proud but sets fast the widow's boundary (Prov 15:25)

**YHWH sayings and royal sayings (man plans, God disposes)**
- Roll (commit) your works to YHWH and your plans will be established (Prov 16:3)
- YHWH has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of evil (Prov 16:4)
- By loyalty and faithfulness (hesed we-emet) iniquity is atoned for (Prov 16:6)
- When a man's ways please YHWH he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him (Prov 16:7)
- Divination (qesem) is on the lips of the king; his mouth does not err in judgment (Prov 16:10)
- The wrath of a king is messengers of death, but a wise man will pacify it (Prov 16:14)
- Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones (Prov 16:24)
- The worker's appetite works for him, for his mouth urges him on (Prov 16:26)
- The worthless man (ish beliyya'al) digs up evil and on his lips is a scorching fire (Prov 16:27)
- A whisperer separates close friends (Prov 16:28)
- The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from YHWH (Prov 16:33)

**Sayings on strife, bribes, friends and the silent fool**
- A wise slave will rule over a shameful son and share the inheritance among the brothers (Prov 17:2)
- The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but YHWH tests hearts (Prov 17:3)
- Grandchildren are the crown of the aged and fathers the glory of their sons (Prov 17:6)
- A bribe is a stone of charm (even hen) in the eyes of its owner; wherever he turns he prospers (Prov 17:8)
- A rebuke goes deeper into a discerning man than a hundred blows into a fool (Prov 17:10)
- Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly (Prov 17:12)
- Whoever returns evil for good, evil will not depart from his house (Prov 17:13)
- The beginning of strife is like letting out water; quit before the quarrel breaks out (Prov 17:14)
- Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom when he has no heart? (Prov 17:16)
- A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones (Prov 17:22)
- Wisdom is before the face of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth (Prov 17:24)
- Even a fool who keeps silent is counted wise (Prov 17:28)

**Sayings on the tongue, the strong tower and the lot**
- The words of a man's mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom a gushing stream (Prov 18:4)
- The name of YHWH is a strong tower; the righteous runs into it and is safe (Prov 18:10)
- He who answers before he hears, it is folly and shame to him (Prov 18:13)
- A man's gift makes room for him and brings him before the great (Prov 18:16)
- The first to plead his case seems right until the other comes and examines him (Prov 18:17)
- The lot puts an end to quarrels and decides between the mighty (Prov 18:18)
- An offended brother is harder to win than a strong city; quarrels are like the bars of a citadel (Prov 18:19)
- Death and life are in the hand of the tongue (Prov 18:21)
- There is a friend who sticks closer than a brother (Prov 18:24)

**Sayings on the poor, the king's wrath and the sluggard**
- A man's folly ruins his way and his heart rages against YHWH (Prov 19:3)
- A son who ruins his father and chases away his mother brings shame (Prov 19:26)

**Sayings on wine, the king's throne and the lamp of YHWH**
- Wine is a mocker and strong drink a brawler; whoever is led astray by it is not wise (Prov 20:1)
- Counsel in a man's heart is deep water; a man of understanding draws it out (Prov 20:5)
- Many proclaim their loyalty, but a faithful man who can find? (Prov 20:6)
- 'Bad, bad,' says the buyer, then goes away and boasts (Prov 20:14)
- Bread gained by deceit is sweet, but afterwards the mouth is filled with gravel (Prov 20:17)
- He who curses father or mother, his lamp is put out in the pupil of darkness (Prov 20:20)
- It is a snare to say rashly 'Holy!' and only afterwards to reflect on vows (Prov 20:25)
- A wise king winnows the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them (Prov 20:26)
- The breath (nishmat) of man is the lamp of YHWH, searching all the inner chambers of the belly (Prov 20:27)
- The glory of young men is their strength, the splendor of the old their grey hair (Prov 20:29)
- Bruising wounds scour away evil; blows cleanse the inner chambers (Prov 20:30)

**Sayings on the king's heart, justice over sacrifice, and the contentious wife**
- Treasures gained by a lying tongue are a driven vapor (hevel), a snare of death (Prov 21:6)
- Whoever stops his ear at the cry of the poor will himself cry and not be answered (Prov 21:13)
- A gift in secret averts anger and a bribe in the bosom strong wrath (Prov 21:14)
- He who loves pleasure, wine and oil will not grow rich (Prov 21:17)
- The desire of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to work (Prov 21:25)
- The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but victory belongs to YHWH; no wisdom avails against him (Prov 21:30, Prov 21:31)

**End of the first Solomonic collection (good name, training a child)**
- Train up a child according to his way; when he is old he will not depart from it (Prov 22:6)

**Words of the Wise begin (Amenemope parallel), introduction and first sayings**
- The teacher says he has written 'thirty' (shalishim) sayings of counsel and knowledge (Prov 22:20)
- If you have nothing to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you? (Prov 22:27)
- A man skillful in his work will stand before kings, not before obscure men (Prov 22:29)

**Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel), dining with rulers, winged riches, the orphan's field**
- Do not eat the bread of the stingy host who says 'eat and drink' while his heart is not with you; you will vomit up the morsel (Prov 23:6, Prov 23:7, Prov 23:8)
- Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words (Prov 23:9)
- Beat the child with the rod and you will save his soul from Sheol; he will not die (Prov 23:13, Prov 23:14)

**Father's appeal, the harlot as pit, and the drunkard's woes**
- The speaker's kidneys (kilyot) exult at the son's upright words (Prov 23:16)
- Buy truth and do not sell it, wisdom, instruction and understanding (Prov 23:23)
- 'My son, give me your heart and let your eyes keep my ways' (Prov 23:26)
- The harlot lies in wait like a robber and multiplies the faithless among men (Prov 23:28)
- Riddle-catalogue: 'Who has woe? who has sorrow? who has strife, wounds without cause, red eyes?' Those who linger over wine (Prov 23:29, Prov 23:30)
- The drunkard is like one lying in the heart of the sea or on top of a mast; struck and feeling nothing, he seeks more on waking (Prov 23:33, Prov 23:34, Prov 23:35)

**End of the Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel section)**
- By wisdom a house is built and by knowledge its rooms are filled with precious riches (Prov 24:3, Prov 24:4)
- Wisdom is too high (like corals, ra'mot) for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the gate (Prov 24:7)
- He who plans evil will be called a master of schemes (ba'al mezimmot) (Prov 24:8)
- Rescue those being taken to death; do not say 'we did not know', for the weigher of hearts knows (Prov 24:11, Prov 24:12)
- Eat honey, my son, for it is good; so is wisdom sweet to your soul (Prov 24:13, Prov 24:14)
- The righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked stumble in calamity (Prov 24:15, Prov 24:16)
- Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, lest YHWH see it, be displeased and turn his anger from him (Prov 24:17, Prov 24:18)

**'These also are of the wise': judgment, retaliation and the sluggard's field**
- He who gives an honest answer kisses the lips (Prov 24:26)
- Prepare your work outside and get your field ready; afterwards build your house (Prov 24:27)
- The wise man passes the field of the sluggard, overgrown with thorns and nettles, its stone wall broken down, and draws a lesson (Prov 24:30, Prov 24:31, Prov 24:32)

**Proverbs of Solomon copied by Hezekiah's men (king, speech, enemies)**
- Proverbs of Solomon 'copied out' (he'tiqu) by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah (Prov 25:1)
- It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out (Prov 25:2)
- As heaven for height and earth for depth, so the heart of kings is unsearchable (Prov 25:3)
- Do not put yourself forward before the king; better to be told 'Come up here' than to be humbled before a noble (Prov 25:6, Prov 25:7)
- A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver (Prov 25:11)
- Like the cold of snow in harvest time is a faithful messenger to those who send him (Prov 25:13)
- Clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give (Prov 25:14)
- With patience a ruler is persuaded and a soft tongue breaks a bone (Prov 25:15)
- If you find honey eat only enough, lest you be sated and vomit it (Prov 25:16, Prov 25:27)
- Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house, lest he grow weary of you and hate you (Prov 25:17)
- Trust in a faithless man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth or a slipping foot (Prov 25:19)
- Singing songs to a heavy heart is like taking off a garment on a cold day or vinegar on soda (neter) (Prov 25:20)
- The north wind brings forth rain, and a backbiting tongue angry looks (Prov 25:23)
- Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a far country (Prov 25:25)
- A righteous man who gives way before the wicked is like a muddied spring or polluted fountain (Prov 25:26)
- A man without self-restraint is like a city broken into, without walls (Prov 25:28)

**Sayings on the fool (the 'book of fools')**
- Like snow in summer or rain at harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool (Prov 26:1, Prov 26:8)
- He who sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks violence (Prov 26:6)
- A proverb (mashal) in the mouth of fools is like lame legs or a thorn in a drunkard's hand (Prov 26:7, Prov 26:9)
- Giving honor to a fool is like binding a stone in a sling (Prov 26:8)

**Sayings on the sluggard, the meddler, the whisperer and the hypocrite**
- As a door turns on its hinge, so does the sluggard on his bed (Prov 26:14)
- The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven who answer with discretion (Prov 26:16)
- Without wood the fire goes out; without a whisperer quarreling ceases (Prov 26:20, Prov 26:21)
- Burning lips with an evil heart are like silver dross glazed over an earthen pot (Prov 26:23)
- When the hater speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven abominations are in his heart (Prov 26:24, Prov 26:25, Prov 26:26)
- He who rolls a stone, it will come back upon him (Prov 26:27)

**Sayings on tomorrow, friends and the care of flocks**
- A stone is heavy and sand weighty, but a fool's provocation is heavier than both (Prov 27:3)
- Open rebuke is better than hidden love; faithful are the wounds of a friend, profuse the kisses of an enemy (Prov 27:5, Prov 27:6)
- The sated soul tramples honey; to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet (Prov 27:7)
- Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his place (Prov 27:8)
- Better a neighbor who is near than a brother far away (Prov 27:10)
- He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse (Prov 27:14)
- Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens the face of his friend (Prov 27:17)
- As in water face answers to face, so the heart of man to man (Prov 27:19)
- The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, and a man is tested by his praise (Prov 27:21)
- Though you crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle among the grain, his folly will not leave him (Prov 27:22)
- Know the condition of your flocks, for riches and the crown do not last forever; lambs and goats provide clothing, field and milk (Prov 27:23, Prov 27:24, Prov 27:25, Prov 27:26, Prov 27:27)

**Sayings on torah, rulers, usury and confession**
- The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion (Prov 28:1)
- When a land transgresses it has many rulers; with a man of understanding it endures (Prov 28:2)
- A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a beating rain that leaves no food (Prov 28:3)
- Those who forsake the torah praise the wicked; those who keep the torah contend with them (Prov 28:4, Prov 28:7)
- He who turns his ear from hearing the torah, even his prayer is an abomination (Prov 28:9)
- He who conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy (Prov 28:13)
- A wicked ruler over a poor people is a roaring lion and a charging bear (Prov 28:15)
- A man burdened with the blood of a life will flee to the pit; let no one support him (Prov 28:17)
- A faithful man has many blessings, but he who hastens to be rich will not go unpunished (Prov 28:20, Prov 28:22)
- He who robs his father or mother and says 'It is no transgression' is companion to a destroyer (Prov 28:24)
- When the wicked rise men hide themselves; when they perish the righteous increase (Prov 28:12, Prov 28:28)

**Last Hezekian sayings (vision, rulers, discipline)**
- He who is often reproved yet stiffens his neck will suddenly be broken beyond healing (Prov 29:1)
- When the righteous increase the people rejoice; when the wicked rule the people groan (Prov 29:2, Prov 29:16)
- He who keeps company with harlots squanders wealth (Prov 29:3)
- A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet (Prov 29:5)
- A fool gives full vent to his spirit, but the wise quietly holds it back (Prov 29:11)
- If a ruler listens to lies, all his servants become wicked (Prov 29:12)
- The poor and the oppressor meet; YHWH gives light to the eyes of both (Prov 29:13)
- Where there is no vision (hazon) the people cast off restraint, but happy is he who keeps the torah (Prov 29:18)
- A slave is not corrected by words; though he understands he will not respond (Prov 29:19)
- He who pampers his slave from youth will in the end find him an heir or a grief (manon) (Prov 29:21)
- The partner of a thief hates his own soul; he hears the adjuration (alah) and does not testify (Prov 29:24)
- The fear of man lays a snare, but he who trusts in YHWH is set on high (Prov 29:25)
- The unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, and the upright an abomination to the wicked (Prov 29:27)

**Words of Agur son of Yakeh, confession of ignorance and prayer**
- Sayings attributed to Agur son of Yakeh, an oracle (massa) addressed to Ithiel and Ucal (Prov 30:1)
- The sage declares himself more brutish than any man, without human understanding or knowledge of the Holy One (Prov 30:2, Prov 30:3)
- Riddle question about God (the creator): 'What is his name, and what is the name of his son?' (Prov 30:4)
- Every word of God is refined (tested); he is a shield to those who take refuge in him (Prov 30:5)
- Do not add to his words lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar (Prov 30:6)
- Prayer for two things: keep falsehood far and give neither poverty nor riches, only my allotted bread, lest I deny God or steal (Prov 30:7, Prov 30:8, Prov 30:9)

**Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures)**
- Do not slander a slave to his master lest he curse you (Prov 30:10)
- Catalogue of a corrupt 'generation' (dor): cursing parents, self-righteous yet unwashed, haughty, with sword-teeth devouring the poor (Prov 30:11, Prov 30:12, Prov 30:13, Prov 30:14)
- The leech ('aluqah) has two daughters: 'Give, give!' (Prov 30:15)
- The eye that mocks a father and scorns a mother will be pecked out by ravens of the valley and eaten by young vultures (Prov 30:17)
- Four wonders: the way of an eagle in the sky, a serpent on a rock, a ship in the sea, and a man with a young woman ('almah) (Prov 30:18, Prov 30:19)
- The adulteress eats, wipes her mouth and says 'I have done no wrong' (Prov 30:20)
- Four small but wise creatures: ants storing food in summer, rock-badgers housed in rock, locusts with no king marching in ranks, the lizard in kings' palaces (Prov 30:24, Prov 30:25, Prov 30:26, Prov 30:27, Prov 30:28)
- The locusts have no king yet all go out in ranks (Prov 30:27)
- Four stately in stride: the lion mightiest of beasts, the strutting rooster (zarzir), the he-goat, and a king with his army (Prov 30:29, Prov 30:30, Prov 30:31)
- If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, put your hand on your mouth (Prov 30:32)
- Pressing milk produces butter, pressing the nose produces blood, pressing anger produces strife (pun on af 'nose/anger') (Prov 30:33)

**Words of King Lemuel taught by his mother**
- Sayings of King Lemuel, an oracle (massa) his mother taught him (Prov 31:1)
- A king's mother instructs her son in royal conduct (Prov 31:1)
- The mother addresses the king as 'son of my womb, son of my vows' (bar, Aramaic 'son') (Prov 31:2)
- The king is not to give his strength to women nor his ways to those who destroy kings (Prov 31:3)
- Give strong drink to him who is perishing and wine to the bitter of soul, that he may forget his poverty (Prov 31:6, Prov 31:7)
- Open your mouth for the mute, for the rights of all the destitute; judge righteously for the poor (Prov 31:8, Prov 31:9)

**The woman of valor (alphabetic acrostic)**
- Poem praising the 'woman of valor' (eshet hayil): who can find her? Her worth is far beyond pearls (Prov 31:10, Prov 31:11, Prov 31:12)
- She is like merchant ships, bringing her food from afar (Prov 31:14)
- She rises while it is still night to feed her household; her lamp does not go out at night (Prov 31:15, Prov 31:18)
- She considers a field and buys it; from her own earnings she plants a vineyard (Prov 31:16)
- She fears no snow, for her household is clothed in scarlet; she wears fine linen and purple (Prov 31:21, Prov 31:22)
- Her husband is known in the gates when he sits among the elders of the land (Prov 31:23)
- Strength and dignity are her clothing and she laughs at the time to come (Prov 31:25)
- She opens her mouth in wisdom and the teaching of kindness (torat hesed) is on her tongue (Prov 31:26)
- Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her: 'Many women have done valiantly, but you surpass them all' (Prov 31:28, Prov 31:29)
- Charm is deceptive and beauty is vapor (hevel); a woman who fears YHWH is to be praised (Prov 31:30)

**Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature**
- All things are wearisome; the eye is not sated with seeing nor the ear filled with hearing (Eccl 1:8)

**Qohelet the king searches out all things by wisdom**
- What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted (Eccl 1:15)
- In much wisdom is much vexation; who increases knowledge increases pain (Eccl 1:18)

**The royal experiment with pleasure, wealth and great works**
- The sage tests himself with pleasure, laughter and wine while keeping his heart guided by wisdom, and finds it vapor (Eccl 2:1, Eccl 2:2, Eccl 2:3)
- The king builds houses, plants vineyards, gardens and orchards (pardesim) with every fruit tree, and makes pools to water a forest (Eccl 2:4, Eccl 2:5, Eccl 2:6)
- The king amasses slaves, herds, silver, gold, the treasure of kings and provinces, male and female singers and many concubines (shiddah) (Eccl 2:7, Eccl 2:8)

**Wise and fool share one fate; hatred of toil; eat and drink**
- Wisdom excels folly as light excels darkness; the wise has eyes in his head, the fool walks in darkness (Eccl 2:13, Eccl 2:14)
- The speaker says 'I hated life' because all is vapor (Eccl 2:17)
- Hating his toil because he must leave it to one who comes after him, who may be wise or a fool (Eccl 2:18, Eccl 2:19, Eccl 2:21)
- All his days are pain and vexation; even at night his heart does not rest (Eccl 2:23)
- God gives the sinner the task of gathering and heaping up to give to the one who pleases God (Eccl 2:26)

**A time for everything; eternity in the heart**
- A time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones (Eccl 3:5)
- God has made everything beautiful in its time (Eccl 3:11)
- God has put 'olam (eternity, or the world) in the human heart, yet man cannot find out the work of God from beginning to end (Eccl 3:11)
- God seeks what has been driven away (et nirdaf); what is has already been (Eccl 3:15)

**Injustice, divine judgment, and humans no better than beasts**
- God tests humans to show them that they are but beasts; man has no advantage over the beast (Eccl 3:18, Eccl 3:19)
- Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward and the spirit of the beast goes down to the earth? (Eccl 3:21)

**Oppression, envy, the lonely miser, and 'two are better than one'**
- The tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; power is in the hand of their oppressors (Eccl 4:1)
- The dead are more fortunate than the living, and better than both is the one who has not yet been (Eccl 4:2, Eccl 4:3)
- All toil and skill in work comes from a man's envy of his neighbor (Eccl 4:4)
- The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh (Eccl 4:5)
- Better one handful with quiet than two handfuls with toil and chasing the wind (Eccl 4:6)
- One alone without son or brother, toiling endlessly, his eye unsated by riches: 'For whom am I toiling and depriving myself?' (Eccl 4:7, Eccl 4:8)

**The poor wise youth and the old king; caution at the house of God**
- Guard your steps when you go to the house of God; to draw near to listen is better than the sacrifice of fools (Eccl 4:17)

**Few words before God and paying vows**
- Do not be rash with your mouth before God, for God is in heaven and you on earth; let your words be few (Eccl 5:1)
- Dreams come with much business and a fool's voice with many words (Eccl 5:2, Eccl 5:6)
- Do not say before the messenger (mal'akh) 'it was a mistake (shegagah)' lest God be angry at your voice (Eccl 5:5)

**Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes**
- If you see oppression of the poor in a province, do not be amazed: a high one watches over a high one, and higher ones over them (Eccl 5:7)
- The profit of the land is for all; a king is for (served by) the cultivated field (Eccl 5:8)
- He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance with income (Eccl 5:9)
- When goods increase, those who eat them increase; the owner only sees them with his eyes (Eccl 5:10)
- Sweet is the sleep of the laborer whether he eats little or much, but the surfeit of the rich will not let him sleep (Eccl 5:11)
- He will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart (Eccl 5:19)

**Wealth unenjoyed, the stillborn better off, desire unfilled**
- A man with a hundred children and long life who is unsatisfied and has no burial: the stillborn (nefel) is better off than he (Eccl 6:3, Eccl 6:4, Eccl 6:5)
- Even if he lived a thousand years twice and saw no good, do not all go to one place? (Eccl 6:6)
- All man's toil is for his mouth, yet the appetite (nefesh) is never filled (Eccl 6:7)
- Better the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire (Eccl 6:9)
- Whatever has come to be has already been named; man cannot dispute with one stronger than he (Eccl 6:10)

**Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing)**
- A good name is better than good oil (shem / shemen), and the day of death than the day of birth (Eccl 7:1)
- Better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning (Eccl 7:2, Eccl 7:4)
- Vexation is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad (Eccl 7:3)
- Like the crackling of thorns (sirim) under a pot (sir), so is the laughter of the fool (Eccl 7:6)
- Oppression makes a wise man foolish and a bribe destroys the heart (Eccl 7:7)
- The end of a thing is better than its beginning; patience is better than pride (Eccl 7:8)
- Do not say 'Why were the former days better than these?', for it is not from wisdom you ask this (Eccl 7:10)
- Wisdom is a shelter (shade) as money is a shelter; wisdom gives life to its possessor (Eccl 7:11, Eccl 7:12)
- Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked? (Eccl 7:13)
- In the day of prosperity be joyful, in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other (Eccl 7:14)

**Do not be overly righteous; the search for the sum of things; the snaring woman**
- There is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness and a wicked man who prolongs his life in his evil (Eccl 7:15)
- Be not overly righteous nor overly wise; be not overly wicked nor a fool: hold to both; the God-fearer escapes them all (golden mean) (Eccl 7:16, Eccl 7:17, Eccl 7:18)
- Wisdom gives the wise more strength than ten rulers in a city (Eccl 7:19)
- There is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins (Eccl 7:20)
- Do not take to heart everything people say, lest you hear your servant curse you; you have often cursed others (Eccl 7:21, Eccl 7:22)
- The woman whose heart is snares and nets and whose hands are fetters is more bitter than death; the sinner is caught by her (Eccl 7:26)
- Qohelet construed once with a feminine verb ('amrah qohelet') (Eccl 7:27)
- One man in a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find (Eccl 7:28)
- God made humankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes (hishshevonot) (Eccl 7:29)

**Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution**
- Who is like the wise and knows the interpretation (pesher) of a thing? Wisdom makes his face shine (Eccl 8:1)
- Keep the king's command because of the oath of God; who can say to him 'What are you doing?' (Eccl 8:2, Eccl 8:3, Eccl 8:4)
- I saw the wicked buried with honor, going in and out of the holy place, and praised in the city where they did such things (Eccl 8:10)
- Because sentence (pitgam) against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil (Eccl 8:11)
- There are righteous men who receive what the wicked deserve and wicked who receive what the righteous deserve (Eccl 8:14)
- Man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it (Eccl 8:16, Eccl 8:17)

**One fate for all; the living dog; eat your bread with joy**
- The righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God; whether love or hate, man does not know (Eccl 9:1)
- One fate for righteous and wicked, clean and unclean, him who sacrifices and him who does not, the one who swears and the one who fears an oath (Eccl 9:2, Eccl 9:3)
- The living know they will die, but the dead know nothing, have no more reward, and their love, hate and envy have perished (Eccl 9:5, Eccl 9:6)
- Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your might, for there is no work, reckoning, knowledge or wisdom in Sheol (Eccl 9:10)

**Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city**
- A great king besieges a small city; a poor wise man delivers it by his wisdom, yet no one remembers him (Eccl 9:13, Eccl 9:14, Eccl 9:15)

**Sayings on folly, rulers and hazards (dead flies, slaves on horses)**
- Dead flies make the perfumer's ointment stink; a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor (Eccl 10:1)
- The heart of the wise is to his right, the heart of the fool to his left (Eccl 10:2)
- If the ruler's anger rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness allays great offenses (Eccl 10:4)
- Folly set in high places, the rich sitting low; slaves on horses and princes walking like slaves (Eccl 10:5, Eccl 10:6, Eccl 10:7)
- He who breaks a wall is bitten by a snake; he who quarries stones is hurt; he who splits logs is endangered (Eccl 10:8, Eccl 10:9)
- If the iron is blunt and one does not whet the edge, he must use more strength; wisdom helps one succeed (Eccl 10:10)
- The toil of fools wearies them, for they do not even know the way to the city (Eccl 10:15)
- Woe to the land whose king is a youth and whose princes feast in the morning; happy the land whose king is noble-born (Eccl 10:16, Eccl 10:17)
- Bread is made for laughter, wine gladdens life, and money answers everything (Eccl 10:19)
- Do not curse the king even in thought nor the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the air will carry the voice (Eccl 10:20)

**Cast your bread upon the waters; rejoice in youth**
- Send out your bread on the face of the waters, for after many days you will find it (Eccl 11:1)
- Give a portion to seven or even to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come (Eccl 11:2)
- If clouds are full they empty rain; where the tree falls, north or south, there it lies (Eccl 11:3)
- He who watches the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap (Eccl 11:4)
- As you do not know the way of the wind (or spirit), or how bones grow in the womb of the pregnant, so you do not know the work of God (Eccl 11:5)
- In the morning sow your seed and in the evening do not withhold your hand, for you do not know which will prosper (Eccl 11:6)
- Light is sweet and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun (Eccl 11:7, Eccl 11:8)
- Rejoice, young man, in your youth and walk in the ways of your heart, but know that for all these God will bring you into judgment (Eccl 11:9)
- Youth and the dawn of life (shaharut, 'blackness of hair') are vapor (Eccl 11:10)

**Remember your Creator; the allegory of old age; dust and spirit return**
- Remember your Creator (bor'ekha) in the days of your youth, before the evil days come (Eccl 12:1)
- The almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, the caper-berry fails (signs of old age) (Eccl 12:5)
- Man goes to his eternal house (beit 'olamo) and the mourners go about the street (Eccl 12:5)
- Before the silver cord is snapped, the golden bowl crushed, the jar broken at the spring and the wheel broken at the cistern (Eccl 12:6)
- The dust returns to the earth as it was and the spirit returns to God who gave it (Eccl 12:7)

**Epilogue on Qohelet, many books, and the whole duty of man**
- Editorial epilogue speaks of Qohelet in the third person: a sage who taught the people, weighed and arranged many proverbs (Eccl 12:9, Eccl 12:10)
- The words of the wise are like goads and like nails firmly fixed, given by one shepherd (Eccl 12:11)
- Of making many books there is no end, and much study wearies the flesh (Eccl 12:12)
- The end of the matter: fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of man (Eccl 12:13)
- God will bring every deed into judgment, every hidden thing, whether good or evil (Eccl 12:14)

**Title; 'let him kiss me'; black and beautiful; the shepherd**
- The love poem is titled 'Song of Songs, which is Solomon's' (Song 1:1)
- 'I am black (or dark) and beautiful', sunburned like the tents of Kedar and the curtains of Solomon (Song 1:5, Song 1:6)

**Mare among chariots, nard and myrrh, lily of the valleys, lovesick under the apple tree**
- The beloved is compared to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots (Song 1:9)
- Our couch is green, the beams of our house cedar, our rafters cypress (lovemaking outdoors) (Song 1:16, Song 1:17)
- 'I am a crocus (havatselet) of Sharon, a lily (shoshannah) of the valleys'; like a lily among thorns (Song 2:1, Song 2:2)
- He brought me to the house of wine and his banner over me was love (Song 2:4)

**The lover like a gazelle; spring song 'Arise, come away'; little foxes**
- The lover stands behind the wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice (Song 2:9)
- 'Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away': winter is past, flowers appear, the time of singing (or pruning) has come, the turtledove is heard (Song 2:10, Song 2:11, Song 2:12, Song 2:13)
- 'My dove in the clefts of the rock, let me see your face and hear your voice' (Song 2:14)
- Catch us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards in blossom (Song 2:15)

**Procession of Solomon's litter on his wedding day**
- Solomon's litter (mittah) escorted by sixty armed warriors against terrors of the night (Song 3:7, Song 3:8)
- King Solomon's palanquin ('appiryon) of Lebanon wood, with silver posts, gold back, purple seat, inlaid with love (Song 3:9, Song 3:10)

**Descriptive song of the bride's beauty**
- 'I will go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense' (Song 4:6)
- 'You are all fair, my love; there is no blemish (mum) in you' (Song 4:7)

**Come from Lebanon; sister-bride; the locked garden and its consummation**
- 'Come with me from Lebanon, bride': from the peaks of Amana, Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions and mountains of leopards (Song 4:8)
- The lover calls the beloved 'my sister, bride' (ahoti kallah) (Song 4:9, Song 4:10, Song 4:12, Song 5:1)
- 'A garden locked is my sister, bride; a spring locked, a fountain sealed' (Song 4:12)
- A garden fountain, a well of living water, streams from Lebanon (Song 4:15)
- 'Awake, north wind, come south wind, blow on my garden'; let my beloved come to his garden and eat its choice fruits (Song 4:16)
- 'I have come to my garden... eaten my honeycomb with my honey'; 'Eat, friends, drink, be drunk with love' (Song 5:1)

**The knock at night, the vanished lover and the watchmen's blows**
- 'I slept but my heart was awake': the lover knocks at night, his head wet with dew (Song 5:2)
- 'I have taken off my robe, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I soil them?' (Song 5:3)
- The lover thrusts his hand through the hole (of the door) and her inward parts yearn for him (Song 5:4)
- Her hands drip myrrh, liquid myrrh on the handles of the bolt (Song 5:5)
- She opens to her beloved but he has turned away and gone; she calls but he does not answer (Song 5:6)
- The watchmen of the walls strike and wound the woman and take away her mantle (Song 5:7)

**Descriptive song of the beloved man ('radiant and ruddy')**
- 'My beloved is radiant and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand' (Song 5:10)
- His locks are wavy (or palm-fronds), black as a raven (Song 5:11)
- His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, bathed in milk, fitly set (Song 5:12)

**Where has your beloved gone; the beloved unique among queens**
- The beloved is unique ('one is my dove') among sixty queens, eighty concubines and countless maidens, who praise her (Song 6:8-9)

**The Shulammite's dance and the palm tree**
- The Shulammite is called to turn back so the onlookers may gaze at her dancing ('dance of the two camps') (Song 7:1)
- The lover will climb the palm (the beloved's stature) and grasp its fruit-clusters (her breasts) (Song 7:8-9)
- Lovers go out to the fields and villages at dawn to see the vines blossom and there make love (Song 7:12-13)

**Seal on the heart; love strong as death; the little sister; Solomon's vineyard**
- The woman wishes her lover were her brother so she could kiss him in public and bring him to her mother's house (Song 8:1-2)
- Woman awakened her lover under the apple tree where his mother conceived and bore him (Song 8:5)
- Lover asks to be set as a seal (hotam) on the beloved's heart and arm (Song 8:6)
- Love is strong as death, jealousy fierce as Sheol; its flames are flames of fire, 'the flame of Yah' (Song 8:6)
- Many waters cannot quench love nor rivers drown it (Song 8:7)
- If a man offered all the wealth of his house for love he would be utterly scorned (Song 8:7)
- Brothers deliberate over a little sister who has no breasts yet: if she is a wall or a door they will build on or board her (Song 8:8-10)
- Solomon's vineyard at Baal-hamon let out to keepers for a thousand silver; 'my own vineyard is before me' (Song 8:11-12)

**Hear, O heavens; the great indictment, sacrifice rejected, the faithful city**
- Daughter Zion left alone like a booth in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field, a besieged city (Isa 1:8)
- The faithful city has become a harlot; silver turned to dross, wine diluted with water (Isa 1:21-22)
- City or people given a new name in the future age (e.g. 'City of Righteousness', 'Hephzibah') (Isa 1:26)
- Worshippers shamed by the sacred oaks (elim) and gardens they chose (Isa 1:29-30)

**The mountain of the Lord's house; the Day of YHWH against all that is proud**
- On that day people throw their silver and gold idols to the moles and bats and flee into clefts of the rocks (Isa 2:20)
- Stop trusting man, who has only breath in his nostrils (Isa 2:22)

**Removal of stay and staff; children rule; the finery of the daughters of Zion; seven women and one man**
- God removes the mighty, judges, prophets, diviners and counselors and makes boys and infants rule (Isa 3:1-4, Isa 3:12)
- In collapse a man begs his brother who has a cloak to become their ruler, and he refuses (Isa 3:6-7)
- Haughty daughters of Zion walking with mincing steps and jingling anklets are stripped of their finery and made bald (Isa 3:16-17, Isa 3:24)
- Amulets, charms or 'houses of the soul' (bottei ha-nefesh) worn as protection (Isa 3:20)
- Seven women seize one man, offering to feed and clothe themselves if only they may bear his name (Isa 4:1)

**The branch of YHWH and the canopy over Zion**
- Survivors are those 'written for life' in Jerusalem (a heavenly register) (Isa 4:3)
- God will create over Mount Zion a cloud by day and flaming fire by night, a canopy (huppah) and booth over all (Isa 4:5-6)

**Song of the vineyard; six woes; the nation from afar**
- Parable-song of the beloved's vineyard that yielded wild grapes despite all care and is abandoned to briars (Isa 5:1-6)
- Prophetic paronomasia: hoped for mishpat (justice) but got mishpah (bloodshed), for tsedaqah but got tse'aqah (outcry) (Isa 5:7)
- Woe to those who join house to house and field to field until there is no room left (Isa 5:8-10)
- Woe to those who rise early for strong drink and feast with lyre and harp but ignore God's work (Isa 5:11-12, Isa 5:22)
- God raises a banner and whistles for a nation from the ends of the earth to come as his instrument (Isa 5:26)
- The invading army never tires, sleeps or loosens belt or sandal; its horses' hooves like flint, its roar like a lion (Isa 5:27-30)

**The throne vision and the call of Isaiah**
- Prophet sees the Lord seated on a high and lifted-up throne, his train filling the temple (Isa 6:1)
- Six-winged seraphim stand above God: two wings cover the face, two the feet, two for flying (Isa 6:2)
- Heavenly beings call 'Holy, holy, holy is YHWH of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory' (Isa 6:3)
- At the heavenly voice the doorposts shake and the house fills with smoke (Isa 6:4)
- Prophet cries 'Woe is me, I am undone, a man of unclean lips' for having seen the King (Isa 6:5)
- A seraph touches the prophet's lips with a burning coal from the altar, removing his guilt (Isa 6:6-7)
- Even the tenth that remains will be burned, like a felled terebinth or oak whose stump is the holy seed (Isa 6:11-13)

**Ahaz, the Syro-Ephraimite threat and the Immanuel sign**
- Aram (Rezin) and Israel (Pekah) ally to attack Jerusalem and install a puppet king (son of Tabeel) (Isa 7:1-2, Isa 7:5-6)
- Enemy kings dismissed as two smoldering stumps of firebrands (Isa 7:4)
- 'If you do not believe (ta'aminu) you will not be established (te'amenu)': faith as condition of survival (Isa 7:9)
- King invited to ask any sign 'deep as Sheol or high as heaven' refuses, saying he will not test God (Isa 7:10-12)
- The child will eat curds and honey until he knows to refuse evil and choose good (Isa 7:15, Isa 7:22)
- God will whistle for the fly of Egypt and the bee of Assyria to settle in the land (Isa 7:18-19)
- God will shave head, 'hair of the feet' and beard with a razor hired beyond the River (the king of Assyria) (Isa 7:20)
- Cultivated land worth a thousand silver reverts to briers and thorns (shamir va-shayit), fit only for grazing and hunting (Isa 7:23-25)

**Maher-shalal-hash-baz; waters of Shiloah; the stone of stumbling; ghosts that chirp**
- Prophet goes in to 'the prophetess' (his wife) who bears a sign-child (Isa 8:3)
- The people reject the gently flowing waters of Shiloah, so God brings the mighty River (Assyria) to flood them up to the neck (Isa 8:6-8)
- Refrain 'Immanuel / for God is with us' against plotting nations (Isa 8:8, Isa 8:10)
- God becomes a sanctuary and a stone of stumbling and rock of offense, a trap and snare to both houses of Israel (Isa 8:14-15)
- Bind up the testimony, seal the teaching among my disciples; the prophet waits for the God who hides his face (Isa 8:16-17)
- The prophet and the children God gave him are signs and portents in Israel (Isa 8:18)
- The land of Zebulun and Naphtali, 'Galilee of the nations' by the way of the sea, first humbled and later glorified (Isa 8:23)

**Great light; a child is born to us; the outstretched hand against Ephraim**
- Every trampling soldier's boot and garment rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for fire (Isa 9:4)
- A child is born to us; his throne names are Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace (Isa 9:5)
- Of the increase of his government and peace there will be no end on David's throne, forever (Isa 9:6)
- Proud boast: 'Bricks have fallen, we will build with hewn stone; sycamores cut down, we will put cedars in their place' (Isa 9:8-9)
- In famine and wrath each devours the flesh of his own arm; Manasseh devours Ephraim and Ephraim Manasseh (Isa 9:18-20)
- Woe to those who write iniquitous decrees to rob the poor, the widow and the orphan (Isa 10:1-2)

**Woe to Assyria, rod of my anger; a remnant will return; the invader's march on Jerusalem**
- Assyria is the rod of God's anger and staff of his fury, sent against a godless nation (Isa 10:5-7)
- Conqueror boasts of cities taken (Calno, Carchemish, Hamath, Arpad, Samaria) and that his own strength and wisdom did it (Isa 10:8-11, Isa 10:13)
- Conqueror boasts he gathered the earth like abandoned eggs and none flapped a wing or chirped (Isa 10:14)
- Shall the axe boast over the one who hews with it, or the saw magnify itself against its wielder? (Isa 10:15)
- The Light of Israel becomes a fire and his Holy One a flame that burns the forest in one day (Isa 10:16-17)
- 'A remnant will return' (she'ar yashuv) to the Mighty God, though Israel be as the sand of the sea (Isa 10:20-22)
- Poetic itinerary of the invader's advance village by village (Aiath, Migron, Michmash, Geba, Ramah, Gibeah, Anathoth, Nob) to Jerusalem (Isa 10:28-32)
- The lofty are lopped and the thickets of the forest and Lebanon felled by the Mighty One (Isa 10:33-34)

**Shoot from the stump of Jesse; the peaceable kingdom; second exodus**
- A shoot (hoter) will come out from the stump of Jesse and a branch (netser) grow from his roots (Isa 11:1)
- The spirit of YHWH rests on him: spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, knowledge and fear of YHWH (Isa 11:2-3)
- The ideal king judges not by what his eyes see or ears hear, but with righteousness for the poor (Isa 11:3-4)
- He strikes the earth with the rod of his mouth and slays the wicked with the breath of his lips (Isa 11:4)
- The nursing child plays over the hole of the asp and the weaned child puts his hand on the adder's den (Isa 11:8)
- The root of Jesse stands as a banner to the peoples; the nations seek him (Isa 11:10, Isa 11:12)
- God will redeem his people a second time with a new exodus: drying the sea, splitting the River, a highway as in the day they came up from Egypt (Isa 11:11, Isa 11:15-16)
- The jealousy of Ephraim and Judah will cease (Isa 11:13)
- God strikes the River with his scorching wind into seven streams so it can be crossed in sandals (Isa 11:15)

**Song of thanksgiving 'on that day'**
- 'With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation' (Isa 12:3)

**Oracle against Babylon; the Day of YHWH darkens the heavens**
- Wordplay: the Day comes 'like destruction (shod) from Shaddai' (Isa 13:6)
- God makes the heavens tremble and the earth shake from its place on the day of his wrath (Isa 13:13)
- God makes mortals rarer than fine gold, humans than the gold of Ophir (Isa 13:12)
- God stirs up the Medes, who care nothing for silver or gold (Isa 13:17)
- Babylon, glory of kingdoms, will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah (Isa 13:19)

**Restoration of Jacob and the taunt over the king of Babylon (Helel son of Dawn)**
- Strangers (gerim) will join themselves to Israel and cleave to the house of Jacob (Isa 14:1)
- Reversal: Israel will take captive those who captured them and rule over their oppressors (Isa 14:2)
- Mocking dirge (mashal) over a fallen tyrant: 'How the oppressor has ceased!' (Isa 14:4-8)
- The cypresses and cedars of Lebanon rejoice that no woodcutter comes up since the tyrant fell (Isa 14:8)
- In the underworld maggots are spread beneath the dead king and worms are his covering (Isa 14:11)
- 'How you have fallen from heaven, Helel son of Shahar (Shining One, son of Dawn)!' - a star-figure cast down to earth (Isa 14:12)
- The would-be god is brought down instead to Sheol, to the recesses of the pit (yarkete bor) (Isa 14:15, Isa 14:19)
- God cuts off from the enemy 'name and remnant, offspring and posterity' (Isa 14:20-22)
- God sweeps the city with the broom of destruction, leaving it to hedgehogs and marshes (Isa 14:23)

**God's oath against Assyria; oracle against Philistia in the year Ahaz died**
- From the serpent's root comes an adder, and its fruit is a flying seraph (saraf me'ofef) (Isa 14:29)
- Smoke (an army) comes out of the north against the doomed people (Isa 14:31)
- YHWH has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people find refuge (Isa 14:32)

**Oracle concerning Moab; lament, plea for refuge, the vine of Sibmah**
- Prophetic lament over Moab's ruin naming its towns (Ar, Kir, Dibon, Nebo, Medeba, Heshbon, Elealeh, Zoar, Nimrim) (Isa 15:1-9, Isa 16:7-11)
- Plea to shelter the outcasts and not betray the fugitive; be a hiding place from the destroyer (Isa 16:1-4)
- A throne established in steadfast love, with a judge in the tent of David seeking justice (Isa 16:5)
- The vine of Sibmah, whose shoots reached Jazer and the sea, is mourned; the harvest shout (hedad) is silenced (Isa 16:8-10)
- The nation wearies itself at its high place and comes to its sanctuary to pray but cannot prevail (Isa 16:12)

**Oracle on Damascus and Ephraim; gardens of the pleasant one; the roaring of the nations**
- On that day people look to their Maker, not to altars, Asherahs and incense-stands (hammanim) made by their fingers (Isa 17:7-8)
- Plantings of 'pleasant ones' (nit'ei na'amanim) and a foreign god's slips that sprout quickly and wither in a day (Isa 17:10-11)
- The nations roar like many waters but God rebukes them and they flee like chaff before wind; by morning they are gone (Isa 17:12-14)

**Oracle to the land of whirring wings beyond the rivers of Cush**
- 'Land of whirring wings' beyond the rivers of Cush, sending envoys in papyrus vessels to a tall, smooth-skinned people (Isa 18:1-2)
- God says he will quietly look on from his dwelling like shimmering heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in harvest heat (Isa 18:4)
- Judgment as pruning the shoots with knives before the harvest; carcasses left for birds of prey and beasts all summer and winter (Isa 18:5-6)
- A distant people (Cush) brings tribute to YHWH at Mount Zion, the place of his name (Isa 18:7)

**Oracle on Egypt; the drying Nile; an altar to YHWH in Egypt; 'Blessed be Egypt my people'**
- God stirs up Egyptian against Egyptian, city against city, kingdom against kingdom (Isa 19:2)
- Egypt consults its idols, the 'ittim (mutterers), ghosts and familiar spirits (Isa 19:3)
- God mixes a spirit of distortion in Egypt so it staggers like a drunkard in his vomit (Isa 19:14)
- Five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear to YHWH; one called 'City of the Sun/Destruction' (ir ha-heres) (Isa 19:18)
- An altar to YHWH in the midst of Egypt and a standing stone (matsevah) at its border (Isa 19:19-20)
- When Egypt cries out because of oppressors God sends them a savior; Egypt knows YHWH and offers sacrifice (Isa 19:20-22)
- A highway from Egypt to Assyria; 'Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance' (Isa 19:23-25)

**Isaiah walks naked and barefoot as a sign against Egypt and Cush**
- Dated to the year the tartan, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, took Ashdod (Isa 20:1)
- Prophet walks naked and barefoot for three years as a sign of captives to be led away (Isa 20:2-4)

**Wilderness of the sea; the watchman; Dumah; Arabia**
- Oracle on 'the wilderness of the sea' (Babylon): whirlwinds from the Negev, Elam and Media summoned to attack (Isa 21:1-2)
- 'Set the table, spread the rugs, eat, drink - rise, princes, oil the shield!' (Isa 21:5)
- Prophet told to post a watchman who reports what he sees (riders in pairs, donkeys, camels) and stands day and night (Isa 21:6-9)
- Oracle of Dumah: 'Watchman, what of the night?' 'Morning comes, and also the night; if you will ask, ask; come back again' (Isa 21:11-12)
- Oracle on Arabia: caravans of Dedanites lodge in the thickets; Tema brings water and bread to fugitives; glory of Kedar ends (Isa 21:13-17)

**Valley of vision; let us eat and drink; Shebna deposed, Eliakim given the key of David**
