- Oracle on 'the valley of vision' (Jerusalem) whose people revel on rooftops while the day of tumult comes (Isa 22:1-2, Isa 22:5)
- Prophet: 'Look away from me, let me weep bitterly; do not try to comfort me over the ruin of my people' (Isa 22:4)
- City prepares for siege (armory of the House of the Forest, counting houses, tearing them down for the wall, a reservoir between walls) but does not look to its Maker (Isa 22:8-11)
- Revelers say 'Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die' when called to mourning (Isa 22:13)
- God swears this iniquity will not be atoned for until they die (Isa 22:14)
- The steward Shebna, 'over the house', rebuked for hewing himself a lofty tomb in the rock (Isa 22:15-16)
- God will wind the official up and hurl him like a ball into a wide land, where he and his glorious chariots will die (Isa 22:17-18)
- Successor clothed with the predecessor's robe and sash and given his authority (Isa 22:20-21)
- God places the key of the house of David on the new steward's shoulder: what he opens none shall shut, what he shuts none shall open (Isa 22:22)
- Official fastened like a peg in a secure place on which his family's honor hangs; the peg will later give way (Isa 22:23-25)

**Oracle on Tyre; seventy years forgotten; the harlot's song**
- Oracle on Tyre and Sidon: ships of Tarshish wail, the merchant city whose traders were princes is laid waste (Isa 23:1-14)
- The Sea, stronghold of the sea, speaks: 'I have not labored nor given birth nor raised young men or virgins' (Isa 23:4)
- A city forgotten for seventy years, 'like the days of one king', then visited again by God (Isa 23:15, Isa 23:17)
- The forgotten city is told to take a lyre and go about like a forgotten harlot singing to be remembered (Isa 23:15-16)
- The city's trade and harlot's hire will be holy to YHWH, feeding and clothing those who dwell before him (Isa 23:17-18)

**The earth laid waste; the host of heaven imprisoned; YHWH reigns on Zion**
- YHWH empties the earth and lays it waste, twisting its surface and scattering its inhabitants: priest as people, master as slave (Isa 24:1-3)
- The earth is polluted under its inhabitants because they transgressed laws and broke the everlasting covenant; a curse devours it (Isa 24:5-6)
- The 'city of chaos' (qiryat tohu) is broken; every house shut, joy banished (Isa 24:10-12)
- Prophet cries 'razi li, razi li' ('my leanness/my secret is mine'), woe to me, the treacherous deal treacherously (Isa 24:16)
- The earth breaks, splits, totters and reels like a drunkard and sways like a hut; it falls and will not rise (Isa 24:19-20)
- On that day YHWH punishes the host of the height in the height and the kings of the earth, gathering them as prisoners in a pit, shut up and punished after many days (Isa 24:21-22)
- The moon is abashed and the sun ashamed, for YHWH reigns on Mount Zion with glory before his elders (Isa 24:23)

**Thanksgiving; the feast on the mountain; death swallowed forever**
- God turned the city into a heap, the foreigners' palace never to be rebuilt; strong peoples fear him (Isa 25:2-3)
- God is a stronghold for the poor, refuge from the storm and shade from the heat (Isa 25:4-5)
- On this mountain YHWH makes for all peoples a feast of rich foods and well-aged wines (Isa 25:6)
- God swallows the shroud (lot) and veil spread over all peoples (Isa 25:7)
- God will swallow up death forever (bila ha-mavet la-netsah) (Isa 25:8)
- 'Behold, this is our God; we waited for him and he saved us' (Isa 25:9)
- Moab trampled like straw in a dung-pit, spreading his hands like a swimmer (Isa 25:10-12)

**Song of the strong city; your dead shall live**
- 'We have a strong city... Open the gates that the righteous nation that keeps faith may enter' (Isa 26:1-2)
- God keeps the steadfast mind in perfect peace (shalom shalom) because it trusts in him (Isa 26:3)
- In Yah YHWH is an everlasting rock (tsur olamim) (Isa 26:4)
- 'My soul yearns for you in the night; my spirit within me seeks you at dawn' (Isa 26:9)
- Other lords ruled us; they are dead, they will not live; shades (rephaim) will not rise; their memory is wiped out (Isa 26:13-14)
- We were pregnant, we writhed, but gave birth only to wind; we brought no salvation to the earth (Isa 26:17-18)
- God's dew is a 'dew of lights' (tal orot) and the earth will give birth to the shades (rephaim) (Isa 26:19)
- 'Go, my people, enter your chambers and shut the doors behind you; hide a little moment until the wrath passes' (Isa 26:20)
- The earth will disclose the blood shed on it and no longer cover its slain (Isa 26:21)

**Leviathan slain; the vineyard of delight; the great shofar**
- Song of the pleasant vineyard that YHWH guards, waters every moment and keeps night and day; he has no wrath, but would burn its briars (Isa 27:2-5)
- Jacob will take root, Israel blossom and bud and fill the face of the world with fruit (Isa 27:6)
- Jacob's guilt is atoned by making all altar stones like crushed chalk, no Asherim or incense-stands standing (Isa 27:9)
- God threshes from the Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt and the Israelites are gathered one by one (Isa 27:12)

**Ephraim's drunkards; tsav la-tsav; covenant with death; the cornerstone; the farmer's wisdom**
- Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim's drunkards, a fading flower on the head of the rich valley, swallowed like an early fig (Isa 28:1-4)
- On that day YHWH of hosts will be a crown of beauty and diadem of glory to the remnant of his people (Isa 28:5-6)
- Priest and prophet reel with strong drink and err in vision; all tables are full of vomit (Isa 28:7-8)
- Mocking babble 'tsav la-tsav, qav la-qav, ze'ir sham' (precept upon precept, line upon line) (Isa 28:10, Isa 28:13)
- God will speak to this people through stammering lips and a foreign tongue (Isa 28:11)
- Rulers boast 'We have made a covenant with Death and a pact with Sheol; the overwhelming scourge will not reach us' (Isa 28:15, Isa 28:18)
- God lays in Zion a tested stone, a precious cornerstone of sure foundation: 'whoever believes will not hasten' (Isa 28:16)
- God makes justice the measuring line and righteousness the plummet (Isa 28:17)
- God will rise as at Mount Perazim and the valley of Gibeon to do his strange deed and his alien work (Isa 28:21)
- Proverb: the bed is too short to stretch out and the blanket too narrow to wrap oneself (Isa 28:20)
- Parable of the farmer who knows when to plow, sow (dill, cumin, wheat, barley, spelt) and how to thresh each crop, taught by God (Isa 28:23-29)

**Woe to Ariel; enemies like a dream; the sealed book; lip service; the potter and the clay**
- Jerusalem called 'Ariel' (altar-hearth / lion of God), the city where David camped, to be besieged and become 'like an ariel' (Isa 29:1-2, Isa 29:7)
- The humbled city's voice will come from the ground like a ghost's (ov) and chirp from the dust (Isa 29:4)
- The multitude of nations fighting Zion will be like a dream of the night: like a hungry man who dreams he eats and wakes empty (Isa 29:5, Isa 29:7-8)
- God pours out a spirit of deep sleep (tardemah) and shuts the eyes of prophets and seers (Isa 29:9-10)
- Vision is like a sealed book: the literate cannot read it because it is sealed, the illiterate because he cannot read (Isa 29:11-12)
- God will do wonders so that the wisdom of the wise perishes and the understanding of the prudent is hidden (Isa 29:14)
- YHWH 'who redeemed Abraham' (a deliverance of Abraham alluded to) (Isa 29:22)

**Woe to the rebellious children going down to Egypt; returning and rest; the Teacher; Topheth prepared**
- Oracle on the beasts of the Negev: a land of lioness, viper and flying seraph through which envoys carry treasure on donkeys and camels (Isa 30:6)
- Egypt's help is vain and empty; God calls her 'Rahab who sits still' (rahav hem shavet) (Isa 30:7)
- People tell the seers 'do not see', and the visionaries 'speak smooth things to us, prophesy illusions' (Isa 30:10-11)
- Iniquity like a bulging breach in a high wall that collapses suddenly, smashed like a potter's jar with no sherd left (Isa 30:13-14)
- 'In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and trust shall be your strength' - but you would not (Isa 30:15)
- 'We will flee on horses' - therefore you shall flee; a thousand flee at the threat of one until left like a flagpole on a hill (Isa 30:16-17)
- YHWH waits to be gracious; blessed are all who wait for him; he answers at the sound of your cry (Isa 30:18-19)
- Your Teacher will no longer hide; your eyes will see him and your ears hear a word behind you: 'This is the way, walk in it' (Isa 30:20-21)
- Silver-plated idols and gold-covered images thrown away like a menstrual cloth: 'Get out!' (Isa 30:22)
- In the future God gives abundant rain, rich bread, broad pastures and fodder; streams flow on every high hill (Isa 30:23-25)
- The moon's light will be like the sun's and the sun's light sevenfold, like the light of seven days (Isa 30:26)
- The Name of YHWH comes from afar, burning with anger, lips full of wrath, tongue like devouring fire, breath like an overflowing torrent (Isa 30:27-28, Isa 30:30)
- God sifts the nations with a sieve of destruction and puts a misleading bridle on the peoples' jaws (Isa 30:28)
- Your song will be as on the night when a festival is hallowed, with gladness like one going with the flute to the mountain of YHWH (Isa 30:29)
- Topheth, long prepared and deep, is ready for the king (melekh/Molech): a pyre of fire and wood kindled by YHWH's breath like a stream of brimstone (Isa 30:33)

**Woe to those who go down to Egypt; YHWH like a lion and hovering birds over Zion**
- 'Egypt is man and not God, their horses flesh and not spirit' (Isa 31:3)
- Like hovering birds YHWH protects Jerusalem; he will 'pass over' (pasoah) and rescue it (Isa 31:5)
- Assyria will fall by a sword not of man; YHWH's fire is in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem (Isa 31:8-9)

**A king will reign in righteousness; complacent women; the spirit poured from on high**
- A king will reign in righteousness and princes rule in justice; each like a shelter from wind and shade of a great rock (Isa 32:1-2)
- The fool (naval) will no longer be called noble nor the knave respectable (Isa 32:5-8)
- Complacent, secure women told to tremble, strip and gird sackcloth and beat their breasts for the lost vintage (Isa 32:9-14)
- Until a spirit is poured on us from on high and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field (Isa 32:15)
- The work of righteousness will be peace, and its effect quietness and trust forever (Isa 32:16-18)

**Woe to the destroyer; who can dwell with devouring fire; the king in his beauty; Zion's broad rivers**
- Woe to the destroyer never destroyed: when you finish destroying you will be destroyed (Isa 33:1)
- The valiant ones (er'elam) cry outside and messengers of peace weep bitterly; covenant broken, highways desolate (Isa 33:7-9)
- Sinners in Zion ask 'Who of us can dwell with the devouring fire, with everlasting burnings?'; answer: one who walks righteously (Isa 33:14-16)
- Your eyes will see the king in his beauty and behold a land stretching afar (Isa 33:17)
- Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tent whose stakes will never be pulled up nor cords broken (Isa 33:20)
- In Zion YHWH is for us a place of broad rivers and streams where no galley with oars can go (Isa 33:21)
- 'YHWH is our judge, YHWH our lawgiver, YHWH our king; he will save us' (Isa 33:22)
- No inhabitant will say 'I am sick'; the people dwelling there are forgiven (Isa 33:24)

**Judgment on the nations and Edom; heavens rolled up like a scroll; Lilith in the ruins**
- God's sword has drunk its fill in heaven and descends on Edom, sated with blood and fat as at a sacrifice in Bozrah (Isa 34:5-7)
- A day of vengeance for YHWH, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion (Isa 34:8)
- Edom's streams turned to pitch and soil to brimstone; its smoke goes up forever, night and day unquenched (Isa 34:9-10)
- God stretches over the land the measuring line of chaos (tohu) and the plummet of emptiness (bohu) (Isa 34:11)
- In the ruins goat-demons call to each other and Lilith (lilit) settles and finds herself a resting place (Isa 34:14)
- 'Seek in the book of YHWH and read: not one of these is missing'; God has allotted the land to the wild creatures by lot (Isa 34:16-17)

**The desert blossoms; the blind see and the lame leap; the Way of Holiness**
- The wilderness and dry land rejoice and blossom like the crocus, given the glory of Lebanon, Carmel and Sharon (Isa 35:1-2)
- 'Strengthen the weak hands and make firm the feeble knees; say to the anxious: be strong, fear not, your God comes' (Isa 35:3-4)
- A highway called 'the Way of Holiness': no unclean one, lion or ravenous beast on it; only the redeemed walk there (Isa 35:8-9)

**Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm**
- A psalm-like 'writing' (mikhtav) of the king composed when he was sick and recovered (Isa 38:9)
- Speaker laments that in the noon of his days he must go to the gates of Sheol, deprived of the rest of his years (Isa 38:10-11)
- My dwelling is pulled up like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off from the loom (Isa 38:12)
- God has cast all the speaker's sins behind his back and held back his soul from the pit of destruction (Isa 38:17)

**Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God**
- 'Comfort, comfort my people': Jerusalem's term of service is ended and she has received double for her sins (Isa 40:1-2)
- A voice cries: 'In the wilderness clear the way of YHWH, make straight in the desert a highway for our God' (Isa 40:3)
- God tends his flock like a shepherd, gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them in his bosom (Isa 40:11)
- Who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off heaven with a span and weighed the mountains in scales? (Isa 40:12)
- Nations are like a drop from a bucket and dust on the scales; Lebanon is not enough fuel nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering (Isa 40:15-17)
- God sits enthroned above the circle (hug) of the earth; its inhabitants are like grasshoppers (Isa 40:22)
- God brings out the starry host by number and calls each by name; none is missing (Isa 40:26)

**Trial of the nations; the one from the east; Israel my servant, fear not; gods challenged to foretell**
- God has stirred up one from the east (and north) whom victory meets at every step, who tramples rulers like a potter treads clay (Isa 41:2-3, Isa 41:25)
- Idol-craftsmen encourage one another, smoothing with the hammer, approving the soldering and fastening it with nails (Isa 41:6-7)
- God addresses Israel as 'worm Jacob' and promises to help (Isa 41:14)
- Israel made a new sharp threshing sledge with teeth that threshes mountains and makes hills like chaff (Isa 41:15-16)
- God plants in the wilderness cedar, acacia, myrtle, olive, cypress, plane and pine together (Isa 41:19-20)

**First servant song; light to the nations; a new song; God as warrior and as woman in labor; the blind servant**
- 'A bruised reed he will not break and a dimly burning wick he will not quench' (Isa 42:3)
- 'I am YHWH, that is my name; my glory I will not give to another nor my praise to idols' (Isa 42:8)
- The former things have come to pass and God now declares new things before they spring forth (Isa 42:9)
- Who gave Jacob to plunder? Was it not YHWH against whom we sinned? Yet they did not take it to heart (Isa 42:22-25)

**I have called you by name; you are my witnesses; behold I do a new thing**
- God gives Egypt, Cush and Seba as Israel's ransom (kofer) and peoples in exchange for her life (Isa 43:3-4)
- God says to north 'Give up' and to south 'Do not withhold': bring my sons from afar and my daughters from the end of the earth (Isa 43:5-7)
- 'I, I am YHWH, and besides me there is no savior' (Isa 43:11)
- 'Do not remember the former things... Behold I am doing a new thing; now it springs forth': a way in the wilderness, rivers in the desert (Isa 43:18-19)
- The wild beasts, jackals and ostriches honor God for the water he gives in the desert (Isa 43:20)
- Israel did not weary itself with offerings for God but wearied him with its sins; he blots out transgressions for his own sake (Isa 43:22-25)
- 'Your first father sinned and your interpreters (melitsim) transgressed against me' (Isa 43:27)

**Spirit on your offspring; the idol made from half a log; Cyrus my shepherd**
- Israel called 'Jeshurun' (the upright one) (Isa 44:2)
- God pours water on the thirsty land and his spirit on Israel's offspring; they spring up like willows by streams (Isa 44:3-4)
- One says 'I am YHWH's', another takes Jacob's name, another writes 'of YHWH' on his hand (a tattoo or brand of allegiance) (Isa 44:5)
- The smith who forges the idol grows hungry and faint and drinks no water (Isa 44:12)
- The carpenter marks out the idol with line and compass and makes it in the form of a man, in human beauty, to dwell in a house (Isa 44:13)
- The idol-maker burns half the tree to cook his meat and warm himself, and of the rest makes a god and prays 'Save me' (Isa 44:14-17, Isa 44:19)
- The idol-worshipper 'feeds on ashes'; a deluded heart leads him astray and he cannot say 'Is there not a lie in my right hand?' (Isa 44:18-20)
- God has blotted out transgressions like a cloud and sins like mist (Isa 44:22)
- Sing, heavens; shout, depths of the earth (tahtiyyot arets); break into song, mountains and every tree of the forest (Isa 44:23)
- God frustrates the omens of the babblers, makes fools of diviners and turns the wise backward (Isa 44:25)
- God says to the deep (tsulah) 'Be dry, I will dry up your rivers' (Isa 44:27)
- God calls Cyrus 'my shepherd' who fulfils his will, saying of Jerusalem 'she shall be rebuilt' and of the temple 'its foundation laid' (Isa 44:28)

**Cyrus the anointed; I form light and create darkness; the potter; every knee shall bow**
- God calls the foreign king Cyrus 'his anointed' (meshiho), whose right hand he grasps to subdue nations (Isa 45:1)
- God goes before his chosen conqueror, levelling heights, breaking bronze doors and cutting iron bars, opening gates that will not be shut (Isa 45:1-2)
- God gives the conqueror 'treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places' (Isa 45:3)
- God names and girds the foreign king though he does not know God, for the sake of Israel (Isa 45:3-5)
- 'Drip, heavens, from above, and let the skies rain righteousness; let the earth open and salvation sprout' (Isa 45:8)
- Woe to him who says to a father 'What are you begetting?' or to a woman 'With what are you in labor?' (Isa 45:10-11)
- God's anointed conqueror will build God's city and free the exiles without price or reward (Isa 45:13)
- Egypt, Cush and the tall Sabeans come over in chains and bow to Israel, saying 'Surely God is with you, there is no other' (Isa 45:14)
- 'Truly you are a God who hides himself (El mistatter), O God of Israel, the Savior' (Isa 45:15)
- God did not create the earth as a chaos (tohu) but formed it to be inhabited (Isa 45:18)
- 'I did not speak in secret, in a land of darkness; I did not say to Jacob seek me in vain (tohu)' (Isa 45:19)
- 'Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God and there is no other' (Isa 45:22)

**Bel and Nebo carried off; God who carries Israel**
- Babylon's gods Bel and Nebo bow and stoop, their images loaded as burdens on weary beasts (Isa 46:1, Isa 46:2)
- Idols must be carried by their worshipers, whereas God has carried his people from the womb to old age (Isa 46:3, Isa 46:4, Isa 46:7)
- God alone announces the end from the beginning and proves his deity by predictions fulfilled (Isa 46:10)
- God summons a bird of prey from the east, the man of his counsel (the conqueror Cyrus) (Isa 46:11)

**Taunt over the virgin daughter Babylon**
- Virgin daughter Babylon is made to come down from her throne and sit in the dust (Isa 47:1, Isa 47:5)
- A proud city says in her heart 'I am, and there is none besides me' and is brought low (Isa 47:8, Isa 47:10)
- The city that said 'I shall not sit as a widow nor know bereavement' suffers both in one day (Isa 47:8, Isa 47:9)
- The wrongdoer says 'No one sees me', trusting in secrecy (Isa 47:10)
- The wicked or their helpers become like stubble burned up by fire (Isa 47:14)

**Obstinate Israel, former and new things, flee from Babylon**
- God foretold the former things long before so no idol could claim credit, and now reveals hidden new things (Isa 48:3, Isa 48:5, Isa 48:6, Isa 48:7)
- A speaker declares 'the Lord YHWH has sent me, and his spirit' (Isa 48:16)

**Second servant song - called from the womb, a light to the nations**
- God makes the servant's mouth a sharp sword and hides him as a polished arrow in his quiver (Isa 49:2)
- The servant of God is addressed as 'Israel', in whom God will be glorified (Isa 49:3)
- The servant complains he has labored in vain and spent his strength for nothing (Isa 49:4)
- Prisoners and those in darkness are told 'Go out' and set free (Isa 49:9)
- Exiles return from far lands including the land of Sinim (later read as China) (Isa 49:12)

**Zion not forgotten; her children return**
- Zion complains 'YHWH has forsaken me, the Lord has forgotten me' (Isa 49:14)
- God has engraved Zion on the palms of his hands; her walls are always before him (Isa 49:16)
- Bereaved, barren Zion is astonished by the multitude of children who crowd her, asking who bore them (Isa 49:20, Isa 49:21)
- Can prey be taken from a mighty man? God will take the captives of the mighty (Isa 49:24, Isa 49:25)

**No bill of divorce; third servant song**
- God asks where is the mother's bill of divorce or to which creditor he sold his children: they were sold for their sins (Isa 50:1)
- At God's rebuke the sea dries up and rivers become desert so the fish stink and die (Isa 50:2)
- God clothes the heavens in blackness and makes sackcloth their covering (Isa 50:3)
- God gives the servant 'a tongue of disciples' and wakens his ear morning by morning to listen (Isa 50:4, Isa 50:5)
- The servant gives his back to smiters and his cheeks to those who pluck the beard and does not hide his face from spitting (Isa 50:6)
- The servant sets his face like flint, knowing he will not be shamed (Isa 50:7)
- The accused speaker challenges his adversaries to trial, since his vindicator is near (Isa 50:8, Isa 50:9)
- Those who kindle their own fire and torches must walk in its flame and lie down in torment (Isa 50:11)

**Look to the rock you were hewn from**
- The people are told to look to the rock from which they were hewn: Abraham their father and Sarah who bore them (Isa 51:1, Isa 51:2)
- God makes Zion's wilderness like Eden and her desert like the garden of YHWH (Isa 51:3)
- The heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth wear out like a garment, but God's salvation endures forever (Isa 51:6)

**Awake, arm of YHWH - Rahab and the dragon**
- God's primeval defeat of the sea monster is identified with drying the sea for the redeemed to cross (Isa 51:10)

**I am your comforter; the cup of staggering**
- A people described as drunk and staggering, but not from wine (Isa 51:21)
- God takes the cup of staggering from his people's hand and gives it to their tormentors (Isa 51:22, Isa 51:23)
- Tormentors told the captive 'Bow down that we may pass over', and she made her back like the ground for them to walk on (Isa 51:23)

**Awake, Zion; the feet of the herald**
- Zion is told to awake, shake off the dust and put on her beautiful garments; the uncircumcised will no longer enter (Isa 52:1, Isa 52:2)
- You were sold for nothing and will be redeemed without money (Isa 52:3)
- Because of the exile God's name is continually blasphemed or profaned among the nations (Isa 52:5)
- Zion's watchmen sing together, seeing eye to eye YHWH's return to Zion (Isa 52:8)
- God bares his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations (Isa 52:10)

**Fourth servant song - the suffering servant**
- God's servant will prosper and be exalted, lifted up and very high (Isa 52:13)
- The servant's appearance is marred beyond that of any man, so that many are appalled (Isa 52:14)
- The servant will 'sprinkle' (or startle) many nations (Isa 52:15)
- 'Who has believed what we have heard, and to whom has the arm of YHWH been revealed?' (Isa 53:1)
- The servant grows up like a tender shoot, a root out of dry ground (Isa 53:2)
- The servant has no form or majesty, no beauty that we should desire him (Isa 53:2)
- The servant is despised and rejected of men, a man of sorrows acquainted with sickness, from whom faces are hidden (Isa 53:3)
- The servant bears others' sickness and is wounded for their transgressions; by his stripes they are healed (Isa 53:4, Isa 53:5, Isa 53:6, Isa 53:8, Isa 53:11, Isa 53:12)
- Onlookers thought the sufferer was stricken and smitten by God, afflicted for his own guilt (Isa 53:4)
- All we like sheep have gone astray, each to his own way, and God laid on him the iniquity of us all (Isa 53:6)
- The sufferer does not open his mouth, like a lamb led to slaughter and a ewe silent before its shearers (Isa 53:7)
- The servant is taken away by oppression and judgment and cut off from the land of the living (Isa 53:8)
- The servant's grave is set with the wicked and with a rich man in his death, though he did no violence (Isa 53:9)
- The servant's life is made a guilt offering (asham) (Isa 53:10)
- After his death the servant will see offspring, prolong his days and see light (Isa 53:10, Isa 53:11)
- The righteous servant will make many righteous and bear their iniquities (Isa 53:11)
- The servant poured out his life to death, was numbered with transgressors, bore the sin of many and interceded for them (Isa 53:12)

**Sing, barren one; covenant of peace; city of jewels**
- 'Sing, barren one': the desolate woman will have more children than the married one (Isa 54:1)
- Zion told to enlarge her tent, lengthen its cords and strengthen its pegs for her expanding offspring (Isa 54:2, Isa 54:3)
- God is Israel's husband and maker, who takes back the forsaken wife of youth (Isa 54:5, Isa 54:6)
- God hid his face or forsook his people for a brief moment but gathers them with everlasting compassion (Isa 54:7, Isa 54:8)
- God swears never again to be angry with Zion as he swore the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth (Isa 54:9)
- Mountains may depart and hills totter, but God's steadfast love and covenant of peace will not depart (Isa 54:10)
- The restored city is built of precious stones: sapphire foundations, ruby battlements, gates of carbuncle (Isa 54:11, Isa 54:12)
- All your children shall be taught by YHWH (Isa 54:13)
- God declares he created the smith who forges weapons and the destroyer who ravages (Isa 54:16)
- No weapon formed against Zion shall prosper and every accusing tongue will be condemned (Isa 54:17)

**Ho, everyone who thirsts; the word that does not return empty**
- Invitation: all who thirst come to the waters and buy wine and milk without money (Isa 55:1, Isa 55:2)
- Nations Israel did not know will run to her for the sake of her God (Isa 55:5)
- Seek YHWH while he may be found, call on him while he is near; let the wicked forsake his way (Isa 55:6, Isa 55:7)
- God's word is like rain and snow that do not return to heaven without watering the earth; it does not return empty (Isa 55:10, Isa 55:11)
- In the restoration cypress grows instead of thorn and myrtle instead of brier (Isa 55:13)

**Eunuchs and foreigners in God's house of prayer**
- Keeping the Sabbath from profanation marks the one who holds fast to God's covenant (Isa 56:2, Isa 56:4, Isa 56:6)
- Foreigners who join themselves to YHWH and keep the Sabbath are accepted at his altar (Isa 56:3, Isa 56:6, Isa 56:7)
- 'My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples' (Isa 56:7)

**Blind watchmen, mute dogs; the righteous taken away**
- The righteous man perishes and is taken away before the calamity, entering peace and resting on his bed (Isa 57:1, Isa 57:2)

**Sons of the sorceress - cult under every green tree**
- The idolatrous people addressed as children of a sorceress, seed of an adulterer and a harlot (Isa 57:3, Isa 57:4)
- Worshipers slaughter children in the wadis under the clefts of the rocks (Isa 57:5)
- Libations and offerings poured to the smooth stones of the wadi, 'your portion and your lot' (Isa 57:6)
- The apostate woman sets her bed on a high mountain and enlarges it for her lovers (cultic harlotry) (Isa 57:7, Isa 57:8)
- Apostates set their memorial sign (zikkaron) behind the door and doorpost, a perverted mezuzah (Isa 57:8)
- The apostate travels to 'the king' (Melek/Molech) with oil and perfumes and sends envoys down to Sheol (Isa 57:9)

**The high and lofty One dwells with the contrite**
- The high and lofty One who inhabits eternity dwells also with the crushed and lowly in spirit to revive them (Isa 57:15)
- God will not contend forever nor always be angry, for the spirits and breaths he made would faint (Isa 57:16)
- God creates the fruit of the lips: 'Peace, peace to the far and to the near' (Isa 57:19)
- The wicked are like the tossing sea that cannot rest, whose waters cast up mire and mud (Isa 57:20)

**The fast that God chooses; the Sabbath a delight**
- The prophet is told to cry aloud and lift his voice like a ram's horn (Isa 58:1)
- When the righteous call, God answers 'Here I am' (hinneni) (Isa 58:9)
- The righteous become like a watered garden and a spring whose waters never fail (Isa 58:11)
- The restorer is called 'repairer of the breach, restorer of paths to dwell in' (Isa 58:12)
- Call the Sabbath a delight (oneg), refraining from one's own business and idle talk on it (Isa 58:13, Isa 58:14)

**Your sins have separated you; God arms himself**
- Not God's weakness but the people's sins separate them from God and hide his face (Isa 59:2)
- The people's hands are defiled with blood and their fingers with iniquity (Isa 59:3)
- The wicked hatch vipers' eggs: whoever eats them dies, and a crushed one hatches a viper (Isa 59:5)
- Their feet run to evil and hasten to shed innocent blood (Isa 59:7, Isa 59:8)
- The people growl like bears and moan like doves as they wait for justice (Isa 59:11)
- Truth stumbles in the public square and uprightness cannot enter; whoever turns from evil is plundered (Isa 59:14, Isa 59:15)
- God puts on righteousness as a breastplate, the helmet of salvation, garments of vengeance and zeal as a cloak (Isa 59:17)
- A redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression (Isa 59:20)
- God's covenant: his spirit and the words in the mouth will not depart from the mouth of the offspring forever (Isa 59:21)

**Arise, shine - the nations come to Zion's light**
- Zion told 'Arise, shine, for your light has come': darkness covers the earth but God's glory rises on her (Isa 60:1, Isa 60:2)
- Camel caravans of Midian, Ephah and Sheba bring gold and frankincense (Isa 60:6)
- 'Who are these that fly like a cloud, like doves to their windows?' (Isa 60:8)
- The gates of the restored city stand open day and night and are never shut (Isa 60:11)
- In the restoration God brings gold instead of bronze, silver instead of iron, bronze instead of wood (Isa 60:17)
- The sun and moon will no longer be needed for light; God himself will be everlasting light (Isa 60:19, Isa 60:20)
- 'I YHWH will hasten it in its time': the timing of redemption (Isa 60:22)

**The spirit of the Lord is upon me**
- 'The spirit of the Lord is upon me because he anointed me to bring good news to the poor and bind up the brokenhearted' (Isa 61:1)
- Mourners of Zion given a garland instead of ashes, oil of joy instead of mourning, a mantle of praise (Isa 61:3)
- Strangers tend Israel's flocks and vineyards while Israel is called priests and ministers of God (Isa 61:5, Isa 61:6)
- God clothes the speaker in garments of salvation and a robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom with a priestly headdress or a bride with jewels (Isa 61:10)
- As earth brings forth its sprouts and a garden its seeds, God makes righteousness and praise sprout (Isa 61:11)

**Hephzibah and Beulah - Zion's new name**
- Zion will be a crown of beauty and royal diadem in the hand of God (Isa 62:3)
- The land is called 'Married' (Beulah) and God rejoices over Zion as a bridegroom over a bride (Isa 62:4, Isa 62:5)
- Watchmen set on Jerusalem's walls never fall silent, reminding God and giving him no rest until he restores her (Isa 62:6, Isa 62:7)
- God swears his people's grain and wine will no longer be eaten by enemies but by those who toiled (Isa 62:8, Isa 62:9)
- 'Behold your salvation comes; his reward is with him and his recompense before him' (Isa 62:11)

**Who is this coming from Edom? The winepress of wrath**
- A figure in crimson garments marches from Edom and Bozrah, mighty to save (Isa 63:1)
- God treads the nations alone in the winepress of his wrath and their juice spatters his garments (Isa 63:2, Isa 63:3, Isa 63:6)

**Remembering the days of Moses - O that you would rend the heavens**
- In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them (Isa 63:9)
- God led his people through the deeps like a horse in the wilderness, like cattle going down to a valley, the spirit giving rest (Isa 63:11, Isa 63:12, Isa 63:13, Isa 63:14)
- 'You are our father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us' (Isa 63:16, Isa 64:7)
- Lament asking why God makes his people stray from his ways and hardens their heart (Isa 63:17)
- 'O that you would rend the heavens and come down, that the mountains would quake at your presence' (Isa 63:19, Isa 64:1, Isa 64:2)
- No ear has heard and no eye has seen any God besides you who acts for those who wait for him (Isa 64:3)
- All our righteous deeds are like a menstrual cloth; we wither like a leaf and our iniquities carry us off like wind (Isa 64:5)

**Found by those who did not seek; rebels and servants**
- God says he let himself be sought and found by those who did not ask for him, saying 'Here I am' to a nation that did not call his name (Isa 65:1)
- God spread out his hands all day to a rebellious people (Isa 65:2)
- Apostates sacrifice in gardens and burn incense on bricks (Isa 65:3)
- Apostates sit in tombs and spend the night in hidden places (necromantic incubation) (Isa 65:4)
- Apostates say 'Keep to yourself, do not come near me, for I am holier than you' (Isa 65:5)
- As one says of a grape cluster with juice 'Do not destroy it, there is blessing in it', so God spares a remnant for his servants' sake (Isa 65:8, Isa 65:9)
- Apostates spread a table for Gad (Fortune) and fill mixed wine for Meni (Destiny) (Isa 65:11, Isa 65:12)
- Reversal: God's servants eat, drink and rejoice while the apostates hunger, thirst and are shamed (Isa 65:13, Isa 65:14)
- God called 'the God of Amen' (Elohei Amen) by whom people bless and swear (Isa 65:16)

**New heavens and a new earth**
- God creates Jerusalem a joy; the sound of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her (Isa 65:18, Isa 65:19)
- In the new age no infant dies in days and one who dies at a hundred is counted a youth (Isa 65:20)
- People will build houses and live in them, plant vineyards and eat their fruit, and not labor for others (Isa 65:21, Isa 65:22, Isa 65:23)
- Before they call God will answer; while they are still speaking he will hear (Isa 65:24)

**Heaven is my throne; sacrifice as abomination**
- 'Heaven is my throne and earth my footstool: what house could you build for me?' (Isa 66:1, Isa 66:2)
- God looks to the poor and contrite in spirit who trembles at his word (Isa 66:2, Isa 66:5)
- Hypocritical sacrifice is equated with crimes: slaughtering an ox is like killing a man, offering a lamb like breaking a dog's neck (Isa 66:3)
- The faithful are hated and cast out by their own brothers for God's name's sake (Isa 66:5)
- A tumult from the city, a voice from the temple: the voice of YHWH repaying his enemies (Isa 66:6)

**Zion gives birth in a day; comforted like a child by its mother**
- Zion gives birth before her labor pains: a land born in a day, a nation at once (Isa 66:7, Isa 66:8)
- Zion's children suck and are satisfied at her consoling breasts, carried on the hip and dandled on the knees (Isa 66:11, Isa 66:12)
- Your bones will flourish like the grass (Isa 66:14)

**Judgment by fire, ingathering of nations, the undying worm**
- God comes in fire with chariots like a whirlwind to judge all flesh by fire and sword (Isa 66:15, Isa 66:16)
- Those who sanctify themselves for the gardens, following one in the middle, eat swine, abominations and mice (Isa 66:17)
- God gathers all nations and tongues to come and see his glory (Isa 66:18)
- God sends survivors to distant nations (Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan, the far islands) to declare his glory (Isa 66:19)
- The nations bring all Israel's brothers to Jerusalem as an offering on horses, chariots, litters, mules and dromedaries (Isa 66:20)
- God will take some of the nations as priests and Levites (Isa 66:21)
- From new moon to new moon and Sabbath to Sabbath all flesh comes to worship before God (Isa 66:23)
- Corpses of the rebels whose worm does not die and fire is not quenched, an abhorrence to all flesh (Isa 66:24)

**Jeremiah's call - known before the womb, words in his mouth**
- God (or a seraph) touches the prophet's mouth or lips to commission him (Jer 1:9)

**Visions of the almond branch and the boiling pot**
- Vision of an almond branch (shaqed) explained as God watching (shoqed) over his word (Jer 1:11, Jer 1:12)
- Vision of a boiling pot tilted from the north, signifying disaster poured out from the north (Jer 1:13, Jer 1:14)

**The bride of the wilderness; broken cisterns**
- God remembers Israel's devotion as a bride who followed him in the wilderness, a land not sown (Jer 2:2)
- Israel was holy to YHWH, the firstfruits of his harvest; all who ate of it incurred guilt (Jer 2:3)
- The heavens are called to be appalled and shudder at the people's apostasy (Jer 2:12)

**Degenerate vine, she-camel in heat, gods of wood and stone**
- God planted a choice vine of pure seed, but it turned into a degenerate foreign vine (Jer 2:21)
- Apostate people likened to a restless young she-camel and a wild ass in heat sniffing the wind (Jer 2:23, Jer 2:24)
- Idolaters say to a tree 'You are my father' and to a stone 'You gave birth to me' (Jer 2:27)
- 'Can a virgin forget her ornaments or a bride her sash?' yet my people have forgotten me (Jer 2:32)
- A shamed person goes out with hands on the head (Jer 2:37)

**Can a divorced wife return? Faithless Israel, treacherous Judah**
- The apostate people sat waiting for lovers by the roads like an Arab in the wilderness (Jer 3:2)
- Two sister nations (Israel and Judah) are both unfaithful wives; the second fails to learn from the first's divorce (Jer 3:6, Jer 3:7, Jer 3:8, Jer 3:10, Jer 3:11)
- God will take the returnees 'one from a city and two from a family' and bring them to Zion (Jer 3:14)
- In the future the ark of the covenant will no longer be spoken of, remembered, missed or made again (Jer 3:16)
- Jerusalem will be called the throne of YHWH and all nations will gather to it (Jer 3:17)
- The houses of Judah and Israel will walk together and come from the land of the north (Jer 3:18)

**If you return - circumcise your hearts**
- 'Break up your fallow ground and do not sow among thorns' as a call to repentance (Jer 4:3)

**Alarm - disaster from the north**
- The invading destroyer of nations comes up like a lion from its thicket (Jer 4:7)
- The prophet protests that God has utterly deceived the people by promising peace (Jer 4:10)
- The invader comes up like clouds, his chariots like a whirlwind and horses swifter than eagles (Jer 4:11, Jer 4:12, Jer 4:13)

**My bowels, my bowels - the vision of uncreation**
- The people are foolish children, skilled in doing evil but not knowing how to do good (Jer 4:22)
- Vision of the earth returned to tohu va-vohu: no light in the heavens, mountains quaking, no humans, birds fled (Jer 4:23, Jer 4:24, Jer 4:25, Jer 4:26)
- The doomed city dresses in scarlet, gold ornaments and eye paint, but her lovers despise her and seek her life (Jer 4:30)

**Search Jerusalem for one just man**
- Search the streets for a single man who does justice and seeks truth, and God will pardon the city (Jer 5:1)
- The prophet thinks only the poor are ignorant, but finds the great have broken the yoke too (Jer 5:4, Jer 5:5)
- A lion from the forest, a wolf of the desert and a leopard watching the cities attack the sinners (Jer 5:6)

**Strip her vines - a nation whose tongue you do not know**
- The people deny God: 'It is not he; no evil will come on us; the prophets are wind' (Jer 5:12, Jer 5:13)

**The sea's sand boundary; houses full of deceit**
- The wicked lie in wait like fowlers setting traps; their houses are full of deceit like a cage full of birds (Jer 5:26, Jer 5:27)

**Sanctify war against her - the siege**
- The attackers 'sanctify war' (qaddeshu milhamah) against the city and plan a noon or night assault (Jer 6:4, Jer 6:5)
- Besiegers cut down trees and pour out a siege ramp against the city (Jer 6:6)
- As a well keeps its water fresh, so the city keeps its wickedness fresh (Jer 6:7)

**Glean the remnant; peace, peace, when there is no peace**
- Glean the remnant of Israel thoroughly as a vine; pass your hand again over the branches like a grape-gatherer (Jer 6:9)
- The people's ears are uncircumcised so that they cannot listen (Jer 6:10)

**Ask for the ancient paths; incense from Sheba rejected**
- God set watchmen to sound the shofar, but the people refused to listen (Jer 6:17)
- God himself lays stumbling blocks before the people, and fathers and sons stumble together (Jer 6:21)

**A cruel people from the north; the prophet as assayer**
- The prophet is set as assayer of the people; the bellows blow and lead is consumed in vain: rejected silver (Jer 6:27, Jer 6:28, Jer 6:29, Jer 6:30)

**The temple sermon - a den of robbers; remember Shiloh**
- Do not trust deceptive words: 'The temple of YHWH, the temple of YHWH, the temple of YHWH are these' (Jer 7:4, Jer 7:8, Jer 7:10)
- God's house has become 'a den of robbers' in the people's eyes (Jer 7:11)

**Obedience not sacrifice; the Topheth becomes the Valley of Slaughter**
- God sarcastically tells the people to add their burnt offerings to their sacrifices and eat the meat (Jer 7:21)
- God says he did not command the fathers about burnt offerings and sacrifices when he brought them out of Egypt, but obedience (Jer 7:22, Jer 7:23)
- Jerusalem told to cut off her hair (nezer) and throw it away and raise a lament on the bare heights (Jer 7:29)
- The bones of kings, priests, prophets and people will be taken from their graves and spread before the sun, moon and host of heaven they loved (Jer 8:1, Jer 8:2)
- The surviving remnant will choose death rather than life (Jer 8:3)

**The stork knows its seasons; the lying pen of the scribes**
- The stork, turtledove, swift and crane know their seasons of migration, but God's people do not know his law (Jer 8:7)
- When God comes to gather there are no grapes on the vine and no figs on the fig tree; the leaf withers (Jer 8:13)

**Is there no balm in Gilead? The prophet's tears**
- The exiled people cry 'Is YHWH not in Zion? Is her King not in her?' (Jer 8:19)
- 'The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved' (Jer 8:20)

**Every brother a Jacob - tongues like bows**
- The prophet wishes he had a wayfarers' lodge in the desert to leave his people (Jer 9:1)
- Trust no brother, for every brother is a supplanter ('aqov ya'qov, playing on Jacob) and every friend a slanderer (Jer 9:3, Jer 9:4, Jer 9:5)

**Summon the keening women - death has climbed in at our windows**
- The land is so desolate that both birds of the sky and beasts have fled and gone (Jer 9:9)
- Death has climbed in through our windows and entered our palaces, cutting off children from the street (Jer 9:20)

**Let not the wise boast; circumcised yet uncircumcised**
- Let not the wise boast of wisdom, the mighty of might or the rich of riches, but of understanding and knowing God (Jer 9:22, Jer 9:23)
- God will punish all circumcised who are uncircumcised: Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab and the desert-dwellers, and Israel uncircumcised in heart (Jer 9:24, Jer 9:25)

**Idols like scarecrows in a cucumber field**
- Do not learn the way of the nations or be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, at which the nations are dismayed (Jer 10:2)
- Idols are like a scarecrow in a cucumber field: they cannot speak and must be carried because they cannot walk (Jer 10:5)
- God addressed as 'King of the nations' whom all must fear (Jer 10:7)

**He made the earth by his power - the Portion of Jacob**
- God made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom and stretched out the heavens by his understanding (Jer 10:12)
- Not like these is the Portion of Jacob, for he is the former of all things (Jer 10:16)

**Pack your bundle; my tent is destroyed; a man cannot direct his steps**
- The besieged inhabitant is told to gather up her bundle from the ground, for God will sling out the inhabitants (Jer 10:17, Jer 10:18)
- Zion laments: my tent is destroyed, my cords snapped, my children gone, and no one to pitch my tent again (Jer 10:19, Jer 10:20)
- A man's way is not in himself; it is not in the one who walks to direct his steps (Jer 10:23)

**Cursed is the man who does not hear this covenant**
- 'Cursed is the man who does not hear the words of this covenant', answered with 'Amen' (Jer 11:3, Jer 11:5, Jer 11:8)
- God named his people 'a green olive tree, fair with goodly fruit', but sets fire to it and its branches are broken (Jer 11:16, Jer 11:17)

**First confession - a gentle lamb led to slaughter; the men of Anathoth**
- The prophet was like a gentle lamb led to slaughter, not knowing they plotted 'Let us destroy the tree with its fruit' (Jer 11:19)

**Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Running with horses**
- The prophet acknowledges God is righteous yet would argue his case with him about justice (Jer 12:1)
- 'If you have run with footmen and they wearied you, how will you compete with horses?' and the thickets of the Jordan (Jer 12:5)
- Even the prophet's brothers and father's house deal treacherously with him; do not trust their fair words (Jer 12:6)

**I have forsaken my house; the speckled bird of prey**
- God says 'I have forsaken my house, abandoned my heritage, given the beloved of my soul into the enemy's hands' (Jer 12:7, Jer 12:8)
- God's heritage is like a speckled bird of prey (or hyena) attacked by birds all around (Jer 12:9)
- Many shepherds have destroyed God's vineyard and trampled his portion into a desolate wilderness (Jer 12:10, Jer 12:11)
- They sowed wheat and reaped thorns; they toiled without profit (Jer 12:13)
- God will uproot the evil neighbor nations, then have compassion and plant them among his people if they learn to swear 'as YHWH lives' (Jer 12:14, Jer 12:15, Jer 12:16, Jer 12:17)

**Symbolic act - the ruined linen loincloth**
- The prophet buries a new linen loincloth by the Perath (Euphrates) in a cleft of the rock; dug up later it is ruined and good for nothing (Jer 13:1, Jer 13:4, Jer 13:7)
- As a loincloth clings to a man's loins, God made Israel and Judah cling to him to be his people, name and glory (Jer 13:9, Jer 13:10, Jer 13:11)

**Every jar shall be filled with wine**
- 'Every jar is filled with wine': God will fill all the inhabitants with drunkenness and smash them against one another (Jer 13:12, Jer 13:13, Jer 13:14)

**Before darkness comes; can the Cushite change his skin?**
- Give glory to God before he brings darkness and your feet stumble on the twilight mountains (Jer 13:15, Jer 13:16)
- 'Can the Cushite change his skin or the leopard its spots?' so neither can those accustomed to evil do good (Jer 13:23)

**The drought - the doe forsakes her fawn; lying prophets**
- In drought nobles send servants for water who find the cisterns dry and return with empty vessels, heads covered in shame (Jer 14:3, Jer 14:4)
- In drought the doe abandons her newborn fawn and wild asses pant for air like jackals, their eyes failing (Jer 14:5, Jer 14:6)
- Lament asks why God is like a stranger in the land, a traveler stopping for a night, a stunned warrior who cannot save (Jer 14:8, Jer 14:9)

**Though Moses and Samuel stood before me**
- Those destined for death to death, for the sword to the sword, for famine to famine, for captivity to captivity (Jer 15:2)
- God appoints four kinds of destroyers: the sword to kill, dogs to drag, birds and beasts to devour (Jer 15:3)
- God says 'I am weary of relenting' (nil'eti hinnahem) (Jer 15:6)
- She who bore seven languishes and breathes out her life; her sun goes down while it is still day (Jer 15:8, Jer 15:9)

**Second confession - woe that my mother bore me; your words I ate**
- The prophet found God's words and ate them, and they became his joy (Jer 15:16)
- The prophet did not sit in the company of merrymakers but sat alone because of God's hand (Jer 15:17)
- The prophet accuses God of being to him like a deceitful brook, waters that fail (Jer 15:18)
- If the prophet returns and brings out the precious from the worthless, he will be as God's mouth (Jer 15:19)

**Symbolic acts - no wife, no mourning, no feasting**
- God forbids the prophet to take a wife or have children in this place, as a sign of the doom of parents and children (Jer 16:2, Jer 16:3, Jer 16:4)
- God forbids the prophet to enter a house of mourning or a house of feasting, as a sign that both will cease (Jer 16:5, Jer 16:8)
- The 'house of the marzeah' (beit marzeah), a house of ritual feasting associated with mourning the dead (Jer 16:5)
- Mourners are given bread broken for them and a 'cup of consolation' for father or mother (Jer 16:7)

**A new exodus from the north; fishers and hunters**
- God sends many fishers to fish them out and then many hunters to hunt them from every mountain and cleft of rock (Jer 16:16)

**Sin engraved with an iron pen**
- Judah's sin is written with an iron pen and a diamond point, engraved on the tablet of their heart and the horns of their altars (Jer 17:1)

**Cursed who trusts in man, blessed who trusts in YHWH; the deceitful heart**
- Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm; he is like a juniper in the desert, in a salt land (Jer 17:5, Jer 17:6)
- The heart is deceitful ('aqov) above all things and desperately sick; who can know it? (Jer 17:9)
- Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay is one who gets riches unjustly; he will leave them in the middle of his days (Jer 17:11)
- 'A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary' (Jer 17:12)
- Those who turn away from God will be written in the earth (or dust), for they forsook the fountain of living water (Jer 17:13)

**Third confession - heal me and I shall be healed**
- 'Heal me, YHWH, and I shall be healed; save me and I shall be saved' (Jer 17:14)

**Carry no burden on the Sabbath day**
- Carrying burdens through the city gates or out of houses on the Sabbath is forbidden (Jer 17:21, Jer 17:22, Jer 17:24, Jer 17:27)
- If the Sabbath is kept, Davidic kings will enter the gates and the city will be inhabited forever; if not, fire will consume its gates (Jer 17:25, Jer 17:26, Jer 17:27)

**At the potter's house - conditional prophecy**
- The prophet watches a potter at the wheel rework a spoiled vessel into another: so God can do with Israel as clay (Jer 18:2, Jer 18:3, Jer 18:4, Jer 18:6)
- If a nation God threatened turns from evil he relents of the evil; if a nation he promised to build does evil he relents of the good (Jer 18:7, Jer 18:8, Jer 18:9, Jer 18:10)

**Does the snow leave Lebanon? A land for hissing**
- Does the snow of Lebanon leave the crags, or do the cold flowing waters dry up? yet my people have forgotten me (Jer 18:14, Jer 18:15)
- God will show the people his back and not his face in the day of their calamity (Jer 18:17)

**Fourth confession - let us smite him with the tongue**
- 'Torah shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet' (Jer 18:18)
- Enemies dig a pit and hide snares for the righteous one who once interceded for them (Jer 18:20, Jer 18:22)

**Pashhur puts Jeremiah in the stocks - Terror on Every Side**
- The prophet gives his persecutor an ominous new name announcing his fate (Jer 20:3)

**Fifth confession - you enticed me; fire shut up in my bones**
- The prophet complains 'You enticed (pittitani) me, YHWH, and I was enticed; you overpowered me and prevailed' (Jer 20:7)

**Cursed be the day I was born**
- The sufferer curses the man who brought his father the news 'A son is born to you' (Jer 20:15, Jer 20:16)

**Zedekiah's inquiry - the way of life and the way of death**
- The besieged king sends to ask the prophet to inquire of God, hoping God will do a wonder and make the enemy withdraw (Jer 21:1, Jer 21:2)
- God himself fights against his own people with outstretched hand and mighty arm, turning their weapons back (Jer 21:4, Jer 21:5)
- Whoever stays in the city will die, but whoever goes out and surrenders to the besiegers will live, his life as spoil (Jer 21:9)

**To the house of David - judge in the morning**
- The royal house is told to execute justice in the morning and rescue the robbed from the oppressor (Jer 21:12)
- The city that sits in the valley says 'Who can come down against us, who can enter our dwellings?' (Jer 21:13)

**Weep for the one who goes away - Shallum**
- Do not weep for the dead but weep bitterly for him who goes away, for he will never return to see his native land (Jer 22:10)

**Woe to him who builds his house by injustice - Jehoiakim**
- Woe to the king who builds his palace by injustice, making his neighbor work for nothing, with cedar paneling and vermilion paint (Jer 22:13, Jer 22:14)
- The good king judged the cause of the poor and needy: 'Is not this to know me?' says YHWH (Jer 22:15, Jer 22:16)

**Cry from Lebanon; Coniah the signet ring torn off**
- Even if the king were the signet ring on God's right hand, God would tear him off (Jer 22:24)
- 'Write this man down as childless': none of his seed will sit on David's throne (Jer 22:30)

**Woe to the shepherds; the righteous Branch**
- Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of God's pasture; God will attend to their evil deeds (Jer 23:1, Jer 23:2)

**Concerning the prophets - who has stood in the council of YHWH?**
- The prophet's heart is broken and all his bones shake; he is like a drunken man because of God's holy words (Jer 23:9)
- The prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and strengthen evildoers; they have become like Sodom and Gomorrah (Jer 23:11, Jer 23:13, Jer 23:14)

**A God near and far; dreams versus the word like a hammer**
- False prophets say 'I have dreamed, I have dreamed'; what has straw to do with wheat? (Jer 23:25, Jer 23:26, Jer 23:27, Jer 23:28, Jer 23:32)
- God's word is like a hammer that shatters rock (Jer 23:29)
- God is against the prophets who steal his words from one another and wag their tongues saying 'oracle' (Jer 23:30, Jer 23:31)

**What is the burden of YHWH?**
- When asked 'What is the burden (massa) of YHWH?' the prophet answers 'You are the burden, and I will cast you off'; the phrase is banned (Jer 23:33, Jer 23:34, Jer 23:36, Jer 23:38, Jer 23:39)

**Vision of the two baskets of figs**
- Vision of two baskets of figs before the temple, very good and very bad: the exiles in Babylon are the good, those left behind the bad (Jer 24:1, Jer 24:2, Jer 24:5, Jer 24:8)
- God will give the people a heart to know him, and they will return to him with their whole heart (Jer 24:7)

**Twenty-three years of warning; seventy years of servitude**
- A prophecy dated by synchronizing an Israelite king's year with a foreign king's (fourth of Jehoiakim = first of Nebuchadrezzar) (Jer 25:1)
- Reference to 'all that is written in this book which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations' (Jer 25:13)

**The cup of the wine of wrath for all nations; Sheshach**
- The prophet makes a long list of nations and kings drink the cup of God's wrath, beginning with Jerusalem (Jer 25:18, Jer 25:19, Jer 25:20, Jer 25:21, Jer 25:22, Jer 25:23, Jer 25:24, Jer 25:25, Jer 25:26)
- Babylon referred to by the cipher 'Sheshach' (atbash substitution of the alphabet) (Jer 25:26)
- If God begins to bring evil on the city called by his name, shall the nations go unpunished? (Jer 25:29)

**YHWH roars from on high; the shepherds wail**
- Shepherds and lords of the flock wail and roll in ashes, for their days of slaughter have come and there is no escape (Jer 25:34, Jer 25:35, Jer 25:36, Jer 25:37)
- God has left his covert like a lion; the land is a waste before the fury of the oppressor (or 'the dove') (Jer 25:38)

**Jeremiah tried for prophesying the temple will become like Shiloh; Uriah executed**
- The Jerusalem temple will be made like ruined Shiloh (Jer 26:6, Jer 26:9)
- A prophet is put on trial for capital charges because of his oracle (Jer 26:8, Jer 26:11, Jer 26:16)
- Royal officials sit at the entrance of the New Gate to judge the prophet (Jer 26:10)
- Killing the innocent prophet will bring innocent blood upon the city and its people (Jer 26:15)
- Elders cite an earlier prophet's unharmed oracle of doom as precedent for sparing a prophet (Jer 26:17-19)
- A prophet flees to Egypt but is brought back by the king's men and executed (Jer 26:20-23)
- A king or people kills a prophet of God (Jer 26:23)
- The executed man's body is thrown into the graves of the common people (Jer 26:23)
- A powerful official protects the prophet from the mob (Jer 26:24)

**Jeremiah wears yoke bars and sends them to the envoys of five kings**
- The prophet wears a yoke on his neck as a sign of submission to the empire (Jer 27:2, Jer 27:8, Jer 27:11-12)
- The prophet sends a message to the neighboring kings through their envoys in Jerusalem (Jer 27:3)
- The creator of earth, humans and beasts gives dominion to whomever he sees fit (Jer 27:5)
- All nations will serve the conqueror, his son and his grandson until his land's own time comes (Jer 27:7)
- List of prophets, diviners, dreamers, soothsayers and sorcerers who give false assurance (Jer 27:9)
- True prophets would intercede with God; the false do not (Jer 27:18)

**Hananiah breaks the wooden yoke and dies within the year**
- Two prophets publicly contradict each other's oracles (Jer 28:1-11)
- A prophet promises the exiles and temple vessels will return within two years (Jer 28:3, Jer 28:11)
- The prophet answers a rival's optimistic oracle with 'Amen, may YHWH do so' (Jer 28:6)
- A prophet who prophesies peace is known as truly sent only when his word comes true (Jer 28:8-9)
- A rival prophet breaks the prophet's sign-object as a counter-sign (Jer 28:10-11)
- The broken wooden yoke will be replaced by a yoke of iron (Jer 28:13-14)
- A false prophet dies within the year as the true prophet foretold (Jer 28:16-17)

**Letter to the exiles; seventy years; Ahab and Zedekiah roasted; Shemaiah's counter-letter**
- The prophet sends a letter to the exiles in a foreign land (Jer 29:1, Jer 29:3)
- The king is deported with the queen mother, eunuchs, officials and craftsmen (Jer 29:2)
- Exiles told to build houses, plant gardens, marry and multiply in the foreign land (Jer 29:5-6, Jer 29:28)
- Exiles told to seek the welfare of the foreign city and pray to God for it (Jer 29:7)
- You will seek me and find me when you seek me with all your heart (Jer 29:12-14)
- Those remaining are made like rotten figs too bad to eat (Jer 29:17)
- Lying prophets are roasted in fire by a foreign king and become a byword in curses (Jer 29:21-22)
- God is the one who knows and is witness against secret sins (Jer 29:23)
- A rival prophet in exile writes letters demanding that the prophet be silenced (Jer 29:24-29)
- A false prophet's descendants will be cut off and he will not see the coming good (Jer 29:32)

**Book of Consolation opens; men in labor; Jacob's trouble; incurable wound healed**
- Men clutch their loins like women in labor and every face turns pale (Jer 30:6)
- A great day of distress unlike any other, 'the time of Jacob's trouble', from which he will be saved (Jer 30:7)
- God will raise up 'David their king' for the restored people (Jer 30:9, Jer 30:21)
- Zion's wound is incurable, with no healing and no one to plead her cause (Jer 30:12-15, Jer 30:17)
- The city will be rebuilt on its own ruin-mound and the palace stand in its place (Jer 30:18)
- The future ruler will draw near to God, for who would risk his life to approach unbidden? (Jer 30:21)

**Return of Ephraim, Rachel weeping in Ramah, sour grapes, the new covenant and the measured city**
- The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness (Jer 31:2)
- God has loved his people with an everlasting love and drawn them with faithfulness (Jer 31:3)
- Virgin Israel will again adorn herself with timbrels and go out in dances (Jer 31:4, Jer 31:13)
- Watchmen on Mount Ephraim call 'Arise, let us go up to Zion to YHWH' (Jer 31:6)
- The blind, the lame and women in labor are among the returning exiles (Jer 31:8)
- The returned people's life will be like a watered garden (Jer 31:12)
- Ephraim likens himself to an untrained calf, chastised, and slaps his thigh in repentance (Jer 31:18-19)
- God's innards yearn (hamu me'ai) with compassion for his wayward son (Jer 31:20)
- Set up road markers and guideposts for the returning exiles (Jer 31:21)
- God creates a new thing on earth: 'a female shall encompass a man' (Jer 31:22)
- The prophet awakes from a vision-sleep that was sweet to him (Jer 31:26)
- God will sow the house of Israel with seed of man and seed of beast (Jer 31:27)
- God will make a new covenant with Israel and Judah, unlike the one broken after the exodus (Jer 31:31-34)
- In the new age no one will need to teach his neighbor 'Know YHWH', for all will know him (Jer 31:34)
- God will forgive iniquity and remember sin no more (Jer 31:34)
- God who stirs up the sea so its waves roar (Jer 31:35)
- If the heavens above could be measured and the earth's foundations searched out, God would reject Israel (Jer 31:37)
- Even the valley of corpses and ashes will be holy to YHWH in the rebuilt city (Jer 31:40)

**Jeremiah buys his cousin's field at Anathoth during the siege**
- The prophet buys a family field during siege as a sign that land will again be bought (Jer 32:6-15, Jer 32:25, Jer 32:43-44)
- A field bought for seventeen shekels of silver (Jer 32:9)
- Deeds are put in an earthenware jar so they may last many days (Jer 32:14)
- God's eyes are open on all the ways of humanity to repay each by his deeds (Jer 32:19)
- Incense offered to Baal and libations to other gods on the roofs of houses (Jer 32:29)
- Sons and daughters passed through fire to Molech at the high places in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom (Jer 32:35)

**Healing of the city, the Righteous Branch and the covenant with day and night**
- God invites the prophet to call so he will reveal great and hidden things (Jer 33:3)
- God promises to bring healing and cure to the ruined city (Jer 33:6)
- The voice of the bridegroom and the bride will again be heard in the ruined land (Jer 33:10-11)
- Flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them in the towns of Judah (Jer 33:13)
- David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of Israel (Jer 33:17, Jer 33:21)
- The Levitical priests will never lack a man to offer sacrifice before God (Jer 33:18, Jer 33:21-22)
- God has a 'covenant with day and night' that fixes their order (Jer 33:20, Jer 33:25)
- People say God has rejected the two families he chose (Jer 33:24)

**Zedekiah's fate and the revoked release of slaves; the calf cut in two**
- Funeral cry 'Hoy, lord!' (alas, master) for a dead king (Jer 34:5)
- Lachish and Azekah are the last fortified cities of Judah holding out (Jer 34:7)
- Owners free their Hebrew slaves under covenant oath, then take them back (Jer 34:11, Jer 34:16)
- Because they revoked the slaves' release, God 'proclaims a release' for them to sword, pestilence and famine (Jer 34:17)

**The Rechabites refuse wine and are held up as a model of obedience**
- The Rechabites keep their ancestor's command never to drink wine (Jer 35:6-10, Jer 35:14)
- The prophet sets wine before abstainers in the temple and they refuse (Jer 35:2, Jer 35:5-6)
- A named chamber in the temple belonging to the sons of a 'man of God' (Jer 35:4)
- A family's faithful obedience to its ancestor's command shames the people who disobey God (Jer 35:13-16)
- Nomads take refuge in Jerusalem from invading armies (Jer 35:11)
- A family is promised that it will never lack a man to stand before God (Jer 35:19)

**Baruch reads the scroll; Jehoiakim cuts it with a penknife and burns it; it is rewritten**
- The prophet dictates God's words and a scribe writes them in a scroll (Jer 36:4, Jer 36:17-18, Jer 36:32)
- A prophetic scroll is read publicly in the temple on a fast day (Jer 36:6, Jer 36:9-10)
- Royal officials turn in fear to one another when the scroll is read to them (Jer 36:16)
- Sympathetic officials tell the prophet and his scribe to hide (Jer 36:19, Jer 36:26)
- The king cuts the prophetic scroll column by column with a scribe's knife and burns it in his brazier (Jer 36:22-23)
- The king and his servants hear the words of judgment and do not tear their garments (Jer 36:24)
- Some officials beg the king not to burn the scroll (Jer 36:25)
- A destroyed sacred book is rewritten from dictation with many words added (Jer 36:28, Jer 36:32)
- The king's corpse will be cast out to heat by day and frost by night (Jer 36:30)
- The king will have no descendant sitting on David's throne (Jer 36:30)

**Egyptian army withdraws; Jeremiah arrested as deserter and imprisoned; secret consultation**
- The conqueror installs a king of his choosing over the vassal kingdom (Jer 37:1)
- Pharaoh's relieving army will turn back home; reliance on Egypt fails (Jer 37:5-7, Jer 37:11)
- Even if only wounded men remained in the enemy camp they would rise and burn the city (Jer 37:10)
- The prophet leaving the city is arrested at the gate as a deserter to the enemy (Jer 37:13-14)
- Officials beat the prophet and imprison him in a dungeon (Jer 37:15-16)
- The imprisoned prophet receives a daily loaf from the bakers' street until bread runs out (Jer 37:21)

**Jeremiah sunk in the muddy cistern and rescued by Ebed-melech the Cushite**
- The king says he can do nothing against his officials and hands the prophet over (Jer 38:5)
- A foreign (Cushite) eunuch at court intercedes for and rescues the prophet (Jer 38:7-13)
- Worn-out rags are lowered for padding under the armpits as the prisoner is drawn up with ropes (Jer 38:11-12)
- Thirty men are sent to lift the prophet out of the pit before he dies (Jer 38:10)
- The king secretly swears to the prophet not to kill him or hand him over (Jer 38:16)
- The king's women led out to the conquerors sing a taunt that his friends deceived him (Jer 38:22)
- Someone's feet sink in the mud or mire (Jer 38:6, Jer 38:22)
- The king tells the prophet to hide what they discussed from the officials (Jer 38:24-27)

**Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety**
- The conquering Babylonian officers, named with their titles (Rab-saris, Rab-mag), sit in the city's Middle Gate (Jer 39:3, Jer 39:13)
- The foreign conqueror orders his officers to look after the prophet and do him no harm (Jer 39:11-14)
- A foreigner who helped the prophet is promised his life will be spared because he trusted God (Jer 39:15-18)

**Nebuzaradan releases Jeremiah; Gedaliah governs at Mizpah; warning of a plot**
- A foreign commander tells the prophet that his God brought this disaster for the people's sin (Jer 40:2-3)
- A captive's chains are removed by the captor (Jer 40:1, Jer 40:4)
- The released prophet is told he may come with the captor or go wherever he likes (Jer 40:4-5)
- The released captive is given food allowance and a present and sent on his way (Jer 40:5)
- The conqueror appoints a native governor over the remnant left in the land (Jer 40:5-7, Jer 40:11)
- Scattered refugees return from neighboring lands and gather an abundant harvest (Jer 40:11-12)
- A leader warned of an assassination plot refuses to believe it (Jer 40:13-16)

**Ishmael murders Gedaliah at table and slaughters eighty pilgrims into Asa's cistern**
- Guests eat bread with their host and then murder him (Jer 41:1-2)
- A member of the royal family carries out a political assassination (Jer 41:1)
- Mourning pilgrims with shaved beards, torn clothes and gashes bring offerings to the ruined temple (Jer 41:5)
- The murderer goes out weeping to lure his victims in (Jer 41:6)
- Victims' corpses are thrown into a cistern (Jer 41:7, Jer 41:9)
- Captives buy their lives by revealing hidden stores of wheat, barley, oil and honey (Jer 41:8)
- The king's daughters are taken captive (Jer 41:10)
- Rival forces meet at the great waters (pool) of Gibeon (Jer 41:12)

**The remnant asks for an oracle, rejects it and drags Jeremiah to Tahpanhes; stones hidden in the pavement**
- The people ask the prophet to pray for them and to tell them God's word (Jer 42:2-3, Jer 42:20)
- The people swear to obey whatever God answers, then reject the oracle (Jer 42:5-6, Jer 42:20-21, Jer 43:2-4)
- The prophet's answer from God comes only after ten days (Jer 42:7)
- God says he repents (nihamti) of the evil he did to his people (Jer 42:10)
- The remnant seeks safety in Egypt, where they think they will see no war nor hunger (Jer 42:14-17, Jer 42:22)
- The sword and famine they fear will overtake them in the very place they flee to (Jer 42:16)
- Opponents tell the prophet 'You are lying; God did not send you' (Jer 43:2-3)
- The prophet is taken down to Egypt against his counsel by the fleeing remnant (Jer 43:6-7)
- The prophet buries large stones in the pavement at Pharaoh's palace where the conqueror will set his throne (Jer 43:9-10)
- The conqueror will wrap (or pick clean) Egypt as a shepherd does his garment (Jer 43:12)
- The conqueror breaks the obelisks (matsevot) of Beth-shemesh/Heliopolis in Egypt (Jer 43:13)
- The conqueror will burn the temples of a foreign land's gods (Jer 43:12-13)

**The Judeans in Egypt defend their cult of the Queen of Heaven**
- Judeans settled in Egyptian cities: Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis and Pathros (Jer 44:1)
- Women bake cakes bearing the image of the goddess they worship (Jer 44:19)
- Women burn incense to a goddess, claiming they did so with their husbands' knowledge (Jer 44:15, Jer 44:19, Jer 44:25)
- Worshipers argue their goddess cult brought plenty and abandoning it brought disaster (Jer 44:17-18)
- The wickedness of the kings of Judah and of their wives (Jer 44:9)
- The prophet ironically tells idolaters to go ahead and fulfill their vows (Jer 44:25)
- God swears by his great name (Jer 44:26)
- God swears his name will no longer be invoked in oaths by apostates in a foreign land (Jer 44:26)
- Events will show whose word will stand, God's or the people's (Jer 44:28)
- Pharaoh Hophra will be handed over to those who seek his life (Jer 44:30)

**Oracle to Baruch: do not seek great things; your life as booty**
- The prophet's scribe laments that God has added sorrow to his pain and he finds no rest (Jer 45:3)
- The prophet's scribe is told not to seek great things for himself; his life will be his reward (Jer 45:5)

**Oracles against Egypt: Carchemish and Nebuchadnezzar's invasion**
- Egypt defeated by Babylon at Carchemish on the Euphrates (Jer 46:2, Jer 46:6, Jer 46:10)
- Ironic summons to an army to arm itself before its rout (Jer 46:3-4, Jer 46:9)
- Egypt rises like the Nile flood, boasting to cover the earth (Jer 46:7-8)
- Egypt's army includes Cushite, Putite and Ludite mercenaries (Jer 46:9)
- God's battle slaughter is called his sacrifice (zevah) (Jer 46:10)
- Egypt's 'mighty one' (abbir, read as the Apis bull) flees and is thrust down (Jer 46:15)
- Pharaoh is mockingly renamed 'Noise who let the appointed time pass' (Jer 46:17)
- The conqueror comes as Tabor among the mountains and Carmel by the sea (Jer 46:18)
- Egypt a beautiful heifer, a gadfly from the north coming upon her (Jer 46:20-21)
- Egypt's voice goes off like a hissing serpent (Jer 46:22)
- Invaders come with axes like woodcutters, more numerous than locusts (Jer 46:22-23)
- God punishes Amon of No (Thebes), Egypt's chief god (Jer 46:25)
- God punishes a nation's gods along with its king and people (Jer 46:25)
- After judgment a foreign land will be inhabited again as in former days (Jer 46:26)

**Oracle against the Philistines; the sword of the Lord addressed**
- Waters rise from the north and become an overflowing torrent (Jer 47:2)
- At the roar of chariots fathers do not turn back for their children (Jer 47:3)
- The prophet addresses the sword of YHWH: how long until you rest in your sheath? (Jer 47:6-7)

**Oracle against Moab: wine settled on its lees, Chemosh into exile**
- Long list of Moabite towns under judgment (Dibon, Nebo, Kiriathaim, Kerioth, Bozrah...) (Jer 48:1-5, Jer 48:18-24, Jer 48:34)
- Puns on the names of towns under judgment (Jer 48:2)
- Fugitives become like a juniper (or wild ass) in the desert (Jer 48:6)
- 'Give wings to Moab', for she must flee away (Jer 48:9)
- Cursed is he who does YHWH's work slackly and keeps his sword from blood (Jer 48:10)
- A nation at ease like wine settled on its lees, never poured from vessel to vessel (Jer 48:11-12)
- Lament: how the mighty staff, the glorious rod, is broken (Jer 48:17)
- A nation made drunk wallows in its vomit and becomes a laughing-stock (Jer 48:26)
- Refugees told to dwell in the rocks like a dove nesting in the sides of a gorge (Jer 48:28)
- The great pride, arrogance and haughtiness of Moab (Jer 48:29-30, Jer 48:42)
- The vine of Sibmah whose tendrils crossed the sea, now despoiled (Jer 48:32)
- The joyful 'hedad' shout of grape-treaders falls silent (Jer 48:33)
- The nation is broken like a vessel no one wants (Jer 48:38)

**Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Hazor, and Elam**
- Milcom (their 'king') dispossessed the tribe of Gad and will go into exile (Jer 49:1, Jer 49:3)
- Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's, God will bring you down (Jer 49:16)
- The cry at a nation's fall is heard as far as the Red Sea (Jer 49:21)
- Fire kindled in the wall of Damascus devours the palaces of Ben-hadad (Jer 49:27)
- Desert peoples described as those with the corners of their hair clipped (Jer 49:32)
- A people at ease that dwells alone with neither gates nor bars (Jer 49:31)
- God breaks the bow of Elam, the chief of their might (Jer 49:35)
- God brings the four winds from the four ends of heaven to scatter a people (Jer 49:36)
- God sets his own throne in a conquered foreign land (Jer 49:38)

**Oracle against Babylon (I): Bel and Merodach shamed, the hammer of the earth broken**
- Babylon's gods Bel and Merodach are put to shame and its idols dismayed (Jer 50:2)
- God's people are lost sheep whose shepherds led them astray on the mountains (Jer 50:6-7, Jer 50:17)
- Repay the city according to her deeds: do to her as she has done (Jer 50:15, Jer 50:29)
- Israel a scattered sheep: first Assyria devoured it, last Babylon gnawed its bones (Jer 50:17-18)
- Israel's iniquity will be sought and not found, for God pardons the remnant (Jer 50:20)
- Babylon addressed by wordplay names: Merathaim ('double rebellion') and Pekod ('punishment') (Jer 50:21)
- Babylon called the 'hammer of the whole earth' is broken (Jer 50:23)
- God opens his armory and brings out the weapons of his indignation (Jer 50:25)
- Repeated 'A sword upon...' litany against every class of a city (Jer 50:35-38)
- Babylon is a land of idols, mad over their terrors (Jer 50:38)

**Oracle against Babylon (II): golden cup, destroying mountain, Sheshach, the scroll sunk in the Euphrates**
- Names hidden by the atbash letter cipher (Sheshach for Babel, Leb-qamai for Kasdim) (Jer 51:1, Jer 51:41)
- God stirs up a destroying wind (or spirit) against the empire (Jer 51:1, Jer 51:11)
- Israel and Judah are not widowed of their God (Jer 51:5)
- Babylon is a golden cup in God's hand that made all the earth drunk (Jer 51:7)
- Ironic call to bring balm for a fallen city that cannot be healed (Jer 51:8-9)
- God stirs up the spirit of the kings of the Medes against Babylon (Jer 51:11, Jer 51:28)
- The doomed imperial city 'dwells on many waters' rich in treasures (Jer 51:13)
- 'The Portion of Jacob' is not like idols, but the former of all things (Jer 51:19)
- God calls a nation his war-club with which he shatters nations, horses, chariots and people (Jer 51:20-23)
- The empire as a 'destroying mountain' to be rolled down and made a burnt mountain (Jer 51:25-26)
- The northern kingdoms Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz are summoned against Babylon (Jer 51:27)
- Runner after runner and messenger after messenger bring the king news of his city's fall (Jer 51:31)
- The city is like a threshing floor at treading time; soon her harvest comes (Jer 51:33)
- The conqueror swallowed the city like a dragon (tannin) and filled his belly (Jer 51:34)
- God dries up Babylon's 'sea' and makes her fountain dry (Jer 51:36)
- God prepares a feast for the empire's leaders, makes them drunk, and they sleep an eternal sleep (Jer 51:39, Jer 51:57)
- The sea rises over Babylon and covers her with its roaring waves (Jer 51:42, Jer 51:55)
- God punishes Bel and makes him vomit out what he swallowed (Jer 51:44)
- Heaven and earth and all in them sing for joy over the empire's fall (Jer 51:48)
- Though Babylon should climb to heaven and fortify its height, destroyers will reach it (Jer 51:53)
- A scroll of oracles is tied to a stone and thrown into a river as a sign the city will sink (Jer 51:59-64)

**Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release**
- The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city (Jer 52:4)
- A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table (Jer 52:31-34)
- A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him (Jer 52:31)

**Lamentations 1: 'How lonely sits the city', Zion as a widow with no comforter**
- The ruined city sits alone like a widow (Lam 1:1)
- Refrain that the city has no one to comfort her (Lam 1:2, Lam 1:9, Lam 1:16-17, Lam 1:21)
- The princes became like deer that find no pasture and flee without strength (Lam 1:6)
- The fallen city is likened to a menstruant (niddah) whose impurity is in her skirts (Lam 1:8-9, Lam 1:17)
- The starving people trade their treasures for food to keep alive (Lam 1:11)
- 'Is it nothing to you, all who pass by? Look and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow' (Lam 1:12)
- From on high God sent fire into the sufferer's bones (Lam 1:13)
- God spread a net for the sufferer's feet and turned him back (Lam 1:13)
- The yoke of the sinner's transgressions is knotted by God's hand onto her neck (Lam 1:14)
- The Lord trod the virgin daughter of Judah as in a winepress (Lam 1:15)
- The sufferer confesses 'YHWH is righteous, for I rebelled against his word' (Lam 1:18)

**Lamentations 2: the Lord became like an enemy; children faint in the streets**
- God did not remember his footstool (Zion or the ark) on the day of his anger (Lam 2:1)
- God cast down the splendor of Israel from heaven to earth (Lam 2:1)
- Enemies raise a shout in the temple as on a festival day (Lam 2:7)
- There is no torah, and the prophets find no vision from YHWH (Lam 2:9)
- The mourner's liver is poured out on the ground (Lam 2:11)
- Infants and sucklings faint from hunger in the city squares, asking their mothers for bread and wine (Lam 2:11-12, Lam 2:19)
