- Compare 1 Kgs 20:30-34 (Ahab spares and releases Ben-hadad) and 1 Sam 15:8-9.
- Compare 2 Sam 10:2 and 1 Kgs 2:7 (kindness repaid to those who sheltered a fugitive king).
- Compare 1 Sam 2:7-8 and Ps 113:7 for 'he casts down, he raises up'.

**Gilgamesh and the Bull of Heaven (version 1): Inana detains Gilgamesh, obtains the Bull from An** (ETCSL 1.8.1.2 1.A:1-1.A:E, ETCSL 1.8.1.2 1.B:1-1.B:103)
- Compare Gilg SB VI (Ištar's proposal, the Bull of Heaven); Gen 39:7-12 (the hero refuses the advances of a powerful woman).
- Compare Deut 14:29 and 26:12 (portions for the widow and orphan).

**Gilgamesh and the Bull of Heaven (version 2): Inana's refusal to release him, the giant weapons, the Bull slain** (ETCSL 1.8.1.2 2.A:1-41, ETCSL 1.8.1.2 2.B:1-25, ETCSL 1.8.1.2 2.C:1-5, ETCSL 1.8.1.2 2.D:1-59)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:5-7 (Goliath's armour by weight).
- Compare Judg 14:5-6 and 1 Sam 17:34-36 (killing a wild beast).

**Death of Gilgamesh (Nibru version): the hero lies down never to rise; Namtar; the gods' verdict on his deeds** (ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.A:1-38, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.B:1-14, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.C:1-20, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.D:1-11)
- Compare Job 14:10-12 ('man lies down and does not rise') and 2 Sam 14:14.
- Compare Eccl 9:12 (men caught like fish in a net, birds in a snare) and Ps 116:3.

**Death of Gilgamesh (Nibru version): the dream interpreted, 'kingship, not eternal life'** (ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.E:1-28, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.F:1-14, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.G:1-22)
- Compare Q 3:185 and 21:35 ('every soul shall taste death'), Ps 89:49 and Heb 9:27; Gen 3:22-24 (eternal life withheld).
- Compare Job 7:9-10 and 2 Sam 12:23 (none returns from Sheol); Isa 14:9-10 (the shades rise to greet the dead king).

**Death of Gilgamesh (Nibru version): the Euphrates diverted, the stone tomb, mourning; the burial with retinue and gifts** (ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.H:1-22, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 1.I:1-9, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 2.I:1-42)
- Compare Deut 34:6 (no one knows Moses' grave) and Jer 16:6 and Deut 14:1 (gashing and baldness for the dead).
- Compare Ezek 32:22-30 and Isa 14:9-18 (the dead kings in the netherworld with their companies); 2 Kgs 23:25 (none like him).

**Death of Gilgamesh (Me-Turan version): lament refrain, Namtar, fragments** (ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.A:1-19, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.B:1-5, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.C:1-9, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.D:1-11, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.E:1-7)
- Compare 2 Sam 1:19-27 (lament for fallen heroes) and Job 14:12.

**Death of Gilgamesh (Me-Turan version): the assembly of the gods, Enki on the flood, Gilgamesh made judge of the dead** (ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.F:1-174)
- Compare Gen 6:3 (God limits human life after the sons of God episode) and Gen 3:22 (lest he live forever).
- Compare Gen 25:8, 35:29 and 49:33 (gathered to his people) and Isa 14:9-10 (the dead kings greet the newcomer).
- Compare Ps 26:6 and Exod 30:18-21 (hand-washing rites).

**Death of Gilgamesh (Me-Turan version): Enki interprets the dream; the tomb in the Euphrates; statues keep names alive** (ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.G:1-5, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.H:1-41, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.I:1-10, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.J:1-11, ETCSL 1.8.1.3 3.K:1-12)
- Compare Isa 56:5 (a monument and a name better than sons) and 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's pillar 'to keep my name in remembrance').
- Compare Deut 34:6 (the unknown grave) and Gen 41:16 (interpretation from God).

**Prologue of the first days and the ḫalub tree planted in Inana's garden (Gilgameš, Enkidu and the nether world)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 1:1-46)
- Heaven parted from earth: compare Gen 1:6-8 and Q 21:30 (ratq/fatq).
- Ki-sikil-lil-la, the 'Lilith' of later tradition: compare Isa 34:14 (lilit settles among the ruins).
- Snake at the root, bird in the branches of a sacred tree in a divine garden: compare Gen 2:9; 3:1 (serpent in Eden), Ezek 31:3-9 and Dan 4:9 (birds in the great tree).
- Snake deaf to charm: compare Ps 58:5-6 (deaf adder) and Jer 8:17 (snakes that cannot be charmed).
- Division of heaven, earth and underworld among three gods: compare Atrahasis I 11-16 and Deut 32:8-9 (nations allotted).

**Inana tells her tale to Utu, who refuses, then to Gilgameš, who stands by her** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 1:47-135)
- Repeated tale in a speech: compare the servant's retelling in Gen 24:34-48.

**Gilgameš kills the snake, drives off Anzud and the phantom maid, and makes throne, bed, ball and mallet** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 1:136-150)
- The Lilith figure driven into desolate places: compare Isa 34:14 (lilit in the waste) and Isa 13:21-22.
- Throne and bed of precious wood: compare 1 Kgs 10:18 (Solomon's throne) and Song 3:9-10 (palanquin of Lebanon wood).

**The ball game oppresses the young men; the widows' outcry sends ball and mallet to the nether world** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 1:151-175)
- Outcry of widows and orphans that brings down punishment: compare Exod 22:21-23 and Q 4:75.
- Who will go down / bring up: compare Deut 30:12-13 and Rom 10:6-7.

**Enkidu offers to descend; Gilgameš's taboos for the nether world; Enkidu breaks them all and is seized** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 1:176-220)
- Taboos for entering the realm of the dead/holy (remove sandals, no anointing): compare Exod 3:5, 2 Sam 12:20 and the mourning rules of Ezek 24:17.
- Inana's Descent (ETCSL 1.4.1) for garments stripped at underworld gates; compare Job 1:21 and Eccl 5:15 (naked one goes).

**Gilgameš petitions Enlil (refused) and Enki (helps); Utu opens a hole and brings Enkidu's spirit up** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 1:221-242)
- Raising a ghost from the earth: compare 1 Sam 28:11-15 (Samuel brought up) and Isa 29:4 (voice from the dust).
- Gilgameš SB XII is the Akkadian translation of this half (lines 1:172-303).

**Enkidu's report on the fate of the dead (main recension)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 1:243-303)
- Gilg SB XII 87-153 (Akkadian translation of this dialogue).
- Sons as status: compare Ps 127:3-5 (quiver full of sons, not ashamed at the gate) and Job 1:2; 42:13.
- Eunuch and childless: compare Isa 56:3-5 (eunuch given 'a name better than sons') and Wis 3:13-14.
- Worm and dust of the dead: compare Job 17:14; 21:26 and Isa 14:11.
- Stillborn at rest: compare Job 3:16 and Eccl 6:3-5.
- Leper living apart: compare Lev 13:46 and 2 Kgs 15:5.
- Tour of the dead by type and fate: compare Ezek 32:17-32 and Luke 16:19-31.

**Enkidu's report, alternative recension (parents, oaths, Ĝirsu, Sumer and Akkad)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 2:1-28)
- Honour and curse of parents: compare Exod 20:12; 21:17; Deut 27:16 and Q 17:23-24.
- False oath in the god's name: compare Exod 20:7 and Lev 19:12.
- Muddy water of the dead: compare Isa 14:9-11 and Job 10:21-22 (the drab land of the dead).

**Return to Unug, the statue, nine days of mourning and the libation for father and mother (Ur version ending)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 4:1-17)
- Mourning periods: compare Gen 50:10 (seven days) and Deut 34:8 (thirty).
- Water poured for the dead: compare 2 Sam 23:16 (water poured out) and Tob 4:17 (bread on the grave of the righteous).

**Enkidu seized, Gilgameš's lament and appeal to Enlil (Nibru recension 5.A)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 5.A:1-24)
- David's lament for Jonathan (2 Sam 1:17-27): a hero mourns his companion.

**Enkidu's report (recension 5.B) and the transition to the search for life** (ETCSL 1.8.1.4 5.B:1-71)
- Gilgameš's quest for life after Enkidu's death: Gilg SB IX-XI; compare Eccl 3:19-21 and Q 21:34-35 ('every soul shall taste death').

**Gilgameš resolves to make his name in the mountains and pleads with Utu (Gilgameš and Ḫuwawa A)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5 1-33)
- Making a name: compare Gen 11:4 (tower builders) and 2 Sam 7:9; the mountain of cedars: Isa 37:24 / 2 Kgs 19:23 (Sennacherib's boast of cutting Lebanon's cedars).
- No one tall enough to reach heaven: compare Deut 30:12, Prov 30:4 and Gen 11:4.
- Facing mortality: compare Ps 49:11-13, Ps 90:10, Eccl 2:16 and Q 21:34.

**Utu grants seven monstrous guides; Gilgameš musters fifty bachelors, arms them and fells timber** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5 34-60)
- Sending home the man with a house or bride: compare Deut 20:5-8 and Judg 7:3 (the fearful go home).
- Tears seen by God: compare 2 Kgs 20:5 and Ps 56:9.

**Crossing seven mountain ranges to the cedars; Ḫuwawa looses his terrors** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5 61-G)
- Cutting the god-guarded cedars: compare Isa 14:8 (cedars of Lebanon rejoice: no feller comes up against us) and Isa 37:24.

**Gilgameš's enchanted sleep, Enkidu's waking him, his oath, Enkidu's fear and the 'two together' sayings** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5 68-129)
- Two together, threefold cord: Eccl 4:9-12 is a close match in wording and sequence.
- Rousing a sleeper: compare Jonah 1:6 ('how can you sleep?') and 1 Kgs 18:27.
- Supernatural sleep on companions: compare 1 Sam 26:12 (deep sleep from YHWH) and Q 18:11.

**Ḫuwawa's welcome; Gilgameš offers his sisters and gifts and wheedles away the seven terrors** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5 130-148AAA)
- Disarming a strong one by guile: compare Judg 16:4-21 (Delilah coaxes out Samson's strength in stages).

**Gilgameš seizes Ḫuwawa, who pleads with Utu; Gilgameš pities him, Enkidu objects and cuts his throat** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5 149-180)
- Sparing a captured king and the companion's objection: compare 1 Kgs 20:31-42 (Ben-Hadad spared, prophet condemns) and 1 Sam 15:9-33 (Agag).
- Feigned kiss and blow: compare 2 Sam 20:9-10 (Joab and Amasa).
- Head in a bag: compare Jdt 13:9-10 and 1 Sam 17:54.

**The head brought to Enlil; his rebuke; Ḫuwawa's seven auras distributed; praise** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5 181-S)
- God rebukes the slayer of a protected figure: compare 2 Sam 1:14-16 and 2 Sam 4:9-12 (heads brought to David).
- Enlil's leaving through the window (variant J): compare Jer 9:20 (death through the windows).

**Gilgameš's meditation on death in Unug, Enkidu's advice and the seven star-guides (Gilgameš and Ḫuwawa B)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5.1 1-50)
- Stars that guide travellers: compare Q 6:97 and Q 16:16 ('by the stars they are guided'); the Seven (Pleiades), Amos 5:8 and Job 38:31.
- Death spares no one: compare Ps 89:49 and Eccl 8:8.

**Ḫuwawa captured, accuses Gilgameš of perjury, is pitied; Enkidu objects; Ḫuwawa born of a mountain cave (version B)** (ETCSL 1.8.1.5.1 130-168)
- Rock and cave as parent: compare Jer 2:27 ('to the stone: you gave me birth') and Deut 32:18.
- Sparing a captive king who then becomes a danger: compare 1 Kgs 20:31-42.

**Primeval prologue and Enmerkar's levy against Aratta (Lugalbanda in the mountain cave)** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:1-46)
- Ancient landmarks fixed: compare Deut 19:14; 32:8 and Prov 22:28.
- Army like a flood and a cloud: compare Jer 46:7-8, Ezek 38:9 and Joel 2:2.

**The march into the mountains and the seven heroes born of Uraš, with Lugalbanda the eighth** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:47-70)
- Officers over thousands and hundreds: compare Exod 18:21-25 and Deut 1:15.
- God riding the storm and lightning-arrows: compare Ps 18:10-15, Ps 68:5 and Hab 3:11.

**Lugalbanda falls sick on the way and is left for dead in a mountain cave with provisions** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:71-140)
- Youngest brother as the chosen hero: compare 1 Sam 16:10-13 (David the eighth son, 1 Sam 17:12) and Gen 37.
- Food placed for the dead: compare Deut 26:14 and Sir 30:18; Tob 4:17.
- Abandoned sick man revived: compare 1 Sam 30:11-13.

**Lugalbanda's prayer to Utu from the mountain cave** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:141-172)
- Prayer from isolation and abandonment: compare Ps 27:10 ('though father and mother forsake me'), Ps 88:9,19 and Jonah 2:3-8.
- Like water spilled on the ground: compare 2 Sam 14:14 and Ps 22:15.

**Inana as evening star and Suen as moon hear Lugalbanda; hymn to the just moon-god** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:173-227)
- God loves righteousness and hates wickedness: Ps 45:8; Ps 11:5-7; Ps 33:5.
- Sleep given by God: Ps 3:6; Ps 4:9; Ps 127:2.
- God sets the feet firm: Ps 18:34; Ps 40:3.

**The sun rises again, the protective gods attend him, and Lugalbanda's hymn to Utu** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:228-263)
- Two travellers with God as the third: compare Q 58:7 ('no three converse in secret but He is their fourth') and Q 9:40 ('the second of two').
- Angel going before: compare Exod 23:20; Ps 139:5 ('behind and before'); Isa 52:12 (God your rear-guard).
- Sun that shines on all: compare Matt 5:45, Ps 19:7 and Ps 104:22-23 (people go out when the sun rises).

**Plants and water of life; Lugalbanda strikes fire from flint and bakes cakes** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:264-299)
- Water of life from the rivers: compare Ezek 47:9-12, Zech 14:8 and Q 21:30 ('from water every living thing').
- Elijah revived in the wilderness with cake baked on coals: 1 Kgs 19:5-8.
- Wild ass running free: compare Job 39:5-8 and Gen 16:12.

**Lugalbanda traps a wild bull and two goats and tethers them** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:300-325B)
- Animal caught for sacrifice in the wild: compare Gen 22:13 (ram caught in the thicket).

**Sleep and the dream-god Zangara command a sacrifice, which Lugalbanda performs at sunrise** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:326-370)
- Dream at night after which a sacrifice is performed: compare Gen 28:10-22 (Jacob wakes: 'surely YHWH is in this place') and 1 Kgs 3:5-15 ('he awoke and it was a dream').
- True and false dreams: compare Jer 23:25-32 and Deut 13:2-6; Q 12:43-44 ('confused dreams').
- Blood poured into a pit: compare Lev 17:13 (cover the blood with earth) and Odyssey 11.

**Lugalbanda's banquet for An, Enlil, Enki and Ninḫursaĝa, and the altars of Utu and Suen** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:371-393)
- Gods smell the savour of sacrifice: compare Gen 8:20-21 and Gilg SB XI 159-161.
- Sacrifice and altar after a revelatory dream in the wilderness: Gen 28:18-22; Gen 35:7.

**The night-demons and the seven (fourteen) torches of battle (fragmentary close)** (ETCSL 1.8.2.1 A:394-499, ETCSL 1.8.2.1 B:1-7)
- Destroyer entering houses by night: compare Exod 12:23 and Jer 9:20 (death climbing in at the windows); Ps 91:5-6.
- Seven spirits / seven lamps: compare Zech 4:2,10 and Rev 4:5.

**Enki's 'eagle'-tree on Inana's mountain and the nest of the Anzud bird** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 28-49)
- Great tree with birds and roots in the waters: compare Ezek 31:3-9 and Dan 4:7-9.
- Mythic bird of terrifying cry: compare Job 39:27-30 and the later Simurgh/Ziz traditions.

**Lugalbanda feeds and adorns the chick; Anzud and his wife cry out when the chick does not answer** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 50-89)
- Eagle and her young: compare Deut 32:11 and the Etana myth (eagle's nest in the tree).
- Cry rising to heaven: compare Exod 2:23 and 1 Sam 5:12.

**Anzud finds his nest honoured like a god's dwelling and vows to fix the doer's fate** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 90-110)
- Who can reverse what God decrees: Isa 14:27; Isa 43:13; Num 23:20; Q 13:41 ('none can reverse his judgment').
- Kindness to a creature's young rewarded: compare Deut 22:6-7 (sparing the mother bird, 'that it may go well with you').

**Lugalbanda praises Anzud and adopts him as father; Anzud's offers of wealth and weapons refused** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 111-166)
- Refusing riches and weapons for a better gift: compare 1 Kgs 3:5-14 (Solomon asks wisdom, not riches or long life) and Q 27:36 (Solomon refuses the gifts).
- Shelter under wings: compare Ps 17:8; Ps 91:4; Ruth 2:12.

**Lugalbanda asks for and receives tireless speed; Anzud's command of secrecy** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 167-219)
- Running and not growing weary: Isa 40:31 (mount up with wings like eagles, run and not weary).
- Swift as a gazelle: 2 Sam 2:18; 1 Kgs 18:46 (Elijah outruns Ahab's chariot).
- Tell no one: compare Gen 37:5-11 (Joseph's dream told to his brothers) and Q 12:5 ('do not tell your dream to your brothers').

**Lugalbanda rejoins his astonished brothers and hides the source of his survival** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 220-250)
- Return of one given up for dead: compare Gen 45:26-28 (Jacob cannot believe Joseph lives).

**The year-long siege of Aratta; Enmerkar seeks a messenger and Lugalbanda alone volunteers** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 251-289)
- 'Here am I, send me': Isa 6:8; compare 2 Sam 18:19-23 (the runner who volunteers).
- Heaven and earth as oath-witnesses: Deut 4:26; 30:19; 32:1.

**Enmerkar's reproachful message to Inana; the brothers' warning; Lugalbanda crosses seven mountains** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 290-344)
- God as the one who drained the waters and made the land: compare Ps 104:5-9; Gen 1:9.
- The deity leaving the king: compare 1 Sam 16:14; 1 Sam 28:15 and Ezek 10:18-19 (glory leaves the temple).
- Amorite/Bedouin who knows no grain: compare Jer 35:7 (Rechabites sow no seed).

**Lugalbanda arrives in Kulaba by midnight and repeats Enmerkar's message before Inana** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 345-387)
- Night journey to a sanctuary: compare Q 17:1 (from the sacred mosque to the farthest mosque by night).

**Inana's oracle of the lone tamarisk and the suḫurmaš fish; Aratta's craftsmen and lapis walls; praise** (ETCSL 1.8.2.2 388-417)
- Carrying off smiths and craftsmen: compare 2 Kgs 24:14-16 and 1 Sam 13:19-22.
- City of precious stones: compare Isa 54:11-12 (lapis foundations) and Rev 21:18-21.
- Tamarisk as sacred tree: Gen 21:33; 1 Sam 22:6; 1 Sam 31:13.

**Enmerkar and the lord of Aratta: primeval Unug and Aratta's failure** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 1-32)
- The 'before ... existed' opening resembles Gen 2:4-5 and Prov 8:24-26 (before the mountains were settled).
- A rival king who pleases the deity less than the chosen one: compare 1 Sam 15:28 and 16:1.

**Enmerkar asks his sister Inana for Aratta's wealth; Inana counsels him to send a messenger** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 33-107)
- Temple materials from a foreign land: compare 1 Kgs 5:6-10 (Hiram's cedars) and Isa 60:5-13 (wealth of nations brought for the temple).
- 'Let them lick the dust': Ps 72:9 and Isa 49:23; submission under a yoke: Jer 27:8-11.
- A king chosen in the deity's heart: 1 Sam 13:14; king as son of the deity: Ps 2:7, 2 Sam 7:14.

**The first message: the ultimatum and the spell of Nudimmud on one language** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 108-159)
- Babel: Gen 11:1-9 (one language, then confusion by God); Zeph 3:9 (God will give the peoples a pure lip to call on his name together) is the closer match if line 146 is a wish for one speech addressing Enlil.
- Diversity of tongues as God's sign: Q 30:22; one community then divided: Q 10:19.
- No snake, lion, wolf, no fear: compare Isa 11:6-9 and 65:25, Hos 2:18 (covenant with the beasts), Ezek 34:25.

**The messenger reaches Aratta; the lord of Aratta refuses, citing Inana** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 160-235)
- Diplomatic messenger dialogue with fixed formulas: compare 2 Kgs 18:19-35 (the Rabshakeh's message) and Judg 11:12-28 (Jephthah's messengers).

**The lord of Aratta sets the first task: grain carried in nets** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 236-307)
- The rival king's despair and search for an answer (236-239) recalls Ahab and the king of Aram's demand in 1 Kgs 20:1-11; a dog chasing carrion: Exod 22:31, 1 Kgs 21:23.
- Contest by riddles between kings: 1 Kgs 10:1-3 (Queen of Sheba), and Josephus Ant. 8.143-149 on Hiram and Solomon exchanging riddles.

**Nisaba's wisdom: Enmerkar sends grain in nets; Aratta's famine is relieved; the sceptre demand** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 308-388)
- Grain to a famine-struck foreign land wins its submission: Gen 41:56-57 and 47:13-25 (Joseph); Q 12:58-59.
- Locusts' share of the grain: compare Joel 1:4 and Deut 28:38.
- Wisdom granted to the king to solve a hard case: 1 Kgs 3:9-12, 3:28.

**The sceptre of no material; Enki's wisdom; the reed sceptre; the challenge of the champion of no colour** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 389-461)
- A rod that is treated and transformed over time: compare Aaron's blossoming rod, Num 17:16-24 (Eng. 17:1-11).
- Single combat of champions to decide a contest: 1 Sam 17:8-10; 2 Sam 2:14-16.

**The garment of no colour; Enmerkar invents writing on clay** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 462-535)
- Tree whose top reaches heaven as an image of the king: Dan 4:7-9 (Eng. 4:10-12); Ezek 31:3-9; the Babel tower 'its top in heaven' Gen 11:4.
- Leading the people like sheep with the king as shepherd: Ps 78:70-72, Ezek 34:23, 2 Sam 5:2.
- Heavy mouth of the messenger: compare Exod 4:10 (Moses 'heavy of mouth', kevad peh); first writing: Exod 24:12, 32:16.

**The tablet received; Iškur's storm makes wheat grow in Aratta; Inana has not abandoned Aratta** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 536-587)
- Rain that answers a challenge and makes crops grow: 1 Kgs 18:41-45; growth 'of itself' (sapiah): Lev 25:5, 2 Kgs 19:29. Rain and grain as divine sign: Q 6:99, Q 80:24-32.
- Survivors of the flood and a life-giving water: Gen 9:1; Ezek 47:9 (wherever the river goes everything lives).
- Writing seen as 'nails': Eccl 12:11 ('the words of the wise are like goads, and like nails firmly fixed').

**The old woman as maiden; Aratta's herds multiply; tribute for E-ana (fragmentary ending)** (ETCSL 1.8.2.3 588-636)
- Tribute of the nations heaped in the temple court: Isa 60:5-7, Hag 2:7-8.
- A woman adorned with kohl, garment and crown: 2 Kgs 9:30 and Ezek 23:40 (used negatively); Ps 45:14-15 (the bride).

**Enmerkar and En-suhgir-ana: Unug's glory and Aratta's ultimatum** (ETCSL 1.8.2.4 A:1-76)
- Waking converse with the deity ranked above dreams: Num 12:6-8 (mouth to mouth, not in dreams); Deut 34:10.
- The city 'reaching to heaven': Gen 11:4, Deut 1:28 (cities fortified up to heaven).
- Yoke of submission: 1 Kgs 12:4, Jer 27:11.

**Enmerkar's reply: Inana dwells in Unug and will not go to Aratta** (ETCSL 1.8.2.4 A:77-113)
- God's chosen dwelling in one city, not another: Ps 132:13-14, Ps 78:67-68 (he rejected the tent of Joseph, chose Zion).
- God shares his plan with his friend: Gen 18:17, Amos 3:7.
- A king nursed on a divine lap and breast: Isa 60:16 (suck the breast of kings); Ps 22:10.

**Aratta's assembly rebukes En-suhgir-ana; the refugee sorcerer of Hamazu offers his services** (ETCSL 1.8.2.4 A:114-169)
- A foreign seer engaged with rich rewards to overcome an enemy by word and magic: Balaam, Num 22:5-7, 22:17-18, 24:11.
- Councillors tell the king he provoked the crisis: 1 Kgs 12:6-11; 2 Kgs 14:8-10 (Amaziah's challenge).
- From the sea to the cedar mountains: compare the ideal borders 'from the sea to the river' Ps 72:8, Deut 11:24.

**The sorcerer makes the cow and goat speak and dries up the milk of Nisaba's byre** (ETCSL 1.8.2.4 A:170-221)
- Animal speaking with a human voice: Num 22:28-30 (Balaam's donkey); Q 27:18 (the ant speaks).
- Byre and pen stripped bare, cattle groaning: Joel 1:18-20, Hab 3:17; cows separated from calves: 1 Sam 6:7-12.
- The oppressed cry to God from the dust: Ps 113:7, Exod 2:23-24.

**Wise woman Sagburu defeats the sorcerer in five rounds and executes him** (ETCSL 1.8.2.4 A:222-273)
- Contest of wonders with creatures: Exod 7:10-12 (Aaron's staff-serpent swallows the magicians'); Q 7:117 and Q 20:69 (the staff swallows what they faked).
- Defeated magicians: Exod 8:15 (Eng. 8:19) 'the finger of God'; in the Quran the magicians confess and are executed by Pharaoh (Q 7:120-126), the reverse of this outcome.
- Wise woman as decisive actor: 2 Sam 20:16-22 (wise woman of Abel), 2 Sam 14:2.

**En-suhgir-ana concedes to Enmerkar; Nisaba be praised** (ETCSL 1.8.2.4 A:274-283)
- Rival acknowledges the chosen one's superiority: 1 Sam 24:21 (Saul to David), Gen 33:9-11; the older brother reversed: Gen 27:29.

**Sumerian king list: kingship descends from heaven; eight kings before the flood** (ETCSL 2.1.1 1-39)
- Gen 5 (ten antediluvian patriarchs with long lives ending with Noah); the last city, Šuruppag, is the flood hero's city. En-men-dur-ana of Zimbir (Sippar) is in other traditions the seventh sage-king who was given divine secrets: compare Enoch, Gen 5:21-24.
- Dumuzid the shepherd as a pre-flood king (15): compare Abel the shepherd, Gen 4:2; Jabal 'father of those who dwell in tents', Gen 4:20.

**Sumerian king list: after the flood, kingship again from heaven to Kish; Etana ascends** (ETCSL 2.1.1 40-94)
- Ascent to heaven: Enoch (Gen 5:24), Elijah (2 Kgs 2:11); denied ascent: Q 17:93; the boast of ascent Isa 14:13-14.
- En-me-barage-si who subdued Elam (83-86): Elam among the early kings, Gen 14:1 (Chedorlaomer king of Elam).

**Sumerian king list: first dynasty of Unug (Meskiaggasher, Enmerkar, Lugalbanda, Gilgamesh)** (ETCSL 2.1.1 95-133)
- A hero of divine or spirit paternity: Gen 6:4 (the nephilim born of the sons of God); Gilgamesh two-thirds god.
- City-founder kings: Gen 4:17 (Cain builds a city), Gen 10:10-11 (Nimrod's kingdom began in Babel, Erech/Unug, Akkad).
- Mysterious disappearance of a ruler: Deut 34:6 (no one knows Moses' grave).

**Sumerian king list: Urim, Awan, Kish, Hamazi, Unug, Adab, Mari, Kish (Kug-Bau), Akshak, Kish, Lugal-zage-si** (ETCSL 2.1.1 134-265)
- Woman ruling: Athaliah, 2 Kgs 11:1-3; Deborah judges, Judg 4:4; the Queen of Sheba, 1 Kgs 10 and Q 27:23 ('a woman ruling over them').
- Kingship transferred from one people to another for its failure: Dan 2:21, 2:37-45 (succession of kingdoms); Q 3:26 (God gives and takes kingship from whom he wills).

**Sumerian king list: Sargon the gardener's son, the Akkad dynasty, anarchy, Unug IV, the Gutians** (ETCSL 2.1.1 266-334)
- No king, everyone his own ruler: Judg 17:6, 21:25; Hos 3:4. Rapid succession of short-lived kings: 1 Kgs 16:8-23, 2 Kgs 15:8-15.
- Cupbearer at a foreign court: Gen 40:1-21, Neh 1:11-2:1.

**Sumerian king list: Utu-hegal, the Third Dynasty of Urim, and Isin** (ETCSL 2.1.1 335-377)
- Blessing on the reigning king in a dynastic list: Ps 72:15-17, 1 Kgs 1:31 ('may my lord King David live forever').

**Sumerian king list: summary totals** (ETCSL 2.1.1 378-431)
- Summary totals of generations: Matt 1:17 (fourteen generations three times); Exod 12:40-41 (430 years); 1 Kgs 6:1 (480 years).

**Rulers of Lagash: after the flood, before agriculture; Ningirsu gives the tools** (ETCSL 2.1.2 1-102)
- Gen 2:5 (no rain yet and no man to till the ground) and Deut 11:10-11 (Egypt watered by foot, the land drinks rain).
- After the flood the seed of mankind preserved: Gen 7:3 ('to keep seed alive'), Gen 9:1, 9:19; Q 11:48, Q 37:77 ('We made his offspring the survivors').
- God teaches agriculture: Isa 28:24-29 ('his God instructs him'); culture heroes Gen 4:20-22; Noah the first farmer Gen 9:20.

**Rulers of Lagash: long-lived ensis, their personal gods and canals; down to Gudea** (ETCSL 2.1.2 103-200)
- God commands the ruler to build his house: 2 Sam 7:5-13, Hag 1:8, Ezra 1:2.
- 'Without father, without mother': Heb 7:3 on Melchizedek (Gen 14:18); Gudea elsewhere calls the goddess Gatumdug his mother.
- Canal-digging king: 2 Kgs 20:20 and 2 Chr 32:30 (Hezekiah's conduit); Sir 48:17.
- Writing not yet invented: compare Gen 5:1 ('this is the book of the generations of Adam').

**History of the Tummal: kings build, sons bring Ninlil, the Tummal falls into ruins five times** (ETCSL 2.1.3 1-33)
- Father prepares, son builds the temple: 1 Chr 22:5-11, 1 Kgs 5:17-19 (Eng. 5:3-5); the ark brought into Solomon's temple 1 Kgs 8:1-6.
- Temple history as repeated destruction and rebuilding: Ezra 5:11-16; Q 17:4-7 (two corruptions and the temple entered twice).
- Priestly office by lot: 1 Chr 24:5, Luke 1:9; Aaron chosen by sign, Num 17.

**Sargon legend: Ur-Zababa's reign ends; Sargon the cupbearer dreams of Inana drowning the king** (ETCSL 2.1.4 A:1-13, ETCSL 2.1.4 B:1-24)
- Cupbearer's dream told to the king: Gen 40:9-13 (Pharaoh's cupbearer); Q 12:36, 12:41.
- Dream of the young rival's rise and the king's fall told to the king: Gen 37:5-10 and 1 Sam 18:8-12; the king who understands but keeps silent: Gen 37:11 ('his father kept the matter').
- King's terror at an omen: Dan 5:6 (loins loosened, knees knocking), Dan 2:1, 4:2.
- The Lord was with him: Gen 39:2-3, 1 Sam 18:12, 18:14.

**Sargon legend: the plot at the E-sikil; Inana bars one polluted with blood; the letter to Lugal-zage-si** (ETCSL 2.1.4 B:25-56, ETCSL 2.1.4 C:1-12)
- Letter ordering the bearer's death: 2 Sam 11:14-15 (Uriah); also the Bellerophon tale (Iliad 6.168-170).
- King plots to have a rising servant killed by others: 1 Sam 18:17-25 (Saul and the Philistines' foreskins).
- Man of blood barred from the holy house: 1 Chr 22:8, 28:3; Num 35:33-34.
- Divine protection of the endangered youth: Dan 3:24-27 (unharmed in the furnace) and Q 21:69 (fire cool for Abraham).

**Cursing of Agade: Enlil gives kingship to Sargon; Inana makes Agade overflow with wealth and tribute** (ETCSL 2.1.5 1:1-56)
- Wealth of nations streaming to the city: Isa 60:5-11, 1 Kgs 10:22-25 (apes and ivory, ships of Tarshish), Ps 72:10.
- Silver and gold common in the capital: 1 Kgs 10:27; city wall reaching heaven: Deut 1:28, Gen 11:4.
- God gives and takes kingship: Dan 2:21, 4:17, Q 3:26.

**Cursing of Agade: the word from the E-kur; Inana abandons Agade; the gods take its gifts; Naram-Suen's dream and silent omens** (ETCSL 2.1.5 1:57-99)
- God's glory leaves the temple and city: Ezek 10:18-19, 11:22-23; Shiloh forsaken: Ps 78:60, Jer 7:12-14.
- No answer by dreams, Urim or prophets: 1 Sam 28:6; the king refused permission to build the temple: 2 Sam 7:5-7, 1 Chr 17:4.
- King in mourning clothes and seven 'times': Dan 4:13, 4:22-30 (Nebuchadnezzar); Jonah 3:6; 1 Kgs 21:27.

**Cursing of Agade: Naram-Suen demolishes and plunders the E-kur** (ETCSL 2.1.5 1:100-148)
- Temple hacked with axes and burned: Ps 74:3-8; Lam 2:7; Jer 52:13-19 (bronze, gold and silver carried away).
- The nations see the hidden sanctuary: Lam 1:10; Num 4:20 (not to look on the holy things even for a moment).
- A king of the god's own people strips the temple: 2 Kgs 16:17-18 (Ahaz), 2 Kgs 18:15-16 (Hezekiah strips the doors); Belshazzar uses the temple vessels, Dan 5:2-4.

**Cursing of Agade: Enlil brings down the Gutians; famine, death, lament of seven days** (ETCSL 2.1.5 1:149-209)
- God brings a savage nation from afar: Deut 28:49-50, Jer 5:15-17, Hab 1:6-10, Isa 5:26-29; Gog from the north Ezek 38-39; Gog and Magog loosed, Q 18:94, Q 21:96.
- Highways deserted: Judg 5:6, Isa 33:8, Lam 1:4.
- Siege-famine prices: 2 Kgs 6:25, Rev 6:6; unburied dead and dogs: Jer 14:16, 15:3, 1 Kgs 14:11.
- The reverse of creation, no rain, no grain: Hag 1:10-11, Jer 4:23-26.

**Cursing of Agade: the gods cool Enlil's heart and curse Agade; the curse is fulfilled** (ETCSL 2.1.5 1:210-281)
- Curse on the destroyer measure for measure: Jer 50:15, 50:29, Obad 15, Ps 137:8.
- Foxes on desolate Zion: Lam 5:18; Babylon a haunt of jackals and demons, never inhabited: Isa 13:19-22, Jer 50:39-40, 51:37; Zeph 2:13-15.
- Brother against brother, no one recognising another: Isa 19:2, Mic 7:6; heads in the wells: compare Jer 41:7-9 (bodies thrown in a cistern).
- Curse and its fulfilment narrated in the same words: Josh 6:26 and 1 Kgs 16:34; 2 Kgs 9:36-37.
- The ruined city's water turned salt and its land sown with salt: Judg 9:45, Deut 29:22, Zeph 2:9.

**Poem of Utu-hegal: Enlil commissions the king to wipe out Gutium; Tirigan captured; kingship returned to Sumer** (ETCSL 2.1.6 1-62)
- Commission to blot out the name of the enemy: Exod 17:14, Deut 25:19, 1 Sam 15:2-3.
- Foot on the necks of captured kings: Josh 10:24; Ps 110:1.
- A city hands over the fugitive rebel to the king's men: 2 Sam 20:15-22 (Sheba son of Bichri); 1 Sam 23:11-12 (Keilah would surrender David).
- Campaign by day-stages: Josh 10:9-28; Judg 20:24-30; the king prays before battle: 2 Chr 14:10 (Eng. 14:11), 2 Chr 20:5-12.
- Oppressors who take wives and children: Lam 5:11; Gutians as a 'snake of the mountains' compare Gen 49:17, Isa 14:29.

**Enlil's decision and Ninĝirsu's command in a night vision (Gudea Cyl. A 1.1-1.23)** (ETCSL 2.1.7 1-23)
- Compare 2 Sam 7:1-13 and 1 Chr 17 (the king and the house for God) and 1 Kgs 3:5 (dream at night).
- Compare Exod 25:8-9 (make me a sanctuary according to the pattern).

- Young and old slain: Lam 2:21, Ezek 9:6.

- Gates and bars broken: Lam 2:9, Neh 1:3, Ps 74:6.

- Who has seen anything like it: Lam 1:12, Lam 2:13, Joel 1:2.

- Not enjoying one's house and wife: Deut 20:5-7, Deut 28:30, Eccl 6:2.
- Music turned to mourning: Job 30:31, Lam 5:15, Ps 137:2 (lyres hung up).

- Who can change God's decree: Isa 14:27, Isa 43:13, Num 23:19-20; Q 13:41 ('none can reverse His judgment').
- Name remembered after death for works: Prov 10:7, Isa 56:5; Absalom's pillar 2 Sam 18:18.

**The death of Ur-Namma, second recension (sources 2.A-2.D)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.1 2.A:1-19, ETCSL 2.4.1.1 2.B:1-22, ETCSL 2.4.1.1 2.C:1-88, ETCSL 2.4.1.1 2.D:1-20)
- Same parallels as the main recension: Isa 14:9-10; 2 Kgs 20:3; Isa 38:10.

**A tigi to Enlil for Ur-Namma, builder of the E-kur** (ETCSL 2.4.1.2 A:1-39, ETCSL 2.4.1.2 B:40-73)
- God chooses the king and commissions the temple: 2 Sam 7:8-13, 1 Chr 28:5-6, 1 Kgs 5:3-5; dedication feast 1 Kgs 8:62-66.
- God's word that does not change: Num 23:19, Mal 3:6, Isa 55:11. King crushing enemies with a rod: Ps 2:9, Ps 110:5-6.

**Praise of Urim; Ur-Namma's gifts from the gods and his justice (Ur-Namma C)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.3 1-42)
- Ideal king brings justice, rain and fertility: Ps 72:1-7, Ps 72:16; 2 Sam 23:3-4; Prov 20:8, 20:26.

**Ur-Namma's divine birth, choice, deeds and kingship from heaven (Ur-Namma C)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.3 43-115)
- Ideal king brings justice, rain and fertility: Ps 72:1-7, Ps 72:16; 2 Sam 23:3-4.
- Formed and named in the womb: Jer 1:5, Isa 49:1, Ps 139:13; compare Ps 2:7 (divine sonship of the king).
- Kingship lowered from heaven: compare the Sumerian King List; Dan 2:37, Dan 4:17 (God gives kingdoms).

**Who will dig the canal? Ur-Namma the canal-digger (Ur-Namma D, version 1)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.4 1:1-18)
- Rivers teeming with fish in a blessed land: Ezek 47:9-10 (the river from the temple), Gen 2:10-14; compare Q 16:14 (God subjected the sea to eat fresh meat from it).

**Ur-Namma chosen by Enlil digs the Keše-kug and Pabi-luḫ canals (Ur-Namma D, version 2)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.4 2:1-40)
- King given sceptre and crook as shepherd: Ps 23:4, Mic 7:14, Ps 2:9; Hezekiah's water-works 2 Kgs 20:20.

**Ur-Namma and Šulgi dig the canals; crown and sceptre from Enlil (Ur-Namma D, version 3)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.4 3:1-40)
- Nose-rope to lead the living: compare Isa 37:29 (hook in the nose) inverted as royal guidance; Ps 78:72.

**A šir-namšub to Nanna for Ur-Namma, praising Urim and the E-kiš-nu-ĝal (Ur-Namma E)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.5 1-40)
- King who scatters evil with his eyes: Prov 20:8, Ps 101:3-8. Gate of heaven: Gen 28:17, Ps 24:7.

**A šir-namšub to Nanna for Ur-Namma, the lapis-bearded lord of Urim (Ur-Namma F)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.6 1-52)
- The tallest chosen: 1 Sam 9:2, 10:23. Gods taking counsel: Ps 82:1, 1 Kgs 22:19-22.

**A balbale to Enlil for Ur-Namma, the faithful farmer (Ur-Namma G)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.7 7-28)
- King and land fertility: Ps 72:6, 72:16; Uzziah 'loved the soil' 2 Chr 26:10; Gen 9:20 (Noah 'man of the soil').

**'I am Šulgi': the king's divine favours, wisdom and justice (Šulgi A)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.01 1-25)
- Royal love of justice and hatred of the lying tongue: Ps 45:8, Ps 101:3-7, Prov 16:12-13; Prov 6:17 (lying tongue).
- Wise king: 1 Kgs 3:9-12, 1 Kgs 5:9-14; the king as lion: Gen 49:9, Prov 19:12.

**Šulgi orders the highways and resolves to run from Nibru to Urim (Šulgi A)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.01 26-47)
- Runner who does not tire: Isa 40:31; Elijah running before Ahab's chariot 1 Kgs 18:46; 2 Sam 18:19-27 (runners).
- Making a name: Gen 11:4, 2 Sam 8:13; way-stations and hospitality: Gen 18:1-8.

**Šulgi feasts at Urim, runs back through the storm, and banquets with Utu and Inana (Šulgi A)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.01 48-83)
- Storm with hail, thunder and lightning: Ps 18:13-15, Exod 9:23-24, Ps 29; upper and lower waters: Gen 7:11.
- Fearless in storm: Ps 46:3-4, Ps 91:5.

**'Truly I am not boasting': An crowns Šulgi; may hymns praise his name (Šulgi A)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.01 84-102)
- God sets a crown on the king's head: Ps 21:4, Ps 132:18; no king like him before or after: 1 Kgs 3:12-13, 2 Kgs 18:5, 2 Kgs 23:25.
- Swearing by the life of the father/god: 1 Sam 20:3; Q 89:1-5 (oaths).

**Šulgi's lasting name; his schooling as a scribe (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 1-20)
- The educated king: 1 Kgs 5:9-14 (Solomon's wisdom and songs), Deut 17:18-19 (king writes a copy of the law); Moses educated in Egyptian wisdom (Acts 7:22).

**Šulgi the warrior, companion of Utu, who yokes Elam (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 21-55)
- God trains the king's hands for war: Ps 18:35, Ps 144:1; David's sling 1 Sam 17:40-50; Judg 20:16 (left-handed slingers who never miss).
- Sun as shield: Ps 84:12; breaking the bow: Ps 46:10, Hos 1:5.

**Šulgi the hunter of lions, wild bulls, boars and wild asses (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 56-117)
- David kills lion and bear: 1 Sam 17:34-36; Benaiah 2 Sam 23:20; Samson Judg 14:5-6. Nimrod the mighty hunter: Gen 10:9.

**Šulgi the tireless runner and the expert diviner (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 118-153)
- Divination by the king: compare the king of Babylon looking at the liver in Ezek 21:26; contrast Deut 18:10-14 (divination forbidden in Israel) and 1 Sam 28:6 (Urim and dreams).
- Inquiry before battle: Judg 20:27-28, 1 Sam 23:2-4, 2 Sam 5:19.

**Šulgi the musician; no one escapes death; his mother's joyful pregnancy (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 154-189)
- David the skilled player: 1 Sam 16:16-18, Amos 6:5, 1 Chr 23:5; Solomon's 1005 songs 1 Kgs 5:12.
- No one escapes death: Ps 49:8-11, Ps 89:49, Eccl 8:8; Q 3:185 ('every soul shall taste death'), Q 4:78.

**Šulgi the star of steadfastness, polyglot judge and wise counsellor (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 190-243)
- Soft words cool anger: Prov 15:1, Prov 25:15, Eccl 10:4; Q 20:44 ('speak to him gently').
- Languages of the nations: Gen 10:5, Gen 11:1-9, Esth 1:22, Dan 3:4; Q 30:22 (diversity of tongues a sign).
- King teaching counsellors: Deut 1:13-17, Exod 18:21-22, 2 Chr 19:5-7.

**Šulgi's service to the gods, preservation of old hymns, and charge to a future king (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 244-296)
- Who has gone up to heaven? Prov 30:4, Deut 30:12; mortality of all gain: Eccl 2:18-19, Ps 39:7, Ps 49:11.
- Collecting old songs: Prov 25:1 (Hezekiah's men copied proverbs), the Book of Jashar (Josh 10:13, 2 Sam 1:18).

**Curse on a hostile successor; the academies of Urim and Nibru; no lies in his inscriptions (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 297-336)
- Curse on whoever alters the record: Deut 4:2, Rev 22:18-19; royal inscription curses.
- No king like him before or after: 2 Kgs 23:25, 1 Kgs 3:12.

**Lions culled like weeds; oath by Utu; Šulgi chosen by Nanna; praise of Nisaba (Šulgi B)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.02 337-385)
- The king's shadow: Lam 4:20 ('in his shadow we shall live among the nations'), Judg 9:15. King as God's servant: 2 Sam 7:5, Ps 89:21.

**Šulgi the wild bull, calf of a divine cow, purified at Eridug (Šulgi C)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.03 A:1-34)
- Seven wisdoms attending the king: Isa 11:2 (the spirit of wisdom, understanding, counsel ...), Prov 9:1 (wisdom's seven pillars).
- King as wild ox: Num 23:22, Deut 33:17; dragon/serpent: contrast Isa 27:1.

**Šulgi in the house of wisdom: stylus, measuring line, plans and assembly (Šulgi C)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.03 A:35-84)
- King skilled in planning and building: 1 Kgs 6-7; justice to the righteous: Ps 101:6-8, Prov 20:26.

**Šulgi, extispicer, dream-interpreter and discerner of hearts (Šulgi C)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.03 A:85-114)
- Royal dream interpretation: Gen 41 (Joseph), Dan 2 and 4; discerning good and evil: 1 Kgs 3:9, 2 Sam 14:17 ('like the angel of God to discern good and evil'); reading the heart: 1 Sam 16:7, Jer 17:10.

**Šulgi speaks Martu and Elamite and is unbeaten at wrestling (Šulgi C)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.03 A:115-146)
- Wrestling: Gen 32:25-29 (Jacob); languages: Neh 13:24, Esth 1:22.

**Šulgi destroys the rebel lands; ruins never to be rebuilt (Šulgi C)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.03 B:1-74)
- Sheep without a shepherd: Num 27:17, 1 Kgs 22:17, Ezek 34:5, Zech 13:7. City never rebuilt: Isa 25:2, Deut 13:17, Josh 6:26.

**Šulgi plays the seven instruments; fragments mentioning Ĝeštin-ana and Gilgameš (Šulgi C)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.03 B:75-110, ETCSL 2.4.2.03 C:1-14)
- David dancing before the ark: 2 Sam 6:14-16; skilled player of the lyre 1 Sam 16:18.

**Shulgi D: opening praise of the king and the refrain 'who rivals you?'** (ETCSL 2.4.2.04 1-39)
- Compare Ps 1:3 and Jer 17:8 (tree planted by streams of water) with line 32; Ps 92:13-15 (righteous flourish like the palm and cedar).
- Compare Ps 45:3-8 (royal praise, the king addressed as elohim) and Ps 89:7-9 (who is like you).
- Compare Num 23:22, 24:8-9 (wild ox horns, lion) and Gen 49:9 (Judah a lion's whelp).

**Shulgi D: the king's divine birth and the fate decreed for him** (ETCSL 2.4.2.04 40-64)
- Compare Ps 2:7 ('You are my son, today I have begotten you') and Ps 110:3 (from the womb of the dawn).
- Compare Ps 139:13-16 (formed in the womb; days written in God's book) and Jer 1:5 (known before formed in the womb).
- Compare Ps 3:4 (God the lifter of my head); 2 Sam 7:8 (taken from the pasture to be ruler).

**Shulgi D: the king's own boast of how he crushes the foreign lands** (ETCSL 2.4.2.04 135-217)
- Compare Josh 10:24 (feet on the necks of kings) and Ps 110:1; Ps 72:9 and Mic 7:17 (enemies lick the dust like a serpent).
- Compare Ps 18:15 and Zech 9:14 (arrows like lightning); Deut 32:42 (arrows drunk with blood); Ps 79:3 (blood poured like water).
- Compare 2 Kgs 8:12 and Hos 14:1 (atrocities of conquest); 2 Sam 8:2 (measuring off who shall live and who die).

**Shulgi D: the king vows to avenge Sumer on the foreign lands; the gods turn against the enemy** (ETCSL 2.4.2.04 218-256)
- Compare Deut 20:19-20 (do not cut down fruit trees in a siege) and 2 Kgs 3:19,25 (felling every good tree, stopping springs).
- Compare Ezek 10-11 and Jer 48:7, 49:3 (gods of the defeated go into exile or depart); Isa 5:6 (vineyard to briers and thorns).

**Shulgi D: Gilgameš and the gods walk beside Šulgi; the revenge carried out** (ETCSL 2.4.2.04 288-333)
- Compare Ps 16:8, 110:5, 121:5 (God at the king's right hand); Exod 23:20-23 and Deut 1:30, 20:4 (God goes before you to fight).
- Compare 2 Sam 22:16 and Ps 18:16 (the blast of God's nostrils lays bare the world) for destruction by a mere glance or breath.

**Shulgi D: the hero's revenge, the booty, the royal barge, and the entry before Enlil** (ETCSL 2.4.2.04 334-381)
- Compare Gen 6:14 (ark covered with bitumen inside and out) and Exod 2:3 for the bitumen-caulked vessel.
- Compare 2 Sam 8:11-12 and 1 Chr 18:11 (David dedicates the silver and gold of conquered nations to YHWH); 2 Chr 20:27-28 (victory procession to the temple with harps).

**Shulgi D: Enlil decrees a good destiny for Šulgi** (ETCSL 2.4.2.04 382-397)
- Compare Ps 21:5 and 61:7 (length of days for the king), Ps 72:16 (may people flourish like grass), Ps 92:13-15.
- Compare Ps 110:2 (the LORD sends your mighty sceptre) and Ezek 17:23, 19:11 (the royal tree and sceptre-branches giving shade).

**Shulgi E: Enlil's favour, and the catalogue of hymns composed about the king** (ETCSL 2.4.2.05 1-38)
- Compare 1 Kgs 5:9-14 (Solomon's 3000 proverbs and 1005 songs) and the Psalm superscriptions naming genres (mizmor, shir, maskil, miktam).
- Compare 1 Chr 15:16-22, 23:5 and Amos 6:5 (David as deviser of musical instruments).

**Shulgi E: the king swears his hymns contain no lies, and commands their performance** (ETCSL 2.4.2.05 39-73)
- Compare Deut 28:27,35 and 2 Kgs 5:27 (skin disease as divine curse).
- Compare 2 Sam 23:1-2 (David's last words: the spirit of YHWH speaks through me) and Ps 45:2 for the claim of true royal song.

**Shulgi E: curse upon whoever removes Šulgi's name from his hymns** (ETCSL 2.4.2.05 74-151)
- Compare Deut 28:15-68 and Lev 26:14-39 (curse catalogues: famine, plague); 2 Kgs 6:25 and 7:1 (famine prices of grain).
- Compare curse-formulas protecting inscriptions, and Rev 22:18-19 / Deut 4:2 (nothing to be added or taken away).

**Shulgi E: the great musician; a negligent king of old; Ninurta's weapons and the unique sceptre** (ETCSL 2.4.2.05 152-201)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:45 and 2 Sam 22:35 (God trains the king's hands for war); 2 Kgs 18:5 and 23:25 (no king like him before or after).

**Shulgi E: the campaign against Gutium, the king alone ahead of his troops** (ETCSL 2.4.2.05 202-239)
- Compare Ps 18:30-43 (the king runs against a troop, leaps a wall; enemies under his feet).

**Shulgi E: the hymns written down in heavenly writing so that they are never forgotten** (ETCSL 2.4.2.05 240-257)
- Compare Job 19:23-24 (words written in a book, engraved forever), Isa 30:8 and Hab 2:2 (write it on a tablet for the last day).
- Compare Exod 32:16 (writing of God engraved on the tablets) for 'heavenly writing'; Ps 102:19 (written for a generation to come).

**Shulgi O: litany of Urim and its shrines, each 'well established'** (ETCSL 2.4.2.15 A:1-24)
- Compare Ps 48 and 87 (Zion praised as God's city, its towers and ramparts); Ps 122:3 (Jerusalem built as a city bound firmly together).

**Shulgi O: Šulgi meets Gilgameš and praises his victory over Kiš** (ETCSL 2.4.2.15 A:25-60)
- Compare 2 Sam 3:10 and 1 Kgs 11:31-35 (kingship transferred from one house to another); Dan 2:21 (God removes and sets up kings).
- Compare Gen 10:8-12 (Nimrod's kingdom begins in Babel, Erech, Akkad) for Uruk (Erech) as an early seat of kingship.

**Shulgi O: further praises of Gilgameš (Huwawa, the seven terrors) and of Šulgi** (ETCSL 2.4.2.15 A:61-142)
- Compare 1 Kgs 17:23 and 2 Kgs 4:36 (the prophet gives the revived son back to his mother).
- Compare Jer 22:7 and Isa 10:34 (cutting the choice cedars) for the cedar-forest expedition.

**Shulgi P: Ninsumun petitions An for her son Šulgi** (ETCSL 2.4.2.16 A:1-21, ETCSL 2.4.2.16 B:1-2)
- Compare 1 Kgs 1:15-31 (Bathsheba petitions the king for Solomon's succession) and 1 Kgs 2:19 (the queen mother's throne).
- Compare 1 Sam 16:1-13 and Ps 89:20-21 (God chooses one from the people to be shepherd); 2 Sam 7:8.

**Shulgi P: An agrees; Ninsumun enthrones Šulgi and blesses him as her son** (ETCSL 2.4.2.16 C:1-66)
- Compare Ps 2:6-7, 110:1 (enthroned at God's right hand), and Isa 66:11-12 (nursed and dandled on the knees).
- Compare Song 1:3 (your name is oil poured out) and Eccl 7:1 (a good name better than fine oil).
- Compare 2 Sam 23:3-4 (the just ruler like the morning light at sunrise) and Mal 3:20.

**Shulgi Q: adab to Utu, who gives Šulgi kingship and chooses him in his heart** (ETCSL 2.4.2.17)
- Compare Mal 3:20 (sun of righteousness) and Ps 19:5-7 (the sun like a hero); Ps 84:12 (God is sun and shield).

**Shulgi R: Ninlil's barge, built by Šulgi, described part by part** (ETCSL 2.4.2.18 A:1-40)
- Compare Gen 6:14-16 (instructions for the ark's construction) and Ezek 27:4-9 (Tyre as a ship described part by part).
- Compare Exod 25-31 (sanctuary commanded by God, built by a chosen craftsman) and 1 Kgs 5:20-23 (cedars cut for the temple).

**Shulgi R: the festival voyage of Enlil and Ninlil to Tummal and back, and their blessing on Šulgi** (ETCSL 2.4.2.18 B:41-91)
- Compare 2 Sam 6 and Ps 68:25-28 (procession of the divine presence with the ark); Ps 132:8 (arise to your resting place).
- Compare Ps 104:25-26 (sea creatures and ships) and Ps 148:7 (sea monsters praise God).
- Compare Ps 21:5 and 61:7-8 (long days for the king, his throne established).

**Shulgi U: hymn to Nergal (Mešlamta-ea) for Šulgi** (ETCSL 2.4.2.21)
- Compare Hab 3:3-6 (God marches, plague and pestilence before him, nations tremble) and Ps 18:8-16.

**Shulgi V: Enlil's favour, Šulgi's run from Nibru to Urim, and his statue** (ETCSL 2.4.2.22 1-35)
- Compare 1 Kgs 18:46 (Elijah runs before Ahab's chariot to Jezreel in the storm) and 2 Sam 18:19-27 (the runners).
- Compare Jer 1:5 and Isa 49:1 (called from the womb); 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's pillar for his name).

**Shulgi X: Šulgi sails to Unug, Inana's love song and her decree of his fate** (ETCSL 2.4.2.24 1-79)
- Compare Song of Songs 1:2-4, 4:16-5:1 and 7:11-13 (lovers' bed, the king brought into his chambers); Song 1:12 and 3:6-11 (Solomon's litter on his wedding day).
- Compare Ezek 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz = Dumuzid) and Ezek 23:40 and 2 Kgs 9:30 (bathing, painting eyes).
- Compare Deut 20:4 and 2 Chr 20:17 (God goes before you in battle); Ps 45 (royal wedding psalm, the king girded with sword).

**Shulgi X: Utu, Ninazu and Nanna-Ašimbabbar decree fates for Šulgi; the just king** (ETCSL 2.4.2.24 80-160)
- Compare Mal 3:24 (turning the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers) and Ps 72:1-4 (the king judges the poor, crushes the oppressor).
- Compare Jer 1:18 (fortified city, bronze walls) and Ps 89:19 (our shield belongs to YHWH, our king).
- Compare Josh 8:28 (Ai made a tel forever) and Deut 13:17.

**Shulgi Y: Šulgi's offerings to Ninlil after victories** (ETCSL 2.4.2.25 1-31)
- Compare 1 Kgs 8:62-64 and 2 Chr 31:3-10 (the king supplies the temple's sacrifices and stores).

**Shulgi Z: love song, 'My sister, I would go with you to my fields and my garden'** (ETCSL 2.4.2.26 A:1-23, ETCSL 2.4.2.26 B:1-30)
- Compare Song 4:9-12, 5:1 (my sister, my bride; the garden), 7:12-14 (come, my beloved, let us go out to the fields ... see if the pomegranates have bloomed) and 2:3, 8:5 (apple tree).
- Compare Song 6:11 (I went down to the nut garden to see ... whether the pomegranates had budded).

**Amar-Suena A: the temple of Enki left in ruins year after year, rebuilt only when Enki speaks** (ETCSL 2.4.3.1)
- Compare 1 Kgs 6:37-38 (Solomon's temple built over seven years) and 2 Sam 7:1-13 (David wishes to build; God's word through Nathan postpones it).
- Compare Hag 1:2-11 (the house lies in ruins while the people delay; drought as sign) and Exod 25:9, 1 Chr 28:11-19 (the divine plan, tavnit, of the sanctuary).
- Compare 1 Sam 28:6 (no answer by dreams, Urim or prophets) for divination withholding approval.

**Shu-Suen A: balbale of Bau, the queen's song of her lord's gifts and sweetness** (ETCSL 2.4.4.1 1-28)
- Compare Song 1:2-4 (your love is better than wine; the king has brought me into his chambers), 4:10-11 and 5:1 (wine, honey, milk).
- Compare Gen 24:22,47 and Ezek 16:11-12 (gold ring and bracelets given to the bride); Song 1:10-11.
- Compare Ps 45:7 (your throne, O god) and Ps 45:10-17 (the queen and the royal bride).

**Shu-Suen B: balbale of Inana, 'Man of my heart, your allure is sweet as honey'** (ETCSL 2.4.4.2 1-30)
- Compare Song 4:11 (your lips drip honey, bride), 5:1 (I ate my honeycomb with my honey) and 1:4 (draw me after you, let us run; the king brought me into his chambers).
- Compare Song 3:4 and 8:2 (I brought him to my mother's house) and Gen 24:50-51, 34:11-12 (the family gives the bride).

**Shu-Suen C: balbale of Inana, 'My hair is lettuce'** (ETCSL 2.4.4.3 1-23)
- Compare Song 4:1 and 6:5 (your hair like a flock of goats), 7:6 (your flowing locks, a king held captive) and Song 1:6 (my mother's sons, the vineyard-keeper).

**Shu-Suen D: tigi to Ninurta, the king's great wall** (ETCSL 2.4.4.4)
- Compare Zech 2:9 (I will be a wall of fire around her), Ps 18:3 and 144:1-2 (my fortress, who trains my hands for war).
- Compare Ps 20:8 and 21:8 (some trust in chariots, the king trusts in YHWH); Ps 91:7 (a thousand fall, ten thousand at your right hand).

**Shu-Suen F: adab to Suen, the moon god who sired and elevated Šu-Suen** (ETCSL 2.4.4.6)
- Compare Ps 104:19 (he made the moon to mark the seasons) and Gen 1:14-16; Ps 89:38 (the king's throne established like the moon forever).
- Compare Ps 72:5 (may he live as long as sun and moon) and Ps 72:10 (kings bring tribute).

**Ibbi-Suen A: tigi to Suen, who makes Ibbi-Suen canal inspector of the Land** (ETCSL 2.4.5.1)
- Compare Ps 73:23 and Isa 42:6, 45:1 (God grasps the king's right hand).

**Ibbi-Suen B: šir-namgala to the twin gods Mešlamta-ea and Lugal-era, lords of the River Ordeal** (ETCSL 2.4.5.2)
- Compare Num 5:11-31 (the ordeal of bitter water) and Ps 45:8 / Ps 11:5-7 (God loves justice, hates wickedness).
- Compare Ps 139:8 and Job 26:6 (Sheol naked before God); Isa 14:9 (the shades of the underworld rise to greet).

**Ibbi-Suen C: adab to Suen, renewer of light, and the gods' gifts to Ibbi-Suen** (ETCSL 2.4.5.3)
- Compare Ps 33:13-15 and Prov 15:3 (God looks down and sees everyone); Isa 11:2 (the spirit's gifts upon the king).
- Compare Gen 2:14 (Tigris and Euphrates flow from Eden).

**Ibbi-Suen D: ululumama to Suen; Suen prays to Enlil for Urim and for Ibbi-Suen** (ETCSL 2.4.5.4)
- Compare Exod 3:8 (land flowing with milk and honey) and Deut 8:7-9 (copper from its hills).
- Compare Ps 132:13-18 (God chose Zion; abundance of its provisions; a lamp for the anointed).

**Ishbi-Erra C: tigi to Nanaya, chosen by Inana, for Išbi-Erra** (ETCSL 2.5.1.3)
- Compare Prov 8:1-21 (Wisdom personified as a lady who instructs, by whom kings reign) and 1 Sam 16:12 (the chosen king's beauty).

**Iddin-Dagan A: greeting the lady who ascends above; Inana receives the divine powers and the gods bow to her** (ETCSL 2.5.3.1 A:1-D:44)
- Compare Jer 7:18 and 44:17-19,25 (the Queen of Heaven) and Isa 14:12 (Helel ben Shahar, the shining star fallen from heaven).
- Compare Ps 82:1 and 1 Kgs 22:19 (the divine council); Ps 81:4 (feast at the new moon).
- Compare Ps 68:25-26 (procession of singers, musicians, maidens with drums).

**Iddin-Dagan A: the procession of cross-dressed and blood-spattering cult personnel before Inana** (ETCSL 2.5.3.1 E:45-G:88)
- Compare Deut 22:5 (a man shall not wear a woman's garment) and Deut 23:18-19 (qadesh); 1 Kgs 18:28 (Baal's prophets gash themselves till the blood flows); Hos 7:14.
- Compare 2 Kgs 23:7 (houses of the qedeshim where women wove for Asherah).

**Iddin-Dagan A: the evening star rises, all creatures rest, she judges at night, and offerings are made on the rooftops** (ETCSL 2.5.3.1 H:89-L:168)
- Compare Jer 19:13, 32:29 and Zeph 1:5 (incense on the rooftops to the host of heaven); 2 Kgs 23:12 (rooftop altars).
- Compare Jer 7:18 and 44:19 (cakes, kawwanim, baked for the Queen of Heaven, and libations poured to her).
- Compare Ps 104:19-23 (at evening the beasts come out, at sunrise man goes to work) and Ps 148.
- Compare Deut 26:1-11 (first fruits basket) and Deut 8:8 (seven species).

**Iddin-Dagan A: the New Year sacred marriage of Inana and the king, and the banquet** (ETCSL 2.5.3.1 M:169-N:230)
- Compare Song 3:11 (King Solomon crowned by his mother on his wedding day), Song 1:12-17 and Ps 45:9-16 (royal wedding with myrrh, the bride brought to the king).
- Compare Prov 8:22-31 (Wisdom born before heaven and earth) for 'born together with heaven and earth'.
- Compare Hos 2:16-25 (YHWH's marriage to the land bringing grain, wine and oil) as the inverted, monotheistic sacred marriage.

**Iddin-Dagan B: praise of Iddin-Dagan as shepherd, lawgiver and patron of the scribal school** (ETCSL 2.5.3.2 1-79)
- Compare Ps 23:2 (he makes me lie down in green pastures), Ezek 34:14-15 and Ps 72:6-17 (the ideal king's reign of abundance and justice).
- Compare Lam 4:20 (the anointed, the breath of our nostrils, under whose shadow we live) and Prov 16:15 (in the light of the king's face is life).
- Compare 1 Kgs 3:12 and 5:9 (God gives the king wisdom and breadth of heart).

**Iddin-Dagan C: adab to Ningublaga, the wild bull who devastates the rebel lands** (ETCSL 2.5.3.3)
- Compare Ps 1:4 and 35:5 (the wicked like chaff the wind drives away), Isa 17:13.
- Compare Zech 3:4-5 and Isa 61:10 (clothed in festal garments by God).

**Iddin-Dagan D: namerima incantation-hymn to Ninisina, An, Enlil, Ninlil and Aruru against the king's enemies** (ETCSL 2.5.3.4 1-85)
- Compare Exod 15:26 (I am YHWH your healer) and Deut 32:39 (I kill and make alive, I wound and I heal).
- Compare Exod 20:7 (you shall not take the name in vain, for YHWH will not hold guiltless) and Lev 19:12.
- Compare Josh 7:9 and Ps 74:10,18 (what will you do for your great name? shall the enemy revile your name forever?).
- Compare Hos 13:7-8 and Lam 3:10 (God like a lion, a bear lying in wait).

**Ishme-Dagan A: praise of Enlil, judge of heaven and earth, who decreed Išme-Dagan's destiny** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:1-42)
- Compare Deut 10:17 and Ps 136:2-3 (God of gods, Lord of lords) with line 40; Dan 2:47.
- Compare Rom 11:33 and Ps 36:7 (judgments a great deep) with line 28; Isa 40:28.
- Compare Ezek 12:13, 17:20 and Hos 7:12 (God spreads his net over the rebel) with lines 30-31.

**Ishme-Dagan A: the king named in the womb and endowed by the gods one after another** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:43-89)
- Compare Isa 49:1 ('YHWH called me from the womb, from my mother's body he named my name') and Jer 1:5 with line 43; Ps 22:10-11 and Ps 71:6.
- Compare Isa 11:2 (sevenfold spirit of wisdom on the shoot of Jesse) and Prov 9:1 (wisdom's seven pillars) with line 71.
- Compare Ps 110:2 (the sceptre sent forth from Zion), Ps 21:4 (crown of fine gold set on his head) and Ps 89:20-21.
- Compare 1 Sam 16:1-13 (the king chosen from among his brothers) and Ps 78:70-71 with line 55.

**Ishme-Dagan A: Utu puts justice in the king's mouth, for a social order of respect and protection of the weak** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:90-99)
- Compare Exod 20:12 and Lev 19:3 (honour/revere father and mother) with lines 94-95; Mal 1:6; Q 17:23-24.
- Compare Ps 72:1-4, 12-14 (the king given God's justice to defend the poor) and Isa 11:3-5 with lines 90-98; Prov 16:10 (a divine decision on the king's lips).
- Compare Lev 25:39-43 and Neh 5:1-13 (no Israelite to be enslaved to his brother) with line 97.

**Ishme-Dagan A: Inana chooses the king as spouse, en-priest and king in Unug** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:100-111)
- Compare Ps 110:4 (king a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek) and Gen 14:18 with lines 106-107.
- Compare Song 1:16 (our bed is green/flourishing) and Song 3:11 (the king crowned on his wedding day) with line 105.

**Ishme-Dagan A: the gods' 'So be it', Enlil's choice by extispicy, and the king's restoration of E-kur's rites and offerings** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:112-182)
- Compare 2 Kgs 23:4-24 and 2 Chr 29-31 (Josiah's and Hezekiah's restoration of neglected rites) with lines 138-140.
- Compare Num 28:11-25 (offerings at new moon and the 15th day of the month) and Num 28:3-8 (daily tamid) with lines 164-165, 180.
- Compare Gen 8:21 and Lev 1:9 (pleasing odour to YHWH) with line 154; Exod 23:19 (first-fruits to the house of YHWH) with line 170.
- Compare Ps 121:4 (he who keeps Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps) for 'untiring'; Num 28:7 (drink offering of strong drink poured out).

**Ishme-Dagan A: freedoms for Nibru, the tithe, and justice for the weak, the orphan and the widow** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:183-235)
- Compare Exod 22:21-23 and Deut 10:18; 24:17 (widow and orphan; their cry heard) and Ps 72:4, 12-14 with lines 216-217; Q 93:9-10; Q 107:2.
- Compare 1 Sam 17:25 (the victor's father's house made free in Israel) and Ezra 7:24 (temple personnel exempt from tribute) with lines 185-189.
- Compare Gen 14:20, 28:22 and Num 18:21-26 (tithes) with line 190.
- Compare Isa 9:5 ('Everlasting Father' as royal title) and Isa 22:21 (a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem) with line 224.
- Compare Deut 17:20 and 1 Kgs 3:14 (the obedient king's days prolonged) with line 235.

**Ishme-Dagan A: the king's self-praise (father, wall, tree, lamp, seed) and the tribute of distant lands and nomads** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:236-273)
- Compare Ps 72:10-11, 15 (kings of Tarshish and Sheba bring tribute) and 1 Kgs 5:1, 10:22-25 with lines 259-270.
- Compare Dan 4:7-9 and Ezek 31:3-9 (the king as a great tree giving shade) with lines 239-241; Lam 4:20 ('in his shadow we shall live').
- Compare 2 Sam 21:17 ('the lamp of Israel') with line 252; Isa 11:1 (shoot from the stump of Jesse) with lines 253-254.
- Compare Jer 35:7-10 (Rechabites build no houses) and Gen 25:27 (Esau, man of the field) with lines 266-267.

**Ishme-Dagan A: thrones for Enlil and Ninlil and copper statues of the king and his ancestors in E-kur** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:274-329)
- Compare 1 Kgs 7:7 and 10:18-20 (Solomon's throne of ivory and gold) and Ps 132:7-8 (arise to your resting place) with lines 282-292.
- Compare 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's pillar so his name be remembered) with lines 297-320; contrast Deut 4:16-18, Exod 20:4.
- Compare 1 Kgs 15:15 (Asa brings his father's dedicated things into the temple) with lines 316-320.

**Ishme-Dagan A: the king's songs, his scribal and musical learning, the oath of their truth and the wish for his dynasty** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 A:330-419)
- Compare 1 Kgs 5:9-14 (Solomon's 3,000 proverbs and 1,005 songs) and 1 Chr 25:1-7 (David organizes the singers) with lines 330-377.
- Compare Ps 89:36-38 and 2 Sam 7:12-16 (dynasty established) and 1 Kgs 1:37, 47 ('may God make Solomon's throne greater than David's') with lines 397-399.
- Compare Ps 72:20 and the Davidic superscriptions; Ps 45:18 ('I will make your name remembered in all generations') with lines 384-393.
- Compare Gen 14:22 and Dan 12:7 (oath with raised hand) with lines 378-380.

**Ishme-Dagan A, segment B: chariot, sedan chair, fifty-headed mace and statues dedicated in Enlil's temple** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 B:1-24)
- Compare 1 Kgs 7:13-51 (bronze and gold furnishings made for the temple) and 2 Sam 8:10-11 (dedicated articles).

**Ishme-Dagan A, segment C: let there be singers of every kind** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 C:1-13)
- Compare 1 Chr 15:16-24, 16:4-7 and 25:1-31 (classes of Levitical singers appointed) and Neh 12:46.

**Ishme-Dagan A, segment D: blessing on the successor who respects the monument, curse on the one who effaces it** (ETCSL 2.5.4.01 D:1-17)
- Compare Deut 27:17 (cursed who moves a landmark) and Rev 22:18-19 (curse on who adds or removes); Prov 22:28.

**Ishme-Dagan B: adab to Bau the healer, who presents the king to Enlil to have his fate decreed** (ETCSL 2.5.4.02 A:1-D:66)
- Compare Exod 15:26 and Ps 103:3 (God the healer) with A:6; Q 26:80.
- Compare Deut 28:3-12 and Ps 72:16 (abundance of grain under the blessed king) and Ps 144:12-15 with C:45-49.
- Compare 1 Sam 1:24-28 (child brought to the sanctuary with an offering) and Ps 2:7 (the decree concerning the king) with C:34-42.

**Ishme-Dagan C: hymn to Nibru and its gods, at whose feet the king throws himself** (ETCSL 2.5.4.03 A:1-17)
- Compare Ps 48:2-4 and Ps 87:1-3 (glorious things are spoken of you, city of God) and Ps 122.
- Compare Ps 2:7 (the king as God's begotten son) with A:8-9.

**Ishme-Dagan D: adab to Enki, distributor of the divine powers, for the king's abundance** (ETCSL 2.5.4.04 A.A:1-B.E:30)
- Compare Gen 27:28 and Deut 33:13-16 (dew of heaven, fatness of the earth, grain and wine), Mal 3:10 (windows of heaven opened) with B.D:24-27.
- Compare Deut 32:8-9 (the Most High apportions the nations among the gods) with B.B:4.

**Ishme-Dagan E: balbale to Enki, counsellor of An, for the king's long life** (ETCSL 2.5.4.05 A.A:2-D.E:9)
- Compare Isa 40:13-14 ('who has been his counsellor?') as an inverse, and Prov 8:14, 22-30 (Wisdom beside God) with A.A:5-8.
- Sections B.B and C.C are very fragmentary (the king's name, 'son of Enlil', 'divine plans'); unknown numbers of lines lost.

**Ishme-Dagan I: the king builds Enlil's chariot; its parts praised; Enlil's procession, Ninurta's ploughing and prayer for the king** (ETCSL 2.5.4.09 A:1-B:97)
- Compare Ezek 1:4-28 and 10:1-22 (the divine chariot-throne described part by part: wheels, rims full of eyes, firmament) and 1 Chr 28:18 (the chariot of the cherubim) with A:9-40.
- Compare Hab 3:8 and Ps 68:18 (God's chariots), 2 Kgs 2:11 (chariot of fire) with B:66-75; 2 Kgs 23:11 (chariots of the sun).
- Compare Ps 18:11 (cloud and darkness as God's vehicle) with A:12; Ezek 12:13 (my net spread over him) with A:15.

**Ishme-Dagan J: 'may the churn sound' for Inana in the cattle-pen, and long days for the king** (ETCSL 2.5.4.10 1-26)
- Compare Song 1:7-8 (where do you pasture your flock?) and Song 6:2-3; Prov 30:33 (churning milk brings forth butter); Deut 32:14 (curds of the herd).

**Ishme-Dagan K: Enlil and Ninlil give Inana her powers, including reversal of gender, and give her Išme-Dagan as husband** (ETCSL 2.5.4.11 1-45)
- Compare Deut 22:5 (a woman shall not wear a man's gear nor a man a woman's garment) with lines 21-24.
- Compare Isa 45:7 (I form light and create darkness) and Amos 5:8 with line 14; Q 3:26-27 (You give dominion to whom You will ... You bring the night into the day).
- Compare 1 Sam 2:6-8 (YHWH brings low and raises up) and Ps 75:8 with line 13.
- Compare Isa 34:5-7 and Deut 32:42 (sword drunk with blood) with line 11.

**Ishme-Dagan P: fragmentary adab to Ninurta, with the fifty-headed mace and a copper throne** (ETCSL 2.5.4.16 A:1-C:27)
- Too fragmentary for close comparison; compare Ps 18 and Ps 68 (divine warrior) in general.

**Ishme-Dagan Q: adab to Nuska, Enlil's minister, who is to speak good words for the king** (ETCSL 2.5.4.17 A.A:1-B.B:27)
- Compare Zech 1:12-13 and Job 33:23-26 (an angelic mediator speaks good words for a man) and Tob 12:12, 15 with B.B:9-16.
- Compare Ps 65:3 (you who hear prayer) and Ps 61:7-8 (prolong the king's life; may he be enthroned forever) with B.B:17-24.

**Ishme-Dagan W: hymn to Nibru, mooring post of the people, its incomparable lord and lady, Ninurta and Nuska** (ETCSL 2.5.4.23 A:1-C:18)
- Compare Gen 11:4 (a tower with its top in the heavens) with A:34-37; Ps 48:2-3 (Zion, beautiful in elevation, joy of all the earth).
- Compare Exod 15:11 and Ps 86:8 (who is like you among the gods?) with A:78-81 and C:12-15.
- Compare Ezek 38:12 (navel of the earth) for Nibru as mooring post; Ps 87:5-7.
- Compare Gen 2:15 and Ps 104:23 (work given to man) and the Atrahasis opening for the gods' labour with A:107-114.

**Ishme-Dagan X: hymn to Enki, creator of the seed of mankind, their father, mother and shepherd** (ETCSL 2.5.4.24 1-41)
- Compare Isa 40:13-14 ('Whom did he consult?') and Job 12:13 with lines 12-16; Prov 9:1-6 (Wisdom opens her house) with lines 27-28.
- Compare Ps 145:15-16 (you give them their food in due season, satisfying every living thing) and Isa 49:15, 66:13 (God as mother) with lines 24-26; Q 26:79 (he who feeds me and gives me drink).

**Lipit-Eshtar A: the king's self-praise: beauty, divine endowments, piety, warfare, justice, and Inana's embrace** (ETCSL 2.5.5.1 1-108)
- Compare 1 Sam 16:12 and 17:42 (David ruddy and handsome) and Ps 45:3 ('you are fairer than the sons of men; grace is poured on your lips') with lines 11-16.
- Compare Ps 45:7 and Ps 82:6 ('you are gods') with line 20.
- Compare Ps 24:3-4 (clean hands and pure heart) with line 23; Exod 23:19 (first-fruits to the house of YHWH) with line 62.
- Compare Deut 1:16-17, 2 Chr 19:6-7 and Prov 18:13, 17 (hear the case fully before answering) with lines 83-90; Gen 18:25 (shall not the judge of all the earth slay the righteous?) with line 89.
- Compare Prov 25:13, 25 (like cold water to a weary soul) with line 80; Isa 32:2 (the king as shade, as streams of water).

**Lipit-Eshtar B: the king taught by Nisaba, wise judge who reads thoughts and pardons, heir of Išme-Dagan, praised in the schools** (ETCSL 2.5.5.2 1-63)
- Compare 1 Kgs 3:9-12, 16-28 (Solomon's discerning heart in judgment) and Prov 20:8; 1 Sam 16:7 (God sees the heart) with lines 31-32.
- Compare 2 Sam 14:1-11 and 19:22-24 (the king spares a man condemned to death) with lines 33-35; Prov 20:28.
- Compare 1 Kgs 2:12 and 2:24 (Solomon's throne established, his father David) with lines 51-56.
- Compare Deut 17:18-19 (the king writes a copy of the Torah) with lines 18-24.

**Lipit-Eshtar C: adab of An, who chooses the king and blesses him in direct speech** (ETCSL 2.5.5.3 A:1-I:60)
- Compare Ps 2:7-9 and Ps 110:1-3 (the god's direct speech to the newly chosen king; rule over the nations) with G:33-50.
- Compare Ps 72:8 (dominion from sea to sea) with G:42; Ps 89:2-5 and 20-30 with G:33-50.

**Lipit-Eshtar D: adab to Ninurta, suckled by Nintur and presented to Enlil for his fate, asked to arm the king** (ETCSL 2.5.5.4 A:1-H:51)
- Compare Ps 22:10 (you made me trust at my mother's breasts) and Isa 66:11 with B:5-6.
- Compare 1 Kgs 1:15-21 (Bathsheba presents Solomon's claim before the king his father) with B:9-11.
- Compare Ps 18:35 and 144:1 (who trains my hands for war) and Ps 2:9 (shatter them like a potter's vessel) with H:48-49; Isa 42:3 (a bruised reed).

**Lipit-Eshtar E: Enlil and Ninisina in dialogue decree an unalterable fate for the king** (ETCSL 2.5.5.5 A:1-F:31)
- Compare Isa 43:1 and 45:3-4 ('I have called you by name') with D:20; Num 23:19-20 and Isa 14:27 (what God has decreed cannot be reversed) with F:29-30.
- Compare Ps 18:43 (beat them fine as dust before the wind) and Mic 4:12 (gathered like sheaves to the threshing floor) with D:24.

**Ur-Ninurta B: tigi to Enki, junior Enlil, commissioned by An to water the land, creator and preserver of mankind** (ETCSL 2.5.6.2 A:1-D:48)
- Compare Deut 11:11-14, Ps 65:10-14 and Ps 104:13-16 (God waters the fields from his upper chambers, grain and wine) with A:8-11; Jer 5:24.
- Compare Deut 4:35, 39 and 6:4 ('in heaven above and on earth beneath he is God, there is no other') with A:15 (dili-ni diĝir-ra-am3, Enlil alone is god).
- Compare Neh 9:6 (you give life to them all) and Job 12:10 with C:33; Q 2:258, 50:43 (he gives life and death).
- Compare Ps 80:11 (its shade covered the mountains) with C:29.

**Ur-Ninurta C: adab of Ninurta, right arm of Enlil, who entrusts the four quarters to Ur-Ninurta** (ETCSL 2.5.6.3 A:1-H:55)
- Compare Exod 15:6, 12 and Ps 118:15-16 (YHWH's right hand) and Ps 80:18 (the man of your right hand) with C:14.
- Compare Exod 15:11 and Ps 89:7-9 (who is like you?) with F:36; Ps 104:32 (he looks on the earth and it trembles) with B:11.
- Compare Jer 1:5 and Judg 13:5 (set apart from the womb for a task) with A:4.

**Ur-Ninurta D: adab of Inana, equal of An, who chose Ur-Ninurta as en and lover** (ETCSL 2.5.6.4 A:1-F:42)
- Compare Ps 23:2 ('he makes me lie down in green pastures') with D:33; Ezek 34:14-15.
- Compare Song 1:3, 12-13 (fragrance of the beloved's oils; myrrh between my breasts) and Song 1:16 with B:18-19.

**Ur-Ninurta E: adab of An, who gives the king throne, crook and sceptre and addresses him: 'trust in my name'** (ETCSL 2.5.6.5 A:1-E:50)
- Compare Isa 44:6, 45:5-7 and Deut 32:39 ('I, I am he, there is no god beside me') with E:46-47; Isa 55:11 (my word will not return empty) with E:48.
- Compare Ps 20:8 (some trust in chariots, we in the name of YHWH) and Prov 18:10 with D:33.
- Compare Ps 2:7-9 and Ps 110 (oracle to the beloved son, rule over enemies) with D:27-44.

**Ur-Ninurta F: hymn to Iškur, the storm whose successive winds and clouds bring the harvest** (ETCSL 2.5.6.6 A.A:1-B.E:17)
- Compare Ps 29 (the voice of YHWH over the waters, the storm) and Ps 65:10-14 (rain and full granaries) with A.B:4-B.C:9; Q 30:48 (winds raise clouds and rain comes forth).
- Compare 1 Kgs 18:41-45 (successive looks toward the sea before the rain cloud appears) with B.C:2-4; Q 7:57.

**Bur-Sîn B: adab to Enlil, whose word none can interpret, who promises the king days like Utu's** (ETCSL 2.5.7.2 A.A:1-B.D:16)
- Compare Ps 72:5, 17 and Ps 89:37-38 (his throne as long as the sun, may his name endure as long as the sun) with B.B:7; Ps 21:5.

**Enlil-bani A: the king created by An, his name set on the tablet of life by Nisaba, a merciful judge** (ETCSL 2.5.8.1 1–3-91)
- Compare Exod 32:32-33, Ps 69:29, Isa 4:3, Mal 3:16 and Dan 12:1 (names written in God's book of life) with lines 37-48; Q 83:18-21 ('illiyyun, a written register).
- Compare Ps 103:3 (who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases) with lines 82-83; Ezek 18:23, 33:11 (no pleasure in the death of the wicked) with lines 84-85.
- Compare Ps 72:1-2 and Isa 11:3-4 (the king judges not by appearance) with lines 68-79.

**Enlil-bani A: kings bow and bring tribute; the gods' gifts; praise in the scribal academy** (ETCSL 2.5.8.1 92-184)
- Compare Ps 72:9-11 (his enemies lick the dust; kings bring tribute and bow down) and Isa 49:23 with lines 98-111.
- Compare Rev 2:10 and Jas 1:12 (the crown of life) with line 145; Ps 21:4.
- Compare 1 Kgs 5:4 (peace on every side) with lines 101-105.

**Gungunum A: adab to Nanna, who is to gather the scattered of Sumer and give the king long life in Urim** (ETCSL 2.6.2.1 A.A:2-B.E:15)
- Compare Deut 30:3-5, Isa 11:12 and Jer 23:3 (God gathers the scattered and restores them) with B.D:3-5.
- Compare Ps 89:38 (enduring like the moon, a faithful witness in the sky) and Ps 72:5.

**Sîn-iddinam A: the king ships new-year first-fruits to Urim; Suen carries them to Enlil and prays for the king** (ETCSL 2.6.6.1 1-25)
- Compare Lev 23:10-14 and Deut 26:1-11 (the first sheaf and first-fruits brought to the sanctuary) with lines 1-10; Exod 23:16, 34:22 (feast at the turn of the year).
- Compare Ps 61:7-8 and Ps 21:5 (he asked life of you; you gave him length of days forever) with lines 14-18.

**Sîn-iqisham A: hymn to Numušda, fated in the womb, lion-faced and eagle-clawed, for whose city Kazallu the king restores canals** (ETCSL 2.6.7.1 A:1-D:60)
- Compare Ezek 1:10 and 10:14 (faces of lion and eagle) and Dan 7:4 (lion with eagle's wings) with B:22, C:26; Hos 13:7-8.
- Compare Isa 58:12 and 61:4 (rebuild the ancient ruins, restore the desolate cities) and Amos 9:14 with D:48-53.
- Compare Jer 1:5 with A:1-2 (destiny fixed in the womb).

**Rim-Sîn A: a servant's prayer that Enlil and the gods of Nibru grant the king throne, reign and life** (ETCSL 2.6.9.1 1-25)
- The speaker calls himself dumu lu2 'son of a man' (lines 11, 15-16), apparently a servant or official; text obscure. Compare Ps 72:1-2, 15 (prayer for the king continually).

**Rim-Sîn B: hymn to Ḫaia, scribe of the tablets of destiny, archivist of heaven and earth, who hears prayer** (ETCSL 2.6.9.2 A:1-B:60)
- Compare Ps 139:16 ('in your book were written all the days'), Exod 32:32, Ps 69:29 and Mal 3:16 (book of remembrance) with A:5 and A:52; Q 57:22 (nothing befalls but it is in a book) and Q 6:59.
- Compare Ezek 9:2-4 (the man clothed in linen with a scribe's inkhorn) with A:5, A:9.
- Compare Deut 33:27 (underneath are the everlasting arms) with B:59; Ps 65:3 (you who hear prayer).

**Rim-Sîn C: prayer to An for the king called by name in the womb: crown, throne of life, sceptre, and the breasts of heaven opened** (ETCSL 2.6.9.3 1-29)
- Compare Gen 49:25 (blessings of heaven above ... of breasts and womb), Deut 28:12 (YHWH will open his good treasury, the heavens, to give rain) and Mal 3:10 with line 23.
- Compare Isa 49:1 and Jer 1:5 with lines 1-3; Ps 45:7-8 (sceptre of equity) with line 20.
- Line 29 is a scribal subscript: '28 lines; a prayer to An'.

**Rim-Sîn D: prayer to the gods of peace at the Great Gate of Urim as the king enters** (ETCSL 2.6.9.4 1-49)
- Compare Ps 24:7-10 ('Lift up your heads, O gates, that the King of glory may come in') and Ps 118:19-20 (open to me the gates of righteousness) with lines 7-23.
- Compare Ps 85:11-14 and 89:15 (righteousness and justice go before God, as personified attendants) with line 3.
- Compare Ps 121:8 (YHWH will keep your going out and coming in) and Ps 91:11 with lines 33-43.

**Rim-Sîn E: prayer that the god accept the king's pure offerings and give him life, stars' years and a fruitful land** (ETCSL 2.6.9.5 1-85)
- Compare Gen 15:5 and 22:17 (descendants as the stars of heaven) and Ps 89:30, 37 (throne as the days of heaven) with lines 67-68.
- Compare Deut 11:13-15 and 28:4-12 (rain in its season; grain, wine, oil, flocks) and Lev 26:4 with lines 78-84.
- Compare Num 28:7, 14 (drink offerings of strong drink and wine) and Deut 32:14 (butter of cattle, milk of sheep, best of wheat, blood of the grape) with lines 8-17; contrast Ps 50:12-13.
- Compare Zeph 3:9 (to serve him with one accord) with line 76.

**Rim-Sîn F: the abzu shrine of E-kiš-nu-ĝal, its eagle emblem, reed doors, sacred marsh and guardian gods** (ETCSL 2.6.9.6 1-46)
- Compare 1 Chr 9:17-27 and 24-26 (Levite gatekeepers in rotating courses guarding the temple) with lines 32-38; Ps 84:11 (doorkeeper in the house of my God).
- Compare 1 Kgs 6:29-35 and Ezek 41:17-20 (carved cherubim and palms on the temple doors) with lines 9-12; Ezek 1:10 (eagle face).
- Compare Exod 30:7-8 and Ps 141:2 (incense rising before God) with line 43.

**Rim-Sîn G: blessing that Nanna and Ningal accept the king's offerings and words, save him from famine and give abundance** (ETCSL 2.6.9.7 1-51)
- Compare Ps 19:15 ('may the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable') with lines 3-6; Ps 141:2.
- Compare Ps 33:19 (to keep them alive in famine) and Ps 37:19 with line 8; Gen 41.
- Compare Ps 20:4-6 (may he remember all your offerings ... grant you your heart's desire) with lines 1-7, 39-47.

**Rim-Sîn H: fragmentary adab of Inana: Nintur's creation of the king, and Inana asked to give him lasting renown and life** (ETCSL 2.6.9.8 A.A:1-B.D:14)
- Compare Ps 72:17 (may his name endure forever) with B.D:8.

**Praise poem of Anam of Unug: god-fearing en of Inana, rebuilder of E-me-urur, who released the people of Nibru** (ETCSL 2.7.1.1 1-41)
- Compare Ezra 1:1-4 and Isa 45:13 (the ruler who lets the exiles go to the holy city and rebuilds the temple) and Jer 34:8-10 (release of slaves) with lines 22-24, 38-41.
- Compare Gen 22:12 and Job 1:1 (one who fears God) with line 6; Prov 3:9-10.
- Lines 12-21 largely broken (Nanaya named at line 17).

**A praise poem of Hammu-rabi (Hammu-rabi A), fragments** (ETCSL 2.8.2.1)
- Gods each contributing a gift to the king compare the prologue of the Laws of Hammurabi; for a king's realm bounded by rivers compare Gen 15:18 and 1Kgs 5:1 (Euphrates boundary).

**A prayer to Marduk (?) for Hammu-rabi (Hammu-rabi B)** (ETCSL 2.8.2.2 1-13)
- Compare Ps 21:4-5 (crown of fine gold, length of days for ever) and Ps 72:17 (may his name endure for ever); 1Kgs 3:12 wisdom given to the king; Q 38:20 'We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom'.

**A praise poem of Hammu-rabi (Hammu-rabi C)** (ETCSL 2.8.2.3 1-14)
- The king restoring the purification rites of the moon-god's temple compares Hezekiah's and Josiah's restorations of the cult (2Chr 29:3-36; 2Kgs 23:21-23).

**A prayer for Hammu-rabi (Hammu-rabi D)** (ETCSL 2.8.2.4 1-37)
- The gods conferring and naming the king compares Ps 2:6-8 and Ps 89:20-28; the divine council deciding (1Kgs 22:19-22, Ps 82:1). God at the king's right hand: Ps 110:5, Ps 16:8, Ps 121:5. 'Trust in our august commands': Ps 21:8.

**A prayer for Hammu-rabi (Hammu-rabi E), ending** (ETCSL 2.8.2.5)
- 'Called by name' compares Isa 45:3-4 (Cyrus called by name) and Isa 43:1.

**A praise poem of Hammu-rabi addressed to Inana (Hammu-rabi F)** (ETCSL 2.8.2.6 1-20)
- Wisdom/a female figure beside God in judgment: Prov 8:15-16 'by me kings reign'; Ps 72:3,16 abundance under the just king.

**A praise poem of Samsu-iluna (Samsu-iluna A)** (ETCSL 2.8.3.1 1-30)
- Protective spirits given to the king's side compare Ps 91:11 (angels to guard you) and 2Kgs 6:16-17; the goddess at the right hand compares Ps 110:5.

**A prayer for Samsu-iluna (Samsu-iluna B)** (ETCSL 2.8.3.2 1-39)
- Ps 72:1-7 (the king judges like the righteous sun-lit rain), Ps 89:29,36-37 (throne as the days of heaven, as sun and moon), Ps 18:35 (God trains my hands for war), Ps 110:1-2. Namma placing water in the king's mouth (line 33) is unique here.

**A prayer for Samsu-iluna (Samsu-iluna C)** (ETCSL 2.8.3.3 1-40)
- Lam 4:20 'the breath of our nostrils, the anointed of YHWH, ... in his shade we shall live among the nations'; Isa 32:1-2 (a king as shade of a great rock); Ps 72:5 (fear him as long as sun and moon); Isa 9:5 'Everlasting Father'; Num 11:12 (Moses: did I conceive this people, that you say carry them like a nurse?).

**A prayer for Samsu-iluna (Samsu-iluna E)** (ETCSL 2.8.3.5 1-46)
- The shining face of the god turned to the king: Num 6:25-26, Ps 4:7, Ps 80:4. Enemies into his hand: Ps 18:38-41, 2Sam 22:41. The king flourishing: Ps 72:16, Ps 92:13-15. Ushered before the god with offerings: Ps 24:3-6.

**A hymn to Enlil for Samsu-iluna (Samsu-iluna F), in syllabic orthography** (ETCSL 2.8.3.6)
- Ps 72:8 'dominion from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth'; Ps 8:7 and Ps 110:1 (under his feet); Ps 21:5 'he asked life of you, you gave it him, length of days for ever'.
