**A prayer for Samsu-iluna (Samsu-iluna G), bilingual** (ETCSL 2.8.3.7 1-6)
- Equation of Asalluḫi with Marduk underlies the Marduk theology later read in Enuma eliš; compare the merging of divine names in Exod 6:2-3.

**A hymn to Enlil for Samsu-iluna (Samsu-iluna H), bilingual** (ETCSL 2.8.3.8 1-13)
- Lines 6-8 broken. The same lines (B:3, B:7) occur in Samsu-iluna F: a hymn reused.

**A praise poem of Abi-Ešuḫ (Abi-Eshuh A), addressed to Marduk** (ETCSL 2.8.5.1)
- Marduk's elevation by An and Enlil compares Enūma eliš IV-VI and the Laws of Hammurabi prologue i 1-15 (Enlilship given to Marduk); compare Ps 82 and Ps 89:6-8 (who among the sons of god is like YHWH?). God as knower of hearts: 1Sam 16:7, Jer 17:10, Q 67:13 (ʿalīm bi-dhāt al-ṣudūr).

**Letter from Aradĝu to Šulgi about Apillaša, the arrogant official** (ETCSL 3.1.01 1-34)
- The envoy who will not sit or eat until he has spoken his master's word: Gen 24:33 (Abraham's servant: 'I will not eat until I have told my errand'). A subordinate who sits enthroned with a footstool: Esth 3:1-2 (Haman, before whom all must bow) and Ps 110:1.

**Letter from Šulgi to Aradĝu about Apillaša** (ETCSL 3.1.02 1-35)
- The king's deputy enthroned with power over officials and life: Gen 41:40-44 (Joseph: 'only in the throne will I be greater than you'), Esth 8:2,8, Dan 2:48; power 'to kill or keep alive': Dan 5:19.

**Letter from Aradĝu to Šulgi about irrigation work** (ETCSL 3.1.03 1-18)
- A realm defined by sea and river boundaries: 1Kgs 5:1,4 (from the River to Gaza), Ps 72:8.

**Letter from Aradĝu to Šulgi about attentive citizens** (ETCSL 3.1.04)
- 'The eyes of all wait upon you': Ps 145:15; the people's acclamation 'Long live the king': 1Sam 10:24, 1Kgs 1:39. 'All that the LORD has spoken we will do': Exod 19:8.

**Letter from Aradĝu to Šulgi about Aba-indasa's missing troops** (ETCSL 3.1.05 1-15)
- Counting the troops after a battle and finding men missing (or none missing): Num 31:49, 2Sam 2:30.

**Letter from Aradĝu to Šulgi about the fortress Igi-ḫursaĝa (bilingual)** (ETCSL 3.1.06)
- 'The word of the king is like an angel of God': 2Sam 14:17,20; 'where the word of a king is, there is power': Eccl 8:4. 'From the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great': Mal 1:11, Ps 113:3.

**Letter from Puzur-Šulgi to Šulgi about the advance of the enemy** (ETCSL 3.1.07 1-34)
- Rebuilding a breached wall by named sectors, each official responsible for so many measures: Neh 3:1-32; basket-carriers and guarding while building: Neh 4:10-17. Resettlement of a conquered population: 2Kgs 17:6,24, 18:31-32.

**Letter from Šulgi to Puzur-Šulgi about work on the fortress Igi-ḫursaĝa (two versions, one syllabic and bilingual)** (ETCSL 3.1.08)
- Night-and-day building under threat, completed quickly: Neh 4:16-17,21-23 and Neh 6:15 (finished in 52 days). Men and women going wherever they please in security: compare 1Kgs 5:5 (each under his vine) and Zech 8:4-5.

**Letter to Šulgi about bandits and brigands** (ETCSL 3.1.11 1-20)
- Sa-gaz/Ḫabiru compare the ʿapiru of the Amarna letters and the debated link with 'Hebrews' (Gen 14:13, 1Sam 14:21). The king who discerns evil like a god: 2Sam 14:17,20; Prov 20:8.

**Letter from the merchant Ur-DUN to Šulgi about the purchase of cedar resin** (ETCSL 3.1.11.1 1-20)
- Cedar products fetched from a distant land with royal silver: 1Kgs 5:6-10; a merchant's complaint of seizure compares the Amarna letters on robbed caravans (EA 8).

**Letter from Šulgi to Išbi-Erra about the purchase of grain (syllabic, bilingual)** (ETCSL 3.1.13.2 1-29)
- Joseph made over Egypt and the grain: Gen 41:40-44 (throne, signet, 'abrek' cried before him), Gen 41:55-57; the trusted house-born servant: Gen 15:2-3, 24:2. 'You are my son': Ps 2:7. Q 12:54-56 (the king makes Joseph 'established and trusted', over the storehouses of the land).

**Letter from Šarrum-bāni to Šu-Suen about keeping the Martu at bay** (ETCSL 3.1.15 1-43)
- Building with one hand and holding a weapon with the other: Neh 4:11-12 (4:17-18 Eng). A wall to keep out invaders compares Q 18:94-97 (Dhu l-Qarnayn's barrier against Gog and Magog).

**Letter from Šu-Suen to Šarrum-bāni about digging a trench** (ETCSL 3.1.16 1-45)
- A son-king insisting his rule differs from his father's: 1Kgs 12:10-14 (Rehoboam: 'my little finger is thicker than my father's loins').

**Letter from Išbi-Erra to Ibbi-Suen about the purchase of grain** (ETCSL 3.1.17 1-58)
- Grain stored for many years for palace and cities, and the official who controls it rising to power: Gen 41:35-49, 47:13-26; Q 12:47-49. 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you': Jer 1:5, Isa 49:1, Ps 22:11.

**Letter from Ibbi-Suen to Išbi-Erra about his bad conduct** (ETCSL 3.1.18 1-18)
- God handing his own city to the enemy: Jer 21:10, 32:28, 2Kgs 21:14; Lam 2:7. The day God turns back to his people: Zech 1:3, Isa 54:7-8. False balances in selling grain: Amos 8:5.

**Letter from Puzur-Šulgi to Ibbi-Suen about Išbi-Erra's claim on Isin** (ETCSL 3.1.19 1-53)
- An invader claiming the god of the land sent him: 2Kgs 18:25 / Isa 36:10 (Rabshakeh: 'YHWH said to me, go up against this land'); 2Chr 35:21 (Necho). 'Just as he said, so he did': cf. Num 23:19.

**Letter from Ibbi-Suen to Puzur-Šulgi hoping for Išbi-Erra's downfall** (ETCSL 3.1.20)
- God raising a lowly or foreign ruler: Dan 4:14 (4:17 Eng) 'he sets over it the lowliest of men'; Deut 28:43-44; 1Sam 2:7-8. God gives kingship to whom he will: Q 3:26, Q 2:247 (Saul not of royal stock). God stirring up one nation against another: Isa 13:17, Jer 51:11.

**Letter from Aba-indasa to Šulgi about his neglect (a petition from disgrace)** (ETCSL 3.1.21 1-24A)
- A disgraced servant asking to be remembered before the king: Gen 40:14-15, 41:9-13; bound and in sackcloth: Ps 30:12, Ps 102:10. 'No one cares for my soul': Ps 142:5. God's care for the poor at table: Ps 113:7-8, 1Sam 2:8. The widow's son: 1Kgs 17:17-24, Luke 7:12.

**Letter from Lipit-Eštar to Nanna-ki-aĝ about driving away the enemy** (ETCSL 3.2.04 1-17)
- Army divisions by weapon: 2Chr 14:7 (shield and spear from Judah, bowmen from Benjamin), 1Chr 12:2,8.

**Letter-prayer from Sîn-iddinam to the god Utu about the distress of Larsa** (ETCSL 3.2.05 1-46)
- Why do the impious foreigners prosper while the pious suffer: Jer 12:1-2, Hab 1:13-17, Ps 73:3-12, Ps 44:18-23. God became like an enemy: Lam 2:4-5. 'Look upon your city': Dan 9:18-19, Ps 74. Lions killing men in the land: 2Kgs 17:25. Young men harvested: Jer 9:21. God who desires not the death of anyone: Ezek 18:32.

**Letter from Ur-saga to a king fearing the loss of his father's household (bilingual)** (ETCSL 3.3.01 1-14)
- Holding on to the father's inheritance against seizure: 1Kgs 21:3 (Naboth), Num 27:4, Ruth 4:5; 2Kgs 8:3-6 (woman petitions the king for her house and field). 'Let the word of my lord be like rain': Deut 32:2, 2Sam 23:4.

**Letter-prayer from Nanna-manšum to Nininsina about his unsuccessful medical treatment** (ETCSL 3.3.21 1-20)
- Physicians who could not heal, so the sufferer turns to the divine healer: Mark 5:26 (woman who spent all on physicians), 2Chr 16:12 (Asa sought physicians, not YHWH), Jer 8:22, Job 13:4. Birds in purification of the sick: Lev 14:4-7. Q 26:80 'when I am sick, He heals me'.

**Letter-prayer from X to the god Nanna (bilingual)** (ETCSL 3.3.22 1-16)
- Exod 34:6 (raḥum we-ḥannun) and Q 1:1-3 (al-raḥmān al-raḥīm) compare 'merciful, relenting god who hears prayer'. Ps 65:3 'you who hear prayer'. Binding and loosing: Job 12:18, Isa 58:6, Matt 16:19.

**A hymn to Bau's beneficent protective goddess (Bau A), partly bilingual** (ETCSL 4.02.1)
- A tablet of life brought from heaven compares the heavenly book of life (Exod 32:32-33, Ps 69:29, Dan 12:1) and Q 56:77-79 / 85:21-22 (the preserved tablet). A name sweet like oil: Song 1:3; sweeter than honey: Ps 19:11. God as husband and father to the widow and orphan: Ps 68:6, Isa 54:5.

**Enlil in the E-kur (Enlil A), part 1, Enlil's word and his city Nibru** (ETCSL 4.05.1 1-83)
- Jerusalem/Zion as the navel and center of the earth: Ezek 5:5, 38:12; Ps 48:2-3. Who may dwell on God's holy mountain (no slander, no evil): Ps 15, Ps 101:5-8, Isa 33:14-16. Honour parents for long life: Exod 20:12, Deut 5:16; Q 17:23-24. Kings bringing gifts to the temple: Ps 68:30, 72:10-11, Isa 60:3-11. Tower with top in heaven: Gen 11:4.

**Enlil in the E-kur (Enlil A), part 2, the shepherd, the 'without Enlil' litany, Enlil's word and Ninlil** (ETCSL 4.05.1 84-171)
- 'Unless YHWH builds the house ...': Ps 127:1; all creation depends on God: Ps 104:27-30, John 1:3. 'Who has directed the spirit of YHWH, or as his counsellor taught him?': Isa 40:13-14, Job 11:7-9, Rom 11:33-34. No one can see God's face and live: Exod 33:20. God's word like rain that does not return empty: Isa 55:10-11. God as shepherd of all: Ps 23, Ps 80:2.

**A balbale to Inana (Inana A)** (ETCSL 4.07.1 1-24)
- God judging in the divine assembly: Ps 82:1; the light that separates righteous and wicked: Mal 3:18-20, Ps 1:5-6.

**The exaltation of Inana (Inana B, nin-me-šar-ra), part 1, the goddess of all the divine powers** (ETCSL 4.07.2 1-65)
- Rivers turned to blood so the people cannot drink: Exod 7:17-21, Ps 78:44, Rev 16:4; Q 7:133 (blood among the signs on Pharaoh's people). The deity whose wrath none can withstand: Nah 1:6, Ps 76:8. Fire raining on the land: Gen 19:24, Ps 11:6.

**The exaltation of Inana (Inana B), part 2, En-ḫedu-ana's expulsion, plea and vindication** (ETCSL 4.07.2 66-154)
- A priestly author expelled, wandering in the thorns, pleading for vindication: compare the laments of Jeremiah (Jer 20:7-18) and Ps 42-43 (driven from the temple), Ps 55:7-8 ('oh that I had wings like a dove, I would fly away'). Weeping child not comforted: Jer 31:15. Protestation of innocence: Job 31, Ps 7:4-6. Tears as offering: Ps 56:9, Ps 126:5. Imprecation on the city of the enemy: Ps 137:7-9.

**A hymn to Inana (Inana C, in-nin šag4-gur4-ra), part 1, the terror of the goddess** (ETCSL 4.07.3 1-114)
- The day turned to darkness at noon: Amos 8:9, Joel 2:10, Jer 15:9. God's net that none escapes: Ezek 12:13, 17:20, Hos 7:12. A deity whose plans the gods cannot know: Isa 40:13-14, 55:8-9. The cup of poison/wrath given to drink: Jer 25:15-16, Ps 75:9; gall to eat: Jer 9:14.

**A hymn to Inana (Inana C), part 2, the 'are yours, Inana' litany and the goddess's sovereignty** (ETCSL 4.07.3 115-218)
- 'A time to tear down and a time to build up, to plant and to uproot': Eccl 3:2-8; Jer 1:10. 'YHWH makes poor and makes rich, brings low and lifts up': 1Sam 2:6-8, Ps 75:8, Luke 1:52; Q 3:26 ('You give kingship to whom You will ... You honour whom You will and humble whom You will'). God judges without bribe: Deut 10:17. Gathering the dispersed: Deut 30:3-4, Isa 11:12. Passing under the shepherd's inspection: Ezek 20:37, Jer 33:13. 'Who is like you among the gods?': Exod 15:11.

**A hymn to Inana (Inana C), part 3, En-ḫedu-ana's closing prayer** (ETCSL 4.07.3 219-274)
- 'Enough! Stay your hand' said to the destroying angel: 2Sam 24:16; God relenting: Joel 2:13, Jon 4:2. 'Your hand was heavy on me ... my body wasted': Ps 32:3-4, 38:2-4. 'Arise, YHWH, to your resting place': Ps 132:8, Num 10:36.

**A hymn to Inana as Ninegala (Inana D), part 1, the astral goddess, her seats and her ways** (ETCSL 4.07.4 1-117)
- The Queen of Heaven: Jer 7:18, 44:17-19. The morning star: Isa 14:12 (helel ben-shaḥar). The harlot at the window and in the streets: Prov 7:6-12; Ezek 16:24-25. Feeding the dead and memorial water: Deut 26:14 (no tithe given to the dead), Ps 106:28. A mother bringing her sick child: 2Kgs 4:18-37, Mark 7:25-30.

**A hymn to Inana as Ninegala (Inana D), part 2, evening star, the broken middle and the divine family** (ETCSL 4.07.4 118-216)
- The woman who goes from house to house and lane to lane: Prov 7:8-12, Song 3:2. 'How you are fallen from heaven, morning star': Isa 14:12.

**A tigi to Inana (Inana E), Inana and King Ama-ušumgal-ana** (ETCSL 4.07.5)
- Renewal like the moon: Ps 72:5-7, Ps 89:38 (established for ever like the moon); 'your youth renewed like the eagle's': Ps 103:5. 'You are my son, today I have begotten you': Ps 2:7, Ps 110:3 (from the womb of dawn).

**A hymn to Inana (Inana F), Inana's self-praise (Emesal)** (ETCSL 4.07.6 1-34)
- 'Heaven is my throne and the earth my footstool': Isa 66:1; 'I am, and there is none besides me': Isa 45:5-6, 47:8 (said by Babylon). 'Who is like me?': Isa 44:7, 46:9. Q 2:255 (His kursī extends over heavens and earth).

**A šir-namšub to Inana (Inana G), Inana's journey, Dumuzid in E-ana, and the breasts that are fields** (ETCSL 4.07.7 1-78)
- Breasts and womb as blessings of fertility: Gen 49:25; the beloved's breasts: Song 4:5, 7:8-9, Prov 5:19. Linen-clad priests: Exod 28:42, 1Sam 2:18, Ezek 44:17. River whose streams gladden the city of God: Ps 46:5.

**A balbale to Inana as Nanaya, main text (Inana H)** (ETCSL 4.07.8 1:1-33)
- Compare Song 4:1-7 and 7:1-9 (wasf, body praised part by part), Song 7:2 (navel).
- The woman as field to be ploughed: compare Q 2:223 (nisa'ukum harthun lakum, 'your women are a tilth for you') and Judg 14:18 ('had you not ploughed with my heifer').
- Compare Song 1:2 ('let him kiss me') and Song 4:9-10 ('my sister, bride').

**A balbale to Inana as Nanaya, fragments of a second version (Inana H, segments 2.A-2.B)** (ETCSL 4.07.8 2.A:1-9, ETCSL 4.07.8 2.B:1-7)
- Compare Song 4:12-16 (the beloved as garden) and Song 7:3 (belly a heap of wheat).

**A shir-namshub to Inana, segment A - Inana's self-praise (Inana I)** (ETCSL 4.07.9 A:1-34)
- Divine self-predication in an 'I am' litany: compare Isa 44:24-28, Isa 45:5-7 and Q 20:14 ('Indeed I am God, there is no god but I').
- The goddess at the tavern gate as harlot: compare Prov 7:10-12 (the woman at the corners, in harlot's garb) and Gen 38:14-15.

**A shir-namshub to Inana, segment B - supplication for the life of the king (Inana I)** (ETCSL 4.07.9 B:1-30)
- Compare Ps 21:4-6 and Ps 61:6-7 (prayer for the king's life and length of days).
- 'Queen of heaven' as Inana/Ištar: compare Jer 7:18 and 44:17-19.

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid - Utu, Inana and the flax (Dumuzid-Inana A)** (ETCSL 4.08.01 1-57)
- Compare Song 8:8-9 (the brothers deliberate over their little sister's marriage) and Gen 24:29-60 (Laban, the brother, arranges Rebekah's marriage).
- Linen-making stage by stage: compare Prov 31:13, 19, 22, 24.
- A bed spread with linen for love: compare Prov 7:16-17.

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid - the oath of women (Dumuzid-Inana B)** (ETCSL 4.08.02 1-33)
- Compare Song 2:6 and 8:3 ('his left hand under my head and his right hand embraces me').
- Hand placed on the genitals for an oath: compare Gen 24:2-9 and 47:29 (hand under the thigh).
- Compare Song 2:3 (the lover as apple tree), Song 5:10-16 (the lover's body as gold and jewels), Song 4:11 (honey on the lips).

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid - bathing, gifts and coming of age (Dumuzid-Inana C)** (ETCSL 4.08.03 A:1-49)
- The girl's coming of age: compare Ezek 16:7-8 ('your breasts were formed and your hair had grown ... it was the time of love') and Song 8:8-10.
- Bathing, anointing and dressing before the lover: compare Ruth 3:3 and Ezek 16:9-13.

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid - the brother's house and the bed of honey (Dumuzid-Inana D)** (ETCSL 4.08.04 1-23)
- Compare Song 1:4 ('the king has brought me into his chambers') and Song 2:4.
- 'Let me go': compare Gen 32:27 (the night wrestler, 'let me go, for dawn is breaking') and Song 3:4 ('I held him and would not let him go').

**The song of the lettuce - a balbale to Inana and Dumuzid (Dumuzid-Inana E)** (ETCSL 4.08.05 1-11)
- Compare Song 2:3 ('as an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved ... his fruit sweet to my taste') and Song 5:10-16.

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid - Inana makes her king sprout like a meš tree (Dumuzid-Inana F)** (ETCSL 4.08.06 1-45)
- Compare Ps 92:13-15 ('planted in the house of the LORD, they flourish in the courts of our God') and Ps 52:10 ('like a green olive tree in the house of God').
- Compare Song 1:16-17 ('our couch is green, the beams of our house are cedar, our rafters cypress').

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid - 'You are our brother' (Dumuzid-Inana G)** (ETCSL 4.08.07 1-17)
- Compare Song 8:1 ('O that you were like a brother to me') and Song 1:16.

**A tigi to Inana and Dumuzid - the lies of women (Dumuzid-Inana H, sa-gida)** (ETCSL 4.08.08 A.A:1-23)
- Compare Song 3:4 and 8:2 (the mother's house) and Prov 7:13-18 (the seductive invitation, by night, to a bed spread with linen).
- A daughter deceiving a parent: compare Gen 31:34-35 (Rachel and Laban).

**A tigi to Inana and Dumuzid - fragment (Dumuzid-Inana H, A.B)** (ETCSL 4.08.08 A.B:24-26)
- Compare Song 3:2 ('I will go about the city, in the streets and in the squares').

**A tigi to Inana and Dumuzid - the lover at Ningal's gate (Dumuzid-Inana H, sa-ĝara)** (ETCSL 4.08.08 B.B:1-22)
- Compare Song 2:9 (the lover standing behind the wall) and Song 3:4, 8:2 (bringing him into the mother's house).

**A kunĝar to Inana and Dumuzid - the quarrel and the ploughing with jewels (Dumuzid-Inana I)** (ETCSL 4.08.09 1-46)
- Compare Song 2:9 and 2:14 (the lover at the wall, the dove in the cleft) and Song 1:10-11 (jewels for her neck).
- A woman leaning from the window or wall: compare 2 Sam 6:16 and 2 Kgs 9:30.

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid - the sister seeks her brother; the singers of Unug (Dumuzid-Inana J)** (ETCSL 4.08.10 1-38)
- Self-laceration in mourning: compare Jer 16:6, 41:5, 48:37 and the ban in Deut 14:1, Lev 19:28.
- Singers who know the stars: compare 1 Chr 12:33 (the sons of Issachar who understood the times) and 1 Chr 25:1-7 (the temple singers).

**A balbale (?) to Inana and Dumuzid, segment A - Inana chooses Dumuzid as god of the land (Dumuzid-Inana P)** (ETCSL 4.08.16 A:1-35)
- Choosing one from all the people: compare 1 Sam 10:24 ('see him whom the LORD has chosen, none like him among all the people'), Ps 89:20, Deut 17:15.

**A balbale (?) to Inana and Dumuzid, segment B - Inana's song of her vulva (Dumuzid-Inana P)** (ETCSL 4.08.16 B:1-34)
- Compare Q 2:223 ('your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish') and Judg 14:18.
- Compare Song 4:12-16 and 5:1 (the beloved's 'garden' and the lover coming into it).

**A balbale (?) to Inana and Dumuzid, segment C - vegetation, milk and long life in E-namtila (Dumuzid-Inana P)** (ETCSL 4.08.16 C:1-66)
- Camels' milk (ga am-si-ḫar-ra-an) in a Sumerian song: compare Gen 32:16 (milch camels) and Gen 24 (camels in a betrothal).
- The bride's fertility spreading to the land: compare Hos 2:23-24 (the heavens answer the earth, the earth answers grain, wine and oil).

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid - Inana goes out to the shepherd (Dumuzid-Inana V)** (ETCSL 4.08.22 1-15)
- Compare Song 1:7-8 ('tell me where you pasture your flock') and Song 6:10 ('who is this that looks forth like the dawn').

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid - 'May my sheep eat my plants' (Dumuzid-Inana W)** (ETCSL 4.08.23 5-44)
- Care for orphan and widow: compare Deut 24:19-21 (gleanings left for the orphan and widow), Ruth 2, and Q 2:215.
- Milk and honey: compare Exod 3:8 and Song 4:11 and 5:1.

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid, segment A - 'my mother bore me for you' (Dumuzid-Inana Z)** (ETCSL 4.08.26 A:1-9)
- Compare Song 8:5 ('there your mother conceived you, there she who bore you was in labour') and Song 6:9 ('the only one of her mother').

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid, segment B - 'Let us lie on my flowered bed' (Dumuzid-Inana Z)** (ETCSL 4.08.26 B:1-19)
- Compare Song 3:11 (the crown with which his mother crowned him on his wedding day) and Song 1:16 ('our couch is green').

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid, segment A - the ushers' gifts and 'Open the house' (Dumuzid-Inana C1)** (ETCSL 4.08.29 A:1-32)
- Compare Song 5:2 ('open to me, my sister, my love') and Gen 24:53 (gifts for the bride's family).

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid, segment B - at her mother's bidding Inana opens to Dumuzid (Dumuzid-Inana C1)** (ETCSL 4.08.29 B:1-23)
- Compare Song 6:10 ('fair as the moon') and Song 5:5-6 (she rises to open to her beloved).

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid, segment C - the bride brought to the house of Dumuzid's god (Dumuzid-Inana C1)** (ETCSL 4.08.29 C:1-24)
- Compare Gen 24:67 (Isaac brings Rebekah into his mother's tent) and Ps 45:15-16 (the bride led into the king's palace).

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid, segment D - 'I have not carried you off to be my slave girl' (Dumuzid-Inana C1)** (ETCSL 4.08.29 D:1-27)
- Contrast Prov 31:13, 19 (the capable wife spins and weaves) and compare Exod 21:7-11 (rights of a slave-woman taken as wife), Ps 45:11-16.

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid - the couch, the sacred marriage and the blessing of the king (Dumuzid-Inana D1)** (ETCSL 4.08.30 1-70)
- Dominion 'from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth': compare Ps 72:8 and Zech 9:10; abundance under the king Ps 72:3, 6, 16.
- Compare Ps 2:6-9 and Ps 110:2 (the king given sceptre and rule), Ps 21:5 (life and length of days).
- Compare Ps 45 (royal wedding song, throne, sceptre of equity).

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid, segments B-C - the toilette of the bride; Durtur (Dumuzid-Inana E1)** (ETCSL 4.08.31 B:1-21, ETCSL 4.08.31 C:1-8)
- Compare Ezek 23:40 (bathed, painted eyes, decked with ornaments), 2 Kgs 9:30, Jer 4:30.

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid - the bed of honey and the brother's garden (Dumuzid-Inana F1)** (ETCSL 4.08.32 1-23)
- Compare Song 6:11, 7:12-13 (going down to the garden, the vines and pomegranates) and Song 2:3, 8:5 (under the apple tree); Song 7:8 (the palm and its clusters).

**Dumuzid and Enkimdu - the shepherd and the farmer woo Inana** (ETCSL 4.08.33 1-90)
- Farmer and shepherd as rivals before the deity: compare Gen 4:2-8 (Cain the tiller and Abel the shepherd; one offering preferred). Here the rivalry ends in reconciliation instead of murder.
- Peaceful grazing agreement between rivals: compare Gen 13:8-9 and Gen 26:19-31.

**A hymn to Martu, segment A - Martu's birth and epithets (Martu B)** (ETCSL 4.12.2 A:1-11)
- Compare Isa 40:13-14, 28 ('his understanding is unsearchable') and Rom 11:33.

**A hymn to Martu, segment B - prayers and blessing (Martu B)** (ETCSL 4.12.2 B:1-15)
- Compare Ps 133:2-3 (oil running down, the dew of Hermon) and Ps 128:3-6 (wife and children, long life).

**A balbale to Nanna - the cows of Suen and his mother's blessing (Nanna A)** (ETCSL 4.13.01 1-61)
- Heavenly bodies as a flock or host numbered and named: compare Isa 40:26 and Ps 147:4.
- Compare Ps 2:7 ('you are my son') and Ps 89:28 (the firstborn).
- The moon as a sign of the god: compare Q 36:39 (the moon's stations till it returns like an old palm stalk) and Ps 104:19.

**A balbale to Nanna - Nanna woos Ningal (Nanna B)** (ETCSL 4.13.02 1-60)
- Compare Song 8:1-2 (the mother's house) and Song 2:14 ('let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet').

**A balbale to Nanna, segment A.A - praise of E-kiš-nu-ĝal and En-ḫedu-ana (Nanna C)** (ETCSL 4.13.03 A.A:1-42)
- A high priestess as wife of the god in the ĝipar: compare the 'god's wife' and the women who serve at the tent (1 Sam 2:22, Exod 38:8).

**A balbale to Nanna, segment B.B - the purity of Suen's palace (Nanna C)** (ETCSL 4.13.03 B.B:1-19)
- Purity of grain offerings: compare Lev 2:11 and 6:9-11 (unleavened, holy) and Lev 11:38 (seed made susceptible once water touches it).

**A balbale to Nanna - Nanna's cattle-pen and the abundance of fish and birds (Nanna D)** (ETCSL 4.13.04 1-41)
- Holy food forbidden to some women: compare Lev 22:12-13 (a priest's daughter married to a layman may not eat the holy portions) and Lev 6:11, 22 (only males of the priests eat).
- Numerous as grass: compare Job 5:25 and Ps 72:16.

**A hymn to Nanna - Nanna's powers and his purification and enthronement (Nanna E)** (ETCSL 4.13.05 1-69)
- The god's dais, linen and crown: compare Lev 8:6-12 (Aaron washed, clothed in linen, anointed, crowned with the diadem) and Exod 30:17-21 (washing hands before approaching the altar).
- Compare Ps 89:6-8 (none among the sons of god is like the LORD) and Ps 97:9.

**The herds of Nanna (Nanna F)** (ETCSL 4.13.06 1-45)
- Huge exact counts of a god's or patriarch's flocks: compare Job 1:3 and 42:12, Num 31:32-47 (the counted booty), and 1 Kgs 8:63.
- Recording a count in writing: compare Num 1 and 2 Sam 24:1-9.

**A hymn to Nanna, segments B-C - 'May your beauty cover my body like a garment'; the E-kiš-nu-ĝal (Nanna G)** (ETCSL 4.13.07 B:1-17, ETCSL 4.13.07 C:1-12)
- Clothed with beauty or with God's righteousness: compare Isa 61:10, Ps 104:1-2, Job 29:14.
- Compare Ps 80:11-12 (its shade covered the mountains, its branches to the sea).

**An adab to Nanna - powers granted by An; litany of cities founded by An (Nanna H)** (ETCSL 4.13.08 A.A:1-12, ETCSL 4.13.08 B.B:1-6, ETCSL 4.13.08 B.C:7-10, ETCSL 4.13.08 B.D:11-15)
- Compare Ps 86:8 and Exod 15:11 ('who is like you among the gods?') and Ps 87:1-5 (the city whose foundation is on the holy mountains, founded by the Most High).

**A tigi to Nanna - Urim in the marsh; 'Where have you tended your cows?' (Nanna I)** (ETCSL 4.13.09 A:1-16, ETCSL 4.13.09 B:17-40, ETCSL 4.13.09 B:A-H, ETCSL 4.13.09 B:41-42)
- Compare Song 1:7 ('tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you pasture your flock?') and Ps 23:1-2, Ps 80:2 (the god as shepherd of his people).

**An ululumama to Nanna - light in dark places and the love of creatures (Nanna J)** (ETCSL 4.13.10 1-33)
- Compare Ps 104:19-23 (the moon for seasons, beasts by night) and Ps 136:9 (the moon and stars to rule the night).
- Compare Isa 9:1 ('the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light') and Q 10:5, 71:16 (the moon made a light).

**A shir-namshub to Nanna - the cowherd Suen and Ningal's 'I will live there' (Nanna K)** (ETCSL 4.13.11 A.A:1-21, ETCSL 4.13.11 B.B:1-28)
- 'Where you go I will go, where you lodge I will lodge': compare Ruth 1:16-17 and Ps 132:13-14 ('this is my resting place forever, here I will dwell').
- The same fertility list as Dumuzid-Inana D1: compare Ps 72:16 and Ps 65:10-14.

**A shir-namgala to Nanna - the moon fixes months and year and regulates abundance (Nanna L)** (ETCSL 4.13.12 A:1-7, ETCSL 4.13.12 B:8-17, ETCSL 4.13.12 C:18-47, ETCSL 4.13.12 D:48-53)
- Compare Ps 104:19 (the moon made for seasons), Gen 1:14 (lights for signs, seasons, days and years), Q 10:5 ('he determined stations for it, that you may know the number of years and the reckoning').
- The 'udders/nipples of heaven' as rain sources: compare Gen 7:11 and 8:2 (windows of heaven) and Gen 49:25 (blessings of heaven above ... of breasts and womb).

**A hymn to Nanna in syllabic Emesal spelling - ruler of Urim, mouth like a dragon (Nanna M)** (ETCSL 4.13.13 1-26)
- Compare Ps 121:1 and 123:1-2 ('to you I lift my eyes') and Ps 145:15 ('the eyes of all look to you').

**A hymn to Nanna in syllabic spelling - moonlight for the king, tigi in the forecourt (Nanna N)** (ETCSL 4.13.14 1-33)
- Compare Ps 122:6-9 ('pray for the peace of Jerusalem ... may there be prosperity within your towers') and Ps 150:3-5.

**A hymn to Nanna, segment A - the Anuna attend, the black-headed raise their eyes (Nanna O)** (ETCSL 4.13.15 A:5-31)
- Compare Ps 145:15 and Isa 45:22 ('turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth').

**A hymn to Nanna, segments B-C - 'We are going' to the temples of Šulgi's realm (Nanna O)** (ETCSL 4.13.15 B:1-32, ETCSL 4.13.15 C:1-2)
- Compare Ps 122:1-4 ('let us go to the house of the LORD'), Isa 2:3, and Ps 24:3-4 ('who shall ascend ... he who has clean hands and a pure heart').

**A hymn to Nanshe, lines 1-31 - Niĝin and the goddess who cares for orphan and widow (Nanshe A)** (ETCSL 4.14.1 1-31)
- Compare Ps 68:6-7 ('father of orphans and protector of widows is God ... God gives the lonely a home'), Deut 10:18, Ps 146:9, and Q 93:6-10 and 4:127.
- Compare Ps 113:9 and Ruth 4:13 (a home for the widow).

**A hymn to Nanshe, lines 32-58 - Ur-Nanše and Gudea, music and the banquet of Nanše (Nanshe A)** (ETCSL 4.14.1 32-58)
- The ruler chosen in the deity's heart and given the sceptre: compare 1 Sam 13:14 ('a man after his own heart') and Ps 45:7.
- Music of horn, harp and drum in the sanctuary: compare Ps 150:3-5 and 1 Chr 15:16-28.

**A hymn to Nanshe, lines 59-93 - regular offerings and Ḫendursaĝa who knows true from false speech (Nanshe A)** (ETCSL 4.14.1 59-93)
- Abuse of the offerings by temple officials: compare 1 Sam 2:12-17 (Eli's sons take more than their share).
- Knowing good and evil, discerning true from false speech: compare 2 Sam 14:17 ('like an angel of God to discern good and evil') and 1 Kgs 3:9.

**A hymn to Nanshe, lines 94-136 - the New Year review, the registration tablet and the river ordeal (Nanshe A)** (ETCSL 4.14.1 94-136)
- Names written in and blotted out of a divine register: compare Exod 32:32-33, Ps 69:29, Dan 12:1, Mal 3:16, and Q 83:7-9, 18-21 (the registers Sijjin and Illiyyun).
- 'Do not add to it or take from it': compare Deut 4:2, 13:1, Prov 30:6, Rev 22:18-19.
- Ordeal: compare Num 5:11-31 (the water of bitterness).

**A hymn to Nanshe, lines 137-174 - the wrongdoers Nanshe rejects; she sees the heart of the land like a split reed (Nanshe A)** (ETCSL 4.14.1 137-174)
- Compare Deut 25:13-16 and Prov 11:1, 20:10 (two kinds of weights), Deut 19:14 and 27:17 (boundary), Prov 30:15-16 and Deut 8:10-14 (the ingrate who eats and is not satisfied), and Q 83:1-3 (woe to the defrauders).
- God searches the heart: compare Jer 17:10, 1 Sam 16:7, Prov 15:3 and 21:2, Q 67:13.

**A hymn to Nanshe, lines 175-222 - Ḫendursaĝa judges between mother and child (Nanshe A)** (ETCSL 4.14.1 175-222)
- Compare Deut 21:18-21 (the rebellious son), Exod 21:15, 17 and Prov 20:20, 30:17 (the eye that mocks a father and scorns a mother), and Q 17:23-24 and 31:14 (kindness to the mother who bore and nursed).

**A hymn to Nanshe, lines 223-256 - standard weights and measures; doxology (Nanshe A)** (ETCSL 4.14.1 223-256)
- Compare Lev 19:35-36, Ezek 45:10-12 (standard ephah, bath, shekel), and Q 55:7-9 ('he set up the balance: do not transgress in the balance').

**A balbale to Nanshe - fish as her regalia and her boat ride home (Nanshe B)** (ETCSL 4.14.2 A:1-2, ETCSL 4.14.2 B:1-23)
- Wordplay on names: compare Jer 1:11-12 (šaqed / šoqed) and Amos 8:1-2 (qayiṣ / qeṣ).
- Compare Ps 104:25-26 (the sea teeming with creatures, where ships go) and Q 16:14 (the sea subjected for fresh fish and ornaments).

**Nanshe and the birds, segment A - the pelican, the assembly of birds, raven, ostrich, peacock, vulture (Nanshe C)** (ETCSL 4.14.3 A:1-63)
- The ostrich and her eggs: compare Job 39:13-18 (she leaves her eggs in the earth, forgetting a foot may crush them) and Lam 4:3. The Sumerian hymn says the opposite.
- God and the birds: compare Job 38:41 and Ps 147:9 (the raven's young), Job 39:26-30 (hawk and eagle), Q 24:41 and 67:19 (every bird knows its prayer and praise), Q 27:16-20 (Solomon taught the speech of birds, the assembly of birds).

**Nanshe and the birds, segments B-E - the catalogue of birds and closing praise (Nanshe C)** (ETCSL 4.14.3 B:3-14, ETCSL 4.14.3 C:1-17, ETCSL 4.14.3 D:1-15, ETCSL 4.14.3 E:1-20)
- Moaning like a dove: compare Isa 38:14 and 59:11, Nah 2:8, Ezek 7:16.
- Catalogues of creatures: compare Lev 11:13-19 and Deut 14:11-18 (the list of birds) and 1 Kgs 5:13 (Solomon spoke of birds).

**A tigi to Nergal, sa-gida - awe of Nergal, given the deciding of destinies (Nergal C)** (ETCSL 4.15.3 A:1-31)
- Compare Ps 29:1-2 and 89:7-8 (the sons of God tremble before the LORD) and Deut 4:34 (outstretched arm).

**A tigi to Nergal, sa-ĝara - Mešlamta-ea, the Enlil of his land and avenger of his father (Nergal C)** (ETCSL 4.15.3 B:32-63)
- Compare Deut 32:41-43 (God avenges the blood of his servants) and Nah 1:2 ('the LORD is an avenging God').
- The god of plague and death: compare Hab 3:5 (pestilence and plague, deber and rešep, go before him) and 2 Sam 24:15-16.

**Nisaba A: epithets of the scribal and grain goddess and her priestly role** (ETCSL 4.16.1 1:1-26)
- Compare Exod 31:18 and Exod 32:16 (tablets written by God) and Ezek 9:2-4 (the scribe with the writing case) for a divine scribe.
- Compare Prov 8:22-31 (Wisdom as the first of God's works, beside him as craftsman) for a goddess of wisdom engendered by the high god.

**Nisaba A: Enki opens the house of learning for Nisaba and blesses her** (ETCSL 4.16.1 1:27-57)
- Compare Gen 41:34-49 and Q 12:55 (Joseph set over the storehouses of the land) for the goddess blessed as steward of grain stores and treasury.
- Compare 1 Kgs 5:9-14 (Solomon's wisdom) and Dan 1:17 (God gives knowledge in every kind of writing and wisdom).

**Nisaba B: lament for Nisaba's destroyed house; the goddess weeps alone in the moonlight** (ETCSL 4.16.2 1-34)
- Compare Lam 1:1-2 (she weeps bitterly in the night, alone, with none to comfort her) and Jer 31:15 (Rachel weeping).
- Compare Isa 34:13 and Hos 9:6 (thorns and nettles grow in the ruined strongholds and tents) for the overgrown temple.
- Compare Lam 2:1-8 (the Lord in his anger destroyed the dwelling, the word he commanded) for the destruction ascribed to the high god's word and anger.

**Ninĝišzida B: the savage warrior god whose word is known only to the knowing** (ETCSL 4.19.2 1-25)
- Compare Isa 40:13 and Rom 11:34 (who has known the mind of the Lord?), and Isa 55:8-9.
- Compare Mark 4:11-12 and Q 3:7 (only those firm in knowledge understand) for knowledge confined to the knowing.
- Compare Num 21:6-9 and 2 Kgs 18:4 (the bronze serpent) for a serpent-god Ninĝišzida.

**Ninĝišzida C: hymn in kirugu sections; the god brings flood and grain** (ETCSL 4.19.3 A:1-A:6, ETCSL 4.19.3 B:7-B:14, ETCSL 4.19.3 C:15-C:23, ETCSL 4.19.3 D:24-D:31, ETCSL 4.19.3 E:32-E:40, ETCSL 4.19.3 F:41-F:45)
- Compare Ps 65:10-14 (God waters the furrows and crowns the year) and Deut 11:14 (the early and late rain).

**Ninĝišzida D: An gives power to the princely son among the Anuna** (ETCSL 4.19.4 1-7)
- Compare Ps 82:1 and Ps 89:6-8 (God among the council of the holy ones).

**Ninisina A: the healing goddess perfects medicine and hands it to her son Damu** (ETCSL 4.22.1 1-26)
- Compare Isa 1:6 (wounds, bruises and sores not pressed out, bound up or softened with oil) and Luke 10:34 (binding wounds, pouring oil and wine).
- Compare Exod 15:26 ('I am YHWH your healer') and Hos 6:1 (he has struck, he will bind us up).

**Ninisina A: the incantation priestess heals the sick man beset by demons and intercedes for him** (ETCSL 4.22.1 27-60)
- Compare Ps 107:17-20 and Ps 30:3-4 (the sick cried to YHWH, he sent his word and healed them) and Ps 41:4.
- Compare 2 Kgs 20:1-7 (Hezekiah's illness, prayer and poultice of figs) and Job 33:19-28 (the sick man, the interceding angel, praise after recovery).
- Compare Ps 91:5-6 (the terror by night, the pestilence that stalks in darkness) for night-entering demons.

**Ninisina A: the goddess invents šuba-stone jewellery and the powers of the midwife** (ETCSL 4.22.1 61-82)
- Compare Ps 22:10-11 and Ps 71:6 (you drew me from the womb) and Job 10:8-11 (fashioned like clay).
- Compare Ezek 16:4 (on the day you were born your cord was not cut) for the midwife's cutting the cord.
- Compare Gen 4:20-22 (Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain as originators of crafts).

**Ninisina A: the goddess's self-praise: her parentage and her house Isin, older than Dilmun** (ETCSL 4.22.1 83-104)
- Compare Prov 8:22-25 ('before the mountains were settled ... I was brought forth') for a precedence claimed 'before X existed'.
- Compare Isa 60:19-20 and Rev 21:23 (the city needs no sun or moon) and Ps 121:6.
- Compare Exod 3:8 (land flowing with milk and honey) and Deut 8:7-8 (wheat, vines, figs, date honey).

**Ninisina A: Enlil sends his daughter against the rebel land; her warlike self-praise** (ETCSL 4.22.1 105-136)
- Compare Ps 102:26-27 and Isa 51:6 (the heavens wear out like a garment, changed like clothing) and Isa 34:4 (heavens rolled like a scroll); Q 39:67 and Q 21:104 (heaven rolled up like a scroll).
- Compare Ps 9:6-7 and Ps 37:10, 36 (the wicked: their memory perished, you look for his place and he is not there).
- Compare Ps 65:3 ('you who hear prayer') and Q 2:186 ('I answer the call of the caller').
- Compare Isa 41:15 and Mic 4:13 (threshing the nations like a threshing sledge).

**Ninisina B: the goddess is anointed with the finest oils** (ETCSL 4.22.2 1-26)
- Compare Exod 30:22-33 (the holy anointing oil of myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia) and Ps 133:2 (oil running down the beard onto the collar).
- Compare Esth 2:12 (six months with oil of myrrh, six with spices) and Song 4:10-14, Ruth 3:3, Ezek 16:9.

**Ninisina C: the goddess sails to Nibru and makes offerings at Enlil's house (fragment)** (ETCSL 4.22.3 15-25)
- Compare 1 Sam 1:3, 24-25 (the yearly journey up to the sanctuary to sacrifice) and Ps 122:1-4 (going up to the house of YHWH).

**Ninisina D: the merciful healer, counsellor of her father, who heals with spells (fragmentary)** (ETCSL 4.22.4 A:1-A:18, ETCSL 4.22.4 B:1-B:22)
- Compare Ps 41:4 (YHWH sustains him on his sickbed) and 2 Kgs 5:7 ('Am I God, to kill and make alive?'); Ezek 47:12 (leaves for healing).

**Ninisina E: adab praising the goddess raised on Uraš's knees and favoured by Enlil** (ETCSL 4.22.5 A.A:1-A.A:28, ETCSL 4.22.5 B.B:1-B.B:7, ETCSL 4.22.5 B.C:8-B.C:9, ETCSL 4.22.5 B.D:10-B.D:14)
- Compare Ps 138:6 (YHWH regards the lowly) and Isa 66:2.

**Ninisina F: Enlil and Enki decree her fate; in city after city she is the local goddess** (ETCSL 4.22.6 A:1-A:15, ETCSL 4.22.6 B:1-B:12, ETCSL 4.22.6 C:1-C:10, ETCSL 4.22.6 D:1-D:13)
- Compare 1 Kgs 12:28-29 and Hos 2:18-19 (one god worshipped under local names, the baalim) for one deity enumerated under city names.

**Ninkasi A: hymn to the beer goddess describing the brewing of beer** (ETCSL 4.23.1 1-48)
- Compare Gen 9:20-21 (Noah, the first vintner) and Ps 104:15 (wine that gladdens the heart); Q 16:67 (from dates and grapes you take an intoxicant).
- Compare Isa 28:23-29 (the farmer taught by God each step of his craft) for a craft process set to praise.

**Ninlil A: adab to Enlil's consort, who decides destinies with him** (ETCSL 4.24.1 A:1-A:11, ETCSL 4.24.1 B:12-B:13, ETCSL 4.24.1 C:14-C:27, ETCSL 4.24.1 D:28-D:29, ETCSL 4.24.1 E:30-E:34)
- Compare Prov 8:30 (Wisdom beside God, his daily delight) and Ps 68:5, 34 (rider through the heavens).

**Ninšubur A: An's minister who soothes the hearts of the gods** (ETCSL 4.25.1 A:1-A:10, ETCSL 4.25.1 B:1-B:9)
- Compare Isa 40:11 (he gathers the lambs in his arms) and Isa 66:13, Hos 11:3-4 (God as mother).
- Compare Ps 103:20-21 (his angels, ministers who do his will) and Isa 6:2 for a heavenly minister before the high god.

**Ninšubur B: the wise suppliant enthroned in Akkil; litany of gods and her self-praise as minister of the universe** (ETCSL 4.25.2 A:1-A:24, ETCSL 4.25.2 B:25-B:41)
- Compare Gen 18:22-33 and Exod 32:11-14 (an intercessor before God) and Heb 7:25.

**Ninurta A: the warrior son of Enlil enthroned on An's dais, shining like moon and sun** (ETCSL 4.27.01 A:1-A:17)
- Compare Ps 110:1-2 (sit at my right hand, the sceptre of your strength) and Ps 2:6-9 (the son set on Zion).
- Compare Ps 89:37-38 (his throne like the sun, established like the moon) and Mal 3:20 (the sun of righteousness).

**Ninurta A: Ninurta greets Enki in the abzu; wisdom fills the land; closing praise** (ETCSL 4.27.01 B:1-B:23)
- Compare Isa 11:9 and Hab 2:14 (the earth filled with knowledge of YHWH as the waters cover the sea).
- Compare Ps 121:3-4 (he who keeps Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps).

**Ninurta B: Ninurta goes from the E-kur to Eridug to decree abundance; Enki receives him** (ETCSL 4.27.02 A:1-A:28, ETCSL 4.27.02 B:1-B:17)
- Compare Isa 40:3-4 and Mal 3:1 (prepare the way of the Lord) and Ps 24:7-10 (the king of glory enters).
- Compare Gen 1:20-25 and Ps 104:10-30 (the waters teem with fish, the beasts of the field are provided for).

**Ninurta B: Ninurta the wall of Sumer, judge and decreer of immutable fates, whose grandeur pleases Enlil** (ETCSL 4.27.02 C:1-C:30, ETCSL 4.27.02 D:1-D:21)
- Compare Num 23:19-20 and Isa 14:27, 46:10 (God's purpose cannot be annulled) and Q 50:29 ('the word is not changed with me').
- Compare Ps 91:1 and Ps 121:5 (the shadow of the Almighty) and Matt 3:17 (the beloved son in whom I am well pleased).
- Compare Ps 72:10, 15 and Isa 60:5-9 (treasures of the nations brought to the king/God).

**Ninurta C: Ninurta's self-praise as Enlil's hero, the man after his father's heart; closing praise** (ETCSL 4.27.03 1-86)
- Compare 1 Sam 13:14 and Acts 13:22 (a man after God's own heart).
- Compare Ps 18:8-16 and Nah 1:3-6 (the mountains quake before him, storm and lightning).
- Compare Exod 15:6, 11-12 (your right hand, O YHWH; who is like you among the gods?) and Ps 98:1.

**Ninurta D: Ninurta's boast of felling forests and razing cities, 'let my mother know it'** (ETCSL 4.27.04 A:1-A:14, ETCSL 4.27.04 B:15-B:34)
- Compare Isa 10:33-34 and Isa 37:24 (felling the forests of Lebanon with an axe) and Jer 46:22-23.
- Compare Josh 8:28 and Deut 13:17 (a city made a perpetual tel, never rebuilt).

**Ninurta G: litany to Ninurta-Pabilsaĝ-Ninĝirsu, devastator of mountains, wall of his city; the house E-ama-lamma** (ETCSL 4.27.07 A:1-A:111)
- Compare Deut 19:14, 27:17 and Prov 22:28, 23:10-11 (do not move the ancient boundary; cursed is he who moves his neighbour's landmark).
- Compare Zech 2:9 (YHWH a wall of fire around Jerusalem) and Ps 46 (God our refuge in the city).
- Compare Mal 3:20 (the sun of righteousness) and Ps 84:12 (YHWH God is sun and shield).

**Ninurta G: the storm god who sacks cities for his father; materials of far lands; curse on the house of the rebel lands** (ETCSL 4.27.07 B:112-B:186)
- Compare Hab 2:11 (the stone cries out from the wall, the beam answers from the woodwork) and Zech 5:4 (the curse consumes the house, its timber and stones).
- Compare Isa 13:9-13 and Jer 4:23-26 (un-creation of a land) for the house reverting to its raw materials.

**Nuska A: Enlil's minister entrusted with the divine powers and plans of the E-kur and its purity** (ETCSL 4.29.1 A:1-A:26, ETCSL 4.29.1 B:1-B:15, ETCSL 4.29.1 C:1-C:24)
- Compare Num 3:5-9, 4:1-15 and 1 Chr 23:28-32 (Levites in charge of the holy vessels and purity of the sanctuary); Exod 30:17-21 (the washing laver).

**Nuska A: Enlil gives Nuska the plough, the granaries and years of plenty; the warrior and judge** (ETCSL 4.29.1 D:1-D:25)
- Compare Ps 7:9-17 and Ps 9:16-17 (the wicked caught in the net; God judges righteously) and Ps 1:6.
- Compare Gen 41:47-49 (the years of plenty and heaped grain) and Deut 28:11-12.

**Nuska B: Enlil's good minister, born by Enlil's decree, wise among the Anuna, who does not alter his just word** (ETCSL 4.29.2 1-79)
- Compare 1 Sam 13:14 (a man after his heart) and Num 23:19 (God speaks and does not go back).
- Compare Isa 9:5 (the child given a name by God: wonderful counsellor) and Isa 11:2 (spirit of wisdom and counsel).

**Šara A: Šara, son of Inana, seated beside his mother and shining from the E-maḫ (fragment)** (ETCSL 4.30.1 30-46)
- Compare Ps 19:6 (the sun like a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber).

**Hymn to Kusu: the fire god's torch, the purification materials, offerings in the oven and the purifying water of heaven** (ETCSL 4.33.2 1-41)
- Compare Lev 14:4-7, 49-53 and Num 19:6 (cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop in purification) and Num 19:17-19 (water of purification).
- Compare Lev 1:9, 6:1-6 (the burnt offering wholly consumed; the perpetual fire) and Ps 51:9 (purge me with hyssop).
- Compare Ezek 36:25 (I will sprinkle clean water on you) and Gen 49:25 (blessings of heaven above, of breasts and womb).

**Temple Hymns 1: Enki's house in Eridug, the ziqqurat grown with heaven and earth** (ETCSL 4.80.1 1-24)
- Compare 1 Kgs 8:12 (YHWH said he would dwell in thick darkness) and 1 Kgs 6:19-20 (the windowless inner sanctuary).
- Compare Gen 11:4 (a tower with its top in the heavens) and Gen 28:12, 17 (gate of heaven).
- Compare Ezek 47:1-12 (the river flowing from under the temple) and Ps 46:5.

**Temple Hymns 2-4: the houses of Enlil, Ninlil and Nuska in Nibru; the river ordeal** (ETCSL 4.80.1 25-60)
- Compare Num 5:11-31 (the water of bitterness ordeal) and Q 19:71-72 / Ps 66:12 for judgment by passing through water.
- Compare Ps 48:2-3 and Isa 2:2 (the mountain of the house of YHWH highest of mountains).

**Temple Hymns 7: Ninḫursaĝa's house in Keš, deep within and tall without** (ETCSL 4.80.1 87-100)
- Compare Ps 29:3-9 (the voice of YHWH thunders, shakes the wilderness) and Ps 18:14.

**Temple Hymns 8-9: Nanna's house in Urim; the deified king Šulgi's E-ḫursaĝ** (ETCSL 4.80.1 101-134)
- Compare Ps 45:7 (the king addressed as elohim) and Ezek 28:2 (the prince of Tyre: 'I am a god, I sit in the seat of gods').

**Temple Hymns 10-12: Asarluḫi in Kuara (the Seven Sages), Ningublaga in Ki-abrig, Nanna in Gaeš** (ETCSL 4.80.1 135-168)
- Compare Prov 9:1 (Wisdom has built her house, hewn her seven pillars).

**Temple Hymns 13-15: Utu in Larsam; Ninazu in Enegir, entrance to the underworld; Ninĝišzida in Ĝišbanda, the net from which none escapes** (ETCSL 4.80.1 169-197)
- Compare Ps 116:3 and Ps 18:5-6 (the cords of Sheol entangled me, the snares of death) and Job 7:9 (who goes down to Sheol does not come up).
- Compare Isa 14:9-11 (Sheol stirs to meet you; all the kings gathered).

**Temple Hymns 16-19: Inana's E-ana of seven corners and fires; Dumuzid's bedchamber; Ninšubur; Ningirim** (ETCSL 4.80.1 198-239)
- Compare Deut 22:5 (a woman shall not wear man's garb) and 1 Cor 11:4-7 (head covering of man and woman).
- Compare Ezek 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz at the temple gate) and Song 1:16 (our couch is green).

**Temple Hymns 20-21: Ninĝirsu's E-ninnu in Lagaš; Bau's Iri-kug, where human seed came forth and the ordeal river clears the just** (ETCSL 4.80.1 240-271)
- Compare Num 5:11-31 (ordeal of bitter water) and Ps 26:1-6 (vindicate me, I wash my hands in innocence).
- Compare Gen 2:7-8 and Gen 4:25 for a place where humanity's seed began.

**Temple Hymns 22-25: Nanše born of the sea, Ninmarki, Dumuzid-abzu, Šara's E-maḫ** (ETCSL 4.80.1 272-314)
- Compare Ps 93:3-4 and Job 38:8-11 (the sea and its waves) for a sea-born goddess.

**Temple Hymns 26-27: Inana in Zabalam, the evening star; Iškur's house in Karkara, the teat of heaven with rain** (ETCSL 4.80.1 315-351)
- Compare Deut 28:12 (YHWH opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain) and Job 38:25-28.
- Compare Ps 29 and 1 Kgs 19:11 (wind splitting the mountains and breaking rocks) for the storm god.

**Temple Hymns 32-35: Marda; Ištaran in Dēr with serpent gate; Ninazu in Ešnunna; Zababa in Kiš** (ETCSL 4.80.1 407-456)
- Compare Num 21:8-9 (the bronze serpent on a pole) and Isa 6:2 (seraphim) for serpent figures at a shrine.
- Compare Exod 15:6 and Ps 118:15-16 (the right hand of YHWH does valiantly).

**Temple Hymns 36-39: Nergal in Gudua; Suen in Urum; Utu in Zimbir, when he sleeps the people sleep; Nintur crowns the newborn king** (ETCSL 4.80.1 457-506)
- Compare Ps 104:19-23 (the sun knows its going down; man goes out to his work until evening).
- Compare Ps 2:6-7 and Ps 110:3 (the king begotten, crowned from the womb) for the newborn king crowned by the birth goddess.

**Temple Hymns 40-42: Inana in Ulmaš, Aba in Agade, Nisaba in Ereš; Enḫeduana's colophon** (ETCSL 4.80.1 507-545)
- Compare Job 38:5 (who stretched the line upon the earth?), Isa 40:12 (measured the heavens with a span) and Zech 2:5-6, Ezek 40:3 (the man with the measuring line).
- Compare Eccl 1:9-10 ('nothing new under the sun') against the author's claim of an unprecedented creation; Ps 45:2 (my tongue the pen of a ready scribe).

**Keš Temple Hymn, houses 1-2: Enlil praises Keš; Nisaba writes the hymn; the temple floats like the boat of heaven** (ETCSL 4.80.2 A:1-A:21, ETCSL 4.80.2 B:22-B:44)
- Compare Ps 48:2-4, 13-14 (walk about Zion, count her towers, consider her ramparts) and Ps 87 for praise of a holy city.
- Compare Gen 28:12 (the ladder reaching heaven) and Gen 9:13 (the bow in the cloud).

**Keš Temple Hymn, house 3 and the added house: the temple's upper and lower ends; the house that gives birth to kings** (ETCSL 4.80.2 C:45-C:58, ETCSL 4.80.2 D:58A-D:58R)
- Compare Exod 25:9, 40 (the pattern shown on the mountain) and 1 Chr 28:19 for a temple plan of heavenly origin; Ezek 40-42 for measurements.

**Keš Temple Hymn, houses 4-5: 'who knows its interior?'; the temple consumes many cattle; the gods within** (ETCSL 4.80.2 E:59-E:74, ETCSL 4.80.2 F:75-F:87)
- Compare 1 Kgs 8:5, 63 (sheep and oxen beyond counting sacrificed at the temple's dedication).

**Keš Temple Hymn, houses 6-7 and added house: lion at the gate, laḫama supporting the terrace; the priests' rite with music** (ETCSL 4.80.2 G:88-G:103, ETCSL 4.80.2 H:103A-H:103L, ETCSL 4.80.2 I:104-I:127)
- Compare 1 Kgs 7:29, 36 (lions, oxen and cherubim on the temple stands) and 1 Kgs 10:19-20 (lions beside the throne).
- Compare 2 Chr 5:12-13 and 1 Chr 15:16-28 (Levites with cymbals, harps, lyres and shofar at the ark's installation) and Ps 150.

**Keš Temple Hymn, close: 'Draw near, man, to the city - but do not draw near!'** (ETCSL 4.80.2 J:128-J:134)
- Compare Exod 3:5 ('Do not come near; take off your sandals'), Exod 19:12-13, 21-24 (set bounds around the mountain) and Ps 24:3 (who shall ascend the hill of YHWH?).
- Compare Jas 4:8 and Heb 12:18-24 (draw near to God; you have not come to a mountain that may not be touched).

**Hymn to the E-kur: every gate and court as great as a mountain; the house shines for those who belong to it** (ETCSL 4.80.4 A:1-A:28, ETCSL 4.80.4 B:29-B:30, ETCSL 4.80.4 C:31-C:42, ETCSL 4.80.4 D:43-D:53, ETCSL 4.80.4 E:54-E:55, ETCSL 4.80.4 F:56-F:69, ETCSL 4.80.4 G:70-G:71)
- Compare Ps 87:4-6 ('this one was born there': belonging to Zion) and Ps 84:11 (a day in your courts); Isa 60:1-3 (your light has come).
- Compare 1 Kgs 6:15-18 and 7:2 (the house of the forest of Lebanon, all cedar within) and Ps 92:13-14 (planted in the house of YHWH, like a cedar in Lebanon).

**Poem of early rulers: where are the kings of old who reigned 36,000 years, ascended to heaven, sought life? Enjoy the day** (ETCSL 5.2.5 6-21)
- Compare Eccl 1:11 and 2:16 (no remembrance of former things; the wise dies like the fool) and Eccl 9:4-10 (a living dog better than a dead lion; eat your bread with joy).
- Compare Gen 5 (antediluvian lifespans of centuries) and Gen 5:24 (Enoch taken by God); Prov 30:4 (who has ascended to heaven?).
- Compare Ps 90:4-10 (a thousand years like yesterday; our years end like a sigh) and Q 23:112-114, Q 20:103-104 (you stayed but a day or part of a day).
- Compare Isa 22:13 and 1 Cor 15:32 (eat and drink, for tomorrow we die).

**Sheep and Grain: the primeval state without grain, sheep or cloth; the gods create Sheep and Grain on the Holy Mound** (ETCSL 5.3.2 1-36)
- Compare Gen 2:5 (no shrub, no plant, no man to till) and Gen 3:21 (garments of skin) for the primeval state without crops or clothing.
- Compare Gen 1:29-30 and Gen 9:3 (food given to humans: plants, then animals) and Ps 104:14-15 (bread to strengthen man's heart).
- Compare Dan 4:22, 29 (Nebuchadnezzar eats grass like oxen) for humans eating grass like animals.

**Sheep and Grain: Enki and Enlil send them down; they bring plenty to the land; the drunken quarrel begins** (ETCSL 5.3.2 37-70)
- Compare Gen 4:2-8 (Abel the shepherd and Cain the farmer; rivalry over offerings) for the farmer-shepherd contest.
- Compare Gen 1:26 and Gen 11:7 ('let us go down') for the divine plural.
- Compare 1 Sam 2:8 and Ps 113:7 (raising the poor from the dust).

**Sheep and Grain: the exchange of boasts and insults** (ETCSL 5.3.2 71-168)
- Compare Ps 104:15 (bread that sustains the heart, oil to make the face shine) and Judg 9:8-15 (Jotham's fable: olive, fig and vine dispute).
- Compare Jer 33:13 (flocks pass again under the hand of the one who counts them) and Lev 27:32 (passing under the rod).
- Compare Gen 31:38-40 (the shepherd's toil, beasts tearing the flock) and Amos 3:12.

**Sheep and Grain: Grain's last retort and Enki's verdict that Grain is the greater** (ETCSL 5.3.2 169-193)
- Compare Gen 41:55-57 and 42:6 (all the earth comes to Joseph for grain; the brothers bow down) and Gen 47:13-20 (money and livestock given for grain).
- Compare Gen 25:23 and 27:29 (the elder shall serve the younger; let your mother's sons bow to you) and Ps 113:3, Mal 1:11 (from sunrise to sunset the name is praised).
- Compare Q 12:58-59 and Q 12:88 (the brothers come to Joseph for grain).

**Silver and Copper, opening speeches; Enlil receives Copper (Silver and Copper, A)** (ETCSL 5.3.6 A:1-128)
- Compare Gen 4:22 (Tubal-cain, forger of bronze and iron tools) and Ecclus 38:24-34 (satire of the trades).
- Compare the Egyptian Satire of the Trades (Dua-Khety) for the list of dirty crafts.

**Copper's account of his creation and his mockery of buried Silver; Silver's answer (Silver and Copper, D)** (ETCSL 5.3.6 D:1-84)
- Compare Job 28:1-11 (silver mined from the dark places of the earth) and Matt 25:25 (talent buried in the ground).
- Compare Jer 32:14 (deeds sealed in an earthenware jar) and Josh 7:21 (silver hidden under the tent floor).
- Compare Gen 2:5-6 (no rain, no one to till) for the before-creation formula; Isa 2:4 for tools of farming.

**Fragments on silver weights, cedar oil and Enlil (Silver and Copper, E-H)** (ETCSL 5.3.6 E:1-14, ETCSL 5.3.6 F:1-10, ETCSL 5.3.6 G:1-11, ETCSL 5.3.6 H:1-7)
- niĝ2-gig 'abomination' compare Hebrew to'evah (Prov 6:16, Deut 25:16).

**Enlil's verdict for Copper; Copper helps Ur-Namma build (Silver and Copper, I)** (ETCSL 5.3.6 I:1-58)
- Compare 1 Kgs 5-6 and 1 Chr 22:14-16 (David and Solomon gather bronze, iron and silver for the temple); Deut 8:9 (a land whose hills yield copper).

**The debate between the Date Palm and the Tamarisk (Sumerian fragment)** (ETCSL 5.3.7 1-19)
- Compare Isa 44:13-19 and Jer 10:3-5, 10:9 (tree cut, carved into a god and overlaid with silver and gold) and Judg 9:8-15 (Jotham's fable: the trees dispute who shall rule).
- Compare Gen 21:33 (Abraham plants a tamarisk at Beersheba).

**He is a good seed of a dog (Diatribe C)** (ETCSL 5.4.12 1-45)
- Compare Prov 6:12-19 (the worthless man with crooked mouth, sowing discord among brothers) and Ps 52:4, 120:2-3 (deceitful tongue).
- Compare Q 68:10-13 (the despicable slanderer, going about with calumnies, 'utull, zanim') and Q 104:1 (humaza lumaza).
- Compare Exod 22:1 and Job 24:16 (the thief who digs through houses in the dark), Matt 6:19.

**The message of Lu-dingira to his mother** (ETCSL 5.5.1 1-F)
- Compare Prov 31:10-31 (the woman of valour: her household, her diligence, her worth above rubies) and Song 4:1-15, 6:10 ('fair as the moon, bright as the sun'; garden, palm, spices).
- Compare Song 2:9, 2:17 (gazelle/doe on the mountains) and Prov 5:19 (loving doe).
- Compare 2 Sam 18:19-32 (messengers bring news to the anxious father) and Gen 37:14 (go see if it is well with your brothers).

**Lu-dingira's elegy on the death of his father Nannaya (Elegy 1)** (ETCSL 5.5.2 1-112)
- Compare 2 Sam 1:17-27 and 3:33-34 (David's laments for Saul, Jonathan and Abner, a man slain by evil men) and 2 Sam 19:1 (father's lament for son reversed).
- Compare Ps 139:11-12 and Job 26:6 (darkness is light to God; Sheol naked before him) for the sun god lighting the underworld; 2 Macc 12:43-45 (prayer that the dead be released from sin).
- Compare Deut 26:14 (no offering given to the dead) and Tob 4:17 for funerary food and drink.

**Lu-dingira's elegy on the death of his wife Nawirtum (Elegy 2)** (ETCSL 5.5.3 1-66)
- Compare Ezek 24:15-18 (death of the prophet's wife, 'the delight of your eyes') and Gen 23:2 (Abraham mourns and weeps for Sarah).
- Compare Eccl 12:6 and Prov 6:5 / Eccl 9:12 (men snared like birds in an evil time) and Jer 9:20 (death climbs in at our windows).
- Compare Ps 112:6 / Prov 10:7 (the memory of the righteous is a blessing) for 'may your name be called on'.

**The song of the hoe** (ETCSL 5.5.4 1-109)
- Compare Gen 2:5-7 (no man to till the ground; man formed of dust) and Gen 1:6-8 (separation of heaven and earth), Q 21:30 (heavens and earth were joined and we split them).
- Compare Isa 45:12, 64:8 and Q 15:26, 55:14 (man made from clay, as a potter's work); Ps 90:3 and Gen 3:19 (return to the ground).
- Compare Gen 2:15 and Q 51:56 (man created to serve/worship) with humans created to provide food for the gods.

**The song of the ploughing oxen (an ululumama of Ninurta)** (ETCSL 5.5.5 1-149)
- Compare Num 22:28-30 (Balaam's ass speaks to its master) and Deut 25:4 (do not muzzle the ox treading grain), Isa 28:24-26 (God teaches the ploughman).
- Compare Ps 128:3 and Ps 127:4-5 (wife and sons of one's youth as blessing) and Luke 9:62 (plough furrows straight).

**Instructions of Shuruppag, prologue (father to his son Ziusudra)** (ETCSL 5.6.1 1-13)
- Compare Prov 1:8, 4:1-4 ('Hear, my son, your father's instruction'), and Prov 1:1 (the sayings of a named sage).
- Ziusudra = the Sumerian Noah; compare Gen 6:9 (Noah righteous) and the Islamic tradition of Luqman's advice to his son (Q 31:13-19).

**Instructions of Shuruppag, first series of precepts** (ETCSL 5.6.1 14-75)
- Compare Prov 6:1-5, 11:15, 17:18, 22:26 (do not stand surety) and Prov 26:17 (meddling in another's quarrel).
- Compare Exod 20:13-16 and Deut 5:17-20 (do not murder, commit adultery, steal); Exod 21:37 / 22:3 (restitution for ox and sheep).
- Compare Prov 6:30-31 (the thief caught must repay sevenfold), Prov 5:3-14 and 7:6-27 (keep from the married woman), Prov 27:2 (let another praise you).
- Compare Prov 26:2 (a causeless curse does not alight) and Ps 109:17-18 (he loved cursing, let it come on him); Deut 15:7-11, Exod 22:24 (the debtor).
- Compare Deut 22:28-29 and Exod 22:15 (rape or seduction of a girl); Lev 19:20 (sex with a slave woman).
- Compare Deut 6:4 / Zech 14:9 (the LORD is one) and Ps 118:6 / Rom 8:31 (on the side of God against many) for 'Utu is one, alone the equal of many'.

**Instructions of Shuruppag, second series of precepts** (ETCSL 5.6.1 76-145)
- Compare Prov 31:4-5 (not for kings to drink wine lest they pervert judgment) and Isa 28:7 (priest and prophet reel with beer in judgment).
- Compare Prov 3:27-28 ('do not say, Go and come again, tomorrow I will give'), Prov 25:14 (clouds without rain).
- Compare Eccl 1:7 (all streams run to the sea, yet the sea is not full) and Prov 27:20, 30:15-16 (things never satisfied).
- Compare Ps 127:3-5 (sons a heritage from the LORD) and Prov 6:6-8 (the ant gathers in harvest); Prov 15:4, 16:24 (gracious words a honeycomb).
- Compare Ps 42:2 and Q 13:28 ('in the remembrance of God hearts find rest') for prayer cooling the heart.

**Instructions of Shuruppag, third series (slaves, kin, the heart)** (ETCSL 5.6.1 146-207)
- Compare Prov 14:1 (the wise woman builds her house, folly tears it down) and Prov 15:17, 17:1.
- Compare Gen 8:21 and Jer 17:9 (the inclination of man's heart is evil); Matt 15:19.
- Compare Gen 42:1-3, Ruth 1:1 (famine sends people to foreign lands) and Prov 18:24 / 17:17 (brother born for adversity).
- Compare Gen 2:18 (not good for man to be alone), Eccl 4:9-12.

**Instructions of Shuruppag, third series (wives, mother and father, the unknown road) and colophon** (ETCSL 5.6.1 208-280)
- Compare Exod 20:12, Deut 5:16, Lev 19:3 (honour/fear mother and father) and Prov 1:8, 23:22; Q 17:23-24 and 31:14 (kindness to parents).
- Compare Prov 31:30 (charm is deceitful, beauty vain) for the wife chosen at a festival in borrowed finery; Prov 7:11-12 (her feet do not stay at home, now in the street, now in the squares).
- Compare Prov 23:20-21 and 21:17 (the drunkard comes to poverty).
- Compare Num 13:32 (a land that devours its inhabitants) for the man-eating mountain gods.

**The three ox-drivers from Adab (a case for the king's judgement)** (ETCSL 5.6.5 1-95)
- Compare 1 Kgs 3:16-28 (Solomon's judgement of the two harlots and the living child) and 2 Sam 14:1-20 and 20:16-22 (the wise woman of Tekoa, of Abel).
- Compare Exod 21:35-36 and 22:9 (disputes over oxen and animals that die or are lost); Q 21:78-79 (David and Solomon judge the sheep that strayed into the field).

**Enlil and Nam-zid-tara (Enlil disguised as a raven)** (ETCSL 5.7.1 1-27)
- Compare Gen 32:27-30 (the night visitor: 'What is your name?' and a new destiny), Gen 18 and Judg 13:17-18 (divine visitor unrecognised).
- Compare Ps 49:17-18, Eccl 5:14, Luke 12:16-21 and Q 104:2-3, 92:11 (wealth does not go with man at death).
- Compare 1 Sam 2:35, Num 25:13 (a perpetual priesthood for one's descendants) and 1 Sam 25:25 (as his name is, so is he).

**Nintinuga's dog (dedication of a dog figure to the healing goddess)** (ETCSL 5.7.2 1-18)
- Compare Tob 5:17, 11:4 (the dog with Tobias and the angel Raphael 'God heals') and Exod 15:26 ('I am the LORD your healer').

**The dedication of an axe to Nergal** (ETCSL 5.7.3 1-16)
- Compare 1 Sam 21:10 (Goliath's sword kept behind the ephod at Nob) and Lev 27 (vows and their redemption).

**The home of the fish, the house built and the invitation (A 1-44)** (ETCSL 5.9.1 A:1-44)
- Compare Prov 9:1-6 and 9:13-18 (Wisdom and Folly each build a house, set a feast and call 'turn in here'; her guests are in the depths of Sheol) and Prov 7:22-23 (like a bird hastening to the snare).
- Compare Eccl 9:12 (as fish taken in an evil net) and Hab 1:14-17 (men made like fish caught in the net).

**The home of the fish, catalogue of fish invited in, and the birds that threaten (A 45-117, B, C)** (ETCSL 5.9.1 A:45-118, ETCSL 5.9.1 B:1-7, ETCSL 5.9.1 C:1-17)
- Compare Lev 11:9-12 and Deut 14:9-10 (fish without fins and scales are an abomination, sheqets/to'evah) for the taboo sting-ray and the 'tasty yet abominable' fish.
- Compare 1 Kgs 5:13 (Solomon spoke of beasts, birds, creeping things and fish) for the catalogue.

**The heron and the turtle, the reedbeds, the heron's nest and the turtle's attack (A 1-106)** (ETCSL 5.9.2 A:1-106)
- Compare Deut 22:6-7 (do not take the mother bird with the young) and Isa 10:14 (gathering eggs, none moved a wing); Ps 84:4 (the bird finds a nest by God's altar).
- Compare Judg 9:8-15 and 2 Kgs 14:9 (fables of trees and animals) and Ps 104:16-17 (the stork's nest in the trees God planted).

**The heron and the turtle, Enki's instructions to Isimud and the creation of flax; fragments (A 107-208, B)** (ETCSL 5.9.2 A:107-208, ETCSL 5.9.2 B:1-9)
- Compare Deut 11:10 (Egypt watered with the foot) for watering 'with the foot'.
- Compare Gen 2:7-9 (the ground made to bring forth plants) and Ezek 12:13, 32:3 (God spreads his net over the offender).

**Proverbs collection 1, on righteousness, loss, wealth and possessions (A.1.1-30)** (ETCSL 6.1.01 A.1.1:1-A.1.30:38)
- Compare Prov 23:4-5 (riches make wings and fly like an eagle), Prov 12:28 and 11:19 (righteousness leads to life), Eccl 5:11 (the rich man's abundance does not let him sleep).
- Compare Eccl 6:2 (a stranger eats his wealth) and Ps 39:7 (heaping up, not knowing who will gather).

**Proverbs collection 1, on bread, libations, curses on food and the poor man (A.1.31-61)** (ETCSL 6.1.01 A.1.31:39-A.1.61:82)
- Compare Prov 14:20 and 19:4, 7 (the poor man is hated even by his neighbour, his brothers avoid him), Eccl 9:15-16 (the poor wise man forgotten).
- Compare Prov 22:7 (the borrower is the lender's slave) and Ps 37:21 (the wicked borrows and does not repay).
- Compare Ps 69:23 (let their table become a snare) for curses on food.

**Proverbs collection 1, on cities, curses, the honest and dishonest boat, and the heart (B.1.62-99)** (ETCSL 6.1.01 B.1.62:1-B.1.99:64)
- Compare Prov 10:9 and 28:18 (he who walks in integrity walks securely), Ps 107:30 (God brings them to their desired haven).
- Compare Eccl 10:20 (a bird of the air will carry your secret word) and Luke 12:3 (what is whispered in private rooms proclaimed from housetops).
- Compare Prov 16:32, 17:27-28, 29:11 (a fool vents all his spirit; the one who controls his spirit is better than the mighty) and Prov 15:1 (a harsh word stirs up anger).
- Compare Matt 7:16-18 (a tree known by its fruit).

**Proverbs collection 1, on eating, sceptre, drought, husband and the raven-mongoose-lion (B.1.100-C.1.129)** (ETCSL 6.1.01 B.1.100:65-C.1.129:15)
- Compare Ps 139:7-12 and Amos 5:19 / 9:2-3 (as if a man fled from a lion and a bear met him; no hiding in Sheol, heaven or sea) for raven, mongoose and lion.
- Compare Eccl 5:11 (the sleep of the labourer is sweet, the rich man's surfeit does not let him sleep).
- Compare Song 2:3 (like an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved).

**Proverbs collection 1, on brothers, sisters, marriage, wives and sons (D.1.140-170)** (ETCSL 6.1.01 D.1.140:1-D.1.170:62)
- Compare Prov 21:9, 19 and 27:15 (better a corner of the roof than a contentious wife; a continual dripping) and Prov 12:4 (a disgraceful wife is rot in his bones).
- Compare Ps 127:3 and Gen 30:2 ('Am I in God's stead who withheld the fruit of the womb?') for 'having children is divine'; Q 42:49-50 (He gives daughters and sons to whom he wills).
- Compare Prov 17:21, 25 and 10:1 (a foolish son is his mother's grief), Job 3:3-16, Eccl 6:3 (better the stillborn).
- Compare Heb 7:3 (without father, without mother) and Ps 128:3 (wife a fruitful vine, sons like olive shoots).

**Proverbs collection 1, on effort, sickness and pregnancy, testing a son-in-law; fragments (D.1.171-G.1.g4)** (ETCSL 6.1.01 D.1.171:63-G.1.g4:8)
- Compare Prov 17:3 and 27:21 (the crucible for silver, the furnace for gold, and the LORD tests hearts) and Gen 3:16 (pain in childbearing).
- Compare Ps 121:4 (he who keeps Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps).

**Proverbs collection 2+6, curse on a place and sayings on fate (A.2.1-14)** (ETCSL 6.1.02 A.2.1:1-A.2.14:29)
- Compare Job 3:1-10 and Jer 20:14-18 (cursed be the day I was born) and Eccl 9:11-12 (time and chance happen to all; men snared in an evil time).
- Compare Deut 12:2-4 (destroy their places ... you shall not do so to the LORD your God) for curse and prohibition about places and rites.

**Proverbs collection 2+6, on the poor man (A.2.15-35)** (ETCSL 6.1.02 A.2.15:30-A.2.35:64)
- Compare Prov 20:4 (the sluggard does not plough in autumn; he begs at harvest and has nothing) and Prov 6:6-11.
- Compare Eccl 9:16 (the poor man's wisdom is despised, his words not heard) and Prov 14:20, 18:23 (the poor uses entreaties, the rich answers roughly).
- Compare Prov 13:24 and 23:13-14 (he who spares the rod hates his son).

**Proverbs collection 2+6, on scribes, singers and disgraced craftsmen (A.2.36-57)** (ETCSL 6.1.02 A.2.36:65-A.2.57:99)
- Compare Ps 45:2 (my tongue is the pen of a ready scribe), Ezra 7:6 (a scribe skilled in the law of Moses) and Ecclus 38:24-39:11 (the scribe's wisdom versus the trades).
- Compare Prov 10:19 (in many words transgression is not lacking) for the chattering scribe.

**Proverbs collection 2+6, the fox, lying and the donkey (A.2.58-82)** (ETCSL 6.1.02 A.2.58:100-A.2.82:143)
- Compare 1 Kgs 20:11 ('let not him who girds on his armour boast like him who takes it off') and Isa 37:24-29 (the boaster turned back) for the fox's boast.
- Compare Ezek 16:44 ('like mother, like daughter') and Prov 12:19 (the lying tongue lasts but a moment).
- Compare Num 22:28-30 (the ass) and Isa 1:3 (the ox knows its owner, the ass its master's crib).

**Proverbs collection 2+6, the ox, the lamentation priest, the dog, finding and losing (A.2.83-126)** (ETCSL 6.1.02 A.2.83:144-A.2.126:207)
- Compare Amos 5:19 (fled from a lion and a bear met him) for the wild bull and wild cow.
- Compare Prov 26:11 (as a dog returns to its vomit) and Deut 25:4 (do not muzzle the threshing ox), 1 Cor 9:9.
- Compare Deut 24:1 (divorce when he finds something unseemly) and Mal 2:16.

**Proverbs collection 2+6, on work, the house and the palace (B.2.131-165)** (ETCSL 6.1.02 B.2.131:1-B.2.165:57)
- Compare Prov 14:1 and 24:3-4 (by wisdom a house is built), Prov 15:25 and 12:7 (the house of the righteous stands); Ps 127:1.
- Compare Prov 19:12, 20:2 (the king's wrath like a lion's roar) and Prov 16:14 for 'the palace is a forest, the king a lion'.
- Compare 1 Sam 8:11-17 and 1 Kgs 5:27 (the king's corvee) and Prov 21:9.

**Proverbs collection 2+6, birds, fish and Enlil's offering table (C.2.c1-D.2.d18)** (ETCSL 6.1.02 C.2.c1:1-D.2.d18:27)
- Compare Prov 27:8 (a man wandering from his place is like a bird wandering from its nest) and Song 2:12 (the voice of the turtledove heard in our land).
- Compare Lev 1:14-17 and Num 28:2 ('my food, my offering ... a pleasing odour') for the gods' offering table.

**Proverbs collection 3, nos. 1-17: the outcast son, procrastination, taboos of Utu, shepherds, friendship** (ETCSL 6.1.03 A.3.1:1-A.3.17:37)
- The outcast son still fed: compare the father of the prodigal (Luke 15:20-24) and Ps 27:10.
- 'I will go tomorrow' and the passing day: compare Prov 3:28 and Prov 27:1; Q 18:23-24.
- Work while there is light: compare John 9:4 and Eccl 9:10, 11:6.
- Abomination to Utu: compare the to'evah sayings, Prov 6:16-19, 11:1, 11:20; Deut 23:13-15 (covering excrement in the camp).
- Shepherd removed, sheep lost: compare Zech 13:7, 1Kgs 22:17, Ezek 34:5.
- Eat modestly, greed kills: compare Prov 23:1-3, 30:8-9; Q 7:31 (eat and drink but do not waste).
- Friendship lasts a day: compare Prov 18:24, 17:17 and 27:10 (a near neighbour better than a far brother); Sir 6:8-10.

**Proverbs collection 3, nos. 18-35: quarrel and slander, tears, reciprocity, Enlil's chaff, Nanni's old age** (ETCSL 6.1.03 A.3.18:38-A.3.35:79)
- The rich man sleeps: contrast Eccl 5:11 (the rich man's surfeit will not let him sleep).
- Mote in the eye: compare Matt 7:3-5.
- Slander even in the place of purification: compare Ps 50:19-20, Prov 10:18, Lev 19:16.
- The king carried off to the netherworld despite his building works: compare Eccl 2:4-17 and Ps 49:11-13.
- 'I will live for today': compare Isa 22:13 and Q 102:1-2.

**Proverbs collection 3, nos. 36-66: slave girls, lies, Unug cursed, the boss, the merchant** (ETCSL 6.1.03 A.3.36:80-A.3.66:130)
- The slave girl in her mistress's place: compare Prov 30:21-23 and Gen 16:4.
- Lies increase evil: compare Prov 19:5, 19:9 and Prov 12:19.
- The merchant's false scales: compare Hos 12:8, Amos 8:5, Prov 11:1, 20:23; Q 83:1-3 (woe to the stinters) and Q 55:9.
- The arrogant bowed like a reed: compare Isa 58:5 and Isa 2:11-17.

**Proverbs collection 3, nos. 67-110: the strong and the weak, the insulter, Iškur's oath, sunrise and kingship, trades, the fool** (ETCSL 6.1.03 A.3.67:131-A.3.110:202)
- Iškur cannot split a waterskin: compare the mockery of gods who cannot act, 1Kgs 18:27, Isa 46:1-7, Ps 115:4-7; Q 22:73 (they cannot create a fly).
- Hunger as the god's greatest punishment: compare Amos 4:6-8, Lev 26:26, Deut 28:48 and Q 16:112.
- He who insults is insulted: compare Matt 7:2 and Prov 26:27; Q 42:40 (the recompense of an evil is an evil like it).
- Nothing changes: compare Eccl 1:9-10.
- The garrulous fool: compare Prov 10:19, 18:2, Eccl 10:12-14.
- The emissary of Bau helping the lame: compare Ps 146:8 and Isa 35:6.

**Proverbs collection 3, nos. 111-147: the goat and the wasteland, mouth and tongue, false witness, offerings, the aching heart, the personal god as shepherd** (ETCSL 6.1.03 A.3.111:203-A.3.147:266)
- The personal god as shepherd finding pasture: compare Ps 23:1-2, Gen 48:15 and Ezek 34:14.
- The aching heart no one finds: compare Prov 14:10, 18:14 and Ps 69:21.
- The false witness an abomination: compare Prov 6:19, 19:5, Exod 20:16, Deut 19:16-19; Q 25:72.
- The runaway tongue: compare Jas 3:5-8 and Prov 13:3.
- Kid in the right hand, bribe in the left: compare Prov 21:14, 17:23 and Isa 1:11-17.
- Offerings give life: contrast 1Sam 15:22 and Ps 50:8-15; Q 22:37.
- Heavens destroyed, people still standing: compare Isa 51:6 and Ps 102:26-28.

**Proverbs collection 3, nos. 148-190: priests and craftsmen, drought, abominations to Suen, Inana and Ninurta, Fate, the leader in the fire, righteousness cut off** (ETCSL 6.1.03 A.3.148:267-A.3.190:328)
- Fate indifferent to just and wicked: compare Eccl 9:2-3 and Job 9:22.
- A word cannot be taken back: compare Prov 18:21, Eccl 5:1-5, Num 30:3.
- Coveting an abomination to Ninurta: compare Exod 20:17 and Deut 5:21.
- Righteousness cut off, injustice grows: compare Isa 59:14-15 and Hab 1:4; Q 30:41.
- A good word a friend to many: compare Prov 15:1, 16:24 and Q 14:24-26 (a good word like a good tree).
- The drought (clouds without rain): compare Prov 25:14 and Jude 12.

**Proverbs collection 4, source A: the shouting statue, the sky-holder, the four winds, the knower who conceals** (ETCSL 6.1.04 A.4.1:1-A.4.20:28)
- The four winds characterised: compare Prov 25:23 (the north wind brings rain), Job 37:9, Song 4:16, Hos 13:15 (east wind) and Q 30:46.
- The one who knows should not conceal it: compare Prov 11:26 and Q 2:159, 2:174.

**Proverbs collection 4, source B: the witness like a fruit tree, each to his task, the man on the roof, the thief and the honest man** (ETCSL 6.1.04 B.4.41:1-B.4.63:38)
- Each to his own task: compare Eccl 11:6 and John 4:37.
- The good witness bears fruit: compare Ps 1:3, Jer 17:8 and Q 14:24-25.
- The man on the roof: compare Prov 21:9 and 25:24.
- What goes into the mouth: compare Matt 15:11, 17-18 and Prov 18:20-21.
- Covered in dust: compare Gen 18:27 (I am dust and ashes) and Job 30:19.

**Proverbs collection 5 (animal fables), sources A-B: the elephant and the wren, wild bull, ox, cow, horse and donkey** (ETCSL 6.1.05 A.5.1:1-B.5.40:24)
- The elephant and the wren: compare the boast of the axe, Isa 10:15, and the small creatures that are wise, Prov 30:24-28; Q 27:18-19 (the ant).
- The wild bull that will not plough: compare Job 39:9-12.
- Gordon's 'from many oxen, is there no dung?' (B.5.26-27): compare Prov 14:4.

**Proverbs collection 5, source C: donkey sayings and fables** (ETCSL 6.1.05 C.5.41:1-C.5.51:22)
- A donkey unfit for an omen sacrifice: compare Exod 13:13 (the firstling of a donkey redeemed with a lamb).
- The talking donkey: compare Num 22:28-30.

**Proverbs collection 5, source D: the lion fables (the clever goat, the boar, the trapped lion and the fox)** (ETCSL 6.1.05 D.5.52:1-D.5.68:33)
- The lion in the pit: compare Ezek 19:4, 8 and Ps 7:16, 57:7.
- When the lion roars (D.5.63): compare Amos 3:8 and Prov 19:12, 20:2.

**Proverbs collection 5, source D: wolf fables (the fox's share, the wolf's oath to Utu, the lonely wolf)** (ETCSL 6.1.05 D.5.x1:34-D.5.x13:70)
- The repentant wolf in the trap: compare the promise made in distress and broken, Exod 9:27-28, 34-35; Q 10:12, 10:22-23.
- Wolf and sheep: compare Isa 11:6, 65:25 and John 10:12.

**Proverbs collection 5, source D: dog sayings and fables (the dog and the door-bolt)** (ETCSL 6.1.05 D.5.75:71-D.5.102:125)
- The dog that goes back for the same blow: compare Prov 26:11 and 2Pet 2:22.
- Dog sayings: compare 1Sam 17:43, 2Sam 9:8 and Q 7:176 (the panting dog).

**Proverbs collection 5, source D: more dog sayings (the snarling dog, the dog at the party, the bitch and her puppies)** (ETCSL 6.1.05 D.5.103:126-D.5.125:161, ETCSL 6.1.05 E.5.e1:1-E.5.e2:3)
- Food of the funeral offering: compare Deut 26:14 (not eaten of it in mourning, nor given of it to the dead) and Ps 106:28.
- A dog on the roof (D.5.109) and a dog with nowhere to sleep (D.5.111): compare Matt 8:20.

**Proverbs collection 7, sources A-B: the curse on the destroyed place, the sinking boat, verdict and curse, flea and fly, borrowed bread** (ETCSL 6.1.07 A.7.1:1-A.7.1:6, ETCSL 6.1.07 B.7.9:1-B.7.53:65)
- Even the flea and the fly are provided for: compare Ps 104:27-28, 145:15-16, Matt 6:26 and Q 11:6.
- Borrowed bread not returned: compare Ps 37:21.
- He went back on his word: compare Num 30:3 and Eccl 5:4-5.
- Never tiring, never sleeping: compare Ps 121:4 and Isa 40:28.

**Proverbs collection 7, source C: Fate a biting dog, the boat that reached port, the stranger's ox, the fatherless reed, the songs of a city** (ETCSL 6.1.07 C.7.70:1-C.7.122:96)
- Crying 'Ah god!' and the boat reaches port: compare Ps 107:23-30, Jonah 1:5-6, 14-15 and Q 10:22, 29:65, 31:32.
- Without father, without mother: compare Heb 7:3 (Melchizedek) and Q 3:59 (Jesus like Adam).
- The stranger's ox eats: compare Song 1:6 and Deut 28:31-33.
- Fate a biting dog: compare Eccl 9:11-12.

**Proverbs collection 8, sources A-B: pig, goat, bear and fox fables** (ETCSL 6.1.08 A.8.a1:1-A.8.a7:11, ETCSL 6.1.08 B.8.b1:1-B.8.b36:70)
- The fox who asked for horns and gave them back: compare the fable of the trees (Judg 9:8-15) and the bramble that wants to rule.
- Sleep as the god's gift: compare Ps 127:2 and Q 25:47, 78:9 (sleep made for rest).
- The pig's ancestors went the same road: compare Josh 23:14, 1Kgs 2:2 and Eccl 3:19-20.
- Foxes: compare Song 2:15, Ezek 13:4, Luke 13:32.

**Proverbs collection 8, sources C-E: birds, the raven and the fox, trees and furniture that speak** (ETCSL 6.1.08 C.8.c1:1-E.8.e10:18)
- Trees that speak: compare Judg 9:8-15 and 2Kgs 14:9.
- A table set before you: compare Ps 23:5 and Q 5:112-114 (the table sent down).

**Proverbs collection 9, source A: the man in authority, strength and intelligence, lost youth, the fattened pig** (ETCSL 6.1.09 A.9.a1:1-A.9.a18:23)
- Strength cannot match intelligence: compare Eccl 9:16-18, Prov 21:22, 24:5.
- The strength of my god completes mine: compare Ps 18:33, Isa 40:29-31, Phil 4:13.
- Lost youthful vigour and white hair: compare Eccl 12:1-5, Ps 71:9, Q 19:4 (my head is aflame with grey).
- The silent knower a fool: contrast Prov 17:28 (even a fool who keeps silent is thought wise).

**Proverbs collection 9, sources B-H: Nanni, the slave as lord, 'Run!' says the king, Utu as judge of the dream, humility** (ETCSL 6.1.09 B.9.b1:1-H.9.h6:15)
- Wealth that undoes its owner when the king says 'Run!': compare Prov 11:4, Zeph 1:18, Ezek 7:19 and Q 69:28-29 (my wealth has not availed me).
- 'Judge me, Utu': compare Ps 7:9, 26:1, 43:1 and Gen 41:16, 25 (God shows the meaning of the dream).
- Who compares with humility: compare Prov 15:33, 18:12, 22:4.
- The slave who plays the lord: compare Prov 30:22 and Eccl 10:7.

**Proverbs collection 10: the man in authority, strength and wisdom, and the old man's lament** (ETCSL 6.1.10)
- The old man's body in images: compare Eccl 12:1-7 (keepers of the house tremble, the almond blossoms) and 2Sam 19:35.
- My black mountain has sprouted white: compare Q 19:4 and Hos 7:9 (grey hairs are sprinkled on him).

**Proverbs collection 11, sources A-D: lies, the strong and the weak, Nanni, the broken word, the whirlwind to Agade** (ETCSL 6.1.11 A.11.4:5-D.11.57:12)
- A palace falling of itself: compare Ps 127:1 and Prov 14:1.
- The whirlwind sent to Agade: compare the curse of Agade and Jer 23:19, 25:32.
- Nanni's unfinished temple: compare 1Chr 22:7-8 and 2Sam 7:5-13.

**Proverbs collection 11, sources E-K: revenge belongs to Ninurta, the friend's harbour, Adapa, debts to Utu, the scribe, the loving heart** (ETCSL 6.1.11 E.11.66:1-K.11.162:8)
- Revenge reserved to the god: compare Deut 32:35, Lev 19:18, Prov 20:22, Rom 12:19 and Q 42:40-43.
- The loving heart builds houses: compare Prov 14:1, 24:3 and 15:17.
- Unpaid debts owed to the sun god: compare Deut 24:14-15 (the wage withheld; he cry to YHWH) and Prov 19:17.
- Looking far but not at oneself: compare Matt 7:3 and Q 2:44.

**Proverbs collection 12, source A: master, steward and household** (ETCSL 6.1.12 A.12.a1:1-A.12.a20:39)
- The master's bed and the mistress's slap: compare Gen 16:4-6 (Sarai deals harshly with Hagar) and Prov 30:23.
