- The master knows, the steward does not: compare John 15:15 and Luke 16:1-8.

**Proverbs collection 12, sources B-F: changed masters, the damp reed, Nintur and paralysis, the millstone that floats for the righteous** (ETCSL 6.1.12 B.12.b1:1-F.12.f4:5)
- The millstone that floats for the righteous: compare the river ordeal in Laws of Hammurabi 2 and Num 5:11-31; and 2Kgs 6:5-7 (the axe-head floats).
- Illness from neglecting a god: compare John 9:2 and Job 4:7-8.
- The weeping farmer whose barley sprouts (C.12.c3): compare Ps 126:5-6.

**Proverbs collection 13, nos. 1-40: thieves and burglars, the crafty, the lame man and his mother** (ETCSL 6.1.13 13.1:1-13.40:64)
- The thief breaking in and the householder's watch: compare Exod 22:1-2, Job 24:16, Matt 24:43 and Jer 9:20 (death comes up through the windows).
- Fleeing a lion to meet a cub: compare Amos 5:19 (as if a man fled from a lion and a bear met him).
- The lame man told to walk: compare Isa 35:6, Acts 3:6-8.

**Proverbs collection 13, nos. 41-59: the ecstatic, the boys in the orchard, the house of debt, the dishonest man, the immigrant** (ETCSL 6.1.13 13.41:65-13.59:104)
- Mistreating the immigrant an abomination to Ninurta: compare Exod 22:20, 23:9, Lev 19:33-34, Deut 10:18-19, Jer 7:6 and Q 4:36 (the neighbour who is a stranger, the wayfarer).
- The ecstatic and a birth in another man's house: compare 2Kgs 4:14-17 (the man of God and the Shunammite's son) and Jer 29:23.
- The house of debt: compare Prov 22:7, Neh 5:1-5, 2Kgs 4:1.

**Proverbs collection 14, source A: repaying favours, the workers' prayer for Enlil's cursed city, the drought** (ETCSL 6.1.14 A.14.1:1-A.14.7:14)
- Each worker lifts his eyes to the god for the cursed city: compare Ps 121:1, 123:1-2 and Lam 5:1, 20-22.
- Repay favour to the one who repays: compare Prov 17:13 and Q 55:60 (is the reward of good anything but good?).

**Proverbs collection 14, sources B-C: Enlil's temple, the palace, wives and children, the malicious spouse, the stranger leader** (ETCSL 6.1.14 B.14.15:1-C.14.64:21)
- Children from the gods: compare Ps 127:3, Gen 30:2, 33:5 and Q 42:49-50.
- The malicious wife: compare Prov 21:9, 21:19, 25:24, 27:15 and Sir 25:16-26.
- The palace one day a birth, the next a mourning: compare Eccl 7:2-4 and 3:2.
- The stranger as leader: compare Gen 41:40-43 (Joseph) and Deut 28:43.

**Proverbs collection 15, sources A-B: the well-wisher, the workers' prayer for Enlil's cursed city, Enlil the helper of the lame** (ETCSL 6.1.15 A.15.a1:1-B.15.b8:15)
- Enlil the helper of the lame: compare Ps 146:8-9, Ps 54:6 and Isa 35:6.
- Rain on one place and not another: compare Amos 4:7.
- The well-wisher, mother of the refugee: compare Isa 16:3-4 and Deut 23:16-17 (the runaway slave sheltered).

**Proverbs collection 15, sources C-F: toughness, oil on the sceptre, the stranger as leader, nothing added to Enlil's temple, the rivers** (ETCSL 6.1.15 C.15.c1:1-F.15.f8:16)
- Nothing to be added to what is counted: compare Deut 4:2, 13:1, Prov 30:6, Eccl 3:14 and Rev 22:18-19.
- The rising waters measured in cubits (C.15.c14): compare Gen 7:20.

**Proverbs collection 16, sources A-C: shepherds, the unjust heir, 'I will go tomorrow', the workers' prayer for Enlil's cursed city** (ETCSL 6.1.16 A.16.a1:1-C.16.c5:10)
- Compare Zech 13:7 (strike the shepherd) and Prov 27:1 (do not boast of tomorrow).

**Proverbs collection 16, sources D-F: friend and colleague, the merchant at the window, the unsound mind, the thief as outcast** (ETCSL 6.1.16 D.16.d1:1-F.16.f2:2)
- The thief an outcast: compare Job 30:5 (driven out from among men; they shout after them as after a thief) and Gen 4:12-14.

**Proverbs collection 17: no one reaches heaven, the old man's lament, the poor man and his son, the merchant, the palace** (ETCSL 6.1.17)
- No one tall enough to reach heaven: compare Gilgamesh and Huwawa A 28-29, Prov 30:4, Deut 30:12 and Q 17:37 (you will not reach the mountains in height).
- The poor man who never strikes his son: compare Prov 13:24, 23:13-14 and 2Sam 12:3 (the poor man's lamb like a daughter).
- Old age: compare Eccl 12:1-7 and Ps 71:9, 18.

**Proverbs collection 18: the idler, the talker who got into the palace, the levelling of hills, the lying dream of Agade** (ETCSL 6.1.18)
- The swift hid, the strong fled, the talker got in: compare Eccl 9:11 and Amos 2:14-16.
- Hills and depths levelled: compare Isa 40:4 and Luke 3:5.
- The lying dream for Agade's king: compare 1Kgs 22:19-23, Jer 23:25-32 and Deut 13:2-4.
- Worth by the lot: compare Prov 16:33.

**Proverbs collection 19, sources A-C: the old man, the fattened pig, build like a lord, accept your lot, Inana's marriage blessing, a man's goods and kin** (ETCSL 6.1.19 A.19.a1:1-C.19.c9:16)
- The marriage blessing for a fruitful wife and strong sons: compare Ruth 4:11-12, Ps 128:3, Gen 24:60.
- Accept your lot: compare Eccl 3:22, 5:17-18, 9:9 and Prov 16:33.
- A son as a man's shade: compare Ps 127:4-5 and Ps 121:5 (YHWH your shade).

**Proverbs collection 19, sources D-H: the um bird, the slave girl's banquet, the fool, the river grave, the insatiable glutton, the early-married youth** (ETCSL 6.1.19 D.19.d1:1-H.19.h1:6)
- The young man who married in his youth: compare Prov 5:18, Mal 2:14-15 and Eccl 11:9.
- The insatiable glutton: compare Prov 30:15-16, Eccl 6:7, Isa 5:14 and Q 50:30.
- Onions and bread as plain fare: compare Num 11:5.

**Proverbs collection 21: the fattened pig, the daughter-in-law, slave girls, the lamentation priest who stole barley** (ETCSL 6.1.21)
- The slave girl and her mistress: compare Gen 16:4-6 and Prov 30:23.
- The thief caught in another man's field: compare Deut 23:25-26 (plucking grain in a neighbour's field) and Exod 22:6.

**Proverbs collection 22, lines 19-101: the husband who picks the fish bones, the younger son driven out, good and evil in the hands, accept your lot** (ETCSL 6.1.22 22.ll.19–20:19-22.ll.98–101:101)
- Driving the younger son from his father's house: compare Gen 21:9-14 (Ishmael), Judg 11:2 (Jephthah driven out by his brothers) and Deut 21:15-17.
- Good and evil are in the hands: compare Deut 30:15-19, Gen 4:7 and Q 91:7-10.
- Let the boat sink with the evil: compare Mic 7:19.

**Proverbs collection 22, lines 127-202: the stranger eats the bread, raven mongoose and lion, the drought, carry it, the liar with the waterskin, the trades** (ETCSL 6.1.22 22.ll.127–133:127-22.ll.201–202:202)
- Raven, mongoose, lion: where shall I go? Compare Ps 139:7-10, Amos 5:19, 9:2-3 and Q 75:10-12 (where is the refuge?).
- The stranger eats what is left: compare Deut 28:33 and Eccl 6:2.

**Proverbs collection 22, lines 203-287: no one reaches heaven, hand at the table, the angry man, the liar, the immigrant, Utu's compassion, the lamentation priest and the lion** (ETCSL 6.1.22 22.ll.203–206:203-22.l.287:287)
- The angry man's empty threats: compare Prov 14:17, 29:11, Eccl 7:9.
- The liar arrogant and slandering: compare Prov 6:12-19, Ps 52:4-6.
- Utu's compassion for his devotee: compare Ps 103:13, Ps 107:30 (he brings them to their desired haven).
- He who has much cannot sleep: compare Eccl 5:11.

**Proverbs collection 23: the husband who picks the bones, the liar and the righteous man's house, the portrait of the adulterer, raven and mongoose, a man's goods and kin** (ETCSL 6.1.23)
- The adulterer shunned, wounded and disgraced: compare Prov 6:26-35, 7:22-27, Job 24:15 and Q 24:2-3.
- The house of the righteous destroyed by the liar: compare Prov 14:11, 12:7 and Ps 127:1.

**Proverbs collection 24: the fattened pig, the destroyer of houses, the kneeling lord, a man's goods and kin, go in at sunset, sweet beer** (ETCSL 6.1.24)
- Compare 6.1.19; the doublets show these collections were copied as fixed sequences in the school curriculum.

**Proverbs collection 25: the drought, the en priest's diet, Unug cursed, Nanni, life better than death, the palace, the king's wealth, the abomination to Suen** (ETCSL 6.1.25)
- Life better than death despite evil days: compare Eccl 9:4-6 and contrast Eccl 4:2-3, Job 3.
- What flows in never fills: compare Eccl 1:7-8, 5:9 and Prov 27:20.
- The palace a slippery place: compare Ps 73:18 and Prov 25:6-7.
- Nanni's unfinished works and death: compare Eccl 2:18-21.

**Proverbs collection 26: the palace, the abominations to Ninurta, Utu and Suen, fear of god and offerings, the curse not returned, the farmer, the unloving beloved** (ETCSL 6.1.26)
- Fear of god begets good fortune: compare Prov 10:27, 14:26-27, 19:23, 22:4 and Q 65:2-3.
- Not answering a curse with a curse: compare Prov 20:22, 24:29, Rom 12:14 and 1Pet 3:9; Q 41:34.
- The farmer who did not plough in the cold season: compare Prov 20:4 and 6:6-11.
- Removing a thing from its place: compare Deut 19:14, 27:17 and Prov 22:28.
- Revenge an abomination: compare Lev 19:18.

**Proverbs collection 27: the rich man's sick heart, the light burden, eating and vomiting, cities and men greeting** (ETCSL 6.1.27)
- The rich man's sick heart: compare Eccl 5:11-16 and Prov 15:16.
- A light burden: compare Matt 11:30.

**Proverbs collection 28: the club and the name, the city's name and mine, the mongoose without fear of god, the godless man unburied, man finds and woman loses, the palace a forest** (ETCSL 6.1.28)
- The godless man unburied, without libation from his heir: compare Jer 22:18-19, 36:30, Eccl 6:3 and Isa 14:19-20.
- Let my name stand: compare 2Sam 18:18 (Absalom's pillar), Ps 49:12 and Isa 56:5.
- The king as a lion in the palace: compare Prov 19:12, 20:2 and 28:15.

**Proverbs from Nibru, segments 1-3: fragments, the exotic animals of distant lands, the courtesan in the street** (ETCSL 6.2.1 1.A:1-3.B:13)
- The kar-kid / harimtu in the street: compare Prov 7:10-12 (the woman in the streets and squares) and Prov 23:27-28.
- Distant lands and their animals (elephant, monkey) as exotica: compare 1 Kgs 10:22 (ivory, apes and peacocks from Tarshish).

**Proverbs from Nibru, segments 4-8: Nanni who went down despondent, the cult not to be changed, the destiny in the water, the mill** (ETCSL 6.2.1 4.A:1-8.B:7)
- A king who built and abandoned, then went down to the underworld unfulfilled: compare Eccl 2:18-21 and Isa 14:9-11 (the king going down to Sheol).
- 'Because of my silver ... I am finished': compare Eccl 5:12-13 (riches kept to the owner's hurt) and Jas 5:1-3.
- A quarrel reveals hidden theft: compare Prov 26:26 (hatred covered by guile, its wickedness revealed before the assembly).

**Proverbs from Nibru, segments 9-19: the clown, the vixen, abominations to the god, great and little men** (ETCSL 6.2.1 9:1-19:6)
- Spitting must be covered with dust: compare Deut 23:13-14 (covering excrement because God walks in the camp); the niĝ2-gig saying recalls the to'evah sayings of Prov 6:16-19.
- The mocker mocked: compare Prov 9:7-8, Prov 19:29 and 2 Kgs 2:23-24.
- Great men stir up strife for the small to fight: compare 2 Sam 2:14-16 (Abner: 'let the young men arise and play before us').

**Proverbs from Nibru, segments 20-44: prayer and life, the just man's hungry son, the widow, Gula, the son before he existed** (ETCSL 6.2.1 20:1-44:1)
- The just man's son lies hungry: a direct counter-voice to Ps 37:25 ('I have not seen the righteous forsaken nor his seed begging bread').
- 'You are our son even from when you did not exist': compare Jer 1:5 and Ps 139:16 (known before formed in the womb).
- Endless talk: compare Prov 10:19, Eccl 5:2-3 and Eccl 10:14.
- The widow's lower status: compare Lev 21:14 (the high priest may not marry a widow) and Ruth 1:11-13.
- Do not weep for the strong, do not oppress the weak: compare Exod 23:3 and Lev 19:15 (neither favour the poor nor defer to the great).
- The ox lying broken in its yoke (29:1-2): compare Isa 1:3 and Hos 10:11.
- Wiping one's bread on a pig (41:1): compare Prov 11:22 and Lev 11:7.

**Proverbs from Susa: the birds' voices, mouth and hand, the fettered dog, Aratta, the divorcing husband** (ETCSL 6.2.2 1:1-29:1)
- What is in the mouth is not in the hand: compare Prov 14:23 and Prov 20:6 (many proclaim their loyalty, but a faithful man who can find?).
- The bird's voice as the glory of the garden: compare Song 2:12 (the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land).
- Divorce sayings: compare Deut 24:1-4 and Mal 2:16.
- 'Let him who has a household go to his household' (17:1-2): compare Deut 20:5-8 (let him go and return to his house).

**Proverbs from Urim 1-13: justice creates life, Utu not idle, wealth and sleeplessness, bread for the stranger, nowhere to flee** (ETCSL 6.2.3 1:1-13:3)
- The rich man cannot sleep: compare Eccl 5:11 (the sleep of the labourer is sweet, but the surfeit of the rich will not let him sleep).
- A stranger eats one's surplus: compare Eccl 6:2 and Deut 28:33.
- Raven above, mongoose below, lion in the desert, 'where shall I go?': compare Amos 5:19 (fleeing a lion and meeting a bear) and Ps 139:7-10 ('where shall I flee?').
- Who can compare with justice, it creates life: compare Prov 12:28 and Prov 11:19 (righteousness leads to life).
- Utu will not be idle against wickedness: compare Ps 121:4 and Ps 94:1-2.
- Greed of the rich an abomination: compare Prov 11:24-26 and Eccl 5:9.

**Proverbs from Urim 14-23: the cult not to be changed, a bitter fate, liars at the gate, scribes and singers, the fox** (ETCSL 6.2.3 14:1-23:1)
- The fox who urinates into the Tigris and claims the flood: compare the boasting bramble of Judg 9:15 and 2 Kgs 14:9 (the thistle and the cedar); also Isa 10:15 (the axe boasting over the hewer).
- Scribe who cannot translate (inim bal): compare Neh 8:8 (reading with interpretation) and Ezra 4:7 (a letter translated into Aramaic).
- A finger pointed at the liar: compare Isa 58:9 ('the pointing of the finger') and Prov 6:13.
- Moving about defeats poverty: compare Prov 10:4 and Prov 6:6-11.
- 'My fate is a disgrace, it makes the mouth bitter' (15:1-2): compare Ruth 1:20 (call me Mara) and Job 7:11.

**Proverbs from Urim 24-33: good and evil in the hands, the palace a forest, the unruly tongue, a man's god his shepherd** (ETCSL 6.2.3 24:1-33:3)
- A man's god is a man's shepherd who gives him food and water: compare Ps 23:1-2 (YHWH is my shepherd ... still waters) and Gen 48:15 (the God who shepherded me all my life).
- The king as a lion, his palace a forest: compare Prov 19:12 and Prov 20:2 (the king's wrath like a lion's roar).
- The tongue like a runaway donkey that does not turn back: compare Prov 21:23, Ps 39:2 and Jas 3:5-8.
- Good and evil are in the hands: compare Deut 30:15-19 and Isa 3:10-11.
- Shaving the head to grow more hair (25:1): compare Judg 16:22.

**Proverbs from Urim 34-64: fables of horse, donkey, dog, lion, goat, boar, pig, bear and fox** (ETCSL 6.2.3 34:1-64:2)
- Fables of talking animals: compare Num 22:28-30 (Balaam's donkey speaks) and Judg 9:8-15 (Jotham's fable).
- A donkey in place of a sheep gives no omen: compare Exod 13:13 and Exod 34:20 (the firstling of a donkey must be redeemed with a lamb).
- Were An not to give sleep, they would expire: compare Ps 127:2 (he gives his beloved sleep) and Ps 3:6.
- The dog who understands 'take it' but not 'put it down': compare Isa 56:11 (greedy dogs that never have enough).
- 'Don't start a fight with a dog; won't it bite you?': compare Prov 26:17 (seizing a passing dog by the ears).
- The fox under the thorn bush: compare Ezek 13:4 (prophets like foxes among ruins) and Song 2:15.

**Proverbs from Urim 65-81: intelligence and strength, the quick and the strong, abominations to Utu, the slanderer, no child without sin** (ETCSL 6.2.3 65:1-81:9)
- No child without sin was ever born: compare 1 Kgs 8:46, Eccl 7:20, Job 14:4, Job 15:14, Ps 51:7 and Ps 143:2.
- The swift and the strong fail, the talker succeeds: compare Eccl 9:11.
- Strength cannot match intelligence: compare Eccl 9:16, Prov 21:22 and Prov 24:5.
- A judge who despises justice is an abomination to Utu: compare Deut 25:16, Prov 17:15 and Prov 11:1; chasing a son from his father's house: compare Gen 21:10 and Judg 11:2.
- Utu who loves justice uproots wickedness and prolongs righteousness: compare Ps 11:7, Ps 37:9-11 and Ps 45:8.
- The slanderer whose head the goddess crushes: compare Ps 101:5 and Ps 140:12.
- Fortune dispersed, no one knows what will come: compare Eccl 5:13-14, Eccl 8:7 and Prov 27:1.
- 'For him who walks the day lasts ...' (81:6-9): compare Ps 104:23 and Eccl 11:7.

**Proverbs from Urim 82-107: the man without a god, honouring elders, the mouse and mongoose, barley and silver, the unburied despiser of god** (ETCSL 6.2.3 82:1-107:3)
- A man without a god catches no fish, no gazelle, fails in everything: compare Ps 127:1-2 (unless YHWH builds the house) and Deut 28:15-19, 38-40.
- Silver-holders wait at the gate of the barley-owner: compare Gen 41:56-57 and Gen 47:13-20 (all lands come to Egypt to buy grain) and Prov 11:26.
- Respect for the old man's word, the mother, the elder brother: compare Lev 19:32, Exod 20:12 and Prov 23:22.
- The man who despises his god is cast unburied into the desert: compare Jer 22:19 (buried with the burial of a donkey), Isa 14:19-20 and 1 Kgs 14:11; water for the dead through the pipe: compare Deut 26:14.
- Speech as hard to hide as a wall: compare Eccl 10:20 (a bird of the air will carry the voice).
- 'Although I spoke, what did I gain?': compare Job 16:6 and Prov 28:13 (he who covers his sins will not prosper).
- Man's intelligence comes from god: compare Prov 2:6 and Job 32:8.

**Proverbs from Urim 108-151: each tool to its craftsman, sins absolved, the mule, each creature to its hole, the just man's long life, abominations to Utu** (ETCSL 6.2.3 108:1-151:1)
- The just man's life is long, life is its reward: compare Prov 3:1-2, Prov 10:27 and Deut 5:33; contrast Eccl 7:15.
- Sins absolved, life renewed: compare Ps 32:1-2 and Ps 103:3-5 (forgives all your iniquity ... your youth is renewed like the eagle's).
- Let the snake find its hole, the scorpion its crevice: compare Isa 11:8 and Ps 104:22 (the beasts withdraw to their dens).
- The mule that knows not its sire: compare Lev 19:19 (no crossbreeding) and Ps 32:9.
- Brotherhood founded in quarrel: compare Prov 17:17 (a brother is born for adversity) and Prov 27:6.
- Following wisdom one becomes wise: compare Prov 13:20 (walk with the wise and become wise).
- Adding inheritance share to share an abomination: compare Deut 21:15-17 and Num 27:7-11; Isa 5:8 (joining house to house).
- Earth is greater than heaven, who can destroy it?: compare Eccl 1:4 (the earth remains for ever).
- The raven watching its own shadow and eyeing the malt (122, 147): compare Job 38:41 and Ps 147:9.

**Proverbs from Unug: Enlil holds up the sky, hunger his greatest punishment, the winds** (ETCSL 6.2.4 1.A:1-4:4)
- Enlil holds the sky, the earth dangling from his hands: compare Job 26:7 (he hangs the earth upon nothing), Isa 40:22 and Ps 75:4 (I keep its pillars steady).
- Hunger as the god's greatest punishment: compare Amos 4:6, Amos 8:11, Ezek 5:16-17 and Deut 28:48.
- The rain-bearing east wind: contrast the Hebrew Bible's scorching east wind (Gen 41:6, Hos 13:15) and compare 1 Kgs 18:44 and Prov 25:23 (the north wind brings rain).
- 2-4 broken; a young girl 'like a nindiĝir priestess' (2:6) is the only legible image.

**Proverbs of unknown provenance 1-3: wealth and sleep, the unique warrior, the slave girls, the Dilmun ship, the lion and the nameless plants** (ETCSL 6.2.5 1.A:1-3:21)
- One warrior equal to many: compare 1 Sam 18:7 (Saul his thousands, David his ten thousands), Lev 26:8 and Josh 23:10.
- Water poured from a river did not cool my anger nor end the sorcery against me (2.A:4-6): compare Prov 25:21-22 and Song 8:7.
- The lion declares a list of named plants 'nameless': compare Gen 2:19-20 (Adam names the creatures).
- The fool's lot made by the sun god: compare Prov 16:4 (YHWH made everything for its purpose, even the wicked) and Eccl 7:14.
- 3:1-21 almost wholly broken.

**Proverbs of unknown provenance 4-5: eyes lifted to Enlil for the cursed city, revenge belongs to Ninurta, poor and rich** (ETCSL 6.2.5 4.A:1-5.B:8)
- Each worker lifts his eyes to the god: compare Ps 123:1-2 (as the eyes of servants to their master's hand) and Ps 121:1; 'may Enlil look on the city he cursed': compare Lam 5:1 and Lam 1:11.
- Retaliation belongs to Ninurta: compare Deut 32:35 (vengeance is mine), Lev 19:18 and Prov 20:22 (do not say, I will repay evil; wait for YHWH).
- Repay favour with favour: compare Prov 17:13 and 2 Sam 10:2.
- A palace falls of its own accord: compare Ps 127:1 and Prov 14:1.

**Proverbs of unknown provenance 6-12: righteousness, the fattened pig, what the god destroyed, Enlil's chaff, the snake charmer** (ETCSL 6.2.5 6:1-12:5)
- The fattened pig says 'let me replace what I eat' (7:1-2): compare Prov 15:17 and Isa 22:13.
- He who has much is always on guard: compare Eccl 5:11-12.
- The snake charmer pulling the snake's tooth: compare Ps 58:5-7 (the deaf adder and the charmer; God breaks their teeth) and Eccl 10:11.
- Touching a woman improperly an abomination to Suen: compare Deut 25:11-12 and Lev 18.
- 'Where is my sow?' says the pig as it nears its fate (9:6-7): compare Prov 7:22-23 (as an ox to the slaughter).

**Proverbs of unknown provenance 13-43: just decisions, the river ordeal, the man without a god, the city of the lame, the king as scribe, the floating millstone** (ETCSL 6.2.5 13:1-43:1)
- The river ordeal admires those who carry true words: compare Num 5:11-31 (the water of bitterness) and Isa 43:2.
- A millstone floats for the righteous man: compare 2 Kgs 6:5-7 (the iron axe-head floats) and contrast Exod 15:5, 10 and Neh 9:11 (the enemy sinks like a stone).
- Despising a just decision, loving a wicked one, is an abomination: compare Prov 17:15 and Deut 25:16.
- In the city of the lame the halt are couriers: compare 2 Sam 5:6-8 (the lame and blind of Jebus) and Isa 35:6.
- The king built a house in the barren marshes (19:1-2): compare Isa 35:1 and Isa 41:18-19.
- If the roof does not stand upright for its owner, the gutter lets no water (20:1-2): compare Eccl 10:18.
- The leader burning while those behind do not ask for him: compare Zech 13:7 (strike the shepherd and the sheep scatter).
- 'May Luma be good to him who does good': compare Ps 18:26 and Ps 125:4.

**Ur III literary catalogues from Nibru (N1) and at Yale (Y1): incipits of Enki and Lilia compositions and of Šulgi hymns** (ETCSL 0.1.1 1-21, ETCSL 0.1.2 1-45)
- Ancient lists of songs and titles: compare Num 21:14 (the Book of the Wars of YHWH), Josh 10:13 and 2 Sam 1:18 (the Book of Jashar), and the psalm collection subscript Ps 72:20.
- A tally of a king's songs: compare 1 Kgs 5:12 (Solomon's 3,000 proverbs and 1,005 songs).

**Old Babylonian literary catalogues N2, L, U1 and U2: incipits of hymns, myths, epics, laments and school compositions** (ETCSL 0.2.01 1-62, ETCSL 0.2.02 5-68, ETCSL 0.2.03 1-25, ETCSL 0.2.04 1-56)
- Myths catalogued by the incipit 'In those days': compare Gen 2:4b (on the day YHWH God made earth and heaven) and Gen 6:4 (in those days).
- Gilgameš epics are catalogued here (en-e kur lu2 til3-la-še3, lu2-kiŋ2-gi4-a ag): compare 1 Kgs 5:13 and Eccl 12:12 (of making many books there is no end).

**Old Babylonian literary catalogues U3, N3, B1, N4, B4, Y2 and N6: hymns, laments, the Instructions of Šuruppak, royal letters** (ETCSL 0.2.05 Seg.A:1-Seg.B:8, ETCSL 0.2.06 1-33, ETCSL 0.2.07 Seg.A:1-Seg.B:22, ETCSL 0.2.08 Seg.A:1-Seg.G:6, ETCSL 0.2.11 1-35, ETCSL 0.2.12 Seg.A:1-Seg.B:11, ETCSL 0.2.13 1-22)
- A catalogue of laments by genre (balaĝ, eršema, širnamšub): compare the lament collections behind Lamentations and the genre superscriptions of the Psalms (mizmor, shiggaion, maskil).
- The Instructions of Šuruppak catalogued by its incipit: compare Prov 1:1 and Prov 25:1 (collections headed by their title).

**Dumuzid's dream: the shepherd's foreboding lament, his dream, and the call for an interpreter** (ETCSL 1.4.3 1-24)
- The dreamer calls for those who know dreams: compare Gen 41:8 and Dan 2:2 (the king summons magicians and wise men).
- The doomed man asks nature to lament for him: compare 2 Sam 1:21 (mountains of Gilboa) and Jer 9:9-10; the mother not knowing the day of death: compare Gen 27:2 and Eccl 9:12.

**Dumuzid's dream: the dream told item by item and Ĝeštinana's interpretation of it as his death** (ETCSL 1.4.3 25-70)
- A dream interpreted figure by figure as foretelling death: compare Gen 40:16-19 (the baker's dream: three baskets are three days) and Dan 4:16-24.
- The interpreter shrinks from telling a bad dream: compare Dan 4:16 (my lord, may the dream be for your enemies).
- The fold left to the wind, the churn overturned, no milk: compare Hab 3:17 (the flock cut off from the fold) and Jer 25:36-37.

**Dumuzid's dream: the sister on the mound sees the demons coming; Dumuzid hides in the grass and binds sister and friend to silence** (ETCSL 1.4.3 71-109)
- A sister keeps watch from a height for her brother: compare Exod 2:4 (Miriam stands at a distance to see what will happen).
- The hunted man hides and asks not to be betrayed: compare 1 Sam 19:2 and 1 Sam 20 (Jonathan hides David), Josh 2:6 and 2 Sam 17:17-20 (the spies hidden).
- Curse on the one who reveals the hiding place: compare Josh 2:14, 20.

**Dumuzid's dream: the demons described, the sister refuses their gifts, the friend betrays him; Dumuzid is caught** (ETCSL 1.4.3 110-163)
- The sister refuses the bribe, the friend accepts it: compare Judg 16:5 (Delilah bribed by the lords of the Philistines), Ps 41:10 and Ps 55:13-15 (betrayed by the familiar friend).
- 'Who has ever seen a sister reveal her brother's place?': compare Prov 17:17 (a brother is born for adversity) and Prov 18:24.
- Demons who eat no bread, drink no water, take no gifts, know no wife's embrace: compare Deut 10:17 (God takes no bribe) inverted, and Job 1:7.
- The captive surrounded, netted and bound: compare Ps 18:5-6 (cords of Sheol, snares of death) and Judg 16:21.

**Dumuzid's dream: Dumuzid prays to Utu his brother-in-law, is changed into a gazelle and a snake, escapes to Kubirešdildareš and to Old Woman Belili, and is caught again** (ETCSL 1.4.3 164-204a)
- The pursued man's hands and feet made like a gazelle's: compare 2 Sam 22:34 and Ps 18:34 (he makes my feet like the feet of deer) and Hab 3:19.
- Tears accepted as a gift: compare Ps 56:9 (put my tears in your bottle) and 2 Kgs 20:5 (I have seen your tears).
- Appeal to divine kinship: compare Ps 89:27 (you are my father) and Isa 63:16.

**Dumuzid's dream: refuge in Old Woman Belili's house, recapture, a last plea, flight to the sister's sheepfold** (ETCSL 1.4.3 205-239a)
- The fugitive who comes to an old woman's house asking water and flour: compare 1 Kgs 17:10-12 (the widow of Zarephath gives water and her last flour) and Josh 2:1-6 (refuge in Rahab's house).
- 'I am not a man, I am the spouse of a god': compare Gen 12:13 and Gen 20:2 (concealed identity to save one's life).

**Dumuzid's dream: the sister's lament, the demons enter the sheepfold seven times, the dream fulfilled and Dumuzid dead** (ETCSL 1.4.3 240-261)
- A dream fulfilled word for word: compare Gen 41:13 (as he interpreted to us, so it was) and Gen 37:5-11 with Gen 42:6.
- The sister's mourning by scratching her face: contrast Lev 19:28 and Deut 14:1 (do not gash yourselves for the dead); compare Jer 16:6 and Jer 48:37.
- The dying shepherd god and the mourning for him: compare Ezek 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz) and Zech 12:11 (mourning for Hadad-rimmon).

**The marriage of Martu: the city of Inab in former days, the food portions, and Martu's request to his mother for a wife** (ETCSL 1.7.1 1-52)
- The young man asks his parents to get him a wife: compare Judg 14:2-3 (Samson: get her for me as a wife) and Gen 24:3-4, Gen 28:1-2.
- Rations doubled for the married and tripled for fathers: compare Deut 24:5 (the newly married man exempt for a year) and Exod 16:16-18 (portions by household).
- 'Inab existed, Kiritab did not': compare Gen 2:4b-6 (no shrub yet, no plant yet).

**The marriage of Martu: the festival of Inab, Martu's wrestling victory, his refusal of silver and request for Numušda's daughter, and his marriage gifts** (ETCSL 1.7.1 53-111)
- The champion who wins the chief's daughter: compare Josh 15:16-17 (Caleb gives Achsah to the one who takes Kiriath-sepher) and 1 Sam 17:25 and 18:17-27 (the king's daughter for the victor).
- Bride-price in herds: compare Gen 24:53, Gen 34:12 and Gen 29:18-20 (Jacob's service for Rachel).
- Wrestling: compare Gen 32:25-29 and 2 Sam 2:14-16.

**The marriage of Martu: gifts to the people of Inab, the friend's warning that Martu is an uncivilised nomad, and Adĝarkidug's answer 'I will marry Martu'** (ETCSL 1.7.1 112-142)
- The nomad who has no house in life and no burial at death, eats raw meat and lives in tents: compare Gen 16:12 (Ishmael a wild ass of a man), Gen 25:27 and Jer 35:6-10 (the Rechabites' tents), and contrast 1 Sam 2:15 and Lev 17:10-14 (meat and blood).
- A friend warns against marrying an uncouth outsider: compare Judg 14:3 (is there no woman among your kin?) and Gen 26:34-35.
- Taboo food of the moon god: compare Deut 14:3 and Lev 11 (abominations in food).

**Ninĝišzida's journey to the nether world: the god boards the barge while his sisters lament at prow and stern** (ETCSL 1.7.3 1-20a)
- The sister who would go down with her brother: compare Ruth 1:16-17 (where you go I will go) and 2 Sam 15:21.
- Lament for the young god: compare Ezek 8:14 (Tammuz) and Zech 12:10-11.

**Ninĝišzida's journey: the sister asks why the demon takes him; the nether world gives no water, flour or wool; she offers her jewels** (ETCSL 1.7.3 28-38a)
- The nether world gives no water, bread or wool: compare Job 10:21-22 (land of darkness) and Isa 14:11; contrast Ps 23:1-2.
- Manacles on the hands, a stock on the neck: compare Jer 20:2, Jer 29:26 and Ps 105:18 (his neck in iron).
- The god as a tamarisk and a date palm: compare Ps 92:13 (the righteous flourish like the palm tree) and Jer 17:8.

**Ninĝišzida's journey: Amašilama pleads with the demon and offers her lapis, the barge sets off, the lament for Urim and its en, and the god's arrival before Ereškigal** (ETCSL 1.7.3 39-90)
- The god received in the nether world, enthroned, eating and drinking: compare Isa 14:9-10 (Sheol rouses the dead kings from their thrones) and Ezek 32:21.
- The lament for the en priestess leaving the ĝipar: compare Lam 1:4 (her priests groan, her virgins afflicted) and Joel 1:13.
- Bread and water for the brother going to the underworld: compare 1 Sam 28:22-25 and Deut 26:14.
- The king's head in the dust, feet in the mire: compare Job 2:12, Lam 2:10 and Ps 69:3.

**Kirugu 1: god after god abandons stall and sheepfold to the wind (Lament for Urim 1-38)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 1-38)
- Compare Ezek 10:18-19; 11:22-23 (the glory leaves the temple) and Jer 12:7 (I have forsaken my house, abandoned my heritage).
- Compare Jer 9:9-10 (lowing of cattle not heard) and Lam 1:4.

**Kirugu 2: 'O city, a bitter lament is set up for you' at each shrine; the city's rites changed (Lament for Urim 39-75)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 39-75)
- Compare Lam 1:1-2 and Lam 2:1-9 (each part of Zion named in its ruin); Ps 74:4-8.
- Compare Ps 79:5 and Zech 1:12 (how long?).

**Kirugu 3: Ningal cannot sleep; she wails day and night for the doom of her city (Lament for Urim 76-135)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 76-100A, ETCSL 2.2.2 101-135)
- Compare Lam 1:2 (she weeps bitterly in the night) and Jer 9:17-20 (women taught to wail).
- Compare Isa 1:8 (Zion like a booth in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field) and Ps 55:7 (O that I had wings like a dove).
- Compare Ps 127:1 (unless YHWH builds the house, its builders labour in vain).

**Kirugu 4: Ningal twice pleads with An and Enlil in the assembly, but their word does not change (Lament for Urim 136-171)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 136-171)
- Compare Gen 18:23-32 (Abraham pleads for Sodom) and Exod 32:11-14, Amos 7:1-6 (intercession that does or does not avert destruction); contrast Jer 15:1 (even Moses and Samuel could not turn my heart).
- Compare Isa 45:23; 55:11 (the word that goes out from my mouth shall not return) and Num 23:19.

**Kirugu 5: Enlil calls the storm; fire, darkness and the sunless day cover Urim like a cloak (Lament for Urim 172-206)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 172-206)
- Compare Amos 8:9 and Joel 2:2, 10 (day of darkness, sun dark at noon) and Zeph 1:15.
- Compare Jer 4:11-13 (a hot wind from the bare heights; chariots like the whirlwind) and Ps 18:8-15.

**Kirugu 6: the city made ruin mounds; corpses in gates and streets; families torn apart; Elam sacks Ekišnuĝal (Lament for Urim 207-253)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 207-209A, ETCSL 2.2.2 210-253)
- Compare Lam 2:21 (young and old lie on the ground in the streets) and Lam 4:5, 2:11-12 (infants faint in the squares).
- Compare Zech 11:12-13 (the lordly price of thirty shekels at which I was valued) and Exod 21:32.
- Compare Isa 49:15 (can a mother forget her nursing child?) and Ps 79:2-3 (blood poured like water round Jerusalem, none to bury).

**Kirugu 7: Ningal's lament in the first person: An cursed my city, my children are carried off, I am no longer its queen (Lament for Urim 254-330)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 254-330)
- Compare Lam 1:1 (she that was great among the nations is become a widow) and Isa 47:5-8 (no longer called mistress of kingdoms).
- Compare Lam 5:18 (foxes prowl on Zion) and Deut 28:68 (taken back in ships).
- Compare Lam 1:10 and 5:2 (strangers seize her treasures) and Jer 6:26; Mic 1:8 (mourning, wailing, tearing).

**Kirugu 8: 'Lady, how can your heart endure?': priests, festivals and music gone; return to your city (Lament for Urim 331-389)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 331-389)
- Compare Lam 5:15 (our dancing turned to mourning), Lam 1:4 (priests groan, festivals forgotten) and Lam 2:6.
- Compare Jer 31:15-17 (lament and the promise of return) and Hos 14:1-8 (return).
- Compare 2 Sam 24:16 (It is enough, stay your hand) and Isa 40:1-2 (her term of service is ended).

**Kirugu 9: the storm that destroyed city, house, stall and fold (Lament for Urim 390-399)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 390-399)
- Compare Jer 23:19; 30:23 (the storm of YHWH has gone forth in wrath) and Nah 1:3.

**Kirugu 10: the storm that knows no mother or father; may it not return; its account hung on Enlil's peg (Lament for Urim 400-417)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 400-417)
- Compare Gen 9:11-15 (never again a flood) and Isa 54:9 (as I swore the waters of Noah would not again cover the earth).
- Compare Isa 40:2 (her iniquity is paid) and Col 2:14 (the record nailed to the cross); Q 80:34-37 (on that day a man flees his brother, mother, father, wife and sons).

**Kirugu 11: closing prayer to Nanna: the humble seize your feet; release their sin; restore the city (Lament for Urim 418-438)** (ETCSL 2.2.2 418-432A, ETCSL 2.2.2 433-438)
- Compare Lam 5:21 (restore us to yourself, YHWH, renew our days as of old) and Ps 51:3-4, 19 (blot out my transgression; a broken heart you will not despise).
- Compare 1 Kgs 8:33-34, 46-50 (when they pray toward this house, forgive their sin and restore them) and Q 39:53; 2:37 (God turns to the penitent).
- Compare Ps 103:13 (as a father has compassion) and Isa 49:15; the arhuš / raḥamim 'womb-compassion' pairing.

**Ur-Namma, white mes tree of Urim, son of Ninsumun, endowed by the great gods (Ur-Namma I, fragments)** (ETCSL 2.4.1.a)
- Compare Dan 4:7-9 and Ezek 31:3-9 (the king as a great tree whose shade shelters all) and Judg 9:15.
- Compare 1 Kgs 3:12 (God gives the king a wise heart).

**Adab to Enlil: Enlil's net and the E-kur; Šulgi born of the en priestess and given sceptre and throne (Šulgi G 1-34)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.07 sa–gida.A)
- Compare 2 Sam 7:12-16 (the son who builds the house: his throne established forever) and Ps 89:30, 37.
- Compare Ps 2:7 and Ps 110:3 (born from the womb of the dawn) and Isa 9:5-6.
- Compare Hab 1:15-17; Ezek 12:13; 17:20 (God's net) and Ps 23:1-2.

**Šulgi as provisioner of E-kur; Urim with its holy chest of the abzu; Enlil's good day for Šulgi's reign (Šulgi G 35-70)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.07 sa–jara.C, ETCSL 2.4.2.07 uru.E)
- Compare Ps 110:4 (a priest forever) and Exod 28 (priestly garments); compare 1 Kgs 8:9 and Heb 9:4 (the ark that no one sees).
- Compare Ps 121:5 (YHWH is your shade) and Ps 91:1.

**Fragments of a tigi for Šulgi: the shepherd, the physician, conquest of the rebel land (Šulgi L)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.12)
- Compare Exod 15:26 (I am YHWH your healer) and Isa 10:17-18 (as a fire consumes the forest).

**A mother's lullaby for a son of Šulgi: come, sleep; a wife and son for you (Šulgi N)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.14 1-114)
- Compare Ps 128:3 (your wife like a fruitful vine, your children like olive shoots) and Ps 92:13-15.
- Compare Ps 4:9 and Prov 3:24 (lie down and your sleep will be sweet); Ps 121:6 (the sun shall not strike you, nor the moon by night).

**Tigi to Ninurta, dragon-eyed warrior of Nibru, for Šulgi's long life (Šulgi T)** (ETCSL 2.4.2.20)
- Compare Ps 18:8-15 and Deut 32:33 (venom of serpents) and Ps 21:5 (he asked life of you).

**Šulgi goes to Eridug, Nibru, Ešumeša, Keš, Urim, Ebabbar, Kulaba and Zabalam, and each god rejoices** (ETCSL 2.4.2.a 1-36)
- Compare Ps 122:1-4 and Ps 84:6-8 (pilgrimage from strength to strength) and 1 Sam 7:16 (Samuel's circuit of Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah).

**Šulgi, true shepherd of Sumer, establishes justice, swears by Enlil his praise is no lie, runs from Nibru to Urim** (ETCSL 2.4.2.b)
- Compare 2 Sam 8:15 and Ps 72:1-4 (the king does justice) and 2 Sam 23:3-4.
- Compare 1 Kgs 18:46 (Elijah runs before Ahab to Jezreel) and 2 Sam 22:34 (feet like hinds').

**Hymn for Šu-Suen: god of abundance born of Uraš, chosen by Enlil and Ninlil, born for godhood (kirugu 1-4 and fragment)** (ETCSL 2.4.4.a)
- Compare Ps 2:7; 110:3 and Isa 9:5 ('el gibbor) for the divine birth and titles of the king.
- Compare Jer 1:5 and Isa 49:1 (named from the womb).

**Išbi-Erra, farmer of Enlil, against Kindattu the Elamite (Išbi-Erra B, fragments)** (ETCSL 2.5.1.2)
- Compare 2 Kgs 3:9-20 (an army without water in the wilderness) and Isa 11:14; Jer 49:34-39 (Elam broken).
- Note: the data has a stray line numbered 40 without a section between Seg.C and Seg.D ('{ŋiš}gigir mah', great chariot).

**Adab to Nergal: storm-warrior, dragon drinking blood, junior Enlil of the netherworld; Nergal plucks the king's enemy like a swallow (Šu-ilīšu A)** (ETCSL 2.5.2.1)
- Compare Ps 139:8 (if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there) and Deut 32:41-42 (arrows drunk with blood).
- Compare Ps 1:4; 83:14 (like chaff before the wind) and Ps 18:9-16.

**Adab to Enlil: the Anuna look to Enlil whose word is unalterable; the E-kur's mystery; long reign for Išme-Dagan (Išme-Dagan H)** (ETCSL 2.5.4.08)
- Compare Ps 89:7-9 (who in the skies is like YHWH, feared in the council of the holy ones) and Isa 40:8, 55:11.
- Compare 1 Kgs 8:12 (YHWH dwells in thick darkness) and Ps 132:13 (YHWH has chosen Zion).

**Adab to Nanna: the crescent orders months and years; Nanna judges in the netherworld on the day of disappearance; offerings and a good reign for Išme-Dagan (Išme-Dagan M)** (ETCSL 2.5.4.13 sa–gida.A, ETCSL 2.5.4.13 unknown.C, ETCSL 2.5.4.13 sa–jara.D, ETCSL 2.5.4.13 uru.F)
- Compare Ps 104:19 (he made the moon for seasons) and Gen 1:14-16; Sir 43:6-8.
- Compare Ps 145:15-16 (the eyes of all look to you) and Num 28:11-15 (new moon offerings).

**Tigi to Ninurta, hero of the fifty divine powers of E-kur, for Išme-Dagan (Išme-Dagan O, first version)** (ETCSL 2.5.4.15 sa–gida.A, ETCSL 2.5.4.15 sa–gida.B, ETCSL 2.5.4.15 unknown.D, ETCSL 2.5.4.15 unknown.E, ETCSL 2.5.4.15 unknown.F)
- Compare Ps 18:35-40 and Ps 144:1 (who trains my hands for war) and Ps 110:1-2.

**Dedication of a statue: Išme-Dagan the tireless runner sets up his running statue in Eniguru; curse on whoever erases its inscription (Išme-Dagan S)** (ETCSL 2.5.4.19 1-34)
- Compare Deut 27:17 and Prov 22:28 (boundary-stone curses), Deut 28:23-24 (heaven bronze, no rain) and Rev 22:18-19 (curse on altering the book).
- Compare 2 Sam 2:18 (Asahel swift as a gazelle) and 2 Sam 18:19-27 (runners).

**Adab to Dagan for Išme-Dagan: E-kur, Egalmah, the lord with great powers of heaven and earth (Išme-Dagan U, fragments)** (ETCSL 2.5.4.21)
- Dagan, the West Semitic grain god (Dagon of Judg 16:23; 1 Sam 5:2-7), here worshipped by an Isin king whose name means 'Dagan has heard'.

**A god given a golden throne, a fifty-headed mace and fifty names in Nibru; Išme-Dagan provisioner of Nibru and king of Isin (Išme-Dagan AA)** (ETCSL 2.5.4.27 1-25)
- Compare Enuma eliš VI-VII (Marduk's fifty names) and, for the many names of God, Q 7:180; 17:110 (the most beautiful names).

**Enki firstborn of An raised to junior Enlil-ship with seven wisdoms; the gods give Ninurta the divine powers; Išme-Dagan's eternal song (fragments)** (ETCSL 2.5.4.29)
- Compare Prov 9:1 (wisdom's seven pillars) and Isa 11:2 (the sevenfold spirit of wisdom).

**Hymn to Inana for Išme-Dagan: the goddess laments her house; Išme-Dagan restores justice and filial order in Sumer and Akkad** (ETCSL 2.5.4.a)
- Compare Exod 20:12; Lev 19:3, 32 (fear mother and father; rise before the elder) and Mal 3:24 (turn the hearts of fathers to sons).
- Compare Ps 102:4-5 (my days vanish like smoke, my bones burn like a hearth) and Lam 2:10.

**Hymn to Enki for Išme-Dagan: marshes, meadows and orchards; Enlil and Ninlil give Enki the divine powers; the song placed in Nibru's mouth forever** (ETCSL 2.5.4.b 1-12)
- Compare Ps 86:8 (there is none like you among the gods).

**Ua-di song to Inana, true princess and spouse of the king, for Lipit-Eštar (Lipit-Eštar H)** (ETCSL 2.5.5.8)
- Compare Ps 45 (royal wedding song: 'I address my verses to the king') and Song 3:11.

**Inana, holder of the plans of kingship, leads Ur-Ninurta humbly into E-kur and speaks for him to An and Enlil; his shepherdship and throne are fixed (Ur-Ninurta A 1-43)** (ETCSL 2.5.6.1 :1-43)
- Compare 1 Kgs 1:15-31 (Bathsheba enters to the king and secures the throne for Solomon) and Ps 45:10.
- Compare Ps 23:1-2 and Ezek 34:14 (the flock finds pasture and water); Ps 89:21-30.

**Ur-Ninurta's foes struck down, An's unchangeable fate for him; the Anuna say 'so be it'; Inana, Suen's daughter, and the king go joyfully to the palace (Ur-Ninurta A 44-95)** (ETCSL 2.5.6.1 :44-90, ETCSL 2.5.6.1 unknown.K)
- Compare Ps 2:9 and Ps 110:2-3 (rule in the midst of your enemies) and Jer 27:8-11 (the yoke of the king of Babylon).
- Compare Ps 45:10-16 (the queen at the king's right; led into the palace with joy).

**Adab to Ninurta, right arm of Enlil, flood no one withstands, helper of Būr-Suen (Būr-Suen A)** (ETCSL 2.5.7.1)
- Compare Exod 15:6 (your right hand, YHWH, shatters the enemy) and Isa 51:9; Ps 18:35.

**Hymn to Nanna for Gungunum: Dilimbabbar, firstborn of Enlil, who fixes the crescent and the months (Gungunum B, fragments)** (ETCSL 2.6.2.a)
- Compare Ps 89:38 (established forever like the moon, a faithful witness in the sky) and Ps 72:5, 7.

**Iškur the storm-lord, shade of Larsa and helper in battle; Sîn-iddinam restores Eridug's plans and makes Iškur a great throne with two bulls (Sîn-iddinam E)** (ETCSL 2.6.6.5 1-85)
- Compare 1 Kgs 10:18-20 (Solomon's throne flanked by lions) and 1 Kgs 7:25 (the sea on twelve oxen); Exod 25:18-22 (cherubim at the throne).
- Compare Ps 29:3-9 and Ps 18:13-14 (YHWH thunders, hailstones and coals of fire) and Job 37:2-6.

**Prayer for Rīm-Sîn: a throne of life firm as heaven, a fate of life, eternal kingship** (ETCSL 2.6.9.a 1-9)
- Compare Ps 89:30, 37-38 (his throne as the days of heaven) and Ps 21:5.

**Praise poem of Abī-Ešuḫ: Utu the judge, Marduk, the king's protective deity, granary and a life of good months (Abī-Ešuḫ B, fragments)** (ETCSL 2.8.5.a)
- Compare Ps 121:8 and Deut 6:7 (in your sitting and lying down) and Ps 16:5-6 (you maintain my lot).

**Hymn to Marduk for a king: 'may you live, be well'; may your lot be life, your dream good, your omen good, your footing safe** (ETCSL 2.8.5.b 1-29)
- Compare Num 6:24-26 (the priestly blessing) and Ps 121:7-8 (YHWH will keep your going out and coming in).
- Compare Ps 3:6; 4:9 (I lie down and sleep and wake) and Prov 3:23-24 (your foot will not stumble; your sleep will be sweet).

**Letter-petition of Lugal-nesaĝe to a king radiant as the moon: like an ox without yoke, a cow without calf, a drifting boat; I eat tears in Nibru's street; restore me** (ETCSL 3.3.02)
- Compare Ps 42:4 and 80:6 (tears my bread), Ps 38:12 and Job 19:13-19 (friends stand aloof), Ps 102:7-8 (like a lonely bird on the roof).
- Compare Jer 31:18 (like an untrained calf) and Jer 50:6 (lost sheep); Lk 13:6-9 (the barren fig tree).

**Letter-petition of Lugal-nesaĝe to a king radiant as the sun: punished without knowing why, moaning like a dove in a foreign city** (ETCSL 3.3.03)
- Compare Isa 38:14 (I moan like a dove) and Ps 102:7; Job 10:2 (let me know why you contend with me) and Ps 124:7 (a bird escaped from the snare).

**Letter from Ugubi to his mother: 'Traveller, tell my mother': I sit behind the door of the chief musician's house in Urim, starving; bread and beer are not fresh** (ETCSL 3.3.07 1-11)
- Compare Luke 15:14-17 (the son far from home in want, recalling his father's bread).

**Letter-petition of Lugal-nesaĝe to Enlil-massu: praise of the honey-mouthed scribe who reveres his parents; I am crushed, hungry and eat tears; my heart filled with blood and pus** (ETCSL 3.3.09 1-24)
- Compare Ps 38:4-11 (no soundness in my flesh, wounds fester, friends stand aloof) and Ps 22:15 (my heart like wax); Exod 20:12.

**Letter-prayer of Inanaka to the healing goddess Nintinuga: twice on my sickbed, friends gone; drive out the Asag demon and I will be your slave, sweeping your courtyard and proclaiming your name** (ETCSL 3.3.10 1-26)
- Compare Ps 30:3-5, 10 (I cried to you and you healed me; will the dust praise you?) and Ps 116:16-19 (I am your servant ... I will pay my vows in the courts of YHWH's house); Ps 84:11 (doorkeeper in the house of my God).
- Compare 1 Sam 1:11 (Hannah's vow) and Ps 38:12.

**Letter from Inim-Inana to Lugal-ibila: do not neglect Sumerian; keep the boy at the scribal school** (ETCSL 3.3.12 1-13)
- Compare Prov 22:6 and Deut 6:7 (teach your children diligently).

**Letter from Gudea to his personal god: like a sheep without a shepherd, a donkey under the whip; you are no stranger, return your heart to me** (ETCSL 3.3.20 1-10)
- Compare Num 27:17; 1 Kgs 22:17; Mark 6:34 (sheep without a shepherd) and Ps 23:1; Ps 13:2 (how long will you hide your face).

**Letter from the scribe Inim-Enlila to a king: I do not know my sin; my clan eats tears; let my bones not be taken to a foreign city** (ETCSL 3.3.27)
- Compare Job 10:2; 13:23 (make me know my transgression) and Gen 47:29-30; 50:25 (do not bury me in Egypt; carry my bones).

**Letter-prayer of Kug-Nanna to the god Ninšubur: in fetters, facing death abroad, ignored in the street; soothe your angry heart, drive out the demon, brighten my dark days** (ETCSL 3.3.39)
- Compare Ps 88:9 (you have made my friends shun me), Ps 6:2-4 (do not rebuke me in your anger), Ps 18:29 (my God lightens my darkness) and Ps 107:10-14 (in darkness, bound in irons).

**Hymn to Asarluḫi (Marduk), firstborn of Enki: the river ordeal refines the just like gold; the god of incantation, pure hands and pure feet; settled in Kuara** (ETCSL 4.01.1 6-41)
- Compare Mal 3:2-3 and Zech 13:9 (refining like silver and gold), Ps 24:3-4 (clean hands and pure heart) and Num 5:11-31 (ordeal).

**Šir-šag-ḫula to Damgalnuna, bride of Enki, great cow, mother of the great gods (fragments)** (ETCSL 4.03.1)
- Compare Hos 11:3-4 and Isa 66:13 (divine mother-care); Num 23:22 (wild ox imagery).

**A hymn to Ḫendursaĝa, segment A 4-41: the night watchman of the streets** (ETCSL 4.06.1 Seg.A:4-41)
- The god as watchman of the city at night: compare Ps 127:1 ('unless YHWH guards the city, the watchman stays awake in vain') and Isa 21:11-12.
- Officials who do not touch the god's property: compare 1 Sam 12:3-4 (whose ox have I taken?) and the temple dues of Num 18.

**A hymn to Ḫendursaĝa, segment A 42-87: the name at night, the priests, and the seven who are neither male nor female** (ETCSL 4.06.1 Seg.A:42-:74)
- Demons 'neither male nor female' (Udug-hul tradition): compare Q 37:150 and Q 43:19 (the angels made female by the unbelievers) and Matt 22:30 (angels neither marry).
- A raven and a vulture among the seven night creatures: compare the unclean birds of Lev 11:13-19 and Isa 34:11-15 (night creatures haunting a ruin).
- Calling on the name for protection at night: compare Ps 91:5-6, 14 and Prov 18:10.

**A hymn to Ḫendursaĝa, segment A 89-105: the gods who stand beside him** (ETCSL 4.06.1 Seg.A:89-105)
- Deities standing at a god's side: compare the heavenly host standing at God's right and left, 1 Kgs 22:19, and Isa 6:2.

**A hymn to Ḫendursaĝa, segment B: Enki's seven sons and their offerings** (ETCSL 4.06.1 Seg.B:1-46)
- Seven brothers in a god's service: compare the seven spirits/angels before the throne (Zech 4:10; Tobit 12:15) and the seven sons of Job (Job 1:2).

**A hymn to Ḫendursaĝa, segment C 1-30: the man who has no god and the man whose god is in heaven** (ETCSL 4.06.1 Seg.C:1-A)
- Success depends on one's god: compare Ps 127:1-2 and Ps 1:3 ('whatever he does prospers').
- A boat sunk by the storm on the sea: compare Jonah 1:4 and Ps 107:23-30.

**A hymn to Ḫendursaĝa, segment C 31-57: Utu at the scales, purchases and marriage** (ETCSL 4.06.1 Seg.C:31-57)
- The sun god at the scales: compare Prov 16:11 ('a just balance and scales are YHWH's') and Q 55:7-9 and Q 57:25 (God set up the balance, mizan).
- A man takes a wife, begets children and builds a house: compare Deut 20:5-7 and Jer 29:5-6.

**A hymn to Ḫendursaĝa, segment C 58-70: the herald's horn and the closing praise** (ETCSL 4.06.1 Seg.C:58-70)
- The horn blown to muster: compare Num 10:1-10, Judg 3:27 and Joel 2:1, 15.

**A hymn to Inana (ETCSL 4.07.a), fragmentary** (ETCSL 4.07.a 1-123)
- The goddess crowned and enthroned in the assembly to judge: compare Ps 82:1 and Prov 8:15-16 (Wisdom by whom kings reign).

**A balbale to Inana (Dumuzid-Inana O): the litany of blessings may-you-be** (ETCSL 4.08.15 1-34)
- A wedding blessing of fertility and wealth: compare Ruth 4:11-12, Gen 24:60 and Ps 128:3.

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid (Dumuzid-Inana R), main text** (ETCSL 4.08.18 sa–gida.A:1-unknown.B:30)
- Compare Song 4:11 and 5:1 (milk and honey of the beloved) and Song 1:7-8 (the shepherd's fold).

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid (Dumuzid-Inana R), versions 2 and 3** (ETCSL 4.08.18 Ver.2:1-Ver.3:19)
- The empty fold: compare Hab 3:17 and Jer 9:10; the anointed head: Ps 23:5 and Song 1:3.

**A kunĝar to Inana (Dumuzid-Inana T)** (ETCSL 4.08.20 sa–gida.A:1-unknown.B:48)
- The bride adorned with jewels: compare Isa 61:10, Ezek 16:10-13 and Song 4:9 and 7:1-6.
- The bed prepared: compare Song 1:16 ('our couch is green') and Prov 7:16-17.

**A song of Inana and Dumuzid (Dumuzid-Inana Y)** (ETCSL 4.08.25 6-65)
- The beloved's body as costly craftsmanship: compare Song 5:10-16 (head of gold, arms rods of gold set with Tarshish, body ivory with sapphires).
- Blessing that God go with the traveller by night and day: compare Ps 121:5-8 and Gen 28:15, 20.

**A balbale to Inana and Dumuzid (ETCSL 4.08.a)** (ETCSL 4.08.a 1-36)
- The shepherd-king's fold full of milk and his days long: compare Ps 23:1-6, Ps 21:5 and Prov 27:23-27.

**A šir-gida to Martu (Martu A)** (ETCSL 4.12.1 1-60)
- A god of pure hands who destroys evil and sets up truth: compare Ps 24:4 and Ps 99:4.
- A god of the mountains: compare 1 Kgs 20:23, 28 ('their gods are gods of the hills').

**An excerpt from a hymn to Nanna (ETCSL 4.13.c)** (ETCSL 4.13.c 1-11)
- A god intercedes with the high god for his city: compare Dan 9:16-19 and Ps 80:4-8.

**A hymn to Nergal (Nergal B)** (ETCSL 4.15.2 1-57)
- The god coming from the mountains with storm before him: compare Hab 3:3-5 (God comes from Teman; pestilence before him, plague behind) and Deut 33:2.
- The sa-gaz/Habiru: compare the 'Hebrews' (ʿivrim) of 1 Sam 13:3, 19 and 14:21.

**A balbale to Ninĝišzida (Ninĝišzida A)** (ETCSL 4.19.1 1-37)
- The god who knows the number of his people and seeks the ewes: compare Ezek 34:11-16, Ps 147:4 and Luke 15:4-6.
- A serpent-god who gives life: compare the bronze serpent Num 21:8-9 and 2 Kgs 18:4.

**A hymn to Ninimma (Ninimma A)** (ETCSL 4.21.1 Seg.A:1-Seg.C:1)
- A heavenly scribe who keeps the tablet of life: compare Exod 32:32-33, Ps 69:29, Dan 12:1, and the man with the scribe's inkhorn in Ezek 9:2-4; Q 50:17-18 and Q 82:10-12 (recording angels).

**A tigi to Nintur (Nintur A)** (ETCSL 4.26.1 sa–gida.A:1-sa–jara.B:45)
- God forms the king and priest in the womb: compare Jer 1:5, Ps 22:10-11 and Isa 49:1.
- The divine mother lowing for her calf: compare Isa 49:15 and Hos 11:1-4.

**A balbale to Ninurta (Ninurta F)** (ETCSL 4.27.06 1-32)
- Blessing of the womb and the herds: compare Deut 28:4, 11 and Deut 7:13-14.

**A hymn to Nungal, 1-26: the house of judgment and its gates** (ETCSL 4.28.1 1-26)
- Gates through which only the righteous enter: compare Ps 118:19-20, Isa 26:2 and Q 39:73 (the gates of the garden opened for the God-fearing) against Q 7:40 (the gates of heaven not opened for the arrogant).
- A net spread over heaven and earth for the wicked: compare Ezek 12:13, Ps 140:6 and Job 18:8-10.
- The arch like a rainbow: compare Gen 9:13 and Ezek 1:28.

**A hymn to Nungal, 27-61: the goddess enthroned, the prisoner led in, the ordeal** (ETCSL 4.28.1 27-61)
- Abandoned by brothers and friends in prison or affliction: compare Ps 88:9, 19, Job 19:13-19 and Ps 31:12.
- A house of judgment that separates the righteous from the wicked: compare Mal 3:18 and Q 36:59 ('stand apart this day, you criminals').

**A hymn to Nungal, 62-121: the goddess's self-praise; compassion and the prisoner's release** (ETCSL 4.28.1 62-121)
- A judge-goddess who holds the tablet of life: compare Dan 7:10 (books opened), Mal 3:16 and Q 17:13-14 (each man's book).
- Refined like silver and restored: compare Mal 3:3, Zech 13:9 and Ps 66:10-12.
- Mother of compassion who lifts sin: compare Exod 34:6-7 and Mic 7:18-19; raḥamim from reḥem 'womb' (Sumerian arhuš 'womb, compassion').

**A hymn to Šul-pa-e (Šul-pa-e A), version 1, 1-40: the hero and lord of the steppe** (ETCSL 4.31.1 Ver.1:1-40)
- The four-legged creatures of the steppe given into a god's hand: compare Ps 50:10-11 and Gen 1:28 / Ps 8:7-9.
- Death walking by night: compare Ps 91:5-6 and Jer 9:20.

**A hymn to Šul-pa-e (Šul-pa-e A), version 1, 41-85: the man who forgot his god is restored** (ETCSL 4.31.1 Ver.1:41-85)
- Prosperity that forgets God: compare Deut 8:10-14, Deut 32:15 and Hos 13:6; Q 96:6-7.
- Brought out of the waves and refined like gold: compare Ps 18:17, Ps 66:10-12 and Job 23:10.

**A hymn to Utu (Utu B)** (ETCSL 4.32.2 1-32)
- The sun of righteousness with healing: compare Mal 3:20 and Ps 19:5-7; the bolts of heaven's door: Ps 78:23.

**The debate between Winter and Summer, 1-79: Enlil begets the seasons and fixes their tasks** (ETCSL 5.3.3 1-79)
- The Creator fixed summer and winter: compare Ps 74:17 and Gen 8:22 ('seed-time and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter shall not cease').
- Two brothers bring their produce as offerings to the god: compare Gen 4:3-5 (Cain and Abel) and Q 5:27.

**The debate between Winter and Summer, 88-152: Winter's gifts, his envy and the quarrel** (ETCSL 5.3.3 88-152)
- Envy of the brother's accepted offering leads to the quarrel: compare Gen 4:4-8 and Q 5:27-30.

**The debate between Winter and Summer, 153-258: insults and replies** (ETCSL 5.3.3 153-258)
- Heat and cold, the seasons of work: compare Prov 6:6-8, 20:4 and Eccl 3:1-8.

**The debate between Winter and Summer, 259-318: Enlil's verdict and the reconciliation** (ETCSL 5.3.3 259-318)
- Quarrelling brothers reconciled: compare Gen 33:4-11 (Jacob's gifts to Esau) and Ps 133:1-2 ('how good when brothers dwell together ... like the fine oil upon the head').
- The verdict no one can reverse: compare Isa 14:27 and 43:13, Num 23:20, and Q 13:41.

**A drinking song (ETCSL 5.5.a)** (ETCSL 5.5.a 1-32)
- Wine that gladdens the heart: compare Ps 104:15, Judg 9:13 and Eccl 9:7 and 10:19.

**The farmer's instructions, 1-40: the father's teaching; irrigation, oxen, tools and ploughing** (ETCSL 5.6.3 1-40)
- The farmer taught by God how to plough, harrow and sow: compare Isa 28:23-29.
- Diligence in the field: compare Prov 20:4, 24:30-34 and 27:23-27.

**The farmer's instructions, 41-73: sowing, the prayer against pests, watering** (ETCSL 5.6.3 41-73)
- Seed rows and the sowing of each crop in its place: compare Isa 28:24-26.
- Prayer against pests and blight in the field: compare 1 Kgs 8:37 and Joel 1:4; Q 2:205.

**The farmer's instructions, 74-111: reaping, gleaners, threshing, winnowing; Ninurta the farmer** (ETCSL 5.6.3 74-111)
- Ears left for the gleaners who sleep among the sheaves: compare Lev 19:9-10, Deut 24:19 and Ruth 2:2-17 and 3:7 (Boaz lies down at the end of the grain heap).
- Threshing with sledge and oxen: compare Deut 25:4, Isa 28:27-28 and Isa 41:15.
- The farmer's knowledge comes from the god: compare Isa 28:26, 29 ('his God instructs him rightly').

**A man and his god, 1-27: the prologue; the young man struck by sickness** (ETCSL 5.2.4 1-27)
- The Sumerian 'Job': compare Job 1-2 (the righteous man struck), Job 30:16-31 and Ps 38.

**A man and his god, 28-81: the young man's complaint** (ETCSL 5.2.4 28-81)
- Friends turned false and kin estranged: compare Job 6:15-21, Job 19:13-19 and Ps 41:10, Ps 55:13-15.
- Light for all, darkness for me: compare Job 3:20-23, Job 30:26 and Lam 3:2.
- 'Why am I bound with the ignorant though wise?': compare Job 12:3-4 and 13:2.

**A man and his god, 82-119: 'you are my father'; no sinless child was ever born; the plea to know his sin** (ETCSL 5.2.4 82-119)
- No one is born without sin: compare Job 14:4, Job 15:14, Job 25:4, Ps 51:7, Ps 143:2, 1 Kgs 8:46 and Eccl 7:20.
- Show me my sin: compare Job 13:23, Ps 19:13 and Ps 139:23-24.
- God as the father who begot me: compare Deut 32:6, Isa 63:16, 64:7 and Ps 89:27.

**A man and his god, 120-146: the god hears and restores; the young man praises** (ETCSL 5.2.4 120-146)
- The sufferer's lot reversed: compare Job 42:10-17, Ps 30:12 ('you turned my mourning into dancing') and Ps 40:2-4.
- A guardian spirit appointed: compare Ps 91:11 and Q 13:11 (attendant angels guard man by God's command).

**The old man and the young girl (ETCSL 5.6.6)** (ETCSL 5.6.6 1-47)
- The failing body of old age in images (white almond blossom, grinders cease): compare Eccl 12:1-7 and 2 Sam 19:35-36 (Barzillai), and Q 19:4 ('my bones have weakened and my head glows white').
- An old man and a young woman: compare 1 Kgs 1:1-4 (Abishag).
- Amar-gi, release: compare deror, the release of Lev 25:10 and Jer 34:8-17.

**Public announcement of the loss of a seal (ETCSL 5.7.a)** (ETCSL 5.7.a 1-12)
- The seal as legal identity, lost and misused: compare Gen 38:18, 25 (Judah's seal) and 1 Kgs 21:8 (Jezebel seals letters with Ahab's seal); lost property proclaimed: Deut 22:1-3.

**Adapa (Middle Babylonian), 1'-38': the broken wing of the South Wind and Ea's instructions** (Adapa MB –:1'-38')
- Food that brings death or life, and a deceptive or mistaken counsel about eating: compare Gen 2:16-17, Gen 3:3-5 and Q 7:20-22 and Q 20:120 (Satan: 'shall I show you the tree of immortality?').
- Seven days without the wind: compare the seven days of Gen 7:4, 10 and 8:10-12.

**Adapa (Middle Babylonian), 39'-78': Adapa before Anu refuses the bread and water of life** (Adapa MB –:39'-78')
- Man kept from the food of eternal life after gaining knowledge: compare Gen 3:22-24 (lest he eat of the tree of life and live forever) and Q 20:120-121.
- Bread and water of life: compare Prov 9:5, Isa 55:1-3 and Ezek 47:12; the bread of life of John 6:35.
- A mortal taken up to heaven: compare Gen 5:24 and 2 Kgs 2:11.

**Adapa (Standard Babylonian), a+1-a+24: the sage of Eridu, given wisdom but not eternal life** (Adapa SB –:a+1-a+24)
- Clean hands as fitness to serve: compare Ps 24:3-4 and Ps 26:6.
- Wisdom granted, but not immortality: compare Gen 3:5, 22 and Solomon's gift of wisdom, 1 Kgs 3:12.

**Adapa (Standard Babylonian), b+1-c+19: the South Wind, the messenger, Ea's preparation** (Adapa SB –:b+1-c+19)
- God who examines hearts: compare Jer 17:10, Ps 7:10 and Prov 17:3.

**Adapa (Standard Babylonian), d+1-f+10: the refusal, Anu's laughter, the view of heaven, the cure for the wind's disease** (Adapa SB –:d+1-f+10)
- A man shown the heights of heaven: compare Gen 28:12, Isa 6:1-5 and the Prophet's ascension, Q 17:1 and Q 53:13-18.
- Adapa 'seed of mankind' (zēr amīlūti), the first man as sage: compare Adam, Gen 2-3, and the knowledge given Adam in Q 2:31.

**Advice to a Prince, 1-15: the king who does not heed justice** (AdvPrince SB –:1-15)
- God raises a foreign adversary against the unjust king: compare 1 Kgs 11:14, 23, Hab 1:5-6 and Isa 10:5-6.
- The king and justice: compare Deut 17:18-20, Prov 29:4, 14 and Ps 72:1-4; Q 38:26 ('judge between people in truth').

**Advice to a Prince, 16-34: fines, forced labour and conscription of the citizens of the holy cities** (AdvPrince SB –:16-34)
- The king who takes horses, fields and people for his service: compare 1 Sam 8:11-17 and Deut 17:16; Rehoboam's heavy yoke, 1 Kgs 12:4-14.
- Forced labour punished by forced labour under the enemy: compare Deut 28:47-48.

**Advice to a Prince, 35-55: seized oxen and taxed sheep; corrupt officials; the gods leave their shrines** (AdvPrince SB –:35-55)
- The wicked driven like chaff before the wind, their works a breath: compare Ps 1:4, Job 21:18 and Eccl 1:14; Q 14:18 (deeds like ashes in a windstorm).
- The gods leave their sanctuaries in anger: compare Ezek 10:18-19 and 11:22-23 (the glory departs).
- Removing landmarks and stelae: compare Deut 19:14 and Prov 22:28.

**Anzû (Neo-Assyrian), a+1-a+40: Ninurta's battle with the four winds and the darkness** (Anzu NA –:a+1-a+40)
- God rides the storm with the winds as messengers: compare Ps 104:3-4, Ps 18:10-16 and Nah 1:3-6.
- Darkness brought on the enemy: compare Exod 10:21-23, Exod 14:20 and Joel 2:10.

**Anzû (Neo-Assyrian), a+41-a+67: the tidings, the body hung on the Ekur, Ninurta blessed** (Anzu NA –:a+41-a+67)
- Good tidings of the champion's victory: compare 2 Sam 18:19-32, Isa 52:7 and Nah 2:1.
- The enemy's body hung up at the sanctuary: compare 1 Sam 31:9-10 (Saul's armour in Ashtaroth's temple, his body on Beth-shan's wall) and 1 Sam 17:54.

**Anzû (Old Babylonian) II 1-35: supremacy stolen; 'who will slay Anzû?'; the gods refuse** (Anzu OB II:1-35)
- 'Who will go for us?' in the divine council: compare Isa 6:8 and 1 Kgs 22:20-22.
- Whoever defeats the enemy is promised greatness: compare 1 Sam 17:25 and Judg 1:12.

**Anzû (Old Babylonian) II 36-82: Mami gives her son; the battle orders; the chariot of seven winds** (Anzu OB II:36-82)
- A mother sends her son into combat: compare 2 Macc 7:20-29 (contrast: martyrdom) and Judg 5:28.
- Chariot of the storm: compare 2 Kgs 2:11, Ps 68:5, 34 and Hab 3:8.

**Anzû (Old Babylonian) III: the combat, the arrow that turns back, Ea's advice to cut the wings** (Anzu OB III:1-a+35)
- The champion and the monster's taunt: compare 1 Sam 17:43-47.
- Weapons turned aside by a word: compare Isa 54:17 ('no weapon formed against you shall prosper') and Ps 91:7.

**Prologue: the singer praises Ninurta, firstborn of Enlil (Anzû SB I 1-14)** (Anzu SB I:1-14)
- Compare Exod 15:1-3 ('I will sing to YHWH ... YHWH is a man of war') and Judg 5:3.
- Compare Ps 74:13-14 and Isa 27:1 (God has slain the sea monster / Leviathan).

**Before the daises: Anzu is born on Mount Sharshar and Ea proposes him as Enlil's doorkeeper (Anzû SB I 15-a+55)** (Anzu SB I:15-a+55)
- Compare Gen 2:5-6 (no rain, no man to till; a spring rising from the earth).
- Compare Gen 3:24 (cherubim posted to guard the way to the tree of life) and Ezek 28:14-16 (the guardian cherub).

**Anzu covets supremacy and steals the tablet of destinies while Enlil bathes (Anzû SB I b+56-b+87)** (Anzu SB I:b+56-b+87)
- Compare Isa 14:12-15 ('you said in your heart: I will ascend ... I will set my throne on high ... I will be like the Most High') and Ezek 28:2, 12-17.
- Compare Isa 6:8 ('Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?') and 1 Kgs 22:20.
- Compare Q 7:12-13 and Q 38:75-76 (Iblis' pride against God's order); the guardian who turns rebel.

**Adad, Girra and Shara are offered the champion's reward and refuse in turn (Anzû SB I b+88-b+153)** (Anzu SB I:b+88-b+153)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:11, 24-25 (Israel afraid of Goliath; the king promises riches, his daughter and freedom to the man who kills him).
- Compare Rev 5:2-4 (no one found worthy) for the motif of no one able, though outside HB/Quran.

**Ea finds the champion: Mami renamed Mistress of All the Gods and asked to give her son Ninurta (Anzû SB I b+154-c+201)** (Anzu SB I:b+154-c+201)
- Compare Gen 17:5, 15 and Gen 32:29 (new names given at a turning point).
- Compare Judg 4:6-9 (a woman commissions the warrior) and 1 Kgs 1:11-31 for a mother securing her son's elevation.

**Mami's battle orders to Ninurta; he sets out with seven ill winds (Anzû SB II 1-34)** (Anzu SB II:1-34)
- Compare Ps 18:8-15 and Hab 3:5-11 (the divine warrior with storm, arrows and lightning; sun and moon stand still).
- Compare Nah 1:3 (whirlwind and storm are his way, clouds the dust of his feet).

**The first battle: the challenge, darkness, and arrows turned back by the tablet's power (Anzû SB II 35-69)** (Anzu SB II:35-69)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:43-47 (the champion's taunt and David's answer naming his God).
- Compare Joel 2:10, 31 and Amos 8:9 (sun darkened on the day of battle).

**Sharur carries the report to Ea; Ea's tactic: tire him, cut his pinions (Anzû SB II 70-154)** (Anzu SB II:70-154)
- Compare Judg 16:17-19 (the secret of invulnerability found and broken).

**Anzu's wings cut, the arrow through his heart; the tablet recovered and the gods rejoice (Anzû SB III 1-31)** (Anzu SB III:1-31)
- Compare Isa 27:1 and Job 26:12-13 (the fleeing serpent pierced); Ps 74:13-14.
- Compare Jer 23:18, 22 and Job 15:8 (standing in the council (sod) of God and hearing his word).

**Ea reports the kill; Enlil sends Birdu to summon Ninurta, who demurs over the tablet (Anzû SB III 32-102)** (Anzu SB III:32-a+77, Anzu SB III:91-102)
- Compare Gen 14:21-24 (the victor refuses to keep the spoil) as a contrast.

**Ninurta praised: he slew the mountains, and his names in the cult cities (Anzû SB III b+103-b+168)** (Anzu SB III:b+103-b+168)
- Compare Ps 110:1 ('sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool').
- Compare Isa 9:5 (the throne-names of the child) and Q 7:180, 59:22-24 (the most beautiful names of God).

**When gods were man: the lots cast, and the Igigi dig the rivers for forty years (Atra-hasis OB I 1-38)** (Atr OB I:1-38)
- Compare Gen 2:5, 15 (no man to till the ground; man placed in the garden to work it) and Gen 2:10-14 (the rivers).
- Compare Ps 82 and Deut 32:8-9 (the world apportioned among the sons of God).

**The Igigi burn their tools and besiege Ekur by night (Atra-hasis OB I 39-104)** (Atr OB I:39-104)
- Compare Exod 1:11-14 and 2:23 (hard labour; the cry goes up) and Exod 5:6-18.
- Compare 1 Kgs 12:4, 18 (the heavy yoke; the overseer of forced labour stoned).

**Nusku's embassy: 'Every one of us has declared war'; Enlil weeps (Atra-hasis OB I 105-173)** (Atr OB I:105-173)
- Compare 1 Kgs 12:16 ('To your tents, O Israel!') for collective refusal of the labour regime.

**Ea's proposal: a god is slain and man made from his flesh, blood and clay (Atra-hasis OB I 174-239)** (Atr OB I:174-239)
- Compare Gen 2:7 (dust and the breath of life) and Gen 1:26 ('let us make man').
- Compare Q 15:26-29, 32:7-9 and 38:71-72 (man from clay, God breathes his spirit into him) and Q 51:56 (jinn and men created to worship/serve).
- Compare Lev 17:11 (the life is in the blood).

**Mami renamed; the fourteen pieces of clay, the birth in the tenth month, the rites of birth and marriage (Atra-hasis OB I 240-333)** (Atr OB I:240-333)
- Compare Gen 1:27 and 2:23-24 (male and female; leaving father and mother) and Gen 29:27 (the wedding week).
- Compare Lev 12:1-5 (days of purification after birth) and Job 10:8-11, Ps 139:13-16 (God's hands fashion the child in the womb).
- Compare Q 23:12-14 and 22:5 (stages of creation in the womb).

**Middle Babylonian fragment: the gods grumble and resolve to slay their steward (Atra-hasis MB Bab2)** (Atr MB Bab2:1'-23')
- Compare Ps 2:3 ('let us break their bonds and cast their cords from us') and Jer 2:20 (breaking the yoke).

**'Wall, wall!': the warning, the round boat and its bitumen, the boarding and the sealing of the door (Atra-hasis MB Priv)** (Atr MB Priv:1-60)
- Compare Gen 6:13-22 (build an ark; dimensions; pitch inside and out; lower, second and third decks) and Gen 7:1-16 (family and animals two by two enter; YHWH shuts him in).
- Compare Q 11:37-44, Q 23:27 and Q 54:13 (the ark of planks and nails; 'load into it two of every kind and your family').
- Compare Matt 24:38 / Luke 17:27 (eating and drinking until the flood), outside HB/Quran.

**Ugarit fragment: Ea in a dream orders a window opened; the dove returns exhausted (Atra-hasis MB Ug2)** (Atr MB Ug2:1-14)
- Compare Gen 8:6-12 (Noah opens the window; the dove finds no rest for the sole of her foot and returns).

**SB version: the gods made yoke and basket; the lots and the digging (Atra-hasis SB I 1-38)** (Atr SB I:1-38)
- Compare Gen 2:5, 15 and Gen 2:10-14.

**SB version: Alla's revolt, the night siege and Nusku's embassy (Atra-hasis SB I 39-120)** (Atr SB I:39-120)
- Compare Exod 1:11-14 and 1 Kgs 12:4, 18.

**SB version: the Igigi's answer, Enlil's tears, and Anu's proposal to create man (Atra-hasis SB II 1-74)** (Atr SB II:1-74)
- Compare Gen 1:26 ('let us make man').

**SB version: Alla slain, man mixed from his flesh and blood; the gods spit on the clay (Atra-hasis SB II 75-116)** (Atr SB II:75-116)
- Compare Gen 2:7 and Q 15:28-29, 38:71-72.

**SB version: Mama renamed; the fourteen pieces, the designs of man and woman, the birth brick (Atra-hasis SB III)** (Atr SB III:1-132)
- Compare Gen 1:27; 2:23-24 and Gen 29:27.

**Prayer to Marduk: 'let me live, establish truth in my mouth, my god at my right' (Bit meseri IT 1-27)** (BitMeseri SB IT:1-27)
- Compare Ps 118:17 ('I shall not die but live and recount the deeds of YHWH') and Ps 6:6.
- Compare Ps 16:8, 121:5, 110:5 (YHWH at my right hand) and Ps 141:3 ('set a guard over my mouth').

**Lugalirra called from the heaven of Anu at midnight against the catalogue of demons (Bit meseri IT 28-66)** (BitMeseri SB IT:28-66)
- Compare Amos 5:8, Job 9:9 and 38:31 (Pleiades and Orion) and Isa 34:14 (Lilith).
- Compare Ps 91:5-6 (terror by night, pestilence stalking in darkness) and Q 113 (refuge from the evil of the darkness and of witches).
- Compare Q 67:3, 71:15 (God's layered heavens).

**'You know them, I do not': the demons of the house and the gods posted in every room (Bit meseri IT 67-150)** (BitMeseri SB IT:67-150)
- Compare Ps 139:1-4 and Ps 19:13 (God knows what I do not know; hidden faults).
- Compare 1 Sam 15:27, Zech 8:23 (seizing the hem of a garment) and Ruth 3:9.
- Compare Lev 16:20-22 (the goat for Azazel carries off the people's iniquities).

**The fourteen life-named standards, the Winged Ones, twin fighters and gate guardians (Bit meseri IT 151-259)** (BitMeseri SB IT:151-259)
- Compare Exod 25:18-20 and 1 Kgs 6:23-29 (winged cherubim carved on doors and walls) and Deut 6:9 (on the doorposts and gates).

**The Divine Heptad and the seven primeval sages, the four of human descent and their offences (Bit meseri IT 260-347)** (BitMeseri SB IT:260-347)
- Compare Gen 5:21-24 (the seventh patriarch Enoch taken by God) and Q 19:56-57 (Idris raised to a high place).
- Compare 1 Kgs 17:1; 18:1 (Elijah: no rain for three years) and Gen 6:4 (mighty men of old after the sons of God).
- Compare Ezek 28:3 and Dan 2:2 (Babylonian wise men) for the sage tradition.

**More sages and standards; the clay man and woman: 'I made you from the clay of Ea, you are godlike' (Bit meseri IT 348-398)** (BitMeseri SB IT:348-398)
- Compare Gen 2:7 and Ps 82:6 ('you are gods') and Isa 64:7 (we are the clay, you our potter).
- Compare Gen 1:16 (the sun to rule the day, the moon the night).

**The watchmen of Ea and Asalluhi and the dogs of four colours at the gate (Bit meseri IT 399-443')** (BitMeseri SB IT:399-443')
- Compare Zech 1:8 and 6:2-6 (horses of different colours patrolling the earth).
- Compare Q 18:18 (the sleepers' dog stretching its paws at the threshold).

**The black goat slaughtered and its hide spread over the patient; 'may he be pure as heaven' (Bit meseri IT 444'-472')** (BitMeseri SB IT:444'-472')
- Compare Gen 22:13 (the ram offered in place of the son) and Gen 27:16 (goatskins laid on Jacob).
- Compare Lev 14:4-7 and 16:5-10 (animals in purification and substitution rites) and Ps 51:9 ('wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow').

**The lamp greets Marduk; Nuska, king of the night, drives off Šulak; the Lugalirra figure thrown in the river (Bit meseri IT 473'-525')** (BitMeseri SB IT:473'-525')
- Compare Ps 91:5-6 ('the terror of the night ... the pestilence that stalks in darkness') and Ps 121:4-8 (the guardian who neither slumbers nor sleeps).
- Compare 2 Sam 22:29 and Ps 18:29 ('you light my lamp; my God lights up my darkness').
- Compare Ps 122:7-8 and Luke 10:5 ('peace be within your walls').

**Feast for the gods of the watch; Death netted and sent down to Ereškigal, banned from the light and river of the living (Bit meseri IT 526'-B+611')** (BitMeseri SB IT:526'-B+611')
- Compare Isa 25:8 (he will swallow up death forever) and Hos 13:14.
- Compare Job 33:28-30 and Ps 56:14 ('to walk before God in the light of the living') and Ps 36:9-10 (the fountain of life).

**Figurine list: number, form, attributes, place, recitation and ration of each figure (Bit meseri FI)** (BitMeseri SB FI:1-39)
- Compare Jer 19:13 and Zeph 1:5 (offerings to the host of heaven on the rooftops).

**Ritual tablet: the room facing sunrise, drawn sages and dogs, mouth-washing of images, scapegoat and Pazuzu (Bit meseri RTA)** (BitMeseri SB RTA:1-77)
- Compare Isa 44:9-20 and Ps 115:4-7 (images with mouths that cannot speak) and Q 7:195.
- Compare Jer 9:20 (death has come up through our windows).

**Catalogue of Texts and Authors: works from the mouth of Ea, revealed to Adapa, by sages, kings and scholars (Neo-Assyrian)** (CatAuth NA –:1-e+7)
- Compare Jer 36:4, 18 (Baruch writes at Jeremiah's dictation) and Exod 24:4; 34:27-28 (Moses writes the words given him).
- Compare Q 25:5 (the charge that the prophet's tales are dictated to him) and Q 53:4-5 (revelation taught by one mighty in power).
- Compare Gen 5:21-24 (Enoch) and the antediluvian books of Enoch/Berossus for writings from before the flood.

**Catalogue of Texts and Authors (Neo-Babylonian fragment): raven dictation, a king's hymn, the Theodicy** (CatAuth NB –:1'-17')
- Compare the psalm headings ascribing psalms to David, Asaph, Solomon (e.g. Ps 72:1, 73:1, 90:1).

**A sage's counsel to his son: honour parents, beware drink, gossip and disputes, repay evil with good (Counsels of Wisdom 1-54)** (CounsWis SB –:1-54)
- Compare Prov 1:8; 6:20 and Exod 20:12 (honour father and mother).
- Compare Prov 23:20-21, 29-35 (drunkards come to poverty) and Prov 20:19 (do not associate with a gossip).
- Compare Prov 26:17 (meddling in another's quarrel) and Prov 25:8.
- Compare Prov 25:21-22; 24:29; Exod 23:4-5 and Q 41:34, Q 23:96, Q 13:22 (repel evil with what is better).

**Pity the weak, feed the hungry; no slave girl over the house, no prostitute for a wife (Counsels of Wisdom A+1-A+31)** (CounsWis SB –:A+1-A+31)
- Compare Prov 30:21-23 (the earth trembles under a slave who becomes king and a maidservant who supplants her mistress).
- Compare Lev 21:7, 14 (priests may not marry a harlot) and Prov 5:3-10; 7:10-27.
- Compare Isa 58:7, Prov 14:31; 19:17 (who is kind to the poor lends to YHWH) and Q 76:8-9, Q 90:14-16.

**The prince's steward must not covet his treasure; conduct in office (Counsels of Wisdom A+32-A+62)** (CounsWis SB –:A+32-A+62)
- Compare Gen 39:8-9 (Joseph, given all his master's house, refuses to take what is withheld) and Luke 16:1-12.
- Compare Prov 16:18 (pride before destruction) and Prov 18:16 (a man's gift makes room for him).

**Read from the tablet: no backbiting, daily worship, reverence begets favour, keep your word (Counsels of Wisdom A+63-A+105)** (CounsWis SB –:A+63-A+105)
- Compare Prov 3:9-10 (honour YHWH with your wealth and your barns will be filled) and Prov 10:27; 3:1-2 (fear of YHWH prolongs days).
- Compare Num 30:3, Deut 23:22-24 and Eccl 5:3-4 (pay what you vow) and Q 17:34, Q 5:1 (fulfil covenants).
- Compare Prov 13:3; 21:23 (who guards his mouth keeps his life) and Q 49:12 (backbiting as eating a brother's flesh).

**Master and servant: palace, dining, hunting, house-building (Dialogue of Pessimism 1-38)** (DialPess SB –:1-38)
- Compare Eccl 1:2-3; 2:4-11 (houses built, all is hevel) and Eccl 6:7-9 on appetite; Eccl 3:1-8 (a time for each thing and its opposite).
- Washing hands before eating: compare Mark 7:3 and the ablution of Q 5:6.

**Silence before an adversary, doing something dishonest, loving a woman (Dialogue of Pessimism)** (DialPess SB –:a+1-52)
- Woman as pit and sword: compare Prov 22:14; 23:27 (a deep pit, a narrow well), Prov 5:4 (sharp as a two-edged sword), Eccl 7:26 (more bitter than death, a snare).
- Crime without dishonest gain leaves one naked and hungry: compare Prov 1:11-19 and Job 24.
- Silence before adversaries: compare Eccl 3:7 (a time to keep silence) and Prov 17:28.

**Sacrifice to one's god, lending, a good deed for the country (Dialogue of Pessimism 53-78)** (DialPess SB –:53-78)
- Loan to God: compare Prov 19:17 (he who is kind to the poor lends to YHWH) and Q 2:245; 57:11 (a goodly loan).
- Skulls on the ruin mounds: compare Eccl 2:14-16; 9:2-3 (one fate for righteous and wicked), Ps 49:11-13, and Q 30:9 / 40:21 (walk the earth and see the end of those before).
- Interest and lending: compare Exod 22:24, Lev 25:36-37, Deut 23:20-21, and Q 2:275-280 on riba.

**What then is good? Death (Dialogue of Pessimism 79-86)** (DialPess SB –:79-86)
- Compare Eccl 2:17; 4:2-3 (the dead more fortunate than the living), Job 3:20-22, and the question 'who has gone up to heaven?' in Prov 30:4 and Deut 30:12; Q 17:37 (you cannot reach the mountains in height).

**When on high: Apsu and Tiamat and the generations of the gods (Enuma elish I 1-20)** (Ee SB I:1-20)
- Compare Gen 1:1-2 (tehom, before heaven and earth are named) and Gen 2:4b-5 (when no shrub was yet); Ps 104:6; Prov 8:24-26 (when there were no depths).
- Gen 5:3 (Adam begot a son in his likeness, after his image) echoes I:16 tamšīlašu.
- Q 21:30 (heavens and earth were a joined mass which We split), Q 11:7 (his throne was upon the water).

**The young gods' noise; Apsu plots and is slain by Ea (Enuma elish I 21-78)** (Ee SB I:21-78)
- Gods' rest disturbed by noise: compare Atrahasis and the flood motive; Gen 11:1-9 and Gen 6:5. Divine rest after the work: Gen 2:2-3; Q 50:38 (no weariness touched Us).
- Mother speaks for her offspring against the father's plan: compare Gen 27 (Rebekah) only loosely.

**Birth and splendour of Marduk (Enuma elish I 79-104)** (Ee SB I:79-104)
- Fire from the god's lips: Ps 18:9; Isa 30:27; Job 41:11. Eyes in every direction: Ezek 1:18; 10:12; Zech 4:10; Rev 4:6-8.
- A hero endowed from birth: Jer 1:5; Judg 13:5.
