**Anu's winds roil Tiamat; she bears the monster army and exalts Qingu with the Tablet of Destinies (Enuma elish I 105-162)** (Ee SB I:105-162)
- Monster army of the sea: Dan 7:2-7 (four winds stir the great sea, beasts arise), Isa 27:1 (Leviathan the twisting serpent), Ps 74:13-14, Job 26:12-13; Rev 12-13 (dragon gives his authority to the beast).
- Eleven monsters: compare Gen 37:9 (eleven stars) only as number; Q 12:4.

**Ea reports Tiamat's war to Anshar (Enuma elish II 1-48)** (Ee SB II:1-48)
- Repeated reports framed verbatim: compare Gen 24:34-49 and Job 1:14-19.

**Anshar's dismay; Ea and Anu go against Tiamat and turn back (Enuma elish II 49-126)** (Ee SB II:49-126)
- Who will go for us? Isa 6:8; 1 Kgs 22:20-22. None dares face the monster: Job 41:2-3 (who can stand before me?).
- God who creates and destroys: Deut 32:39; 1 Sam 2:6; Isa 45:7.

**Marduk volunteers and demands supreme destiny (Enuma elish II 127-162)** (Ee SB II:127-162)
- Compare Deut 33:29 / Josh 10:24 (feet on the necks of kings), Ps 110:1; God riding the storm: Ps 18:11; 68:5; 104:3; Deut 33:26.

**Kakka delivers the message; the gods assemble, feast and decree Marduk's destiny (Enuma elish III 67-138)** (Ee SB III:67-138)
- Feast before the covenant/decision: compare Exod 24:11 (they beheld God and ate and drank) and Isa 25:6.

**Marduk enthroned; the test of his word; 'Marduk is king!' (Enuma elish IV 1-34)** (Ee SB IV:1-34)
- 'YHWH is king' (YHWH malak): Ps 93:1; 96:10; 97:1; 99:1; Ps 29:10. Raising and lowering: 1 Sam 2:7; Ps 75:8. Creation and destruction by word: Ps 33:9; Q 36:82 (Be, and it is).
- Spare him who trusts in you: Ps 2:12; 34:23.

**Marduk arms himself and rides the storm chariot (Enuma elish IV 35-64)** (Ee SB IV:35-64)
- Divine warrior's arming: Hab 3:8-11 (bow bared, arrows, lightning, chariots of salvation, against the sea); Ps 18:8-16; Ps 7:13-14; Isa 59:17; Zech 9:14.
- God's net: Ezek 32:3 (I will spread my net over you ... the dragon of the seas); Hos 7:12.
- Four winds: Zech 6:5; Dan 7:2; Jer 49:36.

**Single combat: Marduk slays Tiamat (Enuma elish IV 65-104)** (Ee SB IV:65-104)
- Ps 74:13-14 (you broke the heads of the dragons on the waters), Ps 89:10-11 (you crushed Rahab like a carcass), Isa 51:9-10, Job 26:12-13 (by his understanding he struck Rahab; by his wind the heavens), Job 9:13.
- Single combat challenge: 1 Sam 17:8-10.

**Captives netted, Tablet of Destinies taken, Tiamat split into heaven (Enuma elish IV 105-146)** (Ee SB IV:105-146)
- Gen 1:6-8 (raqia separating waters above from waters below), Ps 104:2 (stretching heaven like a tent-skin), Ps 148:4, Job 38:8-11 (bars and doors for the sea); Q 21:30 (heavens and earth were joined, We split them).
- Gen 7:11 / 8:2 (windows of heaven, sluices) for guarded upper waters.
- Exod 25:9, 40 (sanctuary after the heavenly pattern, tavnit) and Heb 8:5 for temple as counterpart.

**Marduk orders stars, year, moon and sun (Enuma elish V 1-46)** (Ee SB V:1-46)
- Gen 1:14-18 (lights for signs, seasons, days and years; the lesser to rule the night), Ps 104:19 (the moon for seasons), Ps 136:7-9, Sir 43:6-8; Q 10:5 (moon in stations to know the number of years), Q 36:39-40, Q 6:96-97.
- šapattu (15th day) and Hebrew shabbat: compare Isa 1:13; 2 Kgs 4:23 (new moon and sabbath paired).

**Clouds, rain, rivers and mountains made from Tiamat's body (Enuma elish V 47-66)** (Ee SB V:47-66)
- Gen 2:10-14 (Tigris and Euphrates from Eden), Gen 7:11 (fountains of the deep opened), Job 38:22-30 (storehouses of snow, rain), Ps 147:16-18.

**Trophies, homage, robing and the name Lugaldimmerankia (Enuma elish V 67-116)** (Ee SB V:67-116)
- Monuments 'lest they be forgotten': Josh 4:6-7 (stones as a sign), Exod 17:14. Enemies a footstool: Ps 110:1. 'My beloved son' to king: Ps 2:7.

**Marduk announces Babylon, home of the great gods (Enuma elish V 117-158)** (Ee SB V:117-158)
- Gen 11:4-9 (Babel, 'gate of the gods', its tower with its top in heaven) and Gen 28:12-17 (gods ascending and descending; house of God, gate of heaven).
- God chooses the place for his name to dwell: Deut 12:5, 11; Ps 132:13-14.

**Humankind made from Qingu's blood to bear the gods' toil (Enuma elish VI 1-38)** (Ee SB VI:1-38)
- Gen 1:26 (let us make man) and Gen 2:7, 15 (man formed to work the ground); Gen 9:6 (blood and image); Q 2:30 (I will place a vicegerent ... who sheds blood), Q 96:2 (created man from a clot, ʿalaq), Q 23:12-14 (flesh and bones).
- Guilty one handed over to die so others live: Jonah 1:12-15; John 11:50.

**Gods divided above and below; the gods build Babylon and Esagila and feast (Enuma elish VI 39-81)** (Ee SB VI:39-81)
- Gen 11:3-4 (let us make bricks ... a city and a tower with its top in the heavens); Exod 1:14; 5:7-19 (brick-making toil); 1 Kgs 6:1, 38 (temple built over years).

**The bow set in heaven; oath of allegiance; Marduk to be shepherd of humankind (Enuma elish VI 82-122)** (Ee SB VI:82-122)
- The warrior's bow hung in the sky after subduing the waters: Gen 9:12-17 (my bow in the cloud); Hab 3:9; Lam 2:4; Ezek 1:28.
- On earth as in heaven: Matt 6:10. Each people with its god, yet one god for us: Mic 4:5; Deut 32:8-9; Zech 14:9 (YHWH one and his name one); Q 17:110 (call him Allah or al-Rahman: his are the most beautiful names), Q 7:180.

**The fifty names begin: Marduk to Namru (Enuma elish VI 123-166)** (Ee SB VI:123-166)
- Ps 23:2 (green pastures, still waters), Ps 36:10 (in your light we see light), Isa 2:5; slow to anger yet relenting: Exod 34:6-7, Joel 2:13; Deut 32:39 (I kill and make alive). The beautiful names: Q 59:22-24.

**Names Asari to Zahgurim (Enuma elish VII 1-56)** (Ee SB VII:1-56)
- God who knows the hearts: Jer 17:10; Ps 7:10; 1 Sam 16:7; Q 67:13. The merciful who revives: Q 30:50 (He revives the earth after its death; He revives the dead). Gives the seed and the grain: Ps 104:14; Q 6:95.

**Names Enbilulu to 'Lord of the Lands' (Enuma elish VII 57-136)** (Ee SB VII:57-136)
- Only God knows the term of life: Ps 31:16; 39:5; Job 14:5; Q 31:34. The god gives rain and voice of thunder: Ps 29:3-9; Ps 65:10-14. Calling the stars by name and leading them: Isa 40:26; Ps 147:4. Crossing the sea: Ps 77:20; Isa 51:10.

**Ea gives his own name; epilogue on teaching and writing the names (Enuma elish VII 137-164)** (Ee SB VII:137-164)
- Teach them diligently to your children: Deut 6:6-7; Ps 78:3-6; Exod 17:14 (write this for a memorial). Num 23:19 (God's word does not change). Wherever water is drunk his name invoked: Mal 1:11 (from the rising of the sun my name is great among the nations).

**Hymn to Marduk, provider and absolver (Elevation of Babylon 1-81)** (ElevBab SB –:1-81)
- Ps 104:27-28 and Ps 145:15-16 (the eyes of all wait upon you, you give them their food in season); Q 11:6 (no creature but its provision is with God). Absolving sin: Ps 103:3; 130:4. Shepherd of the weak: Ezek 34:16; Ps 72:12-13.
- Restores in a day what was lost in a year: Joel 2:25; Job 42:10.

**Gods bless Marduk; Esagil and Eridu-Babylon praised (Elevation of Babylon 82-108)** (ElevBab SB –:82-108)
- Ps 148 (heaven, earth and all their hosts praise YHWH) and Ps 103:20-22. Jerusalem's gates and walls of precious stones: Isa 54:11-12; Rev 21:18-21. Gate of heaven: Gen 28:17.

**Babylon's abundance, river, wall, king and privileged citizens (Elevation of Babylon 109-134)** (ElevBab SB –:109-134)
- Lev 25:10 and Jer 34:8-17 (proclaim dəror); Isa 61:1. City like the garden of God: Gen 13:10; Ezek 28:13; Ps 46:5 (a river whose streams gladden the city of God); Ps 87.

**Invocation of Išum; Erra restless for war (Erra I 1-27)** (Erra SB I:1-27)
- Ps 121:4 (he who keeps Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps) vs Ps 44:24; 78:65 (the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior). Rev 6 (destroying riders).

**Anu begets the Seven and fixes their destructive tasks (Erra I 28-44)** (Erra SB I:28-44)
- Seven destroying agents: Ezek 9:1-2 (six/seven executioners), Rev 15-16 (seven angels with seven plagues); Q 69:7 (wind for seven nights).
- Human noise provoking destruction: Gen 6:11-13; Gen 18:20-21 (the outcry of Sodom).

**The Seven goad Erra: the field is better than the city (Erra I 45-91)** (Erra SB I:45-91)
- Joel 4:9-10 (beat your plowshares into swords; let the weak say I am a warrior), Isa 2:4. Rechabite preference for tents over cities: Jer 35:6-10; Gen 4:17 vs 4:20.
- Noise of humans disturbing the gods: compare the outcry of Gen 18:20 and the Atrahasis motif.

**Išum pleads; Erra's 'I am' boast and resolve to unseat Marduk (Erra I 92-123)** (Erra SB I:92-123)
- Intercession of a merciful figure: Gen 18:23-32 (Abraham), Exod 32:11-14 (Moses), Amos 7:2-6. Divine 'I am' self-praise: Isa 44:6-8; 45:5-7; Q 20:14.

**Erra in Esagil; Marduk recalls the flood when he left his throne (Erra I 124-162)** (Erra SB I:124-162)
- Flood as divine wrath and promise not to destroy again: Gen 6-9, esp. Gen 8:21-22 and Isa 54:9; seed of life kept: Gen 7:3; Q 11:40.
- World tree with roots in the deep and top in heaven: Dan 4:7-9 (17-19); Ezek 31:3-9. Craftsmen of the cult image: Isa 40:19-20; 44:12-17 (idol polemic).
- Seven sages (apkallu) as antediluvian bearers of wisdom: compare Gen 6:4 (men of renown) and Q 2:102 (Harut and Marut teaching in Babylon).

**Marduk warns of chaos if he leaves; Erra offers to govern meanwhile (Erra I 163-191)** (Erra SB I:163-191)
- Day turned to darkness: Amos 5:18-20; 8:9; Joel 2:10; 3:4. Gods/powers released when the restraining one departs: 2 Thess 2:6-7. Bulls/cherubim at the entrance: 1 Kgs 6:23-28.

**Oath curses; eagle and serpent share the poplar (Etana MA, Aššur a-b)** (Etana MA Aššur:a+1-b+23)
- Covenant-friendship sworn before God: 1 Sam 18:3; 20:8, 42. Snake and bird motif: Gen 3:1 with Gen 15:11.

**The fledgling's warning; the eagle seized in the ox (Etana MA, Aššur c)** (Etana MA Aššur:c+1-c+31)
- The wise child ignored: Gen 37:21-22 (Reuben); 1 Kgs 12:8. Trapper trapped: Ps 7:16; 57:7; Prov 26:27.

**Etana prays for an heir; dream directs him to the eagle in the pit; rescue (Etana MA, Aššur d-f)** (Etana MA Aššur:d+1-f+18)
- Joseph raised from the pit: Gen 37:24; 41:14; Jer 38:6-13; Ps 40:3. 'Take away my reproach': Gen 30:23; 1 Sam 1:6-11; Luke 1:25.

**Etana's dreams interpreted; first stages of the ascent (Etana MA, Aššur g-i)** (Etana MA Aššur:g+1-i+18)
- Dreams of homage: Gen 37:5-9; Gen 41. Ascent to heaven: 2 Kgs 2:11; Isa 14:13-14; Q 17:93 (until you ascend into heaven).

**Before kingship: the gods take counsel; kingship comes down from heaven (Etana OB Morgan 1-16)** (Etana OB Morgan:1-16)
- No king in those days: Judg 17:6; 21:25; 1 Sam 8:5-7. Kingship from God: Dan 2:37; 4:14; Q 2:247 (God has raised Saul as king), Q 3:26.

**Marriage fragment; eagle plucked and cast in the pit; rescued by Etana (Etana OB Morgan a-c)** (Etana OB Morgan:a+1-c+9)
- Open my eyes to hidden things: Ps 119:18; 2 Kgs 6:17; Dan 2:22. Joseph in the pit/prison then raised: Gen 37; 41.

**Oath, betrayal and the serpent's lament (Etana OB Susa)** (Etana OB Susa:1-a+24)
- Inescapable divine net: Ps 139:7-12; Amos 9:2-3; Obad 4 (though you soar like the eagle, set your nest among the stars, I will bring you down); Jer 49:16.
- Betrayal by a friend: Ps 41:10; 55:13-15.

**Gods found Kish; no king yet; Ishtar seeks a shepherd (Etana SB I)** (Etana SB I:1-a+11)
- God seeks a man after his heart to be shepherd-king: 1 Sam 13:14; 16:1-13; Ps 78:70-72. First city: Gen 4:17; 10:10.

**The poplar by Adad's shrine; oath; eagle eats the serpent's young (Etana SB II 1-52)** (Etana SB II:1-52)
- Obad 3-4 and Jer 49:16 (though you make your nest high as the eagle, I will bring you down). Covenant curses before God: Deut 27-28.

**Serpent's lament; Shamash's plan; eagle seized, plucked and cast in a pit (Etana SB II 53-132)** (Etana SB II:53-132)
- Prayer from the pit: Ps 88:4-7; 69:15-16; Jonah 2:3-7; Lam 3:53-55. Joseph in the pit: Gen 37:24. Rescue sent by God through a man: Gen 45:5-7.

**Etana prays for the plant of birth; sent to the eagle in the pit (Etana SB II 133-152)** (Etana SB II:133-152)
- Gen 30:1, 14-23 (mandrakes; God took away my reproach), 1 Sam 1:10-11 (Hannah's vow), Gen 15:2-3 (childless Abram), Gen 25:21; Q 19:4-6 and Q 3:38 (Zechariah prays for an heir), Q 21:89.

**The eagle seeks the plant; first flight and fall (Etana SB III 1-56)** (Etana SB III:1-56)
- Deut 32:11 (as an eagle stirs its nest, spreads its wings, takes them up, bears them on its pinions) and Exod 19:4. Solomon taught the speech of birds: Q 27:16; 1 Kgs 5:13 (spoke of birds).
- The earth seen from heaven: Isa 40:22 (inhabitants like grasshoppers).

**Return home; the wife and the plant (Etana SB III a)** (Etana SB III:a+1-a+23)
- Gen 30:14-16 (mandrakes, dudaim, as a fertility plant).

**Dream of Ishtar enthroned; second ascent through the gates of heaven (Etana SB III b-c)** (Etana SB III:b+1-c+7)
- Heavenly ascent and throne vision: Isa 6:1-5; Ezek 1:26-28; 1 Kgs 22:19; the Mi'raj through the heavens with a prophet greeted at each (Q 17:1; 53:13-18).
- Lions beside the throne: 1 Kgs 10:19-20.

**The gods call on Aruru to create a match for Gilgameš (MB Nippur fragment)** (Gilg MB Nippur:a+1-e+3)
- The creation of a counterpart compare Gen 2:18-20 ('a helper corresponding to him', kenegdo). The people's cry reaching heaven compare Exod 2:23-24, Exod 3:7 and Gen 18:20-21. Parallels Gilg SB I:79-98.

**Enkidu, sick, curses the trapper and Šamḫat before Šamaš (MB Ur)** (Gilg MB Ur:1-40)
- Parallels Gilg SB VII:90-131. Cursing and later blessing the woman who led him out of the wild compare Gen 3:14-19 (curses that fix the present lot) and Gen 3:7 (knowledge that brings weakness).
- The curse on the prostitute's lot (wall, crossroads) compare Prov 7:12 and Jer 3:2 (she sits by the roads).

**Šamaš answers from heaven; Enkidu turns his curse into a blessing on Šamḫat (MB Ur)** (Gilg MB Ur:41-58)
- Curse turned to blessing compare Num 23-24 (Balaam), Deut 23:6 and Neh 13:2. A voice from heaven answering a complaint compare Job 38:1. Parallels Gilg SB VII:132-161.
- Mother of seven as the blessed wife compare 1 Sam 2:5 and Jer 15:9 ('she who bore seven languishes').

**Enkidu's dream of the Anzû-faced man who seizes him (MB Ur)** (Gilg MB Ur:59-69)
- Parallels Gilg SB VII:165-192 (the figure takes Enkidu to the house of dust). Compare the angel of death, Q 32:11, and the figure in Dan 7:4 (lion with eagle's wings); seized by the hair compare Ezek 8:3.

**The harlot clothes Enkidu and leads him to the shepherds; bread and beer (MB Boğazköy 1)** (Gilg MB Boğ1:a+1a-a+16b)
- Parallels Gilg OB II:51-109 and SB I-II. Enkidu's humanisation compare Gen 2-3 (nakedness, clothing, knowledge) and Gen 3:21.

**Fragments: Gilgameš and Enkidu take hands; Enkidu's praise of Gilgameš's birth (MB Boğazköy 1)** (Gilg MB Boğ1:b+1'-c+8')
- Parallels Gilg OB II:231-240 and SB II.

**Gilgameš resolves to fight Ḫuwawa for an eternal name; the elders object (MB Boğazköy 1)** (Gilg MB Boğ1:d+1'-e+9')
- Parallels Gilg OB III:180-200 and SB II:270-299. A name for eternity compare Gen 11:4, 2 Sam 7:9 and Isa 56:5.

**Fragments: advice against marriage; Enkidu's case judged after Ḫuwawa's death (MB Boğazköy 1)** (Gilg MB Boğ1:a+1'-f+17')
- Parallels Gilg SB VI-VII. The gods judging who must die for the killing compare 1 Kgs 22:19-22 (the heavenly council) and Job 1:6-12.

**Gilgameš's second dream on the road: the mountain and the radiant man (MB Boğazköy 2)** (Gilg MB Boğ2:1'-31')
- Parallels Gilg OB Schøyen2:1-24 and SB IV. Rescue from under the mountain and water to drink compare Ps 18:17 and Ps 23:2; dreams on a journey compare Gen 28:10-17.

**Ištar proposes, is rejected and obtains the Bull of Heaven from Anu (MB Boğazköy 2)** (Gilg MB Boğ2:a+1-a+27)
- Parallels Gilg SB VI:1-120 and ETCSL 1.8.1.2. A hero refusing a powerful woman compare Gen 39:7-12; the goddess's offer of wealth compare Prov 7:16-18 and Prov 9:13-18.

**Fragment: Enkidu asks how they shall answer the people (MB Emar 1)** (Gilg MB Emar1)
- Parallels Gilg SB II.

**Ištar's offer and Gilgameš's catalogue of her lovers (MB Emar 2)** (Gilg MB Emar2:1'-35')
- Wailing for Dumuzi compare Ezek 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz). The goddess who destroys her lovers compare Prov 7:26-27 ('many are the slain she has cast down'). Parallels Gilg SB VI:22-79.
- 'Husband of your youth' compare Prov 2:17 and Joel 1:8.

**Anu questions Ištar and gives her the Bull of Heaven; the river drops seven cubits (MB Emar 2)** (Gilg MB Emar2:a+1'a-b+10'b–b+11')
- Parallels Gilg SB VI:80-125. A father-god questioning the plaintiff compare Job 1:7-12.

**Enkidu recalls Ḫumbaba and the Bull and tells his death dream (MB Megiddo)** (Gilg MB Megiddo:1'-18')
- This copy was found at Megiddo in the Jezreel valley: a Gilgameš tablet in Canaan. Parallels Gilg SB VII:165-192.

**Enkidu lies sick for days; Gilgameš moans like a dove (MB Megiddo)** (Gilg MB Megiddo:a+1'-a+20')
- Moaning like a dove compare Isa 38:14 (Hezekiah's sickness), Isa 59:11 and Ezek 7:16. Days of sickness counted compare 2 Kgs 20:1 and Ps 41:4. Parallels Gilg SB VII:251-VIII.

**The harlot tells Enkidu of Gilgameš's dreams of him and his mother's interpretation (MB private collection)** (Gilg MB Priv1:1-43)
- Two dreams with one meaning compare Gen 41:25-32 and Gen 37:5-10; a love surpassing that of women compare 2 Sam 1:26. Parallels Gilg OB II:1-43, SM and SB I:245-298.

**The harlot persuades Enkidu, clothes him and leads him to the shepherds, who bow before him as a god (MB private collection)** (Gilg MB Priv1:55-a+10')
- Bowing to a man as to a god compare Acts 14:11-15 and Dan 2:46; Gen 18:2. Parallels Gilg OB II:51-119 and SB II.

**Prologue: he who saw the Deep; the tablet in the cedar box; the wall of Uruk (MB Ugarit)** (Gilg MB Ug1:1-28)
- Parallels Gilg SB I:1-28 (closely) and the frame at SB XI:323-328. A book in a sealed box compare Jer 32:14 (deeds in an earthenware jar) and Deut 31:26; wisdom of what was before the flood compare Gen 6:4 and Sir 44:16.
- The outcry reaching heaven compare Gen 18:20-21 and Exod 2:23; the wall and its measured city compare Neh 2-3 and Rev 21:15-17.

**Gilgameš oppresses the young men; his giant stature (MB Ugarit)** (Gilg MB Ug1:29-38)
- Giant stature in cubits compare 1 Sam 17:4 (Goliath six cubits and a span) and Deut 3:11 (Og's bed of nine cubits); the king's hair compare Song 5:11 and Dan 7:9.

**Before the battle with Ḫumbaba: Enkidu's encouragement, 'two are two', the storm (MB Ugarit)** (Gilg MB Ug2:1'-a+24)
- 'Two are better than one' compare Eccl 4:9-12. Do not turn back compare Josh 1:9 and 2 Sam 10:12. Parallels Gilg SB IV-V and ETCSL 1.8.1.5:107-111.

**The earth splits, Ḫumbaba weeps before Šamaš and pleads; Enkidu urges no mercy (MB Ugarit)** (Gilg MB Ug2:b+1-b+42)
- Sparing or killing the pleading captive compare 1 Sam 15:8-33 (Agag) and 1 Kgs 20:31-42 (Ben-Hadad: 'your servant asks, let me live'). 'Mother and father I knew not' compare Heb 7:3 and Ps 27:10. Lebanon and Sirion shaken compare Ps 29:5-6. Parallels Gilg SB V:140-265.

**Fragment: Gilgameš frightened at a figure of great height; 'go back to your city' (NA x)** (Gilg NA x:1'-a+12')
- Parallels Gilg SB IV-V.

**Gilgameš rebukes Enkidu: only the gods live forever; a name if I fall (NA y)** (Gilg NA y:1'a-9')
- Man's days numbered and life a shadow compare Ps 39:5-7, Ps 144:4, Job 14:5 and 1 Chr 29:15. Parallels Gilg OB III:140-160 and SB II-III.

**The senior advisers warn; Gilgameš laughs and vows to cut off Ḫumbaba's head and raft cedars downstream (NA y)** (Gilg NA y:a+1'-b+21')
- Rafts of cedar floated down the water compare 1 Kgs 5:23 (Hiram's rafts to Joppa) and 2 Chr 2:15. The rash young king and his counsellors compare 1 Kgs 12:6-14. Parallels Gilg SB II:270-III:12 and OB III:189-206.

**Gilgameš's dreams of the sky-rock and the axe, interpreted by his mother (OB II)** (Gilg OB II:1-43)
- Two dreams of one meaning and a parent who interprets compare Gen 37:5-11 (Joseph's dreams, Jacob's reaction) and Gen 41:32. A love 'like a wife' between men compare 2 Sam 1:26. Parallels Gilg SB I:245-298.

**Seven days with Šamḫat; she leads him to the shepherds; bread, ale, oil and a garment make him a man (OB II)** (Gilg OB II:44-118–119)
- A woman who brings a wild man from the animals into human life compare Gen 2:18-25 and 3:6-7, 3:21 (clothing); bread as 'the thing of life' compare Gen 3:19 and Deut 8:3.
- The barber treating his hairy body (OB II:106-107) compare Gen 25:25 and Gen 27:11 (Esau the hairy man of the field) and Gen 41:14 (Joseph shaved before the king).
- A shepherd guarding the flock from lions compare 1 Sam 17:34-36 and Amos 3:12. Parallels Gilg SB I:188-II and MB Boğ1 / Priv1.

**The wedding guest tells of the king's right to the bride; Enkidu goes to Uruk (OB II)** (Gilg OB II:120–121-188–189)
- A ruler who takes the brides compare Gen 6:2 (sons of God take women), 2 Sam 11 and Esth 2:12-14. Destined from birth compare Jer 1:5 and Ps 139:16. Parallels Gilg SB II (wedding guest).

**Enkidu bars the door of the bride's house; the wrestling; Enkidu hails Gilgameš (OB II)** (Gilg OB II:190-242)
- Wrestling a stranger who then blesses compare Gen 32:25-30. Kingship given by God compare 1 Sam 16:1 and Dan 2:37. Parallels Gilg SB II:100-115.

**The friends kiss and bond; 'I have acquired a friend, the counsellor of my dreams' (OB III)** (Gilg OB III:10–11-44)
- A friendship sealed after rivalry compare 1 Sam 18:1-4 (Jonathan and David) and Prov 18:24. Parallels Gilg SB II.

**Ninsun's words; Enkidu's tears at the plan to slay Ḫuwawa (OB III)** (Gilg OB III:56-90)
- Tears of foreboding compare 2 Kgs 8:11-12 (Elisha weeps). Parallels Gilg SB III:1-12 and II:160-180.

**Debate on the forest: Ḫuwawa's terrors, 'only the gods live forever', a name, the forge (OB III)** (Gilg OB III:96-171)
- 'Only the gods live forever, man's days are numbered, all he does is wind' compare Eccl 1:14, Eccl 2:11, Ps 39:6, Ps 90:10, Job 7:7 and Q 21:34-35.
- Weapons weighed in talents compare 1 Sam 17:5-7; the forge compare 1 Sam 13:19-20. Parallels Gilg SB II-III.

**Gilgameš addresses the assembly; the elders warn; he laughs; a blessing for the road (OB III)** (Gilg OB III:172-215)
- The young king rejecting old counsel compare 1 Kgs 12:6-14 and 1 Kgs 20:11 ('let not him who girds on boast'). A god who straightens the path compare Prov 3:6, Ps 5:9 and Gen 24:40. Parallels Gilg SB II:260-III:12.

**Gilgameš kneels before Šamaš, weeps and vows a house; arming and departure (OB III)** (Gilg OB III:216-246)
- A vow before a journey ('if God brings me back in peace ... this stone shall be God's house') compare Gen 28:20-22; the god's shade over the traveller compare Ps 121:5-8. Parallels Gilg SB III:13-115.

**The elders' advice and blessing; Enkidu takes the lead; the crowd sent home (OB III)** (Gilg OB III:247–248-295)
- 'Do not rely on your strength' compare Ps 33:16-17, Jer 9:22 and Zech 4:6; may God open the closed paths compare Isa 45:2 and Isa 40:3-4. Washing the feet and pouring water compare Gen 18:4 and 1 Sam 7:6. Parallels Gilg SB III:1-12, 213-228.

**Enkidu thanks the harlot for showing him a friend (OB Schøyen 1)** (Gilg OB Schøyen1)
- Compare MB Ur:48-58 (blessing of Šamḫat) and OB III:151-153.

**First journey dream: the mountain that fell and the radiant man (OB Schøyen 2)** (Gilg OB Schøyen2:1a-24)
- God takes the hand in the day of trouble compare Isa 41:13, Ps 73:23 and Ps 50:15. Parallels Gilg SB IV:1-33 and MB Boğ2.

**Toward Ebla: the dream of thunder, darkness and raining death (OB Schøyen 2)** (Gilg OB Schøyen2:25-53)
- Thunder, darkness and fire in which a god appears compare Exod 19:16-18, Ps 18:8-16 and 1 Kgs 19:11-12; fire raining death compare Gen 19:24. Parallels Gilg SB IV.

**At the Amorite mountain: Ḫuwawa watches; Enkidu blanches at the cedar's splendour (OB Schøyen 2)** (Gilg OB Schøyen2:54-84)
- God promises 'I will go with you; do not fear' compare Exod 33:14, Deut 31:6-8 and Josh 1:9; faces paling with terror compare Jer 30:6 and Joel 2:6. The cedar mountain of the Amorite compare Amos 2:9 (the Amorite tall as cedars) and Deut 1:7.

**Near the forest: the dream of the Anzû-bird; the old man is Lugalbanda, the man Šamaš (OB Nippur)** (Gilg OB Nippur)
- A man who binds the wings of a monstrous bird and casts it down compare Rev 20:1-3. Parallels Gilg SB IV (fourth dream).

**The dream of the wild bull and the waterskin; Šamaš and Lugalbanda (OB Harmal 1)** (Gilg OB Harmal1)
- Water given from a god's waterskin in the wilderness compare Gen 21:19 and Exod 17:6. Parallels Gilg SB IV.

**At Ḫuwawa's gate; Ḫuwawa begs for his life and offers the tallest trees (OB Harmal 2)** (Gilg OB Harmal2)
- A defeated enemy offering servitude and goods compare 1 Kgs 20:32 and Josh 9:8-11. Cedar, cypress and juniper as palace timber compare 1 Kgs 5:22 and Isa 60:13. Parallels Gilg SB V.

**Enkidu urges the kill; Ḫuwawa slain, his auras escaping; the secret abode of the gods (OB Ishchali)** (Gilg OB Ishchali)
- Sirion and Lebanon shaking compare Ps 29:5-6 and Deut 3:9 (Hermon called Sirion). Taking the mother bird with the young compare Deut 22:6-7. The mountain of the gods in the north compare Isa 14:13 and Ezek 28:14-16. Parallels Gilg SB V:240-300.

**The slaying; the secret abode; Enkidu's cedar door for Enlil floated down the Euphrates (OB IM)** (Gilg OB IM)
- A cedar whose top reaches heaven compare Ezek 31:3 and Dan 4:8; cedar doors for the temple compare 1 Kgs 6:31-35; 'no stranger shall come near' compare Num 1:51. Parallels Gilg SB V:290-302.

**Gilgameš roams in skins; Šamaš: 'you will not find the life you seek' (OB VA+BM)** (Gilg OB VA+BM:1'-15')
- 'Light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun' compare Eccl 11:7-8; the dead do not see light compare Job 10:21-22, Ps 49:20 and Ps 88:11-13. Wandering in skins compare Heb 11:37 and 2 Kgs 1:8. Parallels Gilg SB IX-X.

**Gilgameš and the ale-wife: Enkidu's death and the counsel to enjoy life (OB VA+BM)** (Gilg OB VA+BM:a+1-a+43)
- The ale-wife's counsel is closely matched by Eccl 9:7-10 (eat your bread with joy, let your garments be white, oil on your head, enjoy life with the wife you love). Gods kept life for themselves compare Gen 3:22-24 and Q 21:34-35; 'all go to one place' compare Eccl 3:19-20.
- Refusing to bury the dead hoping for revival compare 2 Sam 12:16-23 and John 11:39 (four days, he stinks); 'go the way of all the earth' compare Josh 23:14 and 1 Kgs 2:2. Parallels Gilg SB X:1-90.

**Gilgameš smashes the Stone Ones; Sursunabu the boatman and the Waters of Death (OB VA+BM)** (Gilg OB VA+BM:b+1-b+29)
- Asking a stranger's name compare Gen 32:28-30 and Judg 13:17-18. Crossing waters of death to the land of the immortal compare Ps 69:2-3 and Ps 18:5-6. Parallels Gilg SB X:91-183.

**Enkidu gains understanding; the harlot leads him into Uruk (OB CUNES)** (Gilg OB CUNES)
- Knowledge gained as the animals withdraw compare Gen 3:5-7 and Gen 2:20 (no helper among the animals). Parallels Gilg SB I:196-212 and OB II.

**The harlot retells Gilgameš's sky-rock dream to Enkidu (OB SM)** (Gilg OB SM)
- Parallels MB Priv1:1-42 and SB I:245-298.

**Prologue: he who saw the Deep; the wall of Uruk and the lapis tablet (Gilgameš SB I)** (Gilg SB I:1-28)
- Compare Ps 48:13-14 (walk about Zion, count her towers, consider her ramparts, to tell the next generation) with I:18-21.
- Knowledge from before the flood: compare Enoch (Gen 5:21-24) and Josephus Ant. 1.70-71 (antediluvian wisdom on two pillars); seven sages compare Prov 9:1 (wisdom's seven pillars).
- The hero's story written in a book: compare Q 18:9 (al-Raqīm, the inscription) and Deut 27:2-8 (words written on plastered stones).

**Hymn to Gilgameš: two-thirds god, eleven cubits tall, the far traveller (Gilgameš SB I)** (Gilg SB I:29-60)
- Giant offspring of divine-human union: Gen 6:4 (the Nephilim, 'men of renown', gibborim); compare Og's bed of nine cubits (Deut 3:11) and Goliath six cubits (1Sam 17:4).
- The leader going out and coming in before his people: Num 27:17; 1Sam 18:16.
- Wells dug by the hero: compare Isaac's wells, Gen 26:18-22.

**Gilgameš oppresses Uruk; the gods hear and Aruru creates Enkidu from clay (Gilgameš SB I)** (Gilg SB I:61-112)
- Creation of a man from a pinch of clay: Gen 2:7; Job 33:6 (qoratsti, 'I too was nipped from clay'); Q 15:26-28, 38:71-72.
- The cry of the oppressed reaching heaven: Exod 2:23-25, 3:7; Gen 18:20-21.
- Enkidu among the beasts eating grass: compare Nebuchadnezzar in Dan 4:22, 4:29-30 and Ishmael 'a wild ass of a man' Gen 16:12; Esau the hairy man of the field Gen 25:25-27.
- The king who takes your daughters and sons: 1Sam 8:11-17.

**The trapper, his father's counsel and the sending of Šamḫat (Gilgameš SB I)** (Gilg SB I:113-175)
- A woman sent to undo a strong man: Judg 14:15-17, 16:4-21 (Delilah and Samson).

**Šamḫat and Enkidu: six days and seven nights, the animals flee, 'you are like a god' (Gilgameš SB I)** (Gilg SB I:176-212)
- Gen 3:5-7, 3:22 (knowing good and evil, 'like God', eyes opened, nakedness) and Gen 2:18-24 (the woman as companion); Enkidu later curses Šamḫat (VII) as Adam blames the woman (Gen 3:12).
- Six days and seven nights: compare the creation week (Gen 2:2) and the seven-day feasts (Judg 14:12-17).

**Šamḫat describes Uruk and tells Gilgameš's dreams of the star and the axe (Gilgameš SB I)** (Gilg SB I:213-298)
- Dreams told to a parent and interpreted: Gen 37:5-11 (Joseph's dreams, his father's rebuke); doubled dreams Gen 41:32.
- Love surpassing the love of women: David and Jonathan, 2Sam 1:26 and 1Sam 18:1-3.
- A star falling from heaven: Isa 14:12; Num 24:17 (a star from Jacob).

**Enkidu clothed, among the shepherds, taught bread and ale (Gilgameš SB II)** (Gilg SB II:1-62)
- First clothing: Gen 3:7, 3:21; bread as human food after the garden: Gen 3:19 ('by the sweat of your face you shall eat bread').
- The shepherd who drives away lions and wolves: 1Sam 17:34-36 (David).

**Enkidu bars Gilgameš from the wedding house; the heroes wrestle (Gilgameš SB II)** (Gilg SB II:63-115)
- Wrestling: Gen 32:25-31 (Jacob at the Jabbok). The wedding feast and the bridegroom's companions: Judg 14:10-20.

**Ninsun on Enkidu's lack of kin; Enkidu weeps; Gilgameš proposes the Cedar Forest (Gilgameš SB II)** (Gilg SB II:162-215)
- Covenant of friendship of two heroes: 1Sam 18:1-4, 20:41-42 (Jonathan and David weeping).

**Enkidu's warning about Ḫumbaba; 'man's days are numbered'; the forge; the elders' counsel (Gilgameš SB II)** (Gilg SB II:216-322)
- Man's days numbered and his works wind: Ps 39:5-7, 90:10-12, 144:4; Job 7:7, 14:5; Eccl 1:14 (hevel, 'chasing wind'); compare Q 57:20 (this life is play and vanity).
- Young king rejecting / weighing the elders' counsel: 1Kgs 12:6-14 (Rehoboam); 'I am but a youth': Jer 1:6-7; 1Sam 17:33 (Saul to David: 'you are but a youth').
- Monster breathing fire: Job 41:11-13 (Leviathan, flames from its mouth, breath kindles coals).

**The elders' counsel: 'do not trust in your strength'; Gilgameš goes to Ninsun (Gilgameš SB III)** (Gilg SB III:1-34)
- Do not trust in strength: Ps 33:16-17, Jer 9:22 (let not the mighty boast of his might), Isa 30:15; Q 18:39 and 28:78 (Qārūn: 'I was given it by my own knowledge').
- Elders send off and bless: Gen 24:60; 'go in peace': Judg 18:6.

**Ninsun purifies herself, censes on the roof and prays to Šamaš for her son (Gilgameš SB III)** (Gilg SB III:35-116)
- Prayer on the roof with incense: Jer 19:13, 32:29, Zeph 1:5 (offerings to the host of heaven on roofs); 2Kgs 23:12.
- God sending winds against enemies: Ps 18:11-16, 135:7; Exod 14:21; four winds Dan 7:2, Zech 6:5.
- Hands raised in prayer: Exod 9:29, 1Kgs 8:22, Ps 141:2.

**Ninsun adopts Enkidu; rites at the Gate of Cedar (Gilgameš SB III)** (Gilg SB III:117-173)
- Adoption of a foundling and temple upbringing: Exod 2:10 (Moses), 1Sam 1:24-28, 2:11 (Samuel at the sanctuary); Q 3:37 (Mary in Zechariah's care).

**The departure from Uruk: 'judge the cause of the weak'; the officers kiss his feet (Gilgameš SB III)** (Gilg SB III:202-244)
- Judge the cause of the weak: Ps 82:3, Isa 1:17, Jer 22:16, Prov 31:8-9.

**The march to Lebanon and the first dream: the mountain falls (Gilgameš SB IV)** (Gilg SB IV:1-33)
- Did a god pass by? flesh numb: Job 4:15-16 (a spirit passed before my face, the hair of my flesh stood up); 1Kgs 19:11 (YHWH passing by); compare 1Sam 3:4-9 (Samuel woken: 'did you call me?').
- Dream sought on a mountain or at a sanctuary: 1Kgs 3:4-5 (Solomon at Gibeon), Gen 28:11-17 (Jacob's stone pillow).

**Second and third dreams: heaven cries out, death rains down (Gilgameš SB IV)** (Gilg SB IV:34-109)
- Heaven roaring, darkness, lightning, fire raining: Exod 19:16-18 (Sinai), Ps 18:8-15, Gen 19:24 (fire from heaven); Q 41:13 (a thunderbolt like that of ʿĀd and Thamūd).
- Deep sleep falling on a man: Gen 2:21, 15:12 (tardemah), Job 4:13.

**Fourth and fifth dreams and the approach to Ḫumbaba (Gilgameš SB IV)** (Gilg SB IV:a+1'-d+1')
- Five dreams on a journey: compare the dream-series of Gen 37 and 40-41; morning brings Šamaš's favourable word, compare Ps 30:6, Lam 3:23.

**The Cedar Forest: dwelling of the gods, birdsong, resin like rain; terror falls (Gilgameš SB V)** (Gilg SB V:1-30)
- The cedar garden of God on the mountain: Ezek 28:13-16 and 31:3-9, 31:16-18 (the cedars in the garden of God, Eden), Ps 104:16-17 (cedars of Lebanon where birds nest), Isa 14:8 and 37:24 (the boast of cutting Lebanon's cedars).
- Dove moaning: Isa 38:14, 59:11; Nah 2:8.

**'Forget death and seek life': mutual encouragement at the forest's edge (Gilgameš SB V)** (Gilg SB V:31-54)
- Be strong and courageous: Josh 1:6-9, Deut 31:6; 'choose life' Deut 30:19; fame for days to come: Gen 11:4, 2Sam 7:9.

**'Two are two'; Šamaš: 'Fear not!'; Ḫumbaba roars and taunts (Gilgameš SB V)** (Gilg SB V:55-142)
- Two are better than one ... a threefold cord is not quickly broken: Eccl 4:9-12 (an almost verbatim parallel to V:75-79).
- Goliath: 'I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field' (1Sam 17:43-46).
- 'Fear not' from heaven: Gen 15:1, 21:17; Josh 8:1.

**The combat: earth splits, thirteen winds blind Ḫumbaba, the weapons reach him (Gilgameš SB V)** (Gilg SB V:143-165)
- God fighting with winds and storm: Ps 18:8-16, Josh 10:11 (hailstones), Judg 5:20-21 (the stars fought); Sirion and Lebanon skipping: Ps 29:5-6.

**Ḫumbaba begs for his life; Enkidu urges death; Ḫumbaba's curse (Gilgameš SB V)** (Gilg SB V:166-280)
- Sparing the defeated king against advice: 1Sam 15:8-9, 15:32-33 (Agag); 1Kgs 20:31-42 (Ahab spares Ben-hadad).
- The bird and her young: Deut 22:6-7.

**Ḫumbaba slain, the forest laid waste, a cedar door for Enlil's temple (Gilgameš SB V)** (Gilg SB V:281-324)
- Cedars of Lebanon floated by raft for the temple: 1Kgs 5:20-23 (5:6-9), 2Chr 2:15; temple doors of cedar/olive: 1Kgs 6:31-35.
- Felling the cedars of Lebanon as hubris: Isa 14:8, 37:24; Hab 2:17 (the violence done to Lebanon); Ezek 31:12.
- The severed head carried home: 1Sam 17:51-54 (Goliath's head to Jerusalem); 2Sam 4:7-8.

**Gilgameš washes and is crowned; Ištar proposes marriage (Gilgameš SB VI)** (Gilg SB VI:1-21)
- Potiphar's wife sees Joseph's beauty and demands 'lie with me' (Gen 39:6-12; Q 12:23-24); the strange woman's invitation with perfumed bed (Prov 7:13-18).
- Washing and changing garments after a crisis: Gen 41:14; 2Sam 12:20.

**Gilgameš rejects Ištar and lists her ruined lovers (Gilgameš SB VI)** (Gilg SB VI:22-79)
- Women weeping for Tammuz at the temple gate: Ezek 8:14.
- Refusing the seductress: Gen 39:8-9 (Joseph), Q 12:23 (ma'adha llah); Prov 5:3-6 (her lips drip honey but her end is bitter as wormwood).
- The goddess who turns men into animals: compare Circe (Odyssey 10); the shepherd hounded by his own dogs: Actaeon.

**Ištar weeps before Anu, threatens to raise the dead, and obtains the Bull of Heaven (Gilgameš SB VI)** (Gilg SB VI:80-114)
- Seven years of storing grain against disaster: Gen 41:29-36, 41:47-49 (Joseph); Q 12:47-49.
- The dead rising and outnumbering the living: Ezek 37:1-10 (inverted, as threat), Isa 26:19.

**The Bull of Heaven ravages Uruk and is slain; its heart offered to Šamaš (Gilgameš SB VI)** (Gilg SB VI:115-150)
- Earth opening and swallowing men: Num 16:30-33 (Korah); the sacred bull: Exod 32 (golden calf); 'horns of the wild ox' Ps 22:22.

**Ištar's lament, the haunch hurled, the horns dedicated, 'Who is finest among men?'; Enkidu dreams (Gilgameš SB VI)** (Gilg SB VI:151-183)
- Women singing the victor's praise: 1Sam 18:6-7; Exod 15:20-21; Judg 5.
- Jezebel at the window (2Kgs 9:30-33) as the goddess on the wall; the thigh/haunch (imittu) compare Exod 29:22 and Lev 7:32 (the right thigh).

**The gods' counsel; Enkidu curses the cedar door (Gilgameš SB VII)** (Gilg SB VII:1-63)
- Cherubim and guardian figures at temple doors: 1Kgs 6:23-35, Ezek 41:18-25.
- A later king erasing his predecessor's name: compare the curse formulae on monuments and 2Kgs 23:15-18.

**Gilgameš weeps, vows a golden statue; Enlil's word cannot be rescinded (Gilgameš SB VII)** (Gilg SB VII:64-89)
- No ransom can redeem a life from death: Ps 49:8-10; Q 3:91 and 5:36 (the earth's fill of gold would not be accepted as ransom).
- God's word does not return: Isa 45:23, 55:11; Num 23:19; Esth 8:8 (the irrevocable written decree).

**Enkidu curses the hunter and Šamḫat (Gilgameš SB VII)** (Gilg SB VII:90-131)
- Cursing the agent of one's fall from innocence: Gen 3:12-13 (the woman whom you gave me); Job 3:1-10 (cursing the day of birth); Jer 20:14-15 (cursing the man who brought news of his birth).
- The harlot by the roadside and the ruins haunted by owls: Gen 38:14; Isa 13:21-22, 34:11-15; Zeph 2:14.

**Šamaš rebukes Enkidu; Enkidu turns his curse into a blessing (Gilgameš SB VII)** (Gilg SB VII:132-161)
- God recalls his benefits to the ungrateful: Deut 8:2-16, Hos 2:10 (11:1-4); Q 55 (fa-bi-ayyi ālāʾi rabbikumā).
- Curse turned into blessing: Num 22-24, Deut 23:6, Neh 13:2; Q 2:152 (gratitude).
- Mourner in skins in the wilderness: Elijah's hairy mantle (2Kgs 1:8), John the Baptist in camel hair (Mark 1:6).

**Enkidu's dream of the House of Dust (Gilgameš SB VII)** (Gilg SB VII:162-226)
- Sheol, land of darkness and dust, of no return: Job 7:9-10, 10:21-22, 17:16; Ps 88:11-13; Isa 14:9-11 (the dead kings rise from their thrones to greet the newcomer); Ezek 32:21-32.
- Books read out before a heavenly or netherworld tribunal: Dan 7:10, Mal 3:16, Ps 139:16; Q 17:13-14 and 69:19-25 (the book of deeds handed over).
- Souls as birds: compare the ba-bird and Q 2:260 (the four birds).

**'Remember me'; Enkidu lies sick twelve days, lamenting he does not die in battle (Gilgameš SB VII)** (Gilg SB VII:249-298)
- 'Remember me' : Gen 40:14 (Joseph to the cupbearer); Judg 16:28; Luke 23:42.
- Dying of illness rather than in battle: 1Sam 26:10 and 31:4 (Saul's death); Hezekiah's sickness unto death, Isa 38:1-3.

**Gilgameš's lament: may all creation weep for Enkidu (Gilgameš SB VIII)** (Gilg SB VIII:1-41)
- David's lament for Saul and Jonathan: 2Sam 1:17-27 ('mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew'; 'your love was wonderful to me, passing the love of women'); Zech 12:10-14.
- Nature summoned to mourn: Jer 4:28, 12:4, Amos 1:2, Joel 1:10; Ezek 31:15 (Lebanon in mourning for the cedar); Q 44:29 (neither heaven nor earth wept for them).

**'What sleep has seized you?': Enkidu's heart stops; Gilgameš veils him like a bride (Gilgameš SB VIII)** (Gilg SB VIII:42-64)
- Bear robbed of her cubs: 2Sam 17:8, Hos 13:8, Prov 17:12.
- Tearing hair and garments in grief: Ezra 9:3, Job 1:20, 2Sam 13:31; mourning for an only friend: 2Sam 1:26.
- The dead as asleep: Ps 13:4, Jer 51:39, Dan 12:2; Q 39:42.

**The statue of Enkidu; Gilgameš's vow of mourning (Gilgameš SB VIII)** (Gilg SB VIII:65-91)
- Absalom's pillar to keep his name (2Sam 18:18); teraphim/images (1Sam 19:13).

**Treasures displayed to Šamaš as gifts for the gods of the Netherworld (Gilgameš SB VIII)** (Gilg SB VIII:92-210)
- Burnings and spices for a king's burial: 2Chr 16:14, Jer 34:5; the azazel goat: Lev 16:8-10, 16:21-22.

**Gilgameš plans the damming of the river; the offering table for Šamaš (Gilgameš SB VIII)** (Gilg SB VIII:211-250)
- Honey forbidden on the altar: Lev 2:11; 'butter and honey' Isa 7:15; burial in a hidden place: Deut 34:6 (Moses' unknown grave).

**'I shall die, and shall I not be like Enkidu?': Gilgameš sets out; lions at night (Gilgameš SB IX)** (Gilg SB IX:1-29)
- Fear of death: Ps 55:5, Heb 2:15; 'I shall go to him, he will not return to me' (2Sam 12:23); Eccl 2:14-16, 3:19-20 (the same fate befalls all).
- Killing lions: Judg 14:5-6 (Samson), 1Sam 17:34-36 (David), 2Sam 23:20 (Benaiah).

**The twin mountains of Māšu and the scorpion-man and his wife (Gilgameš SB IX)** (Gilg SB IX:37-93)
- Cherubim with a flaming sword guarding the way to the tree of life: Gen 3:24; mountains as pillars between heaven and the deep: Job 26:7-11, Ps 104:5-8.
- Dhū l-Qarnayn travels to the setting and rising of the sun: Q 18:86-90.

**Twelve double-hours of darkness on the path of the sun; the garden of jewel-trees (Gilgameš SB IX)** (Gilg SB IX:125-196)
- The garden of God with every precious stone, walking among stones of fire: Ezek 28:13-14; trees 'pleasant to the sight and good for food' Gen 2:9, 3:6; the gold and onyx of Havilah Gen 2:11-12.
- Thorns and briars replaced by crystal: compare the curse 'thorns and thistles' (Gen 3:18) reversed; the jewelled city Rev 21:18-21, Isa 54:11-12.

**Šiduri the ale-wife bars her gate; 'my friend has turned to clay' (Gilgameš SB X)** (Gilg SB X:1-71)
- Return to clay/dust and never rise: Gen 3:19, Job 10:9, 14:10-12 (man lies down and does not rise till the heavens are no more), Ps 103:14; Eccl 3:20.
- Seven days of mourning: Gen 50:10, Job 2:13; the corpse and worms Isa 14:11, Job 21:26.
- 'How can I keep silent?': Job 7:11, Jer 4:19.

**The way across the ocean and the Waters of Death; Ur-šanabi and the Stone Ones (Gilgameš SB X)** (Gilg SB X:72-111)
- The waters no one has crossed: Deut 30:13 ('who will cross the sea for us and bring it?'); Q 18:60-61 (Moses at the meeting of the two seas, majmaʿ al-baḥrayn) and 55:19-20 (two seas with a barrier between).
- Charon and the Styx in Greek myth.

**Ur-šanabi's questions; three hundred punting-poles; the crossing; Ūta-napišti watches (Gilgameš SB X)** (Gilg SB X:112-203)
- Ark/boat imagery prefigured; the improvised sail of a garment: compare Jonah's sea voyage (Jonah 1).

**Gilgameš meets Ūta-napišti and tells of his toil (Gilgameš SB X)** (Gilg SB X:204-265)
- What profit has a man of all his toil? Eccl 1:3, 2:22-23 (his days are pain, even at night his heart does not rest); Ps 127:2.

**Ūta-napišti's discourse: the fool's lot, man snapped like a reed, the mayfly, the hidden day of death (Gilgameš SB X)** (Gilg SB X:266-322)
- A time for everything: Eccl 3:1-8; transience Eccl 1:4, 9:11-12; Ps 90:5-6, 103:15-16, Isa 40:6-8, Job 14:1-2 (man flees like a shadow).
- The hidden hour of death: Eccl 8:8, 9:12; Q 31:34 (no soul knows in what land it will die), 7:34 and 16:61 (an appointed term, ajal, neither delayed nor advanced).
- Folly honoured: Prov 26:1 (honour is not fitting for a fool), Eccl 10:5-7.

**'You are just like me': how did Ūta-napišti find life? (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:1-7)
- Enoch and Elijah taken alive (Gen 5:24, 2Kgs 2:11); Q 19:56-57 (Idrīs raised to a high place).

**The gods decide on the Deluge; Ea warns through the reed wall: 'demolish the house, build a boat' (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:8-47)
- Gen 6:13-14 (God tells Noah the end of all flesh; make an ark), 6:18-21 (bring in your family and two of every kind), Gen 7:1-4; Q 11:36-37 and 23:27 (make the ark under our eyes and by our revelation).
- Contrast: Noah warns/preaches to his people (Q 11:25-26, 71:1-20; 2Pet 2:5 'herald of righteousness'), while Ūta-napišti is told to deceive them.
- Gen 6:15-16: 300 x 50 x 30 cubits, roof (tsohar), three decks; the SB boat is a cube.
- Abandon possessions to save life: compare Lot's flight (Gen 19:17), Matt 16:25-26.

**The boat built: a cube of six decks, bitumen by the myriad, the builders feasted; loading and sealing the hatch (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:48-96)
- Gen 6:14-16 (gopher wood, qinnim, pitch inside and out, three decks, door, tsohar), 6:22 and 7:5 (Noah did all as commanded); Gen 7:1-3, 7:7-9, 7:13-16 (family and animals enter, 'YHWH shut him in'); Q 11:40 (load two of every kind and your family), 11:38 (the people mock), 54:13 (planks and nails/fibres), 23:27 (the oven boils as signal).
- Seven-day wait and the signal: Gen 7:4, 7:10; the boiling oven (fāra l-tannūr) Q 11:40, 23:27.

**The Deluge: the black cloud, the gods cower like dogs, Bēlet-ilī's lament; seven days; the vent opened (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:97-139)
- Gen 7:11-12 (fountains of the deep and windows of heaven), 7:17-24 (all flesh died, waters prevailed 150 days), 8:1 (God remembered Noah, wind), 8:6 (Noah opened the window, ḥallon); Q 54:11-12 (gates of heaven opened with pouring water, earth burst with springs), 11:42 (waves like mountains), 11:44 (earth swallow your water; sky withhold).
- Genesis has forty days of rain (Gen 7:12, 7:17) against six days and seven nights here; God's regret Gen 6:6-7 versus the goddess's regret; the 'like a woman in labour' image Isa 42:14.
- No grief of a deity over the drowned in Genesis or Quran: contrast Q 11:37 ('do not address me about the wrongdoers'), 11:45-47 (Noah's plea for his son).

**Mount Nimuš; dove, swallow and raven; the sacrifice; the gods gather like flies (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:140-163)
- Gen 8:4 (the ark rests on the mountains of Ararat), 8:5 (mountain tops seen), 8:6-12 (raven sent out goes to and fro; dove finds no resting place, returns; then olive leaf; then does not return); Q 11:44 (the ark settled on al-Jūdī).
- Gen 8:20-21: Noah's altar, burnt offerings of every clean animal and bird, 'YHWH smelled the pleasing odour' (reaḥ ha-niḥoaḥ) - compare irīša ṭāba; the gods as flies has no biblical counterpart.
- Seven days of waiting: Gen 8:10, 8:12 (seven more days).

**The lapis necklace; Enlil's rage; Ea's rebuke; Ūta-napišti and his wife made like gods (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:164-206)
- Gen 8:21-22 and 9:8-17: God's promise never again to curse the ground or flood the earth, the covenant and the bow in the cloud 'that I may remember' (9:15-16) - compare the necklace 'that I may remember these days and never forget'.
- Gen 9:1 (God blessed Noah and his sons); Q 11:48 ('descend with peace from us and blessings on you').
- Each punished for his own sin: Deut 24:16, Ezek 18:4, 18:20, Jer 31:29-30; Abraham's plea Gen 18:23-25 ('will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked?'); Q 6:164, 17:15, 35:18 (no bearer bears another's burden).
- Lesser punishments - sword, famine, wild beasts, plague: Ezek 14:12-21 (with Noah named, 14:14), Lev 26:22-26, 2Sam 24:13.
- Revelation through a dream: Num 12:6; Job 33:15-16.

**The sleep test: seven loaves mark seven days asleep (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:207-246)
- Q 2:259 (the man made to die a hundred years, whose food and drink had not spoiled, and his donkey) and Q 18:19, 18:25 (the sleepers of the cave: 'we stayed a day or part of a day'); compare 1Kgs 19:5-8 (bread-cake by Elijah's head).
- Death comes up into our windows: Jer 9:20; 'wherever you are, death will find you': Q 4:78, 62:8.

**Ur-šanabi banished; Gilgameš washed and robed; the secret plant of rejuvenation (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:247-300)
- The tree of life guarded so that man may not 'eat and live forever' (Gen 3:22-24); 'your youth renewed like the eagle's' Ps 103:5; Job 33:25.
- Garments that did not wear out on the long journey: Deut 8:4, 29:4; Neh 9:21.
- Q 18:60-82: Moses and his servant at the meeting of the two seas lose a fish that 'took its way into the sea' - often compared with the plant and the snake, and the waters of life of the Alexander romance.

**The snake steals the plant and sheds its skin; return to Uruk and its wall (Gilgameš SB XI)** (Gilg SB XI:301-328)
- The serpent and lost immortality: Gen 3:1-5, 3:22-24 (the way to the tree of life barred); the serpent's renewal by skin-shedding, compare Isa 65:25 (dust the serpent's food).
- Return to the city wall framing the epic: Ps 48:13-14; Neh 12:27-43 (procession on the walls).

**The ball and mallet fall into the Netherworld; Gilgameš's instructions to Enkidu (Gilgameš SB XII)** (Gilg SB XII:1-30)
- Sheol as silence: Ps 94:17, 115:17; the dead do not praise: Isa 38:18.

**Enkidu breaks every taboo and the Netherworld seizes him (Gilgameš SB XII)** (Gilg SB XII:31-54)
- Korah swallowed alive into Sheol (Num 16:30-33); 'Sheol has enlarged its throat' Isa 5:14.

**Gilgameš appeals to Enlil, Sîn and Ea; Šamaš raises Enkidu's ghost (Gilgameš SB XII)** (Gilg SB XII:55-87)
- Saul and the medium of En-dor: 1Sam 28:7-19 (Samuel's ghost brought up 'from the earth', 28:13-15: 'why have you disturbed me?').
- God answered him not: 1Sam 28:6 (neither by dreams, Urim nor prophets).

**'Tell me the order of the Netherworld': the fates of the dead (Gilgameš SB XII)** (Gilg SB XII:88-153)
- The unburied and their fate: 1Kgs 14:11, Jer 22:19, Isa 14:19-20; 'blessed is the man whose quiver is full' Ps 127:3-5; the eunuch's consolation Isa 56:3-5 ('a name better than sons and daughters').
- Dust on the head in grief: Josh 7:6, Job 2:12; grubs and worms Isa 14:11, 66:24.
- The rich man and Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31): a report of the fates of the dead.

**Gula's self-praise as Nintinugga; her husband Ninurta, slayer of Anzu (Gula Hymn 1-17)** (GulaHymn SB –:1-17)
- Compare Ps 91:1-16 and Exod 15:26 (God as healer); the healing deity's self-predication resembles Isa 45:5-7 'I am YHWH and there is no other'.

**Chosen as Ninurta's bride; the farmer-god and Gula as Nanše of the field boundary (Gula Hymn 18-43)** (GulaHymn SB –:18-43)
- Compare Isa 28:23-29 (God teaches the farmer to plow and sow) and Prov 31:13-27 (the capable wife who manages the household).

**The husband as Ninazu, rider of the winds; Gula as queen in heaven and netherworld, Ninkarrak (Gula Hymn 44-67)** (GulaHymn SB –:44-67)
- Compare Ps 104:3 and Ps 18:11 (God rides on the wings of the wind) and Isa 55:11 (my word shall not return empty); Num 23:19.

**Ninurta's might; 'I am the physician': the healing goddess as Ninigizibara (Gula Hymn 68-91)** (GulaHymn SB –:68-91)
- Compare Exod 15:26 ('I am YHWH your healer'), Deut 32:39, Ps 147:3 (he binds up their wounds) and Hos 6:1.
- Compare Q 26:80 ('when I am ill, it is He who heals me').

**Zababa the comely; Bau who has mercy on the weak; Ninurta launcher of the deluge; Šarrat-Nippuri's beauty (Gula Hymn 92-129)** (GulaHymn SB –:92-129)
- Compare Ps 113:7 and 1Sam 2:8 (raises the poor), Prov 3:6 and Ps 25:9 (he makes straight the paths of those who seek him).
- For 'launcher of the deluge' compare Ps 29:10 (YHWH enthroned over the mabbul).

**The husband wears heaven as tiara and earth as sandals; Anu, Antu and Ea endow Gula with the physician's craft (Gula Hymn 130-148)** (GulaHymn SB –:130-148)
- Compare Isa 66:1 (heaven my throne, earth my footstool) and Q 2:255 (his kursi encompasses heavens and earth).

**Lugalbanda the avenger; Ninsun adorned; 'I fetch up the dead from the netherworld': Ninlil, mistress of life (Gula Hymn 149-187)** (GulaHymn SB –:149-187)
- Compare 1Sam 2:6 and Deut 32:39 (he brings down to Sheol and raises up), Ps 30:4.
- Compare Q 3:49 and 5:110 (healing and raising the dead 'by God's leave').

**Closing prayer: have mercy on the servant Bullussa-rabi, intercede with your spouse (Gula Hymn 188-200)** (GulaHymn SB –:188-200)
- Compare Ps 30:12 (you loosed my sackcloth and girded me with joy), Isa 61:3, Zech 3:3-5 (filthy garments exchanged); Ps 18:29 (my God lights my darkness).

**Gula as creatress of heaven and earth, endowed by Anu, Enlil and Ea (Syncretistic Gula Hymn 1-17)** (GulaSyncr SB –:1-17)
- Compare Gen 2:19-20 and Ps 147:4 (naming as mastery); Prov 8:22-31 (Wisdom present at creation).

**Litany of the goddess's names: Panunnaki, Zarpanitu, Ama, Mamê, Šuzianna, Namma, Ninkarrak, Ninmah ... (Syncretistic Gula Hymn 18-58)** (GulaSyncr SB –:18-58)
- Compare Deut 6:4 and Zech 14:9 ('YHWH will be one and his name one') as a counterpoint to collapsing many deities into one; also Q 7:180 (the most beautiful names belong to God).

**Fragmentary column: the secret place of the gods, divination, and the goddess who removes misdeeds and hears prayer (Syncretistic Gula Hymn A+1-A+50)** (GulaSyncr SB –:A+1-A+50)
- Compare Ps 103:3 (who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases) and Ps 65:3 (you who hear prayer).
- Lines A+1-A+14 and A+34-A+50 are mostly broken (traces only).

**Her wisdom by leave of each great god; her abodes Esharra, Ekur, Esagil, Duku (Syncretistic Gula Hymn A+51-A+74)** (GulaSyncr SB –:A+51-A+74)
- Compare Ps 113:3 and Mal 1:11 (from the rising of the sun to its setting); Job 38:8-11 (God's control of the sea).

**City by city, shrine by shrine: the goddess is Ningal in Ur, Aya in Sippar, Ningirimma in Babylon, Ninlil in Hursagkalama ... (Syncretistic Gula Hymn A+75-A+139)** (GulaSyncr SB –:A+75-A+139)
- Compare Ps 91:1 and 121:5 (dwelling in God's shade); Ps 87 (birth registers of the cities); Deut 12:5 (the one chosen place versus many shrines).

**Fragmentary column B: the goddess who cleans away sins in E-dadaglal and Duku (Syncretistic Gula Hymn B+1-B+20)** (GulaSyncr SB –:B+1-B+20)
- Compare Ps 51:4,9 (wash me from my iniquity, purge me).

**Fragmentary column C: battle, Erra, the entrance of Ganzir and the princes of the netherworld (Syncretistic Gula Hymn C+1-C+15)** (GulaSyncr SB –:C+1-C+15)
- Compare John 1:3 / Ps 127:1 (without him nothing) as a distant formula.

**Neo-Assyrian Descent of Ishtar: the opening, the house of darkness (Ishtar's Descent NA 1-11)** (IshDesc NA –:1-11)
- Compare Job 10:21-22 (land of darkness and deep shadow, without order) and Job 7:9-10; Ps 88:13.

**Ishtar sets her mind on the netherworld, the house none leaves who enters (Ishtar's Descent 1-11a)** (IshDesc SB –:1-11a)
- Compare Job 10:21-22, 17:16 (bars of Sheol, rest in the dust), Isa 14:11 and Ps 88:6-13; Job 7:9 and 2Sam 12:23 (the dead do not return).
- Compare Gen 3:14,19 and Isa 65:25 (dust as the serpent's food) and Q 23:99-100 (barzakh, no return).

**At the gate: Ishtar threatens to raise the dead; Ereškigal's dismay and lament for the untimely dead (Ishtar's Descent 12-41)** (IshDesc SB –:12-41)
- Compare Isa 26:19 and Ezek 37 (the dead rise) as a reversal: here raising the dead is a threat; Rev 20:13.
- Compare Isa 14:9-11 (Sheol stirred at an arrival) and Ps 107:16 (he shatters the doors of bronze, cuts the bars of iron).

**The seven gates: Ishtar stripped of crown, earrings, beads, pins, birth-stone girdle, bangles and loincloth; seated above Ereškigal, struck with sixty diseases (Ishtar's Descent 42-75)** (IshDesc SB –:42-75)
- Compare Job 1:21 and Eccl 5:14 (naked I came from my mother's womb, naked I shall return) and Q 6:94 (you come to Us alone as We created you).
- Compare Deut 28:27-35, 59-61 (catalogue of diseases from sole to crown) and Job 2:7.

**With Ishtar below, no creature mates; Papsukkal mourns before Sîn and Ea; Ea creates Asûšu-namir (Ishtar's Descent 76-99)** (IshDesc SB –:76-99)
- Compare Hos 2:9-13 and Joel 1:10-12 (fertility withdrawn) and Jer 7:34 (voice of bride and groom ceases).
- Compare the Sumerian Inana's Descent (ETCSL 1.4.1), where Enki makes the kurgarra and galatur from the dirt under his fingernail.
- Compare Dan 6:8-9 and Esth 8:8 (an oath or decree that cannot be revoked used against its maker).

**Ereškigal curses Asûšu-namir; Namtar sprinkles Ishtar with the water of life (Ishtar's Descent 100-118c)** (IshDesc SB –:100-118c)
- Compare Gen 3:14-19 and Gen 4:11-12 (curse fixing a way of life) and Gen 49:7.
- Compare Ezek 47:9, Zech 14:8 and Rev 22:1 (living water) and Q 21:30 (every living thing from water).

**Return through the seven gates; the ransom; Tammuz bathed and dressed; Belili's cry; the dead come up to smell the incense (Ishtar's Descent 119-138)** (IshDesc SB –:119-138)
- Compare Ezek 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz at the north gate of the temple) and Zech 12:11 (mourning for Hadad-rimmon).
- Compare Isa 65:3-4 and 1Sam 28:13 (bringing up the dead) and Deut 26:14.

**Praise of Ishtar's might: as great as Anu, rays like Sîn, wings that are the winds (Ishtar 2, 1-56)** (Ishtar2 SB –:1-56)
- Compare Ps 18:11 and 104:3-4 (wings of the wind; winds his messengers) and 1Sam 2:7 (he brings low and lifts up).
- Lines 3-4, 33-45, 53-56 are mostly traces.

**A sick man confesses unwitting sins; Ishtar can rescue; description of the afflicted (Ishtar 2, 57-128)** (Ishtar2 SB –:57-128)
- Compare Ps 19:13 and Lev 4:2,13 (unwitting sins), Ps 38:4-11 (sickness and sin), Ps 62:4 (like a leaning wall), Isa 38:14 (I moan like a dove), Ps 27:10.

**The sick man mourned while alive, abandoned by friends, driven mad by a god's evil wind; plea 'take his hand' (Ishtar 2, 142-199)** (Ishtar2 SB –:142-199)
- Compare Ps 88:9,19 and 38:12 (friends stand aloof), Job 19:13-19, Ps 73:21-22, Lam 1:14 (yoke of my transgressions), Ps 73:23 (you hold my right hand).

**Plea for release: open the doors of heaven, have pity like father and mother; she frees the captive; gods, bow to her; 'Ishtar, have mercy!' (Ishtar 2, 206-247)** (Ishtar2 SB –:206-247)
- Compare Ps 27:10, Isa 49:15 and 63:16 (God as father and mother), Ps 103:13; Ps 146:7 and 107:10-14 and Isa 42:7, 61:1 (freeing prisoners, light to those in darkness).
- Compare Exod 34:6, Ps 30:6 (anger a moment, favor a lifetime), Ps 113:3, Ps 97:7 (all gods bow down to him) and Q 1:3.

**Syncretistic hymn: Ishtar as Zarpanitu, Tašmetu, Ninlil, Dilbat, the Wagon star, the viper, the net; she tramples the land like a snake (1-25)** (IshtarSyncr SB –:1-25)
- Compare Isa 14:12 (Helel ben Shahar, morning star) and Jer 7:18, 44:17 (queen of heaven); Ps 91:13 (tread on lion and serpent); Mic 1:4, Ps 97:5 (mountains melt).
- Compare Ezek 12:13 and 17:20 (God spreads his net) and Hab 1:15.

**The god who gathered the share of seven brothers; wings and legs as winds; colophon: secret for experts (IshtarSyncr 26-36)** (IshtarSyncr SB –:26-36)
- Compare 1Sam 16:11-13 and Gen 49 / 1Chr 5:1-2 (the youngest of the brothers preferred).
- Compare Dan 12:4,9-10 (sealed words; the wise will understand) and Mark 4:11.

**Lipit-Eštar A: the king's self-praise and the gifts of An, Enlil, Ninlil, Nanna, Enki, Inana, Nisaba, Utu (1-42)** (IsinDyn OB 2.5.5.1_Lipit–Eštar_A:1-42)
- Compare Ps 2:7 (you are my son) and 2Sam 7:14; Ps 92:13 (the righteous flourish like a cedar of Lebanon) and Ezek 17:22-23; 1Sam 16:12 (ruddy, beautiful eyes) and Ps 45:3.

**Lipit-Eštar A: the king as farmer, shepherd and provider, and as humble servant of the gods of Nippur, Kesh, Ur and Eridu (43-66)** (IsinDyn OB 2.5.5.1_Lipit–Eštar_A:43-66)
- Compare Ps 72:16 (abundance of grain under the king) and 1Kgs 3:7 (Solomon's humility); Deut 26:1-11 (first fruits).

**Prologue: 'I will praise the lord of wisdom' - Marduk furious by night, relenting by day, who wounds and heals (Ludlul I 1-40)** (Ludlul SB I:1-40)
- Compare Job 5:17-18 and Hos 6:1 (he wounds and binds up), Deut 32:39 and 1Sam 2:6 (he kills and makes alive), Ps 30:6 (anger a moment, favor a lifetime; weeping at night, joy in the morning).
- Compare Isa 49:15 and 66:13 (God as mother), Job 9:12 and Dan 4:32 (who can stay his hand?), Isa 40:13-14 and Job 11:7, Rom 11:33-34 (who has known the mind of the Lord?).
- Compare Ps 51:15 (I will teach transgressors your ways) and Ps 22:23 (I will tell your name to my brothers); Jonah 2:1-7 (from the belly of the fish).

**From the day the Lord punished me: god, goddess and protective spirits desert; dignity flees; evil omens and dreams (Ludlul I 41-54)** (Ludlul SB I:41-54)
- Compare Job 7:13-14 (you scare me with dreams), Job 19:9 (stripped my glory), Job 29:2-5 (when God watched over me), Ps 22:2 and 88:15.
- Compare 1Sam 28:6 (YHWH did not answer him by dreams, Urim or prophets).

**The king turns against him; seven courtiers conspire; friends, kin and slaves become enemies; goods and offices given to others (Ludlul I 55-104)** (Ludlul SB I:55-104)
- Compare Job 19:13-19 (brothers, kin, guests, maidservants estranged; servant does not answer), Job 30:1-10 (mocked by outcasts), Ps 31:12-14, 38:12, 41:10 and 55:13-15 (my familiar friend lifted his heel), Ps 88:9,19.
- Compare Dan 6:4-9 (officials conspire against Daniel before the king), Esth 3, Gen 39 and Ps 109:8 (let another take his office); Jer 20:10 (all my familiar friends watch for my fall).
- Compare Ps 39:3,10 and 38:14-15 (I am mute, I do not open my mouth) and Ps 22:7-8 (all who see me mock me).

**Sighing by day, lament by night; moaning like a dove; tears; 'my sun will shine' (Ludlul I 105-120)** (Ludlul SB I:105-120)
- Compare Isa 38:14 and 59:11 (moaning like doves), Ps 6:7-8 and 42:4 (tears my food day and night), Ps 31:10-11, Lam 1:20 and 2:11 (my bowels churn), Job 30:26-27, Ps 102:4-12.
- Compare Ps 30:6, Mal 3:20 (sun of righteousness) and Job 11:17.

**A year passes and it worsens; diviners fail; treated like one who neglected the gods though he was pious; the unknowable will of the gods; human fickleness (Ludlul II 1-48)** (Ludlul SB II:1-48)
- Compare Job 1:1,5 and 29:1-25 (Job's former piety), Job 31 (oath of clearance), Job 13:24 and Ps 13:2, 88:15 (why do you hide your face?), Ps 44:18-23 (all this has come upon us though we have not forgotten you).
- Compare Isa 55:8-9 (my thoughts are not your thoughts), Job 11:7-8 and 28:12-28 (where shall wisdom be found?), Eccl 8:17, Prov 16:2 and 21:2 (every way of a man is right in his own eyes but YHWH weighs the heart), Isa 5:20; Q 2:216 ('you may dislike a thing which is good for you').
- Compare Ps 90:5-6 and 103:15-16, Job 14:1-2, Deut 8:12-14 and 32:15 and Prov 30:8-9 (sated, they forget God), Isa 14:13-15 (I will ascend to heaven ... brought down to Sheol).

**Demons from the netherworld attack; the body broken limb by limb; wallowing in dung; wasting; exorcist baffled; the tomb readied; enemies rejoice (Ludlul II 49-120)** (Ludlul SB II:49-120)
- Compare Job 2:7-8 (sore boils, sitting in ashes), Job 7:3-5 and 30:16-18,30 (nights of misery, gnawing pains, skin blackens), Job 19:20 (bone clings to skin), Job 33:19-22 (loathes bread, bones stick out, soul draws near the Pit), Ps 22:15-18 (bones out of joint, I can count my bones), Ps 102:4-6 (bones cleave to skin), Ps 38:3-11, Lam 3:4.
- Compare Job 17:1 (the graves are ready for me), Ps 88:4-6, Isa 38:10-12, and Ps 35:15,19-21, 41:6-9 and 38:17 (enemies gloat: 'when will he die?'); Job 19:9-12 and 13:27 (feet in the stocks).
- Compare 2Kgs 20:1-11 / Isa 38 (Hezekiah's illness, also with an omen) and 2Chr 16:12 (seeking physicians).

**Heavy was his hand upon me: day and night groaning, dreaming and waking alike wretched (Ludlul III 1-8)** (Ludlul SB III:1-8)
- Compare Ps 32:4 (day and night your hand was heavy on me), Ps 38:3 and 39:11, Job 23:2 (his hand is heavy despite my groaning), Job 19:21 and 1Sam 5:6,11.

**Three dreams: the radiant young man, the exorcist of Nippur with holy water, the fair young woman who says 'Fear not'; Ur-Nintinugga sent by Marduk (Ludlul III 9-50)** (Ludlul SB III:9-50)
- Compare Job 4:12-16 and 33:14-18 (God speaks in dreams; a spirit passes by), Gen 41:32 (dream repeated as confirmation), Dan 10:5-11 (a man clothed in linen, the seer's strength fails), Gen 15:1 and Dan 10:12,19 (Fear not), Isa 6:6-7 (purification by an envoy).
- Compare Num 19:18 and Ps 51:9 (purge me with hyssop) and 2Kgs 5:10-14 (healing by washing at a prophet's word), Job 33:23-26 (the interceding angel announces recovery).
- Compare Q 12:4-6 and 37:102 (dreams as revelation) and Q 2:260.

**Marduk's heart is quieted; he disregards the sin and lets the wind carry away the faults (Ludlul III 51-67)** (Ludlul SB III:51-67)
- Compare Ps 103:3,10-12, Mic 7:18-19 (casts sins into the depths of the sea), Isa 38:17 (cast my sins behind your back), Ps 30:6, Lev 16:21-22 (sins borne away to the wilderness).
- Lines 63-67 are broken.

**The demons driven back; eyes, ears, nose, lips, mouth, teeth, tongue, throat, lungs, bowels, neck and nails healed (Ludlul III 68-120)** (Ludlul SB III:68-120)
- Compare Isa 35:5-6 (blind see, deaf hear, mute tongue sings), Job 33:25 (his flesh fresher than a child's), Job 42:10-12 (fortunes restored), 2Kgs 5:14 (flesh like a little child's), Mark 7:32-35.
- Compare Dan 4:30 and 4:33 (Nebuchadnezzar's nails like birds' claws, then restored).
- Lines 108-110 and 113-117 are traces; 119-120 a word each.

**Tablet IV fragments: restored body, darkness turned to light, the river ordeal, the slave mark removed, walking Kunush-kadru Street redeemed; let the impious learn from me (Ludlul IV)** (Ludlul SB IV)
- Compare Ps 51:15 (I will teach transgressors your ways), Ps 34:12 (come, children, I will teach you the fear of YHWH), Ps 32:8-9; Num 5:11-31 (ordeal).
- Compare Exod 21:6 and Deut 15:17 (slave mark, the bored ear) and Isa 61:1 and 52:2 (loose the bonds from your neck); Ps 18:29 and Isa 9:1 (darkness to light).
- Most of Tablet IV is fragmentary: a+1-2, a+11-15, a+22-23, c+1-3, c+11-15, c+17, d+10 are traces or broken.

**'My lord granted me relief': taken by the hand, the lion muzzled, the gravedigger's shovel wrested, pulled back from the river of death; 'had it not been for the lord' (Ludlul V 1-36)** (Ludlul SB V:1-36)
- Compare Ps 124:1-5 ('Had it not been YHWH who was for us ... then the waters would have swept us away') and Ps 94:17 (unless YHWH had been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence), Ps 119:92.
- Compare Ps 30:2-4,12, 40:3, 86:13, 103:4 (who redeems your life from the Pit), Jonah 2:7, Ps 3:4 (lifter of my head), Ps 73:23 (you hold my right hand), Ps 22:21-22 and Dan 6:23 (rescued from the lion's mouth), Ps 35:26 and 41:12 (my enemy does not triumph over me).
- Compare Q 21:83-84 (Ayyub cried out and God removed his harm) and Q 38:41-44 (Ayyub told to strike with his foot: a spring to wash and drink).

**Purified, the redeemed man passes the named gates of Esagila: Gate of Life, Gate of Release from Guilt, Gate of Pure Water ...; kisses Zarpanitu's foot; sacrifices and feasts (Ludlul V 37-68)** (Ludlul SB V:37-68)
- Compare Ps 118:19-21 (open to me the gates of righteousness ... this is the gate of YHWH), Ps 100:4 and 24:7-10, Ps 116:12-19 and 66:13-15 (I will pay my vows, offer fatlings), Ps 22:26-27 and Lev 7:11-15 (thanksgiving offering eaten as a feast).
- Compare Ps 2:12 (kiss the son / kiss his feet) and Luke 7:38.
- Compare 2Kgs 20:5,8 (on the third day you shall go up to the house of YHWH) and Isa 38:20-22.

**The Babylonians see how Marduk revives: 'Who would have said he would see his sun?'; all who live, praise Marduk; blessing on the sufferer and the king (Ludlul V 69-120)** (Ludlul SB V:69-120)
- Compare Ps 150:6 (let everything that has breath praise YHWH), Ps 148, Ps 117, Ps 40:4 (many will see and fear), Ps 107:1-22 (let the redeemed say so), Job 42:11 (kin come to console after the restoration).
- Compare Job 33:6 (I too was pinched from clay) and Gen 2:7; Q 15:26 and 55:14 (man from clay).
- Compare Ps 1:3 and 92:13-15 (planted, flourishing), Ps 72 (prayer for the king), Ps 147:1 (it is good and pleasant to praise).

**Maqlû I 1-36: 'I call upon you, gods of the night' — lawsuit against the witch** (Maqlu SB I:1-36a)
- Compare Ps 51:9 (purge me with hyssop, wash me whiter than snow) for I:23-26.
- Compare Ps 88:9, Ps 31:12 and Job 19:13-19 (made loathsome to acquaintances) for I:6-7; Job 30:31 (my lyre turned to mourning) and Lam 5:15 for I:12.
- Compare Ps 7:7-10 and Ps 35:23-24 ('awake to my judgment ... judge me') for the lawsuit frame.
- Compare Q 113:3-4 (refuge from the evil of darkness when it settles and of the women who blow on knots).

**Maqlû I 37-41: 'Netherworld, netherworld' — Gilgameš enforcer of the oath** (Maqlu SB I:37-41a)
- Compare Ps 139:1-4 (God knows all I do) inverted: here the speaker claims superior knowledge over his enemies.

**Maqlû I 42-49: 'My city is Zabban' — two gates, water for the gods of heaven** (Maqlu SB I:42-49)
- Compare Ezek 43:1-4 and 44:1-2 (the east gate of the temple) and Mal 1:11 (from the rising of the sun to its setting) for the gate imagery.

**Maqlû I 50-60: 'I have enclosed the ford' — Anu and Antu send the speaker to Bēlet-ṣēri** (Maqlu SB I:50-60)
- Compare Isa 6:8 ('Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?') for I:53.
- Compare Ps 4:2 and Ps 27:7 ('when I call, answer me') against Prov 1:28 and Mic 3:4 (the wicked call and are not answered) for I:56-59.

**Maqlû I 61-72: 'I have been sent and I will go' — heaven, netherworld, river and land listen** (Maqlu SB I:61-72)
- Compare Deut 32:1 and Isa 1:2 ('Hear, O heavens, give ear, O earth') for I:63-64.
- Compare Isa 6:8-9 and Jer 1:7 ('to whomever I send you, you shall go; whatever I command you, you shall speak') for I:61.
- Compare Josh 10:12-13 (sun and moon stand still) for commanding cosmic elements to stand still during a speech.

**Maqlû I 73-121: 'O Nuska, these are the figurines of my sorcerer' — the indictment and Girra as judge** (Maqlu SB I:73-121)
- Compare Ps 35:11-16 and Ps 109:2-5 (false witnesses and accusers repay good with evil) for the catalogue of accusers.
- Compare Ps 19:13 and Ps 139:23-24 (hidden faults / search me) for the god knowing what the speaker does not.
- Compare Num 23:19 and Esth 8:8 (a decree that cannot be revoked) for I:120-121.

**Maqlû I 122-134: Nuska kindled with a reed torch — 'bewitch him with the witchcraft with which he bewitched me'** (Maqlu SB I:122-134a)
- Compare Ps 7:16-17 and Ps 57:7 (he falls into the pit he dug; his mischief returns on his own head) and Esth 7:10 for I:126-130.
- Compare 1Sam 24:5 (David cuts the hem of Saul's robe) and 1Sam 15:27 for the hem as a token of the person.

**Maqlû I 135-145: 'I raise the torch and burn their figurines' — demons melt, smoke rises; catchline** (Maqlu SB I:135-145)
- Compare Ps 68:3 (as smoke is driven away, as wax melts before fire, so the wicked perish) for I:140-141.
- Compare Isa 34:14 (lilit settles in the ruins) for lilītu, I:138.

**Maqlû II 1-18: 'O Grand Nuska, counselor of the great gods' (tallow figurine)** (Maqlu SB II:1-18)
- Compare Ps 30:10, Ps 88:11-13 and Isa 38:18-19 (the living, not the dead, praise God) for the vow of praise.
- Compare John 1:3 / Ps 127:1 ('unless YHWH builds the house') for the 'without you' praise form.

**Maqlû II 19-76: 'O Girra, perfect lord' — seizing the hem, crossed bronze figurines, the demon catalogue, sulphur** (Maqlu SB II:19-76)
- Compare Zech 8:23 (ten men seize the hem of a Jew's garment) and 1Sam 15:27 for seizing the hem.
- Compare Ps 91:5-6 (terror by night, pestilence in darkness) for II:67-69; Gen 19:24 (sulphur and fire) for II:71.
- Compare Ps 27:1 and Ps 36:10 ('in your light we see light') for Girra as light.

**Maqlû II 77-104: 'O blazing Girra, scion of Anu' — 'you alone are my god'** (Maqlu SB II:77-104)
- Compare Ps 16:2 ('you are my Lord'), Ps 18:3 and Ps 140:8 for II:101-103; Deut 32:35 and Ps 94:1 (God of vengeance) for 'my avenger'.
- Compare Ps 18:38-39 and Ps 20:9 ('they collapse and fall, but we rise and stand upright') for the antithetic series II:94-97.

**Maqlû II 105-126: 'O blazing Girra, warlike son of Anu' — burn them; robbers take their goods; the seven sages (dough figurine)** (Maqlu SB II:105-126)
- Compare Ps 109:11 ('let the creditor seize all he has, let strangers plunder his toil') for II:119-121.
- Compare Prov 9:1 (wisdom's seven pillars) and Isa 11:2 (seven spirits) loosely for the seven sages.

**Maqlû II 127-135: 'O powerful Girra, wild storm' — justice for the oppressed (clay figurine)** (Maqlu SB II:127-135)
- Compare Ps 103:6 and Ps 146:7 (God executes justice for the oppressed).

**Maqlû II 136-149: 'O splendid Girra' — as these figurines melt (bitumen figurine)** (Maqlu SB II:136-149)
- Compare Ps 68:3 and Mic 1:4 (mountains melt like wax before fire).

**Maqlû II 150-160: 'keš libiš kedeš' — the torch-bearer, rider of the wind (sesame-pomace figurine)** (Maqlu SB II:150-160b)
- Compare Ps 18:11 and Ps 104:3 (God rides on the wings of the wind) and Ugaritic rkb ʿrpt for 'rider of the wind'.
- Compare Isa 8:19 (mediums who chirp and mutter) and Isa 28:10 (ṣaw lāṣāw qaw lāqāw) for unintelligible ritual speech.

**Maqlû II 161-182: 'They perform sorcery against me ... to wrap me like a reed mat' — the similes turned back (bitumen-and-gypsum figurine)** (Maqlu SB II:161-182)
- Compare Ps 35:7-8 and Ps 57:7 (they hid a net for me; let the net they hid catch themselves) and Ps 141:10.
- Compare 1Kgs 14:10 (as one sweeps away dung) and Lam 3:45 (made us offscouring and refuse) for the sweepings.

**Maqlû II 183-204: 'Whoever you are, O witch, who took clay for me from the river' — the burning oven (clay-and-tallow figurine)** (Maqlu SB II:183-204)
- Compare Ps 20:8 (some trust in chariots, but we in the name of YHWH) and Jer 17:5-7 for II:200-201.
- Compare Ps 35:7 and Ps 109:3-4 (without cause they hid their net; in return for my love they accuse me) for II:198-199.
- Compare Ps 21:10 (you will make them as a fiery oven) and Mal 3:19 (the day burning like an oven) for the oven.

**Maqlû II 205-228: 'Whoever you are, O witch, who keeps seeking me' — 'I do not know your name'; the pure oven, daughter of Anu; catchline** (Maqlu SB II:205-228)
- Compare Dan 3:19-22 (the furnace heated seven times) and Gen 15:17 (smoking oven) for the divine oven.
- Compare Ps 9:6 and Deut 29:19 (God blots out their name) and Ps 12:4 (YHWH will cut off the boastful tongue) for II:215-216.

**Maqlû III 1-30: 'The witch, she who roams the streets' — her evil eye; fire above and below her city** (Maqlu SB III:1-30a)
- Compare Prov 7:10-12 (the strange woman, now in the street, now in the squares, lurking at every corner) for III:1-5.
- Compare Q 113:5 (the envier when he envies) and Prov 23:6 (the evil eye) for III:10-12.
- Compare Job 7:9-10 and Job 16:22 (the way of no return).

**Maqlû III 31-38: the Daughters of Anu descend from heaven by a rope** (Maqlu SB III:31-38a)
- Compare Gen 28:12 (messengers ascending and descending on a ladder) and Gen 18:2, 19:1 (heavenly envoys come down to investigate) for III:33-35.
- Compare the 'two, three' numerical pattern of Prov 30:15-31 and Amos 1:3.

**Maqlû III 39-60: 'Witch, murderess' — her titles and her surrender to Girra (wax figurine)** (Maqlu SB III:39-60a)
- Compare Gen 38:21 and Deut 23:18 (qedeshah) and Hos 4:14 for qadištu; Exod 22:17 (you shall not let a sorceress live).
- Compare Ezek 13:17-23 (women who sew bands and hunt souls) for female ritual specialists denounced.

**Maqlû III 61-76: 'Pure River and holy Sun am I'** (Maqlu SB III:61-76)
- Compare Q 3:106 (faces turned black on the day of judgment) for III:74; Ps 7:17 for III:72-73.
- Compare Mal 3:20 and Ps 84:12 (sun of righteousness, God as sun) for the speaker as Sun.

**Maqlû III 77-87: 'The Sutean surrounds me, the Elamite pursues me' (bitumen-and-sulphur figurine)** (Maqlu SB III:77-87a)
- Compare Ps 42:8 and Jonah 2:4 (all your breakers and waves have passed over me) and Ps 69:2-3 for III:78.

**Maqlû III 88-101: 'Whoever you are, O witch' — I have seized your mouth; the yellow seal** (Maqlu SB III:88-101a)
- Compare Prov 5:5 and 7:27 (her feet go down to death; her house is the way to Sheol) for III:91.

**Maqlû III 102-115: 'O you who have performed sorcery against me' — slag and soot on her head** (Maqlu SB III:102-115b)
- Compare Job 19:13-19 and Ps 88:9, 19 (friend and neighbour removed far from me) for III:113.
- Compare 2Sam 13:19 (ashes on the head) as a contrast.

**Maqlû III 116-124: 'She who has performed sorcery against me ... this be her boat'** (Maqlu SB III:116-124a)
- Compare Ps 7:16-17 for III:123.

**Maqlû III 125-135: Sîn's boat — the witches set adrift to the ocean** (Maqlu SB III:125-135a)
- Compare Zech 5:5-11 (Wickedness, a woman, shut in an ephah and carried off to Shinar) and Mic 7:19 (all their sins cast into the depths of the sea).
- Compare Lev 16:21-22 (the scapegoat carries the sins away to a remote land).

**Maqlû III 136-153: 'O sherd of the streets' — 'I myself am heaven, you cannot defile me'** (Maqlu SB III:136-153a)
- Compare Ps 91:7-10 (it shall not come near you) for III:153; Jer 9:20 (death has come up through our windows).

**Maqlû III 154-179: 'Hand, hand, strong hand of humankind' — rising like fish from water** (Maqlu SB III:154-179)
- Compare Ps 124:7 (our soul escaped like a bird from the fowler's snare) and Ps 140:6 for the trap images.
- Compare Ps 69:29, Exod 32:32 and Ezek 9:4 (the book of life; the mark on the forehead) for 'designs of life' — loose.

**Maqlû III 180-189: 'Hand, hand' — bring your hand that I may cast it into the fire; catchline** (Maqlu SB III:180-189)
- Compare Matt 5:30 (if your hand causes sin cut it off and throw it away) only loosely.

**Maqlû IV 1-79: 'Burn, burn, blaze, blaze!' — the great litany of the witch's deeds, 'may Girra release'** (Maqlu SB IV:1-79a)
- Compare Ps 27:10 ('my father and my mother have forsaken me') and Job 19:13-17 (wife and brothers estranged) for IV:68-72.
- Compare 2Kgs 23:5 and Jer 8:2 (worship of the moon, constellations and host of heaven) for IV:52-60; Isa 47:13 (star-gazers of Babylon).
- Compare Deut 18:10-11 and Isa 8:19 (inquiring of ghosts and the dead) and Isa 65:4 (sitting among tombs) for the necromantic acts.

**Maqlû IV 80-94: 'Whoever you are, O witch ... whether friend or companion' — Night, the veiled bride, breaks their weapon** (Maqlu SB IV:80-94a)
- Compare Ps 41:10 and Ps 55:13-15 (my close friend who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me) for IV:81.

**Maqlû IV 95-106: 'My murderess, my witch' — height of heaven, depth of netherworld (broken)** (Maqlu SB IV:95-106)
- Compare Ps 139:8 and Amos 9:2 (if they dig into Sheol ... if they climb to heaven) and Isa 7:11 (deep as Sheol or high as heaven).

**Maqlû IV 107-114: 'Of the Sun, who is his father?' — he is the judge** (Maqlu SB IV:107-114)
- Compare Ps 1:4 and Ps 35:5 (like chaff before the wind) for IV:114; Heb 7:3 (without father, without mother) as a contrasting riddle of genealogy.

**Maqlû IV 115-122: 'Six are their bindings, seven are my undoings'** (Maqlu SB IV:115-122)
- Compare Job 5:19 (in six troubles he will deliver you, in seven no evil shall touch you) and Prov 6:16.
- Compare Q 113:4 (those who blow on knots); Ezek 13:18-20 (bands sewn on wrists).

**Maqlû IV 123-153: 'My friend is a witch, but I am a releaser' — the seven and seven witches burned; catchline** (Maqlu SB IV:123-153)
- Compare Mic 7:5-6 (trust not a friend ... a man's enemies are the men of his own house) for IV:123.

**Maqlû V 1-10: 'My sorceress ... sits in the shade of a pile of bricks' — thyme and sesame** (Maqlu SB V:1-10)
- Compare Ps 7:16-17 and Prov 26:27 (whoever digs a pit falls into it).

**Maqlû V 11-18: 'Who has twined chaff together?' — the colocynth, daughter of the great gods** (Maqlu SB V:11-18a)
- Compare Job 8:11 (can papyrus grow without marsh?) and Jer 13:23 (can the Ethiopian change his skin?) for impossibility questions; Num 23:23 (no enchantment against Jacob).

**Maqlû V 19-47: 'Strong one, who decides our verdict' — the judge roars; plant-pun curses; the witch driven off like a dog** (Maqlu SB V:19-47)
- Compare Mic 5:1 and 1Kgs 22:24 (striking the cheek) for V:25; Jer 1:11-12 (šāqēd/šōqēd) and Amos 8:1-2 (qayiṣ/qēṣ) for plant-name puns.
- Compare Job 30:1-8 (driven out like a thief, lower than the dogs) for V:40-46.
