**Maqlû V 48-56: 'Whoever you are, O witch ... three months, ten days' — cord of the qadištu; blown away like chaff** (Maqlu SB V:48-56)
- Compare Ps 1:4 and Hos 13:3 (like chaff swirling from the threshing floor) for V:53.

**Maqlû V 57-75: 'Hate-magic that you performed against me I perform against you' — smoke an abomination to heaven** (Maqlu SB V:57-75)
- Compare Deut 18:10-12 (whoever practises sorcery is an abomination, tô'ēbâ, to YHWH) for V:74; Ps 109:17-18 (he loved cursing, let it come on him).
- Compare Obad 15 (as you have done, it shall be done to you) and Judg 1:7 (Adoni-bezek) for the talionic litany.

**Maqlû V 76-82: 'Whoever you are, O witch, who like the South wind has piled up' — scattered by the North wind** (Maqlu SB V:76-82)
- Compare Prov 25:23 (the north wind brings forth rain) and Job 37:21-22 (wind clears the skies; out of the north comes golden splendour).

**Maqlû V 89-97: 'The sinews you have bound up Ea has unbound' — pure before Nuska and Girra** (Maqlu SB V:89-97)
- Compare Q 113:4 for V:91; Ps 26:6 and Ps 73:13 (I wash my hands in innocence) for V:97.

**Maqlû V 98-111: 'You, Water, that flows over all the lands' — adjured by the seven sages** (Maqlu SB V:98-111)
- Compare Num 19:17-19 (living water sprinkled for purification) and Ezek 36:25 (I will sprinkle clean water upon you).

**Maqlû V 112-131: 'My sorcerers ... you shall not cross the Tigris and Euphrates to me'** (Maqlu SB V:112-131)
- Compare 2Sam 17:14 and Ps 33:10 (God frustrates the counsel of the nations) and Isa 19:3 (I will confound their counsel) for V:121-122.
- Compare Ps 91:10 (no evil shall befall you, no plague come near your tent) for V:129.

**Maqlû V 132-141: 'Raging, furious are you' — who but Ea can calm you; my mouth is water, your mouth is fire** (Maqlu SB V:132-141)
- Compare Prov 15:1 (a soft answer turns away wrath) and Jas 3:5-6 (the tongue is a fire).

**Maqlû V 142-148: 'I trample down my foe' and 'Melt, dissolve, drip away'** (Maqlu SB V:142-148)
- Compare Ps 18:38-43 (I crushed them, they fell under my feet) and Mal 3:21 (you shall tread down the wicked).

**Maqlû V 149-157: 'May the mountain cover you'** (Maqlu SB V:149-157)
- Compare Hos 10:8 and Luke 23:30 (say to the mountains, cover us; to the hills, fall on us) and Rev 6:16.

**Maqlû V 158-177: 'Be off, be off, begone, begone' — adjured by the life of the gods; catchline** (Maqlu SB V:158-177)
- Compare Mark 5:7-8 and Acts 19:13 (I adjure you by God / by Jesus) and Matt 4:10 ('Begone, Satan') for the exorcistic adjuration.
- Compare Ps 6:9 and Ps 119:115 ('Depart from me, all you evildoers').

**Maqlû VI 1-15: 'Enlil is my head, my face is Ūmu' — gods at the doorway** (Maqlu SB VI:1-15)
- Compare Eph 6:13-17 (the armour of God part by part) and Isa 59:17 (righteousness as breastplate, salvation as helmet) for VI:1-8.
- Compare Exod 12:23 (the destroyer not allowed to enter the door) and Ps 121:5-8 (YHWH your keeper at your right hand) for VI:13.

**Maqlû VI 16-23: 'My sorceress is a qumqummatu' — why do you carry my life to the princes?** (Maqlu SB VI:16-23)
- Compare Isa 57:3 (sons of a sorceress) for the witch's mother; Isa 57:9 (you sent your envoys far off and sent down to Sheol, possibly to the mlk).

**Maqlû VI 24-33: 'Kukru, kukru, inhabitants of the pure, holy mountains'** (Maqlu SB VI:24-33)
- Compare Ezek 13:10-15 (the whitewashed wall that falls) for VI:32.

**Maqlû VI 45-51: 'Before Ningirsu called out the alāla in the land' — scattering the hailstorm** (Maqlu SB VI:45-51)
- Compare Prov 8:24-26 ('before the mountains were settled') and Gen 2:5 for the 'before' opening.

**Maqlû VI 52-64: 'On the day that the witch bewitched me' — she took my shadow from the wall; the kukru twigs** (Maqlu SB VI:52-64)
- Compare 2Kgs 20:9-11 and Isa 38:8 (the shadow on the dial) only loosely; Acts 5:15 (Peter's shadow) for the shadow as part of the person.

**Maqlû VI 69-77: 'Pure Sulphur, daughter of the great heavens am I'** (Maqlu SB VI:69-77)
- Compare Gen 28:12 (a ladder set on earth whose top reached heaven) and Dan 4:8 (a tree reaching to heaven) for the cosmic body.

**Maqlû VI 85-97: 'Pure Sulphur and atāʾišu, the holy plant, am I' — rising like fish; 'Ha, you of the Baliḫ'** (Maqlu SB VI:85-97)
- VI:95-97 ('Ha, you of the Baliḫ ... hide in the ground, you who shook out your hair at me') is obscure; compare Isa 2:10, 19 (go into the rocks, hide in the dust).

**Maqlû VI 98-105: 'River is my head, Sulphur my physique'** (Maqlu SB VI:98-105)
- Lines 104-105 broken.

**Maqlû VI 118-125: 'You, Salt, who were created in a pure place'** (Maqlu SB VI:118-125)
- Compare Lev 2:13 (every grain offering salted; the salt of the covenant) and Ezek 43:24; 2Kgs 2:20-22 (Elisha heals the spring with salt).

**Maqlû VI 126-133: 'Ha, my witch, who has lit a fire at one league' — a watch on my roof, twine round my bed** (Maqlu SB VI:126-133)
- Compare Deut 6:9 (on the doorposts of your house) and Ps 127:1 (unless YHWH guards the city the watchman wakes in vain); Song 3:7-8 (sixty warriors around the bed against terror by night).

**Maqlû VI 134-141: 'Ha, my witch' — twelve wooden figures at the head of my bed** (Maqlu SB VI:134-141)
- Compare Song 3:7-8 (warriors around Solomon's bed because of terror by night).

**Maqlû VI 142-150: 'Ha, my witch, who roams over all lands' — Lugalirra and Meslamtaʾea at right and left of my gate** (Maqlu SB VI:142-150)
- Compare Job 1:7 and 2:2 (Satan roaming the earth, going to and fro) for VI:143-144; Ps 121:5 for the guardian at the right hand.

**Maqlû VII 1-21: 'My hand is the Rainbow, the Scorpion' — the ford and quay asleep, locks on the door** (Maqlu SB VII:1-21)
- Compare Gen 9:13-16 (the bow in the cloud) and Ezek 1:28 for the rainbow; Ps 121:4 (the keeper of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps) against the sleeping ford.
- Compare Neh 7:3 and Song 5:5 (bolts on the door) for VII:10.

**Maqlû VII 22-28: 'I am impregnating you, my self, my body' — as Šakkan his herd, the plough the earth** (Maqlu SB VII:22-28)
- Compare Isa 55:10-11 (as the rain makes the earth bring forth, so my word shall not return empty) for the analogy of seed and word.

**Maqlû VII 29-46: 'Pure oil, clear oil, bright oil' — anointing to soothe the sinews** (Maqlu SB VII:29-46)
- Compare Jas 5:14 and Mark 6:13 (anointing the sick with oil) and Isa 1:6 (wounds not softened with oil); Ps 133:2 (precious oil).

**Maqlû VII 47-54: 'Enlil is my head, Sirius my form' — as tin and iron, sorcery cannot approach** (Maqlu SB VII:47-54)
- Compare Jer 1:18 (an iron pillar and bronze walls against the land) and Ezek 3:8-9 (forehead hard as diamond).

**Maqlû VII 55-79: 'Whoever you are, O witch, who has made a figurine of me' — I draw your likeness before Šamaš; the substitute bears my sin** (Maqlu SB VII:55-79a)
- Compare Lev 16:21-22 (the goat bears their iniquities) and Isa 53:4-6, 12 (he bore the sin of many) for the substitute bearing sin.
- Compare Deut 32:35, 41 (I will render vengeance to my adversaries) for gimillu returned.

**Maqlû VII 80-100: 'Huntress of huntresses, witch of witches, whose net is cast in the streets'** (Maqlu SB VII:80-100)
- Compare Ezek 13:18-21 (women who hunt souls with bands; I will tear them from your arms) and Prov 6:26 (the adulteress hunts for the precious life); Prov 7:12.

**Maqlû VII 101-113: 'Your sorcery ... Ea undoes'; 'Your tightly knotted knots' — may your mouth be full of earth** (Maqlu SB VII:101-113)
- Compare Q 113:4 (blowers on knots); Ps 63:12 (the mouth of liars shall be stopped), Ps 72:9 and Mic 7:17 (lick the dust).

**Maqlû VII 114-140: 'I wash my hands, I cleanse my body in pure Eridu spring water' — bad dreams, entrails and curses onto the substitute** (Maqlu SB VII:114-140h)
- Compare Ps 26:6 and Ps 73:13 (I wash my hands in innocence), Deut 21:6-8 (elders wash hands over the heifer), Matt 27:24.
- Compare Lev 16:21-22 and Lev 14:4-7 (the living bird released carries off impurity) for the substitute.

**Maqlû VII 141-144: 'Rise up, morning, wash my hands; open up, earth, receive my sin'** (Maqlu SB VII:141-144)
- Compare Gen 4:11 (the earth opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood) and Num 16:32; Ps 51:4 (wash me from my iniquity).

**Maqlû VII 145-152: 'Dawn has broken, doors are opened' — cleansed by the rising sun** (Maqlu SB VII:145-152)
- Compare Ps 30:6 (weeping lodges at evening, joy comes in the morning), Ps 46:6 (God helps her at break of dawn) and Mal 3:20 (sun of righteousness with healing in its wings).

**Maqlû VII 162-169: 'At dawn my hands are washed' — may the dream I dreamt be made favourable** (Maqlu SB VII:162-169)
- Compare Gen 41:25-32 and Dan 2 (dream interpreted) and the later rabbinic prayer for a dream to be turned to good (b. Ber. 55b) on Deut 23:6 (God turned the curse into a blessing).

**Maqlû VIII 1-16: 'Until you rose, I was awaiting you, my lord, Šamaš' — her witchcraft downstream, I upstream** (Maqlu SB VIII:1-16)
- Compare Ps 130:6 (my soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen for the morning) and Ps 5:4 (in the morning I prepare and watch).

**Maqlû VIII 17-27: 'Šamaš has risen' — the plant of release sent to Šamaš's daughter; unknot the hand that bound** (Maqlu SB VIII:17-27)
- Compare Q 113:4 (the women blowing on knots) and Isa 58:6 (to loose the bonds of wickedness).

**Maqlû VIII 28-45: 'When the witch crossed the river' — Ea darkens her face; hands washed over her figurines** (Maqlu SB VIII:28-45a)
- Compare Num 5:11-31 (the ordeal of bitter water) and Exod 15:16 (terror and dread fall on them) for VIII:36-38.

**Maqlû VIII A+26-A+37: 'The mouth spoke evil' — may your witchcraft fill the sewer** (Maqlu SB VIII:A+26-A+37)
- Compare Ps 10:7 (his mouth is full of cursing, deceit and oppression) and Rom 3:14.

**Maqlû VIII A+38-B+8: 'The sorceress who sets witchcraft in motion' — may Ereškigal refuse her, dog and bitch tear her flesh** (Maqlu SB VIII:A+38-B+8)
- Compare 1Kgs 21:23 and 2Kgs 9:10, 33-37 (dogs eat Jezebel, whose sorceries are many, 2Kgs 9:22) and Deut 28:26, Jer 16:4 (corpses food for birds).

**Maqlû VIII B+9-B+22: 'You are my reflection, you are my vigour' — 'you are mine and I am yours'; colophon** (Maqlu SB VIII:B+9-B+22)
- Compare Song 2:16 and 6:3 ('my beloved is mine and I am his') and Isa 43:1 ('you are mine') for B+18; Ps 121:5 (YHWH your shade, ṣēl) for ṣillu as protective double.

**Maqlû Ritual Tablet 1-31': the night rite begins — mouth-washing, the tallow figurine on the torch, prostration, Nuska on the roof** (Maqlu SB RT:1-31')
- Compare Jer 19:13 and 32:29 (offerings on rooftops) and Zeph 1:5 for the rooftop altar; Isa 6:5-7 (lips purified) for mouth-washing.

**Maqlû Ritual Tablet 60'-95': the reed cross, knots in wool, burning herbs, quenching the fire and throwing it out the gate** (Maqlu SB RT:60'-95')
- Compare Lev 16:27 (the remains burned outside the camp) and Lev 14:40-45 (unclean material cast outside the city).

**Maqlû Ritual Tablet 96'-137': fumigation, salt and asafoetida at the bed's head, twine round the bed, doorposts smeared, the body anointed** (Maqlu SB RT:96'-137'b)
- Compare Exod 12:7, 22-23 (blood on the lintel and doorposts at night against the destroyer) for RT:127'-129'.

**Maqlû Ritual Tablet 138'-180': the morning rites — handwashing over the witch's likeness, bread-figurines for dogs, the face in the water** (Maqlu SB RT:138'-180')
- Compare Num 5:17-23 (the curse dissolved in water in an earthen vessel) and 1Kgs 21:23 (dogs eat Jezebel) for the dog rite.

**Marduk's Address to the Demons 1-9: 'Begone, Evil' — the demon list** (MardDemons SB –:1-9)
- Compare Isa 34:14 (lilit) and Isa 14:12 (fallen from heaven, Day Star) for 'that which falls from heaven, the flash of a star'.

**Marduk's Address to the Demons 10-55: 'I am Asalluḫi' (first half of the litany)** (MardDemons SB –:10-55)
- Compare Deut 32:39 and 1Sam 2:6 (I kill and I make alive) for –:13, 20, 22; Ps 145:14 (YHWH upholds all who fall) for –:35.
- Compare Isa 44:24-28 and Exod 3:14 for divine 'I am' self-predication; John 8-15 'I am' sayings.

**Marduk's Address to the Demons 56-107: 'I am Asalluḫi' (second half) — physician of mankind, releaser of guilt** (MardDemons SB –:56-107)
- Compare Exod 15:26 ('I am YHWH your healer'), Ps 103:3 (who forgives all your iniquities, heals all your diseases) and Mic 7:18-19 for –:94-103.
- Compare Isa 49:15 and 66:13 (as a mother comforts) and Ps 27:10 for the god as father and mother; Ps 113:7 (raises the poor from the dust).

**Marduk's Address to the Demons 108-A+123: Marduk sees the demons and speaks to Nabû (fragmentary)** (MardDemons SB –:108-A+123)
- Compare Hos 13:3 (like the morning mist) for –:118.

**Marduk's Address to the Demons 1'-63': 'Or you who ...' — the demons at the invalid's bedside** (MardDemons SB –:1'-63')
- Compare Ps 91:5-6 (terror by night, destruction that wastes at noonday) for –:7' and 23'; Ps 22:13-17 (bulls, lions, dogs encircle the sufferer) for the animal behaviours at the sickbed.
- Compare Jer 9:20 (death has come up into our windows) for –:17'-19'.

**Marduk's Address to the Demons 64'-99': demons of streets, river and forest; the restless dead with no kin** (MardDemons SB –:64'-99')
- Compare Isa 14:19 (the slain pierced by the sword, cast out of the grave) and 2Sam 18:18 (Absalom: I have no son to keep my name).

**Marduk's Address to the Demons 100'-128': 'May Asalluḫi extirpate you' — handed to the gatekeepers of the netherworld; exorcised by heaven and earth** (MardDemons SB –:100'-128')
- Compare Mark 5:7-13 and Luke 8:31 (the demons beg not to be sent into the abyss) and Rev 20:1-3 (the dragon bound and shut in the abyss) for the demons consigned to the netherworld.
- Compare Matt 12:43-45 (the unclean spirit wanders waterless places and returns) for –:120'.

**Syncretistic Hymn to Marduk 1-17: 'He of insightful thinking' — heaven his tiara, the netherworld his sandals** (MardSyncr SB –:1-17)
- Compare Isa 66:1 (heaven my throne, earth my footstool) and Isa 40:15, 22 (nations like a drop, inhabitants like grasshoppers) for –:9, 14-15; Zech 4:10 and 2Chr 16:9 (the eyes of YHWH range through the whole earth).

**Syncretistic Hymn to Marduk 18-60: 'Your name is Anšar ... Dagan ... Adad ... Šamaš ... your name is indeed Marduk'** (MardSyncr SB –:18-60)
- Compare Ps 29:3-9 (the voice of YHWH over the waters, shaking the wilderness) for –:30-32; Ps 104:3 and Ps 68:5 (rider of the clouds) for –:41.
- Compare John 1:3 (without him was not anything made) for –:26; Isa 45:5-7 (I form light and create darkness) and Deut 6:4 for the absorption of other gods into one.

**Syncretistic Hymn to Marduk 61-88: 'You have become great, O lord' — fifty auras, fire his breath; 'Extol the Lord!'** (MardSyncr SB –:61-88)
- Compare Ps 18:9 (smoke from his nostrils, devouring fire from his mouth); Deut 10:17 (God of gods and Lord of lords) and Ps 136:2-3 for 'Lord of Lords'; Neh 9:6 ('you alone are YHWH').

**Great Prayer to Nabû 9-44: 'O Lord ... O Nabû' — anger a dragon, yet heaper of plenty; calm yourself, have pity** (NabuPr SB –:9-44)
- Compare Ps 136 and Ps 118:1-4 (repeated refrain) for the doubled couplets; Ps 6:2 and Ps 38:2 (do not rebuke me in your anger) and Hab 3:2 (in wrath remember mercy) for –:37-40.

**Great Prayer to Nabû 45-90: 'You are angry with your servant' — cast into the billow and the morass; 'you called my name'** (NabuPr SB –:45-90)
- Compare Ps 69:2-3, 15-16 (I sink in deep mire, the flood sweeps over me; do not let me sink) and Ps 40:3 (he drew me up from the miry bog) for –:49-56.
- Compare Ps 22:10-11 and 71:6 (you took me from the womb), Isa 49:1 and Jer 1:5 (called from the womb) for –:81-84.

**Great Prayer to Nabû 91-116: 'O Forgiver ... without you no forgiveness' — the god cast his servant out; 'How long?'** (NabuPr SB –:91-116)
- Compare Ps 130:3-4 (if you kept a record of iniquities, who could stand? but with you is forgiveness) and Mark 2:7 (who can forgive sins but God alone?) for –:99-102.
- Compare Job 2:7-8, 7:5 (worms and scabs), Job 19:21 (the hand of God has struck me) and Ps 6:4, 13:2 ('How long?').

**Great Prayer to Nabû 117-165: 'Let me praise your fury and anger' — former wealth, the dream spirit, the servants' pity (fragmentary)** (NabuPr SB –:117-165)
- Compare Ludlul bēl nēmeqi I 1 (ludlul bēl nēmeqi) and Job 33:14-18 (God speaks in a dream to turn a man from the pit); 2Sam 24:16 ('It is enough').

**Great Prayer to Nabû 173-225: 'Loose his fetters' — bitter dates turn sweet; leave him a vent to breathe; restore his fields** (NabuPr SB –:173-225)
- Compare Prov 3:11-12 and Heb 12:5-11 (the Lord disciplines the son he loves) for –:185-190; Ps 30:12 and Job 42:10-12 (fortunes restored) for –:200-211.
- Compare John 16:20-21 and Ps 126:5-6 (sorrow turned to joy, sowing in tears) for the bitter-then-sweet sayings.

**Cuthaean Legend (MB) A b+1-29: Enmerkar left no stela; the six kings and their host created by Ea** (NaramSin MB A:b+1-b+29)
- Compare Isa 2:19-21 and Rev 6:15-16 (people enter caves of the rocks before the terror) and Judg 6:2 for A:b+4.
- Compare Ezek 38-39 (Gog's horde brought by God from the north) and Joel 2:1-11 (the divine army).

**Cuthaean Legend (MB) A c+1-d+9: the host reaches the gate of Akkad and sends a message to Narām-Sîn (fragmentary)** (NaramSin MB A:c+1-d+9)
- Compare 2Kgs 18:17-35 (the Rabshakeh's message at the walls of Jerusalem).

**Cuthaean Legend (MB) B: kings brought into a cave (fragment)** (NaramSin MB B:a+1-b+1)
- Compare Josh 10:16-27 (five kings shut in the cave at Makkedah and brought out).

**Cuthaean Legend (OB) I a+1-b+22: three armies annihilated — 'What has god brought upon my reign?'** (NaramSin OB I:a+1-b+22)
- Compare 2Kgs 6:26-33 (the king of Israel: 'this evil is from YHWH, why should I wait?') and 1Kgs 22:17 (sheep without a shepherd) for b+11-14; Judg 7:2-7 for successive army numbers.

**Cuthaean Legend (OB) I c+1-d+17: Akkad levelled as by the deluge of former times** (NaramSin OB I:c+1-d+17)
- Compare Isa 24:1-13 and Jer 4:23-26 (the land laid waste, as before creation) and Gen 6-8 for the flood comparison.

**Prologue: Narām-Sîn's hardships, Enmerkar's precedent (Cuthaean Legend)** (NaramSin SB –:1-30)
- Compare the 'book of the generations' and memorial writing: Exod 17:14 (write this in a book as a memorial); Job 19:23-24 (that my words were engraved on rock).
- Compare the doom of a sinner's descendants, Exod 20:5 (to the third and fourth generation).

**The gods create the raven-faced host, which sweeps the world (Cuthaean Legend)** (NaramSin SB –:31-62)
- Compare the northern foe of Jer 1:14-15; 4:6; 6:22-23 and Gog of Ezek 38-39, and Gog and Magog spreading over the earth in Q 18:94; 21:96.
- Compare the coalition of kings in Gen 14:1-9 and Josh 10-11.

**Blood test, refused oracle, Narām-Sîn's defiance and three lost armies (Cuthaean Legend)** (NaramSin SB –:63-103)
- Compare Saul inquiring and receiving no answer, 1 Sam 28:6, and then acting on his own; and the hubris of the king who says 'by the strength of my hand I have done it', Isa 10:13-15.
- Compare the shepherd who does not care for the flock, Ezek 34:2-10; Num 27:17.
- Ea's reminder that the gods decided humankind should endure: compare the post-flood promise, Gen 8:21-22; 9:11.
- Compare 'a king is not saved by a great army', Ps 33:16-17.

**New Year rites, favourable omen, Ištar's oracle: spare the enemy (Cuthaean Legend)** (NaramSin SB –:104-148)
- Compare 'vengeance is mine', Deut 32:35; and the nations as instrument later punished, Isa 10:5-12.
- Compare Mic 7:5-6 (enemies of one's own household), Isa 19:2 (Egyptian against Egyptian, city against city), and Mark 13:12.
- Compare siege famine prices, 2 Kgs 6:25; 7:1; Rev 6:6.

**Narām-Sîn's counsel to a future ruler; the stela in Nergal's cella at Cutha (Cuthaean Legend)** (NaramSin SB –:149-180)
- Compare Prov 25:21-22 (feed your enemy), Rom 12:20-21, Matt 5:39-44; Q 41:34 and 23:96 (repel evil with what is better).
- Compare Josh 1:6-9 ('be strong and courageous, do not fear or be dismayed'), and Hezekiah's siege preparations, 2 Chr 32:3-5 and Isa 22:9-11.
- Compare Jer 27:11-12 and 38:17 (submit to the king of Babylon and live).
- Compare Deut 17:18-19 (the king reads the written law all his life).

**The gods' banquet, Namtar's visit and Nergal's slight (Nergal and Ereškigal, Amarna version)** (NergEresh MB –:1-17, NergEresh MB –:a+1-a+29)
- Compare the slight to a messenger and its punishment, 2 Sam 10:1-5.

**Nergal storms the fourteen gates, seizes Ereškigal and is offered marriage (Nergal and Ereškigal, Amarna version)** (NergEresh MB –:a+30-a+44, NergEresh MB –:b+1-b+26)
- Compare the underworld queen's 'house' and its gates in Prov 7:27; 9:18; and Death's covenant, Isa 28:15.
- Compare Isa 25:8 (wipes away tears) only as an image.

**Anu sends Kakka down to Ereškigal; Namtar sent up for her portion (Nergal and Ereškigal, SB)** (NergEresh SB –:a+1-a+51)
- Compare the ladder (sullam) between heaven and earth with messengers going up and down, Gen 28:12; and Q 70:3-4 (ma'arij).

**Nergal does not kneel to Namtar; Ea has him build a chair and warns him (Nergal and Ereškigal, SB)** (NergEresh SB –:b+1-b+50)
- Compare 1 Kgs 13:8-9, 16-22 (the man of God forbidden to eat bread or drink water there), and the Persephone / pomegranate motif; also Gen 3:3 (eating as the binding act).
- Compare the warnings against the strange woman whose house leads down to Sheol, Prov 5:3-8; 7:10-27; 9:13-18.

**Nergal goes down, passes the seven gates and refuses all she offers (Nergal and Ereškigal, SB)** (NergEresh SB –:c+1-c+65)
- Compare Job 10:21-22 (land of darkness from which one does not return); Isa 14:9-11 (worms your covering in Sheol).

**Six days of love, Nergal's flight, Ereškigal's lament and threat, the search in heaven (Nergal and Ereškigal, SB)** (NergEresh SB –:d+1-d+115)
- Compare the lover who has slipped away and is sought, Song 3:1-4; 5:6.
- The dead rising to outnumber the living: compare Isa 26:19 and Ezek 37 only as contrast.

**Nergal storms back down, seizes Ereškigal; Anu grants him to dwell with her forever (Nergal and Ereškigal, SB)** (NergEresh SB –:e+1-e+51, NergEresh SB –:f+1)
- Compare Death as king and consort of the underworld in Job 18:13-14 ('king of terrors').

**Ninurta's body as the pantheon (Macranthropic Hymn to Ninurta)** (NinurtaMacr SB –:1-33)
- Compare the tendency to one God bearing all divine names: Deut 6:4; Isa 44:6; Q 7:180; 59:22-24 (the most beautiful names).
- Compare the cosmic body imagery of the divine glory, Ezek 1:26-28, and Ps 104:1-4 (clothed with light).

**Ninurta's weapons and bow (Macranthropic Hymn to Ninurta)** (NinurtaMacr SB –:34-68)
- Compare God's bow and arrows, Hab 3:9-11; Ps 7:13-14; Lam 2:4; 3:12-13; and the bow in the cloud, Gen 9:13.
- Compare mountains melting like wax, Ps 97:5; Mic 1:4; and reed shaken by wind, 1 Kgs 14:15.
- Compare 'I will not pity nor spare', Ezek 5:11; 7:4; Lam 3:44 (a cloud so that no prayer passes).

**Ninurta who reverses fortunes and rescues the helpless (Hymn to Ninurta as Savior)** (NinurtaSavior SB –:1-55)
- Compare Eccl 9:11 (race not to the swift) and 1 Sam 2:4-8 (bows of the mighty broken, the feeble girded with strength).
- Compare Ps 124:7 (bird escaped from the fowler's snare); Ps 107:23-30 (storm-tossed sailors brought to their haven); Ps 107:35 and Isa 43:19-20 (rivers in the desert).
- Compare John 15:5 / Ps 127:1 ('apart from me you can do nothing'); Isa 1:9 (a small remnant).
- Compare Eccl 9:15-16 and 10:5-7 (the poor wise man forgotten, folly set on high).

**Prologue: the spring flood brings pasture; Ox's opening speech (Ox and Horse)** (OxHorse SB –:1-A+38)
- Compare Ps 65:10-14 and 104:10-14 (springs in the valleys, grass for cattle); Job 39:19-25 (the war-horse) and Prov 14:4 (where there are no oxen the crib is clean).

**The exchanges of Ox and Horse: war, chariot, labour, the king's stable (Ox and Horse)** (OxHorse SB –:D+1-G+6)
- Compare the horse not to be multiplied by the king, Deut 17:16; 'some trust in chariots and some in horses', Ps 20:8; Q 16:8 (horses, mules and donkeys to ride and as adornment).
- Compare the ox that treads the grain unmuzzled, Deut 25:4.

**Palm's boast and Vine's reply (Palm and Vine)** (PalmVine SB –:1'-54')
- Compare Jotham's fable of the trees choosing a king, Judg 9:8-15 (olive, fig, vine: 'my wine that cheers God and men').
- Compare Ps 104:15 (wine gladdens the heart), Prov 31:6-7 (give wine to the bitter of soul), and the palm in Ps 92:13.

**Gimil-Ninurta's poverty, his goat and the mayor's insult (Poor Man of Nippur)** (PoorMan SB –:1-69)
- Compare Nabal's insult of David's men, 1 Sam 25:10-11, and the rich man's feast in Nathan's parable, 2 Sam 12:1-4.
- Compare the law that a poor man's garment taken in pledge be returned before night, Exod 22:25-26; Deut 24:12-13.

**The borrowed chariot, the box of birds and the first revenge (Poor Man of Nippur)** (PoorMan SB –:70-114)
- Compare the clever-trickster tales of Jacob and Laban (Gen 30-31) and Ehud alone with Eglon (Judg 3:15-26); and Mordecai paraded in royal honour, Esth 6:7-11.

**The false physician and the decoy: second and third revenge (Poor Man of Nippur)** (PoorMan SB –:115-160)
- Compare the reversal of the proud and lifting of the poor, 1 Sam 2:7-8; Ps 113:7; Luke 1:52; and Haman's fall, Esth 7.

**Poplar and Ash dispute (Series of the Poplar)** (Poplar SB –:a+1-d+25)
- Compare Prov 10:13; 26:3 (a rod for the back of fools) and 13:24; 22:15.
- Compare Jotham's fable, Judg 9:8-15, and the trees of Ezek 31:3-9.

**Exhortation to worship the Queen of Nippur alone (Hymn to the Queen of Nippur)** (QueenNippur SB –:1-A+13)
- Compare the first commandment, Exod 20:3; 34:14; Deut 6:13-15; and Q 112:1-4; 17:22; 'take my yoke upon you', Matt 11:29 and Jer 2:20 (broke the yoke).
- Compare 'meditate on it day and night', Josh 1:8; Ps 1:2.

**The man who did not bow to Ištar is struck down (Hymn to the Queen of Nippur)** (QueenNippur SB –:B+1-B+34)
- Compare the sufferer forsaken by friends and kin, Job 19:13-20 and Ps 38:12; 88:9; and Nebuchadnezzar's hair and nails, Dan 4:30.
- Compare Lilith in Isa 34:14 and death that climbs through windows, Jer 9:20.

**Litany: no one but she can (Hymn to the Queen of Nippur)** (QueenNippur SB –:C+1-C+35)
- Compare 1 Sam 2:6 and Deut 32:39 ('I kill and I make alive'); Q 2:258 and 3:26-27 (giver of kingship, bringer of the living from the dead).
- Compare Exod 34:6-7 (merciful, slow to anger) and Ps 30:6 (his anger is but a moment).

**Ištar's sovereignty and her great names (Hymn to the Queen of Nippur)** (QueenNippur SB –:C+36-C+92)
- Compare the Queen of Heaven in Jer 7:18; 44:17-19, 25.
- Compare 'who is like you among the gods', Exod 15:11; and the bestowal of names, Phil 2:9.

**Nippur, the Ebaradurgara and the goddess presiding over the gods (Hymn to the Queen of Nippur)** (QueenNippur SB –:D+1-D+55)
- Compare Zion as God's chosen dwelling and the joy of all the earth, Ps 48:2-3; 132:13-14; the nations streaming to it, Isa 2:2-3; and Ps 104:34 ('may my meditation be pleasing to him').

**Feast with the great gods and blessings on the cities (Hymn to the Queen of Nippur)** (QueenNippur SB –:E+1-E+38)
- Compare the meal before God on the mountain, Exod 24:11, and the feast for all peoples on Zion, Isa 25:6.

**Incantation: the curse, the inviolable drawing of the gods (Saĝba, bilingual)** (Sagba SB I:1-25)
- Compare the curse that enters the house and consumes it, Zech 5:3-4; Num 5:21-27 (oath-curse); and Lilith, Isa 34:14.
- Compare 'I YHWH do not change', Mal 3:6; Num 23:19.

**Šamaš illuminator of heaven and earth, shepherd above and below (Great Hymn to Šamaš)** (ShamashHymn SB –:1-56)
- Compare Ps 19:2-7 (the sun's circuit; nothing hidden from its heat), Ps 139:7-12 (darkness is not dark to you), Ps 104:19-22.
- Compare 'the eyes of YHWH run to and fro through all the earth', 2 Chr 16:9; Prov 15:3; and Q 6:59; 34:3 (not an atom's weight hidden).
- Compare Ps 121:4 (neither slumbers nor sleeps) and Isa 40:28 (does not faint or grow weary).

**Šamaš the judge and rescuer of travellers, captives, the sick and the dead (Great Hymn to Šamaš)** (ShamashHymn SB –:57-82)
- Compare Ps 107:4-30 (wanderers, prisoners in darkness, the sick, sailors rescued), Ps 146:7-9, Isa 42:7; 61:1.
- Compare Deut 1:17; 10:17 (God shows no partiality, nāśāʾ pānîm, 'lift the face'), the same idiom as pāna ul tubbal.
- Compare 1 Sam 2:6 and Ps 30:4 ('you brought up my soul from Sheol').

**Šamaš's net for the wicked: adulterer, corrupt judge, usurer, false weigher (Great Hymn to Šamaš)** (ShamashHymn SB –:83-129)
- Compare Deut 25:13-16 and Prov 11:1; 20:10 (diverse weights an abomination; just weights for long life); Amos 8:5; Mic 6:10-11; Q 83:1-3; 55:9; 17:35.
- Compare Exod 22:24; Lev 25:36-37; Ps 15:5 (does not lend at interest nor take a bribe); Prov 28:8; Q 2:275-279; 30:39.
- Compare Exod 20:17 and Prov 6:26-35 (the adulterer's ruin); Exod 23:8; Deut 16:19 (bribe blinds).
- Compare Ps 37:28 and 21:11 (the seed of the wicked cut off); Ps 1:3 and Jer 17:8 (tree by streams).

**All who pray turn to Šamaš; his feast on the twentieth (Great Hymn to Šamaš)** (ShamashHymn SB –:130-166)
- Compare Ps 65:3 ('to you all flesh shall come'), Ps 145:15-19, and 1 Kgs 8:27 / 2 Chr 6:18 (heaven cannot contain you).
- Compare Ps 107:23-30 (rescue of sailors) and Jonah 1:5-6, 14-16 (sailors each crying to his god).

**Closing praise: all creatures led before Šamaš; blessings from the gods and Aya (Great Hymn to Šamaš)** (ShamashHymn SB –:167-200)
- Compare Ps 147:16-18 (snow like wool, frost, ice) and Job 38:22-30; Ps 24:7-9 (lift up your heads, O gates); Ps 72:10-11 (kings bring tribute).

**Lifted-hand prayer to Adad, with Sargon's insertion against an eclipse (šuʾila Adad 1a)** (Shuila Adad SB 1a:1-30)
- Compare Ps 29 (the voice of YHWH over the waters, breaking cedars, making the wilderness writhe, ḥûl) and Ps 65:10-14; Ps 18:8-16.
- Compare 'do not be dismayed at the signs of the heavens', Jer 10:2.

**Lifted-hand prayer to Adad against enemies and witchcraft, with thunder ritual (šuʾila Adad 1b)** (Shuila Adad SB 1b:1-17, Shuila Adad SB 1b:1'-25')
- Compare Ps 6:2-5 and 38:2 (rebuke me not in your anger); Ps 54:3-7 (destroy my enemies).

**Lifted-hand prayer to Adad: mountains rejoice at his sound (šuʾila Adad 2)** (Shuila Adad SB 2:1-17)
- Compare Ps 65:13-14 and 96:11-12; 98:8 (the mountains sing for joy, the fields exult).

**Lifted-hand prayers to Adad after lightning strikes a temple (šuʾila Adad 3 incipit and 4)** (Shuila Adad SB 3:1, Shuila Adad SB 4:1-43)
- Compare fire of God falling from heaven, Job 1:16; 2 Kgs 1:10-12; and Amos 4:7-11; Exod 9:23-24.

**Lifted-hand prayer to Anu, releaser of evil dreams (šuʾila Anu 1)** (Shuila Anu SB 1:1-20)
- Compare Ps 116:12-19 and 66:13-15 (vows paid in the house of God); Dan 2:28 (God who reveals mysteries of dreams).

**Lifted-hand prayer to Bēlet-ilī, with Šamaš-šuma-ukīn's eclipse insertion (šuʾila Bēlet-ilī 1)** (Shuila Bēlet-ilī SB 1:1-27)
- Compare grasping the hem (kānāp) of a Jew's garment, Zech 8:23, and the woman touching the hem, Mark 5:27-28; Saul tearing Samuel's hem, 1 Sam 15:27.

**Lifted-hand prayer to Bēlet-ilī, creator of the womb (šuʾila Bēlet-ilī 2)** (Shuila Bēlet-ilī SB 2:1-22)
- Compare God who opens and closes the womb, Gen 29:31; 30:22; 1 Sam 1:5-6; Ps 139:13.

**Lifted-hand prayer to Damkina, with Ashurbanipal's insertion (šuʾila Damkina 1)** (Shuila Damkina SB 1:1-25)
- Compare Ps 51:15 ('then I will teach transgressors your ways') and Ps 32:4 (your hand was heavy upon me).

**Lifted-hand prayer to Dilbat (Venus): how long, my lady? (šuʾila Dilbat)** (Shuila Dilbat SB 1:1'-22')
- Compare Ps 13:2-3 ('how long will you hide your face from me?') and Ps 89:47; Job 7:20-21 ('what have I done?').

**Lifted-hand prayer to Ea, with Banītu-tēreš's insertion against portents and witchcraft (šuʾila Ea 1a)** (Shuila Ea SB 1a:1-32, Shuila Ea SB 1a:11'-16')
- Compare Ps 3:4 ('the lifter of my head'), Ps 65:10 (the river of God full of water, providing grain).

**Lifted-hand prayers to Ea, creator of everything (šuʾila Ea 1b and 2)** (Shuila Ea SB 1b:1'-8', Shuila Ea SB 2:1-17)
- Compare Ps 104:24 and Prov 3:19-20 (by wisdom he founded the earth); Q 6:101-102 (creator of all things).

**Lifted-hand prayer to Enlil, lord of lords and king of kings, against an eclipse (šuʾila Enlil 1a)** (Shuila Enlil SB 1a:1-29, Shuila Enlil SB 1a:26'-27')
- Compare Deut 10:17 (God of gods and Lord of lords), Dan 2:21, 37 (he sets up kings), 1 Sam 2:7-8, Ps 75:8; Q 3:26.
- Compare Ps 25:2-3; 35:26 (let those who rejoice at my hurt be put to shame).

**Lifted-hand prayers to Enlil: personal gods at right and left (šuʾila Enlil 1b and 2)** (Shuila Enlil SB 1b:1-39, Shuila Enlil SB 1b:x+1-x+2, Shuila Enlil SB 2:1-6)
- Compare Ps 16:8; 121:5 (YHWH at my right hand, your shade at your right hand) and Ps 104:33 (I will sing to YHWH as long as I live).

**Lifted-hand prayer to Gula, merciful mother and intercessor (šuʾila Gula 1a)** (Shuila Gula SB 1a:1-28)
- Compare the intercessor who 'stands in the breach', Ezek 22:30; Ps 106:23; and Job 33:23-24 (an angel mediator).

**Lifted-hand prayers to Gula and Baba against illness, eclipse and frightening dreams (šuʾila Gula 1b and 2)** (Shuila Gula SB 1b:1-32, Shuila Gula SB 1b:10'-17', Shuila Gula SB 2:1'-6')
- Compare Ps 43:1 ('judge me, O God, and plead my cause'); Ps 56:14 and Job 33:28-30 (to see the light of life).

**Šuʾila to Ištar 1: 'O valiant Ištar, cherished among the goddesses'** (Shuila Ištar SB 1)
- With 'how near is your hearing' compare Deut 4:7 and Ps 145:18; Q 2:186 ('I am near, I answer the call of the caller').
- Justice at the right hand, favour at the left, guardian going before: compare Ps 89:15 and Ps 85:14 (righteousness goes before him).
- Reversal of fates compare 1Sam 2:7-8 and Ps 113:7-9; 'Who is your equal among the gods' compare Exod 15:11.

**Šuʾila to Ištar 2: 'I beseech you, lady of ladies' (the great prayer to Ištar)** (Shuila Ištar SB 2)
- 'How long?' and turned face: compare Ps 13:2-3 and Ps 6:4; moaning like a dove Isa 38:14, Isa 59:11; heart flying like a bird Ps 55:7.
- 'What have I done?': compare Job 7:20, Job 10:2, Mic 6:3 (inverted); the extinguished brazier/torch compare 2Sam 14:7 and 2Sam 21:17, Prov 13:9.
- Rooftop offerings to the heavenly goddess: Jer 19:13, Jer 44:17-19, Zeph 1:5; the dead living at her gaze: Deut 32:39, 1Sam 2:6.
- Not looking back: Gen 19:17, 26.

**Šuʾila to Ištar 3: 'O sublime Ištar, illuminator of the world' (against slander)** (Shuila Ištar SB 3)
- Truth in my mouth / slanderers: compare Ps 120:2, Ps 141:3, Ps 31:19; raising the fallen Ps 145:14, Ps 146:8.

**Šuʾila to Ištar 4: a woman's prayer with offerings, for healing and a child** (Shuila Ištar SB 4)
- A woman praying for a child at the sanctuary: 1Sam 1:10-11 (Hannah); compare Q 3:35-38. 'Eat and drink' food set before the deity: contrast Ps 50:12-13; incense 'pleasing fragrance' Gen 8:21, Lev 1:9.

**Šuʾilas to Ištar 5-9: fragments and incipits with rituals** (Shuila Ištar SB 5, Shuila Ištar SB 6, Shuila Ištar SB 7, Shuila Ištar SB 8, Shuila Ištar SB 9)
- Animals look to the deity: compare Ps 104:27, Ps 145:15-16. Queen of Heaven: Jer 7:18, Jer 44:17-25.

**Šuʾila to Ištar 10: 'O Ištar of the stars, goddess of the morning'** (Shuila Ištar SB 10)
- Goddess of the morning star: Isa 14:12 (Helel ben Shahar); mercy formula Exod 34:6-7, Joel 2:13, Jonah 4:2; like father and mother Ps 27:10, Ps 103:13, Isa 49:15, Isa 66:13.
- Food bitter, tears and dust: Ps 102:5,10 (ashes like bread, tears in drink), Ps 42:4, Job 3:24, Job 7:13-14 (dreams terrify me).

**Šuʾila to Ištar 11: 'The one with Innin-status among the gods'** (Shuila Ištar SB 11)
- Weak made strong: Joel 4:10 (reversed), 2Cor 12:9; light shining in darkness Ps 18:29, Isa 9:1.

**Šuʾila to Ištar 12: 'She is splendid' (daughter of Sin, against witchcraft)** (Shuila Ištar SB 12)
- Sorcery against the sufferer: compare Ps 58:6 (charmers), Mic 5:11; Q 113:4 (those who blow on knots).

**Šuʾila to Ištar 13: ritual for a slandered man and the prayer 'I implore you' (an eršahunga)** (Shuila Ištar SB 13)
- Courtiers' slander and the king's disfavour: compare Ps 31:14, Ps 41:6-9, Dan 6:4-5, Esth 3:8; leaning wall Ps 62:4.

**Šuʾilas to Ištar 23 and 30: 'O Ištar, lady of heaven and earth'; a fragment** (Shuila Ištar SB 23, Shuila Ištar SB 30)
- A she-kid 'unopened' as offering: compare Num 19:2 (heifer never yoked), Deut 21:3.

**Šuʾila to Ištar 31: 'O Ištar, lady of the cities, creator of the peoples' with its sickbed ritual** (Shuila Ištar SB 31)
- Cakes and libations for the star-goddess: Jer 7:18, Jer 44:19 (kawwanim 'to portray her'); twelve loaves set out compare Lev 24:5-6 (bread of the presence, two rows).

**Šuʾila to Šamaš 1: 'O supreme, perfect one, heir of Namraṣit' (against evil portents)** (Shuila Šamaš SB 1)
- Giving the lonely a home, the blind sight, freeing prisoners: Ps 68:7, Ps 146:7-8, Isa 42:7; opening the bolts/windows of heaven Mal 3:10, Gen 7:11; God who sees all Ps 33:13-15, Q 6:59 (knowledge of the unseen).
- Eclipse as evil portent: Jer 10:2 ('do not be dismayed at the signs of heaven'), Joel 3:4.

**Šuʾila to Šamaš 2: 'O great lord, who in the pure heavens...' (Ashurbanipal's copy)** (Shuila Šamaš SB 2)
- Sins of youth: Ps 25:7, Job 13:26; removed far away: Ps 103:12 ('as far as east from west'); purify me Ps 51:4,9.

**Šuʾilas to Šamaš 3 and 4: 'O brilliant, resplendent one' and a fragment** (Shuila Šamaš SB 3, Shuila Šamaš SB 4)
- Holding the hem of a garment: 1Sam 15:27, 1Sam 24:5, Zech 8:23. All wait for you: Ps 104:27, Ps 145:15. Šamaš 4:7' [a]na lā ā[l]itt[i]: to the barren woman (broken), compare Ps 113:9.

**Šuʾila to Šamaš 5: 'whose yes means yes' (namburbi against an evil portent)** (Shuila Šamaš SB 5)
- 'Let your yes be yes and your no be no': Matt 5:37, Jas 5:12; God's word unchanging Num 23:19. 'Let me see your light': Ps 36:10.

**Šuʾila to Šamaš 6: 'King of heaven and earth', against a curse seizing the chest, with an effigy rite** (Shuila Šamaš SB 6)
- Deeds return on the adversary's head: Ps 7:17, 1Kgs 2:32, Obad 15; washing hands in innocence Ps 26:6, Deut 21:6; sins unknown Ps 19:13; reviving the dead and freeing the bound Ps 146:7, 1Sam 2:6.

**Series of the Spider: creation in assembly, two creatures named, and their quarrel rebuked** (Spider SB)
- Creatures each given their place and named: Gen 1:24-25, Gen 2:19-20, Ps 104. 'Lord of flies': Baal-zebub of Ekron, 2Kgs 1:2-6. Q 29:41 (the spider's house is the frailest) is a contrasting spider image.
- Lines 34-107 largely lost (columns ii-iv broken): the second creature's reply (45-53) survives only in fragments.

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 1-2: the orphaned sufferer addresses his wise friend; death is the way of the fathers** (Theod SB –:1-22)
- Dialogue of sufferer and friends: Job 3-27; father and mother forsake me Ps 27:10; the way of all the earth 1Kgs 2:2, Josh 23:14; who fears God prospers Ps 112:1-3, Prov 3:9-10; acrostic poems: Ps 119, Lam 1-4.

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 3-5: poverty of the sufferer; wild ass, lion and rich man prosper without offerings** (Theod SB –:23-55)
- Job 21:7-15 and Jer 12:1 (why do the wicked prosper); Ps 73:3-12; Mal 3:14-15 ('what profit that we kept his charge?'). The wild ass in Job 39:5-8.

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 6-8: the friend predicts the fall of beast and rich man; the godless prosper; the divine plan is remote as heaven** (Theod SB –:56-88)
- God's ways high as heaven: Isa 55:8-9, Job 11:7-8, Rom 11:33; Q 2:216. The wicked fall into the pit they dug: Ps 7:16, Ps 9:16, Prov 26:27; the rich man's sudden end Ps 49:17-18, Luke 12:20.

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 9-13: broken passage; the sufferer resolves to renounce the god and roam** (Theod SB –:89-143)
- Despair and renunciation: Job 2:9 ('curse God and die'), Job 21:14-15, Mal 3:14; wandering for bread Ps 59:16, Ps 109:10.

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 14-19: the friend reproves; the sufferer on social inversion; wealth and poverty ordained** (Theod SB –:144-211)
- Fowler caught in his own net: Ps 9:16, Ps 35:8, Ps 57:7, Eccl 9:12. Social inversion: Eccl 10:6-7 (slaves on horses, princes walking), 1Sam 2:5-8, Luke 15:16 (carob pods). The Lord makes poor and rich: 1Sam 2:7, Prov 22:2.

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 20-24: the scoundrel will fall; god does not block the demon; firstborn and younger son** (Theod SB –:212-264)
- The wicked wither like grass: Ps 37:1-2, Ps 92:8; Job's friends accuse him of impious words Job 15:4-6; profit of serving God Mal 3:14, Job 21:15. Younger over elder: Gen 25:23, Gen 48:14-19, 1Sam 16:6-12.

**Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 25-27: society honours murderers; the gods gave humans lies; final plea** (Theod SB –:265-297)
- They call evil good: Isa 5:20,23, Amos 5:7,12, Hab 1:4; the poor maligned Ps 10:8-10. Gods implanting falsehood: contrast Gen 8:21 (yetser of the heart), 1Kgs 22:22 (lying spirit), Q 91:8 (soul inspired with wickedness and piety). Humble walk Mic 6:8, Ps 131:1.

**The Story of the Poor, Forlorn Wren: the wren appeals to Šamaš against the eagle** (Wren SB)
- Eagle's lofty nest brought down: Obad 1:4, Jer 49:16; the sparrow finds a nest by God's altar Ps 84:4; God cares for small birds Matt 10:29; lowly exalted Luke 1:52, Ezek 17:24 (high tree brought low, low tree raised).

**SAA 2 9: Loyalty oath of Babylonian allies to Ashurbanipal after Šamaš-šuma-ukīn's revolt** (SAA 02 009)
- No other king/lord and love of the overlord: Exod 20:3, Deut 6:4-5 (love YHWH), Deut 17:15; reporting inciters Deut 13:7-12; walking in darkness Deut 28:28-29; kneeling before the enemy Deut 28:25, Lev 26:17.

**SAA 2 1: Treaty of Šamšī-Adad V with Marduk-zākir-šumi of Babylon (clauses and curses)** (SAA 02 001)
- Deut 28:20-24 (curse, confusion, rain turned to dust, sky bronze), Deut 28:64 (scattered among peoples); life poured out like water Ps 22:15, 2Sam 14:14.

**SAA 2 11: Treaty of Sîn-šarru-iškun with Babylonian allies; curse section** (SAA 02 011)
- Not altering the tablet: Deut 4:2, Deut 13:1, Rev 22:18-19; skin disease Deut 28:27,35, 2Kgs 5:27; torch quenched 2Sam 14:7, 2Sam 21:17.

**SAA 2 4: First-person loyalty oath to Esarhaddon; curses** (SAA 02 004)
- Plague curses Deut 28:21; bow broken Hos 1:5, Jer 49:35; false scales (r:22' zibānītu lā kitti) Deut 25:13-16, Amos 8:5.

**SAA 2 8: Zakūtu (Naqiʾa), queen mother, imposes a loyalty oath for her grandson Ashurbanipal** (SAA 02 008)
- Deut 13:7-10: 'if your brother, son, daughter, wife or friend entices you secretly ... do not conceal him, your hand shall be first upon him'. A queen mother's power: 1Kgs 15:13, 2Kgs 11:1 (Athaliah), Jer 13:18.

**SAA 2 2 i: Aššur-nērārī V and Matiʾ-il of Arpad: the spring lamb identified with the vassal** (SAA 02 002 o.i)
- Cutting animals at covenant-making: Gen 15:9-18 and Jer 34:18-20 (passing between the parts of the calf); 1Sam 11:7 (oxen cut up: 'so shall it be done to his oxen'); never returning to his land Jer 22:10-12.

**SAA 2 2 iii-vi: Matiʾ-il's obligations, curses (famine, cannibalism, prostitutes, mule) and the divine witnesses** (SAA 02 002 o.iii, SAA 02 002 r.iv, SAA 02 002 r.v, SAA 02 002 r.vi)
- Deut 28:53-57 and Lev 26:29 (eating sons and daughters), 2Kgs 6:28-29, Lam 4:10; Deut 28:38,42 (locust); Deut 28:23-24 (no rain); Amos 5:3 ('the city that went out a thousand shall have a hundred left'), Isa 30:17; soldiers become women Nah 3:13, Jer 50:37, Jer 51:30; eyes gouged 2Kgs 25:7, 1Sam 11:2; 'Woe, we have sinned' Lam 5:16, Jer 3:25; dung and urine 2Kgs 18:27.

**SAA 2 12: Sîn-šarru-iškun treaty fragment: Nergal's curse** (SAA 02 012)
- Blood poured on the ground like water: Deut 12:16 (inverted), Ps 79:3; loyalty to the dynasty's sons and grandsons Exod 20:5-6, Deut 5:9.

**SAA 2 5: Esarhaddon's treaty with Baal, king of Tyre: deputy, shipwreck, ports, and curses by the gods of the West** (SAA 02 005)
- Deut 28:27,35 (boils from sole to crown); lions sent on those who do not fear God at Bethel: 1Kgs 13:24, 2Kgs 17:25; ships broken by the east wind Ps 48:8, Ezek 27:26, Jonah 1:4; Deut 28:30-33,48,51 (stranger eats your produce; without food, clothing; oil withheld 28:40); Tyre's ports Ezek 27; Bethel as a god Jer 48:13.

**SAA 2 14: Literary account of Esarhaddon's succession oath for Ashurbanipal and Šamaš-šuma-ukīn** (SAA 02 014)
- Succession arranged and sworn by the people: 1Kgs 1:30-40 (Solomon), 1Chr 29:22-24 (all officials pledge themselves to Solomon); the stars fight from their courses Judg 5:20.

**SAA 2 10: Ashurbanipal's treaty with Qedarite Arabs against Yautaʿ** (SAA 02 010)
- Oil as a covenant token: Hos 12:2 ('they make a covenant with Assyria and oil is carried to Egypt'); Qedar Isa 21:16-17, Jer 49:28-33, Ps 120:5; anointed vassal 1Sam 10:1.

**SAA 2 13: Treaty with an Arab ruler: no peace with the enemy, no secret messages, report every hostile word** (SAA 02 013)
- 'A bird of the air will carry the voice, and a winged creature tell the matter': Eccl 10:20; Deut 13:9 ('you shall not conceal him').

**SAA 2 3: Sennacherib's succession treaty in favour of Esarhaddon** (SAA 02 003)
- Deut 28:15-20 (all these curses shall come upon you), Deut 29:19-20 (every curse written in this book); the chosen younger son: 1Kgs 1:17, 1Chr 28:5.

**SAA 2 15 (Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty, Tayinat copy) i: seals of Aššur, parties, future generations, divine witnesses** (SAA 02 015 o:i_T_1-?_T_i_52')
- Deut 29:13-14 (not with you alone but with whoever is not here with us today); heaven and earth as witnesses Deut 4:26, 30:19, 32:1, Isa 1:2. Kunalia = Calneh/Kalno: Amos 6:2, Isa 10:9.

**SAA 2 15 i-iii: no other king, no oath to another lord, report evil words even from the prince's kin** (SAA 02 015 o:58_T_i_62'-_T_iii_12)
- Deut 13:7-12 (brother, son, daughter, wife, friend who entices you: do not conceal, report and execute); Exod 20:3 (no other gods before me); Deut 17:15 (set over you a king whom YHWH chooses, not a foreigner).

**SAA 2 15 iv: no poison or sorcery against the crown prince; love him as your own lives** (SAA 02 015 o:257_T_iv_1-268_T_iv_11)
- Love as one's own life: Deut 6:5 (love YHWH with all your heart and soul), Lev 19:18, 1Sam 18:1-3 and 20:17 (Jonathan loved David as his own soul, covenant). Poisoning a king: compare 2Kgs 9:22 (sorceries of Jezebel).

**SAA 2 15 v: the prince's brothers, succession at the king's death, no annulment rites, whole-hearted oath taught to sons, the sealed tablet** (SAA 02 015 o:344_T_v_1-413_T_v_77)
- Deut 6:6-7 and 11:18-19 (these words on your heart, teach them to your sons); Isa 29:13 (honour me with their lips, their heart far); Deut 29:13-14 (future generations); Deut 31:26 (book placed beside the ark as witness), Exod 25:16; destroying a written covenant: Jer 36:23 (scroll burned), Jer 51:63 (book sunk in the river); 'YHWH your God' formula Deut 6:2, 6:13.

**SAA 2 15 v-vi: curses god by god (Aššur to Kubaba): disease, leprosy, famine and cannibalism, unburied corpses, darkness** (SAA 02 015 o:414_T_v_78-493_T_vi_76)
- Deut 28 point by point: 28:22 and 28:65-67 (consumption, fever; no rest, sleeplessness), 28:27,35 (boils, itch, incurable), 28:18 (fruit of the womb), 28:23-24 (no rain), 28:38,42 (locust), 28:53-57 (eat sons and daughters; the tender mother's eye evil against her daughter), 28:26 (corpse food for birds and beasts, none to frighten), 28:25 (smitten before enemies), 28:29 (grope at noon), 28:21 (pestilence). Jer 25:10 (sound of millstones ceases); Jer 16:4 and 22:19 (no burial); 2Kgs 1:2 (Baal-zebub god of Ekron); Lev 26:26 (bread by weight).

**SAA 2 15 vi: the sworn speak: 'if we rebel, make terms with his enemy, or conceal sedition'** (SAA 02 015 o:494_T_vi_77-517_T_vii_6)
- Self-curse in the first person: compare Deut 27:15-26 (the people answer Amen), Neh 10:30 (they enter into a curse and an oath); concealment Deut 13:9.

**SAA 2 15 vii: further curses and simile curses (bronze sky, mule's seed, iron plough, ewe and lambs, oath entering the body)** (SAA 02 015 o:517–518_T_vii_7-605_T_vii_91)
- Deut 28:23-24 (heaven over you bronze, earth iron; the rain of your land powder and dust); Lev 26:19; Mic 3:12 and Jer 26:18 (Zion ploughed as a field); Ps 109:18 (curse entered his body like water, like oil into his bones) and Num 5:22,27 (the cursing water enters the bowels); 2Kgs 6:25, Ezek 4:16 (bread by weight); Deut 28:30 (betroth a wife, another lies with her; build a house, not dwell in it); Deut 28:39,42 (worm, locust); Isa 66:24 (their worm shall not die); Lam 4:8 (visage blacker than soot); Isa 19:5-6 (rivers dry, turned back); Isa 3:24 (stench instead of perfume).

**SAA 2 15 viii: last simile curses (wax figure, crab, right or left, dove, water-skin, sandal, tablet of fates) and date** (SAA 02 015 o:606_T_viii_1-670_T_viii_71)
- Deut 28:14 and 5:32, 17:11,20, Josh 1:7, 23:6 (turn not aside to the right or the left); Deut 28:65 (no rest for the sole of your foot); Jer 8:22 (no balm in Gilead); Ezek 12:13, 17:20, Hos 7:12 (God spreads his net); Gen 3:14 (on your belly you shall go); Exod 32:32-33, Ps 69:29, Deut 29:19 (name blotted out); Ps 68:3 (as wax melts before fire); Nah 3:13 (troops become women); Judg 1:6-7 (thumbs and big toes cut off).

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: seal of Aššur, preamble and divine witnesses (SAA 2 6:i-40B)** (SAA 02 006 o:i-40B)
- Heaven and earth as witnesses of the covenant: compare Deut 4:26, 30:19, 31:28, 32:1; Isa 1:2.
- An unalterable sealed royal document: compare Esth 8:8 and Dan 6:9,13,16 (law of the Medes and Persians that cannot be altered).
- Covenant binding sons and grandsons not yet born: Deut 29:13-14 (Heb 29:14-15) and Deut 5:3.
- From the rising of the sun to its setting: Mal 1:11; Ps 50:1, 113:3.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: guard Assurbanipal, enthrone him, swear to no other king (SAA 2 6:41-72)** (SAA 02 006 o:41-72)
- No other king beside the designated lord: compare Exod 20:3 / Deut 5:7 (no other gods before me) and Deut 6:14.
- Serve with the whole heart: Deut 6:5, 10:12, 11:13; Josh 24:14 'in sincerity and in truth'; 1 Sam 12:24.
- Do not alter the king's word: Deut 4:2, 13:1 (Heb 13:1) 'do not add to it or take from it'.
- Younger son chosen as heir over elder brothers: 1 Kgs 1 (Solomon over Adonijah), 1 Chr 28:5.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: report any evil word from kin, officials, prophets or anyone; protect Šamaš-šumu-ukin (SAA 2 6:73-122)** (SAA 02 006 o:73-122)
- Deut 13:2-6 (prophet or dreamer of dreams urging rebellion) and 13:7-12 (brother, son, daughter, wife or friend who entices secretly; do not conceal him). The ESA's sequence (kin, prophets, all people) is often taken as the model for Deut 13.
- Compare also Deut 18:20-22 and Jer 28-29 (prophets speaking rebellion).
- Mic 7:5-6 (trust not a friend; enemies are members of one's own household).

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: do not harm the prince; seize and kill instigators; no conspiracy oath (SAA 2 6:123-161)** (SAA 02 006 o:123-161)
- Deut 13:9-11 (do not spare or conceal him; your hand shall be first against him) and 13:13-19 (the city that rebels is put to the sword).
- Covenant meal and cup: Gen 31:46-54; Exod 24:11. Conspiracy sealed by oath: 2 Sam 15:10-12 (Absalom), Ps 2:2.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: sieges, desertion, after the king's death, the palace coup and the false message (SAA 2 6:162-211)** (SAA 02 006 o:162-211)
- Kills and makes alive, brings low and exalts: 1 Sam 2:6-7; Deut 32:39; 2 Kgs 5:7.
- 'Lift up your head' as a message of release or restoration: Gen 40:13,20; 2 Kgs 25:27.
- Palace intrigue at the death of a king and rival heirs: 1 Kgs 1 (Adonijah's feast); 2 Kgs 11 (Athaliah).

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: no assembly to make a king, usurpers from royal kin, minority of heirs, the pregnant wife, poison and sorcery (SAA 2 6:212-265)** (SAA 02 006 o:212-265)
- Joash hidden and raised for the throne after the queen's murder of the royal seed: 2 Kgs 11:1-3.
- Blood for blood: Gen 9:6; Num 35:19-33; 2 Kgs 9:7, 26 (avenging the blood of the prophets/Naboth).
- Conspiracy by servants killing the king: 2 Kgs 12:20-21, 21:23-24 (the people of the land kill the conspirators and enthrone the son).

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: love him as yourselves; slander and royal gifts; teach this treaty to your sons (SAA 2 6:266-301)** (SAA 02 006 o:266-301)
- Deut 6:6-7 and 11:19 (teach these words diligently to your children); Deut 4:9-10; Ps 78:5-6.
- Love as your own soul: Deut 13:7 (Heb; 13:6 Eng) 'your friend who is as your own soul'; 1 Sam 18:1,3 and 20:17 (Jonathan loved David as his own soul); Lev 19:18.
- Lose your life and your land: Deut 4:26-27, 30:17-18; Deut 28:63-64.
- Favour with gods and men: 1 Sam 2:26; Prov 3:4; Luke 2:52.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: fight a usurper; resist incitement to set the prince against his father and brothers (SAA 2 6:302-372)** (SAA 02 006 o:302-372)
- Instigators who sow discord between a king and his son or brothers: 2 Sam 14-15 (Absalom), 1 Kgs 2:13-25.
- 'Where is the word?' mocking a divine promise: Jer 17:15; 2 Pet 3:4; Ps 42:4,11.
- Kingship confirmed by divine word against envious rivals: 2 Sam 7:12-16; Ps 2.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: no ritual to annul the oath; swear wholeheartedly; Aššur your god; guard the sealed tablet (SAA 2 6:373-413)** (SAA 02 006 o:373-413)
- Lip service vs. whole heart: Isa 29:13; Jer 12:2; Ps 78:36-37; Deut 30:2, 10.
- Covenant formula 'I will be your God': Lev 26:12; Deut 26:17-18; Jer 7:23.
- Fear YHWH and the king: Prov 24:21; 1 Pet 2:17.
- Tablets kept in the ark before God: Deut 10:1-5, 31:24-26; Exod 25:16. Destroying a written scroll in fire: Jer 36:23. Do not add or take away: Deut 4:2, 13:1; Rev 22:18-19.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: curses by the gods one by one (SAA 2 6:414-493)** (SAA 02 006 o:414-493)
- Deut 28 curse sequence: disease and boils (28:21-22, 27, 35), blindness and groping in darkness at noon (28:28-29), carrion birds (28:26), wife lain with by another, house and vineyard taken (28:30), stranger takes your goods (28:31-33, 43), locusts (28:38), cannibalism in siege (28:53-57: the delicate woman begrudges her own children).
- No sound of millstone or lamp: Jer 25:10; Rev 18:22-23. Wild-ass existence: Job 39:5-8; Dan 4:25.
- Dogs licking blood and eating the body in public: 1 Kgs 21:19,23-24; 2 Kgs 9:35-37 (Jezebel); Jer 22:19 (burial of an ass).
- Bethel as a god: Jer 48:13 ('Moab ashamed of Chemosh as Israel was ashamed of Bethel'). Lion sent: 1 Kgs 13:24; 2 Kgs 17:25.
- Quran: dogs and stripped bodies, or famine and fear as punishment: Q 16:112; disbelievers' deeds as darkness upon darkness: Q 24:40.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: the vassals' first-person oath and further curses by Aššur, Palil, Ea, Girra (SAA 2 6:494-525)** (SAA 02 006 o:494-525)
- The people answer 'Amen' to curses on themselves: Deut 27:15-26; Num 5:22; Neh 5:13.
- Water of bitterness causing the belly to swell: Num 5:22-27; compare Ps 109:18.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: analogical and simile curses I: iron earth and bronze sky to the stinking bug (SAA 2 6:526-611)** (SAA 02 006 o:526-611)
- Deut 28:23-24: 'your heaven over your head shall be bronze, and the earth under you iron; YHWH will make the rain of your land powder and dust'. The ESA order (earth iron, sky bronze) matches Deuteronomy against Lev 26:19 (sky iron, earth bronze).
- Eating children's flesh: Deut 28:53-57; Lev 26:29; Jer 19:9; Lam 2:20, 4:10; 2 Kgs 6:28-29; Ezek 5:10.
- Zion ploughed like a field: Mic 3:12; Jer 26:18. Cannot stand before enemies: Lev 26:37; Josh 7:12-13; Deut 28:25.
- Curse entering the body like water, like oil into the bones: Ps 109:18; Num 5:22. Drinking own blood like wine: Isa 49:26.
- Worms on the living or the corpse: Isa 14:11, 66:24; Job 7:5; Acts 12:23; Deut 28:39 (worm eats the vine).
- Avenger of blood: Num 35:19-27; Deut 19:6,12. Bird in a snare: Amos 3:5; Eccl 9:12; Prov 7:23. Flesh black: Lam 4:8, 5:10.
- Melt like wax before fire: Ps 68:3 (Heb), 97:5; Mic 1:4. Rivers turned back: Ps 114:3,5; Isa 19:5-6.
- Quran: those who break the covenant after its ratification are cursed: Q 13:25, 2:27; the hypocrites' saying with their tongues what is not in their hearts: Q 48:11.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: analogical curses II: bloody chariot to the overturned throne (SAA 2 6:612A-663)** (SAA 02 006 o:612A-663)
- Do not turn aside to the right or to the left: Deut 5:32, 17:11,20, 28:14; Josh 1:7. Sword devours: Deut 32:42; Jer 46:10.
- Warriors become women: Jer 50:37, 51:30; Nah 3:13; Isa 19:16. Moaning like doves: Isa 38:14, 59:11; Ezek 7:16; Nah 2:8.
- Bones that do not come together (reversed in Ezek 37:7). No balm in Gilead: Jer 8:22, 46:11; Isa 1:6 (wounds not softened with oil).
- Shaken like a reed in the water: 1 Kgs 14:15. Mutilation of thumbs and toes / blinding: Judg 1:6-7; 2 Kgs 25:7; Judg 16:21.
- Gall and wormwood: Deut 29:17 (Heb 29:17-18), 32:32-33. Blot out his name from under heaven: Deut 29:19 (Heb 29:19); Ps 9:6, 109:13.
- Overturning the throne of kingdoms: Hag 2:22. A snare/net of God: Ezek 12:13, 17:20; Hos 7:12.

**Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: date and subscript (SAA 2 6:664-670)** (SAA 02 006 o:664-670)
- Dated covenant documents: Jer 32:9-14 (sealed deed); Neh 9:38-10:1 (sealed covenant).

**Love lyrics of Nabû and Tašmetu (SAA 3 14)** (SAA 03 014)
- Song of Songs: 'I went down to the nut garden' 6:11; 'come to his garden and eat its choicest fruits' 4:16-5:1; 'I sat in his shade with great delight' 2:3; praise of the body part by part 7:2-10 (thighs, feet, navel); 'the voice of the turtledove is heard' 2:12.
- 'Who trusts' confession: Ps 20:8; Ps 115:9-11. Ring as love token: Song 8:6 (seal on your arm); Gen 24:22.

**Fragment on Elamite affairs and a eunuch (SAA 3 20)** (SAA 03 020)
- Eunuch officials in royal plots and reversal of fortunes: Esth 2:21-23, 6:1-2; Dan 1; 2 Kgs 9:32.

**Pasquinade against Bēl-ēṭir son of Ibâ (SAA 3 29)** (SAA 03 029)
- The boaster who praises himself: Prov 27:2 ('let another praise you and not your own mouth'); 1 Kgs 20:11. Byword and taunt among peoples: Deut 28:37; 1 Kgs 9:7; Jer 24:9.
- Mocking an upstart: Isa 22:15-19 (Shebna's tomb); Quran insult-poetry against an opponent: Q 68:10-13 ('every contemptible swearer, slanderer ... ignoble, besides that, of doubtful birth (zanim)').

**Prophetic or scholarly blessing-address to Assurbanipal: gods at his right and left, propitious planets, cheap grain (SAA 3 25)** (SAA 03 025)
- Abundance and cheap grain as royal blessing: Ps 72:3,6-7,16; 2 Kgs 7:1. God at the right hand: Ps 16:8, 110:5, 121:5.
- Long life and firm throne for the king: Ps 21:5, 61:7-8; 2 Sam 7:16.

**Fragmentary address to Assurbanipal: Šamaš older than heaven and earth; 'do not fear battle' (SAA 3 26)** (SAA 03 026)
- God before the mountains were born: Ps 90:2; Prov 8:22-26. 'Fear not' to the king before battle: Isa 7:4; 2 Chr 20:15-17. Not be put to shame: Ps 25:2-3; Isa 50:7.

**Dialogue between Assurbanipal and Nabû: 'Fear not, I will give you long life' (SAA 3 13)** (SAA 03 013)
- Fear not, I am with you: Isa 41:10-14, 43:1-5, 44:2; Gen 15:1, 26:24; Q 20:46 ('fear not, I am with you both, I hear and see').
- Reliance on God from the womb and the mother's breasts: Ps 22:10-11, 71:6; Isa 49:1. God as nursing mother: Isa 66:11-13; Num 11:12; Isa 60:16 ('you shall suck the breast of kings').
- Life written in God's book: Ps 139:16, 69:29; Exod 32:32; Mal 3:16. Do not hand me to my enemies: Ps 27:12, 41:3, 140:9.
- Enemies like chaff before the wind: Ps 1:4, 35:5; Isa 17:13, 29:5; trodden under feet: Mal 3:21 (Eng 4:3).

**Fragment mentioning Ummanaldašu of Elam and a daughter as gift (SAA 3 24)** (SAA 03 024)
- Royal daughters given in diplomatic marriage: 1 Kgs 3:1 (Pharaoh's daughter), 9:16; Dan 11:6,17.

**Fragment of a royal text about Nabû-bēl-šumāti and the goddess of Arbela (SAA 3 21)** (SAA 03 021)
- Nets spread for the enemy: Ezek 12:13; Ps 140:6.

**Hymn to Nineveh and its goddess, with blessing for Assurbanipal (SAA 3 7)** (SAA 03 007)
- Kings of Tarshish and the isles bring tribute: Ps 72:8-11; Isa 60:5-11. A city praised as a woman: Ps 48:2-3; Lam 1:1.
- Woman clothed with the sun, crown of stars: Rev 12:1. Festival procession to the sanctuary: Ps 68:25-28.

**Hymn to Nanaya with blessing on Assurbanipal (SAA 3 5)** (SAA 03 005)
- Nations hear and tremble: Exod 15:14; Ps 99:1. Priest-king: Ps 110:4; Gen 14:18.

**Assurbanipal's hymn to Marduk: creation, the defeat of Anzû and Tiamat (SAA 3 2:1-44)** (SAA 03 002 o:1-44)
- God crushes the sea-monster and the deep: Ps 74:13-14, 89:10-11; Isa 51:9-10; Job 26:12-13. Rahab's helpers bow beneath him: Job 9:13.
- God who opens the windows of heaven and sends rain: Ps 65:10-14; Mal 3:10. All gods bow down to him: Ps 97:7.

**Assurbanipal's hymn to Marduk: prayer for appeasement; hymn to Zarpanitu (SAA 3 2:r 1-25)** (SAA 03 002 r:1-25)
- Turn from your fierce anger: Exod 32:12; Ps 85:4-6; Ps 6:2. Let me live that I may praise you: Ps 6:6, 30:10, 118:17, 119:175; Isa 38:18-19.
- God of gods, lord of lords: Deut 10:17; Ps 136:2-3. Set the stars in their paths: Job 38:31-33; Ps 147:4.

**Assurbanipal's hymn to Aššur (SAA 3 1)** (SAA 03 001)
- Let me proclaim his name to a generation to come: Ps 22:31-32, 78:4-6, 102:19, 145:4. His understanding is unsearchable: Isa 40:28; Ps 145:3; Rom 11:33.
- Word of God stands firm like heaven: Ps 119:89-90; Isa 40:8. The writing of the heavens: Ps 19:2-5.

**Hymn to Nanaya with blessing for Sargon II (SAA 3 4)** (SAA 03 004)
- God raises the poor from the dust: 1 Sam 2:7-8; Ps 113:7-8. Without me you can do nothing / apart from you who can act: Ps 127:1.
- Locusts removed by God: Exod 10:19; Joel 2:20,25; 1 Kgs 8:37. Seizing the hem: Zech 8:23; 1 Sam 15:27.

**Incantation: a goddess asks her brother Adad for beauty and healing; women in labour (SAA 3 48)** (SAA 03 048)
- 'What shall I give you? Ask!' and the choice of a non-material gift: 1 Kgs 3:5-12; 2 Kgs 2:9; Esth 5:3,6.
- God does not need the flesh of bulls: Ps 50:12-13. Birth pangs imagery: Isa 26:17; Jer 4:31.

**Elegy on a woman who died in childbirth (SAA 3 15)** (SAA 03 015)
- Rachel dies in childbirth: Gen 35:16-19; the wife of Phinehas: 1 Sam 4:19-22. Death has come up through our windows: Jer 9:20.
- The land of no return: Job 7:9-10, 10:21, 16:22; 2 Sam 12:23. God hides his face from the suppliant: Ps 13:2, 88:15; Lam 3:44.

**Literary letter of Ninurta to the king, with Assurbanipal's library colophon (SAA 3 47)** (SAA 03 047)
- A written message from God/prophet to a king: 2 Chr 21:12-15 (Elijah's letter to Jehoram). God's anger: 'Where is the oath?': Ezek 17:16-19.
- Wise king who collected proverbs and writings: 1 Kgs 5:9-14 (Heb); Prov 25:1 (copied by Hezekiah's men); Eccl 12:9.

**Mystical cultic commentary: the king's rites explained as Marduk's victory (SAA 3 37)** (SAA 03 037)
- Mythic combat behind cultic acts: Ps 74:13-17, 89:10-11; Isa 27:1, 51:9. The scapegoat/animal standing for an enemy: Lev 16:21-22.
- Typological re-reading of ritual as divine victory: Col 2:15; Heb 9:11-14.

**Letter of Aššur to Assurbanipal on the defeat of Šamaš-šumu-ukin (SAA 3 44)** (SAA 03 044)
- Fulfilment of covenant curses in history (siege cannibalism): 2 Kgs 6:26-29; Lam 2:20, 4:10; Ezek 5:10 after Deut 28:53-57.
- Breaking the oath sworn in God's name brings judgment: Ezek 17:13-21 (Zedekiah's broken oath to Nebuchadnezzar); 2 Chr 36:13. Gods abandoning their city/king: Ezek 10-11.
- Good news to God and king: 2 Sam 18:19-31; Isa 52:7. Led like a sheep to slaughter: Jer 11:19.

**Fragmentary letter of a god to Assurbanipal: Elam's nobles tremble (SAA 3 45)** (SAA 03 045)
- A reed shaken by the wind: 1 Kgs 14:15; Matt 11:7. Nations tremble before Israel's king: Ps 2:11, 18:45-46.

**Fragmentary letter of Aššur to the king: chosen for shepherdship and sent with arrows (SAA 3 46)** (SAA 03 046)
- God took David from the sheepfold to shepherd his people: 2 Sam 7:8; Ps 78:70-72. Arrows sharp in the heart of the king's enemies: Ps 45:6.

**Fragmentary lament: wailing like an ecstatic; 'who taught you kingship?' (SAA 3 23)** (SAA 03 023)
- Prophets/ecstatics wailing: Mic 1:8; 1 Sam 10:5-6. Rachel weeping for her children: Jer 31:15. Lament taught to daughters: Jer 9:19.

**Assurbanipal's prayer to Ištar of Arbela against Teumman and the victory (SAA 3 31)** (SAA 03 031)
- Hezekiah spreads the blasphemous letter before YHWH: 2 Kgs 19:14-19; Isa 37:14-20. Enemy's boast 'I will pursue, I will divide the spoil': Exod 15:9.
- Captured king brought in chains before the god: 1 Sam 15:32-33 (Agag before YHWH at Gilgal); Judg 1:6-7.

**God's answering letter on the campaign against Der and the flight to Elam (SAA 3 41)** (SAA 03 041)
- Gods of a city carried off: Jer 48:7, 49:3; Isa 46:1-2; 2 Kgs 18:34. Terror of God's glory makes peoples flee: Exod 23:27; Isa 2:19-21.

**Hymn to Tašmetu and the procession of Nabû, with prayer for Assurbanipal (SAA 3 6)** (SAA 03 006)
- Liturgy of entrance through the temple gates: Ps 24:7-10, 118:19-20; Ps 68:25. He brings low and lifts up: 1 Sam 2:7; Ps 75:8.

**Mystical miscellanea I: the body of a god, Ištar as Tiamat, the three heavens and three earths (SAA 3 39:o)** (SAA 03 039 o:1-38)
- Heaven and the heaven of heavens: Deut 10:14; 1 Kgs 8:27; 2 Cor 12:2 (third heaven). Sapphire pavement under God's feet: Exod 24:10; Ezek 1:26.
- Seven heavens in layers: Q 67:3, 71:15, 41:12 ('adorned the lowest heaven with lamps'); Q 65:12 (seven earths likewise). Compare 'the lowest heaven of jasper' with the stars drawn on it.

**Mystical miscellanea II: Tiamat split like a dried fish, ghosts of the slain gods, secret colophon (SAA 3 39:r)** (SAA 03 039 r:1-31)
- Do not give what is holy to dogs: Matt 7:6; 'the secret things belong to YHWH': Deut 29:28. Rivers from Eden: Gen 2:10-14.
- The sea monster split: Ps 74:13; Gen 1:6-8 (waters divided). Sun and moon set in their courses: Ps 19:5-7, 104:19; Q 36:38-40 ('the sun runs to its resting place ... the moon we have measured in stations').

**Coronation hymn of Assurbanipal: 'Aššur is king!' (SAA 3 11)** (SAA 03 011)
- 'YHWH is king': Ps 93:1, 96:10, 97:1, 99:1; 1 Chr 16:31. Coronation psalms: Ps 2, 72, 110; the king's crown given by God: Ps 21:4.
- Justice and abundance in the king's days: Ps 72:1-7,16. Chaff before the wind: Ps 1:4. Small and great hear alike: Deut 1:17.

**Hymn in praise of Arbela and its goddess (SAA 3 8)** (SAA 03 008)
- Zion praised: Ps 48:2-4,13-14, 87:1-3, 122; 'this is the gate of heaven': Gen 28:17. Founded like the heavens: Ps 78:69.
- Goddess on a lion: the Qudshu iconography; compare the cherubim throne Ezek 1.

**Cultic calendar commentary: Marduk binds Anu, Qingu thrown from the roof (SAA 3 40)** (SAA 03 040)
- A younger god dethrones the old sky god: compare Ps 82 (God judges the gods), Dan 7:9-14 (Ancient of Days and the one like a son of man).
- Day of wrath: Zeph 1:15; Isa 13:9.

**The Marduk Ordeal I: Bēl held in the house of confinement, Nabû searches, Bēl prays for life (SAA 3 35:1-27)** (SAA 03 035 1-27)
- Jeremiah lowered into the cistern/dungeon, drawn out by a messenger: Jer 37:16, 38:6-13. Joseph in the pit and prison: Gen 37:24, 39:20-41:14.
- The bride searching the streets for her beloved: Song 3:1-3, 5:6-8. Prayer from confinement 'keep me alive': Ps 88; Jonah 2.
- Some read the text against Christian passion narratives (seized, beaten, tried, guarded, sought by a woman at the tomb): Mark 15-16; Luke 23-24; the comparison is contested.

**The Marduk Ordeal II: Enūma eliš recited, Zarpanitu prays, Bēlet-ilī at the grave, Ninurta defeats Anzû, curse colophon (SAA 3 35:28-72)** (SAA 03 035 28-72)
- Women go to the tomb and seek the dead lord: Mark 16:1-6; Luke 24:1-5; John 20:11-15 (contested comparison). 'What is my sin?': 1 Sam 20:1; Job 10:2, 13:23.
- Good news brought to the gods/the city: Isa 40:9, 52:7. Before the mountains God existed: Ps 90:2; Prov 8:23-25.
- Curse on whoever erases the book: Rev 22:18-19; ESA's tablet curses (SAA 2 6:397-413). Name and seed removed, flesh to dogs: 1 Kgs 14:11, 21:24.

**Fragment naming Gilgameš, scribes and a goddess with writing reeds (SAA 3 49)** (SAA 03 049)
- The man clothed in linen with a writer's case at his waist: Ezek 9:2-3,11.

**Assurbanipal's hymn to the Ištars of Nineveh and Arbela: 'I knew no father or mother' (SAA 3 3)** (SAA 03 003)
- Not by my bow do I trust: Ps 44:4-7; Hos 1:7; Zech 4:6; 1 Sam 17:47; Ps 20:8. Though father and mother forsake me, YHWH takes me up: Ps 27:10.
- God taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms: Hos 11:1-3. Called from the womb: Isa 49:1,5; Jer 1:5. Q 8:17 ('you did not kill them, but God killed them; you did not throw when you threw').

**Fragment from a Sargonid epic: guards, horsemen, the bow of Elam (SAA 3 18)** (SAA 03 018)
- 'I will break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might': Jer 49:35.

**Fragment: Assurbanipal trod the path of the sea; 'ask, ask!' (SAA 3 19)** (SAA 03 019)
- God's path in the sea: Ps 77:20; Isa 43:16. 'Ask, and it shall be given': Ps 2:8; Matt 7:7.

**Epic fragment of Assurbanipal's Elamite war: Madaktu broken, graves violated, Nabû-bēl-šumāti (SAA 3 22)** (SAA 03 022)
- Bones of kings brought out of their graves: Jer 8:1-2; 2 Kgs 23:16-18; Amos 2:1 (burning the bones of the king of Edom).

**Fragment of a royal praise poem: Šamaš who does not accept slander; products from the upper sea, Tyre and Elam (SAA 3 28)** (SAA 03 028)
- God raises the righteous and judges the oppressed: Ps 146:7-9; slander not accepted: Ps 15:3, 101:5. The least becomes a thousand: Isa 60:22.
- Tyre's trade catalogue: Ezek 27:12-25.

**Mock incantation against Bēl-ēṭir son of Ibâ (SAA 3 30)** (SAA 03 030)
- Mockery songs against an enemy: Ps 69:13; Lam 3:14,63. Q 111 (curse-sura on Abu Lahab and his wife).

**The Sin of Sargon: Sennacherib divines why his father died unburied (SAA 3 33)** (SAA 03 033)
- David inquires why a famine came and learns of Saul's sin against a treaty (the Gibeonites): 2 Sam 21:1-14; also the unburied king: Isa 14:18-20 (often read as Sargon II); Jer 22:18-19, 36:30.
- Sins of the fathers visited on sons: Exod 20:5; 2 Kgs 23:26, 24:3-4. Who can know the work of God: Eccl 3:11, 8:17; Isa 55:8-9.
- Deathbed charge to the successor: 1 Kgs 2:1-9; 1 Chr 22, 28. Witness agreement 'with one mouth': 1 Kgs 22:13; 2 Chr 18:12.

**Fragment of a mythological-ritual text: the Lady of Kidmuri, Aššur gives arrows to Lahmu (SAA 3 36)** (SAA 03 036)
- God gives arrows to the king: 2 Kgs 13:15-19 (Elisha and the arrow of victory). God's bow and arrows: Hab 3:9,11; Ps 7:13-14.

**Fragment of a divine letter quoting the king's report (SAA 3 42)** (SAA 03 042)
- Compare the divine letter form of SAA 3 41 and 44.

**Fragment of a divine letter: 'Which god is it who ...? Which king ...?' (SAA 3 43)** (SAA 03 043)
- Which god is like you: Exod 15:11; Mic 7:18; 2 Kgs 18:33-35 (Rabshakeh: which of the gods of the nations delivered?).

**Fragment of an invective: 'the bread of slander of your lips' (SAA 3 51)** (SAA 03 051)
- Slanderous words like delicacies swallowed: Prov 18:8, 26:22. Q 49:12 (backbiting as eating a dead brother's flesh).

**Fragment: 'I am your god who guards you, the herald of the land' (SAA 3 52)** (SAA 03 052)
- Your keeper does not slumber: Ps 121:3-5. I am YHWH your God: Exod 20:2.

**Divine love lyrics: the goddess loves Uruk, Babylon and the cult cities; their fires consume her (SAA 3 9)** (SAA 03 009)
- Love strong as death, its flashes flashes of fire: Song 8:6-7; love-sick: Song 2:5, 5:8. God's love for Zion over all the dwellings of Jacob: Ps 87:2, 132:13-14; Zion chosen: Ps 78:68.

**Underworld Vision of an Assyrian Prince: the king's deeds and Kummaya's prayer (SAA 3 32 obv.)** (SAA 03 032 o:1-34)
- The prologue (largely lost) contrasts a pious king and his negligent son; compare 2 Kgs 21 (Hezekiah and Manasseh) and Ps 78:5-8.

**Underworld Vision: Ereškigal appears in a dream; Kummaya weeps like a dove (SAA 3 32 obv. 35-40)** (SAA 03 032 o:35-40)
- Moaning like a dove: compare Isa 38:14 (Hezekiah 'I moan like a dove') and Isa 59:11, Nah 2:7.

**Underworld Vision: the fifteen hybrid gods of the netherworld (SAA 3 32 rev. 1-10)** (SAA 03 032 r:1-10)
- Composite beings of a vision: compare Ezek 1:5-14 (four-faced creatures) and Dan 7:3-8 (beasts from the sea); the man treading a snake recalls Gen 3:15 and Ps 91:13.

**Underworld Vision: before Nergal's throne; Išum intercedes; the prince is sent back (SAA 3 32 rev. 11-21)** (SAA 03 032 r:11-21)
- Taken by the forelock and carried before God: Ezek 8:3; seer falling at the feet of a terrifying figure: Dan 10:5-10, Rev 1:17, Isa 6:5. Interceding angel: Zech 3:1-5.
- Compare Q 96:15-16 (seized by the forelock, nāṣiya) and Q 55:41.

**Underworld Vision: the dead king, Nergal's warning, the prince's terror and the scribe's report (SAA 3 32 rev. 22-35)** (SAA 03 032 r:22-35)
- Dust in the mouth in grief: Lam 3:29, Josh 7:6, Job 2:12. A king's son warned through a vision of his father's judgment: compare 1 Sam 28:15-19 (Samuel brought up) and Q 2:260.

**Epic of Shalmaneser III's campaign against Urartu (SAA 3 17)** (SAA 03 017 o:1-32, SAA 03 017 r:1-33)
- Enemies fleeing to mountains and forests before the king's terror: compare Isa 2:19-21 and Judg 6:2; burning of the enemy's trees: Deut 20:19-20.

**A righteous sufferer's prayer to Nabû (SAA 3 12)** (SAA 03 012 o:1-23, SAA 03 012 r:1-19)
- Compare Job 30:9-26 and Ps 88:4-7 (at the gates of death), Ps 69:22 (gall and vinegar) and Lam 3:15; Ps 22:7-8 and Ps 35:19-26 (do not let those who rejoice at my calamity gloat). 'By your breath may the dead live': Ezek 37:9, Ps 104:29-30.
- Compare Q 21:83 (Job: 'harm has touched me and You are the most merciful').

**Cultic song of blessing on the Inner City (Assur) and Esarhaddon (SAA 3 10)** (SAA 03 010 o:1-34, SAA 03 010 r:1'-18')
- Oil on the head and blessing on city and king: Ps 133:2, Ps 23:5, Ps 128:5-6 and Ps 72:15-17.

**Lyric lament: the sorcerer-merchant of Babylon and the felled tree (SAA 3 16)** (SAA 03 016 o:1-30, SAA 03 016 r:1-29, SAA 03 016 e:1-2)
- The tree that stood tall in the garden and is cut down: Ezek 31:3-14, Dan 4:10-14, Isa 10:33-34.

**Fragment of a Middle Assyrian royal epic: the Ahlamû and Naʾid-Šihu (SAA 3 50)** (SAA 03 050 o:21-29)
- Enemies feasting and drunk before defeat: 1 Sam 30:16, 1 Kgs 20:16; Aramaean nomads (Ahlamû) as raiders: Gen 31:20-24 (Laban the Aramaean).

**Mystical cultic commentary: Ištar weeps for her brother, the flayed god, Orion, Dumuzi (Q009249, SAA 3)** (Q009249 o:1-63, Q009249 r:1-20)
- Bound Orion: Job 38:31 ('can you loose the cords of Orion?', kesil) and Amos 5:8. Treading the neck of enemies: Josh 10:24, Ps 110:1. Weeping for Tammuz: Ezek 8:14. Parched grain cast on Dumuzi: compare Lev 2:14 and Lev 23:14.
- A child hidden from a killer: Exod 2:2-3, 2 Kgs 11:2-3 (Joash hidden).

**The Marduk Ordeal: Bēl held captive, sought by the goddess, the criminal killed with him (SAA 3 34, obv. 1-33)** (SAA 03 034 o:1-33)
- A god held prisoner, sought by a woman in the streets: Song 3:1-3; a criminal executed together with him: Isa 53:12 and Luke 23:32-33; blood-dyed garment: Isa 63:1-3. Son coming to his captive father: compare Gen 37:14.

**The Marduk Ordeal: Enūma eliš recited, Aššur before heaven and earth, Anzû defeated, the god freed; curse (SAA 3 34, obv. 34-76)** (SAA 03 034 o:34-76)
- Before heaven and earth: Prov 8:22-26, Ps 90:2. Name and seed cut off, flesh to dogs: 1 Kgs 14:10-11, 2 Kgs 9:36, Ps 109:13. Curse on altering a text: Deut 4:2, Rev 22:18-19.

**Prophecy for Assurbanipal: vision of a golden star (SAA 9 11)** (SAA 09 011 r:1-13)
- Vision of a star and a table: compare Num 24:17 (a star from Jacob) and Ps 23:5; Zech 4:2 (golden lampstand in a vision).

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.1: Ištar of Arbela, through Issār-lā-tašiyaṭ (SAA 9 1 i)** (SAA 09 001 o.i:1'-29')
- 'Fear not' oracles of salvation: Isa 41:10-14, 43:1-5, 44:2; God going before and behind: Isa 52:12, Isa 58:8. Enemies under the king's feet: Ps 110:1, 1 Kgs 5:3.
- Compare Q 20:46 ('fear not, I am with you both, hearing and seeing') and Q 28:7.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.2: through Sinqīša-āmur (SAA 9 1 i-ii)** (SAA 09 001 o.i:30'-39', SAA 09 001 o.ii:1'-10')
- Kings brought in fetters and tribute: Isa 45:14, Ps 149:8, Ps 72:10.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.3: rejoicing with the king, through Rēmūt-Allati (SAA 9 1 ii)** (SAA 09 001 o.ii:11'-15')
- Call to a city to rejoice with the king: Zech 9:9, Zeph 3:14-17.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.4: Bēl, Ištar and Nabû speak, through Bayâ (SAA 9 1 ii)** (SAA 09 001 o.ii:16'-40')
- Do not trust in man, lift your eyes: Jer 17:5-7, Ps 146:3, Ps 121:1-2, Ps 123:1. A mother who cannot forget: Isa 49:15, Isa 66:13. Carried from childhood: Isa 46:3-4, Hos 11:3.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.6: midwife and wet-nurse; the golden chamber of heaven, through Issār-bēlī-daʾʾini (SAA 9 1 iii-v)** (SAA 09 001 o.iii:7'-32', SAA 09 001 o.iv:1-35, SAA 09 001 o.v:1-11)
- God as nurse and midwife: Num 11:12, Ps 22:10-11, Ps 71:6; 'I am your shield': Gen 15:1, Ps 3:4. Pillar of cloud (smoke) and fire: Exod 13:21-22. Through rivers: Isa 43:2. 'The apple of the eye' kept: Deut 32:10, Ps 17:8. 'You are my son': Ps 2:7.
- Ezek 8:3 (lifted by a lock of hair between earth and heaven).

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.7: the Lady of Arbela answers the queen mother, through Ahāt-abīša (SAA 9 1 v)** (SAA 09 001 o.v:12-25)
- The banished son wandering in the wilderness and restored to kingship: compare David in 1 Sam 23-26 and 2 Sam 15-19; mother interceding for her son's kingship: 1 Kgs 1:15-31 (Bathsheba).

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.8: Ištar went out to the steppe, peace to her calf (SAA 9 1 v)** (SAA 09 001 o.v:26-36)
- The king as calf of the divine cow; compare Hos 11:1-4 (Ephraim taught to walk) and Jer 31:18-20.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 1.9: former word fulfilled, sons and grandsons, through Lā-dāgil-ili (SAA 9 1 vi)** (SAA 09 001 o.vi:1-32)
- Former and latter things: Isa 42:9, Isa 43:9-19, Isa 48:3-6. Dynasty promise: 2 Sam 7:12-16, Ps 132:11-12. Eating bread and drinking water in safety: Isa 33:16, Ps 4:9.

**Words of the Elamite god: the snake in the javelin (SAA 9 8)** (SAA 09 008 o:1-8, SAA 09 008 b.e:9, SAA 09 008 r:1-2)
- God breaks bow and spear: Ps 46:10, Hos 1:5, Jer 49:35 ('I will break the bow of Elam'). Repeated oracle: Gen 41:32.

**Covenant of Aššur 3.1: peace to heaven and earth and Esarhaddon; dominion east to west (SAA 9 3 i-ii)** (SAA 09 003 i:1-37, SAA 09 003 ii:1-9)
- Peace to heaven and earth, enemies under the king's feet: Ps 110:1, Ps 2:8, Ps 72:8; sun-like king: 2 Sam 23:4, Mal 3:20.

**Covenant of Aššur 3.2: 'I heard your cry' from the gate of heaven; fire and stones on the rebels (SAA 9 3 ii)** (SAA 09 003 ii:10-25)
- Ps 18:7-15 (God hears from his temple, hailstones and coals of fire); Josh 10:11; Exod 9:23-24; 'that they may know that I am YHWH': Exod 7:5, Ezek passim. Compare Q 105:4 (stones of baked clay on the enemy).

**Covenant of Aššur 3.3: the covenant tablet brought in; the water of the oath (SAA 9 3 ii-iii)** (SAA 09 003 ii:26-36, SAA 09 003 iii:1-15)
- Covenant made with sacrifices and the book read: Exod 24:4-8; drinking the water as ordeal or covenant: Exod 32:20, Num 5:17-27. 'When you have eaten and are full, beware lest you forget': Deut 6:10-12, Deut 8:10-14.

**Covenant of Aššur 3.4-5: Ištar's complaint about her meal; rebels impaled, through Lā-dāgil-ili (SAA 9 3 iii-iv)** (SAA 09 003 iii:16-37, SAA 09 003 iv:1-35)
- God complains of being given nothing: Mal 1:6-14, Mal 3:8-10, Isa 43:23-24. Conspirators hanged: Esth 2:23, Esth 7:9-10. Treading the mountains: Amos 4:13, Mic 1:3.
