**Oracle to Assurbanipal through the prophetess Mullissu-kabtat: the nurse goddess (SAA 9 7)** (SAA 09 007 o:1-14, SAA 09 007 r:1-11)
- Kings conspiring 'come, let us go': Ps 2:1-3, Ps 83:4-6. Carried on the hip and dandled on the knees: Isa 66:12-13, Num 11:12, Isa 49:22-23. 'Who watches by night': Ps 121:3-4, Isa 27:3. Thorns and briers burned: Isa 27:4. Egypt: Isa 19.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.2: the good sailor; sixty gods at right and left, through Bayâ (SAA 9 2 i)** (SAA 09 002 i:15'-35')
- God brings sailors to their desired haven: Ps 107:30. The Lord encamped around: Ps 34:8, Ps 125:2. Thousands at the right hand: Ps 91:7; host at right and left: 1 Kgs 22:19.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.3: bird over its young, the good puppy, 'I am the speaker and doer', through Lā-dāgil-ili (SAA 9 2 i-ii)** (SAA 09 002 i:36'-38', SAA 09 002 ii:1'-28')
- Like birds hovering, so YHWH protects Jerusalem: Isa 31:5; Deut 32:11; Ps 91:4. 'I have spoken and I will do it': Isa 46:11, Ezek 17:24, Num 23:19. 'All men are liars': Ps 116:11, Jer 17:9.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.4: 'I see and I hear'; Elamites, Manneans, Urartians, through Urkittu-šarrat (SAA 9 2 ii-iii)** (SAA 09 002 ii:29'-39', SAA 09 002 iii:1'-18')
- 'I have seen and heard': Exod 3:7, Q 20:46 ('I am with you both, I hear and I see'). 'Be still': Exod 14:14 ('YHWH will fight for you, and you shall keep silent'), Ps 46:11. 'How long?': Ps 13:2, Hab 1:2.

**Oracles to Esarhaddon 2.5-6: 'I am your father and mother'; Urkittu, between my arms (SAA 9 2 iii-iv)** (SAA 09 002 iii:19'-36', SAA 09 002 iv:1'-31')
- Father and mother: Ps 27:10, Isa 63:16, Isa 66:13; between the arms: Deut 33:27 ('underneath are the everlasting arms'), Deut 33:12.

**Oracle: Mullissu heard the cry of her calf; Ninurta at the king's right and left (SAA 9 5)** (SAA 09 005 1-8, SAA 09 005 b.e:9-10, SAA 09 005 r:1-7)
- Gird your loins: Jer 1:17, Job 38:3; God hears the cry: Exod 2:23-25, Exod 3:7.

**Oracle to Assurbanipal through Dunnaša-āmur: the goddess roams the steppe for his life (SAA 9 9)** (SAA 09 009 o:1-28, SAA 09 009 r:1'-7')
- The tireless guardian and intercessor: Isa 62:6-7, Isa 40:28-31; the shepherd searching mountains and rivers: Ezek 34:11-16. Advocate in the divine council: Zech 3, Job 33:23.

**Record of a rite in the Aššur temple, Sargon II year 9: the basalt seat, the sacrificial table and the scribes' portions (SAA 20 55)** (SAA 20 055 o:1-27, SAA 20 055 r:1'-23')
- Rededication of a damaged altar and the priests' portions: 2 Chr 29:18-24, Lev 7:31-36, 1 Sam 2:13-16. Offerings of oil, honey, milk, beer, wine on the table: contrast Lev 2:11 (no honey on the altar).

**Assur cultic calendar: gods at Aššur's right and left at the akītu; the chariot procession (SAA 20 53 obv.)** (SAA 20 053 o.i:1'-29', SAA 20 053 o.ii:1'-31')
- The god's chariot and horses: 2 Kgs 23:11 (horses dedicated to the sun, chariots of the sun), Hab 3:8, Ps 68:18. Gods at right and left: 1 Kgs 22:19.

**Assur cultic calendar: seating in the Dagan temple tested by oracle; baths and drums of the gods (SAA 20 53 rev.)** (SAA 20 053 r.v:1'-27', SAA 20 053 r.vi:1'-29')
- East gate of the temple where the glory enters: Ezek 43:1-4, 44:1-2. Drums and music at the rising of the deity: Ps 68:25-26, Ps 150:5.

**Fragment of a royal ritual: mouth-washing on the 23rd; the king in the Dagan temple (SAA 20 6)** (SAA 20 006 o:1-16, SAA 20 006 r:1'-8')
- Salt with every offering: Lev 2:13; incense and torch before the deity: Exod 30:7-8. 'Make your face shine': Num 6:25, Ps 80:4.

**Middle Assyrian coronation ritual: 'Aššur is king!'; the crown blessing (SAA 20 7 i-ii)** (SAA 20 007 i:19'-46', SAA 20 007 ii:1-49)
- 'YHWH is king' (YHWH malakh): Ps 93:1, Ps 96:10, Ps 97:1, Ps 99:1; acclamation 'Long live the king': 1 Sam 10:24, 1 Kgs 1:39. Crown and testimony: 2 Kgs 11:12. Sceptre of equity: Ps 45:7. 'Kiss the son': Ps 2:12.

**Middle Assyrian coronation ritual: enthronement, gifts, the officials lay down their staffs; offerings to all gods (SAA 20 7 iii-iv)** (SAA 20 007 r.iii:1-42, SAA 20 007 r.iv:1-7)
- Officials confirmed by the new king: 1 Kgs 4:1-6, 2 Sam 8:15-18; Saul at Gilgal 1 Sam 11:15. Enthronement with music and homage: 1 Kgs 1:39-48.

**Ritual in the Bit-Eqi of Ištar: offering to 'Mouth-and-Tongue' and the charge to keep Ištar's secret (SAA 20 29)** (SAA 20 029 o:1-15, SAA 20 029 r:1'-10')
- Guard your mouth: Ps 141:3, Prov 13:3, Prov 21:23; revealing a secret: Prov 11:13, Prov 20:19. 'Whoever reveals the mysteries ... shall die': compare Deut 29:28 (secret things belong to YHWH). Lamp/light blessing: Num 6:25, Prov 4:18.

**List of temple doorkeepers, images and courts: the Papahu holy of holies and the Apsû court (SAA 20 43)** (SAA 20 043 1'-9')
- Temple guardians at the gates: Ezek 40-44 (gatekeepers), 1 Chr 26; a basin called 'sea' in the temple court: 1 Kgs 7:23-26.

**Assurbanipal's new rites of Shebat-Adar: the king kisses the ground; 'Šeruʾa has given birth!' (SAA 20 9)** (SAA 20 009 o.i:1-24, SAA 20 009 o.i:25'-40', SAA 20 009 o.ii:5-44, SAA 20 009 o.iii:13-23, SAA 20 009 r.ii:2'-27', SAA 20 009 r.iii:1'-29', SAA 20 009 r.iv:13'-23')
- Birth of a divine child proclaimed as good news: Isa 9:5 ('a child is born to us'), Isa 66:7-9, Ps 2:7, Luke 2:10-11. Taking the hand of the god (Marduk) at the New Year: compare Isa 45:1 (Cyrus whose right hand I grasped) and Ps 73:23.

**Assur ritual compendium: gods at Aššur's right and left; provisions; Ištar's akītu; the Sarrānu dance (SAA 20 52 obv. iv-v, rev. i)** (SAA 20 052 o.iv:1'-12', SAA 20 052 o.v:1'-18', SAA 20 052 r.i:1'-47')
- Dancing before the god: 2 Sam 6:14-16, Ps 149:3; dancers who raise their arms and limp around the altar: 1 Kgs 18:26.

**Assur ritual compendium: baths and drums; bowls set by the stars; oracle queries 'good / not good' (SAA 20 52 rev. ii)** (SAA 20 052 r.ii:1'-54')
- Women dancing in procession before the deity: Exod 15:20, Judg 21:21, Ps 68:26. Ministering women at the sanctuary gate: Exod 38:8, 1 Sam 2:22.

**Assur ritual compendium: incense burners tested; names of Aššur's gates; stars identified as Aššur (SAA 20 52 rev. iii)** (SAA 20 052 r.iii:1'-63')
- Named gates of the temple: Jer 20:2 (upper gate of Benjamin), Ezek 8:3-16 (north gate, women weeping for Tammuz); star worship: 2 Kgs 23:5, Amos 5:26 (Kaiwan = Saturn), Jer 8:2.

**Assur ritual compendium: Sargon's provisions to the tomb; positions of Sennacherib's gods fixed by extispicy; the queen may enter before Aššur (SAA 20 52 rev. iv)** (SAA 20 052 r.iv:1'-65')
- Truth and Justice personified before the throne: Ps 85:11-14, Ps 89:15, Ps 97:2. Offerings for the dead: Deut 26:14; a queen entering unbidden before the king: Esth 4:11-5:2.

**Assur ritual compendium: extispicy, Mullissu's offerings; 'Šeruʾa, wife of Aššur' sung (SAA 20 52 rev. v)** (SAA 20 052 r.v:2'-58')
- A consort for the high god ('YHWH and his Asherah', Kuntillet Ajrud): compare Jer 7:18, Jer 44:17-19 (queen of heaven), 2 Kgs 21:7. Head of the sea monster: Ps 74:13-14.

**Royal ritual for days 23-25: the king goes down to the temple, sacrifices, raised-hand prayer (SAA 20 3)** (SAA 20 003 o:1-10, SAA 20 003 b.e:11-13, SAA 20 003 r:1-10)
- Lifting hands in prayer: Ps 141:2, Ps 134:2, 1 Kgs 8:22.

**Ritual of Ištar and the bed: ribs, seven jars of wine and beer, head and feet (SAA 20 20)** (SAA 20 020 i:1'-23')
- Head and legs of the sacrifice: Exod 12:9, Lev 1:8-9; sevenfold libations: compare 1 Kgs 18:34 (water poured three times).

**List of the gods of the Aššur temple, 'their names invoked' (SAA 20 45)** (SAA 20 045 i:1'-8', SAA 20 045 ii:1'-9')
- Queen of heaven: Jer 7:18, Jer 44:17-25.

**Ritual of the Daughter of the River: the 'man of judgment', the lamb dressed as a bride, the seven Judges (SAA 20 32)** (SAA 20 032 o:1-36, SAA 20 032 r:1-25)
- Ritual of guilt carried away by a substitute animal: Lev 16:20-22 (scapegoat), Lev 14:4-7 (bird released over water); ordeal water: Num 5:11-31. The 'daughter' given to the river: compare Judg 11:34-40.

**Rituals of Ninittu and Kulittu: offerings poured into a pit; the king sets his foot on it (SAA 20 19)** (SAA 20 019 o.i:1-26, SAA 20 019 o.ii:1-29, SAA 20 019 r.i:1'-29', SAA 20 019 r.ii:1'-30')
- Offerings poured into a pit for underworld powers: compare 1 Sam 28:13 and Lev 17:13 (blood covered with earth); honey forbidden on the altar: Lev 2:11.

**Tākultu of Aššur-etel-ilani, obverse - the gods, temple and its parts bidden to drink** (SAA 20 042 o.i, SAA 20 042 o.ii)
- Compare Deut 32:37-38 (gods 'who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their libations') and Ps 50:12-13 (God does not eat bull's flesh or drink goats' blood).
- The summons of heaven, earth, gates and creation compares with Ps 148 and Ps 24:7-9 (gates addressed).

**Tākultu of Aššur-etel-ilani, reverse - land, rivers, cosmos invoked; blessings for the king who gave the meal** (SAA 20 042 r.iii, SAA 20 042 r.iv)
- Compare Ps 21:5 and 61:7-8 (length of days for the king), Ps 72:15-17 (prayer and blessing for the king, abundance), 1 Kgs 3:14.
- The blessing on all who share the meal compares with 1 Kgs 8:62-66 (Solomon's feast; the people go home joyful) and Deut 12:7, 14:26.

**Royal ritual - entry to the akītu-house, blood offered into the spring, offerings before the gods of heaven and earth** (SAA 20 015 o.i, SAA 20 015 o.ii)
- The festival in Nisan with the king officiating compares with Num 28:16-25 and 2 Chr 30, 35 (king-led Passover); the akītu procession with Ps 24 and Ps 68:25-28.
- Blood offered into a spring: contrast Lev 17:13 and Deut 12:16 (blood poured on the ground); compare 1 Kgs 1:9, 38-39 (ritual at the spring Gihon and En-rogel).

**Royal ritual - what the officiant says at each libation, salt-offering and kiss in the gods' cities** (SAA 20 015 r.i, SAA 20 015 r.ii)
- Spoken formulae tied to each act compare with Deut 26:1-15 (declarations at the offering of firstfruits and tithe) and Num 6:22-27.
- Gods asked to bless and heaven blessing the worshipper: compare Ps 103:20-22, 134:3, Ps 148.

**Royal ritual - a message and a seal received before Aššur and Nergal; colophon of the priests of Aššur** (SAA 20 015 r.iii)
- A letter laid before the deity: compare Hezekiah spreading Sennacherib's letter before YHWH, 2 Kgs 19:14 and Isa 37:14.
- Priestly genealogy as authority: compare Ezra 7:1-5 and 1 Chr 6:1-15.

**Assur temple ritual, day 18 - the king purified, the table set, salt and incense, kispu and calves** (SAA 20 001 o)
- The king handling the bull's horn and the fat compares with Ps 118:27 (bind the festal offering to the horns of the altar) and Lev 4:7, 8:15.
- Table set before the god with bread compares with Exod 25:23-30 and Lev 24:5-9 (showbread); salt on the offering with Lev 2:13.
- King officiating at the sanctuary: compare 1 Kgs 8:62-64, 9:25, and the censure of Uzziah, 2 Chr 26:16-21.

**Assur temple ritual - Aššur and the gods go to Bīt-Dagan; offerings in the palace courtyard; mouth-washing on day 23** (SAA 20 001 r)
- A procession of the god with his entourage between shrines: compare Ps 68:25-28, Ps 24, and the ark's procession 2 Sam 6:12-19; 1 Kgs 8:1-6.
- Mouth-washing of cult images compares with the prophetic polemic Isa 44:9-20, Jer 10:3-5 and Ps 115:4-8 (mouths that do not speak).

**Assur temple ritual, day 8 - the king kisses the ground, the god goes to Bīt-Adad, incantations recited** (SAA 20 011 o, SAA 20 011 b.e, SAA 20 011 r)
- Kissing the ground before the god: compare 1 Kgs 19:18 and Hos 13:2 (kissing calves); Ps 2:12.

**Assur temple ritual, days 17-21 - sacrifices before the god's weapons and chariot, the god seated on the Dais of Destinies** (SAA 20 010 o, SAA 20 010 b.e, SAA 20 010 r)
- Making the god's face shine compares with the priestly blessing Num 6:25 and Ps 80:4, 8, 20; Ps 67:2.
- Seating the god on the dais of destinies: compare 1 Kgs 8:6-13 (the ark brought to its place) and Ps 132:8.

**Tākultu ritual - spoken formulae for salt, purification, incense, bread, wine and the kissing of feet** (SAA 20 037 o, SAA 20 037 r)
- Morning and evening offerings with invocation compare with Num 28:3-8 (tamid) and Ps 141:2.
- The bread on the table with salt: Lev 2:13 and Lev 24:5-9.

**Ritual before Aššur and the Lady of the Mountain - libations, rams, kispu, dust on the king's head, dancing loaves** (SAA 20 021 o, SAA 20 021 r)
- Dust on the head compares with Josh 7:6, 1 Sam 4:12, Lam 2:10, Neh 9:1.
- Kamānu-cakes: compare the kawwānîm baked for the Queen of Heaven, Jer 7:18 and 44:19; the raising of loaves may compare with the wave offering (tenûpâ), Lev 7:30, 23:17-20.

**Nisan ritual at the temple of Assyrian Ištar - early-morning and evening rites, singers, colophon** (SAA 20 017 o, SAA 20 017 r)
- Compare the Levitical singers 1 Chr 25 and 2 Chr 29:25-30.

**Ritual for Gula and Šarrat-ēqi - the banquet hosts, exchange, hair burned, kispu, cakes before Šamaš** (SAA 20 030 o, SAA 20 030 r)
- Hair cut and burned compares with the Nazirite's hair put in the fire under the peace offering, Num 6:18.
- Prayer for name and seed: compare 1 Sam 24:22, Isa 56:5, 66:22; Ruth 4:10.
- Kamānu-cakes: Jer 7:18, 44:19.

**Duties of the Aššur temple personnel - who bears responsibility for what** (SAA 20 050 o.i, SAA 20 050 o.ii, SAA 20 050 r.i, SAA 20 050 r.ii)
- Compare the Levitical duty rosters Num 3:25-37, 4:4-33; 1 Chr 9:17-32 (gatekeepers, utensils, flour, oil, incense, showbread); 1 Chr 23:28-32; 26.

**Cups established by Shalmaneser; officials and priests of the Aššur temple; an order of Sennacherib** (SAA 20 051 o.i, SAA 20 051 o.ii, SAA 20 051 r.i, SAA 20 051 r.ii)
- Kings ordering temple personnel: compare David's ordering of priests, Levites and singers, 1 Chr 23-26, and Hezekiah 2 Chr 31:2.

**List of penitential psalms (eršahunga) to Ea and other gods** (SAA 20 014)
- Compare the Psalm headings and lists of liturgical songs, e.g. Ps 120-134 (Songs of Ascents) and the penitential Psalms 6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143.

**Tākultu of Sennacherib - gods of the Aššur temple and of the temples of Assur, gates and braziers** (SAA 20 038 o.i, SAA 20 038 o.ii, SAA 20 038 o.iii, SAA 20 038 o.iv)
- A god-list grouped by sanctuaries: compare 2 Kgs 17:29-31 (each nation's gods in its cities) and 2 Kgs 23:4-13 (Josiah removes the vessels for Baal, Asherah and the host of heaven).

**Tākultu of Sennacherib - heaven and earth asked to receive and bless; blessings for Sennacherib and the meal-sharers** (SAA 20 038 o.v, SAA 20 038 r.i, SAA 20 038 r.ii, SAA 20 038 r.iii, SAA 20 038 r.iv)
- Compare Ps 72:1-17 and Ps 20:2-6 for blessings on the king, and 1 Kgs 8:66.
- A god called 'He hears prayer': compare Ps 65:3 ('O you who hear prayer') and the name Ishmael, Gen 16:11.

**God-list fragment with Humbaba and the Ištar of Egypt** (SAA 20 039)
- Foreign gods given cult in the imperial capital: compare 2 Kgs 16:10-16 and 1 Kgs 11:5-8.

**Calendar of laments (eršemma) and hand-lifting prayers for Aššur and Mullissu, Šabāṭ-Addar to Nisan** (SAA 20 012 o, SAA 20 012 r)
- Psalm superscriptions with liturgical assignment compare with Ps 92 ('for the sabbath day'), Ps 38 and 70 (lehazkir), and the Levites' daily song (Mishnah Tamid 7:4; 1 Chr 16:4-7, 37-42).

**Laments and penitential psalms of Aššur 'for removing the enemy', day by day to each god** (SAA 20 013 o, SAA 20 013 r)
- Communal lament to remove an enemy: compare 2 Chr 20:3-19, Ps 44, 74, 79, 83; 'How long?' Ps 13:2-3, 79:5, 89:47.

**Funerary ritual for a royal woman - the bed displayed, feet washed, cedar burned, tables for Antu, Gilgameš and the boatmen** (SAA 20 034 o, SAA 20 034 b.e, SAA 20 034 r)
- Funeral burnings for royalty: 2 Chr 16:14, 21:19, Jer 34:5.
- Mourners lacerating themselves: forbidden in Lev 19:28, 21:5, Deut 14:1; practised Jer 16:6, 41:5; professional women mourners Jer 9:16-19.
- Feet of the dead washed and the body displayed: compare Gen 50:2-3; 2 Sam 3:31-34 (the king follows the bier).

**Tākultu (Assur version) - gods of the temples, gods named at the sun's and moon's sacrifices, Nineveh's gods; blessings** (SAA 20 040 o.i, SAA 20 040 o.ii, SAA 20 040 o.iii, SAA 20 040 o.iv, SAA 20 040 o.v, SAA 20 040 o.vi)
- Gods addressed as 'hearer of prayer': Ps 65:3; the night-gods and astral cult: 2 Kgs 23:5, Jer 8:2.

**Tākultu (Assur version) - gods of Kurbail, Arbela, Tuʾe and foreign cities; heaven, the four winds and the land** (SAA 20 040 r.i, SAA 20 040 r.ii, SAA 20 040 r.iii)
- Gods of many cities and nations at the imperial table compare with 2 Kgs 17:29-33 and 18:34.

**Tākultu (Assur version) - blessings for the king; gods of Esagil; sacrifices before the stars; colophon of the chief scribe** (SAA 20 040 r.iv, SAA 20 040 r.v, SAA 20 040 r.vi)
- Sacrifice to the stars: 2 Kgs 21:3-5, 23:4-5, 12 (altars to the host of heaven in the temple courts), Jer 8:2, 19:13, Zeph 1:5, Deut 4:19.
- Opening gates for the god: Ps 24:7-10.

**Ritual of Šarrat-nipha - the goddess brought to the bath-house** (SAA 20 022)
- Ritual bathing compares with the priestly washings at the laver, Exod 30:17-21, and Lev 16:4, 24.

**Ištar ritual - the king's meal before the goddess, the sīru brought in and led seven times by the singers** (SAA 20 016 o.i)
- Sevenfold procession: Josh 6:3-16; the gesture of humility compares with 1 Kgs 18:42 and Ps 95:6.

**Ištar ritual - braziers, bulls, cakes danced on the table, 'Ištar lady of heaven' sung** (SAA 20 016 r.iv)
- Cakes, incense and libations to the 'Queen of Heaven': Jer 7:18, 44:17-19, 25.

**Tukulti-Ninurta's rite for the Lady of the River - tent on the bank, metals, strewn offerings and hymns to each god** (SAA 20 025 o)
- The list of metals compares with Num 31:22-23 (gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead passed through fire).
- Fat portions offered: Lev 3:3-5, 7:30-31.

**Tukulti-Ninurta's rite for the Lady of the River - the client released, his evil loosened, hymns to Bēlet-ili and Ea's spouse** (SAA 20 025 r)
- Release from the god's anger compares with Ps 6:2, 38:2 and the penitential Ps 51; the client's 'seed' with Ps 112:2.

**A rite led by the singer for the sacrificer - seated on fleeces, hands bound, offering graded by rank** (SAA 20 031 o, SAA 20 031 r)
- Offerings graded by means: Lev 5:7-13, 12:8, 14:21-22 (turtledoves for the poor; here inverted: the prince offers a turtledove as burnt offering).
- The sun god who opens darkness and treads the wicked: Mal 3:20 (4:2-3); Ps 37:6.

**Protocol of the king's banquet - officials' entry, braziers, towels, hand-water, torches at sunset, the cups** (SAA 20 033 o.i, SAA 20 033 o.ii, SAA 20 033 r.i)
- Compare Solomon's table and attendants, 1 Kgs 10:5 (2 Chr 9:4); Nehemiah as cupbearer, Neh 2:1; the banquets of Esth 1:5-8 and Dan 5:1-4; the brazier in the winter house, Jer 36:22.

**War ritual - the god-impersonators face the enemy, the king bends the bow before Šamaš, arrows shot, the enemy conquered** (SAA 20 018 o, SAA 20 018 r)
- The arrow of victory: Elisha has king Joash shoot and strike with arrows, 2 Kgs 13:15-19; arrows in war divination, Ezek 21:26 (21:21).
- Ritual before battle: Num 10:9, 35; 1 Sam 7:9-10; Deut 20:2-4; Ps 20.

**Tukulti-Ninurta I's nāṭu rite for Sîn (SAA 20 26)** (SAA 20 026 o:1-l.e:2)
- The repeated strew-offering, libation and song at each station recalls the psalm-singing at sacrifices in 2 Chr 29:27-28.

**Tukulti-Ninurta I's nāṭu rite for the Lady of the Mountain, in a tent by the river (SAA 20 24)** (SAA 20 024 o:1-r:45')
- A rite in a tent pitched for a deity can be set beside the tent of meeting (Exod 33:7-11).

**Tukulti-Ninurta I's rite for Nusku in the temple of Sîn (SAA 20 27)** (SAA 20 027 o:1-r:41')
- Seven pure men (r:31') and messengers kept within the gate while bread, meat and water are consumed (r:35'); compare the purity rules for a sacred meal, Lev 7:19-21.

**Fire rite before Aššur on the evening of the 16th (SAA 20 8)** (SAA 20 008 1'-14')
- A ram burnt on a brazier before the god in the evening: compare the evening burnt offering (Exod 29:38-42).

**Divine directory of Assur, part 1 (gods in the Aššur temple and the other temples) (SAA 20 49)** (SAA 20 049 1-119)
- Tammuz worshipped in the temple of the goddess: compare the women weeping for Tammuz at the temple gate, Ezek 8:14.
- Justice and Truth as attendants of the god: compare Ps 85:11-14 and Ps 89:15.

**Divine directory of Assur, part 2 (gates, city guardians, temple names, ziggurats, colophon) (SAA 20 49)** (SAA 20 049 120-201)
- A temple called 'house where one weeps for the wronged' (line 170) and 'house of the guardian of graves' (175): compare the temple as place of the oppressed's cry, Ps 9:10-13.

**Nabonidus' impiety, Marduk's anger and pity, and the call of Cyrus (Cyrus Cylinder 1-19)** (Cyrus II 01 1-19)
- Marduk grasps Cyrus' hand and calls his name: Isa 45:1-4 ('Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped ... I call you by your name'); Isa 44:28 ('my shepherd').
- The god stirs up and leads Cyrus: Isa 41:2-3, 41:25, Ezra 1:1 (YHWH stirred up the spirit of Cyrus); 2 Chr 36:22-23.
- God searches the earth for one after his heart: 1 Sam 13:14; 2 Chr 16:9.
- Peaceful surrender of Babylon and the fall of its last king: Dan 5:30-31; Isa 47.

**Cyrus' titles, peace in Babylon, return of the gods and peoples (Cyrus Cylinder 20-36)** (Cyrus II 01 20-36)
- Return of the exiles and of the temple vessels under Cyrus: Ezra 1:1-11, Ezra 6:3-5, 2 Chr 36:22-23; Isa 44:28, 45:13.
- The cylinder's return of gods to their sanctuaries, beside the return of the vessels of YHWH's house (Ezra 1:7-11) and the restoration of Jerusalem (Isa 44:26-28).
- Babylon's fall to Cyrus prophesied: Jer 25:11-12 (seventy years then punish Babylon), Jer 51; Isa 45:1-3.
- Kings bring tribute and lick the dust of the feet: Isa 49:23, Ps 72:9-11.

**Offerings increased, the Imgur-Enlil wall rebuilt, Ashurbanipal's inscription found (Cyrus Cylinder 37-46)** (Cyrus II 01 37-46)
- Rebuilding Babylon's wall here; rebuilding Jerusalem's wall and gates in Neh 2-6.

**Sennacherib's titles and world rule (Sennacherib 22 i 1-19)** (Sennacherib 022 i:1-19)
- The Assyrian king's boast of world conquest: Isa 10:13-14 and 2 Kgs 19:11-13.

**First campaign against Merodach-baladan and the Arameans (Sennacherib 22 i 20-64)** (Sennacherib 022 i:20-64)
- Merodach-baladan is the Babylonian who sends envoys to Hezekiah: 2 Kgs 20:12-19, Isa 39.
- The Hagarites (Hagaranu) and Nabateans appear among Arab and Aramean tribes: 1 Chr 5:10,19-20; Gen 25:13 (Nebaioth).

**Second campaign to the Kassites, Ellipi and the Medes (Sennacherib 22 i 65 - ii 36)** (Sennacherib 022 i:65-ii:36)
- Assyrian resettlement of conquered peoples in other lands: 2 Kgs 17:6, 17:24.

**Third campaign, part 1 - Lulî of Sidon, the tribute of the western kings, Ṣidqâ of Ashkelon (Sennacherib 22 ii 37-72)** (Sennacherib 022 ii:37-72)
- Moab, Ammon, Edom, Ashdod, Sidon and Tyre in the prophets' oracles of the Assyrian age: Isa 15-16, 20, 23; Amos 1:6-2:3.
- A god's statue carried off with the deported king: Jer 48:7 (Chemosh into exile), Jer 49:3, Isa 46:1-2.
- Joppa, Bene-berak, Azor and Beth-Dagon: Josh 19:45-46 (Dan's allotment), Josh 15:41.

**Third campaign, part 2 - Ekron, the Egyptians at Eltekeh, Hezekiah shut up in Jerusalem (Sennacherib 22 ii 73 - iii 49)** (Sennacherib 022 ii:73-iii:49)
- 2 Kgs 18:13-16: Sennacherib takes all the fortified cities of Judah; Hezekiah pays 300 talents of silver and 30 talents of gold (the gold figure agrees). Also Isa 36:1, 2 Chr 32:1-9.
- 2 Kgs 18:17-19:37 and Isa 36-37: the Rabshakeh at Jerusalem, Hezekiah's prayer, the angel striking the camp, Sennacherib's return to Nineveh; the prism records no capture of Jerusalem.
- 2 Kgs 19:9 and Isa 37:9: Tirhakah king of Kush marches out; Isa 30:1-7, 31:1-3, 36:6 (Egypt a broken reed) condemn reliance on Egypt.
- Isa 1:7-9: daughter Zion left 'like a booth in a vineyard, like a besieged city'; Isa 10:28-32 the Assyrian advance; Mic 1:10-16 the towns of the Shephelah (Lachish).
- Lachish is not named in this prism; its siege is shown on Sennacherib's palace reliefs. Compare 2 Kgs 18:14,17, 19:8 (Sennacherib at Lachish) and 2 Chr 32:9.
- 2 Chr 32:2-5,30: Hezekiah strengthens Jerusalem's defences and water supply; 2 Chr 32:23 gifts brought to Hezekiah.

**Fourth campaign to Bīt-Yakin; Merodach-baladan flees with his gods by sea (Sennacherib 22 iii 50-74)** (Sennacherib 022 iii:50-74)
- Gods loaded and carried away as a burden: Isa 46:1-2 (Bel bows, Nebo stoops, their images on beasts).

**Fifth campaign to Mount Nipur and Ukku (Sennacherib 22 iii 75 - iv 31)** (Sennacherib 022 iii:75-iv:31)
- Though you build your nest high as the eagle's, I will bring you down: Obad 1:3-4, Jer 49:16.
- The Assyrian boast of climbing the heights of the mountains: 2 Kgs 19:23, Isa 37:24.

**Sixth campaign across the sea to Nagitu in Elam; Šūzubu captured (Sennacherib 22 iv 32-53)** (Sennacherib 022 iv:32-53)
- Ships of Hatti (western shipwrights) on the Gulf: compare Solomon's fleet with Phoenician sailors, 1 Kgs 9:26-28.

**Seventh campaign against Elam; the Elamite king dies before his time (Sennacherib 22 iv 54 - v 16)** (Sennacherib 022 iv:54-v:16)
- A tyrant cut off before his day: Ps 55:24, Job 22:16, Eccl 7:17; Sennacherib's own death in 2 Kgs 19:37.

**Eighth campaign - Babylon's bribe to Elam and the battle of Halule (Sennacherib 22 v 17 - vi 35)** (Sennacherib 022 v:17-vi:35)
- Armies as numerous as locusts: Judg 6:5, 7:12; Nah 3:15-17; Joel 2:1-11.
- Hearts melt and knees give way before the conqueror: Nah 2:11, Isa 13:7-8.
- Treasures of the temple sent to buy a foreign ally: 1 Kgs 15:18-19, 2 Kgs 16:8.

**The rear palace (ekal kutalli) at Nineveh; blessing and curse for a future king (Sennacherib 22 vi 36-85B)** (Sennacherib 022 vi:36-85B)
- Cedar-built palace: 1 Kgs 7:1-12 (House of the Forest of Lebanon); Jer 22:14-15.

**Esarhaddon chosen over his elder brothers; their revolt; his march on Nineveh (Esarhaddon 1 i 1 - ii 11)** (Esarhaddon 001 i:1-ii:11)
- 2 Kgs 19:37 and Isa 37:38: Sennacherib's sons Adrammelech and Sharezer kill him and escape to the land of Ararat; Esarhaddon his son reigns in his place. Here the brothers fight in Nineveh and flee to an unknown land, and the battle is in Hanigalbat (i:70).
- The youngest son chosen over his brothers: David (1 Sam 16:6-13), Solomon over Adonijah (1 Kgs 1), Joseph and his brothers' hatred (Gen 37:4-11).
- The king tears his garment on hearing bad news: 2 Kgs 19:1, 22:11.
- Prophetic oracles of encouragement before battle: 1 Kgs 22:6, 2 Kgs 19:6-7 (Isaiah's 'do not be afraid').

**Esarhaddon's titles, the restorer of the gods, and the gifts of the gods (Esarhaddon 1 ii 12-39)** (Esarhaddon 001 ii:12-39)
- The king who restores the deported gods: compare Cyrus' return of the vessels and exiles, Ezra 1:7-11.

**Nabû-zēr-kitti-līšir breaks his oath, flees to Elam and is killed there (Esarhaddon 1 ii 40-64)** (Esarhaddon 001 ii:40-64)
- 2 Kgs 19:7: 'I will make him fall by the sword in his own land' (of Sennacherib); Ezek 17:15-19 (the king who broke his oath will die in Babylon).

**Sidon destroyed, Abdi-milkutti and Sanduarri beheaded, Arzâ by the Brook of Egypt (Esarhaddon 1 ii 65 - iii 42)** (Esarhaddon 001 ii:65-iii:42)
- Tyre and Sidon who trusted in the sea: Isa 23, Ezek 26-28 (Tyre cast into the midst of the sea), Zech 9:2-4.
- Fishermen and hooks to catch the people like fish: Hab 1:14-17, Amos 4:2, Ezek 29:4.
- Heads displayed at the gate: 2 Kgs 10:7-8; Saul's head and body displayed, 1 Sam 31:9-10.

**Cimmerians, Hilakku, Mannea, Bīt-Dakkūri and Gambulu (Esarhaddon 1 iii 43-83)** (Esarhaddon 001 iii:43-83)
- Gomer (the Cimmerians) among the northern hordes: Gen 10:2-3, Ezek 38:6.

**The gods of the Arabs returned to Hazael; Tabūa made queen; Uabu caged at the gate (Esarhaddon 1 iv 1-31)** (Esarhaddon 001 iv:1-31)
- The queen of Sheba and Arabian queens: 1 Kgs 10:1-13; Dumah/Adummatu among Ishmael's sons, Gen 25:14, Isa 21:11.
- Captured idols returned: compare the Philistines returning the ark, 1 Sam 6.

**Median chiefs, Patušarri, and the desert land of Bāzu (Esarhaddon 1 iv 32-77)** (Esarhaddon 001 iv:32-77)
- Deut 8:15: the great and terrible wilderness with fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground; Isa 30:6.

**Kings of the sea tremble; enemies scattered; envoys sue for peace (Esarhaddon 1 iv 78 - v 39)** (Esarhaddon 001 iv:78-v:39)
- Ships of Tarshish and the coastlands tremble: Isa 23:1-2, Ezek 26:15-18.

**The arsenal palace of Nineveh, built with cedars hauled by twenty-two western kings including Manasseh (Esarhaddon 1 v 40 - vi 75G)** (Esarhaddon 001 v:40-vi:75G)
- Manasseh as Assyrian vassal: 2 Kgs 21:1-18; 2 Chr 33:11-13 (taken to Babylon in fetters, then restored).
- Cedars of Lebanon hauled by vassal kings for a building: 1 Kgs 5:6-18 (Hiram), Ezra 3:7, Isa 14:8 (no woodcutter comes up).
- Anointing the head with oil at a feast: Ps 23:5, Ps 133:2.

**Babylon's sin, Marduk's anger, the flood, and seventy years reduced to eleven (Esarhaddon 104 i 1 - ii 9)** (Esarhaddon 104 i:1-ii:9)
- Seventy years of desolation for Judah and Babylon: Jer 25:11-12, Jer 29:10, 2 Chr 36:21, Zech 1:12, Dan 9:2; seventy years for Tyre, Isa 23:15-17.
- God's anger shortened for mercy's sake: Isa 54:7-8 ('for a brief moment I forsook you'), Ps 30:6, Mark 13:20; Dan 9:24 reinterprets the seventy years.
- The glory of God departs the sinful city: Ezek 10:18-19, 11:22-23; the city sinned by lying and false speech, Jer 9:2-8.
- Temple treasure sent to a foreign king: 2 Kgs 16:8, 18:15-16.

**Esarhaddon chosen to rebuild; signs, Ea's wisdom, extispicy; the king carries the basket and rebuilds Esagil (Esarhaddon 104 ii 10 - iii 53)** (Esarhaddon 104 ii:10-iii:53)
- Cyrus' charge to rebuild Jerusalem's temple (Ezra 1:2-4, 6:3-5; Isa 44:28) beside Marduk's charge to Esarhaddon.
- Rebuilding on the old foundations: Ezra 3:3,10-12, 5:15, 6:7 ('build the house of God on its site').
- The sanctuary made after a heavenly pattern: Exod 25:9,40; 1 Chr 28:11-19.
- The king himself carrying the basket and the people with free-will offerings: 1 Chr 29:1-9; Hag 1:8.

**The temple adorned, the gods renewed, Babylon's citizens freed and led home (Esarhaddon 104 iv 1 - v 38)** (Esarhaddon 104 iv:1-v:38)
- Jer 29:5-7: build houses and live in them, plant gardens; Isa 65:21, Amos 9:14 (rebuild ruined cities, plant vineyards).
- Release of slaves and return of people to their land: Lev 25:10 (deror), Jer 34:8-17, Isa 61:1.
- Returnees gathered from where they were scattered: Ezra 2:1, Neh 7:6; Isa 43:5-7.
- The temple vessels and images renewed: compare Ezra 1:7-11 (vessels returned) and Isa 46:1-7 (idols that must be carried).

**Prayers for the king's reign, the inscribed stones, and the curse on whoever annuls Babylon's privilege (Esarhaddon 104 vi 1 - vii 46)** (Esarhaddon 104 vi:1-vii:46)
- A king's reign as life-giving: Ps 72:6-7,16 (like rain on the mown grass), 2 Sam 23:3-4.
- Old age and long reign for the righteous king: Ps 21:5, 61:7, Prov 16:31.

**Babylon's sin and Marduk's anger; seventy years turned to eleven (Esarhaddon 105 i 1 - ii 22)** (Esarhaddon 105 i:1-ii:22)
- Jer 25:11-12 and 29:10 (seventy years for Babylon), 2 Chr 36:20-23 (the land's sabbaths, then Cyrus), Dan 9:2,24.
- Ezek 10:18-19 and 11:22-23: the glory departs the temple and city.

**Esarhaddon chosen; signs and extispicy; the basket and the foundation of Esagil (Esarhaddon 105 ii 23 - iv 41)** (Esarhaddon 105 ii:23-iv:41)
- Ezra 3:10-13 and 6:3-7: the foundation of the house of God laid on its old site.

**Esagil completed, deep foundation, gods' images, personnel, Etemenanki and the wall; the gods of the lands and Babylon's citizens restored (Esarhaddon 105 v 1 - vii 43)** (Esarhaddon 105 v:1-vii:43)
- Restoration of temple personnel and singers: Ezra 2:40-42, 3:10-11, Neh 12:27-47; restored daily offerings, Ezra 3:3-5.
- Jer 29:5 (build houses, plant gardens) and Isa 65:21.
- The tower whose top is in heaven (Etemenanki, 'House, foundation of heaven and earth'): Gen 11:4.

**Prayers for the king, the inscribed foundation stones, and the curse (Esarhaddon 105 viii 1 - x 36)** (Esarhaddon 105 viii:1-x:36)
- Ps 72:6-7,16; 2 Sam 23:4 (the righteous ruler like rain on the grass).

**Babylon stele: the Assyrian king's evil against Babylon and Marduk's 21 years in Assur (Nabonidus 3 col. i)** (Nabonidus 03 i)
- Compare 2 Kgs 19:37 and Isa 37:38 (Sennacherib killed by his sons) and 2 Chr 32:21.
- The term of divine anger fulfilled: Jer 25:11-12; 29:10; Dan 9:2; 2 Chr 36:21; Isa 40:2.
- God's image taken captive: 1 Sam 4-5 (the ark at Ashdod); Jer 48:7; 49:3 (Chemosh and Milcom go into exile).

**Babylon stele: Marduk gives Nabopolassar the Medes as ally; Assyria's shrines destroyed (Nabonidus 3 col. ii)** (Nabonidus 03 ii)
- The Medes as God's instrument against an empire: Isa 13:17; Jer 51:11, 28.
- King sleeping on the ground: 2 Sam 12:16 (David lies on the ground); 2 Sam 13:31. The flood-like enemy: Isa 8:7-8; Dan 9:26; 11:10.

**Babylon stele: Ištar of Uruk departs in anger and her image is restored (Nabonidus 3 col. iii)** (Nabonidus 03 iii)
- Improper image in the sanctuary removed: 2 Kgs 21:7; 23:6 (the Asherah taken out of the temple); Ezek 8:3-5 (the image of jealousy).
- The seven lions of Ištar's throne: 1 Kgs 10:19-20 (lions on Solomon's throne).

**Babylon stele: Anunītu restored by Neriglissar; the child-king Lābāši-Marduk (Nabonidus 3 col. iv)** (Nabonidus 03 iv)
- Woe to the land whose king is a child: Eccl 10:16; Isa 3:4, 12.
- Dying 'when his days were fulfilled': 2 Sam 7:12; 1 Chr 17:11.

**Babylon stele: Nabonidus brought to the palace and acclaimed king (Nabonidus 3 col. v)** (Nabonidus 03 v)
- Evil-merodach (Amēl-Marduk) son of Nebuchadnezzar: 2 Kgs 25:27; Jer 52:31.
- Acclamation and obeisance to the new king: 1 Kgs 1:39-40; Ps 72:9-11.

**Babylon stele: the dream of the great star and the moon, and Nebuchadnezzar in the dream (Nabonidus 3 col. vi)** (Nabonidus 03 vi)
- Nebuchadnezzar's dreams and their interpretation: Dan 2 and 4; a king of Babylon troubled by heavenly signs, Dan 5. The 'young man' standing beside the dreamer: Dan 8:15-17; 10:5-11; Zech 1:8-11.
- Being called by name in revelation: 1 Sam 3:4-10; Isa 43:1; 45:3-4 (Cyrus called by name).

**Babylon stele: offerings to the stars, Gula's face turned, prayer to Marduk (Nabonidus 3 col. vii)** (Nabonidus 03 vii)
- A king lifted from obscurity who did not seek the throne: 1 Sam 9:21; 10:22; Ps 78:70-72; Isa 45:4-5 ('I call you by name though you do not know me', to Cyrus).
- Astral offerings for long life contrast Deut 4:19; 2 Kgs 23:5; Jer 7:18. Hezekiah granted added years: 2 Kgs 20:1-6; Isa 38.
- The Prayer of Nabonidus (4Q242) and Dan 4:31-34 (the king healed and restored after praying).

**Babylon stele: a throne for Ea, garments for the gods, silver-clad cedar doors (Nabonidus 3 col. viii)** (Nabonidus 03 viii)
- Temple doors of olivewood or cypress overlaid with gold: 1 Kgs 6:31-35; the bronze serpent in the temple: 2 Kgs 18:4.

**Babylon stele: New Year gifts of silver and gold, 2,850 captives for the gods, journeys to Uruk, Larsa and Ur (Nabonidus 3 col. ix)** (Nabonidus 03 ix)
- Captives made temple servants: Josh 9:23-27 (Gibeonites as hewers of wood for the house of God); Ezra 8:20 (Nethinim).
- Kings' gifts of silver and gold to the temple: 1 Kgs 7:51; Ezra 7:15-16; Hag 2:8.

**Babylon stele: Ehulhul of Harran desolate for 54 years; Sîn returns at the appointed time (Nabonidus 3 col. x)** (Nabonidus 03 x)
- A fixed term of desolation before the god returns: Jer 25:11-12; 29:10; Zech 1:12 ('these seventy years'); Ezek 43:1-5 (the glory returns to the temple); Hag 1:4.
- Compare 'the God of heaven stirred up' and the return of temple vessels in Ezra 1:7-11.

**Babylon stele: the favourable extispicy (Nabonidus 3 col. xi)** (Nabonidus 03 xi)
- Liver divination by the king of Babylon: Ezek 21:21 (Heb 21:26), 'he looked at the liver'.

**Sippar cylinder: titulary; destined for kingship in his mother's womb (Nabonidus 28 i 1-6)** (Nabonidus 28 i:1-6)
- Called from the womb: Jer 1:5; Isa 44:2, 24; 49:1, 5; Ps 22:10-11; Gal 1:15.

**Sippar cylinder: Sîn's anger at Harran; the dream of Marduk and Sîn; Cyrus scatters the Medes (Nabonidus 28 i 7-33)** (Nabonidus 28 i:7-33)
- Cyrus raised by God to overthrow nations: Isa 41:2, 25; 44:28; 45:1-4 ('my shepherd', 'his anointed'); Ezra 1:1-2. Note Marduk calls him 'his young servant' (ardušu ṣehru).
- Dan 2:1; 4:2 and 7:15, 28 (the king troubled and pale at a dream, 'my face was changed').
- A temple rebuilt at divine command in a dream: Hag 1:2-8; Zech 4:9.

**Sippar cylinder: Ehulhul rebuilt on Ashurbanipal's foundation; Sîn's return and prayer (Nabonidus 28 i 34-ii 46)** (Nabonidus 28 i:34-43, Nabonidus 28 ii:1-46)
- Temple foundations relaid in joy: Ezra 3:10-13; Solomon's cedar from Lebanon, 1 Kgs 5:6-10; 6:15-18.
- Gaza at the border of Egypt as the southwestern limit: Gen 10:19; 1 Kgs 5:4 (Heb 4:24, from Tiphsah to Gaza).

**Sippar cylinder: Ebabbar of Sippar rebuilt on Naram-Sin's foundation, 3,200 years old (Nabonidus 28 ii 47-iii 21)** (Nabonidus 28 ii:47-65, Nabonidus 28 iii:1-21)
- The temple plan shown to the builder: Exod 25:9, 40; 1 Chr 28:11-19; Ezek 40-43.
- Founding exactly on the old site: Ezra 2:68; 3:3 ('on its foundations', al-mekhonotav); 6:7.

**Sippar cylinder: Eulmaš of Anunītu rebuilt; charge to a future king (Nabonidus 28 iii 22-51)** (Nabonidus 28 iii:22-51)
- A future king who finds the old record: 2 Kgs 22:8-13 (the book found in the temple); Ezra 6:1-3 (Cyrus' decree found in the archive).

**Harran stele: Sîn's great deed; the only son named king; the sin of Babylon (Nabonidus 47 i 1-22)** (Nabonidus 47 i:1-22)
- Prophetic indictment of priests and people who forget torah and speak lies: Hos 4:1-6; Jer 7:8-9; 9:2-5; Ezek 22:26.
- Devouring one another: Gal 5:15; Isa 9:19-20 (each eats the flesh of his arm); Mic 3:2-3.
- God gives the nations into the king's hand: Jer 27:6; Dan 2:37-38.

**Harran stele: ten years in Tema and the Arabian oases (Nabonidus 47 i 23-ii 2)** (Nabonidus 47 i:23-48, Nabonidus 47 ii:1-2)
- Dan 4:22, 29-30 (Aram. 4:25, 32-33): the king driven away from men for 'seven times'; the Prayer of Nabonidus (4Q242) sets the king's illness and healing in Tema.
- Tema, Dedan and the Arabian caravans: Isa 21:13-14; Jer 25:23; Gen 25:15. Yathrib (Medina) is named in Q 33:13.

**Harran stele: hymn to Sîn, lord of the gods (Nabonidus 47 ii 3-42)** (Nabonidus 47 ii:3-42)
- God's word does not return void and is not spoken twice: Num 23:19; Isa 45:23; 55:11; Ps 62:12 ('once God has spoken, twice I heard').
- God plants and uproots nations at will: Jer 18:7-10; Dan 2:21; 4:17; Q 3:26.
- Mountains and the deep quake before God: Ps 29:5-9; 114:4-7; Hab 3:6, 10.

**Harran stele: return from Tema, homage of kings, Ehulhul completed, charge to future king (Nabonidus 47 iii)** (Nabonidus 47 iii)

**Gilgameš I (SpTU 4, 122): the trapper's report and Šamhat's invitation to Uruk** (GKAB P273250)

**Šurpu III (SpTU 2 14): the litany of 'oaths' (māmītu) each released by the exorcist of the gods, Asalluhi** (GKAB P348619)
- Do not eat with the wicked / keep no company with the sinner: Ps 1:1, Ps 101:5-7, Prov 23:6, 1 Cor 5:11; Achan's ḥerem contaminates all Israel: Josh 7.
- Hands unwashed and lifted in prayer: Ps 24:3-4, Ps 26:6, Isa 1:15-16; a covenant friend killed: 2 Sam 3:27, 2 Sam 20:9-10; taking God's name in vain: Exod 20:7.

**Šurpu VIII (SpTU 2 15): curses of field and garden, boundary stone, ship and quay, broken table, cut hem, small and large measures** (GKAB P348620)

- Cursing father and mother: Exod 21:17, Lev 20:9, Prov 20:20.

**House-building ritual (SpTU 2 16 obv.): pots broken at the gates, the brick god Kulla goes down into the house, prayer to Ea and Marduk as builders who decree fates; 'hostile one, go out!'** (GKAB P348621 o.i, GKAB P348621 o.ii)
- Dedication of a new house: Deut 20:5, Ps 30:1 (song for the dedication of the house); a house purified with two birds, cedar and hyssop: Lev 14:49-53.
- Unless YHWH builds the house: Ps 127:1; the Lord draws the plan of life: Ps 139:16.

**House-building ritual (SpTU 2 16 rev.): Kulla escorted to the river bank with provisions and adjured by heaven, earth and the primeval divine pairs never to return** (GKAB P348621 r.i, GKAB P348621 r.ii)
- Primeval gods in pairs as the oldest witnesses: compare Gen 1:2 (tohu and bohu, deep and darkness); heaven and earth called as witnesses: Deut 30:19, Deut 32:1, Isa 1:2.
- The evil sent away 'not to return': Lev 16:22, Zech 5:5-11 (wickedness carried off in a basket to Shinar).

**Ritual to see a ghost and get a decision (SpTU 2 20): oil anointed on the eyes, Namtar made to speak, the Anunnaki talk with you** (GKAB P348625)
- Consulting the dead for a verdict: 1 Sam 28:7-19 (the woman of Endor brings up Samuel), Isa 8:19 (should a people consult the dead for the living?), Isa 29:4 (a voice from the ground like a ghost); forbidden: Deut 18:10-12, Lev 19:31, Lev 20:6,27.
- 'Turned into clay': Job 10:9 ('you made me like clay, will you return me to dust?'), Job 30:19.

**Amulet stones against evil (SpTU 2 22+ obv. i): eye disease, the man who sees flashes ('I belong to Enlil and Ninlil'), the man always afraid, slandered and dreaming of the dead** (GKAB P348627 o.i)

- Terror by night and day: Deut 28:66-67, Ps 91:5-6; amulets on hand and neck: Deut 6:8, Prov 3:3, Prov 6:21.

**Amulet stones (SpTU 2 22+ obv. ii): incantations to Ea, Asalluhi, Šamaš and Sîn as creators; to Gula against the adversary's sorcery; to Marduk for bright days** (GKAB P348627 o.ii)
- Potter-God forming people from clay: Gen 2:7, Job 10:9, Job 33:6, Isa 64:7, Jer 18:6; his mischief returns upon his own head: Ps 7:17, Esth 9:25, Prov 26:27.
- God as shepherd: Ps 23, Ps 80:2; 'stand up for me in my case': Ps 35:1-2,23, Ps 43:1.

**Amulet stones (SpTU 2 22+ rev. i): gift to the exorcist and to Šamaš the judge, 'may my adversary be reconciled, may who spoke evil speak good'; stones to undo the knot of the angry god's heart** (GKAB P348627 r.i)
- When a man's ways please YHWH, he makes even his enemies be at peace with him: Prov 16:7; a gift pacifies anger: Prov 21:14, Gen 32:21; soft answer turns away wrath: Prov 15:1.

**Amulet stones (SpTU 2 22+ rev. ii and edges): for favour, love, against the sin of father and mother, curses turned back, safety in battle, 'I am lapis, I break the mountain'; colophon of Iqīšâ** (GKAB P348627 r.ii, GKAB P348627 b.e, GKAB P348627 l.e..i, GKAB P348627 l.e..ii)

**Šurpu III, second Uruk copy (SpTU 3 70): the māmītu litany, ending with the oaths of the great gods** (GKAB P348673)

- Procession of the deity into the sanctuary with singers and musicians: Ps 68:25-28; 2Sam 6:5, 6:14-15; Ps 118:27 (bind the festal procession with cords to the horns of the altar).
- Cross-dressed cult personnel: Deut 22:5, 23:18-19 (qadesh); 1Kgs 14:24; 2Kgs 23:7.

**Namburbi for a prince whose chariot yoke, pole or lance breaks on the road, or who falls from his chariot (TCL 6, 50)** (GKAB P363722)
- Kings who fall from or die in chariots: 1Kgs 22:34-35; 2Kgs 9:24, 9:27; chariot wheels jammed: Exod 14:25.
- Confession of sins known and unknown: Ps 19:13, 51:5-6.

**Uruk akītu ritual: gods seated right and left of Anu, the king prostrates before Antu, procession of chariots and gods to the akītu house (KAR 132)** (GKAB P369109)
- The LORD goes up with a shout, procession of the King into the sanctuary: Ps 47:6, 68:25; enthroned with 'the host of heaven at his right and his left': 1Kgs 22:19.
- Asherah and the Queen of Heaven in Judah's cult: 2Kgs 21:7, 23:4-7; Jer 44:17-19.

**Anzu I (Uruk copy): 'I will sing of the son of the king of the inhabited world', Ninurta beloved of Mami (SB Anzu I 1-14)** (GKAB Q002769 1-14)
- Sing of the warrior: Exod 15:1; Ps 18; the monster of the sea slain: Isa 27:1, 51:9; Ps 74:13-14.

**Anzu I: before the daises, the rivers dry; Anzu born of the earth; Enlil sets him at the shrine door; he steals the Tablet of Destinies while Enlil bathes (SB Anzu I 15-87)** (GKAB Q002769 15-87)
- The proud one plotting in his heart to ascend above the stars and sit on the mount of assembly: Isa 14:13-14; Ezek 28:2.
- Before there was rain or plants: Gen 2:5-6.

**Anzu I: Anu asks which god will slay Anzu; Adad, Girra and Šara refuse in identical words (SB Anzu I 88-156)** (GKAB Q002769 88-156)
- Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?: Isa 6:8; 1Kgs 22:20-22 (who will entice Ahab?).
- The utterance that turns to clay whom it curses: compare the divine word's power in Isa 55:11.

**Anzu I: Ea's plan; Mami renamed Mistress of All the Gods; she commissions her son Ninurta (SB Anzu I 157-213, colophon)** (GKAB Q002769 157-213)
- Name changed to mark a new role: Gen 17:5, 17:15, 32:29.
- Who will go for us?: Isa 6:8.

**Anzu tablet 2 (Sultantepe): Mami's battle orders to Ninurta, end (GKAB Q002770 1-27)** (GKAB Q002770 1-27)
- Compare Ps 18:14-15 (he sent out his arrows, lightnings) and Hab 3:11.

**Anzu tablet 2 (Sultantepe): the challenge, the darkness and the arrows turned back (GKAB Q002770 28-69)** (GKAB Q002770 28-69)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:43-47 (the champion's taunt and the answer naming his God) and Joel 2:10.

**Anzu tablet 2 (Sultantepe): Sharur's reports, Ea's advice, Ninurta sets out again; colophon (GKAB Q002770 70-155)** (GKAB Q002770 70-155)
- Compare Judg 16:17-19 (the secret of invulnerability found and broken).

**Anzu tablet 3 (Sultantepe): the wings cut, Anzu slain, the tablet recovered; the gods rejoice (GKAB Q002771 1-32)** (GKAB Q002771 1-32)
- Compare Isa 27:1 and Ps 74:13-14; Jer 23:18, 22 (standing in God's council).

**Anzu tablet 3 (Sultantepe): Ninurta's praise and his names in the cult cities (GKAB Q002771 113-181)** (GKAB Q002771 113-181)
- Compare Ps 110:1, Exod 15:11 ('who is like you among the gods?') and Q 59:22-24 (the names of God).

**Milkilu (of Gezer) to the king: the city is safe; 46 girls, 5 boys and 5 servants sent (EA 268)** (EA 268)
- Compare Gen 33:3 (Jacob bows to the ground seven times before Esau) and Ps 72:9-11 (his enemies lick the dust; kings bring gifts).

**The king (Pharaoh) to Intaruta of Akshapa: guard your place, obey Hanni, provision the archers (EA 367)** (EA 367)
- Akshapa is Achshaph of Josh 11:1 and 12:20; the land of Canaan (Kinahhi) is named in the original (o:8): compare Gen 12:5.
- Compare 2 Sam 23:4 and Ps 72:5 (the king like the sun) and Judg 5:31 ('may those who love him be like the sun rising in its might').

**Zishamimi: servant and son for ever; may the gods strike my head if I do not guard your cities (EA 209)** (EA 209)
- Compare 2 Kgs 16:7 ('I am your servant and your son') and the self-curse formula of Ruth 1:17 and 1 Sam 3:17 ('so may God do to me and more').

**Rib-Addi of Byblos: send archers or we die; the land is not plagued; the commissioner Piwuri killed (EA 362)** (EA 362)
- Compare 2 Sam 24:13-15 (plague in the land) and the vassal's word skn with Isa 22:15 (Shebna the sōkēn).

**Ayyab (of Ashtaroth): dust of the king's feet; the man of Hazor has taken three cities (EA 364)** (EA 364)
- The sender's name ʾAyyab is the name of Job (ʾIyyov). Compare Gen 18:27 (Abraham 'I am dust and ashes').
- Hazor attacking its neighbours: compare Josh 11:1-10 (Jabin of Hazor, 'head of all those kingdoms') and Judg 4:2.

**Shuwardata: I killed the Habiru the king's god gave me; Abdi-Heba and I alone fight; Akko and Akshapa came with fifty chariots (EA 366)** (EA 366)
- Abdi-Heba is the ruler of Jerusalem (Urusalim); compare Josh 10:1-5 (Adoni-zedek of Jerusalem leads a coalition of southern kings).
- 'The god gave him into my hand': compare Judg 3:28, 1 Sam 17:46 and Josh 10:8. Akko and Achshaph: Judg 1:31, Josh 11:1.

**Abdi-risha of Enishasi: Etakkama of Qadesh led Hittite troops and set the king's cities on fire (EA 363)** (EA 363)
- Compare 2 Kgs 7:6 (the kings of the Hittites hired against Israel) and Judg 1:8 (a city set on fire).

**Biridiya of Megiddo: I alone plough at Shunem and bring corvée workers; the other mayors do not (EA 365)** (EA 365)
- Hebrew mas, 'forced labour': compare 1 Kgs 5:13-14 (9:15-21), Josh 16:10 and Judg 1:28-35 (Canaanites made forced labour). Shunem: Josh 19:18, 1 Sam 28:4, 2 Kgs 4:8. Megiddo and Shunem in the Jezreel valley.

**Guard the king's land, Puhuru, Qadesh and Kumidu: I am coming with chariots, Cushites, Suteans and Habiru (EA 190)** (EA 190)
- Cushite troops in Canaan: compare 2 Chr 14:9-15 (Zerah the Cushite) and 2 Sam 18:21 (the Cushite runner).

**Abdi-Ashirta of Amurru: clay of your feet, dog of the king's house (EA 061)** (EA 061)
- Compare 2 Kgs 8:13 ('what is your servant, a dog?'), 1 Sam 24:15 and 2 Sam 9:8 ('a dead dog such as I').

**Fragment: I guard the commissioners; they seized Sumur, burned the city and palace (EA 371)** (EA 371)
- Compare 1 Chr 12:33 and Ps 12:3 ('a heart and a heart' / 'not of double heart') for 'I have no other heart'.

**The king to Yidya of Ashkelon: guard the king's place; the king is well like the sun from sunrise to sunset (EA 370)** (EA 370)
- Ashkelon: Judg 1:18, 14:19. Compare Ps 113:3 and Mal 1:11 ('from the rising of the sun to its setting') and Ps 72:8.

**Rib-Addi: the peasants have no life and will desert to the sons of Abdi-Ashirta; Yanhamu the loyal servant (EA 118)** (EA 118)
- Akkadian hupšu is the word of Hebrew ḥopšî ('free, released'): compare Exod 21:2, Deut 15:12 and the lowly ḥopšît of 2 Kgs 15:5.

**Rib-Addi: like a bird in a cage; Abdi-Ashirta tells Ammiya 'kill your lord and be like us'; children sold for food (EA 074)** (EA 074)
- Canaanite kĕlûb, 'bird cage': compare Jer 5:27 ('like a cage full of birds'); and Sennacherib's 'like a bird in a cage' of Hezekiah.
- Compare Neh 5:2-5 (we pledge our sons, daughters, fields for grain); Isa 54:1, 62:4 (the land as a forsaken wife / 'Married').
- Compare 2 Kgs 9-10 and 1 Kgs 16:9-16 (servants conspire and kill their lord); Ps 124:7 (the bird escaped from the snare).

**Rib-Addi: Aziru seized twelve of my men for a ransom of fifty silver; my ships taken; who will love me if I die? (EA 114)** (EA 114)
- Compare Ps 142:5 ('no one cares for my soul') and Ps 88:9, 19 (friends removed far away).
- Ransom of captives: compare Exod 21:30 and Lev 27:2-8 (valuation in silver).

**Rib-Addi: my messenger robbed; give me grain or I will abandon the city; Ummahnu, maid of the Lady of Byblos, prays for the king (EA 083)** (EA 083)
- Compare Jer 29:7 (pray for the welfare of the city) and Ezra 6:10 (prayer for the life of the king); 1 Sam 1:9-11 (a woman praying at the sanctuary).

**Rib-Addi to Amanappa 'my father': come with archers; Abdi-Ashirta says 'kill your lord and join the Habiru' (EA 073)** (EA 073)
- Compare Gen 45:8 (Joseph made 'a father to Pharaoh') and 2 Kgs 5:13, 6:21 ('my father' to a superior).

**Rib-Addi: my city, house and wife urged peace with Abdi-Ashirta's son; returning from Beirut I found my house shut against me (EA 136)** (EA 136)
- Compare 2 Sam 15:13-14 (a king flees as his own city goes over to a rebel) and Job 2:9 (the wife urges giving up).

**Rib-Addi: what is Abdi-Ashirta, the slave, the dog, that he does as he pleases? We cannot go out of Byblos's gate (EA 088)** (EA 088)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:43 ('am I a dog?'), 2 Sam 3:8, 2 Sam 16:9 ('this dead dog') and 2 Kgs 18:27-35 (the besieged city taunted).

**Rib-Addi to the new king: I wrote to your father; Aziru has gathered all the Habiru; send 500 men, 300 Nubians and 50 chariots (EA 132)** (EA 132)
- Nubian (Cushite) troops: compare 2 Sam 18:21 and 2 Chr 12:3 (Shishak's Cushites).

**Rib-Addi: 'guard yourself', the king says, but with what? Aziru took my cattle, the peasants have gone where there is grain (EA 125)** (EA 125)
- Compare Gen 47:13-19 (famine; the people have no bread) and 2 Kgs 6:25.

**Rib-Addi: a deed never done before: Pihura's Suteans killed a Sherdan and took three of my men to Egypt (EA 123)** (EA 123)
- Compare Judg 19:30 ('such a thing has never happened or been seen') and Deut 4:32.
- The Sherdan are among the later Sea Peoples, with the Philistines (Gen 10:14, Amos 9:7).

**Rib-Addi to Amanappa: may Amon give you honour; three years our grain has been seized; Ummahnu, maid of the Lady (EA 086)** (EA 086)
- Compare 2 Sam 21:1 (famine three years) and 1 Kgs 18:1-5 (no grass for the horses).

**Rib-Addi to Amanappa: may Amon and the Lady give you honour; come with help; if you are dead, I am dead (EA 087)** (EA 087)
- Canaanite ʿezrâ, 'help': compare Ps 121:1-2 and Ps 46:2.

**Rib-Addi to Yanhamu: may the Lady of Byblos give you honour before the Sun of the lands; the chief and lords of Ambi are at peace with the enemy (EA 102)** (EA 102)
- The 'lords of the city' (bēlī āli) recall the baʿalê ha-ʿîr of Judg 9:2-3, 46 (Shechem) and Josh 24:11.

**Rib-Addi: Sumur taken; send 300 men, 30 chariots, 100 men of Kush; otherwise there will be no lands of Canaan for the king (EA 131)** (EA 131)
- Compare Jer 16:4-6 and Ps 79:3 (none to bury them); Canaan as a land name: Gen 12:5, Num 34:2.

**Ammunira of Beirut to the king, 'my Sun, my gods, breath of my life': I am the footstool of his feet; I am ready with horses and chariots (EA 141)** (EA 141)
- Compare Lam 4:20 ('the breath of our nostrils, YHWH's anointed') and Ps 110:1 (your enemies your footstool), Ps 99:5, 132:7.

**Ammunira: my eyes shone at the king's tablet; I keep the man of Byblos; his brother gave Rib-Addi's sons to the king's enemies (EA 142)** (EA 142)
- Compare 1 Sam 14:27-29 (his eyes brightened) and 2 Sam 15:10-14 (a usurper seizes the city while the king is away).

**Abimilki of Tyre: you are like the Sun, like Baal in heaven; who lives without the king's breath? Zimrida and Arwad have sworn an oath to seize Tyre (EA 149)** (EA 149)
- Compare Ps 18:14 and Ps 29:3-9 (the Lord thunders in heaven), Lam 4:20 (the breath of our nostrils) and Ps 104:29-30 (you take away their breath, they die).
- Tyre besieged from the sea: Ezek 26-27 and Isa 23. 'To see the king's face': 2 Sam 14:24, 28, 32; Ps 42:3 ('when shall I come and see the face of God?').

**Abimilki: my lord is the Sun who rises over all lands, gives life by his sweet breath, thunders like Baal; the servant who obeys keeps his name for ever (EA 147)** (EA 147)
- Compare Ps 104:2-4, 29-30 and Ps 19:5-7 (the sun going forth; the hymn's Egyptian sun-language), Ps 29:3-9 and Ps 18:14 (the voice of the LORD thunders, the land trembles).
- Compare Jer 1:18 and 15:20 ('walls of bronze'), Lam 4:20 (breath of our nostrils), Deut 30:15-19 and Ps 1 (the obedient keep house and name), Ps 42:3 ('when shall I see the face of God?').

**Abimilki: Tyre is in the midst of the sea without water or wood; news from Canaan: the king of Danuna dead, half of Ugarit's palace burned (EA 151)** (EA 151)
- 'In the midst of the sea': compare Ezek 27:4, 25-27 and 28:2 (Tyre 'in the heart of the seas'). 'I set my face': Jer 42:15, 2 Kgs 12:18. Gifts of 5 talents of bronze: 1 Kgs 7:13-14 (Hiram of Tyre, bronze worker).

**Abimilki, servant of Mayati: Tyre has no wood, water, straw or clay; before the king I was afraid and could not speak (EA 155)** (EA 155)
- Compare Exod 4:10 (slow of speech before Pharaoh), Dan 10:16-17 and Esth 4:11, 5:1-2 (entering before the king).
- Compare Ezek 27:3-9 and Isa 23:1-8 (Tyre's dependence on the sea and the mainland).

**Satatna of Akko to the king, the Sun from heaven: I guard the cities; I send raw glass (EA 235 (+) 327)** (EA 235)
- Compare Job 28:17 (glass beside gold) and the shekel-weights (mišqāl) of Gen 24:22, Ezek 4:10.

**Abdi-Ashtarti: seven times on belly and back; the enemy is strong; ten women sent (EA 064)** (EA 064)
- Compare Gen 33:3 and Ps 95:6 (bowing down). Women sent to a king: Esth 2:2-3.

**Aziru defends himself: do not listen to the false men who slander me; I was in Tunip, may your gods and the Sun know it (EA 161)** (EA 161)
- Aramaic ʾăkalû qarṣêhôn, 'they ate the pieces of' = slandered: Dan 3:8 and 6:25 (the same idiom).
- Compare Num 11:12 ('carry them in your bosom as a nurse carries a child') and 1 Sam 12:3-5 ('YHWH is witness').

**Akizzi of Qatna to Naphuriya, son of the Sun: the Hittite king took the Sun god of my fathers; send gold to remake him (EA 055)** (EA 055)
- Compare 1 Sam 5:1-2 (the ark carried off by the Philistines), Judg 18:17-24 (Micah's gods taken: 'you took my gods which I made') and Jer 48:7, 49:3 (gods go into exile).
- Compare Isa 46:1-2 (Bel and Nebo carried off) and Exod 32:2-4 (gold for an image).

**Akizzi: Etakkama urged me to the Hittite king; Upi is being burned; as Damascus falls at your feet, so does Qatna (EA 053)** (EA 053)
- Damascus (Dimašqu): compare Gen 14:15, 2 Sam 8:5-6 and 1 Kgs 11:24; Upi as a land around Damascus.

**Shubandu: I am tired and very sick; I send another servant to see the king's face; your cities and threshing floors are burned (EA 306)** (EA 306)
- Compare Judg 15:4-5 and 2 Sam 14:30 (grain fields set on fire); Gen 46:29-30 and 2 Sam 14:24 (seeing the face).

**The citizens of Tunip: the gods of Thutmose III dwell in Tunip; for twenty years we have written; now Tunip weeps and its tears flow (EA 059)** (EA 059)
- Compare Lam 1:2, 16-17 ('she weeps bitterly in the night, tears on her cheeks ... there is none to comfort her') and Deut 32:7 ('ask your father, your elders').

**The city of Irqata and its elders: we guard Irqata for the king; may our enemies eat dust; the gate is shut until the breath of the king reaches us (EA 100)** (EA 100)
- Compare Ps 72:9 and Mic 7:17 (enemies lick the dust) and Ruth 4:2, Deut 21:19 (the elders of the city act for it).

**Biryawaza: Biridashwa gave the chariots of Ashtaroth to the Habiru; the kings of Busruna and Halunni said 'let us kill Biryawaza'; I guard Kumidi (EA 197)** (EA 197)
- Ashtaroth (Aštarti): Deut 1:4, Josh 9:10, 12:4; Busruna as Bozrah / Bosor (1 Macc 5:26); Yanoam is named on Merneptah's stele with Israel.
- 'Come, let us kill him': Gen 37:20 and Ps 83:5 ('come, let us wipe them out as a nation').

**Abdi-Ashirta was killed when the army's ships did not reach Amurru; Arwad's ships stand against me; are Tyre, Sidon and Beirut not the king's? (EA 101)** (EA 101)
- Arwad (Arvad): Gen 10:18, Ezek 27:8, 11. Tyre and Sidon together: Josh 19:28-29, Jer 47:4.

**Ili-rapih and Byblos, the king's maidservant: Byblos is to the king like Memphis; Aziru killed the kings of Ammiya, Ardata, Irqata and the commissioner (EA 139)** (EA 139)
- Byblos as a woman and 'maidservant' (amtu): compare Lam 1:1 and Isa 47:1-5 (the city as a woman). Gebal: Ezek 27:9, 1 Kgs 5:32.

**EA 176: a ruler in Amqu reports Etakkama and Hittite troops burning the king's cities** (EA 176)
- Compare cities set on fire in conquest, Josh 11:11-13 and Judg 1:8; Qadesh on the Orontes, 2 Sam 24:6 (LXX).

**EA 227: the king of Hazor guards the cities and rejoices at the king's word** (EA 227)
- Compare the king of Hazor as head of the northern coalition, Josh 11:1-10; Jabin king of Hazor, Judg 4:2.
- Rejoicing at a king's word: Prov 16:15 (light of the king's face is life).

**EA 228: Abdi-Tirši of Hazor, loyal servant, asks the king to remember Hazor** (EA 228)
- Compare the plea 'remember' addressed to God, Neh 5:19, 13:14; Ps 132:1; Hazor in Josh 11:10.

**EA 299: Yapaḫu of Gezer, the Sun from heaven, and the strong Habiru** (EA 299)
- Compare Gezer in Josh 10:33, 16:10 and 1 Kgs 9:16; the 'Hebrews' (ʿivrim) as an outsider class, 1 Sam 13:3-7 and 14:21.
- Compare 'deliver me from the hand of my enemies', Ps 31:16 and Ps 144:7.

**EA 298: Yapaḫu's younger brother goes over to the Habiru at Muḫḫazu** (EA 298)
- Compare the fratricidal Abimelech who hires 'empty men', Judg 9:1-5, and Absalom's revolt, 2 Sam 15.

**EA 297: Yapaḫu, 'like a copper pot in pledge' to the Suteans, revived by the king's sweet breath** (EA 297)
- Compare the king's favour as breath and life, Lam 4:20 ('the breath of our nostrils') and Prov 16:15.

**EA 325: Yidya of Ashkelon prepares bread, beer, oxen, goats, grain and straw** (EA 325)
- Compare provisions brought to a king's host, 2 Sam 17:27-29 and 1 Kgs 4:27-28.
- Compare 'what is your servant, a dog?', 2 Kgs 8:13 and 2 Sam 9:8.

**EA 323: Yidya sends thirty pieces of glass to the son of the Sun whom the Sun loves** (EA 323)
- Compare the king as God's son, Ps 2:7 and 2 Sam 7:14; 'beloved of God', 2 Sam 12:25 (Jedidiah).

**EA 316: Pu-Baʿlu of Yurza, with a postscript to the Egyptian scribe** (EA 316)
- Compare the scribe (sofer) as royal official, 2 Sam 8:17; letters with greetings to officials, Ezra 4:8-11.

**EA 315: Pu-Baʿlu guards day and night the word of the king, strong like the Sun in heaven** (EA 315)
- Compare 'those who love him are like the sun rising in its might', Judg 5:31; keeping a lord's word day and night, Josh 1:8 and Ps 1:2.

**EA 296: Yaḫtiru, raised in Egypt, will not move from under the king's feet; he carries the king's yoke** (EA 296)
- Compare 'I lift my eyes to the hills... my help comes from YHWH', Ps 121:1-2, and Ps 123:1-2.
- Compare a foreign youth raised at Pharaoh's court, Exod 2:10 and 1 Kgs 11:19-20; standing at the king's gate, Esth 2:19-21.
- Compare bringing one's neck under the king's yoke, Jer 27:11-12 and 1 Kgs 12:4; Gaza and Joppa, Josh 15:47 and 19:46.

**EA 248: Yašdata driven out by the men of Taanach** (EA 248)
- Compare Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, Judg 5:19; Josh 12:21 and 17:11.

**EA 252: Labʾaya of Shechem: 'when an ant is struck it bites the hand that strikes it'** (EA 252)
- Compare the ant as model of wisdom, Prov 6:6-8 and 30:25, and the ant that speaks in Q 27:18.
- Compare Shechem's rebel ruler Abimelech and Jotham's fable, Judg 9:7-21; the 'god of my father', Gen 31:5,42 and Exod 15:2.

**EA 270: Milkilu of Gezer: Yanḫamu demands silver, 'give your wife and your sons'** (EA 270)
- Compare a creditor taking children as slaves, 2 Kgs 4:1 and Neh 5:5; extortion by a governor, Neh 5:15.

**EA 269: Milkilu asks for archers and myrrh for healing** (EA 269)
- Compare 'is there no balm in Gilead?', Jer 8:22 and 46:11; myrrh traded down to Egypt, Gen 37:25 and 43:11.

**EA 256: Mut-Baʿli denies hiding Ayyab and lists the towns of Garu taken** (EA 256)
- Compare the oath 'as YHWH lives' and 'by the life of Pharaoh', Gen 42:15-16 and 1 Sam 20:3; the names Ayyab (Job) and Yašuya (Joshua).
- Compare Jabesh(-gilead), Judg 21:8-14 and 1 Sam 31:11-13; Ashtaroth, Josh 9:10 and 12:4; Pella (Pihil).

**EA 284: Šuwardata, left alone, asks that the king's strong hand fetch him** (EA 284)
- Compare 'by a strong hand' (be-yad ḥazaqah), Exod 3:19 and Deut 26:8; 'I alone am left', 1 Kgs 19:10.

**EA 282: Šuwardata: 'I am alone; send many archers'** (EA 282)
- Compare 'I, I alone am left', 1 Kgs 19:10,14.

**EA 264: Tagi: 'if we go up to heaven or go down to the earth, our head is in your hand'** (EA 264)
- Compare Ps 139:7-8 and Amos 9:2-3 (if they climb to heaven or dig into Sheol); 'my times are in your hand', Ps 31:16.

**EA 294: Zimreddi complains that Peya son of Gulatu took his men guarding the king's granary at Joppa** (EA 294)
- Compare Joseph's granaries in Egypt, Gen 41:48-56; 'your servant for ever', Deut 15:17 and 1 Sam 27:12.

**EA 245: Biridiya of Megiddo: Labʾaya was taken alive, but Surata released him for a ransom** (EA 245)
- Compare 'those who honour me I will honour, and those who despise me shall be lightly esteemed' (kbd/qll), 1 Sam 2:30.
- Compare a captured king spared or released against the overlord's will, 1 Kgs 20:31-43; Megiddo, Josh 12:21 and Judg 5:19.

**EA 069: Rib-Addi to 'my father': no one to save me from their hand; be warlike to the king** (EA 069)
- Compare 'there is none to deliver from my hand' (ein miyyadi matsil), Deut 32:39; Mizpah and Migdal as place-names, Judg 11:29 and Josh 15:37.

**EA 318: Dagan-takala: 'Save me from my mighty enemies, the Habiru, the robbers and the Suteans'** (EA 318)
- Compare Ps 18:18 ('he delivered me from my strong enemy') and Ps 142:7; Dagan as divine name, Judg 16:23 and 1 Sam 5.

**EA 213: Zitri-Yaraḫ, dust of the king's feet and clay he treads** (EA 213)
- Compare treading peoples like clay, Isa 41:25 and Mic 7:10; 'enemies lick the dust', Ps 72:9.

**EA 187: Šadiya of Enišasi sends his daughter to the palace** (EA 187)
- Compare Solomon marrying Pharaoh's daughter and foreign princesses, 1 Kgs 3:1 and 11:1-3.

**EA 205: the man of Ṭubu prepares for the archers with his troops and chariots** (EA 205)
- Compare the land of Tob, Judg 11:3-5 and 2 Sam 10:6; 'peoples' (leʾummim), Ps 2:1 and Gen 25:23.

**EA 272: Baʿlu-ṯipṭi: the mayors are finished, the land lost to the Habiru** (EA 272)
- Compare the Hebrews who had gone over to the Philistines, 1 Sam 14:21.

**EA 292: Baʿlu-ṯipṭi: the brick and the king's feet; Manḫatu taken; Gezer plundered by Peya** (EA 292)
- Compare Manahath, Gen 36:23 and 1 Chr 8:6; thirty silver as a slave's price, Exod 21:32 and Zech 11:12.
- Compare Ps 121:1 ('I lift my eyes'), Ps 123:2; a city as a maidservant or daughter, Lam 1:1.

**EA 082: Rib-Addi to Amanappa: a man struck me nine times with a dagger; I will leave the city** (EA 082)
- Compare Ehud's dagger, Judg 3:16-22, and Joab stabbing Amasa, 2 Sam 20:9-10.

**EA 378: Yapaḫu: 'Who am I, a dog, and what is my house?'** (EA 378)
- Compare 2 Sam 7:18 ('who am I and what is my house?'), 2 Sam 9:8 and 2 Kgs 8:13 (a dog), 1 Sam 18:18.

**EA 099: the king of Egypt orders the ruler of Ammiya to send his daughter and gifts** (EA 099)
- Compare 1 Kgs 3:1 and 9:16 (Pharaoh's daughter with a dowry); Ps 45:10-13.

**EA 104: Rib-Addi: the sons of Abdi-Aširta, slave and dog, take Ullaza and act like great kings** (EA 104)
- Compare 'who is David, who is the son of Jesse?', 1 Sam 25:10, and 'Who is Abimelech?', Judg 9:28; a dead dog, 2 Sam 16:9.

**EA 116: Rib-Addi: Ṣumur like a bird in a trap; the gods set you on your father's throne** (EA 116)
- Compare a cage full of birds, Jer 5:27; the bird escaped from the snare, Ps 124:7; Sennacherib's 'like a bird in a cage' of Hezekiah.
- Compare God setting the king on his father's throne, 1 Kgs 2:24 and 1 Kgs 1:48.

**EA 113: Rib-Addi on Yapa-Hadda's crimes and his robbed ships** (EA 113)
- Compare 'what is my sin?', 1 Sam 20:1 and 26:18.

**EA 134: from eternity the gods have not gone out of Byblos; Aziru sends troops to seize it** (EA 134)
- Compare gods carried off into exile, Jer 48:7 and 49:3, Isa 46:1-2; the glory leaving the city, Ezek 10:18-19 and 11:23.

**EA 124: Rib-Addi: Aziru has taken all my cities; Byblos alone remains** (EA 124)
- Compare 'the daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard', Isa 1:8; 'I alone am left', 1 Kgs 19:10.

**EA 094: Rib-Addi: there is no evil in your servant's words; Abdi-Aširta keeps the GAZ alive** (EA 094)
- Compare 'there is no wrong in my hands', 1 Sam 24:12 and Ps 7:4-6.

**EA 075: Rib-Addi: the field like a wife without a husband; Ammiya kills its lord; Hatti seizes the lands** (EA 075)
- Compare the land called 'married' (beʿulah) and not 'forsaken', Isa 62:4, and Isa 54:1; children given for food, Neh 5:2-5 and Lam 1:11.
- Compare Aram-naharaim, Judg 3:8 and Gen 24:10; a king killed by his own men, 2 Kgs 12:20-21.

**EA 158: Aziru to Tutu: 'you are my father, my house is your house'** (EA 158)
- Compare Jehoshaphat's 'I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses', 1 Kgs 22:4; love and hate in covenant language, Deut 7:9-10 and Mal 1:2-3.

**EA 052: Akizzi of Qaṭna to 'my lord, my storm god'** (EA 052)
- Compare the storm god Hadad/Baal titles and Ps 29; Hamath and Qaṭna region, 2 Sam 8:9-10.

**EA 191: Arzawya of Ruḫizu prepares for the archers and will give the enemy into the king's hand** (EA 191)
- Compare 'YHWH has given them into your hand', Josh 10:8 and Judg 3:28.

**EA 195: Biryawaza, the king's footstool, awaits the words from his lord's mouth** (EA 195)
- Compare Ps 110:1 (enemies as footstool) and Isa 66:1; 'by every word that goes out of the mouth of YHWH', Deut 8:3.
- Compare 'as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master', Ps 123:2; 'he shall be like the light of morning when the sun rises', 2 Sam 23:4.

**EA 198: Araššā of Kumidu, without horse or chariot, sends his son** (EA 198)
- Compare a vassal sending his son to the overlord, 2 Sam 8:10 (Toi sends Joram to David).

**EA 148: Abimilki of Tyre asks for Usu for water; the king of Hazor has joined the Habiru; the land of Canaan** (EA 148)
- Compare Tyre the island fortress, Ezek 26-27 and Josh 19:29; the king of Hazor, Josh 11:1-10; the land of Canaan, Gen 12:5 and Num 34:2.
- Compare seeing the king's face, Gen 43:3 and 2 Sam 14:24-32; 'may YHWH lift his face to you', Num 6:26.

**EA 150: Abimilki will enter to see the king's face; Usu for drinking water** (EA 150)
- Compare 'when shall I come and see the face of God?', Ps 42:3; and Prov 16:15.

**EA 233: Satatna of Akko, ground the king treads** (EA 233)
- Compare Akko, Judg 1:31.

**EA 244: Biridiya: Labʾaya besieges Megiddo; we cannot harvest; pestilence in the city** (EA 244)
- Compare the pestilence (dever) as judgment and siege, Jer 21:6-9 and Ezek 5:12; Ps 91:6.
- Compare Megiddo, Judg 5:19 and 1 Kgs 9:15.

**EA 250: Baʿlu-mehir: the two sons of Labʾaya continue their father's war** (EA 250)
- Compare the sons of Abimelech's line and Shechem, Judg 9; Shunem, Josh 19:18 and 1 Sam 28:4; Gath-rimmon, Josh 19:45 and 21:24.

**EA 280: Šuwardata: Keilah restored; Labʾaya is dead, but Abdi-Ḫeba is another Labʾaya** (EA 280)
- Compare Keilah, 1 Sam 23:1-13; Jerusalem's ruler Abdi-Ḫeba and Jerusalem's kings, Josh 10:1-5.

**EA 274: Bēlet-nešē, 'Lady of the lions', asks the king to rescue his land from the Habiru** (EA 274)
- Compare a woman leader in Canaan, Deborah, Judg 4-5; Labaoth / Beth-lebaoth ('lionesses'), Josh 15:32 and 19:6.

**EA 328: Yabni-ilu of Lachish obeys the commissioner Maya** (EA 328)
- Compare Lachish, Josh 10:3,31-32; Jabin's name type (Yabni-), Josh 11:1.

**EA 322: Yidya of Ashkelon heeds the commissioner of the son of the Sun** (EA 322)
- Compare Ashkelon, Judg 1:18 and 14:19.

**EA 301: Šubandu has given 300 oxen and 20 girls** (EA 301)
- Compare captive girls counted with cattle as spoil, Num 31:32-35.

**EA 313: thirteen Egyptian merchants beaten in a Habiru raid** (EA 313)
- Compare merchants of Tyre and Egypt, Ezek 27; travellers robbed on the roads, Judg 5:6.

**EA 262: Dašru: all the king does for his land is very good** (EA 262)
- Compare 'whatever the king did pleased all the people', 2 Sam 3:36.

**EA 049: Niqmaddu of Ugarit asks the Sun for Kushite palace boys and a physician** (EA 049)
- Compare Jer 8:22 ('is there no physician there?'); Egyptian physicians, Gen 50:2; a Cushite at the court, 2 Sam 18:21 and Jer 38:7.

**EA 199: an unnamed vassal escorts the king's caravans as far as Buṣruna** (EA 199)
- Compare Bozrah / Bostra and the King's Highway, Num 20:17.

**EA 247: Biridiya: 'who am I, a dog, that I would not give the king's demand?'** (EA 247)
- Compare 2 Kgs 8:13 and 1 Sam 24:15.

**EA 070: Rib-Addi asks for men of Egypt and Meluḫḫa; Amurru seeks the archers day and night** (EA 070)
- Compare Cushite troops in Egyptian service, 2 Chr 12:3 and Jer 46:9.

**Rib-Addi in exile at Beirut: driven out of Byblos by his brother; old and sick; send archers and give me a town (EA 137)** (EA 137)
- Puruzu (r:64, 67, 85) is the West Semitic word behind Hebrew pərāzôt 'open villages' (Esth 9:19; Ezek 38:11; Zech 2:8) and pərāzî (Deut 3:5; 1 Sam 6:18); the land of Canaan (Kinaʿanu) is named at r:76: compare Gen 12:5.
- The aged ruler unable to go before the king: compare 2 Sam 19:35-38 (Barzillai too old to go with the king). Illness as sin against the gods: compare 2 Kgs 1:2-4 and Ps 38:4.
- The breath of the king's mouth: compare Lam 4:20 ('the breath of our nostrils, YHWH's anointed'). Brother turning the city over: compare Judg 9:1-6 (Abimelech and Shechem).

**Aziru of Amurru: I have done all the king commanded; I will build Sumur this year; do not listen to slanderers (EA 160)** (EA 160)
- akālu karṣī 'eat the pieces (of someone)' = slander is the idiom of Aramaic ʾăkalû qarṣêhôn dî yəhûdāyēʾ, Dan 3:8 and 6:25.
- Building night and day: compare Neh 4:16-17. Servant 'for ever' (adi dārīti): compare Deut 15:17 ('he shall be your servant for ever').

**Tell el-Hesi letter: Payapu reports that Shipti-Baal and Zimredda plotted to get bows and swords (EA 333)** (EA 333)
- Zimredda is the ruler of Lachish (compare EA 288 r:43-44, killed by his servants); Tell el-Hesi lies near Lachish. A plot reported to the overlord: compare 2 Sam 15:31 and Esth 2:21-23 (a plot overheard and reported).

**Abi-Milku of Tyre: I have done what the king said; ships readied before the king's troops (EA 153)** (EA 153)
- Tyrian ships at the service of a king: compare 1 Kgs 9:27 and 10:22 (Hiram's ships).

**The king to Milkilu of Gezer: Hanya brings silver for forty fine cup-bearer women; the king is well like the Sun (EA 369)** (EA 369)
- Women without blemish gathered for the king: compare Esth 2:2-4 and 1 Sam 8:13 ('he will take your daughters as perfumers, cooks and bakers'); Gezer as a royal Egyptian concern: 1 Kgs 9:16.
- The god sets the lands under the king's feet: compare Ps 110:1, Ps 8:7 and Ps 2:8; sunrise to sunset: Ps 113:3 and Mal 1:11.

**Baʿlu-mehir of Tinni: the Sun from heaven; I heard the king's word (EA 260)** (EA 260)
- Compare 2 Sam 23:3-4 (the just ruler like the morning sun) and Mal 3:20 (the sun of righteousness).

**Rib-Addi: I cannot send ships for boxwood; the king gives to the other mayors but not to me; Hittite troops burn the lands (EA 126)** (EA 126)
- 'If the king hates his city, let him abandon it': compare Ps 74:1 and Lam 5:20-22 (has God utterly rejected his city?). Silver and gold of the king given to the enemy (t.e:63-l.e:66): compare 2 Kgs 18:15-16.

**Rib-Addi: the sons of Abdi-Ashirta have entered Amurru; the commissioner is sick and has left Sumur; send help quickly (EA 103)** (EA 103)
- The last men of the garrison 'sick and few' (r:49-50): compare Isa 1:8-9 (a remnant left).

**The army commander to Rib-Addi, 'my son': is there plague in Sumur on men or on donkeys? Send men to guard the city (EA 096)** (EA 096)
- Exclusion for fear of contagion: compare Lev 13:46 and Num 5:2-3; the lost royal donkeys searched for (r:17-24): compare 1 Sam 9:3-5 and 9:20.

**Rib-Addi: Byblos, the king's faithful maid, is safe, but the Habiru war is strong; the king neglects Sumur (EA 068)** (EA 068)
- The city as the king's maid: compare Lam 1:1 (the city 'like a widow', princess become a vassal) and Isa 47:1-5.

**Rib-Addi: two cities remain; like a bird in a trap, so am I in Byblos (EA 078, damaged)** (EA 078)
- Compare Sennacherib's 'like a bird in a cage' (of Hezekiah in Jerusalem), Ps 124:7 and Jer 5:27.

**Rib-Addi: Abdi-Ashirta incited my murder; the peasants sold their children for food; like a bird in a cage; send archers in two months (EA 081)** (EA 081)
- Sons and daughters given for food: compare Neh 5:2-5 and 2 Kgs 4:1; the field like a wife without husband: compare Isa 54:1 and 62:4 ('your land Married').
- Incitement to kill one's lord: compare 2 Kgs 10:1-7 and 2 Sam 4:5-8.

**Milkilu (of Gezer): war on me and Shuwardata; rescue the land from the Habiru; send chariots (EA 271)** (EA 271)
- Compare Josh 10:33 (Horam king of Gezer) and the plea of Gibeon, Josh 10:6 ('come up quickly and save us').

**Ammunira of Beirut: to the king, breath of my life; I am the dust of your feet; Beirut serves; I am like a groom of the king's horses (EA 143)** (EA 143)
- 'Dust of your feet': compare Isa 49:23 (kings shall lick the dust of your feet) and Ps 72:9; the breath of life: Lam 4:20.

**Biri of Hashabu: Etakkama of Qadesh led the Hittite troops and set the king's cities in Amqu on fire; give archers (EA 174)** (EA 174)
- A joint letter repeated nearly word for word in EA 175 (Ili-dayyani of Hazi) and other Amqu letters. Cities set on fire: compare Josh 11:11-13 and Judg 1:8.

**Labaya: I am the king's servant as my father and grandfather; I am not guilty: my only sin is that I entered Gezer (EA 253)** (EA 253)
- Labaya's land is the hill country of Shechem: compare Judg 9 (Abimelech of Shechem) and Josh 24. 'What is my sin?': compare 1 Sam 20:1 and 26:18; Gezer: Josh 16:10.

**Tagi: I looked here and there and there was no light; I looked to the king and there was light; I will not move from under his feet (EA 266)** (EA 266)
- Compare Ps 34:6 ('they looked to him and were radiant'), Ps 36:10 and Prov 16:15 (light of the king's face). The brick image: compare Exod 1:14 and 5:7 (bricks, ləbēnîm).

**An official at Sumur: the Egyptians have left Sumur; he, like the Habiru, a runaway dog, has seized Sumur (EA 067, damaged)** (EA 067)
- The runaway dog: compare 1 Sam 25:10 ('many servants break away from their masters') and Judg 9:4 and 11:3 (worthless men gather round a leader).

**Biryawaza (of Damascus): all the king's servants have gone over to the king of Hatti; I alone remain; send 200 men (EA 196)** (EA 196)
- Wives and daughters-in-law 'placed in the lap' (r:27-29, broken context) may refer to their seizure: compare 1 Sam 30:3-5. 'Such a deed was never done': Judg 19:30.

**Ipte-...: there is no faithful servant like me; the king like the Sun and like Baal; Puhuru does not protect me; the cities are lost to the Habiru (EA 207)** (EA 207)
- The king like the sun and the storm god: compare Ps 18:8-15 and 2 Sam 22:13-15; 'the word of the king twice' (o:10-11): compare Gen 41:32.

**A daughter, 'your maid', to her lady: seven and seven times I fall at my lady's feet (EA 050, fragment)** (EA 050)
- A woman's letter of homage: compare 1 Sam 25:23-24 (Abigail falls at David's feet, 'let your maidservant speak').

**Yapah-Addu to Shum-Haddu: your name is bad before the king; do not ruin the king's lands; the land given to the sons of Abdi-Ashirta (EA 097)** (EA 097)
- A bad name before the king: compare 1 Sam 27:12 and 2 Sam 10:6 ('they had made themselves odious').

**A ruler, servant, dust and ground under the king's feet, to the Sun from heaven: as the king wrote, I guard the city (EA 231)** (EA 231)
- 'The ground he treads on': compare Josh 1:3 and Deut 11:24 (every place the sole of your foot treads).

**Abdi-Heba of Jerusalem: I am not a mayor but a soldier of the king; why does the king not send his messenger? Send archers or a commissioner (EA 285)** (EA 285)
- Abdi-Heba ('servant of Hebat') rules Urusalim, the Jerusalem later held by Adoni-zedek (Josh 10:1-5) and the Jebusites (Judg 1:21; 2 Sam 5:6-9).

**Baʿlu-UR.SAG: Milkilu wrongs my men and gives his servants to Tagi his father-in-law; Milkilu and Labaya make war (EA 249)** (EA 249)
- Rival rulers allied by marriage (Milkilu and his father-in-law Tagi): compare 1 Kgs 3:1 and 2 Kgs 8:18, 27.

**A vassal: I have prepared everything; who is the dog that would not listen to Maya the commissioner? (EA 217)** (EA 217)
- 'Who is your servant, a dog, that ...': compare 2 Kgs 8:13, 2 Sam 9:8 and 1 Sam 24:15.

**Yapahu of Gezer: life is lost from my land; send archers to bring me into my cities; Sun from heaven, son of the Sun (EA 300)** (EA 300)
- Son of the Sun (Egyptian sa-Ra): compare Ps 2:7 ('you are my son') and Ps 89:27-28.

**Tiwate: I am ready with horses, troops and chariots to go with the archers; the man who does not serve the king, the king curses him (EA 193)** (EA 193)
- Compare Judg 5:23 ('curse Meroz ... because they did not come to the help of YHWH') and Deut 27:26.

**Shipturiza: my city is safe; I plough, sow and harvest, and have prepared oil, bread and beer before the king's caravans (EA 226)** (EA 226)
- Provisions laid ready for the king's march: compare 2 Sam 17:27-29 and 1 Kgs 4:27.

**Abdi-Ashtarti: Turbazu and Yaptih-Hadda slain; Lachish hostile, Muhrashti taken, Jerusalem hostile; send archers (EA 335)** (EA 335)
