- Lachish and Jerusalem side by side: compare Josh 10:3-5 and 10:31-32; Moresheth (Muhrashti?): Mic 1:1, 14.

**Your servants: what we heard about the Ahlamu and the king of Karduniash (EA 200, fragment)** (EA 200)
- The Aḫlamû are forerunners of the Aramaeans: compare Deut 26:5 ('a wandering Aramaean was my father') and Gen 25:20.

**Rib-Addi: the king says 'guard yourself', but who will guard me? The mayors are killed by their towns like dogs; I live among the Habiru (EA 130)** (EA 130)
- 'No one seeks after them' (yānu ša yubaʾʾu): compare Ps 142:5 ('no one cares for my soul') and Ezek 34:6. Rulers killed like dogs: 1 Kgs 16:4 and 2 Kgs 9:10.

**Rib-Addi: I guard myself alone; Pahura did a great crime: he sent Suteans who killed the Sherden; a deed never done (EA 122)** (EA 122)
- Compare Judg 19:30 ('nothing like this has been done since the day Israel came out of Egypt') and Jer 2:10-11.

**Rib-Addi: for three years my grain is taken; the peasants gave sons and daughters for food; send grain by ship; who is Abdi-Ashirta, the slave, the dog? (EA 085)** (EA 085)
- Famine, children pledged and selling of houses: compare Neh 5:2-5 and Gen 47:13-25. An army turning back for lack of water: 2 Kgs 3:9.
- 'Who is X, the slave, the dog?': compare 1 Sam 25:10 ('who is David? ... many slaves break away') and 2 Sam 16:9 ('this dead dog').

**Rib-Addi: the mayor of Tyre was killed with my sister and her children; Tyre's wealth is like the sea, its palace like Ugarit's (EA 089)** (EA 089)
- Tyre's wealth and the sea: compare Ezek 27:33, Ezek 28:4-5 and Zech 9:3 ('Tyre heaped up silver like dust'); Isa 23:8.

**Rib-Addi: Sumur is like a bird in a cage; the sons of Abdi-Ashirta by land and Arwad by sea; Yapa-Addu withholds grain (EA 105)** (EA 105)
- Besieged by land and sea, day and night: compare Neh 4:3 and Ezek 26:7-12 (Tyre).

**Rib-Addi: the sons of Abdi-Ashirta, slave and dog, take the king's cities; once Canaan's kings fled from an Egyptian, now they treat Egyptians like dogs; death is good for me (EA 109)** (EA 109)
- Kings of Canaan fleeing before Egypt: compare Exod 15:14-16 and Josh 2:9-11 (the inhabitants melt). 'Death is good for me': Jonah 4:3, 8 and 1 Kgs 19:4. Temple silver as ransom: 2 Kgs 18:15.

**Rib-Addi to Haya the vizier: may Amun give you honour; you are a wise man; why are you silent? Abdi-Ashirta the dog has taken the king's land (EA 071)** (EA 071)
- Compare Gen 41:33, 39 (a 'discerning and wise man' over Egypt) and Joseph as the official whom petitioners approach (Gen 42:6).

**Rib-Addi, footstool of the king's feet: Abdi-Ashirta the dog lay in my lord's bedchamber and opened his treasury; Byblos is like Memphis to the king (EA 084)** (EA 084)
- The usurper in the king's bedchamber: compare 2 Sam 16:21-22 (Absalom and his father's concubines) and 1 Kgs 2:13-22; the opened treasury: 2 Kgs 20:13.
- The footstool of the king's feet: compare Ps 110:1. Damu, the dying god of Byblos: compare Ezek 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz).

**Rib-Addi to Amanappa: may Amun and the Lady of Byblos give you honour; I have no copper or ivory; if no archers this year all lands go to the Habiru (EA 077)** (EA 077)
- Invoking a god as witness of one's poverty: compare 1 Sam 12:3-5.

**Inventory of the goods with Yapa-Addu (vessels, weapons, gold-plated beds and chairs, slaves) and the lawsuit with Abdi-Addu (EA 120)** (EA 120)
- Coverlets (marbaddîm): Prov 7:16 and 31:22; a lawsuit over seized goods before the king: compare 2 Kgs 8:3-6.

**Rib-Addi: who are they, the sons of Abdi-Ashirta, dogs? Without archers this year Byblos falls; send ships to take me with the living gods to my lord (EA 129)** (EA 129)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:43 ('am I a dog?') and 2 Sam 3:8. Fleeing with the gods: compare Gen 31:19, 30 (Rachel and the teraphim) and Jer 48:7. The great kings named (r:75-76): Mittani, Kassite Babylonia, Hatti.

**Byblos, the king's maid, and Ili-rapih: why did the king release Aziru? He killed the kings of Irqata, Ammiya and Ardata and took Sumur (EA 140)** (EA 140)
- A city speaking as a woman: compare Lam 1:9-22 and Isa 49:14. Kings of neighbouring cities killed one after another: Josh 10:28-39.

**Surata of Akko: dust and ground under the king's feet, I prostrate on belly and back; who would not obey the word of the Sun from heaven? (EA 232)** (EA 232)
- Akko: Judg 1:31. Obedience to what comes out of the king's mouth: compare Eccl 8:2-4 and Deut 8:3.

**Satatna of Akko: Zirdamyashda deserted Biryawaza; Akko is like Magdalu in Egypt; Shuta demands him (EA 234)** (EA 234)
- Magdalu = Migdol on Egypt's border (Exod 14:2; Jer 44:1); Megiddo: Josh 12:21 and Judg 5:19. Extradition of a fugitive demanded: compare 1 Kgs 2:39-40 and 1 Kgs 18:10.

**Abdi-Heba: what have I done? they slander me; not my father or mother but the king's strong arm set me here; why do you love the Habiru and hate the mayors? (EA 286)** (EA 286)
- The strong arm: compare Deut 26:8, Ps 89:14, 22 and Ps 44:4. Installed not by parentage: compare Ps 2:6-7 and Heb 7:3 (Melchizedek of Salem, 'without father, without mother').
- Seeing the king's face: compare 2 Sam 14:24, 28 and Ps 42:3 ('when shall I come and see the face of God?').

**Abdi-Heba: the king has set his name at sunrise and sunset; I am a soldier, the king's companion; like a ship in the sea; rulers slain at the gate; we will die with the king (EA 288)** (EA 288)
- The name set at sunrise and sunset: compare Mal 1:11 and Ps 113:3; the place where God sets his name: Deut 12:5, 11 and 1 Kgs 9:3. The strong arm: Exod 6:6 and Deut 4:34.
- Like a ship in the sea: compare Ps 107:23-27 and Jonah 1. Gintikirmil (o:26) is Gath-carmel (compare Josh 15:55 Carmel); Silu = Sile on Egypt's frontier.

**Abdi-Heba: Milkilu and the sons of Labaya gave the king's land to the Habiru; the king is righteous to me; Cushites nearly killed me; my caravan was robbed in Ayyalon; the king has set his name in Jerusalem for ever (EA 287)** (EA 287)
- God sets his name in Jerusalem for ever: 1 Kgs 9:3, 11:36, 2 Kgs 21:4, 7 and Ps 132:13-14; the land not given by father or mother: compare Ps 2:6-8.
- Ayyalon: Josh 10:12 ('moon, in the valley of Aijalon') and 1 Sam 14:31; Gezer, Ashkelon, Lachish: Josh 10:3, 33 and Judg 1:18. 'The king is righteous': compare Ps 11:7 and Ps 72:1-2.

**ʿAbdi-Ḫeba of Jerusalem: Milkilu, the sons of Labʾaya, Shechem given to the Habiru, send 50 men (EA 289)** (EA 289)
- Compare Josh 10:1-5 (Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem with the kings of Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, Jarmuth) and Josh 10:33 (Horam king of Gezer).
- Compare Judg 9 (Abimelech and the lords of Shechem; Shechem passing outside central control) and Gen 34; Josh 24:1.
- Compare 1 Sam 13:3, 13:7 and 14:21 (the 'Hebrews' (ʿibrim) who go over to the Philistines) and Gen 14:13 ('Abram the Hebrew').
- Places named also in the Hebrew Bible: Gaza, Beth-shean (Bit-šani), Gath-carmel, Keilah (Qiltu, 1 Sam 23:1-13), Rabbah (Rubbutu, Josh 15:60).

**ʿAbdi-Ḫeba: Milkilu and Šuwardata gather Gezer, Gath and Keilah; a town of Jerusalem's land lost; send archers (EA 290)** (EA 290)
- The town 'of the land of Jerusalem' written Bit-NIN.URTA is read by some as Bethlehem (Bit-Laḫmi) or Beth-horon; compare Josh 10:10-11 and Ruth 1:1.
- Compare Josh 10:3-5 (a coalition of southern kings) and 1 Sam 23:1-5 (Keilah attacked; David sent to save it).

**Šuwardata: the king's land is ruined; send archers against the enemies (EA 279)** (EA 279)
- Compare 1 Sam 23:1-5 (Keilah, Qiltu, under attack).

**Zitriyara: the king is like the Sun from heaven; we cannot neglect his word (EA 211)** (EA 211)
- Compare Ps 84:12 (YHWH God is a sun and shield) and Mal 3:20 (the sun of righteousness).

**Biridiya of Megiddo: the two sons of Labʾaya pay silver to the SA.GAZ and Suteans to make war on me (EA 246)** (EA 246)
- Compare Judg 9:4 (Abimelech hires 'empty and reckless men' with silver from the temple of Baal-berith) and Judg 11:3.

**A ruler (Baʿlu-ṯipṭi): dust under the king's sandals, servant from head to foot; Yabni-ilu of Sidon did evil (EA 295)** (EA 295)
- Compare Ps 60:10 / 108:10 ('upon Edom I cast my sandal') and Isa 1:6 ('from the sole of the foot to the head').

**ʿAziru: you are like Baal and like the Sun; I am the king's dog, rebuilding Ṣumur; the mayors lie (EA 159)** (EA 159)
- Compare Ps 18:8-16 and Ps 29 (God as storm god) with Ps 84:12 (sun); and 2 Sam 9:8, 2 Kgs 8:13 (the servant as dog).

**ʿAziru: I have arrived safely to see the king's face; my brothers and sons are the king's servants (EA 168)** (EA 168)
- Compare Gen 43:3-5 and 2 Sam 14:24, 28 (seeing / not seeing the king's face).

**A son of ʿAziru: you give life and you kill; release ʿAziru quickly, the Suteans and Nuḫašše threaten (EA 169)** (EA 169)
- Compare Deut 32:39 and 1 Sam 2:6 ('YHWH kills and makes alive'); and Q 2:258 (the king who says 'I give life and cause death').
- Compare Gen 42-44 (a son kept in Egypt as surety) and Ps 123:2 (eyes of servants to the hand of their master).

**Rib-Hadda: Byblos alone; ʿAbdi-Aširta the dog; like a bird in a trap; a field like a wife without husband (EA 090)** (EA 090)
- Compare Ps 124:7 (our soul escaped like a bird from the fowler's snare) and Lam 3:52.
- Compare Isa 54:1, 62:4 (the land 'married' or 'forsaken') and Neh 5:2-5 (sons and daughters given for grain).

**Rib-Hadda: 'guard yourself' - with what? from my enemies and my own peasants; a Habiru hired to carry a tablet to Ṣumur (EA 112)** (EA 112)
- Compare Judg 3:11, 5:31 ('and the land had rest') with yušapšiḫu mātāti.

**Rib-Hadda: my fathers had garrisons; the sons of ʿAbdi-Aširta speak to the GAZ; mayors killed like dogs (EA 121)** (EA 121)
- Compare 1 Kgs 14:11, 16:4 (dogs and the slain); Q 7:176 (the parable of the dog).

**Rib-Hadda: the sons of ʿAbdi-Aširta; ʿAziru; the army's ships must not leave Canaan (EA 110)** (EA 110)
- Kinaḫḫi = Canaan; compare Gen 10:15-19 and Num 13:29.

**Rib-Hadda to an Egyptian magnate: Amun and the Lady of Byblos; the king of Mittani looks on Amurru; ʿAbdi-Aširta very sick (EA 095)** (EA 095)
- ʿAbdi-Aširta marṣu magal, 'who knows whether he has died' (r:41-42): compare 2 Kgs 1:2-4, 8:7-10 (an enemy king's sickness).

**Biridiya: I guard Megiddo day and night, by day with chariots, by night on the walls; the SA.GAZ are strong (EA 243)** (EA 243)
- Compare Neh 4:16-17 (guard by night, work by day) and Isa 62:6, Ps 127:1 (watchmen on the walls).

**Yidya of Ashkelon: may the king's gods and his two strong hands guard his land (EA 326)** (EA 326)
- Compare Deut 4:34, 5:15 ('a mighty hand and an outstretched arm') and Ps 121:4-5.

**Zimreddi of Lachish: the Sun from heaven; I have heard the messenger's words (EA 329)** (EA 329)
- Lachish: compare Josh 10:3, 10:31-32 (Japhia king of Lachish).

**Yapaḫ-Hadda to Yanḫamu: all lands from Byblos to Ugarit hostile; ships of Arwad block grain to Ṣumur (EA 098)** (EA 098)
- Arwad: compare Gen 10:18 and Ezek 27:8, 11.

**Ḫibiya to the magnate: we have gone up into the mountains; much grain in Amurru (EA 178)** (EA 178)
- Compare Judg 6:2 (Israel took refuge in the mountains) and 1 Sam 13:6.

**Rusmanya of Šaruna: dust of your feet, clay you tread, footstool of my lord's feet (EA 241)** (EA 241)
- Compare Ps 110:1 ('until I make your enemies your footstool'), Ps 99:5, 132:7 and Isa 66:1.
- Šaruna is perhaps the Sharon (Josh 12:18 'Lasharon').

**ʿAbdi-Aširta to Paḫḫanate: I am no enemy of Egypt; I saved Ṣumur and four men from the Šeḫlali troops; the mayors lie (EA 062)** (EA 062)
- Compare Josh 22:21-29 (the accused tribes protest they meant no rebellion) and 1 Sam 24:10-16.

**The Lady of the Lionesses, 'your maidservant': the land lost to the SA.GAZ; they were sent to Aijalon and Zorah (EA 273)** (EA 273)
- Aijalon and Zorah: compare Josh 10:12, 19:41-42; Judg 1:35, 13:2 (Zorah, Samson's town).
- Compare Judg 4-5 (Deborah, a woman leader) and Q 27:29-44 (the queen of Sheba writing to and submitting to Solomon).

**...-Ḫeba to her Lady: a jar of balsam (EA 048)** (EA 048)
- Compare Gen 37:25, 43:11 (ṣŏrî carried to Egypt as a gift) and Jer 8:22, 46:11 (balm in Gilead).

**Zimreddi to an official: the breath of the king's mouth restored me; all your servants wait for you (EA 145)** (EA 145)
- Compare Ps 25:3, 37:9, Isa 40:31 (those who wait, qwy, for YHWH) and Ps 123:2 (eyes of servants on the master's hand).
- Compare Lam 4:20 ('the breath of our nostrils, YHWH's anointed') and Gen 2:7.

**A ruler: my brother in Tubiḫu went over to the GAZ; the king's god gave and I seized Tubiḫu and cursed my brother (EA 179)** (EA 179)
- Compare Judg 9:1-6, 56-57 (Abimelech, his brothers and Jotham's curse) and Gen 49:7.

**Biryawaza: we serve the king from of old like Šuttarna my father; the caravan to Naharima (EA 194)** (EA 194)
- Naḫrima: compare Aram-naharaim, Gen 24:10, Judg 3:8.

**Akizzi of Qaṭna: I trust in my lord's troops and chariots; Etakkama has seized the cities; the kings allied with Hatti (EA 056 + EA 361)** (EA 056 + EA 361)
- Compare Ps 20:8 (some trust in chariots and some in horses), Isa 31:1 and 2 Kgs 18:24 (trusting in Egypt for chariots).

**Baʿlu-meher: I have put my neck in the yoke I carry; I serve the king very much (EA 257)** (EA 257)
- Compare Jer 27:8, 11-12 ('bring your neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him and live') and 1 Kgs 12:4.

**Abi-Milku of Tyre: dust from the king's sandals; Sidon kills my men who go to the mainland for wood and water (EA 154)** (EA 154)
- Compare Ezek 26-28 (Tyre in the midst of the sea) and Isa 23.
- Compare Josh 9:21-27 ('hewers of wood and drawers of water').

**Abi-Milku: my city is the king's maidservant; Zimreddi of Sidon is hostile; give me 80 men (EA 152)** (EA 152)
- Compare Lam 1:1 (the city become a vassal) and Isa 47:1-2.

**Ṣur-Ašar of Ginti-ašna: groom of your horses; who is the dog that would not obey the king, the Sun from heaven, son of the Sun? (EA 319)** (EA 319)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:43, 24:15; 2 Sam 9:8, 16:9 and 2 Kgs 8:13 ('what is your servant, a dog?').
- Compare Ps 2:7 (the king as God's son).

**Mayarzana of Ḫasi: the SA.GAZ sack and burn the king's cities, and Amanḫatpe of Tušulti gives them bread and oil (EA 186)** (EA 186)
- Compare 1 Sam 30:1-3, 14 (Ziklag raided and burned with fire) and Judg 18:27.
- Magdali: compare the Migdal- place names (Josh 15:37, 19:38); compare 1 Sam 22:2 (malcontents gather to a leader).

**Šuwardata: my gods, my suns, my breath; all my cities hostile; who are these dogs that sin against the king? (EA 281)** (EA 281)
- Compare Ps 96:9, 114:7 (ḥîlû, 'tremble before him') and Ps 59:7, 15 (enemies like dogs).

**Bayadi to the magnate: the cities entrusted to me are taken; send 50 men; you give us life and you kill us (EA 238)** (EA 238)
- Compare Deut 32:39, 1 Sam 2:6, 2 Kgs 5:7; and Q 2:258, Q 53:44.

**Abi-Milku: you are the Sun, the sweet breath; I guard Tyre awaiting the king's breath; Zimreddi gives us no water (EA 146)** (EA 146)
- Compare Ps 104:30 and Job 33:4 (the breath that gives life); compare Lam 4:20.

**Šipṭi-Baʿlu of Lachish: dust of your feet, groom of your horse (EA 332)** (EA 332)
- Lachish: Josh 10:3; the name Šipṭi-Baʿlu ('Baal judges') compare Shephatiah (2 Sam 3:4).

**The king's letter (fragment): all lands live by seeing him; the king is well like the Sun in heaven from sunrise to sunset (EA 163)** (EA 163)
- Compare Ps 113:3, Mal 1:11 (from the rising of the sun to its setting) and Ps 72:5, 8, 17.
- Compare Q 55:17 (Lord of the two easts and the two wests).

**ʿAziru to Tutu: Ḫatip brought good words; the Hittite king is in Nuḫašše; let Tutu and the magnates swear by my gods and by Aten (EA 164)** (EA 164)
- Compare Gen 26:28-31 and 31:44-53 (oaths of non-aggression), 1 Sam 20:42 and 2 Sam 19:23 (oath that no harm will come).

**ʿAziru to his 'brother' Ḫaya: I seek the king's good face; I fear the Hittite king in Nuḫašše (EA 166)** (EA 166)
- Compare Ps 27:8, 105:4 (seeking the face) and Prov 29:26.

**Zimreddi of Sidon: breath of my life; my head was lifted and my eyes shone at the king's word; cities given to the SA.GAZ (EA 144)** (EA 144)
- Compare Ps 3:4 (the lifter of my head), Ps 19:9 (the commandment enlightening the eyes), 1 Sam 14:27-29 and Ps 13:4.
- Compare Lam 4:20 (the breath of our nostrils).

**Rib-Addi of Byblos: Abdi-Ashirta the dog is taking the king's cities, the Habiru gathered against Shigata and Ambi; send 400 men and 30 pairs of horses (EA 076)** (EA 076)
- 'Is he the king of Mittani?' scorn: compare 1 Sam 25:10 ('Who is David? who is the son of Jesse?') and Exod 5:2 ('Who is YHWH?').
- Enemy called a dog: compare 1 Sam 17:43, 2 Sam 3:8 and 2 Sam 16:9 ('this dead dog').
- Troops going out yearly: compare 2 Sam 11:1 ('at the return of the year, the time when kings go out').

**Aziru of Amurru to the king: I seek to see your good face; the king of Hatti is in Nuhashshe, I fear for Amurru (EA 165)** (EA 165)
- 'To see the face of the king': compare 2 Sam 14:24, 28, 32 (Absalom 'did not see the king's face') and Gen 43:3.

**Aziru to Tutu, 'my lord, my father': I will not depart from the king's words; the king of Hatti is in Nuhashshe (EA 167)** (EA 167)
- A courtier addressed as 'my father': compare Gen 45:8 (Joseph 'a father to Pharaoh') and 2 Kgs 5:13.

**Baaluya and Bet-ili to their lord (Aziru): Hittite troops under Lupakku took the cities of Amqu; Zitana comes with 90,000 foot soldiers (EA 170)** (EA 170)
- Numbered foreign hosts: compare 2 Chr 14:9 (Zerah the Cushite with a million) and Judg 4:3.
- Note the Canaanite-type personal names Rabi-Ṣidqi ('ṣedeq is great') and Bin-ʿAnu, and the greeting to ʿAnatu (r:37, l.e:43); compare Melchizedek (Gen 14:18) and Adoni-zedek (Josh 10:1).

**The man of Qanu: you wrote to prepare for the archers; I go with my troops and chariots before the king's troops (EA 204)** (EA 204)
- Qanu is probably biblical Kenath (Num 32:42) in Bashan. Compare 1 Kgs 22:4 ('I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses').

**Baal-meher: true servant; all the king has done for his land is very good (EA 258)** (EA 258)
- The sender's name Baʿlu-meher ('Baal is a warrior'); compare 2 Sam 19:27-28 (Mephibosheth: 'the king is like an angel of God, do what is good in your eyes').

**Abdi-Milki of Shashimi: ready with troops and chariots before the king's archers (EA 203)** (EA 203)
- Same form letter as EA 201, 202 and 204, from rulers of Bashan; compare the summons of the Transjordanian tribes in Josh 1:12-16.

**Amayashe: who am I, a dog, that I should not go? I go with troops and chariots before the archers (EA 202)** (EA 202)
- Compare 2 Kgs 8:13 ('What is your servant, the dog, that he should do this great thing?') and 2 Sam 9:8; 1 Sam 24:15.

**Shubandu to the king, 'the Sun from heaven': I have heard the messenger's words and am preparing (EA 302)** (EA 302)
- Compare Gen 33:3 (Jacob bows to the ground seven times) and the Hebrew prostration verb hištaḥăwâ (Gen 18:2).

**Mut-Baal, son of Labaya: who am I not to send on the caravans to Hanigalbat and Karduniash? (EA 255)** (EA 255)
- Mut-Baal is son of Labaya of Shechem (o:15). Caravan routes through Canaan: compare Gen 37:25 (Ishmaelite caravan to Egypt) and Judg 5:6 ('the caravans ceased').

**Baduzana: all the king's words are carried out; let the great one come out and learn our guilt (EA 239)** (EA 239)
- Compare 1 Sam 26:18-19 ('what have I done? what evil is in my hand?... if men have stirred you up').

**Labaya of Shechem: I am a loyal servant, no guilt; I said in assembly the king may take my property; my son walks with the Habiru unknown to me; if the king said, I would put a bronze dagger in my heart (EA 254)** (EA 254)
- Labaya ruled the hill country of Shechem; compare Abimelech of Shechem (Judg 9) and Jacob's sons at Shechem (Gen 34).
- 'I have not sinned... why do you listen?' compare 1 Sam 24:12 and 26:18; the obedience to the death compare Gen 22 and 2 Sam 15:26 ('let him do to me what seems good to him').
- Accusation 'in assembly' (puhriš, r:24) of Milkilu: compare Job 31:34-35.

**Etakkama of Qadesh: Biryawaza slanders me; he gave the king's cities to the Habiru, and with the king's gods and Sun I restored them (EA 189)** (EA 189)
- The overlord's gods going before the vassal: compare Deut 1:30, 31:8 and 2 Sam 5:24 ('YHWH has gone out before you').
- Upi (Apu) is the region of Damascus: compare Gen 14:15 (Hobah, north of Damascus).

**Aziru: servant for ever; I send two servants, my sons, to do all the king commands (EA 156)** (EA 156)
- Compare 2 Kgs 16:7 ('I am your servant and your son') and Gen 42:37 (sons given as pledge).

**Artamanya of Ziribashani: who am I, a dog, that I should not go? Ready with troops and chariots (EA 201)** (EA 201)
- Ziri-Bashan, 'Bashan' as in Num 21:33; compare 2 Kgs 8:13 and 2 Sam 9:8.

**Shuwardata: 'seven and seven times'; who would refuse to come to the king? Thirty cities make war on me, I am alone; send archers (EA 283)** (EA 283)
- Shuwardata ruled in the Shephelah (Gath/Keilah region); compare 1 Sam 23:1-5 (Keilah besieged) and the 'thirty' cities against one with Josh 12.

**Yiktasu to the king, 'the Sun from heaven': I guard the king's city until his word reaches me (EA 221)** (EA 221)
- Compare Mal 4:2 (Heb 3:20) 'the sun of righteousness' and Ps 84:12 'YHWH God is a sun and shield'.

**Abdi-Ashirta of Amurru: I am the king's servant and the dog of his house; I guard Amurru and Sumur against the Hurrian kings; I harvest Sumur's grain (EA 060)** (EA 060)
- The same man is 'the dog' in Rib-Addi's letters (EA 076): compare 2 Sam 9:8 and 16:9.

**Rib-Addi: I am the footstool of the king's feet; Sumur attacked up to its gate, its commissioner dead; send Yanhamu, a wise man whom all love, and 20 pairs of horses (EA 106)** (EA 106)
- Footstool of the king's feet: compare Ps 110:1 ('until I make your enemies your footstool') and 1 Chr 28:2.
- Yanhamu, a Semite high in Egyptian service, loved by all: compare Joseph (Gen 41:38-45) and Mordecai 'liked by most of his brothers' (Esth 10:3).

**Rib-Addi: the king is like Baal and the Sun in heaven; the sons of Abdi-Ashirta took the king's horses and chariots and gave men to Subaru; who are they, dogs, to resist the archers? Send 20 men of Meluhha and 20 of Egypt (EA 108)** (EA 108)
- The king likened to Baal and the Sun: compare Ps 84:12 and 2 Sam 23:4 (the just ruler 'like the light of morning, the sun rising').
- Nubian (Meluhha) soldiers in a Canaanite garrison: compare the Cushite runner in 2 Sam 18:21 and Ebed-melech the Cushite (Jer 38:7).

**Rib-Addi: my mouth speaks truth; let Haip be questioned; Aziru and his brothers are in Damascus; no silver left, give me 30 pairs of horses with chariots (EA 107)** (EA 107)
- Damascus first named here as a refuge of the rebels; compare 1 Kgs 11:23-24 (Rezon flees and rules in Damascus).
- 'The land will have rest': compare Judg 3:11, 3:30 ('the land had rest').

**The king to Aziru of Amurru: you received the man of Byblos whose brother cast him out at the gate; you ate and drank with the man of Qadesh; serve the king and live, or die by the king's axe with all your family; come or send your son; send these enemies of the king in copper chains (EA 162)** (EA 162)
- 'Serve the king and live': compare Jer 27:12, 17 ('bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, serve him and live') and 2 Kgs 18:31-32.
- Family destroyed with the guilty: compare Josh 7:24-25 and 2 Kgs 9:7-8. The axe of the king: Isa 10:15.
- Eating bread together as a covenant: compare Gen 26:30, Gen 31:46-54 and Ps 41:10. The king 'by seeing whom all lands live': Prov 16:15 ('in the light of the king's face is life').
- Extradition of the king's enemies by name in chains: compare 1 Kgs 2:39-40 (Shimei's slaves fetched from Gath) and Jer 26:21-23 (Uriah fetched from Egypt).
- ḥnp: compare Job 8:13, 13:16 (ḥānēp) and Isa 9:16; on the resident alien compare Exod 22:20 and Deut 10:19.

**Rib-Addi: the king writes 'guard yourself', but with what? Alive I guard the king's city, dead who will? The archers died while the commissioners lived; no one speaks my loyalty; this is my lawsuit (EA 119)** (EA 119)
- 'I have no other heart': compare 1 Chr 12:34 ('not with a double heart') and Ps 12:3. Rib-Addi's protest of loyalty: 1 Sam 24:10-16 and Job 31.

**Rib-Addi: why do you write to me? I have no successor; the king did not take Abdi-Ashirta; who are the sons of Abdi-Ashirta, slave and dog? Aziru killed Piwuru; I fear my peasants; send garrison and Meluhhan men (EA 117)** (EA 117)
- 'I have no heir/successor (ina warkītīya)': compare Gen 15:2-3 and 2 Sam 18:18 ('I have no son to keep my name').
- The ruler who fears his own peasants: compare 1 Kgs 12:16-18 (Israel rebels; Adoram stoned) and 2 Kgs 9-10.

**Rib-Addi in exile in Beirut: my brother swore to the city and gave it to the sons of Abdi-Ashirta; half the city loves them, half my lord; they say 'Rib-Addi is dead'; I sit in Beirut like a dog (EA 138)** (EA 138)
- Half the people follow one claimant, half the other: compare 1 Kgs 16:21 (Tibni and Omri) and 2 Sam 15:13; 19:10-11.
- The exiled king in a neighbour's city while the capital goes over: compare David at Mahanaim (2 Sam 17:24-27) and Absalom's oath-bound conspiracy (2 Sam 15:10-12).
- 'Rib-Addi is dead' rumour: compare 2 Sam 13:30 (false report all the king's sons are dead) and 1 Kgs 1:5-25.
- kzb 'lie': compare Ps 116:11 ('every man is a liar', kōzēb), Prov 30:6; ḥmd 'precious things': Dan 11:8, 2 Chr 32:27.

**Addu-nirari of Nuhashshe: Thutmose III made my grandfather Taku king and put oil on his head; the king of Hatti presses me with tablets and treaties; come out, or send a counsellor with troops and chariots (EA 051)** (EA 051)
- The overlord makes a king and pours oil on his head: compare 1 Sam 10:1, 16:13, 1 Kgs 1:39 and 2 Kgs 9:3, 6 (anointing of kings), and Judg 9:8-15 (the trees anoint a king).
- Riksu 'binding, treaty' with tablets: compare bərît and the treaty tablets of Deut 31:26 and Josh 24:25-26.

**Aziru: I have loved service to the king from of old; the magnates of Sumur did not let me in; if the king of Hatti attacks, let my lord give me archers and chariots (EA 157)** (EA 157)
- Aziru of Amurru later went over to Hatti: compare the Amorites of Num 21:21-31 and Josh 10:5. 'I have loved service from of old': compare Exod 21:5 ('I love my master, I will not go free').

**Rib-Addi: Abdi-Ashirta the dog; the king wrote to the kings of Beirut, Sidon and Tyre to help me, but none came; we are three brothers; if no troops, I will leave the city (EA 092)** (EA 092)
- Neighbours who fail to come to help: compare Judg 5:15-17 and 23 (Reuben, Gilead, Dan, Asher, Meroz did not come) and Judg 8:5-8 (Succoth and Penuel).
- Tyre and Sidon as neighbouring kingdoms: Josh 19:28-29; 1 Kgs 5:15.

**Rib-Addi: why do you sit idle while the Habiru dog takes your cities? He cuts my orchards and fields; Byblos alone is left; without archers there is no life for Byblos (EA 091)** (EA 091)
- 'Why do you sit still?': compare Judg 18:9 and Ps 44:24 ('Awake, why do you sleep, O Lord?'). The besieged city 'left alone like a booth in a vineyard': Isa 1:8.
- Orchards and fields cut down: compare Deut 20:19-20 and 2 Kgs 3:19, 25.

**The king of Ushnatu to Uzzenu: your slave whom the son of Heyanu ransomed from the Egyptians I return with the silver; let no bad word come between us (RSO 07, 016)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 016)
- Return of a fugitive or ransomed slave: compare Deut 23:16-17 (do not return an escaped slave) against 1 Kgs 2:39-40, and Lev 25:47-49 (redemption of a slave sold to a foreigner).

**The king's daughter, your sister, to the queen of Ugarit: may the gods guard you; whatever you wish I will give (RSO 07, 018)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 018)
- Royal women corresponding as 'sisters': compare 1 Kgs 10:13 ('the king gave the queen of Sheba all she desired').

**Ari-Kirnihe to his brothers Ewri-huda and Tadie: send blue wool and linen; I will not send my messenger empty-handed (RSO 07, 022)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 022)
- Blue-purple wool (uqniātu, Hebrew təkēlet) as prized trade good: compare Exod 25:4, Ezek 27:7, 24 and Num 15:38.

**Mattenu to Padiya: guard the messenger of Uzzenu and send him back to me (RSO 07, 024)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 024)
- Safe-conduct for a messenger: compare Neh 2:7-9 (letters to the governors that they let him pass).

**Dagan-belu (of Emar) to Shipti-Baal: may the gods of Ugarit, Ea the honoured lord and the gods of Emar guard you and your wife the king's daughter; may the king's eyes look on you; send oil and linen, I will send a good bow (RSO 07, 030)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 030)
- A royal son-in-law who must win the king's eye: compare 1 Sam 18:18-27 (David as the king's son-in-law) and Gen 39:4.

**Dagan-belu to Urtenu and to Uri-Te: gods of Ugarit, Ea and the gods of Ashtata guard you; send alum, blue and red wool and linen under your seal by the sons of Urtenu: it is death and life (RSO 07, 031)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 031)
- Goods sent under seal: compare Jer 32:10-14 (sealed deed). 'Death and life' set before a person: Deut 30:15, 19.

**Dagan-baal to Urtenu, his good brother: may the gods of the king seize your hand before him; the custom between brothers is gifts, but no one sends gifts into the house of his enemy; send tin, copper, wool, alum and oil by Anani-Sharruma: it is death and life (RSO 07, 032)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 032)
- ṣārâ 'rival, enemy': compare 1 Sam 1:6 (Peninnah, Hannah's ṣārâ) and Lev 18:18; the enemy's house compare Ps 69:4-5.
- 'Gods ... take your hand': compare Ps 73:23 ('you hold my right hand') and Isa 42:6.

**Issur-Rashap to his big brothers Anani-Sharruma and Baal(?): from afar I fall at my brothers' feet; may the gods of Ugarit and the gods of the tablet-house guard you (RSO 07, 034)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 034)
- Worshipping 'from afar': compare Exod 24:1 and Gen 22:4; a school of scribes compare 1 Chr 2:55 (families of scribes).

**Tuna to Uzziltu, my son: may the thousand gods, Ea the honoured lord and Nabu lord of stylus and tablet make you honoured before your lords; you are bad, you never ask anything of me; send asafoetida, blue wool and alum (RSO 07, 036)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 036)
- Teacher and pupil as 'father' and 'son': compare Prov 1:8, 2 Kgs 2:12 and the 'sons of the prophets'.

**The king of Beirut to the prefect of Ugarit: I heard my brother set out from Ugarit; my heart is with him day and night; send me word (RSO 07, 037)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 037)
- Compare Isa 22:15 (Shebna the sōkēn over the house) and 2 Kgs 10:15 ('is your heart right with my heart?').

**Shalmaneser I of Assyria to Ibiranu of Ugarit: Tudhaliya of Hatti sent tablets of war and of peace, refused to return fugitives or to touch the oath-tablet before the Sun; at Nihriya I entered the Hittite army and made a great slaughter (RSO 07, 046)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 046)
- Lifting the hand in oath: compare Gen 14:22 ('I have lifted my hand to YHWH'), Deut 32:40 and Dan 12:7.
- sariyam 'coat of mail' is the word of Hebrew širyôn (1 Sam 17:5, 38; 1 Kgs 22:34).
- 'Why should we be enemies, being brothers?': compare Gen 13:8 ('let there be no strife between us, for we are brothers') and 2 Sam 2:26.
- Return of fugitives between kings: 1 Kgs 2:39-40; the Assyrian claim against Hatti over fugitives compare 2 Kgs 17:4.

**Hellu to his lord: may I go as your substitute; may Addu, Dagan and Itur-Mer, the great gods of Mari, guard you; my heart laughed to see you; send good horses for the king's chariot, save my life (RSO 07, 047)** (Ugarit Ras Shamra-Ougarit 07, 047)
- 'May I be your substitute': compare 2 Sam 18:33 ('would I had died instead of you, Absalom'), Exod 32:32 and Gen 44:33 (Judah offers himself in Benjamin's place).
- 'Who will show us good?' / seeing the lord's good face: Ps 4:7 and Gen 33:10.

**To my brother: may the thousand gods, the gods of Beirut and the gods of the queen of Ugarit guard you; I send a woman, my maid, with her brother: judge them truly (RIH 81/04)** (Ugarit RIH 81/04)
- Judge truly between a man and his brother: Deut 1:16-17, Exod 21:2-11 (status of a slave woman) and Lev 25:39-46.

**Fragment: servant to king Akihinni(?), prostrating; Hazilu, Panishtayu, Halbini; the bull of the oath; the men of Halbini and Hazilu made an oath with each other (RS 01.0056)** (Ugarit RS 01.0056)
- Oaths between towns over land and water: compare Gen 21:22-32 and 26:26-33 (the wells of Beersheba and the oath).

**Belu-bur to Ilimilku, his brother: why did Numenu come without your greeting? Speak my good words before the queen (RS 06.0198)** (Ugarit RS 06.0198)
- Ilimilku is the name of the Ugaritic scribe of the Baal, Kirta and Aqhat tablets. Compare Esth 4:8 (Esther sent to plead before the king) and 1 Kgs 2:13-19 (Adonijah asks Bathsheba to speak for him).

**Imtu-? king of Sidon to the king of Ugarit, my brother: may the gods guard you; about makuhu-cloths and kilts (RS 11.0723)** (Ugarit RS 11.0723)
- Kings of Sidon and Ugarit as 'brothers': compare 1 Kgs 9:13 (Hiram calls Solomon 'my brother').

**The king of Beirut to the prefect of Ugarit, my son: I send my messenger for my business in your land; set your good eyes on him (RS 11.0730)** (Ugarit RS 11.0730)
- 'Set my eyes on him': compare Gen 44:21 and Jer 39:12, 40:4 ('I will set my eye on you').

**Fragment: I made you swear before Nabu and the gods of your land and of Emar, and you have thrown my oath behind you; you do not remember me, have mercy on me (RS 12.0005)** (Ugarit RS 12.0005)
- 'You cast my words behind you': compare Ps 50:17, 1 Kgs 14:9, Neh 9:26 and Ezek 23:35. Remember me / have mercy: Gen 40:14, Neh 13:22.

**Muarihu to the prefect: you bought back my slaves for 400 silver from Hehea the Egyptian; you swore in the house of the gods; give me their ransom silver and the rest, let there be no debt between us, we are one man (RS 15.0011)** (Ugarit RS 15.0011)
- 'As one man': compare Judg 20:8, 11 and Num 14:15. Redemption of slaves from a foreigner: Lev 25:47-49 and Neh 5:8.
- Oath in the temple: compare 1 Kgs 8:31-32 (an oath before your altar in this house).

**Abushkanu to the prefect, his brother: may the gods of Amurru, of Ugarit and of the king your lord guard you; as man to companion, write your wish and I will give it (RS 15.0024 + RS 15.0050)** (Ugarit RS 15.0024 + RS 15.0050)
- Compare Exod 33:11 ('as a man speaks to his companion', kəʾăšer yədabbēr ʾîš ʾel-rēʿēhû).

**Hishmi-Kushuh to the prefect: I sent no gift because I was in Hatti; the Sun has treated Iltahmu well; my father's man comes to buy: let no one block him and no toll-collector tax him (RS 15.0033)** (Ugarit RS 15.0033)
- Compare Ezra 4:13, 20 and 7:24 (mindâ, bəlô and hălāk: tribute, custom and toll) and Num 20:17-19 (passage through a land).

**Abiramu to Silabanu, his brother: take 45 silver from Pilsu son of Ebe for the merchants; the stones sealed with my seal, weigh and pay; guard my seal until I come (RS 15.0063)** (Ugarit RS 15.0063)
- The sender's name ʾAbi-rāmu is the name Abram (Gen 11:26). Silver weighed for merchants: Gen 23:16 ('current with the merchant'); sealed goods: Deut 32:34, Jer 32:10-14.

**Prince Alihešni to the king of Ugarit: the palace writes that the borders Arma-ziti set for you stay in place, no one may alter them; Ebinnae and Kurkalli come to set your borders (RS 15.0077)** (Ugarit RS 15.0077)
- Do not move a neighbour's boundary: Deut 19:14, 27:17, Prov 22:28 and 23:10.

**Deed of Niqmepa, sealed with the dynastic seal of Yaqaru: Ammistamru transfers to Sinaranu son of Siginu houses and fields in Mahraba and Atallig, each for its silver, for ever; no stranger, royal messenger or Habiru may enter his house; whoever alters the tablet, may the gods destroy his name (RS 15.0109 + RS 16.0296)** (Ugarit RS 15.0109 + RS 16.0296)
- A royal estate given for ever to a servant and his descendants: compare 1 Sam 22:7, 2 Sam 9:7-10 (Mephibosheth's fields) and 1 Kgs 21:3 (Naboth's ancestral inheritance).
- 'May his name perish': Ps 109:13 and Deut 29:19; the curse on altering a document: Deut 4:2 and Ezra 6:11-12.
- The resident stranger (ubru) excluded: compare Exod 12:43-45 (no foreigner or tôšāb shall eat).

**Before Niqmaddu son of Ammistamru, Ahi-malku fixes the shares of his sons: Tubammu is clear of his father and brothers as the pure sun; houses, fields, cattle and slaves go to Mashshu and Sheniyanu (RS 15.0120)** (Ugarit RS 15.0120)
- A father settles one son apart with a share and the inheritance on the others: Gen 25:5-6 (sons of the concubines sent away with gifts), Judg 11:2 (Jephthah driven out) and Deut 21:15-17.
- 'Clear as the sun': compare Song 6:10 ('clear as the sun') and Ps 37:6 ('he will make your righteousness shine like the light'). El as creator: Gen 14:19 ('El Elyon, creator of heaven and earth').

**Ulmi to the queen of Ugarit, my daughter: may the gods of Ugarit and Amurru guard you; you know my whole house was put to fire; chairs for my daughter and the king (RS 16.0111)** (Ugarit RS 16.0111)
- An Amorite mother writing to her daughter the queen: compare 1 Kgs 3:1 and 2 Kgs 8:18, 26 (dynastic marriages); the house burned: Judg 12:1, 15:6.

**Deed of Niqmaddu son of Ammistamru: Kushar-abi son of Taiya bought fields on the Rahbanu river; Abdi-ilimu redeemed with silver; the king clears them of feudal service; no one may take them from him or his sons (RS 16.0133)** (Ugarit RS 16.0133)
- The buyer's name Kušar-ʾabi contains Kothar, the Ugaritic craftsman god. Land redemption and royal sale: Lev 25:23-28, Jer 32:6-15 and Ruth 4:3-9; Rahbanu compare Rehoboth (Gen 26:22).

**Fragment of a deed: in feudal service, the post of administrator; he gave Ishtar-Hurri, the gods of Harganu, and his house and share, and that of Attanu (RS 16.0173)** (Ugarit RS 16.0173)
- Household gods passing with the inheritance: compare Gen 31:19, 30-35 (Laban's teraphim) and Judg 17:5, 18:14-20 (Micah's gods).

**Baal-danu (?) king of Tyre to Baal-zakaptu, prefect of Ugarit: Abdu son of Ayahhu, overseer of the quay, took a tax of silver on 14 jars of oil from my man; my own merchants never paid tax from of old: ask the elders of Ugarit (RS 17.0039 + RS 17.0397,b + RS 17.0424)** (Ugarit RS 17.0039 + RS 17.0397,b + RS 17.0424)
- Tyre's merchant shipping: Ezek 27; 'ask your father and your elders': Deut 32:7 and Job 8:8. Customs on royal merchants: 1 Kgs 10:15.

**Mursili II, great king of Hatti, gives Niqmepa of Ugarit the border towns of Mukish named in Suppiluliuma's treaty, town by town and mountain by mountain, for ever; whoever contests or changes these words, may the thousand gods, the Storm god of Mount Hazzi and the others know it (RS 17.0062 + RS 17.0237)** (Ugarit RS 17.0062 + RS 17.0237)
- Border description town by town and to waters and mountains: compare Josh 15-19 and Num 34:1-12. Magdala = Migdal (Josh 19:38); ʿEn-Zuriya with the many ʿEn- names of Josh 15.
- Mount Hazzi is Ṣāpôn: compare Ps 48:3 ('Mount Zion, the heights of Zaphon') and Isa 14:13; Baal-zephon Exod 14:2.
- 'Tomorrow' a claim: compare Josh 22:24, 27-28 ('in time to come your sons may say ...') and Gen 30:33.

**Ebinnae to the prefect, my good son: I send my man to my son; let him take what he needs, let no one obstruct him and no toll-collector levy toll on him; look on him kindly while he stays (RS 17.0078)** (Ugarit RS 17.0078)
- Ebinnaʾe is one of the two officials sent to fix Ugarit's borders in RS 15.0077. Compare Ezra 7:24 and Neh 2:7-8.

**Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+)** (Ugarit RS 17.0079 + RS 17.0374 + RS 17.0338)
- The blessing-and-curse close conditioned on keeping 'the words written in this tablet' compare Deut 28:1-68 and Deut 29:19-20 (the curses written in this book); Lev 26.
- Heaven and earth (with mountains) as witnesses compare Deut 4:26, 30:19, 31:28, 32:1; Isa 1:2; Mic 6:1-2; Ps 50:4.
- Mount Hazzi (Ṣapon, Jebel Aqraʿ) among the divine witnesses: compare Ps 48:3 (Zion 'the heights of Zaphon') and Isa 14:13.
- Friend of my friend, enemy of my enemy compare Exod 23:22 (I will be an enemy to your enemies) and Gen 12:3.
- Return of fugitives: contrast Deut 23:16-17 (do not hand back an escaped slave) and 1 Kgs 2:39-40 (Shimei's slaves at Gath).
- Punishment extending to wife, sons and grandsons and house compare Exod 20:5, Josh 7:24-25 (Achan with his sons and daughters and all he had).

**Letter of Ari-Tešub king of Ušnatu to the king of Ugarit, 'my father': let the servants' case be judged on the road (RS 17.0083)** (Ugarit RS 17.0083)
- Kings addressing each other as father and son compare 2 Kgs 16:7 (Ahaz to Tiglath-pileser: 'I am your servant and your son') and 1 Kgs 20:32-33 ('my brother').

**Letter to a 'brother': the wife who wronged her husband sent back to her brothers; 'we are brothers, sons of one man' (RS 17.0116)** (Ugarit RS 17.0116)
- 'We are brothers, sons of one man' compare Gen 42:11, 13 ('we are all sons of one man') and Gen 13:8 ('let there be no strife between us, for we are brothers').
- A wife returned to her family compare Judg 19:2 and Deut 24:1-4.

**Verdict of Ini-Tešub of Carchemish: ʿAmmistamru of Ugarit v. ʾAmar-Baʿlu; Amar-Baal refuses the oath and the goods stay with the king's side (RS 17.0129)** (Ugarit RS 17.0129)
- An oath imposed when evidence is lacking compare Exod 22:7-10 (the oath of YHWH between the two) and 1 Kgs 8:31-32.
- Estate with olive grove and vineyard compare 1 Kgs 21 (Naboth's vineyard) and 1 Sam 8:14.

**Šuppiluliuma I to Niqmaddu of Ugarit: do not fear Nuhašše and Mukiš; keep the treaty, and the booty and fugitives you take are yours (RS 17.0132)** (Ugarit RS 17.0132)
- 'Do not fear them' addressed by a great king to an ally compare the divine 'fear not' in Deut 3:2, Josh 10:8, Isa 41:10, and Ahaz in Isa 7:4.
- Neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty compare Ezek 17:15-19 (Zedekiah broke the covenant).

**Zulanna to the prefect, 'my brother': iron dagger, linen, a slave, a horse and a mule; requests for gold, glass and bronze cauldrons (RS 17.0144)** (Ugarit RS 17.0144)
- An iron dagger as a luxury gift in the Late Bronze Age compare Judg 3:16 and 1 Sam 13:19-22 (iron-working monopoly).

**Verdict of Ini-Tešub: Aballa's merchants killed in Ugarit; Aballa assigned the oath, then released from it by settlement for 1,200 shekels (RS 17.0145)** (Ugarit RS 17.0145)
- Compensation instead of blood vengeance compare Num 35:31-32 (no ransom for a murderer) and Exod 21:30.

**Treaty of Ini-Tešub of Carchemish with Ugarit on murdered merchants: compensation of 3 minas a man, or an oath of the town that it does not know the killers (RS 17.0146)** (Ugarit RS 17.0146)
- The town oath of not knowing the killer of an unsolved murder is the closest ANE partner of Deut 21:1-9 (the elders of the nearest city declare 'our hands did not shed this blood, our eyes did not see').
- Blood requires compensation compare Gen 9:5-6 and Num 35:33.

**Šuppiluliuma I's tribute treaty for Niqmaddu: Ugarit refused to join Nuhašše and Mukiš against Hatti; tribute to king, queen, crown prince and court; the thousand gods know (RS 17.0227)** (Ugarit RS 17.0227)
- Tyrian blue/purple wool (takiltu, argamannu) as royal tribute compare Exod 25:4, 26:1 (tekhelet and argaman) and Ezek 27:7, 16.
- Loyal vassal under neighbours' pressure to revolt compare 2 Kgs 16:5-7 (Ahaz pressed by Rezin and Pekah, appeals to Assyria) and Isa 7:1-9.
- Tribute graded to the king, queen and officials compare 2 Kgs 18:14-16 and Ezra 7:15.

**Ini-Tešub's agreement with the men of Ugarit: a man of Carchemish killed in Ugarit is compensated threefold, and his lost goods threefold (RS 17.0230)** (Ugarit RS 17.0230)
- Undiscovered killer compare Deut 21:1-9; multiple restitution compare Exod 21:37-22:3 and 2 Sam 12:6 (fourfold).

**King of Amurru to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': the Umman-manda, enemy lords of your father, made peace and sent on to you (RS 17.0286)** (Ugarit RS 17.0286)
- The Umman-manda as a mysterious northern horde compare the 'foe from the north' in Jer 1:13-15, 6:22 and Gog in Ezek 38:6, 15.

**King of Ušnatu to the prefect of Ugarit: the men of Araniya with their witnesses should swear; the thieves of my slaves are in Araniya (RS 17.0288)** (Ugarit RS 17.0288)
- An accused clears himself by oath ('be clean', zakû) compare Exod 22:10 and Num 5:19-22.

**Šuppiluliuma I's edict of Ugarit's borders: Mukiš, Nuhašše and Niya attack Ugarit, Niqmaddu appeals, the Hittites rescue him; the frontier towns sealed for ever (RS 17.0339,a+)** (Ugarit RS 17.0339,a + RS 17.0340 + RS 17.0366)
- A border traced town by town and mountain by mountain compare Josh 15:1-12, Num 34:1-12 and Ezek 47:15-20.
- 'Save me from the hand of the enemy, I am your servant' compare 2 Kgs 16:7 (Ahaz to Tiglath-pileser) and Ps 31:16.
- The place name Magdala (migdal 'tower') compare Exod 14:2 (Migdol) and Magdala in Galilee.

**Hittite verdict between Ugarit and Siyannu: oaths about Habiru of the tower, cut vines, provisions to raiders from Beirut, and the return of slaves (RS 17.0341)** (Ugarit RS 17.0341)
- The Habiru as raiders compare the ʿibrim of 1 Sam 13:3-7, 14:21 and the outlaw band of Judg 11:3 and 1 Sam 22:2.
- Cutting down vines or trees in conflict compare Judg 15:5 and Deut 20:19-20.

**Verdict of Ini-Tešub: the prefect v. Mašanda over 4,000 shekels and a broken sealed tablet; Mašanda to swear or repay (RS 17.0346)** (Ugarit RS 17.0346)
- A document of obligation cancelled compare Jer 32:10-14 (sealed deed) and Neh 10:32 (remission of debts).

**Before Ini-Tešub: queen Ahat-milku gives her sons Hišmi-Šarruma and ʿAbdi-Šarruma, who sinned against ʿAmmistamru, their share and sends them to Alašiya, under oath before Ištar of the steppe (RS 17.0352)** (Ugarit RS 17.0352)
- Sons given gifts and sent away so the heir inherits alone compare Gen 25:5-6 (Abraham's sons of the concubines sent east) and Gen 21:10-14.
- Rebel princes and the throne compare 1 Kgs 1-2 (Adonijah) and Judg 11:2 (Jephthah driven out from his inheritance).

**Šauška-muwa of Amurru swears not to do murder against ʿAmmistamru of Ugarit, his ships or troops, over the daughter of the Great Lady; heaven and earth and the gods to know (RS 17.0365+)** (Ugarit RS 17.0365 + RS 18.0006)
- Heaven and earth called to witness compare Deut 30:19 and Deut 32:1.
- A royal wife of foreign birth as a political issue compare 1 Kgs 3:1 and 1 Kgs 11:1-3; a king's divorce of a queen compare Esth 1:19.

**Taguhli to the king of Ugarit: I fall twice seven times; the king is angry at the fake lapis; I was near death but recovered, and owe the god Apšukka offerings; send blue wool (RS 17.0383)** (Ugarit RS 17.0383)
- Bowing seven times from a distance compare Gen 33:3 (Jacob bows seven times as he approaches Esau).
- Near death and recovered, with a vow of offerings compare Isa 38:1-22 (Hezekiah), Ps 116:3, 8, 14 and Ps 66:13-15.

**Fragmentary letter: the gods of Mount Hazzi and Irridu guard you; men of the great queen, the daughter of the Sun; barley for his donkey (RS 17.0429)** (Ugarit RS 17.0429)
- Mount Ṣapon (Hazzi) as divine abode compare Ps 48:3 and Isa 14:13.

**The scribe Matkali-Nabû to the scribe Naheši-šalmu: why are you angry with your brother? write my sin on a tablet; send peas and lentils; the wax tablet and the sandals (RS 19.0053)** (Ugarit RS 19.0053)
- 'What is my sin?' / 'why is your face fallen?' compare Gen 31:36 (Jacob to Laban: what is my trespass?), 1 Sam 20:1, Gen 4:6 and Gen 31:2, 5 (Laban's face not as before).
- Lentils and pulses as a desired food compare Gen 25:34 and 2 Sam 17:28.

**Oath between Niqmaddu of Ugarit and Aziru of Amurru: all old claims broken, Aziru clear as the sun; 5,000 shekels paid; Aziru to fight Ugarit's enemies and Habiru raiders (RS 19.0068)** (Ugarit RS 19.0068)
- Aziru of Amurru is the same ruler as in the Amarna letters (EA 156-171); compare the Habiru raiders of the Amarna letters and 1 Sam 13:3-7.
- A covenant ending old claims between neighbours compare Gen 31:44-54 (Jacob and Laban's covenant heap) and Gen 21:22-32 (Abraham and Abimelech at Beersheba).

**King and queen of Ugarit to Kilaʾe 'our father': messenger ʾIli-milku sent to ask after the well-being of Tudhaliya, the king our lord (RS 19.0070)** (Ugarit RS 19.0070)
- Sending to ask after a king's well-being compare 2 Sam 8:10 (Toi sends Joram 'to ask him of peace') and 1 Sam 17:18.

**Deed: Agi-Tešub cleared before witnesses; the overseer of a thousand would not consent to his oath, and he and his sons are free of his hand (RS 19.0078)** (Ugarit RS 19.0078)
- Officers of thousands compare Exod 18:21, 25 and 1 Sam 8:12.

**Letter fragment about a great ship's mast: you wrote 'release it to me', but now there is none (RS 19.0115)** (Ugarit RS 19.0115)
- A ship's mast as precious timber compare Ezek 27:5 (cedar from Lebanon for Tyre's mast) and Isa 33:23.

**King of Carchemish to ʿAmmistamru: Takiya and his witnesses to swear about the 800 shekels; vineyard cut at Šurašu; the men of Arzigana to swear they did not kill the woman's husband and do not know who did (RS 20.0022)** (Ugarit RS 20.0022)
- The town's oath 'we did not kill, we do not know who killed' is a close partner of Deut 21:7 ('our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it').
- The theophoric name ʿAbdi-ʿAnati ('servant of Anat') compare Shamgar ben Anath (Judg 3:31) and Anathoth (Jer 1:1).

**Šumi-[...] to the king his lord: five months in Amurru guarding the passes; winter cold has destroyed my chariots and horses; a captive says the king of Egypt is coming out; if the gods give him into our hands (RS 20.0033)** (Ugarit RS 20.0033)
- 'The LORD will give them into your hand' compare Josh 10:8, Judg 3:28, 1 Sam 23:4 and 1 Kgs 22:6.
- Military operations in the rainy season compare 2 Sam 11:1 ('at the return of the year, when kings go out') and Ezra 10:9, 13.
- Chariots stationed at Lebanon and by the sea compare 1 Kgs 9:19 and 1 Kgs 10:26.

**King of Kadesh to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': my servant Beti-ʾilu says my offerings are in Ugarit; I send goats, donkeys and asafoetida for his sacrifices; let no one bar his way (RS 20.0172)** (Ugarit RS 20.0172)
- A foreign king's offerings at another land's sanctuary compare 2 Kgs 5:17 (Naaman's earth for sacrifice) and 1 Kgs 8:41-43 (the foreigner's prayer at the temple).

**'The king' (of Carchemish?) to the king of Ugarit: the king of Ušnatu complains you took his borders and a town; why have you done this? (RS 20.0174,a)** (Ugarit RS 20.0174,a)
- Moving a neighbour's boundary compare Deut 19:14, 27:17 and Prov 22:28; a king's complaint 'why have you done this?' compare Judg 11:12-13.

**Rapʾanu to Bin-šipṭi 'my sister': the gods of Baṭruna, of Ugarit and of our father's house sate you with old age; with a second letter of her son, who falls at his mother's feet (RS 20.0178)** (Ugarit RS 20.0178)
- 'The gods of our father's house' compare Gen 31:53 ('the God of their father'), Gen 35:2-4 and Josh 24:2, 15 (gods your fathers served).
- Sated with old age compare Gen 25:8, 35:29, Job 42:17 and Ps 91:16 ('with long life I will satisfy him').

**Letter fragment: Baal and the god of Haballa, city of trust, the gods my helpers, guard you and sate you with good old age before the king your lord for ever (RS 20.0225)** (Ugarit RS 20.0225)
- God as 'my helper' compare Ps 54:6, Ps 118:7 and the name Eliezer (Exod 18:4).

**Madaʾe to the prefect: my oxen stolen by men of Rakba; finish the case and return my oxen, or let the named elders of Rakba enter the house of the god and be cleared (RS 20.0239)** (Ugarit RS 20.0239)
- Clearing oneself before God in his house compare Exod 22:7-10 (the case comes 'before God'; an oath of YHWH between them) and 1 Kgs 8:31-32 (oath before your altar in this house).
- Elders of a town answerable for wrongdoing in its territory compare Deut 21:2-6 and Ruth 4:2.

**Letter to 'my son': send the black ʾalgbṯ stones and the heavy white stones; bring your ships and go up to the Sun your lord, who has spoken before me; a thousand shekels of gold (RS 20.0255,a)** (Ugarit RS 20.0255,a)
- Black stone and building stones for kings compare 1 Kgs 5:31 and 1 Chr 29:2 (onyx, stones of antimony).

**King of Siyannu to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': my messenger Šamhu-Rašap; settle the case with the man of Pala on the road; men of Beirut did hostility from Ugarit (RS 21.0183)** (Ugarit RS 21.0183)
- Resheph in a personal name compare Resheph as a plague-figure in Hab 3:5, Deut 32:24 and Ps 78:48; the name Resheph in 1 Chr 7:25.
- The logogram TÚL.MEŠ 'wells' for Beirut reflects Semitic beʾerōt 'wells' compare the place name Beeroth (Josh 9:17).

**Lady Aruš-Heba to the prefect, 'my son': while my husband lived you were his good friend; whatever you asked he gave; a sash sent; give bronze for the godhead I make (RS 25.0131)** (Ugarit RS 25.0131)
- A woman providing metal for a divine image compare Judg 17:3-4 (Micah's mother and the silver image) and Exod 32:2-4.

**Deed before the mayor of Ugarit and elders: Rapʾanu takes ʾAbi-malku into brotherhood with 100 shekels; whoever hates the other leaves; the childless one's goods pass to the other; seven witnesses (RS 25.0134)** (Ugarit RS 25.0134)
- 'Hate' as the term for divorce compare Deut 22:13, 24:3 and Mal 2:16; the Elephantine marriage contracts use the same formula.
- Brotherhood sworn between two men compare 1 Sam 18:3, 20:16-17 (David and Jonathan) and 1 Kgs 20:32-33.
- An heirless man's estate passing to a non-son compare Gen 15:2-3 (Eliezer of Damascus) and Num 27:8-11.

**Verdict of Ini-Tešub: ʾAmar-Baʿlu v. ʿAbdu, who seized his brother as a replacement and the brother died; ʿAbdu offered the oath, Amar-Baal refuses, ʿAbdu is clear of the blood (RS 27.0052)** (Ugarit RS 27.0052)
- Being 'clear of blood' (zakû ištu dāmī) compare 2 Sam 3:28 ('I and my kingdom are innocent before the LORD of the blood of Abner') and Deut 19:10, 21:8-9.

**Beya (Bay), chief of the troops of the Great King of Egypt, to ʿAmmurapi of Ugarit: I speak to Amun, Re and Seth, gods of Egypt, that they guard you (RS 86.2230)** (Ugarit RS 86.2230)
- Egyptian gods equated with Semitic sun and storm gods compare Exod 12:12 ('against all the gods of Egypt') and Jer 46:25 (Amon of No).

**Letter to Urtenu, 'my brother': when the king of the smiths took from me the table ... (RS 86.2232)** (Ugarit RS 86.2232)
- A guild chief of smiths compare 1 Sam 13:19-20 and Gen 4:22 (Tubal-cain, forger of bronze and iron).

**A 'brother' to Šipiṭ-Baʿlu: the man who fell before you and stayed a month with Ari; speak rightly before the king about Beltaya's words; a talent of wool, silver, fish and turmeric (RS 86.2236)** (Ugarit RS 86.2236)
- An intermediary asked to speak for one before the king compare Gen 40:14 and 2 Kgs 4:13.

**Urhi-Tešub to Urtenu, Yabninu, Baʿlu-danu, Dananu and the great men and elders of the city: the king of Carchemish has returned from Hatti; troops of help come quickly; guard the city until we arrive (RS 88.2009)** (Ugarit RS 88.2009)
- Holding a city until relief comes compare 1 Sam 11:3, 9 ('tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have deliverance') and 2 Kgs 19:9 (Tirhakah's relief army).
- Letters to 'the elders of the city' compare 1 Kgs 21:8-11 and 2 Kgs 10:1-6.

**Dagan-bēlu to Urtenu, 'my good brother, whom I love like good oil and the scent of cedar': the gods of Ugarit, Ea lord of the wide sea and the gods of Aštata guard your life; guard your mouth before the king (RS 92.2006)** (Ugarit RS 92.2006)
- Love compared to good oil and fragrance compare Song 1:3 ('your name is oil poured out'), Ps 133:2 and Eccl 7:1; the scent of Lebanon Song 4:11, Hos 14:7.
- Guarding one's mouth before the king compare Prov 13:3, 21:23, Eccl 8:2-4 and Ps 141:3.

**Iṣṣur-Rašap to Urtenu his lord: from afar I fall at my lord's feet; my heart laughs to see my lord; with letters to Adad-dayyan and Tamar-Hebat (twice three times I fall) and to Ziminu (RS 92.2017)** (Ugarit RS 92.2017)
- Seeing the lord's face as joy compare Gen 33:10 ('to see your face is like seeing the face of God'), Gen 46:30 and Ps 17:15.
- Bowing from afar compare Gen 33:3 and Exod 24:1 ('worship from afar').

**King of Amurru to the king of Ugarit, 'my son': the storm god killed some of my troops and great men; search the sea for seven days; release the goods of the troops; if a man loves his wife let him take her by ransom (RS 94.2091)** (Ugarit RS 94.2091)
- A storm at sea sent by the god compare Jonah 1:4 and Ps 107:23-29; the storm god as killer compare Job 1:16, 19.
- Seven days of searching compare 2 Kgs 2:16-17 (three days' search for Elijah) and Gen 8:10-12.

**Baʿla-dani king of Tyre to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': my man has come to me: a man of Ugarit took silver from him (RS 94.2174)** (Ugarit RS 94.2174)
- A king of Tyre in correspondence with a neighbouring king compare 1 Kgs 5:15-26 (Hiram and Solomon, 'my brother' 1 Kgs 9:13).

**Hili-Šarruma to the queen his lady: my heart pounds because of the king's illness; send me news about it (RS 94.2277)** (Ugarit RS 94.2277)
- Anxious inquiry about a sick king compare 2 Kgs 8:7-9 (Ben-hadad's sickness) and 2 Kgs 20:12 (envoys on hearing Hezekiah had been sick).

**Ehli-Tešub to Uri-Tešub, 'my brother': 30 jars of oil for the palace owed by the men of Gibaʿla; collect it with an elder and store it; silver of ʾAppu and Pedu; 111 jars on Maʿraba (RS 94.2285+)** (Ugarit RS 94.2285 + RS 94.2286)
- Oil owed to the palace by villages compare the Samaria ostraca and 1 Kgs 5:25 (oil to Hiram), 1 Chr 27:28.

**King of Kadesh to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': there is no barley in my land; give barley, and I will send sheep for offerings (RS 94.2287)** (Ugarit RS 94.2287)
- Famine in the land and grain sought from a neighbour compare Gen 42:1-5, 43:1-2 and 1 Kgs 5:25 (wheat for Hiram's household).

**Letter: your man sold my troops for 20 shekels; I send the scribe Kam-[...] about his case; settle it on the road; if you say 'I will not release him', send word (RS 94.2350)** (Ugarit RS 94.2350)
- Selling people taken from another land compare Amos 1:6, 9 (Gaza and Tyre handed over whole communities) and Joel 4:6.

**Tutu-[...] king of [...] to the king of Ugarit: a chariot overlaid with gold for the Sun; send fine ankle-stones; by the god of Mount Hazzi let us bind a treaty; send the prefect (RS 94.2364)** (Ugarit RS 94.2364)
- Gold-overlaid chariots compare 1 Kgs 10:29 and the gold-plated objects of Exod 25:11; Mount Ṣapon compare Ps 48:3.

**Yapaʿ-Haddu king of Sidon to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': you know the news of the people of [...] how in all lands, in Hatti, Babylonia and Assyria ... (RS 94.2369)** (Ugarit RS 94.2369)
- A king of Sidon in the north Levantine world compare Gen 10:15, 19 and 1 Kgs 16:31 (Ethbaal king of the Sidonians).

**A servant to his lord: twice seven times I fall; the gods of the king and Nin-egalla keep you well; bread, flour, fish, oil and the merchants' donkeys sent; the rivers are swollen; do not be sick at heart (RS 94.2387)** (Ugarit RS 94.2387)
- Bowing seven times compare Gen 33:3; rivers in flood blocking passage compare Josh 3:15 (Jordan overflowing its banks at harvest).

**Ziti-[...] to the king of Ugarit: a two-wheeled chariot and a quartz-studded harness sent; I wrote 'do not take my toll' and he wrote 'I will not take your toll'; but 70 shekels were taken last year (RS 94.2390+)** (Ugarit RS 94.2390 + RS 94.2420)
- Tolls on merchants compare 1 Kgs 10:15 (revenue from traders) and Ezra 4:13, 20 (tribute, custom and toll).

**To 'my lady': I prostrate myself at my lady's feet; may all be well in my lady's land; the oxen of ʾApsuna; I will make good all your wrongly seized property (RS 94.2402)** (Ugarit RS 94.2402)
- Prostration to a royal lady compare 1 Kgs 1:16, 31 (Bathsheba bows to the king) and 1 Kgs 2:19 (Solomon bows to his mother).

**Ehli-Tešub to Uri-Tešub, 'my brother': 300 jars of oil remain here; tell the king to send ships for the jars, or say 'I will not give'; ask Nuʿmenu; tremble and fear with them (RS 94.2412)** (Ugarit RS 94.2412)
- Oil shipped by sea between Levantine courts compare 1 Kgs 5:22-25 and Ezek 27:17 (Judah and Israel traded oil with Tyre).

**ʾAhi-malku to Uri-Tešub, 'my good brother': the gods of Tyre and of Ugarit sate you with good old age for ever; oil on my ship; your son the apprentice is negligent with his tablet; my runaway man is in a press there; 20 fish as gift (RS 94.2416+)** (Ugarit RS 94.2416 + RS 94.2418)
- talmīdu 'apprentice' compare 1 Chr 25:8 (talmîd, the pupil among the temple singers).
- Hiding in a wine press compare Judg 6:11 (Gideon threshing wheat in the wine press to hide it).

**King of Ušnatu to the king of Ugarit, 'my brother': I send the elders of ʾUllamu with ʾIli-malku to stand before you; I appeal: I love these men but my brother hates them (RS 94.2445)** (Ugarit RS 94.2445)
- Love and hate as terms of political loyalty compare 2 Sam 19:7 ('you love those who hate you and hate those who love you') and 2 Chr 19:2.

**The king of Beirut to the king of Ugarit, his brother: silver of Yadlunu; he sends his servant with his witnesses for judgement (RS 94.2478)** (Ugarit RS 94.2478)
- A dispute referred with witnesses to another's judgement compare Deut 17:8-9 and Deut 19:15 (two or three witnesses).

**The king of Ugarit to the king of Sidon: guard my ship going to Tyre; the extispicy for the ship's captain was not good; the ship entrusted to Yabni-ilu (RS 94.2483)** (Ugarit RS 94.2483)
- Consulting omens before a sea voyage compare Jonah 1:7 (lots cast on the ship) and Prov 16:33.
- Ships of Tyre and Sidon compare Isa 23:1-2 and Ezek 27:8-9.

**Ahi-malku to Uri-Teššub his brother: may the gods of Ugarit and Tyre sate you with good old age; the oil for the wool, my ship to Egypt (RS 94.2485)** (Ugarit RS 94.2485)
- The wish of 'good old age' (šībūtu damiqtu) compare Gen 15:15 and Gen 25:8 (be-seva tova), 1 Chr 29:28 (sated with days).
- Tyrian trade in oil and wool compare Ezek 27:17-18 (Judah and Israel traded oil; Damascus white wool).

**Tehi-Teššub to Sakinu his father: may the Lady guard you; my heavy burden; the servants; do not rob (RS 94.2494)** (Ugarit RS 94.2494)
- A son's letter pleading weariness compare Gen 47:9 (few and evil days).

**Letter to the prefect: the scatterers with their wives and sons; why do you send me back? my heart is very dark; wheat, milk, cheese, oil (RS 94.2524)** (Ugarit RS 94.2524)
- The darkened heart of grief compare Lam 5:17 (our eyes are darkened) and Ps 38:11.

**Letter on Ušnatu, Amurru and Kadesh: a king would not give troops and chariots; Sutean raiders' captives returned, half to Amurru, half to Kadesh, by oath (RS 94.2559)** (Ugarit RS 94.2559)
- Suteans as raiders compare the Sabeans and Chaldeans raiding in Job 1:15-17.
- Kadesh on the Orontes compare 2 Sam 24:6 (Kadesh of the Hittites, LXX).

**Taʾasi, the king's son, to the prefect: ships from Canaan with provisions; formerly Ugarit lived by Siyannu; send the rest and keep me alive (RS 94.2571)** (Ugarit RS 94.2571)
- Provisions brought by ship to keep a land alive compare 1 Kgs 5:9-11 (Hiram's timber for Solomon's grain and oil) and Gen 42:1-2 (go down and buy, that we may live).
- Sowing this year so that next year there will be plenty compare Gen 47:23-24 and Isa 37:30.

**The king of Amurru to the king of Ugarit, his son: my merchants were killed in your land; why have you done this? make compensation; return my man from Egypt (RS 94.2597)** (Ugarit RS 94.2597)
- Demand for compensation for blood shed in another's land compare Deut 21:1-9 (the town nearest the slain) and 2 Sam 21:1-6.

**The king of Byblos to the king of Ugarit, his brother: my ship's captain; my messengers were not given bread and beer in Ugarit (RS 94.2598)** (Ugarit RS 94.2598)
- Refusal of bread to messengers or travellers compare Deut 23:4-5 (Ammon and Moab did not meet Israel with bread and water) and Judg 8:5-8 (Succoth refuses bread).

**The king of Tyre to the king of Ugarit: Baʿlu-mišlu's great doors taken from the house of Dadamu without payment; let the price be paid (RS varia 25)** (Ugarit RS varia 25)
- Great doors for a house, traded between Tyre and its neighbours, compare 1 Kgs 6:31-35 (Solomon's doors of olive and cypress) and Hiram's craftsmen in 1 Kgs 7:13-14.

**Palace list: a garment of lapis and red for Iyya-Baʿlu, wool for the singer of ʿAṯtart, a cloak, seven garments, 300 linen (KTU3 4.168)** (Ugarit KTU3 4.168)
- Blue and red garments compare the tekhelet and argaman of Exod 28:5-6; singers of the temple supplied by the king compare Neh 12:47.

**Letter to the king my lord: at my lord's feet from afar seven times and seven times I fall; I spoke to Baal of Ṣapan, to the eternal Sun, ʿAṯtart, ʿAnat and the gods of Alašiya; Nmry the eternal king; ships and merchants (KTU3 2.42)** (Ugarit KTU3 2.42)
- Seven-and-seven-times prostration compare Gen 33:3 (Jacob bows seven times) and the Amarna formula.
- 'Eternal king' (melekh ʿolam) compare Jer 10:10 and Ps 10:16; Baal of Ṣapan compare Baal-zephon in Exod 14:2.

**The king of Beirut to the king of Ugarit: a man of Ashkelon robbed my harbour master's house, fled to Ugarit and went up to Alašiya; seize him and give him to my man (SMEA 42, p. 5-17)** (Ugarit SMEA 42, p.5-17)
- Ashkelon named in the Hebrew Bible compare Judg 1:18 and 1 Sam 6:17; extradition of a fugitive slave or thief compare 1 Kgs 2:39-40 (Shimei's slaves fled to Achish of Gath) and contrast Deut 23:16-17.

**Baal Cycle 1.1 II: El's messengers bow at Anat's feet in Inbb and deliver his summons: put war from the earth, pour peace, hasten to me** (KTU 1.1 II)
- Removing war from the earth compare Ps 46:10 (he makes wars cease to the end of the earth), Isa 2:4 and Hos 2:20.

**Baal Cycle 1.1 III: messengers sent to Kothar in Crete and Memphis; the word of tree and stone; Kothar comes to El's tent; 'build a house quickly'** (KTU 1.1 III)
- 'Ancient of days' compare El 'father of years' (ab šnm) with Dan 7:9 and Job 36:26 (the number of his years is unsearchable).
- Caphtor compare Amos 9:7, Deut 2:23, Jer 47:4; Memphis (Noph) Isa 19:13.
- Heaven and deeps speaking without words compare Ps 19:2-5 and Ps 42:8 (deep calls to deep).

**Baal Cycle 1.1 IV: El proclaims the name of his son Yamm, 'beloved of El', promises a house of silver and orders him to drive Baal from his throne; El's feast** (KTU 1.1 IV)
- A divine name proclaimed for the chosen son compare Ps 2:7 and Isa 9:5; 'Yw' has been compared with the name YHWH, though the reading is disputed.
- Feast for the gods with slaughtered oxen and fatlings compare 1 Kgs 1:9, 19 (Adonijah's feast) and Isa 25:6.

**Baal Cycle 1.2 I: Baal curses Yamm; Yamm's envoys come to the assembly on Mount Ll; the gods bow their heads; 'Give up Baal!'; El makes Baal Yamm's slave; Anat and Athtart restrain Baal** (KTU 1.2 I)
- The sea's arrogant demand and its 'rivers' compare Ps 93:3-4 (the rivers have lifted up their voice) and Ps 89:10.
- Gods with heads bowed in a council compare 1 Kgs 22:19 and Ps 82:1, Ps 89:6-8 (the council of the holy ones).
- Messengers as flaming fire compare Ps 104:4; a tongue like a sharp sword compare Ps 57:5, Ps 64:4, Isa 49:2.
- Inviolability of envoys compare 2 Sam 10:1-5 (Hanun's insult to David's envoys).

**Baal Cycle 1.2 III: Kothar goes to El at the source of the rivers and is told to build Yamm's palace; Athtar complains he has no house and no wife; Shapsh warns him El will overturn his throne** (KTU 1.2 III)
- The pillars of the throne and the sceptre broken compare Ps 89:45 (you have hurled his throne to the ground), Isa 14:5 (YHWH broke the staff of the wicked).
- Athtar, the would-be king, compare the 'Day Star, son of Dawn' who would ascend the mount of assembly in Isa 14:12-15.

**Baal Cycle 1.2 IV: Kothar promises Baal eternal kingship and makes the clubs Yagrush and Ayyamur; they strike Yamm's shoulder, then his skull; Yamm falls; 'Yamm is dead, Baal shall be king'** (KTU 1.2 IV)
- 'Your enemies, O YHWH, now your enemies shall perish' compare Ps 92:10 (hinneh oyvekha) with ht ibk bʿlm ht ibk tmḫṣ; eternal kingship compare Ps 145:13 and Exod 15:18.
- YHWH's rebuke of the sea compare Ps 104:7, Ps 106:9, Nah 1:4, Isa 50:2; Sea and River in parallel compare Hab 3:8 and Ps 93:3.
- 'YHWH is king' after the combat compare Ps 93:1, Ps 29:10 (YHWH sits enthroned over the flood), Exod 15:18; the god's victory over the sea compare Job 26:12 and Ps 74:13.
- Compare Q 44:24 (leave the sea at rest) for a late echo of the parted, subdued sea.

**Baal Cycle 1.3 I: a servant feasts Baal, lord of the earth: brisket carved, a holy cup no woman may see, a thousand jars of wine; a youth sings of Baal on the heights of Ṣapan; Baal looks on his daughters** (KTU 1.3 I)
- Wine mixed in the bowl for a feast compare Prov 9:2, 5 and Isa 5:22; cymbals and the singer before the god compare Ps 150:5, 1 Chr 15:16-19.
- Mount Zion 'in the recesses of Zaphon' compare Ps 48:3.

**Baal Cycle 1.3 II: Anat shuts her house and slaughters the people of the seashore and the sunrise: heads like balls, hands like locusts, knee-deep in blood; she fights tables and chairs, rejoices, washes her hands and bathes in dew of heaven and oil of earth** (KTU 1.3 II)
- The avenger wades or washes his feet in the blood of the wicked compare Ps 58:11, Ps 68:22-24 and Isa 63:1-6 (garments stained from the winepress).
- 'Dew of heaven and fatness of the earth' compare Gen 27:28, 39 and Deut 33:13, 28.
- Slaughter in the valley compare Joel 4:2, 12-14 (the valley of decision).

**Baal Cycle 1.3 III 1-31: Anat perfumes herself; a song of Baal's love; Baal's message: put war from the earth, hasten to me; the word of tree and stone, of heaven to earth and deeps to stars; 'come, I will reveal it in my mountain, divine Ṣapan, the holy mount of my inheritance'** (KTU 1.3 III:1-31)
- 'The mountain of your inheritance, the place you made for your dwelling, the sanctuary' compare Exod 15:17 (be-har naḥalatkha) and Ps 78:54 (his holy border, this mountain).
- 'My holy mountain' compare Ps 2:6 and Ps 48:2-3 (his holy mountain, beautiful in elevation, the recesses of Zaphon).
- Heavens and deep speaking compare Ps 19:2-5 and Hab 3:10 (the deep gave its voice); a secret word revealed compare Job 4:12 and Amos 3:7.

**Baal Cycle 1.3 III 32 - IV 4: Anat trembles at the messengers: what enemy has risen against Baal? 'Did I not smite Yamm, beloved of El, River the great god, muzzle Tunnanu, smite the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads ...'** (KTU 1.3 III:32-IV:4)
- Leviathan the fleeing and twisting serpent, Tannin in the sea compare Isa 27:1; the heads of Leviathan and of the tanninim compare Ps 74:13-14; Rahab and the fleeing serpent compare Job 26:12-13; Isa 51:9-10.
- 'Am I Yam or Tannin, that you set a guard over me?' compare Job 7:12; muzzling Leviathan compare Job 40:25-26.
- Loins shaking, knees giving way, face pale at bad news compare Isa 21:3-4, Nah 2:11, Ezek 21:12, Dan 5:6.
- Driven like a bird from its nest compare Isa 16:2 and Prov 27:8.

**Baal Cycle 1.3 IV 5-55: the lads repeat Baal's message; Anat agrees to put war from the earth; she crosses a thousand fields to Ṣapan; Baal sends the women away and sets an ox before her; she bathes in dew; lament: Baal has no house like the gods; Anat will make El turn to her** (KTU 1.3 IV:5-55)
- Dew poured by the heavens compare Deut 33:28, Prov 3:20 and Judg 5:20 (the stars fought from heaven); the god's horns/rays compare Hab 3:4 (rays from his hand).
- The god without a house compare 2 Sam 7:2-6 (YHWH has dwelt in a tent) and 1 Kgs 8:13.

**Baal Cycle 1.3 V: Anat threatens to bloody El's grey beard unless Baal gets a house; she storms into El's tent; El answers from his seven chambers; 'your word is wise; our king is Baal, our judge, none above him'; Shapsh glows, the heavens weak in Mot's hand** (KTU 1.3 V)
- El 'the king' who created (kwn) Baal compare Deut 32:6 (is he not your father who created you, who made you and established you, ykhonenekha).
- 'YHWH is our judge, YHWH our lawgiver, YHWH our king' compare Isa 33:22; 'none above him' compare Ps 97:9.
- The God of seven chambers compare Ps 104:3, 13 (his upper chambers) and Amos 9:6.

**Baal Cycle 1.3 VI: a gift for Athirat; Baal sends Gapn and Ugar across sea, mountains and the heights of heaven to Qudšu-Amrur and on to Kothar in Memphis and Caphtor** (KTU 1.3 VI)
- Athirat 'creatress' (qnyt) compare the verb qnh of Gen 14:19, 22 (El Elyon qoneh shamayim va-areṣ) and Gen 4:1.

**Baal Cycle 1.4 I: Baal has no house; prepare a gift for Athirat; Kothar goes up to the bellows and pours silver and gold into a canopy, couch, throne, footstool, sandals?, a table full of all the beasts of earth's foundations and a bowl with wild bulls** (KTU 1.4 I)
- The craftsman casting the sanctuary's gold furnishings (table, lampstand, bowls) compare Exod 25:23-40 and Exod 37 (Bezalel), 1 Kgs 7:48-50 (Hiram).
- The bronze sea on twelve oxen compare the bowl decorated with wild bulls (1 Kgs 7:23-25).

**Baal Cycle 1.4 II: Athirat with her spindle washes her garment in the sea; she trembles at the approach of Baal and Anat, 'have they come to slay my sons?', then sees the gleam of silver and gold and rejoices; she calls her fisherman** (KTU 1.4 II)
- The capable woman with spindle and distaff compare Prov 31:19; the creator 'banah'/'bny bnwt' compare Gen 2:22.
- A gift that opens the way before the great compare Prov 18:16 and Gen 32:21 (Jacob's present to appease Esau).

**Baal Cycle 1.4 III: Baal complains he was mocked and spat on in the assembly of the sons of El; Baal hates three feasts: of shame, of strife and of the handmaids' lewdness; Baal and Anat give gifts to Athirat; feast** (KTU 1.4 III)
- 'Six things YHWH hates, seven are an abomination' compare Prov 6:16-19 and Prov 30:15-31; God hating feasts compare Amos 5:21, Isa 1:13-14, Hos 4:13-14 (sacrifice with temple women).
- 'Blood of grapes' for wine compare Gen 49:11 and Deut 32:14.
- Spitting and mockery in the assembly compare Job 30:9-10 and Isa 50:6.

**Baal Cycle 1.4 IV: Athirat rides a saddled donkey to El at the source of the rivers; El laughs and offers her food, wine or his love; 'our king is Baal'; Baal has no house; El: am I a slave, is Athirat a handmaid, to mould bricks?** (KTU 1.4 IV)
- Making bricks as the slave's work compare Exod 1:14 and Exod 5:7-8.
- A queen approaching the king who asks 'what is your wish?' compare Esth 5:2-3 and 1 Kgs 2:19-20 (Bathsheba before Solomon).

**Baal Cycle 1.4 V: El's grey beard instructs him; let Baal give his rain, his voice in the clouds and his lightning; let a caravan bring silver, gold and lapis; Anat brings the good news; Kothar arrives and sits at Baal's right; 'shall I put a window in the house?' - 'No'** (KTU 1.4 V)
- Gold, silver, gems gathered for building the temple compare 1 Chr 29:2-8 and Exod 25:3-7, Exod 35:21-29; 'he gives his voice' in thunder compare Ps 18:14, Ps 29:3-9, Jer 10:13.
- The herald's good news across the mountains compare Isa 40:9, Isa 52:7 and Nah 2:1.
- Sit at my right hand compare Ps 110:1.

**Baal Cycle 1.4 VI: 'you will come back to my word'; cedars from Lebanon and Sirion; fire burns in the house six days and on the seventh the silver has become plates and the gold bricks; Baal feasts his brothers, the seventy sons of Athirat** (KTU 1.4 VI)
- Cedars of Lebanon for the temple compare 1 Kgs 5:20-24 and Ps 29:5-6 (Lebanon and Sirion).
- Seven days (or seven years) of building and a dedication feast compare 1 Kgs 6:38, 1 Kgs 8:2, 62-66 (fourteen days, 22,000 oxen).
- Seventy sons of the mother goddess compare Deut 32:8 (LXX/4Q 'sons of God'), Gen 10 (seventy nations), Judg 9:5 (seventy sons of Jerubbaal).

**Baal Cycle 1.4 VII: Baal takes sixty-six cities; he orders the window opened, a rift in the clouds; he gives his holy voice, the earth quakes, the mountains tremble, his enemies flee to the forests; 'I alone rule the gods'; messengers to Mot** (KTU 1.4 VII)
- The voice of YHWH breaking the cedars, shaking the wilderness, and the enemies' flight compare Ps 29:3-9, Ps 18:8-16, Ps 68:2-9, 34; YHWH roars from Zion compare Amos 1:2, Joel 4:16.
- The windows (ʾarubbot) of heaven opened compare Gen 7:11, 2 Kgs 7:2, Mal 3:10, Isa 24:18; death entering through windows compare Jer 9:20.
- 'I alone' ruler of gods and men, who satisfies all flesh compare Ps 145:15-16, Ps 104:27-28; 'is there a king or not?' compare 1 Sam 8 and Judg 17:6.

**Baal Cycle 1.4 VIII: Baal's messengers are to go to the mountains at earth's edge, lift them, and go down to the 'house of freedom' and Mot's city Miry: a pit his throne, filth his land; beware lest Mot put you in his mouth like a lamb; colophon of Ilimilku** (KTU 1.4 VIII)
- 'Free among the dead', 'counted with those who go down to the pit' compare Ps 88:5-7 and the bet ha-ḥofšit of 2 Kgs 15:5.
- The miry pit compare Ps 40:3 (bor shaʾon, ṭiṭ ha-yawen) and Ps 69:3, 15.
- Death swallowing like a beast compare Hab 2:5 and Prov 1:12 (swallow them alive like Sheol).

**Baal Cycle 1.5 I: Mot's message: though you smote Lotan the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent, Šalyaṭ of seven heads, you shall go down into my throat; my appetite is the lion's of the steppe, the whale's in the sea; you did not invite me to the feast** (KTU 1.5 I)
- Leviathan, the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent compare Isa 27:1; Job 26:13 (naḥaš bariaḥ) and Job 3:8.
- Sheol enlarging its throat (nafsheh) compare Isa 5:14 and Hab 2:5 (his appetite like Sheol, like Death never sated); Prov 30:15-16.
- The lion of the steppe and the monster of the sea for an insatiable devourer compare Ezek 32:2 and Jer 51:34.

**Baal Cycle 1.5 II: Mot's lip to earth, lip to heaven, tongue to the stars; Baal fears him and sends word: 'hail, Mot, I am your slave for ever'; Mot rejoices** (KTU 1.5 II)
- Their mouth set against heaven, their tongue walks the earth compare Ps 73:9; Death swallowing compare Isa 25:8.
- 'Will he make a covenant with you, that you take him as a slave for ever (ʿeved ʿolam)?' compare Job 40:28 and Deut 15:17, Exod 21:6.
- A covenant with Death compare Isa 28:15, 18.

**Baal Cycle 1.5 III-IV: fragments of a message to Mot (a broad seat; flocks in great number; 'I will call Mot'); 'where is Baal, where is Haddu?'; the gods eat and drink** (KTU 1.5 III, KTU 1.5 IV)
- 'Where is (the god)?' compare Ps 42:4, 11 and Ps 115:2; Joel 2:17.

**Baal Cycle 1.5 V: 'take your clouds, your wind, your rain, your seven lads, your eight boars, Pidray and Tallay, and go down; be counted among those who go down to the earth'; Baal loves a heifer in the field at the shore of death, seventy-seven times; she bears a boy** (KTU 1.5 V)
- The god of the storm going down with his clouds compare Ps 18:10-12; the 'shore of death' (šḥlmmt) compare Ps 107:18 (gates of death).
- Seventy-seven and eighty-eight compare Gen 4:24 and Judg 8:30; a calf idol connected with Baal compare Hos 13:1-2 and 1 Kgs 12:28.

**Baal Cycle 1.5 VI: the messengers found Baal fallen in the land of the shore of death: 'mighty Baal is dead'; El comes down from throne to footstool to earth, pours dust on his head, gashes cheek and chin, ploughs his chest: 'Baal is dead, what of the peoples?'; Anat roams every mountain** (KTU 1.5 VI)
- Coming down from the throne, sitting on the ground, dust on the head compare Jonah 3:6, Ezek 26:16, Job 2:8, 12-13, Lam 2:10.
- Gashing for the dead compare Lev 19:28, Deut 14:1, Jer 16:6, Jer 41:5, Jer 47:5 and 1 Kgs 18:28 (the prophets of Baal gash themselves).
- 'He is dead; what of the people?' compare 2 Sam 1:19-27 and the lament for Tammuz, Ezek 8:14.
