**Baal Cycle 1.6 I 1-31: Anat mourns, drinks her tears like wine; Shapsh lifts Baal onto Anat's shoulder; she carries him up to Ṣapan, weeps and buries him in the pit of the gods of the earth; seventy wild bulls, oxen, sheep, deer, ibex and roebucks are slaughtered** (KTU 1.6 I:1-31)
- Tears as food and drink day and night compare Ps 42:4, Ps 80:6, Ps 102:10.
- A funeral burning or offering for a king compare Jer 34:5 and 2 Chr 16:14; burial on the mountain compare Deut 34:6.

**Baal Cycle 1.6 I 32-67: Anat tells El 'let Athirat rejoice, Baal is dead'; El asks Athirat for one of her sons to make king; Athtar the Terrible ascends Ṣapan, but his feet do not reach the footstool nor his head the top: 'I cannot be king on Ṣapan'; he rules the earth** (KTU 1.6 I:32-67)
- 'You said in your heart, I will ascend ... I will sit on the mount of assembly in the recesses of Zaphon ... but you are brought down to Sheol' compare Isa 14:12-15 (Helel ben Shaḥar) with Athtar ascending and descending.
- A throne too large for the would-be king compare Saul's armour too big for David (1 Sam 17:38-39), loosely.

**Baal Cycle 1.6 II: like a cow's heart for her calf, Anat's heart longs for Baal; she seizes Mot by the hem: 'give me my brother'; Mot: 'I put him in my mouth like a lamb'; Anat splits Mot with a blade, winnows, burns, grinds and sows him; birds eat him** (KTU 1.6 II)
- Moses burns the calf, grinds it to powder, scatters it on the water compare Exod 32:20 and Deut 9:21; Josiah burns and grinds the Asherah 2 Kgs 23:6.
- God will swallow Death for ever compare Isa 25:8; 'O Death, where are your plagues?' Hos 13:14.
- As a cow longs for her calf compare Hos 4:16 and Isa 49:15 (can a woman forget her nursing child?).
- Winnowing the enemy compare Jer 15:7, Jer 51:2, Isa 41:15-16.

**Baal Cycle 1.6 III-IV: in El's dream the heavens rain oil and the wadis run with honey; El laughs: 'Baal lives, the prince, lord of the earth, exists'; 'the furrows of the fields are parched, O Shapsh: where is mighty Baal?'; Shapsh will seek him** (KTU 1.6 III, KTU 1.6 IV)
- The rains (or mountains) dripping with sweet wine and wadis with milk and honey compare Joel 4:18, Amos 9:13, Exod 3:8 and Job 20:17; oil from heaven compare Ps 133:2-3.
- 'In a dream, a vision of the night' compare Job 33:15, Gen 20:3, Num 12:6.
- 'Where is the God of Elijah?' and a god sought in drought compare 1 Kgs 18:27 (perhaps he is asleep) and 1 Kgs 18:41-45; the cracked furrows compare Jer 14:4 and Joel 1:10-20.
- 'As YHWH lives' and 'my redeemer lives' compare Job 19:25 and Ps 18:47 (ḥay YHWH).

**Baal Cycle 1.6 V: Baal strikes the sons of Athirat and sits on his throne; in the seventh year Mot returns: 'because of you I suffered shame, winnowing, burning, grinding, sifting, scorching, sowing in the sea; give me one of your brothers to eat'** (KTU 1.6 V)
- Seven-year cycles of plenty and famine compare Gen 41:25-36, 2 Kgs 8:1; the sabbatical year Lev 25:2-7.
- The adversary's fury that will 'turn back' (yṯb ap) compare Hebrew šuv ʾaf (Isa 5:25, Hos 14:5).

**Baal Cycle 1.6 VI: Mot eats his own brothers; Baal and Mot fight like wild bulls, serpents, stallions; both fall; Shapsh warns Mot that El will overturn his throne; Mot fears; Baal is enthroned; hymn: Shapsh rules the Rephaim, the dead gods; Kothar drives off Arš and Tunnanu in the sea; colophon** (KTU 1.6 VI)
- The Rephaim, the shades, compare Isa 14:9, Isa 26:14, 19, Ps 88:11, Job 26:5, Prov 2:18; the Sun over the dead compare Job 26:5-6 (Sheol naked before him).
- The dragon (tannin) in the sea compare Isa 27:1, Ps 74:13, Ezek 29:3 and Ezek 32:2.
- Bread of offering, terumah, and libation wine compare Num 15:5-10, Num 18:8-11.
- Amos 'among the herdsmen (noqdim) of Tekoa' compare Amos 1:1 with rb nqdm; Mesha the noqed 2 Kgs 3:4.

**KTU 1.7: fragmentary duplicate of Anat's battle and washing and of Baal's message (1.3 II-III): heads like balls, knees in blood, oil poured, Pidray and Arṣay, the whisper of stone, 'come and I will reveal it'** (KTU 1.7 I, KTU 1.7 II, KTU 1.7 III, KTU 1.7 IV)
- As for KTU 1.3 II-III: Ps 58:11, Isa 63:1-6; Ps 19:2-5.

**KTU 1.10 I: fragment: what the sons of El do not know; the assembly of the stars; the circle of heaven; mighty Baal, Rider of the Clouds; Anat** (KTU 1.10 I)
- Sons of God and morning stars compare Job 38:7; the host of heaven as the council compare 1 Kgs 22:19 and Isa 14:13 (above the stars of El).

**KTU 1.10 II: Baal is not in his house; he takes his bow and arrows and goes to the marsh of Šamak, full of wild bulls; Anat lifts her wings and flies after him; Baal kneels before her: 'may your life be long; Baal will anoint your horns'; she sees a cow** (KTU 1.10 II)
- The horn exalted like the wild ox, anointed with fresh oil compare Ps 92:11; horns of the wild ox compare Deut 33:17, Num 23:22.
- Lifting one's eyes and seeing compare Gen 18:2, Gen 22:4, 13.
- Under the wings compare Ps 91:4; the winged deity compare Deut 32:11.

**KTU 1.10 III: the cow bears an ox for Anat; Baal goes up the mountain and sits on his throne; the cow gives birth to a bull for Baal, a wild ox for the Rider of the Clouds, covers it with her udder; Anat climbs Ṣapan with the good news: 'a bull is born to Baal!'; Baal rejoices** (KTU 1.10 III)
- 'For a child is born to us' compare Isa 9:5 and Jer 20:15 (the man who brought my father the news, 'a son is born to you'); good news brought on the mountain compare Isa 40:9, Isa 52:7.
- A bull or calf associated with the storm god compare Exod 32:4 and 1 Kgs 12:28-29 (golden calves), Hos 8:5-6.

**KTU 1.12 I: the handmaids complain to El that 'they' devour their liver; El laughs in his heart and sends them into the wilderness to crouch and bear the Devourers and Renders, horned like bulls, with Baal's face; Baal hunts them at the edge of the steppe, burning with desire** (KTU 1.12 I)
- Hagar sent into the wilderness and the birth of Ishmael, a 'wild ass of a man' compare Gen 16:7-12 and Gen 21:14-21; the oak of Moreh at Shechem (Gen 12:6, Gen 35:4) has been compared with 'the oaks of Tkm'.
- Laughter at an announced birth compare Gen 17:17 and Gen 18:12.

**KTU 1.12 II: Baal approaches the Devourers and seizes them, or is seized; he falls like a bull in the marsh, clothed in his brothers' blood; for seven years, eight cycles, El lets the fields wither; the king ceases to judge, the water-drawers leave the spring, the noise in El's house ceases** (KTU 1.12 II)
- The sounds of millstones, bride and groom, and the drawers of water cease compare Jer 25:10, Jer 7:34, Eccl 12:4-6 (the pitcher broken at the spring), Rev 18:22-23.
- Seven years of famine compare 2 Kgs 8:1, Gen 41:27, 2 Sam 24:13; garments rolled in blood compare Isa 9:4 and Isa 63:3.

**KTU 1.13: hymn-incantation to Anat: she will kill for two, three, four days; blood for her girdle, heads for her warriors, eagles and birds of prey; a seat promised on the roof of the high heavens where the stars fall like bricks; she bathes and goes up to El her father; the cow of Baal gives birth** (KTU 1.13 I, KTU 1.13 II)
- A throne set above the stars of El compare Isa 14:13; eagles gathering at the slain compare Job 39:27-30 and Ezek 39:17-20.

**Kirta's house destroyed; his wives and heirs lost; he weeps himself to sleep (Kirta I)** (KTU 1.14 I:1-34)
- Compare Job 1:13-19 and 42:13 (the righteous man stripped of all his children, then given new ones); Job 1:2 'seven sons'.
- Tears on the bed: Ps 6:7; 1Sam 1:7-10 (Hannah weeping, not eating, before the promise of a son); Ps 56:9.
- Resheph as a destroyer: Hab 3:5; Deut 32:24; Job 5:7.

**El descends in Kirta's dream and asks why he weeps (Kirta I-II)** (KTU 1.14 I:35-52, KTU 1.14 II:1-5)
- Compare 1Kgs 3:5-13 (God appears to Solomon in a dream: 'Ask what I shall give you'; he does not ask riches); Gen 15:1-3 ('what will you give me, seeing I go childless?').
- God asks the weeping: Gen 21:17 ('What troubles you, Hagar?'); 1Sam 1:8.

**El's instructions - sacrifice on the tower, muster of the whole people, seven-day march, siege of Udum, demand for Hurriya (Kirta II-III)** (KTU 1.14 II:6-III:49)
- Rooftop sacrifice and raised hands: 2Kgs 23:12; Jer 19:13; 32:29; Zeph 1:5; 1Kgs 8:22, 54.
- Total levy with the newlywed: contrast Deut 20:5-7 and 24:5 (the new husband is exempt for a year); Joel 2:16 ('let the bridegroom leave his chamber').
- Army like locusts: Judg 6:5; 7:12; Joel 2:2-11; Nah 3:15-17. Army like a storm cloud: Ezek 38:9.
- Seven days of encirclement before action: Josh 6:3-4, 14-15 (Jericho); 1Kgs 20:29.
- Peace gifts to buy off a besieger: 2Kgs 18:14-16; 1Kgs 20:2-6 (silver, gold, wives and children demanded); 1Kgs 15:18-19.
- Bride's beauty and eyes: Song 4:1-9; 6:4-7; 7:5; Gen 29:17.

**Kirta wakes from the dream and carries out El's instructions; the army marches (Kirta III-IV)** (KTU 1.14 III:50-IV:31)
- Waking from the dream: Gen 41:7; 1Kgs 3:15 ('Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream', then sacrificed and made a feast); Gen 28:16.

**At the shrine of Athirat of Tyre Kirta vows silver and gold if he wins Hurriya (Kirta IV)** (KTU 1.14 IV:32-43)
- Conditional vows on a journey: Gen 28:20-22 (Jacob at Bethel); Judg 11:30-31 (Jephthah); 1Sam 1:11 (Hannah); 2Sam 15:7-8; Num 21:2.
- 'Ashtoreth goddess of the Sidonians': 1Kgs 11:5, 33; 2Kgs 23:13.

**Siege of Udum; King Pabil offers ransom; Kirta demands Hurriya (Kirta IV-VI)** (KTU 1.14 IV:44-VI:41')
- Compare 1Kgs 20:1-11 (Ben-hadad besieging Samaria sends messengers demanding silver, gold, wives and children); 2Sam 3:13-16 (David demands Michal as condition of peace).

**Hurriya is handed over; Udum laments like a cow for her calf (Kirta 1.15 I)** (KTU 1.15 I)
- Charity of the noble woman: Prov 31:20; Isa 58:7, 10; Job 31:16-20.
- A city weeping for its lost children: Jer 31:15 (Rachel); Lam 1:1-2; Mic 1:8 (mourning like jackals and ostriches).

**The assembly of the gods visits Kirta; at Baal's request El blesses him with cup in hand and promises sons (Kirta 1.15 II)** (KTU 1.15 II)
- Melchizedek brings bread and wine and blesses Abram: Gen 14:18-19; the cup of blessing Ps 116:13.
- 'Better to you than seven sons': Ruth 4:15; 1Sam 2:5 ('the barren has borne seven'); Job 1:2; 42:13.
- Royal child nursed by queens: Isa 49:23; 60:16 ('you shall suck the breast of kings'); Ps 2:7.
- Divine visitors at a human house and a promised son: Gen 18:1-14.

**Kirta exalted among the Rephaim; daughters promised, the youngest made firstborn; the children born; Athirat remembers the vow (Kirta 1.15 III)** (KTU 1.15 III)
- Rephaim as royal shades: Isa 14:9-10; 26:14, 19; Ps 88:11; Job 26:5; Prov 9:18.
- The younger made firstborn: Gen 48:13-20 (Ephraim over Manasseh); 1Chr 26:10 ('though he was not the firstborn his father made him chief'); Gen 25:23.
- God (gods) going up from the patriarch after speaking: Gen 17:22; 18:33; 35:13. 'Tents' and 'dwellings' (ohel / mishkan) in parallel: Num 24:5.
- Vows that must be paid: Deut 23:22-24; Eccl 5:3-5; Ps 76:12. Compare Q 9:75-77 (those who vowed to God and broke it).

**Hurriya's feasts for the nobles; weeping for the dying Kirta and talk of succession (Kirta 1.15 IV-VI)** (KTU 1.15 IV:1'-VI:10)
- Feast with the nobles and talk of succession during the king's decline: 1Kgs 1:9, 18-25 (Adonijah's feast while David lies dying).
- Dying as 'going the way of all the earth' or 'being gathered to one's fathers': 1Kgs 2:2; Judg 2:10.

**Ilihau laments over his dying father - 'shall gods die?'; Kirta sends for his daughter Thitmanat (Kirta 1.16 I)** (KTU 1.16 I)
- Ps 82:6-7 ('You are gods ... yet you shall die like men'); compare gods-condemned-to-die-like-men.
- Mountains called to mourn: 2Sam 1:21; Ezek 31:15; Jer 4:24-28. The king as son of God: Ps 2:7; 89:27-28; 2Sam 7:14.
- Women with tambourines: Exod 15:20; Judg 11:34 (Jephthah's daughter); 1Sam 18:6. Meeting at the well: Gen 24:15-20; 29:9-12.

**Thitmanat learns the truth and laments her father (Kirta 1.16 II)** (KTU 1.16 II)
- Mourning stripped: Mic 1:8 ('I will go stripped and naked'); Isa 20:2-4.

**Search for Baal's rain; the ploughmen look up, bread, wine and oil exhausted (Kirta 1.16 III)** (KTU 1.16 III)
- Rain of the Most High (ʿly): compare ʿElyon; Ps 68:10; Deut 11:14; Hos 6:3.
- Jar of flour and jug of oil in drought: 1Kgs 17:12-16; 18:5 (search the land for grass); Joel 1:10-12; Hag 1:11.
- King's righteousness and the land's rain: Ps 72:6; 2Sam 21:1; 23:3-4.

**El summons Ilish, herald of the gods, and his wife (Kirta 1.16 IV)** (KTU 1.16 IV)
- Wisdom calling from the heights: Prov 8:2-3; 9:3. Herald proclaiming: Isa 40:9; 52:7.

**El asks seven times which god will drive out the sickness; none answers; El fashions Shaatiqat (Kirta 1.16 V)** (KTU 1.16 V)
- Whom shall I send? Isa 6:8; 1Kgs 22:20-22 (who will entice Ahab? a spirit volunteers); Isa 63:5 ('no one to help').
- Creature nipped from clay: Gen 2:7; Job 33:6 ('I too was nipped (qoratsti) from clay'), the same verb qrṣ.

**Shaatiqat drives Death from the city and heals Kirta; he eats and returns to his throne (Kirta 1.16 VI)** (KTU 1.16 VI:1-24)
- Death swallowed and defeated: Isa 25:8; Hos 13:14; 1Cor 15:55. Healing with a staff: 2Kgs 4:29-35 (Gehazi's staff, Elisha revives the child).
- Hezekiah's illness and recovery: 2Kgs 20:1-11; Isa 38:1-22. Eating after a crisis: 2Sam 12:20; 1Kgs 19:5-8.

**Yassib accuses his father of neglecting justice and demands the throne; Kirta curses him (Kirta 1.16 VI)** (KTU 1.16 VI:25-59)
- Absalom at the gate: 2Sam 15:1-6 ('there is no one deputed by the king to hear you'); Adonijah: 1Kgs 1:5.
- Royal duty to widow, orphan and poor: Ps 72:2-4, 12-14; 82:3-4; Isa 1:17, 23; Jer 5:28; 22:15-16; Job 29:12-16; Prov 31:8-9.
- Kinship with the sickbed and the grave: Job 17:14 ('to the worm: my mother and my sister'); Prov 7:4.
- Fathers' curses on sons: Gen 9:25; 49:3-7. 'Name of Baal' (šm bʿl) as a divine hypostasis: compare the Name in Deut 12:11; Ashtoreth 'name of Baal' in the Eshmunazar inscription.

**Childless Danel feeds the gods for seven days; Baal intercedes; El blesses him with a son who will do a son's duties (Aqhat 1.17 I-II)** (KTU 1.17 I:0'-II:23')
- Childlessness and prayer: Gen 15:2-3; 25:21; 1Sam 1:9-18 (Hannah at the sanctuary); 2Kgs 4:14-17.
- Duties of a son: Exod 20:12; Gen 9:20-27 (Noah drunk; Shem and Japheth cover him); Isa 51:17-18 ('none to take her by the hand of all the sons she has raised'); Prov 23:22.
- A pillar to keep one's name: 2Sam 18:18 (Absalom: 'I have no son to keep my name'); Isa 56:5 (yad va-shem); Gen 28:18; 35:20.
- Laughter at the promise of a son: Gen 17:17; 18:12; 21:6. Danel (Dan'el) the righteous and wise: Ezek 14:14, 20; 28:3.

**Danel feasts the Kotharat for seven days; he counts the months of pregnancy (Aqhat 1.17 II)** (KTU 1.17 II:24'-47')
- 'Can you number the months they fulfil?' Job 39:1-2; Job 3:3-6 (the night of conception). Women attending a birth: Ruth 4:14-17; 1Sam 4:20.

**Danel judging at the gate sees Kothar-wa-Hasis approach with a bow; hospitality; the bow given to Aqhat (Aqhat 1.17 V)** (KTU 1.17 V)
- Judging at the gate: Ruth 4:1-2; Deut 21:19; 2Sam 15:2; Job 29:7-17 ('I delivered the poor and the orphan ... I made the widow's heart sing'); 1Kgs 22:10 (kings seated on the threshing floor at the gate). Danel: Ezek 14:14; 28:3.
- Lifting the eyes to see divine visitors, then a meal: Gen 18:1-8; Judg 6:18-21; 13:15-20.
- Bow and hunting son: Gen 27:3-4 (Isaac: 'take your bow, hunt game for me'); Gen 21:20.

**At the feast Anat covets Aqhat's bow, offers wealth and then immortality; he refuses and mocks her; she goes to El (Aqhat 1.17 VI)** (KTU 1.17 VI)
- Offer of eternal life by a supernatural tempter: Gen 3:4-5, 22; Q 7:20 and 20:120 ('shall I lead you to the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays?'); compare tempter-promises-angelhood-or-immortality and tree-of-immortality-and-unending-kingdom.
- Man's common death: Num 16:29; Josh 23:14; 1Kgs 2:2; 2Sam 14:14; Ps 49:8-13; 89:49; Eccl 3:19-20; Q 3:185; 21:34-35.
- Gilgamesh rebuffing Ishtar (SB VI) is the closest ANE parallel; for 'women hunting' compare Judg 4:9 (glory to a woman) and 9:54.
- Path of transgression (ntb pšʿ): Prov 4:14-19; Ps 1:1.

**Anat threatens El and gets leave; she offers Aqhat to be his sister and teach him to hunt (Aqhat 1.18 I)** (KTU 1.18 I)
- 'Say you are my sister': Gen 12:13; 20:2; 'my sister, my bride' Song 4:9; 8:1; Prov 7:4.
- A goddess demanding a mortal's death of the high god: Gilgamesh SB VI (Ishtar and the Bull of Heaven).

**Anat carries Yatpan as a bird of prey among the eagles; Aqhat is struck down at his meal; Anat weeps (Aqhat 1.18 IV)** (KTU 1.18 IV)
- Killing for a coveted possession: 1Kgs 21 (Naboth's vineyard).
- Birds of prey over a victim: Gen 15:11; Job 39:27-30; Deut 28:26; Jer 7:33.
- Life as breath and smoke: Job 7:7; Ps 78:39; 102:4; Hos 13:3; Jas 4:14.
- Shed blood: Gen 4:10-11; 9:6. Weeping over one's own victim: 2Sam 3:31-37 (David over Abner, killed by Joab).

**The bow is broken and lost; Danel at the gate; Pughat sees the withering; Danel's rain spell; seven years without Baal (Aqhat 1.19 I)** (KTU 1.19 I)
- Rider of the clouds: Ps 68:5 (rokhev ba-ʿaravot), 34; Deut 33:26; Isa 19:1; Ps 18:11; 104:3.
- No dew or rain for a slain hero's land: 2Sam 1:21 (Gilboa); 1Kgs 17:1 (Elijah: neither dew nor rain these years); seven years' famine Gen 41:27-30; 2Sam 24:13; 2Kgs 8:1.
- Blessings of the deep lying below: Gen 49:25; Deut 33:13. Baal's voice as thunder: Ps 29:3-9.
- Tearing garments at bad news: Gen 37:29, 34; 2Sam 13:31; Job 1:20.

**Pughat saddles the donkey; Danel kisses the surviving stalks; messengers bring news of Aqhat's death (Aqhat 1.19 II)** (KTU 1.19 II)
- Gideon's fleece and dew: Judg 6:37-40 (the dew wrung from the fleece). Daughter knowing the stars: Gen 15:5; Job 38:31-33.
- Dismounting or riding with a parent: Josh 15:18-19; Judg 1:14; 1Sam 25:20; Gen 22:3.
- News of a son's death: 2Sam 18:19-33 (Ahimaaz and the Cushite; David weeps for Absalom); 1Sam 4:12-18; Job 1:14-19.
- 'While the word was in the king's mouth': Dan 4:28; Gen 24:15; Isa 65:24.
- Bodily collapse at bad news: Dan 5:6 (knees knock, loins loosened); Isa 21:3-4; Nah 2:11; Ezek 21:12.

**Baal breaks the eagles' wings; Danel searches their entrails, finds Aqhat in Ṣamal, buries him, curses the places near the murder (Aqhat 1.19 III)** (KTU 1.19 III)
- Rizpah keeping birds from the bodies by day: 2Sam 21:10. Graves disturbed: Isa 14:18-20; 1Sam 28:15 ('why have you disturbed me?').
- Sleep of death: Ps 13:4; Jer 51:39; Job 14:12; Dan 12:2. Curse on a place of death: 2Sam 1:21; Gen 4:11; Josh 6:26.
- 'For ever, to all generations' (ledor vador): Ps 33:11; 89:2; 102:13.
- Pharaoh's baker and the birds: Gen 40:19; birds eating the slain: 1Sam 17:44-46; Ezek 39:4, 17-20.

**Abilum cursed with blindness; seven years of mourning with wailing women; mourning ends with sacrifice (Aqhat 1.19 IV)** (KTU 1.19 IV:1-27)
- Wailing women and gashing: Jer 9:16-20; 16:6; 41:5; 47:5; Lev 19:28; Deut 14:1; 2Chr 35:25.
- Long mourning for a son: Gen 37:34-35; 2Sam 13:37; 14:2. Ending mourning and worshipping: 2Sam 12:20.
- Blindness as curse: Deut 28:28-29; Gen 19:11; 2Kgs 6:18.

**Pughat asks her father's blessing to avenge her brother; armed under a woman's dress, she plies Yatpan with wine (Aqhat 1.19 IV)** (KTU 1.19 IV:28-#)
- Jael gives Sisera milk in her tent and kills him: Judg 4:17-21; 5:24-27. Judith adorns herself, plies Holofernes with wine and beheads him: Jdt 10:3-4; 12:17-13:10.
- Hidden weapon under clothing: Judg 3:16 (Ehud). Killing when the victim is merry with wine: 2Sam 13:28. Avenger of blood: Num 35:19-21.
- Strike thousands: 1Sam 18:7 ('Saul has slain his thousands').

**Liturgical opening of the Gracious Gods - peace to king and queen; Mot-wa-Shar pruned like a vine; songs over fire and basin (KTU 1.23 1-29)** (KTU 1.23 I:(Vs.)_1-29)
- Kid in its mother's milk: Exod 23:19; 34:26; Deut 14:21 (the old interpretation of KTU 1.23:14 as a Canaanite rite; now doubted).
- Pruning (zmr) and the vine: Lev 25:3-4; Isa 5:6; 18:5; Song 2:12 ('the time of pruning/singing (zamir) has come'); John 15:1-2. Death's staff: Isa 14:5; Ps 23:4.
- Greeting of peace to the king's house: 1Sam 25:6; Ps 122:6-8. Lines 17-22 have no translation in the source.

**El takes two women at the shore; they bear Shahar and Shalim and the gracious gods, who are sent to the holy desert for seven years (KTU 1.23 30-76)** (KTU 1.23 I:(U.R.)_30-76)
- Sons of God taking human women: Gen 6:1-4. Dawn (Shahar): Isa 14:12 (Helel ben Shahar); Ps 139:9 (wings of the dawn); Ps 110:3. Shalem as a divine name behind Jerusalem: Gen 14:18; Ps 76:3.
- Mouths reaching heaven and earth: Ps 73:9 ('they set their mouths against heaven, their tongue struts on earth'); Isa 5:14; Hab 2:5; compare death-lip-to-earth-lip-to-heaven (Mot).
- Holy desert (mdbr qdš): Ps 29:8 ('YHWH shakes the wilderness of Qadesh'). Wilderness sojourn: Num 14:33-34; Deut 8:2; Hos 2:16.
- Asking for bread and water on the way: Num 20:17-19; 21:22; Deut 2:28-29; Judg 8:5-6. Sweet lips: Song 4:3, 11.

**Hymn to Nikkal-wa-Ib - the moon god Yarikh woos Nikkal, pays the bride-price, the family weighs it; the Kotharat (KTU 1.24)** (KTU 1.24)
- Bride-price to the father: Gen 24:53; 29:18; 34:12 ('ask of me ever so great a mohar'); Exod 22:15-16; 1Sam 18:25. Silver weighed on scales: Gen 23:16; Jer 32:9-10.
- Brother and mother negotiate the marriage: Gen 24:50-55. Substitute bride offered: Gen 29:23-26 (Leah for Rachel); compare substituted-bride.
- Vineyard of the beloved: Song 8:11-12; Isa 5:1. 'Behold the young woman (ʿalmah) shall conceive and bear a son': Isa 7:14, a phrase close to hl ġlmt tld b[n] here.
- Moon and sun as lamps: Gen 1:16; Ps 136:7-9. A list of names counted on the lips: Ps 147:4.

**The mare, daughter of spring, stone, heaven and deep, sends Shapsh to each god in turn for a spell against snakebite (KTU 1.100 1-60)** (KTU 1.100 I:(Vs.)_1-60)
- Snakebite and its cure: Num 21:6-9 (the bronze serpent); compare fiery-serpents. Snake charming: Ps 58:5-6; Jer 8:17; Eccl 10:11.
- Gods who do not answer: 1Kgs 18:26-29 (Baal's prophets cry from morning till noon, 'but there was no voice').
- Caphtor: Amos 9:7; Deut 2:23; Jer 47:4. Resheph: Hab 3:5; Deut 32:24.

**Horon expels the venom with the tree of death among tamarisks; the mare asks snakes as her bride-price (KTU 1.100 61-79)** (KTU 1.100 I:61-79)
- A tree thrown into water to heal it: Exod 15:25 (Marah); 2Kgs 2:21 and 4:41 (Elisha's salt and flour). Horon: the place-name Beth-horon (Josh 10:10).
- Gruesome bride-price: 1Sam 18:25-27 (a hundred Philistine foreskins); compare foreskins-as-bride-price.
- Bronze serpent (Num 21:8-9) and the healer's power over snakes: Mark 16:18; Luke 10:19.

**Prologue of the Instruction of Amenemope - purpose of the teaching, titles of the author and of his son (Amenemope 1.1-3.7)** (Amenemope W1:1.1-2.13)
- Prov 22:17-21 ('Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise ... that you may give a true answer to those who sent you'), modelled on this prologue; Prov 1:2-6; 4:10-13 (the way of life).
- Father to son: Prov 1:8; 4:1-4.

**Chapter 1: give your ears, set your heart on the words, keep them in the casket of your belly (Amenemope 3.8-3.17)** (Amenemope W1:3.8-3.17)
- Prov 22:17-18 ('apply your heart to my knowledge; it is pleasant if you keep them within you (bevitnekha), that they be ready together on your lips'); Prov 4:20-22; 3:1-2.

**Chapter 2: do not rob the wretched; the heated man swept away; leave the evildoer to God and feed him (Amenemope 4.3-5.8)** (Amenemope W1:4.3-5.7)
- Prov 22:22 ('Do not rob the poor because he is poor, nor crush the afflicted at the gate'); Prov 25:21-22 (feed your enemy, heap coals); Prov 20:22 ('wait for YHWH'); Prov 24:29; Rom 12:19-20.
- Rise before the aged: Lev 19:32. Swept away like chaff: Ps 1:4; Job 27:20-21.

**Chapter 3: do not quarrel with the hot-mouthed; sleep a night before speaking; God knows how to answer him (Amenemope 5.9-5.19)** (Amenemope W1:5.9-5.18)
- Prov 22:24-25 ('Make no friendship with an angry man'); 15:18; 26:20-21 (fire and quarrels); 29:22; Jas 1:19.

**Chapter 4: the heated man in the temple is a tree that withers and is burned; the silent man is a tree that flourishes with sweet fruit (Amenemope 5.20-6.12)** (Amenemope W1:5.20-6.12)
- Ps 1:3-4 (tree by streams vs. chaff); Jer 17:5-8 (the shrub in the desert vs. the tree planted by water); Ps 92:13-15; Ps 37:35-36.

**Chapter 5: do not embezzle temple shares; 'today is not like tomorrow' - the flood falls, crocodiles exposed; join the silent (Amenemope 6.13-7.10)** (Amenemope W1:6.13-7.9)
- Isa 56:12 ('tomorrow will be like this day'), compare carousers-say-tomorrow-like-today; Prov 27:1 (do-not-boast-of-tomorrow); Jas 4:13-14.
- Robbing God of tithes: Mal 3:8. Reversal of fortunes: 1Sam 2:4-8; Ps 113:7-8.

**Chapter 6: do not move the boundary stone or encroach on the widow's field; one bushel from God is better than five thousand by wrong; riches fly to heaven (Amenemope 7.11-9.8)** (Amenemope W1:7.11-9.7)
- Prov 22:28 and 23:10-11 ('Do not remove the ancient landmark, nor enter the fields of the fatherless, for their Redeemer is strong'); Deut 19:14; 27:17; Hos 5:10; Job 24:2.
- Prov 15:16-17 ('better a little with the fear of YHWH than great treasure and trouble with it'); 16:8; 17:1; Ps 37:16.

**Chapter 7: do not set your heart on riches; ill-gotten wealth is swallowed by the earth or flies to heaven like geese; pray to the sun at dawn (Amenemope 9.9-10.15)** (Amenemope W1:9.9-10.14)
- Prov 23:4-5 ('Do not toil to be rich ... for riches make themselves wings, like an eagle that flies toward heaven'); Prov 28:20, 22; Matt 6:19-20.
- Earth opening its mouth: Num 16:30-33; compare earth-swallows-rebels. Daily bread: Prov 30:8; Matt 6:11.

**Chapter 8: put your goodness in people's bellies; spit on Apophis; guard your tongue; do not proclaim another's sin (Amenemope 10.16-11.11)** (Amenemope W1:10.16-11.10)
- Prov 22:1 (a good name); Prov 11:13; 17:9 (he who covers an offence seeks love); Deut 23:16-17 (do not hand back the escaped slave); Ps 34:14; Prov 21:23.

**Chapter 9: do not befriend the heated man; his portrait - ferryman of words, wolf-cub, crocodile, cloud before the wind; Khnum his potter (Amenemope 11.12-13.9)** (Amenemope W1:11.12-13.8)
- Prov 22:24-25; Prov 6:19 ('one who sows discord among brothers'); 16:28; 26:21-25 (burning lips and a wicked heart; he disguises with his lips); Ps 55:22 (smoother than butter); Jas 3:5-6.
- Potter shaping hearts: Isa 29:16; 45:9; 64:7; Jer 18:1-6; Ps 33:15 ('he fashions their hearts').

**Chapter 10: do not greet the heated man falsely; do not separate your heart from your tongue; God hates falsified words (Amenemope 13.10-14.3)** (Amenemope W1:13.10-14.3)
- Prov 26:24-26 (he who hates disguises it with his lips); Ps 12:3; 28:3 ('speak peace with their neighbours while evil is in their hearts'); Prov 12:22 ('lying lips are an abomination to YHWH'); Jer 9:7.

**Chapter 11: do not covet the poor man's goods - they choke the throat; the big mouthful swallowed and vomited (Amenemope 14.4-15.7)** (Amenemope W1:14.4-15.7)
- Prov 23:6-8 ('do not eat the bread of the stingy ... the morsel you have eaten you will vomit up'); Job 20:15 ('he swallows riches and vomits them up').

**Chapter 12: do not covet an official's property; as steward, avoid his goods (Amenemope 15.8-15.18)** (Amenemope W1:15.8-15.17)
- Prov 23:1-3 (do not desire a ruler's delicacies); Luke 16:1-12 (the steward); Prov 25:13; 26:6 (sending a message by a fool).

**Chapter 13: do not cheat with the pen; remit two-thirds of a poor man's debt; praise better than riches (Amenemope 15.19-16.14)** (Amenemope W1:15.19-16.13)
- Luke 16:5-7 (the steward reduces debts); Deut 15:1-11 (release of debts); Neh 5:10-12; Prov 22:1; Prov 15:16.
- Pen of the scribes made into a lie: Jer 8:8; Isa 10:1.

**Chapter 14: do not ingratiate yourself; greet with your mouth (Amenemope 16.15-17.3)** (Amenemope W1:16.15-17.3)
- Prov 19:6 ('many seek the favour of a generous man'); Prov 25:6-7; Exod 23:8; Prov 17:8.

**Chapter 15: do good; the beak of the Ibis is the scribe's finger; the baboon's eye roams the Two Lands (Amenemope 17.4-17.16)** (Amenemope W1:17.4-17.15)
- God's eyes roaming the earth: 2Chr 16:9; Zech 4:10; Prov 15:3; Job 34:21. Children reap the father's righteousness: Ps 37:25-26; 112:2; Prov 20:7.

**Chapter 16: do not tamper with the scales or weights; the baboon sits by the balance, his heart the plummet (Amenemope 17.17-18.13)** (Amenemope W1:17.17-18.12)
- Prov 11:1; 16:11 ('a just balance and scales are YHWH's; all the weights in the bag are his work'); 20:10, 23; Lev 19:35-36; Deut 25:13-16; Amos 8:5; Mic 6:11. Compare heart-weighed-against-maat (BD 125).

**Chapter 17: do not falsify the corn-measure, the Eye of Re; the threshing-floor's power greater than an oath by the throne (Amenemope 18.14-19.9)** (Amenemope W1:18.14-19.8)
- Deut 25:14-15 ('you shall not have in your house two kinds of ephah'); Prov 20:10 ('diverse weights and diverse measures, both are an abomination to YHWH'); Amos 8:5; Mic 6:10-11.

**Chapter 18: do not lie awake fearing tomorrow; man's words are one thing, God's deeds another; no one is sinless; the tongue is the rudder, the Lord of All the pilot (Amenemope 19.10-20.6)** (Amenemope W1:19.10-20.6)
- Prov 16:1, 9 ('the heart of man plans his way, but YHWH directs his steps'); 19:21; 20:24; Prov 27:1; Matt 6:34; Jas 4:13-15.
- Prov 20:9 ('who can say, I have made my heart clean?'); 1Kgs 8:46; Eccl 7:20; 1John 1:8. Tongue as ship's rudder: Jas 3:4-5.

**Chapter 19: in court do not falsify your words or seek a royal oath; speak the truth before the official (Amenemope 20.7-20.19)** (Amenemope W1:20.7-20.18)
- Exod 20:16; 23:1-2; Prov 14:5; 19:5, 9; Matt 5:33-37 ('let your yes be yes'); Jas 5:12.

**Chapter 20: do not pervert justice, take no bribe from the powerful; truth is God's gift; do not forge oracles (Amenemope 20.20-21.20)** (Amenemope W1:20.20-21.19)
- Exod 23:2-3, 6-8; Lev 19:15; Deut 16:19 ('a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise'); Jas 2:1-4 (fine clothes vs. shabby); Prov 2:6 (YHWH gives wisdom).
- False prophecy in God's name: Jer 23:16-32; Deut 18:20; Ezek 13:6-7.

**Chapter 21: do not seek a powerful protector; you do not know God's plans - set yourself in the arms of God; keep your report in your belly (Amenemope 21.21-22.18)** (Amenemope W1:21.21-22.18)
- Prov 20:22 ('do not say, I will repay evil; wait for YHWH'); Ps 118:8-9; 146:3; Isa 30:15 ('in quietness and trust'); Exod 14:14 ('you shall be silent'); Deut 33:27 ('underneath are the everlasting arms').
- Prov 11:13; 20:19; 29:11. God's ways unknown: Isa 55:8-9; Eccl 11:5.

**Chapter 22: do not provoke your opponent; let him empty his belly; set yourself in the arms of God (Amenemope 22.19-23.11)** (Amenemope W1:22.19-23.11)
- Prov 26:4-5; 29:11 ('a fool vents all his anger'); 15:1 (soft-answer-turns-wrath); Prov 18:13 (answering before hearing).

**Chapter 23: do not eat bread before an official; chew as pretence; look at the cup before you (Amenemope 23.12-23.20)** (Amenemope W1:23.12-23.19)
- Prov 23:1-3 ('When you sit down to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what is before you, and put a knife to your throat'); Sir 31:12-18; Luke 14:7-11.

**Chapter 24: do not repeat an official's words outside; the heart of man is the beak of God (Amenemope 23.21-24.7)** (Amenemope W1:23.21-24.6)
- Prov 25:9-10 (do not reveal another's secret); Prov 20:27 ('the spirit of man is the lamp of YHWH'); Prov 4:23.

**Chapter 25: do not laugh at the blind, mock the dwarf, harm the lame; man is clay and straw, God his builder (Amenemope 24.8-24.20)** (Amenemope W1:24.8-24.19)
- Lev 19:14 ('do not curse the deaf nor put a stumbling block before the blind'); Deut 27:18; Prov 17:5.
- Man as clay: Job 4:19; 10:9; 33:6; Isa 64:7; Gen 2:7. God brings low and raises: 1Sam 2:6-8; Ps 75:8; 113:7-8; Eccl 3:3; Jer 1:10.

**Chapter 26: do not sit in the beer-house with a greater man; befriend your equal; give your hand to an old man full of beer (Amenemope 24.21-25.15)** (Amenemope W1:24.21-25.14)
- Prov 23:20-21 ('be not among winebibbers'); Lev 19:32; Isa 51:17-18 (no one to take her hand); Prov 25:6-7 (do not claim a place among the great).

**Chapter 27: do not revile one older than you, for he saw Re before you; let him beat you while your hand is in your lap (Amenemope 25.16-26.7)** (Amenemope W1:25.16-26.6)
- Lev 19:32; Exod 21:17; Prov 20:20; 30:11, 17. Silence under abuse: Isa 50:6; 53:7; Lam 3:30; Matt 5:39.

**Chapter 28: do not pounce on a widow gleaning in the field; do not pass the stranger with your oil-jar; God loves him who honours the poor (Amenemope 26.8-26.14)** (Amenemope W1:26.8-26.13)
- Deut 24:19-21; Ruth 2:2-16 (Boaz and the gleaning widow); Deut 10:18-19; Prov 14:31; 19:17; Jas 2:5.

**Chapter 29: do not stop anyone crossing the river; take fare from the rich, waive it for the poor (Amenemope 26.15-27.5)** (Amenemope W1:26.15-27.4)
- Prov 3:27-28 ('withhold not good from those to whom it is due'); Deut 15:7-8; Q 2:177 (giving to the wayfarer).

**Chapter 30: 'see these thirty chapters' - they entertain and instruct; colophon (Amenemope 27.6-28.1)** (Amenemope W1:27.6-28.1)
- Prov 22:20 ('Have I not written for you thirty sayings (shilshom, read sheloshim) of counsel and knowledge'); Prov 22:29 ('a man skilled in his work will stand before kings'); Prov 1:4.

**Louvre writing board - titles of the son with daily dates (Amenemope W2, = 2.15-18)** (Amenemope W2)
- Evidence that the text was copied in school; compare Deut 6:7 and Prov 22:6 on teaching.

**Cairo ostracon - chapters 1-2 in a variant copy (Amenemope W3, = 3.11-4.10)** (Amenemope W3)
- Parallels W1 3.8-4.11; see Prov 22:17-22.

**Moscow writing board - chapters 4-5 (Amenemope W4, = 6.10-7.1)** (Amenemope W4)
- Parallels W1 6.10-7.1; Ps 1:3; Isa 56:12.

**Stockholm papyrus - chapters 8-11 (Amenemope W5, = 10.18-14.5)** (Amenemope W5)
- Parallels W1 10.18-14.5; Prov 22:24-25; 26:24-26.

**Turin writing board - chapters 24-26 with day-dates (Amenemope W6, = 24.1-25.9)** (Amenemope W6)
- Parallels W1 23.21-25.9; Lev 19:14; Job 10:9; 1Sam 2:6-8.

**Great Hymn to the Aten - titulary of the Aten, Akhenaten and Nefertiti; the sun rises beautiful in the horizon (AtenHymn 1-3/1)** (AtenHymn 1-3)
- Ps 104:1-2 ('clothed with honour and majesty, wrapped in light as a garment'); Ps 19:5-7 (the sun's circuit from end to end of heaven, nothing hidden from its heat); Mal 3:20.

**Great Hymn to the Aten - night: the land in darkness as in death; lions leave their dens, serpents bite (AtenHymn 3/2-4/3)** (AtenHymn 3/2-4/3)
- Ps 104:20-21 ('you make darkness and it is night, wherein all the beasts of the forest creep forth; the young lions roar after their prey'); the closest of the Psalm 104 parallels. Job 24:13-17 (thieves and murderers love the dark); 1Thess 5:2.
- Night as image of death: Ps 88:13; Job 10:21-22.

**Great Hymn to the Aten - day: people wake and work, cattle graze, birds praise, ships sail, fish leap (AtenHymn 4/4-6/2)** (AtenHymn 4/4-6/2)
- Ps 104:22-23 ('the sun rises, they slink away ... man goes out to his work and to his labour until evening'); 104:14 (grass for cattle); 104:12, 17 (birds nesting and singing); 104:25-26 ('the sea, great and wide ... there go the ships'). Ps 148:7-10; Q 24:41 (birds in flight know their prayer).

**Great Hymn to the Aten - the god makes seed grow in women, nurses the child in the womb, gives breath to the chick in the egg; 'O sole god, there is no other' (AtenHymn 6/3-7/7)** (AtenHymn 6/3-7/7)
- Ps 139:13-16 (knit in the mother's womb); Job 10:10-12 ('did you not pour me out like milk'); Ps 22:10-11; Jer 1:5; Q 23:12-14 (sperm-drop, clot, bones clothed with flesh); Q 39:6 ('in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses').
- Ps 104:24 ('How manifold are your works, O YHWH! In wisdom you made them all'); Ps 104:29-30 (breath withdrawn/sent: breath-withdrawn-return-to-dust).
- 'I am YHWH and there is no other, besides me there is no god': Isa 45:5-7, 18, 21-22; Deut 4:35, 39; 32:39; Q 112:1-4; Q 2:163; Q 28:70.

**Great Hymn to the Aten - creation alone according to his heart; Syria, Kush and Egypt each in its place, tongues and skins distinguished; the Nile below and the Nile in the sky (AtenHymn 8-10/6)** (AtenHymn 8-10/6)
- Ps 104:10-13 (springs in the valleys; he waters the mountains from his upper chambers); 104:27-28 (all wait for you to give them food in season); 104:19 (moon for seasons); Gen 8:22.
- Gen 10:5, 31 (nations by their tongues); Gen 11:1-9; Acts 17:26 ('made from one every nation ... fixing their boundaries'); Q 30:22 ('the diversity of your tongues and colours'); Q 49:13.
- Rain as heaven's watering in contrast with Egypt's river: Deut 11:10-12. Days numbered by God: Ps 139:16; Job 14:5.

**Great Hymn to the Aten - the sky made to behold creation; millions of forms from the one; 'you are in my heart, none knows you but your son' Akhenaten (AtenHymn 11-13/4)** (AtenHymn 11-13/4)
- Ps 104:29-30 ('you hide your face, they are dismayed; you take away their breath, they die ... you send forth your spirit, they are created'); Job 34:14-15; Q 3:27; 10:31.
- Matt 11:27 ('no one knows the Father except the Son'); Ps 2:7; John 1:18. God near and far: Jer 23:23; Ps 139:7-12.
- Ps 104:31-35 ends in the psalmist's personal praise, as this hymn ends in the king's: compare 'you are in my heart'.

**BD 125 (pNu): arrival at the Hall of the Two Truths and the first declaration of innocence** (BD125 W1:1-20)
- The A list compares with the 'negative' self-justifications of Job 31:1-40 (esp. 31:5-7, 13, 16-21, 38-39), the entrance liturgies Ps 15:2-5 and Ps 24:3-6, Isa 33:15, the righteous man of Ezek 18:5-9, and the negative tithe declaration Deut 26:13-14.
- Not killing / ordering a killing: Exod 20:13; Deut 5:17; 2 Sam 12:9 (David killed Uriah by order). Quran: Q 17:33, Q 25:68, Q 6:151.
- Overworking labourers and making the poor poorer: Lev 19:13, Lev 25:43, Deut 24:14-15, Exod 22:20-26 (MT), Amos 2:6-7; Q 107:2-3, Q 89:17-20.
- False measures and balances: Lev 19:35-36, Deut 25:13-16, Prov 11:1, 16:11, 20:10, Amos 8:5, Mic 6:10-11; Q 83:1-3, Q 55:7-9, Q 17:35, Q 6:152, Q 11:84-85 (Shu'ayb).
- Diminishing fields: compare moving a neighbour's boundary, Deut 19:14, 27:17, Prov 22:28, 23:10, Hos 5:10; Mic 2:2.
- Milk from the infant's mouth: compare Job 24:9 (they snatch the orphan from the breast).
- Not quenching the fire: compare the perpetual altar fire that must not go out, Lev 6:5-6 (MT).
- Sex with a male: Lev 18:22, 20:13; Q 7:80-81, Q 26:165-166.
- Purity: Ps 24:4 (clean hands, pure heart), Ps 51:9, 12 (MT).

**BD 125 (pNu): the second declaration of innocence, addressed to the 42 judges** (BD125 W1:21-62)
- The four Decalogue items appear as denials: Exod 20:13-16, Deut 5:17-20; compare Jer 7:9, Hos 4:2, and the women's pledge Q 60:12.
- Adultery with a neighbour's wife: Lev 18:20, 20:10, Job 31:9-11, Ezek 18:6; Q 17:32.
- Greed: Exod 20:17 (covet); Q 59:9 (saved from the avarice of the soul), Q 104:1-3.
- Speech: Ps 15:3 (no slander on his tongue), Ps 34:14 (MT), Prov 10:19, Lev 19:16 (no tale-bearing); eavesdropping/spying Q 49:12; loud voice Q 31:19; Q 25:63, 72.
- Reviling god and king: Exod 22:27 (MT) 'do not revile God nor curse a ruler of your people'; 1 Kgs 21:10, 13 (Naboth accused of cursing God and king); Lev 24:15-16.
- Grain usury: Exod 22:24 (MT), Lev 25:36-37 (food at interest), Deut 23:20, Ps 15:5, Ezek 18:8; Q 2:275-279, Q 3:130.
- Arrogance: Ps 131:1, Prov 16:5, 18; Q 17:37, Q 31:18.

**BD 125 (pNu): address to the gods of the hall, works of mercy, purity and the examination at the gate** (BD125 W1:63-88/4)
- 'No witness against me / no one I have wronged': 1 Sam 12:3-5 (Samuel: whose ox have I taken? ... the LORD is witness), Job 31:35; Q 36:65, Q 41:20-21 (limbs and skins witness).
- Bread to the hungry, water to the thirsty, clothes to the naked: Isa 58:7, Ezek 18:7, 16, Job 31:16-20, Job 22:6-7, Prov 25:21; Q 76:8-9, Q 90:11-16, Q 107:1-3, Q 69:34; also Matt 25:35-36.
- Pure mouth and hands: Ps 24:4, Ps 26:6, Job 17:9, Job 31:7.
- Babi, devourer of the guilty on the day of reckoning: Q 101:8-11 (light scales: 'his mother is Hawiya, a blazing fire'), Q 104:4-6 (al-Hutama).
- Interrogation at the gate: Q 39:71-73 (keepers of hell and paradise question those arriving), Q 67:8-9.

**BD 125 (pNu): the gate demands its names; Thoth announces the dead to Osiris** (BD125 W1:89-108)
- Gates that admit only the righteous: Ps 118:19-20, Isa 26:2, Ps 24:7-10; Q 39:73 (the gates of paradise opened and its keepers greet the righteous), Q 7:40 (gates of heaven not opened for the deniers).
- The doorkeeper 'who perceives hearts and searches bodies': Jer 11:20, 17:10, Ps 7:10 (MT), Prov 17:3, 21:2, 24:12; Q 3:29, Q 67:13.
- Dwelling of fire with walls of serpents and floor of flood: compare the divine throne of fire Dan 7:9-10, Ezek 1:27; Ps 29:10 (YHWH enthroned over the flood).

**BD 125 (pNu): rubric for reciting the spell** (BD125 W1:109-115/2)
- Purity and clean garments before approaching the deity: Exod 19:10, 14-15, Gen 35:2; pigs as unclean: Lev 11:7, Deut 14:8, Isa 65:4, 66:17; Q 2:173, Q 5:3.

**BD 125 (pYuya): arrival in the hall and first declaration of innocence** (BD125 W2:685-707/2)
- Same parallels as the Nu witness: Job 31, Ps 15, Ps 24:3-6, Ezek 18:5-9, Deut 26:13-14; Q 83:1-3, Q 17:31-37.

**BD 125 (pTurin 1791): the 42 addresses, late version** (BD125 W7)
- Reviling one's father: Exod 21:17, Lev 20:9, Deut 27:16; Q 17:23 (say not 'uff' to parents).
- Sinning against God in the heart: Job 1:5 (perhaps my sons cursed God in their hearts); Q 2:284.

**BD 125 (pTurin 1791): address to the gods, works of mercy, gate and Thoth, late version** (BD125 W8)
- Counting/recording of hearts: Mal 3:16 (book of remembrance), Dan 7:10; Q 82:10-12, Q 50:17-18 (recording angels).

**BD 125 vignette (pTurin 1791): captions of the weighing of the heart before Osiris** (BD125 W10)
- Weighing in the scales at the judgment: Q 7:8-9, Q 21:47 (just scales on the Day of Resurrection, even a mustard seed), Q 23:102-103, Q 101:6-11; Job 31:6 (let God weigh me in just balances), Dan 5:27, Prov 16:2, 21:2, 24:12 (the weigher of hearts), Ps 62:10 (MT).
- Fate deities at the judgment: Q 17:13-14 (each man's fate, ta'irahu, fastened on his neck; read your book), Ps 139:16.
- Thoth as recorder: Mal 3:16, Dan 7:10, Ezek 9:2-4 (the man with the scribe's kit); Q 82:10-12.
- The justified heart given back: Ezek 36:26; Ps 51:12 (MT).

**The Doomed Prince: a son granted, three fates decreed, the prince shut away and set free** (DoomedPrince 4_1-5_2/2)
- Childless king/father granted a son after asking the gods: Gen 15:2-4, 1 Sam 1:10-20, 2 Kgs 4:14-17; Q 3:38-40, Q 19:2-9 (Zechariah).
- Fate fixed at birth: Jer 1:5, Ps 139:16; Q 17:13, Q 57:22.
- Shutting the child away cannot stop fate: Q 4:78 ('wherever you are, death will overtake you, even if you are in lofty towers'), Q 3:154 (had you stayed in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their places of death), Q 62:8.

**The Doomed Prince: the princess in the high window of Naharina** (DoomedPrince 5_3-7_4/4)
- A king's daughter promised to whoever performs a feat: Josh 15:16-17, Judg 1:12-13 (Caleb's daughter to the taker of Kiriath-sepher), 1 Sam 17:25, 18:17-27.
- An Egyptian fugitive receives the local chief's daughter: Exod 2:15-21 (Moses in Midian, 'an Egyptian man saved us'), Q 28:22-28.
- Love as strong as death: Song 8:6-7; the daughter's hunger oath compare 1 Sam 14:24, Acts 23:12.

**The Doomed Prince: the wife kills the snake, the dog and the crocodile pursue the prince** (DoomedPrince 7_5-8_14)
- A woman kills a sleeping or drunken enemy: Judg 4:17-21 (Jael), Judg 5:24-27, Judith 13:2-8; the guarded bed and snake compare Tob 8:1-3.
- 'Your god has given (him) into your hand': 1 Sam 24:5, 26:8, Judg 3:28, Josh 2:24; Q 8:17.
- Fate catches up: Q 4:78, Q 62:8 ('the death you flee will meet you'), Amos 5:19 (flees a lion and a bear meets him, a snake bites him in the house).
- Crocodile and water monsters: Job 40:25-41:26 (MT, Leviathan), Ezek 29:3.

**Eloquent Peasant (version R): the journey, the trap on the path and the robbery** (EloquentPeasant W1:1_1/alt_1-12_3/alt_80)
- The powerful seizing the poor man's property: 2 Sam 12:1-4 (the poor man's ewe lamb), 1 Kgs 21 (Naboth), Mic 2:1-2, Isa 5:8, Amos 2:6-7; Q 38:21-24 (the litigants and the one ewe).
- Beaten and silenced: Jer 20:2, Ps 39:2-4; Q 26:167.

**Eloquent Peasant (version R): to Rensi; the officials' advice; the first petition** (EloquentPeasant W1:12_5/alt_82-16_7/alt_116/2)
- Father of orphans, husband (protector) of widows: Ps 68:6 (MT), Job 29:12-16, Ps 146:9, Deut 10:18; Q 93:6-10, Q 4:127.
- The just man's prosperity pictured as safe sailing and full nets: Ps 107:23-30, Ps 1:3.

**Eloquent Peasant (version R): the king orders the peasant kept talking and his family fed** (EloquentPeasant W1:16_8/alt_117-19_7/alt_138)
- Provision given secretly to the poor: Ruth 2:14-16 (Boaz orders grain dropped for Ruth without rebuking her); Q 2:271 (giving alms secretly is better).
- Words of a petition written and read to the king: Esth 6:1-2, Ezra 4:18.

**Eloquent Peasant (version R): second and third petitions, fragmentary** (EloquentPeasant W1:20_1/alt_139-31_8/alt_229)
- Restored text; see the B1 units for the full wording and parallels (Isa 28:17, Amos 5:24, Hab 1:14-17).

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the journey, the trap and the robbery** (EloquentPeasant W2:1/alt_Amherst_I_A_1-62/alt_31)
- 2 Sam 12:1-4 (the rich man takes the poor man's lamb), 1 Kgs 21:1-16, Mic 2:2, Isa 3:14-15; Q 38:21-24.
- The poor man despised: Eccl 9:16 (the poor man's wisdom is despised), Prov 14:20.

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): to Rensi; the officials' advice; the first petition** (EloquentPeasant W2:63/alt_32-102/alt_71)
- Ps 68:6 (MT), Ps 146:9, Job 29:12-17 ('I was eyes to the blind ... a father to the needy'), Isa 1:17, Jer 22:3; Q 93:9-10 ('do not oppress the orphan, do not repel the petitioner'), Q 107:1-2.

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the king orders silence, writing and secret provision** (EloquentPeasant W2:102/alt_71/2-117/alt_86)
- Ruth 2:15-16; 1 Kgs 17:4-6 (fed by ravens unseen); Q 76:9 ('we feed you for God's face only').

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the second petition (the scales tilt, the officials are inverted)** (EloquentPeasant W2:119/alt_88-169/alt_138)
- The judge's mortality: Ps 82:6-7 ('you are gods ... yet you shall die like men'), Ps 49:8-13 (MT).
- Justice turned upside down: Isa 5:7, 20, 23, Isa 10:1-2, Amos 5:7, 6:12, Hab 1:4, Eccl 3:16; Q 4:135, Q 5:8.
- Theft by the hungry excused: Prov 6:30-31 ('men do not despise a thief if he steals to satisfy his hunger').
- Eyes that do not see, ears that do not hear: Isa 6:9-10, Jer 5:21, Ezek 12:2; Q 7:179, Q 2:18.
- Truth fled: Isa 59:14-15 ('justice is turned back ... truth has stumbled in the square').

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the third petition (Re and Hapi, the balance of Thoth); the peasant is flogged** (EloquentPeasant W2:170/alt_139-223/alt_192)
- Justice as line and plummet: Isa 28:17 ('I will make justice the line and righteousness the plummet'), Amos 7:7-8; honest balances are God's: Prov 16:11; Q 55:7-9, Q 57:25 (the Book and the Balance).
- The judge as Nile/rain giving life: Ps 72:6 (the king like rain on mown grass), 2 Sam 23:3-4; Amos 5:24 ('let justice roll down like waters').
- Bribes: Exod 23:8, Deut 16:19, Prov 17:23, Isa 1:23, Mic 3:11; Q 2:188.
- Rulers as predators: Ezek 22:27, Zeph 3:3, Mic 3:1-3; fishermen taking men with nets: Hab 1:14-17.
- Do not boast of tomorrow: Prov 27:1; Q 31:34, Q 18:23-24.
- Like sheep without a shepherd, a ship without pilot: Num 27:17, 1 Kgs 22:17, Zech 10:2.
- Do not repay good with evil: Prov 17:13, Ps 35:12, 1 Sam 25:21.

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the fourth petition at the temple of Herishef** (EloquentPeasant W2:225/alt_194-256/alt_225)
- Ps 121:5-6 (YHWH your shade ... the sun shall not strike you), Isa 25:4, 32:2 (a shade from the heat, a refuge); Prov 29:20 (a man hasty in words).

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the fifth petition (the fishermen; the poor man's goods are his breath)** (EloquentPeasant W2:256/alt_225/2-269/alt_238/2)
- The poor man's livelihood not to be taken: Deut 24:6 (no millstone as pledge, 'he takes a life in pledge'), Exod 22:25-26 (MT), Sir 34:21-22 (bread of the needy is their life); Q 4:2, 10 (devouring orphans' property is eating fire).
- Hab 1:14-17 (people like fish, taken by net and hook).

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the sixth petition (full measure; the gardener of evil)** (EloquentPeasant W2:270/alt_239-294/alt_263)
- Full measure: Lev 19:35-36, Deut 25:15; Q 17:35, Q 6:152, Q 26:181-183, Q 83:1-3.
- Sowing and watering wickedness: Hos 10:13 ('you plowed wickedness, reaped injustice, ate the fruit of lies'), Job 4:8, Prov 22:8.
- Only God knows the heart: 1 Sam 16:7, Jer 17:9-10, 1 Kgs 8:39; Q 67:13.

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the seventh petition (colleague of Thoth; the breached dyke)** (EloquentPeasant W2:297/alt_266-320/alt_289)
- Speech bursting out of a full belly: Job 32:18-20 ('I am full of words, the spirit in my belly constrains me; my belly is like wine with no vent'), Jer 20:9.
- Opening the mouth of the mute, making the deaf hear: Isa 35:5-6, Exod 4:11; Q 5:110 (Jesus heals the blind and the leper).
- Do not worry about tomorrow: Prov 27:1, Eccl 7:14; Q 31:34.

**Eloquent Peasant (version B1): the eighth petition (Maat goes down to the necropolis with its doer)** (EloquentPeasant W2:320/alt_289/2-356/alt_325)
- Righteousness that endures for ever and the remembered name: Prov 10:7 (the memory of the righteous is a blessing), Ps 112:3, 6, Prov 12:19, Isa 56:5; Q 18:46 (the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord), Q 36:12.
- Righteousness delivers from death: Prov 10:2, 11:4, 12:28.
- Greed brings ruin: Prov 15:27, 28:22, 1 Tim 6:9-10; Q 102:1-2, Q 104:1-3.

**Eloquent Peasant (version B2): end of the fifth and the sixth to eighth petitions** (EloquentPeasant W3:Amherst_II_F_1-89)
- As for B1 petitions 5-8: Hos 10:13, Job 32:18-20, Prov 10:7, Isa 28:17; Q 55:7-9, Q 83:1-3.

**Eloquent Peasant (version B2): the ninth petition, the despairing peasant, the verdict** (EloquentPeasant W3:91-142)
- Do not repel the petitioner: Q 93:10; Prov 21:13 (who shuts his ear to the cry of the poor), Prov 31:8-9; the importunate widow and unjust judge, Luke 18:1-8.
- Longing for death: Job 3:20-22 ('who long for death ... and dig for it more than for hidden treasures'), Job 6:8-9, 1 Kgs 19:4, Jonah 4:3.
- The wicked man's wealth without heirs: Job 18:19, Ps 109:13, Ps 37:28, Prov 13:22.
- Restitution from the oppressor: Exod 22:3 (MT), 2 Sam 12:6, Luke 19:8; the enemy's goods given to his victim: Esth 8:1-2.

**Harper's Song of Antef (pHarris 500): generations pass, follow your heart** (HarpersSongs W1)
- Eccl 1:4 (a generation goes, a generation comes), Eccl 2:16, Ps 49:11-13 (MT) and 49:18 (when he dies he takes nothing), Job 1:21, Eccl 5:14 (MT; naked he goes as he came, nothing in his hand).
- Follow your heart, oil on the head, fine clothes: Eccl 9:7-10 (white garments, oil on your head, enjoy life with the wife you love), Eccl 11:9 ('walk in the ways of your heart'), Isa 22:13; Wis 2:1-9 rejects this outlook.
- No one returns: Job 7:9-10, Job 10:21, 2 Sam 12:23; Q 23:99-100 (barzakh: 'let me return', 'no!'), Q 36:31.
- Tombs and great houses gone: Q 26:128-129 (monuments on every height, fortresses as if to live for ever), Q 89:6-10, Q 46:25 (nothing seen but their dwellings), Ps 49:12 (MT) (their graves their houses for ever).
- The worldly life as play and adornment: Q 57:20, Q 102:1-2, Q 3:185, Q 6:94 (you have come to us alone, leaving behind what We gave you).

**Harper's Song of Antef, Saqqara copy (Paatenemheb)** (HarpersSongs W2)
- Eccl 9:7-10, Eccl 11:9-10 ('remove vexation from your heart').

**Harper's Song of Neferhotep, first song (TT 50)** (HarpersSongs W3)
- Eccl 1:4-5 (a generation goes ... the sun rises and the sun sets), Eccl 9:9 (enjoy life with the wife you love), Isa 5:12.
- Give bread to the landless for a good name: Prov 22:1, Eccl 7:1, Prov 19:17, Eccl 11:1-2; Q 2:261, Q 76:8.
- Days counted by fate: Ps 39:5-6 (MT), Ps 90:12, Job 14:5; Q 7:34, Q 16:61.
- Death unseen and unannounced: Jer 9:20 (death has climbed into our windows), Prov 27:1; Q 31:34 (no soul knows in what land it will die), Q 63:10-11.

**Harper's Song of Paser (TT 106)** (HarpersSongs W4)
- Nothing added to one's span: Ps 39:5-6 (MT), Job 14:5, Matt 6:27; Q 7:34, Q 35:11, Q 63:11.

**Harper's Song of Inherkhau (TT 359)** (HarpersSongs W5)
- The river and the wind: Eccl 1:6-7 (the wind goes to the south and turns to the north; all rivers run to the sea); each man at his hour: Eccl 3:1-2, Q 7:34, Q 10:49.
- A tomb or monument to keep one's name: 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's pillar), Isa 22:16 (Shebna's tomb), Isa 56:5; Q 26:128-129.
- Drink and be merry: Eccl 8:15, 10:19, Isa 22:13, Isa 56:12.
- The quiet, upright man: Ps 37:37, Ps 15:2-3.

**Harper's Song of Amenemheb (TT 364)** (HarpersSongs W7)
- Ps 49:11 (MT; they leave their wealth to others), Eccl 2:18-21, Ps 39:7 (MT), Luke 12:20; Q 6:94.

**Harper's Song of Thothemheb (TT 194)** (HarpersSongs W8)
- Ps 103:15-16 (the wind passes over it and its place knows it no more), Job 7:10, Ps 37:10, 36; Q 19:98 (do you perceive any one of them or hear from them a whisper?).

**Harper's Song of Tjay (TT 23)** (HarpersSongs W10)
- Death the unseen visitor: Jer 9:20, Eccl 9:12 (man does not know his time, like fish in a net); Q 4:78, Q 62:8.

**Harper's Song of Neferhotep, second song (TT 50): against the old songs, praise of the land of eternity** (HarpersSongs W11)
- The hereafter better than this life: Q 87:16-17 ('you prefer the life of this world, but the hereafter is better and more lasting'), Q 29:64 (the home of the hereafter is life indeed), Q 93:4; Wis 3:1-3, 2:1-9 (rejects the carpe diem of the ungodly).
- Life like a dream: Ps 90:5, Ps 73:20, Job 20:8, Isa 29:7-8; Q 23:112-114, Q 10:45 (as if they had stayed but an hour of a day).
- All go to the one place: Eccl 3:20, 6:6, Job 30:23 (the house appointed for all living); Q 3:185, Q 21:35.
- A land without fear: Isa 11:9, 65:25; Q 10:62, Q 15:46-48 (enter in peace, secure; no rancour).

**Harper's Song of Amenmose (TT 373): blessings on the dead** (HarpersSongs W12)
- Call and be answered: Isa 58:9, Isa 65:24, Ps 91:15, Jer 33:3; Q 40:60, Q 2:186.
- Light in the darkness of the grave: Ps 139:11-12, Isa 9:1; nursing at the breast of comfort: Isa 66:11-12.

**Harper's Song of Tjanefer, second song (TT 158)** (HarpersSongs W15)
- Eating in the world to come as on earth: Isa 25:6; Q 2:25 ('this is what we were given before'), Q 52:22-24.

**Harper's Song of Panniut (TT 331): sweet to dwell in Thebes** (HarpersSongs W16)
- Ps 84:2-5, 11 (how lovely your dwellings; a day in your courts), Ps 122:1-2; rising like eagles: Isa 40:31.

**Harper's Song of Neferhotep, third song (TT 50): the good journey and the name not forgotten** (HarpersSongs W17)
- The name of the righteous remembered: Ps 112:6, Prov 10:7, Isa 56:5; Q 19:50 (a lofty tongue of truth), Q 37:78-81 (We left for him among later generations: peace upon Noah).
- Death the equalizer: Job 3:17-19, Job 21:23-26, Eccl 9:2-3.
- Welcomed in peace: Q 39:73 ('peace be upon you, you have done well, enter'), Q 16:32, Q 15:46.

**Harper's Song of Piay (TT 263)** (HarpersSongs W18)
- Waking in peace: Isa 57:2 (he enters into peace, they rest in their beds), Dan 12:2, Ps 17:15.

**Transfiguration song of Amenemhet (TT 163)** (HarpersSongs W19)
- 'Arise' and the living body: Isa 26:19, Ezek 37:5-10, Dan 12:2; Q 75:3-4 (We are able to restore even his fingertips).

**Harper's Song of Djehutimes (TT 32)** (HarpersSongs W22)
- Protected from the womb to old age: Isa 46:3-4, Ps 22:10-11 (MT), Ps 71:6, 17-18.
- As for Neferhotep song 2: Q 87:16-17, Ps 90:5.

**Harper's Song of Nefersekheru (Zawyet el-Meitin)** (HarpersSongs W23)
- Who lives for ever? Ps 89:49 (MT; what man can live and not see death?), Ps 49:8-10 (MT); Q 21:34 ('We granted no man before you immortality'), Q 55:26-27.

**The aged Re, the plot of mankind, the council of the gods and the Eye sent as Hathor (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:1-15/2)
- Compare Gen 6:5-7 (God sees humankind's wickedness and decides to blot them out) and Gen 11:5-7 (the divine plural deliberation 'let us go down'); here the gods meet in council as in Gen 1:26 and 1 Kgs 22:19-22.
- The rebels flee into the desert: compare the mountains and the ark in Gen 7:19-23 and the son who seeks refuge on a mountain in Q 11:42-43.
- Compare Atrahasis and Gilgamesh XI: the gods' assembly decides on destruction, but here the means is the god's own Eye (Hathor-Sakhmet) rather than a flood.

**Red beer, the drunken goddess and the rescue of mankind (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:15/3-26/3)
- Compare the end of the flood in Gen 8:21-22 (God resolves never again to destroy all living things) and Gilgamesh XI 180-196 (Ea rebukes Enlil); here the high god himself contrives to stop the destroyer he sent.
- The red liquid flooding the fields 'like human blood' may be compared with the water that looks like blood to Moab in 2 Kgs 3:22-23 and with Nile water turned to blood in Exod 7:17-21.
- Compare Q 11:44 (the earth swallows its water, the matter is decided) for the abrupt ending of a divine destruction.

**Re, weary of men, rides Nut the sky-cow; men fight; the sky, the fields of the hereafter and the stars come into being (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:27-43/2)
- Compare Gen 6:3 and 6:6 (God's spirit will not remain with man; God is grieved in his heart) for the creator's weariness with humankind; and Gen 11:8-9 for divine withdrawal after human revolt.
- Origin of violence among men after the divine withdrawal: compare Gen 4:8 and Gen 6:11-13 (the earth filled with violence, ḥamas) and Q 2:30 (the angels: will you place there one who sheds blood?).
- Compare Ps 104:2-3 and Isa 40:22 (the heavens spread like a tent), and Job 26:7, 11 (the pillars of heaven tremble) for the supported, trembling sky.
- Compare the Field of Reeds with Eden (Gen 2:8-9) and the gardens of Q 47:15.

**Instructions for drawing the sky-cow with Shu, the Heh-gods and the barques, and its captions (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:44-55/2)
- The caption jw =j jm =j invites comparison with Exod 3:14 ('ehyeh asher ehyeh') and with Q 20:14 ('I am God, there is no god but me'); the Egyptian sense is uncertain.
- 'You will not grow weary' compares with Isa 40:28 (the Creator does not faint or grow weary) and Ps 121:4 (he who keeps Israel does not sleep); Q 2:255 (neither slumber nor sleep overtakes him).
- Compare Job 9:9 and 38:31-33 for the constellations set in the sky.

**Re charges Geb with the serpents of the earth and hands them to Osiris (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:56-61/2)
- Compare Gen 3:14-15 (the serpent cursed to the dust, enmity set) and Num 21:6-9; for snake-charming and spells against snakes compare Ps 58:5-6 and Jer 8:17.

**Thoth made Re's deputy; the ibis, the moon and the baboon of Thoth (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:62-74/2)
- Compare Gen 1:16-18 (the lesser light to rule the night) and Ps 104:19; Q 10:5 (God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light); Q 36:39-40.
- A god's deputy who acts in his place: compare Exod 7:1 (Moses 'as God' to Pharaoh, Aaron his prophet).

**Purity rules for reciting the book and the blessings of the reciter (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:74/3-84/2)
- Compare the purification before revelation in Exod 19:10-15 (wash garments, three days), the priestly linen and washing of Lev 16:4, and Q 56:79 (none touch it but the purified).
- Compare the blessing on the one who meditates on the Torah, Ps 1:2-3 and Josh 1:8 (prosperity and success).

**Spells of the book - Re the creator of heaven, the bas of the gods, the reciter as magician, names Eternity and Everlastingness (Heavenly Cow, Seti I)** (HeavenlyCow W1:84/3-95/27)
- For divine eternity and the names of God compare Ps 90:2, Exod 3:15 ('this is my name for ever') and Q 57:3 (He is the First and the Last).
- 'Maker of heaven who set it fast': compare Ps 33:6, Isa 42:5 and Q 79:27-28 (he raised its canopy and fashioned it).

**The spells of the Heavenly Cow in the tomb of Ramesses VI** (HeavenlyCow W2)
- Variant 'the ba of Shu is the wind': compare Gen 1:2 and Ps 104:4 (wind/spirit, rûaḥ) and Q 15:22 (We send the fertilising winds).

**Frame texts of Nut and Osiris for Tutankhamun on his outer shrine** (HeavenlyCow W3)
- Compare Isa 56:5 (a monument and a name better than sons) and Ps 72:17 (may his name endure for ever).

**Heavenly Cow texts on Tutankhamun's outer shrine - the learned scribe in heaven, Mehet-weret welcomes the king** (HeavenlyCow W4)
- 'He will not die again': compare Q 44:56 (they will not taste death there except the first death) and Rev 2:11, 20:6 (the second death).
- Knowledge of the writings exempts from judgment: contrast Ezek 18:20 and Q 99:7-8 (every atom's weight of evil is seen).

**Atum's words to Tutankhamun at sunset (outer shrine frame text)** (HeavenlyCow W5)
- Compare Ps 2:7 ('You are my son, today I have begotten you') for the divine sonship of the king.

**The lawsuit of Horus and Seth opens before the Lord of All; Ba-neb-Djed counsels writing to Neith (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 1_1-2_13/2)
- Compare the divine council of 1 Kgs 22:19-22 and Ps 82:1 (God judges among the gods); and Job 1:6-12.
- A succession dispute between the dead king's son and his brother: compare the struggle of Adonijah and Solomon (1 Kgs 1-2) and the claims of uncle against nephew in Judg 9:1-6.

**Neith's letter, the insult of Baba, the sulking of Re and Hathor's exposure (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 3_1-4_3/2)
- Ahab sulking on his bed (1 Kgs 21:4) and Jonah angry under the plant (Jonah 4:1-9) compare with the sulking high god.
- Anat and Astarte as Canaanite goddesses given to Seth: compare Judg 2:13 and 10:6 (the Ashtaroth), 1 Kgs 11:5; the place name Beth-anath (Josh 19:38).
- The threat that heaven will fall: compare Isa 34:4 and Q 22:65 (he holds back the sky from falling on the earth except by his leave).

**Seth's claim of strength, Isis's oath, Seth's threat to kill a god a day (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 4_3/3-5_3)
- Compare the right of the firstborn son against a brother in Deut 21:15-17 and the law of inheritance in Num 27:8-11.
- Oath 'as X lives' compare 1 Sam 14:39, 2 Sam 15:21 ('as YHWH lives').

**The island in the middle, the bribed ferryman, and Isis's parable by which Seth condemns himself (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 5_3/2-8_1)
- Isis's disguised case makes Seth pronounce his own verdict exactly like Nathan's parable to David, 2 Sam 12:1-7 ('You are the man'), the wise woman of Tekoa, 2 Sam 14:1-20, and the disguised prophet of 1 Kgs 20:38-42; compare also Q 38:21-24 (the two litigants before David).
- The goddess transformed into a beautiful girl to tempt the enemy compares with Judith 10-12 and with Jael (Judg 4:17-22).

**The white crown for Horus, Seth's protest, the hippopotamus contest, Isis's harpoon and the beheading of Isis (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 8_1/2-10_1/3)
- Compare Behemoth and Leviathan in Job 40:15-41:34 and Isa 27:1 for the river beasts; Ezek 29:3-5 (Pharaoh as the monster hooked in the Nile).
- Compare 2 Sam 14:6-7 (two brothers fight in the field and one kills the other) and Gen 4:8.

**Seth tears out Horus's eyes; Hathor heals him with gazelle milk (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 10_2-10_11)
- Cain's lie, Gen 4:9 ('Am I my brother's keeper?') and the brothers' deceit of Jacob, Gen 37:31-33, compare with Seth's lie.
- Blinding of a rival: Judg 16:21 (Samson), 2 Kgs 25:7 (Zedekiah); healing of eyes: Tob 11:10-13; Q 12:93-96 (Jacob's sight restored by Joseph's shirt).

**The feast, Seth's assault, the semen on the lettuce and the golden disk (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 10_11/2-13_2/3)
- Sexual domination as humiliation: compare Gen 19:4-9 (Sodom) and Judg 19:22-25; and Ham's offence against Noah, Gen 9:20-25; Q 7:80-81 (Lot's people).
- Spitting in the face as public shaming: Num 12:14, Deut 25:9, Isa 50:6.
- A hidden thing that speaks from inside to convict the guilty: compare the ordeal of the bitter water, Num 5:11-28.

**The race in stone ships and Horus's appeal to Neith at Sais (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 13_2/4-14_4/3)
- Compare the widow who keeps coming to the unjust judge (Luke 18:1-8) and the long-drawn lawsuit of Job (Job 31:35-37).

**The letters to and from Osiris - barley and emmer, the messengers of the underworld, all go down to the West (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 14_5-15_10/2)
- Grain as the gift that keeps humans alive: compare Gen 1:29, Ps 104:14-15 and Q 80:24-32 (We cause grain to grow ... provision for you and your cattle).
- The angel of death and messengers who take the souls of evildoers: Q 32:11, Q 6:93 (the angels stretching out their hands: deliver up your souls), Q 8:50; 2 Kgs 19:35.
- All go down to the one place: Eccl 3:20 and 9:10, Job 3:13-19 and 30:23 (the house appointed for all living).

**Seth brought in fetters; Horus crowned king; Seth becomes Re's thunderer; colophon (Contendings of Horus and Seth)** (HorusSeth 15_10/3-16_8)
- Compare Ps 2:6-9 and Ps 110:1-2 for the son enthroned and his enemies subdued; and the reconciled rival given a role, 2 Sam 9 (Mephibosheth at David's table).
- The storm god thundering in the sky: Ps 29:3-9, Ps 18:13; Job 37:2-5; Q 13:13 (the thunder glorifies his praise).

**Broken opening - doorkeepers plunder, the Delta bears shields, a man sees his son as enemy (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 1:1-1:12)
- Compare Mic 7:6 (a man's enemies are the men of his own house) and Matt 10:35-36.
- Compare Lam 5:2 (our inheritance turned over to strangers) and Deut 28:43 (the stranger rises above you).

**'O, yet' - the Nile unploughed, women barren, pestilence and blood, the river is blood (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 2:1-2:14/3)
- The river of blood from which men drink and the thirst for water compare with the first plague, Exod 7:17-24 (the Egyptians dig round the Nile for water), Ps 78:44 and 105:29; Q 7:133 (flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood).
- Pestilence and blood everywhere: Exod 9:3-6 (cattle pestilence), Exod 12:29-30 (no house without its dead), Ezek 5:17 and 38:22.
- Reversal of rich and poor: 1 Sam 2:5-8, Lam 4:5 (those raised in purple embrace dung heaps), Lam 5:8, Eccl 10:6-7, Luke 1:52-53.
- Women barren because of the state of the land: Hos 9:11-14; Lam 4:3-4.

**'O, yet' - foreign bowmen, jewels on maidservants, no ships to Byblos, laughter perished (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 3:1-3:14/3)
- Compare Lam 5:15 (the joy of our hearts has ceased, our dancing turned to mourning) and Jer 7:34, 16:9; Amos 8:10.
- Lebanon wood for Egypt and the merchant ships: Ezek 27:5-9 (cedars of Lebanon for Tyre's masts), 1 Kgs 5:6-10.
- Strangers devour the land: Isa 1:7, Lam 5:2.

**'O, yet' - hair fallen out, endless noise, 'I wish I could die', children dashed against walls, the embalmed cast out (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 4:1-4:14/3)
- 'I wish I could die': Job 3:20-22 and 6:8-9, Jer 8:3 (death chosen rather than life), Rev 9:6; Q 19:23 (Mary: would that I had died before this).
- Children dashed: Ps 137:9, Hos 10:14 and 14:1, Nah 3:10, 2 Kgs 8:12.
- Bones of kings and priests thrown out of their graves: Jer 8:1-2; 2 Kgs 23:16.
- Lam 4:5 and 5:11-14 (princes hung up, young men at the millstones) for nobles reduced to the quern.

**'O, yet' - 'if I knew where god is', cattle weep, cult is futile, brother strikes brother, end of humankind wished (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 5:1-5:14/2)
- 'If I knew where god is': Job 23:3-9 ('Oh that I knew where I might find him'), Ps 42:3, 10 ('Where is your God?').
- Cattle mourn and the beasts groan: Joel 1:18-20, Jer 12:4, Hos 4:3.
- Brother against brother: Isa 19:2 (Egyptian against Egyptian, brother against brother), Jer 9:4, Mic 7:2-6.
- The wish that humankind end, with no birth: Job 3:3-10, Jer 20:14-18; compare the reverse wish of Gen 9:1.
- Futility of offerings: Isa 1:11-15, Mal 1:10.

**'O, yet' - hunger, magic stripped bare, scribes slain and registers destroyed, the poor in the Ennead's place (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 6:1-6:14/2)
- Famine in the siege: Lam 1:11, 2:12, 4:4-10; 2 Kgs 6:25; and the prodigal eating swine's food, Luke 15:16.
- The book of the law cast down and lost: 2 Kgs 22:8-13; the scrolls burned, Jer 36:23.
- Wise and fool disagree: 'the wise says yes, the fool says no' (6:13-6:13/2) compares with Prov 26:4-5.

**'Look' - fire risen, the king carried off by wretches, the pyramid emptied, the Residence fallen in an hour, the inversion of owners (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 7:1-8:7)
- Eat your food in joy, the gift that god gives to the one he favours: Eccl 2:24-26, 3:13, 5:17-19, 9:7 ('go, eat your bread with joy').
- The city fallen in a single hour: Rev 18:10, 17, 19; Lam 4:6 (Sodom overthrown in a moment).
- Slaves rule and princes walk: Eccl 10:5-7, Prov 30:21-23, Lam 5:8.
- Kings taken from their graves: Jer 8:1-2, Isa 14:18-20.

**'Look' - ladies give children for beds, chiefs flee, offices like a herd without herdsman, a man slain beside his brother (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 8:7/2-9:14/3)
- Sheep without a shepherd: Num 27:17, 1 Kgs 22:17, Ezek 34:5-6, Zech 10:2, Matt 9:36.
- Mothers trading children: Lam 4:10, 2 Kgs 6:28-29, Joel 3:3 (they sold a girl for wine).
- The darkness of the ninth plague (Exod 10:21-23) has sometimes been compared with 'day does not dawn' (9:11), but the line is too broken to be sure.

**'Destroy the enemies of that august Residence' - the plundered royal estate (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 10:1-10:11/3)
- Compare the imprecations for Zion's enemies, Ps 137:7-9 and Lam 1:21-22, 3:64-66.

**'Remember' - the lost rites; Re's decree; why does he create? (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 10:12-11:13)
- Remembering the lost temple festivals: Lam 1:4, 7 and 2:6-7 (the LORD has made Zion forget festival and sabbath); Ps 42:5 (how I went with the throng to the house of God).
- Why did God make man? Job 7:17-20 ('what is man that you make so much of him'), Ps 89:47-48 ('for what vanity have you created all the sons of men'); Q 23:115.

**The reproach of the creator - shepherd of all, 'is he asleep?', 'is he a shepherd who loves death?' (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 12:1-13:8/2)
- God as shepherd who neglects the flock: Ps 44:11-12, 22 (you made us like sheep for slaughter), Ps 74:1, Ps 80:1-2; contrast Ps 23 and Ezek 34:11-16.
- 'Is he asleep?' Ps 44:23-24 ('Awake! Why do you sleep, O Lord?'), Ps 121:4, 1 Kgs 18:27; contrast Q 2:255.
- God should have destroyed the first generation: Gen 6:5-7 (God regrets having made man and resolves to blot him out) and Gen 8:21 (the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth).
- Accusing God of deception: Jer 4:10, 20:7; Job 9:22-24.
- Statues burned and temples entered: Ps 74:3-8, Lam 1:10, 2:7.

**'Indeed it is good when' - the restored order: ships, pyramids, canals, feasts (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 13:9-14:6)
- Visions of restored peace: Isa 65:21-23, Mic 4:4 (each under his vine and fig tree), Zech 8:4-5, Jer 31:12-13; Ps 104:15 (wine to gladden the heart).

**Asiatics, Nubians and Libyans; 'Egypt will not be given to the sand' (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 14:9-15:11/2)
- The nations named as attackers: Nah 3:9 (Cush, Egypt, Put and Libya her helpers), Ezek 30:4-5, Jer 46:9.
- Strangers learn the secrets of the land: Lam 1:10 (the nations have entered her sanctuary).

**What Ipuwer said in answer to the Lord of All, and the Lord of All's reply (Admonitions of Ipuwer)** (Ipuwer 15:13-17:3)
- A dialogue in which the complainant answers God and God replies: Job 38-42, Hab 1:2-2:4, Jer 12:1-6.
- Do not worry about tomorrow: Matt 6:34; Prov 27:1.

**Empty heading lines and the pAmherst fragments of the Dispute of a Man with his Ba** (ManAndBa 0-0/2, ManAndBa pAmherst.3.Fragm, ManAndBa pAmherst.3)
- Too broken for comparison; the beginning of the dialogue is lost.

**The man complains that his ba drags him to death and appeals to the gods as judges (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa pBerlin.P.3024:(x+)1, ManAndBa 2-29)
- Self-address to the soul: Ps 42:6, 12 and 43:5 ('Why are you cast down, O my soul?'), Ps 103:1; Q 75:2 (the self-reproaching soul).
- Life passes, the tree falls: Job 14:1-2, 7-10, Ps 90:5-6, Eccl 11:3.
- Appeal to God to judge one's case: Ps 7:9, 26:1, 43:1 ('Vindicate me, O God'); Job 16:19-21 (my witness is in heaven).

**The ba replies 'you are no man'; the man promises the ba a well-provided burial (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa 30-51)
- The name that survives: Ps 49:12 (they call lands by their names), Prov 10:7, Isa 56:5; 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's pillar, 'I have no son to keep my name in remembrance').
- Burial by the heir: Gen 25:9, 35:29, 50:12-13.

**The ba: burial is heartbreak; 'follow the beautiful day'; two parables of a peasant (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa 55-84)
- 'Follow the beautiful day, forget care': Eccl 9:7-10, 11:9-10 and 2:24; Isa 22:13 ('let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die'); Q 57:20 (the life of this world is play and amusement).
- No return to see the sun: Job 7:9-10 and 10:21-22, 2 Sam 12:23, Eccl 6:5; Q 23:99-100 (a barrier until the day they are raised).
- Children who died before seeing the light: Job 3:16, Eccl 4:3 and 6:3-5, Ps 58:9.
- Even the great builders' monuments perish: Eccl 2:4-11, 16; Job 3:14 (kings who built ruins for themselves); Q 26:128-129 (you build monuments on every height as if you will live for ever).

**'Behold, my name stinks because of you' (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa 85-101)
- The stench of one's name: Gen 34:30 ('you have made me stink to the inhabitants'), Exod 5:21, 1 Sam 13:4, 2 Sam 10:6; Eccl 10:1 (dead flies make the perfumer's oil stink).
- Job's reproach of his reputation among men: Job 30:1-10, Ps 31:12-14, Ps 69:12.

**'To whom shall I speak today?' (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa 103-129/2)
- No one is righteous, all have turned aside: Ps 12:2-3, Ps 14:1-3 and 53:2-4, Mic 7:2-6, Jer 5:1, 9:3-5 (let every one beware of his neighbour, put no trust in any brother).
- The friend become enemy: Ps 41:10, Ps 55:13-15, Job 19:13-19.
- Compare the 'woe is me' of Mic 7:1-2 and Isa 57:1 (the righteous perish and no one lays it to heart).

**'Death is before me today' (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa 130-140)
- Death longed for as rest: Job 3:13-22 (the weary at rest, the prisoners at ease), Job 7:15, Eccl 4:2, Phil 1:21-23; contrast Eccl 9:4-5.
- Longing for home after captivity: Ps 126:1, Ps 137:1-6.

**'He who is yonder will be a living god' (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa 142-145)
- The righteous dead with God: Ps 49:16 and 73:24 (afterward you will receive me to glory), Wis 3:1-8, Dan 12:3; Q 3:169 (those slain in God's way are alive with their Lord, provided for).

**The ba's last word - cling to life, and we shall make a landing place together; colophon (Dispute of a Man with his Ba)** (ManAndBa 147-154/2)
- Choose life: Deut 30:19; Eccl 9:4 (a living dog is better than a dead lion); and the soul's return to God at death, Eccl 12:7.

**The rebel, the agitating talker and his followers; mild punishment (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:1_1-3_6/3)
- Blot out the name and memory: Deut 25:19, 29:20, Ps 9:6-7, 109:13; the rebel and his house destroyed, 1 Kgs 16:11-12, 2 Kgs 9:7-10.
- The whisperer who separates friends and stirs the city: Prov 16:28, 26:20-21, Prov 29:8 (scoffers set a city aflame).

**Speech is stronger than fighting; imitate the ancestors; life on earth is short; do Maat (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:3_7-4_11/3)
- Wise speech stronger than weapons: Prov 25:15 (a soft tongue breaks a bone), Eccl 9:16-18 (wisdom better than weapons of war), Prov 18:21.
- Seek the words of the ancestors: Deut 32:7, Job 8:8-10, Ps 78:2-4.
- 'Is it for ever that a man lives?' Ps 49:8-10, 89:48-49, Job 14:1-2; the remembered righteous, Prov 10:7, Ps 112:6.
- Bribes pervert the judge: Exod 23:8, Deut 16:19.

**Comfort the weeper, oppress no widow; do not kill; the judges of the dead (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:5_1-5_10/3)
- Do not wrong the widow or fatherless: Exod 22:21-23, Deut 24:17, Isa 1:17, Jer 22:3, Zech 7:10; Q 4:2-10 and Q 93:9-10 (do not oppress the orphan).
- God avenges blood: Gen 9:5-6, Deut 32:43, Ps 9:13.
- A thousand years as a day, a lifetime as an hour: Ps 90:4-6, 2 Pet 3:8; Q 23:112-114 (how many years did you tarry? a day or part of a day); Q 30:55.
- Deeds set out before the judge: Q 18:49 (the book leaves nothing small or great), Q 99:6-8, Q 21:47 (scales of justice); Eccl 12:14, Dan 7:10, Rev 20:12.
- The spirit returns to the place it knows: Eccl 12:7, Job 7:10.

**Raise the youth, choose men by their deeds, serve the temple; one day gives for eternity (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:5_11-6_10)
- Choosing officials for ability: Exod 18:21, Deut 1:13-15, Prov 22:29 (a man skilful in his work will stand before kings).
- Better is one day in your courts than a thousand: Ps 84:11; Ps 27:4.
- God knows those who serve him: Mal 3:16-18, Nah 1:7, 2 Tim 2:19.

**Strife foretold, the tombs of Thinis, peace with the south, do not wreck another's monument (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:6_10/2-7_11/2)
- Prophecies of strife between generations: Isa 3:5 (the youth insolent to the elder), Mic 7:6.
- Do not remove the ancient landmark: Prov 22:28, 23:10; desecration of tombs, 2 Kgs 23:16-18.

**The pacified Delta and the wretched Asiatic, a crocodile on its bank (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:8_1-9_13/2)
- The nomadic Asiatic who cannot be beaten: Gen 16:12 (Ishmael, 'his hand against every man'), Gen 21:20-21; Judg 6:3-5 (Midianites and the people of the east raiding like locusts).
- Egypt's eastern border defences and the 'Way of Horus': Exod 13:17 (the way of the land of the Philistines), Gen 46:28-34 (Goshen).
- Pharaoh as crocodile: Ezek 29:3, 32:2.

**Build in the Delta; god attacks the temple-rebel; kingship a goodly office; the king's guilt at Thinis (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:10_1-11_2)
- A king's confession of guilt: 2 Sam 12:13 and 24:10, 17 (David: 'I have sinned'), Ps 51:5-6.
- Chosen from the womb: Jer 1:5, Isa 49:1, Ps 22:10-11.
- God punishes those who violate the temple: 2 Chr 26:16-21 (Uzziah), 2 Macc 3.

**A blow is repaid; the hidden god who knows characters; the upright's loaf preferred to the evildoer's ox (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:11_3-11_10)
- The upright's loaf better than the wicked man's ox: Prov 15:8, 21:3 and 21:27; 1 Sam 15:22; Hos 6:6; Amos 5:22-24; Ps 51:18-19; Q 22:37 (neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God, but your piety reaches him); Q 5:27 (God accepts only from the God-fearing: Cain and Abel).
- Measure for measure: Obad 15, Judg 1:7, Gal 6:7; Q 42:40 (the recompense of evil is evil like it).
- The hidden God: Isa 45:15 ('truly you are a God who hides himself'), Job 23:8-9, Ps 139:1-4 (you know my sitting down and rising up).
- None can stay his hand: Dan 4:32, Job 9:12, Isa 43:13.
