**Hymn to the creator - men the cattle of god, heaven and earth made for their sake, his images from his body; god knows every name (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:11_10/2-12_8)
- Heaven and earth made for humankind and everything given them: Ps 8:4-9 ('what is man ... you have put all things under his feet'), Gen 1:26-30, Ps 115:16; Q 2:29 (he created for you all that is on earth), Q 45:12-13, Q 14:32-34, Q 16:5-14 (cattle, sea creatures for food).
- The creator provides food for all his creatures: Ps 104:14-15, 27-28 and 145:15-16; Gen 1:29-30 and 9:3; Q 80:24-32.
- Humans as god's images from his body: Gen 1:26-27 and 5:1-3; and as god's flock: Ps 95:7, 100:3, Ezek 34:31.
- Breath of life in the nostrils: Gen 2:7, Job 27:3, Isa 2:22; Q 15:29 and 32:9 (he breathed into him of his spirit).
- The waters subdued before creation: Ps 104:6-9, Ps 74:13-14, Job 38:8-11, Gen 1:2, 9-10.
- When they weep he hears: Exod 2:23-25, 3:7, Ps 34:18, Ps 145:19; and god disciplines as a father, Deut 8:5, Prov 3:12.
- God knows every name: Ps 147:4 and Isa 40:26 (he calls the stars by name), Isa 43:1, Exod 33:12 and 17 ('I know you by name'), John 10:3; Q 2:31 (he taught Adam all the names).
- He destroyed his children for rebellion: compare the Heavenly Cow (HeavenlyCow W1:1-15/2) and Gen 6-7, Q 11:25-49.

**Closing counsel - do not kill your intimate, the king's followers are gods, spread love of yourself; colophon of Khaemwaset (Instruction for Merikare)** (Merikare W1:12_8/2-13_3/2)
- The father's closing charge: Prov 4:1-9, 1 Kgs 2:1-4 (David to Solomon), Deut 32:46-47.
- Love of the people as the king's best defence: Prov 14:28, 20:28 and 29:14.

**Instruction for Merikare, pCarlsberg VI (from the Asiatic passage to the closing)** (Merikare W2)
- Same parallels as W1 (Ps 8, Ps 104, Gen 1:26-30, Ps 147:4); the variant 'it did not happen through what I did' changes the king's confession into a disclaimer, compare 2 Sam 12:13 versus 1 Sam 15:20-21.

**Instruction for Merikare, pMoscow 4658 (fragments of the whole text)** (Merikare W3)
- Same parallels as W1; for 'rulers made in the egg' compare Jer 1:5 (before I formed you in the womb) and Ps 139:13-16.

**Snefru summons Neferti, who chooses to speak of the future (Neferti 1-18)** (Neferti 1-18)
- Compare Isa 19:1-15 (oracle on Egypt) and the prophet called before a king (1 Kgs 22:5-28; Dan 2:2-11).
- The king who writes the prophecy: compare Jer 36:2-4 (Baruch writes Jeremiah's words) and Hab 2:2.
- Past or future: compare Isa 41:22-23; 46:9-10 ('declaring the end from the beginning').

**Neferti laments the coming ruin of land and cosmos (Neferti 20-38/2)** (Neferti 20-38/2)
- Compare Isa 19:5-8 (the Nile dried, fishermen mourn) and Isa 19:2 (Egyptian against Egyptian); Ezek 30:12 ('I will make the Nile dry').
- Darkened sun: compare Isa 13:10, Joel 2:10; 3:4 (2:31), Amos 8:9 and Q 81:1-2.
- No one weeps for the land: compare Jer 12:11 ('desolate, and no one lays it to heart') and Isa 57:1.
- Creation undone and begun anew: compare Jer 4:23-26 (tohu wa-bohu returns) and Isa 65:17.

**The land in sickness - civil war, social reversal, the sun withdrawn (Neferti 38/3-57/2)** (Neferti 38/3-57/2)
- Son against father, brother against brother: compare Mic 7:6, Isa 19:2, Isa 3:5 and Matt 10:21, 35-36.
- Social reversal: compare Lam 5:2-8 ('our inheritance turned over to strangers', 'slaves rule over us'), Isa 3:4-5 and Prov 30:21-22; Deut 28:43.
- Unmourned dead: compare Jer 16:4-7 and Jer 22:18.
- Weapons and blood for bread: compare Lam 5:9.

**The coming king Ameni restores maat (Neferti 57/3-71)** (Neferti 57/3-71)
- Compare the messianic oracles Isa 9:1-6 (5-6) and Isa 11:1-9 (righteousness, the wicked slain by his breath) and Isa 32:1.
- A deliverer for Egypt after its civil strife: Isa 19:20 ('he will send them a saviour').
- A future king named in advance: 1 Kgs 13:2 (Josiah) and Isa 44:28-45:1 (Cyrus).
- Fulfilment as the test of a prophet: Deut 18:21-22; Jer 28:9.
- Justice returning: compare Ps 72:1-7, 12-14 and Jer 23:5-6.

**Praise of Hapi who comes forth to make Egypt live (Nile Hymn, pSallier II, 11,6-12,9)** (NileHymn W1:11_6-12_9)
- Rain as a 'Nile in the sky' for foreign lands: compare Deut 11:10-11 (Egypt watered by foot, Canaan drinks rain from heaven) and Ps 104:10-13.
- Compare Ps 65:10-14 and Ps 104:14-15 (God makes grass and grain grow) and Q 16:10-11; Q 80:24-32.
- Hidden god whose way is unknown: compare Isa 45:15, Job 11:7-9 and Ps 77:20 ('your path in the great waters, your footsteps unknown').

**Hapi's absence, his gifts and his festival (Nile Hymn, pSallier II, 13,1-14,11)** (NileHymn W1:13_1-14_11/2)
- Gold and lapis cannot be eaten: compare Job 28:15-19 and Prov 16:16; Ezek 7:19 ('their silver and gold cannot satisfy their hunger').
- Fear the flood god's majesty, 'O mankind': compare Ps 33:8.

**The Great Nile Hymn on ostracon Golenischeff 4470 (opening, with date notes)** (NileHymn W3)
- Dew from heaven: compare Gen 27:28, Deut 33:13 and Hos 14:6. The ostracon interleaves day dates (3_4, 3_6, 3_8, 3_10/2: months of Shemu), perhaps a schoolboy's daily stints.

**PT 213 (Unas): 'You did not go away dead, you went away alive'** (PT213 W1)
- Compare Q 2:154 and 3:169 ('do not say of those slain in God's way: dead; rather they are alive') and Wis 3:2-4.
- Ruler over living and dead: Rom 14:9.

**PT 217 (Unas): 'Atum, your son comes to you' - the king announced to the four quarters** (PT217 W1)
- Whom he will he kills, whom he will he keeps alive: compare Deut 32:39, 1 Sam 2:6 and Q 2:258 (Abraham and the king: 'I give life and cause death').
- Received into the father's embrace: compare Ps 2:7 and Ps 73:24.

**PT 219: the Osiris litany to the Ennead - 'If he lives, this Unas lives'** (PT219 240-254/4)
- Because he lives, you will live: compare John 14:19; Rom 6:5-8.

**PT 219: Osiris in his names and cult places; his body is the king's body** (PT219 254/5-268/7)
- Compare Gen 2:23 ('bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh') and the union formulas of John 6:56.
- Named constellations (Orion): Job 9:9; Amos 5:8.

**Cannibal Hymn (Unas) I: the sky quakes; the king, mightier than Atum, has the gods hunted** (PT273-274 W1:496-511/2)
- Theophany shaking heaven and earth: compare Judg 5:4-5, Ps 18:8-16 and Ps 68:9.
- A name no one knows: compare Rev 19:12 and Judg 13:18; Gen 32:30.
- Gods eaten: contrast Ps 50:12-13 ('do I eat the flesh of bulls?') and the mocking of gods who eat, Bel and the Dragon; Deut 32:38.

**Cannibal Hymn (Unas) II: the gods as meals; the king swallows their wisdom and gains eternity** (PT273-274 W1:512-524/2)
- Eating to gain knowledge: compare Gen 3:5-6, 22 (the fruit that makes 'like gods, knowing').
- He does whatever he pleases: compare Ps 115:3, Ps 135:6, Dan 4:32 (35) and Q 85:16 ('doer of what he wills', fa''al li-ma yurid), Q 11:107.
- Older than the eldest: compare Dan 7:9 ('Ancient of days') and John 8:58.

**PT 302 (Unas): ascent to Re with Sothis and Upuaut, no accusation against him** (PT302 W1)
- Ascent on wings: compare Isa 40:31, Ps 55:7 ('O for wings like a dove') and Exod 19:4.
- No charge against him: compare Rom 8:33-34 and Q 4:110 (forgiveness); Job's protest of innocence, Job 31.
- Throne not given to another: compare 2 Sam 7:16 and Isa 42:8 ('my glory I will not give to another').

**PT 306 (Unas): the gods rejoice to see him ascend; he climbs 'in its name of Ladder'** (PT306 W1)
- Compare Gen 28:12 (Jacob's ladder, sullam), Q 6:35 and 52:38 (a ladder, sullam, to heaven) and Q 70:3-4 (the ascents, maʿarij).
- Heaven and earth given: compare Ps 2:8, Dan 7:14 and Matt 28:18.

**PT 527 (Pepi I): Atum masturbates and Shu and Tefnut are born** (PT527 W1)
- Contrast the creation of the first pair in Gen 1:27 (male and female by word) and Gen 2:21-23 (woman from the man alone, without a mother); Q 4:1 and 39:6 (spouse created from one soul).
- Creation without a consort or sexual act: compare Gen 1 generally, and Q 6:101 ('how could he have a child when he has no consort?'), Q 112:3.

**PT 600 (Pepi II): Atum-Khepri rose as the hill and the Benben, spat out Shu and Tefnut; protect this pyramid** (PT600 N/F/E.inf.17.=, PT600 N/F/E.inf.18.=, PT600 N/F/E.inf.19.=, PT600 N/F/E.inf.20.=, PT600 N/F/E.inf.21.=, PT600 N/F/E.inf.22.=, PT600 N/F/E.inf.23.=)
- Creation beginning from a first mound or dry land: compare Gen 1:9-10 and Ps 104:5-9.
- First beings produced from the creator's mouth: compare Gen 2:7 (breath), Ps 33:6 ('by the breath of his mouth all their host') and Q 15:29.
- Heliopolis (On) and its sun-sanctuary: Gen 41:45, Jer 43:13.

**Ptahhotep prologue: the vizier's old age, the 'staff of old age', none is born wise** (Ptahhotep W1:4_1-5_6/2)
- Old age catalogue: compare Eccl 12:1-7 (the keepers of the house tremble, the grinders cease, the windows darken) and 2 Sam 19:35 (Barzillai: can I taste what I eat?); Q 16:70 and 22:5 (returned to the most abject age, knowing nothing after knowing).
- Compare Prov 1:1-6 and Prov 4:1-4 (a father hands on teaching), and Q 31:12-13 (Luqman instructs his son).

**Ptahhotep maxims 1-4: do not be proud of knowledge; good speech found with maidservants; three kinds of disputant** (Ptahhotep W1:5_8-6_3/2)
- Compare Prov 3:7, 26:12 and Prov 3:13-15; 8:11 (wisdom more precious than jewels); Prov 26:4-5 (answering a fool); Prov 15:1.

**Ptahhotep maxims 5-6: great is maat; human schemes fail, what the god commands happens** (Ptahhotep W1:6_3/3-6_10/2)
- Compare Prov 19:21 ('many plans in a man's heart, but the counsel of YHWH stands'), Prov 16:9, Ps 33:10-11 and Q 8:30; Q 3:54.
- Maat lasting: compare Prov 12:19; 10:25; Ps 119:160.
- Ill-gotten wealth: Prov 10:2; 13:11; Jer 17:11.

**Ptahhotep maxims 7-8: at a great man's table; the faithful messenger** (Ptahhotep W1:6_11-7_5)
- Compare Prov 23:1-3 ('when you sit to dine with a ruler, consider well what is before you') and Sir 31:12-18.
- Faithful messenger: Prov 25:13; 13:17; 'abomination of YHWH' formula, Prov 6:16; 11:1.
- Do not turn aside right or left: Deut 5:32; Josh 1:7; Prov 4:27.

**Ptahhotep maxims 9-10: the god-given harvest, the childless, serving the man who rose from poverty** (Ptahhotep W1:7_5/2-7_9)
- Compare Prov 10:22 ('the blessing of YHWH makes rich'), Deut 8:17-18, and Ps 127:2 (he gives to his beloved in sleep).
- The childless honoured: Isa 54:1; 56:3-5; 1 Sam 2:5; contrast Hannah mocked, 1 Sam 1:6.

**Ptahhotep maxim 11: follow your heart as long as you live** (Ptahhotep W1:7_9/2-7_10/2)
- Compare Eccl 11:9 ('walk in the ways of your heart'), Eccl 9:7-10 and Eccl 2:24; contrast Num 15:39 ('do not follow your own heart').

**Ptahhotep maxim 12: the son who follows your ways, and the son the gods rejected in the womb** (Ptahhotep W1:7_10/3-8_1/3)
- The rebellious son: Deut 21:18-21; Prov 17:25; 19:26. Destined from the womb: Ps 58:4 (3) ('the wicked go astray from the womb'), Jer 1:5, Rom 9:11-13.
- Whom God guides none can lead astray: Q 39:36-37; Q 18:17; Ps 37:23-24.

**Ptahhotep maxims 13-15: in the antechamber, the trusted man, the one who listens to his belly, reporting** (Ptahhotep W1:8_2-8_13/3)
- Compare Prov 25:6-7 and Luke 14:8-11 (take the lower seat until called up); Ps 75:7-8 (God exalts).
- Belly as master: Phil 3:19; Rom 16:18; Prov 23:2.

**Ptahhotep maxims 16-17: the leader's lasting work; hear the petitioner out** (Ptahhotep W1:8_14-9_6)
- Compare Prov 18:13 (answering before hearing) and Job 29:12-16; 31:13 (Job hears his servants' cause); Exod 22:21-23.

**Ptahhotep maxim 18: do not approach the women where you are a guest** (Ptahhotep W1:9_7-9_13)
- Compare Prov 6:24-35; 7:22-27 ('as an ox to the slaughter... her house is the way to Sheol'); Prov 5:3-5.
- Joseph and his master's wife: Gen 39:7-12 and Q 12:23-25.

**Ptahhotep maxims 19-20: beware of greed, the incurable sickness** (Ptahhotep W1:9_13/2-10_7/2)
- Compare Prov 1:19; 15:27 ('he who is greedy for gain troubles his house'); 1 Tim 6:10 (love of money a root of all evils); Q 59:9 and 64:16 (saved from the greed of his soul).
- The meek: Ps 37:11; Matt 5:5.

**Ptahhotep maxim 21: found a household and love your wife - she is a fertile field** (Ptahhotep W1:10_8-10_12/3)
- Compare Q 2:223 ('your women are a tilth for you'), Exod 21:10 (food, clothing and conjugal rights), Eccl 9:9 and Prov 5:18-19.

**Ptahhotep maxims 22-23: satisfy your dependents; do not repeat slander** (Ptahhotep W1:11_1-11_8/2)
- Compare Prov 27:1 ('you do not know what a day may bring'), Q 31:34 ('no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow') and Jas 4:13-14.
- Rumour: Prov 18:8; 26:20-22; Lev 19:16; Q 49:6 and 49:12.
- A friend in adversity: Prov 17:17; 18:24; 27:10.

**Ptahhotep maxims 24-27: silence in council; master the hot temper; teach the great** (Ptahhotep W1:11_8/3-12_13/2)
- Compare Prov 17:27-28 ('even a fool who keeps silent is thought wise'), Prov 10:19, Jas 1:19; Prov 16:18 and 29:23; Prov 15:18; 22:24-25.
- Laughter and grief: Eccl 3:4; 7:2-4.

**Ptahhotep maxims 28-31: the impartial judge; the man risen from poverty; bow to your superior** (Ptahhotep W1:13_1-13_12)
- Compare Lev 19:15, Deut 1:17; 16:19, Prov 24:23 ('to show partiality in judgment is not good'); Q 4:135; 5:8.
- Remember your humble past: Deut 8:11-18; 1 Sam 15:17.

**Ptahhotep maxims 32-33: do not rob your neighbour; do not force one who resists** (Ptahhotep W1:13_12/2-14_6)
- Compare Exod 20:15-17 and Deut 5:19-21; Prov 3:29 ('do not plan harm against your neighbour who dwells trustingly beside you').
- Compare the rape laws Deut 22:25-27 and 2 Sam 13:12-14 (Tamar's refusal).

**Ptahhotep maxims 34-37: test a friend alone; be generous; punish rightly; keep a cheerful wife** (Ptahhotep W1:14_6/2-15_7/3)
- Compare Matt 18:15 and Prov 25:9 (argue your case with your neighbour himself); Prov 11:24-25; 3:27-28; Eccl 11:1-2.
- Divorce: Mal 2:14-16.

**Ptahhotep epilogue I: the worth of hearing; the son who hears and the fool who does not** (Ptahhotep W1:15_8-17_9)
- Compare Prov 1:8-9; 4:1-10 and Exod 20:12 (honour father, long life); Prov 4:23 (from the heart are the issues of life); 1 Kgs 3:9 (a 'hearing heart', lev shomea').
- Hearing preferred to sacrifice: 1 Sam 15:22; Deut 6:4. God hardens or opens hearts: Exod 7:3; Q 2:7; Q 7:179 ('they have ears but do not hear').
- Fools as dead while alive: 1 Tim 5:6; Q 6:122; Q 35:22.

**Ptahhotep epilogue II: the obedient son, a follower of Horus; 110 years of life; colophon** (Ptahhotep W1:17_10-19.9)
- 110 years: Joseph (Gen 50:22, 26) and Joshua (Josh 24:29), the ideal Egyptian lifespan.
- Teach your children: Deut 6:6-7; 11:19; Ps 78:3-6.
- Guard your mouth: Prov 13:3; 21:23; Ps 141:3.

**Ptahhotep in the London papyrus L1 (Middle Kingdom), maxims 19-27** (Ptahhotep W2:0-m_3)
- Compare Prov 15:27; Q 2:223; Prov 18:8; Prov 17:28 as for the pPrisse units.

**Ptahhotep in L2: maat, plans, table manners, the disowned son, the petitioner** (Ptahhotep W3:2_6-4_14)
- The disowned son: Deut 21:18-21; Gen 21:10-12 (Ishmael sent away); Q 11:45-46 (Noah's son: 'he is not of your family').

**Ptahhotep in L2: greed, women, wife, rumour, judge ('partiality is the god's abomination'), friends** (Ptahhotep W3:4_14/2-Fragm._3_4)
- 'Abomination of YHWH': Prov 11:1; 17:15; 20:10, 23; partiality: Prov 24:23; 28:21; Deut 16:19; Exod 23:8.
- The strange woman: Prov 7; Prov 6:26.

**Shipwrecked Sailor: the expedition returns; the follower urges the anxious prince to speak well (1-21)** (ShipwreckedSailor 1-21)
- Compare Prov 12:14; 18:20-21 ('death and life are in the power of the tongue'); Prov 22:29 (the skilled man stands before kings).

**Shipwrecked Sailor: the storm, the sinking, three days alone, the island of plenty, the burnt offering** (ShipwreckedSailor 23-55)
- Compare Jonah 1:4-16 (storm, the ship about to break up, the sailors' sacrifice) and Jonah 2:1, 11 (three days, cast out on dry land); Ps 107:23-30.
- Sole survivor: Job 1:15-19 ('I alone escaped to tell you').
- Island of plenty: Gen 2:9 and the Garden; Q 18:32-33 (the two gardens that lacked nothing).
- Sacrifice on reaching land: Gen 8:20; Jonah 1:16.
- Ship's dimensions in cubits: Gen 6:15 (300 by 50 by 30).

**Shipwrecked Sailor: the golden serpent appears - 'Who brought you here?' - 'Do not fear'** (ShipwreckedSailor 56-123)
- God's question to the one who arrives: compare 1 Kgs 19:9, 13 ('What are you doing here, Elijah?') and Gen 16:8.
- Fear not: Gen 15:1; Judg 6:23; Dan 10:12, 19; Q 20:21 and 28:31 (Moses and the serpent: 'take it and do not fear').
- Swallowed or carried in a creature's mouth and set down unharmed: compare Jonah 2:1, 11 and Q 37:142-145 (the fish swallowed him; cast onto the shore).
- God brought him to a place of life: compare Q 18:60-82 (Moses' journey to the meeting of the two seas, a divine servant, a fish) and Gen 50:20.

**Shipwrecked Sailor: the serpent's own tale - a falling star burned his family of 75** (ShipwreckedSailor 124-136)
- Fire from heaven destroying a family: Job 1:16, 18-19 (fire of God, the house falls on the children); Gen 19:24. Star fallen from heaven: Isa 14:12; Rev 8:10; 9:1.
- Be strong and courageous: Josh 1:6-9; Ps 27:14. The divine being consoling with its own loss: compare Q 12:86 (Jacob: 'I complain of my grief to God').

**Shipwrecked Sailor: the promised offerings; the serpent laughs - 'I am the ruler of Punt'; the ship comes** (ShipwreckedSailor 138-159/2)
- God needs no gifts, all is his: Ps 50:9-13 ('every beast of the forest is mine'), 1 Chr 29:14; Q 22:37 ('neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God') and Q 51:57.
- Vows of the rescued: Jonah 1:16; 2:10 (9); Ps 66:13-15; 107:22.
- Recount God's deeds among the people: Ps 9:12 (11); 96:3; Mark 5:19.
- A vanishing island: compare Q 18:79-82 only as a mysterious encounter whose place is not found again; Rev 16:20 ('every island fled').

**Shipwrecked Sailor: the cargo of Punt, the return to the Residence, the promotion, the prince's cynical reply** (ShipwreckedSailor 161-186)
- Gifts of a southern land: 1 Kgs 10:10, 22 (gold, ivory, apes and peacocks from Ophir; the queen of Sheba's spices) and Ps 72:10.
- Rescued man rewarded and promoted before the court: Gen 41:39-43; Esth 6:6-11; Dan 2:48.
- Renewed youth: Ps 103:5; Job 33:25; Isa 40:31.
- The ending refusal of consolation, like Jonah's unresolved last scene (Jonah 4:9-11).

**Sinuhe (B): Amherst fragments of the opening: the king's death and the falcon's flight** (Sinuhe W1:Am.1-Aq)
- Most of the opening is lost in B; the full text is in W2 (R) and W5 (AOS).

**Sinuhe (B): the flight from Egypt across the border to the desert, rescue from thirst** (Sinuhe W1:1-27)
- Flight of a courtier after a crisis at court: compare Moses' flight from Pharaoh (Exod 2:15) and Jacob's flight from Esau (Gen 27:41-45; 28:10), and especially Hadad the Edomite and Jeroboam fleeing to Egypt (1 Kgs 11:17-22, 40).
- Rescue from thirst in the desert: compare Hagar and Ishmael (Gen 21:15-19) and Israel at Marah and Massah (Exod 15:22-25; 17:1-7); Q 28:22-24 Moses arrives exhausted at the water of Midian.

**Sinuhe (B): passed from land to land to Qedem; Ammunenshi of Retenu receives him; the eulogy of Senwosret I** (Sinuhe W1:28-77)
- Compare the foreign hosts of Israel's fugitives: Laban receiving Jacob (Gen 29:13-14), Jethro/Reuel receiving Moses (Exod 2:20), Achish receiving David (1 Sam 21:10-15; 27:1-7), Pharaoh receiving Hadad (1 Kgs 11:18-19).
- 'You will hear the speech of Egypt': compare Joseph's use of an interpreter (Gen 42:23).
- The eulogy of the king to a foreign ruler: compare the royal psalms (Ps 2; 72; 110) and the conqueror-from-the-womb idea in Ps 110:3 and Jer 1:5.

**Sinuhe (B): married to the ruler's eldest daughter; the land of Yaa; prosperity, hospitality and command in Retenu** (Sinuhe W1:78-107)
- Marriage to the host's daughter: compare Moses and Zipporah, daughter of the priest of Midian (Exod 2:21; Q 28:27) and Jacob and the daughters of Laban (Gen 29:15-30); Hadad married to Pharaoh's sister-in-law (1 Kgs 11:19).
- The land of Yaa: compare the promised land of wheat, barley, vines, figs, pomegranates, olive oil and honey (Deut 8:7-9) and 'flowing with milk and honey' (Exod 3:8); the spies' report (Num 13:23-27).
- Prosperity in exile and children multiplied: compare Jacob in Laban's service (Gen 30:43) and Moses in Midian (Exod 2:22; 18:3-4).
- Giving water to the thirsty and guiding the lost: compare Job 31:16-21, 31-32 and Isa 58:7.

**Sinuhe (B): the strongman of Retenu challenges Sinuhe; the duel and the victory** (Sinuhe W1:109-146)
- The duel is the closest ANE parallel to David and Goliath (1 Sam 17): an unequalled champion (1 Sam 17:4, 8-10), the people's fear (17:11, 24), the hero who has no armour, the missile that strikes the head/neck (17:49), the champion falls on his face (17:49) and is finished with his own weapon (17:51), followed by the plunder of his tent (17:54).
- 'What he planned to do to me I did to him': compare Haman hanged on his own gallows (Esth 7:10) and Ps 7:15-16.

**Sinuhe (B): the god who ordained the flight is appeased; sayings of the fugitive; prayer to return and to be buried at home; old age** (Sinuhe W1:147-172/2)
- God's hidden guidance of an exile: compare Joseph's 'it was not you who sent me here but God' (Gen 45:5-8; 50:20) and Q 12:100.
- Longing for burial in the homeland: compare Jacob (Gen 47:29-30; 49:29-32), Joseph's bones (Gen 50:24-25; Exod 13:19), Barzillai (2 Sam 19:37) and Nehemiah's 'the city of my fathers' graves' (Neh 2:3-5).
- Old age limb by limb: compare Eccl 12:1-7 and Barzillai's complaint (2 Sam 19:35); Q 19:4 Zechariah's 'my bones have weakened and my head is aflame with grey'.

**Sinuhe (B): Senwosret's decree recalling Sinuhe and promising burial in Egypt; Sinuhe's joy** (Sinuhe W1:173-203)
- Royal recall of an exile: compare David recalling Absalom (2 Sam 14:21-24, 33) and Pharaoh's letting Hadad go home (1 Kgs 11:21-22); Jacob told by God to return to the land of his birth (Gen 31:3, 13).
- Burial abroad versus burial at home and Egyptian embalming: compare Joseph's embalming and coffin in Egypt (Gen 50:2-3, 26) and Jacob's wish not to be buried in Egypt (Gen 47:29-30).
- Prostration and earth on the body at a royal message: compare the bowing to the ground of Gen 33:3 and 2 Sam 14:4, 22, 33.

**Sinuhe (B): Sinuhe's reply to the decree** (Sinuhe W1:204-237)
- 'The god who ordained the flight drew me': compare Jonah fleeing yet driven by God (Jonah 1:3-4) and Ps 139:7-10.
- 'One lives on the breath you give': compare the Amarna vassals' 'the breath of my life' and Lam 4:20, 'the breath of our nostrils, the LORD's anointed'.

**Sinuhe (B): the return to Egypt; reception at the palace; Sinuhe swoons before the king** (Sinuhe W1:238-263/3)
- The exile's return and reception: compare Jacob's return and fear before Esau (Gen 32:3-21; 33:1-4), Moses' return to Egypt (Exod 4:18-20) and Absalom's return (2 Sam 14:33).
- 'Here I am; do as you wish': compare David before Absalom's rebellion (2 Sam 15:26) and Jer 26:14.

**Sinuhe (B): the queen and royal children fail to recognise 'the Asiatic'; the princesses' hymn for his pardon; the king receives him as courtier** (Sinuhe W1:263/4-282)
- Non-recognition of the man returned from abroad in foreign guise: compare Joseph unrecognised by his brothers (Gen 42:7-8) and Jacob's 'are you really my son Esau?' (Gen 27:21-24); here the queen and children say 'it is not he' and the king insists 'it is he'.
- Royal women interceding before the king: compare Esther (Esth 4:11-16; 5:1-3; 8:3-6) and the wise woman of Tekoa (2 Sam 14:1-20).

**Sinuhe (B): Sinuhe made new: bathed, dressed in linen, given a house, and a pyramid tomb among the royal children; colophon** (Sinuhe W1:283-311)
- Change of clothes and new status at the foreign court: compare Joseph shaved, changed and later clothed in fine linen by Pharaoh (Gen 41:14, 42), Jehoiachin's prison clothes changed (2 Kgs 25:29) and Q 12:54-56.
- A tomb prepared by royal favour: compare Joseph's burial (Gen 50:26) and the burial privileges of Jehoiada among the kings (2 Chr 24:16).

**Sinuhe (R): Sinuhe's titles; year 30: King Amenemhat ascends to his horizon; the crown prince hears and flies home** (Sinuhe W2:1-22)
- A succession crisis at the king's death with a prince hurrying back while a rival party is informed: compare 1 Kgs 1 (Adonijah and Solomon) and 2 Kgs 11:1-3.
- The court in silence and the gates sealed at the king's death: compare 2 Sam 19:1-4 and the mourning for Jacob in Egypt (Gen 50:3).

**Sinuhe (R): the flight, rescue by the sheikh, Ammunenshi and the excuse** (Sinuhe W2:24-65)
- Compare Moses' flight to Midian (Exod 2:15) and Q 28:21-22 ('he left it fearful, watchful; he said: my Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people').

**Sinuhe (R): fragments of the challenge and duel** (Sinuhe W2:133-171/2)
- Compare 1 Sam 17:48-51 (David runs to meet Goliath, the stone, the fall on his face, Goliath's own sword).

**Sinuhe (AOS): the strongman's challenge and the duel** (Sinuhe W5:43/3-56/2)
- Compare 1 Sam 17 (David and Goliath) and 1 Sam 18:1-4 (Jonathan's love after the victory).

**Sinuhe (AOS verso): Sinuhe's reply** (Sinuhe W5:Verso_21-Verso_37/2)
- Self-abasement as the king's dog: compare 2 Sam 9:8 ('what is your servant, that you look on a dead dog like me?') and the Amarna and Lachish letters ('who is your servant, a dog?').

**Two Brothers: Anubis and Bata; the younger brother as son and servant of the household; the talking cattle; ploughing** (TwoBrothers 1_1-2_6)
- Two sons of one father and mother, one a herdsman: compare Cain and Abel (Gen 4:1-2) and Jacob and Esau (Gen 25:24-27).
- 'The strength of a god was in him' and the herds thriving under him: compare Gen 39:2-6 (YHWH with Joseph, the blessing on Potiphar's house and field) and Gen 41:38 ('a man in whom is the spirit of God'); Jacob's herding for Laban (Gen 30:29-30, 43; 31:38-40).
- Joseph as handsome (Gen 39:6, yefeh-toʾar) and the beauty of Joseph in Q 12:31.
- Talking animals: Balaam's ass (Num 22:28-30) and Solomon understanding the ant (Q 27:18-19).

**Two Brothers: sent home for seed, Bata is propositioned by his elder brother's wife and refuses** (TwoBrothers 2_7-4_2/4)
- The seduction of Joseph by his master's wife (Gen 39:7-12): 'lie with me' (39:7, 12; Bata's sḏr =n), seized (39:12, wa-titpeśehu; 3_7 mḥ jm =f), the refusal citing the master's trust (39:8-9) and 'this great wickedness' (39:9; btꜣ,w ꜥꜣ), the day-to-day contact of the household (39:10-11).
- Q 12:23: she sought to seduce him, closed the doors and said 'come' (hayta laka; compare mꜥ~j 'come!'); he said 'God forbid: he is my lord who made my lodging good'. Q 12:24: she desired him and he would have desired her but for the proof of his Lord.
- Unlike Gen 39:12 and Q 12:25, no garment is torn or left behind; instead the woman promises to make him garments (3_7/5). Compare also Prov 7:10-23 (the seductress).

**Two Brothers: the wife fakes a beating and accuses Bata to her husband** (TwoBrothers 4_3-5_3/4)
- Potiphar's wife's accusation (Gen 39:13-18): she reverses roles, calls the household and her husband and claims 'he came to lie with me' (39:14, 17); here too the woman quotes her own proposition as his.
- Q 12:25: at the door she says to her husband 'what is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but prison or a painful punishment?'; Q 12:26-28 the witness and the torn shirt test, which the Egyptian tale lacks (the husband believes her).
- Feigned sickness as a ruse: compare Amnon (2 Sam 13:5-6) and Rachel on the camel saddle (Gen 31:35).

**Two Brothers: Anubis' rage and ambush; the cows warn Bata, who flees** (TwoBrothers 5_4-6_3/3)
- The master's anger at the accusation (Gen 39:19, 'his anger burned') leads here to an attempted killing instead of prison (Gen 39:20; Q 12:35).
- Flight from a brother's murderous anger: Jacob from Esau (Gen 27:41-45); David from Saul's spear (1 Sam 19:9-10).
- An animal sees the danger first and warns its master: Balaam's ass (Num 22:22-33).

**Two Brothers: Bata prays to Re-Harakhti, who puts a crocodile-filled water between the brothers; the dialogue at dawn** (TwoBrothers 6_4-7_6/3)
- Prayer to the judge who separates the guilty from the innocent: Gen 18:25, Ps 7:9-12, 1 Kgs 8:31-32; Joseph's 'my Lord knows' (Q 12:50) and Q 12:33-34 (Joseph prays and his Lord answers him).
- A divinely placed barrier between pursuer and pursued: the pillar of cloud between Egypt and Israel (Exod 14:19-20), the waters of the sea (Exod 14:21-29); Laban stopped by God's warning in a dream (Gen 31:24, 29).
- Case brought before the rising sun: compare Zeph 3:5 ('morning by morning he brings his justice to light') and Ps 37:6.

**Two Brothers: Bata's oath and self-castration; his heart to be placed on the cedar; Anubis kills his wife** (TwoBrothers 7_7-8_8/2)
- Oath of innocence and self-mutilation: compare the eunuchs who 'made themselves eunuchs' (Matt 19:12) and the eunuch's exclusion and promise (Deut 23:1; Isa 56:3-5); the phallus swallowed by a fish recalls Plutarch's Osiris (De Iside 18).
- The husband convinced of the wife's guilt: Potiphar (Q 12:28-29, 'it is of your women's guile; Joseph, turn from this; and you, seek forgiveness'); in Gen 39 the master never recognises it.
- Life held in a separate object and a sign that reveals the hero's death: compare Samson's strength in his hair (Judg 16:17) and Jacob's recognition by a garment (Gen 37:33).
- Earth on the head as mourning: Josh 7:6, 1 Sam 4:12, 2 Sam 1:2, 13:19 (Tamar's hand on her head). A wicked wife thrown to the dogs: Jezebel (1 Kgs 21:23; 2 Kgs 9:33-37).

**Two Brothers: Bata alone in the Valley of the Cedar; the Ennead has Khnum fashion him a wife; the Seven Hathors** (TwoBrothers 8_8/3-10_3/2)
- 'That he not dwell alone': Gen 2:18 ('it is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper') and Gen 2:22 (God builds the woman); the potter god Khnum compares with Gen 2:7 and Isa 64:8.
- Fates decreed at birth by goddesses: compare the Hathors with the decreeing of a destiny (Ps 139:16) and Q 57:22.
- The hero opening his whole heart to a woman who will betray him: Samson and Delilah, 'he told her all his heart' (Judg 16:17-18, wayyagged-lāh ʾet-kol-libbo).
- Yam, the Sea, as a hostile power: Ps 74:13; 89:9-10; Job 7:12; 38:8-11.

**Two Brothers: the Sea steals a lock of hair; Pharaoh's search for its owner; she is brought to Egypt, betrays Bata, the cedar is felled and he dies** (TwoBrothers 10_4-12_7)
- A beautiful woman taken into Pharaoh's house after his officials praise her: Sarah (Gen 12:14-15) and the 'wife-sister' stories (Gen 20; 26); a king who sends for a woman he has heard of: David and Bathsheba (2 Sam 11:2-4), Ahasuerus' search for maidens (Esth 2:2-4, 8).
- Court scholars consulted on a mystery: Pharaoh's magicians and wise men (Gen 41:8; Exod 7:11) and the 'scribes and wise men' of Dan 2:2.
- The wife who reveals her husband's secret to his enemies: Delilah (Judg 16:4-21); 'I alone escaped to tell you' (Job 1:15-19); successive companies sent to take a man who destroys them: 2 Kgs 1:9-14.

**Two Brothers: the beer foams; Anubis searches years for the heart, finds it as a grape and revives Bata; the plan of the bull** (TwoBrothers 12_7/2-14_9)
- Reunion embrace of brothers: Jacob and Esau (Gen 33:4) and Joseph with Benjamin and his brothers (Gen 45:14-15).
- Revival of the dead: Elijah and Elisha (1 Kgs 17:17-22; 2 Kgs 4:32-35) and Ezek 37:1-10; the dead raised by God's leave (Q 2:259-260; 3:49).
- A bull as divine manifestation: compare the golden calf (Exod 32:4) and Jeroboam's calves (1 Kgs 12:28-30); the Egyptian Apis bull lies behind Bata's form.

**Two Brothers: the bull at Pharaoh's court; Bata reveals himself to his wife; she makes Pharaoh swear and asks for the bull's liver** (TwoBrothers 15_1-16_5/2)
- A king trapped by an oath sworn at a feast to grant a woman's request: Herod and the daughter of Herodias (Mark 6:21-28), Ahasuerus to Esther 'up to half the kingdom' (Esth 5:3, 6; 7:2).
- 'I am Bata' as a recognition formula: compare 'I am Joseph' (Gen 45:3-4; Q 12:90).

**Two Brothers: the bull slaughtered; two drops of blood at the palace doorposts become persea trees; the trees felled; the splinter swallowed** (TwoBrothers 16_6-18_5/2)
- Blood at the two doorposts of a house: the Passover blood on the two doorposts and lintel (Exod 12:7, 22-23); here it is the blood of a slaughtered sacred bull.
- Trees as the abode of a living person: compare the sacred tree of Gen 21:33 and the burning bush (Exod 3:2-4).
- Miraculous conception: compare the annunciations of Gen 18:10-14; Judg 13:3; Q 19:16-22 (Mary under the palm tree).

**Two Brothers: Bata reborn as the queen's son, crown prince and king; he judges his wife and makes Anubis his heir; colophon** (TwoBrothers 18_6-20_1)
- The younger brother raised over the elder, who bows to him and is then honoured: Joseph and his brothers (Gen 42:6; 45:4-13; 50:18-21; Q 12:100).
- The once-wronged hero becoming ruler of Egypt: Joseph as second only to Pharaoh (Gen 41:40-44; Q 12:54-56).
- Curses on those who alter or speak against a book: Deut 4:2; Rev 22:18-19.

**Truth and Falsehood: the lost dagger; Falsehood has his elder brother Truth blinded and orders him thrown to lions** (TruthFalsehood 1_6-3_3)
- Brother against brother out of envy at his goodness: Cain and Abel (Gen 4:3-8; Q 5:27-31) and Joseph's brothers (Gen 37:4, 11, 18-20).
- Servants spare the victim and report that a beast devoured him: compare Joseph's brothers and the 'evil beast' (Gen 37:20, 31-33; Q 12:13-17 'the wolf ate him').
- Thrown to lions: Daniel (Dan 6:16-23).

**Truth and Falsehood: a lady finds the blind Truth, conceives by him; the son mocked as fatherless learns who his father is** (TruthFalsehood 3_4-5_8)
- 'Knew her as a man knows': the Hebrew yādaʿ of Gen 4:1, 25 and 19:8; conception in one night: Gen 19:33-36, 38:18.
- The son of a disgraced father mocked by his fellows: Jephthah driven out by his half-brothers (Judg 11:1-2); 'is not this the carpenter's son?' (Matt 13:55).

**Truth and Falsehood: the son honours his blind father and goes to avenge him; the ruse of the ox** (TruthFalsehood 6_1-9_6/2)
- Honouring the blind father with food: Isaac blind and fed by his son (Gen 27:1-4, 25-31); 'honour your father' (Exod 20:12).
- A story told to make the wrongdoer condemn himself: Nathan's parable of the poor man's lamb (2 Sam 12:1-7), where a rich man takes another's beast to eat.
- The son as avenger of his father: the goʾel and the avenger of blood (Num 35:19; Deut 19:6).

**Truth and Falsehood: the trial before the Ennead; Falsehood swears his own punishment; Truth found alive; Falsehood blinded** (TruthFalsehood 10_1-11_5/2, TruthFalsehood Recto.1.=, TruthFalsehood Recto.2.=, TruthFalsehood Verso.1.=)
- The wicked caught in their own trap and given the punishment they devised: Haman (Esth 7:9-10), Daniel's accusers (Dan 6:24), Ps 7:15-16; the lex talionis 'eye for eye' (Exod 21:24; Q 5:45).
- An oath 'as the LORD lives' (1 Sam 14:39; 2 Sam 12:5, where David condemns himself unknowing) and 'as the king lives' (1 Sam 17:55; 2 Sam 15:21).
- Truth (Maat) and Falsehood as personified brothers: compare personified Wisdom and Folly (Prov 8-9) and 'truth has stumbled in the street' (Isa 59:14-15).

**Westcar: Khafre's tale: Ubaoner's wife and the commoner; the wax crocodile; the adulteress burned** (Westcar 1:17-4:17)
- A magician's object turning into a living reptile before the king: Aaron's staff becomes a serpent (tannin) and Pharaoh's magicians do the same (Exod 7:8-12); Q 7:107, 117; 20:66-69; 26:32, 45.
- Adultery punished by death for both (Lev 20:10; Deut 22:22) and burning (Gen 38:24; Lev 21:9).
- Wonder tales told to the king about the past: the king who has the chronicles read when he cannot sleep (Esth 6:1-3).

**Westcar: Baufre's tale: Snefru's rowing maidens; Djadjaemankh folds back the lake to recover the fish pendant** (Westcar 4:17/2-6:22)
- The waters folded back to lay the bottom dry: the parting of the sea (Exod 14:21-22, 'the waters a wall to them on the right and on the left'; Exod 15:8 'the floods stood up as a heap'; Q 26:63 'each part like a great mountain'); Elijah and Elisha dividing the Jordan with the mantle (2 Kgs 2:8, 14).
- A prophet recovers a lost iron axe-head from the water for its owner (2 Kgs 6:1-7).

**Westcar: Djedefhor tells of the living sage Djedi, aged 110; the prince fetches him** (Westcar 6:22/2-8:2)
- A man of 110 years: the age of Joseph (Gen 50:22, 26) and Joshua (Josh 24:29), the Egyptian ideal lifespan; a sage still vigorous in old age: Moses (Deut 34:7), Caleb (Josh 14:10-11).
- The king sends for a holy man living in the country: Naaman and Elisha (2 Kgs 5) or Saul and Samuel (1 Sam 9); Pharaoh sending for Joseph (Gen 41:14).

**Westcar: Djedi before Khufu: he refuses to use a prisoner and rejoins the severed heads of a goose, a bird and an ox** (Westcar 8:3-8:26)
- Wonders tested before Pharaoh: Moses and Aaron's signs (Exod 7:8-12) and Q 26:30-37.
- Restoring life to the dead by a holy man (1 Kgs 17:21-22; 2 Kgs 4:34-35; 13:21) and Ezekiel's bones joining (Ezek 37:7-8); Abraham's birds cut up and called back to life (Q 2:260); Jesus' 'by God's leave' wonders with birds of clay (Q 3:49).
- Humans as the 'noble cattle' of God: Merikare's 'well tended are men, the cattle of god'; compare Ps 100:3, 'we are his people and the sheep of his pasture', and the sanctity of human life (Gen 9:6).

**Westcar: Djedi foretells the three children of Re in the womb of Ruddedet who will rule; Khufu is troubled** (Westcar 9:1-9:21)
- A king troubled by the foretold birth of a child who will take the throne: Herod and the magi (Matt 2:1-16); Pharaoh's fear of Israel's sons (Exod 1:8-22) and the Jewish and Islamic traditions of Pharaoh's astrologers foretelling Moses; Q 28:4-6.
- Children fathered by the god on a priest's wife: compare the annunciation of a divinely given son to a woman (Judg 13:2-5; Luke 1:26-35).

**Westcar: Ruddedet's hard labour; Isis, Nephthys, Meskhenet, Heqet and Khnum come as musicians and deliver the three kings** (Westcar 9:21/2-11:9)
- Divine visitors in disguise received in a house and announcing kings: Abraham's three guests (Gen 18:1-15) and the angels of Q 11:69-73; 51:24-30.
- Birth stories with names explained by puns: Gen 25:24-26 (Esau and Jacob), 29:32-30:24 (Jacob's sons), 38:27-30 (Perez and Zerah).
- Midwives at a perilous royal birth: Exod 1:15-21.

**Westcar: the goddesses make three crowns and hide them in the sack of barley; the sack sounds with royal music** (Westcar 11:10-12:8)
- Purification of fourteen days after childbirth: Lev 12:5 (two weeks of impurity for a girl; seven days for a boy, Lev 12:2).
- Something hidden in a grain sack that will later reveal itself: Joseph's money and cup in the sacks (Gen 42:25-28, 35; 44:1-12; Q 12:70).

**Westcar: the beaten maidservant sets out to betray the royal birth to Khufu and is taken by a crocodile (breaks off)** (Westcar 12:8/2-12:25/3)
- The threat to newborn future kings from the reigning king, foiled: the infancy of Moses (Exod 1:22-2:10; Q 28:7-13) and of Jesus (Matt 2:13-18).
- A betrayer struck down: Judas (Matt 27:3-5; Acts 1:18).

**Anitta (KBo 3.22): Anitta son of Pithana; dear to the Storm-god; the king of Kuššara takes Neša by night and spares it** (CTH 1 W2:obv._1-obv._12)
- A god's favour as the ground of a royal career: 'the LORD was with him' of David (1 Sam 18:12-14; 2 Sam 5:10) and Hezekiah (2 Kgs 18:7).
- A city taken by a night attack: Gideon (Judg 7:19-22), Abraham against the kings (Gen 14:15), Ai by ambush (Josh 8:3-19).
- The conqueror who does no harm to the captured city's people: contrast the ban (ḥerem) of Josh 6:21; compare David sparing (2 Sam 8:2 partially) and the clemency of 1 Kgs 20:31.

**Anitta (KBo 3.22): campaigns to Ullamma, against the king of Hatti, Harkiuna, Wašhaniya; the inscription set at the city gate** (CTH 1 W2:obv._13-obv._35)
- A conqueror's words written up at the city gate with a curse on whoever damages them: compare Deut 27:2-8 (words written on plastered stones), Josh 8:32, and the curse formula of Deut 27:15-26; Rev 22:18-19.
- A curse on whoever rebuilds the destroyed city: Josh 6:26, fulfilled at 1 Kgs 16:34.

**Anitta (KBo 3.22): Piyušti of Hatti defeated; the god Šiušummi brought back from Zalpa; Huzziya captured; Hattusa taken by night, sown with weeds and cursed** (CTH 1 W2:obv._36-rev._51)
- A city sown after its destruction: Abimelech razes Shechem and sows it with salt (Judg 9:45); Jericho cursed for whoever rebuilds it (Josh 6:26; 1 Kgs 16:34).
- A captured god returned to its city: the ark taken by the Philistines and returned (1 Sam 5-6); Cyrus restoring the temple vessels (Ezra 1:7-11).
- A god handing over a city to the king: 'I have given Jericho into your hand' (Josh 6:2; 8:1).

**Anitta (KBo 3.22): Šalatiwara; temples built in Neša; the vowed hunt; the man of Purušhanda brings an iron throne and sceptre** (CTH 1 W2:rev._52-rev._79)
- A defeated king given a seat of honour at the conqueror's court: Jehoiachin lifted up and given a seat above the kings with Evil-merodach (2 Kgs 25:27-30; Jer 52:31-34); Mephibosheth at David's table (2 Sam 9:7-13).
- Iron throne and sceptre as tribute: compare the iron sceptre of Ps 2:9 and Og's iron bed (Deut 3:11).
- Booty dedicated to the god's house: David dedicating the spoils (2 Sam 8:11-12; 1 Chr 26:27).

**Anitta (KUB 26.71): temples, the vowed hunt, the burning of Šalatiwara, Purušhanda's iron gifts** (CTH 1 W5:obv._I_1'-obv._I_19´)
- The conqueror's hunt of lions and wild beasts as royal deed: Nimrod 'a mighty hunter before the LORD' (Gen 10:9); David's lion and bear (1 Sam 17:34-36); Benaiah (2 Sam 23:20).

**Telipinu Proclamation W2: Labarna, Ḫattusili and Mursili, united, conquer to the sea, Aleppo and Babylon** (CTH 19 W2:{€1}_obv._I_1'-{€1}_obv._I_29')
- A historical prologue of royal succession and good order before decline: compare Judg 2:6-19 and the cycle of Judges, and 2 Kgs 17:7-23 as retrospective history serving a present law.
- Unity of 'brothers' as the condition of strength: Ps 133:1; Gen 13:8.
- Kings of the past conquering to the sea: 1 Kgs 5:1 [4:21] (Solomon ruled from the River to the land of the Philistines); Ps 72:8 (from sea to sea).
- Servants who grow fat and turn on their masters: Prov 30:21-22; 1 Kgs 16:9-10 (Zimri, servant, kills his king).

**Telipinu Proclamation W2: Ḫantili and Zidanta murder Mursili; the gods seek his blood** (CTH 19 W2:{€1}_obv._I_30'-{€1}_obv._I_57')
- Regicide by a court officer and in-law: 2 Kgs 9-10 (Jehu), 1 Kgs 16:9-10 (Zimri, commander of chariots, kills Elah while drunk); 2 Kgs 12:21 [20] and 14:19 (servants conspire and kill the king).
- Blood of the slain king sought by God: Gen 9:5-6 ('your blood I will require'); 2 Sam 4:11 ('shall I not require his blood of your hand?'); 2 Kgs 9:7, 26 (blood of Naboth requited on the house of Ahab); Hos 1:4 (blood of Jezreel visited on Jehu's house).
- Remorse of the murderer 'what have I done?': 2 Sam 24:10 (David's heart smote him); Jer 8:6 ('no man says, what have I done?'); Q 5:31 (Cain becomes one of the remorseful).

**Telipinu Proclamation W2: Ammuna's failures, the murders of Zuru and Taruḫšu, Ḫuzziya, Telipinu spares his rivals** (CTH 19 W2:{€1}_obv._II_1-{€1}_obv._II_15)
- Not repaying evil for evil to rival claimants: 1 Sam 24:18-20 [17-19] and 26:21-25 (David spares Saul); 2 Sam 19:23-24 [22-23] (David spares Shimei: 'shall any man be put to death this day?'); Prov 20:22; Q 41:34.
- Deposed royals given food and a place: 2 Kgs 25:27-30 (Jehoiachin eats at the king's table); 2 Sam 9:7-13 (Mephibosheth).
- A sequence of court killings of kings and princes: 1 Kgs 15:27-16:22 (Baasha, Zimri, Omri) and 2 Kgs 15:10-30.

**Telipinu Proclamation W2: Telipinu's campaigns, the conspiracy, mercy to the conspirators, 'blood has become common'** (CTH 19 W2:{€1}_obv._II_16-{€1}_obv._II_33)
- Weapons taken away and the men made ploughmen: compare Isa 2:4 and Mic 4:3 (swords into ploughshares), here as a judicial commutation.
- Commuting a death sentence the people demand: 1 Sam 11:12-13 (Saul: no man shall be put to death this day); 2 Sam 19:22-23 [21-22].
- Prophetic denunciation of bloodshed in the capital: Ezek 22:2-4 (city of blood); 2 Kgs 21:16 and 24:4 (Manasseh filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, which YHWH would not pardon); Mic 3:10.
- Deaths in the royal house as the price of bloodguilt: 2 Sam 12:10-14 (the sword shall never depart from your house); 2 Sam 21:1.

**Telipinu Proclamation W2: the assembly, the law of succession and the law protecting the royal family** (CTH 19 W2:{€1}_obv._II_34-{€1}_obv._II_73)
- Law of the king in writing, to be read and to restrain the king from turning against his brothers: Deut 17:14-20 ('that his heart be not lifted up above his brothers'); 1 Sam 10:25 (Samuel writes the manner of the kingdom in a book).
- Children not to be put to death for the father: Deut 24:16; 2 Kgs 14:5-6 (Amaziah kills his father's murderers but not their sons); Ezek 18:20; Q 6:164 (no bearer bears another's burden).
- Royal seizure of an executed man's estate: 1 Kgs 21:15-16 (Ahab takes Naboth's vineyard); 2 Sam 16:4 and 19:30 [29] (Mephibosheth's estate given away); Ezek 46:18 (the prince shall not take the people's inheritance).
- Succession through a daughter's husband when there is no son: Num 27:1-11 and 36 (daughters of Zelophehad); 1 Chr 2:34-35 (Sheshan gives his daughter to his slave Jarha).
- Assembly as judge of the royal house: 1 Kgs 12:1-16 (assembly at Shechem); 2 Sam 19:10-15; 2 Kgs 11:4-20.
- Example made of offenders as a warning: Deut 13:12 [11], 17:13 and 21:21 ('all Israel shall hear and fear'); Num 17:25 [17:10] (a sign to rebels).

**Telipinu Proclamation W2: the list of seal-house towns and the decree on storehouses** (CTH 19 W2:{€3}_rev._III_1'-{€1}_rev._III_55')
- Store-cities and royal granaries: Gen 41:34-36, 47-49 (Joseph stores grain in the cities); 1 Kgs 9:19 (Solomon's store-cities); 2 Chr 32:27-29 (Hezekiah's storehouses for grain, wine and oil); Q 12:47-49 and 12:55 ('set me over the storehouses of the land').
- Falsifying measures; rulers who devour the people: Amos 8:5 (making the ephah small); Mic 3:2-3 (who eat the flesh of my people); Ezek 22:27 (officials like wolves shedding blood); Q 83:1-3 (woe to those who give short measure).

**Telipinu Proclamation W3: the prologue (duplicate of W2 I), 'the land was small'** (CTH 19 W3:{€1}_obv._I_1-{€1}_obv._I_39)
- Small beginnings made great: Deut 7:7 (you were the fewest of all peoples); Deut 26:5 (few in number, became a great nation); Isa 60:22.

**Telipinu Proclamation W3: Zidanta killed by his son Ammuna; the gods seek his blood; the land does not prosper** (CTH 19 W3:{€1+2}_obv._II_1-{€1}_obv._II_31'')
- Famine and failure of crops and herds for royal bloodguilt: 2 Sam 21:1-14 (three years of famine for Saul's blood on the Gibeonites); Deut 28:17-18 (cursed your basket, the young of your cattle and flocks); Hag 1:10-11.
- Son who murders his father the king: 2 Kgs 19:37 // Isa 37:38 (Sennacherib killed by his sons); 2 Chr 32:21.
- The murderer's line repaid in kind: 1 Kgs 16:1-13 (the house of Baasha); 1 Kgs 21:19 ('where dogs licked the blood of Naboth').

**Telipinu Proclamation W3: laws on dividing the estate, on blood, and on sorcery in the family** (CTH 19 W3:{€1}_rev._IV_1'-{€1}_rev._IV_26')
- A son claiming his share while the father lives: Luke 15:11-13 (the prodigal); Sir 33:20-24 [19-23] (do not give your property to a son while you live; distribute it at the time of death); Deut 21:15-17.
- Homicide and the next of kin who decides: Num 35:19-21, 31 (no ransom for a murderer; contrast the Hittite choice of compensation); Deut 19:12 (the elders hand him to the avenger of blood); 2 Sam 14:5-11 (the woman of Tekoa pleads with the king against the blood avenger); Exod 21:30 (ransom); Q 2:178 (retaliation or compensation remitted by the victim's kin).
- Sorcery and the duty of kin to hand over the offender: Exod 22:17 [18]; Deut 13:7-12 [6-11] (your brother, son, daughter or wife who entices you: your hand first against him); Deut 18:10-11; Lev 20:27; to the gate: Deut 21:19, 22:24.

**Telipinu Proclamation W5: the prologue; the queen of Šukziya murdered, Ḫantili's revenge, Zidanta kills Pišeni** (CTH 19 W5:{€1}_obv._I_1-{€1}_obv._II_14)
- A king avenges a murder in the royal family and executes the killers: 2 Sam 4:5-12 (David executes Ishbaal's murderers); 2 Kgs 14:5.
- Murder of a queen and her sons: 2 Kgs 11:1 (Athaliah destroys the royal seed); Judg 9:5 (Abimelech kills his seventy brothers).

**Telipinu Proclamation, Akkadian version W7: famine, granaries, sumptuary rules, laws on division and sorcery** (CTH 19 W7:{€5}_rev._III_1'-{€2}_rev._IV_31'')
- Famine in the reign of a king and the royal response: Gen 41:53-57; 2 Kgs 6:25-7:20; 2 Kgs 8:1-6; Ruth 1:1.
- Prodigal son and the forfeited share: Luke 15:12; Sir 33:20-24.
- Sorcerer to be put to death, handed over by kin: Exod 22:17 [18]; Deut 13:7-12 [6-11].

**Telipinu Proclamation W8-W10: small duplicates (Zidanta and Ammuna, storehouses, princes' estates, assembly)** (CTH 19 W8, CTH 19 W9, CTH 19 W10)
- Not a thread nor a sandal-strap: Gen 14:23; compare 1 Sam 12:3-4 (whose ox have I taken?).

**Treaty of Zidanza II with Pilliya of Kizzuwatna (CTH 25)** (CTH 25 §1, CTH 25 §2, CTH 25 §3, CTH 25 §4, CTH 25 §5, CTH 25 §6)
- A non-aggression pact over towns between neighbouring kings: 1 Kgs 20:34 (Ben-hadad restores the towns his father took); 1 Kgs 15:19-20.

**Treaty with Paddatiššu of Kizzuwatna (CTH 26): fugitives, envoys, plotters and migrating settlements** (CTH 26 §1, CTH 26 §2, CTH 26 §3, CTH 26 §4, CTH 26 §5, CTH 26 §6)
- Return of runaways between kings: 1 Kgs 2:39-40 (Shimei's slaves who fled to Achish king of Gath are brought back); contrast Deut 23:16-17 [15-16] (do not hand back a slave who has escaped to you).
- Envoys mistreated as a cause of war: 2 Sam 10:1-6 (Hanun shames David's envoys).

**Treaty with Paddatiššu (CTH 26): cattle theft by herdsmen, thieves, homicide 'a man like the man'** (CTH 26 §7, CTH 26 §8, CTH 26 §9, CTH 26 §10, CTH 26 §11)
- Double restitution for theft: Exod 22:3 [4] and 22:6-8 [7-9] (the thief pays double); contrast Exod 21:37 [22:1] (five oxen for an ox).
- Kidnapping and selling a man: Exod 21:16; Deut 24:7 (death penalty). Compensation by a person: Exod 21:23 ('life for life'), 21:30 (ransom), Num 35:31 (no ransom for murder).
- The thief who may be killed: Exod 22:1-2 [2-3] (the night burglar).

**Treaty of Tutḫaliya I with Šunaššura, Akkadian version KBo 28.110 (CTH 41.I.1): the ox and its stall, the tablet, the gods** (CTH 41.I.1 §1, CTH 41.I.1 §2)
- Ox and its stall: Isa 1:3 ('the ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib; Israel does not know'): the Hittite uses the image for a people who return to their rightful lord.
- Heaven, earth, mountains as witnesses of a covenant: Deut 4:26, 30:19, 31:28, 32:1; Isa 1:2; Mic 6:1-2 ('hear, you mountains, the controversy of YHWH').
- Name and seed destroyed: Deut 29:19 [20] (YHWH will blot out his name from under heaven); Ps 21:11 [10]; Ps 109:13; Isa 14:22.
- A new tablet replacing a former covenant: Exod 34:1 (two new tablets in place of the broken ones); Jer 31:31-32.

**Šunaššura treaty, Akkadian KBo 1.5 (CTH 41.I.2) §1-10: seal, historical prologue, the cattle know their stall, release and status** (CTH 41.I.2 §1, CTH 41.I.2 §2, CTH 41.I.2 §3, CTH 41.I.2 §4, CTH 41.I.2 §5, CTH 41.I.2 §6, CTH 41.I.2 §7, CTH 41.I.2 §8, CTH 41.I.2 §9, CTH 41.I.2 §10)
- Historical prologue of a covenant recounting the overlord's benefits and the partner's past: Deut 1-3; Josh 24:2-13; Exod 20:2 ('who brought you out of the house of slaves'); 1 Sam 12:6-11.
- Cattle recognizing their stall: Isa 1:3; Jer 8:7 (the stork knows her seasons, but my people know not).
- Judged out of his own mouth: 2 Sam 12:1-7 (Nathan: 'you are the man'); 1 Kgs 20:39-42; Luke 19:22.
- Release (andurāru) from a former master's claim: Lev 25:10 (proclaim liberty, dĕrôr); Jer 34:8-17; Isa 61:1.
- Seeing the king's face, the seat above the other kings: 2 Kgs 25:28 (Jehoiachin's throne set above the kings with him); Esth 1:14 (who saw the king's face and sat first); Gen 43:3; 2 Sam 14:24.

**Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys** (CTH 41.I.2 §11, CTH 41.I.2 §12, CTH 41.I.2 §13, CTH 41.I.2 §14, CTH 41.I.2 §15, CTH 41.I.2 §16, CTH 41.I.2 §17, CTH 41.I.2 §18, CTH 41.I.2 §19, CTH 41.I.2 §20, CTH 41.I.2 §21, CTH 41.I.2 §22, CTH 41.I.2 §23, CTH 41.I.2 §24, CTH 41.I.2 §25, CTH 41.I.2 §26, CTH 41.I.2 §27, CTH 41.I.2 §28, CTH 41.I.2 §29, CTH 41.I.2 §30, CTH 41.I.2 §31, CTH 41.I.2 §32, CTH 41.I.2 §33, CTH 41.I.2 §34, CTH 41.I.2 §35, CTH 41.I.2 §36, CTH 41.I.2 §37, CTH 41.I.2 §38, CTH 41.I.2 §39, CTH 41.I.2 §40, CTH 41.I.2 §41, CTH 41.I.2 §42, CTH 41.I.2 §43, CTH 41.I.2 §44, CTH 41.I.2 §45, CTH 41.I.2 §46, CTH 41.I.2 §47)
- Mutual defence pact: 1 Kgs 22:4 and 2 Kgs 3:7 ('I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses'); 1 Kgs 15:19 (a covenant between me and you, as between my father and yours).
- As his own head/soul: 1 Sam 18:1-3 (Jonathan loved him as his own soul and made a covenant); Deut 13:7 [6] (your friend who is as your own soul).
- Guaranteeing the partner's heir: 2 Sam 7:12-16; 1 Sam 20:14-17, 42 (covenant of Jonathan and David for their descendants).
- Booty divided, the land reserved: Num 31:25-47; 1 Sam 30:22-25.

**Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §48-60: war on Hurri, refusing Hurrian gifts, a new tablet, trusting messengers** (CTH 41.I.2 §48, CTH 41.I.2 §49, CTH 41.I.2 §50, CTH 41.I.2 §51, CTH 41.I.2 §52, CTH 41.I.2 §53, CTH 41.I.2 §54, CTH 41.I.2 §55, CTH 41.I.2 §56, CTH 41.I.2 §57, CTH 41.I.2 §58, CTH 41.I.2 §59, CTH 41.I.2 §60)
- Breaking with a former overlord's envoys and gifts: 2 Kgs 18:7 (Hezekiah rebels against Assyria); 2 Kgs 20:12-19 (envoys of Merodach-baladan); Isa 30:1-7 (envoys to Egypt).
- Testing a messenger against the written word: Deut 18:21-22 (how shall we know the word?); Jer 29:24-32 (Shemaiah's letters); Gal 1:8.
- Fixed quotas of troops for the overlord: 1 Kgs 4:26-28 [5:6-8]; 2 Kgs 3:7.

**Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §61-65: the frontier from the sea, measuring and dividing, the river Šamri not to be crossed** (CTH 41.I.2 §61, CTH 41.I.2 §62, CTH 41.I.2 §63, CTH 41.I.2 §64, CTH 41.I.2 §65)
- A boundary that neither party will cross: Gen 31:51-52 ('I will not pass over this heap to you, and you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me for harm'); Judg 11:13-27 (the Arnon and Jabbok as borders).
- Borders listed town by town and by river: Num 34:1-12; Josh 15:1-12; Ezek 47:15-20.
- Do not move the ancient boundary: Deut 19:14; Prov 22:28.

**Šunaššura treaty, Hittite version (CTH 41.II.1): defectors, fugitives, the penalty of twelve persons** (CTH 41.II.1 §1, CTH 41.II.1 §2, CTH 41.II.1 §3, CTH 41.II.1 §4, CTH 41.II.1 §5, CTH 41.II.1 §6, CTH 41.II.1 §7, CTH 41.II.1 §8, CTH 41.II.1 §9, CTH 41.II.1 §10)
- Penalty for harbouring a fugitive: 1 Sam 22:6-19 (Ahimelech and the priests of Nob killed for helping David); Josh 2:3-6 (Rahab hides the spies); contrast Deut 23:16-17 [15-16].

**Šunaššura treaty, Hittite version (CTH 41.II.2): Mittani, help 'if it suits him', fugitives, wife and children as compensation** (CTH 41.II.2 §1, CTH 41.II.2 §2, CTH 41.II.2 §3, CTH 41.II.2 §4, CTH 41.II.2 §5, CTH 41.II.2 §6, CTH 41.II.2 §7, CTH 41.II.2 §8, CTH 41.II.2 §9, CTH 41.II.2 §10, CTH 41.II.2 §11, CTH 41.II.2 §12, CTH 41.II.2 §13)
- Wife and children handed over for a debt or penalty: 2 Kgs 4:1 (the creditor comes to take her two children as slaves); Neh 5:5; Matt 18:25.
- Exculpatory oath of a keeper: Exod 22:7-10 [8-11] (an oath of YHWH between them both).

**Treaty of Šuppiluliuma I with Ḫuqqana of Ḫayaša (CTH 42) §1-6: the last dog, the sister given, 'recognize only me', love as your own soul** (CTH 42 §1, CTH 42 §2, CTH 42 §3, CTH 42 §4, CTH 42 §5, CTH 42 §6)
- Raised from 'a dead dog': 2 Sam 9:8 (Mephibosheth: 'what is your servant that you should look on a dead dog like me?'); 1 Sam 24:15 [14]; 2 Kgs 8:13.
- The overlord's exclusive lordship: Exod 20:3 and Deut 5:7 (no other gods before me); Deut 6:13-14; Josh 24:14-15, 23; Q 112:1-4 and 3:64.
- Love as the language of loyalty: Deut 6:5 (love YHWH with all your heart, soul and might); Deut 10:12, 11:1, 13:4 [3]; 1 Sam 18:1-3; 1 Kgs 5:15 [5:1] (Hiram 'loved' David).
- Covenant kept for sons after you: Deut 7:9 (keeping covenant and steadfast love to a thousand generations); 2 Sam 9:1, 7.
- The divine council summoned as witnesses: Ps 82:1; 1 Kgs 22:19.

**Ḫuqqana treaty (CTH 42) §7-8: the list of divine witnesses, mountains, rivers, springs, clouds, heaven, earth and the great sea** (CTH 42 §7, CTH 42 §8)
- Heaven and earth summoned as witnesses: Deut 4:26; 30:19; 31:28; 32:1; Isa 1:2; Ps 50:4.
- Mountains and the foundations of the earth as witnesses: Mic 6:1-2; Josh 24:27 (the stone has heard all the words).
- Queen of Heaven: Jer 7:18; 44:17-25.
- Gods of the Hapiru: compare the 'Hebrews' (ʿibrîm) in Exod 3:18 ('YHWH, the God of the Hebrews') and 1 Sam 14:21.

**Ḫuqqana treaty (CTH 42) §9-26: oath gods destroy the oath-breaker, blessing for the loyal, enemy of the king, no excuse of neutrality** (CTH 42 §9, CTH 42 §10, CTH 42 §11, CTH 42 §12, CTH 42 §13, CTH 42 §14, CTH 42 §15, CTH 42 §16, CTH 42 §17, CTH 42 §18, CTH 42 §19, CTH 42 §20, CTH 42 §21, CTH 42 §22, CTH 42 §23, CTH 42 §24, CTH 42 §25, CTH 42 §26)
- Curse on the covenant-breaker 'YHWH will not forgive him': Deut 29:18-20 [19-21] (he who says in his heart 'I shall have peace'; YHWH will not pardon him and every curse written in this book will settle on him).
- Blessing and curse set side by side: Deut 11:26-28; 28:1-68; 30:15-20; Lev 26:3-39; Josh 8:34.
- No neutrality in loyalty: Judg 5:23 (curse Meroz, for they came not to the help of YHWH); Judg 21:8-10 (Jabesh-gilead); Matt 12:30.
- Enemies of my lord are my enemies: Ps 139:21-22; Exod 23:22 ('I will be an enemy to your enemies').
- Duty to report treason even when one is sworn: Lev 5:1 (the one who hears the adjuration and does not tell bears guilt); Deut 13:9 [8] (do not conceal him).

**Ḫuqqana treaty (CTH 42) §27-28: the customs of the palace, keeping the king's words** (CTH 42 §27, CTH 42 §28)
- Talebearing of the king's words: Prov 11:13 and 20:19 (a talebearer reveals secrets); Eccl 10:20 (do not curse the king even in your thought, a bird will carry the voice); 2 Kgs 6:12.

**Ḫuqqana treaty (CTH 42) §29-32: no intercourse with the wife's sisters and kinswomen; avoid palace women; the death of Mariya for a glance** (CTH 42 §29, CTH 42 §30, CTH 42 §31, CTH 42 §32)
- Forbidden unions with close kinswomen and the foreign custom: Lev 18:3, 6-18, 24-30 ('you shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt and Canaan'); Lev 20:11-21; Deut 27:20-23; Q 4:23 (forbidden to you: two sisters together).
- Wife's sister forbidden during the wife's life: Lev 18:18; contrast Gen 29:21-30 (Jacob marries the sisters Leah and Rachel).
- Coveting a neighbour's woman; the look that kills: Exod 20:17; Deut 5:21; Job 31:1 (a covenant with my eyes); Matt 5:28; Q 24:30-31 (lower your gaze).
- The king at the window sees a woman: 2 Sam 11:2 (David from the roof sees Bathsheba) - inverted: here it is the subject's look that is punished.
- Approaching the king's women as treason: 2 Sam 16:21-22 (Absalom and the concubines); 1 Kgs 2:13-25 (Adonijah asks for Abishag and dies); Esth 2:3, 12-14.

**Ḫuqqana treaty (CTH 42) §33-34: no brother's wives in Ḫayaša, no further Azzi wives, return the prisoners; colophon** (CTH 42 §33, CTH 42 §34)
- Levirate as the foreign or ancestral custom: Deut 25:5-10; Gen 38:8; Ruth 4:5; contrast Lev 18:16, 20:21.
- A wife's rank guarded by her father: Gen 31:50 (Laban: 'if you take wives besides my daughters ... God is witness'); 1 Kgs 3:1 (Pharaoh's daughter); Deut 17:17 (the king shall not multiply wives).
- Return of captives as a covenant term: 2 Chr 28:8-15 (the captives of Judah returned from Samaria).

**Installation of prince Telipinu as 'priest' of Kizzuwatna (CTH 44)** (CTH 44 §1, CTH 44 §2, CTH 44 §3, CTH 44 §4, CTH 44 §5, CTH 44 §6, CTH 44 §7, CTH 44 §8, CTH 44 §9, CTH 44 §10, CTH 44 §11', CTH 44 §12', CTH 44 §13', CTH 44 §14, CTH 44 §15, CTH 44 §16, CTH 44 §17)
- The king's sons as priests: 2 Sam 8:18 ('David's sons were priests'); 1 Kgs 4:5; a royal appointee as priest at a provincial sanctuary: 1 Kgs 12:31-32; Judg 17:5.
- Disputes among brothers referred to the king: 2 Sam 15:2-6; 1 Kgs 3:16-28; Deut 17:8-12.

**Šuppiluliuma's decree for his son Šarri-Kušuḫ, king of Karkemiš (CTH 50): borders, the gold tablet, the gods of Karkemiš as witnesses** (CTH 50 §1)
- Tribal or vassal borders traced by mountains: Josh 15:8-11; Num 34:7-8.
- Kubaba, goddess of Karkemiš: Kybele of later Anatolia; compare the gods of the nations in 2 Kgs 17:29-31.
- Tablets of precious material for a covenant: Exod 31:18 and 32:15-16 (tablets written by the finger of God); 1 Macc 8:22 (bronze tablets of the Roman treaty).

**Šuppiluliuma's treaty with Šattiwazza (CTH 51.I) §1-5: historical prologue, Tušratta's arrogance, the one-year campaign** (CTH 51.I §1, CTH 51.I §2, CTH 51.I §3, CTH 51.I §4, CTH 51.I §5)
- Historical prologue grounding the covenant: Deut 1:6-3:29; Josh 24:2-13; 1 Sam 12:7-11; Judg 11:15-27 (Jephthah's history of the land as legal argument).
- Boastful royal challenge and its punishment: 2 Kgs 14:8-14 (Jehoash to Amaziah, the thistle and the cedar); 2 Kgs 18:19-35; Isa 10:12-15 (the arrogant boasting of the king of Assyria); Isa 37:23-29.
- Borders from a mountain to the Euphrat: Deut 1:7, 11:24 (from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the River, the Euphrat, to the western sea); Gen 15:18; Josh 1:4.
- Campaign that takes many kings in one year: Josh 10:42 ('all these kings and their land Joshua took at one time'); Josh 12.

**CTH 51.I §6-8: Tušratta killed by his son, the storm god's verdict, not a straw taken, Šattiwazza set on his father's throne and given a daughter** (CTH 51.I §6, CTH 51.I §7, CTH 51.I §8)
- A king slain by his son: 2 Kgs 19:37 (Sennacherib killed by his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer, who flee to Urartu); 2 Chr 32:21.
- Death of a ruler as divine judgement in a lawsuit: 1 Sam 25:39 ('blessed be YHWH who has judged the case of my reproach from the hand of Nabal'); 1 Sam 24:16 [15] (YHWH judge and plead my cause).
- Not a thread nor a sandal strap: Gen 14:22-23 (Abram to the king of Sodom); Num 16:15 (not one donkey have I taken); 1 Sam 12:3-4.
- A dead people brought back to life: Ezek 37:1-14; Hos 6:2.
- Taking by the hand and seating on the throne: Isa 42:6 and 45:1 (Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped); Ps 73:23; 1 Kgs 2:12.
- The overlord's daughter as chief wife: 1 Kgs 3:1, 7:8, 9:16 (Pharaoh's daughter); Gen 31:50.

**CTH 51.I §9-15: stipulations - the treaty, aid, fugitives returned one way only, the Euphrat border, brotherhood of Piyaššili and Šattiwazza** (CTH 51.I §9, CTH 51.I §10, CTH 51.I §11, CTH 51.I §12, CTH 51.I §13, CTH 51.I §14, CTH 51.I §15)
- Asylum for the runaway: Deut 23:16-17 [15-16] ('you shall not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped to you'), here as a religious rule of the Sun goddess; contrast 1 Kgs 2:39-40.
- Do not transgress the covenant or turn aside: Deut 5:32 and 17:20 (turn not aside to the right or left); Josh 23:6; Hos 8:1.
- Covenant of brotherhood between rulers: Amos 1:9 (Tyre forgot the covenant of brothers); 1 Kgs 9:13 and 20:32-34 ('he is my brother').

**CTH 51.I §16: deposit before the Sun goddess and the storm god of Kaḫat, repeated public reading, curse on tampering, the divine witnesses** (CTH 51.I §16)
- Deposit of the covenant document in the sanctuary: Deut 10:1-5 and 31:24-26 (the book placed beside the ark as witness); Exod 25:16, 21 and 40:20 (the testimony placed in the ark); 1 Sam 10:25 (laid up before YHWH); Josh 24:26.
- Periodic public reading of the covenant: Deut 31:9-13 (every seven years at Sukkot before all Israel); Josh 8:34-35; 2 Kgs 23:1-3; Neh 8:1-8.
- Not to add to or take away from the words: Deut 4:2 and 13:1 [12:32]; Prov 30:6; Rev 22:18-19; tampering with the scroll: Jer 36:23 (Jehoiakim burns the scroll).
- Heaven, earth, mountains, rivers as witnesses: Deut 32:1; Isa 1:2; Mic 6:1-2; Jer 2:12; Ps 50:4.
- Gods of the Hapiru: Exod 3:18, 5:3 ('the God of the Hebrews').

**CTH 51.I §17-18: the gods of Mittani incl. Mitra, Varuna, Indra; curses on the oath-breaker; blessings for the loyal** (CTH 51.I §17, CTH 51.I §18)
- Curses of the covenant: Deut 28:15-68 and Lev 26:14-39; poverty and nakedness: Deut 28:48 ('in hunger, thirst, nakedness and want of all things'); the throne overturned: Hag 2:22; crushed like a reed: 1 Kgs 14:15 (smite Israel as a reed is shaken), 2 Kgs 18:21, Isa 42:3; slippery ground: Ps 35:6 and 73:18, Jer 23:12; seed and name: Deut 29:19 [20], Ps 109:13.
- Pursued by the gods: Deut 28:22, 45 (they shall pursue you until you perish); Lev 26:36 (the sound of a driven leaf shall chase them).
- Blessing of the land at rest: Lev 26:3-6 ('you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid'); Deut 28:1-14; Ezek 34:14-15, 25-28.
- Eternal dynasty for the loyal: 2 Sam 7:16; Ps 89:29-38 [28-37] (if his sons forsake my law ... my covenant I will not break); 1 Kgs 9:4-7.

**Šattiwazza's treaty with Šuppiluliuma (CTH 52.I) §1-2: Šuttarna ruins the palace, gives the trophy door to Assyria, blinds and impales the nobles; Šattiwazza escapes** (CTH 52.I §1, CTH 52.I §2)
- Temple and palace doors stripped as tribute to Assyria: 2 Kgs 18:15-16 (Hezekiah strips the gold from the doors of the temple for the king of Assyria); 2 Kgs 16:8 (Ahaz sends the temple treasure to Tiglath-pileser).
- Nobles blinded and taken away: 2 Kgs 25:7 (Zedekiah's sons killed before his eyes, his eyes put out); Judg 16:21.
- God leads the fugitive on the way: Gen 24:27 (YHWH led me on the way); Gen 28:15, 20; Ps 23:3; Ps 107:7.

**CTH 52.I §3-7: Šattiwazza at the great king's feet, adoption as son, the word that does not turn back, the campaign to Irride and Waššukanni** (CTH 52.I §3, CTH 52.I §4, CTH 52.I §5, CTH 52.I §6, CTH 52.I §6a, CTH 52.I §7)
- Adoption formula for the king: Ps 2:7 ('you are my son, today I have begotten you'); 2 Sam 7:14; Ps 89:27-28 [26-27].
- Falling at the feet of the powerful protector: 1 Sam 25:23-24 (Abigail at David's feet); 2 Kgs 4:27, 37; Esth 8:3.
- The word that does not return void: Isa 55:11 (my word shall not return to me empty); Isa 45:23; Num 23:19.
- Gods (God) going before the army: Deut 1:30, 20:4, 31:8; Judg 4:14; 2 Sam 5:24; Exod 13:21.
- Arriving with nothing but one's staff and clothes: Gen 32:11 [10] ('with my staff I crossed this Jordan'); Job 1:21.

**CTH 52.I §8-10: deposit and reading, tampering, the Hittite gods as witnesses, curses and blessings (duplicate of CTH 51.I §16-18)** (CTH 52.I §8, CTH 52.I §9, CTH 52.I §10)
- As for CTH 51.I §16-18: Deut 31:9-13, 24-26 (deposit and reading); Deut 28 and Lev 26 (curses and blessings); Deut 4:2 (no change to the words).

**CTH 52.I §11-12: the gods of Mittani; Šattiwazza and the Hurrians curse themselves - tamarisk, water of the gutter, smoke, salt; their blessing in the lord's shade** (CTH 52.I §11, CTH 52.I §12)
- Self-curse formulas of the oath: Num 5:21-22 (the woman says 'Amen, Amen'); Deut 27:15-26 (all the people shall say Amen); Neh 10:30 [29] (they entered into a curse and an oath); Ps 7:4-6 [3-5].
- A felled tree without a shoot: Job 14:7-9 (there is hope for a tree that it will sprout again) - inverted; Isa 6:13; Mal 3:19 [4:1] (leave them neither root nor branch).
- Water spilled that cannot be gathered: 2 Sam 14:14; Ps 58:8 [7].
- Vanishing like smoke: Ps 37:20; 68:3 [2]; 102:4 [3]; Hos 13:3.
- Salt and barrenness: Judg 9:45 (Abimelech sows Shechem with salt); Deut 29:22 [23] (the whole land brimstone and salt, not sown); Jer 17:6; Zeph 2:9.
- Living in the shadow of the anointed: Lam 4:20 ('under his shadow we shall live among the nations'); Judg 9:15 (come, take refuge in my shade); Isa 32:2.

**Šuppiluliuma rescues Šarrupša of Nuḫašše (CTH 53 §§1-4, historical prologue)** (CTH 53 §1:1-§4:27)
- The great king as rescuer of the servant who cries for help: compare Q 8:9 (they called on their Lord for help and He answered) and Q 3:123-125; the claim 'I am your servant, save me' echoes the prayers of Q 21:87-88 (Jonah). HB secondary: 2 Kgs 16:7 (Ahaz to Tiglath-pileser: 'I am your servant and your son; come up and save me').
- The prologue that grounds obligation in past favour: compare Q 2:40 and 2:47 ('remember My favour which I bestowed on you, and fulfil My covenant') and Q 106:3-4; Deut 1-4 and Exod 20:2 are the classic HB analogues.

**Tribute, audience, friend and enemy, wholehearted war (CTH 53 §§5-7)** (CTH 53 §5:28-§7:70)
- Friend of my friend, enemy of my enemy as covenant loyalty: compare Q 60:1, 58:22 and 5:51-56 (alliance and disavowal, walāʾ and barāʾ). Tribute: compare Q 9:29 (jizya 'from the hand, humbled').
- The excuse 'I am under oath, but whether the enemy kills them or they kill him I do not care' is the treaty's picture of the half-hearted ally: compare Q 4:72-73, 9:42-49 and 33:18-20 (those who hang back from the fight); Deut 20:8.
- Leaking the campaign to the enemy: compare Q 60:1 (secretly sending affection, i.e. information, to the enemy; Ḥāṭib's letter) and Q 4:83.

**Help against enemies and the feeding of Hittite troops (CTH 53 §§8-9)** (CTH 53 §8:71-§9:95)
- Mutual aid within an alliance: compare Q 8:72 (help those who ask help in religion, except against a people with whom you have a treaty) and Q 9:4 (those who did not aid anyone against you). HB secondary: 1 Kgs 22:4 'I am as you are, my people as your people'.

**Captives, instigators, Nuḫašše folk in Hatti, refugees and requests (CTH 53 §§10-14)** (CTH 53 §10:96-§14:138)
- The return of fugitives was the most bitter clause of the Ḥudaybiya treaty; compare Q 60:10 (believing women who emigrate are not to be returned to the disbelievers) and Q 4:97-100; HB secondary: Deut 23:16-17 (do not hand back an escaped slave).
- Taking only what the lord grants: compare Q 59:6-7 (the fayʾ is distributed by God and the Messenger: 'take what the Messenger gives you and refrain from what he forbids you').

**As I revived a dead man (CTH 53 §15)** (CTH 53 §15:139-141)
- Compare Q 6:122 ('is he who was dead and We gave him life ... like one in darkness?') and Q 2:28; Ezek 37 as HB secondary. CTH 92 §6 uses the same image in the vassal's own mouth.

**The gods of Hatti, Kizzuwatna and Nuḫašše as witnesses (CTH 53 §§17-20)** (CTH 53 §17:142-§20:154)
- Treaty gods as witnesses vs. the Quran's single witness: 'God is witness over what we say' (Q 12:66, 28:28), 'you have made God your surety' (Q 16:91), 'sufficient is God as witness' (Q 4:79, 13:43). Oaths by the moon: Q 74:32, 84:18, 91:2.
- The roll-call of local storm gods and city goddesses is the kind of plurality the Quran polemicises against (Q 12:39-40 'many lords or God the One?', 53:19-23, 71:23).

**Mountains, rivers, heaven and earth as witnesses; curse and blessing (CTH 53 §§21-22)** (CTH 53 §21:155-§22:164)
- Heaven, earth and mountains as parties to covenant: compare Q 33:72 (the trust offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, which refused it), Q 41:11 (heaven and earth: 'we come willingly'), Q 44:29 (heaven and earth did not weep for them) and the mountain raised over Israel when the covenant was taken (Q 2:63, 2:93, 7:171). HB secondary: Deut 4:26, 30:19, 32:1 and Isa 1:2 (heaven and earth called as witnesses).
- Curse on the whole household vs. Quranic individual responsibility: compare Q 6:164, 17:15, 35:18 ('no bearer bears another's burden') and Deut 24:16 / Ezek 18; blessing and curse set side by side as in Deut 28 and Q 14:7 ('if you are grateful I will increase you').
- Keeping 'all the words written on this tablet': compare Q 5:1 ('fulfil the contracts'), 17:34 ('fulfil the covenant; the covenant will be asked about') and Deut 27:26.

**Muršili's tablet for Pijaššili of Kargamiš and his descendants (CTH 57)** (CTH 57 §1:1-§3:15)
- The great king's word that may not be cast aside or broken: compare Q 6:34 and 6:115 ('none can change His words'), 10:64, 18:27; and the sin of altering a bequest, Q 2:181. HB secondary: Esth 8:8, Dan 6:9 (the law of the Medes and Persians cannot be revoked).
- Whoever alters it has the gods as his legal adversary: compare Q 4:105-107 and the prophet as plaintiff against his people, Q 25:30.

**Aziru's loyalty and tribute (CTH 62 §§1-4, historical prologue, Akkadian and Hittite)** (CTH 62 §1:1-§4:38)
- A vassal 'faithful' (tarṣu) to father and son: compare Q 33:23 (men true to their covenant with God) and Q 23:8 (who keep their trusts and covenants); HB secondary: 2 Sam 9 and 1 Kgs 2:7 (kindness kept to a father's friend's house).
- '§5'' (lines 39-46) is a fragmentary manuscript placed by the edition between §2 and §3; nothing taggable survives.

**The sick heir installed; tribute to Hatti, not Egypt (CTH 62 §§5-7)** (CTH 62 §5:47-§7:77)
- The father naming his son before the lord while still alive: compare Q 2:133 (Jacob at death asks his sons whom they will serve) and Q 19:5-6 (Zechariah asks for an heir); HB secondary: 1 Kgs 1:30-35 (David names Solomon).
- 'Do not turn your eyes to another': compare Q 20:131 and 15:88 ('do not stretch your eyes toward what We have given others to enjoy') and Q 9:23 on not taking others as patrons.

**Egypt, secret envoys, the half-hearted ally (CTH 62 §§8-11)** (CTH 62 §8:78-§11:111)
- Secretly sending messengers to the enemy: compare Q 60:1 ('you send them affection secretly') and Q 58:7-10 (secret counsel, najwā); HB secondary: 2 Kgs 17:4 (Hoshea sends envoys to So of Egypt and withholds tribute).
- Pushing away the lord's hand: compare Q 48:10 ('the hand of God is over their hands; whoever breaks his pledge breaks it against himself').

**Aid in revolt, feeding troops, captives, evil words and secret orders (CTH 62 §§12-16)** (CTH 62 §12:112-§16:158)
- The vassal may refuse what he cannot do: compare Q 2:286 and 2:233 ('God charges no soul beyond its capacity') and the right to object to a command, Q 9:91 (no blame on the weak, the sick and those who find nothing to spend). HB secondary: 2 Sam 19:27-28.
- Not concealing evil words: compare Q 4:83 ('when news of security or fear comes to them they spread it; had they referred it to the Messenger and those in authority...') and Q 49:6 (verify the report of a sinner). HB secondary: Deut 13:7-12.
- 'Go wherever you will, I do not want to know you': compare Q 9:6 (grant asylum to an idolater who seeks it, then convey him to his place of safety), the opposite policy.

**Refugees set on the road, booty by request, the gods to see and hear (CTH 62 §§17-20)** (CTH 62 §17:159-§20:192)
- Setting the passer-by safely on the road with good words: compare Q 9:6 ('grant him protection until he hears the word of God, then convey him to his place of safety') and Q 4:94 (do not say to one who greets you 'you are not a believer').
- Witnesses who see and hear: compare Q 20:46 ('I am with you both, I hear and I see'), 58:1 and 16:91 (God made surety of the oath). HB secondary: Gen 31:49-50 ('God is witness between me and you').

**The witness gods of Hatti and Amurru (CTH 62 §§21-24)** (CTH 62 §21:193-§24:203)
- Heaven and earth and the mountains as witnesses: compare Q 33:72, 41:11, 2:63 and 7:171 (the mountain lifted above them when the covenant was taken); Deut 32:1 and Mic 6:1-2 (mountains hear the covenant lawsuit). Milku of Amurru: compare the Molech/Milcom of 1 Kgs 11:5-7.

**Curse and blessing on the words of the tablet (CTH 62 §§25-27)** (CTH 62 §25:204-§27:209)
- Compare Q 2:27 ('those who break God's covenant after its ratification ... they are the losers'), 13:25 (curse and evil abode for covenant breakers) and 13:20-22 (reward for those who fulfil it); Deut 28 and Lev 26 as HB secondary.

**Extraditing offenders, rumours of revolt, aid (CTH 67 §§1-4)** (CTH 67 §1:1-§4:51)
- 'Let that evil happen' as passive complicity: compare Q 5:78-79 (they did not forbid one another the wrong they did) and 8:25 (a trial that strikes not only the wrongdoers); HB secondary: Lev 5:1 (the witness who hears the curse and does not speak).

**The garrison, whispered rumours, fugitives (CTH 67 §§5-7)** (CTH 67 §5:52-§7:91)
- 'Because mankind is corrupt, rumours spread; check with the king and do not act rashly': compare Q 49:6 ('if a sinner brings you news, verify it, lest you harm a people in ignorance') and Q 4:83, 24:15-17 (rumour of the slander). HB secondary: Prov 18:8, 26:20-22.
- Asymmetric extradition: the Ḥudaybiya treaty (Muslims return Meccan fugitives, Mecca does not return Muslims), qualified by Q 60:10; HB secondary: Deut 23:16-17.

**Three vassals under one oath; disputes before the king (CTH 67 §§8-11)** (CTH 67 §8:92-§11:160)
- One oath, one community, disputes taken to the lord: compare Q 49:9-10 ('if two parties of believers fight, make peace between them ... the believers are brothers'), Q 4:59 and 4:65 (refer disputes to God and the Messenger), Q 3:103 ('hold fast all together to the rope of God and do not be divided').
- 'You alone shall be lord; I will not give your land to another' though the land asks for another: compare Q 3:26 (God gives kingship to whom He wills) and 1 Sam 8:7 (the people ask for another king).

**Calling for troops, runaway soldiers, Arzawa captives (CTH 67 §§12-14)** (CTH 67 §12:161-§14:234)
- 'Go, strike and carry off; I want to know nothing': compare Q 4:75 (why do you not fight for the oppressed?) and Q 9:38-39; the clause polices complicity by inaction. HB secondary: Judg 5:23 (curse on Meroz which did not come to help).

**The thousand gods; curse and blessing (CTH 67 §§15-16)** (CTH 67 §15:235-§16:242)
- Prosperity as the reward of loyalty: compare Q 7:96 (blessings from heaven and earth had they believed) and 16:97 (a good life); Deut 28:1-14.

**Manapa-Tarḫunta's flight, the oath gods seize the rebels, his plea for life (CTH 69 §§1-4)** (CTH 69 §1:1-§4:74)
- The rebel who falls at the king's feet asking 'let me live, take me as your servant' and is pardoned: compare Q 12:91-92 (Joseph to his brothers: 'no blame on you today'), Q 9:6 and 9:11 (repentant enemies become brothers), and the general amnesty at the conquest of Mecca; HB secondary: 1 Kgs 20:31-34 (Ben-Hadad's men in sackcloth: 'your servant says, let me live').
- Brothers who seek to kill the youngest, who escapes abroad and is later restored by a great king: compare the Joseph story, Q 12:8-15 and 12:100; HB secondary: Gen 37; Judg 9:5 (Jotham escapes).
- The oath gods 'seized' the oath-breaker: compare Q 3:11, 8:52-54 ('God seized them for their sins') and 16:94 ('do not take your oaths as a means of deceit, lest a foot slip after it was firm').

**The land given; covet nothing of Hatti; past betrayal; revolt (CTH 69 §§5-12)** (CTH 69 §5:75-§12:134)
- 'Do not covet a subject or a border of Hatti': compare Q 4:32 ('do not covet what God has given some of you over others') and 20:131; Exod 20:17 and Deut 5:21 as HB secondary.
- Ingratitude to the benefactor who spared him: compare Q 14:28 (those who exchanged God's favour for ingratitude) and 2:27.

**Manapa-Tarḫunta, Mašḫuiluwa and Targašnalli to live at peace; fugitives (CTH 69 §§13-18)** (CTH 69 §13:135-§18:185)
- Compare Q 49:9-10 (reconcile two fighting parties; the believers are brothers) and Q 8:46 ('do not dispute, lest you lose heart'); HB secondary: Ps 133:1.

**The thousand gods called to assembly; heaven, earth and the Šeḫa River's waters (CTH 69 §§19-25)** (CTH 69 §19:186-§25:229)
