- Captive wives made to grind at the mill: Isa 47:2, Judg 16:21 (Samson grinding).

**Deeds of Gurparanzah - the hunt, the archery contest at Akkad, the wedding night (CTH 362.1, 362.2, 362.3)** (CTH 362.1, CTH 362.2, CTH 362.3)
- The hero who wins a bride or honour by shooting: compare Odysseus' bow (Od. 21) and the archery of Jonathan (1 Sam 20:20-22); for a deferred wedding night, Tobit 8 and Gen 29:21-27.
- Sixty and seventy as round numbers of retinues: compare Song 3:7 (sixty mighty men round Solomon's bed).

**Deeds of Gurparanzah - the river Aranzah consoles the weeping hero and visits the mother goddess (CTH 362.4)** (CTH 362.4)
- A river that speaks to a weeping hero: compare the rivers that 'clap their hands' (Ps 98:8) and Hagar's well (Gen 21:16-19); 'why do you weep?': 1 Sam 1:8, John 20:13.
- Handantatar 'divine providence' (the gods' just ordering): compare the Quranic qadar (Q 54:49).

**Deeds of Gurparanzah - small fragments (CTH 362.5, 362.6, 362.7)** (CTH 362.5, CTH 362.6, CTH 362.7)
- Lying beside a bride without approaching: compare Ruth 3:7-14 and 2 Sam 11:11-13 (Uriah who will not go to his wife).

**The Sun god and the cow - the sun god's desire, the cow's human child and her attempt to devour it (CTH 363.1 §1-10)** (CTH 363.1 §1:1-§10:83)
- A god in human form who desires a creature: contrast Q 19:17-21 (the spirit as a man to Mary, who seeks refuge) and Gen 6:2.
- A mother who would destroy her newborn: compare Q 81:8-9 (the buried infant girl asked for what sin she was killed) and the abandoned infant of Ezek 16:4-6.

**The Sun god, the cow and the fisherman - the child guarded by birds, found and adopted by the childless fisherman (CTH 363.1 §11-19, 363.2)** (CTH 363.1 §11:84-§19:169, CTH 363.2)
- Exposed child protected under God's care and adopted by a childless household: compare Moses taken up by Pharaoh's house (Q 28:7-9: 'perhaps he will benefit us or we take him as a son'; Q 20:39 'that you be reared under My eye') and Exod 2:1-10; Sargon's birth legend.
- 'Whom the sun god loves he gives bread': compare Q 3:37 (Mary's provision, 'God provides for whom He wills without reckoning') and Ps 127:2.
- Pretended childbirth to legitimate an adopted child: compare Gen 30:3 (born on my knees), Ruth 4:16-17 ('a son is born to Naomi').

**Song of Silver - proem (CTH 364.1)** (CTH 364.1)
- 'I sing of ...' openings: compare Exod 15:1 ('I will sing to YHWH') and the hymn proems; the claim that no one honours the god against Q 55 (Which of your Lord's favours will you deny?).

**Song of Silver - the orphan Silver learns his father is Kumarbi and becomes king over the gods (CTH 364.2)** (CTH 364.2)
- 'Fear only the one god': a striking pre-echo, within polytheism, of Q 2:40-41 ('fear Me alone', iyyaya fa-rhabun), Q 16:51 ('do not take two gods; He is One God, so fear Me') and Deut 6:13; and of 1 Sam 2:6-8 / Q 3:26-27 (He exalts whom He wills and abases whom He wills).
- The fatherless son asking his mother about his father: compare Jesus 'son of Mary' (Q 19:27-33, the infant defending his mother) and Jephthah (Judg 11:1-2).

**Song of Silver - the orphans' rebuke; the sun and moon bow to Silver (CTH 364.3, 364.4, 364.5, 364.6)** (CTH 364.3, CTH 364.4, CTH 364.5, CTH 364.6)
- Sun and moon bowing: compare Joseph's dream of the sun, moon and eleven stars prostrating to him (Q 12:4, 12:100; Gen 37:9-10), and as divergence Q 41:37 ('do not prostrate to the sun or the moon, but to God who created them').
- 'We are the lights of heaven and earth': compare Gen 1:14-18 and Q 10:5, 71:16 (sun a lamp, moon a light); the threat of a world of darkness, Q 28:71-72.
- The orphan's rebuke: compare Q 93:6-9 ('did He not find you an orphan? ... so do not oppress the orphan'), Q 107:2 (who repulses the orphan) and Exod 22:21-23.

**Myth and ritual of the Euphrates (Mala) - primeval gods, the king son of the sun god, plague (CTH 365)** (CTH 365)
- Primeval gods who fixed the earth and released the rivers: compare Q 13:3 and 27:61 (He set firm mountains and made rivers), Q 79:30-31, and Gen 2:10-14 (Euphrates among the four rivers).
- Plague after the creation of man and the first king made by the gods: compare 2 Sam 24:15-25 (plague and David's altar) and, for divine appointment of a ruler on earth, Q 2:30 (khalifa) and Q 38:26 (David made vicegerent).

**Prayer of the king to the Sun goddess of the Earth and her underworld court (CTH 371.1)** (CTH 371.1)
- Intercessors in the court of the underworld goddess, bribed with food to speak well of the king: the sharpest divergence from the Quran's polemic against intercessors, Q 2:255 ('who can intercede with Him except by His leave?'), Q 10:18 ('these are our intercessors with God'), Q 39:3 ('we worship them only to bring us near'), Q 74:48.
- Do not listen to slander even from father, mother or brother: compare Q 49:6 (verify the report of a wrongdoer), Q 31:14-15 (do not obey parents in associating partners) and Ps 27:10 ('though my father and mother forsake me').
- 'Look with kind eyes, incline your ear': Ps 17:6, 2 Kgs 19:16, Dan 9:18; Quranic 'He hears and sees' (Q 58:1).
- 'Take him from evil, set him in a good place': compare the Lord's Prayer 'deliver us from evil' and Q 23:29 ('my Lord, land me at a blessed landing place'), Q 7:23 (confession, forgiveness).

**Prayer to the Sun goddess of the Earth, fragment (CTH 371.2)** (CTH 371.2)
- Gods with 'good lips' asked to speak well: compare Q 20:109 (no intercession avails except for whom the Merciful permits) and Q 19:87.

**Hymn to the Sun god, opening epithets (CTH 372 §1-4)** (CTH 372 §1:1-§4:33)
- Compare Q 1:2-4 (Lord of the worlds, Master of the Day of Judgment) and Q 2:255 (no weariness in guarding heaven and earth) with 'no fatigue at the place of judgment' (§3:22).
- Compare Q 93:6-9 and Q 4:127 (orphans) and Ps 68:6 (father of orphans).

**The Sun judges beasts and men and is sent to the angry god (CTH 372 §5-8)** (CTH 372 §5:34-§8:74)
- Compare Q 6:38 (animals are communities like you, gathered to their Lord) and Q 81:5 (beasts gathered) for judgment of the dumb animals.
- The Sun as go-between to a distant angry god diverges from Q 2:255 and Q 39:44 (intercession belongs to God alone); compare Job 33:23.

**The man's plea to his personal god, illness and unknown sin (CTH 372 §9-19)** (CTH 372 §9:75-§19:179)
- Compare Q 7:23 and Q 28:16 (confession: 'we have wronged ourselves') with asking to be shown one's sin; and Ps 19:13, Ps 139:23-24 ('search me').
- Compare Q 57:22 (no affliction but it is in a Book before we create it) with illness 'written from the womb' (§18:153).
- Compare Ps 27:10 ('father and mother forsake me, YHWH takes me in') and Ps 22:10-11 (from the womb you are my God).

**Vow of praise, enemies, the soothing words of invocation (CTH 372 §20-27)** (CTH 372 §20:180-§27:211)
- Compare Ps 6:6 and Ps 30:10 (vow to praise if saved) and Q 21:83-84 (Job's plea answered).

**Kantuzzili's prayer to the Sun god (CTH 373)** (CTH 373 §1:1-§13':103)
- Compare Job 31:17 (ate my morsel alone) and Job 31 as a whole oath of innocence; Q 76:8 (feeding the needy) and Q 107:1-7.
- Compare Q 83:1-3 and Q 55:9 (those who give short measure) with the cheating merchant before the Sun.
- Compare Q 3:185 and Q 21:34-35 (every soul tastes death; no mortal given eternity) with 'a child of mortality does not live forever'.
- Compare Ps 39:5 and Ps 90:12 (number our days).

**A king's prayer to the Sun god, hymnic part (CTH 374 §1-21)** (CTH 374 §1:1-§21:45)
- Compare Q 6:38 and Ps 68:6 as for CTH 372.

**The sick king's plea through the Sun to his god (CTH 374 §22-44)** (CTH 374 §22:46-§44:114)
- Compare Ps 22:15 ('poured out like water') and Ps 107:23-30 (seafarers brought to the haven).
- Compare Q 6:63-64 and Q 10:22 (God saves from the darknesses of land and sea).
- §39:97 mentions Arzawa being humbled: a historical allusion in a royal prayer.

**Arnuwanda I and Ašmunikal lament the Kaška devastation of the gods' lands (CTH 375.1)** (CTH 375.1 §1:1-§35:92)
- Compare Q 2:114 (who is more unjust than one who bars God's places of worship from his name being mentioned and strives to ruin them) and Q 22:40 (cloisters, churches, synagogues and mosques in which God's name is much mentioned).
- Compare Q 9:12-13 (those who break their oaths after their covenant and attack your religion), Q 8:56 (they break their covenant every time), Q 16:91-92.
- Compare Ps 74:3-8 and Ps 79:1 (enemies destroy the sanctuary, burn the meeting places) and Lam 1:10; 2 Kgs 25:13-17.

**Arnuwanda prayer, opening and colophon of tablet 1 (CTH 375.2)** (CTH 375.2)
- The invocation (§3:9) of Sun goddess, storm god, protective god, mountains, rivers and springs of Hatti recalls treaty witness lists; compare the oaths by natural phenomena in Q 91:1-7.

**Duplicate fragment; the royal pair will find out by oracle what the gods lack (CTH 375.4)** (CTH 375.4)
- Compare 2 Sam 21:1 (David seeks the face of YHWH to learn the cause of the famine).

**Muršili II's hymn and prayer to the Sun goddess of Arinna in plague and war (CTH 376.1)** (CTH 376.1 §1:1-§17:170)
- Compare Gen 18:23-32 ('will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked?'), Num 16:22 and Q 6:164, Q 17:15 (no bearer bears another's burden), Q 8:25 (a trial that strikes not only the wrongdoers).
- Compare Num 14:13-16 and Exod 32:12 (what will the Egyptians say) for the god's own name being humbled; Q 7:155 (Moses: will you destroy us for what the fools among us did?).
- The assembly's 'so be it' compares with Deut 27:15-26 and Neh 8:6 (Amen) and the Muslim āmīn after al-Fātiḥa.
- Compare 2 Sam 24:1-25 (plague on the whole land) and Ps 79:6 ('pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you').
- Compare Q 112:4 (none is comparable to him) and Q 42:11 with 'no other god is weighty and great'.

**Hymn to the Sun goddess of Arinna with a plea for queen Gaššuliyawiya (CTH 376.4)** (CTH 376.4)
- Compare 2 Kgs 20:1-6 and Isa 38 (prayer for the sick royal person).

**Muršili II's hymn and prayer to Telipinu, recited daily by the scribe (CTH 377)** (CTH 377 §1:1-§18:63)
- Compare Q 7:133 (flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood sent on Pharaoh's people) and Exod 10 for locusts sent against enemies.
- Compare Q 7:57 and Q 30:46 (winds sent as good tidings before rain) with the 'winds of prosperity'.
- Compare Q 37:180-182, Q 59:24 (the most beautiful names) with the god's name 'weightiest among names'.

**Muršili II's 'first' plague prayer, on the murder of Tudḫaliya the Younger (CTH 378.1)** (CTH 378.1 §1:1-§11:148)
- Compare 2 Sam 21:1-14: a three-year famine traced by inquiry of YHWH to Saul's breach of the sworn treaty with the Gibeonites; expiation by the king.
- Compare Q 6:164, Q 17:15, Q 35:18, Q 53:38 (no bearer of burdens bears another's burden) and Ezek 18:2-20 (sour grapes) against the son paying for the father's oath-breaking.
- Compare Q 16:91-94 (do not break oaths after confirming them, with God as surety) and Q 2:27.
- The argument that the gods will lose their offerers compares with Ps 6:6, Ps 88:11-13, Ps 115:17, Isa 38:18 (the dead do not praise) and with Moses' plea in Num 14:13-19.
- Delayed punishment after prosperity: compare Q 6:44 and Q 7:94-95, Q 22:48 (God gives respite, then seizes).

**Muršili II's 'second' plague prayer, the causes found (CTH 378.2 §1-10)** (CTH 378.2 §1:1-§10:112)
- Compare 2 Sam 21:1 (David seeks the face of YHWH; the cause is Saul's oath-breach) and 2 Kgs 22:8-13 (an old book found reveals the cause of divine wrath).
- Compare Q 7:23 and Q 28:16 (confession 'we have wronged ourselves', 'I have wronged myself') with 'it is so; we did it'.
- The murdered Hittite prince sent to marry into Egypt's throne is the Zannanza affair; the Egyptian queen's request has no Quranic echo, but the Hittite-Egyptian treaty framework compares with the covenant language of Q 8:56-58.

**Muršili confesses his father's sin and argues for mercy (CTH 378.2 §11-15)** (CTH 378.2 §11:113-§15:184)
- Compare Q 35:18 and Q 6:164 (no bearer bears another's burden), Q 2:134 and 2:141 ('that was a nation that has passed; theirs is what they earned'), against 'the father's sin comes to the son'; and Ezek 18:2-4, Jer 31:29-30, Deut 24:16, Exod 20:5.
- Compare Ps 84:4 (the sparrow finds a home, the swallow a nest, at your altars) and Ps 91:4.
- Compare 2 Sam 12:13 and 2 Sam 24:10,17 (David: 'I have sinned … these sheep, what have they done?') and Q 38:24 (David seeks forgiveness).
- Compare Q 10:98 (the people of Jonah believed and the punishment was lifted).

**Muršili II's 'third' plague prayer to the Sun goddess of Arinna (CTH 378.3)** (CTH 378.3 §1:1-§5:40)
- Compare Ps 88:11-13 and Ps 6:6 (who will praise you in Sheol?) and Q 51:56-57 (I created jinn and men only to worship me; I want no provision from them) as a divergence: the Quranic God needs no feeding.
- Compare Q 22:37 (neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God).

**Muršili II's 'fourth' plague prayer to the assembly of the gods (CTH 378.4)** (CTH 378.4 §1:1-§18:123)
- Compare 1 Sam 28:6 (Saul inquires and YHWH does not answer by dreams, Urim or prophets) with the failed oracle.
- Compare Q 9:18 and Q 2:127 (maintaining God's houses) and Ezra 1-6 for the vow to rebuild temples.

**Muršili II's plague prayer to the assembly of the gods; the Egyptian affair (CTH 379)** (CTH 379 §1:1-§16:57)
- Compare Deut 4:2 and 13:1 (do not add to or take from the word), Q 2:79 and Q 2:75 (those who write the book with their hands and alter the word) and Q 15:9.
- Compare Q 2:190 and 2:229 (do not transgress the limits, ḥudūd Allāh) with not overstepping the god-set borders.

**Prayer and substitute ritual for the recovery of Gaššuliyawiya, addressed to Lelwani (CTH 380.1)** (CTH 380.1 §1:1-§7:58)
- Compare Gen 22:13 and Lev 16 (substitute animals) and Q 37:107 (ransomed with a great sacrifice).
- Compare Q 22:37 (neither flesh nor blood reaches God) and Ps 50:13 ('do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?') as divergences from 'eat the fat, drink the blood'.

**Muwatalli II's plea to the assembly of gods, ritual setting and preamble (CTH 381 §1-5)** (CTH 381 §1:1-§5:30)
- Compare Jer 19:13, Zeph 1:5 and 2 Kgs 23:12 (offerings on rooftops to the host of heaven).
- Compare Q 2:286 ('do not take us to task if we forget or err') with asking the gods to overlook unaccepted words.

**Catalogue of the gods of Hatti's cities invoked by Muwatalli (CTH 381 §X1-X59)** (CTH 381 §X1:31-§X59:95)
- Compare Q 7:180 and Q 17:110 (God's names) and the polemic against many gods in Q 12:39-40 ('separate lords … names you have named, you and your fathers').
- Compare Acts 17:23 (to an unknown god) with the gods 'not named'.

**Muwatalli's prayer to the Sun god and the storm god piḫaššašši (CTH 381 §X60-X68)** (CTH 381 §X60:96-§X68:159)
- Compare Q 40:60 ('call on me, I will answer you'), Q 2:186, and Ps 50:15 ('call on me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you and you shall glorify me').
- Compare Ps 22:10-11 and Ps 71:6 (taken from the womb) and Q 19:12-15 (Yaḥyā).
- Compare Ps 121:5-6 (YHWH at your right hand; the sun shall not strike you by day nor the moon by night) and Q 91:1-2.

**The bread-breaking offering that accompanies the plea (CTH 381 §6-24)** (CTH 381 §6:160-§24:223)
- The burning of the broken loaves before the two tables (§24:220-222) compares with the shewbread (Lev 24:5-9) and burnt grain offerings (Lev 2).

**Muwatalli II's plea to the storm god of Kummanni, the cases of offence (CTH 382 §1-7)** (CTH 382 §1:1-§7:105)
- Compare Deut 30:19 and 31:28 (I call heaven and earth to witness) and Isa 1:2.
- Compare Gen 18:23-32 and Q 6:164 for limiting vengeance to the guilty city or house; and Q 17:16 (a town destroyed when its affluent transgress).

**Kummanni prayer, further cases, unknown offences and colophon of Lūrma (CTH 382 §8-13)** (CTH 382 §8:106-§13:153)
- Compare Q 2:286 ('do not take us to task if we forget or err') and Ps 19:13 ('who can discern errors? clear me from hidden faults') with offences 'that did not come out of our mouth'.
- Compare Gen 49:25 (blessings of breasts and womb) and Q 16:66 (milk from the bellies of cattle).

**Ḫattušili III and Puduḫepa to the Sun goddess of Arinna, disclaiming past offences (CTH 383.1 §1-8)** (CTH 383.1 §1:1-§8:90)
- Compare Q 3:26 ('you give kingship to whom you will and take it from whom you will; you exalt whom you will and abase whom you will').
- Compare 1 Kgs 21:29 ('I will not bring the evil in his days') and 2 Kgs 22:20 with 'do not revive the matter in my days'.
- Compare Q 6:164 and Q 2:134 with the plea that the guilty paid with his own head.

**Ḫattušili's restoration of Nerik as merit against inherited sin (CTH 383.1 §9-12)** (CTH 383.1 §9:91-§12:164)
- Compare Exod 2:9 and Q 28:7-13 (Moses' mother given wages to nurse her own son) with the wet-nurse's wage.
- Compare Job 1:6-12, Zech 3:1-5 (the accuser in the heavenly council) and Q 7:16-17 (Iblīs vows to sit in wait), and Q 11:114 (good deeds remove evil deeds).
- Compare Neh 9:2, Lev 26:40 and Dan 9:16 (iniquities of the fathers confessed).

**Fragment of a prayer of Muršili or Ḫattušili concerning the queen and an oath (CTH 383.2)** (CTH 383.2)
- The oath over shared beer-bread and water (§2:20-24) compares with covenant meals (Gen 31:46-54).

**Puduḫepa to the Sun goddess of Arinna, the story of Nerik and Ḫattušili (CTH 384.1 §1-5)** (CTH 384.1 §1:1-§5:57)
- Compare Q 17:110 ('call on God or call on the Merciful: whichever you call, to Him belong the best names') and Q 7:180 with one goddess taking different names in different lands.
- Compare Q 2:127-129 and Q 22:26 (Abraham restoring the House) and Neh 2:17-18 with the prince who rebuilds the god's neglected holy city.
- Compare 1 Chr 24:5, 31 and Luke 1:9 (priests assigned by lot) and Q 3:44 (lots cast for Mary's guardian).

**Puduḫepa's plea, the woman of the birth-stool, and the vow to Lelwani (CTH 384.1 §6-9)** (CTH 384.1 §6:58-§9:120)
- Compare Q 7:189 (the couple who pray when the pregnancy grows heavy: 'if you give us a good child we will be grateful') and Q 3:35 (Imran's wife vows her unborn) with the conditional vow and the woman in labour.
- Compare Q 19:23-26 (Mary in labour at the palm) and Gen 35:16-18 with the woman of the birth-stool to whom the deity yields.
- The petitioner's statue vow diverges from Q 7:148 and Q 21:52 (images); compare 1 Sam 6:4-5 (golden images given in place of the afflicted).
- Compare Q 113:4-5 and Q 2:102 (those who work harm through others) with the man who gave the gods a gift for Ḫattušili's harm.

**Zintuḫi, Mezzulla and the Storm god of Zippalanda asked to carry the plea (CTH 384.1 §10-17)** (CTH 384.1 §10:121-§17:163)
- The chain of divine go-betweens diverges sharply from Q 39:3 ('we only serve them that they bring us near to God'), Q 10:18 ('these are our intercessors with God') and Q 2:255 (who intercedes except by His leave?).
- Compare 1 Sam 1:11 (Hannah's conditional vow) and Gen 28:20-22 (Jacob: 'if God is with me … I will give a tenth').
- The line §17:163 carries the edition's footnotes run into the text.

**The enemies covet the gods' vessels, servants, temples and fields (CTH 385.8)** (CTH 385.8)
- Compare Ps 74:3-8 and Ps 79:1 (the enemy in the sanctuary) and Q 2:114 (who is more wrong than one who bars God's places of worship and strives to ruin them?).

**Tudḫaliya confesses curtailing the festivals and vows a temple (CTH 385.9)** (CTH 385.9)
- Compare Q 9:36-37 (the twelve months, four sacred; al-nasī' shifting the sacred month is an increase in unbelief) with the vow no longer to exchange spring and autumn festivals.
- Compare Q 7:23 ('our Lord, we have wronged ourselves') and 2 Sam 24:10 with the king's confession; and Num 21:2 (Israel's vow 'if you give this people into my hand').
- Compare 1 Sam 4-6 (the ark lost in a former generation) with the lost divine image.

**The king's dawn rite and the priest's prayer on the roof of the Sun goddess's temple (CTH 385.10)** (CTH 385.10)
- Compare Q 17:78 (the dawn recitation is witnessed) and Q 5:6 (washing before prayer) with the cloudless dawn, washing and silence.
- The sun prayer facing the sun at dawn diverges from Q 41:37 ('do not prostrate to the sun or the moon') and Q 27:24 (Sheba bowing to the sun); compare Ezek 8:16 (men facing east bowing to the sun) and Jer 19:13 (offerings on rooftops).
- Compare Q 8:17 ('you did not throw when you threw') and Ps 2:8-9 (nations given to the king) with the goddess's victorious spear.

**Analogic prayer, the soul shall not trickle away; be sweet to the king (CTH 385.11)** (CTH 385.11)
- Compare 2 Sam 14:14 (water spilt on the ground that cannot be gathered) and Q 14:24-25 (the good word like a good tree).

**The Storm god of Nerik woken and summoned from all places (CTH 386.1)** (CTH 386.1)
- Compare Q 27:20-28 (the hoopoe carries Solomon's message) with the goddess who calls the god's message like a bird.
- Compare Q 2:115 ('to God belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is God's face') and Q 55:17 (Lord of the two easts and two wests), against a god who must be summoned from wherever he roams; also 1 Kgs 18:27 (perhaps he is asleep).
- Compare Q 2:255 (neither slumber nor sleep seizes Him) and Ps 121:4 with waking the god from his dreams.

**The Storm god, gentle rain of all lands (CTH 386.2)** (CTH 386.2)
- Compare Q 7:57 and Q 42:28 (He sends down the rain after they despaired) and Q 56:68-70, and Deut 11:14-17 (the rain withheld).

**The king who passed over the oracles makes his plea from afar (CTH 386.3)** (CTH 386.3)
- Compare 1 Sam 15:22-23 (Saul rejects the word) and Q 7:146 (they see every sign and do not believe) with the king who passed over the oracle.

**The thirsty, hungry, wounded gods (CTH 386.8)** (CTH 386.8)
- Diverges from Q 6:14 ('He feeds and is not fed') and Q 51:57 and Ps 50:12-13 ('if I were hungry I would not tell you').

**Muršili III (Urḫi-Teššub) pleads innocence in his father's quarrels (CTH 387.1)** (CTH 387.1)
- Compare Q 49:6 (verify the report of a wicked man) and Q 24:11-16 (the slander) with the evil words between son and father; and 2 Sam 15:1-6 (Absalom).
- Compare Q 4:135 and Q 6:164 ('no bearer of burdens bears another's') with 'I acted at another's word'; compare 1 Sam 24:13 ('let YHWH judge between me and you') with 'that was the god's lawsuit'.

**Muršili III to the deity of Arušna, Tanuḫepa and the gods' silver (CTH 387.5)** (CTH 387.5)
- Compare Josh 7:1, 21 (Achan takes the devoted silver into his tent) and Q 3:161 (no prophet would defraud; whoever defrauds will bring it on the Day).

**Ayatarša's ritual for a sick child, sheep for the Sun god of illness, herbs and purification water (CTH 390 §1-21)** (CTH 390 §1:1-§21:65)
- Compare Lev 14:4-7, 49-53 (two birds: one killed, the living one set free over the field for the healed leper) with the goose waved over the child and released to the Sun.
- Compare Q 26:80 ('when I fall ill, He heals me'), against a sun god of illness who takes it away; and Q 16:69 (honey with healing) for the herbal potion.

**Wattitti's ritual for eaten entrails, bread on the spit, entrails eaten, the bundle under the stars (CTH 390 §22-32)** (CTH 390 §22:66-§32:138)
- Compare Q 113:1-5 (refuge with the Lord of daybreak from the evil of night and of the blowers on knots) and Q 37:6-10 (stars as protection) with the bundle conjured by the stars.

**Against evil tongues, the Old Woman cleans the tongue with honey (CTH 390 §33-35)** (CTH 390 §33:139-§35:166)
- Compare Q 20:27-28 (Moses: 'loosen the knot from my tongue') and Q 113:4; and Isa 6:6-7 (the lips touched with a coal) for the cleansed tongue.

**The great river bound everything; Kamrušepa conjures and looses it; the child bound and loosed limb by limb (CTH 390 §36-46)** (CTH 390 §36:167-§46:259)
- Compare Q 113:4 ('the women who blow on knots') and Q 20:27 with binding and loosing; and Matt 16:19 (whatever you bind … loose).
- Compare Job 38:31 ('can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loose the cords of Orion?') with the cosmic binding catalogue.

**Ambazzi's ritual for Zarniza and Tarpatassa, quenching, wool, the launderers, the mouse (CTH 391.1 §1-12)** (CTH 391.1 §1:1-§12:47)
- Compare Lev 16:21-22 (the goat carries the iniquities to a solitary land) and Lev 14:7, 53 (the living bird let go); and 1 Sam 6:4-5, 11 (golden mice sent away with the ark from the Philistines).
- Compare Isa 1:18 and Ps 51:9 (wash me, I shall be whiter than snow) with the launderers whitening the linen; Q 74:4 ('and your garments purify').

**Ambazzi's ritual for Alauwaima, the mouse released, a goat in its place, metals for good speech before the gods (CTH 391.1 §13-28)** (CTH 391.1 §13:48-§28:121)
- Compare Q 37:107 ('We ransomed him with a great sacrifice') and Gen 22:13 (the ram in place of the son) with the goat given to the deity in place of the carrier.
- The deity who 'speaks good before all the gods' for a gift diverges from Q 2:255, Q 20:109 and Q 34:23 (no intercession except by His leave).

**The eya-tree at the gate, the goat's blood in pots, the evil driven into the enemy land (CTH 391.1 §44-54)** (CTH 391.1 §44:194-§56:260)
- Compare Exod 12:7, 22-23 (blood at the door so the destroyer passes over) with the goat's blood in pots on either side of the gate.
- Compare Q 38:41-44 (Job: 'Satan has touched me with hardship'; strike with your foot, here is cool water to wash and drink) with driving the illness away.

**Second version of Ambazzi's ritual for the king, impurity drawn out, the bolt that opens the door (CTH 391.2)** (CTH 391.2)
- Compare Lev 18:24-30 (the land defiled by sexual abominations) and Lev 16:16 (atonement for the uncleanness of Israel); Q 33:33 (God would remove impurity, rijs, from you and purify you).

**Anniwiyani's ritual, the virgin at the door, the puppy cut in two at the hawthorn gate (CTH 393 §1-18)** (CTH 393 §1:1-§18:92)
- Compare Gen 15:9-17 and Jer 34:18-19 (passing between the halves of the calf) with the puppy halved at the gate.
- Compare Deut 21:3-4 (an untilled valley that is neither ploughed nor sown) and Num 19:2 with the untouched place 'where the plough does not reach'; and Q 2:71 (a cow 'not trained to plough the earth or water the tillage').

**Calling the Lamma of the hunting bag, the lost chaff and the nine pebbles; the colophon (CTH 393 §19-31)** (CTH 393 §19:93-§31:152)
- Compare Q 3:134 (those who restrain anger) and Exod 32:12 ('turn from your fierce anger') with the god's wrath 'lost like chaff'; Ps 1:4 and Ps 35:5 (chaff driven by the wind).

**Ašḫella's plague ritual, the rams and the adorned woman sent to the enemy's border (CTH 394 §1-5)** (CTH 394 §1:1-§5:41)
- Compare Lev 16:20-22 (Aaron lays both hands on the goat and sends it to a solitary land), 1 Sam 6:2-12 (the Philistines send the plague-bringing ark back to Israel's border on a cart with golden tumours and mice, 'let it go its way') and Zech 5:5-11 (the woman in the ephah carried to Shinar).
- Compare Q 37:107 (ransomed with a great sacrifice) and Q 22:37 (neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God, but piety) with the plague god asked to take fat rams instead of human flesh; Q 2:67-73 (the cow demanded and slaughtered) for the animal set apart.

**Ašḫella's ritual, days two to four, eat in a god's way; salt water and two fires; the colophon (CTH 394 §6-9)** (CTH 394 §6:42-§9:107)
- Compare Num 19:2 (a red cow on which no yoke has come), Deut 21:3 (a heifer that has not drawn the yoke) and Q 2:71 ('a cow not trained to plough') with the ewe 'to which no ram has gone'.
- Compare Num 31:19-24 (purify yourselves outside the camp; what can stand fire through fire, the rest through water) and Lev 16:26 (he who sent the goat washes before entering the camp).
- Compare Q 5:27 (from one it was accepted, from the other not) and Q 22:37 with 'eat in a god's way and leave nothing to man'; contrast Q 22:28, 36 ('eat of them and feed the needy').

**Ḫantitaššu's ritual for disturbed years, the table on the roof, 'take the gold, give me back the man' (CTH 395.1 §1-12)** (CTH 395.1 §1:1-§12:88)
- Compare Q 3:91 and Q 5:36 (an earthful of gold offered as ransom is not accepted) and Q 37:107 (the great sacrifice as ransom) with 'take the gold, give back the man'; Ps 49:8-9 (the ransom of a life is too costly).
- Compare Q 6:76-78 (Abraham and the sun: 'this is my lord … it set') and Q 41:37 with the Sun asked to lick the incantations like salt.
- Agni (dAgni), the Vedic fire god, appears in a Hittite-Luwian spell.

**Ḫantitaššu's ritual, the piglet in the pit for the old gods, the bolt that opens the dark earth, the sealed bundle (CTH 395.1 §13-25)** (CTH 395.1 §13:89-§25:165)
- Compare 1 Sam 28:7-14 (the woman of Endor brings up a god from the earth; Hebrew ʾôb, cf. Hittite āpi 'pit') and Isa 29:4; Q 2:102 (what was sent down in Babylon) for traffic with the powers below.
- Compare Q 34:14 (Solomon's death unknown to the jinn) and Q 72:6 for seeking refuge with powers below; the 'old gods' of the dark earth diverge from Q 6:100.

**Second manuscript of Ḫantitaššu's ritual, 'who of the gods made me a servant again' (CTH 395.2.1)** (CTH 395.2.1)
- Compare Q 3:26 ('You exalt whom You will and abase whom You will') and 1 Sam 2:7-8 with 'who of the gods made me a servant again, a master again'.

**Ḫantitaššu's ritual, the Sun's feast and the vanished patron (CTH 395.2.2)** (CTH 395.2.2)
- Compare Q 27:20 (Solomon: 'why do I not see the hoopoe, or is he among the absent?') with the Sun noticing a missing guest at his feast.

**Ḫatiya's ritual for the demoness Wišuriyant at the river (CTH 396.1.1 §1-6)** (CTH 396.1.1 §1:1-§6:51)
- Compare Q 2:102 and Q 113:4 (sorcery and the blowers on knots) and Q 114 (refuge from the whisperer) with appeasing a female demon; Isa 34:14 (Lilith).
- Compare Q 4:166 and Q 3:98 ('God is witness of what you do') and Gen 31:50 ('God is witness between me and you') with the Sun called as witness.
- Compare Q 18:61-63 (the fish slips into the sea and makes its way) with the fish released into the river as messenger.

**Ḫatiya's ritual, the sheep for the Sun, the bones burned, the goddess returned to her temple (CTH 396.1.1 §7-12)** (CTH 396.1.1 §7:52-§12:97)
- Compare Exod 12:10, 46 (no bone broken; what is left burned) and Lev 7:17 with the bones gathered and burned; and 1 Sam 2:13-16 (the priest's portion) with the ritualist who keeps the utensils.

**Ritual naming Wišuriyant, offerings set before the deity (CTH 396.1.2)** (CTH 396.1.2 §1:1-§5:37)
- Compare Q 22:37 (neither the flesh nor the blood reaches God, only piety) as a divergence from food set 'before the deity'.
- Compare Lev 7:11-15 and Deut 12:7 (sacrificial meal eaten before the LORD).

**Ritual naming Wišuriyant, address and river disposal (CTH 396.2)** (CTH 396.2 §1:1-§2:9)
- Compare Mic 7:19 (sins cast into the depths of the sea).

**Ḫepattarakki of Zuḫaruwa releases a bewitched man with dough figures (CTH 397 §1-5)** (CTH 397 §1:1-§5:30)
- Compare Q 35:43 (evil plotting encompasses only its own authors) and Q 113:4 (those who blow on knots) for sorcery sent back on the sorcerer.
- Compare Q 20:69 (the sorcerer does not prosper wherever he comes) and Ps 7:16 (his mischief returns on his own head).

**Ḫepattarakki ritual, fragments and colophon (CTH 397 §6-13)** (CTH 397 §6:31-§13:80)
- Compare Q 113:1-5 and 114:1-6 (refuge from sorcery, envy and the whisperer) and Q 2:102 (sorcery taught in Babylon).

**The augur Ḫuwarlu against terrible birds, clay birds and roasted seeds (CTH 398 §1-3)** (CTH 398 §1:1-§3:22)
- Compare Q 17:13 (every man's 'bird', his omen, fastened to his neck) and Q 27:47 / 36:18-19 / 7:131 ('your augury is with God') against augury from birds.
- Compare Isa 44:25 (God frustrates the omens of diviners) and Deut 18:10.

**Ḫuwarlu ritual, tallow puppy, binding cords, soap and riverbank clay (CTH 398 §4-9)** (CTH 398 §4:23-§9:65)
- Compare Q 74:4-5 (purify your garments, shun defilement) and Q 8:11 (water sent to purify you and remove the taint of Satan).
- Compare Lev 14:49-53 (purification of a house) and Ps 51:9, Isa 1:18, Mal 3:2 (fuller's soap).

**Ḫuwarlu ritual, dough of life, waving and the living puppy as carrier (CTH 398 §10-16)** (CTH 398 §10:66-§16:126)
- Compare Lev 16:10, 21-22 (the living goat bears iniquities to a solitary land) and Lev 14:7, 53 (living bird released over the open field).
- The animal that carries evil away diverges from Q 6:164, 17:15, 35:18 and 53:38 (no bearer of burdens bears another's burden).
- Compare Zech 5:5-11 (wickedness carried off in a basket to a place prepared for it).

**Ḫuwarlu ritual, buried head, goat on foliage, gates, washing and prayer to the Sun (CTH 398 §17-27)** (CTH 398 §17:127-§27:215)
- Compare Q 17:13 and Q 27:47 (one's 'bird'/omen is with God) as against asking for favourable birds.
- Compare Q 41:37 (do not prostrate to the sun) for rites addressed to the Sun.
- Compare Gen 15:9-17 and Jer 34:18-19 (passing between) and Deut 21:6 (washing hands over the heifer).

**Jarri of Lallupiya against bloodshed and impurity in a house (CTH 399)** (CTH 399 §1:1-§5:20)
- Compare Q 5:32 and Q 2:72-73 (a killing disputed, revealed through the slaughtered cow) and Num 35:33-34 (blood pollutes the land).
- Compare Lev 14:33-53 (purifying a house with two birds, cedar, scarlet and hyssop).

**Iriya purifies a city of blood, perjury and curse, the riverbank clay and the ancient gods (CTH 400.1 §1-11)** (CTH 400.1 §1:1-§11:53)
- Compare Deut 21:1-9 (a city purges unsolved bloodshed with a heifer at a perennial stream) and Num 35:33.
- Compare Q 2:72-73 (the disputed killing and the cow) and Q 5:32 for bloodguilt of a community.

**Iriya ritual, the springs answer and the frog swallows the impurity (CTH 400.1 §12-13)** (CTH 400.1 §12:54-§13:69)
- Compare Q 33:72 (the trust offered to heavens, earth and mountains) and Q 41:11 (heaven and earth answer 'we come willingly') for nature answering.
- Compare Q 7:133 (frogs among the signs) and Mic 7:19 (sins cast into the sea).

**Iriya ritual, the šurašura-bird, the goat burned and buried, eagle and falcon released (CTH 400.1 §14-20)** (CTH 400.1 §14:70-§20:112)
- Compare Lev 14:4-7, 49-53 (one bird slain, the living bird released over the open field) and Lev 16:8-10, 20-22 (two goats, one sent away); Lev 16:27 (the sin-offering goat burned outside the camp).
- Compare Q 22:31 (one who associates others with God is as if he fell from the sky and the birds snatched him) for birds carrying off.
- The cry of the wronged reaching heaven: compare Q 4:148 and Gen 4:10, Exod 22:22-23.

**The augur Banippi when a friend has slandered his companion, the clay tongue (CTH 401.1 §1-4)** (CTH 401.1 §1:1-§4:23)
- Compare Q 24:11-19 (the slander, ifk, against the innocent), Q 49:12 and Q 104:1 (woe to the slanderer).

**Banippi ritual, the mountains answer and the evil is given to the ancient gods (CTH 401.1 §5)** (CTH 401.1 §5:24-43)
- Compare Q 33:72 and Q 59:21 (the mountains addressed) and Q 34:10 (mountains echo David).
- Compare Ps 7:15-16 (he falls into the pit he made).

**Banippi ritual, the burning of the seven kippa-tents and the bewitched driven off (CTH 401.1 §6-7)** (CTH 401.1 §6:44-§7:62)
- Compare Q 2:200 and the stoning of the pillars (jamarat) at Mina; Q 67:5 (lamps of heaven as missiles against devils).
- Compare Lev 16:26-28 (those who led away and burned the remains washed before return).

**Ritual like CTH 400, the king addresses the mountains about blood, tears and the tongue of the multitude (CTH 401.2 §1-6)** (CTH 401.2 §1:1-§6:28)
- A king answerable for wronging a just man: compare Q 4:148 (God does not love evil spoken aloud except by one wronged) and 1 Kgs 21 (Naboth).

**Ritual like CTH 400, the springs answer, the frog swallows, the water does not return (CTH 401.2 §7-9)** (CTH 401.2 §7:29-§9:51)
- Compare Q 13:17 (the scum passes away as dross, what profits people remains) and 2 Sam 14:14 (water spilt on the ground that cannot be gathered).

**Ritual like CTH 400, eagle to heaven and falcon to the pure mountains, the king purified (CTH 401.2 §10-19)** (CTH 401.2 §10:52-§19:94)
- Compare Lev 14:7, 53 (the living bird released) and Lev 16:22.
- Eating fat and blood as a cause of impurity: compare Lev 3:17, 7:23-27 and Q 5:3, 6:145 (blood forbidden).

**Ritual to purify a city of disease and plague, Muršili and the great gate (CTH 401.5)** (CTH 401.5 §1:1-§3:51)
- Compare Q 7:134-135 (Pharaoh's people ask Moses to have the plague, rijz, removed) and 2 Sam 24:15-25 (plague stopped at the threshing floor).

**Alli of Arzawa against sorcery, the clay figurines with tongues and the sorcery handed back (CTH 402 §1-8)** (CTH 402 §1:1-§8:55)
- Compare Q 113:4 (the blowers on knots), Q 2:102 (sorcery that separates man and wife) and Q 35:43 (evil plotting encompasses only its authors).
- Each bears her own deed: compare Q 6:164, 17:15 and 52:21; and Ps 7:16.

**Alli ritual, coloured threads take off the colours of sorcery, white wool purifies (CTH 402 §9-19)** (CTH 402 §9:56-§19:119)
- Compare Isa 1:18 (sins red as crimson made white as wool) and Lev 14:4 (scarlet thread).
- Compare Q 113:4 and Q 2:102 for sorcery, and Q 24:23 (those who accuse innocent women).

**Alli ritual, the sorcery buried and pegged, bread for the gods of the roads and the gate (CTH 402 §20-23)** (CTH 402 §20:120-§23:169)
- Compare Q 113:4 and Q 20:69, and Zech 5:8-11 (wickedness weighted down with a lead cover and set on its base).
- Compare Ezek 21:21 (the king at the parting of the ways).

**Alli ritual, the basket under the bed, wax figurines and the hunter who carries off (CTH 402 §24-32)** (CTH 402 §24:170-§32:235)
- Compare Q 113:4 and Q 114 (refuge from the whisperer) and Zech 5:5-11 (the basket of wickedness carried away).

**Alli ritual, the bath, the five cups, burial, sacrifice to the Sun and the river (CTH 402 §33-44)** (CTH 402 §33:236-§44:317)
- Compare Q 5:6 (ablution) and Q 4:43; Lev 14:8-9 and 16:24-28 (washing after the rite).
- Compare Q 22:36-37 (eat of the sacrificed animals; their flesh does not reach God).

**Mallidunna's ritual for the Sun god, the three pairs of eyes of the Sun (CTH 403.1)** (CTH 403.1 §1:1-§8:45)
- Compare Q 6:76-79 (Abraham sees the sun set and says 'I love not those that set') and Q 41:37 (prostrate not to the sun).
- God who sees: compare Q 40:19 (He knows the treachery of the eyes) and Zech 4:10, 2 Chr 16:9 (the eyes of the LORD range through the earth).

**Mallidunna's ritual to rouse the angry Ḫannaḫanna (CTH 403.2)** (CTH 403.2 §1:1-§8:45)
- Compare Q 42:49-50 (God gives daughters or sons or makes barren whom He wills) against a goddess who withholds fertility.
- Compare 1 Sam 1 (Hannah's barrenness) and Gen 30:1-2 ('am I in God's place who withheld from you the fruit of the womb?').

**Offerings to the Sun god, 'as the ewe recognises her lamb' (CTH 403.3.1)** (CTH 403.3.1 §1:1-§4:29)
- Compare Q 2:146 and 6:20 (they recognise him as they recognise their own sons) for the 'recognition' formula.
- Compare Isa 49:15 (can a woman forget her nursing child?) and Ps 103:13 (as a father has compassion on his children).

**Maštigga of Kizzuwatna against family quarrel, incipit and materials (CTH 404.1.I §1-5)** (CTH 404.1.I §1:1-§5:17)
- Compare Q 49:9-10 (make peace between brothers) and Q 4:35, 128 (arbiters to reconcile husband and wife), Q 8:46 (do not quarrel).
- Compare Q 2:102 (sorcery that separates a man from his wife) and Ps 133:1.

**Maštigga ritual, the tongues of that day cut, the fish and the tiššatwa thrown into the fire (CTH 404.1.I §6-19)** (CTH 404.1.I §6:18-§19:92)
- Compare Q 49:11-12 (do not defame one another, do not backbite) and Q 104:1; Jas 3:5-8 (the tongue a fire).
- Compare Ps 64:3 and 120:2-4 (lying tongues and sharp arrows) and Ps 12:3 (the LORD cuts off flattering lips).

**Maštigga ritual, sheep and black sheep as substitutes, the patients spit into their mouths, the piglet buried (CTH 404.1.I §20-25)** (CTH 404.1.I §20:93-§25:136)
- Compare Q 37:107 (We ransomed him with a great sacrifice) and Q 2:67-73 (the cow slaughtered), Q 22:37 (neither flesh nor blood reaches God).
- Substitution diverges from Q 6:164, 35:18 (no soul bears another's burden); compare Lev 16:21-22 and Lev 5:5-6.

**Maštigga ritual, clay and cumin, the salamander and puppy, Šaušga's vessel, the carrier sheep and the seven nails (CTH 404.1.I §26-38)** (CTH 404.1.I §26:137-§38:210)
- Compare Lev 16:8-10, 21-22 (the live goat bears the iniquities) and Lev 14:7; the sheep kept by the practitioner is a divergence.
- Compare Q 37:107, 22:37 and 2:67-73; the substitute and the carrier vs Q 53:38-39 (no bearer bears another's burden; man has only what he strove for).
- Breaking vessels: compare Jer 19:10-11 (the flask broken before witnesses) and Ps 2:9.

**Maštigga ritual, through the fire past the fallen huwaši-stones, the vessels broken by foot, washing and the sealed horn (CTH 404.1.I §39-46)** (CTH 404.1.I §39:211-§46:256)
- Passing through fire: compare Q 21:68-69 (fire made cool and safe for Abraham) as a contrast; and Num 31:23, Isa 43:2.
- The seal until the ancient kings return: compare Q 18:9-26 (the sleepers raised in a later age) only loosely; Dan 12:4 (seal the book until the time of the end) and Isa 8:16.
- Compare Q 5:6 (wash faces and hands) for washing hands and eyes.

**Maštigga ritual, second manuscript group, tiššatwa to the clay and cumin (CTH 404.1.II §1-19)** (CTH 404.1.II §1:1-§19:103)
- As in group I: compare Q 37:107, 22:37 and Lev 16:21-22.

**Maštigga ritual, second manuscript group, salamander to the sealed horn and colophon of Ḫanikkuili (CTH 404.1.II §20-44)** (CTH 404.1.II §20:104-§44:215)
- Compare Dan 12:4, 9 (words sealed until the end) and Q 18:9-26.

**Paškuwatti of Arzawa against impotence, the reed gate, the spindle taken and the bow given (CTH 406 §1-4)** (CTH 406 §1:1-§4:28)
- Compare Q 42:49-50 (He gives females or males to whom He wills and makes barren whom He wills) and Q 3:38-40, 19:8-9 (Zechariah given a son).
- Compare 2 Sam 3:29 (a man 'who holds the spindle' as a curse on Joab's house) and Deut 22:5 (garments of the other sex).

**Paškuwatti ritual, the invocation of Uliliyašši to come to the man and be his wife (CTH 406 §5-10)** (CTH 406 §5:29-§10:81)
- Compare Q 32:8 and 77:20 (man created from a despised fluid) and Q 80:17-19 for 'excrement and urine'.
- The vow to make the goddess his deity: compare Q 7:189-190 (the couple promise thanks for a child, then give partners to God) as polemic.
- Compare Gen 28:20-22 (Jacob's vow: if God gives, 'the LORD shall be my God').

**Paškuwatti ritual, three days of invocation, incubation and the goddess in the dream, her image as vessel or stone (CTH 406 §11-20)** (CTH 406 §11:82-§20:149)
- Compare Gen 28:11-22 (dream at Bethel, the stone set up as a pillar, a vow) and 1 Kgs 3:5-15 (Solomon's dream at Gibeon).
- Against images: compare Q 21:52 (what are these images to which you are devoted?), Q 7:138 and Q 71:23.
- A goddess as consort diverges from Q 72:3 (He has taken neither consort nor son) and Q 6:101.

**Puliša against plague brought from the enemy, captive and woman in the king's garments, the ringed bull and ewe sent back (CTH 407)** (CTH 407 §1:1-§8:56)
- Compare 1 Sam 6:1-12 (the Philistines send the plague-bringing ark home on a cart drawn by two milch cows, with gold offerings) and 2 Sam 24:15-25.
- Compare Q 7:133-135 (the plague, rijz, removed from Pharaoh's people) and Q 37:107; a human substitute diverges sharply from Q 6:164, 17:15 and 5:32.
- Compare Lev 16:21-22 (the goat bears iniquity to a land apart).

**Uḫḫamuwa of Arzawa against dying in the land, the wreathed ram driven to the enemy and the god's horses fed (CTH 410)** (CTH 410 §1:1-§4:33)
- Compare Q 5:2 and 5:97 (the sacrificial animals and the garlands, al-qala'id) and Q 22:36 for the garlanded animal.
- Compare Lev 16:10, 21-22 and 1 Sam 6:7-12 (cows sent on the road out of the land).

**Uruwanda against the effects of slander, the tongue pulled down with sinew and seven fires each side (CTH 411)** (CTH 411 §1:1-§7:27''')
- Compare Q 24:11-19 (the slander against the innocent and its punishment), Q 49:12 and Q 68:10-11 (the slanderer going about with calumnies), Q 104:1.
- Compare Ps 120:2-4 and Ps 52:4-7 (the deceitful tongue uprooted).

**Building ritual for a new temple, copper nailed under the pillar and foundation stones of nine materials (CTH 413.1 §1-11)** (CTH 413.1 §1:1-§11:51)
- Compare Q 2:127 (Abraham and Ishmael raising the foundations of the House) and Q 9:108-109 (a mosque founded on piety vs one founded on a crumbling bank).
- Iron from heaven: compare Q 57:25 (We sent down iron, in which is great might).
- 'Not we built it': compare Ps 127:1 (unless the LORD builds the house) and Q 8:17 (you did not slay them, God slew them).
- Materials from afar: compare 1 Kgs 5:6-18, 7:13-14 and Q 34:12-13 (molten copper for Solomon; the jinn build for him).

**Building ritual, pegs of precious metal, the golden lion and iron oxen, models of hearth, door and trees (CTH 413.1 §12-22)** (CTH 413.1 §12:52-§22:77)
- Compare 1 Kgs 7:23-29 (the sea on twelve oxen, lions and oxen on the stands) and 1 Kgs 6:29-35 (palm trees and cherubim of gold).
- Compare Q 34:13 (they made for Solomon sanctuaries, statues, basins like reservoirs) and Q 9:109.

**An incantation ritual, the AZU-priest, the bound bird, the reed gate, the arrow shot against oath and curse (CTH 413.2)** (CTH 413.2 §1:1-§12:30)
- Compare Q 16:91-92 (do not break oaths after confirming them) and Q 5:89 (expiation of oaths).
- Compare 2 Kgs 13:15-19 (Elisha has the king shoot the arrow of victory).

**Parallel incantation ritual, the ancient gods, offerings to the Hurrian gods one by one, seven tongues in the hearth and seven oaths (CTH 413.3)** (CTH 413.3 §1:1-§35:53)
- The list of gods each given its share diverges from Q 112:1-4 and Q 21:22 (were there gods besides God, heaven and earth would be ruined).
- Compare Q 16:91 and Q 3:77 (those who sell God's covenant and their oaths) for the dangers of the oath.

**Another building ritual fragment, plastering and scraping (CTH 413.4)** (CTH 413.4 §1:1-§2:6)
- Compare Lev 14:41-45 (the house with disease scraped and replastered).

**Palace-building ritual opens - plaster long years inside, awe outside (CTH 414.1 §1-2)** (CTH 414.1 §1:1-§2:10)
- Building as a sacred act sanctioned by God: compare Q 2:127 (Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations, praying 'accept it from us') and Q 9:108-109 (a building founded on piety versus one on a crumbling bank); HB Ps 127:1 ('unless YHWH builds the house').

**The king, the throne-goddess and the mountain's trees (CTH 414.1 §3-14)** (CTH 414.1 §3:11-§14:65)
- Kingship and land handed over by the gods: compare Q 3:26 ('You give kingship to whom You will') and Q 2:247 (God gives Saul kingship); HB 1 Kgs 3:7.
- Timber cut from the mountain for the royal house: compare 1 Kgs 5:6-10 (cedars of Lebanon for Solomon's temple and palace) and Q 34:12-13 (the jinn build for Solomon).
- The throne as speaking companion of the king: contrast Q 27:38-42 (the queen's throne brought to Solomon) and Q 38:34 (a body cast on Solomon's throne).

**The eagle sees the fate goddesses spinning the king's years; the king renewed (CTH 414.1 §15-33)** (CTH 414.1 §15:66-§33:155)
- Goddesses spinning the length of a life: compare the Greek Moirai; in the Quran the term (ajal) of each life is fixed by God alone and written: Q 35:11 ('no one is given long life or has his life shortened but it is in a Book'), Q 7:34, Q 3:145.
- Old age removed, youth restored: contrast Q 36:68 ('whom We give long life We reverse in creation') and Q 16:70, 22:5 (returned to the most decrepit age); HB Ps 103:5 ('your youth renewed like the eagle').
- Mountains told to stay in place: compare the Quranic mountains as pegs that keep the earth from shaking, Q 16:15, 21:31, 78:7.
- Gods assembled on the mountain rejoicing in the king: contrast the Quranic denial of a divine council, Q 21:22, 23:91.

**Provisions for the building stages; the new hearth and the tree analogies; colophon (CTH 414.1 §34-55)** (CTH 414.1 §34:156-§55:224)
- The vine with roots below and fruit above, the evergreen tree: compare the good word as a good tree, its root firm and branches in heaven, Q 14:24-25, and Ps 1:3, 92:13-15 (the righteous flourish like a palm, still green in old age); contrast Amos 2:9 (fruit above and roots below destroyed).
- Offering at the laying of foundations: compare Ezra 3:10-11 and 1 Kgs 16:34 (Hiel's sons at Jericho's foundation).

**Palace-building ritual, second manuscript - thigh and vine analogies, effigies, a man's new house (CTH 414.2)** (CTH 414.2 §1:1-§8:19)
- The rite applied to any man building a house: compare Deut 20:5 (who has built a new house and not dedicated it).

**Temple-building ritual - offering in the pit; the place told to admit no other god (CTH 415 §1-13)** (CTH 415 §1:1-§13:79)
- Let no other god enter the sacred place: compare Q 72:18 ('the places of prostration belong to God, so call on no one with God') and Q 2:114; HB Exod 20:3.
- The ground of the sanctuary as a being that eats and drinks: contrast Q 22:37 ('neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God, but your piety').

**Temple-building ritual - the foundation deposit with bronze statues and winged bull for Ea (CTH 415 §14-39)** (CTH 415 §14:80-§39:165)
- Foundation deposits and the winged bull: compare the cherubim and the bronze bulls of Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 7:25, 29) and the precious stones of the foundations (Isa 54:11-12; Rev 21:19).
- Statues in a sanctuary's foundations: contrast the Quranic smashing of idols, Q 21:57-58, and the Kaaba founded by Abraham on monotheism, Q 22:26.

**Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple I - iron tongues, slanders taken, the Ḫantašepa deities (CTH 416 §1-19)** (CTH 416 §1:1-§19:87)
- The 'tongues' of the populace taken from the king: compare the Quranic refuge from the evil of whisperers and envy (Q 113:5, 114:4-6) and the slanderer in Q 68:10-11, 104:1.
- Spitting to remove evil: the Prophet's spitting thrice to the left after a bad dream (hadith, cf. Q 113:4 'blowers on knots'); contrast Q 113 as the Quranic ritual of refuge.

**Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple II - the eagle waved over them and released to the sky (CTH 416 §20-32)** (CTH 416 §20:88-§32:172)
- A bird set free to carry evil or a message: compare Lev 14:4-7, 53 (the living bird released over the field for the leper) and the dove of Gen 8; in the Quran Abraham's four birds (Q 2:260) and Solomon's hoopoe as messenger (Q 27:20-28).
- Eternal as heaven and earth: compare Q 11:107-108 ('as long as the heavens and earth endure') and Ps 89:29-37 (David's throne as the days of heaven).

**Old Hittite rituals for the royal couple III-IV - the goat driven off, coloured threads, startled by birds (CTH 416 §33-51)** (CTH 416 §33:173-§39:211, CTH 416 §40:212, CTH 416 §39:213-§51:285)
- The goat driven away bearing evil: compare Lev 16:10, 20-22 (the goat for Azazel). The Quran has no scapegoat: each soul bears its own burden (Q 6:164, 17:15, 35:18), a direct divergence.
- Coloured threads tied to the fingers: compare the scarlet thread on Zerah's hand (Gen 38:28-30) and the crimson wool of purification (Lev 14:4, Num 19:6); contrast Q 113:4 (the women who blow on knots).

**Ritual against the king's enemies - figurines of cedar and clay bearing names (CTH 417.1)** (CTH 417.1 §1:1-§3:13)
- Writing a name on a figurine to harm its bearer: contrast Q 113:4 and Q 2:102 (sorcery learned from Harut and Marut harms only by God's leave).

**Ritual against the king's enemies - oath-breakers addressed, rites in the enemy's field (CTH 417.3)** (CTH 417.3 §1:1-§5:24)
- Oath-breakers and the field of the enemy: compare Q 16:91-92 (do not break oaths after confirming them, like the woman who unravels her yarn) and Q 2:27.

**Ritual when a foreigner offends against the royal couple I - substitutes, burnt animals, washing, hawthorn gates, pit offerings (CTH 418 §1-13)** (CTH 418 §1:1-§13:53)
- Burning animals and burying the remnant at an untouched place: compare Lev 4:12, 16:27 (the sin-offering burnt outside the camp in a clean place) and Lev 14:40-45; the red heifer (Num 19:2-9).
- An offering to the netherworld goddess to compensate her for the life released: contrast the Quranic denial that any soul can be ransomed (Q 2:48, 2:123, 3:91).

**Ritual when a foreigner offends against the royal couple II - hearths nailed, arrows turned down, the foreigner thrown on his face (CTH 418 §9'-29)** (CTH 418 §9':36-§29:92)
- The foreigner who plots against the king thrown on his face: compare Q 67:22 ('is one who walks prone on his face better guided?'), Q 17:97 and 25:34 (the wicked gathered on their faces); HB Ps 35:4-8.
- Arrows turned downward as a curse: contrast 2 Kgs 13:15-19 (Elisha's arrow of victory and the striking of arrows on the ground).

**Ritual of Zarpiya of Kizzuwatna I - in a plague year, an oath sworn with Šanta and the armed Innarawanteš (CTH 757 §1-15)** (CTH 757 §1:1-§15:95)
- Pestilence through armed divine agents: compare the destroying angel with drawn sword at the plague (2 Sam 24:15-17; 1 Chr 21:16) and the destroyer at the door (Exod 12:23); the Quran's plague (rijz) sent on the Israelites (Q 2:59, 7:134-135).
- A covenant with demons sealed by eating together: contrast Q 6:128 and 72:6 (men seeking refuge with jinn, who only increased them in burden) and Q 34:41.
- Boys who have not known a woman serving in a rite: compare 1 Sam 21:5-6 (holy bread only if the young men kept from women).

**Ritual of Zarpiya II - Luwian incantation at the gate, the door anointed; colophon (CTH 757 §16-24)** (CTH 757 §16:96-§24:120)
- Door anointed so evil stays out: compare the blood on doorposts at Passover (Exod 12:7, 22-23) and the mezuzah (Deut 6:9); in the Quran protection is sought from God alone against 'the evil of what He created' (Q 113:1-2).
- 'Eat sheep and cattle, not a human being': compare the substitution of the ram for Abraham's son (Gen 22:13; Q 37:107 'We ransomed him with a great sacrifice').

**Arad ostraca - orders to Eliashib to issue wine, flour and bread to the Kittim (Arad 1-4, 17)** (Arad ostraca W1:1-W7:2)
- The Kittim in the service of Judah: compare Num 24:24 (ships from Kittim in Balaam's last oracle), Jer 2:10, Dan 11:30.
- Measured rations and the storehouse official: compare Joseph's storehouses, Q 12:47-49, 12:55 ('set me over the storehouses of the land').

**Arad ostracon 18 - 'YHWH ask after your welfare'; the man in the house of YHWH** (Arad ostraca W8:1-W9:1)
- Greeting in God's name: compare the Quranic salam greeting from God, Q 6:54 ('Peace be upon you; your Lord has prescribed mercy on Himself'), 10:10, 33:44.
- Compare 1 Sam 25:6 and the 'house of YHWH' in 1 Kgs 6-8.

**Arad ostracon 24 - men sent to Ramat-Negev 'lest Edom come there'** (Arad ostraca W10:1-9)
- Edom's hostility at Judah's fall: compare Obad 10-14, Ps 137:7, Ezek 25:12 and existing motif mount-seir-eternal-enmity (Ezek 35:5).

**Elephantine Passover letter - Hananiah to Yedaniah and the Jewish garrison, by order of Darius** (Elephantine (selection) W1:1-10)
- Persian sanction for Jewish law: compare Ezra 7:12-26 (Artaxerxes' letter) and Ezra 6:19-22 (Passover after the temple's rebuilding).
- Feasts and the prohibition of work: compare Q 2:183-185 (the fixed fast of Ramadan) and 62:9-10 (leave trade at the call to Friday prayer); the Sabbath of the Jews, Q 2:65, 16:124.

**Petition to Bagohi (excerpt) - the temple of YHW at Elephantine, spared by Cambyses** (Elephantine (selection) W2:1-4)
- A temple of the God of Israel abroad: contrast Deut 12:5-14 (one chosen place); compare Isa 19:19 (an altar to YHWH in the midst of Egypt).
- The conqueror who spares the house of God: compare Cyrus in Ezra 1:1-4, and the Quranic sanctity of places of worship, Q 22:40 ('monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques in which God's name is much remembered').

**Marriage document of Ananiah, servitor of YHH, and Tamet the handmaid of Meshullam** (Elephantine (selection) W3:1-W4:2)
- Divorce initiated by the wife who returns what she received: compare khulʿ, Q 2:229 ('no blame on them for what she gives up to free herself'), and 4:20-21 (do not take back what you gave); HB Deut 24:1-4 (only the husband writes the bill).
- Marrying a slave woman: Q 4:25 (marry believing slave girls with their people's leave and give them their dowries), and the formula 'from this day forever' against Mal 2:16.
- The written, witnessed contract: compare Q 2:282 (write the debt, call two witnesses).

**Ahiram sarcophagus - the son's coffin for his father and the curse on whoever uncovers it (KAI 1)** (KAI 1 main:1-11)
- Curse that the sceptre depart: compare Gen 49:10 ('the sceptre shall not depart from Judah'), Hag 2:22 ('I will overturn the throne of kingdoms'), Ezek 19:14.
- The grave as eternal home: compare Eccl 12:5 (bet ʿolam) and Q 102:1-2 (until you visit the graves).

**Yehimilk of Byblos - the temple restored; may the gods prolong the days of a just and upright king (KAI 4)** (KAI 4 W1:1-7, KAI 4 W2:1-7)
- 'Assembly of the holy ones': compare Ps 89:6-8 (qehal qedoshim), Ps 82:1; the Quran's 'exalted assembly' (al-malaʾ al-aʿla), Q 37:8, 38:69.
- Righteous and upright king: compare Deut 32:4 (God ṣaddiq we-yashar) and Q 38:26 (David as khalifa told to judge with truth).

**Shipitbaal of Byblos - the wall built; may the Lady prolong his days (KAI 7)** (KAI 7 main:1-5)
- Long days as reward: compare Exod 20:12, Deut 5:16 ('that your days may be long'), Prov 3:2; contrast Q 2:96 (the one who wishes to live a thousand years).

**Yehawmilk stele - the Lady of Byblos made him king and heard his voice; altar, gold door, curse (KAI 10)** (KAI 10 main:1-16)
- 'I called and she heard my voice': compare Q 2:186 ('I answer the call of the caller when he calls Me'), Q 40:60, 27:62; HB Ps 18:7, Jonah 2:3.
- Favour in the eyes of God and people: compare Prov 3:4, 1 Sam 2:26; Q 20:39 ('I cast upon you love from Me', Moses).
- Make him stink before the gods: compare Gen 34:30, Exod 5:21 (hivʾish reiḥenu).

**Tabnit sarcophagus - priest of Astarte and king; no silver, no gold; do not open me (KAI 13)** (KAI 13 main:1-11)
- 'An abomination of the deity': compare the Hebrew formula tôʿēbat YHWH (Deut 7:25, 18:12, Prov 11:1).
- 'Under the sun': compare Eccl 1:3, 9 and passim; 'no rest with the Rephaim': Isa 14:9-10, 26:14, Prov 21:16.
- No treasure in the grave, only the man: compare Q 6:94 ('you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, leaving behind what We bestowed on you'), Q 19:80, Job 1:21.

**Eshmunazar II - carried off before his time, the orphan son of a widow; curses on the tomb-opener (KAI 14 Lid 1-13)** (KAI 14 Lid:1-13)
- Root below and fruit above: Amos 2:9, Isa 37:31, Job 18:16 ('his roots dry up below and his branch withers above'); compare Q 14:26 (the bad tree uprooted, having no stability).
- Snatched away before his time: compare Ps 102:24-25 ('take me not away in the midst of my days'), Isa 38:10; in the Quran no soul dies before its appointed term, Q 3:145, 63:11.
- The orphan and the widow's son: Q 93:6 ('did He not find you an orphan and shelter you?').

**Eshmunazar II - temples built with his mother the priestess; Dor and Joppa granted by the lord of kings (KAI 14 Lid 13-22)** (KAI 14 Lid:13-22)
- God's Name as a divine presence: compare Deut 12:5, 11 (the place where YHWH sets his name) and Exod 23:21 ('my name is in him').
- Dagon of the coastal plain: compare 1 Sam 5:1-5, Judg 16:23; Sharon in Isa 35:2.

**Kilamuwa of Samʾal - kings before achieved nothing; hired Assyria; father and mother to his people; curse (KAI 24)** (KAI 24 main:1-16)
- The king as father and mother of the poor: compare Job 29:12-16 ('I was a father to the needy') and Isa 9:5; in the Quran the Prophet is 'closer to the believers than themselves, his wives their mothers', Q 33:6.
- Hiring the king of Assyria against a neighbour: compare Ahaz's appeal to Tiglath-pileser, 2 Kgs 16:7-9, and Isa 7:20 (the razor hired beyond the River).
- A girl for a sheep, a man for a garment: compare Joel 4:3 ('they gave a boy for a harlot and sold a girl for wine') and Amos 2:6 ('the poor for a pair of sandals').

**Arslan Tash amulet 1 - incantation against the Fliers and Stranglers; eternal covenant; the doorpost (KAI 27 AT1)** (KAI 27 W1:1-29)
- Refuge from night-time evils: Q 113:3 ('from the evil of darkness when it gathers') and Q 114 (the whisperer who withdraws); Ps 91:5-6 (terror of the night, pestilence stalking in darkness).
- Words on the doorpost: Deut 6:9, 11:20 (mezuzah); compare Exod 12:23 (the destroyer not allowed to enter).
- Hauron's wife and her seven rivals: compare the Quranic denial that God has a consort, Q 72:3, 6:101.

**Arslan Tash amulet 2 - against the Splatterers: Baal's chariot, 'Flee, Eye!' (KAI 27 AT2)** (KAI 27 W2:1-13)
- The evil eye: compare Q 68:51 ('those who disbelieve would almost strike you down with their eyes') and 113:5 ('the envier when he envies').

**Mesha Stele - Mesha son of Chemosh-[yat], the high place for Chemosh who saved him (KAI 181 lines 1-4)** (KAI 181 main:1-4)
- Mesha of Moab: 2 Kgs 3:4-27 (Mesha the sheep-breeder rebels after Ahab's death).
- 'He let me look upon my enemies': Ps 54:9, 118:7, 59:11.
- High places for Chemosh: 1 Kgs 11:7 (Solomon builds one); the Quranic polemic against gods of the nations, Q 7:138-140 (Israel asks Moses for a god like theirs).

**Mesha Stele - Omri oppressed Moab because Chemosh was angry with his land; Israel perished forever (KAI 181 lines 4-9)** (KAI 181 main:4-9)
- God angry with his own people and handing them to oppressors: the Deuteronomistic pattern of Judg 2:14, 3:8, 2 Kgs 13:3; in the Quran God sends against Israel 'servants of Ours of great might' because of their corruption, Q 17:4-7, and Q 7:167.
- Omri and Ahab: 1 Kgs 16:23-28, 2 Kgs 1:1, 3:4-5 (Moab rebelled after Ahab's death).
- The enemy's boast and his perishing: compare Pharaoh's 'I am your lord most high' and his drowning, Q 79:24-25, 28:38-40.

**Mesha Stele - Ataroth taken, the ariel of Dawdoh; Nebo devoted to Ashtar-Chemosh, the vessels of YHWH dragged before Chemosh; Jahaz (KAI 181 lines 9-21)** (KAI 181 main:9-21)
- Ḥērem, the ban: compare Josh 6:17-21 (Jericho devoted to YHWH), 1 Sam 15:3, Deut 7:2, 20:16-17; and Num 21:2-3. The Quran has no ḥērem; it limits fighting to those who fight (Q 2:190-193) and forbids transgression; compare also Q 59:2-5 (expulsion of the Banu Nadir).
- 'Go, take Nebo': compare Judg 4:6-7, 1 Sam 23:2-4 (divine command to attack); Q 5:21-24 (Moses: 'enter the holy land God has written for you').
- The vessels of YHWH dragged before a foreign god: the ark brought to Dagon's house, 1 Sam 5:1-2; Nebuchadnezzar's removal of the temple vessels, 2 Kgs 25:13-15, Dan 5:2-4; Q 2:248 (the ark returned by angels).
- Gad in Ataroth: Num 32:3, 34 (the Gadites built Ataroth).

**Mesha Stele - Qarḥoh built with Israelite prisoners, a cistern in every house, the highway by the Arnon; Chemosh sends him against Horonen (KAI 181 lines 21-34)** (KAI 181 main:21-34)
- Mesha as sheep-breeder (nōqēd) paying Israel 100,000 lambs: 2 Kgs 3:4; Amos 1:1 (Amos among the nōqedim).
- Each man his own cistern: 2 Kgs 18:31, Isa 36:16 (the Assyrian promise), Prov 5:15.
- Horonaim of Moab: Isa 15:5, Jer 48:3-5, 34; Chemosh's judgment in Jer 48:7, 13, 46.

**Gezer calendar - the months of the agricultural year** (KAI 182 main:1-8)
- The year as sowing and harvest: Gen 8:22 ('seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter'), Exod 23:16 (the feasts of harvest and ingathering, ʾāsîp); Q 6:141 (give its due on the day of harvest), 9:36 (the twelve months with God).

**Siloam tunnel inscription - the cutters meet axe to axe; the water flows 1200 cubits** (KAI 189 main:1-6)
- Hezekiah's tunnel: 2 Kgs 20:20 ('he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city'), 2 Chr 32:3-4, 30; Isa 22:9-11; Sir 48:17.
- Water brought through rock: compare Moses striking the rock, Q 2:60, 7:160; and Solomon's flowing spring of molten brass, Q 34:12.

**Lachish ostracon 1 - list of names (Gemariah son of Hissiliah, Mattaniah son of Neriah, Mibtahiah son of Jeremiah)** (KAI 192-199 W1:1-5)
- Compare Jer 36:10-12 (Gemariah son of Shaphan), Jer 32:12 and 36:4 (Baruch son of Neriah), Jer 35:3 (Jaazaniah).

**Lachish ostracon 2 - 'May YHWH let my lord hear news of peace'; 'who is your servant but a dog'** (KAI 192-199 W2:1-6)
- The servant as dog: 2 Sam 9:8 (Mephibosheth: 'what is your servant, that you should look on a dead dog like me?'), 2 Kgs 8:13 (Hazael), 1 Sam 24:15.

**Lachish ostracon 3 - 'As YHWH lives, no one has ever read me a letter'; the commander goes down to Egypt; the prophet's letter 'Beware!'** (KAI 192-199 W3:1-W4:5)
- Elnathan and the embassy to Egypt: Jer 26:20-23 (Elnathan son of Achbor sent to Egypt to bring back the prophet Uriah); Judah's reliance on Egypt, Jer 37:5-7, Ezek 17:15.
- The unnamed prophet of Judah's last days: Jeremiah or Uriah (Jer 26:20); in the Quran the Prophet himself is 'the unlettered prophet', Q 7:157-158, a reversal of the officer's pride in reading.

**Lachish ostracon 4 - watching for the signals of Lachish; Azekah can no longer be seen** (KAI 192-199 W5:1-W6:5)
- Lachish and Azekah the last fortified cities: Jer 34:7 ('for these were left of the cities of Judah, fortified cities'); maśʾēt as fire-signal: Jer 6:1 ('raise a signal on Beth-haccherem'), Judg 20:38.

**Lachish ostraca 5-6 - letters returned; the words of the officials 'weaken the hands of the land'** (KAI 192-199 W7:1-W8:14)
- Jer 38:4: the officials say of Jeremiah 'he weakens the hands of the soldiers left in this city and the hands of all the people'. The Lachish letter turns the charge against the officials themselves (or a prophet, depending on the reading).
- Discouraging the fighters: compare the hypocrites who say 'do not go out in the heat', Q 9:81, and 33:18 (those who hinder others).

**Lachish ostraca 8-22 - greetings, 'the prophet', rations, the day of the ninth, names and Beth-Achzib** (KAI 192-199 W9:1-W23:10)
- Achzib: Mic 1:14 ('the houses of Achzib shall be a deceitful brook').

**Yavne-Yam ostracon - the reaper's petition for his seized garment** (KAI 200 main:1-14)
- The poor man's garment: Exod 22:25-26 and Deut 24:12-15 (return the pledge by sunset; pay the hired labourer's wage the same day), Amos 2:8.
- Justice for the labourer: compare Q 83:1-3 (woe to those who give short measure), Q 4:135 (stand firm for justice even against yourselves), and the hadith 'give the worker his wage before his sweat dries'.

**Zakkur stele face A - besieged by Bar-Hadad and sixteen kings, Zakkur lifts his hands and Baalshamayn answers through seers 'Do not fear' (KAI 202 A)** (KAI 202 W1:1-17)
- Ben-Hadad son of Hazael: 2 Kgs 13:3, 24-25. The siege of Samaria by Ben-Hadad and thirty-two kings, 1 Kgs 20:1.
- 'Do not fear, I am with you': Isa 41:10, 43:1-5; 2 Chr 20:15-17 (Jehoshaphat's prayer answered through a Levite: 'the battle is not yours'). In the Quran: God tells Moses and Aaron 'Do not fear, I am with you both, hearing and seeing', Q 20:46; and Q 9:40 ('do not grieve, God is with us').
- Answered through prophets: compare 2 Kgs 19:20 (Isaiah sends Hezekiah God's answer during the siege) and Q 8:9 ('when you sought help from your Lord and He answered you: I will reinforce you').

**Hadad statue of Panamuwa I - the gods gave him the sceptre; let the heir sacrifice and say 'may Panamuwa's soul eat and drink with Hadad'; curses on kin-murder (KAI 214)** (KAI 214 main:1-34)
- The dead king's soul (nbš) feasting with the god: contrast the Quranic martyrs 'alive with their Lord, provided for', Q 3:169-170, and the believers' souls; HB 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's pillar 'to keep my name in remembrance').
- Hadad who withholds sleep at night: compare Esth 6:1 and Dan 6:19.
- Kin-killing for the throne: Judg 9:5 (Abimelech kills his seventy brothers), 2 Kgs 11:1 (Athaliah), 2 Chr 21:4; the Quranic first fratricide, Q 5:27-32.

**Panamuwa II memorial by Bar-Rakib - usurper's massacre, flight to Tiglath-pileser, death at Damascus, the Assyrian king weeps (KAI 215)** (KAI 215 main:1-23)
- Seventy kinsmen killed: Judg 9:5 (Abimelech), 2 Kgs 10:1-7 (Jehu and the seventy sons of Ahab).
- Tiglath-pileser III: 2 Kgs 15:29, 16:7-10 (Ahaz meets him at Damascus).
- Seizing the hem: 1 Sam 15:27, 24:5, Zech 8:23; the vassal as servant at the overlord's chariot wheel.
- 'Before God and men': Prov 3:4, 1 Sam 2:26.

**Sefire I face A - the treaty of Bar-Gaʾyah of KTK with Matiʿel of Arpad and the gods as witnesses (KAI 222 A 1-13)** (KAI 222 W1:1-13)
- El and Elyon: Gen 14:18-22 (ʾēl ʿelyôn), Ps 78:35; heaven and earth as witnesses: Deut 4:26, 30:19, 32:1, Isa 1:2.
- God as witness of covenants in the Quran: Q 3:81 ('bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses'), 16:91 ('you have made God your surety'), 7:172 (the covenant of Alast).

**Sefire I face A - futility curses, seven years of locust, Arpad a tell, simile curses of wax, bow, calf (KAI 222 A 14-41)** (KAI 222 W1:14-41)
- Breaking the covenant and its curses: Q 2:27 and 13:25 ('those who break God's covenant after its confirmation and cut what God ordered to be joined and spread corruption on earth: for them is the curse (laʿna) and the evil abode'); Q 5:13 (for breaking their covenant We cursed them and hardened their hearts).
- Eating and not being satisfied: Lev 26:26, Hos 4:10, Mic 6:14, Hag 1:6; seven years of locust: Joel 1:4, Deut 28:38-42; the plague of locusts on Pharaoh's people, Q 7:133.
- A city made a tell, haunt of beasts, sown with salt: Josh 8:28, Judg 9:45, Deut 29:22, Isa 13:20-22, 34:11-15, Zeph 2:9; Q 22:45 ('how many a town We destroyed ... a deserted well and a lofty palace').
- The calf cut in two: Jer 34:18-20 (those who passed between the parts of the calf), Gen 15:9-17.
- No sound of the lyre: Ezek 26:13, Isa 24:8, Jer 25:10.

**Sefire I face B - the treaty of the gods, its extent; stipulations on loyalty, avenging the overlord's son, fugitives and bread (KAI 222 B)** (KAI 222 W2:1-46)
- A treaty set by the gods themselves: compare Q 2:40 ('fulfil My covenant and I will fulfil yours'), 2:27, 13:20 ('those who fulfil God's covenant and do not break the pact').
- Let not one word fall: compare Josh 21:45, 23:14, 1 Sam 3:19 (none of his words fell to the ground).

**Sefire I face C - 'thus we have written for remembrance'; whoever effaces the words, the gods overturn him and his house (KAI 222 C)** (KAI 222 W3:1-24)
- Overturning like Sodom: Gen 19:25 (hāpak), Jer 20:16; in the Quran the overturned cities (al-muʾtafikat), Q 9:70, 53:53, 69:9, and 'We turned it upside down' (jaʿalna ʿaliyaha safilaha), Q 11:82, 15:74 - the same 'lowest made highest' image.
- Those who change the words after hearing them: Q 2:181 ('whoever alters it after hearing it, the sin is on those who alter it'), 2:75, 4:46.

**Sefire II - the futility curses repeated; the kingdom a heap; the mouth of the lion and panther (KAI 223)** (KAI 223 1-16)
- Name forgotten, grave destroyed: Ps 9:6-7, Prov 10:7; Q 19:98 ('do you perceive any of them or hear from them a whisper?').

**Pyrgi tablet (Phoenician) - Thefarie Velianas builds a holy place for Astarte at her request; years like the stars (KAI 277)** (KAI 277 1-5)
- The burial of the god: compare Ezek 8:14 (women weeping for Tammuz) and the Quranic denial that God dies, Q 25:58 ('the Living who does not die').
- Years like the stars: Gen 15:5, 22:17 (descendants as the stars).

**Tel Dan stele - Hadad made me king and went before me; the king of Israel and the king of the House of David slain (KAI 310)** (KAI 310 1-13)
- Hazael and the deaths of Joram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah: 2 Kgs 8:28-29, 9:14-28 (in the Bible Jehu kills them); 2 Kgs 10:32-33 (Hazael cuts off Israel's territory); 1 Kgs 19:15-17 (Elijah to anoint Hazael and Jehu).
- The House of David: 2 Sam 7:11-16, Isa 7:2, 13; in the Quran David is a king and prophet given wisdom and the Psalms, Q 2:251, 38:20, 4:163.
- The god who goes before the king: Deut 1:30, 31:8, Judg 4:14 ('has not YHWH gone out before you?'); contrast Q 8:17 ('you did not kill them, but God killed them').
- Seventy kings: Judg 1:7 (Adoni-bezek and the seventy kings).

**Deir ʿAlla plaster - the book of Balaam son of Beor, seer of the gods: night vision, fasting and weeping, the council of the Shaddayin decrees darkness, the world reversed (KAI 312)** (KAI 312 1-17)
- Balaam son of Beor: Num 22-24 (the seer who sees visions of Shaddai, Num 24:4, 16; God comes to him at night, Num 22:8-20), Num 31:8, 16, Deut 23:5-6, Josh 13:22, Mic 6:5; Bela son of Beor in Gen 36:32.
- Quran first: Q 7:175-176 ('recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped away from them ... his likeness is that of a dog: if you attack it, it pants'), traditionally identified with Balaam (Balʿam ibn Baʿura) in the tafsir.
- The heavens closed, darkness and no light: Amos 5:18-20, Joel 2:2, 10, Zeph 1:15; Q 81:1-2 (the sun wrapped up, the stars darkened), 77:8-9.
- The divine council deciding doom: 1 Kgs 22:19-22, Ps 82:1; contrast the Quranic one God who needs no council, Q 21:22-23.

**Ketef Hinnom amulet I - the great God who keeps covenant and kindness; blessing from every snare and evil; the priestly blessing** (KH 1-2 W1:1-19)
- Deut 7:9 ('the faithful God who keeps covenant and kindness for those who love him and keep his commandments'), Neh 1:5, Dan 9:4; Num 6:24-26 (the priestly blessing).
- Quran first: God's covenant kept with those who keep theirs, Q 2:40; refuge from evil (Q 113-114, the protective suras carried as amulets in later practice); the face of God, Q 2:115, 55:27.

**Ketef Hinnom amulet II - blessed by YHWH the helper and rebuker of evil; 'May YHWH bless you and keep you, make his face shine upon you and grant you peace'** (KH 1-2 W2:1-12)
- Num 6:24-26; Ps 67:2, 4:7 ('lift up the light of your face'); the rebuke of evil: Zech 3:2 ('YHWH rebuke you, Satan'), Mal 3:11.
- Quran first: 'peace' as God's own name and greeting, Q 59:23 (al-Salam), 36:58 ('Peace: a word from a merciful Lord'); refuge from evil, Q 113:1-2; the turning of God's face, Q 6:52, 18:28 (seeking His face).

**Khirbet el-Qom tomb inscriptions - Uriyahu blessed by YHWH, saved from his enemies by his asherah; tomb owners named** (Khirbet el-Qom 3 W1:1-4, Khirbet el-Qom 3 W2:1-3, Khirbet el-Qom 3 W3:1)
- Quran first: Q 6:100 ('they make the jinn partners of God ... and impute to Him sons and daughters'), Q 4:117 ('they call besides Him only on females'), Q 72:3 ('our Lord has taken neither consort nor son'), Q 53:19-23 (al-Lat, al-ʿUzza, Manat).
- HB: the Asherah condemned beside YHWH's altar, Deut 16:21; 2 Kgs 21:7, 23:4-7 (the Asherah in the temple burned by Josiah); Jer 7:18, 44:17-19 (the Queen of Heaven).

**Kuntillet ʿAjrud pithos A - 'I bless you by YHWH of Samaria and by his asherah' (Meshel 3.1)** (Kuntillet Ajrud W1:1-2, Kuntillet Ajrud W2:1-2, Kuntillet Ajrud W10:1)
- Quran first: Q 6:100 and 4:117 (calling on female deities beside God), 72:3 (no consort), 17:111 ('who has not taken a son and has no partner in sovereignty'), 112:3-4; the calf of Samaria / the Samiri: Q 20:85-97.
- HB: the calf of Samaria (Hos 8:5-6), the Asherah in Samaria (1 Kgs 16:33, 2 Kgs 13:6), Amos 8:14 ('those who swear by the guilt of Samaria').

**Kuntillet ʿAjrud pithos B - 'I bless you by YHWH of Teman and his asherah: may he bless you and keep you and be with my lord' (Meshel 3.6, 3.9)** (Kuntillet Ajrud W3:1-10, Kuntillet Ajrud W4:1-3, Kuntillet Ajrud W5:1-6, Kuntillet Ajrud W11:1-11, Kuntillet Ajrud W12:1-3)
- Quran first: Q 6:100, 4:117 (females called on beside God) and Q 40:60 ('call on Me, I will answer you'); 'what the heart desires', Q 41:31 ('therein you will have whatever your souls desire').
- HB: God from Teman, Hab 3:3 ('God comes from Teman'), Deut 33:2, Judg 5:4; Ps 20:5 ('may he grant you your heart's desire'), Ps 37:4; Num 6:24.

**Kuntillet ʿAjrud plaster inscriptions - may he lengthen days; when El shone forth the mountains melted; blessing Baal on the day of war (Meshel 4.1.1, 4.2)** (Kuntillet Ajrud W6:1-2, Kuntillet Ajrud W7:1-6, Kuntillet Ajrud W8:1-6, Kuntillet Ajrud W13:1-2, Kuntillet Ajrud W14:1-6)
- Theophany: mountains melt before God, Judg 5:4-5, Mic 1:3-4, Ps 97:5, Hab 3:3-6 (God from Teman, the eternal mountains shattered); Deut 33:2 (YHWH shone forth from Seir, zāraḥ).
- Quran first: the mountain crumbled when the Lord manifested Himself, Q 7:143 (Moses at the mount: 'when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain He made it crumble to dust'); mountains crushed on the Day, Q 69:14, 20:105-107, 56:5.
- Baal and El in a Yahwistic shrine: compare Elijah's contest, 1 Kgs 18; Q 37:123-126 (Elias: 'do you call on Baal and abandon the best of creators?').

**Kuntillet ʿAjrud fragments - pithos C names; the poor and oppressed, blood, famine and sword (Meshel 4.3)** (Kuntillet Ajrud W9:1-4, Kuntillet Ajrud W15:1-7)
- Pestilence, famine and sword: Jer 14:12, 21:7, Ezek 5:12; the poor and needy, Ps 72:12-13, Amos 8:4-6; the sea dried up, Isa 51:10, Ps 106:9, Q 20:77 ('strike for them a dry path in the sea').

**Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest** (Gen 1:1-2:3)
- Enuma Elish: Tiamat (cf. tehom), division of the waters with a heaven-half; Quran 21:30 heavens and earth were joined and split.
- Quran 50:38 'no weariness touched Us' answers divine rest; Quran 7:54 six days; 2:30 khalifa.
- Egyptian Memphite theology: creation by Ptah's word. Rabbinic: Gen R. 8 on 'let us make' as consulting angels.

**Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman** (Gen 2:4-25)
- Atrahasis/Enki: humans from clay mixed with a god's blood; Quran 15:26-29 clay and spirit breathed in; Quran 2:31 Adam taught the names.
- Sumerian Dilmun / Enki and Ninhursag: the 'lady of the rib' (Nin-ti) pun; Quran 4:1 created from a single soul and its mate.

**The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion** (Gen 3:1-24)
- Gilgamesh XI: the serpent steals the plant of rejuvenation; Adapa refuses the food of life.
- Quran 7:19-25 and 20:120-121: Iblis whispers, 'tree of immortality', both eat, leaves of the garden as covering; no blame on the woman alone.
- Pandora (Hesiod) as first woman bringing evils; Christian proto-evangelium reading of 3:15.

**Cain and Abel** (Gen 4:1-16)
- Quran 5:27-31: the two sons of Adam, the accepted offering, a raven teaches burial; Sumerian Dumuzi and Enkimdu (shepherd vs farmer).
- Targum/Midrash supply the field dispute; Hebrews 11:4 and 1 John 3:12; Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5.

**Cain's line, the first city, culture heroes and the Song of Lamech** (Gen 4:17-24)
- Mesopotamian apkallu sages bring the arts; Phoenician history of Philo of Byblos lists inventor-generations; 1 Enoch 8 Azazel teaches metalwork.
- Matthew 18:22 seventy-seven times forgiveness answers Lamech.

**Birth of Seth and Enosh; calling on the name of the LORD** (Gen 4:25-26)
- Gnostic Sethians; Life of Adam and Eve on Seth; Gen Rabbah 23:7 on Enosh's generation and idolatry.

**The book of the generations of Adam, Adam to Noah** (Gen 5:1-32)
- Sumerian King List: ten (or eight) antediluvian kings with reigns of tens of thousands of years; seventh king Enmeduranki taken to the gods, cf. Enoch.
- 1 Enoch, Jubilees 4, Quran 19:56-57 Idris raised to a high place; Hebrews 11:5.

**Sons of God, daughters of men, and the Nephilim** (Gen 6:1-4)
- 1 Enoch 6-11 Watchers led by Shemihazah; Jubilees 5; Jude 6, 2 Peter 2:4; Greek demigods (Hesiod's race of heroes); Quran 2:102 Harut and Marut.

**The Flood (full read)** (Gen 6:5-8:22)
