- Gilgamesh XI (Utnapishtim): reed-hut warning, cubic boat sealed with bitumen, dove, swallow, raven that does not return, gods gather like flies at the sacrifice; Atrahasis seven-day warning.
- Quran 11:25-49, 23:27 (God's eye), 54:13 planks and nails; 1 Enoch 89; Berossus' Xisuthrus; Deucalion.

**Blessing of Noah, blood laws and the covenant of the bow** (Gen 9:1-17)
- Rabbinic Noahide laws (b. Sanh. 56a); Acts 15:20 abstain from blood; Gilgamesh/Atrahasis: Ishtar's lapis necklace as memorial; Enuma Elish: Marduk's bow set in heaven.

**Noah's vineyard, Ham's sin and the curse of Canaan; Noah's death** (Gen 9:18-29)
- b. Sanh. 70a Ham castrated or sodomized Noah; Hesiod's Kronos castrating Ouranos and Hurrian Kumarbi; Dionysus/Icarius as first wine-maker.
- Quran 29:14 Noah among his people 950 years (here his total life).

**The Table of Nations** (Gen 10:1-32)
- Nimrod as builder of Babel and persecutor of Abraham in midrash (Pirqe R. El. 24) and Islamic qisas; Ninurta or Tukulti-Ninurta as historical models.
- Deut 32:8 nations by number of the sons of God; Jubilees 8-9 division of the earth by lot; 1 Chr 1.

**The Tower of Babel** (Gen 11:1-9)
- Sumerian 'Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta' spell of Nudimmud on the confusion of tongues; Etemenanki ziggurat; Quran 28:38 and 40:36-37 Pharaoh's tower by Haman with baked clay.
- Acts 2 Pentecost reverses Babel; 3 Baruch on the tower builders.

**Generations of Shem to Terah; Terah's family leaves Ur** (Gen 11:10-32)
- Midrash (Gen R. 38:13): Haran dies in Nimrod's furnace after Abram survives; ties to abraham.yaml thrown-into-fire and sibling-dies-in-fire; Quran 21:68-69.
- Josh 24:2 Terah served other gods; Jubilees 12; Apocalypse of Abraham 1-8.

**The call of Abram and his journey through Canaan** (Gen 12:1-9)
- Abram aged 75 leaving Harran; 'the souls they made in Harran' (12:5) read by Gen R. 39:14 as converts; Quran 29:26 and 37:99 'I am going to my Lord'.

**Abram and Sarai in Egypt (first wife-sister episode)** (Gen 12:10-20)
- Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen 19-20) Abram's dream of cedar and palm, Sarai's beauty catalogue, Pharaoh's paralysis; Sahih al-Bukhari hadith on Sarah and the tyrant whose hand withered, gift of Hagar.

**War of the four kings, rescue of Lot, Melchizedek** (Gen 14:1-24)
- Ps 110:4 priest forever after the order of Melchizedek; Hebrews 7 (without father or mother); 11QMelchizedek heavenly figure; 2 Enoch 71-72 miraculous birth of Melchizedek.
- Abram 'the Hebrew' (ha-ivri) only here; Ugaritic El qny 'rs, creator of earth.

**The covenant between the pieces** (Gen 15:1-21)
- Jer 34:18-20 passing between the calf's parts; Hittite and Mari donkey-cutting treaty rites; Paul in Romans 4 and Galatians 3 on 15:6.
- Apocalypse of Abraham 9-15 expands the sacrifice with the bird of prey as Azazel; Quran 2:260 Abraham and the four birds cut and called.

**Hagar and the birth of Ishmael** (Gen 16:1-16)
- Code of Hammurabi 144-147 and Nuzi contracts on slave-wives who claim equality; Galatians 4:21-31 allegory; Islamic tradition of Hagar as wife and mother of the Arabs.

**El Shaddai, new names and the covenant of circumcision** (Gen 17:1-27)
- Islamic khitan, tradition of Abraham's circumcision at 80 with an adze (Bukhari); Herodotus 2.104 on Egyptian circumcision; Jubilees 15; Ishmaelite age of 13 behind Muslim practice in Josephus Ant. 1.214.

**Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac** (Gen 18:1-15)
- Quran 11:69-73 and 51:24-30: guests do not eat (Abraham fears them), roasted calf, the wife laughs and strikes her face; Tob 12:19 angel only appeared to eat; Christian Trinity icon (Rublev).
- Ovid Met. 8 Baucis and Philemon (gods hosted, flood/punishment of inhospitable neighbours); Hyrieus given a son Orion by three gods.

**Abraham bargains for Sodom** (Gen 18:16-33)
- Quran 11:74-76 Abraham pleads for Lot's people; Jer 5:1 one just man; tiqqun soferim at 18:22 (originally 'YHWH still stood before Abraham').

**Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah** (Gen 19:1-29)
- Quran 11:77-83, 15:61-77, 54:33-39: Lot offers 'my daughters', attackers' eyes blotted out, city turned upside down, stones of baked clay, wife left behind; Wisdom 10:7 pillar as memorial.
- Greek Orpheus/Eurydice and Baucis-Philemon don't-look-back; Ezek 16:49 Sodom's sin as neglect of the poor; Bera king of Sodom.

**Lot's daughters and the origin of Moab and Ammon** (Gen 19:30-38)
- Parallels Noah's drunkenness after the flood (9:21); Myrrha and Cinyras (Ovid Met. 10); Ruth the Moabite as David's ancestor; Islam rejects the episode (prophetic impeccability).

**Abraham and Sarah at Gerar (second wife-sister episode)** (Gen 20:1-18)
- Abraham's 'no fear of God in this place' (20:11); hadith of Abraham's three 'lies' (Bukhari, Sarah 'my sister' in Islam); Lev 18:9 later forbids marrying a half-sister.

**Birth of Isaac and expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael** (Gen 21:1-21)
- Islamic tradition (Bukhari, Ahadith al-Anbiya) Hagar runs between Safa and Marwa and Zamzam springs at Mecca; Quran 14:37 'a valley without cultivation'.
- Galatians 4:29 Ishmael 'persecuted' Isaac; Gen R. 53:11 on metsaheq as idolatry, sexual immorality or bloodshed.

**Abraham's treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba** (Gen 21:22-34)
- Gen R. 54:6 eshel as an inn for hospitality (acrostic of eating, drinking, lodging); Philistines here are anachronistic.

**The binding of Isaac (Aqedah)** (Gen 22:1-19)
- Quran 37:99-111: dream of sacrifice, the unnamed son consents, 'great sacrifice' ransom; Islamic debate whether Ishmael or Isaac; Eid al-Adha.
- Iphigenia at Aulis replaced by a deer; Phrixus and the golden ram; 2 Chr 3:1 Moriah = temple mount; Christian Isaac-carrying-wood typology (John 19:17); Pseudo-Philo LAB 32 and Targum Isaac asks to be bound.

**The children of Nahor and the birth of Rebekah** (Gen 22:20-24)
- Uz and Buz: Job's land of Uz (Job 1:1) and Elihu the Buzite (Job 32:2); twelve-tribe pattern as with Ishmael and Jacob.

**Death of Sarah and purchase of the cave of Machpelah** (Gen 23:1-20)
- Hittite land law and Neo-Babylonian dialogue documents; Gen R. 58 Ephron's name defective (Ephrn) for his greed; Haram al-Ibrahimi in Hebron; Acts 7:16 conflates with Shechem purchase.

**Abraham's servant finds Rebekah for Isaac** (Gen 24:1-67)
- Type-scene of betrothal at a well: Jacob-Rachel (Gen 29), Moses-Zipporah (Exod 2), Quran 28:23-28; John 4 Samaritan woman; Odyssey 10 / 6 water-drawing maidens.
- Gen R. 60: the servant is Eliezer; Rebekah aged three in some midrash; Laban greedy for the gold (24:30).

**Keturah's sons, the death of Abraham, and Ishmael's line** (Gen 25:1-18)
- Gen R. 61:4 Keturah = Hagar; gifts to concubines' sons as 'names of impurity' (b. Sanh. 91a, Indian magic); Kedar and Nebaioth as Arab ancestors in Islamic genealogy (Adnan).
- Testament of Abraham: Abraham resists death and is shown the world.

**Birth of Esau and Jacob; the sale of the birthright** (Gen 25:19-34)
- Twin rivalry in the womb: Acrisius and Proetus (Apollodorus 2.2.1); Iranian Ohrmazd/Ahriman twins of Zurvan, Ahriman thrusting out first; Romans 9:10-13; rabbinic Esau = Rome.

**Isaac in Gerar, the wife-sister episode, wells and treaty** (Gen 26:1-33)
- b. Yoma 28b: Abraham observed the whole Torah; Quran 2:135, 3:67 Abraham hanif before Torah; doublet of Gen 20 and 21:22-34.

**Jacob steals Esau's blessing** (Gen 27:1-45)
- Odysseus recognized by Eurycleia by touch (scar) vs. Isaac deceived by touch; Hebrews 12:16-17 Esau found no place for repentance; Gen R. 65 Esau's garments were Adam's/Nimrod's.
- Jacob's smell of Paradise (Gen R. 65:22) links to joseph.yaml father-smells-son and Quran 12:94.

**Jacob's dream at Bethel** (Gen 28:10-22)
- Babylonian ziggurat stairway (simmiltu) and bab-ilu 'gate of god'; John 1:51 angels ascending and descending on the Son of Man; Ladder of Jacob (pseudepigraphon); Mithraic ladder of seven gates.
- Greek baetyl (Bethel) sacred stones anointed with oil; stone of Scone legend as Jacob's pillow; Quran 3:93 Israel's self-imposed food prohibition (sinew) linked elsewhere.

**Jacob meets Rachel; Laban's substitution of Leah** (Gen 29:1-30)
- Quran 28:27 Moses serves eight or ten years for Shu'ayb's daughter; Lev 18:18 forbids marrying two sisters; Gen R. 70 Leah's eyes weak from weeping lest she marry Esau.

**Births of Jacob's children; the mandrakes** (Gen 29:31-30:24)
- Mandragora as aphrodisiac in Greek (Aphrodite Mandragoritis) and Song 7:14; Hurrian Nuzi adoption-by-knee rites; Rachel's death in childbirth follows later (Gen 35).

**Jacob's wages and the speckled flocks** (Gen 30:25-43)
- Ancient maternal-impression belief (Hippocratic, Oppian on Spartan horse-breeders, Jerome Quaest. in Gen.); Hermes the trickster herdsman.

**Jacob's flight from Laban and the theft of the teraphim** (Gen 31:1-42)
- Nuzi tablets: possession of household gods tied to inheritance; Aeneas carrying the Penates out of Troy; Code of Hammurabi 266 shepherd not liable for losses to a lion; Exod 22:12.
- Gen R. 74:5 Rachel stole the teraphim to wean her father from idolatry; Rachel's death (35:16-19) read as fulfillment of Jacob's curse.

**Covenant of Jacob and Laban at Galeed/Mizpah** (Gen 31:43-54)
- Aramaean-Israelite border at Gilead; 'God of Abraham and God of Nahor' with plural verb (31:53) suggests two deities; Kudurru boundary stones.

**Jacob wrestles at the Jabbok and becomes Israel** (Gen 32:23-33)
- Hosea 12:4-5 he strove with the angel and wept; river-demons and night spirits who flee at dawn; Gilgamesh and Enkidu wrestling; Menelaus wrestling Proteus to extract an answer; Judg 13:18 angel withholds his name.
- Gen R. 77-78: Esau's guardian angel (Samael); Prayer of Joseph: Jacob as archangel Israel; Quran 3:93 the food Israel forbade himself.

**Jacob and Esau reconcile; Jacob at Succoth and Shechem** (Gen 33:1-20)
- Josh 24:32 Joseph's bones buried in this plot; John 4:5 Jacob's well at Sychar; Esau reconciliation contrasts with Joseph's brothers (joseph.yaml hero-forgives-brothers).

**Dinah, Shechem and the massacre by Simeon and Levi** (Gen 34:1-31)
- Jubilees 30 and Judith 9:2-4 praise Simeon's zeal; Testament of Levi 5-7 has an angel commission Levi's sword.
- Compare 2 Sam 13 (Amnon and Tamar) and the abduction of maidens in Greek myth (Persephone, Europa).

**Purge of foreign gods, Bethel, Rachel's death in childbirth, Reuben and Bilhah, Isaac's death** (Gen 35:1-29)
- Gen 35:22 reported tersely with a masoretic gap (pisqa); cf. Reuben's punishment Gen 49:4 and Absalom with David's concubines 2 Sam 16:22.
- Rachel weeping for her children, Jer 31:15 / Matt 2:18.

**Generations of Esau, Horite chiefs, kings of Edom** (Gen 36:1-43)
- Rabbinic tradition (b. Pesachim 54a) makes Anah the inventor of mule-breeding; Targum Neofiti reads 'mules'.
- Eliphaz the Temanite reappears as Job's friend (Job 2:11); Uz (36:28) is Job's land.

**Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt** (Gen 37:1-36)
- Quran 12:4-20; Testaments of Zebulun and Gad. Twenty silver later read as typological for Judas's thirty (Matt 26:15).
- The Egyptian Tale of Two Brothers parallels the coming seduction episode.

**Judah and Tamar** (Gen 38:1-30)
- Perez is ancestor of David (Ruth 4:18-22) and appears in Matthew's genealogy (Matt 1:3). Testament of Judah 10-12.
- Middle Assyrian Laws A 33 and Hittite Laws 193 on levirate obligations of the father-in-law.

**Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison** (Gen 39:1-23)
- Egyptian Tale of Two Brothers (Anubis and Bata); Phaedra-Hippolytus and Bellerophon-Stheneboea (Iliad 6.155-170); Quran 12:21-35.

**The cupbearer's and baker's dreams** (Gen 40:1-23)
- Quran 12:36-42 (Joseph preaches to the prisoners first). Herod's birthday feast (Mark 6:21) is the other biblical birthday-feast execution.

**Pharaoh's dreams and Joseph's elevation** (Gen 41:1-57)
- Famine Stela of Sehel (seven-year famine under Djoser, Imhotep advises); Gilgamesh VI seven years of chaff; Joseph and Aseneth expands 41:45.
- 'Whatever he tells you, do' (41:55) echoed by Mary at Cana, John 2:5. Quran 12:43-56.

**The silver cup and Judah's plea** (Gen 44:1-34)
- Quran 12:70-79 (cup/measure in Benjamin's bag; 'the penalty is the one in whose bag it is found'). Cup divination in Mesopotamian oil-omen texts.

**Joseph makes himself known; the wagons sent for Jacob** (Gen 45:1-28)
- Quran 12:89-93 (Joseph's shirt sent to restore Jacob's sight); here it is wagons, not a shirt.

**Vision at Beersheba, the seventy who went down, reunion in Goshen** (Gen 46:1-34)
- Serah bat Asher becomes in midrash the woman who tells Jacob Joseph lives, and who shows Moses Joseph's coffin (Mekhilta Beshallah). Seventy echoes the seventy nations (Gen 10) and Deut 32:8.
- Nunc dimittis (Luke 2:29) echoes 46:30.

**The Testament (Blessing) of Jacob and his death** (Gen 49:1-33)
- Gen 49:10 read messianically in Targum Onqelos, 4Q252, and Christian exegesis; 49:11 echoed in Zech 9:9 and the triumphal entry. Lion of Judah in Rev 5:5.
- Tribal blessings parallel Deut 33; zodiacal readings of the twelve tribes in Philo and Josephus.

**Embalming and burial of Jacob; Joseph's last words and death** (Gen 50:1-26)
- 110 years is the ideal Egyptian lifespan. Midrash: Joseph's coffin sunk in the Nile and raised by Moses (Mekhilta, b. Sotah 13a).

**Israel multiplies; oppression; the Hebrew midwives; decree to drown sons** (Exod 1:1-22)
- Quran 28:4 and 2:49 (Pharaoh slaughtering sons, sparing women). Josephus Ant. 2.205 adds a scribe's prophecy of a deliverer; Sargon, Cyrus, Krishna (Kamsa) and Herod (Matt 2:16) infanticide parallels.
- Rabbinic identification of Shiphrah and Puah with Jochebed and Miriam (b. Sotah 11b).

**Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry** (Exod 2:1-25)
- Sargon of Akkad birth legend (basket of rushes sealed with bitumen, set in the river). Quran 28:7-28 (Moses' mother inspired, the two daughters at the water of Madyan, eight or ten years' service).
- Acts 7:23-29 (Moses aged 40). Compare Jacob at the well (Gen 29) and the Egyptian Tale of Sinuhe (flight from Egypt).

**The burning bush and the divine name** (Exod 3:1-22)
- Quran 20:9-24, 27:7-12, 28:29-35 ('take off your sandals, you are in the sacred valley Tuwa'). Acts 7:30-34; Mark 12:26 (God of the living).
- Philo, Mos. 1.65-75 and LXX 'ego eimi ho on'. Compare Zoroaster's vision and theophany in fire.

**Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood** (Exod 4:1-31)
- Quran 20:17-23, 27:10-12, 28:31-32 (staff becomes a snake, hand comes out white 'without harm'); 20:25-32 (Moses asks for Aaron, 'untie the knot from my tongue').
- Exod 4:24-26 compared with Jacob at the Jabbok (Gen 32) and apotropaic blood rites; Exod Rabbah has the serpent swallowing Moses to the feet.

**First audience with Pharaoh; bricks without straw** (Exod 5:1-23)
- Egyptian brickmaking quotas (Papyrus Anastasi IV/V, Louvre leather roll) and the Rekhmire tomb paintings of foreign brickmakers.

**'I am YHWH': the name not known to the patriarchs; genealogy of Moses and Aaron** (Exod 6:1-30)
- Four cups of the Passover seder (y. Pesahim 10:1) keyed to 6:6-7. Quran 28:34 (Aaron more eloquent).

**Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs** (Exod 7:1-13)
- Quran 7:107-122, 20:65-70, 26:32-48 (Moses' staff swallows the magicians' illusions; the magicians fall prostrate and believe). The magicians are named Jannes and Jambres in CD 5:18-19 and 2 Tim 3:8.
- Westcar Papyrus: magician Webaoner's wax crocodile comes alive; Egyptian snake-charming wands.

**Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice** (Exod 7:14-8:15)
- Admonitions of Ipuwer ('the river is blood'). Quran 7:133 (flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood as 'distinct signs'). Luke 11:20 'finger of God'.

**Plague 7: hail and fire** (Exod 9:13-35)
- Wisdom of Solomon 16:16-22 (fire burning in water, not melting the hail). Rev 8:7, 16:21 (hail and fire).

**Plagues 8-9: locusts and darkness** (Exod 10:1-29)
- Wisdom of Solomon 17-18 elaborates the darkness (phantoms, terror) and the light for Israel. Joel 1-2 locusts.

**Passover law, matzot, the night of the firstborn, departure from Egypt** (Exod 12:1-51)
- John 19:36 applies 12:46 to Jesus; 1 Cor 5:7 'Christ our Passover'. Jubilees 49 (Mastema). Apotropaic doorway blood in Mesopotamian namburbi rites and Arab fidya customs; Mishnah Pesahim.
- Samaritan Pentateuch and LXX at 12:40 add 'and in the land of Canaan'; Gal 3:17 counts 430 years from Abraham.

**Consecration of the firstborn, sign on hand and forehead, Joseph's bones, pillar of cloud and fire** (Exod 13:1-22)
- Mishnah Menahot and the Qumran tefillin; Deut 6:8. Midrash (b. Sotah 13a) on Moses retrieving Joseph's coffin from the Nile with Serah's help.
- Quran 20:77; Isa 4:5 cloud by day and fire by night over Zion.

**The pursuit and the parting of the sea** (Exod 14:1-31)
- Quran 26:61-66 ('strike the sea with your staff' and it parts like a great mountain), 10:90-92 (Pharaoh's last-moment faith and preserved body), 20:77-78.
- Midrash of Nahshon entering the sea first (b. Sotah 37a); Joshua 3 (Jordan), 2 Kings 2:8 (Elijah). Ugaritic Baal vs Yam; Baal-zephon as the storm god's mountain.

**The Song of the Sea and Miriam's song** (Exod 15:1-21)
- Ugaritic Baal cycle (Baal defeats Yam, builds palace on Zaphon, kingship) maps onto 15:8-18. Rev 15:3 'song of Moses'. Mekhilta Shirata; Quran 10:90.
- 'Miriam sister of Aaron' (15:20) is the title behind Quran 19:28 'O sister of Harun' addressed to Maryam.

**Bitter water sweetened at Marah; Elim's twelve springs and seventy palms** (Exod 15:22-27)
- Elisha sweetens water with salt (2 Kgs 2:19-22). Quran 2:60 and 7:160 have twelve springs gushing from the rock struck by the staff, one per tribe.

**Manna and quail; the first Sabbath** (Exod 16:1-36)
- Quran 2:57, 7:160, 20:80 (al-mann wa-l-salwa). John 6:31-58 (bread from heaven); Heb 9:4 (golden jar of manna in the ark); Rev 2:17 (hidden manna). Wisdom 16:20-21 (manna suited to every taste); 2 Baruch 29:8 (manna returns in the messianic age).
- Tamarisk-scale honeydew of Sinai (Arabic mann).

**Battle with Amalek; Moses' raised hands** (Exod 17:8-16)
- Raised hands in prayer at battle: compare Quranic and hadith motifs of prophetic supplication at Badr; Christian typology (Barnabas 12) reads the outstretched arms as the cross.

**Jethro's visit and the appointment of judges** (Exod 18:1-27)
- Quran 28:22-28 (Moses and the Midianite elder, often identified with Shu'ayb/Jethro). Deut 1:9-18 retells the judges without Jethro.

**Arrival at Sinai, covenant offer and theophany** (Exod 19:1-25)
- Quran 7:171 and 2:63 (the mountain raised over Israel); rabbinic 'na'aseh ve-nishma'; Acts 2 Pentecost imagery (fire, sound).

**The Ten Words and the people's fear** (Exod 20:1-21)
- Quran 17:22-39 and 6:151-153 as decalogue-like lists; Egyptian Book of the Dead 125 negative confession.

**Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox** (Exod 21:12-37)
- Laws of Hammurabi 196-201 (talion), 209-214 (pregnant woman), 250-252 (goring ox); Laws of Eshnunna 53-55. Thirty pieces of silver: Zech 11:12, Matt 26:15. Quran 5:45 cites talion as in the Torah.

**Covenant Code - theft, deposits, seduction** (Exod 22:1-16)
- Laws of Eshnunna 12-13 and LH 21 (burglar killed at breach); LH 266 (lion kills animal in fold, shepherd clears himself before god).

**Covenant Code - sorceress, stranger, widow, loans, firstborn** (Exod 22:17-30)
- Quran 2:275-279 on riba; Quran 5:3 forbids flesh killed by a beast (ma akala al-sabu).

**The angel sent ahead and promises of conquest** (Exod 23:20-33)
- Rabbinic and Christian identification of the name-bearing angel with Metatron (b. Sanh 38b) or the Logos.

**Covenant ratified in blood; the elders see God** (Exod 24:1-11)
- Blood of the covenant: Mark 14:24, Heb 9:18-22. Sapphire pavement: Ezek 1:26; rabbinic tradition of the sapphire brick as a memorial of the bondage.

**Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days** (Exod 24:12-18)
- Quran 2:51 and 7:142 (forty nights appointment of Moses); Jesus' forty days, Matt 4:2.

**Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand** (Exod 25:1-40)
- Heavenly pattern: Heb 8:5; Gudea cylinders (temple plan in a dream); Wisdom 9:8. Lampstand as stylized tree: compare tree-of-life imagery; Zech 4; Rev 1:12.

**Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil** (Exod 26:1-37)
- Veil torn at the crucifixion, Matt 27:51; Heb 10:20 veil as flesh. Feminine idiom 'a woman to her sister' for joined curtains (26:3).

**The high priest's vestments** (Exod 28:1-43)
- Twelve gems: Rev 21:19-20 foundations; Ezek 28:13 king of Tyre's stones. Bells on hem: Sir 45:9; Josephus on cosmic symbolism of the vestments. Seamless robe: John 19:23.

**The daily offering and God's dwelling** (Exod 29:38-46)
- Daily offerings parallel to Islamic fixed prayer times (rabbinic derivation of shaharit and minhah from the tamid).

**Incense altar, half-shekel ransom and bronze laver** (Exod 30:1-21)
- Census danger: 2 Sam 24. Ritual washing of hands and feet before worship: compare Islamic wudu (Quran 5:6).

**Recipes of the holy anointing oil and incense** (Exod 30:22-38)
- Christian chrism; Egyptian kyphi incense recipes; Greek Magical Papyri on sacred recipes kept secret.

**Bezalel and Oholiab; Sabbath as sign; the tablets** (Exod 31:1-18)
- Quran 50:38 'no weariness touched us' reads as a rebuttal of God resting/refreshing. Bezalel and divine wisdom in craft: Ugaritic Kothar-wa-Hasis.

**The golden calf** (Exod 32:1-14)
- Quran 20:83-98 and 7:148-154: the Samiri fashions the calf that lows; Aaron pleads 'do not seize me by my beard'; Moses burns and scatters it in the sea. 1 Kgs 12:28 Jeroboam's calves use the same formula.

**Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer** (Exod 32:15-35)
- Quran 20:97 (the Samiri's calf burned and scattered in the sea); Quran 2:54 'kill yourselves' as atonement for the calf; Paul's wish to be accursed for his kin, Rom 9:3; Rev 3:5 book of life; Num 5 ordeal of drinking.

**Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back** (Exod 33:1-23)
- Quran 7:143: Moses asks 'my Lord, show yourself to me', is told 'you will not see me, but look at the mountain', which crumbles and Moses falls unconscious. 1 Kgs 19 Elijah at the cave on Horeb. Rom 9:15 quotes 33:19.

**New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue** (Exod 34:1-28)
- The thirteen attributes recited in synagogue liturgy; cf. Quranic divine names al-Rahman al-Rahim; Jonah 4:2, Joel 2:13 reuse 34:6.

**Moses' shining face and the veil** (Exod 34:29-35)
- Horned Moses of Michelangelo; 2 Cor 3:7-18 veil allegory; Matt 17:2 transfiguration; Quran 7:108 / 20:22 Moses' hand shining white (different organ).

**Sabbath fire ban and the people's donations** (Exod 35:1-29)
- Jewelry for the sanctuary versus jewelry for the calf (32:2-3): rabbinic contrast. Karaite and rabbinic dispute over Sabbath fire.

**Altar, laver of mirrors, court and the metal inventory** (Exod 38:1-31)
- Women serving at the tent door: 1 Sam 2:22. Rabbinic midrash (Tanhuma) on the mirrors the women used to arouse their husbands in Egypt.

**The tabernacle erected; cloud and glory fill it** (Exod 40:1-38)
- 1 Kgs 8:10-11 glory fills Solomon's temple; Quranic sakina (2:248) with the ark (tabut); Enuma Elish's temple-building after victory.

**The burnt offering of cattle, flock and birds** (Lev 1:1-17)
- Greek holocaust; Vedic animal sacrifice (pasubandha) with dismemberment; Luke 2:24 poor parents' offering of doves. Bird split but not divided: Gen 15:10.

**The grain offering; no leaven or honey; salt of the covenant** (Lev 2:1-16)
- Salt covenant: Num 18:19, 2 Chr 13:5; Mark 9:49; salt in Roman mola salsa and Homeric sacrifice. Honey excluded: contrast honey offerings in Mesopotamian and Vedic ritual.

**The well-being (shelamim) offering and the ban on fat and blood** (Lev 3:1-17)
- Mesopotamian extispicy focused on the liver lobe (yoteret); Greek gods' portion of fat-wrapped thigh bones (Hesiod, Prometheus at Mekone). Quran 22:37 'neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God'.

**The purification (hattat) offering for unintentional sin** (Lev 4:1-35)
- Heb 13:11-12 (Jesus suffered outside the gate as the sin-offering burned outside the camp).

**Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering** (Lev 5:1-26)
- Matt 5:23-24 reconcile with your brother before the altar; Mishnah Yoma 8:9; Islamic rule that rights of people (huquq al-'ibad) must be restored before repentance is complete.

**Priestly instructions for burnt, grain and sin offerings; the perpetual fire** (Lev 6:1-23)
- Perpetual fire: Zoroastrian Atash Behram; Roman Vestal fire; Mal 1:11. Earthen vessels absorbing holiness/impurity: Lev 11:33; rabbinic kashering of vessels; Islamic rules on vessels.

**Guilt and well-being offerings; priests' portions; fat and blood bans** (Lev 7:1-38)
- Acts 15:20, 29 (abstain from blood); Quran 2:173, 5:3, 6:145 (blood forbidden); Greek priest's perquisite of the hide (dermatikon).

**Moses ordains Aaron and his sons** (Lev 8:1-36)
- Seven-day liminal seclusion during initiation: compare rites of passage (van Gennep); Christian ordination anointing.

**The eighth day - Aaron's first offerings and the divine fire** (Lev 9:1-24)
- Compare 1Kgs 18:38 (Elijah), 2Chr 7:1 (Solomon), Judg 6:21 and 13:20; Quran 3:183 on the demand for an offering consumed by fire.

**Strange fire - death of Nadab and Abihu; priestly rules** (Lev 10:1-20)
- Rabbinic tradition links 10:9 to the brothers' drunkenness (Lev. Rab. 12). Compare Num 16:35 (Korah's 250 burned) and Greek stories of illicit fire (Prometheus).

**Clean and unclean animals; carcass impurity** (Lev 11:1-47)
- Compare Deut 14; Quran 2:173, 5:3, 6:145 (pig, carrion); Acts 10 (Peter's vision); Zoroastrian classifications of noxious creatures (khrafstra); the hoopoe in Quran 27:20.

**Impurity after childbirth** (Lev 12:1-8)
- Luke 2:22-24 cites 12:8 for Mary's offering; compare Zoroastrian and Hindu (sutaka) postpartum impurity periods; Islamic nifas (40 days).

**Diagnosis of tsara'at in skin, scalp and fabric** (Lev 13:1-59)
- Compare Num 12 (Miriam), 2Kgs 5 (Naaman), 2Chr 26:19-21 (Uzziah); Mark 1:40-44 ('show yourself to the priest'); Quran 3:49 and 5:110 (Jesus heals the leper, al-abras).

**Purification of the healed leper; plague in houses** (Lev 14:1-57)
- The bird released over the field parallels the scapegoat (Lev 16) and Mesopotamian/Hittite elimination rites carrying impurity away on a living animal; rabbinic tradition (Arakhin 16a) links tsara'at to slander.

**Impurity of bodily discharges, semen and menstruation** (Lev 15:1-33)
- The woman with an issue of blood (Mark 5:25-34) presupposes 15:25; compare Quran 2:222 on menstruation (adhan), Islamic ghusl after janaba, Zoroastrian Vendidad 16 on menstruants.

**The Day of Atonement and the goat for Azazel** (Lev 16:1-34)
- Azazel appears as a fallen angel in 1 Enoch 8-10 (Asael), Apocalypse of Abraham 13-14; Mishnah Yoma 6 (goat pushed off a cliff, scarlet thread turning white); Hebrews 9; Greek pharmakos and Hittite/Babylonian elimination rites (Ashella, akitu kuppuru with sheep carcass); Ashura fasting on the 10th of Muharram in Islamic tradition.

**Slaughter only at the tent; the blood is the life** (Lev 17:1-16)
- Acts 15:20, 29 (apostolic decree: abstain from blood and things strangled) applies these alien-binding laws to gentiles; Noahide prohibition Gen 9:4; Quran 2:173, 5:3 (blood, carrion, al-munkhaniqa); Hebrews 9:22.

**Forbidden sexual unions; the land vomits out its inhabitants** (Lev 18:1-30)
- Quran 4:22-23 lists forbidden degrees (including two sisters together and father's wife); Paul cites 18:5 (Rom 10:5, Gal 3:12); 1Cor 5:1; Mark 6:18 (Herod and his brother's wife); Zoroastrian xwaetwadatha (next-of-kin marriage) as the opposite pole.

**Be holy - ethical laws and love of neighbor** (Lev 19:1-18)
- 19:18 quoted by Jesus (Mark 12:31), Paul (Rom 13:9, Gal 5:14), James 2:8; Hillel's negative Golden Rule (Shabbat 31a); Akiva calls it the great principle (Sifra); compare Confucian shu (Analects 15:24), Mahabharata 13.114.8; Quran 2:177 and Ruth 2 for gleanings.

**Mixtures, orlah fruit, mourning cuttings, alien and just weights** (Lev 19:19-37)
- Peot (side-locks) custom from 19:27; Deut 22:9-11 parallels on mixtures; Quran 83:1-3 and 55:9 on just measure; Egyptian Book of the Dead 125 ('I have not diminished the bushel'); tattoo prohibition vs. hadith cursing al-washima.

**Penalties for Molech worship, necromancy and sexual offenses** (Lev 20:1-27)
- John 8:5 (woman taken in adultery) invokes 20:10; rabbinic sages derive four modes of execution; Rabbinic Molech interpretation (passing through fire, Sanhedrin 64b) vs. Punic molk child sacrifice at Carthage tophet.

**Priests' mourning and marriage limits; blemished priests** (Lev 21:1-24)
- Compare Ezek 44:20-25; the Roman flamen Dialis and Vestal rules; Hindu bodily qualifications for Brahmin officiants (Manu 3.150ff); Qumran exclusion of the blemished from the congregation (1QSa 2).

**Who may eat holy food; unblemished sacrificial animals** (Lev 22:1-33)
- Mal 1:8 (blind and lame offered); Deut 22:6-7 (mother bird); Quran 2:67-71 on the specifications of the sacrificial cow; Islamic udhiya defects (one-eyed, lame, sick, emaciated) in hadith.

**The appointed times - sabbath and annual festivals** (Lev 23:1-44)
- John 7:37 and the Hoshana Rabbah water/willow rites; Acts 2 (Pentecost); Jubilees and Qumran 364-day calendar dispute about 'morrow of the sabbath'; Babylonian akitu new-year festival in Nisan/Tishri; palm branches in John 12:13 and Rev 7:9.

**Perpetual lamp, showbread, and the blasphemer stoned** (Lev 24:1-23)
- Matt 5:38 ('eye for eye'); Code of Hammurabi 196-200; Quran 5:45 (life for life, eye for eye); Mark 2:26 (David eats showbread); Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:5 on the blasphemer and the Name; Num 15:32-36 parallel case held 'until it be declared'.

**Sabbatical year and the jubilee; the land is mine** (Lev 25:1-24)
- Liberty Bell inscription (25:10); Mesopotamian mīšarum/andurāru royal debt-release edicts; Isa 61:1-2 and Luke 4:18-19; 2Chr 36:21 links exile to unkept sabbaths; Jubilees' chronology of jubilee periods; Daniel 9's seventy weeks.

**Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen** (Lev 25:25-55)
- Ruth 4 and Jer 32 (redemption of land by kin); Quran 2:275-279 (riba); Deut 23:20 permits interest to foreigners; Neh 5; Christian medieval usury debates relied on 25:36-37.

**Covenant blessings for obedience** (Lev 26:1-13)
- 2Cor 6:16 quotes 26:12; Deut 32:30 and Josh 23:10 (one chases a thousand); Quran 8:65-66 (twenty steadfast overcome two hundred); Assyrian treaty blessings.

**Covenant curses, exile, and remembered covenant** (Lev 26:14-46)
- Deut 28 parallel curses; 2Kgs 6:28-29 and Lam 4:10 (siege cannibalism); Vassal Treaties of Esarhaddon (sky of bronze, earth of iron, §63-64); 2Chr 36:21; Jer 4:4 and Rom 2:29 (circumcised heart); Quran 2:88 and 4:155 'our hearts are wrapped' (ghulf).

**Valuation of vowed persons, animals, houses, fields; herem and tithes** (Lev 27:1-34)
- Judg 11 (Jephthah's vow) and 1Sam 14:24-45 against 27:29; Matt 26:15 thirty pieces of silver vs. female valuation and Exod 21:32; Mishnah Arakhin; Quran 5:1 and 22:29 on fulfilling vows; Greek dekate tithes to Apollo.

**The census of fighting men in the wilderness of Sinai** (Num 1:1-54)
- 2Sam 24 and 1Chr 21 (David's census brings plague); Exod 30:12-16 half-shekel ransom for census; the 603,550 equals the half-shekel sum of Exod 38:26; gematria proposals (bny ysr'l kl r's = 603,551 in Hebrew numerology) discussed in modern scholarship.

**The camp in four standards around the tent** (Num 2:1-34)
- Rabbinic midrash assigns the four standards the cherub faces of Ezek 1:10 (lion Judah, man Reuben, ox Ephraim, eagle Dan) (Num. Rab. 2:10); compare the four living creatures of Rev 4:7, the Qumran War Scroll's banners, and Roman/Egyptian square army camps (Ramesses II at Qadesh).

**Aaron's sons; Levite clans counted and taken in place of the firstborn** (Num 3:1-51)
- Pidyon ha-ben (five shekels) and Luke 2:23; rabbinic explanations of the 300 discrepancy (Bekhorot 5a: the 300 Levite firstborn); the dotted word discussed in Sifre Num 69 and ARN 34 (ten dotted places).

**Wrapping and carrying the sanctuary; Levites aged 30 to 50** (Num 4:1-49)
- 2Sam 6:6-7 (Uzzah struck for touching the ark) and 1Sam 6:19 (Beth-shemesh men struck for looking into it); Egyptian processional barques carrying shrouded divine images; Num 8:24 gives 25 years instead of 30 (rabbinic harmonization: 5 years of training).

**Unclean sent out of the camp; confession and restitution** (Num 5:1-10)
- Luke 19:8 (Zacchaeus' restitution); Matt 5:23-24 (reconcile before offering); Islamic doctrine that wrongs against people (huquq al-'ibad) require restitution beyond repentance.

**The suspected adulteress and the bitter water** (Num 5:11-31)
- Code of Hammurabi 131-132 (river ordeal for accused wife); Mishnah Sotah (abolished by Yohanan b. Zakkai, Sotah 9:9); Protevangelium of James 16 (Mary and Joseph drink the 'water of the Lord's conviction'); Quran 24:6-9 li'an oath procedure for husband's accusation; Hindu and medieval ordeals by drinking (Yajnavalkya 2.95ff kosha ordeal: drinking water used to bathe an idol); Egyptian magic of drinking dissolved written spells.

**The Nazirite vow** (Num 6:1-21)
- Samson (Judg 13-16) and Samuel (1Sam 1:11, 4QSam 'nazir'); Amos 2:11-12; Acts 18:18 and 21:23-26 (Paul pays for Nazirites' offerings); John the Baptist Luke 1:15; Greek hair offerings to river gods (Achilles' lock, Iliad 23.141); Islamic ihram restrictions on cutting hair until the final shaving (halq); Sikh kesh.

**The priestly blessing** (Num 6:22-27)
- Ketef Hinnom silver amulets (7th-6th c. BCE) inscribe this blessing - the oldest attested biblical text; Ps 67:2 and 4:7; Ugaritic and Akkadian 'shining face' of a god/king (Amarna letters); used as Christian Aaronic benediction.

**The chieftains' covered wagons and oxen** (Num 7:1-9)
- 2Sam 6:3-7 - David moves the ark on a new cart and Uzzah dies (1Chr 15:13-15 blames not carrying it on shoulders); 1Sam 6:7 Philistine cart and two milch cows.

**Altar dedication gifts, days one to six** (Num 7:10-47)
- Rabbinic midrash (Num. Rab. 13-14) gives each identical gift a different symbolic meaning per tribe; 1Kgs 8:63 and 2Chr 7:5 (Solomon's dedication); 1Macc 4:56 and the eight-day Hanukkah; Num 7 is read at Hanukkah.

**Altar dedication gifts, days seven to twelve; totals; the voice from between the cherubim** (Num 7:48-89)
- Exod 25:22 promised meeting place; rabbinic bat qol; Islamic account of Moses hearing God's speech (kalam, Quran 4:164, 7:143) and the Sakina in the ark (Quran 2:248).

**Passover in Sinai and the second Passover** (Num 9:1-14)
- Num 9:12 'no bone broken' is applied to Jesus in John 19:36.
- Mishnah Pesahim 9 (Pesach Sheni); the dot over he of rehoqah discussed in Sifre.

**Silver trumpets and departure from Sinai** (Num 10:1-28)
- Qumran War Scroll (1QM 2-3) inscribes trumpets for each stage of battle; Islamic eschatology: trumpet blasts (sur).

**Hobab invited as guide; the Song of the Ark** (Num 10:29-36)
- Ps 68:2 reuses 'Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered'. Rabbinic: the inverted nuns make 10:35-36 a 'book' of its own (b. Shabbat 115b-116a).

**Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail** (Num 11:1-35)
- Quran 2:57, 7:160, 20:80 (manna and salwa); Quran 2:61 the Israelites ask for herbs, cucumbers, garlic (fum), lentils and onions.
- Lost apocryphon 'Eldad and Modad' quoted in Shepherd of Hermas Vis. 2.3.4; Acts 2 / Joel 3 universal prophecy.
- Seventy elders as model for the Sanhedrin of 71 (m. Sanhedrin 1:6).

**Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses** (Num 12:1-16)
- Josephus Ant. 2.252-253 and Artapanus: Moses' Ethiopian campaign and marriage to an Ethiopian princess (Tharbis).
- Hebrews 3:2-5 cites 'faithful in all his house'. Quran 33:69 'do not be like those who hurt Moses'.

**The twelve spies and their report** (Num 13:1-33)
- Quran 5:20-26: two God-fearing men urge entry into the holy land; the people say 'go, you and your Lord, and fight'; forty years of wandering (tih).
- Gen 6:4 Nephilim; 1 Enoch giants; Og legends (b. Niddah 61a) and the giant who carried a mountain.

**Rebellion after the spies' report and the forty-year sentence** (Num 14:1-45)
- m. Avot 5:4 ten trials in the wilderness; Ezek 4:6 'a day for a year' prophetic reckoning used by later apocalyptic chronology (Dan 9).
- Quran 5:26 'forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the earth'.

**The Sabbath wood-gatherer; the law of tassels** (Num 15:32-41)
- Num 15:37-41 is the third paragraph of the Shema. Matt 9:20, 14:36 (hem/kraspedon of Jesus' garment); Quran 7:163 Sabbath-breakers of the town by the sea.
- Targum and rabbinic tradition identify the wood-gatherer as Zelophehad (b. Shabbat 96b).

**Korah, Dathan and Abiram rebel; the earth swallows them** (Num 16:1-35)
- Quran 28:76-82 Qarun (Korah), proud of wealth whose keys burdened strong men, swallowed by the earth with his house.
- Num 26:11 'the sons of Korah did not die'; Psalms of the sons of Korah. m. Avot 5:17 'dispute of Korah'; Jude 11.
- 1Sam 12:3 Samuel's parallel protest ('whose ox or donkey have I taken?').

**Censers as altar plating, Aaron stops the plague, Aaron's rod blossoms** (Num 17:1-28)
- Heb 9:4 rod in the ark; Protevangelium of James 9 (dove from Joseph's rod) and Pseudo-Matthew 8 (Joseph's rod blossoms); Tannhauser's staff blossoming; Quran 2:248 relics of the family of Moses and Aaron in the ark.
- Wisdom of Solomon 18:21-25 on Aaron's intercession.

**Duties and revenues of priests and Levites** (Num 18:1-32)
- Pidyon ha-ben ceremony; Luke 2:22-24 presentation of Jesus. Covenant of salt also 2Chr 13:5; Lev 2:13.

**The red heifer and corpse impurity** (Num 19:1-22)
- Heb 9:13-14 ashes of a heifer; m. Parah (only nine heifers ever burned); Barnabas 8. Quran 2:67-73 the cow Israel was commanded to slaughter (yellow, unyoked) to reveal a murderer.
- Zoroastrian Vendidad: corpse impurity (nasu) and purification with bull's urine (gomez); Indic pañcagavya.

**Miriam's death; water from the rock at Meribah** (Num 20:1-13)
- Quran 2:60, 7:160: Moses strikes the rock, twelve springs gush out; 1Cor 10:4 'the rock that followed them was Christ'; rabbinic Miriam's well (b. Ta'anit 9a) ceases at her death.

**Edom refuses passage; death of Aaron at Mount Hor** (Num 20:14-29)
- Elijah's mantle passes to Elisha (2Kgs 2:13); midrash on Aaron's death in a cave (Yalkut). Islamic tradition places Aaron's tomb on Jabal Harun near Petra.

**Hormah; the fiery serpents and the bronze serpent** (Num 21:1-9)
- 2Kgs 18:4 Hezekiah destroys Nehushtan; John 3:14; Wis 16:5-7; Asclepius' serpent staff; copper serpent found at Timna Midianite shrine.

**Stations to Moab; Book of the Wars of YHWH; Song of the Well** (Num 21:10-20)
- Rabbinic: the well accompanied Israel (t. Sukkah 3:11); CD 6:3-9 (Damascus Document) allegorizes the well as Torah and the staff as the Interpreter of the Law.

**Defeat of Sihon and Og; the Heshbon ballad** (Num 21:21-35)
- Mesha Stele: Chemosh angry with his land; cf. Jer 48:45-46 reuses this ballad. Og the giant (Deut 3:11) and Og legends in midrash and Islamic 'Uj ibn 'Anaq.

**Balak sends for Balaam** (Num 22:1-20)
- Deir Alla plaster inscription (8th c. BCE): 'Balaam son of Beor, seer of the gods', night vision of a divine council.
- 2Pet 2:15, Jude 11, Rev 2:14: Balaam loved the wages of wrongdoing. Quran 7:175-176 (traditionally Bal'am ibn Ba'ura) likened to a panting dog.

**Balaam's donkey and the angel** (Num 22:21-41)
- m. Avot 5:6: the mouth of the she-ass among ten things created at twilight of the first Sabbath eve; Achilles' horse Xanthos speaks (Iliad 19.404-417); 2Pet 2:16 'a speechless donkey spoke with a human voice'.
- 2Kgs 6:17 Elisha's servant's eyes opened to see fiery chariots.

**Balaam's first and second oracles** (Num 23:1-30)
- 1Sam 15:29 'the Glory of Israel does not lie or repent, for he is not a man'.

**Balaam's third and fourth oracles; the Star from Jacob; oracles against nations** (Num 24:1-25)
- Num 24:17 read messianically: Bar Kokhba ('son of the star'), CD 7:18-21, 4QTestimonia, Targum Onkelos; Matt 2:2 star of the Magi (Origen links Magi to Balaam); Dan 11:30 'ships of Kittim'.
- Mah tovu (24:5) opens the Jewish morning service.

**Baal Peor and the zeal of Phinehas** (Num 25:1-19)
- 1Macc 2:26 Mattathias' zeal 'as Phinehas did'; Ps 106:30-31; Sir 45:23; rabbinic identification of Phinehas with Elijah (Pirqe R. El. 47). Josephus Ant. 4.126-155 and Philo link Peor to Balaam's advice (cf. Num 31:16; Rev 2:14).

**Census of the second generation on the plains of Moab** (Num 26:1-65)
- Serah bat Asher: midrash makes her long-lived, tells Jacob Joseph lives (with a harp), shows Moses Joseph's coffin, enters paradise alive.
- Rabbinic tradition: Jochebed born 'between the walls' as they entered Egypt, mother at 130 (b. Bava Batra 123b).

**Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned** (Num 27:1-23)
- Mark 6:34 / Matt 9:36 'sheep without a shepherd'; semikhah as basis of rabbinic ordination; Quran 4:11-12, 4:176 daughters' inheritance shares.

**Calendar of public offerings** (Num 28:1-29:39)
- b. Sukkah 55b: seventy bulls for the seventy nations, one bull on the eighth day for Israel. Num 28-29 read as Musaf readings in synagogue; the dotted vav in Num 29:15.

**Vows of men and women** (Num 30:1-17)
- Kol Nidre and m. Nedarim (hatarat nedarim); Quran 5:89 expiation for oaths; Matt 5:33-37.

**War against Midian and division of the spoils** (Num 31:1-54)
- 1Sam 30:24-25 David's rule of equal shares; Quran 8:41 one-fifth of spoils (khums) for God and the Messenger; m. Avodah Zarah 5:12 kashering vessels by fire and water (hag'alah, libun).

**Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh settle east of the Jordan** (Num 32:1-42)
- Josh 22 altar of witness of the Transjordan tribes. Mesha Stele mentions Ataroth and 'men of Gad' living there 'from of old'.

**The stages of Israel's journey from Egypt to Moab** (Num 33:1-49)
- Num Rabbah 23 / Midrash: 42 stations allegorized; Origen Homily 27 on Numbers reads the 42 stations as stages of the soul's ascent; the 42-letter divine name in Kabbalah. Matt 1:17 has 3x14 = 42 generations.

**Borders of Canaan and the land commission** (Num 34:1-29)
- Ezek 47:15-20 borders of the restored land; Gen 15:18 river of Egypt to Euphrates.

**Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide** (Num 35:1-34)
- Quran 2:178-179, 17:33 qisas and the heir's authority, diyah accepted (contrast 35:31); Greek asylia at temples; Draco's homicide law (involuntary homicide and exile). b. Makkot 11a: mothers of high priests fed refugees so they would not pray for the priest's death.

**Marriage of heiresses within the tribe; colophon of Numbers** (Num 36:1-13)
- Athenian epikleros (heiress married to nearest kinsman); Tob 6:12-13 and 7:10-13 (Sarah must marry within her father's kin).

**Setting of Moses' speech; appointment of judges** (Deut 1:1-18)
- Exod 18 Jethro's advice; Sifre Deut 1 reads the place names of 1:1 as veiled rebukes (Di-zahav = golden calf). Lam 1:1 and Isa 1:21 share 'eikhah' with Deut 1:12 and are read together on Tisha b'Av.

**The spies episode retold** (Deut 1:19-46)
- Isa 7:15-16 the child who does not yet know to refuse evil and choose good; Gen 2-3 knowledge of good and evil. Ps 118:12 'they surrounded me like bees'.

**Passing Edom, Moab and Ammon; the giant aboriginal peoples** (Deut 2:1-23)
- Caphtor is usually identified with Crete (cf. Amos 9:7); Rephaim also appear as shades of the dead in Ugaritic texts (rpum).
- Giant pre-inhabitants: compare Quranic 'Ad (tall people, Q 7:69, 89:6-8) and Greek Titans/Gigantes.

**Defeat of Og of Bashan and allotment of Transjordan** (Deut 3:1-22)
- Og legends: rabbinic Og survived the Flood (b. Niddah 61a), was killed by Moses leaping ten cubits (b. Berakhot 54b); Islamic 'Uj ibn 'Anaq is a giant of immense height.
- The 'bed' (eres) may be a basalt dolmen/sarcophagus; compare relics of heroes' oversized bones in Greek tradition (Orestes' bones, Herodotus 1.68).

**Moses pleads to cross the Jordan and is refused** (Deut 3:23-29)
- Midrash Petirat Moshe expands Moses' 515 prayers (gematria of ואתחנן) to be allowed to enter.

**Exhortation at Horeb's memory; no image; exile and return** (Deut 4:1-40)
- Compare Abraham's rejection of star, moon and sun worship (Q 6:76-79) and Quranic idols that cannot hear or see (Q 19:42).
- Rev 22:18-19 adds the no-adding/no-subtracting formula; also Codex Hammurabi epilogue curse on altering the stela.

**The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb** (Deut 5:1-33)
- Quran 17:22-39 contains a commandment list often compared with the Decalogue; Q 2:55-56 the people ask to see God and are struck.

**The Shema and the instruction to teach** (Deut 6:1-25)
- Mark 12:29-30 (Jesus quotes the Shema); Matt 4:7, 4:10 (Jesus quotes Deut 6:13, 6:16 against Satan); Quran 112:1 'Say: He is God, One'.
- Passover Haggadah's four sons draws on Deut 6:20.

**Dispossession of the seven nations; Israel the treasured people** (Deut 7:1-26)
- שגר אלפיך ועשתרות צאנך preserves deity names Shagar and Ashtart as terms for offspring of cattle and flock (cf. Deir Alla inscription 'Shagar and Ishtar').

**Lessons of the wilderness; the good land; beware of pride** (Deut 8:1-20)
- Matt 4:4 / Luke 4:4: Jesus answers Satan with Deut 8:3. Quran 28:78: Qarun says 'I was given it because of knowledge I have' — the 'my power made this wealth' motif.
- Rabbinic Birkat ha-Mazon is derived from Deut 8:10 (b. Berakhot 21a).

**Not for your righteousness; the golden calf and Moses' intercession recalled** (Deut 9:1-29)
- Quran 20:83-97 and 7:148-154: the calf, Moses casts down the tablets, seizes Aaron's head, the Samiri; the calf is burned and scattered into the sea (Q 20:97).

**Second tablets and ark; Levites set apart; what God requires** (Deut 10:1-22)
- Rom 2:29 circumcision of the heart; Quran 2:88 'our hearts are uncircumcised' (ghulf). Rev 17:14 Lord of lords.
- Rabbinic tradition: both the broken and the whole tablets lay in the ark (b. Bava Batra 14b).

**The land that drinks rain; blessing and curse; Gerizim and Ebal** (Deut 11:1-32)
- Samaritan Pentateuch makes Gerizim the chosen place; cf. John 4:20.

**The chosen place; profane slaughter; blood prohibition** (Deut 12:1-31)
- Quran 6:145 / 2:173 prohibit flowing blood (dam masfuh) and pork; Acts 15:20 prohibits blood for gentile believers.

**False prophet, enticing kin, and the apostate city** (Deut 13:1-19)
- Matt 24:24 false prophets showing great signs; Dajjal traditions in Islam (false wonder-worker).

**Mourning rites forbidden; clean and unclean food; tithes** (Deut 14:1-29)
- Hoopoe (dukhifat, 14:18) is Solomon's messenger bird in Quran 27:20-28; the unclean-bird list is the only Torah mention of the hoopoe.
- Quran 5:3 forbids carrion (mayta) and pork; Q 6:146 says God forbade the Jews every animal with claws.

**Release of debts, release of Hebrew slaves, firstlings** (Deut 15:1-23)
- Matt 26:11 / John 12:8 'the poor you have always with you' echoes Deut 15:11. Mesopotamian misharum/andurarum royal debt-release edicts are the closest ANE parallel.

**Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah** (Deut 16:1-22)
- Jesus' Passover and Pentecost (Acts 2) map on to these feasts; Quran 2:185 Ramadan compared with Shavuot as a month of revelation.

**Idolater's trial; witnesses; high court; law of the king** (Deut 17:1-20)
- John 8:7 ('let him who is without sin cast the first stone') and 2 Cor 13:1 (two or three witnesses) draw on 17:6-7. Solomon (1 Kgs 10-11) violates every clause of 17:16-17.

**Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses** (Deut 18:1-22)
- Acts 3:22, 7:37 apply 18:15 to Jesus; Muslim apologetics apply 18:18 ('from among their brothers') to Muhammad (cf. Q 7:157, 46:10); Samaritan Taheb; Qumran 4QTestimonia.

**Cities of refuge, boundary stones, false witnesses** (Deut 19:1-21)
- Matt 5:38; Quran 5:45 (life for life, eye for eye ... prescribed in the Torah). Laws of Hammurabi §§1-4 (false accuser suffers the penalty); Amenemope ch. 6 and Prov 22:28 on boundary stones; Greek horoi.

**Rules of war: exemptions, peace terms, fruit trees** (Deut 20:1-20)
- Abu Bakr's instructions to the army (do not cut fruit trees; Muwatta' Malik, Jihad) parallel 20:19. Gilgamesh/Kirta: Kirta's army includes the newlywed — inverse of the exemption.

**Broken-necked heifer; captive bride; firstborn; rebellious son; hanged body** (Deut 21:1-23)
- Pilate washes his hands (Matt 27:24); Gal 3:13 'cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree'; John 19:31 bodies removed before the Sabbath. Hittite and Ugaritic (Aqhat) rituals for a corpse found in open country; Laws of Hammurabi §23-24 (city liable for unsolved robbery/murder).
- Quranic cow story (Q 2:67-73) concerns an unsolved murder solved by slaughtering a cow — commonly linked to the heifer of Deut 21.

**Lost property, bird's nest, mixtures, tassels, virginity and sexual offences** (Deut 22:1-29)
- Mother-bird law and honoring parents are the two commandments promising long life (Elisha ben Abuya legend, b. Qiddushin 39b). Quran 24:4 (punishing those who slander chaste women) compares with 22:13-19. 2 Cor 6:14 'unequally yoked' alludes to 22:10.

**Admission to the assembly; camp purity; slaves, interest, vows** (Deut 23:1-26)
- Disciples plucking grain (Mark 2:23) rests on 23:26. Isa 56:3-5 and Acts 8 reverse the eunuch exclusion; Ruth the Moabite vs 23:4. Escaped-slave rule contrasts with Laws of Hammurabi §15-16 (harboring a slave is capital). Quran 2:275 and Islamic riba law; Qumran Temple Scroll 46 latrines 3000 cubits from the city.

**Divorce, newlyweds, pledges, wages, gleanings** (Deut 24:1-22)
- Matt 5:31-32, 19:7-9 on the bill of divorce; Quran 2:230 reverses 24:4 (a thrice-divorced wife may return to the first husband only after marrying another). Hadith: 'give the worker his wage before his sweat dries' (Ibn Majah). 2 Kgs 14:6 quotes 24:16; Q 6:164 'no bearer of burdens bears another's burden'.

**Forty lashes, muzzled ox, levirate and halitzah, weights, Amalek** (Deut 25:1-19)
- Paul cites 25:4 (1 Cor 9:9); 2 Cor 11:24 'forty lashes less one'; Sadducees' levirate question (Mark 12:19); Ruth 4:7-8 sandal ritual; Middle Assyrian Laws A 8 (woman who crushes a man's testicle has a finger cut off). Quran 83:1-3, 11:85 on honest weights (Shu'ayb).

**First-fruits creed, tithe declaration, mutual covenant** (Deut 26:1-19)
- 26:14 'not given to the dead' implies offerings to the dead (cf. Ugaritic kispu/marzeah cult). The Passover Haggadah is built on midrash of 26:5-8 ('Laban sought to destroy my father'). Egyptian Book of the Dead 125 negative confession is compared with the tithe declaration.

**Inscribed stones and altar on Ebal; the twelve curses** (Deut 27:1-26)
- Gal 3:10 quotes 27:26. Mount Ebal altar (Zertal's site) archaeology; Josh 8:30-35 fulfils the command. Hittite and Assyrian treaties end with curses answered by assent.

**Blessings and the great curses** (Deut 28:1-69)
- Close literary dependence on the Succession Treaty of Esarhaddon (VTE §§39-42, 63-64: Sin's leprosy, Shamash's darkness, sky bronze and earth iron, eating one's children). Siege cannibalism realised in 2 Kgs 6:28-29, Lam 4:10, Josephus War 6.201-213 (Mary of Bethezuba).

**Covenant at Moab; the secret apostate; the land like Sodom** (Deut 29:1-28)
- Rabbinic tradition: all souls of future generations (and converts) stood at Sinai/Moab (b. Shevuot 39a); compare Quran 7:172 primordial covenant with the children of Adam. Heb 12:15 'root of bitterness'. 1 Kgs 9:8-9 and Jer 22:8-9 reuse the 'why has God done this' dialogue, as do Assyrian annals (Ashurbanipal on Arabs).

**Return from exile; the near commandment; choose life** (Deut 30:1-20)
- Rom 10:6-8 reinterprets 30:12-14 christologically; b. Bava Metzia 59b (oven of Akhnai: 'it is not in heaven') rejects a heavenly voice. Didache 1:1 two ways; Jer 31:33 new covenant on the heart.

**Joshua commissioned; Torah written and deposited; the Song commanded** (Deut 31:1-30)
- b. Hullin 139b finds Esther in 'haster astir panai'. Hittite treaties require deposit of the tablet before the god and periodic public reading — close structural parallel.

**The Song of Moses (Ha'azinu)** (Deut 32:1-43)
- Rom 10:19 / 11:11 (jealousy by a no-people), Rom 12:19 and Heb 10:30 (vengeance is mine), Heb 1:6 quotes the LXX plus of 32:43. Resheph is a Canaanite plague/archer god (Ugarit, Egypt); 'sons of God' allotment parallels Ugaritic 70 sons of El. Rev 15:3 'song of Moses'. Exod 19:4 eagle's wings.

**The Blessing of Moses on the tribes** (Deut 33:1-29)
- Muslim polemic reads 33:2 (Sinai, Seir, Paran) as Moses, Jesus and Muhammad (Ibn Qutayba, al-Qurtubi); cf. Quran 95:1-3 (fig, olive, Sinai, the secure city). Gen 49 is the parallel testament; Baal as 'rider of the clouds' (rkb 'rpt) at Ugarit parallels 33:26.

**Death and burial of Moses** (Deut 34:1-12)
- Jude 9: Michael disputes with the devil over Moses' body (Assumption of Moses); b. Bava Batra 15a on who wrote the last eight verses; Josephus Ant. 4.326 cloud envelops Moses. Islamic hadith: Moses slaps the angel of death and asks to be buried a stone's throw from the holy land (Bukhari 1339); the maqam Nabi Musa near Jericho. Compare disappearance/unknown graves of Romulus and Oedipus at Colonus.

**God commissions Joshua; Transjordan tribes pledged** (Josh 1:1-18)
- Ps 1:2 'meditates day and night'; Quran 5:23 two God-fearing men urge entry into the land (Joshua and Caleb in tafsir).

**Rahab hides the spies in Jericho** (Josh 2:1-24)
- Rahab in Matt 1:5 (ancestress of Jesus), Heb 11:31, Jas 2:25; 1 Clement 12 reads the scarlet cord as Christ's blood. Paul let down in a basket through a window in the wall at Damascus (2 Cor 11:33, Acts 9:25). Compare the Passover blood on the door (Exod 12:22) and Muhammad hiding three days in the cave of Thawr while pursuers search.

**The ark goes before; the Jordan stands in a heap** (Josh 3:1-17)
- Repeats the Red Sea crossing (Exod 14-15 'stood as a heap', נד); Elijah and Elisha part the Jordan (2 Kgs 2:8, 14); Jesus' baptism in the Jordan. Arab chronicler al-Nuwayri reports the Jordan blocked near Damiya (Adam) by a landslide in 1267 CE.

**Twelve memorial stones from the Jordan; the river returns** (Josh 4:1-24)
- Compare Gen 31:46 (cairn of witness), Exod 24:4 (twelve pillars), 1Kgs 18:31 (Elijah's twelve stones); 2Kgs 2:8 (Elijah and Elisha part the Jordan).
- Matt 3:9 'God can raise children to Abraham from these stones' has been linked by commentators to the Gilgal stones near the baptism site.

**Mass circumcision at Gilgal, Passover, end of manna, the commander of YHWH's army** (Josh 5:1-15)
- Compare Exod 4:25 (Zipporah's flint), Num 22:31 and 1Chr 21:16 (angel with drawn sword); Dan 10:13 and 12:1 (Michael the prince); Quran 20:12 (Moses told to remove his sandals in the sacred valley Tuwa).
- Rabbinic tradition identifies the commander as Michael; patristic reading as the pre-incarnate Logos.
- LXX Josh 24:31a says the flint knives were buried with Joshua at Timnath-serah.

**Fall of Jericho; Rahab spared; curse on the rebuilder** (Josh 6:1-27)
- Fulfilled in 1Kgs 16:34 (Hiel of Bethel loses Abiram and Segub): foundation-sacrifice motif.
- Heb 11:30-31; Jas 2:25; Matt 1:5 (Rahab in Jesus' genealogy); rabbinic tradition has Rahab marry Joshua and become ancestor of prophets (b. Meg 14b).
- Compare ritual processions around a city; seven-day cycles in Ugaritic epic (Kirta's siege of Udm).

**Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan** (Josh 7:1-26)
- 1Chr 2:7 names him Achar 'troubler of Israel'; Hos 2:17 'the valley of Achor a door of hope'. Compare Acts 5:1-11 (Ananias and Sapphira keep back devoted goods).
- Rabbinic: Achan's confession earned him a share in the world to come (m. Sanh 6:2).

**Ambush and capture of Ai; altar and Torah inscribed on Mount Ebal** (Josh 8:1-35)
- The Mount Ebal altar is central to Samaritan claims (Samaritan Pentateuch reads Gerizim in Deut 27:4). Compare Judg 20:29-48 (the same ambush tactic at Gibeah).

**The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty** (Josh 9:1-27)
- 2Sam 21:1-14: Saul's violation of the Gibeonite oath brings famine. Compare Gen 9:25 (curse of Canaan to servitude) and Greek stories of oaths kept despite deception.
- Rabbinic Netinim are identified with the Gibeonites (b. Yev 79a).

**Battle of Gibeon, hailstones, sun and moon stand still, five kings in the cave, southern campaign** (Josh 10:1-43)
- Compare Iliad 2.412-418 (Agamemnon prays the sun not to set before victory), Iliad 18.239-242 (Hera hastens sunset); Hab 3:11; Sir 46:4. Islamic tradition (Sahih Bukhari, hadith of a prophet whose sun was held back, identified as Joshua/Yusha').
- Hailstones: compare Exod 9:23-25, Rev 16:21. Book of Jashar also quoted in 2Sam 1:18; medieval pseudepigraphal Sefer ha-Yashar expands it.
- Feet on necks: Assyrian and Egyptian royal iconography of kings treading on enemies; Ps 110:1.

**Northern coalition under Jabin of Hazor; hamstrung horses; Anakim destroyed** (Josh 11:1-23)
- Jabin of Hazor reappears in Judg 4. Hazor is attested in Mari letters and Amarna (Abdi-Tirshi). Compare Exod 14 (hardening of Pharaoh's heart).

**List of the kings defeated by Moses and Joshua (thirty-one kings)** (Josh 12:1-24)
- Compare Egyptian topographical lists of conquered towns (Thutmose III at Karnak, Shishak list), which share names such as Megiddo, Taanach, Aphek.

**Land still to be conquered; Transjordanian allotments; Balaam's death** (Josh 13:1-33)
- Balaam son of Beor is named in the Deir Alla plaster inscription (8th c. BCE), a 'seer of the gods'. Compare Num 31:8 and 2Pet 2:15; Rev 2:14.

**Allotment by lot begins; Caleb at eighty-five claims Hebron** (Josh 14:1-15)
- Compare Deut 34:7 (Moses' eye not dim). Caleb 'the Kenizzite' — a Kenizzite (Edomite-linked, Gen 36:11) clan absorbed into Judah.

**The boundaries of Judah** (Josh 15:1-12)
- Gehenna as place of punishment: 1 Enoch 27, Matt 5:22, rabbinic Gehinnom, Quranic Jahannam (from the same name).
- Rephaim as shades of the dead: Ugaritic rpum, Phoenician funerary inscriptions (Tabnit, Eshmunazar).

**Caleb drives out the three sons of Anak; Othniel wins Achsah; she asks for springs** (Josh 15:13-19)
- Repeated almost verbatim in Judg 1:11-15. Compare folk motif of the hero who wins a princess by a deed (Saul's offer, 1Sam 17:25; Greek suitor contests).

**City list of Judah by districts; Jebusites remain in Jerusalem** (Josh 15:20-63)
- Ir ha-Melah is often identified with Khirbet Qumran (Qumran community). The LXX inserts an extra district including Bethlehem and Tekoa after 15:59.

**Lot of the sons of Joseph; Ephraim's border; Gezer under forced labor** (Josh 16:1-10)
- Gezer was given to Solomon as dowry by Pharaoh (1Kgs 9:16).

**Manasseh's lot; the daughters of Zelophehad receive land** (Josh 17:1-13)
- Num 27:1-11 and 36. Samaria ostraca (8th c.) name districts Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida, Noah, Hoglah. Compare Mesopotamian and Greek epikleros (heiress) law.

**Joseph's complaint of one lot; clear the forest; iron chariots** (Josh 17:14-18)
- Compare Judg 1:19; 4:3 (900 iron chariots of Sisera). Forest clearing as land-making: Gilgamesh's Cedar Forest expedition is a royal analogue.

**Tent of meeting set up at Shiloh; land surveyed in a book; seven lots cast** (Josh 18:1-10)
- Compare cadastral surveys in Egypt and Mesopotamia; Greek colonial land division by lot (kleros).

**Benjamin's borders and cities** (Josh 18:11-28)
- Jerusalem assigned to Benjamin here but to Judah's border in 15:8, 63 — a rabbinic topic (temple courts split between Judah and Benjamin, b. Yoma 12a).

**Simeon's inheritance within Judah** (Josh 19:1-9)
- Gen 49:7 'I will scatter them in Jacob' (Simeon and Levi) is often read as fulfilled here.

**Lots of Zebulun, Issachar, Asher and Naphtali** (Josh 19:10-39)
- Kinnereth (19:35) gives its name to the Sea of Galilee. Shunem (19:18) is home of the Shunammite (2Kgs 4). Compare Ugaritic Anat; Egyptian lists naming Beth-anath.

**Dan's lot; Danites capture Leshem and rename it Dan** (Josh 19:40-48)
- Expanded in Judg 18 (Laish). Zorah/Eshtaol is Samson's country (Judg 13:25).

**Joshua's own inheritance at Timnath-serah; end of allotment at Shiloh** (Josh 19:49-51)
- Judg 2:9 spells it Timnath-heres ('portion of the sun'); rabbinic tradition linked it to a sun image on Joshua's tomb (Rashi on Judg 2:9).

**Six cities of refuge designated** (Josh 20:1-9)
- Num 35; Deut 19. Compare Greek asylia of sanctuaries and the Athenian court at Phreatto for exiled homicides; the death of the high priest as expiation (b. Makkot 11b).

**Forty-eight Levitical cities by lot; all promises fulfilled** (Josh 21:1-45)
- 1Chr 6:39-66 parallel. 21:36-37 (Reuben's cities) are missing in some Masoretic manuscripts and printed with a note; present in this WLC text.

**Eastern tribes dismissed; the altar 'Ed' by the Jordan nearly causes civil war** (Josh 22:1-34)
- Compare Gen 31:44-52 (Galeed, heap of witness); Isa 19:19 (altar in Egypt as witness). Debates on central sanctuary vs. outside altars: Samaritan Gerizim, the Elephantine and Leontopolis temples.

**Joshua's farewell warning against intermarriage and foreign gods** (Josh 23:1-16)
- Compare Deut 32:30, Lev 26:8; Gen 47-49 and Deut 33 (testaments); the genre of the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs; 1Kgs 2:2 (David: 'I go the way of all the earth').

**Covenant at Shechem; 'choose this day whom you will serve'; deaths of Joshua and Eleazar** (Josh 24:1-33)
- Quran 6:74, 19:42-48 and 21:52 (Abraham's father Azar an idolater); Jubilees 11-12 and Apocalypse of Abraham (Terah makes idols); Genesis Rabbah 38 (Terah's idol shop).
- Hornet: Exod 23:28, Deut 7:20. Speaking/hearing stones: Luke 19:40; Hab 2:11. Compare Hittite vassal treaties (historical prologue, witnesses, deposit of text).
- LXX adds that the flint knives of circumcision were buried with Joshua.

**Judah goes up first; Adoni-bezek's thumbs; Luz betrayed; list of unconquered cities** (Judg 1:1-36)
- Mutilation of thumbs so captives cannot wield weapons: Athenians and Aeginetans (Aelian, Var. Hist. 2.9); Assyrian practice.
- Rabbinic legend: the new Luz is the city where the angel of death has no power (b. Sotah 46b); also the Luz bone of resurrection.

**Angel at Bochim; death of Joshua; the cycle of apostasy and deliverance** (Judg 2:1-23)
- Cyclical history: compare Polybius' anacyclosis, Hesiod's ages; Quran's repeated pattern of nations sent messengers then punished (e.g. Q 7).

**Nations left to teach war; Othniel defeats Cushan-rishathaim** (Judg 3:1-11)
- Othniel is the only judge from Judah; rabbinic tradition identifies him with Jabez (1Chr 4:9-10).

**Left-handed Ehud assassinates fat King Eglon; Shamgar's oxgoad** (Judg 3:12-31)
- Compare Judg 20:16 (700 left-handed Benjaminite slingers). Assassination by a tribute-bearer: Mucius Scaevola, the assassination of Philip II; Jael's killing of Sisera (Judg 4).
- Shamgar ben Anath: compare Ugaritic warrior goddess Anat; Judg 5:6; 2Sam 23:11-12 (Shammah).

**Deborah and Barak defeat Sisera; Jael kills him with a tent peg** (Judg 4:1-24)
- Compare Judith 13 (Judith beheads drunken Holofernes in his tent); Luke 1:42 ('blessed among women'); Rabbinic: Jael gave him milk to make him drowsy (b. Nid 55b; Targum).
- Sisera's name may be non-Semitic (Luwian/Sea Peoples). Harosheth-ha-goiim 'smithy of the nations'.

**The Song of Deborah** (Judg 5:1-31)
- Woman at the window: Phoenician ivory plaques; Michal (2Sam 6:16); Jezebel (2Kgs 9:30). Stars fighting: Josephus says a storm with hail blinded the Canaanites (Ant. 5.205); compare cosmic battle motifs, Baal's storm theophany.
- Theophany from Seir/Teman: Deut 33:2, Hab 3:3; Kuntillet Ajrud inscriptions 'YHWH of Teman'.
- Luke 1:42 (Elizabeth to Mary: 'blessed are you among women') echoes 5:24.

**Midianite oppression like locusts; an anonymous prophet rebukes Israel** (Judg 6:1-10)
- Earliest biblical scene of mass camel-riding raiders; compare Assyrian reliefs of Arab camel riders (Ashurbanipal).

**Angel calls Gideon at the winepress; fire from the rock; YHWH-shalom** (Judg 6:11-24)
- Compare Gen 18 (meal for visitors under the oaks of Mamre); Judg 13:19-20 (angel ascends in the flame); Exod 3-4 (Moses' objections); 1Sam 9:21 (Saul 'least of the tribes'); Lev 9:24, 1Kgs 18:38 (fire consumes offering).

**Gideon pulls down his father's Baal altar; Jerubbaal; the fleece signs** (Judg 6:25-40)
- Quran 21:58-68 and 37:91-98 (Abraham smashes idols; people demand punishment; 'ask them if they can speak'); 1Kgs 18:27 (Elijah mocks Baal). Gideon's fleece in Christian typology for Mary's virginal conception (Ps 72:6 Vulgate).

**The army reduced to 300 lappers; the barley-loaf dream; jars, torches and horns** (Judg 7:1-25)
- Quran 2:249: Talut (Saul) tests his army at a river — those who drink are excluded except a scoop by hand; the few defeat Goliath. Clear transfer of Gideon's test.
- Ruse of torches and noise: Hannibal's oxen with torches on their horns (Livy 22.16-17); Isa 9:3 and 10:26 recall 'the day of Midian' and the rock of Oreb.

**Ephraim appeased; Succoth and Penuel punished; the kings of Midian slain** (Judg 8:1-21)
- Ps 83:12 (make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna). Crescent amulets: Isa 3:18; pre-Islamic Arabian lunar symbols.

**Gideon refuses to rule; the golden ephod; seventy sons and Abimelech** (Judg 8:22-35)
- Exod 32:2-4 (golden calf from earrings); 1Sam 8:7 (rejecting God as king). Ishmaelites = Midianites here as in Gen 37:28, 36.

**Abimelech kills his seventy brothers on one stone; Jotham's fable of the trees** (Judg 9:1-21)
- Plant-dispute fables: Sumerian/Akkadian disputation poems (Tamarisk and Palm), Aesop; 2Kgs 14:9 (thistle and cedar). Compare the Persian/Greek fable of the trees' king; Rabbinic and Christian allegory of the bramble.
- Massacre of royal brothers by a usurper: compare 2Kgs 10:1-7 (seventy sons of Ahab), 2Kgs 11:1-2 (Joash hidden), Ottoman fratricide.

**Evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; Gaal's revolt; Shechem sown with salt; millstone at Thebez** (Judg 9:22-57)
- 2Sam 11:21 recalls the millstone at Thebez. Pyrrhus of Epirus killed at Argos by a roof tile thrown by a woman (Plutarch, Pyrrhus 34). Saul asks his armor-bearer to kill him (1Sam 31:4).
- Sowing with salt: Hittite and Assyrian curses on destroyed cities (Ashurbanipal at Susa); the later legend of Carthage. Navel of the earth: Ezek 38:12; Delphi's omphalos; Samaritan tradition of Gerizim as the earth's navel.

**Minor judges Tola and Jair; apostasy to seven gods; God refuses, then is moved** (Judg 10:1-18)
- Compare Deut 32:37-38 ('where are their gods... let them rise up and help you'); Jer 2:28. Sons riding donkeys as status: Judg 12:14; Zech 9:9.

**Jephthah son of a harlot recalled from Tob; his historical argument with the king of Ammon** (Judg 11:1-28)
- Chemosh is properly Moab's god (Mesha stele); here attributed to Ammon. Compare Deut 32:8-9 (nations allotted to divine beings); Mic 4:5. Outcast hero recalled: Coriolanus, David at Ziklag, Idrimi of Alalakh (lived among Habiru).

**Jephthah's vow and the sacrifice of his only daughter** (Judg 11:29-40)
- Iphigenia sacrificed by Agamemnon; Idomeneus' vow to sacrifice the first he meets (Servius on Aeneid 3.121); Gen 22 (only son). Pseudo-Philo LAB 40 names her Seila and gives her lament.
- Annual mourning rites by women: Adonis/Tammuz (Ezek 8:14), Persephone/Kore. Medieval exegetes (Kimhi) argued she was secluded, not killed.

**Ephraim slaughtered at the fords by the Shibboleth test; Ibzan, Elon, Abdon** (Judg 12:1-15)
- Shibboleth tests: the Sicilian Vespers (1282, 'ciciri'), the Parsley Massacre (1937), Flemish 'schild en vriend' (1302). Rabbinic tradition identifies Ibzan with Boaz of Bethlehem (b. Bava Batra 91a).

**Annunciation of Samson's birth to Manoah's wife** (Judg 13:1-25)
- Compare Luke 1 (annunciation to Elizabeth/Mary; John the Baptist abstains from wine, Luke 1:15) and Gen 18 (visitors and meal). Name 'Wonderful' recalls Isa 9:5; Samson's name from shemesh 'sun' invites solar-hero comparisons (Heracles, Gilgamesh).

**Samson's Philistine bride, the lion and the riddle** (Judg 14:1-20)
- Heracles and the Nemean lion; the bugonia (bees born from a carcass) in Virgil Georgics 4. Riddle contests at weddings: Turandot, Oedipus and the Sphinx.

**Samson's revenge, the foxes, the jawbone and the spring** (Judg 15:1-20)
- Ovid Fasti 4.681-712: foxes with burning torches released at the Roman Cerialia. Compare the spring of Hagar/Zamzam and Moses striking the rock.

**Gaza gates, Delilah, and Samson's death in Dagon's temple** (Judg 16:1-31)
- Nisus and Scylla (purple lock), Pterelaus and Comaetho: strength/life in a lock of hair cut by a betraying woman. Heracles' death; Enkidu and the harlot. Rabbinic: Samson's strength and lameness (b. Sotah 10a).

**Danite migration, theft of Micah's idol and conquest of Laish** (Judg 18:1-31)
- Rabbinic tradition (b. Bava Batra 109b) explains the suspended nun as sparing Moses' honor. Compare Rachel's theft of Laban's teraphim (Gen 31) and the Hittite/Mesopotamian practice of capturing enemy gods.

**The Levite's concubine at Gibeah** (Judg 19:1-30)
- Close verbal parallel to Sodom (Gen 19:4-8); Quran 11:78 and 15:71 (Lot offers 'my daughters'). Compare Saul's dismembered oxen (1Sam 11:7) and Mari letters on summoning by cutting a body.

**Wives for Benjamin from Jabesh-gilead and Shiloh** (Judg 21:1-25)
- Rape of the Sabine women (Livy 1.9). The dance in the vineyards resembles m. Ta'anit 4:8 (daughters of Jerusalem dancing in vineyards on 15 Av and Yom Kippur), which links it to this passage.

**Naomi's losses in Moab and Ruth's vow of loyalty** (Ruth 1:1-22)
- Ruth's oath is the rabbinic model of conversion (b. Yevamot 47b). Compare Gen 12:10 and Gen 26:1 (famine migration).

**Ruth gleans in Boaz's field** (Ruth 2:1-23)
- Gleaning laws Lev 19:9-10, Deut 24:19. Greeting 'YHWH be with you' / 'YHWH bless you' (2:4) is cited in m. Berakhot 9:5 as warrant for greeting with the divine name.

**Ruth at Boaz's threshing floor** (Ruth 3:1-18)
- Ezek 16:8 (God spreads his skirt over Jerusalem); Tamar's initiative with Judah (Gen 38). Six measures of barley given as sign (3:15) were read in Ruth Rabbah as six righteous descendants.

**Redemption at the gate, Obed's birth and David's genealogy** (Ruth 4:1-22)
- Deut 25:5-10 (halitzah, removal of the sandal, there as shaming). Matthew 1:3-6 includes Tamar and Ruth among Jesus' ancestresses. Nuzi texts on shoe/foot symbolism in land transfer.

**Hannah's vow and Samuel's birth** (1Sam 1:1-28)
- Hannah's silent prayer is the rabbinic model for the Amidah (b. Berakhot 31a). Compare Quran 3:35-37 (wife of Imran) and Protevangelium of James 4-7 (Anna dedicates Mary, brought to the Temple at three). Elkanah's 'Am I not better to you than ten sons?' (1:8) parallels Ruth 4:15.

**Song of Hannah** (1Sam 2:1-10)
- Model for the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55). 1Sam 2:6 is a classic rabbinic proof-text for resurrection (b. Sanhedrin 92b; Amidah 'mehayyeh metim'). Compare Deut 32:39.

**Sins of Eli's sons and the oracle against Eli's house** (1Sam 2:11-36)
- Luke 2:52 echoes 1Sam 2:26 for Jesus. Protevangelium of James: Mary weaves for the temple veil.

**The call of Samuel in the temple at Shiloh** (1Sam 3:1-21)
- Compare Muhammad's first revelation and the call of the boy in many hagiographies; incubation in temples (Greek Asclepieia, Mesopotamian dream incubation).

**Battle of Ebenezer, capture of the ark and death of Eli** (1Sam 4:1-22)
- Midrash Shmuel / Pseudo-Philo: the runner is Saul carrying the tablets. Capture of divine statues in ANE warfare (Marduk's statue taken to Elam/Hatti).

**The ark in Dagon's temple and the plague of tumors** (1Sam 5:1-12)
- Idols falling before the true God: Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew 22-23 (Egyptian idols fall when the infant Jesus enters), Abraham smashing idols (Quran 21:58). LXX adds mice to 5:6, linking with bubonic plague.

**The ark returned on a cart drawn by milk cows** (1Sam 6:1-21)
- Apollo Smintheus (mouse-god) sends plague in Iliad 1; votive models of afflicted body parts in Greek healing cults.

**Ark at Kiriath-jearim; Samuel's repentance assembly and victory at Mizpah** (1Sam 7:1-17)
- Water libation recalls the Sukkot water-pouring (m. Sukkah 4:9); Targum reads it as pouring out the heart in repentance.

**Israel demands a king; the 'manner of the king'** (1Sam 8:1-22)
- Compare Deut 17:14-20 and Ugaritic/Alalakh royal prerogatives. Rabbinic debate (b. Sanhedrin 20b) whether 1Sam 8 grants royal rights or only warns. Josephus Ant. 6 frames it as theocracy rejected.

**Saul seeks his father's donkeys and meets Samuel** (1Sam 9:1-27)
- Folk motif of the youth who goes looking for lost animals and finds a kingdom (cf. Cyrus raised among herdsmen; Chinese and Indic tales of a cowherd-king).

**Saul anointed, prophesies, and is chosen by lot at Mizpah** (1Sam 10:1-27)
- Reluctant ruler who hides (cf. Moses' objections; Chinese sage-kings refusing the throne, e.g. Xu You). Lot as in Josh 7 (Achan) and Acts 1:26 (Matthias).

**Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead from Nahash the Ammonite** (1Sam 11:1-15)
- Cincinnatus called from the plow (Livy 3.26). 4QSamuel-a has an extra paragraph before 11:1 on Nahash gouging the right eyes of Gadites and Reubenites (also in Josephus Ant. 6.68). Bond with Jabesh recalls Judg 21.

**Samuel's farewell speech and the sign of thunder** (1Sam 12:1-25)
- Moses' denial in Num 16:15; Paul's farewell Acts 20:33. Rabbis read 'Bedan' as Samson (ben Dan), b. Rosh Hashanah 25a.

**Saul's unlawful sacrifice at Gilgal; Philistine monopoly on iron** (1Sam 13:1-23)
- The pim weight is attested on inscribed stone weights, an archaeological anchor. Acts 13:22 cites 'man after my heart' for David.

**Jonathan's exploit at Michmash and Saul's rash oath** (1Sam 14:1-52)
- Jephthah's vow (Judg 11) and Agamemnon/Iphigenia: a father's oath endangers his child, but here the people redeem him. Achan's lot (Josh 7).

**War on Amalek, Agag spared, and Saul's rejection** (1Sam 15:1-35)
- Agag is the ancestor of Haman the Agagite (Esth 3:1); rabbinic tradition says Agag fathered a child the night he was spared. Compare Hosea 6:6, Matt 9:13, Quran on obedience vs. sacrifice (22:37).

**David anointed; the evil spirit and David's lyre** (1Sam 16:1-23)
- Josephus Ant. 6.166-168 and LAB 60 (David's exorcistic psalm, 11Q11 apocryphal psalms against demons). Orpheus' lyre; Pythagorean music therapy. Quran 38:17-20 on David.

**David and Goliath** (1Sam 17:1-58)
- Quran 2:249-251 (Talut's army tested at the river; Dawud kills Jalut). Iliad 7 (Hector's challenge) and the Sinuhe story's duel with the strongman of Retjenu. Judith beheading Holofernes with his own sword (Jdt 13:6-8).

**Jonathan's covenant, Saul's jealousy and Michal's marriage** (1Sam 18:1-30)
- Bellerophon sent by Proetus with a deadly task and given the king's daughter (Iliad 6.155-195); Uriah letter (2Sam 11). Achilles and Patroclus; Gilgamesh and Enkidu. Egyptian reliefs of counting severed hands/phalli of slain enemies (Medinet Habu).

**David escapes through Michal's window; Saul among the prophets at Naioth** (1Sam 19:1-24)
- Rachel hiding Laban's teraphim (Gen 31:34-35). Three sets of messengers, cf. 2Kgs 1 (Elijah and three captains of fifty).

**Jonathan tests Saul at the new moon; the arrow signal** (1Sam 20:1-42)
- David's 'there is but a step between me and death' (20:3). Rabbinic Avot 5:16: love not dependent on anything, like David and Jonathan. Arrow omens: Elisha and Joash (2Kgs 13:15-19); belomancy, Ezek 21:26.

**David at Nob (showbread and Goliath's sword) and feigning madness at Gath** (1Sam 21:1-16)
- Jesus cites the showbread episode (Mark 2:25-26, naming Abiathar). Odysseus feigning madness to avoid the war; Brutus feigning stupidity; Solon feigning madness (Plutarch). Superscription of Ps 34 names the king Abimelech.

**Cave of Adullam and the massacre of the priests of Nob** (1Sam 22:1-23)
- Ps 52 superscription ties to Doeg. Rabbinic lore makes Doeg a great scholar who lost his share in the world to come (m. Sanhedrin 10:2). Robin Hood-type outlaw bands; Muhammad's hijra companions.

**David saves Keilah; Jonathan's visit; pursuit in the wilderness of Ziph and Maon** (1Sam 23:1-28)
- Medieval theology used 23:11-12 as the proof-text for God's 'middle knowledge' of conditional futures (Molina). Ps 54 superscription refers to the Ziphites.

**David spares Saul in the cave at En-gedi** (1Sam 24:1-23)
- Ps 57 and 142 superscriptions ('in the cave'). Compare the Quranic and hadith tradition of Muhammad in the cave of Thawr with pursuers at the mouth, and the spider-web legend. Judah's 'she is more righteous than I' (Gen 38:26).

**Death and burial of Samuel at Ramah** (1Sam 25:1)
- Burial within the house recurs for Joab (1Kgs 2:34). Compare the Islamic practice of burying the Prophet in Aisha's chamber where he died.

**Nabal the fool, Abigail the wise and David's averted vengeance** (1Sam 25:2-44)
- 'Bundle of the living' (25:29) became the Jewish epitaph formula ת.נ.צ.ב.ה on tombstones. Nabal's petrified heart compares with hardening and stone-death motifs (Niobe). Rabbinic tradition counts Abigail among seven prophetesses (b. Megillah 14a).

**David takes Saul's spear and water jug in the camp at Hachilah** (1Sam 26:1-25)
- Doublet of ch. 24. The stolen spear and cup recall Odysseus and Diomedes' night raid (Iliad 10) and the folk motif of the token taken from a sleeper to prove one could have killed him. 26:19 links land and deity, cf. Naaman's earth (2Kgs 5:17).

**David becomes a vassal of Achish and raids from Ziklag** (1Sam 27:1-12)
- The exiled hero who serves a foreign king and deceives him: Themistocles at the Persian court, Alcibiades in Sparta, Coriolanus with the Volsci.

**Saul and the necromancer of En-dor raise Samuel** (1Sam 28:1-25)
- Odysseus' nekyia (Odyssey 11) and Teiresias' prophecy; the Gilgamesh XII raising of Enkidu's spirit. Sir 46:20 and 1Chr 10:13 judge the episode; church fathers debated whether Samuel really appeared (Origen vs. Eustathius). Quranic jinn/sorcery debates also cite it.

**The Philistine lords refuse David in their ranks** (1Sam 29:1-11)
- The comparison of a person to an angel of God recurs in 2Sam 14:17, 20 and 19:28. Achish swearing by YHWH parallels pagan characters invoking the God of Israel (Balaam, Hiram).

**Amalekites burn Ziklag; David recovers all and makes the spoil law** (1Sam 30:1-31)
- Num 31:27 and Josh 22:8 on dividing spoil; Islamic law of ghanima (Quran 8:41; hadith on those who stayed behind, e.g. Uthman at Badr receiving a share). The Egyptian slave guide recalls guides in Arabic maghazi literature.

**Saul and his sons fall on Mount Gilboa** (1Sam 31:1-13)
- Hector's body abused and ransomed (Iliad 22-24); Antigone burying the exposed brother. Saul's suicide paralleled with Ajax and with Brutus/Cato in Roman exempla; the rabbis debated suicide law from it (Genesis Rabbah 34:13).

**The Amalekite who claims to have killed Saul** (2Sam 1:1-16)
- Killing the messenger who claims credit for slaying the king: compare Alexander's execution of Bessus' captors, and Roman reactions to Pompey's head brought to Caesar. Rabbinic midrash identifies the Amalekite as Doeg's son.

**David's lament over Saul and Jonathan (Song of the Bow)** (2Sam 1:17-27)
