- Kesatot have been compared with Mesopotamian binding magic (Maqlu) and with wrist-amulets; soul-trapping as birds has parallels in Egyptian ba-birds and in later Jewish and folk soul-catching.
- The whitewashed wall is taken up in CD 8:12 and 19:24-25 ('builders of the wall ... daubers of whitewash') and in Acts 23:3 / Matt 23:27.

**Idols in the heart; Noah, Daniel and Job could not save the land** (Ezek 14:1-23)
- Dan'el is the righteous judge-king of the Ugaritic Aqhat epic (KTU 1.17-19); compare also Ezek 28:3. Abraham's bargaining for Sodom (Gen 18) is the inverse principle; Jer 15:1 names Moses and Samuel.

**Parable of the useless vine-wood** (Ezek 15:1-8)
- Compare the Israel-as-vine image (Ps 80, Isa 5) and John 15:6 (branches gathered and burned).

**Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot** (Ezek 16:1-43)
- Infant exposure and rescue: Sargon of Akkad legend, Moses (Exod 2), Romulus and Remus, Oedipus; Arabian pre-Islamic burial of infant girls (Quran 81:8-9).
- Neonatal salting: b. Shabbat 129b; Galen on rubbing newborns with salt.
- m. Megillah 4:10 lists Ezek 16 as a chapter not to be read as haftarah (R. Eliezer).

**Like mother like daughter; Sodom and Samaria her sisters; the everlasting covenant** (Ezek 16:44-63)
- The social sin of Sodom recurs in rabbinic lore (m. Avot 5:10 'what is mine is mine'; b. Sanhedrin 109a-b, the bed of Sodom and the girl punished for feeding the poor).

**Riddle of the two eagles, the cedar and the vine; the messianic cedar shoot** (Ezek 17:1-24)
- The tree in which birds nest: Dan 4:9-18 (Nebuchadnezzar's tree), Matt 13:31-32 (mustard seed). Eagle-and-tree fable: the Etana myth (eagle and serpent in the tree); Aesop's eagle and fox. Eagle allegory reused in 4 Ezra 11-12.

**Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance** (Ezek 18:1-32)
- Jer 31:29-30 has the same proverb. Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18 ('no bearer of burdens bears another's burden'). Contrast Exod 20:5. Ezek 18:23/32 underlies 1 Tim 2:4 and 2 Pet 3:9 and the Yom Kippur liturgy.

**Dirge for the princes of Israel - the lioness and her cubs, the uprooted vine** (Ezek 19:1-14)
- Lion-capture imagery (cage, pit, net) matches Assyrian royal lion hunts and the caged-king image in Ashurbanipal's inscriptions; compare Gen 49:9 (Judah as lion's whelp).

**Israel's history of rebellion from Egypt; the second exodus into the wilderness of the peoples** (Ezek 20:1-44)
- The 'laws that were not good' troubled later readers: compare Justin Martyr and the Didascalia on the 'second legislation' as punishment for the calf, and Quran 4:160 (good things forbidden to the Jews for their wrongdoing).
- Ezek 20:32-33 ('I will be king over you') is cited in b. Rosh Hashanah 32b among the Malkhuyot verses.

**Fire in the southern forest; the song of the sword; Babylon's divination at the crossroads; against Ammon** (Ezek 21:1-37)
- Babylonian hepatoscopy (barutu) is amply documented in clay liver models; arrow-divination (istiqsam bi-l-azlam) is condemned in Quran 5:3 and 5:90 and was practiced at the Kaaba before Hubal.

**The city of blood; the dross in the furnace; no man in the breach** (Ezek 22:1-31)
- Zeph 3:3-4 has the same sequence of princes as lions, judges as wolves, prophets and priests; Ps 106:23 has Moses 'standing in the breach'.

**Oholah and Oholibah, the two harlot sisters** (Ezek 23:1-49)
- Nose-and-ear mutilation of adulteresses is attested in Middle Assyrian Laws A 15 and in Egyptian practice (Diodorus 1.78).
- Pekod (Puqudu), Shoa (Sutu) and Koa (Qutu) are Aramean and Mesopotamian peoples in Assyrian records.

**The rusted cauldron; death of the prophet's wife without mourning** (Ezek 24:1-27)
- The 'bread of men' and the covering of the upper lip are the basis of halakhic mourning customs (se'udat havra'ah; b. Moed Qatan 15a-b, 27b, derive many avelut laws from this chapter).
- Blood that cries until covered: Gen 4:10; Job 16:18; the Zechariah blood legend (b. Gittin 57b) in which the priest's blood bubbles in the temple court.

**Oracles against Ammon, Moab, Edom and Philistia** (Ezek 25:1-17)
- Moabite towns Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon and Kiriathaim appear also in the Mesha Stele.

**Oracle on the fall of Tyre and the princes of the sea** (Ezek 26:1-21)
- The later failure of Nebuchadnezzar's 13-year siege is acknowledged in Ezek 29:17-20; Alexander's causeway (332 BCE) was later read as fulfilment (Jerome). Rev 18 reuses the lament of kings and merchants over Babylon.

**Lament over Tyre the great merchant ship** (Ezek 27:1-36)
- Rev 18:11-19 copies the merchant cargo list and the lament of shipmasters and sailors standing far off; compare the ship-of-state allegory (Alcaeus, Horace Odes 1.14).

**The prince of Tyre who said 'I am a god'** (Ezek 28:1-10)
- Ruler claiming divinity and seated on the waters: Quran 28:38 and 79:24 (Pharaoh 'I am your lord most high'); Isa 14:13-14; Acts 12:21-23 (Herod Agrippa). Rabbinic lore (Gen. Rabbah 9:5; Tanhuma Bereshit 7) lists Hiram among those who made themselves gods and had seven heavens built on the sea.

**Lament over the king of Tyre - the gem-covered cherub in Eden cast from God's mountain** (Ezek 28:11-19)
- Read by Origen (De Principiis 1.5.4), Tertullian and later Christian tradition, together with Isa 14:12, as the fall of Satan/Lucifer; compare the Quranic Iblis (proud of being made of fire, 7:12; expelled from the garden, 7:13) and 2 Enoch 29:4-5.
- A different primal-man version of Eden (Adam on the mountain, robed in glory/gems) appears in Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 12 and in the Syriac Cave of Treasures; Mesopotamian jewel-garden of Gilgamesh XI (garden of gem-trees).

**Pharaoh the great dragon of the Nile; Egypt as a reed; Egypt given as Nebuchadnezzar's wages** (Ezek 29:1-21)
- Pharaoh as crocodile/dragon: Isa 27:1, 51:9 (Rahab), Ps 74:13-14; Egyptian Sobek and Apophis; the Ugaritic tnn bound by Anat. Quran 10:90-92 (Pharaoh's body cast out as a sign) and 28:38-39 for Pharaoh's hubris.

**The day of YHWH on Egypt; the cities of Egypt; Pharaoh's broken arms** (Ezek 30:1-26)
- Egyptian royal ideology of the pharaoh's 'strong arm' (khopesh) - Hophra's epithet; compare Exod 6:6. Aven/On = Heliopolis, Pi-beseth = Bubastis of Bastet.

**The great cedar of Eden felled and sent down to Sheol** (Ezek 31:1-18)
- World-tree imagery: Dan 4 (Nebuchadnezzar's tree), the Mesopotamian kiskanu tree of Eridu with roots in the Apsu, the Norse Yggdrasil, the Gilgamesh cedar forest of Humbaba.

**Dirge over Pharaoh the sea dragon caught in God's net** (Ezek 32:1-16)
- Monster netted by a god: Marduk catches Tiamat in a net (Enuma Elish IV 95) and makes heaven and earth from her body; Ninurta and Anzu. Carcass on the mountains recalls 1 Enoch 60:7-9 and 4 Ezra 6:49-52 (Leviathan and Behemoth as food for the righteous).

**Egypt's descent to the Pit among the uncircumcised nations** (Ezek 32:17-32)
- Stratified underworld with ranks of the dead: Isa 14:9-20; Gilgamesh XII and the Descent of Ishtar; Odyssey 11 (the nekyia with heroes); 1 Enoch 22 (compartments of the dead). Burial with weapons under the head matches warrior burials and 1 Macc 13:29.

**The watchman; turn and live; the fugitive's news; Abraham was one; the prophet as love-singer** (Ezek 33:1-33)
- Watchman passage cited in rabbinic discussions of the duty of rebuke (b. Shabbat 54b-55a) and in Christian pastoral tradition (Gregory the Great, Regula Pastoralis); compare Quran 5:105 and 6:69 on not bearing another's guilt once warned.
- Abraham as 'one' (ehad): Isa 51:2; Mal 2:15; Quran 16:120 ('Abraham was a nation (umma)').

**The bad shepherds; God the shepherd; one shepherd David; the covenant of peace** (Ezek 34:1-31)
- John 10:1-16 (the good shepherd, one flock one shepherd); Luke 15:4-7 (seeking the lost sheep); Matt 25:31-46 (separating sheep from goats). b. Yevamot 61a reads 'you are adam' (34:31) to say only Israel is called adam. Mesopotamian kings as 'shepherd' (re'u), e.g. Hammurabi's prologue.

**Against Mount Seir** (Ezek 35:1-15)
- Edom becomes the rabbinic cipher for Rome (Gen. Rabbah 65:21); compare Obadiah and Ps 137:7.

**For my holy name - clean water, new heart, my spirit within; the land like Eden** (Ezek 36:16-38)
- 36:25 is read in m. Yoma 8:9 (R. Akiva: God as the mikveh of Israel) and in Christian baptismal theology (John 3:5); 1QS 4:20-21 (God sprinkles the spirit of truth like waters of purification); Jer 31:31-34 (new covenant on the heart).

**The valley of dry bones** (Ezek 37:1-14)
- b. Sanhedrin 92b debates whether the dead revived were Ephraimites who left Egypt early, and says they married and had children ('a parable' says another view); the Dura-Europos synagogue paints the scene. Zoroastrian Bundahishn 34 (bones reassembled at the frashokereti); Quran 2:259 (the man and his donkey: 'look at the bones, how we raise them and clothe them with flesh') and 2:243 (thousands who died and were revived).

**The two sticks joined - one kingdom under David, an everlasting covenant and sanctuary** (Ezek 37:15-28)
- Rev 21:3 ('the dwelling of God is with men') quotes 37:27; the Joseph/Ephraim stick fed later Messiah ben Joseph traditions and, in Latter-day Saint reading, the Bible and Book of Mormon.

**Gog of Magog invades the land dwelling at the navel of the earth** (Ezek 38:1-23)
- Gog and Magog: Rev 20:8; Quran 18:94-98 and 21:96 (Ya'juj and Ma'juj walled in by Dhu'l-Qarnayn, released at the end); Alexander Romance (Alexander's gate against the unclean nations); rabbinic war of Gog and Magog before the messianic age (b. Berakhot 7b, Sanhedrin 97b). Gog has been linked to Gyges (Gugu) of Lydia.
- Tabbur ha-arets: Judg 9:37; Jubilees 8:19; Tanhuma Kedoshim 10 (Jerusalem the navel, the Foundation Stone); Greek omphalos at Delphi.

**Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds** (Ezek 39:1-29)
- Rev 19:17-18 (the angel calls the birds to 'the great supper of God' to eat the flesh of kings, horses and riders); Joel 3:1 (outpoured spirit). The bone-marker (tsiyyun) underlies the halakhic practice of marking graves to warn priests (m. Shekalim 1:1, m. Moed Qatan 1:2; b. Moed Qatan 5a derives it from 39:15).

**The new temple vision begins - the man of bronze with the measuring reed on a very high mountain** (Ezek 40:1-4)
- The angelic guide with a measuring rod: Zech 2:5-6; Rev 11:1 and 21:15-17 (gold measuring reed of the New Jerusalem on a great high mountain, Rev 21:10); 11QTemple and the Qumran New Jerusalem texts (4Q554). 'Rosh ha-shanah on the tenth' coincides with the jubilee date (Lev 25:9-10); 25 years is half a jubilee.

**Measuring the gates and courts of the visionary temple** (Ezek 40:5-37)
- The three-chambered gate plan matches excavated Iron Age gates at Megiddo, Hazor and Gezer. Middot (Mishnah tractate) and 11QTemple build their temple plans in dialogue with these measurements.

**Slaughtering tables, the priests' chambers, the Zadokites, the inner court and the porch** (Ezek 40:38-49)
- Zadokite exclusivity is the root of the Qumran 'sons of Zadok' self-designation (CD 3:21-4:4 quotes Ezek 44:15) and of the Sadducee name. Compare the two pillars Jachin and Boaz (1 Kgs 7:21).

**The river from the temple and the healing of the sea** (Ezek 47:1-12)
- Compare Rev 22:1-2 (river of the water of life, tree bearing twelve fruits monthly, leaves for healing), Joel 4:18, Zech 14:8.

**Borders and tribal allotment of the land; the city 'YHWH is there'** (Ezek 47:13-48:35)
- Compare Rev 21:12-13 (twelve gates named for the tribes) and the New Jerusalem text from Qumran.

**The statue of four metals and the stone cut without hands** (Dan 2:24-49)
- Compare Hesiod, Works and Days 106-201 (gold, silver, bronze, heroic, iron races) and the Zoroastrian Bahman Yasht tree of four metal branches.

**The golden image and the fiery furnace** (Dan 3:1-30)
- Compare Abraham in Nimrod's furnace (Gen. Rab. 38:13; Quran 21:68-69), the Greek Additions (Prayer of Azariah, Song of the Three) and the Quranic People of the Ditch (85:4-8).

**Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the great tree dream and his madness** (Dan 3:31-4:34)
- Compare the Qumran Prayer of Nabonidus (4Q242), Nabonidus' sojourn at Teima, and Ezek 31 (the cosmic cedar).

**Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall** (Dan 5:1-30)
- Compare Herodotus 1.191 and Xenophon Cyropaedia 7.5 (Babylon taken during a festival).

**Daniel in the lions' den** (Dan 6:1-29)
- Compare Bel and the Dragon 31-42 (Habakkuk carried to the den), and Islamic qibla and fixed daily prayers.

**The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man** (Dan 7:1-28)
- Compare 1 Enoch 14 and 46-48 (Head of Days and Son of Man), Mark 14:62, Rev 1:13-14, 13:1-2, 20:12 and the Ugaritic El/Baal enthronement.

**Daniel's penitential prayer and the seventy weeks** (Dan 9:1-27)
- Compare Mark 13:14 / Matt 24:15 and Christian messianic computations; 1 Macc 1:54; Baruch 1:15-3:8 penitential prayer.

**The vision by the Tigris and the angelic princes of the nations** (Dan 10:1-21)
- Compare Rev 1:13-16, the Zoroastrian yazatas, and the seventy angels of the nations in 1 Enoch 89 and rabbinic sarim.

**Michael arises, the resurrection, and the sealed book** (Dan 12:1-13)
- Compare Rev 10:5-6 (angel swears with raised hand), 1 Enoch 104:2 (righteous shine like stars), Zoroastrian frashokereti and Quranic resurrection from the earth.

**Judgment on priests and kings; 'on the third day he will raise us'** (Hos 5:1-6:11)
- Hos 6:6 is quoted in Matt 9:13 and 12:7; Hos 6:2 is read with the third-day resurrection in Christian and rabbinic tradition.

**The luxuriant vine, the calves of Beth-aven, sow righteousness** (Hos 10:1-15)
- Hos 10:8 is echoed in Luke 23:30 and Rev 6:16.

**'Out of Egypt I called my son'; God's compassion overturns his anger** (Hos 11:1-11)
- Matt 2:15 applies Hos 11:1 to the flight to Egypt.

**Ephraim's idols, God as predator, 'O Death, where are your plagues?'** (Hos 13:1-14:1)
- Hos 13:14 is quoted in 1 Cor 15:55.

**'Return, O Israel'; God as dew and evergreen** (Hos 14:2-10)
- Hos 14:2-10 is the haftarah of Shabbat Shuvah; compare rabbinic teshuvah doctrine (b. Yoma 86a-b).

**The locust army of the Day of YHWH; 'rend your hearts'; restoration** (Joel 2:1-27)
- The phrase moreh li-tsdaqah (Joel 2:23) is linked to the Qumran 'Teacher of Righteousness' (moreh ha-tsedeq).

**The spirit poured on all flesh and signs before the Day** (Joel 3:1-5)
- Quoted at Pentecost in Acts 2:17-21 and in Rom 10:13; compare Num 11:29 ('would that all YHWH's people were prophets').

**Judgment of the nations in the Valley of Jehoshaphat; the fountain from the temple** (Joel 4:1-21)
- Reverses Isa 2:4 / Mic 4:3; compare Rev 14:14-20 (sickle and winepress). The Kidron valley has been identified with Jehoshaphat in Jewish, Christian and Islamic burial tradition.

**Lament for virgin Israel; seek me and live; the Day of YHWH is darkness** (Amos 5:1-27)
- Amos 5:25-27 is quoted (LXX form) in Acts 7:42-43; compare Babylonian Kayamanu (Saturn).

**Woe to the complacent; the marzeah ends; the plague-house** (Amos 6:1-14)
- The marzeah is attested in Ugaritic texts as a feast-association linked with the dead.

**The Lord at the altar, no escape, the sieve, and the fallen booth of David** (Amos 9:1-15)
- Amos 9:11-12 (LXX) is quoted by James in Acts 15:16-17; the 'fallen booth of David' gives the rabbinic messianic epithet bar niflei (b. Sanh. 96b). Compare Ps 139:7-12 on no escape from God.

**Obadiah's vision against Edom's pride** (Obad 1:1-9)
- Obad 1-9 is closely paralleled by Jer 49:7-22. The fall of the star-high proud one recalls Isa 14:12-15 (Helel ben Shahar).
- Rabbinic tradition identifies Edom/Esau with Rome; Obadiah was said (b. Sanh. 39b) to be an Edomite proselyte.

**Edom's crimes against Jacob and the Day of YHWH** (Obad 1:10-21)
- Ps 137:7 also condemns Edom for the day of Jerusalem. Medieval Jewish naming of Spain (Sefarad) and France (Tsarfat) derives from Obad 20.

**Jonah flees to Tarshish and is thrown into the sea** (Jonah 1:1-16)
- Quran 37:139-141: Yunus 'fled (abaqa) to the laden ship', cast lots (sahama) and was among the losers. Quran 21:87: Dhu'l-Nun 'went off in anger' thinking God would not constrain him.
- Mark 4:35-41 (Jesus asleep in the boat in the storm; the sea stilled). Cf. Greek tales of jettisoning a guilty passenger (Arion; Antiphon on the shipwreck as evidence of guilt).

**Jonah swallowed by the great fish and his psalm** (Jonah 2:1-11)
- Quran 21:87-88: in the darknesses he called 'There is no god but You, glory be to You; I have been among the wrongdoers', and God saved him from distress. Quran 37:142-145: the fish swallowed him while blameworthy; had he not glorified God he would have stayed in its belly until the Day of Resurrection; he was cast onto the bare shore, sick. Quran 68:48-49: 'the companion of the fish' who called out while choked with grief (makzum).
- Matt 12:40 (sign of Jonah: three days and nights in the heart of the earth). Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 10 (Jonah sees the sea floor and Leviathan from inside the fish). Greek: Heracles swallowed by the sea monster at Troy; Perseus-Andromeda localized at Joppa.

**Jonah preaches and Nineveh repents down to its animals** (Jonah 3:1-10)
- Quran 10:98: of all towns only the people of Yunus believed and their punishment of disgrace was lifted. Quran 37:147-148: sent to a hundred thousand or more, who believed. Mishnah Taanit 2:1 cites Jonah 3:10 for public fasts; Jonah is read on Yom Kippur afternoon.
- Herodotus 9.24 (Persians shear their horses in mourning for Masistius); Judith 4:10 (cattle in sackcloth).

**Jonah's anger, the qiqayon plant and God's question** (Jonah 4:1-11)
- Quran 37:146: 'We caused a gourd plant (shajaratan min yaqtin) to grow over him'; the Quran sets the plant after the fish, as shelter for the sick prophet, not as a lesson. Quran 21:87 'went off in anger' (mughadiban) parallels Jonah 4:1.
- Jerome's cucurbita/hedera dispute with Augustine over qiqayon. Matt 12:41 (men of Nineveh will rise in judgment).

**YHWH comes down against Samaria; the prophet wails naked** (Mic 1:1-9)
- Isa 20:2-4 (Isaiah walks naked and barefoot three years). Ps 97:5 (mountains melt like wax).

**Punning lament over the towns of the Shephelah** (Mic 1:10-16)
- Isa 10:28-32 is a similar town-by-town march poem. Assyrian annals of Sennacherib's 701 campaign and the Lachish reliefs.

**Woe to those who seize fields; the breaker goes before the flock** (Mic 2:1-13)
- Gen. Rab. 85 and later midrash read ha-porets (Mic 2:13) as the Messiah descended from Perez. Isa 5:8 (woe to those who join house to house).

**Cannibal rulers, hireling prophets and Zion plowed as a field** (Mic 3:1-12)
- Jer 26:18 quotes Mic 3:12 as said in Hezekiah's days. Lev 13:45 (leper covers his upper lip). Ezek 22:27 (officials like wolves).

**Nations stream to Zion; swords into plowshares** (Mic 4:1-8)
- Near-verbatim in Isa 2:2-4; reversed in Joel 4:10 (plowshares into swords). Targum Ps.-Jonathan Gen 35:21: the Messiah will be revealed at Migdal Eder.

**Daughter Zion in labor, exiled to Babylon, threshing the nations** (Mic 4:9-14)
- Rev 12:1-6 (woman in labor). Mark 14:65 / Matt 26:67 (Jesus struck); Lam 3:30.

**The ruler from Bethlehem and the remnant among the nations** (Mic 5:1-8)
- Matt 2:5-6 cites Mic 5:1 for the Messiah's birthplace. b. Sukkah 52b names the seven shepherds (David with Adam, Seth, Methuselah; Abraham, Jacob, Moses) and eight princes (Jesse, Saul, Samuel, Amos, Zephaniah, Zedekiah, Elijah, the Messiah).

**YHWH's lawsuit with his people; what YHWH requires** (Mic 6:1-8)
- The Good Friday Improperia ('Popule meus, quid feci tibi?') build on Mic 6:3. b. Makkot 24a: Micah reduced the 613 commandments to three.

**False scales and futility curses** (Mic 6:9-16)
- Deut 28:38-40 and Amos 5:11 (futility curses); Assyrian treaty curses (Esarhaddon's succession treaty) have the same form.

**No godly man left; who is a God like you?** (Mic 7:1-20)
- Matt 10:35-36 / Luke 12:53 quote Mic 7:6. Mishnah Sotah 9:15 applies it to the generation before the Messiah. The Tashlikh rite on Rosh Hashanah recites Mic 7:18-20 at water.

**The jealous and avenging God against Nineveh** (Nah 1:1-14)
- The Nineveh of Jonah repents; Nahum's Nineveh is destroyed (612 BCE). Tobit 14:4 (Nahum's prophecy against Nineveh).

**The herald of peace and the sack of Nineveh** (Nah 2:1-14)
- Isa 52:7 has the same herald line. Diodorus 2.26-27 and Xenophon (Anabasis 3.4) tell of Nineveh/Larisa falling when the river broke the wall. Assyrian royal lion-hunt reliefs from Nineveh.

**Woe to the bloody city, harlot and sorceress** (Nah 3:1-19)
- Thebes was sacked by Ashurbanipal in 663 BCE. Rev 17-18 (Babylon the harlot and sorceress). Isa 47 (virgin Babylon stripped).

**Habakkuk's complaint and the Chaldean fisherman** (Hab 1:1-17)
- Acts 13:41 quotes Hab 1:5 (LXX). The Qumran Pesher Habakkuk (1QpHab) reads the Chaldeans as the Kittim (Romans) and notes they sacrifice to their standards. Mesopotamian 'net of the god' imagery (Stele of the Vultures; Ninurta's net).

**The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes** (Hab 2:1-20)
- Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11 and Heb 10:37-38 quote Hab 2:3-4. b. Makkot 24a: Habakkuk based all the commandments on one, 'the righteous shall live by his faith'. b. Sanh. 97b reads Hab 2:3 on calculating the end; Maimonides' twelfth principle: 'though he tarry, I will wait for him'. Luke 19:40 (the stones would cry out). Isa 11:9 has the waters-cover-the-sea line.

**Habakkuk's prayer; God marches from Teman** (Hab 3:1-19)
- Ugaritic Baal versus Yamm and Nahar ('Prince Sea, Judge River'); Resheph as a Canaanite plague and war god. Deut 33:2 and Judg 5:4 (God from Seir/Teman). Exod 34:29 qaran (Moses' face 'horned'). Hab 3 is the haftarah for the second day of Shavuot.

**Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah** (Zeph 1:1-18)
- The Latin sequence 'Dies irae, dies illa' is built on Zeph 1:15 (Vulgate). b. Pesahim 7b derives searching for leaven by candlelight from Zeph 1:12. Ezek 7:19 repeats the silver-and-gold line.

**Seek humility; oracles on Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush and Assyria** (Zeph 2:1-15)
- Isa 47:8,10 (Babylon: 'I am, and none besides me'), a phrase otherwise used by God (Isa 45:5-6). Isa 34:11 (owl and hedgehog in ruined Edom).

**The oppressing city, a pure speech for the peoples and God's song over Zion** (Zeph 3:1-20)
- Maimonides (Mishneh Torah, Kings 11) cites Zeph 3:9 for the messianic age. Ethiopian Christian and Beta Israel tradition reads 'beyond the rivers of Cush' (3:10) as their own. Luke 1:28 (rejoice, daughter Zion) echoes 3:14.

**Haggai rouses Zerubbabel and Joshua to rebuild** (Hag 1:1-15)
- Ezra 5:1-2 and 6:14 (Haggai and Zechariah encourage the builders). Mesopotamian temple-rebuilding texts (Gudea cylinders) also link fertility to the temple.

**The glory of this latter house** (Hag 2:1-9)
- Heb 12:26-27 quotes Hag 2:6. Vulgate 'veniet desideratus cunctis gentibus' (2:7) was read as the Messiah. b. Yoma 21b lists five things missing from the second temple.

**A priestly ruling on holiness and impurity; blessing from this day** (Hag 2:10-19)
- Amos 4:9 (blight and mildew 'yet you did not return'). Mishnaic degrees of impurity (rishon, sheni) and m. Hagigah 2 develop this kind of ruling.

**Zerubbabel as God's signet ring** (Hag 2:20-23)
- Reverses Jer 22:24, where Zerubbabel's grandfather Jehoiachin is a signet torn off God's hand. Sir 49:11 praises Zerubbabel 'like a signet on the right hand'.

**Zechariah's call to return** (Zech 1:1-6)
- Mal 3:7 repeats 'Return to me and I will return to you'. Lam 5:21; Quran 2:160 (God turns to those who turn).

**First night vision, the horsemen among the myrtles** (Zech 1:7-17)
- Rev 6:1-8 (four horsemen of different colors). b. Sanh. 93a reads the myrtles as the righteous (Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah) and the rider as Gabriel; Esther's name Hadassah (myrtle). Job 1:7 (the satan roams the earth).

**Second night vision, four horns and four craftsmen** (Zech 2:1-4)
- b. Sukkah 52b: the four craftsmen are Messiah son of David, Messiah son of Joseph, Elijah and the Righteous Priest (Melchizedek). Dan 7-8 (horns as kings); 1 Enoch 90.

**Third night vision, the measuring line and the wall of fire** (Zech 2:5-17)
- Ezek 40-42 and Rev 11:1 and 21:15-17 (measuring the temple/city); Rev 21 (city of God). 'Admat ha-qodesh' is the source of the later term 'Holy Land' (terra sancta).

**Fourth vision, the high priest, the satan and the Branch** (Zech 3:1-10)
- Jude 9 ('The Lord rebuke you' to the devil disputing over Moses' body); Rev 12:10 (the accuser cast down). Job 1-2 (the satan in the court). Amos 4:11 (brand plucked from burning). Zoroastrian heavenly-trial imagery; Iranian 'adversary' figures. Rabbinic midrash (b. Sanh. 93a) explains Joshua's soiled clothes by his sons' foreign marriages.

**Fifth vision, the lampstand, the two olive trees and Zerubbabel** (Zech 4:1-14)
- Rev 11:4 (the two witnesses are the two olive trees and two lampstands). Qumran messianism of two anointed (Aaron and Israel), 1QS 9:11. Zech 2:14-4:7 is the haftarah of Shabbat Hanukkah. Iranian seven Amesha Spentas and Mesopotamian seven-eyed imagery have been compared to the seven eyes.

**Sixth vision, the flying scroll** (Zech 5:1-4)
- Twenty by ten cubits are the dimensions of Solomon's temple porch (1Kgs 6:3). Ezek 2:9-3:3 (scroll written front and back). Greek and Near Eastern curse tablets (defixiones) that 'go out' against thieves and perjurers.

**Seventh vision, the woman in the ephah carried to Shinar** (Zech 5:5-11)
- Rev 17-18 (the woman Babylon). Gen 11:2 (Shinar, the plain of Babel). Commentators compare winged female genii in Assyrian art and the removal of a goddess image (Asherah/Queen of Heaven) to Babylon. 1 Enoch's binding of sin under stones.

**Eighth vision, four chariots between bronze mountains** (Zech 6:1-8)
- Shamash rises between twin mountains on Mesopotamian cylinder seals; Mashu twin-peaked mountain in Gilgamesh IX. Rev 6:1-8; 2Kgs 23:11 (horses of the sun).

**Crowns for Joshua; the man named Branch** (Zech 6:9-15)
- Jer 23:5 and 33:15 (righteous Branch of David). Targum renders Tsemah as 'Messiah'. Heb 7 (priest-king); Qumran priestly and royal messiahs. Christian 'Ecce homo' readings of 6:12 (LXX Anatole, 'Dawn', later a name for Christ).

**The Bethel delegation's question about fasting** (Zech 7:1-14)
- Isa 58:3-7 (the fast God chooses). Shamir is, in rabbinic legend (m. Avot 5:6; b. Gittin 68a), the stone-cutting creature Solomon used to build the temple without iron tools; Ezek 3:9 and Jer 17:1 use shamir for adamant.

**Ten promises for Zion; fasts become feasts; ten men grasp a Jew's garment** (Zech 8:1-23)
- The four fasts are traditionally 17 Tammuz, 9 Av, the Fast of Gedaliah and 10 Tevet (b. Rosh Hashanah 18b). Zech 8:16 is cited in m. Avot 1:18 (truth, judgment and peace). Zech 8:23 and the kanaf (tassel corner) of Num 15:38; Matt 9:20 (the woman touches the hem of Jesus' garment).

**Oracle against Hadrach, Tyre and Philistia** (Zech 9:1-8)
- Often linked to Alexander's march (332 BCE) and siege of Tyre (Arrian, Anabasis 2.15-24). Ezek 28 (wisdom and wealth of Tyre).

**Zion's humble king on a donkey; sons of Zion against Javan** (Zech 9:9-17)
- Matt 21:5 and John 12:15 quote Zech 9:9 for the entry into Jerusalem (Matthew has two animals). b. Sanh. 98a: if Israel is worthy the Messiah comes on the clouds (Dan 7), if not, poor and riding on a donkey. Hellenistic-era reading of 'Javan'.

**Rain from YHWH, false teraphim and the regathering of Judah and Joseph** (Zech 10:1-12)
- Targum Jonathan renders the cornerstone and tent peg of 10:4 as king and Messiah. Isa 5:26 and 7:18 (God whistles for nations).

**The shepherd of the flock of slaughter, two staffs and thirty pieces of silver** (Zech 11:1-17)
- Matt 26:15 and 27:3-10 (Judas' thirty silver thrown in the temple, the potter's field; attributed to Jeremiah). b. Taanit 9a reads the three shepherds as Moses, Aaron and Miriam who died in one month. Exod 21:32 (thirty shekels for a gored slave).

**Jerusalem a cup of reeling; mourning for the one they pierced** (Zech 12:1-14)
- John 19:37 and Rev 1:7 cite Zech 12:10. b. Sukkah 52a applies the pierced one to Messiah son of Joseph and derives the separate women's gallery at the water-drawing celebration from 12:12. Hadad-rimmon recalls rites for the storm god Hadad/Rimmon (cf. Tammuz wailing, Ezek 8:14), or the lament for Josiah slain at Megiddo (2Chr 35:22-25, Targum).

**A cleansing fountain, the end of prophecy, and the struck shepherd** (Zech 13:1-9)
- Mark 14:27 / Matt 26:31 quote Zech 13:7 at the disciples' flight. Damascus Document (CD 19:7-9) cites it too. Amos 7:14 ('I am no prophet'). 2Kgs 1:8 (Elijah's hairy garment), Matt 3:4 (John's camel hair). t. Sotah 13 and b. Bava Batra 12b on the cessation of prophecy.

**The final day on the Mount of Olives; living waters; Sukkot for the nations** (Zech 14:1-21)
- Zech 14:9 closes the Aleinu prayer. Zech 14 is the haftarah of the first day of Sukkot; the water libation and rain prayers of Sukkot (m. Sukkah 4-5). Ezek 47 and Rev 22:1 (river from the temple); Joel 4:18. Acts 1:11-12 (return to the Mount of Olives); Jewish burial on the Mount of Olives. John 2:16 (no trading in my Father's house). Josephus, Ant. 9.225 (Uzziah's earthquake split a hill west of Jerusalem). Amos 1:1 (earthquake).

**I loved Jacob, Esau I hated** (Mal 1:1-5)
- Rom 9:13 quotes Mal 1:2-3. b. Megillah 15a identifies Malachi with Ezra or Mordecai; Targum adds 'whose name is Ezra the scribe'.

**Priests who despise God's name with blemished offerings** (Mal 1:6-14)
- Mal 1:11 became a proof text for the Christian Eucharist as the 'pure sacrifice' (Didache 14; Justin, Dialogue 41; Council of Trent). Rabbinic readings (b. Menahot 110a) apply it to Torah scholars or to prayer in the diaspora.

**The covenant with Levi and the corrupt priests** (Mal 2:1-9)
- m. Avot 1:12 (Aaron loved peace and pursued peace) builds on Mal 2:6. Deut 33:8-11 (blessing of Levi); Num 25:12-13 (covenant of peace with Phinehas). Aramaic Levi Document and Testament of Levi.

**One father, one God; foreign wives and the wife of one's youth** (Mal 2:10-16)
- b. Gittin 90b: 'the altar sheds tears over one who divorces the wife of his youth'. Matt 19:3-9 and Mark 10 (divorce and 'from the beginning'). Ezra 9-10 and Neh 13:23-27 (foreign wives). 4Q271 and CD 4 (Qumran marriage rules).

**Where is the God of justice? The messenger who prepares the way** (Mal 2:17-3:5)
- Mark 1:2, Matt 11:10 and Luke 7:27 apply Mal 3:1 to John the Baptist; Luke 2:22-38 (the Lord comes to his temple). Exod 23:20 ('I send an angel before you') is the model. Handel's Messiah ('But who may abide', 'And he shall purify'). Elijah as 'angel of the covenant' at circumcision (Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 29; chair of Elijah).

**Return to me; will a man rob God? Test me with the tithe** (Mal 3:6-12)
- b. Taanit 9a: tithing is the one commandment in which one may test God ('aser bishvil she-tit'asher'). Neh 10:38-40 and 13:10-12 (tithes brought to the storehouse chambers). Deut 6:16 (do not test God) is the contrast.

**The book of remembrance and the sun of righteousness** (Mal 3:13-21)
- The winged sun disk of Egyptian, Assyrian and Achaemenid iconography (Ahura Mazda's faravahar) is commonly compared with Mal 3:20. Charles Wesley's 'Risen with healing in his wings'; Luke 1:78 (dayspring). Esth 6:1 and Dan 7:10, Rev 20:12 (books of record); Ps 56:9.

**Remember Moses; Elijah sent before the great day** (Mal 3:22-24)
- Sir 48:10 (Elijah to restore the tribes of Jacob); Luke 1:17 (John comes in the spirit and power of Elijah); Matt 11:14, 17:10-13 and Mark 9:11-13. m. Eduyot 8:7 (Elijah comes not to declare clean or unclean but to make peace); Elijah's cup at the Passover seder; 'teiku' (Elijah will resolve undecided questions). Quran 6:85 and 37:123-132 name Ilyas among the prophets, though not his return. LXX and Christian Bibles place this passage at the end of the Old Testament as a bridge to the Gospels.

**The Opening (al-Fatiha)** (1:1-7)
- Compare Psalm 1 (two ways), Psalm 86:11 'teach me your way', and the Lord's Prayer (Matt 6:9-13) as communal prayer opening a corpus.

**Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites** (2:1-20)
- Compare Isa 6:9-10 (hearts fat, ears heavy, eyes shut) and Matt 13:13-15.

**Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat** (2:21-29)
- Seven heavens: compare b. Hagigah 12b, 2 Enoch, Ascension of Isaiah.

**Adam, the angels and Iblis** (2:30-39)
- Angels' objection: Gen. Rabbah 8:5, b. Sanhedrin 38b. Angels bowing and Satan's refusal: Life of Adam and Eve 12-16, Cave of Treasures 2-3. Adam naming beyond the angels: Gen. Rabbah 17:4.

**Exodus, the calf and the wilderness** (2:49-61)
- Hitta: compare targumic/rabbinic midrash on entering the land; 'kill yourselves' corresponds to Exod 32:27-28.

**Covenant at the mountain and the Sabbath-breakers** (2:62-66)
- Mountain held over Israel like a cask: b. Shabbat 88a, b. Avodah Zarah 2b.

**The cow and the slain man** (2:67-74)
- Combines Num 19 (red heifer) and Deut 21:1-9 (eglah arufah). Compare b. Yoma 42 and Num. Rabbah 19 on the red heifer; a Dama ben Netinah story (b. Qiddushin 31a) about buying a red heifer.

**Polemic with the People of the Book** (2:75-101)
- 'We hear and disobey' plays on Deut 5:27 / Exod 24:7 'we will do and we will hear' (na'aseh ve-nishma).

**Solomon, the devils and Harut and Marut** (2:102-103)
- Fallen angels teaching sorcery: 1 Enoch 6-8 (Shemihazah and Asael), Midrash of Shemhazai and Azael; Haurvatat and Ameretat (Zoroastrian Amesha Spentas) as possible name-source. Solomon and demons: Testament of Solomon, b. Gittin 68.

**Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God** (2:104-121)
- Ra'ina: compare the Hebrew/Aramaic ra' 'evil' or re'enu; cf. Q 4:46.

**Abraham, Ishmael and the House** (2:122-141)
- Jacob's deathbed confession: Gen. Rabbah 98:3, b. Pesahim 56a (sons answer 'Hear O Israel'). Abraham's trials: m. Avot 5:3 (ten trials). Sibgha may echo Christian baptism (Syriac sb'). Gen 21 Ishmael in the wilderness.

**The change of qibla** (2:142-152)
- Prayer toward Jerusalem: Dan 6:11, 1 Kgs 8:44-48, m. Berakhot 4:5-6.

**Patience, Safa and Marwa, signs of creation** (2:153-167)
- Safa-Marwa running is traditionally tied to Hagar's search for water (Gen 21:14-19).

**Lawful food and true piety** (2:168-177)
- Compare the Noahide/apostolic decree, Acts 15:20, 29 (idol food, blood, strangled, fornication), and Lev 17. Necessity: pikuach nefesh.

**Retaliation and bequests** (2:178-182)
- Ransom for murder allowed here, contrast Num 35:31 (no kofer for a murderer).

**The fast of Ramadan** (2:183-188)
- White and black thread: m. Berakhot 1:2 (distinguish blue from white for the Shema at dawn). Day of Atonement fast and Lent as precedents; Manichaean fasting month.

**New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites** (2:189-203)
- Nazirite shaving at completion of the vow (Num 6:18) vs shaving after the offering. Entering houses from the back: pre-Islamic ihram custom.

**The corrupter, God in clouds, one community, fighting in the sacred month** (2:204-218)
- God coming in clouds with angels: Dan 7:13, Matt 24:30, Zech 14:5.

**Oaths, divorce, nursing and widowhood** (2:224-242)
- Deut 24:1-4 forbids return to the first husband after a second marriage; the Quran makes the intervening marriage a precondition. Two-year nursing: b. Ketubot 60a (24 months). Widow's three-month wait in m. Yevamot 4:10.

**The thousands who died and were revived; a loan to God** (2:243-245)
- Ezek 37:1-14 (valley of dry bones); b. Sanhedrin 92b names them as Ephraimites who left Egypt early. Prov 19:17 'he who is kind to the poor lends to YHWH'.

**Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath)** (2:246-252)
- Judg 7:4-7 (Gideon's water test), 1 Sam 8-10, 1 Sam 6 (ark returns on a cart), 1 Sam 17. Sakina = Hebrew shekhinah. Talut likely a rhyme-name on Jalut, from tul 'height'.

**Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse** (2:253-257)
- Isa 66:1 'heaven is my throne and the earth my footstool'; Isa 40:28.

**Abraham disputes with the king** (2:258)
- Nimrod and Abraham: Gen. Rabbah 38:13, Pseudo-Jonathan Gen 11:28; Tanna debe Eliyahu.

**The man who passed a ruined town** (2:259)
- Abimelech's 66-year sleep in 4 Baruch (Paralipomena Jeremiae) 5, with fresh figs; Honi the Circle-Drawer's 70-year sleep (b. Taanit 23a); Ezra/Uzayr in tafsir.

**Abraham and the four birds** (2:260)
- Gen 15:9-11 (heifer, goat, ram, dove and pigeon; birds not divided); Apocalypse of Abraham 12-15.

**Parables of charity** (2:261-274)
- Parable of the sower (Mark 4:8, thirty, sixty, hundredfold); Matt 6:2-4 (secret alms); m. Shekalim 5:6 (chamber of secrets).

**The debt verse** (2:282-283)
- Jer 32:10-14 (sealed deed and witnesses); rabbinic shetar.

**Closing confession and prayer** (2:284-286)
- Sami'na wa-ata'na answers 2:93; cf. Deut 5:27. Burden (isr) of predecessors: Matt 11:30, Acts 15:10.

**Owner of sovereignty** (3:26-32)
- Dan 2:21, 4:14 (gives kingdom to whom he wills); 1 Sam 2:7-8 (Song of Hannah).

**The family of Imran, Mary and Zechariah** (3:33-44)
- Protevangelium of James 4-9 (Anna's vow, Mary in the temple fed by an angel, Joseph chosen by rods); Luke 1:5-25 (Zechariah struck mute until birth, here three days). 1 Sam 1 (Hannah). Imran = Amram, father of Miriam (Num 26:59).

**The annunciation and the mission of Jesus** (3:45-63)
- Luke 1:26-38 (annunciation); Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2 (clay birds); Arabic Infancy Gospel 1 (speaks in the cradle); Rom 5:14 / 1 Cor 15:45 (Adam typology); Num 5 ordeal and 1 Kgs 18 contest as forms of divine adjudication.

**The common word; Abraham neither Jew nor Christian** (3:64-80)
- Abraham before the law: Rom 4:9-16, Gal 3:17; Jubilees and Sirach 44:20 make him keep the law in advance (cf. Gen 26:5).

**Israel's self-imposed food law and the House at Bakka** (3:92-101)
- Gen 32:33 (gid ha-nasheh); tafsir also names camel meat and milk. Ps 84:7 'valley of Baca'.

**Badr and Uhud** (3:121-175)
- Josh 7 (Achan's theft of the herem causes defeat); 2 Kgs 6:16-17 (heavenly army); 2 Macc 10:29-30 (angelic horsemen); Ps 78:9 (Ephraimites turned back).

**Misers, those who called God poor, and the fire-consumed offering** (3:176-189)
- 1 Kgs 18:24, 38 (Elijah's fire-consumed offering as test of the true god); Lev 9:24. 'God is poor': cf. Prov 19:17 read as lending to God (2:245).

**One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift** (4:1-10)
- 4:1 'created from it its mate' is the Quran's Eve-from-Adam; compare Gen 2:21-22 and Gen Rabbah 17-18.
- Bride-gift to the woman herself vs. the mohar paid to the father (Exod 22:15-16; Gen 34:12) and the rabbinic ketubbah.

**The fixed shares of inheritance** (4:11-14)
- Compare the daughters of Zelophehad (Num 27; 36) and Mishnah Bava Batra 8 on order of heirs; the rabbinic husband inherits his wife, the wife does not inherit (Quran gives both).
- Compare Job 42:15, where Job's daughters inherit among their brothers.

**Indecency, four witnesses, and the limits of repentance** (4:15-18)
- Contrast m. Avot 2:10 'repent one day before your death' and m. Sanh. 6:2 confession at execution; Wisdom of Solomon and Pharaoh's last-minute faith (Quran 10:90-91).

**Inheriting women, the dowry, and the forbidden degrees** (4:19-28)
- 4:23 'except what is past' (illā mā qad salaf) on two sisters invites Jacob, Leah and Rachel (Gen 29); rabbinic discussion of the patriarchs before Sinai.
- Compare Lev 18 and 20 and the rabbinic extension to milk-kinship (absent in Judaism; present in Islam).

**Wealth by consent, major sins, and discord in marriage** (4:29-35)
- Rabbinic categories of grave vs. light commandments (ḥamurot / qalot) and the three cardinal sins, cf. 'kabāʾir'.

**The circle of kindness, misers, and the atom's weight** (4:36-42)
- 4:38 giving to be seen: compare Matt 6:1-4.
- 4:42 compare Hos 10:8, Luke 23:30 and Rev 6:16 (mountains, fall on us).

**Prayer not while drunk; bathing and dry ablution** (4:43)
- b. Berakhot 15a: one without water wipes his hands with earth or a pebble before prayer; and m. Berakhot on not praying drunk (b. Eruvin 64a).

**Shifted words, 'we hear and disobey', and the people of the Sabbath** (4:44-57)
- Exod 24:7 na'aseh ve-nishma; b. Shabbat 88a-b and the Aramaic/Hebrew pun shamaʿnu ve-ʿaṣinu (Targum/rabbinic 'we heard and rebelled', cf. Deut 5:24).
- 4:56 renewed skins: compare later Jewish and Christian hell-tours (Apocalypse of Peter) on perpetual torment of the body.

**Trusts, obedience to authority, and the hypocrites who seek other judges** (4:58-70)
- 4:66 'kill yourselves' is the Quranic reading of Exod 32:26-29; compare Targum and midrash on the Levites' slaughter.

**Fighting for the oppressed; death in lofty towers** (4:71-87)
- 4:78 compare Amos 9:2-3 and Obad 4 (though you build high, I will bring you down) and the 'appointment in Samarra' tale (b. Sukkah 53a, the two scribes of Solomon).

**Accidental and deliberate killing of a believer** (4:92-94)
- Num 35 and Deut 19 (refuge) vs. ancient Near Eastern composition payments (Hittite laws, Middle Assyrian) that the Quranic diya resembles.

**Those who strive and those who sit; the angels' question at death** (4:95-100)
- Num 32:6 'shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?' (ha-aḥeikhem yavo'u la-milḥamah ve-attem teshvu poh).
- Angels questioning the dead: later Munkar and Nakir; cf. rabbinic ḥibbut ha-qever and the angel Dumah.

**Shortened prayer and prayer in shifts under arms** (4:101-104)
- Neh 4:11-17 (builders with one hand on the work and a weapon in the other, half standing guard).
- 4:103 compare Deut 6:7 'when you sit, walk, lie down and rise' (the Shema).

**Guilt cast on the innocent and the Prophet who must not defend traitors** (4:105-115)
- Tradition ties 4:105-112 to a theft blamed on a Jew (Ṭuʿma b. Ubayriq): a Quranic case of a Muslim court exonerating a Jew.

**Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend** (4:116-126)
- Satan's 'appointed share' of humans: Jubilees 10:8-9 (Mastema keeps a tenth of the spirits), and the Devil's portion in the Life of Adam and Eve.

**Orphan girls, reconciliation, the suspended wife, and justice against oneself** (4:127-135)
- 4:129 'like one suspended' (kal-muʿallaqa) and the rabbinic ʿagunah, the 'anchored' wife (cf. Ruth 1:13 te'agenah).

**Articles of faith; hypocrites wavering between two sides** (4:136-152)
- 4:143 compare 1 Kgs 18:21 and Rev 3:15-16 (neither cold nor hot).

**The indictment of Israel; the Messiah not crucified but raised** (4:153-162)
- 4:154 mountain raised over Israel: b. Shabbat 88a (God held Sinai over them like a cask).
- 4:157 shubbiha lahum: Basilides in Irenaeus Adv. Haer. 1.24.4 (Simon of Cyrene crucified in Jesus' likeness); Second Treatise of the Great Seth; Apocalypse of Peter (Nag Hammadi).
- 4:156 slander against Mary: Toledot Yeshu and b. Shabbat 104b on Pandera.

**The chain of revelation; Jesus, word and spirit; 'say not three'** (4:163-175)
- 4:172 'servant of God' recalls Isaiah's servant songs and Acts 3:13; 4:171 Logos and Spirit Christology (Syriac 'word of God').

**The final ruling on kalāla** (4:176)
- Compare Num 27:9 (brothers inherit when no son or daughter) and the rabbinic exclusion of sisters when brothers exist.

**Contracts, pilgrim sanctity and the forbidden foods** (5:1-5)
- Acts 15:20, 29 (abstain from idol sacrifices, blood and what is strangled) is the closest parallel to 5:3.
- Rabbinic terefah categories (m. Ḥullin 3) include animals mauled, fallen or with crushed organs; Exod 22:30.

**Ablution, the covenant 'we hear and obey', and justice despite hatred** (5:6-11)
- Exod 30:17-21 and 40:31; rabbinic netilat yadayim and the priests' qiddush yadayim ve-raglayim.

**Israel's covenant and twelve chiefs; the Christians' forgotten portion** (5:12-19)
- 5:18 compare m. Avot 3:14 'beloved are Israel, for they are called children of God'.

**The refusal to enter the holy land and forty years of wandering** (5:20-26)
- Num 13-14 and Deut 1:26-40; 'two men' = Joshua and Caleb, unnamed here.

**The two sons of Adam, the raven, and whoever saves one life** (5:27-32)
- Raven teaching burial: Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 21 and Tanḥuma Bereshit 10 (a raven buries its fellow before Adam and Eve).
- 5:32 is m. Sanhedrin 4:5, derived from 'the bloods (deme) of your brother' (Gen 4:10); 'written for the Children of Israel'.
- Abel's speech before the murder: Targum Neofiti/Pseudo-Jonathan Gen 4:8 (dispute in the field).

**Penalty for waging war on God; the ransom of the earth; the thief's hand** (5:33-40)
- Contrast biblical theft law (double, fourfold and fivefold restitution, Exod 21:37-22:3) with amputation; Code of Hammurabi uses mutilation for some offenses.

**Judging by the Torah, the Gospel and the Quran; eye for eye** (5:41-50)
- 5:45 quotes Exod 21:23-25 / Lev 24:20 / Deut 19:21 with nose and ear added; 'whoever remits it' parallels Matt 5:38-39 and rabbinic monetary commutation (b. Bava Qamma 83b).
- 5:41-43 linked by tradition to the stoning-verse case of two Jewish adulterers brought to Muhammad.

**Allies, apostates replaced, the mocked call to prayer, apes and swine** (5:51-63)
- Transformation of sinners into apes: b. Sanhedrin 109a (builders of Babel became apes, spirits and demons).

**'God's hand is fettered'; the blessings of observing the Torah** (5:64-71)
- 5:64 compare Isa 50:2, 59:1 (is my hand shortened?), Lam 2:3 (he drew back his right hand) and Num 11:23.
- 5:66 compare Lev 26:3-5, Deut 28:12 and Mal 3:10 (windows of heaven).

**Against the deification of Jesus; the weeping Christians** (5:72-86)
- 5:75 'they both ate food': anti-docetic and anti-divinity argument; cf. Luke 24:42-43.
- 5:78 curse 'on the tongue of David' (Ps 69:23-29; 109) and of Jesus (Matt 23).

**Lawful good things, oath expiation, wine and gambling, game in iḥrām** (5:87-100)
- Lev 5:4-13: graded expiation for a rash oath (lamb, birds, flour) parallels the graded kaffāra of 5:89.
- 5:87 against self-imposed abstinence: compare the Nazirite's sin offering (Num 6:11; b. Taʿanit 11a).

**Questions not to ask; the freed camels of the pagans** (5:101-105)
- Ben Sira 3:21-22 'seek not what is too wonderful for you' and m. Ḥagigah 2:1.

**Witnesses to a bequest made far from home** (5:106-108)
- Deathbed gift (matenat shekhiv meraʿ) and witness rules in m. Bava Batra 9; oath of witnesses in Lev 5:1.

**Jesus' miracles, the table from heaven, and Jesus questioned at judgment** (5:109-120)
- Ps 78:19-20 'Can God set a table in the wilderness?' (ha-yukhal el la-ʿarokh shulḥan ba-midbar) and manna; John 6:30-31; the Last Supper and Acts 10:11 (sheet let down from heaven).
- Clay birds: Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2; speaking in cradle: Arabic Infancy Gospel 1.
- 5:116 Mary as deity: Epiphanius, Panarion 78-79 (Collyridians).

**Darkness and light, clay and two terms, and those who would not believe** (6:1-11)
- 6:1 against dualism (Zoroastrian/Manichaean light and darkness), as Isa 45:7 against Persian dualism.

**Mercy written on himself; the idolaters' denial at the gathering** (6:12-32)
- 6:12 'mercy written on himself': b. Berakhot 7a (God prays that his mercy overcome his anger) and the hadith 'my mercy precedes my wrath'.
- 6:27-28 compare Luke 16:27-31 (the rich man asks to warn his brothers).

**The Prophet consoled; a ladder to the sky; animals as communities** (6:33-50)
- 6:35 compare Amos 9:2 (dig into Sheol, climb to heaven) and Ps 139:8; Jacob's ladder (Gen 28:12).
- 6:38 animals gathered to their Lord: animal judgment in later hadith; Jonah 4:11 and Ps 104 on animals in God's care.

**Do not drive away the poor; the keys of the unseen and the falling leaf** (6:51-62)
- 6:59 compare Matt 10:29-30 (no sparrow falls without your Father) and Gen Rabbah 79:6 (no bird is caught without heaven's decree).
- 6:60 sleep as one-sixtieth of death (b. Berakhot 57b) and the Jewish morning blessing for the returned soul (Elohai neshamah).

**Rescue in the darkness of land and sea; the bewildered man; the trumpet** (6:63-73)
- 6:68 compare Ps 1:1 (nor sit in the seat of scoffers) and m. Avot 3:2.
- 6:63-64 compare Ps 107:23-32 and the sailors of Jonah 1.

**Abraham, Azar and the star, moon and sun** (6:74-83)
- Apocalypse of Abraham 7 (fire, water, earth, sun, moon, stars rejected in turn); Jubilees 12:16-18; Josephus Ant. 1.155-156; Ma'aseh Avraham (Abraham in the cave worships sun then moon).
- Āzar: Eusebius' Athar? Theories link to Eliezer or Terah; cf. Hebrew 'ezer.

**Abraham's line of eighteen prophets; Torah in sheets; the false claimant** (6:84-94)
- 6:94 compare Job 1:21, Qoh 5:14 and m. Avot 6:9 (at death neither silver nor gold accompany a man).
- 6:91 'sheets' (qarāṭīs, Greek chartēs): written Torah scrolls vs. the oral 'much you hide'.

**Splitter of seed and dawn; stars for navigation; do not revile their gods** (6:95-108)
- 6:108 Josephus Ant. 4.207 and Against Apion 2.237; Philo Spec. Leg. 1.53 (do not blaspheme others' gods) on Exod 22:27 LXX.
- 6:103 compare Exod 33:20 and John 1:18.

**Sworn oaths for a sign; even the dead speaking would not convince** (6:109-117)
- 6:111 Luke 16:31: 'neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead'.

**Eat what God's name is spoken over; the opened breast; jinn and humans judged** (6:118-135)
- 6:121 compare the rabbinic requirement of the blessing at shechitah and m. Ḥullin 2:8 (slaughter in the name of mountains etc. forbidden).
- 6:122 compare Eph 5:14 and John 8:12.

**Pagan portions and taboos; eight pairs; what is forbidden to all and to the Jews** (6:136-150)
- 6:146 fat 'on the backs' and 'mixed with bone' tracks the rabbinic distinction of forbidden ḥelev vs. permitted shuman (b. Ḥullin 49b, 93a); entrails (al-ḥawāyā).
- 6:136 portion for God and for idols: compare 2 Kgs 17:33 (they feared YHWH and served their own gods).

**The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue)** (6:151-157)
- Ibn ʿAbbās and later exegetes compare 6:151-153 to the Ten Commandments (and to 17:22-39); the 'two ways' of Didache 1-6 and Deut 30:15-19.

**Tenfold reward; my life and death for God; no bearer bears another's burden** (6:158-165)
- 6:160 compare t. Sotah 4:1 and b. Sanhedrin 100b (the measure of good exceeds the measure of punishment) and Exod 20:5-6 (to the third generation vs. to thousands).
- 6:164 Ezek 18:20 and Deut 24:16.

**Opening letters, destroyed towns and the weighing of deeds** (7:1-10)
- Compare the Egyptian weighing of the heart (Book of the Dead 125), Testament of Abraham 12-13 (A) and Dan 5:27 (tekel).

**The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall** (7:11-25)
- Compare Life of Adam and Eve (Vita) 12-16, where Satan refuses to worship the image of God; Cave of Treasures 2-3; Gospel of Bartholomew 4.
- The respite granted to the devil compares with Jubilees 10:8-9 (Mastema's tenth of the spirits) and Rev 20:2-3.

**Children of Adam - clothing, Satan's enmity, what God forbids** (7:26-34)
- The pre-fall garment matches rabbinic/targumic traditions of garments of light or glory (Gen Rab 20:12, 'or' vs 'or).

**Hell's quarrels, the camel and the needle, the people of the Heights** (7:35-53)
- Camel and needle: Matt 19:24 / Mark 10:25 / Luke 18:25; b. Berakhot 55b and b. Bava Metzia 38b (elephant through a needle's eye).
- Water begged across the gulf: Luke 16:19-31 (rich man and Lazarus); 1 Enoch 22 (compartments of the dead); the A'raf compares with the Zoroastrian hamestagan and the Christian limbus.

**Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection** (7:54-58)
- Good and bad land: compare the parable of the sower (Mark 4:3-20) and 4 Ezra 8:41.
- Rain and resurrection: b. Ta'anit 7a ('the day of rain is greater than the resurrection of the dead'), the second benediction of the Amidah (mashiv ha-ruah).

**Hud and the people of Ad** (7:65-72)
- Ad and Iram are tied by commentators to giant pre-Israelite peoples (Rephaim, Emim, Deut 2:10-11, 20-21).

**Salih, Thamud and the she-camel** (7:73-79)
- Thamud are attested in Assyrian annals (Sargon II) and the Ruwafa inscription; the rock-cut tombs of Hegra (Mada'in Salih) are Nabataean.

**Shu'ayb and Midian** (7:85-93)
- Shu'ayb of Midian is traditionally identified with Jethro/Reuel (Exod 2-3, 18).

**Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues** (7:103-137)
- Cross-amputation and crucifixion is also the penalty of Q 5:33; Pharaoh's crucifixion threat compares with Gen 40:19 and Persian impalement.
- The magicians' conversion and martyrdom match Jannes and Jambres traditions (2 Tim 3:8; Targum Ps.-Jonathan Exod 7:11).
- Five plagues with tufan (flood) unlike any biblical plague; compare Wis 16-19 and the plague lists of Ps 78 and 105.

**Forty nights, the request to see God and the tablets** (7:142-147)
- The mountain test compares with 1 Kgs 19:11-12 and the rabbinic motif of mountains melting at Sinai (Judg 5:5, Mekhilta).

**The lowing calf and the seventy** (7:148-156)
- The lowing calf parallels Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 45 and Tanhuma Ki Tissa 19 (the calf comes out lowing; Samael inside).

**The unlettered prophet foretold in Torah and Gospel** (7:157-158)
- Ummi may render Hebrew ummot ha-olam ('gentile'); compare the Paraclete (John 14:16) and Matt 11:30 on the easy yoke.

**Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate** (7:159-162)
- Hitta: Hadith has the mockers say hintatun (wheat) instead; compare the Shibboleth test (Judg 12:6).

**The Sabbath-breaking seaside town turned into apes** (7:163-168)
- Commentators locate the town at Eilat/Ayla; compare Neh 13:15-22 (Sabbath trade) and b. Sanhedrin 109a (builders of the tower turned into apes).

**Heirs of the book and the mountain lifted over Israel** (7:169-171)
- Mountain over Israel: b. Shabbat 88a and b. Avodah Zarah 2b (God held Sinai over Israel like a tub: accept the Torah or be buried there), from Exod 19:17 'beneath the mountain'.

**The primordial covenant ("Am I not your Lord?")** (7:172-174)
- Compare Deut 29:13-14 read in Tanhuma Nitzavim 3 and Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 41 (all souls of future generations present at Sinai), and Platonic anamnesis.

**The man who sloughed off God's signs (the panting dog)** (7:175-177)
- Exegetes identify the man with Bal'am b. Ba'ura (Balaam, Num 22-24; cf. 2 Pet 2:15-16, Jude 11).

**Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour** (7:178-188)
- Hour unknown: Mark 13:32 / Matt 24:36; 'comes suddenly' like a thief, 1 Thess 5:2.

**The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols** (7:189-198)
- Some exegetes (al-Tabari) read the couple as Adam and Eve naming their child 'Abd al-Harith at Iblis' suggestion; compare Ps 115:4-7 and 135:15-17.

**Badr - angels, slumber, rain and God's throw** (8:5-19)
- Angelic armies: 2 Kgs 6:17, 2 Macc 10:29-30 and 2 Macc 5:2-3 (horsemen in the sky); the War Scroll (1QM) has angels fighting with the sons of light.
- God's throw (the handful of pebbles in sira) compares with Josh 10:11 (hailstones) and Exod 14:14.

**The plot against the prophet and the worship of the pagans** (8:30-40)
- Asatir al-awwalin may echo Greek historia / Syriac shu'raya; compare Gen 18:23-32 for the righteous presence averting punishment.

**The fifth of the spoils, the dream of few, Satan's desertion** (8:41-48)
- Sira says Satan came in the form of Suraqa b. Malik; compare Judg 7:13-15 (dream encouraging Gideon) and the royal fifth of Gen 47:24.

**The ratio of the steadfast, captives and ransom** (8:64-71)
- Compare Lev 26:8 and Deut 32:30 ('one chase a thousand'); 1 Sam 15 (Saul spares Agag and spoil) for the captives rebuke.

**The disavowal - treaties, sacred months and asylum** (9:1-16)
- Asylum and safe-conduct compare with Deut 23:16-17 (escaped slave) and the Greek proxenia; three-pilgrimage law Exod 23:17.

**Who maintains the mosques; God above family** (9:17-24)
- Compare Matt 10:37 / Luke 14:26 and Deut 33:9.

**Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya** (9:25-29)
- Pride in numbers: Judg 7:2 (Gideon's army reduced lest Israel boast) and 2 Sam 24 (David's census).

**'Uzayr and the Messiah called sons of God; rabbis and monks as lords** (9:30-35)
- 'Uzayr: 4 Ezra 14 (Ezra restores the scriptures and is taken up), Ezra as 'scribe of the Most High'; compare also the angel 'Azael/Uzziel and Metatron as 'lesser YHWH' (3 Enoch 12).
- Rabbis as lords: Matt 23:8-10 ('call no one rabbi or father').

**Twelve months and the ban on intercalation** (9:36-37)
- Compare the 364-day solar calendar polemic of Jubilees 6:32-38 and 1 Enoch 72-82 (heavenly tablets fix the calendar; human tampering condemned).

**The call to go forth; the second of two in the cave** (9:38-41)
- Compare David hiding in the cave (1 Sam 22, 24) and the spider/dove cave legend in sira paralleled in Jewish legend (David and the spider).

**The excuses of those who stayed behind** (9:42-59)
- Compare Deut 20:8 and Judg 7:3 (the fearful sent home) and Judg 5:16-17 (tribes who stayed behind).

**The eight recipients of alms** (9:60)
- Compare the poor tithe for Levite, stranger, orphan and widow (Deut 14:28-29; 26:12) and Mishnah Pe'ah.

**Hypocrites who mock and the destroyed peoples** (9:61-72)
- Mu'tafikat echoes Hebrew hafakh / mahpekhah (Gen 19:25, Deut 29:22, Amos 4:11).

**The broken vow of charity; seventy prayers in vain** (9:73-80)
- Seventy times inverts Matt 18:22; compare Jer 7:16, 11:14 (prophet forbidden to pray) and the widow's mite (Mark 12:41-44) for the poor givers.

**The forerunners, alms that purify, and the mosque of harm** (9:100-110)
- Compare Matt 7:24-27 (house on rock and sand) and Ezek 13:10-14; the rival mosque recalls the rival altar of Josh 22:10-34.

**The bargain of lives for paradise; Abraham's prayer for his father** (9:111-116)
- Abraham's father: Jubilees 12, Apocalypse of Abraham 1-8; Abraham as awwah halim (sighing, forbearing).

**The wise Book, creation, sun and moon, the prayer of paradise** (10:1-10)
- Moon's stations: Sir 43:6-8, Ps 104:19, 1 Enoch 73-74 (lunar stations) and the Arabian manazil al-qamar.

**Prayer in distress, a changed Quran, the storm at sea** (10:11-23)
- Storm at sea and prayer: Ps 107:23-32 and Jonah 1:4-16 (sailors' prayers and vows).

**Life like a crop, the abode of peace, darkened faces** (10:24-30)
- Compare Isa 40:6-8, Ps 103:15-16, Jas 1:10-11 for the withering crop.

**A messenger for every nation; no ransom** (10:46-56)
- No ransom: Ps 49:8-9 ('the ransom of their life is costly'); Matt 16:26.

**Healing for hearts, the atom's weight, God has no son** (10:57-70)
- Compare Matt 10:29-30 (sparrows and hairs) for the atom's weight.

**Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith** (10:75-93)
- Pharaoh's repentance in the sea: Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 43 and Mekhilta Beshallah (Pharaoh survives, repents, becomes king of Nineveh); Exod 14:25 ('let us flee, YHWH fights for them').
- Houses as prayer places compare with Exod 12:7-13 (marked houses) and Dan 6:11.

**Ask the readers of scripture; the people of Jonah** (10:94-103)
- Jonah 3:5-10; Matt 12:41; compare b. Ta'anit 16a and y. Ta'anit 2:1 on Nineveh's repentance (feigned or real).

**The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs** (11:1-24)
- Throne on the water: Gen 1:2, Ps 29:10 and 104:3 (beams of his chambers on the waters), b. Hagigah 12b; compare Egyptian creation from Nun.

**Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi** (11:25-49)
- The boiling oven: b. Sanhedrin 108b and Gen Rab 28:9 (the flood waters were boiling); al-Judi = Syriac Qardu (Peshitta/Targum Onqelos Gen 8:4 'mountains of Qardu').
- The lost son has no biblical counterpart; compare Ham's curse (Gen 9:22-25) and the drowned giant 'Og legends.

**Abraham's guests, the roasted calf and the laughing wife** (11:69-76)
- Angels who do not eat: Tob 12:19, Gen Rab 48:14, b. Bava Metzia 86b (they only appeared to eat); Testament of Abraham 4.

**Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil** (11:77-83)
- Sijjil from Persian sang-gil; compare the hailstones of Josh 10:11 and the marked stones of the sira's elephant story (Q 105:4).

**The witnessed day; the wretched and the blessed** (11:103-111)
- Limited duration 'except as God wills' fed debates on the finitude of hell; compare m. Eduyot 2:10 (judgment of the wicked in Gehenna twelve months) and Origen's apokatastasis.

**Stand firm; prayer times; good deeds remove bad** (11:112-123)
- Prayer times: Ps 55:18 (evening, morning, noon), Dan 6:11; 'good deeds remove evil' compares with Dan 4:24 (redeem sins by righteousness/alms) and Prov 16:6.

**Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)** (12:4-101)
- 12:77: the brothers' charge that Joseph once stole echoes later Jewish and Islamic legends (Joseph taking an idol of his maternal grandfather, or his aunt's belt); Gen 31:19 has Rachel, Joseph's mother, steal Laban's teraphim.
- 12:53 'the soul that commands evil' invites comparison with the rabbinic yetzer ha-ra (Gen 6:5; 8:21).

**Abraham's prayer at the sacred house (Surah 14:35-41)** (14:35-41)
- Compare Gen 21:14-21 (Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness of Beersheba) and the later Islamic Zamzam tradition.

**Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)** (15:26-50)
- Compare Life of Adam and Eve (Vita 12-16) and the Cave of Treasures, where Satan refuses to worship Adam and is cast out.
- 15:44: seven gates or levels of hell recur in rabbinic Gehinnom traditions (b. Eruvin 19a: seven names of Gehinnom).

**The slave and the free, the mute man, the woman who unravels her yarn (Surah 16:71-100)** (16:71-100)
- 16:92: Penelope unravelling her web (Odyssey 2) is the familiar image, though the Quranic woman undoes her work as a figure of broken oaths.

**The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8)** (17:1-8)
- 17:4-7 reads naturally against the Babylonian (586 BCE) and Roman (70 CE) destructions of the Jerusalem temple; compare 2 Kgs 25 and the rabbinic two-destructions schema (b. Yoma 9b).
- 17:1: later tradition joins the isrāʾ to the miʿrāj ascent; compare Enoch's and Paul's heavenly journeys (1 En 14; 2 Cor 12:2-4) and the Persian Ardā Wirāz Nāmag.

**Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111)** (17:101-111)
- 17:101: nine signs vs ten plagues; compare the variant plague counts of Ps 78 and 105 (variant-plague-list).

**The Companions of the Cave and al-Raqim (Surah 18:9-31)** (18:9-31)
- The Seven Sleepers of Ephesus (Jacob of Serugh's homily; Gregory of Tours; Syriac versions): youths under Decius sleep in a cave until Theodosius II, wake, send one with an old coin, and a church is built over them.
- Compare Honi the circle-drawer's seventy-year sleep (b. Taanit 23a), Abimelech's sleep in 4 Baruch 5, and Epimenides.

**The parable of the two gardens; this life as rain-fed plants; the book of deeds (Surah 18:32-49)** (18:32-49)
- Compare Luke 12:16-21 (the rich fool) and Isa 40:6-8 (all flesh is grass).

**Iblis was of the jinn; the partners do not answer (Surah 18:50-59)** (18:50-59)
- 18:51 echoes God's challenge in Job 38:4: 'Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?'

**Moses and the servant of God at the meeting of the two seas (Surah 18:60-82)** (18:60-82)
- The tale of Elijah and Rabbi Joshua ben Levi (Nissim of Kairouan, Ḥibbur Yafeh) has the same structure of three shocking acts explained at the end; the Alexander Romance and Gilgamesh XI supply the fish revived by the water of life and the journey to the mouth of the rivers.

**Dhul-Qarnayn, the setting and rising sun, and the barrier against Gog and Magog (Surah 18:83-101)** (18:83-101)
- Syriac Alexander Legend (Neṣḥānā, c. 630) and the Alexander Romance: Alexander, two-horned on coins as son of Ammon, reaches the fetid sea where the sun sets and builds an iron-and-brass gate against Gog and Magog; compare Ezek 38-39 and Josephus, War 7.245.

**Those whose works are weightless; the sea as ink (Surah 18:102-110)** (18:102-110)
- 18:109: compare John 21:25 and the rabbinic topos 'if all the seas were ink' (b. Shabbat 11a; Song Rabbah 1).

**Zechariah's secret prayer and the birth of John (Surah 19:1-15)** (19:1-15)
- Luke 1:5-25, 57-80. Hannah's silent prayer (1 Sam 1:13) is the HB parallel to 19:3.

**Mary, the spirit in human form, the birth under the palm, the speaking infant (Surah 19:16-40)** (19:16-40)
- Pseudo-Matthew 20-21: on the flight to Egypt the palm bends to give Mary dates at the infant Jesus' command and a spring flows from its roots. Protevangelium 17-19: birth in a cave away from people.
- Arabic Infancy Gospel 1 and Syriac infancy traditions: Jesus speaks in the cradle declaring he is the Word.
- 19:28: Miriam is 'the sister of Aaron' in Exod 15:20; Mary and Miriam share the name Maryam.

**Abraham pleads with his father (Surah 19:41-50)** (19:41-50)
- Jubilees 12:1-8: Abraham pleads with Terah to abandon idols; Terah agrees privately but fears the people. Genesis Rabbah 38:13: Terah's idol shop.

**Moses, Ishmael and Idris remembered; the later generation that neglected prayer (Surah 19:51-65)** (19:51-65)
- 19:56-57: Idris is usually identified with Enoch, whom 'God took' (Gen 5:24) and who is enthroned in heaven in 1 Enoch and 3 Enoch (Metatron).

**Moses at the fire in the holy valley Tuwa** (20:9-36)
- The knot in the tongue: Exodus Rabbah 1:26 (the infant Moses burns his tongue on a coal); compare Exod 4:10.

**Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians** (20:42-76)
- Named magicians Jannes and Jambres (2 Tim 3:8; Targum Ps.-Jonathan Exod 7:11); their conversion is not in Exodus.

**Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf** (20:83-98)
- Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 45: Samael enters the calf and it lows; the dust from the hoofprint of the angel's horse (or Joseph's coffin plate) animates the calf.
- Samiri ~ Samaria/Samaritans (calf of Samaria, Hos 8:5-6); Samaritan 'lā misās' purity custom.

**Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent** (20:115-127)
- Life of Adam and Eve (Vita) 12-16 and Cave of Treasures: Satan refuses to worship Adam.

**The split heavens, water of life, orbits, mortality and the scales** (21:30-50)
- Mustard seed as least quantity: Matt 13:31, 17:20; Mishnah Niddah 5:2.

**Abraham breaks the idols and is cast into the fire** (21:51-75)
- Genesis Rabbah 38:13 (Abraham in Terah's idol shop, the largest idol blamed; Nimrod's furnace).

**Noah answered; David and Solomon's judgment, the praising mountains, mail and wind** (21:76-82)
- Solomon's wise judgment as a youth: 1 Kgs 3:16-28; compare Ps 148 for mountains and birds praising.

**Job, Ishmael, Idris, Dhul-Kifl, Dhul-Nun, Zechariah and Mary** (21:83-91)
- Jonah 2:1-10 (prayer from the belly of the fish); Luke 1:5-25 (Zechariah).

**Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice** (22:25-37)
- Jubilees 22 and Gen 21:33: Abraham's cultic foundations; Ps 50:13 against God eating flesh.

**Rejected prophets, ruined towns, the thousand-year day and Satan's insertion** (22:42-57)
- 22:52 is the verse tied to the 'satanic verses' (gharānīq) report; compare Deut 18:20-22 on false prophetic words.
- Thousand years as a day: Ps 90:4, 2 Pet 3:8, Jubilees 4:30.

**Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven** (23:23-30)
- The boiling oven: b. Sanhedrin 108b and Genesis Rabbah 28:9 (the flood waters were boiling).

**Moses and Aaron rejected; the son of Mary and his mother on a height** (23:45-50)
- Compare 19:22-26 and Pseudo-Matthew 20-21 (palm and spring on the flight to Egypt); Rev 12:6, 14 (the woman given refuge).

**Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales** (23:93-118)
- Luke 16:19-31 (the rich man asks for a messenger to his brothers; a great chasm fixed).

**Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath** (24:1-10)
- Num 5:11-31 (sotah) and Mishnah Sotah; the five-fold oath structure vs. the sotah's 'Amen, amen'.

**The affair of the lie (ifk) against a chaste woman** (24:11-26)
- Susanna (false accusation of a chaste woman by elders, refuted by examining witnesses).

**The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures** (24:35-46)
- Light verse and the Christian lamp/monastery imagery; Philo and later al-Ghazali's Mishkat al-anwar; compare Exod 27:20-21, Zech 4:2-3, Ps 104:2 (light as garment).

**The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations** (25:45-62)
- Two seas with a barrier: Gilgamesh XI 'mouth of the rivers'; Alexander Romance; compare 18:60 and 55:19-20.

**The virtues of the servants of the Merciful** (25:63-77)
- b. Yoma 86b (Resh Lakish): repentance from love turns deliberate sins into merits.

**Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains** (26:10-68)
- Pharaoh's reproach of ingratitude: Exod Rabbah 1; 'waters heaped up' Exod 15:8.

**Shuayb and the People of the Thicket; the day of the canopy** (26:176-191)
- Shuayb is traditionally identified with Jethro of Midian (Exod 2-3, 18).

**Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs** (27:1-14)
- Exod 3:2-6 and 4:3 ('Moses fled from it'); nine signs vs ten plagues (Exod 7-12; Ps 78, 105 variant lists).

**Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba** (27:15-44)
- Targum Sheni to Esther 1:2: the wild cock (bird) brings Solomon news of the queen of Sheba, carries his letter tied to its wing; she sees the glass floor, lifts her skirt, and her hairy legs are revealed.
- b. Gittin 68 (Ashmedai the demon king serving Solomon); Testament of Solomon; 1 Kgs 10:1-13.

**The Quran and Israel's disputes; the beast of the earth, the trumpet and the sacred town** (27:76-93)
- The beast of the earth: Rev 13:11 (beast from the earth); Dan 7.

**Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water** (28:1-13)
- b. Sotah 12b (Moses refuses Egyptian breasts); Exod Rabbah 1:23-25.

**Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian** (28:14-22)
- Exod 2:11-15; Acts 7:23-29 (Moses reaches forty, 'mighty in words and deeds').

**At the water of Midian; the two women, their old father and the marriage contract** (28:23-28)
- Exod 2:15-22 (seven daughters of the priest of Midian; Zipporah); Gen 29:18 (Jacob).

**Pharaoh, 'no god but me', Haman's tower of fired brick, and the drowning** (28:36-43)
- Haman as Pharaoh's builder fuses Esther's Haman with Babel; Josephus Ant. 1.4 makes Nimrod the tower builder.

**Qarun's treasures and his swallowing by the earth; closing** (28:76-88)
- Num 16 (Korah); b. Sanhedrin 110a and b. Pesahim 119a: Korah's treasure-house keys loaded on 300 white mules.

**Believers tested; parents and idolatry; the false offer to carry sins** (29:1-13)
- 29:8 and 31:14-15 parallel Deut 13:6-10 (do not heed kin who entice to other gods) more than the Decalogue.
- 29:13 (carrying own loads and others') compare the rabbinic idea that one who causes many to sin bears their sins (m. Avot 5:18).

**Noah remains a thousand years less fifty among his people** (29:14-15)
- Gen 9:29 gives Noah 950 years in total; the Quran puts the 950 years into his mission, compare the 120 years of preaching in Gen. Rab. 30:7 and b. Sanh. 108b.

**Abraham preaches against idols, is saved from the fire, and Lot believes** (29:16-27)
- Abraham in the furnace of Nimrod: Gen. Rab. 38:13, b. Pesah. 118a; Ur Kasdim read as 'fire of the Chaldeans'.

**Lot and the destruction of his town** (29:28-35)
- The robbery of travelers by the Sodomites (29:29) matches rabbinic legends of Sodom's cruelty to wayfarers (b. Sanh. 109a-b, the Procrustean bed).

**Parable of the spider's house** (29:41-44)
- Job 8:14 and Isa 59:5-6 (webs of the godless); the spider legend at the cave of Thawr is later Islamic tradition.

**Recite the Book; dispute with the People of the Book; the unlettered prophet** (29:45-55)
- 'Our God and your God is one' (29:46) echoes the Shema (Deut 6:4) and 1 Cor 8:6.

**God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary** (29:56-69)
- 29:60 compare Matt 6:26 (the birds neither sow nor reap) and Ps 147:9.

**The Romans defeated and the promise of their victory** (30:1-7)
- Historical context: the Persian conquests of 613-614 (Jerusalem) and Heraclius's victories of 622-628.

**The Hour, the times of praise, and the signs of God** (30:8-27)
- 30:17-18 (evening, morning, afternoon, noon) were read by exegetes as the five prayer times; compare Ps 55:18 (evening, morning, noon) and Dan 6:11.

**The slave-partner parable, the fitra, and the social duties** (30:28-45)
- Fitra (30:30) compares with the imago Dei (Gen 1:27) and the Christian idea of natural law (Rom 2:14-15).

**Luqman's advice to his son** (31:1-19)
- Luqman is often compared to Ahiqar (whose sayings to his nephew Nadin include the braying ass) and to Aesop; also Balaam son of Beor in some exegesis.
- Weaning at two years: compare 2 Macc 7:27 (three years) and b. Ketub. 60a (24 months).

**God's signs, the inexhaustible words, and the five things only God knows** (31:20-34)
- 31:27 (seas as ink) compare the rabbinic saying of Yohanan ben Zakkai: if all the heavens were parchment and all trees pens... (b. Shabb. 11a; Soferim 16:8) and John 21:25.

**Al-Sajda: creation, the angel of death, and the two fates** (32:1-30)
- 32:17 is quoted in a hadith qudsi beside 'what no eye has seen, no ear heard' (Isa 64:3; 1 Cor 2:9).
- 32:5 compare Ps 90:4 and 2 Pet 3:8.

**Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers** (33:1-8)
- 33:4-5 reverses the biblical adoption models (Gen 48:5, Esther 2:7 'as a daughter'); compare Roman adoptio.
- Covenant with the prophets (33:7): compare the five 'great covenants' (Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus) in Christian covenant theology and Philo.

**The confederates besiege Medina; hypocrites and the faithful** (33:9-27)
- The wind and unseen hosts (33:9) compare 2 Kgs 7:6 (Arameans hear the sound of a great army) and 2 Kgs 19:35.

**Zayd's wife, the seal of the prophets, and the prophet as a lamp** (33:37-48)
- David's taking of Bathsheba (2 Sam 11) was contrasted with the Zayd episode in Christian polemic.
- 'Seal of the prophets' compare Mani's self-designation as seal of the prophets.

**Divorce before consummation; the prophet's marriages; the curtain and the cloaks** (33:49-62)
- Marriage of the king's widows forbidden: compare the rabbinic rule that a king's widow may not remarry (m. Sanh. 2:2).

**The Hour, the blaming of leaders, Moses cleared, and the Trust** (33:63-73)
- 33:69: hadith (Bukhari) tells of Moses bathing apart, his clothes carried off by a stone, proving he had no defect; compare b. Ned. 38a on Moses' body.
- 33:72 compare the rabbinic legend of the Torah offered to the nations (Sifre Deut 343) and 4 Ezra 7:62-72.

**David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff** (34:10-14)
- Solomon's command of demons: Testament of Solomon, b. Gittin 68a-b (Ashmedai and the shamir). Solomon flying on the wind/carpet: Targum Sheni to Esther 1:2.
- Copper spring: compare 1 Kgs 7:13-47 (Hiram's bronze casting) and Wisdom of Solomon 7:20. Solomon's death on his staff, unnoticed by the jinn, has no clear biblical source; look in the Solomon-and-demons literature.

**Sheba's two gardens and the bursting of the dam** (34:15-21)
- The Marib dam's historical breaches (c. 449-450 and c. 570 CE); compare the Sabaean inscriptions and the Arab legend of the rat undermining the dam.
- Gardens on right and left: compare Gen 2:8-10 and the Ezekiel 47 river.

**Partners own nothing; intercession; the weak and the arrogant at judgment** (34:22-33)
- 34:23 (angels stunned at God's word) is glossed in hadith of the angels fainting at revelation like a chain on a rock; compare 1 Enoch 14 and Hekhalot traditions.

**The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas** (35:1-17)
- Lifespan in a book (35:11) compare Ps 139:16 and the book of life (Exod 32:32).

**No soul bears another's burden; the blind and the seeing; the colors of creation** (35:18-28)
- 35:18 restates Ezek 18:20 and Deut 24:16.

**The heirs of the Book, the Gardens of Eden and the cries of the damned** (35:29-45)
- 35:43 compare Ps 7:16-17 and Prov 26:27 (he who digs a pit falls into it).
- 35:32 three classes compare the rabbinic three books opened on Rosh Hashanah: wholly righteous, wholly wicked, intermediate (b. Rosh Hash. 16b).

**The people of the town, the three messengers and the man who came running** (36:13-32)
- Exegetes place this at Antioch with apostles of Jesus and Habib the carpenter; compare Acts 11-14 (Barnabas and Paul at Antioch, Silas joining) and Acts 14:19 (Paul stoned at Lystra).

**Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship** (36:33-50)
- Sun's resting place: hadith of the sun prostrating beneath the Throne each night; compare 1 Enoch 72 (the gates of the sun) and Eccl 1:5.

**The trumpet, the sleepers raised, the Garden and the witnessing limbs** (36:51-70)
- Trumpet of resurrection: 1 Cor 15:52, 1 Thess 4:16; Isa 27:13. Separation of the guilty: Matt 25:31-33.
- Limbs testifying (36:65) compare b. Hag. 16a and b. Taan. 11a (a man's own limbs testify against him).

**Who revives rotten bones? Fire from the green tree; Be and it is** (36:71-83)
- Fire from the green tree: exegetes cite the markh and 'afar trees used as fire-drills; compare the burning bush not consumed (Exod 3:2).

**The ranks, the guarded heaven and the shooting stars** (37:1-21)
- Demons eavesdropping behind the heavenly curtain: b. Hag. 16a (demons hear 'from behind the curtain' like angels); 1 Enoch 16:3.

**The damned questioned; the blessed on facing couches; the tree of Zaqqum** (37:22-74)
- The blessed viewing the damned: Luke 16:23-26 (Lazarus and the rich man), 4 Ezra 7:85-93, and the rabbinic motif of the righteous seeing the punishment of the wicked.
- The 'second death' language: Rev 2:11, 20:14; Targum to Deut 33:6.

**Abraham, the stars, the smashed idols and the fire** (37:83-98)
- Apocalypse of Abraham 1-8 and Gen. Rab. 38:13 (Abraham in Terah's idol shop asks the idols to eat the offering).

**Abraham's dream and the near-sacrifice of his son** (37:99-113)
- The willing son: Targum Neofiti/Pseudo-Jonathan Gen 22:10 (Isaac asks to be bound well), 4 Macc 13:12, Josephus Ant. 1.232; the Akedah as Isaac's consent.
- Isaac or Ishmael as dhabih was debated by early exegetes (al-Tabari favored Isaac). Compare Jephthah's daughter (Judg 11) and the Iphigenia substitution.

**Moses and Aaron; Elias against Ba'l** (37:114-132)
- Compare 1 Kgs 18:21-40 (Elijah on Carmel). 'The best of creators' (ahsan al-khaliqin) compare Ps 86:8.

**Lot's old woman; Jonah and the fish** (37:133-148)
- Jonah 1-4: the Quran shifts the gourd to after the fish, makes it a comfort rather than a lesson, and omits the worm and Jonah's anger.

**Daughters of God denied; the angels' stations; closing doxology** (37:149-182)
- Banat Allah (al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat); compare Gen 6:2 'sons of God' and 1 Enoch 6-7 for the angels-jinn genealogy.

**David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes** (38:17-29)
- 2 Sam 12:1-7 (Nathan's parable of the poor man's ewe); the Quran's litigants are read by exegetes as angels and the sin as the Uriah affair, which the text does not name.
- Ps 51 (David's penitential psalm) and b. Shabb. 56a (David did not sin).

**Solomon's steeds, the body on his throne, and the unmatched kingdom** (38:30-40)
- The body on the throne: b. Gittin 68b (Ashmedai takes Solomon's form and throne while Solomon wanders); compare the ring legend.
