- Solomon's prayer (38:35) compare 1 Kgs 3:12-13 (none like you before or after).

**Job, the spring and the bundle of twigs** (38:41-44)
- Exegesis: Job swore to beat his wife a hundred strokes; compare Testament of Job 23-25 (Sitis sells her hair to Satan) and b. B. Bat. 15b. The legal fiction parallels rabbinic ha'aramah.

**Adam made from clay; Iblis refuses and is granted respite** (38:71-88)
- Life of Adam and Eve (Vita) 12-16: Michael orders the angels to worship God's image; the devil refuses since he was created first. Compare Cave of Treasures 2-3 and Gen. Rab. 8 (angels dispute man's creation).

**Pure religion; no son for God; creation from one soul in three darknesses** (39:1-10)
- Three darknesses (belly, womb, placenta in exegesis) compare Ps 139:13-15 ('woven in the depths of the earth') and Job 10:10-11.

**The first of those who submit; canopies of fire; chambers above chambers** (39:11-29)
- 39:29 compare Matt 6:24 (no one can serve two masters).

**The prophet's mortality; souls taken in sleep; intercession belongs to God** (39:30-52)
- 39:42 compare the Jewish morning blessing Elohai neshamah (God returns the soul each morning) and b. Ber. 57b (sleep is one sixtieth of death).

**Do not despair of mercy; the earth in God's grip; the throngs to hell and Garden** (39:53-75)
- 39:67 compare Isa 34:4 and Rev 6:14 (sky rolled up), Isa 40:12 (heavens measured with a span).
- 39:74 inheritance of the land compare Ps 37:11 and Matt 5:5 (the meek inherit the earth); also Quran 21:105 citing the Psalms.
- 39:68 the exception 'except whom God wills' compare 1 Thess 4:16-17.

**Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers** (40:1-22)
- 40:16 compare the eschatological 'YHWH will be king over all the earth; on that day YHWH will be one' (Zech 14:9), and the Apocalypse of Elijah.
- Angels interceding for humans (40:7) compare Zech 1:12, Tobit 12:12 and 1 Enoch 40:6.

**Moses, Pharaoh, Haman and the believer of Pharaoh's family** (40:23-50)
- The believer's argument (40:28) closely matches Gamaliel in Acts 5:38-39 (if this is of men it will fail, if of God you cannot overthrow it).
- A sympathetic Egyptian at court: compare Jethro, Job and Balaam as Pharaoh's counselors (b. Sotah 11a; Exod. Rab. 1:9).
- 40:46 punishment in the grave before the Hour; compare the intermediate state in 1 Enoch 22.

**Dragged in chains; messengers told and untold; faith on seeing punishment** (40:69-85)
- 40:78 compare John 21:25 and Heb 11:32 (time would fail to tell of others).

**Ha-Mim Fussilat: the veil between; creation in days; heaven as smoke** (41:1-12)
- Heaven formed from smoke/vapor: Gen. Rab. 4:7 (shamayim from esh u-mayim) and b. Hag. 12a; the talking heaven and earth compare the rabbinic legend that the earth answered God at creation.

**Skins testify; evil companions; the misled ask to trample their misleaders** (41:19-29)
- Body parts witnessing (41:20-22): b. Hag. 16a ('the limbs of a man testify against him', citing Isa 43:12) and Wisdom of Solomon 1:9.

**Angels descend on the steadfast; repel evil with good; signs on the horizons** (41:30-54)
- 41:34 compare Prov 25:21-22, Rom 12:20-21 (overcome evil with good) and Matt 5:44.
- Angels never wearying of praise (41:38) compare Isa 6:3, Rev 4:8 and 1 Enoch 39:12-13.

**Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf: revelation, the angels' intercession and the one religion of the prophets** (42:1-24)
- 42:5 angels interceding for earth-dwellers: compare 1 Enoch 40:6 and 1 Enoch 9 (angels petition for humanity).
- 42:13 chain Noah-Abraham-Moses-Jesus resembles the Noahide/patriarchal 'one law' idea and Pseudo-Clementine 'True Prophet' succession.

**Provision in measure, rain, ships like mountains and the ethics of consultation and pardon** (42:25-43)
- 42:40 talion with preference for pardon: compare Exod 21:24 with Matt 5:38-39 and rabbinic monetary interpretation of talion (b. Bava Qamma 84a).

**The damned seek a way back; God gives children as he wills; three ways God speaks to man** (42:44-53)
- 42:51 'from behind a veil': compare Num 12:8 and Exod 33:20-23; also the rabbinic notion that Moses saw through a clear 'aspaqlaria' while other prophets through a dim one (b. Yevamot 49b).

**Ha-Mim: the Mother of the Book, the riding prayer and the 'daughters' of God** (43:1-25)
- 43:4 umm al-kitab: compare the heavenly tablets of Jubilees (e.g. Jub 3:10) and the preexistent Torah of Gen. Rabbah 1:1.
- 43:19 angels as daughters: the pre-Islamic banat Allah (al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat), cf. Q 53:19-21.

**Moses before Pharaoh: the laughing courtiers, the rivers beneath Pharaoh and the drowning** (43:46-56)
- 43:53 gold bracelets as insignia of a messenger: compare Gen 41:42 (Joseph's gold chain) and Exod. Rabbah on Moses' royal status.

**The son of Mary as an example and sign of the Hour; the Garden with golden dishes; Malik of hell** (43:57-89)
- 43:60 'had we willed we would have made angels successors on earth' echoes the angels' objection in 2:30.
- 43:61 Jesus as sign of the Hour: Christian parousia (Matt 24:30) and hadith of his descent.
- 43:77 Malik: compare angels over Gehenna in 1 Enoch and the rabbinic 'prince of Gehenna' (b. Shabbat 104a).

**Ha-Mim: the blessed night and the day of the smoke** (44:1-16)
- 44:3-4 night when every matter is decreed: compare Rosh Hashanah as the day of judgment when fates are inscribed (m. Rosh Hashanah 1:2).
- 44:10 smoke: Joel 3:3 (2:30) 'blood, fire and columns of smoke' before the Day of YHWH; Rev 9:2.

**Moses asks Pharaoh to hand over God's servants; the sea left parted; heaven did not weep** (44:17-33)
- 44:29 heaven not weeping: contrast Jer 4:28 / Isa 24:4 (earth mourns); rabbinic idea that God silenced the angels' song when the Egyptians drowned (b. Megillah 10b).
- 44:28 Egypt 'inherited by another people' (cf. 26:59 Israel): compare debates on Israel returning to Egypt.

**Deniers demand their fathers; the people of Tubba'; the tree of Zaqqum; silk, brocade and the houris** (44:34-59)
- 44:43 Zaqqum: an inverted tree of life (Gen 2:9); compare the Avestan and Mandaean infernal trees.
- 44:56 'no death but the first death': contrast Rev 2:11, 20:6 'the second death'.

**Ha-Mim: the signs, the scornful liar, Israel's book and the Prophet's shari'a** (45:1-20)
- 45:13 universal subjection: compare Ps 8:7 'you put all things under his feet'.

**Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book** (45:21-37)
- 45:24 al-dahr: pre-Islamic Arabian fatalism; compare Zurvan (Time) in Zoroastrian thought and Eccl 3 / 9:11.
- 45:29 transcribed deeds: Dan 7:10 'the books were opened'; m. Avot 2:1 'all your deeds are written in a book'.

**Ha-Mim: the idols created nothing; a witness from Israel; the Book of Moses** (46:1-14)
- 46:10 the Israelite witness is identified in tafsir with 'Abdallah ibn Salam; compare Deut 18:18 as read in Muslim polemic.

**Kindness to parents, thirty months of bearing and weaning, the prayer at forty and the son who says 'Uff'** (46:15-20)
- 46:15 maturity at forty: m. Avot 5:21 'at forty, understanding (binah)'.
- 46:20 'you received your good things in your lifetime': Luke 16:25 (the rich man and Lazarus).

**Hud warns 'Ad at the dunes; the cloud that was not rain; the jinn listen to the Quran** (46:21-35)
- 46:24 cloud mistaken for rain: compare 1 Kgs 18:44 (the small cloud) inverted; Ad and Iram in pre-Islamic poetry.
- 46:29 jinn hearing scripture: compare rabbinic traditions of demons (shedim) who study Torah (b. Hagigah 16a, demons resemble humans in three ways).

**Muhammad: deeds nullified, striking necks and freeing captives, and the four rivers of the Garden** (47:1-19)
- 47:15 rivers of milk, wine and honey: 2 Enoch 8:5 (paradise with springs of honey, milk, oil and wine); Apocalypse of Paul 23 (rivers of honey, milk, wine and oil).

**The sick-hearted faint at the call to fight; locks on hearts; the twist of speech; God rich, you poor** (47:20-38)
- 47:38 replacement people: compare Deut 32:21 'I will provoke them with a no-people' and Matt 21:43.

**Al-Fath: the clear opening, the sakina, the hand of God over their hands and the bedouin who stayed behind** (48:1-17)
- 48:4 sakina: Hebrew/Aramaic shekhinah (divine indwelling presence) of the Targums and rabbinic literature; cf. Q 2:248 sakina in the ark.

**The pledge under the tree, the hidden believers in Mecca, the dream of entering the sanctuary, and the seed parable from Torah and Gospel** (48:18-29)
- 48:25 a city spared for hidden righteous: Gen 18:23-32 (Abraham bargains for Sodom for ten righteous).
- 48:29 seed growing: Mark 4:26-28 (seed grows of itself: blade, ear, full grain) and Mark 4:31-32 (mustard seed).
- 48:29 mark on foreheads: Ezek 9:4 (tav on the foreheads of the faithful); Rev 7:3.

**Al-Hujurat: lowering voices, verifying reports, reconciling believers, backbiting and the peoples and tribes** (49:1-18)
- 49:12 slander as eating flesh: Aramaic idiom akal qurtsin 'eat the pieces of' = slander (Dan 3:8, 6:25); Ps 27:2.
- 49:6 verify reports: Deut 13:15 / 17:4 'inquire, search and ask diligently'.

**Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness** (50:16-45)
- 50:17-18 two recording angels: compare b. Ta'anit 11a and b. Hagigah 16a (two ministering angels accompany a person and testify); 1 Enoch 89-90 recording angel; Hermas Mand. 6.2 (angels of righteousness and wickedness).
- 50:30 hell asks for more: Isa 5:14 'Sheol has enlarged her throat'; Hab 2:5.
- 50:38 no weariness: the Syriac and Jewish debate over Gen 2:2-3 and Exod 31:17; Isa 40:28 'he does not faint or grow weary'.

**Al-Dhariyat: the oath by the winds, the conjecturers, the night-wakeful righteous and the beggar's due** (51:1-23)
- 51:1-4 the oaths by winds and distributors: compare Ps 104:4 (winds as messengers) and the four winds/angels of Rev 7:1.

**Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah** (51:24-46)
- 51:27 angels not eating: Tob 12:19 (Raphael only appeared to eat); Gen. Rabbah 48:14 and b. Bava Metzia 86b (the angels only seemed to eat).
- 51:36 one household found: Gen 18:32 / 19:12 (not ten righteous; only Lot's household).

**The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship** (51:47-60)
- 51:57 God needs no food: Ps 50:12-13; contrast Mesopotamian gods fed by temple offerings (Atrahasis).

**Al-Tur: the oath by the Mount, the inscribed parchment and the frequented House; the sky heaves** (52:1-16)
- 52:4 al-bayt al-ma'mur: the heavenly temple of 2 Bar 4:5, Testament of Levi 3, and b. Hagigah 12b (Zevul, where Michael offers in the heavenly temple).
- 52:3 raqq manshur: Isa 34:4 / Rev 6:14 scroll; the unrolled scroll of Ezek 2:10.

**The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges** (52:17-49)
- 52:38 sullam: the very word of Jacob's ladder (Gen 28:12); compare the jinn eavesdropping at the heavenly council (Q 72:8-9, 37:6-10).

**Al-Najm: the star that sets, the mighty one on the horizon two bow-lengths away, and the Lote-Tree of the Boundary** (53:1-18)
- 53:14 sidrat al-muntaha: the cosmic tree of 1 Enoch 24-25 and the tree of life beside God's throne in Apocalypse of Moses 22; the Hekhalot ascent.
- 53:9 two bow-lengths: compare Ezek 1:28 (rainbow/bow around the throne) and the angel Metatron/Yahoel of the Apocalypse of Abraham.

**Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius** (53:19-62)
- 53:19-20 the 'Satanic verses' episode (al-Tabari) attaches here.
- 53:38 no one bears another's burden: Ezek 18:20 and Deut 24:16, against Exod 20:5.
- 53:36-37 'scrolls of Abraham': Testament/Apocalypse of Abraham and Sefer Yetzirah attributed to Abraham.

**Al-Qamar: the moon split, the dead like locusts, and Noah's ark of planks and fibres** (54:1-17)
- 54:1 moon split: compare signs of the end in Joel 3:4 (moon to blood) and the splitting of the moon miracle in Sira.
- 54:13 dusur (fibres/nails): compare the Mesopotamian reed-and-rope coracle of the Ark Tablet and Gilgamesh XI.

**Refrains over 'Ad, Thamud's she-camel, Lot's guests and Pharaoh; everything by measure; the seat of truth** (54:18-55)
- 54:50 command like a blink: 1 Cor 15:52 'in the twinkling of an eye'.
- 54:28 water shared by turns: compare Bedouin water-turn customs and Gen 29:2-3 (flocks watered by turn at the well).

**Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier** (55:1-30)
- 55:13 refrain: Ps 136's 'ki le-'olam hasdo' after each line; the Syriac madrasha refrain (Ephrem).
- 55:15 jinn from fire: compare rabbinic shedim and the angels created of fire (2 Enoch 29:3; Ps 104:4).
- 55:19-20 two seas with barrier: the Gilgamesh 'mouth of the rivers' and the Alexander Romance's meeting of the two waters (cf. Q 18:60).

**Passing the regions of heaven, the rose-red sky, forelocks and feet, and the two pairs of gardens with secluded maidens** (55:31-78)
- 55:46-62 graded gardens: compare the rabbinic seven compartments of Gan Eden and the Ephremic Hymns on Paradise (paradise on a slope with higher and lower levels).
- 55:56 maidens 'untouched by jinn': assumes jinn can have intercourse with humans (cf. Gen 6:1-4 sons of God and daughters of men).

**Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden** (56:1-40)
- 56:7-11 three classes: compare b. Rosh Hashanah 16b (three books/groups: wholly righteous, wholly wicked, intermediate) and Dan 12:2-3.
- 56:33 fruit never cut off: Ezek 47:12 (trees bearing fruit every month); Rev 22:2.

**The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat** (56:41-96)
- 56:79 'none touch it but the purified': the rabbinic rule that scripture 'defiles the hands' (m. Yadayim 3:5) and the halakhic ban on touching a Torah scroll unwashed.
- 56:63-64 'do you sow or do we?': 1 Cor 3:6-7 (God gives the growth).

**Al-Hadid: First and Last, Outward and Inward; stewards of wealth; the goodly loan** (57:1-11)
- 57:3 compare Rev 1:8, 22:13 (Alpha and Omega).

**The believers' light, the hypocrites who would borrow it, and the wall with a gate; hearts hardened by long time** (57:12-19)
- 57:13 borrowing light: the parable of the ten virgins (Matt 25:8-12, 'give us of your oil'; the door is shut).
- 57:13 the wall between: the great chasm of Luke 16:26 and the A'raf wall of Q 7:46.

**Life like withering plants; the Garden as wide as heaven and earth; every calamity written; iron sent down; Jesus' followers and invented monasticism** (57:20-29)
- 57:25 iron 'sent down': meteoric iron; compare Enoch's Asael teaching metallurgy (1 Enoch 8:1) and Tubal-cain (Gen 4:22).
- 57:27 rahbaniyya: Syriac monasticism (ihidaye, bnay qyama); compare Matt 19:12 and later Christian debate on monastic vows.

**Al-Mujadila: the woman who disputed, the zihar formula and its expiation; God the fourth of three; the party of God** (58:1-22)
- 58:7 God present with three: m. Avot 3:2/3:6 'when two (or three, or ten) sit and study Torah, the Shekhinah is among them'; Matt 18:20.
- 58:3-4 expiation by freeing a slave / fasting / feeding: compare the kaffara of Q 5:89 and rabbinic graded atonement offerings (Lev 5:7-11).

**Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay'** (59:1-10)
- 59:5 palm-cutting at a siege: Deut 20:19-20 prohibition and 2 Kgs 3:19, 25 (good trees felled in Moab) as the biblical exception.

**The hypocrites' false promises, Satan's disowning, the Quran on a mountain, and the litany of beautiful names** (59:11-24)
- 59:16 Satan disowns his dupe: the Barsisa monk legend (tafsir) and the Faust motif.
- 59:23 al-Quddus al-Salam: Isa 6:3 qadosh; the divine names of Exod 34:6 and the 'Shalom' as a divine name (Judg 6:24; b. Shabbat 10b).

**Al-Mumtahana: no affection for God's enemies, Abraham's excellent example, examining emigrant women, and the women's pledge** (60:1-13)
- 60:10 dissolution of mixed marriages: Ezra 10 (foreign wives sent away) as an inverse parallel.
- 60:12 compare Pliny, Ep. 10.96 (Christians bind themselves by oath not to commit theft, robbery, adultery, or break faith).

**Al-Saff: ranks like a solid structure; Moses hurt by his people; Jesus foretells Ahmad; the disciples as God's helpers** (61:1-14)
- 61:6 Ahmad: the Johannine Paraclete (John 14:16, 16:7), periklytos/parakletos reading; Ibn Ishaq cites the Palestinian Syriac 'Menahhemana'.
- 61:5 Moses 'hurt': Num 12 and 16 complaints; Q 33:69.
- 61:14 hawariyyun: Ge'ez hawarya 'apostle'.

**Al-Jumu'a: the messenger among the unlettered, the donkey carrying books, wishing for death, and the Friday prayer** (62:1-11)
- 62:5 the donkey laden with books: a proverb also in Persian and rabbinic idiom ('a donkey carrying books', cf. Midrash on scholars without deeds; Sa'adi).
- 62:9-10 Friday vs. Sabbath: no rest commanded after the prayer; compare Gen 2:2 and Q 50:38 rejecting divine rest.

**Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay** (63:1-11)
- 63:4 impressive bodies but empty: Jer 10:5 idols 'like a scarecrow in a cucumber field'; Matt 23:27 whitewashed tombs.

**Al-Taghabun: forms made beautiful, the Day of Mutual Loss, enemies among wives and children, and the goodly loan** (64:1-18)
- 64:14 household enemies: Mic 7:6 and Matt 10:36.

**Al-Talaq: divorce and the waiting period, two witnesses, nursing wages, and the seven heavens and earths** (65:1-12)
- 65:4 three-month wait: rabbinic havḥanah, a ninety-day wait before remarriage to establish paternity (m. Yevamot 4:10; b. Yevamot 42a).
- 65:12 seven earths: rabbinic seven earths (Lev. Rabbah 29:11; Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 18) alongside seven heavens (b. Hagigah 12b).

**Al-Tahrim: the prohibited thing and the divulged secret; fire fed with stones; the wives of Noah and Lot, Pharaoh's wife and Mary daughter of 'Imran** (66:1-12)
- 66:10 Noah's wife: in Jewish and Gnostic lore Noah's wife Norea/Naamah opposes the ark (Gen. Rabbah 23:3; Hypostasis of the Archons).
- 66:11 Pharaoh's righteous wife: compare Bithiah (b. Megillah 13a, Lev. Rabbah 1:3) who enters paradise alive (Derekh Eretz Zuta 1).
- 66:12 'daughter of Imran': Exod 6:20 / Num 26:59 Miriam daughter of Amram; Protevangelium of James for Mary's dedicated chastity.

**Al-Mulk: death and life as test, seven flawless heavens, stars as missiles against devils, hell nearly bursting with rage** (67:1-14)
- 67:14 'does he who created not know?': Ps 94:9 'He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see?'
- 67:5 shooting stars against eavesdropping devils: compare 1 Enoch 18 and the Testament of Solomon 20:16-17 (demons struck by falling stars).

**Nun: by the pen; the prophet's great character; the swearer, slanderer and base-born man branded on the snout** (68:1-16)
- 68:1 the Pen: the primordial pen of hadith (the first thing created) and the heavenly scribe of Ezek 9:2 / Enoch the scribe.

**The companions of the garden who swore to harvest without 'if God wills' and to exclude the poor** (68:17-33)
- 68:17-33 compare the parable of the rich fool (Luke 12:16-21) and Jas 4:13-15 ('if the Lord wills'); rabbinic stories of fields struck for withholding tithes and gleanings (b. Bava Metzia / Sifre on Deut 24:19).

**Do you have a book or oaths binding God?; the shin laid bare; the companion of the fish; the evil eye** (68:34-52)
- 68:42 shin laid bare: the hadith of God revealing his shin at judgment; compare the Gnostic and Jewish anthropomorphic Shi'ur Qomah.
- 68:51 evil eye: Prov 23:6 ra' 'ayin; b. Bava Metzia 107b ('ninety-nine die of the evil eye').

**Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne** (69:1-18)
- 69:17 eight throne-bearers: compare the four hayyot of Ezek 1 and the four creatures of Rev 4:6; later Islamic tradition: four now, eight on the Day.

**The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger** (69:19-52)
- 69:19-25 right/left books: Matt 25:33 (sheep at the right, goats at the left); the weighing scenes of the Testament of Abraham (recording angels on right and left).
- 69:44-46 the forger punished: Deut 18:20 (the prophet who speaks presumptuously in God's name shall die).

**The ascending stairways: the day of fifty thousand years and the steadfast worshippers** (70:1-44)
- Compare Jacob's ladder (Gen 28:12) and the 'ma'arij' of heavenly ascent literature (Hekhalot, Mi'raj).
- Ps 90:4 / 2 Pet 3:8 (a thousand years as a day); Ps 49:8 (no ransom for a brother).

**Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood** (71:1-28)
- Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr are attested in Ibn al-Kalbi's Book of Idols as Arabian deities; Nasr ('vulture/eagle') compare Mesopotamian and South Arabian NSR.
- Noah's preaching is absent from Genesis but present in 2 Pet 2:5, Sib. Or. 1.125-198, b. Sanh. 108a-b and Gen. Rab. 30.7.

**The jinn hear the recitation** (72:1-28)
- Spirits eavesdropping behind the heavenly curtain (pargod) and overhearing decrees: b. Hag. 16a, b. Ber. 18b; falling stars as weapons against demons is also a late antique idea.
- Compare the demons of the Testament of Solomon 20.12-17, who fly up to the firmament and fall as stars.

**The enwrapped one: the night vigil** (73:1-20)
- Elijah wraps his face in his mantle at Horeb (1 Kgs 19:13); compare the Syriac and monastic night vigils with measured psalmody.
- Prov 19:17 (who is kind to the poor lends to YHWH).

**The cloaked one: the call, the opponent, and the nineteen** (74:1-56)
- The number nineteen as a test for 'those given the Book' (74:31); compare angelic numbers in 1 Enoch 20 and the 'nineteen' in rabbinic/gnostic angel lists.
- Rich man and Lazarus (Luke 16:23-26) for the blessed questioning the damned across the divide.

**The resurrection: bones, fingertips and the collarbone** (75:1-40)
- The resurrection of the bones down to the fingertips: compare Ezek 37 and the rabbinic luz bone (Gen. Rab. 28.3); the Persian Bundahishn 30 on reassembling bones.

**The human: the mingled drop and the camphor cup** (76:1-31)
- Ephrem's Hymns on Paradise (wine, fruit-laden low branches, no heat or cold) are the closest Syriac parallel for 76:13-21.

**Those sent forth: the refrain of woe** (77:1-50)
- The refrain structure resembles Ps 136 and the 'woe' series of Isa 5:8-23.

**The great tiding: signs of creation and the day of sorting** (78:1-40)
- 'Would that I were dust': compare 4 Ezra 7:62-69 where the mind envies the beasts that have no judgment.

**Those who drag forth: Moses at Tuwa, Pharaoh's claim, and the spreading of the earth** (79:1-46)
- Pharaoh's claim to divinity: Ezek 29:3 ('my Nile is mine, I made it'), Exod. Rab. 5.14 and 9.8 (Pharaoh claims to be a god who created himself).

**He frowned: the blind man and the honored scrolls** (80:1-42)
- safara (80:15) for the heavenly scribes is cognate with Hebrew/Aramaic sofer/safra; compare Enoch as heavenly scribe (Jub 4:23; 2 Enoch 22-23).

**The folding up: twelve signs of the end and the messenger on the horizon** (81:1-29)
- Compare the cosmic catalogues of Isa 34:4, Joel 3:4, Mark 13:24-25 and Rev 6:12-14 (the sky rolled up like a scroll).

**The cleaving: the noble scribes** (82:1-19)
- Recording angels: m. Avot 2:1 and 3:16 ('all your deeds are written in a book'), Apocalypse of Paul 7-10, Testament of Abraham 12-13.

**The defrauders: Sijjin and 'Illiyyun** (83:1-36)
- Wisdom of Solomon 5:1-5 (the mocked righteous stand in confidence before those who scorned them).
- 'Wine preserved in its grapes since the six days of creation' (b. Ber. 34b) for the sealed nectar.

**The splitting: the book in the right hand** (84:1-25)
- Prostration at recitation (84:21) is a sajda verse; compare Neh 8:6.

**The constellations: the people of the ditch and the preserved tablet** (85:1-22)
- Exegetes link the ditch to the massacre of the Christians of Najran by Dhu Nuwas (c. 523), known from the Letter of Simeon of Beth Arsham and the Book of the Himyarites; compare Dan 3 and 2 Macc 7.
- The heavenly tablets of Jubilees 3:10, 4:5 and 1 Enoch 81:1-2.

**The night-comer: fluid from between backbone and ribs** (86:1-17)
- Semen from the spine/brain: Hippocratic 'On Generation' 1-2, Plato Timaeus 73-74 and 91a-b (the marrow); compare b. Nid. 31a on the contributions of father and mother.

**The Most High: the scrolls of Abraham and Moses** (87:1-19)
- The scrolls of Abraham: compare the Apocalypse of Abraham, the Testament of Abraham and the Sefer Yetzirah attributed to Abraham.

**The overwhelming event: dari' and the carpets of paradise** (88:1-26)
- Esth 1:6 (the garden court of Susa with couches of gold and silver) for paradise as a royal pleasure garden.

**The dawn: Iram of the pillars and the soul at peace** (89:1-30)
- Iram: compare the many-pillared ruins associated with Ubar and Shaddad's city in later legend; Thamud's rock tombs at Hegra (Mada'in Salih).

**The city: the two highways and the steep ascent** (90:1-20)
- The two ways: Deut 30:15-19, Didache 1-6, Epistle of Barnabas 18-20, and Ps 1.

**The sun: the soul's two inspirations and the she-camel of God** (91:1-15)
- The soul inspired with its wickedness and piety: compare the rabbinic good and evil inclinations (yetzer ha-ra' and yetzer ha-tov) and the two spirits of 1QS 3-4.

**The forenoon and the expansion: the orphan prophet consoled** (93:1-11, 94:1-8)
- Exod 22:21-23 (do not afflict the orphan). The opening of the breast is later narrated as a physical operation by angels (Muslim, Iman 261).

**The fig and the olive, Mount Sinai and the secure city** (95:1-8)
- Deut 33:2 (Sinai, Seir, Paran) is read in Muslim polemic as Moses, Jesus and Muhammad, a triad that matches the medieval reading of 95:1-3.

**The clot: recite! and the forelock** (96:1-19)
- Isa 40:6 ('a voice says: call/read! qera')' and Isa 29:12 (the one who cannot read); compare the 'recite' commission of the prophet with Ezek 2:8-3:3.

**The Night of Decree** (97:1-5)
- Compare Shavuot as the night of the giving of the Torah (with all-night study), and Rosh Hashanah or Yom Kippur as the night when the year's decrees are written (m. Rosh Hash. 1:2).

**The clear proof** (98:1-8)
- Hanif: compare Syriac hanpa ('pagan') and the Abrahamic 'pure monotheist' of 3:67.

**The earthquake: the earth tells its news** (99:1-8)
- Isa 26:21 ('the earth will disclose her blood'); Gen 4:10-11 (the earth that opened its mouth to the blood).

**The chargers** (100:1-11)
- Job 39:19-25 (the war-horse) and Judg 5:22 (galloping hooves).

**The striking day: moths, wool and the scales** (101:1-11)
- Weighing of souls: Egyptian Book of the Dead 125, Testament of Abraham 12-13, Dan 5:27, Zoroastrian Rashnu's scales at the Chinvat bridge.

**Rivalry, time and the slanderer** (102:1-8, 103:1-3, 104:1-9)
- Luke 12:16-21 (the rich fool) for wealth thought to make one immortal.

**The companions of the elephant** (105:1-5)
- Tradition: Abraha's Abyssinian army with an elephant marching on Mecca (c. 570); compare 2 Kgs 19:35 (the angel destroys Sennacherib's army before Jerusalem) and Herodotus 2.141 (mice destroy Sennacherib's army).
- Sijjil also rains on Lot's city (11:82, 15:74).

**Quraysh, small kindnesses and al-Kawthar** (106:1-4, 107:1-7, 108:1-3)
- Isa 1:11-17 and Amos 5:21-24 for ritual without justice; Matt 6:5 for praying to be seen.

**The disbelievers, the help, and the flame** (109:1-6, 110:1-3, 111:1-5)
- 1 Sam 25:25 (Nabal, 'as his name is, so is he').

**Sincerity, daybreak and mankind: God's unity and the two refuges** (112:1-4, 113:1-5, 114:1-6)
- Ps 91 was recited against demons (y. Shabb. 6:2; 11QApocryphal Psalms). Knot magic: Akkadian Maqlu incantations untie the witch's knots; compare Ezek 13:18-20 (women sewing bands to hunt souls).
- Deut 6:4 for 112:1; the Nicene 'begotten not made' as the polemical target of 112:3.
